Kif11 perturbation was uncoupled from a canonical mitotic spindle assembly/chromosome congression mRNA program in this dataset: Kif11-associated neighbors including Nek6, Nek9, Tpx2, Kif23, Cep55, Cenpe, Cdc20, Cdk1, Bub1, Bub1b, Aspm, Dlgap5, and Ttk did not show coordinated shifts, with reported mitotic neighbors remaining at FDR=1.0. This suggests the literature-derived KIF11 spindle pathway was not engaged in the sampled neuronal transcriptomic readout, though absent mRNA changes do not exclude effects on spindle protein function, progenitor phenotypes, or morphology outside the measured mostly postmitotic brain cell classes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Max perturbation repeatedly de-repressed the meiotic cohesin gene Stag3 across five neuronal subclasses—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut—and Mga perturbation induced Stag3 in the two Mga-responsive glutamatergic classes, consistent with a shared MAX/MGA/PRC1.6 germline-meiotic silencing axis in post-mitotic neurons. Stag3 was the only genome-wide recurrently significant meiotic gene response, while Obscn also rose in this pathway context, and the pineal glutamatergic class had very few Max-perturbed cells.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Fmr1 perturbation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut produced an exploratory, internally mixed RHO/ROCK signal: Rock1 was nominally up while Rock2 was nominally down, so the two ROCK paralogs did not support a single pathway direction. Because this STRING pathway annotation was driven only by Rock1 and Rock2, both nominal DE rows with FDR=1.0, the result is better interpreted as possible pathway uncoupling rather than generic ROCK activation or inhibition. This cell type also showed the strongest downstream Fmr1-perturbation row despite only weak measured Fmr1 depletion and weak cross-perturbation correlations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ppp2r5d loss was sparse and did not resemble a scaled-down copy of Ppp2r1a loss: across the same 22 cell classes, Ppp2r1a produced broad transcriptional engagement, whereas Ppp2r5d yielded only two FDR-significant gene-level effects and near-zero same-cell signed correlations with Ppp2r1a in engaged classes including 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. In 191 MB P MY GABA, Ppp2r5d mRNA was depleted without significant non-target changes, and Ppp2r2b lacked usable target engagement, so it could not serve as a biological B55-beta contrast; Ppp2r1a also had somewhat higher cell counts than Ppp2r5d.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Cux2 perturbation produced almost no robust non-target transcriptional response overall; the lone significant hit was Sun1 up-regulation in 053 Sst Gaba, where Cux2 itself showed no detectable decrease. This makes the signal more consistent with an exploratory Sst/Sun1 biomarker candidate than with a coherent CUX2-linked nuclear-envelope program. Interpretation is limited because only 51 perturbed Sst cells were analyzed and on-target Cux2 engagement was absent, so off-target, guide-composition, or sampling effects remain plausible.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Ptpa knockdown produced focal, buffered transcriptional effects that were not interchangeable with loss of the PP2A scaffold Ppp2r1a. In the same engaged cell types—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut—Ppp2r1a showed broad responses with 1666, 649, and 43 FDR<0.1 genes, whereas Ptpa had only 16, 2, and 4, and the all-gene score correlations were near zero. This divergence recurred across other Ptpa-responsive cell types, although the comparison is transcriptional and Ppp2r1a knockdown was deeper than Ptpa in some contexts.

Ppp2r2b did not recapitulate the strong PP2A-scaffold perturbation seen with Ppp2r1a in this in vivo transcriptomic screen. Whereas Ppp2r1a produced a large response, with 3,147 significant gene-by-cell-type effects and a clear self-transcript reduction, Ppp2r2b produced no significant effects and Ppp2r5d only two, and Ppp2r2b profiles were essentially uncorrelated with both comparators. These results separate core-scaffold loss from B-regulatory-subunit perturbation in PP2A holoenzyme biology, although the readout does not directly measure PP2A phosphatase activity or subunit-specific substrates.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut
full_finding_text: Npr2 showed no useful convergent or opposite signature neighbor in the assayed dataset. In the two nominally engaged IT glutamatergic classes, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 001 L5-6 IT Glut, Npr2 self-transcript was mostly down, but there were no FDR-corrected downstream genes and whole-library neighbors remained tiny, with strongest non-self correlations |r|<0.077. Loose cGMP-related perturbations Gucy2c, Gucy2e, and Pde3a correlated only from -0.088 to +0.061 with Npr2, and direct CNP ligand or NPR1/NPR3 perturbations were not assayed, limiting interpretation of the CNP/NPR2 to cGMP signaling context.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Timp3 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal class showed the only FDR-significant Timp3 mRNA depletion across profiled cell types, yet its response was transcriptionally buffered with sparse downstream differential expression. In the same class, the related paralog Timp2 was knocked down even more strongly, but the two perturbations remained almost purely on-target and their score vectors were weakly anticorrelated rather than convergent. Thus, within this assay, Timp2 did not mimic Timp3, although this divergence is based on mRNA signatures and only Timp2 was available as a TIMP-family comparator.

Tlk2 perturbation left the known TLK2–TLK1–ASF1 chromatin-assembly module largely transcript-uncoupled: across all measured cell types, Tlk1, Asf1a, and Asf1b mRNA were not significantly changed, even though Tlk2 itself was only modestly reduced. This suggests downstream RNA output is buffered and that the expected direct effects of the TLK2–ASF1 axis are more likely to be evident at the level of TLK2 activity, heterodimerization, autophosphorylation, ASF1 phosphorylation, or protein stability rather than transcript abundance.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Nr1d2 perturbation most reproducibly increased the paralog Nr1d1, with FDR-significant Nr1d1 upregulation in three neuronal groups: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. Across the Nr1d2 perturbation slice, the only FDR<0.05 genes were Nr1d1 rows, and nonparalog differential expression was otherwise weak, consistent with a focused de-repression/paralog-buffering response in the REV-ERB/ROR circadian and broader nuclear receptor transcription context. In the thalamic group, Rora showed an opposite-signed effect on Nr1d1, while the pineal glutamatergic result was based on only 32 perturbed cells and Nr1d2 mRNA itself was not FDR-depleted.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nr1d2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells increases Nr1d1, whereas Rora perturbation in the same thalamic glutamatergic group decreases Nr1d1, giving an opposite-signed contrast on the same readout. This pattern is consistent with a REV-ERB/ROR circadian transcriptional feedback or broader nuclear receptor repressor-versus-activator relationship, and Nr1d1 is the strongest FDR hit in the primary Nr1d2-responsive group, with only a weak shared nonparalog module. However, the data show signed perturbation effects rather than direct RORA or NR1D2 occupancy at the neuronal Nr1d1 locus.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Thoc2 showed weak same-direction signature convergence with other TREX components rather than a strong interchangeable effect: in 052 Pvalb Gaba, Thoc1 was the top positive all-gene neighbor of Thoc2 and Ddx39b ranked second, consistent with a shared TREX-mediated mRNA export and mRNA 3'-end processing context, and this was the only cell type with genome-wide FDR-significant genes after Thoc2 perturbation, without a stress-marker program. However, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Thoc2 produced only a ranked non-FDR response, whereas Thoc1 showed a much stronger signature, with 303 FDR genes versus 0 for Thoc2; these correlations were modest overall, and Thoc2 had fewer perturbed cells than Thoc1 in the thalamic comparison.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ranbp2 depletion produced its clearest target-engaged signature in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons, where Ranbp2 itself was significantly reduced and a 56-gene FDR-significant response included RNA-processing or nuclear-protein genes such as Rbm15, Srrm2, Snrnp200, Rbm8a, Pcbp1, Utp3, and Kmt2a. The pattern was mixed in direction and showed weak positive similarity to Tpr and Tnpo3 signatures, consistent with a SUMOylation/nuclear-pore RanGTPase and RNA-processing response. This pathway interpretation is enrichment-based, and the transcriptome does not identify direct SUMOylation substrates.

Zswim6 did not phenocopy Sin3a in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq assay, despite a SIN3-like repressive chromatin context in prior reports. Across the same 20 profiled classes, Sin3a produced 2,653 FDR-significant rows, whereas Zswim6 produced none, and full-transcriptome Zswim6-versus-Sin3a correlations remained near zero. The divergence was evident in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, where Sin3a responses were strong but Zswim6 target-RNA effects were weak or absent; however, weak Zswim6 engagement leaves open that ineffective perturbation, rather than distinct biochemistry, explains the lack of similarity.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Tpr showed a nuclear-pore perturbation pattern that partially converged with Ranbp2 but diverged sharply from Nup93, indicating subcomplex-specific rather than generic nucleoporin effects. In 155 MB Glut, Tpr had the strongest response with 2,578 significant genes and measurable Tpr/Ranbp2 similarity, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Tpr had 1,768 significant genes with strong Xpo1 and Ranbp6 induction but no significant Ranbp2 or Nup93 response; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed an intermediate Tpr response with partial Ranbp2 similarity. Nup93 was transcriptionally silent across tested subclasses and lacked a significant self-transcript decrease, so differences in guide efficiency remain a caveat.

Zfp1 showed no coherent Zfp1-like or anti-Zfp1 perturbation in restricted signature-neighbor scans across all 23 profiled mouse-brain cell types. Using only the 100 largest absolute Zfp1 Wilcoxon-score genes per cell type, correlations with other perturbations never reached |r| ≥ 0.48, so convergence or opposition with assayed targets such as Rusc2, Igsf8, Satb2, or Elp1 was not evident. This weak, noisy analysis, together with mixed nonsignificant on-target RNA changes and no q<0.10 downstream genes, argues against over-assigning the faint Zfp1 signature to another receptor, transcription factor, or signaling pathway.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Nr1d1 shows an asymmetric transcript-level compensatory response to Rev-erb paralog perturbation: targeting Nr1d2 increases Nr1d1 RNA in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells, whereas reciprocal Nr1d1-to-Nr1d2 compensation in the TH class is only weak. In the responsive TH stratum, core and clock-output genes change selectively and mostly positively, with Bmal1 and Nr1d1 perturbations broadly concordant over the TH effector signature but opposite for Dbp/Nr1d genes. This compensation is inferred from RNA, not NR1D1 or NR1D2 protein, and the pineal result has a 32-cell caveat.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Nr2c2 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut showed an opposing relationship with Nr2f2: Nr2f2 was the strongest anti-neighbor among tested nuclear receptors, with anticorrelated score vectors across 17,067 genes (r = -0.252). This contrasts with a curated NR2C2-NR2F2 NuRD/telomeric-chromatin relationship from human ALT cancer cells, suggesting that NR2 family cooperation may be context specific rather than directly transferable to mouse excitatory neurons. The result is exploratory because Nr2f2 had only 48 perturbed CA3 cells and no FDR < 0.05 genes in CA3.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Slc6a17 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic responding class showed only weak mixed signature-neighbor convergence: the top positive neighbors included synaptic genes such as Grin1, Atp6v0c, and Cask, while Wdfy3 was the strongest negative neighbor, and Cacna1g also appeared among comparators. However, the largest absolute correlation was below 0.15, so these transcriptomic correlations nominate comparators for future work rather than supporting a strong convergent perturbation module, and they do not establish direction or mechanism.

Shank3 did not show an interchangeable Perturb-seq signature with its paralog Shank2: across all shared cell classes, Shank2-versus-Shank3 all-gene score correlations were approximately zero, with Shank2 also engaging a different target cell class. This divergence was seen in the postsynaptic-density glutamatergic scaffold context, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, involving Shank3, Shank2, Dlg4, Dlgap4, Homer2, Grin1, and Grin2b. Both signatures were sparse, so the near-zero correlation may reflect weak acute transcriptional coupling rather than opposite synaptic physiology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Usp48 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed an exploratory, restricted 38-gene nominal top-tail signature that aligned positively with Kdm4c, Adnp, and Chd4, while opposing Trip12 and Arid2, suggesting a chromatin-regulator-like module with an opposite ubiquitin-ligase neighbor. This pattern was limited to the Usp48 nominal tail: whole-transcriptome correlations were weak, and no direct USP48–ADNP–CHD4 mechanism was established. In this dominant Usp48-responsive population, target mRNA decreased nominally and ten genes were FDR-significant.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Trio perturbation showed a recurrent but cell-type-restricted Jun upregulation rather than a universal transcriptional program. Jun was FDR-significantly increased in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 155 MB Glut, and was nominally up in 8 of 23 Trio contrasts. This pattern is consistent with a restricted JUN/AP-1 immediate-early stress or activity-like response. In two of the FDR-significant Jun contexts, Trio target depletion itself was only nominal, so the module is hypothesis-generating and would benefit from guide-level or orthogonal validation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Trrap showed an exploratory, cell-type-restricted signature-neighbor pattern in six strongest responsive classes—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut—where the top-100-gene Trrap signature was modestly similar to Camta1, Phf12, Brd4, Supt16, and Prpf6 perturbations, but opposite to Kansl1. This places Trrap within a broader NuA4/SAGA histone-acetylation scaffold response or chromatin/transcriptional state, while remaining exploratory because correlations were modest, limited to restricted gene sets, and do not imply direct protein interaction.

Sos2 did not phenocopy Sos1: across 20 matched cell types, whole-transcriptome Sos2 and Sos1 perturbation signatures were centered near zero correlation, indicating uncorrelated single-gene effects despite both genes belonging to the SOS-family RAS-GEF module. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Sos2 was not detected while related RTK-SOS-RAS/MAPK nodes such as Nf1, Map2k1, Braf, Ntrk2, Vgf, Ptpn5, Atp2a2, and Etv5 were detectable. Because the Sos2 signature was weak and no Sos1/Sos2 double perturbation was tested, the safest interpretation is paralog buffering or failed engagement rather than an opposite mechanism.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Snrpn showed a buffered perturbation profile across eight target-engaged neuronal classes, diverging sharply from the related snRNP gene Snrnp70. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Snrpn generally had almost no downstream FDR-significant response, with only Pja1 detected in 005, whereas Snrnp70 showed tens to hundreds of hits; score correlations were near zero, consistent with distinct spliceosomal positions and sparse signature comparisons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Zfhx2 did not form a detectable shared module with the related zinc-finger-homeobox paralogs Zfhx3 or Zfhx4, nor with its strongest genome-wide signature neighbors. In the assayed cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Zfhx2 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Zfhx3 and Zfhx4, and no same-cell comparison exceeded |r|=0.0847; the best positive or negative genome-wide neighbors also stayed below |r|=0.2. This weak, near-null Zfhx2 signature means the low correlations indicate no detectable shared perturbation state rather than mechanistic opposition, even though Zfhx3 or Zfhx4 showed isolated hits such as Tagln3 or Sccpdh in other contexts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Slc9a9 showed weak, largely uncorrelated transcriptional signatures even where the V-ATPase accessory-gene comparator Atp6ap1 produced strong on-target knockdown and reduced Atp6v0a1, notably in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and with detectable target knockdown in 054 CNU-MGE GABA. This contrast in the V-ATPase-mediated organelle acidification context suggests that the assay could detect a pH-related perturbation, yet Slc9a9 did not engage a comparable or opposite robust transcriptional axis. Because Atp6ap1 is a pathway neighbor rather than an obligate SLC9A9 partner, the comparison is informative but not a direct complex test.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zfat showed no strong whole-transcriptome neighbor in the perturbation library, including essentially zero correlation with Setd1a, in the two engaged glutamatergic cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. Although Setd1a RNA was recurrently increased and D6Wsu163e decreased, this appeared to be a local shared feature rather than a global SETD1A-like state, despite the SET1A/COMPASS H3K4 methyltransferase complex context. In these cell types, the best non-Zfat genome-wide correlations were weak (|r|≤0.075), and sparse signatures may have limited correlation magnitude.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ap3b2 showed no robust convergent signature with its AP-3 beta paralog Ap3b1. In the four Ap3b2-engaged cell types—005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut—Ap3b2 knockdown was FDR confirmed, but secondary AP-3/BLOC-1 pathway transcripts were not FDR remodeled, and genome-wide neighbors were weak. The Ap3b1 comparator was underpowered, with only 23–85 perturbed cells per shared cell type and no FDR-significant on-target depletion, yielding very small Ap3b2–Ap3b1 correlations (r=0.009–0.022).

Agtr1a did not phenocopy the available angiotensin receptor-neighborhood perturbations Agtr2 or Agtrap in this Perturb-seq dataset. None of the three perturbations produced an FDR-significant transcriptional signature, and the genome-wide Wilcoxon-score vectors for Agtr2 and Agtrap were nearly uncorrelated with Agtr1a. Because all three signatures were weak and the target library sampled only a small subset of the angiotensin receptor neighborhood, this mainly indicates a failure to recover a shared angiotensin module in this readout rather than evidence of true biological opposition.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gabrb1 diverged from related GABA-A receptor subunit perturbations rather than phenocopying them. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Gabrb2 strongly depleted its target and upregulated the activity-response genes Nr4a1 and Vgf, with Fos and Npas4 near the significance threshold, whereas Gabrb1 left these genes near baseline. In 155 MB Glut, Gabrg2 induced Vgf but Gabrb1 did not, despite nominal Gabrb1 depletion. This separates beta1 from beta2/gamma2 at the transcriptional-phenotype level, although the stronger on-target effects for Gabrb2 and Gabrg2 mean weaker Gabrb1 perturbation could contribute to the difference.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|308 CB GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Qrich1 perturbation produced a recurrent, mostly downregulated neuronal transcriptomic module centered on Scn2b, Celf3, Ldhd, and Tlcd3b across responsive classes, with 120 of 142 significant rows decreased overall. The strongest signature was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, and the same direction recurred in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, hypothalamic, thalamic, and cerebellar classes, arguing against a single thalamic outlier. These genes appear to be better downstream readouts than the weak Qrich1 mRNA row, although the dataset is transcriptomic only and does not measure protein levels or electrophysiology.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Bcap31 depletion in five on-target neuronal classes—066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—did not induce a canonical ER-stress or integrated-stress transcriptional program: Bcap29, Tomm40, Ndufs4, Ndufb11, Dnm1l, Atf4, Ddit3, Xbp1, Hspa5, and Herpud1 showed no adjusted expression changes. This separates the acute neuronal phenotype from a typical UPR readout and, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, diverged from Dnm1l, which induced Asns, Cars, Ddit3, and Chac1. A fixed marker panel, however, could miss Xbp1 splicing, organelle morphology, respiration, or delayed cell-state effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ap2m1 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed strong convergence with Ap2s1, the top positive perturbation neighbor: 121 of 139 Ap2m1 FDR genes were also significant after Ap2s1 perturbation, and all changed in the same direction. This supports an AP-2 complex phenotype within clathrin-mediated endocytosis rather than an idiosyncratic Ap2m1 guide effect, with Tfrc induction among the reproduced features. Similar convergence was noted in 155 MB Glut, although Ap2s1 often had more perturbed cells and stronger target engagement, so its broader response cannot be attributed solely to subunit biology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rb1 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class showed an S-phase, DNA-replication–enriched 37-gene response whose closest tested signature neighbor was Tfdp1, consistent with an E2F/DP-centered interpretation. By contrast, E2f1, Cdkn2a, and Trp53 perturbations did not converge on this Rb1 loss signature, despite being well powered, and a separable E2f4 module was noted. This comparison was restricted to the 37 Rb1-responsive genes, and on-target mRNA engagement for several comparators was weak or not significant, so upstream or downstream single hits were not interchangeable with Rb1.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Alkbh8 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was uncoupled from the strong Elp1/Elp2 amino-acid-starvation and integrated-stress-response-like program: whereas Elp1 and Elp2 induced a large ASNS, CHAC1, CARS, and DDIT3 module, Alkbh8 showed no corrected hits and did not coherently induce these markers. Alkbh8 still had weak positive similarity to Elp1 and Elp2 in this cell type, suggesting at most a faint pathway echo within tRNA wobble-uridine modification rather than an opposite response. Interpretation is limited because Alkbh8 target mRNA knockdown was not measurable, and related-target comparisons were restricted mainly to Elp1, Elp2, and Cdkal1.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Ascc3 produced a recurrent down-regulated App/Aplp2/Atp1a3/Atp2a2/Clstn1/Serinc1/Srrm2 module across otherwise distinct neurons, rather than cell-type-private top genes. This compact negative signature appeared in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, with the strongest response in midbrain glutamatergic neurons and only a nominal tail in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. The recurrent down genes were enriched for neuronal endomembrane, vesicle, synapse, and neurite compartments, but the inference is from RNA changes and does not establish protein-level APP or ATP1A3 pathway direction.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pola1 did not show detectable convergence with a canonical replication-stress or p53 module in this dataset. Across diverse neuronal cell types, including multiple cortical glutamatergic classes, GABAergic populations, thalamic, midbrain, pineal, and cerebellar cells, the available Atr and Trp53 perturbations were weak and score-uncorrelated with Pola1. Direct Polα-primase comparators such as Pola2, Prim1, Prim2, and Wdhd1 were not assayed, so the lack of convergence reflects missing matched complex partners and weak neighbour signatures rather than demonstrated divergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Stag2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a signature that converged with the core cohesin/cohesin-loader axis: Smc1a, Smc3, and Nipbl phenocopied the Stag2 top-gene pattern, and Smc1a and Nipbl shared corrected down-regulation of Ptprm, Necab2, Smtn, and Adamts2. In contrast, Stag1 was near zero and Pds5a was weak, suggesting the Stag2 response tracks core cohesin/loader perturbations more than the Stag1 paralog or Pds5a in this neuronal class. This comparison is caveated because correlations were computed only over the Stag2 top 200 genes, and Stag1/Pds5a target engagement was weak at the transcript level.

Nsmce2 showed a largely orthogonal transcriptomic response in this dataset, with essentially zero whole-signature correlation to assayed DNA-damage, cohesin, and SUMO-pathway neighbors including Atr, Mcph1, Trp53, Ranbp2, Smc1a, Smc3, Stag1, Stag2, and Nipbl. Although curated pathway resources place NSMCE2 near SMC5/6, SUMOylation, and cohesin biology, perturbing these nearby genes did not phenocopy the Nsmce2 mRNA profile, and no robust positive or negative transcriptional neighbor was detected. A caveat is that most core SMC5/6 subunits were not themselves perturbed here.

Atr perturbation did not detectably induce canonical ATR replication-stress or p53-mediated DNA-damage transcriptional programs: Cdkn1a, Mdm2, Gadd45a, Ddb2, Rrm2b, Trp53inp1, Bbc3, Pmaip1, Bax, Ccng1, Ddit4, and ATR-pathway neighbors including Chek1, Clspn, Cdc25a, Topbp1, Atm, and Prkdc were all FDR-null. Thus, the dataset lacks an expected CHK1/TP53 mRNA footprint of productive ATR checkpoint perturbation, although this may reflect that ATR signaling is phosphorylation-centered and that steady-state mRNA after weak Atr perturbation can miss pathway activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nr1d1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a selective Rev-erb-compatible clock-output response rather than wholesale core-clock derepression: Npas2, Cry2, Dbp, Ciart, and Nfil3 increased, Arntl was only nominally induced, and Clock and Nr1d2 were not FDR-significant. The target RNA itself was not significantly depleted, and the readout comes from steady-state single-cell RNA rather than a time course, so some core-clock effects may be phase-diluted. Within pathway context, Nr1d1 loss increased selected clock outputs, with broad concordance to Bmal1 over the TH effector signature but opposite behavior for Dbp and Nr1d genes.

Rars2 perturbation did not produce a canonical mitochondrial-translation or OXPHOS RNA program: across mtDNA-encoded and nuclear respiratory-chain transcripts, signals were FDR-null and mixed in direction, including mt-Co2, mt-Cytb, mt-Nd1, Uqcrc2, Ndufb10, and Ndufa2. This was also FDR-null in 308 CB GABA cells, arguing against a pontocerebellar-selective RNA signature. The pattern was nonconvergent with related mitochondrial tRNA aminoacylation and translation perturbations such as Fars2, Lars2, and Gfm2, and is consistent with a primary defect acting at aminoacylation, translation, respiration, or protein homeostasis rather than acute mRNA loss, with the caveat that only mRNA was measured.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gpx4 showed low transcriptomic similarity to its direct ferroptosis/redox neighbors: across DE score profiles, correlations with STRING-linked genes such as Gclc, Gclm, Nfe2l2, Acsl4, Tfrc, and Fth1 were essentially absent, with maximum |r| below 0.17. Its strongest genome-wide neighbors were still weak, concentrated in the 308 CB GABA cell type, and even included a safe-targeting control among top positive correlations, alongside targets such as Ranbp2 and Wdr26. This pattern suggests no clearly recoverable GPX4-specific module, while noting that STRING links are functional associations rather than expected same-direction transcriptomic effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cic showed its strongest positive signature neighbor as Atxn1 specifically in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where Cic and Atxn1 perturbations converged transcriptome-wide in the same direction. In this thalamic subclass, the shared pattern included increased Aldh1l2, Ankrd55, and Scg3 and decreased Trim9, Lrrc7, and Grin2c, supporting activity of the CIC-ATXN1 transcriptional repressor complex in these neurons. This convergence is based on RNA signatures rather than protein-complex occupancy, and ATXN1L was not available as a comparator.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Kmt2e showed weak but reproducible empirical signature neighbors, with Hnrnpu the top positive whole-transcriptome neighbor in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells and Ddx23 also positive in both. The strongest anticorrelations, including with Phf12, Huwe1, Nrf1, and Camta1, were also small. In these two resolved cell types, Kmt2e responses did not align with KMT2-family or Ogt comparators, so the Hnrnpu/Ddx23 relationship is best viewed as a low-amplitude signature-level follow-up hypothesis rather than a demonstrated direct interaction.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Adamts17 showed no hidden robust Adamts17-like module in signature-neighbor analysis. The strongest all-gene score correlations were weak, mixed in direction, and concentrated in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 308 CB GABA, with examples including Cd3d (r=0.250) and Sec31a (r=-0.302) in 066, and Wdr26 (r=-0.247) in 308; other neighbors included B9d1 and Adam22. Because all reported correlations were below |r|=0.31 and leading genes remained FDR=1.0, these results are best treated as negative or exploratory evidence rather than support for a shared ADAMTS17 complex or pathway.

Wdr48 perturbation showed no detectable transcript-level induction of the canonical WDR48-USP deubiquitinase/Fanconi-PCNA module: across 190 perturbation-by-cell-type tests, Usp1, Usp12, Usp46, Wdr20, Fanci, Fancd2, Pcna, Rad18, Rad51ap1, and Atad5 had no nominally significant expression changes. This suggests the assayed RNA readouts were transcriptionally uncoupled from expected WDR48-linked activity, with the important caveat that only selected pathway transcripts were examined and direct protein-level endpoints such as FANCD2 or PCNA ubiquitination were not measured.

Lrrfip1 did not phenocopy nearby beta-catenin/Wnt or innate nucleic-acid-signaling perturbations in this Perturb-seq compendium: signatures from Ctnnb1, Apc, Tcf7l2, Gsk3b, Ddx3x, Dhx9, Tbk1, Irf3, and Irf7 were essentially uncorrelated with Lrrfip1, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells where several of those neighbors showed FDR-significant programs while Lrrfip1 did not. This argues against a shared basal neuronal axis here, although weak Lrrfip1 perturbation could deflate correlations, and direct comparators Flii and Lrrfip2 were not tested.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Stx16 showed a buffered Perturb-seq response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with target repression but no FDR-significant Stx16 trans genes, and its signature was only weakly correlated with related endosome-to-trans-Golgi SNARE/GARP trafficking perturbations including Vps54, Vps53, and Stxbp1. In the same cell type, Vps54 produced a strong downstream signature with 31 significant rows, yet Vps54 mRNA was not detectably reduced, so this GARP/STX16 contrast is exploratory and suggests that pathway membership alone did not yield transcriptomic interchangeability here.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Trpm7 showed a weak, cell-type-restricted convergence in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT glutamatergic neurons, where its signature was selectively closest to a Cnnm2-linked magnesium-homeostasis neighborhood. In this cell type, Cnnm2 ranked sixth among Trpm7 signature neighbors and shared seven same-direction p<0.01 genes with Trpm7, alongside neighbors such as Cadm2, Kcnj6, and Prkaa2. However, the Trpm7 row and all 009 Trpm7 genes had FDR=1.0, so this appears to be a modest signature-level similarity rather than a broad ion-channel response, and it was not seen broadly across other assayed channel or PI3K-mTOR perturbations.

Hivep3 perturbation in resting mouse brain cells showed no coordinated induction of the NF-kappa-B/TNF/JNK/AP-1 inflammatory program across the 23 measured cell classes. Marker transcripts including Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Rela, Relb, Nfkbia, Nfkbiz, Traf1, Traf2, Tnf, Tnfrsf1a, Mapk8, Mapk9, Fos, Jun, and Il6 were not coordinately induced, and no corrected target-transcript reduction was detected. This contrasts with literature placing ZAS3/HIVEP3 upstream of TRAF2, RELA nuclear transport, and kappa-B-mediated transcription, but the assay context was unstimulated brain and Hivep3 transcript engagement was weak, limiting pathway-direction inference.

Ptpn11 perturbation did not show the expected strong inverse relationship with the RASopathy regulators Nf1 or Spred1 in these mature neuronal transcriptomes. Instead, cross-perturbation similarities were weak to near zero, with mean absolute restricted correlations around 0.06, arguing that these positive and negative RAS/MAPK regulators are not interchangeable as a simple pathway switch. This pattern was noted in the 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cell type, where nominal Nf1-down context appeared, but the Spred1 comparison is less certain because on-target knockdown was weak in this dataset.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Alx4 was uncoupled from the detectable LEF1/CTNNB1 Wnt-linked transcriptional program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. In the same dataset, Ctnnb1 perturbation produced a strong signature with hundreds of significant genes, including decreases in Ctnnb1, Lef1, and Axin2, but the Alx4–Ctnnb1 score-vector correlation in this class was essentially zero (r=0.00077). Alx4 also showed no rank-shifted expression response in any tested mouse-brain cell type, suggesting absent or very sparse target expression rather than validated knockdown; this comparison reflects separately summarized signatures, not direct ALX4–CTNNB1 co-occupancy or protein interaction in neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Akap11 loss in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class did not phenocopy Prkaca, Prkar1a, or Gsk3b perturbation: full-signature transcriptomic correlations were near zero even though these comparator genes were detectably perturbed in the same class. This suggests the Akap11 signature is not simply explained by reduced bulk PKA catalytic activity, PKA regulatory subunit abundance, or GSK3B abundance within the localized AKAP11-PKA-PP1-GSK3B scaffold signaling context. The comparison is transcriptomic, however, and does not exclude shared phosphoproteomic or subcellular signaling effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Setx showed no corrected differential-expression response in this dataset, even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells where Setx counts were highest or transcript reduction was nominally seen. In contrast, the RNA-processing neighbors Dhx9, Ddx23, and Xrn1 were clearly detectable in the same assay, with 243, 346, and 36 significant calls concentrated in thalamic and midbrain populations. This suggests the Setx null is specific to this perturbation or to SETX biology rather than a general inability to detect RNA-helicase or RNA-processing stress, though these comparators are pathway neighbors rather than SETX complex members.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ppp2r1a knockdown produced much larger transcriptional responses than Ppp2r5d, Ppp2r2b, or Ptpa knockdown in matched cell classes, notably 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. In these classes, Ppp2r1a yielded hundreds to over 1000 FDR genes, with recurrent sterol/cholesterol-biosynthesis signals including repression of Srebf2 and Hmgcr in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Ptpa showed on-target reduction but much smaller downstream effects, Ppp2r5d showed little non-target response, and Ppp2r2b engagement was weak.

Zbtb38 perturbation in the assayed mouse-brain cell types did not transcriptionally engage the reported RBBP6-ZBTB38-MCM10 replication-stability axis: Mcm10 was unchanged at the RNA level across all 22 signatures, and Rbbp6 and Usp9x were also not adjusted-significant. This uncoupling is consistent with weak target engagement in mostly postmitotic neuronal contexts, low Mcm10 expression, or differences from the human cycling-cell literature in which excess ZBTB38 represses MCM10. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, the response instead appeared narrow, with Msra significant and near-threshold Abhd12b, without broader MCM10-related engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Foxj1 was largely inactive and uncorrelated with E2f4 in this atlas, whereas E2f4, unlike Foxj1 and E2f5, induced a distinct chromosome/kinetochore/DNA-repair/microtubule program in a restricted set of neurons, notably 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA. The strongest responses included Aaas, Rad18, Tacc3, Tube1, Cenpw, Blm, Ddx11, Polq, Tinf2, and Ccna1, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. These data suggest a cell-cycle or centriole-associated module separate from the Foxj1 motile-cilium branch, but they do not show centriole amplification or cilia formation.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Nr1i2 in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons showed only a weak, FDR-supported two-gene mixed-direction signature, centered on Akr1a1 and Nup214, and this transcriptomic response did not phenocopy perturbations of the RXR partners Rxra, Rxrb, or Rxrg, the CAR paralog Nr1i3, or nearby ligand-activated nuclear receptors Nr1h2, Nr1h3, Nr1h4, and Vdr. In this cell class, those comparators had no FDR hits and near-zero genome-wide correlation with Nr1i2, arguing that the Akr1a1/Nup214 signal is not a generic PXR/RXR xenobiotic-metabolism or drug-transporter module response, although biochemical RXR heterodimerization was not tested.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Got1 showed its strongest positive signature convergence with Mdh1 in thalamic glutamatergic neurons, especially the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, where Mdh1 was the top positive perturbation neighbor and changed several Got1-responsive genes, including Gls, Zcchc7, and Spock2, in the same direction. A second class, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, also showed Got1–Mdh1 convergence despite lacking non-target FDR hits for Got1. In the main responsive class, mitochondrial Got2 was anti-correlated, consistent with a cytosolic malate-aspartate shuttle interpretation, although the comparison used Got1-preselected genes and did not measure metabolite flux directly.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pgk1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed convergence with the spliceosomal perturbation Snrnp70: Snrnp70 knockdown was a positive neighbor of the restricted 27-gene Pgk1 signature and both perturbations decreased Pnisr, Rsrp1, Arglu1, Ogt, and Nrxn1 in the same direction. This pattern, together with shared nuclear-speckle and spliceosomal RNA-processing genes such as Pnisr, Rsrp1, Srrm2, Arglu1, and Snrnp70, supports an RNA-processing or nuclear-speckle state within the Pgk1 module rather than an unrelated set of down-regulated genes, while not implying direct physical regulation by PGK1.

Auts2 did not phenocopy assayed pathway neighbors in this dataset: across same-cell-type whole-transcriptome score-vector comparisons with Csnk2b, Ep300, Nrf1, Rac1, Cdc42, Ctnnb1, and Ski, correlations were essentially absent, with a median Pearson r of 0.008 and maximum |r| of 0.174. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class, where Auts2 showed its only FDR-significant downstream gene, Dpysl4, Nrf1, Ctnnb1, and Csnk2b had stronger signatures yet remained uncorrelated with Auts2, arguing that AUTS2-complex, RAC1/CDC42, or β-catenin perturbations are not interchangeable RNA-seq readouts here, while not excluding non-transcriptional AUTS2 effects or variable editing efficiency.

Kbtbd7 perturbation did not recapitulate known KBTBD7-CUL3 substrate pathways at the mRNA level in this mouse brain dataset. Across all 21 Kbtbd7-tested cell classes, on-target Kbtbd7 rows were present but showed weak target engagement, with no significant knockdown, no FDR-significant changes in Nf1, Tiam1, Rac1, or Pten, and near-zero signature correlation with Cul3, Tiam1, Rac1, or Cdc42 perturbations. This was largely uncoupled in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut as well, aside from exploratory inverse Rac1-restricted patterns in those two classes.

Zfp280c did not phenocopy Ctcf, cohesin-subunit, or Smchd1 perturbations in the assayed mouse brain nuclei: across matched neuronal classes, its transcriptomic signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Ctcf, Smc1a, Smc3, Stag1, Stag2, and Smchd1 perturbations. Thus, the colorectal-cancer mechanism linking ZNF280C to H3K27me3-marked repression at CTCF/cohesin-bound loci through SMCHD1 was not recapitulated here, suggesting that any Zfp280c-dependent chromatin regulation is cell-state dependent or absent under these conditions. This comparison is transcriptomic and does not directly measure chromatin occupancy, H3K27me3, or CTCF/cohesin binding.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mest perturbation in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal class did not activate a coherent LRP6/canonical Wnt program: a 21-gene Wnt/β-catenin panel showed no FDR-significant or directionally consistent response, including genes such as Axin2 and Fzd3, and the Mest signature was essentially uncorrelated with Ctnnb1, Lrp5, Lrp6, or Gsk3b perturbations. This class could mount a β-catenin-related response under comparator perturbation, so the result suggests that in these assayed neurons, Mest is uncoupled from acute canonical Wnt transcriptional output, with the caveat that the assay measured pooled transcriptomes rather than LRP6 glycosylation or β-catenin protein activity.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Purg did not produce a reproducible downstream transcriptional module: across measured genes and cell types, the perturbation showed no transcriptome-wide significant response, and the small nominal gene lists were sparse, sign-inconsistent, and lacked any FDR-supported direction. In 308 CB GABA, where the strongest signature neighbors appeared, full-signature correlations to other perturbations were still weak, with the largest absolute correlation only |r|=0.245, so isolated nominal hits such as Slc12a5, Kif1a, Vps39, and Calr, or weak neighbors including Msx2 and Ranbp2, should be interpreted cautiously. Because signatures were compared by global score correlation, a small shared subset could have been missed, but the starting Purg signature itself lacked FDR-supported genes.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Kdm6a in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut showed only a subthreshold transcriptional response: Kdm6a itself decreased nominally, Vrk1 was the strongest induced gene with FDR 0.066, and no gene reached FDR<0.05. In restricted top-500 signature space, however, the Kdm6a profile was closest in the same direction to Hdac5, Kmt2b, and Sin3a, with genes such as Camk2n1, Kcnip2, and Tafa1 contributing to an exploratory chromatin-regulator neighborhood. This pattern is hypothesis-generating only, as the correlations may reflect shared weak or generic effects rather than a definitive pathway.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Snf8 showed a weak but reproducible positive signature convergence with a restricted proteostasis-like module in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 155 MB Glut: Psmc1, Psmc5, Psmb4, and Pomp were repeatedly the strongest positive Snf8 neighbors, alongside Vps37a. This pattern was more consistent than isolated hits such as Rap1gap or Chpf2, but it is exploratory, because the convergence rests on modest all-gene Pearson correlations of weak signatures rather than shared FDR genes or direct evidence that SNF8 regulates proteasomes.

Akap9 loss did not transcriptomically phenocopy other AKAPs or kinase/phosphatase perturbations in this dataset: across correlations with Akap6, Akap11, Prkaca, Prkar1a, Pde4d, Pde4b, Pde10a, and calcineurin or PP2A subunits such as Ppp3ca, Ppp3r1, Ppp2r1a, Ppp2r2b, and Ppp2r5d, the largest absolute Pearson correlation was only 0.096. This suggests the measured AKAP9 response is buffered, localized, or weak rather than a generic centrosomal AKAP9-PKA-PDE cAMP microdomain transcriptional state, although the comparison is limited to transcriptomic signatures and some comparators are pathway neighbors rather than direct AKAP9 complex members.

Kcnb2 showed a transcriptionally weak or null pattern, with nominal hits failing to converge into a recurrent module across the assayed cells. Among 84 nominal p<0.001 rows, 83 were different genes, and the only repeated gene, Max, changed in opposite directions in two cell types. The smallest adjusted p values were isolated Slc30a4, Prrc2b, Kat6a, and Adam23 events, all remaining far from significance with FDR ≥ 0.678. This nominal recurrence analysis therefore supports the primary FDR-level null and argues against a shared Kcnb2-induced pathway, despite related Kv2 channel biology and Kcnb1 divergence in L4-5 IT.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Selenoi in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a sterol/SREBP-related transcriptional signature, and the upstream CDP-ethanolamine enzyme Pcyt2 phenocopied and amplified this response in the same 151 cells. Pcyt2 was the top positive whole-signature neighbor of Selenoi and induced a stronger 21-gene FDR-corrected program including Insig1, Cyp51, Nsdhl, Msmo1, Fdft1, Ldlr, Hmgcr, and Srebf2, consistent with convergence of CDP-ethanolamine/phosphatidylethanolamine synthesis loss on sterol-gene induction. A caveat is that Pcyt2 mRNA itself was not decreased in the Pcyt2 perturbation test, so the comparison rests on concordant downstream signatures rather than measured transcript knockdown.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Far1 showed a weak but coherent sterol-regulatory signature that converged directionally with Marchf6 loss and opposed Srebf2 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. Across these classes, Far1 or Marchf6 perturbation tended to upregulate SREBP2/lanosterol/cholesterol biosynthesis genes including Insig1, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Fdft1, Dhcr24, Msmo1, Cyp51, and Ldlr, whereas Srebf2 loss downregulated the same module. The effect was strongest as nominal induction in middle-brain glutamatergic cells, while global transcriptome similarity to Marchf6 or Srebf2 was weak, so these were pathway-informed comparators rather than robust Far1 phenocopies.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Nf1 perturbation repeatedly produced a Vgf-centered, activity/neurotrophin-like transcriptional response across neurons, with Vgf up in 17 of 22 cell types and FDR-supported in 7, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Selected populations, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, also showed Etv4/Etv5, Egr1, Ptpn5, Scg2, and Unc13a induction, with nominal rather than FDR-level support for Dusp4, Dusp6, and Spry4; these outputs were opposite to Braf/Map2k1/Mapk1 perturbation signatures, although Vgf itself is not specific to NF1.

Greb1l did not recover a coherent RAR/RXR retinoic-acid coactivation module in these sampled brain cells: its Perturb-seq signatures were low, mixed, and not stably aligned in the same direction with Rara, Rarb, Rarg, Rxra, Rxrb, Rxrg, Ncoa1, Ncoa3, or Stra6 perturbations. In 308 CB GABA cells, the restricted top-200 Greb1l projection even placed several Safe_target controls among near neighbors, suggesting proximity to the empirical null. Because comparator signatures were also weak and protein-level target engagement was not validated, the result is best read as weak or uncoupled RA-axis engagement rather than a new wiring model.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Adnp showed its strongest cross-perturbation convergence with Chd4, consistent with a ChAHP/CHD4-associated chromatin-regulation module. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Chd4 was the nearest non-self genome-wide Adnp signature neighbor, and 19 of 25 FDR-significant Adnp genes, including Xylt2, Cpne7, and Ddb2, shifted in the same direction under Chd4; Chd4 was also the nearest non-self neighbor in 155 MB Glut. However, the score correlations were only modest, especially in 155 MB Glut, and Chd4 was not a direct rescue of Adnp.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ahdc1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells reduced Wls, but this response did not resemble canonical Apc-driven Wnt activation: Axin2 and Nkd1 were not significantly induced, and Apc in the same cell class strongly increased Axin2, Nkd1, Notum, and Spock3 while showing only weak overall anticorrelation with Ahdc1. These data nominate Wls as a local Ahdc1-responsive marker within WNT ligand biogenesis and trafficking, but RNA measurements alone do not establish altered WNT secretion or beta-catenin activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Slc9a7 knockdown showed a largely negative RNA-signature result: across the engaged cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 155 MB Glut, Slc9a7 itself was reduced, but no recurrent Golgi, endosomal, synaptic, or other nominal module emerged, every non-target differentially expressed gene remained above FDR 0.05, and the strongest cross-perturbation correlations were near zero (|r|≤0.124). Weak nominal genes such as Slc26a2, Ss18l2, Shisa7, Ppp1r21, and Tnr were cell-type isolated and mixed in direction, with no strong signature neighbors including Scamp5-related comparators, consistent with pathway uncoupling at the transcript level while not excluding post-transcriptional effects on NHE7-dependent compartments.

Setbp1 in the mouse brain Perturb-seq data did not recapitulate the canonical SETBP1–SET–PP2A or SETBP1–HOXA/MYB leukemia programs: across matched cell types, Set and PP2A subunit perturbations (Ppp2r1a, Ppp2r2b, Ppp2r5d) were essentially uncorrelated with the weak Setbp1 signature, Hoxa9 and Hoxa10 were not measured in the Setbp1 rows, and Myb was null. These results refine rather than contradict prior myeloid gain-of-function literature and suggest the brain loss-of-function readout should not be used as a surrogate for oncogenic SETBP1 activation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Akt3 showed only a weak signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, but its nearest perturbation neighbors still recapitulated PI3K-AKT-mTOR topology: Pik3ca, Mtor, and Igf1r were among the closest positive neighbors, whereas Pten, Tsc1, Tsc2, and Gsk3b were among the strongest negative neighbors. This directional pattern is consistent with loss of Akt3 opposing loss of PI3K/mTOR brakes, yet all correlations were small, confined to this borderline-engaged thalamic cell class, and should be treated as an exploratory topology hint rather than a validated pathway activation score.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fzd9 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells did not activate the canonical Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional readout: despite 242 perturbed cells, there were no FDR-significant genes and no evident Axin2 or Nkd1 response. In the same cell class, downstream Wnt-core perturbations were clearly active, with Ctnnb1, Apc, Tcf7l2, Gsk3b, and Lrp6 producing transcriptional effects, indicating that the pathway was competent to report perturbation. Other Frizzled-family receptor perturbations were also mostly weak, and because Fzd9 showed no on-target mRNA depletion, the result cannot distinguish receptor redundancy from ineffective knockdown.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ap2m1 in 155 MB Glut cells showed a compact sterol-response signature in which Srebf2 and Dhcr24 were reduced, with Tfrc increased, suggesting a restricted connection to SREBP-regulated cholesterol biosynthesis rather than the broader thalamic program. This interpretation is strengthened because Ap2s1 reproduced the Srebf2/Dhcr24 decreases and extended them to additional cholesterol-pathway genes including Insig1, Hmgcs1, and Fdft1 in the same cell class. However, Ap2m1 itself had only five FDR genes in 155 MB Glut, so the sterol link remains indirect.

Hoxd13 perturbation in the brain screen did not mobilize the canonical embryonic limb and digit morphogenesis program: across 22 assayed Hoxd13 brain cell types, genome-wide differential expression was broadly FDR-null, and the expected limb-network genes Hand2, Meis1, Meis2, Bmp2, Bmp4, Emx2, Fbn1, Sfrp1, Barx1, Dach1, Shh, Fgf8, Gli3, and Evx2 were absent, filtered, or unchanged after correction. The only nominal Shh changes had opposite signs in two GABA classes, so these neuronal signatures should not be extrapolated to HOXD13 synpolydactyly mechanisms that depend on limb-specific chromatin and target-gene context.

Atp11c targeting did not produce a consistent transcriptional response of the P4-ATPase/aminophospholipid flippase complex across the 20 Atp11c-assayed neuronal cell types. In all assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic subclasses, Atp11a, Atp11b, Atp8a1, Atp8a2, Atp9a, and Tmem30a showed no FDR-supported mRNA changes after Atp11c perturbation; the strongest Tmem30a signals were only nominal and opposite in sign. This pan-neuronal negative result comes from steady-state mRNA measured after weak Atp11c engagement, so it does not address ATP11C-TMEM30A protein localization, flippase activity, or phosphatidylserine exposure.

Cd80 showed no strong convergence with related perturbations or transcriptome-wide signature neighbors in this atlas. Cd40, Icos, and Tnfrsf4 were likewise FDR-null, and the best Cd80-wide neighbor correlation was weak at |r| = 0.180, arguing against a coherent positive or inverse Cd80-like module. Nominal Cd80-ranked genes were not reused across cell types in a consistent direction; in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, the weak top positive and negative neighbors helped underscore the absence of a Cd80-Ngfr-like axis. These correlations are limited to DE score vectors, and the named neighbors are statistical rather than established pathway members.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Herc1 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA showed a transcriptional signature that was uncoupled from Tsc1/Tsc2 loss, arguing against a simple TSC2-mTORC1 explanation in this dataset. Tsc1 and Tsc2 perturbations were stronger than Herc1, with near-zero correlation to the Herc1 signature, and Mtor, Rptor, Tfeb, as well as canonical autophagy and trafficking markers such as Sqstm1, Atg5, Atg16l1, and Ulk1, were not FDR-supported. Interpretation is limited because Herc1 had fewer perturbed cells, and HERC1 effects may be post-translational or require starvation or gain-of-function contexts not modeled here.

Npas3 showed a weak acute Perturb-seq signature in mature neurons, with no genome-wide differentially expressed genes after multiple-testing correction and no clear directional regulation of the previously reported NPAS3-linked program. In this dataset, Fgfr1, Reln, Fmr1, Ube3a, Notch1, Nptxr, and Cnr1 were measured but had mixed score signs and FDR = 1.0, so FGF, reelin, Notch, and Fmr1/Ube3a-related readouts were not recovered. This absence is specific to the weak acute perturbation here and does not refute chronic knockout, hippocampal, or human genetic findings.

Glis2 perturbation in mouse neuronal cell classes did not reveal the renal GLIS2 Hedgehog/Wnt/EMT program: there was no coordinated or significant shift in Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Shh, Wnt4, Snai1, Axin2, Ccnd1, or related cofactors such as Ctnnb1, Ctbp1, Hdac3, Ctnnd1, and Sufu. This contrasts with kidney literature predicting relief of repression on Hedgehog-dependent Wnt4 and Snai1 after stronger GLIS2 loss, so the null neuronal result may reflect weak perturbation or tissue-context differences rather than absence of regulation elsewhere.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kmt2a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons did not phenocopy related H3K4/chromatin perturbations: its score vector was near-orthogonal to Kmt2b, Setd1a, and Brd4, and only weakly anti-correlated with Kmt2d, which was nonetheless the strongest negative signature neighbor genome-wide in this cell type. Several Kmt2a-up genes, including Car4, Cry2, and Cfap74, shifted negative after Kmt2d perturbation. Absolute correlations were small, and this contrast is limited to same-assay score vectors rather than matched chromatin occupancy.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Agps perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells induces an upregulated cholesterol/sterol biosynthetic program centered on Dhcr24, with nominal increases in Cyp51, Sqle, Mvd, Stard4, Fdft1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Ldlr, and Insig1. This was the primary Agps-responsive class and the only Agps stratum with an FDR-significant gene, but only Dhcr24 itself passed FDR<0.05, so the broader module call rests on coherent nominal positive effects and sterol-pathway annotation. The same class shows weak convergence after Far1, Pex13, and Pex14 perturbation, and opposite regulation after Srebf2.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Braf in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed the dataset’s strongest multi-gene response, with down-regulation of a Vgf-centered module including Ptpn5, Atp2a2, and Unc13a, and convergence with Map2k1 plus partial convergence with Shoc2 and Ntrk2 in the same direction. This pattern is consistent with a BDNF–NTRK2–RAF–MEK/ERK transcriptional output, while Nf1 opposed the module and Raf1 did not phenocopy it. Full-transcriptome correlations were positive but small, and Shoc2 target-transcript reduction was weak, so the shared phenotype is best viewed as a transcriptional-signature observation rather than a strong genome-wide match.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Smad2 perturbation showed a weak, recurrent decrease in the SMAD feedback gene Skil/SnoN, with Skil down in 17 of 21 classes and nominally decreased in five, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. This direction is consistent with reduced basal SMAD2-SMAD4 pathway maintenance of a negative-feedback inhibitor, but no Skil result survived FDR correction, so the signal is exploratory and the broader canonical TGF-beta/activin pathway was otherwise mostly FDR-silent.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smc1a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut defined a cohesin-linked expression module that converged with related perturbations: Nipbl and Stag2 reused 18/24 and 9/24 of the Smc1a FDR genes, respectively, all in the same direction, and on the restricted 24-gene Smc1a vector Nipbl, Smc3, and Stag2 ranked 2nd, 3rd, and 6th among 2,046 perturbations by cosine similarity. The shared module included genes such as Ptprm, Necab2, Spon1, Sema5a, and Inhbb. This convergence was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with related contexts appearing null or buffered, and caveats include that the Smc3 similarity was restricted-vector only and Nipbl and Stag2 target transcripts themselves were not FDR significant.

Dock7 showed little transcriptional convergence with Dock3 or with Rac1/Cdc42-PAK/JNK neighbor perturbations, with near-zero score-vector correlations across Dock3, Rac1, Cdc42, Pak1, Pak2, Pak3, Mapk8, and Mapk9. Thus, in these mouse-brain cells, the acute Dock7 RNA signature did not phenocopy the canonical small-GTPase module that prior work places downstream of DOCK7. This was an exploratory score-vector analysis, including a top-200 Dock7-gene restriction, and weak Dock7 engagement could mask true pathway relationships.

Tiam1 did not phenocopy neighboring RAC1/Rho-family GTPase signaling perturbations in this screen: unlike Pten, Nf1, Trio, and Pak1, Tiam1 produced no FDR-significant gene rows, and score-vector correlations with neighbors such as Rac1, Cdc42, Mapk1, and Srgap3 were uniformly weak, with the largest absolute correlation only |r|=0.204 versus Nf1 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut. This remained true even in high-cell-count profiles such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where related perturbations showed corrected DE effects. These comparisons are based on transcriptomic score correlations and FDR-hit counts, not direct RAC1-GTP or PAK activity measurements.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kremen1 was transcriptionally neutral in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, despite this same thalamic population showing clear canonical Wnt-axis responses to Ctnnb1, Apc, Lrp6, and Gsk3b perturbation. In these cells, Apc loss activated Axin2 and Nkd1, whereas Ctnnb1 or Lrp6 loss suppressed Wnt-response genes such as Axin2, Lef1, and Nkd1; Kremen1 left these markers essentially unchanged and had no FDR-level genes despite 175 targeted cells. This contrast is expression-based, and Kremen1 itself did not show strong target-transcript knockdown, so the result suggests a context-gated rather than default role in DKK/KREMEN/LRP5/6 regulation of WNT/TCF signaling here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fzd2 was transcriptionally flat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells despite a large matched perturbation set, with 0 FDR-supported hits among 281 perturbed cells. In the same cell class, canonical Wnt/β-catenin core perturbations were clearly active: Ctnnb1 produced 383 hits, Apc 303, Gsk3b 6, and Lrp6 4, with downstream genes such as Axin2 and Nkd1 implicated in the pathway contrast. This suggests Fzd2 was uncoupled from a transcriptionally responsive β-catenin/APC/GSK3 module in this cell type, although the finding is transcriptomic and cell-type restricted, and Apc itself was not transcriptionally depleted despite its strong downstream response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp6ap2 showed its clearest, but still weak, response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where only two genes were FDR-significant, yet the nominal Atp6ap2 tail aligned with the much larger Atp6v0c V0 program. In this subclass, Atp6ap2 nominal p<0.01 genes overlapped 29 Atp6v0c FDR genes versus 3.42 expected, all in the same direction, and both perturbations shared decreased Atp6v0a1. This pattern is consistent with a restricted, V-ATPase V0 assembly/endo-lysosomal acidification-related response, but most overlapping Atp6ap2 genes were nominal rather than FDR-significant.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|053 Sst Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Prkar1a perturbation produced a distinct, buffered transcriptomic response that was not interchangeable with nearby cAMP-dependent PKA holoenzyme components. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 053 Sst Gaba, and 155 MB Glut cells, Prkar1a showed strong target depletion but little downstream FDR-supported transcriptional change; in 155 MB Glut, only a nominal immediate-early tail including Fos, Egr1, Crem, and Nr4a1 was evident. By contrast, Prkaca and Akap11 perturbations were efficient on-target yet essentially target-only, and their score-vector correlations with Prkar1a were near zero. These comparisons are limited because other close PKA subunits were not directly perturbed.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ylpm1 showed its clearest downstream program in 155 MB Glut, where the only broad FDR-significant signature converged on a nuclear speck/nuclear body RNA-processing compartment. In this cell type, Srsf6 and Srsf5 transcripts were significantly decreased, alongside a mixed response involving Fam193b, Atxn2l, and Ube2o, and the same general direction recurred weakly across other classes. This links the strongest Ylpm1 phenotype to nuclear RNA-processing rather than a generic activity or stress response, although the data reflect RNA abundance and enrichment only, without direct measurements of speckle morphology or alternative splicing.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Ppip5k2 showed a very small, weak transcriptomic phenotype that was effectively orthogonal to indirect phosphoinositide and mTOR-linked perturbations. In the inhibitory classes 191 MB P MY GABA, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, signature correlations with Pten, Mtor, Plcb1, and Inpp5k were near zero, with no close positive or negative transcriptomic neighbors. Notably, even where Ppip5k2 had nominal self-transcript decreases, downstream genes did not reach FDR significance, so the null resemblance is unlikely to reflect a global failure to detect differential expression.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: S1pr2 showed a null phenotype in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with no adjusted differentially expressed genes, but this does not appear to reflect a general failure to detect intracellular signaling perturbations in those neuronal classes. In the same classes, Pten, Mtor, Mapk1, and Ctnnb1 produced significant transcriptional responses, consistent with detectable pathway-level effects in the Rho-Rac-PI3K-YAP cytoskeletal signaling context. The contrast should be interpreted cautiously because these comparators are downstream intracellular nodes rather than S1pr2 paralogs, and guide efficacy or expression differences may contribute.

Myo9a showed a transcriptomic signature that was essentially uncorrelated with the available Rho-family and RhoGAP perturbations, including Cdc42, Rac1, Arhgap18, and Arhgap32, with all matched comparisons remaining very weak. Thus, in this dataset, these perturbations did not phenocopy Myo9a despite curated pathway placement of Myo9a near Rho-family GTPase signaling. This should be interpreted cautiously, because the most literature-matched nodes Rhoa, Rhob, and Rhov, as well as the paralog Myo9b, were not perturbed, and Myo9a itself may have a weak signature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ryk showed a flat profile in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with zero FDR<0.05 genes, and did not phenocopy canonical WNT-pathway perturbations in the same cell type. By contrast, Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Gsk3b, and Lrp6 each produced large corrected signatures, indicating that this assay could detect WNT effector biology. Across measured genes, Ryk’s weak signatures also failed to align with related WNT perturbation signatures, supporting pathway uncoupling in this context, although receptor-level versus effector-level perturbations are not strictly equivalent and the Ryk arm was only weakly engaged.

Orc6 showed no strong transcriptomic convergence with related DNA-replication perturbations: the same-complex member Orc4 and replication factor Pola1 were both FDR-null and essentially uncorrelated with Orc6, with global score-vector correlations of r=0.0069 and r=-0.0013, respectively. Across the full matrix, Orc6 also lacked strong positive or negative signature neighbors, with extrema no larger than |r|≤0.140, including weak neighbors such as Tacr1 and Slc7a14. These results suggest no recoverable hidden Orc6-like signature, although this conclusion is limited by weak signatures and under-engagement of Orc4 and Pola1, with the weakest extrema noted in the low-count 217 P MY Pineal Glut class.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ror2 was null in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, even though canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling was clearly detectable in the same cell type: Apc and Ctnnb1 perturbations produced 303 and 383 FDR-level genes, and Apc induced the Wnt targets Axin2 and Nkd1. Ror2 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with these canonical Wnt responses, suggesting branch- or receptor-context specificity rather than a blanket absence of Wnt responsiveness. This contrast is transcriptomic and cell-type-specific, and it does not test WNT5A stimulation or ROR2-dependent RAC, JNK, or PCP signaling biochemically.

Trio showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signature correlations with the related perturbations Kalrn, Rac1, Cdc42, and Pak1, indicating no transcriptional convergence in this screen despite their shared TRIO/Rho-family GTPase signaling context. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Trio depletion was strongest, Trio itself was the only FDR-significant gene, and even Cdc42 and Pak1 perturbations correlated only weakly with the Trio signature. This negative result suggests these nearby pathway nodes were not interchangeable mRNA surrogates for Trio here, while leaving open similarity at protein-activity or morphology levels; Kalrn and Rac1 also had weak self-depletion.

Glis3 did not phenocopy Glis2 or GLI-family perturbations in this adult brain Perturb-seq setting. Across matched cell-type pairs, whole-transcriptome correlations between Glis3 and Glis2 were near zero, and correlations between Glis3 and Gli1, Gli2, or Gli3 were likewise near zero, indicating no coherent concordance within GLIS/GLI-like zinc-finger transcriptional regulation. This argues against treating these relatives as interchangeable here, although the contrast is limited by a weak Glis3 source signature and the absence of Glis1 from the comparator set.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Champ1 showed weak global similarity to other neurodevelopmental chromatin-regulator perturbations rather than a shared differentiated-neuron RNA program. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Champ1 had 194 cells and no FDR-significant genes, whereas Chd8 in the same stratum had 61 and Nipbl had 188, indicating that strong chromatin-regulator responses were detectable while Champ1 remained weak; Pogz was also weak. Restricted-signature similarity was low, including with Pogz and Chd8. This interpretation is tempered by an incomplete comparator set, sgRNA-efficiency differences, and the fact that transcriptomes may miss kinetochore or chromosome-segregation phenotypes.

Efemp1 perturbation in neurons did not yield any transcriptome-wide significant differentially expressed genes, and the data did not support a neuronal EGFR/MAPK or TIMP-family output. Timp3, an extracellular EFEMP1-related partner, was largely flat in the same neuronal contexts, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where Timp3 showed any FDR<0.05 row but Efemp1 still had no FDR-supported response. The only recurrent restricted-signature ECM-adjacent neighbor was exploratory anti-correlated Timp2, and Egfr itself was not a comparator, so extracellular EFEMP1–EGFR/Akt/MAPK reports should not be projected onto this weak neuronal perturbation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Map2k1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a TH module in which loss of Map2k1 lowered Vgf, Ptpn5, Unc13a, and Etv5. Braf loss produced the same directional changes, while Nf1 loss reversed several of these markers, supporting the expected Braf-to-Map2k1-to-Nf1 polarity within RAF/BRAF-MAP2K1-ERK signaling. In contrast, Map2k2 and several adjacent pathway perturbations did not reproduce this module, suggesting MEK1 and MEK2 are not interchangeable here. A caveat is that comparator transcripts were only nominally depleted and whole-transcriptome correlations were weak, even for Braf and Nf1.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Adra1a in 052 Pvalb Gaba showed effective target engagement, but its transcriptomic signature was essentially uncorrelated with other adrenergic-family perturbations and available Gq/PLC/PKC neighbors, including Adra2a, Adra2b, Plcb1, and Prkca. The strongest non-self correlations across the library were still very small, with Slit2 at r=0.081 and Wdfy3 at r=-0.074, and there was no high-correlation positive or negative neighbor. Thus, in this Pvalb context, known alpha-1 adrenergic receptor Gq-phospholipase C-protein kinase C pathway membership did not translate into a shared steady-state mRNA module, although Adra1b, Adra1d, Gnaq, and Gna11 were not perturbed and Plcb1 and Prkca engagement was weak.

Tfap4 targeting in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq did not detectably engage the MYC-AP4-CDKN1A/E2F cell-cycle relay. Although there was an on-target Tfap4 transcript readout, Cdkn1a, E2f1, E2f2, E2f3, Mki67, Pcna, Mdc1, Myc, and Mycn showed no corrected downstream response, with all reported at minimum FDR=1.0. The most parsimonious interpretation is pathway uncoupling in a weakly engaged, mainly postmitotic neuronal setting rather than reversal of the proliferative MYC/AP4 model, especially since only transcript outputs were tested without AP4 ChIP or MYC activation assays.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ctnnd2 knockdown showed an uncoupled RNA response from cadherin/Rho-GTPase/Wnt-catenin scaffold signaling in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons. In the thalamic class with the strongest Ctnnd2 mRNA depletion, Ctnnd2 produced a self-only, weak signature and did not phenocopy Ctnnb1 or Apc, whereas those perturbations produced broad downstream responses in the same cells. Transcripts such as Cdh2, Cdc42, Rac1, Srgap2, Zbtb33, Tcf7l2, and Ctnnbl1 were not detectably shifted, and score-correlation searches found no robust phenocopy or anti-phenocopy; interpretation is tempered because Apc effects occurred without detectable Apc mRNA depletion and the Ctnnd2 signatures were weak.

Mapk9 perturbation did not produce a detectable JNK/AP-1 transcriptional response: canonical pathway transcripts remained largely unchanged, with Jun and Atf2 never even nominal, Fos and Jund nominal in only 1 of 21 cell classes each, and Mapk8, Mapk10, Map2k4, Map2k7, and Map3k7 not FDR-significant. This buffered mRNA-level output was also seen in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut despite nominal on-target Mapk9 decreases. The result suggests that reduced Mapk9 transcript is uncoupled from the canonical stress-activated JNK phosphorylation cascade at the mRNA level, with the caveat that protein phosphorylation and transient immediate-early responses were not measured.

Wwox perturbation showed transcriptional uncoupling from canonical WWOX-linked pathways: genes in p53/p73 and extrinsic apoptotic signaling (Atm, Bak1, Bax, Casp3, Casp9, Trp53, Trp73), Wnt/GSK3β/β-catenin signaling (Ctnnb1, Dvl1-3, Gsk3b), and ERBB4/TFAP2C/AP-2 signaling (Erbb4, Tfap2a, Tfap2c) were not detectably FDR-regulated, and Ctnnb1 or Gsk3b perturbations did not converge with the Wwox RNA signature. In 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, Wwox decreased nominally but still produced zero corrected response genes. These results argue against a broad acute transcriptomic readout of WWOX pathways in this screen, while leaving open post-translational, localization, phosphorylation, and apoptosis mechanisms.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Tbcd perturbation produced a focused tubulin-homeostatic mRNA signature rather than a broad cytotoxic program, with Tuba1a increased in all 22 analyzed cell classes and significant in 6, and Tuba1b often co-induced. The strongest response was in 155 MB Glut, where Tuba1a and Tuba1b were the top hits, while 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and CNU-HYa/HY glutamatergic and GABAergic cells showed the same direction, sometimes only weakly. This pattern aligns with post-chaperonin tubulin folding and α/β-tubulin heterodimer homeostasis, but the assay measured mRNA only; Tubb3 was mostly nominal, and soluble tubulin, microtubule mass, and TBCD protein were not measured.

Ddb2 perturbation showed an on-target Ddb2 transcript response but did not robustly alter basal expression of canonical UV-DDB/global-genome NER genes or TP53-linked DNA-damage and apoptosis markers.
