Across measured cells, transcripts including Ddb1, Xpc, Xpa, Ercc1-5, Cul4a, Cul4b, Rbx1, Gtf2h1, Trp53, Cdkn1a, Ccng1, Bax, Bbc3, Pmaip1, Gadd45a, Mdm2, Atm, Atr, Rad50, and Rad51 were not significantly induced or repressed, arguing against a basal p53 or GG-NER feedback signature under unstressed neuronal conditions; this assay measured transcript abundance, not repair activity or UV-triggered chromatin recruitment.

Foxl1 showed an essentially orthogonal Perturb-seq profile in the assayed brain cell types, with near-zero correlations to tested Hedgehog, Wnt, and Forkhead-family neighbors including Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Foxl2, Foxa2, Foxg1, Foxp1, and Foxp2; even the best related comparison was weak (|r| = 0.119), and the top genome-wide signature neighbor was also weak (|r| = 0.176). Thus, gut mesenchymal Foxl1/GLI/Wnt relationships were not recovered as shared neuronal signatures here, although missing perturbations such as Lgr5, Wnt2b, Rspo3, and Foxj2 and the near-null Foxl1 vector limit mechanistic conclusions.

Pibf1 perturbation was uncoupled from a measurable Shh/Gli/Fgf developmental transcriptional readout in the assayed differentiated neuronal cell classes: Shh, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Fgf8, Fgfr1, and Lhx6 remained FDR-null, and genome-wide testing found no significant differentially expressed genes in any assayed cell class. This suggests no detectable Hedgehog or related morphogen-response transcription under these conditions, with the important caveat that these developmental markers are often lowly expressed in postmitotic brain cells and embryonic patterning conditions were not tested.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Atp6ap2 perturbation recurrently associated with decreased Atp6v0a1, nominating Atp6v0a1 as a sensitive transcript for disturbed V-ATPase V0-sector homeostasis rather than a random hit. The clearest FDR-significant decreases were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, while the direction was negative across all 21 Atp6ap2 signatures even when most cell types did not pass multiple-testing correction. This same-direction decrease also recurred after Atp6ap1 and Atp6v0c perturbation, including in 052 Pvalb Gaba, although Atp6v0c produced broader expression changes than Atp6ap2.

Adra2b perturbation showed no FDR-supported transcriptional output in the canonical alpha2-adrenergic Gi/o–adenylyl cyclase/PKA pathway or in immediate-early activity-response genes: receptor and signaling components such as Adra2a, Adra1a, Adrb1-3, Gnao1, Gnas, Gnb1/5, Adcy1/3/5, Prkaca, Prkar1a, Prkca, and Rgs6 were unchanged, as were Fos/Fosb, Jun/Junb/Jund, Egr1-4, Nr4a1/2, Npas4, Arc, Bdnf, Sik1, and Dusp1. In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, the only FDR<0.10 row was Macroh2a1, with nominal Prkaca remaining non-significant, suggesting a weak, exploratory phenotype rather than a coherent cAMP response; because these were mRNA readouts in unstimulated cells, acute cAMP, calcium, or phosphorylation effects may have been missed.

Kat6a showed a selectively weak transcriptional phenotype in this dataset: the directly assayed KAT6/MOZ-MORF neighborhood was also quiet, with Kat6b yielding no FDR-significant genes and Brd1/Brpf2 only a small corrected response, while other chromatin regulators such as Setd1a, Trrap, Kansl1, Kmt2d, and Kmt2b produced much larger corrected signatures. This pattern was seen even in high-cell-count groups including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, suggesting the flat Kat6a signal was concentrated around the KAT6 module rather than reflecting a general inability to detect chromatin-regulator phenotypes; however, Brpf1, Brpf3, Ing5, and Meaf6 were not directly assayed.

Arhgap32 showed no convergence with stronger perturbation signatures from neighboring pathway genes in this atlas. In the same 22 cell types, Ctnnb1, Apc, Grin1, and Grin2b perturbations produced many FDR-significant transcriptional changes, whereas Arhgap32 produced none, and its score-vector correlations with Rac1, Cdc42, Pak1/2/3, Dlg4, Arhgap18, and the Grin and beta-catenin/N-cadherin pathway genes were uniformly weak, with maximum absolute Pearson r ≤ 0.160. This contrast suggests a specific lack of transcriptomic alignment rather than a globally insensitive dataset, although a true protein-level effect could still occur without score-vector correlation.

Nek9 targeting did not produce a coordinated transcript-level response in its canonical mitotic or ciliary/autophagy neighbors across the queried cell types: Nek6, Nek7, Plk1, Cdk1, Nedd1, Bicd2, Dynll1, Invs, Gabarapl1, Gabarapl2, and Myh9 all showed no significant mRNA change, with similarly uncoupled behavior in the broader NIMA kinase/mitotic spindle set. This suggests the expected NEK9-centered kinase cascade was not captured by steady-state scRNA readouts, while remaining compatible with perturbation effects at phosphorylation, localization, ciliary, or cell-cycle levels rather than transcript abundance.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Dync1h1 knockdown in neurons elicited a compact SREBP/sterol-biosynthesis transcriptional program rather than a broad stress signature, most clearly in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Across these classes, Insig1, Msmo1, Fdps, Fdft1, Hmgcr, Dhcr24, Cyp51, Sqle, Srebf2, and Ldlr were upregulated after Dync1h1 loss, with the largest response in midbrain glutamatergic neurons; the direction opposed Srebf2 knockdown. In 110 glutamatergic neurons, the sterol module was significant even though Dync1h1 itself did not pass the per-class FDR cutoff. This inference is transcriptomic only, as cellular cholesterol, SREBP cleavage, and dynein motility were not directly measured.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ncapd3 showed weak or absent signature convergence across all 22 tested neuronal subclasses, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic types, with no detectable coupling to available condensin-loading or regulatory neighbors. In comparisons with Phf8, Rb1, and Mcph1, maximum absolute correlations to the Ncapd3 score vectors were only 0.096, 0.086, and 0.059, and the strongest unbiased neighbors, Wdr26 and P2ry14, were exploratory rather than known condensin components, including in 308 CB GABA where the top unbiased correlations occurred. Because the library lacked other core condensin subunits, these analyses did not reveal a hidden condensin II-like transcriptional module, but the inference is limited by the weak Ncapd3 scores themselves.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chrna4 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a distinct transcriptomic effect that was not interchangeable with Chrnb2 or Ache perturbation in the same nicotinic acetylcholine receptor cation-channel signaling context. Chrna4 had FDR-confirmed on-target depletion and a Chrna4-specific decrease in Cyp46a1, which was the only significant secondary transcript, whereas Chrnb2 and Ache each showed strong self-transcript loss without a Cyp46a1 response; the full Chrna4-versus-Chrnb2 signature correlation was weakly negative. This contrast is transcriptomic only, and other nAChR subunit perturbations in this cell class generally lacked interpretable self-knockdown.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ddx39b in 191 MB P MY GABA showed a Thoc1-biased transcriptional response rather than a broadly spliceosome-like one: its whole-signature similarity was strongest with Thoc1 (r=0.379) and only weak with other RNA-processing perturbations such as Srrm2, Rnpc3, and Srsf1, even though those perturbations produced much larger gene-expression signatures. This points to a selective TREX-coupled state in this neuronal context, within RNA splicing and nuclear-speckle-associated processing, while noting that only transcriptional consequences were compared and the library lacked direct TREX partners including Alyref and Nxf1.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Slc9a7 showed little to no transcriptomic similarity to its reported trafficking interactor Scamp5 across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 155 MB Glut cells. Although Scamp5 was efficiently knocked down, Slc9a7–Scamp5 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, and Slc9a7 itself often showed a target-only, neighborless signature, with Slc9a7 as the only FDR-significant gene in some cell types. This refines the NHE7-SCAMP trafficking axis toward membrane localization rather than a shared transcriptional program, with the caveat that only Scamp5, not Scamp1 or Scamp2, was tested and RNA correlations cannot assess subcellular trafficking directly.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ufc1 loss produced a transcriptional signature that tracked the UFM1 E1 enzyme Uba5 much more closely than Atf6, Hspa5, or Vcp, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA. This pattern, together with Ddit3 induction and selected proteostasis changes, argues that the Ufc1 response reflects UFMylation defect output rather than a generic ER-stress or proteostasis knockdown profile, although the comparator set did not cover all UPR branches and some had fewer matched cells.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Lrba did not show an interchangeable BEACH-family perturbation signature in this assay: across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, its transcriptomic responses were essentially uncorrelated with Nbea, Lyst, and Wdfy3. In the key thalamic glutamatergic class, Lrba remained below genome-wide significance with no FDR<0.05 response, whereas Wdfy3 produced a corrected response, indicating that the absence of an Lrba-like program was not simply because all large BEACH-domain vesicle trafficking genes were invisible here. This comparison is transcriptome based, and Nbea and Lyst were themselves weak, so low target engagement could attenuate correlations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zdhhc17 perturbation did not produce a coherent mRNA-loss module matching the canonical HIP14/ZDHHC17 palmitoylation network in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells. Although Zdhhc17 target engagement was detected, transcripts for Htt, Snap25, Dlg4, Dnajc5, Gad2, Syt1, and Map6 were not FDR-significant, and perturbations of Htt, Hap1, Snap25, Dlg4, Dnajc5, and Tubb3 were only weakly correlated with Zdhhc17. This suggests the acute transcriptional readout is largely uncoupled from ZDHHC17-mediated neuronal S-palmitoylation, with the caveat that palmitoylation or substrate mislocalization could occur without transcript changes and Zdhhc13 was not tested.

Antxr1 perturbation did not converge transcriptionally with selected ANTXR/adhesion/vascular pathway neighbors in the library, including Antxr2, Itgb1, Lrp6, Mapk1, Pdgfrb, Tek, and Arhgap18; the strongest reported absolute correlation to the Antxr1 signature was only 0.1275. In the assayed neuronal strata, this supports uncoupling of canonical adhesion, EGFR/ERK, and vascular-stromal ANTXR-related biology at the RNA-signature level, with Antxr1 and Antxr2 also appearing divergent in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut. This is exploratory because the neighbor set was hand-selected and restricted, and many ECM ligands and post-translational readouts were not assayed.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
full_finding_text: Trpm3 showed, at most, a nominal and mixed calcium-to-transcription signature rather than a robust program in the profiled unstimulated neurons. In 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, Arc, Egr1, and Dusp6 were nominally increased, and in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, Grm5 and Kcnd3, along with Gria1, Scn1a, and Kcna2, showed nominal changes, but all cited genes had FDR = 1.0. Overall, TRPM3 calcium/cation-channel signaling appeared globally buffered with only isolated non-adjusted signals, consistent with exploratory pathway uncoupling rather than validated activation.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pdcd10 showed a weak, idiosyncratic transcriptional response across many neuronal cell types, and its perturbation signature was essentially uncorrelated with available related perturbations including Krit1, Cdc42, Mef2a, Mef2c, and Rdx in matched glutamatergic and GABAergic populations such as L2-3/L4-6 IT and ET cortical neurons, hippocampal glutamatergic neurons, and Pvalb and Sst interneurons. Thus, in this mouse neuronal Perturb-seq setting, the CCM/STRIPAK-GCKIII network was not transcriptionally interchangeable. A caveat is that Ccm2 and core GCKIII kinases such as Stk24, Stk25, and Stk26 were measured but not perturbed, so the related-gene scan was incomplete.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Zic4 perturbation did not reproduce the reported Zic1/4-to-SHH cerebellar output program: in the 308 CB GABA population, there was no FDR-supported Zic4 response and the expected SHH-output genes Ptch1, Gli1, and Mycn did not show coordinated down-regulation. Gli1 and Mycn were not even nominally changed, and Ptch1’s strongest nominal signal in 308 CB GABA was an up-change with FDR = 1. This negative result is caveated by context mismatch, since the dataset lacks an explicitly assayed cerebellar granule progenitor population.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ddb2 showed essentially no meaningful perturbation signature across the assayed basal cell states, with near-zero whole-transcriptome correlations to other perturbations and no phenocopy of the DNA-damage-related Trp53, Atr, or Cdkn2a perturbations. This null pattern was seen in cell types including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Ddb2 contrasts had weak nominal effects but 0 FDR hits, while Pten, Rb1, and Atf2 produced robust FDR-level signatures in the same library. These results argue against a general assay-power failure and suggest the UV-DDB/global-genome nucleotide excision repair neighborhood was transcriptionally quiet, though correlation-based analyses could miss small pathway-specific overlaps.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Trim2 showed a target-specific expression program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: the thalamic module was not reproduced by the available TRIM-family comparator Trim37 or by knockdown of the canonical substrate Nefl or the downstream genes App and Cntn1. In this cell type, Trim37 had stronger self-knockdown yet no non-self FDR<0.05 hits and only a weak correlation with Trim2, and Nefl, App, and Cntn1 also correlated weakly, consistent with uncoupling at the mRNA-signature level in the TRIM2-NEFL ubiquitin proteostasis pathway. This remains exploratory because the library lacked direct Trim3 perturbation and the correlations come from one cell type.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nr4a3 showed no detectable adjusted transcriptional signal in this dataset, even though overlapping neuronal cell types such as 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut yielded significant activity/plasticity perturbation signals for Mef2c, Ntrk2, Creb1, and Jund. In particular, Mef2c and Ntrk2 had adjusted self-transcript hits, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ntrk2 and Creb1 were detected while Nr4a3 was not despite 218 perturbed cells. This suggests the null is more likely specific to Nr4a3 guide behavior, basal expression, or timing than a general failure to recover activity-regulated NR4A/CREB pathway effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Csnk2b perturbation showed a recurrent caudal upregulated module marked most reproducibly by Carmil3 and Rap1gap across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells, with Dgkz, Dnm1, and App often co-induced. Carmil3 passed FDR in 155, 191, and 217, whereas Rap1gap passed FDR in 151, 155, and 191; thus Rap1gap was not FDR-significant in 217 and Carmil3 was not FDR-significant in 151. The 155 MB Glut response was smaller but shared this module, while 191 MB P MY GABA also repressed Rnpc3 and Kat2a; these genes serve as candidate readouts rather than direct biochemical CK2beta substrates.

App perturbation did not converge on an interchangeable transcriptomic module with APP-processing or trafficking neighbors in this atlas. Compared with Sorl1, Itm2b, Adam10, and Psen1, App score-vector correlations to Sorl1, Psen1, and Adam10 were near zero, and Sorl1 and Itm2b perturbations were mostly quiet despite measurable self-knockdown in some classes. Interpretation is limited because Adam10 and Psen1 did not show detectable depletion of their own transcripts, and Bace1 plus Aplp paralogs were not perturbed, making the comparison restricted-signature-based and incomplete.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Kcnj6 showed weak on-target transcript engagement in this screen and never reached multiple-testing significance in any of 23 cell types, indicating a target- and context-specific null rather than a generic failure to detect potassium-channel perturbations. In contrast, other neuronal potassium-channel genes, especially Kcnq2, showed significant on-target depletion, with Kcnq2 significant in 13 of 23 cell types, and Kcnq3 and Kcnma1 also stronger than Kcnj6. This contrast was evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA; even in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Kcnj6 signals remained only nominal while comparator perturbations were significant. These comparators are broad potassium-channel family members, not Kir3 complex partners.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ptprm knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells did not engage a cadherin/catenin transcriptional program: Ctnnd1, Ctnnb1, Cdh2, and L1cam mRNAs were unchanged, and the Ptprm signature was essentially uncorrelated with direct Ctnnb1, Cdh2, or L1cam perturbations in the same thalamic group. Although matched comparator perturbations showed the assay can detect broad catenin-responsive changes, Ptprm loss mostly reduced its own transcript, suggesting an adhesion output that is nontranscriptional or context-gated; notably, the experiment measured steady-state mRNA, not p120-catenin phosphorylation or cell-cell adhesion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Rest was phenotypically uncoupled from the REST-proximal chromatin repression network in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba cells. Although Sin3a, Chd4, Kdm5c, Mecp2, and Phf21a are REST-proximal or REST-interacting factors, their Perturb-seq signatures were much stronger than, and only weakly correlated with, Rest. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Rest groups were FDR-null despite strong Sin3a responses, and in 052 Pvalb Gaba Rest showed one of the lowest nominal signals. Because several comparators are pleiotropic chromatin factors and Rest signatures were weak, these data suggest that loss of individual broad chromatin regulators does not simply phenocopy Rest in these cell types.

Trp63 did not show convergent Perturb-seq signatures with related assayed p53-family or TP63-neighbor perturbations in this mouse brain dataset. Trp53 and Trp73 were themselves weak, with no genome-wide significant expression changes, and Trp63 score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Trp53, Trp73, Notch1, Notch2, and Fas. This argues against imputing a shared neuronal response from curated TP63–TP53–TP73 pathway membership here, although the comparison is limited by weak score vectors and by only a subset of canonical TP63 targets being assayed.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Mapk1 in 155 MB Glut showed strong target-transcript depletion, yet after multiple-testing correction the transcriptomic effect was restricted to Mapk1 itself. This self-only pattern was shared by Map2k1, Fgfr1, and Ntrk2 in the same cell type, suggesting that loss of several receptor-to-ERK entry points converged on no shared MAPK/ERK output module rather than a guide-specific failure. A caveat is that only target mRNA depletion was measured, and Braf, Raf1, and Map2k2 showed weaker or non-FDR target-transcript changes in this context.

Nefl perturbation did not produce reciprocal FDR-level mRNA changes in the other neurofilament or intermediate-filament genes Nefm, Nefh, Ina, or Prph, and conversely Nefm and Nefh perturbations showed no non-self FDR < 0.05 genes. Across these related perturbations, signatures were dominated by target-transcript depletion and were not positively correlated, arguing against an immediate transcriptional collapse of neurofilament and neuronal intermediate-filament assembly. This contrasts with protein-level knockout observations and should be interpreted with the caveats that Nefm and Nefh engagement was weaker than Nefl in many cell types and that protein abundance or filament assembly was not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ireb2 perturbation was not strongly recapitulated by direct perturbation of related iron-pathway genes. Across cells, median signature correlations between Ireb2 and Fth1, Tfrc, Cisd2, or Hif1a were near zero; Fth1 depletion was efficient but transcriptomically local, with no recurrent FDR-supported downstream program, and the Tfrc perturbation itself showed weak on-target mRNA depletion and sparse hits. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Tfrc was the closest Ireb2 neighbor by whole-transcriptome correlation, but the effect was small, and correlations were derived from noisy summary z-scores.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnc1 showed target transcript reduction in engaged classes, including 052 Pvalb Gaba and 191 MB P MY GABA, but its downstream mRNA response was limited, and related potassium-channel perturbations were not transcriptomically interchangeable. In overlapping cell types, Kcnc2 and Kcnc3, and in Pvalb also Kcnq2, produced stronger self-knockdown yet their Wilcoxon score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with the Kcnc1 vector; this near-zero relationship also appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. These comparisons reflect differential-expression scores rather than channel assembly, ionic currents, or firing phenotypes, and Kcnc4 was not available as a direct comparator.

Ndufs1 perturbation did not produce a coordinated respiratory-chain mRNA response: across the measured panel, oxidative phosphorylation/electron-transport transcripts such as Cox5a, Ndufs3, and Uqcrfs1 showed no FDR-significant, coordinated change, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells. Within the mitochondrial respiratory chain Complex I assembly context, the Ndufs1 effect was weaker than related Complex I perturbations. Because the assay read out steady-state mRNAs only and the Ndufs1 knockdown was weak, any mitochondrial defect would likely require functional rather than transcript-level assays to detect.

Itga6 was transcriptionally uncoupled from the laminin-integrin neighborhood: its Perturb-seq signature was essentially uncorrelated with Agrn, Itgb1, Itga7, and Dag1 perturbations, and Itga6 did not induce FDR-controlled compensation of measured laminin-receptor or matrix-neighbor transcripts. In the largest Itga6 strata, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, no FDR-controlled Itga6 response was detected. Related perturbations were also largely FDR-silent, while Agrn mainly showed self-transcript loss in several classes. These comparisons are transcriptomic, and ITGB4 and laminin genes were not directly perturbed here.

Nkx3-1 did not recapitulate the prostate NKX3-1/PTEN/androgen/AKT network in this mouse-brain neuronal dataset: its signatures were nearly orthogonal to Ar, Akt3, Pten, Myc, Mycn, Trp53, and Foxa2 perturbations, with all maximum absolute correlations at or below 0.078. This was not simply a lack of pathway detectability, because Pten showed FDR-significant effects in neuronal classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut (33 genes) and 155 MB Glut (11 genes), where Nkx3-1 had none. Most prostate effectors were weak dataset hits, and Akt1, Akt2, Foxa1, and Spdef were not available as same-file comparators.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nr4a1 did not broadly phenocopy its NR4A paralogs in this unstimulated adult brain single-nucleus dataset: Nr4a1–Nr4a2 and Nr4a1–Nr4a3 full-signature correlations were near zero in 20 of 22 shared neuronal cell types, with 308 CB GABA as the only moderate exception. In that cell class, the Nr4a1 signature showed the densest nominal tail and modest alignment with Nr4a2/Nr4a3, although neighboring signatures were led more by non-NR4A perturbations such as Jund, Fosl2, and Egr2. These correlations were based on weak signatures and do not imply direct regulatory relationships.

Tgfbr3 perturbation did not produce a coherent canonical transcriptional response in the measured neuronal classes, with no genome-wide differentially expressed genes passing adjusted significance and no adjusted changes in TGF-β/BMP/activin, FGF2, or NF-κB sentinel genes such as Smad7, Id2, Fgfr1, and Nfkbia. Nominal hits were isolated rather than programmatic, including Acvr2b in 053 Sst Gaba and Jund in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 217 P MY Pineal Glut showed only a nominal Sec22a signal. Because on-target knockdown was weak, these negative pathway readouts cannot distinguish biological buffering from ineffective editing.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Rrn3 in the two responsive glutamatergic classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, showed positive transcriptomic convergence with Nop56 and with the UFMylation genes Uba5 and Ufc1, with Uba5/Ufc1 among the strongest positive neighbors in both classes. This pattern links partial Rrn3 loss more closely to nucleolar rRNA processing, ribosome biogenesis, and an ER-ribosome quality-control signature than to a weakly engaged SL1 comparator, while canonical p53/apoptosis genes were not induced. The UFMylation connection is hypothesis-generating and does not establish a direct biochemical RRN3-UFMylation pathway.

Hivep2 acute neuronal perturbation did not robustly engage canonical chronic-knockout programs: across the sampled neuronal groups, the MHC/NF-kappaB proxy genes H2-K1, H2-D1, and Nfkb1 were not significantly altered, and the reported MIBP1/Hivep2 target Sstr2 did not show consistent down-regulation. In 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, Sstr2’s smallest signal was instead a nominal up-regulation. These results suggest that immediate cell-autonomous neuronal consequences of Hivep2 loss are uncoupled from inflammation and Sstr2 regulation reported in chronic whole-body settings, with the caveat that these markers are proxies and the experiment lacks glia-rich, whole-brain context.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Snrnp70 depletion showed its strongest response in 155 MB Glut cells, where the perturbation was accompanied by a mixed RNA-processing and splicing-factor expression program rather than a uniform decline of spliceosome genes. In this state, Clasrp, Sart1, Prpf6, Sf3b2, Cpsf1, and Drosha increased, while Pnisr, Luc7l2, Luc7l3, and Srsf5 decreased, consistent with remodeling after loss of the U1 snRNP component U1-70K. These named genes are expression responses, not direct splicing substrates, and the dataset does not measure isoforms.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Robo2 showed no convincing transcriptional convergence with related guidance perturbations: across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Robo1, Slit2, Unc5c, Epha4, and Trio, with only extremely weak whole-transcriptome neighbors and even a safe-target among top correlations. This lack of convergence persisted despite strong Robo2 self-knockdown in several cell types, although many compared signatures were weak or dominated by null downstream effects, and some pathway neighbors lacked robust self knockdown.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Kansl1 showed only weak signature-neighbor relationships in this analysis. In 155 MB Glut, the closest positive neighbors were Bap1, Setd1a, and Kmt5b, while the strongest negative neighbors were Trrap, Wdr26, Phf12, and Sin3a, but all correlations were modest, with the largest absolute r only 0.221. This pattern suggests a biologically pointed yet weak Kansl1-like state, and no neighboring perturbation strongly recapitulated it. The comparison was limited to Wilcoxon score-vector correlations across 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Eef2 perturbation produced a recurrent Vgf-centered module across responsive neuronal classes, with Vgf, Son, Ranbp2, Smpd1, and often Syt4 increased, while Uchl1 and Eno2 were repeatedly reduced. This pattern appeared in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 155 MB Glut, strongest in superficial cortical IT glutamatergic neurons and smaller but supported in Pvalb GABA and L5 ET neurons. The module aligns with a mostly upregulated BDNF/VGF-associated synaptic plasticity response, but the recurrent genes were not significant in every cell type, and only Vgf has direct literature support here as a BDNF-linked synaptic peptide gene.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Thoc1 perturbation showed only partial convergence with other assayed TREX partners, indicating that Ddx39b and Thoc2 were not interchangeable across cell types. Signatures were positively related in 191 MB P MY GABA and 052 Pvalb Gaba, with Ddx39b sharing downregulation of Snhg11 and Amy1 in 191 MB P MY GABA, but Ddx39b and Thoc2 did not reproduce the large Thoc1 responses in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, or 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA within the THO/TREX-mediated mature mRNA export context. This contrast is caveated by lower matched-cell counts and weak direct target-transcript knockdown for Ddx39b and Thoc2 in several classes.

Zfp236 showed only weak transcriptomic similarity to the hexosamine/O-GlcNAc axis: in a restricted 440-feature signature, Gfpt1 and Ogt were the closest positive neighbors, but the correlations were small. Direct Ogt knockdown produced a much stronger Ogt-loss state and did not reproduce the full Zfp236-associated Ogt/Eif4a2/Cpt1c pattern, including no FDR-level Eif4a2 or Cpt1c loss. These results link Zfp236 to O-GlcNAc and hexosamine-biosynthetic signaling, but argue against treating Zfp236 perturbation as a simple phenocopy of Ogt or Gfpt1 loss; interpretation is further limited because Gfpt1 lacked corrected target-transcript depletion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cdkl5 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic population showed an engaged but distinct transcriptional state that was not MECP2-, FOXG1-, or broader developmental epileptic encephalopathy-like at the whole-transcriptome level. Correlations with Mecp2, Foxg1, Mef2c, Chd2, Ddx3x, Grin2b, Stxbp1, Kcnq2, and Tcf4 were near zero, ranging from -0.029 to 0.061, and Cdkl5 had no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor in the perturbation library. This comparison is limited to a single well-engaged cell type, and comparator target engagement may differ.

Rab28 showed no detectable FDR-scale transcriptomic response in this assay, unlike the Rab-family comparator Rab7, which produced a strong response across seven brain classes. Rab18 and Rab27a were likewise FDR-quiet, indicating that Rab-family perturbations were not interchangeable and that the assay can detect an acute Rab GTPase effect when present. Because Rab7 functions in a different Rab pathway, this contrast serves as a family-level control rather than a direct mechanistic paralog comparison.

Stx16 perturbation did not produce a coordinated FDR-significant mRNA response among measured canonical endosome-to-Golgi SNARE/GARP/COG or autophagy-adjacent partners, including Stx6, Vti1a, Vamp3, Vamp4, Vps51-54, Atg9a, Stx17, and Map1lc3b. Across 638 gene-by-cell-type tests, no partner transcripts were significantly induced or repressed, and no recurrent multi-cell-type trans-gene module emerged even at permissive thresholds. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the best-powered context, Stx16 itself was repressed but trans effects remained absent, aside from an exploratory Vps54 contrast. This negative result is limited to measured mRNA abundance, so trafficking complex activity could still change without transcript changes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sox18 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a flat signature, even though this same neuronal class mounted strong developmental transcription-factor responses to Prox1 and Ctnnb1, with Prox1 yielding 50 FDR<0.05 genes and Ctnnb1 383. The larger Sox18 sample was essentially uncorrelated with either comparator signature, indicating that the Sox18 null result is perturbation-specific rather than a general lack of responsiveness in this cell type. These neuronal responses do not establish the endothelial SOX18-to-PROX1 hierarchy, which was not detectably engaged here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Prox1 perturbation in the responsive thalamic glutamatergic class 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced a mixed, mostly upregulated neuronal and cell-junction module rather than only a self-transcript change. The strongest increases included Tmem145, Vgf, Pianp, Tafa4, and Gjb6, while Rreb1 was the dominant downregulated gene, with additional negative-arm genes such as Nexn, Snx25, and Kcnd2; Hrh2, Adora1, Vipr2, and Mef2c were also responsive. Formal enrichment was limited to a low-count cell-junction term, and Gjb6 and extracellular-matrix signals could reflect a rare state or contamination and need validation.

Adam22 behaved mostly as a target-only perturbation in this dataset: across 21 matched cell classes, the direct ligand Lgi1 showed essentially no transcriptomic similarity to Adam22, with score-vector correlations from -0.068 to 0.041, and a broader scan of STRING-connected synaptic partners such as Dlg4, Gria1-4, Kcna1/2, Grin1, and Cacng2 likewise did not reveal strong convergent or inverse signatures. This was most evident in the LGI1-ADAM22-MAGUK synaptic adhesion context, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but interpretation is limited because Lgi1 had weak target-transcript engagement and most Adam22 signatures lacked downstream FDR genes, compressing correlation dynamic range.

Kcnq1 targeting showed no detectable transcriptional compensation among Kv7-family transcripts in this assay: Kcnq2, Kcnq3, Kcnq4, and Kcnq5 did not exhibit FDR-supported induction after Kcnq1 perturbation, despite occasional nominal p values. This suggests that, within the KCNQ/Kv7 neuronal M-current context, Kcnq1 was uncoupled from neuronal Kv7 paralog RNA feedback here. The result is limited to an RNA-only test after weak Kcnq1 engagement and does not address channel trafficking, subunit assembly, or acute excitability.

Kcnq1 was not interchangeable with neuronal Kv7 paralogs in this dataset: across the neuronal classes tested, Kcnq1 showed no detectable target engagement, and its perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Kcnq2, Kcnq3, and Kcnq5. By contrast, Kcnq2 was robustly depleted in 13 neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where the highest-count Kcnq1 context still lacked Kcnq1 depletion or FDR-significant hits. This supports uncoupling Kcnq1 from the neuronal KCNQ/Kv7 M-current module, while noting that the comparison is dominated by absent Kcnq1 engagement rather than equal-strength knockdowns.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nr3c1 perturbation produced transcriptional signatures that were not recapitulated by the paralog Nr3c2 or by Hsp90ab1, Hspa8, Tsc1, or Tsc2 perturbations in the main Nr3c1-responsive cell types, including 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. Nr3c2 showed no FDR-significant genes in these contexts and only very low restricted correlations with Nr3c1, while HSP90/TSC perturbations were weakly or negatively correlated despite broader Tsc1/Tsc2 effects. These comparisons used Nr3c1 nominal p<0.01 gene sets, and failure to phenocopy does not exclude biochemical interaction with GR.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Fto perturbation most reproducibly reduced Rsrp1, with decreases seen in nine cell types at nominal p<0.001 and FDR-significant effects in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. This recurrence, alongside Dazap1 up and Atp11b down in parts of the dataset, points to an RNA-processing/spliceosome-related output rather than a neurotransmitter-lineage-specific or overt stress response. The strongest signal was in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic classes, while 191 MB P MY GABA showed only nominal Rsrp1 and Atp11b decreases; only three Rsrp1 observations passed FDR<0.05, so the broader pattern should be treated as a cross-cell-type consistency signal.

Nefm perturbation produced strong self-depletion but no detectable compensatory mRNA response from other neurofilament genes: Nefl, Nefh, and Ina did not reach FDR significance after Nefm knockdown, and reciprocal Nefl and Nefh perturbations were likewise self-dominated. This pattern was seen across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells within neurofilament bundle assembly and intermediate-filament cytoskeleton organization, suggesting transcript-level buffering was limited; Ina was only queried as a response gene, and protein-level compensation was not tested.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Fgfr3 perturbation in 155 MB Glut did not resemble Fgfr1, Fgfr2, or Fgfrl1 perturbations: all-gene score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, even though Fgfr1 showed a strong on-target knockdown in this cell type. Where measured, Fgfr3 itself did not show significant transcript depletion, no cell-type-specific Fgfr3 signature reached conventional multiple-testing significance, and the canonical FGFR3-FRS/PLC/PI3K/RAF-MAPK program was not evident after Fgfr3 perturbation. Because Fgfr2 and Fgfrl1 yielded few robust events, the contrast rests mainly on the overall correlation pattern plus the strong Fgfr1 event in 155 MB Glut.

Cd81 depletion in neurons showed little transcriptional coupling to its known interaction network: measured partner or proximal membrane mRNAs, including Cd9, Cd63, Tspan7, Tspan12, Ptgfrn, Igsf8, Itgb1, and Cd19, were not significantly changed across 176 partner-by-cell-type tests, and no strong genome-wide positive or negative signature neighbor emerged, with top non-Cd81 similarities all weak (|cosine| < 0.12) in four robust contexts. This buffered pattern held in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, while 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut showed selective Grsf1 upregulation. The partner list is incomplete, STRING is partly human-derived, and mRNA changes do not test CD81-dependent protein trafficking.

Cd81 showed broad on-target transcript depletion across assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic mouse-brain cell classes but an extremely sparse downstream expression response, yielding a near self-only neuronal RNA phenotype. Tspan7, a same-family neuronal comparator, converged on the same pattern, with on-target depletion in 16 of 21 tested cell types and no nonself genes at FDR ≤ 0.05. In contrast, Tspan12, Itgb1, and Itga6 were not transcriptionally engaged at FDR scale, so only Tspan7 is an informative comparator, consistent with buffered effects in tetraspanin-enriched membrane microdomains.

Cdk13 perturbation produced a small but recurrent expression module rather than a broad transcriptional collapse: across 22 cell types, only 165 gene-by-cell-type tests were significant, with Bend6 down in 12 cell types, Amy1 up in 11, and Rnpc3 up in 7. The strongest response was in thalamic glutamatergic neurons, and the same Bend6-down, Amy1-up, Rnpc3-up pattern also appeared in midbrain glutamatergic, Pvalb GABAergic, pons/medulla GABAergic, and hypothalamic/CNU GABAergic classes. Rnpc3 induction is the clearest dataset-level link to CDK13-associated RNA-processing biology, although the data do not measure splicing, CTD phosphorylation, or direct CDK13 substrates.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Sos1 showed a weak but pathway-consistent signal in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Vgf was the clearest nominal response gene and decreased with Sos1 perturbation. This local effect matched the direction seen with Braf, Map2k1, and Ntrk2 perturbation, while opposing Nf1 perturbation, which increased Vgf in the same class. Although the Sos1–Vgf association did not pass FDR<0.05 and the overall Sos1 signature was buffered, the convergent pattern supports Vgf as a local readout of reduced SOS1-RAS-RAF-MAPK and BDNF/NTRK2-linked signaling in this hypothalamic GABA population.

Kctd1 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage canonical KCTD1-associated AP-2, Hedgehog, or AC5/cAMP readouts in this mature mouse brain screen: Kctd15, Tfap2a, Tfap2b, Tfap2c, Adcy5, Gli1, and Ptch1 were not FDR-significant, and in the two responsive cell types, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Kctd1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Tfap2a, Adcy5, or Gli1 perturbations. In those classes, the main changes were Resp18 upregulation, plus Cluap1 downregulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, suggesting context- or engagement-dependent effects; weak Kctd1 engagement, post-transcriptional AC5/cAMP regulation, and differing literature cell types remain caveats.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Serpine2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a distinctive transcriptomic signature that was not phenocopied by the related serpin Serpini1, the clearance receptor Lrp1, or Prnp: correlations with the 151-TH Serpine2 profile were near zero, no perturbation in the same TH population was a close positive or negative neighbor, and key Serpine2-responsive transcripts such as Clip2 were not reproduced. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Serpine2 and Prnp showed only nominal co-decrease without an FDR-significant response. Canonical extracellular SERPINE2 plasminogen-activator/thrombin/LRP1 axis mRNAs were unchanged, and the contrast is strongest for TH Prnp and broad Serpini1 comparisons because Lrp1 in TH and Prnp in L5 ET had incomplete FDR-level target engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp148 shows a weak but recurrent RNA-splicing signature centered on Srrm2: Srrm2 is nominally down in nine cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, while Luc7l2 is nominally down in six. The strongest response is in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Srrm2 and Srsf9 are FDR-significantly down and most significant genes occur; outside 151, recurrence is mostly nominal, and Celf2 is only a very weak full-signature neighbor.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Esrrb showed no detectable transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, whereas the ERR-family paralog Esrra in the same thalamic class depleted its own transcript and produced 57 FDR-significant genes; Esrrg was likewise not correlated with the Esrrb profile. Across matched cell classes, Esrrb signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Esrra or Esrrg, arguing that these paralogs are not interchangeable in this atlas. This comparison is transcriptomic and based on independent perturbed-cell sets for each target, so the null appears gene- and context-specific rather than a universal failure of nuclear-receptor perturbation readout.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chd2 perturbation in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population produced the strongest measured response, marked by downregulation of RNA-splicing or prespliceosome-linked genes Ddx5, Snrnp70, Sf3b1, and Snrpn, alongside mostly lower ion-channel transcripts including Kcnc2, Kcnj9, Kcnt1, Tmem38a, and Tmem63b, while P2rx4 increased. These changes point to RNA processing and neuronal excitability outputs in this cell type, but the data reflect expression shifts only, with weak measured Chd2 mRNA knockdown and no direct assessment of splicing, potassium currents, or CHD2 binding at these loci.

Tbx21 perturbation produced no genome-wide significant differential-expression hit in any profiled neuronal class, consistent with a broader lack of activity of the T-bet helper-lineage transcriptional program in this atlas. Nearby helper-lineage regulators were also largely silent: Stat4, Runx3, Gata3, Rorc, and Foxp3 were FDR-silent, while Stat1 showed only two significant on-target transcript rows. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Tbx21 had nine nominal p<0.001 genes but no FDR hit. This interpretation is limited because only a small TF neighborhood was tested, not cytokine ligands or receptors such as Ifng or Il12rb2.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Depdc5 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells was associated with an upregulated ER/cholesterol-biosynthesis program, consistent with the expected direction for mTORC1 gain. FDR-supported response genes included Hmgcs1, Insig1, Ldlr, and Msmo1, with nominally increased sterol-pathway genes such as Cyp51, Dhcr7, Dhcr24, and Mvk, plus lipid-related Fads1 and Acsl3. This was the only Depdc5 cell type with FDR-resolved downstream genes, but several sterol enzymes were only nominal, and the dataset measured RNA rather than SREBP activity or cholesterol abundance.

S1pr2 perturbation did not detectably remodel canonical S1P/S1PR or Rho-Rac-PI3K-YAP pathway transcripts in this dataset. Across a 39-gene panel including S1pr1-5, Sphk1/2, G-protein subunits, Rhoa/Rac/Cdc42, Rock1/2, Pak1/2, Pten-Akt-Mtor, Mapk1/3, and Yap1-Lats1/2, no adjusted differential expression was observed, and this null pattern also held in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells despite detectable expression of selected intracellular nodes. These data suggest that known S1PR2 biochemical links did not manifest as a stable scRNA-seq transcriptional program, while leaving open rapid second-messenger, phosphorylation, calcium, or cytoskeletal effects.

Esrrb perturbation did not detectably engage the classical ESRRB stem-cell/cofactor transcriptional circuitry in this brain Perturb-seq readout. Among measured genes, Sox2, Nanog, Kdm1a, Ncoa3, Nr0b1, Elf5, Eomes, Esrra, and Esrrg showed no FDR-significant differential-expression rows after Esrrb perturbation, suggesting that canonical ESRRB-linked pluripotency and nuclear-receptor programs were uncoupled, inactive, or not captured in these differentiated mouse brain cells. This interpretation is limited because the assessment was restricted to genes measured in the differential-expression table rather than a full gene-set enrichment analysis.

Mafa showed brain signatures that were uncoupled from the canonical MAFA/PDX1/NEUROD1/PAX6 beta-cell regulatory module: in this brain dataset, Pdx1, Neurod1, and Pax6 perturbations had essentially zero mean score-vector correlation with Mafa, and an all-library neighbor scan found no strong positive or negative Mafa signature neighbor, with maximum non-self |r| only 0.175. These results suggest that pancreatic endocrine MAFA pathway annotations do not transfer directly to this brain screen, with the caveat that the comparison is signature-based rather than a biochemical assay.

Scn1a did not share a reproducible transcriptomic signature with the related NaV alpha paralogs Scn2a, Scn3a, and Scn8a in this Perturb-seq dataset. Although these genes encode related voltage-gated sodium-channel alpha subunits, the comparator perturbations showed weak target engagement, near-zero correlation with Scn1a, and no reproducible off-target program; Scn3a was not FDR-depleted at its own transcript, while Scn2a and Scn8a were engaged in few cell types. Thus, the observed nonconvergence is partly technical and should not be taken as definitive paralog biology.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Epha4 perturbation showed only scattered, nominal changes in axon-guidance and cytoskeletal genes rather than a recurrent Eph/ephrin transcriptional module. In 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 155 MB Glut, plausible downstream genes such as Lrrc4c, Slit3, Sema4d, Plxna1, Unc5a, Unc5c, and Wasl were FDR-negative and did not recur across signatures; in L5-6 IT Glut this was especially weak because Epha4 itself was only nominal. Overall, the data are more consistent with buffered or membrane-proximal structural signaling than with a robust secondary RNA program.

S1pr2 did not show a convergent transcriptional signature with the assayed S1P-producing neighbor Sphk1 or with Nogo-receptor-pathway neighbors Rtn4r, Lingo1, and Ngfr. Sphk1 correlations with S1pr2 were weak across cell types, ranging from −0.067 to +0.097, and the Nogo-pathway perturbations were essentially orthogonal to S1pr2 at the whole-signature level, including in hippocampal glutamatergic cell types 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut. This lack of convergence is tempered by the caveat that Sphk1 alters extracellular lipid metabolism and the Nogo-pathway genes do not encode S1PR2 itself, so identical RNA signatures were not expected.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zbtb38 showed near-zero signature correlations with Mecp2, Mbd2, Mbd5, Dnmt3a, and Usp9x in the two cell types where Zbtb38 had adjusted-significant genes, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, arguing against treating it as an interchangeable methyl-CpG, DNA-methylation, or USP9X response in these neurons. In 008, the Zbtb38 response was limited to Rcn2 and was weakly correlated with all assayed perturbations; in 151, Msra was significant with a near-threshold Abhd12b increase, suggesting a narrow oxidative-protein-repair readout. Caveats include the absence of direct perturbations for Zbtb4, Zbtb33, and Rbbp6, and limited Usp9x cell numbers in these contexts.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Dnal1 showed only a weak, background-like similarity to Cep290 in 308 CB GABA cells: the largest screened ciliary-neighbor correlation was modest, and Dnal1 target engagement in that same cell type was weak. In fact, the Dnal1–Cep290 correlation was comparable to correlations between Dnal1 and Safe_target_15 or Safe_target_70, arguing against interpreting this as biological convergence with Cep290. This observation is restricted to 308 CB GABA, and these correlations do not directly measure guide efficacy or pathway activity.

Slc22a17 showed near-zero signature similarity to perturbations of the related receptor and iron-uptake genes Lrp1, Lrp2, Lrp8, and Tfrc, so these perturbations did not phenocopy Slc22a17 in the dataset. This argues against treating Lrp2/Lrp1/Lrp8/Tfrc loss as interchangeable with Slc22a17 loss in the assessed neuronal classes, within the LCN2-SLC22A17 siderophore and iron endocytosis context. However, the comparison is limited because Lrp2, Lrp8, and Tfrc lacked detectable on-target transcript knockdown, and Lrp1 engagement was restricted to two cell types.

Tbx5 showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to other assayed T-box factors and to canonical cardiac cofactors in the mouse brain atlas, indicating that T-box membership and known cardiac partnerships did not translate into interchangeable perturbation outputs here. Correlations with nine other T-box perturbations, including Tbr1 and Tbx1/2/3/4/6/19/21/22, ranged only from -0.099 to 0.096, and available Nkx2-5, Gata4, Gata6, Mef2c, Mef2a, Mef2d, and Ctnnb1 perturbations were similarly uncorrelated. These comparisons reflect transcriptomic outputs rather than physical interactions.

Foxk2 perturbation in steady-state mouse-brain neurons did not detectably de-repress the canonical FOXK/SIN3A-HDAC macroautophagy program. Across Reactome macroautophagy genes, there were no adjusted-significant effects and no coordinated positive response; the most nominal ATG signal, Atg9a in CA3/CA2-FC/DG Glut, was decreased rather than increased. Even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where the strongest on-target Foxk2 transcript decrease was seen, there were still no adjusted-significant non-target genes or macroautophagy activation. This caveat-bound result is based on mRNA only, without starvation or insulin stimulation, and individual ATG signals were nominal at best.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tsc2 in 308 CB GABA showed a distinct, FDR-supported response that did not resemble the usual Tsc1/Mtor pattern: 37 significant genes were enriched for synaptic and calcium-associated transcripts, including Shank3, Stxbp1, Cacna1d, Grm8, Cabp1, and Slc8a3. In this cerebellar GABA class, Tsc1 was only weakly positive and fell far down the full-signature correlation ranking, while Mtor was not inverse, unlike other responsive classes. This outlier signal is tempered by weak Tsc2 RNA engagement and by top positive neighbors that were not canonical TSC/mTOR genes.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Phox2b showed no strong convergence with PHOX2B-associated autonomic-network perturbations in 308 CB GABA cells: it did not phenocopy Phox2a, and related targets including Ret, Ednrb, Sox10, Gata2, Gata3, Tlx3, Lbx1, Ebf2, and Mafb were also mostly transcriptionally silent. Genome-wide signature matching found only weak neighbors, with the largest positive and negative correlations at r=0.235 and r=-0.266, while the Phox2b differential-expression profile itself remained FDR-negative. This should be read as context refinement, since several relevant partners such as Ascl1, Hand2, Dbh, and Th were not perturbed and the comparison is exploratory because Phox2b itself was weak.

Tlx3 did not yield a robust convergent transcriptomic module in this adult brain Perturb-seq dataset: perturbations of literature-linked neighbors such as Pax2, Ptf1a, Lmx1b, Phf6, Runx3, and Bcl11b, as well as the strongest computed signature neighbors Fbxo11, Dstyk, Max, and Lrp6, showed at most exploratory correlations with a weak Tlx3 vector. Consistent with this, the embryonic dorsal-horn excitatory-versus-inhibitory fate program involving Slc17a6, Slc17a7, Slc32a1, Gad1, and Gad2 was not detected, and the correlation screen was limited to the largest weak Tlx3 rows, so these relationships should not be taken as proof of functional interaction.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Nr2c2 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut showed its broadest neuronal response, anchored by FDR-significant Ralgps1 and Ccdc84 and extending into a mixed-direction nominal synaptic module that included Stxbp1, Camk2b, Ppp3ca, Lrrtm4, Slc8a2, and L1cam. This nominal gene tail was enriched for synapse and glutamatergic-synapse cellular components, suggesting synaptic homeostasis as a follow-up context in CA3. However, the pathway signal is exploratory: only Ralgps1 and Ccdc84 met FDR < 0.05 in this cell class, whereas the broader synaptic enrichment relied on genes with nominal p < 0.01.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Vps37a perturbation recurrently up-regulated a lysosome and vacuolar V-type ATPase response, especially in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, with a lower-depth concordant signal in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. The induced module centered on Atp6v1h and Atp6v0b, with additional increases in Atp6v1b2, Atp6ap2, Clcn7, Gla, Gns, Neu1, and Psap. In 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, this lysosomal/stress program accompanied down-regulation of synaptic membrane genes. These RNA changes are consistent with an acidification response to disrupted ESCRT-dependent cargo delivery, although the dataset measured transcript abundance rather than lysosomal pH, receptor turnover, or autophagic flux.

Sox17 showed no convincing transcriptional signature in this neuronal Perturb-seq atlas and did not converge with Sox18 or any empirical neighbor. The Sox17–Sox18 global score correlation was only r=0.0162, other assayed SOX-family correlations were likewise near zero, and the strongest empirical neighbors were very weak, with P2ry14 at r=0.0326 and Dscam at r=-0.0130. Consistent with this, no corrected SOX-family module was shared; only Sox2 and Sox5 had sparse significant effects. These results suggest that the reported Sox17/Sox18 redundancy in angiogenesis was not evident in the neuronal classes assayed here, with the caveat that Sox7 was not tested and near-zero correlations are expected when Sox17 lacks a robust signature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Wac perturbation most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, and secondarily in 155 MB Glut with a smaller coherent effect in 052 Pvalb Gaba, paired downregulation of synaptic and neuronal transcripts with upregulation of a nuclear speckle and pre-mRNA processing program marked by Luc7l2, Luc7l3, Sf3b1, Rbm25, Rbm4, Srsf11, Clk1, Jmjd1c, and Ube2b. This pattern suggests a compensatory nuclear RNA-processing or chromatin-linked response rather than uniform transcriptional loss, but the data did not measure H2B ubiquitination, WAC binding, or splicing outputs directly.

Slc25a4 knockdown showed no detectable transcriptional compensation within the measured SLC25 mitochondrial carrier set: the closest ANT paralog Slc25a5, as well as Slc25a12, Slc25a13, and Slc25a46, were not significantly induced. This suggests that any buffering of Slc25a4 loss is not evident as paralog mRNA up-regulation in this assay. However, only transcript-level compensation was tested, and Slc25a5 and Slc25a31 were not perturbation targets, so buffering through baseline isoform capacity, protein-level regulation, transporter activity, metabolism, or unmeasured carriers cannot be excluded.

Ndn perturbation did not share a common acute transcriptomic state with other imprinted/PWS comparators. In 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Ndn showed strong self-depletion but no FDR-significant non-Ndn response, while Snrpn and Peg3 were likewise mostly self-knockdown-only and had near-zero whole-transcriptome correlation with Ndn. Magel2 lacked measurable target engagement, and the weak Ndn neighbor signal was limited to nominal, control-contaminated rows, arguing against a robust shared downstream signature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp2a2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced a signature that aligned more with stress/proteostasis neighbors than with available ER calcium-release, store-operated calcium-entry, or stress-sensor perturbations. Whole-transcriptome correlations with Itpr1, Stim1, Ryr2, Ryr3, and Atf6 were near zero, arguing that the measured Atp2a2 state is not simply a generic ER calcium-homeostasis perturbation. However, this contrast is exploratory because most top positive neighbors, including Atp6v0c and other stress-associated comparators, lacked clean self-transcript silencing, and several calcium-pathway comparators showed only weak or nominal target engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Glmn in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons produced a modest response that was uncoupled from the canonical GLMN–SCF/FBW7 axis at the RNA level. In this main responsive cell type, Fbxw7, Myc, Ccne1, Rbx1, Cul1, and Skp1 were unchanged, and the Glmn signature was essentially uncorrelated with Fbxw7 perturbation, with only at-most weak positive relationships to related targets such as Cul3 and Fbxo11. This contrasts with prior GLMN-FBW7 work focused on protein turnover in non-neuronal systems rather than mature mouse neuron transcriptomes.

En2 did not phenocopy En1 or the assayed midbrain-hindbrain developmental neighbors in the same dataset: across shared cell classes, the En2–En1 full-signature correlation was near zero on average, and correlations with Pax2, Otx2, Zic1, Zic2, Hoxd10, and Eif4e were similarly small. This pattern suggests the canonical RNA polymerase II/homeobox developmental module involving En1/En2, Pax/Otx/Wnt/Fgf/Zic was not acutely recovered here, although weak guide engagement for both En2 and En1 could have attenuated true biological similarity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Unc5c in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed weak or absent signature convergence with related netrin-receptor perturbations: score-vector correlations with Dcc, Dscam, Neo1, Unc5d, Flrt3, and App were all very small (about -0.044 to 0.070), and the strongest non-self neighbor genome-wide was only Aff2 at r=0.150. Although UNC5C has curated links to NTN1:DCC:UNC5C, DSCAM, and SRC/PTK2/PTPN11 signaling, this transcriptomic result is a cautious non-convergence finding limited to mRNA correlations in one cell type, and several comparator perturbations lacked FDR-level self knockdown.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Sec63 showed a distinct ER-stress signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and, more weakly, 155 MB Glut: it induced Hspa5, whereas ER-adjacent secretory-pathway perturbations Ssr4, Stt3b, Sec23a, and Sar1b showed self-depletion or nominal self-depletion but did not induce Hspa5 or the broader Sec63 ER-stress module in these same glutamatergic cell types. This uncouples the Sec63 phenotype from generic COPII export, OST activity, or TRAP/SSR-associated translocation loss, although the closest SEC61/SEC62 core translocon comparators were not present.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Musk in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut showed the strongest restricted signature, but its top 100-gene profile aligned with Safe_target controls among the highest cosine neighbors, alongside mixed unrelated perturbations, rather than a credible convergent biological module. As a result, the nominal Vps4a/Cabin1/Igf1r trend is better viewed as a sampling or guide-context signal than a supported pathway hypothesis, pending independent replication. This interpretation is limited because the neighbor search used only the 100 largest-magnitude genes from a non-significant Musk signature rather than a full replicated signature score.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mcph1 showed no significant transcriptomic signal under this analysis, and the available comparators were not interchangeable with it: Ncapd3, the main Condensin II comparator, was likewise FDR-silent, while Wdfy3 produced a strong, 17-gene response specifically in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic cells, including Stmn4, Jun, and Gls, that was essentially uncorrelated with Mcph1. This contrast suggests the Mcph1 null result was not simply a generic failure to detect brain-size genes, although interpretation is limited because Wdfy3 is a broader neurodevelopmental comparator and most close MCPH1 partners were not perturbed.

Fntb did not phenocopy available Hras or Kras knockdowns: across full transcriptome signatures, Fntb–Hras and Fntb–Kras correlations were near zero, and audits of the strongest Fntb-responsive genes found only idiosyncratic, cell-restricted neighbors rather than a recurrent canonical RAS-processing comparator. In this assay, Fntb mRNA knockdown therefore should not be read as a simple surrogate for RAS-transcript knockdown. Interpretation is limited because Fnta, Rce1, and Icmt perturbations were absent, several small-GTPase perturbations were weakly engaged, and the neighbor audit used only the top 200 Fntb genes per cell type.

Flnb showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to Actg1, Actb, Itgb1, Cdc42, and Rac1 perturbations, even though FLNB lies in an actin-cytoskeleton and focal-adhesion neighborhood. In these mouse brain cell classes, this argues against using Flnb knockdown as a simple transcriptional proxy for integrin, Rho-GTPase, or core actin perturbation. The interpretation is tempered because Flnb itself showed weak engagement, related perturbations differed in knockdown strength, and the comparison relied on genome-wide Wilcoxon score correlations rather than protein-level phenotypes.

Lgr4 perturbation did not produce a coherent canonical RSPO/LGR4-Wnt transcriptional response in this dataset: across 563 assayed Wnt/RSPO/FZD/LRP/ZNRF pathway rows, no change passed multiple-testing correction in any cell type. The strongest nominal signals were Dvl1 down in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Ctnnb1 and Axin2 up in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, but all had FDR=1 and did not converge into a module involving genes such as Apc or Wls. This suggests mature brain cell classes were not in a ligand-competent Lgr4-Wnt state under the assay, although only transcript-level components were measured and weak Lgr4 knockdown could have obscured a true effect.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Prr12 showed its only cohesin-like convergence in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where depletion was modest and the adjusted hits were only marginal, namely Tmem30a, Hsp90b1, and Auts2 at q≈0.18–0.40. In this same cell type, Nipbl and Smc1a were the top non-control positive signature neighbors of Prr12, but the correlations were small (r=0.120 and r=0.105). Overall, the PRR12-cohesin loading/genome integrity signal appeared weak, cell-type-restricted, and largely orthogonal outside this neuronal context.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ide knockdown in the two glutamatergic classes with on-target depletion, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, did not transcriptionally engage APP or insulin receptor/PI3K/mTOR programs. App, Insr, Igf1r, Pik3ca, and Mtor mRNAs were not significantly changed, and perturbations of App or proximal insulin-signaling nodes did not mimic the Ide signature. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, secondary changes were not FDR-significant and nearest-neighbor similarities were weak or near zero. This interpretation is limited because insulin peptides and amyloid-beta were not measured, and several compared genes are pathway neighbors rather than direct IDE substrates.

Htr1f perturbation did not produce a durable transcriptional signature of the canonical Gi/o-coupled adenylate-cyclase and cAMP pathway: across Htr1f cell types, adenylyl-cyclase, PKA, phosphodiesterase, and immediate-early sentinel mRNAs including Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Creb1, Fos, Jun, Egr1, Arc, Prkaca, Prkacb, Pde1b, and Pde4b were not significantly altered. This suggests that basal Htr1f perturbation was uncoupled from stable mRNA readouts of cAMP signaling, with the caveat that the assay measured mRNA sentinels rather than cAMP levels, PKA activity, phosphorylation, receptor occupancy, or acute activity-dependent transcription.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp612 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells strongly increased Notum, but this response was uncoupled from a broader canonical Wnt feedback program, as Axin2 and Nkd1 were not significantly induced. In the same cell class, Apc perturbation upregulated Notum together with Axin2 and Nkd1, whereas Ctnnb1 perturbation downregulated Notum, supporting the view that the Zfp612 effect reflects a selective NOTUM/Wnt-modulatory output rather than global Apc/β-catenin activation. This evidence is transcriptomic and based on a single-gene signal, with no measured Zfp612 binding at Notum and no significant mature Zfp612 RNA knockdown.

Zswim6 perturbation did not produce a detectable Hedgehog transcriptional-output state in this dataset: canonical pathway genes Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, and Sufu were neither induced nor repressed, with all at FDR = 1.0 and Ptch1 showing only a small maximum absolute score of 1.60. This remained true even in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, the class with the strongest nominal Zswim6 RNA decrease, where no FDR-supported downstream Hedgehog or module response was seen. These neuronal reduced-function data therefore refine, rather than recapitulate, the AFND Arg1163Trp missense report from patient osteoblast/fibroblast assays.

Pak2 signatures were nearly orthogonal to Pak1, Pak3, Rac1, Cdc42, and Limk1 perturbations across shared cell types, with score-vector correlations close to zero and no strong whole-dataset neighbor, despite curated pathway connectivity within RHO GTPase to group-I PAK signaling. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Pak1 and Cdc42 showed direct engagement while Pak2 had many cells but no on-target FDR and almost zero correlation; similarly, in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, Pak2 had nominal rows yet a minimum FDR of 0.751 and only a weak best neighbor. Because Pak2 and Pak3 lacked FDR-supported on-target knockdown, the safest interpretation is weak or buffered Pak2 engagement rather than true functional uncoupling.

Pak1 perturbation did not produce a transcriptomic state that converged with its canonical actin-signaling neighbors. Across matched cell types, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, no perturbation showed a strong Pak1-like or anti-Pak1-like signature; correlations were at most |r|=0.083 for Pak2/Pak3 and |r|=0.065 for Cdc42/Rac1/Limk1. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Pak1 was self-depleted but Cdc42, though also self-depleted, remained nearly uncorrelated, and there was no detectable compensatory Pak2 or Pak3 mRNA change. Because several related perturbations showed weak own-target mRNA depletion, this mainly argues against a detectable shared transcriptomic module rather than against biochemical pathway connectivity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ap2s1 showed an exploratory restricted-signature relationship in excitatory neurons in which Grin2b and Grin1 perturbations were positive neighbors, while Kcnq2 and Kcnq3 lay on the opposing axis, particularly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut cells. This pattern suggests that AP-2 loss intersects postsynaptic glutamate-receptor trafficking rather than only generic vesicle recycling, with an inverse Kcnq-defined excitability state, but the comparison was computed only on the top 200 Ap2s1-responsive genes and does not demonstrate a direct AP-2 cargo relationship for Kcnq2/Kcnq3.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Tbr1 perturbation produced a transcriptome-wide signature in responsive glutamatergic classes that was not phenocopied by perturbing known TBR1 partners or laminar regulators. In 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and the near-responsive 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut class, Cask, Foxp2, Bcl11b, Sox5, and Satb2 showed near-zero full-transcriptome correlation with Tbr1, indicating divergence across the TBR1 protein-partner and laminar-regulator network. These comparisons reflect perturbation-signature similarity, not protein interaction strength, and may be affected by guide efficacy and expression differences.

Kcnq2 knockdown in the KCNQ2/KCNQ3 voltage-gated potassium M-current context did not produce significant RNA-level compensation by Kcnq1, Kcnq3, or Kcnq5, and the expected KCNQ2/KCNQ3 partnership was not mirrored by symmetric Perturb-seq signatures. Compared with Kcnq2, Kcnq3 and Kcnq5 perturbations were much less transcriptionally engaged, although this contrast is difficult to interpret because those paralog perturbations showed weak target-transcript depletion. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, the strongest Kcnq2 effect was largely self-only, while Kcnq3 self-depletion was significant only in this class and Egr1 remained sub-FDR.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zbtb10 perturbation in mouse brain neurons did not broadly engage the canonical miR-27a–ZBTB10–Sp specificity-protein axis. In 155 MB Glut cells, Sp4 showed only a nominal increase that did not pass FDR, while Sp1, Sp3, and the Sp-linked effector genes Vegfa, Birc5, and Ccnd1 were not significantly changed, consistent with the absence of a robust downstream Zbtb10 transcriptomic program. This contrasts with human breast cancer gain-of-function or miR-27a inhibition studies and is limited here to mouse brain cells with an RNA-only readout.

Ptprd showed no strong convergence with related type-IIa phosphatases, extracellular partners, or unbiased nearest neighbors in this Perturb-seq readout. Genome-wide signature correlations with Ptprf, Il1rap, Il1rapl1, Il1rapl2, Slitrk1, and Nlgn3 were all near zero, and no positive or negative neighbor exceeded |r|=0.201, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 155 MB Glut. The main caveat is that the Ptprd primary signature itself was weak, limiting interpretation of correlation-based neighbor analyses.

Cadm2 perturbation did not measurably change Cadm1, Cadm3, or Cadm4 mRNA, indicating no detectable transcriptional compensation within the SynCAM/CADM adhesion family in this dataset. This is notable because CADM2 participates in heterophilic CADM-family adhesion pairs, so a paralog switch would have been a plausible buffering response, but it was not observed. The result is limited to mRNA abundance: Cadm1, Cadm3, and Cadm4 were not directly perturbed, and any compensation through protein localization, complex formation, or adhesion strength would not be captured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Setd1a knockdown produced its strongest signature in 155 MB Glut, where a dominant down-regulated module was accompanied by a smaller up-regulated RNA-processing arm: 75 of 465 FDR hits increased, including Pnn, Srsf2, Srsf6, Srsf7, Srrm2, Ddx41, Dhx16, and Brd9, with enrichment for spliceosomal complex and mRNA splicing genes. This positive arm recurred weakly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, but interpreting it as compensatory is tentative because the assay measured RNA abundance rather than splicing output or nuclear-speckle function.

Ahr showed a shared buffered null phenotype across all 21 Ahr-assayed neuronal classes, rather than an AHR/ARNT-like transcriptional program. Perturbing the related bHLH-PAS factors Ahrr, Arnt, Arnt2, and Hif1a also produced zero FDR-significant genes, and their transcriptome score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Ahr. This suggests the screen did not engage a common AHR/ARNT or HIF/ARNT transcriptional state, although this conclusion is based on weak transcriptomic signatures and the lack of correlation is consistent with all of these perturbations failing to engage their target transcripts.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ndufa13 perturbation produced mostly buffered transcriptomic effects rather than a shared oxidative-phosphorylation mRNA program with nearby Complex I genes. Across 33 mitochondrial or respiratory-chain perturbations, only 10 non-target hits appeared in 725 target-by-cell-type tests, and the few singleton signals seen for Ndufs2 in 052 Pvalb Gaba or for Ndufb10 in 191 MB P MY GABA were not reproduced in matched Ndufa13 signatures. This suggests target downregulation with pathway mRNA buffering in respiratory electron transport/Complex I and no detectable shared response in Complex I biogenesis; weaker on-target depletion for many neighbors and exploratory singleton hits are important caveats.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Arx showed a transcriptional response in 052 Pvalb Gaba and, more sparsely, in 046 CTX-CGE GABA that was not phenocopied by Dlx5, Dlx6, Foxg1, or Nkx2-1 perturbation. In both inhibitory classes, these comparators had no FDR-significant genes, and their score-vector correlations with the Arx signature were near zero, indicating a divergent low-correlation relationship rather than an interchangeable adult-like GABAergic state. In Pvalb cells the Arx response was anchored by Tle2 down-regulation, whereas CTX-CGE showed only Tmsb4x at FDR. This refines, rather than negates, developmental Dlx→Arx relationships because Dlx2 was not perturbed here and the data come from differentiated cell classes.

Dlx3 showed no convergence with Dlx5, Dlx6, Msx2, or Nkx2-1 perturbation signatures in the assayed brain states, and Dlx5/Dlx6 were themselves largely flat, with no FDR-significant downstream genes across 23 cell classes. In GABAergic classes including CTX-CGE GABA, Pvalb Gaba, Sst Gaba, CNU-MGE GABA, CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and others, the forebrain GABAergic DLX effector program was uncoupled, with no significant changes in Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, or Nrp2. A nominal Dlx3 signal in CNU-LGE LSX GABA did not survive correction, and Dlx1/Dlx2 were not tested.

Oprl1 did not behave like an interchangeable μ-, δ-, or κ-opioid receptor perturbation: across matched cell types, its whole-signature correlations with Oprm1, Oprd1, and Oprk1 were near zero, indicating little concordance within NOP/opioid-family GPCR signaling. This matters because NOP is the fourth opioid receptor family member, so some shared loss signature might have been expected. However, the comparison is exploratory, since the classical opioid receptor perturbations also showed weak target-transcript knockdown in their own rows, limiting firm receptor-specific interpretation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: H3f3a did not phenocopy Atrx, despite ATRX/DAXX being an H3.3 deposition pathway.
