Atrx produced FDR-significant responses concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, whereas H3f3a left Atrx marker genes such as Resp18, Csf2ra, and Limd2 unchanged and showed near-zero whole-signature correlation with Atrx across shared cell types. This contrast suggests the ATRX-linked response is not a generic H3.3 depletion signature, although H3f3a target engagement was weak and Daxx and Hira were not perturbed.

Trpm3 showed little correspondence to other available TRP-channel perturbations: in matched brain cell types, genome-wide Trpm3 score vectors were nearly decorrelated from Trpm7, Trpv1, and Trpv4, arguing against a generic TRP-channel transcriptional module in these cells. However, this comparison is limited because the Trpm7, Trpv1, and Trpv4 perturbations were themselves weak, with few FDR-significant differential-expression hits, so the lack of correlation may partly reflect limited perturbational information rather than a definitive biological separation.

Slc12a2 did not share an mRNA-signature program with the WNK-SPAK pathway neighbors Wnk1, Wnk3, or Stk39: perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated. This negative pathway-level result fits a model in which WNK–SPAK regulation of cation-chloride cotransporters is mediated mainly through transporter phosphorylation and activity rather than a shared downstream transcriptional program. Interpretation is limited, however, because Wnk1, Wnk3, and Stk39 also showed weak engagement of their own RNA targets, so the data do not argue that kinase activity is unimportant.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Ddx3x perturbation showed a nominally recurrent response module across several posterior or GABAergic/glutamatergic classes, centered on Bicd2 induction and more limited Ddx5 induction, with Tcea2 repression and Wsb1 induction in smaller subsets. The recurrence was seen in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, but most per-class signals were weak; among highlighted recurrent rows, only Bicd2 in 155 MB Glut passed FDR<0.05. Ddx5 up-regulation is therefore a plausible but exploratory RNA-helicase compensation marker, while Bicd2 may reflect a broader Ddx3x-stress response.

Vps13b did not phenocopy Vps13a, Vps13c, or Vps13d in this Perturb-seq dataset: across matched cell types, Vps13b score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with those of its paralogs, and Vps13b had no FDR-significant rows, whereas Vps13c and Vps13d showed stronger self-depletion or FDR-significant effects. In 155 MB Glut, Vps13b showed its strongest nominal self decrease, but the related Vps13c perturbation in the same broad class achieved FDR-significant Vps13c self-depletion. Because guide efficacy and perturbed-cell counts differed across paralogs, this comparison is suggestive rather than a clean biochemical test of paralog specificity within the VPS13-family lipid-transfer context.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Lrp1 showed a VGF/neurosecretory peptide response that appeared specific in posterior neuronal classes rather than a generic Alzheimer-family or LDL-receptor chaperone effect: in 155 MB Glut, Lrp1 knockdown produced both significant target depletion and FDR-significant Vgf induction, while equally robust App, Lrpap1, and Mapt perturbations did not reproduce the Vgf signal; in 191 MB P MY GABA, Lrp1 again gave FDR-significant Vgf induction despite only nominal Lrp1 transcript depletion, whereas Lrpap1 only trended upward and App and Lrpap1 did not pass FDR. This comparison is transcriptomic and guide-count matched at the cell-class level, without direct assays of LRP1 protein depletion, LRPAP1-dependent trafficking, or APP/Aβ flux.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Oprd1 in 052 Pvalb Gaba showed weak or no transcriptomic convergence with other opioid receptor family perturbations: correlations with Oprm1, Oprk1, and Oprl1 were near zero, and a same-cell neighbor scan found no strong positive or negative non-self neighbors. In this cell type, Oprd1 also lacked an adjusted non-target signature, PI3K-mTOR mRNA module, and notable cAMP-pathway correlations. Because Oprm1, Oprk1, and Oprl1 were themselves only weakly engaged in Pvalb, this should be read as a failure to detect convergence rather than proof of receptor-family divergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nfic showed a divergent, non-interchangeable perturbation profile relative to Nfia, Nfib, and Nfix in the two main glutamatergic response classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In both classes, Nfic-versus-paralog score correlations were near zero, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut only Nfic induced Bambi, consistent with NFI-family transcriptional regulation that is cell-state- and paralog-specific rather than a generic NFI-family output. However, target-transcript engagement for Nfia, Nfib, and Nfix was weak in several classes, so lack of phenocopy does not rule out paralog function.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nfib did not phenocopy other NFI-family perturbations in this assay. Across the matched cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Nfib score vectors were only weakly correlated with Nfia, Nfic, and Nfix, and Nfib produced no FDR-significant family-level rows, whereas Nfic alone had two hits, including a Bambi response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and reduced Nfic transcript in 155 MB Glut. An expected Nfix- or Gfap-linked gliogenesis program was not detected after Nfib perturbation, although Nfic had more perturbed cells than Nfib, so potency and power may partly explain the contrast.

Cyld perturbation did not produce a coherent TNFR1/NF-kappaB or interferon inflammatory transcriptional program across the 21 Cyld-sampled neuronal cell types. Canonical sentinels such as Nfkbia, Tnf, Ccl2, Cxcl10, Isg15, and Ifit1 were not induced, and genome-wide testing found no adjusted-significant Cyld response in any assayed cell type; the only nominal exception was Traf2 in 308 CB GABA. This absence of the expected inflammatory direction should be interpreted in the context of resting neuronal cells without exogenous TNF, NOD, RIG-I-like receptor, or Wnt stimulation, and DDX58 was not measured.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Foxi1 showed only weak, mixed similarity in restricted signature-neighbor checks, with no robust convergence with Forkhead-family perturbations or other biologically interpretable neighbors. In 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, the strongest correlations to the Foxi1 top-200 signature were weak, and comparators such as Foxk2, Foxe3, Foxj3, and Foxc2 were weaker still; diffuse neighbors included Slc6a5 and Adgrg1. Because this analysis used only the 200 largest absolute Foxi1 scores from weak signatures, it should be read as an exploratory screen for missed convergence rather than a validated network analysis.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zic2 showed only weak convergence with Zic1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the only cell type with a near-threshold Zic2 response. In this class, Zic1 produced a small FDR-supported self/Slc29a1 signal, whereas the Zic2 score vector correlated only weakly with Zic1 (r = 0.088) and was near-zero with Zic3 or Zic4; even the strongest off-target neighbors were weak, including Nefl (r = 0.088) and Rab7 (r = -0.070). Because the Zic2 signature was sub-threshold, these are restricted-signature contrasts rather than definitive epistasis.

Mertk showed no robust shared signature with the TAM-family comparator Axl in the assayed neuronal classes: Axl was also effectively silent, all-gene Axl–Mertk signature correlations were near zero across 22 shared cell types, and top-neighbor relationships were weak and unstable. In 046 CTX-CGE GABA, the smallest Mertk signal was only a non-significant Slc37a3 change, with a weak restricted Axl neighbor relationship. These results suggest the Gas6/Protein S–TAM efferocytosis program was unengaged here, while interpretation is limited because only Axl was directly perturbed and Tyro3, Gas6, Pros1, Mfge8, and Megf10 were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Zic3 was not interchangeable with other assayed Zic paralogs in these mouse-brain Perturb-seq signatures. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, only Zic1 showed an FDR-significant response, with detectable Zic1 self-depletion and Slc29a1 induction, whereas Zic2, Zic3, and Zic4 lacked FDR-significant hits; whole-signature correlations between Zic3 and the other Zic perturbations were weak. This divergence was observed across the Zic paralog transcription-factor program, including 308 CB GABA, although the contrast is transcriptomic and could reflect biological specificity as well as differences in guide efficiency or basal paralog expression.

Fars2 did not converge with the available mitochondrial aminoacylation or translation neighbors Lars2, Rars2, and Gfm2 in this assay. Although FARS2, LARS2, and RARS2 are grouped in mitochondrial tRNA aminoacylation and GFM2 in mitochondrial translation, Fars2-to-neighbor score correlations were near zero, and none of the four perturbations produced FDR<0.05 differential-expression hits. This suggests that the expected mitochondrial-translation state was not transcriptionally recovered here, with the caveat that all four perturbations were weak and Gfm2 is only a broader pathway neighbor.

Nfib perturbation in the postnatal neuronal classes represented here did not reproduce the developmental NFIB programs reported in embryonic progenitors and gliogenesis: Ezh2, Gfap, and Nfix were not FDR-significant, and a global scan found no FDR-significant differential-expression result after Nfib knockdown. This is best interpreted as a stage- and cell-state-restricted effect rather than a direct contradiction, because the dataset lacks embryonic ventricular-zone and astroglial maturation states, and the Nfib knockdown was weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Adgrl1 perturbation showed RNA signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of TENM/FLRT/UNC5 adhesion-neighborhood genes across the four FDR-engaged cell types—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA—with Tenm3, Tenm4, Flrt3, Unc5c, and Unc5d correlations ranging from -0.036 to 0.040. Thus, these assayed adhesion-network perturbations did not phenocopy Adgrl1, and even the nearest positive or negative full-signature neighbors were weak. This decoupling should be interpreted cautiously because Tenm2 was not assayed and acute cell-autonomous RNA readouts may miss non-cell-autonomous ligand-receptor effects.

Tbck could not be evaluated for convergence with the FERRY/Rab5 early-endosomal mRNA-transport complex in this screen because other relevant complex members, including Ppp1r21, Ferry3, Cryzl1, and Gatd1, were not obviously perturbed. Among the represented family neighbors, Tbc1d23, Tbc1d24, and Tbc1d32 did not show Tbck-like transcriptomic profiles. Thus, the most informative current comparison for Tbck was effectively not tested, with the additional caveat that possible FERRY-gene aliases may have been missed and that these family-neighbor comparisons rely only on transcriptomic score vectors.

Snai2 perturbation did not produce the canonical cadherin/vimentin EMT output in the assayed mouse brain cell classes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Cdh1, Cdh2, and Vim were all FDR-null after Snai2 guides, and no downstream gene reached multiple-testing-corrected significance in any measured class. Thus, despite pathway expectations linking SNAI2 to CDH1 repression and EMT, these neuronal populations did not show an EMT-like response, with the caveat that Snai2 engagement was weak and Cdh1 and Vim may be lowly expressed.

Six3 showed a weak perturbation signature, and the screened SIX-family paralogs Six1, Six5, and Six6 were similarly weak rather than transcriptionally interchangeable with Six3. Across matched cell types, Six1, Six5, and Six6 had no FDR<0.05 differential-expression rows, and their score-vector correlations with Six3 stayed near zero (r = -0.0859 to 0.0807), so these perturbations did not define a shared SIX/Sine oculis homeobox response module. This comparison is limited to weak-signature score correlations, and Six2 and Six4 were not tested.

Xpr1 perturbation did not produce a recurrent phosphate-homeostasis or mineralization-marker transcriptional response in neurons: genome-wide differential expression detected no multiple-testing-significant Xpr1 effect in any assayed cell type, and Slc20a1, Slc20a2, Ppip5k1, Ppip5k2, Spp1, Runx2, and Alpl were not recurrently or FDR-significantly regulated. This suggests that acute, weak neuronal Xpr1 engagement was transcriptionally buffered rather than accompanied by a strong feedback loop in the XPR1-dependent inorganic phosphate export pathway, with the caveat that these were mRNA readouts rather than intracellular phosphate or phosphate-efflux measurements.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Tbr1 perturbation did not re-induce classic neonatal layer-6 Tbr1 targets in this Perturb-seq: across 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, Wnt7b, Grin2b, Fezf2, Foxp2, Sox5, Bcl11a, Tle4, and Nr4a2 showed no FDR-level response, indicating a cortical projection-neuron Tbr1 program that was restricted and partly uncoupled from published neonatal Tbr1 layer-6 mutants. This negative transcript-level result, together with weak measured target engagement, suggests a later or buffered state and does not exclude earlier developmental regulation or protein-level effects.

Fmn2 perturbation was not transcriptionally interchangeable with its paralog Fmn1: across 22 shared cell types, the Fmn2–Fmn1 ranked differential-expression or Wilcoxon-score correlations were essentially zero, despite both genes residing in the FMN2/SPIRE actin-nucleation neighborhood with Spire1 and Spire2. Both perturbations produced weak single-cell signatures, so the near-zero same-cell correlations mainly argue against a strong shared mRNA program, not against a possible shared cytoskeletal role. Consistent with this, Fmn2 showed no corrected actin-partner mRNA response, whereas Actb induced Actg1 and Flna.

Etfa perturbation did not produce FDR-supported compensatory transcriptional changes in canonical ETF partners or respiratory-chain genes. Etfb, Etfdh, and nearby fatty-acid or amino-acid catabolism transcripts, including Acadm, Acadl, Acadvl, Acads, Gcdh, and Dld, were not significant Etfa-response genes, and OXPHOS-family transcripts such as Ndufs7, Ndufa2, and Atp5g1 likewise showed no adjusted hits. This suggests the measured mRNA response is buffered and uncoupled from the annotated ETF electron-transfer and OXPHOS pathways, with the caveat that only transcript abundance was assayed, not ETF protein activity, turnover, or acylcarnitine accumulation.

Foxn1 perturbation in the brain did not mobilize the canonical FOXN1 thymic epithelial differentiation and T-cell-support program. Across assayed brain cell types, Foxn1-designated perturbations produced no multiple-testing-significant transcriptome changes, and established thymic FOXN1 effector genes including Dll4, Ccl25, Ctsl, Cd40, Pax1, MHC-II genes (H2-Ab1, H2-Aa, H2-Eb1), Psmb11, and Kitl showed no validated response. Because many of these TEC genes have low or sporadic expression in brain, this null result should not be treated as a thymic Foxn1 loss-of-function benchmark.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ehmt1 showed a narrow thalamic convergence with Setdb1 rather than broad H3K9-pathway interchangeability. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, 2 of 4 Ehmt1 FDR genes, Abhd12b and Smtn, were also Setdb1 FDR hits in the same direction, but Ehmt1–Setdb1 whole-signature correlations were near zero globally and within every cell type. This suggests only a tiny shared H3K9-sensitive node within otherwise distinct H3K9me1/2 versus H3K9me3 responses, with the caveat that the shared module contains just two genes and Ehmt2 was not screened.

Rars2 did not share a detectable transcriptomic signature with the related mitochondrial translation perturbations Fars2, Lars2, and Gfm2 in this screen. Those comparator perturbations were weak and FDR-null, and their same-cell-type full-signature Pearson correlations with Rars2 were near zero, ranging from -0.0448 to +0.1277. Thus, within the mitochondrial tRNA aminoacylation and mitochondrial translation pathway context, the dataset does not support a generic shared stress module across these perturbations, although the uniformly weak signatures mean this reflects lack of detectable convergence rather than antagonism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hivep3 did not phenocopy Hivep1 or Hivep2 in this neuronal Perturb-seq dataset: across 22 shared Hivep1/Hivep2/Hivep3 cell classes, full-signature correlations between Hivep3 and the two paralogs were near zero, and in the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class the Hivep3-associated R3hdm2/Mgat3/Ndst1 peak, including the only FDR-significant Hivep3 gene R3hdm2, was not recapitulated by Hivep1 or Hivep2. This divergence is based on full-signature comparisons, with weak Hivep1/Hivep3 target-transcript engagement and clear Hivep2 engagement seen in only one shared cortical class.

Zfp182 showed a null perturbation profile in this screen, including in the large 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut stratum, whereas other zinc-finger perturbations in the same dataset were clearly detectable: Zfp423 had 157 FDR-significant tests, Zfp236 had 47, and Zfp148 also produced significant signatures. This contrast suggests the Zfp182 null is not simply a general failure of the Wilcoxon pipeline to detect zinc-finger transcription factor perturbations, although these comparators are broad family members rather than close paralogs or known Zfp182 complex partners.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp664 showed no FDR-supported differential-expression genes in any assayed cell type, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 308 CB GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, despite nominal repression signals in some strata. In the same cell-type space, other broad C2H2 zinc-finger perturbations were clearly detectable: Zfp236 yielded 47 FDR-supported genes and Zfp423 yielded 157, arguing that the quiet Zfp664 phenotype is target-distinct rather than a generic assay failure for C2H2 zinc-finger transcriptional regulation. These comparators are broad relatives, however, not validated paralogs or members of a shared Zfp664 complex.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Cit perturbation did not produce a robust thalamic or hippocampal RNA response. In the largest Cit stratum, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, there were many perturbed cells but only a nominal Cit decrease and no FDR-significant downstream genes. The 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut class showed the broadest nominal signal, including weak subthreshold changes such as Stxbp5l, Pdss1, and Syt17, yet still no genes met conventional FDR significance. Overall, this suggests reported Citron-N thalamic postsynaptic and dendritic-spine roles may reflect structural or protein-localization biology rather than an acute whole-transcriptome response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hic1 was flat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the best-powered Hic1 context, with 240 perturbed cells but no FDR-significant genes and only a nominal Ccser2-led peak. In the same thalamic glutamatergic class, Ctbp1, Arid1a, Tcf7l2, and Ctnnb1 produced active programs whose whole-signature correlations with the weak Hic1 vector were near zero. This suggests the class was not globally refractory, although these neighbors are not interchangeable with Hic1 and the missing Hic1 target-mRNA knockdown limits interpretation of the HIC1-CTBP and Wnt/β-catenin axis contrast.

Hic1 perturbation did not derepress the canonical HIC1-associated axes in this mouse brain dataset: Sirt1, Trp53, Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Atoh1, Ctbp1, Ctbp2, Arid1a, and Mta1/2/3 all remained FDR-nonsignificant, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells Hic1 was flat while neighboring Ctbp1, Ctbp2, Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, and Arid1a were active. This contrasts with prior HIC1 links to SIRT1-p53, Wnt/TCF/β-catenin, CtBP, and Atoh1 regulation, but the assay lacked DNA-damage, Wnt, or cochlear-differentiation cues, and Hic1 RNA depletion was not observed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Adk perturbation did not produce robust adenosine receptor or A2A/TrkB plasticity transcript feedback in the six nominally engaged neuronal cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut. Adora1, Adora2a, Bdnf, and Ntrk2 were nonsignificant, and even the strongest 151 contrast showed only nominal p values without FDR support. This suggests that brain-wide ADK-deficiency physiology is not reflected as immediate mRNA changes here, with the caveat that transcript rows do not capture adenosine tone, TrkB phosphorylation, or electrophysiology.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Pik3r2 showed a muted transcriptional response in this Perturb-seq dataset, with no detectable alignment or anti-alignment to proximal class-IA PI3K, PTEN, TSC, NTRK2, MTOR, or RAPTOR signatures. In contrast, downstream disease-family nodes were responsive: Pten, Tsc1, Tsc2, and Ntrk2 produced FDR-level signatures, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, while 052 Pvalb Gaba showed Ntrk2 self-transcript effects without comparable Pik3r2 or class-IA catalytic-subunit responses. These cross-perturbation comparisons are based on RNA signatures, and some proximal perturbations also had weak self-transcript knockdown.

Htr2b perturbation across 21 sampled Htr2b neuronal classes did not yield a consistent immediate-early transcriptional response, despite the receptor’s expected coupling to G alpha(q)-PLC-IP3-DAG-Ca2+/ERK signaling. In steady-state scRNA-seq, Fos, Egr1, Egr3, Jun, Junb, Dusp1, Dusp6, Mapk1, Mapk3, and Rgs4 were not reproducibly shifted, and perturbations of pathway neighbors such as Plcb1, Prkca, Prkcg, and Mapk1 were also weak or sparse. This supports a buffered or negative steady-state transcriptional phenotype rather than a shared Htr2b module, with the caveat that ligand-evoked calcium or phospho-ERK dynamics were not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Prkca was transcriptionally silent in the high-count 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic glutamatergic population: despite 169 Prkca cells, there was no on-target RNA depletion or corrected downstream response, while related DAG/Ca2+-dependent PKC signaling perturbations in the same cell class showed significant self-depletion for Prkcg, Dgke, Camk2b, Grm1, and Cacna1c. This suggests the null response is specific to Prkca rather than a general inability of these thalamic neurons to respond, although comparator guide counts and knockdown magnitude differed, and transcriptomics cannot distinguish PKCα buffering from ineffective protein depletion.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Cxcr2 in 308 CB GABA cells showed an exploratory pattern most notable for anti-correlation with Akt3, rather than a canonical same-direction PI3K/Akt relationship. In this cerebellar GABA context, Cxcr2 was only weakly positively related to Tlr9, Il6ra, and Il1rap, and the largest pathway-adjacent contrast pointed to uncoupling within MAPK/PI3K-Akt/NF-kB proximal inflammatory signaling. Important caveats are that Cxcr2 itself was not present in the 308 CB GABA target-transcript rows and no cerebellar GABA Cxcr2 differential-expression rows passed FDR, so this should be read as a warning signal rather than a mechanism.

Gata1 perturbation did not detectably engage the canonical erythroid and megakaryocyte GATA1 transcriptional program in this mouse brain context. Across curated cofactors and effector genes, including Zfpm1, Tal1, Lmo2, Ldb1, Klf1, Runx1, Itga2b, Gp1ba, Thbs1, Alas2, and globins such as Hba-a1, Hba-a2, Hbb-bs, Hbb-bt, and Hbb-y, no significant changes were observed; even the smallest nominal signals for Lmo2 and Ldb1 had FDR of 1. This negative pathway-level result is consistent with many erythroid genes having near-zero baseline expression in brain cells.

Agtrap showed a transcriptionally uncoupled profile from the expected angiotensin II/AT1R receptor-trafficking neighborhood in this unstimulated brain screen. Agtrap signature vectors were nearly orthogonal to Agtr1a, Agtr2, and Atp6ap2 perturbations, and canonical adjacent genes including Agtr1a, Agtr2, Atp6ap2, Rack1, Mas1, Clcn6, and Pitpnc1 were not FDR-regulated after Agtrap perturbation. This absence of an AT1R-like signature suggests the screen did not capture an active Ang II/AT1R axis, with the caveat that Agtr1a and Agtr2 perturbations were themselves weakly engaged and Atp6ap2 is a pathway neighbor rather than a direct AGTRAP complex member.

Chrnb4 perturbation did not yield a convergent α3β4α5 receptor-cluster signature: across the shared profiled cell classes, whole-transcriptome score-vector correlations with Chrna3, Chrna5, and Chrnb3 were near zero, and these related perturbations also showed no FDR-significant on-target mRNA decrease. Within nicotinic acetylcholine receptor / acetylcholine-gated cation channel signaling, the α3/β4/α5 cluster therefore appeared mostly unengaged, despite curated links among these subunits. This likely reflects low measurable expression or weak perturbation capture rather than evidence that α3β4α5 biology is unrelated, and no receptor currents were measured.

Atp6ap2 targeting in mouse-brain neurons did not produce a canonical renin-angiotensin transcriptional response: Agt, Ren1, Renbp, Ace, Ace2, Agtr1a, Agtr1b, Agtr2, and Mas1 remained unchanged at FDR significance. This suggests the perturbation readout is more consistent with V-ATPase/V0-related effects than with a detectable angiotensin-production or angiotensin-receptor feedback program. The negative result is qualified because renin-angiotensin signaling is often ligand- and protein-activity-driven, Ren2 was not measured, some pathway genes may be lowly expressed, and lack of mRNA changes does not exclude non-transcriptional signaling.

Nr3c2 showed a selective null within the nuclear receptor perturbation responses in this dataset: unlike other assayed family members in the same file, including Nr1d1, Nr1d2, Nr2c2, Nr2f1, and Nr3c1, Nr3c2 had zero FDR-significant hits. This pattern makes a purely analytic explanation less likely and instead suggests Nr3c2-specific context or a weaker perturbation, although nuclear receptor family membership alone does not imply identical expression, guide cutting efficiency, or ligand state.

Igsf1 perturbation in the assayed neural cell classes was uncoupled from the canonical pituitary TRH/TSH/FSH endocrine axis: Trh, Trhr, Tshb, Fshb, Tshr, Gnrhr, Lhb, Prl, and Gh were unchanged, with no detectable neuronal readout of the expected hormone pathway. This should be interpreted as a context mismatch rather than a contradiction, because the dataset profiles brain cells rather than anterior-pituitary thyrotropes or gonadotropes, and several pituitary hormone transcripts are sparsely detected. Endocrine-axis receptor perturbations and the Ig-superfamily comparator Igsf8 also did not phenocopy the Igsf1 signature.

Igsf1 perturbation produced a signature that was essentially uncorrelated with Trhr, Tshr, Gnrhr, and the membrane Ig-superfamily comparator Igsf8 in matched cell types, so expected endocrine-axis or IgSF neighbors did not phenocopy Igsf1. This differs from prior endocrine wiring that links Igsf1 with Trhr, Tshb, Trh, Pou1f1, and Prop1, but the contrast comes from an indirect neural assay rather than pituitary cells. Interpretation is further limited because Trhr, Tshr, and Gnrhr showed weak measured transcript engagement, and Igsf8, despite stronger on-target depletion, still remained uncorrelated with Igsf1.

Las1l knockdown did not produce coordinated polyadenylated mRNA changes in the expected LAS1L-NOL9/Rix1/5FMC neighborhood: Nol9, Tex10, Wdr18, Senp3, Pelp1, Kmt2a, Wdr5, Rbbp5, and Ash2l were measured but were not FDR-significantly altered. This left the rRNA processing and 60S ribosomal-subunit biogenesis pathway transcriptionally null in the dataset, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, Las1l was not Kmt2a-like. A caveat is that LAS1L complex function may change via localization, modification, or pre-rRNA cleavage without changing component polyadenylated mRNAs, and several core partners were not directly perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfat perturbation recurrently increased Setd1a RNA, with the clearest effect in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where Setd1a reached gene-level significance; across signatures, Setd1a was the dominant positive Zfat-responsive transcript but was often only nominally up. In contrast, measured SET1A/COMPASS partners Wdr5, Rbbp5, Ash2l, Dpy30, Cxxc1, and Wdr82 were not coordinately induced, including in broader thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic contexts, arguing for a selective Setd1a transcript effect rather than stoichiometric up-regulation of the full H3K4 methyltransferase complex; mRNA data alone do not establish complex abundance or activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zeb1 perturbation upregulated a compact polarity/adhesion/trafficking cassette rather than a broad canonical EMT program, with the strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a smaller overlapping module in 155 MB Glut. Across these cell types, Ap1m2, Stxbp2, Patj, and Spint2 recurred, while F11r and Cdc42bpg were strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This pattern is consistent with Zeb1 suppressing epithelial-like polarity genes, but the narrow module suggests a specialized neuronal regulon, and the dataset does not demonstrate physical junction formation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sorl1 showed only weak engagement in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic population, where it had no corrected downstream genes, whereas the pathway-neighbor perturbation Vps35 produced a corrected retromer-core transcriptional signature in the same class. This indicates that core retromer loss and Sorl1 loss were not interchangeable at the transcriptome level in this cell type, although the contrast is tempered by the nominal Sorl1 target engagement, so weaker depletion rather than biology alone could contribute to the difference.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pafah1b1 showed an exploratory, cell-type-focused sterol/ER-stress up-shift, most evident in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Fdps, Msmo1, Insig1, Dhcr24, Sqle, Fasn, Derl1, and Ddit3 rose at nominal or near-threshold levels. Weaker same-direction recurrence appeared in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This did not resemble a generic cell-type signature: the same cholesterol/SREBP-associated genes, including Hmgcr and Hmgcs1, were robustly induced after Dctn1 or Dync1h1 perturbation in matched classes. However, no Pafah1b1-regulated gene reached FDR<0.05, so the signal remains exploratory.

Eif5a did not phenocopy available translation or polyamine-adjacent perturbations in this dataset. Although EIF5A is functionally linked to DHPS/DOHH and translation, the Eif5a transcriptional signature was almost uncorrelated with Eif4e, Eef2, and Sms over shared differential-expression rows, arguing against interpreting this perturbation as broad hypusination or translation-elongation inhibition. This pattern was mostly buffered or divergent across examined cell types, with only an exploratory Eef2-concordant signal in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; Dhps, Dohh, and Eif5a2 were not screened, so those mechanistic neighbors were not directly tested.

Sms perturbation did not converge with the available polyamine-neighborhood perturbation in this dataset: the only assayed polyamine-dependent effector, Eif5a, showed essentially uncorrelated score-based expression signatures with Sms across shared cell types, including r = −0.0037 in 191 MB P MY GABA. Across examined classes, Sms was down while broader polyamine-pathway transcripts such as Odc1, Srm, Smox, Paox, Sat1, Sat2, Azin1, Azin2, Oaz1, and Oaz2 were not FDR-regulated, so Sms should not be used here as a generic proxy for polyamine depletion or eIF5A loss; this inference is limited because most core polyamine enzymes were not directly perturbed and comparisons were based on expression rather than metabolite or hypusination measurements.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Kras showed no FDR-significant transcriptional response in this dataset, and Hras likewise had none, including across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population, Kras displayed only a nominal, weak RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK MAPK-like pattern involving genes such as Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, Atp2a2, and Unc13a, whereas Nf1 produced an opposite, upward MAPK-output module and Braf or Map2k1 decreased the same module. Because Nf1, Braf, and Map2k1 yielded significant responses in the same dataset, the weak Kras result appears target- and context-specific rather than a general failure to detect MAPK transcription, although guide counts and target-transcript behavior differed across perturbations.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Lyst did not transcriptionally phenocopy AP-3, Rab27a, or other endolysosomal perturbations in the four best-engaged neuronal cell types—155 MB Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. Across these cells, all-gene correlations with comparators such as Ap3b1, Rab27a, Rab7, Lamp2, Wdfy3, Nbea, Vps13b, and Vps35l were near zero, with Ap3b1 and Rab27a correlations ≤0.031 in magnitude. Although STRING links Lyst to this lysosome-related-organelle network, the Lyst signatures were weak, canonical pathway mRNAs were not FDR-significant or convergent, and only one exploratory restricted-signature convergence with Vps35l was noted in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.

Bpnt2 knockdown showed no compensatory mRNA response in the Golgi PAPS/PAP turnover and glycosaminoglycan-sulfation pathway: Bpnt1, Papss1, Papss2, Slc35b2, Slc35b3, Hs6st2, Ust, Chst11, Chst12, Ndst1, Ndst2, B3gat3, and Csgalnact1 remained flat, with no downstream transcript reaching even a relaxed adjusted-P threshold. This was also seen in glutamatergic populations including 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut. The result refines prior BPNT2 biochemical phenotypes toward post-transcriptional Golgi metabolite or glycan-state readouts, with the caveat that only a small curated transcript set was examined and extracellular GAG sulfation was not measured.

Zhx3 showed no meaningful internal Perturb-seq signature neighbor: across matched score vectors, the strongest positive correlation was only with Gad2 (r=0.02897) and the strongest inverse correlation was with Cfl2 (r=-0.01481), while the largest per-cell-type correlation reached only Dnm2 (r=0.12856). This left the weak Zhx3 scalar signal without convergence from another perturbation. Interpretation is further limited because the most relevant comparators, Zhx1, Zhx2, and Nfya, were not perturbed in the screen, and weak target engagement could suppress both true and artifactual similarity.

Zhx3 did not recover the expected ZHX/NF-Y transcriptional-repression biology as a neuronal derepression module in this acute mouse-brain Perturb-seq screen. Across the tested neuronal strata, Zhx3 perturbation yielded no multiple-testing-corrected differentially expressed genes, no coherent convergent module, and no strong positive or inverse transcriptional-signature neighbor; even Zhx3 mRNA showed only weak, mixed, non-significant shifts after guide assignment. These results suggest a context-restricted or technically unengaged response relative to prior biochemical, fibroblast, and senescence studies involving ZHX-family dimerization and NF-YA-associated repression.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ifngr1 perturbation showed a coherent but only nominal decrease of a selected IFNγ receptor–JAK–STAT1/MHC-I antigen-presentation module in four non-cortical neuronal classes—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Across these cells, Stat1, B2m, H2-K1, H2-D1, Tap1, Tap2, Psmb8, Psmb9, Irf9, and Socs1 all trended downward; Stat1 was among the strongest negative genes in 151 and 191, and B2m was also strongly negative in 191. This direction fits reduced tonic IFNGR-to-STAT1 signaling, but all Ifngr1 module rows had FDR=1.0 and the module was hand-curated rather than discovered unbiasedly.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pgr in 308 CB GABA showed its closest perturbational convergence with Hmgcr rather than with another steroid receptor or nuclear-receptor coregulator, aligning the nominal Pgr synaptic program with a cholesterol/mevalonate-related signature. In this cell type, the shared pattern involved genes including Syp, Cadm3, Mapk10, Prkar1b, Gria2, B3galnt2, Pde5a, and Rreb1. However, both the Pgr and Hmgcr signatures were modest and subthreshold, so this similarity is only suggestive and does not directly demonstrate altered progesterone synthesis in the profiled cells.

Fbxw7 depletion did not produce a recurrent Notch/MYC/SREBP transcript program in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across a 15-gene panel including Myc, Mycn, Notch1/2/3, Srebf1/2, Ccne1/2, Mcl1, Mtor, Jun, Hes1, and Hey1, there were no FDR-significant rows, and perturbation signatures for Myc, Mycn, Notch1/2/3/4, and Srebf1/2 were essentially orthogonal to the sparse Fbxw7 signature. This near-null mRNA-level result should be interpreted cautiously because the assay reads RNA rather than FBXW7 substrate protein stability.

Gal showed a weak Perturb-seq profile, and the only assayed canonical receptor, Galr1, was similarly weak, with Gal versus Galr1 rank-score signatures essentially orthogonal across matched cell types (Spearman -0.0265 to 0.0447) rather than convergent. This suggests that the known galanin ligand-receptor relationship did not produce similar cell-autonomous transcriptional responses here. Interpretation is limited because the library covered only part of the family: Galr2, Galr3, Galp, and Spx were not assayed, and neither Gal nor Galr1 showed strong engagement.

F2 targeting left the measured coagulation and thrombin protease-activated receptor transcript program unchanged: F2, Thbd, F2r, F2rl1, F2rl2, F2rl3, and assayed clotting genes including F3, F5, F7, F9, F10, F11, F12, Proc, Procr, Serpinc1, Serpind1, and fibrinogen genes showed no detected transcriptional activation or repression. This argues against an autocrine thrombin-feedback loop in these Perturb-seq cells, although PAR signaling may be acute and post-transcriptional, and some fibrinogen genes were detected only in a subset of cell-type differential-expression tables.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Pomp perturbation in 155 MB Glut cells produced a proteasome “bounce-back” signature rather than a simple shutdown, with significant up-regulation of 13 Psm* genes including Psmd4, Psmd6, Psmc6, Psma1, Psmd2, Psme4, Psmc4, Psmd3, Psmc5, Psmc3, Psma5, Psmd1, and Psma3. This pattern is consistent with a compensatory proteasome-recovery program and converged with positive PSM signatures seen across perturbations such as Psmb4, Psmc1, and Psmc5, although Nfe2l1 mRNA itself was not significantly induced, so NRF1 pathway activation is inferred rather than directly measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Yy1 perturbation repeatedly produced a mixed-direction nuclear RNA-processing and spliceosomal program, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, with similar signatures in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and even 308 CB GABA despite fewer DE genes. Drosha, Rnpc3, Snrnp70, and Rsrp1 increased, whereas Akap8l, Clk1, Tial1, Metap1d, Dtx3, Lman2l, and Usp11 decreased; STRING terms highlighted RNA splicing, mRNA processing, ribonucleoprotein complex, nuclear speckle, and primary miRNA processing. These RNA-processing changes are expression responses from a recurrent-gene list, not proven direct YY1 targets.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tcf20 showed no FDR-significant transcriptional signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic cells, despite 143 perturbed cells and only nominal signals in its best-powered contrast. In the same thalamic cell type, several other neurodevelopmental regulators—Chd8, Mecp2, Setd5, Crebbp, and Rai1—did yield FDR-significant responses, indicating that this class was not globally insensitive and that Tcf20 was nonconvergent with otherwise active neurodevelopmental transcription-regulator perturbations. Because guide efficiency and cell numbers differed across perturbations, this contrast supports assay-specific divergence rather than proving TCF20 is biologically irrelevant in thalamic neurons.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mark3 showed no obvious transcriptional phenocopy across the assayed mouse brain cell classes: whole-mRNA score vectors were nearly orthogonal to tau/microtubule, AMPK-family, MAPK, and mTOR perturbations, including Brsk2, Mapt, Map1b, Mapk1, Mapk8, and Mtor, and no all-perturbation nearest neighbor was strong, with correlations not exceeding |r|=0.242. This pattern was seen across many glutamatergic and GABAergic types, with 308 CB GABA showing the strongest nominal Mark3 knockdown and the largest, yet still weak, neighbor correlations. Because these correlations use whole-transcriptome vectors, post-translational convergence or weak/delayed pathway coupling could have been missed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf9 showed a weak transcriptional convergence with Sin3a specifically in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the main cell type with a multi-gene Klf9 response. In restricted signature-neighbor analysis, Sin3a was the top positive neighbor of Klf9 and shared several Klf9-induced genes, including Hcn3, Dzip1, Aplp1, Wsb1, and Trrap, consistent with a KLF9-SIN3A corepressor neighborhood. However, the correlation was small (r=0.157) and Sin3a perturbation was much broader than Klf9, so this is best viewed as an exploratory prioritization rather than evidence of a direct complex in this cell type.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Camk2b was the only CaMKII paralog perturbation in this dataset with repeated FDR-level self-knockdown, including in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut, yet its significant signatures were essentially target-only after excluding the targeted transcript and showed no detectable CaMKII-family or non-target RNA module. By contrast, Camk2a lacked FDR-level self-knockdown and showed isolated non-self hits, while Camk2g had only one marginal self-hit in 155 MB Glut. Thus, CaMKII alpha, beta, and gamma perturbations were not interchangeable here, although this contrast is confounded by weaker on-target efficacy for Camk2a and Camk2g.

Nhs perturbation showed no detectable transcriptional response in the measured RAC/WAVE-Arp2/3 actin-remodeling program or related transcripts: Nhsl1, Nhsl2, Cyfip1, Cyfip2, Rac1, Wasf1, Wasf2, Wasf3, Brk1, Abi1, Abi2, Abi3, Actr2, Actr3, and Tjp1 were all FDR-negative. Thus, despite literature links between NHS and RAC/WAVE signaling at actin-rich junctional or lamellipodial structures, this dataset did not reveal a compensatory mRNA program, consistent with either weak engagement, post-transcriptional buffering, or effects on protein localization or actin structure that RNA profiling would miss.

Cux1 showed a mostly buffered acute transcriptomic response, and the direct paralog Cux2 did not rescue this as a shared CUT-family signature: across 22 matched groups, Cux2 produced only two FDR-significant rows and Cux1-versus-Cux2 signatures were essentially uncorrelated at both whole-transcriptome and top-gene levels. In 053 Sst Gaba, the strongest nominal Cux1 hit was Zfp30 while the only non-self FDR-significant Cux2 hit was Sun1, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Cux2 significantly lowered Cux2 mRNA whereas Cux1 showed almost no self response. Because Cux2 itself was weak in most groups, this mainly argues against a strong shared acute signature, not against possible developmental Cux1/Cux2 cooperation.

Trmt1 did not share a transcriptional signature with the assayed tRNA methylation neighbors Nsun2 or Alkbh8. Across matched cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Trmt1-versus-Nsun2 and Trmt1-versus-Alkbh8 score correlations remained near zero, and Trmt1 was also uncoupled from the Elp1/Elp2 ISR-like output within the broader tRNA modification network. This argues against a single interchangeable RNA-modification signature, although Nsun2 and Alkbh8 perturbations were themselves weak here, with no FDR<0.05 genes, so limited target engagement may contribute to the lack of convergence.

Zfp451 showed no robust Perturb-seq transcriptional response in this atlas, in contrast to the SUMO-associated E3 ligase Ranbp2, which produced a much clearer phenotype, while Nsmce2 was also weak. In the shared comparison set spanning SUMO2/3 conjugation and PML nuclear body neighbors, including Pml, Sumo1, Sumo2, and Sumo3, Zfp451 lacked a high-correlation signature neighbor, arguing against a generic shared SUMO-E3 transcriptomic response. However, this divergence could reflect poor Zfp451 knockdown rather than true dispensability or substrate specificity.

Camk2a showed a cell-type-restricted Perturb-seq response that was not recapitulated by the CaMKII paralogs Camk2b or Camk2g. The strongest FDR-supported Camk2a signal was in L4/5 IT CTX glutamatergic neurons, where Scn1b decreased and Pnisr and Fhl1 increased, while in L5 ET CTX glutamatergic neurons the response was limited to a single FDR-controlled gene, Rasal1. Across cell types, Camk2b and Camk2g had near-zero score correlations with Camk2a and more or different on-target depletion patterns, indicating divergent behavior within Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent CaMKII and NMDA receptor postsynaptic signaling, although Camk2a target engagement was weaker than Camk2b in several cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Naa15 produced strong, selective perturbation signatures in mouse-brain cells that were not recapitulated by related N-terminal acetyltransferase perturbations: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Naa10 showed no corrected differentially expressed hits, while Naa20 often gave broader, stronger signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with Naa15. This suggests NatA subunit perturbations were not interchangeable in this assay, although the Naa10 divergence is tempered by the lack of measurable Naa10 mRNA suppression, raising the possibility of guide inefficacy rather than biology.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Igf1r showed no FDR-significant differential expression in this screen, even in brain cell types where the same dataset detected strong PTEN-TSC2-mTOR growth-signaling responses to downstream regulator perturbation. Across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, 308 CB GABA, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Tsc2 and Pten produced many significant calls, whereas Igf1r remained silent, with only nominal decreases in some cells. This argues against global assay failure, but upstream IGF1R loss need not phenocopy direct loss of the downstream negative regulators Pten and Tsc2.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Igf1r, compared with Insr and Igf2r, did not behave as an interchangeable IGF-family receptor perturbation in 052 Pvalb Gaba cells. In this cell type, Igf2r—not Igf1r or Insr—showed a significant on-target transcript decrease, and matched target-transcript measurements indicated heterogeneous engagement across the three receptors. Igf1r-related restricted signatures also failed to align consistently with either Insr or Igf2r, with no stable IGF1R-proximal or PI3K/mTOR-like neighbor, although this comparison is driven mainly by target-transcript engagement rather than receptor-specific biology.

Hbs1l did not phenocopy the available indirect surveillance comparators Xrn1 or Rack1: across matched cell types, Hbs1l score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Xrn1 and Rack1 perturbations. This suggests the modest Hbs1l signal is unlikely to reflect a generic mRNA-decay or ribosome-associated perturbation artifact, and in the PELO-HBS1L-ABCE1 ribosome rescue/no-go and non-stop decay context there was no robust Hbs1l differential-expression pattern and no Xrn1/Rack1 phenocopy. A key caveat is that the direct partners PELO and ABCE1 were not screened.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Naa20 produced strong neuronal transcriptional signatures that did not phenocopy the assayed NatA-family perturbations. Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Naa20 was strong, whereas Naa10 showed no FDR-significant genes and Naa15 effects were weaker and essentially uncorrelated with Naa20 despite all being N-terminal acetyltransferase family members. The largest response was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with recurrent Cyp46a1 suppression; exploratory neighbors suggested convergence with proteostasis and RNA-processing perturbations. Naa25 was not assayed, and the null Naa10 result could reflect guide performance rather than dispensability of NatA.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rarg showed no detectable corrected downstream signal in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population despite 168 perturbed cells, whereas Ctnnb1 and Thra perturbations in the same high-count cell type produced FDR-supported effects and self-transcript depletion. This suggests the Rarg null in this population was not simply a low-power artifact or a general insensitivity of the cell type to guide perturbation. However, because Ctnnb1 and Thra are not direct RARG complex members, this comparison supports dataset power rather than a mechanistic retinoid-specific contrast.

Irs1 showed little transcriptional similarity to perturbations of its receptor-proximal or mTOR-axis neighbors: across Insr, Igf1r, Igf2r, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Pik3r2, Pten, Ptpn11, Sos1, Mapk1, Akt3, Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1, and Tsc2, the largest absolute Wilcoxon-score correlation with the Irs1 signature was only 0.085. In contrast, Tsc1 and Tsc2 produced broad FDR-supported programs, including in 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, suggesting Irs1 loss was transcriptionally uncoupled from canonical IRS-mediated insulin/IGF and PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in this screen; however, these comparisons rely on single-cell Wilcoxon summaries, and weak Irs1 knockdown could have obscured expected similarities.

Ror2 did not show convergence with a WNT5A receptor-neighborhood module across all shared neuronal classes: its score vectors were only weakly correlated with Ror1, Ryk, Frizzled/LRP receptors (Fzd2, Fzd3, Fzd4, Fzd6, Fzd9, Lrp5, Lrp6), Celsr2, or downstream noncanonical Wnt/PCP-adjacent nodes such as Mapk8, Mapk9, Fyn, Cdc42, and Rac1. Ror1 and Ryk were likewise transcriptionally silent in this dataset, and the strongest Ror2 neighbors were low amplitude, including a safe-target anti-neighbor. Interpretation is limited because Wnt5a and several core PCP components were not perturbed, and Ror2/Ror1/Ryk self-transcripts were not detectably knocked down.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gtf2ird1 showed a distinct RNA signature in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class, arguing that related Williams-Beuren locus perturbations are not interchangeable in this cell type. Although Gtf2i and Baz1b had strong decreases of their own transcripts, their FDR<0.1 genes did not overlap the seven Gtf2ird1 hits, while Clip2 and Limk1 had no FDR<0.1 genes; score correlations between Gtf2ird1 and these four perturbations were near zero, and nearest-neighbor matching found no strongly correlated perturbation. This comparison is based on RNA signatures only, with differing perturbed-cell counts and target-transcript behavior across perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Hras was largely buffered in this screen and did not phenocopy downstream RAS/MAPK or mTOR-axis perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Hras had no corrected response genes despite nominal target depletion, whereas Braf, Map2k1, Mapk1, Nf1, Pten, Tsc1, and Tsc2 showed corrected signatures; similarly, in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Tsc1/Tsc2 remained significant while Hras stayed silent. Restricted score correlations likewise did not show a strong signed Hras phenocopy, although differences in editing efficiency, pathway position, and loss-of-function consequence temper direct comparison.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Peg3 showed a largely self-specific Perturb-seq signature rather than behaving like a generic imprinted-gene or predicted-interactor module. Across 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, robust Ndn and Snrpn knockdowns had near-zero same-cell-type score-vector correlations with Peg3, and exhaustive comparisons found no strong non-self neighbor; the best was only weak, Fzd3 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA at r=0.176. These correlations reflect transcriptional similarity, not protein interaction, and some imprinted-domain genes such as Zim1 were not perturbed or detected.

cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Nr2e3 showed no convergent brain signature with related retinal transcriptional regulators in the assayed cells, including 217 P MY Pineal Glut. Broad score-vector correlations were uniformly tiny, with the largest |r| only 0.106 and Nr2e3 correlations with Crx and Nrl in pineal cells of 0.027 and 0.016, respectively. Crx, Rorb, Esrrb, and Nr2e1 produced no shared-class FDR-significant genes, and although Nrl had two isolated FDR hits, there was no coherent shared module, arguing against a hidden rod/cone-like NR2E3-CRX-NRL program in these brain cells.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Arid1a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed its strongest convergence with canonical BAF core perturbations: across 2,045 other perturbations, Smarcc2, Smarcb1, and Smarce1 were the top three positive signature neighbors. In this cell type, which was the only group with FDR-corrected Arid1a downstream genes, Smarcc2 and Smarcb1 changed all 21 non-Arid1a corrected genes in the same direction as Arid1a, including Nexn, Clstn2, Begain, Ptprz1, and Ptpn3. Full-rank correlations were modest in absolute value, and Arid1b, Arid2, Smarca2, and Smarca4 were uncoupled.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Gfpt1 perturbation did not phenocopy direct Ogt perturbation, even though Ogt was strongly downregulated within the Gfpt1 signature. Whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon score correlations between Gfpt1 and Ogt were low in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba; notably, Pvalb cells showed a large local response to Ogt knockdown but no FDR-significant Gfpt1 signature. In Gfpt1-sensitive neurons, the state combined Ogt/Oga downregulation with ER/integrated-stress genes such as Ddit3 and Hspa5, suggesting that reduced UDP-GlcNAc may affect N-glycosylation or other glycan routes in addition to O-GlcNAc cycling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Cyfip2 knockdown reduced Cyfip2 mRNA in six engaged cell classes—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA—but did not significantly change transcripts for WAVE regulatory complex and related pathway genes, including Cyfip1, Abi1/2, Nckap1/Nckap1l, Brk1, Wasf1/2, Actr2/3, Fmr1, Rac1, Shank3, Tmem108, Bdnf, or Ntrk2. Thus canonical WRC, RAC1 GTPase cycle, and BDNF-NTRK2 endocytic-trafficking transcripts appeared uncoupled from the perturbation, although only mRNA was measured and unchanged transcripts do not exclude altered complex activity.

Scn1a did not show a convergent transcriptomic response with the sodium-channel beta-subunit perturbation Scn1b. Although Scn1b had broader on-target knockdown than Scn1a, it still produced only four FDR off-target genes, and across the 23 shared cell types the Scn1a–Scn1b whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon score-vector correlations were near zero, ranging from -0.037 to 0.073. This indicates that SCN1A–SCN1B channel-complex membership did not translate into interchangeable single-cell RNA signatures here, with the caveat that the comparison reflects transcriptional convergence rather than electrophysiological beta-subunit modulation.

Tead1 perturbation did not produce a detectable canonical Hippo/YAP-TAZ-TEAD transcriptional output in the assayed neuronal cells: established TEAD/YAP targets Ccn1, Ccn2, Apoe, and Dab2 all showed no corrected response, with FDR = 1 across Tead1 results. This lack of movement also did not converge with Nf2 in the same pathway context. A key caveat is that TEAD1 protein was not measured, and some TEAD targets were lowly expressed, which can make logFC estimates uninformative; moreover, the Tead1 transcript itself was not significantly depleted or enriched in any cell type with a Tead1 result.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ppp3r1 knockdown produced its only multi-gene FDR-level response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, revealing a mixed-direction synapse and cell-junction module with Pcsk1n, Ptprs, Tle2, and Ndrg2 increased and Atp2a2, Coro6, Septin4, and Slc6a17 decreased. This was the strongest non-target Ppp3r1 response module in the dataset and sharpens the transcriptional output of calcineurin biology to a thalamic glutamatergic class, but the effect is RNA-level, cell-type restricted, and does not directly measure phosphatase activity, NFAT localization, vesicle cycling, or synaptic physiology.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ghr showed a weak perturbation profile: although the intended transcript was measured, Ghr-targeted cells did not show reproducible Ghr RNA depletion, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. This was not a generic failure to detect signaling-gene perturbations in the atlas, because Stat1, Mapk1, and Akt3 displayed detectable self-transcript depletion in selected neuronal classes, including the same Ghr-relevant contexts. These comparators are downstream or parallel JAK/STAT, MAPK, and PI3K/AKT pathway nodes rather than receptor paralogs, so their phenotypes are not expected to phenocopy GHR.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Arhgap18 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut showed its strongest transcriptomic signal, marked by weak Arhgap18 mRNA output and exploratory Myo6 up-regulation, yet it did not phenocopy Rho-family neighbors. Correlations with Arhgap32, Rac1, and Cdc42 were only 0.119, 0.085, and -0.009, and no other perturbation reached |r|≥0.20, even though related Rho-family perturbations were present and sometimes produced stronger scalar signatures. This uncoupling is transcriptomic and may partly reflect weak target engagement, while canonical Rhoa and Rhoc perturbations were not available.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Cplx2 showed a null transcriptional signature in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut: there were zero FDR-significant rows and essentially no Cplx2 mRNA shift. In the same cortical IT population, the comparator perturbation Stxbp1 produced a strong presynaptic-neighbor response with 67 FDR-significant rows, including target depletion and synaptic genes such as Nrxn2, Slc30a3, Mast3, and Fcho1, indicating that SNARE-dependent synaptic vesicle exocytosis perturbations can be detected in this compartment. Because Stxbp1 is not a Cplx2 paralog and may differ in exocytosis breadth or guide engagement, it serves as an assay-capacity control rather than a mechanistically matched control.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hdac5 in the two best-engaged cell types, 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, showed signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with available perturbations of Hdac4, Mef2c, Mef2d, Camk2b, Ppp3ca, and Ppp2r1a, arguing that these class IIa HDAC and calcium-signaling neighbors are not interchangeable transcriptional proxies in the assayed basal brain states. In 155 MB Glut, Hdac5 knockdown was FDR-supported but otherwise buffered, with only an exploratory nominal Npas4 increase, while 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the largest nominal Hdac5 score and rank-1 target depletion but no FDR-significant genes; low Hdac5 signal amplitude and the absence of perturbations for direct interactors such as Hdac3, Hdac7, Hdac9, Ncor1, and Ncor2 limit correlation power.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Creb1 perturbation recurrently induced the paralog-family gene Crem, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas efficient perturbation of upstream cAMP/PKA, NMDA-receptor, and CaMKII pathway neighbors—Prkaca, Camk2b, Grin2b, Grin2a, and Adcy3—depleted their own transcripts in the same responsive classes but did not induce Crem. This argues that the Creb1-to-Crem signature reflects a CREB-family identity or compensation response rather than simple loss of upstream drive, with the caveat that these are basal transcriptomic comparisons and may not capture acute kinase activity or ligand-evoked CREB phosphorylation.

Fzd4 perturbation in the assayed neuronal classes did not engage a coherent canonical Wnt/FZD transcriptional program: across 22 glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, no gene reached FDR significance, target mRNA was not significantly shifted, and a curated panel including Wls, Dvl3, Ctnnb1, Axin2, Lrp6, and Csnk1e showed no coordinated response. This argues against a hidden canonical Wnt or beta-catenin signature in these neuronal data, although the check was a curated gene-panel inspection rather than a full pathway-enrichment test, and all signals remained below FDR significance.

Actg1 did not show strong transcriptomic convergence with perturbations of curated actin-network neighbors. Across the full neighbor scan, Cfl2, Cdc42, Cyfip2, Cyfip1, Rac1, and Limk1 failed to produce a shared ACTG1-like RNA signature, and the closest positive or negative neighbor to Actg1 had |Pearson r| ≤ 0.142 in the eight well-engaged Actg1 cell classes. This held in robust Actg1 knockdown classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, despite pathway links to RHO/WAVE/cofilin actin remodeling; many neighbor perturbations mainly showed self knockdown, so the conclusion is limited to transcriptomic similarity rather than actin biochemistry.

Ulk4 did not show convergence with the available Hedgehog, ciliary, or autophagy-neighbor perturbations in the assayed neurons: Sqstm1, Trak1, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, and Cspp1 all had median z-score correlations with Ulk4 near zero, roughly 0 to 0.015. This restricted-signature comparison therefore does not support a broad linear Hedgehog–cilium transcriptional output from Ulk4 in these neurons, but the result is exploratory because direct GLI target-transcript engagement was weak and key comparators, notably Stk36 and Sufu, were not perturbed.

Yeats2 was isolated in perturbation-signature space across all 21 Yeats2-profiled cell types: nearest positive and negative neighbors had very small correlations (|r| < 0.17), and related chromatin or acetylation perturbations including Atxn7, Brd4, Kansl1, and Msl2 also showed only small correlations. Consistent with this, pan-cell-type analysis found weak Yeats2 target-transcript engagement, no FDR-resolved genes, no coordinated ATAC-subunit feedback, and no recurrent shared module. Because canonical ATAC members were not available as comparators and the Yeats2 signatures were weak, these data do not support using Yeats2 as a surrogate for broader acetyl-lysine reader, SAGA, or MSL/KANSL programs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fhit was uncoupled from beta-catenin transcriptional regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: after Fhit perturbation, canonical Wnt/beta-catenin genes including Ctnnb1, Lef1, Tcf7l2, Axin2, Myc, and Ccnd1 did not pass FDR correction, and Fhit signatures were nearly orthogonal to Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 signatures. In the same dataset, Ctnnb1 perturbation produced a strong thalamic response, so the contrast suggests that FHIT-Wnt expectations from cancer-cell literature do not transfer directly here, although this is a pathway-neighbor comparison and weak Fhit transcript engagement leaves the negative arm underpowered.

Limk1 did not share a convergent mRNA signature with canonical neighbors in the Rho GTPase–PAK/ROCK–LIMK–cofilin actin regulation pathway: perturbations of Pak1, Pak2, Pak3, Cdc42, Rac1, and Cfl2 were nearly uncorrelated with Limk1 and were mostly limited to self-only or FDR-negative transcriptional effects. This suggests the expected pathway coupling did not emerge at the steady-state mRNA level in the queried set, with the caveat that Rock1, Rock2, Limk2, Cfl1, and Ssh1/2/3 were not recovered and the readout was mRNA rather than kinase activity, cofilin phosphorylation, or actin morphology.

Ptchd1 was uncoupled from canonical Smoothened/Hedgehog signaling in the assayed neurons: whole-transcriptome signatures showed near-zero correlation between Ptchd1 perturbation and perturbations of Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Gli1, Gli2, and Gli3, and canonical Hedgehog receptor/effector transcripts were not detectably changed by Ptchd1 perturbation. This argues against Ptchd1 phenocopying canonical Smoothened/Gli Hedgehog output in this dataset, although the inference is limited because the comparison is transcriptome-based and the Ptchd1 perturbation response itself was weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tspan12 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed an isolated, FDR-significant response marked by B4gat1 induction, but its perturbation signature did not converge with Fzd4, Lrp5, Lrp6, Ctnnb1, or Tspan7. In this thalamic class, canonical Norrin/FZD4/LRP5/6/beta-catenin readouts such as Axin2 were absent, score-vector correlations with these comparators were near zero, and the strongest contrast was with Ctnnb1, which produced a large transcriptional response. However, Fzd4 and Lrp5 themselves had little detectable downstream signal, so the nonconvergence is clearest versus Ctnnb1 and only partial versus Lrp6.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zscan26 knockdown in 155 MB Glut cells, the only subclass with FDR-confirmed target-transcript depletion, did not show an FDR-supported serum-response/immediate-early RNA program: Fos, Jun, Egr1, Dusp1, Arc, and Npas4 were not significantly changed. This refines the older annotation of ZSCAN26 as SRE-ZBP, a human cDNA clone identified by binding the c-fos serum-response element, by indicating that constitutive Fos/Egr/Jun-like regulon engagement was not detected in unstimulated mouse midbrain glutamatergic neurons; stimulation dependence or post-translational regulation remains possible.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Akt3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed little downstream transcriptional response despite this cell class being capable of strong PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling signatures: in the same neurons, Pten, Tsc1, and Tsc2 perturbations produced 33, 321, and 86 FDR-significant genes, whereas Akt3 produced none, even where target-transcript depletion was near threshold. This pattern argues that Akt3 is a buffered kinase node relative to the PTEN/TSC brake genes, although perturbation efficiencies differed across genes, so differential expression counts should not be read as equal molecular effect sizes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gsk3b knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells did not reproduce the canonical Wnt/β-catenin destruction-complex transcriptional output seen with Apc or Ctnnb1 perturbation: Apc and Ctnnb1 produced strong Axin2/Lef1-associated signatures, whereas Gsk3b left Axin2 unchanged and correlated poorly with those Wnt signatures, including Tcf7l2-linked output. This contrast is therefore better read as single-isoform pathway uncoupling rather than pan-GSK3 or canonical Wnt activation, with the caveat that Gsk3a was not targeted, so inferred GSK3A/GSK3B redundancy was not directly tested here.

Arnt2 showed no convergence with its expected bHLH-PAS partner network in this basal Perturb-seq setting: genome-wide score-vector correlations with Arnt, Ahr, Hif1a, Sim1, and Npas3 were near zero, and the measured activity-dependent Npas4/Bdnf axis was not detectably altered. This result rests on weak Arnt2 signatures and does not exclude context-dependent coupling, since AHR, HIF, SIM1, and NPAS4 programs are typically ligand-, hypoxia-, developmental-, or activity-gated and those conditions were not established in the assayed cells.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Elp2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a concordant signature with the Elongator core subunit Elp1: 129 of 150 Elp2 FDR genes overlapped Elp1 with the same sign, consistent with Elongator-dependent tRNA wobble-uridine modification and proteostasis stress involving Asns, Chac1, and Slc7a5. However, Elp1 was quantitatively broader, with 645 FDR genes in 151 and additional FDR responses in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; guide efficiency and protein depletion were not directly measured, so this difference could be technical, biological, or both.

Folr1 showed near-zero concordance with related perturbations in this dataset, arguing against a hidden Folr1 module captured by another target. In a restricted signature-neighbor analysis based on the top Folr1 genes, the only perturbed STRING-proximal folate neighbor, Tfrc, had a mean cosine of -0.0248. Aggregate signature neighbors were also weak, with Zfp949 at 0.1469 and Tfdp2 at -0.0966. This interpretation is limited because Folr2, Slc19a1, and Slc46a1 were not perturbation targets, and the comparison used only the restricted Folr1 signature.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Sec23a showed a divergent profile from the related Sec31a perturbation rather than a same-complex phenocopy. In 155 MB Glut, Sec31a produced a strong 60-gene program with upregulation of Sec23a, Copa, and Copb1, plus broader COPI/Golgi-associated changes, while the Sec23a knockdown itself showed target-only Sec23a reduction without COPII compensation or a comparable genome-wide signature. A similar Sec31a-associated state appeared in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. However, this contrast is caveated because measured Sec31a mRNA increased rather than decreased, so it cannot be interpreted as a clean SEC31A loss-of-function effect.

Eif2ak4 was essentially silent in this assay, even in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population where editing was most evident and the target transcript decreased nominally, while neighboring translational-control perturbations were clearly detected: Tsc1, Tsc2, and Eif4e produced 1,162, 423, and 184 FDR-significant rows, whereas Atf6 and Eif2ak4 produced none. Global score correlations between Eif2ak4 and those perturbations were near zero, suggesting the null result is branch-specific and consistent with separation of the GCN2/eIF2-alpha arm from the TSC–mTOR–EIF4E cap-dependent arm, rather than a generic assay failure.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cyfip1 did not phenocopy the EIF4E/TSC translation-growth transcriptional programs in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, or 155 MB Glut. In matched analyses, Eif4e, Tsc1, and Tsc2 produced detectable downstream mRNA programs, including 10–478 FDR-significant genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, whereas Cyfip1 produced no FDR-significant secondary hits. Even where Cyfip1 showed its best self-depletion in 155 MB Glut, it remained just above FDR 0.05, so Cyfip1 knockout should not be used here as a proxy for Eif4e loss or TSC/mTOR pathway activation; this contrast is pathway-level rather than a direct complex-member comparison.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp521 showed no detectable transcriptomic response in the sampled neuronal signatures where its related factor Zfp423 was strongly active: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Zfp423 produced 150 FDR-significant genes whereas Zfp521 produced none with comparable cell numbers, and a smaller Zfp423-only response also appeared in 308 CB GABA, where Zfp423 had seven significant genes and Zfp521 again had none. This separates the Zfp521-Zfp423 transcriptional regulation axis in these neurons, although the comparison is transcriptomic and does not establish Zfp521 editing efficiency; notably, Zfp423 target mRNA increased rather than decreased, underscoring that target-transcript direction is an imperfect proxy.

Serpini1 showed no convergent RNA-signature neighborhood for its expected tPA/plasminogen serine-protease inhibition pathway: the core axis genes Plat, Plau, Plaur, and Plg were not perturbed in the panel, and the measured STRING-linked partners App, Lrp1, and Prnp did not phenocopy Serpini1. In cell types with confident target knockdown, including 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, no perturbation strongly converged with the Serpini1 signature, with at most weak or nominal neighbors. This negative result is tempered by the absence of key proteases and by whole-transcriptome correlation being an indirect readout of extracellular protease activity.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Foxp3 perturbation in the profiled mouse brain cell classes, including multiple glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, and pineal populations, did not detectably decrease Foxp3 itself and did not robustly alter the canonical FOXP3/RUNX/NFAT regulatory-T-cell module, with Ctla4, Il2ra, Tnfrsf18, Il2, Ifng, Runx1, Nfatc2, and Rela all failing significance. This pattern suggests the expected FOXP3 program was uncoupled in these brain contexts, likely reflecting cell-type mismatch or weak target engagement rather than evidence against FOXP3 regulation in T cells.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Sp4 perturbation produced a cell-class-selective transcriptional response in glutamatergic neurons, with both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut converging on an upregulated Tsga10/Abhd11-centered module. Tsga10 and Abhd11 were FDR-significant in both classes, while Dnajc4, Svip, and Strada recurred with one FDR call plus strong nominal support, making them plausible shared Sp4-response biomarkers. The thalamic class showed the strongest overall signature, but canonical NMDAR/NT3/Nwk2-related mRNAs were not FDR-changed, and additional downregulation such as Stxbp2/Tspan17 appeared more 151-specific.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nr3c1 perturbation produced a weak, cell-restricted Wnt/β-catenin feedback signal in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic neurons: Axin2 was the top up-regulated gene and narrowly missed FDR<0.05, while Aifm3 and Ptprm were near-FDR and downregulated. Most other assayed cell types showed no robust FDR-level transcriptional response to Nr3c1 loss, so this pattern argues against a pan-neuronal effect. Because other Wnt components were not coordinately significant, Axin2 alone does not establish pathway direction, and the finding refines rather than proves GR–Wnt cross-talk.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Phf12 produced its strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where an induced RNA splicing/ribonucleoprotein program, including Srsf11, Dhx38, and Sf3b2, was coupled to repression of synaptic and glutamatergic neuronal effector genes such as Gls, Syt7, Grin2c, Snap25, and Tubb3. A similar but smaller pattern appeared in 155 MB Glut, indicating a mixed response rather than simple de-repression. The down-regulated synaptic genes may reflect an indirect endpoint state, since chromatin occupancy and nascent-transcription data were not measured.

Pax8 perturbation in 22 assayed brain subclasses did not induce or repress the canonical thyroid follicular-cell program: Tg, Tpo, Slc5a5, Tshr, Nkx2-1, Foxe1, and Hhex showed no measurable coordinated movement, with FDR = 1.0 wherever measured. Thus, despite the known Pax8–Nkx2-1 thyroid differentiation circuit, the PAX8 thyroid differentiation and thyroid hormone biosynthetic pathway was not detected in these brain contexts.
