This inference is limited to transcriptomic readouts from brain cells, where many thyroid-pathway genes are likely near the detection floor.

Tshr knockdown in these receptor-low mouse brain neurons did not measurably activate or repress the canonical TSHR–GNAS/GNAQ–cAMP and thyroid differentiation module: Gnas, Gnaq, Tshb, Cga, Tg, Tpo, Slc5a5, Nkx2-1, and Pax8 were all nonsignificant, with no detected response across tested brain classes. This transcriptional uncoupling contrasts with curated thyroid biology and favors a context-missing explanation rather than a thyroid-like response, although the lack of detectable Tshr target depletion means a fully effective loss-of-function perturbation cannot be confirmed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Rab7 showed strong positive signature similarity with Vps41, Tsc1, and Tsc2 in Rab7-responsive cell types, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In these classes, Rab7-associated changes were linked to endo-lysosomal trafficking and vacuolar acidification genes such as Atp6v0b, Lamp2, Mcoln1, and Dpp7, with Tsc1/Tsc2 convergence and opposing Mtor/Rptor patterns consistent with a lysosomal mTOR/TFEB stress axis. This similarity was defined on a 529-gene Rab7-restricted signature, and Vps41 itself had weak genome-wide FDR support, so the Vps41 relationship appeared strongest within the Rab7-focused gene set rather than as a broad differential-expression program.

Wdr48 showed weak or absent convergence in this dataset: the library did not include perturbations of its known USP-complex partners Usp1, Usp12, Usp46, or Wdr20, so direct complex-member comparisons could not be made. Consistent with that limited coverage, no strong positive or negative signature neighbor emerged, and the closest non-safe-target same-cell neighbor reached only r=0.194, arguing against using unrelated top neighbors such as Atp6ap1, Bicra, Sptb, or Sacs as mechanistic substitutes. These correlations were derived from Wilcoxon score vectors rather than replicate-level cells.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Gabrg2 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed a weak, Bdnf-led activity response that sits in a restricted excitability-signature neighborhood shared with Gphn and especially Kcnb1. In this cortical glutamatergic cell type, a top-50 non-target gene neighbor scan placed Gphn and Kcnb1 as the closest positive neighbors over the Gabrg2 response genes, and Kcnb1 independently produced a stronger Bdnf/Vgf program in the same cells. This suggests convergence on BDNF/VGF activity-dependent trophic transcription, but the pattern is exploratory because the scan was restricted and no formal correlation FDR was applied, while Gphn itself showed limited direct differential expression.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kif1b was not transcriptionally interchangeable with the related perturbations Kif1a or Kifbp in this dataset. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, where Kif1b showed the clearest downstream effect, Kif1a did not reduce Snap25, Gad1, or Pvalb, and Kifbp produced only a much weaker nominal Snap25 decrease, indicating divergence in a presynaptic SNARE and inhibitory-marker response. In 155 MB Glut, strong Kif1a or Kifbp engagement likewise did not recreate a Kif1b-like transcriptome, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Kif1a was only weakly closer. These contrasts are based on RNA signatures, so shared cargo-transport biology may still exist without transcriptional interchangeability.

Fosl2 perturbation did not mobilize published AP-1/FOSL2 neuronal readouts in this assay: Bdnf, Rgs4, and nearby BDNF-TrkB/MAPK-axis genes Ntrk2, Mapk1, and Mapk3 all remained unchanged, with no FDR-supported response in any Fosl2-assigned cell class. This suggests that the reported AP-1/BDNF and FRA-2/FOSL2–Rgs4 relationships were not reproduced under these basal guide-assigned brain-cell conditions, and may reflect stimulated contexts or other cell types rather than the mouse classes assayed here.

Nsun2 depletion did not elicit transcriptional compensation in its proximal RNA-modification network: across aggregated cell types, Trdmt1, Ftsj1, Pus7, Nat10, Mettl1, Gtpbp4, Pum3, Nop58, Brix1, and Noc2l remained near zero, and canonical/proximal RNA-modification genes were not detectably shifted as a block. This suggests that acute Nsun2 perturbation is not sensed through a compensatory mRNA-feedback loop in the RNA cytosine-5 methylation, tRNA stabilization, and ncRNA-processing/ribosome-biogenesis neighborhood, although unchanged partner mRNA does not exclude altered enzyme activity, localization, substrates, or RNA modifications.

Rbm28 could not be directly compared with its expected complex neighbors in this Perturb-seq dataset because none of the top 20 mouse STRING functional partners—Nifk, Ddx27, Cebpz, Rbm34, Ebna1bp2, Gtpbp4, Noc2l, Ddx24, Rrp12, Pum3, Pdcd11, Rpf2, Ppan, Bms1, Rsl1d1, Pes1, Nat10, Ddx56, Nvl, and Lsg1—were present as perturbation targets. As a result, direct convergence or divergence within the RBM28 functional neighborhood was untestable, and the strongest available full-transcriptome similarities to Rbm28 should be interpreted as modest, indirect state similarities rather than evidence of interchangeability with a specific complex member.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Diaph2 showed an uncoupled transcriptional signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells: it did not phenocopy same-cell perturbations of Cdc42, Rac1, Rho, Fmn1, Fmn2, Mrtfa, actin-family targets such as Actb, Actg1, and Actn4, or Rho regulators including Arhgap18, Arhgap32, and Arhgef9. Canonical actin/SRF and mDia-linked transcripts, including Srf, Mapre1, Pfn1, and Pfn2, were not detectably altered, but these near-zero correlations come from weak, underpowered Diaph2 signatures with no observed target-transcript knockdown or FDR-significant genes.

Arhgap32 knockdown did not elicit a detectable acute transcriptional response in the expected NMDA receptor, cadherin, Rho-family GTPase, Pak/MAPK, or synaptic scaffold module: across 704 tested rows, no measured changes in Rac1, Cdc42, Pak1/2/3, Grin1/2a/2b/2d, Dlg4, Cdh2, Ctnnb1, Ctnna2, Fyn, Mapk1, Camk2g, Shank2, or Shank3 reached FDR 0.10. This suggests the ARHGAP32/RICS mechanism is not captured as a robust acute mRNA program here, with the caveat that transcript profiling cannot measure GTP loading, receptor trafficking, or spine morphology.

Kcnma1 perturbation did not elicit a detectable transcriptional compensation in the canonical BK beta/gamma accessory-subunit program: Kcnmb1, Kcnmb2, Kcnmb3, Kcnmb4, and the gamma-subunit genes Lrrc26, Lrrc38, Lrrc52, and Lrrc55 showed no FDR-significant mRNA changes. This suggests accessory-subunit abundance was not detectably rewired at the transcript level to offset alpha-subunit knockdown, although some accessory genes were likely lowly expressed in droplet profiles, and the dataset measured mRNA rather than BK-channel assembly or surface localization.

Nr1i2 perturbation did not elicit the canonical PXR/RXR xenobiotic-metabolism and drug-transporter program in the assayed brain cells. Across representative CYP, ABC, UGT, SLCO, and ALDH genes, including Abcb1a, Abcb1b, Abcc2, Abcc3, Aldh1a1, Cyp1a2, Cyp2b10, Slco1a4, Ugt1a1, Sult2a1, and the expected liver PXR targets Cyp3a11 and Cyp3a44, no activation or repression was detected in any assayed brain cell class. This uncouples the neuronal Perturb-seq signature from the textbook hepatic or intestinal PXR state, with the caveat that loss of a lowly expressed, unliganded receptor in neurons is not equivalent to ligand activation in hepatocytes or enterocytes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ap2s1 showed convergence with the AP-2 complex subunit Ap2m1 rather than a generic endocytic-neighbor pattern. In the clearest responsive classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Ap2m1 knockdown closely matched the Ap2s1 signature, including 139 FDR-significant genes in 151 with 138 in the same direction, while Dnm1 knockdown was largely buffered and had little transcriptomic impact beyond Dnm1 itself. A smaller Ap2s1-responsive program was also seen in 191 MB P MY GABA. Only Ap2m1, not AP-2 alpha or beta core subunits, was available as a direct complex comparator.

Gpc6 showed no stable restricted-signature convergence with other HS-GAG or cell-surface glypican biology genes. Direct family comparators were not available as perturbation targets, with Gpc1-Gpc5 and Sdc1-Sdc4 absent from the perturbation table, so the nearest-neighbor analysis relied on the top 200 absolute Gpc6-score genes per cell type. Under that constraint, the closest neighbors were modest and cell-type idiosyncratic, including Cacna1g, Tsc2, and Nfe2l1, arguing against a paralog-rescue or direct HS-proteoglycan module interpretation and instead highlighting a coverage caveat.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Frmd5 showed little acute transcriptional coupling to expected adherens-junction or Wnt neighbors in adult neurons. In the best-sampled 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Frmd5 had 174 perturbed cells but no FDR<0.05 response, while Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 produced strong corrected signatures in the same class; across assayed comparators including Cdh2 and Akt3, no perturbation closely matched or opposed the Frmd5 signature, with the strongest neighbor only r=0.166. Interpretation is limited because direct interactors such as Ctnnd1, Itgb5, and Rock1 were not assayed, and prior FRMD5 biology comes mainly from cancer or epithelial systems.

Cc2d1a knockdown did not transcriptionally resolve canonical NF-kB or Rac1-associated synaptic signaling: Nfkb1, Rela, Map3k7, and Rac1 mRNAs were not FDR-significant, and Map3k7 or Nfkb1 perturbation signatures were nearly orthogonal to the Cc2d1a profile. Across tested comparators, including ESCRT, receptor, transcription-factor, and intellectual-disability genes, none reproduced the Cc2d1a score vectors. This null result is consistent with the caveat that NF-kB and Rac1 are often controlled by localization, phosphorylation, ubiquitination, and GTP loading rather than steady-state mRNA, which this assay does not capture.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Rapgef4 showed little detectable transcriptional impact in this dataset: across assayed cell types, including 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, it had no FDR-supported differential expression, and the related Rapgef2 likewise lacked an FDR-supported downstream program. In contrast, the nearby cAMP-pathway perturbation Pde10a produced a stronger response in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, with on-target knockdown and an FDR-supported Scg2 signal. This suggests cAMP-pathway perturbations were not interchangeable here, although the contrast may reflect perturbation engagement and expression as much as pathway wiring.

P2ry14 showed nonconvergent transcriptional signatures in this neuronal assay: across matched cell types, its whole-transcriptome score correlations were nearly orthogonal to P2ry12, P2rx2, and broader GPCR/G-protein comparators including Gnao1, Gnas, Adora2a, and Cnr1, with the highest reported correlation only r = 0.099 for P2ry12. These results do not support treating purinergic receptors or Gi/o-coupled GPCR perturbations as interchangeable here, although the comparison used restricted whole-score correlations and P2ry14 target engagement itself was not quantified.

Cdh2 showed a largely target-only Perturb-seq profile that recurred across a broader neural cell-surface adhesion module rather than being unique to this guide. In the 22 Cdh2-tested classes, Ncam1 and Ctnnd2, like Cdh2, had FDR-significant self-knockdown without FDR-level downstream genes, whereas Ctnnb1 was a clear exception with broad non-self responses; related neighbors in the screened set included Ctnna2, Pcdh19, Nectin1, and Fyn. This pattern suggests buffering of several adhesion perturbations in this RNA assay, with the caveat that the comparator set was limited to screened perturbations and target engagement varied by gene and cell type.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Amfr perturbation in the two Amfr-responsive cell types, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of assayed ER-associated degradation and ER protein quality-control neighbors, including Vcp, Edem3, Atf6, Hspa5, and Rnf13. A broader signature-neighbor scan likewise did not reveal a robust Amfr-like or anti-Amfr perturbation, suggesting these ER-stress or ERAD genes were not transcriptionally interchangeable with Amfr in this brain Perturb-seq setting. This comparison is limited because several core AMFR partners, such as Ube2g2, Derl1, Insig1, and Hmgcr, were not perturbed, and guide efficacy differed across comparators.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnpa2b1 perturbation showed its strongest, cell-class-specific response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where an RNA-processing program was apparent with Rbm25, Tcerg1, Hnrnpa1, and Drosha up-regulated and Hnrnpu down-regulated. This pattern links Hnrnpa2b1 to an hnRNP and RNA-processing response in this class, while related family signatures were only weakly similar in 155 MB Glut. Notably, Drosha increased only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas core m6A/DGCR8-pathway transcripts remained unchanged, and the dataset measured steady-state mRNA rather than splicing, miRNA maturation, alternative polyadenylation, or m6A marks directly.

Cebpe perturbation in this mouse brain screen did not produce detectable induction of the canonical granulopoiesis program: measured transcripts for Spi1, Gfi1, Gfi1b, Csf3r, Rara, Rxra, Gata1, and Sp1 all remained unchanged, consistent with an uncoupled or buffered transcriptional regulation of granulopoiesis in the assayed brain cell classes. This matters because CEBPE is canonically linked to hematopoietic differentiation, yet that expected SPI1/GFI1/CSF3R/RARA/RXRA-associated program was silent here. Interpretation is limited to genes passing expression filters, and the lack of changes in brain does not test granulocytes.

Prdm12 perturbation did not detectably engage the PRDM12 nociceptor-lineage transcriptional program in any assayed brain class: Ntrk1, Isl1, Neurod1, Pou4f1/BRN3A, and Trpv1 all remained unchanged, with adjusted p values of 1.0 across Prdm12-assayed cell types. This makes the negative result specific rather than merely reflecting a global lack of significant genes. A key caveat is that the expected PRDM12 effector relationships were defined in developing nociceptive neurons, whereas these measurements were made in adult central brain classes.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|215 MB Dopa
full_finding_text: Rnf220 perturbation did not phenocopy available Shh/Gli, Wnt, AMPAR, Phox2, STAT, or RLIM neighbor perturbations at the whole-signature level: correlations with Smo, Gli1/2/3, Ctnnb1, Ptch1, Gria1/2, Phox2a/b, Stat1/3, and Rlim were uniformly weak, with the largest absolute related-gene correlation only r=0.158. The modest pattern was driven mainly by 308 CB GABA, with only weak Smo/Gli2 similarity there, while 215 MB Dopa contributed a weak Phox2a correlation but had sparse perturbed cells. Interpretation is limited by weak Rnf220 target-transcript engagement, mostly FDR-negative signatures, and missing comparator perturbations including Zc4h2, Eed, Sin3b, Usp7, and Olig genes.

Rnf220 perturbation did not produce an FDR-significant mRNA response in reported RNF220 substrate pathways: transcripts for Shh/Gli components (Ptch1, Smo, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3), AMPA-receptor genes (Gria1, Gria2), STAT factors (Stat1, Stat3), CTNNB1-linked partners, and Phox2, Sin3b, Eed, Olig1, and Olig2 remained unchanged. A weak Smo/Gli2 similarity was noted only in 308 CB GABA, and oligodendroglial development was not sampled as a cell state. These null transcriptional readouts are consistent with RNF220 acting mainly through protein stability, ubiquitin linkage, nuclear export, or receptor localization rather than steady-state mRNA.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Pax1 showed its only coherent transcriptomic hint in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut cells, where a mixed nominal synaptic membrane signature included Gabrg2, Gabrb2, Gpm6a, Grm1, Cacna2d1, Synpr, Sez6, Psd, Rims1, Dgki, and Syt7. This CA3-restricted pattern was enriched for synaptic genes, but it did not pass perturbation-level correction, with a minimum cell-type FDR of 0.5072, so it remains an exploratory hypothesis rather than a resolved pathway effect. Nearby cross-perturbation similarities were modest and confined to the same CA3 group, including Nr2c2, Dnm2, Fgfr2, Gabbr1, Mpdz, Syn1, Mbd5, and Ptcd3.

Twist2 perturbation did not induce the expected NF-kappaB/pro-inflammatory cytokine feedback program across all 23 measured cell types: Tnf, Il1b, Il6, Cxcl10, Nfkb1, and Rela were inert, with no corrected downstream response or Twist1-like ranked signature. This should be read as pathway-context uncoupling rather than a definitive contradiction of inflammatory Twist literature, because Twist2 mRNA was not detectably knocked down and the assayed populations were unstimulated, largely neuronal rather than cytokine-challenged immune or mesenchymal cells.

Dnm1 showed a target-only transcriptomic response: its perturbation produced FDR-level suppression of Dnm1 without any genome-wide significant secondary transcripts in any cell type. This pattern converged with Bin1, Synj1, and especially Syp, which also yielded target-only or near target-only FDR profiles, suggesting buffered basal whole-transcriptome readouts across a broader presynaptic/endocytic module rather than an isolated Dnm1 assay failure. In pathway context, Dnm1/Bin1/Synj1/Syp appeared buffered, whereas AP2 and Cltc genes were transcriptionally active only in selected classes; however, these comparisons are transcriptomic only and were not matched for protein half-life or functional assays.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Gfra1 did not phenocopy Ncam1 in this Perturb-seq dataset, despite the reported GFRα1/NCAM/Fyn/RET signaling relationship. Across 10 shared cell classes—005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut—Ncam1 showed strong on-target depletion whereas Gfra1 showed none, and Gfra1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Ncam1, Ret, or Fyn. This contrast could reflect weaker Gfra1 knockdown rather than true absence of GFRA1-NCAM coupling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Timp3 knockdown in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population showed a transcriptionally buffered response: Timp3 itself was the only FDR-significant gene, with no trans genes reaching significance and no FDR-level changes in Adam10, Adam17, App, Lrp8, or Timp2. This suggests that, in this cell type, the TIMP-family extracellular metalloproteinase inhibition pathway and the APP/ApoER2 alpha-secretase axis are uncoupled at the mRNA level, while the most proximal TIMP3 biology may have been missed because protease activity, APP fragments, secreted proteins, and ECM remodeling were not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Naa20 perturbation produces a recurrent negative neuronal module across responsive glutamatergic and GABAergic populations, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA. The shared down-regulated transcripts include Snhg11, Kifc2, Repin1, Atp11b, Peg3, Flnb, Srsf5, Maged1, Arglu1, Leng8, Tafazzin, Abhd14b, and Cyp46a1, suggesting a common downstream state rather than fully private signatures; several GABAergic classes show this module with lower overall burden than the thalamic glutamatergic class. These recurrent genes are transcript biomarkers, and direct NatB substrates among them were not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Mbd2 was transcriptionally uncoupled from the assayed NuRD neighbors Chd4 and Gatad2b. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Mbd2 showed no detectable signature, whereas Chd4 and Gatad2b produced stronger or self-knockdown effects; across this class and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, score-vector correlations between Mbd2 and either comparator were near zero. The main interpretable Mbd2 response was limited to 046 CTX-CGE GABA, with a single FDR-positive Uhrf1bp1l hit and a mixed nominal synaptic tail, suggesting NuRD-related requirements may be paralog-, module-, or cell-state-specific, though differing guide potency or paralog compensation cannot be excluded.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gatad2b in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not phenocopy the NuRD ATPase Chd4: despite their shared NuRD chromatin remodeling context, Gatad2b perturbation yielded only its own FDR-significant transcript, with a Rasgrp2-led but mostly sub-FDR tail and no strongly correlated perturbation neighbors, whereas Chd4 produced a broad 100-gene response including strong Begain and Cpne7 changes and shared Rasgrp2 upregulation. Genome-wide similarity was weak (r=0.1306), and direct NuRD-family comparison here was limited to Chd4 and Mbd2 using transcriptomic, not chromatin, readouts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Stag2 showed its only FDR-corrected downstream transcriptional program in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class, where 29 of 37 genes were downregulated and enrichment mapped the set to neuronal projection, synapse, and cell-junction biology rather than obvious cell-cycle genes. Representative genes included Ptprm, Ptprz1, Lrrc7, Sema5a, Stmn2, Npy1r, Gabra1, Syt11, Asic2, Nin, and Sez6. This suggests that neuronal adhesion and projection-gene regulation is the dominant Stag2-associated signal in this responsive class, although the pathway assignment is based on enrichment and does not directly measure synapses or projections.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Katnip did not show a convergent acute transcriptomic state with other ciliary/Joubert perturbations in the library. Across matched cell types, Katnip signature correlations with Ahi1, Cep290, and Tbc1d32 were near zero, indicating that a shared Joubert or primary-cilium annotation was not sufficient to produce a common neuronal response. The main related comparator effect was in 155 MB Glut, where Ahi1 perturbation strongly depleted Ahi1 itself but yielded only a self-limited on-target signal rather than a broader FDR-supported module. These comparisons were limited to Ahi1, Cep290, and Tbc1d32, and Katnip target engagement was not directly measured.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Xpo1 targeting produced a recurrent RNA-processing response in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with endogenous Snrnp70 and several Srsf-family transcripts, including Srsf1, Srsf5, Srsf6, and Srsf11, generally reduced. Yet perturbation signatures for Snrnp70 and Srsf1 correlated positively with the Xpo1 signature across responsive classes, suggesting convergence on a shared RNA-processing stress state rather than a simple signed causal edge; because the comparison used restricted signatures and target activation, it supports network convergence, not direct mechanism.

Cntn1 showed a convergent sparse transcriptional response with related neuronal adhesion perturbations: its direct partner Cntnap1, as well as L1cam and Nrcam, were also largely devoid of secondary transcriptome-wide FDR hits. In the 155 MB Glut cell type, where the Cntn1 knockdown signature was strongest, there were still no secondary FDR hits, supporting the idea that Cntn1 and Cntnap1 loss may be transcriptionally buffered within a paranodal axon-glia adhesion module whose main phenotype is structural rather than RNA-state switching. This interpretation is tempered because Nfasc and Cntn2-Cntn6 were not available as direct comparators, and L1cam/Nrcam are family or pathway comparators rather than members of the CNTN1-CNTNAP1 cis complex.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnph2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced its strongest signature with Hnrnph2 and Rsrp1 decreased and the TCA-cycle genes Idh3g and Ogdh increased, with mitochondrial genes such as Timm44 also among the positive signals. This links loss of an RNA-processing factor to a metabolism-associated response in this specific cell type, but the interpretation is limited because the metabolic arm rests mainly on two FDR genes in one population, and neither metabolite flux nor mitochondrial activity was measured.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cisd2 showed no strong perturbational neighbor: in its three best-engaged cell types—066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut—the nearest positive and negative transcriptomic correlations were very weak, and assayed mitochondrial, autophagy, BCL2/IP3R, and calcium-transfer comparators including Park7, Prkn, Opa1, Sdha, Ndufa13, Bcl2, Itpr1, and Atg5 were near-orthogonal to the Cisd2 signature. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Opa1 induced a stress program absent after Cisd2 knockdown. Interpretation is limited to transcriptomic similarity, and direct comparisons with Cisd1, Cisd3, and Wfs1 were unavailable.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Usp48 showed a distinct perturbation profile in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons that was not phenocopied by Usp9x, Uchl1, Arl3, or Gsdme. In this population, Usp9x and Uchl1 were efficiently knocked down yet mainly altered their own transcripts and did not reproduce the Usp48-associated Abhd12b, Cyp46a1, and Resp18 module. Arl3 and Gsdme also failed to match the Usp48 signature, although the relevant literature for those comparators comes from retina or cancer systems, Gsdme RNA was not measured here, and protein stabilization cannot be inferred from mRNA differential expression alone.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Cdh2 knockdown was largely buffered relative to Ctnnb1 knockdown, despite both targets being efficiently reduced. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, each perturbation had 171 cells with significant self-knockdown, yet Cdh2 showed no non-self FDR genes whereas Ctnnb1 produced 383, indicating an uncorrelated and broader transcriptional program. The same qualitative split appeared in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where Ctnnb1 propagated to downstream genes but Cdh2 remained target-only. This transcriptomic comparison does not test physical beta-catenin release from cadherin junctions.

Tardbp depletion produced a recurrent, directionally coherent noncanonical response module across sensitive neuronal cell types, with Ppp6c, Fam219a, Usp15, Brms1l, Uggt2, Gabpa, Abcc5, Fam135a, and Sec24b repeatedly increased and Snrnp70 repeatedly decreased. The effect was strongest in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells and was also prominent in midbrain glutamatergic and hindbrain/pontine/myelencephalic GABAergic cells; pineal glutamatergic cells showed a similar pattern but with limited sample size. This module serves as a dataset-derived scalar biomarker of Tardbp loss, but it reflects gene-level abundance changes rather than direct TDP-43 binding, isoform shifts, or an established pathway enrichment.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Epha5 perturbation did not produce a coherent transcriptional Eph/ephrin-Rho response across 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 308 CB GABA. Efnb2, Pak1, Ptk2, Rasa1, Nck2, Ngef, Sdcbp, Cfl1, and Vav3 appeared only as scattered nominal, mixed-direction changes, typically with no non-target FDR support. In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, Lnpep was the only non-target FDR hit, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed receptor-paralog divergence rather than a shared EphA signature.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Phactr2 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells showed a weak, specific response: Lrfn4 was the only gene reaching FDR<0.05, while the canonical actin/cytoskeleton program seen with core actin perturbations was not detected. In the same cell type, Actb and Actg1 perturbations produced significant Actg1/Flna readouts, yet they did not reproduce the Lrfn4 increase, indicating that the Phactr2 signal was uncoupled from the stronger PP1/actin cytoskeleton perturbation pattern. Because Ppp1ca was not perturbed and Phactr2 engagement was weak, this does not rule out protein-level coupling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zmym2 showed weak but reproducible convergence with Chd4 and Zmynd8 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where the Zmym2-responsive program was concentrated, while Sin3a produced a broader pattern and Rest and Sall4 were essentially flat rather than phenocopying Zmym2. This places the phenotype closer to a selective chromatin-regulator axis than to all nuclear repressors assayed, but the all-gene score correlations were small, direct CoREST comparators were unavailable, and the Chd4/Zmynd8 link reflects chromatin-functional similarity rather than a known shared ZMYM2 complex.

Herc2 perturbation did not produce a coherent basal mRNA response in HERC2-linked DNA-damage, autophagy, iron-homeostasis, or IGF1R axes: transcripts for Rnf8, Rnf168, Ube2n, Usp20, Ulk1, Xpa, Fbxl5, Ncoa4, Igf1r, Map1lc3b, and Sqstm1 showed mixed signs without FDR-supported changes. This pattern held across all 22 assayed Herc2 cell classes and in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class with the strongest knockdown, where Ube3a, Herc1, and Igf1r did not phenocopy Herc2. The result is tempered by the assay measuring basal RNA, whereas much prior HERC2 biology is protein-level or stress-induced.

Hdac8 showed a divergent, largely null Perturb-seq phenotype in this assay: unlike the strong chromatin-regulator signatures seen for Sin3a and Zmynd8, Hdac8 was nearly or completely FDR-null and did not converge with the assayed class IIa HDAC perturbations Hdac4 or Hdac5. In 155 MB Glut cells, the largest Hdac8 stratum had no Hdac8 mRNA engagement and no FDR-significant downstream genes, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells Hdac8 showed only weak positive correlations with cohesin genes. Because other chromatin regulators produced large effects in the same dataset, the Hdac8 result appears target-specific rather than a general failure to detect chromatin repression, although Hdac1, Hdac2, and Hdac3 were not assayed.

Psap showed a self-only lysosomal perturbation profile: like Ctsb, Ppt1, Atp13a2, and Arsb, it had on-target knockdown but no non-self FDR<0.05 transcriptional hits across the same 20 Psap cell types. In contrast, Atp6v0c, a core V-ATPase acidification component, produced 767 non-self FDR<0.05 rows, including in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class. This suggests the assay can detect broad lysosome-linked transcriptional stress, so the buffered Psap signature is unlikely to reflect a generic inability to score lysosomal phenotypes, although the comparison is qualitative because Atp6v0c is more central to acidification than PSAP.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Smad6 perturbation did not recover a coherent canonical BMP/TGF-beta feedback module: only isolated nominal pathway-adjacent signals were seen, including decreased Skil in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, a nominal Smad3 row in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and Id2 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut. In this screen, canonical SMAD/BMP-adjacent genes were not corrected Smad6 hits, and all named Smad6-pathway rows had FDR=1.0, so the data do not support robust derepression of the expected BMP-SMAD1/SMAD4 axis.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chd2 showed a distinct, non-phenocopying transcriptomic response in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic glutamatergic class, where it produced the strongest measured effect, including 34 FDR genes spanning RNA-splicing and ion-channel modules and a marked decrease in Snhg11. In this same cell class, Chd4, Chd7, and Chd8 were also active, but Chd2-vs-Chd4, -Chd7, and -Chd8 whole-signature correlations were near zero, consistent with divergence within CHD-family ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling rather than interchangeability. This contrast is tempered by weak measured Chd2 target engagement, so the assay shows non-phenocopying rather than biochemical independence.

Appl1 knockdown did not produce a shared APPL1-like transcriptional state with perturbations of Adipor2, Insr, Igf1r, Ntrk1/2/3, or core PI3K-AKT-TSC/mTOR genes across the 20 profiled cell types; correlations were usually near zero, suggesting these neighbors were not transcriptomic phenocopies of Appl1 in this dataset. An exploratory exception was a mostly uncoupled but detectable Akt3/Tsc2-related signal in 308 CB GABA cells. This interpretation is limited by weak Appl1 signatures, the absence of Appl2, Adipor1, and Rab5 isoforms from the perturbation panel, and only indirect matching of non-neuronal literature to brain cell types.

Met did not phenocopy active receptor-tyrosine-kinase/PI3K perturbations in this cell-type panel: canonical HGF/MET signaling transcripts, including Hgf, Gab1, Grb2, Ptpn11, and Stat3, as well as downstream PI3K/AKT and RAS/MAPK components, showed no FDR-supported response to Met perturbation, and Met score vectors were only weakly correlated with Pik3cb, Nrg1, Nrg3, Pten, or other neighbors. This uncoupling was evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, where comparators such as Pten, Nrg3, Erbb4, Fgfr1, Mapk1, and Mtor produced significant signatures; weak Met target engagement may partly explain the transcriptomic null.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Hdgf did not show a convincing cross-perturbation module in this dataset. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA cells, where the Hdgf table was nominally active but had no FDR-significant genes, the available same-cell-type signature neighbors formed only a weak mixed pattern, with modest positive similarity to Macf1, Wnk3, and Agrn and modest anticorrelation with Pcdh19, Htr2a, and Gabrg2. Direct HDGF-family perturbations and top STRING-linked partners such as Ptn, Ncl, Mdk, Cdyl, and Ybx1 were not measured, so these observations remain exploratory rather than mechanistic.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Lrp1 perturbation produced a narrow acute mRNA program rather than detectable transcriptional rewiring of the nearby App/Aβ–tau–LRP chaperone network. In the key response classes—066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—App, Mapt, Lrpap1, and Sort1 remained FDR-stable even when Lrp1 or Vgf responded. The clearest on-target knockdown in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA had no FDR-significant downstream transcript, while 155 MB Glut showed both significant Lrp1 depletion and Vgf induction, and 191 MB P MY GABA showed Vgf induction despite only nominal Lrp1 depletion. These mRNA results do not rule out changes in receptor-mediated endocytosis, intracellular trafficking, or lipid/Aβ handling at the protein or flux level.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Chrnb4 perturbation showed a single FDR-supported downstream change: Pcca decreased in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells. This effect did not extend to a coherent mitochondrial propionyl-CoA carboxylase or propionate-catabolism program, because Pccb and related genes including Mcee, Mmut, Mmaa, and Mmab were not concordantly altered in the same contrast. Given the weak Chrnb4 target engagement and lack of orthogonal validation, this is best treated as a low-confidence, single-gene observation rather than evidence for a broader metabolic pathway effect.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Kif3b showed near-zero or very weak signature similarity in 155 MB Glut, with no FDR hits for Kif3b itself and no convergence with available intraflagellar transport, dynein, or RFX-family perturbations. In the matched cell type, Ift88 had a single FDR-level hit, Pcsk1n, but its score correlation with Kif3b was essentially zero, and correlations with Dync2h1, Dync2i1, Rfx3, and Rfx7 were likewise near zero. The strongest positive and negative Kif3b neighbors were too weak to support a shared program, and interpretation is limited because Kif3a and Kifap3 were not tested and Kif3b engagement was weak.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Hsp90ab1 depletion produced only a weak, nominally compensatory HSF1-linked heat-shock signal rather than a resolved stress program: Hsp90aa1 increased nominally in 7 of 23 cell types and Hspa8 in 5 of 23, with additional nominal Ahsa2 and Fkbp8 rows, but all chaperone-axis rows had FDR=1.0. The recurrent signal appeared in cell types including 308 CB GABA, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, with the strongest nominal Hsp90aa1 increase in 308 CB GABA and the largest nominal Hspa8 increase in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; notably, Hsp90aa1 induction did not scale with target-depletion strength across cell types.

Ywhae perturbation showed a sparse downstream response across the assayed 14-3-3 family: despite weaker self-depletion than Ywhag or Ywhaz, it did not induce detectable mRNA compensation from Ywhab, Ywhag, Ywhah, Ywhaq, Ywhaz, or Sfn, and no non-self genes reached FDR<0.05. The same sparse pattern was seen for Ywhag and Ywhaz knockdowns, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 155 MB Glut, consistent with buffering of single-isoform loss in the 14-3-3 phosphoserine/phosphothreonine adaptor network, although only two paralog perturbations were tested and partial editing or protein redundancy could explain the effect.

Ywhaz perturbation did not show consistent transcriptional compensation by other 14-3-3 isoforms: across the assayed family members Ywhae, Ywhag, Ywhah, Ywhaq, Ywhab, and Sfn, no FDR-adjusted induction was detected, arguing that the muted Ywhaz phenotype in this dataset is not explained by acute mRNA upregulation within the 14-3-3 isoform/adaptor network. In 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, a nominal Ywhae change and Cadps FDR 0.139 were observed, but neither survived correction. This leaves open buffering through pre-existing paralog proteins, heterodimer exchange, or delayed compensation not captured by differential mRNA testing.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ppargc1b in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed an exploratory, restricted metabolic signature in which Esrra was the closest positive signature neighbor among other perturbations, and both perturbations shared depletion of a small set of mitochondrial/TCA genes including Idh3b, Uqcrc1, Mdh1, and Dlst. This convergence is consistent with a PGC-1beta-ERRalpha coactivation axis and with the nominal Ppargc1b TCA/OXPHOS tail in this cell type, but the genome-wide correlation was weak and no FDR-significant Ppargc1b genes were detected, so the result is hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ext2 did not phenocopy its EXT1 complex partner or selected heparan-sulfate–related neighbors at the transcriptome level. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and especially 155 MB Glut, Ext2 showed on-target depletion, yet Ext1 was only weakly engaged and did not achieve FDR-supported self-depletion in these Ext2-responsive contexts. In 155 MB Glut, strongly engaged Hs6st2, Agrn, Bmpr2, Fgfr1, and Fgf13 perturbations had essentially zero correlation with the Ext2 signature, leaving no high-correlation positive or negative signature neighbor.

Thap11 perturbation produced a recurrent 20-gene core signature across many cell types rather than a single cell-type-specific program, with repeated decreases in Sdccag8, Rabac1, Acp6, Ndufa3, Gdap1, Cdk5, Slc38a7 and other mitochondrial genes including Cox7c, Coa3, Sirt4, Timm21, Timm22, and Uqcr10, alongside repeated increases in Thoc6, Prkn, and Ttc41. The strongest response was in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells, with similarly strong full-core responses in midbrain glutamatergic neurons and even a low-cell-count pineal/hindbrain glutamatergic class. These data show transcript-level changes, not mitochondrial or electron-transport-chain phenotypes.

Csf1r showed no reproducible target-RNA depletion and no downstream genes passing FDR correction in the assayed Glut/GABA/Dopa neuronal panel, and this null was not unique: Cx3cr1, Trem2, Spi1, and Irf8 perturbations were likewise FDR-silent across the tested neuronal cell-type signatures. Together, these results suggest absent or buffered immune-lineage programs in this off-context neuronal setting rather than a uniquely anomalous Csf1r result, although among these comparators only Spi1 was noted as a STRING-confirmed Csf1r partner.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Eif4g1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a distinct mRNA signature that other translation-control perturbations did not phenocopy. Despite robust direct knockdown, Eif4a2 and Ddx3x remained essentially uncorrelated with Eif4g1 (r=0.023 and r=0.028), and Eif4h, Mtor, Rptor, Fmr1, and Cyfip1 also did not resemble the Eif4g1 state. This divergence across cap-dependent translation initiation and the EIF4E regulatory axis suggests branch-specific or post-transcriptional outputs, with the caveat that Cyfip1 and Eif4h had weak self knockdown and Mtor, Rptor, and Fmr1 self knockdown was only nominal.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ncoa1 perturbation did not phenocopy Thra perturbation in thyroid-hormone-responsive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Thra perturbation significantly reduced Hr, Adgrb1, and Thra, whereas Ncoa1 only weakly reduced its own transcript and did not significantly alter Hr, Adgrb1, or Thra; Ncoa1-versus-Thra score correlations were near zero in both classes. This pattern in nuclear receptor transcriptional coactivation is consistent with redundancy among SRC coactivators or insufficient Ncoa1 depletion, rather than an acute obligate dependence of Hr or Adgrb1 on Ncoa1.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Thrb showed no clear thyroid-hormone receptor transcriptional response in this atlas: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Thrb perturbation left the thyroid-hormone-responsive Hr locus unchanged, whereas the Thra comparator produced a small adjusted module with Hr downregulation and Adgrb1, and matched Thra–Thrb signatures were near zero. In 155 MB Glut, Thrb was the strongest nominal on-target context but still had no downstream adjusted genes, while Thra showed adjusted on-target depletion only. This contrast suggests a Thra-biased, cell-type-restricted response rather than proof of TRβ inactivity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Csnk2b perturbation mostly up-regulated synaptic and neuronal projection genes rather than a generic collapse program in specific mouse-brain classes. In 191 MB P MY GABA and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, Dnm1 and App were induced, with Snap25 also induced in 217 P MY Pineal Glut; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Shank1 and Prkcg were induced, alongside recurrent Syt7 and Grk3 signals. The pineal glutamatergic class showed the largest gene-count response despite few perturbed cells, and prior CK2 literature comes from Drosophila presynapse or mouse neuromuscular junction, so directionality in these adult brain classes remains indirect.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Arl6ip1 acute knockdown signatures were not interchangeable with related ER-shaping or glutamate-transporter perturbations: across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, restricted top-500 correlations with Atl1, Reep1, Reep2, and Slc1a1 were near zero or weakly negative even when those comparators were themselves depleted. In the best-powered TH/MB contexts, Arl6ip1 showed a buffered transcriptional response, did not primarily reduce Slc1a1 mRNA, and did not phenocopy ATL/REEP/SLC1A1 perturbations, though this comparison used restricted correlations and some related targets had fewer perturbed cells or weaker engagement outside these cell types.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Kcna2 did not show a shared transcriptomic program with the available Kv1-complex perturbations. Across shared classes, Kcna1, Kcna2, and Kcnab1 were FDR-null, while Kcnab2 showed only strong self-knockdown in five classes, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, without non-self FDR hits. Kcna2 signature correlations with Kcna1, Kcnab1, and Kcnab2 were very weak, indicating a transcriptionally buffered, uncorrelated Kv1 voltage-gated potassium-channel complex response; however, only three related perturbations were available, and the assay captured RNA rather than channel conductance or localization.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf11 showed no detectable transcriptional signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, even though this was its largest matched cell class with 273 perturbed cells. In the same cell type, related perturbations were detectable: Klf9 and Sp4 were stronger than Klf11, and Klf7 and Smad2 also produced at least one significant gene, indicating the Klf11 null is not simply due to low power here. This suggests broad KLF/SP family similarity does not imply interchangeable neuronal signatures, although these comparators are family or pathway neighbors whose guide efficiency and basal expression may differ from Klf11.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pcyt2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons produced a strong sterol/lipogenic transcriptional response, but this was not accompanied by detectable induction of nearby CDP-ethanolamine PE-synthesis or PS-rescue transcripts, including Etnk1/2, Selenoi, Cept1, Pisd, Ptdss1/2, Pcyt1a/b, Chka, and Chkb. In this cell type, Pcyt2 and Selenoi appeared to converge on sterol and lipid-remodeling programs rather than simple mRNA upregulation of parallel PE routes. This is an mRNA-only negative result, so altered flux through PE, PC, PS, Lands-cycle, or etherlipid pathways cannot be excluded.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ptf1a showed no convergence with assayed PTF1A complex-adjacent or developmental-neighbor perturbations in 308 CB GABA, where canonical Ptf1a fate biology would be most relevant. All-gene score correlations between Ptf1a and Tcf3, Tcf12, Atoh1, Notch-pathway perturbations, or pancreatic-developmental neighbors were near background; the largest related-gene correlation was only weak for Notch2 (r = 0.199). This suggests the PTF1A/PTF1 bHLH transcriptional fate program was not recovered at scale here, although Rbpj and Rbpjl were not targeted and the weak Ptf1a vector can only exclude large phenocopies.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ptprt in 155 MB Glut showed an isolated, weak transcriptional regime: in the only cell class with FDR-significant target depletion, its signature had near-zero or divergent correlations with other receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase perturbations, including Ptprm, Ptprd, Ptprf, Ptprn, and Ptprn2, and no strong positive or negative neighbors emerged in the all-target scan. Strong signature neighbors such as Esrrg, Rora, Kif11, and En1 also did not phenocopy Ptprt, suggesting a buffered, non-reusable family-level signature, with the caveat that signature-based comparisons may differ because receptor phosphatases vary in substrates, domains, and engagement strength.

Il2ra did not converge with assayed IL-2 receptor/JAK-STAT neighbors in these neurons: Il2rb, Il2rg, and Stat5b perturbation signatures were near-uncorrelated with Il2ra, and these comparator perturbations also lacked FDR-supported transcriptional phenotypes. This suggests the canonical IL-2 receptor/JAK-STAT signaling axis was not engaged in the assayed neuronal populations. The contrast is tempered by weak self-transcript effects for several comparator perturbations, and Jak1 and Jak3 were not tested as perturbation targets.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
full_finding_text: Cd46 perturbation in neurons was not phenocopied by C3, Cr2, or Itgb2 in the subclasses where Cd46 was most detectably reduced—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut. Across these contexts, signature correlations with Cd46 were near zero, and the related perturbations also showed poor self-transcript engagement. Thus, within the CD46-mediated regulation of complement C3b/C4b pathway, the screen suggests uncoupled or weakly captured neuronal RNA signatures rather than an interchangeable complement-receptor module.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pitx2 was largely flat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells and did not phenocopy the strong Wnt/beta-catenin effector signatures seen after Ctnnb1 or Tcf7l2 perturbation, even though Pitx2 had more assigned cells than either comparator. In the same thalamic neuronal class, Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 produced large FDR-significant programs, arguing that the absence of a Pitx2 response is not due to poor detection of transcription-factor or Wnt-axis effects. This uncoupling should be interpreted with the caveat that prior Wnt/PITX2 links come mainly from developmental epithelial contexts, and Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 are pathway effectors rather than PITX2 complex subunits.

Pank2 perturbation did not produce a coherent FDR-supported transcriptional program for canonical pantothenate-to-CoA biosynthesis or mitochondrial energy metabolism. Transcripts for Pank1, Pank3, Pank4, Coasy, Ppcs, Ppcdc, and Dcakd were measured but showed no compensatory response, while mitochondrial and oxidative-energy genes such as mt-Nd2, mt-Nd5, and Sdha appeared only sporadically and with mixed direction. Thus the nominal Pank2 signature should not be read as a canonical CoA-depletion program, with the caveat that this is a transcriptomic negative result and CoA metabolites or respiration were not assayed.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mcts1 showed near-zero signature correlation with available core translation-factor and RNA-surveillance perturbations, especially in 155 MB Glut where correlations with Hbs1l, Eif4a2, Eif4e, Eif4g1, Eif5a, Eef2, Eef1a2, Dhx9, Xrn1, and Upf3b were all weak (about r=-0.029 to 0.041), and no strong positive or inverse neighbor emerged in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA or 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This suggests the Mcts1 neuronal phenotype does not simply phenocopy general translation stress, although the most direct mechanistic comparators, Denr and Eif2d, were not present in the library.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Eif4h perturbation was not transcriptomically interchangeable with other eIF4F-associated perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: Eif4e, Eif4a2, and Eif4g1 showed measurable target-transcript depletion, whereas Eif4h did not, and Eif4e was much stronger, producing 160 FDR-significant genes versus one for Eif4h. The only significant Eif4h-associated gene in that cell type was Hexim1, and the restricted Eif4h signature aligned with Eif4e/Eif4a2 within cap-dependent translation initiation, but this contrast may reflect guide or transcript-detection performance as much as biological buffering of EIF4H.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Epha4 was not interchangeable with Eph-family or other axon-guidance perturbations at the RNA-signature level. Across target-engaged classes including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, the strongest non-self whole-signature neighbors were weak, and Eph-family comparators such as Epha2, Epha7, and Ephb2 were not stronger than Sema5a or Robo1. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Epha4 and Epha7 were both efficiently depleted yet uncorrelated. This may reflect score vectors dominated by null genes and the lack of ephrin ligand perturbations.

Bckdhb showed no transcriptomic convergence with the available branched-chain amino acid catabolism perturbations Bckdk, Dld, and Ivd: across shared cell types, genome-wide Wilcoxon-score correlations with Bckdhb were approximately zero, and none of these perturbations, including Bckdhb, had FDR-significant expression effects. This separates Bckdhb RNA depletion from a BCKDH regulator, a shared E3 dehydrogenase subunit, and downstream branched-chain catabolism at the RNA-signature level, although interpretation is limited because these comparator perturbations were weak and Bckdha and Dbt were not tested.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Adgrl2 knockdown showed an FDR-significant effect only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where the signature was self-only, with target mRNA down and no meaningful positive or negative genome-wide signature neighbor. In the same thalamic class, Adgrl1, Adgrl3, and the teneurin-family perturbation Tenm3 were also efficiently knocked down yet each yielded only one FDR-significant gene, the target itself, so these related adhesion perturbations did not converge on a shared downstream transcriptome. This single-cell RNA endpoint therefore points to self-dominated, possibly protein-local, connectivity-related, or redundant biology not captured here.

Pth1r did not phenocopy canonical PTH1R pathway neighbors in this neuronal screen: across matched cell types, its transcriptional signature showed near-zero similarity to Gs/cAMP/PKA, PLC/calcium, and CREB-adjacent perturbations, including Gnas, Adcy1/3/5, Prkaca, Prkar1a, Pde4b/d, Plcb1, Prkca, Creb1, Rapgef2/4, Ppp3ca/r1, Calm1/3, and Camk2b. Even in the best-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut context, Pth1r lacked target repression and remained uncoupled from active downstream-neighbor signatures. This conclusion is limited to the in-library neighbor set, and no Pth2r perturbation was available for a direct paralog comparison.

Gpc6 showed no detectable convergence with the available Hedgehog, Wnt, BMP, or FGF pathway perturbations in this acute neuronal Perturb-seq dataset. Across same-cell full-transcriptome differential-expression score comparisons, Gpc6 was essentially uncorrelated with Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Gli1/2/3, Cdon, Fzd2/3/4/6/9, Lgr4, Lrp5/6, Acvr1, Bmpr1a/b, and Fgfr1/2/3, with a maximum absolute correlation of 0.123. This null result is tempered by weak Gpc6 target engagement and by the limited subset of pathway genes that were perturbed.

Fgfr2 perturbation did not measurably recover the canonical FGFR2-FRS2-RAS/MAPK feedback program: across assayed perturbations, Dusp1/5/6, Spry1/2/4, Etv4/5, Fos/Jun, and core pathway genes including Frs2, Grb2, Sos1, Braf, Raf1, Mapk1/3, Akt1/2, and Pik3ca were not adjusted hits, even in the otherwise most responsive 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut class, where the only adjusted signal was Ccsap up-regulation and Ctnnb1 remained nominal. This uncoupling persisted despite detectable comparator effects from other perturbations such as Map2k1/Braf, and may reflect inefficient perturbation of the Fgfr2 transcript.

Lyrm4 perturbation did not produce a coherent transcript-level response in mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis: key mRNAs including Nfs1, Iscu, Fxn, Ndufab1, Fdx2, Glrx5, Isca2, and the Lyrm4 target itself were not significantly adjusted, and targeted inspection of Fe-S biogenesis and maturation transcripts likewise showed no adjusted pathway response. Thus, despite LYRM4/ISD11 being a core ISC factor, these data should not be read as pathway-wide Fe-S shutdown at the mRNA level, especially because Fe-S disruption may be enzymatic or post-transcriptional and protein activity was not directly assayed.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Maf perturbation in 052 Pvalb Gaba produced a small but distinct signature, with downregulation of Cacnb3, Lifr, and Tmem108, whereas the related perturbations were not interchangeable: Mafb had only Ccdc88a as an FDR-supported hit, Mafa had no FDR-supported hit, and Mafg instead showed a strong Hmox1 oxidative-stress response in the small Maf/antioxidant response element module, with Uchl1 also noted in this context. These family signatures were all small, and the Mafg transcript reduction in Pvalb was only nominal rather than FDR-significant.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Csmd1 showed no reusable transcriptomic state across six evaluated glutamatergic cell types: its score-vector signatures were nearly orthogonal to C3, Cd46, Cr2, and Trem2, and even the strongest non-Csmd1 genome-wide neighbor reached only r=0.110. This pattern was seen in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, despite the largest nominal gene tail in 001 and clearest RNA decrease in 151. These correlations were based on Wilcoxon score vectors and do not test protein-level or cell-cell complement biology.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Myt1l was not interchangeable with the measured developmental network neighbors across the five most responsive cell types—001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut—as Neurod1, Neurod2, Lmx1a, Lhx3, and Tubb3 did not reproduce the Myt1l-associated Rreb1 induction with Kifc2 and Slc22a17 repression. Instead, Phf21a and Naa20 were the nearest positive transcriptome neighbors, but correlations were weak, suggesting only partial convergence. This supports a Myt1l-specific module with a separate Phf21a/Naa20 chromatin or protein-acetylation hypothesis, while noting that key contrasts were unavailable because the library lacked Myt1, St18, Ascl1, Pou3f2, and Neurog2.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Usp9x knockdown in the best-engaged thalamic glutamatergic class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, depleted the Usp9x transcript and was associated with a nominal decrease in mRNA-processing and splicing genes, including Pabpn1, Srrm2, Hnrnpu, and Srsf11, rather than a canonical Wnt, Notch, TGF-beta, or mTOR developmental signaling signature. This suggests a noncanonical, exploratory hypothesis that adult thalamic glutamatergic neurons may experience RNA-processing stress after USP9X loss, but the individual RNA-processing genes did not pass FDR < 0.05.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Mafb perturbation did not recover the published Maf/Mafb MGE-derived PV/SST interneuron maturation program in 052 Pvalb Gaba or 053 Sst Gaba. In these classes, literature-linked markers Mef2c, Snap25, Pnoc, Sst, Elmo1, and Igfbp4 were unchanged, and the measured Mafb transcript itself showed no detectable depletion. The only reported FDR hit was a Ccdc88a decrease in 052 Pvalb Gaba, without correlation to Maf or Mafa signatures. This likely reflects context or engagement mismatch rather than contradiction, because prior work used embryonic or neonatal Maf/Mafb double-mutant settings, whereas this dataset tested single Mafb perturbation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ufc1 most closely phenocopied Uba5, rather than Ufsp2, among the directly assayed UFMylation neighbors. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Uba5 was the strongest non-self neighbor of Ufc1, and positive Ufc1–Uba5 correlations also persisted in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas Ufsp2 was much weaker and showed little FDR-supported response. The dominant Ufc1-responsive class was the thalamic population, with Ddit3 induction and synaptic-gene repression; smaller signatures included Sqstm1 and Rnf11 up in 155 MB Glut and Ddit3 as the top induced gene in 191 MB P MY GABA. This comparison was transcriptome-only, and other core UFMylation components were not assayed.

Cep85l perturbation did not produce a coherent downstream mRNA signature for the published centrosome/CDK5-linked neuron-migration module. Across all 22 cell types, Dync1h1, Pafah1b1/Lis1, Kif2a, Dcx, Nde1, Ndel1, and Cdk5 were measured but not FDR-significantly regulated downstream of Cep85l, and in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 308 CB GABA, only Cdk5r1 was nominally increased while core migration-complex mRNAs remained uncoupled. This absence of transcript-level coordination does not contradict literature mechanisms centered on CEP85L localization and kinase activation during neuronal migration.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Ufc1 loss induced a Ddit3-centered proteostasis and integrated-stress program, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Ddit3 was FDR-up; Ddit3 was also nominally up in 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut. The thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class showed the largest response, with broad downstream changes, while 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA showed smaller coherent signatures that tracked Uba5. Additional up-regulated genes included Sqstm1 and Rnf11, but the pattern was not a generic Atf6/Hspa5/Vcp UPR profile, and several recurrent signals were nominal rather than FDR-significant.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Pax4 was largely neutral in the mouse-brain Perturb-seq screen: in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, Arx produced clear GABAergic signatures, including significant hits such as Tmsb4x, whereas Pax4 had no multiple-testing-significant downstream transcripts and showed near-zero correlation with Arx or PAX-family/endocrine-program perturbations including Pax6, Pax7, Pdx1, Mafa, Mafb, and Neurog3. These matched-cell-type correlations are signature-level rather than direct epistasis, and the prior Pax4–Arx relationship comes mainly from pancreatic endocrine differentiation, so the pancreatic antagonism did not transfer to these brain neuronal transcriptomes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ctcf perturbation produced a recurrent Zcwpw2/Dennd6b/Abhd14b module in the two strongest Ctcf-responsive neuronal classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, but this downstream signature was not reproduced by perturbing the related architectural genes Nipbl, Pds5a, Smc1a, Smc3, Stag1, Stag2, Yy1, Chd7, or Chd8. This suggests the Ctcf phenotype is relatively specific within the CTCF/cohesin chromatin-loop architecture context, although comparator guide potency, protein perdurance, and the use of transcriptional rather than direct loop measurements remain important caveats.

Oprk1 showed a shared null phenotype with the opioid GPCR paralogs Oprd1, Oprl1, and Oprm1: across assayed cell classes, Oprk1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response, and its measured target transcript did not show a reproducible negative shift. The related delta-, nociceptin-, and mu-opioid receptor perturbations likewise had no FDR-significant family-level effects, so these paralogs cannot serve as interchangeable positive controls for Oprk1. This negative convergence may reflect opioid-receptor-family capture or engagement limits, with the caveat that no ligand perturbations or receptor protein/signaling measurements were included.

Trpa1 showed near-zero transcriptomic signature correlation with related TRP-channel perturbations, including Trpv1, Trpv4, Trpm3, and Trpm7, in matched neuronal cell types, and these perturbations were also largely flat in the sampled brain neuronal classes. Thus, despite the known TRPA1/TRPV1 relationship in nociceptors, the TRP-channel calcium-transport pathway did not appear as a shared or interchangeable brain-neuron transcriptomic module here. This inference is limited to sparse CRISPR-based transcriptomic signatures, and other TRP channels such as Trpm8 were not assayed.

Trak1 showed no same-direction convergence with the measured RHOT/TRAK transport branch: like Trak1, Rhot1 had no adjusted hits across 21 cell classes, and score-vector correlations between Trak1 and 13 related transport or mitochondrial targets were near zero, with maximum |r| = 0.140. This lack of convergence extended to Kif5a, Kif5c, Klc1, Klc2, Dctn1, Dync1h1, Dnm1l, Opa1, Hspa9, Ogt, Prkn, and Mff, even though several neighbors were strong in some cell types while Trak1 was not. Interpretation is limited because Trak2 and Rhot2 were not perturbed, and correlations were computed from transcriptomic scores rather than organelle-position phenotypes.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ddx23 perturbation produced its largest transcriptional response in 155 MB Glut neurons, a second strong response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, and a smaller but FDR-supported response in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells. Across these responsive populations, an RNA-processing/spliceosome module was induced, with upregulation of Prpf8, Prpf40a, Son, Srsf10, U2af1, Sf3b4, Ptbp1, Snrpc, and Snrpd1, alongside recurrent Tspyl2 and Ssb upregulation and Rsrp1 and Snhg11 downregulation. This pattern is consistent with a compensatory or stress response in the RNA-processing compartment, but the dataset does not measure splicing outcomes or protein abundance.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Prdm10 perturbation produced a predominantly down-regulated neuronal signature, with a small recurrent module centered on Madd, Cadm3, and Ptov1 that was repressed across many cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, 308 CB GABA, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. The thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class showed the largest response, but even low-cell-count pineal/pons/myelencephalic glutamatergic cells reproduced the shared module, suggesting a core PRDM10-dependent neuronal state rather than purely cell-type-specific effects, although most recurrent genes are not proven direct PRDM10 targets.

Prdm10 perturbation in brain neurons did not recapitulate the embryonic PRDM10–Eif3b global-translation axis: Eif3b showed no detectable transcript response and did not reach even nominal significance in any measured Prdm10-targeted brain cell type, despite strong effects on other genes in some of those same classes. Instead, the recurrent brain response centered more on genes such as Cadm3, Madd, and Ptov1. This weakens extrapolation from mouse embryonic stem cells, with the caveat that the assay measured RNA abundance rather than EIF3B protein or total translation and profiled neurons rather than pluripotent embryonic cells.

Pi4ka showed a transcriptomic signature that was not interchangeable with Pi4kb or other assayed phosphoinositide-pathway perturbations: across 22 shared cell types, Pi4ka–Pi4kb signed-score correlations were near zero, and correlations with Pik3ca, Pten, Ppip5k2, Synj1, Ocrl, and Plcb1 were likewise near zero. In this neuronal Perturb-seq readout, measured phosphoinositide-pathway perturbations did not recapitulate the Pi4ka whole-transcriptome score vector, although interpretation is limited because Pi4kb on-target engagement was weak and the comparison relies on signed transcriptome scores rather than lipid measurements or matched perturbation efficiencies.

Irf2bpl perturbation in this mouse neuronal Perturb-seq dataset did not reproduce the expected Wnt/β-catenin activation: canonical pathway genes such as Ctnnb1, Wnt1, Csnk1a1, Axin2, Porcn, Dvl1, and Dvl3 showed no FDR-supported or directionally coherent response, and Irf2bpl mRNA itself was not significantly reduced in any assayed cell type. Thus, although Wnt overactivation remains a plausible IRF2BPL mechanism from other systems, it was not the dominant acute transcriptional output here, with weak target engagement limiting mechanistic falsification.

Cit did not phenocopy the available Rho-family, MAPK, microcephaly-family, or tubulin comparator perturbations: across overlapping cell types, Cit score-vector correlations with Cdc42, Rac1, Mapk1, Mcph1, Diaph2, Tuba1a, and Tubb3 were near zero, with a maximum absolute Spearman rho of only 0.087. This weak similarity is notable because Tuba1a and Tubb3 perturbations produced strong detectable cytoskeletal responses in the same dataset, arguing against a hidden generic cytoskeletal signature. A caveat is that direct midbody partners such as KIF14, KIF23, ANLN, ASPM, and RHOA were not available as matched comparators, and in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut stratum Cit showed only a nominal RNA decrease without transcriptome-wide FDR-significant effects.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Srgap3 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut showed an isolated transcriptional signature in which the only FDR-significant downstream change was reduced Stxbp1, and this signature was not reproduced by perturbing canonical SLIT-ROBO-RAC1/CDC42 actin-guidance neighbors. In the same cell class, Slit2, Robo1, Robo2, Robo4, Cdc42, Rac1, and Cyfip1 had no FDR-significant genes and near-zero correlation to the Srgap3 profile, arguing that the measured Stxbp1 response is not a simple transcript-level readout of the SLIT-ROBO-RAC1/CDC42 axis; however, this comparison may miss pathway effects mediated through local GTPase activity and actin remodeling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zic1 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut state showed an engaged response that was uncoupled from a canonical Hedgehog/GLI transcriptomic program: Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, and Shh were not significantly altered after Zic1 perturbation, and the Zic1 signature was essentially uncorrelated with Gli, Ptch, or Smo perturbation signatures in the same cell type. This is best interpreted as no detectable matched Hedgehog/GLI signature in this context, since several Hedgehog-pathway perturbations also lacked target-transcript evidence here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lrp6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a weak but coherent transcriptional signature that aligned with Ctnnb1 loss and opposed Apc loss, most clearly in the top 50 Lrp6-response genes where Ctnnb1 was the strongest positive neighbor and Apc the strongest negative neighbor. Axin2 decreased after Lrp6 or Ctnnb1 perturbation and increased after Apc perturbation, supporting a canonical beta-catenin destruction-complex interpretation rather than an unrelated thalamic stress program. Genome-wide correlations were directionally consistent but small, and other receptor-node components appeared buffered or uncoupled in this assay.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ddx23 showed a transcriptomic phenotype that was most similar to Prpf6, not to other assayed DEAD-box helicases or non–tri-snRNP splicing regulators. In the main responsive cell types—155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA—Ddx23/Prpf6 score-vector correlations were strongest, whereas Ddx3x, Ddx39b, Dhx9, Srrm2, Srsf1, and U2af2 were weaker neighbors, consistent with a U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP and spliceosomal B-complex axis. A weaker echo was seen in 191 MB P MY GABA, but these correlations reflect transcriptome-wide similarity rather than direct molecular epistasis.

Specc1l perturbation did not produce a coordinated neuronal RNA module matching the expected actin, microtubule, adherens-junction, or PI3K-AKT biology: measured transcripts for network neighbors such as Actg1, Arpc2, Map3k1, and Tmod3 were not recurrently changed, and the Specc1l signature correlated only weakly with comparator perturbations including Actg1, Pten, Pik3ca, and Rac1. This uncoupling is specific to the transcriptomic assay context, because the dataset could recover corrected responses for some actin- or PI3K-adjacent perturbations, while Specc1l did not, and these data do not directly measure F-actin, microtubules, AKT phosphorylation, or junction stability.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Pten showed a restricted-signature pattern in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and more weakly in 191 MB P MY GABA cells in which Pten-responsive genes aligned with Tsc1 and Tsc2 knockdown and opposed Mtor and Pik3ca knockdown, within PTEN-TSC-PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling. This polarity was observed on genes nominally changed by Pten rather than the whole transcriptome, so it should be read as a focused neighbor score. Cell-type details included Akt3 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Pik3r1 as the lone FDR gene in 191 MB P MY GABA.

Dgke showed a non-convergent transcriptomic signature relative to assayed lipid-signaling neighbors: the related DGK family perturbation Dgkd did not phenocopy Dgke, and correlations between Dgke and Dgkd, Plcb1, Prkca, Prkcg, Pik3ca, Pik3cb, and Pten were all essentially zero. Pten produced its own FDR-level response, including a separate downstream signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. Across the assayed classes, this pattern is consistent with DGKε acting as a specialized arachidonoyl-DAG recycler rather than an interchangeable bulk DAG, PKC, or PI3K/PTEN node, although several comparator perturbations had weak on-target depletion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Fgf1 showed a pathway-uncoupled null signature rather than an assay-wide failure of FGFR/MAPK/PI3K biology. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Map2k1, Braf, and Pten perturbations produced significant Vgf or Ypel3 responses, whereas Fgf1, despite more cells than Pten or Braf, had no FDR-significant genes. In 155 MB Glut neurons, Fgfr1, Mapk1, Map2k1, Cdh2, Ncam1, and Fgf13 were directly depleted at FDR < 0.01, but Fgf1 again showed no significant genes; across a selected related-perturbation panel, Fgf1 score correlations stayed near zero, though this comparison relies on restricted perturbations and Wilcoxon score correlations rather than full causal pathway reconstruction.

Ptch1 showed little transcriptomic convergence with the assayed Hedgehog-neighborhood perturbations Ptch2, Smo, Cdon, Gpr161, Gli1, Gli2, and Gli3: Ptch1-versus-neighbor signature correlations averaged about zero across shared cell types, and Ptch1 had the least significant best genome-wide row in this local panel. Although these genes map to the same Hedgehog ligand–PTCH–SMO signaling pathway, the result indicates a lack of Ptch1-centered convergence rather than support for an alternative pathway, especially because most neighboring perturbations were themselves weak and the assay did not confirm edited proteins.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Paqr8 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced the only FDR-significant reduction of the Paqr8 transcript, yet the engaged thalamic signature did not show an FDR-supported ERK or immediate-early transcriptional response: Fos, Egr1, Jun, Dusp1, Dusp6, Spry2, and Arc were all not detected by FDR. This basal mouse-brain Perturb-seq result therefore separates steady-state Paqr8 knockdown from an mRNA imprint of ERK signaling, with the caveat that the check was a targeted gene panel and ERK phosphorylation can change without sustained transcript changes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Apc perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced a strong response that was not recapitulated by Gsk3b or proximal Wnt receptor perturbations. Gsk3b knockdown showed a corrected self-hit but only six total FDR hits and did not induce the Wnt feedback markers Axin2, Nkd1, or Notum. Lrp5 and Fzd3 had no corrected hits, while Lrp6 had only four and was only weakly, anti-correlated with the Apc-restricted signature. These receptor comparisons are exploratory because Lrp5, Lrp6, and Fzd3 lacked FDR-validated self-hits, and Gsk3a plus Axin paralogs were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ift88 perturbation was not detectably coupled to canonical Smoothened/Gli Hedgehog transcriptional output in the highlighted neuronal classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, and Gpr161 were not nominally changed. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, nominal co-directional decreases of Ift88, Ift57, and Tulp3 suggested some target engagement, yet no gene passed FDR and Hedgehog effector transcripts remained quiet; in 155 MB Glut, the only strong hit was Pcsk1n up-regulation without detectable Ift88 knockdown or Hedgehog response. Because these readouts are lowly expressed in some neuronal classes, absence of differential expression does not directly assess ciliary trafficking or Gli protein processing.

Smo did not produce a shared transcriptional program with other assayed Hedgehog components: whole-transcriptome signatures for Smo were nearly orthogonal to Cdon, Ptch1, Ptch2, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, and Gpr161, with the strongest within-cell-type correlation only r=0.154 for Smo–Ptch2 in 308 CB GABA. This weak, mixed pattern was also seen across Hedgehog / SMO-GLI signaling contexts such as 155 MB Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, but all of these perturbations showed weak target-transcript engagement, so the lack of convergence may reflect poor pathway perturbation rather than true biological uncoupling.
