In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Pten induced corrected signatures, and Braf did so in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, even where Epha2 was null; however, Pak1, Cdc42, and Mapk1 were themselves largely buffered, so these contrasts show inducibility of adjacent pathways rather than direct EPHA2-to-PTEN/BRAF wiring.

Slc2a1 loss did not collapse onto nearby metabolic-signaling perturbation states in these neurons: correlations with Hif1a/Arnt, insulin-receptor pathway genes Insr and Igf1r, and mTOR/TSC components Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1, and Tsc2 were all near zero overall, including in the largest Slc2a1 cell class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. A similar lack of convergence was seen in 308 CB GABA, where Slc2a1 showed a nominal transcript decrease but no FDR-significant downstream genes. This signature-neighborhood result is exploratory and does not directly measure glucose, HIF, PI3K, or mTOR activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zic2 showed only a weak, near-threshold response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where the observed signature was Rap1gap-led and appeared uncoupled from its established embryonic programs. In this thalamic class, perturbations of Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, and Smo were essentially uncorrelated with Zic2, and the retinal guidance markers Ephb1 and Slc6a4 were unchanged after Zic2 perturbation. These results separate the assayed mouse-brain response from reported GLI/Hedgehog, anterior neural-plate, and retinal EphB1/Sert contexts, which were not matched in this dataset.

Nf2 did not show transcriptomic convergence with assayed ERM/Hippo/PAK neighbors in this neuronal Perturb-seq readout: same-cell-type full-transcriptome correlations between Nf2 and Rdx, Tead1, Pak1, Pak2, Pak3, Rac1, Cdc42, or Rho perturbations were near zero, and these perturbations did not phenocopy a broad Nf2 signature. This argues against a broad Merlin-to-PAK or Merlin-to-TEAD transcriptional module here, with the caveat that the comparison is correlation-based and does not test PAK kinase activity or direct protein-level effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ctnna2, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, was uncoupled from the thalamic beta-catenin/APC transcriptional module: unlike Apc and Ctnnb1, it did not significantly change the Wnt sentinel genes Axin2, Nkd1, Notum, Lef1, Spock3, or Tiam1, and it showed near-zero transcriptomic correlation with related catenin/adhesion perturbations. This suggests that, despite its cadherin-catenin adhesome membership, alpha-N-catenin was not transcriptionally interchangeable with the APC/beta-catenin arm here, although this was a transcriptional comparison in one strongest-response cell type and Ctnna2 engagement was only partial.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cplane1 knockdown in the best-engaged neuronal strata, 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, did not produce a Hedgehog or ciliary transcriptional response: Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Smo, Adcy3, Ahi1, Ift88, and Ttc8 remained unchanged, with the clearest stratum showing significant depletion of the target mRNA but no non-target FDR response. This separates acute neuronal Cplane1 RNA loss from fibroblast reports of CPLANE1-dependent ciliogenesis and Hedgehog signaling, while leaving open cell-state, species, ligand-stimulation, and assay-endpoint differences as explanations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnpa2b1 perturbation did not transcriptionally activate the canonical m6A-associated primary miRNA processing branch in the main responsive neuron classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: Dgcr8, Mettl3, Mettl14, Wtap, Ythdc1, Ythdf1, and Ythdf2 were not FDR-supported differentially expressed as a block, while Drosha was the only microprocessor-adjacent transcript with supported upregulation and only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This suggests transcript abundance of core m6A writer/reader and DGCR8 components was uncoupled from Hnrnpa2b1 loss, although altered binding, m6A stoichiometry, miRNA processing, protein levels, or isoforms are not excluded.

Flvcr1 did not phenocopy the assayed iron-handling or ethanolamine-branch Kennedy-pathway perturbations: its score vectors were near-zero correlated with Fth1, Tfrc, Ireb2, Abcb7, and Pcyt2, and Flvcr1 showed no FDR-significant self or downstream signal, whereas Fth1 was readily detected in 10 of 22 cell types. These results argue that weak Flvcr1 nominal hits should not be read as a generic heme/iron or phospholipid-synthesis response, although several close comparators were not screened and Pcyt2 target engagement was itself weak.

Crx showed a shared null response in this brain perturbation dataset: Otx2, Nr2e3, Nrl, Rax, Rorb, and Rxrg likewise failed to reveal a Crx-like retinal transcription-factor module. Across 2,585,954 related-target tests, Crx, Nr2e3, Otx2, Rorb, and Rxrg had zero FDR-significant rows, while Nrl and Rax each had only singleton hits, and none of these targets’ own transcripts showed FDR-significant depletion. Crx signatures were also only weakly correlated with these neighbors, suggesting the absent phenotype reflects lack of the expressed retinal network state rather than demonstrated functional interchangeability after confirmed knockout.

Il1rapl2 showed essentially zero global transcriptomic correlation with Il1rapl1, the canonical IL-1 receptor subunits Il1rap and Il1r1, and the receptor-PTP perturbations Ptprd and Ptprf, so the RPTPδ–IL1RAPL trans-synaptic adhesion and IL-1 receptor-family signaling neighborhoods did not converge transcriptionally in this screen. These related perturbations were themselves mostly weak, no meaningful positive or negative Il1rapl2 signature neighbor emerged across the experiment, and the one low-count cell class noted only exploratory signals; Ptprs was not targeted.

Psen1 knockdown did not produce detectable mRNA-level compensation among the measured gamma-secretase complex components: Psen2, Ncstn, Psenen, and Aph1a were all FDR-negative, with no clear induction or repression. This suggests that any buffering of PSEN1 loss in this dataset is not explained by a simple transcriptional feedback loop that up-regulates these core complex transcripts. However, only four related transcripts were assayed as readouts, other subunits were not separately perturbed, and compensation could occur at the protein rather than mRNA level.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
full_finding_text: Plec in 001 L5-6 IT Glut showed the only corrected downstream hit in this neuronal panel, where Eprs was up despite only nominal Plec self-depletion, and the Plec whole-transcriptome signature had essentially no strong positive or negative neighbor. Although PLEC is curated in a cytolinker and hemidesmosome-adjacent network with Dst, Dag1, Itga6, Itgb1, Actn4, Gfap, Dmd, and Macf1, these assayed comparators largely did not phenocopy Plec: Dst, Dag1, Itgb1, Gfap, Dmd, and Actn4 had no FDR-significant neuronal rows, and Macf1 showed only self-depletion. This comparison is limited because ITGB4 and COL17A1 were not assayed.

Sox18 showed only weak similarity to related SOXF and endothelial pathway perturbations and to its nearest signature neighbors in all assayed Glut, GABA, and Dopa neuronal groups. Across 44,110 whole-transcriptome correlations, the best positive and negative neighbors were modest (r=0.150 and r=-0.128), and the SOXF paralog Sox17 reached only r=0.124; other comparators including Prox1, Flt4, Kdr, Foxc1, Foxc2, Ctnnb1, Adam22, and Sec31a likewise did not phenocopy Sox18. This argues against a strong compensated SOXF or off-target-like signature, although many related perturbations also had weak on-target transcript statistics in these neuronal groups, limiting epistasis inference.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Magel2 showed a much weaker and largely transcriptionally orthogonal response in 155 MB Glut cells relative to other imprinted or Prader-Willi-region perturbations. In this matched cell type, Ndn, Snrpn, and Peg3 produced strong FDR-supported signatures, whereas Magel2 had only a minimal signal, and its full differential-expression score correlations with Ndn, Snrpn, and Peg3 were near zero (r=0.0057, 0.0083, and 0.0030). Thus, within the Prader-Willi/imprinted-gene perturbation module, Magel2 did not phenocopy Ndn, Snrpn, Peg3, Ube3a, or Herc2, although this comparison is based on transcriptomic correlations in one cell type and does not directly test shared protein-complex activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Rbfox1 showed a divergent perturbation signature: in the two strongest Rbfox1-responsive cell types, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, perturbations of LASR/RBP neighbors Hnrnpc, Hnrnpu, Hnrnph2, and Matr3 had near-zero correlations with the Rbfox1 gene-level abundance signature, and an unrestricted search found no close positive or negative phenocopy, with no |r| above 0.18, including in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. These results suggest that shared RBFOX/LASR assembly membership does not translate into interchangeable abundance phenotypes, although the comparison was limited to gene-level abundance rather than alternative-splicing events, and Hnrnpm and RBFOX paralogs were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Sin3a targeting produced a recurrent state across responding neurons, with Odf2, Dzip1, Ift22 and often Cyp46a1 and Grn increased, while RNA-processing and splicing factors such as Srrm2, Snrnp70, Rnpc3, Ddx17 and Pnisr decreased. This pattern appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, with the strongest signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The cilium/centrosome and spliceosome labels are inferred from recurrent marker genes and curated annotations rather than formal enrichment statistics.

Akap6 showed no conventionally significant or near-significant transcriptome-wide effects in any stratum, and related perturbations in the cAMP/PKA AKAP signalosome were similarly buffered or self-only: Akap9 and Pde4d had no FDR-significant hits, Akap11 had only one self hit, and Prkaca and Prkar1a showed strong self-depletion without nonself FDR hits. Although AKAP6 is connected to PKA and PDE4D-containing signalosomes, these data suggest weak coupling of this local cAMP scaffold to steady-state transcription, with the caveat that guide efficiencies and cell counts differed and Prkar1a is not the canonical AKAP6-bound type II regulatory subunit.

Cdk13 showed a distinct perturbational signature: across whole-transcriptome comparisons, its expression changes were essentially uncorrelated with Cdk8, Med12, and Med13, and in a nearest-neighbor scan across 2,045 perturbations restricted to an 820-gene Cdk13-enriched set, only weak positive neighbors were found. This argues against Cdk13 representing a generic Pol II or Mediator-kinase stress state and instead supports a more specific CDK13/Cyclin K-associated response program. Important caveats are that Cdk12 and Ccnk were not in the panel, and the neighbor scan used a restricted gene set.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cog5 showed a weak or null Perturb-seq response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, but this did not reflect a general inability of this cell class to respond to Golgi/TGN trafficking perturbations. In the same cells, Vps54 produced 31 FDR-significant genes and Stx16 showed strong on-target knockdown, whereas Cog5 had no FDR-significant genes and only weak score-vector correlations with Vps54, Vps53, or Stx16. Thus, Cog5 was uncoupled from nearby retrograde/TGN trafficking perturbations here, although these comparators are pathway neighbors rather than members of the same obligatory complex.

Slc2a1 perturbation was not transcriptomically phenocopied by curated SLC2A1 physical interactors: across 88 shared comparisons, Add1, Add2, Add3, and Bsg signatures were almost orthogonal to Slc2a1, with a maximum absolute correlation of 0.1195. In these neuronal transcriptomes, this suggests the membrane-associated SLC2A1 physical-interactor module is not an interchangeable readout of Slc2a1 loss. A caveat is that Dmtn was not perturbed, and weak-signature correlations may miss post-transcriptional or trafficking relationships; in 308 CB GABA, Slc2a1 showed the strongest nominal transcript decrease but no FDR-significant genes.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Mef2c perturbation in cortical IT glutamatergic neurons, especially 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, produced convergent synaptic membrane/receptor signatures rather than unrelated top-gene changes. In both classes, Chgb, Stac2, Gria2, and Serinc2 increased while Slit2 decreased, and the broader FDR-supported set included Grm3, Nptx1/Nptxr, Ptk2b, Cacna2d1, Rasgrf1, Rasgrf2, and Rasal1, with enrichment for glutamatergic-synapse and neurotransmitter-receptor regulation. These RNA changes indicate mixed synaptic remodeling after Mef2c loss, but do not directly measure synapse number, input specificity, dendritic spines, or electrophysiology.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Slit2 showed only modest, cell-type-restricted signature similarity rather than recurrent Slit/Robo-family convergence. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, the strongest neighbors were Syn1 (r=0.267) and Nr2c2 (r=-0.263), while in 308 CB GABA the top neighbors were Wdr26 (r=0.250) and Ranbp2 (r=-0.237). These correlations arose from weak Slit2 signatures, most top neighbors were not known direct SLIT2 pathway members, and the cerebellar GABA pattern occurred without FDR-significant Slit2 genes, so these findings are best treated as exploratory restricted-signature hypotheses.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf12 did not phenocopy Ctbp1 or related KLF/SP transcription-factor perturbations in the best-powered thalamic class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In this cell type, Klf12 had 124 cells but no FDR-significant genes, no corrected shifts in the AP-2/CtBP-linked KLF repression context, and no detectable changes in the canonical AP-2 alpha target or three Shh-pathway readouts; the best-sampled contrast remained nominal and did not show target-transcript reduction. By contrast, Ctbp1, Klf9, Sp4, and Klf7 showed corrected signatures in the same class, although stronger signals may partly reflect higher cell counts or different biology, and Klf3/Klf8 were not tested.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cltc perturbation reproducibly produced a Jun/Stmn4-high neuronal stress-remodeling program rather than a uniform induction of clathrin machinery genes. Across 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 308 CB GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Jun and Stmn4 were the most recurrent increases, while Atp8b2, Ecel1, Crem, Ddit3, Bcl2l11, and Rhoq appeared in narrower, cell-type-specific contexts, often alongside repression of synaptic, secretory, or excitability genes. The strongest target-engaged response was in 155 MB Glut; however, Jun and Stmn4 are not specific reporters of clathrin failure, and several recurrent genes were supported only at FDR < 0.1.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cntnap2 showed a quiet, target-specific profile in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: despite strong on-target depletion, it produced no non-target FDR-significant genes in either glutamatergic stratum. This was not a general failure to detect responses in these cell types, because the internal comparator Pten induced broad non-target programs in the same strata, with 33 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 11 in 155 MB Glut, including Igsf8, Ypel3, and Pcsk1n. The contrast supports Cntnap2 buffering, although the comparator is an ASD/NDD disease gene rather than a Cntnap2 complex member.

Cxcr4 perturbation did not significantly change steady-state expression of the canonical CXCL12–CXCR4/ACKR3 signaling module: across 32 assayed transcripts, including Cxcl12, Ackr3, Gi subunits, adenylyl-cyclase genes, MAPK, PI3K/AKT, Rho-family, and arrestin genes such as Arrb1 and Arrb2, there were no FDR-significant transcriptional shifts. This suggests the Perturb-seq endpoint did not capture canonical CXCR4 pathway activation or inhibition at the mRNA level, with the caveat that GPCR second messengers and MAPK or AKT phosphorylation can change without detectable transcript changes.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Myo5a in the 308 CB GABA cerebellar GABA aggregate did not reproduce a clear Purkinje-like transcriptomic program: depletion was only nominal, no downstream genes reached FDR significance, and alignment with comparator signatures for Grm1, Grm5, Dlg4, and Rab27a was weak. This leaves the Myo5a perturbation largely uncoupled from the expected Purkinje dendritic-spine endoplasmic-reticulum localization pathway in this assay, with the important caveat that 308 CB GABA is an aggregate label rather than an isolated Purkinje-neuron population and may mismatch this subcellular phenotype.

Fntb knockdown showed no robust transcriptional compensation in the protein farnesylation and RAS CaaX-processing pathway: the assayed transcripts Fnta, Pggt1b, Rabggtb, Rce1, Icmt, Fdps, Ggps1, Hras, Kras, Nras, Rheb, Rala, and Ralb were all FDR-negative, indicating no multiple-testing-significant induction or repression after perturbation. This argues against mRNA-level feedback at these pathway nodes as the dominant observed response, while leaving open compensation through enzyme activity, alternative prenylation, substrate localization, or protein turnover.

Pax7 perturbation in brain neurons left canonical PAX7-associated developmental and myogenic neighborhoods uncoupled: Reactome neural plate border genes such as Ctnnb1, Zic1, Sox2, and Pax3, and STRING/UniProt myogenic partners including Foxo1, Myod1, Myog, Myf5, and Myf6 showed no corrected expression change. This argues against detectable transdifferentiation or injury-like reactivation of canonical PAX7 circuitry in these cells, although the assessment was based on a literature-selected panel and some lowly expressed myogenic genes were not detected in every cell type.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Trps1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons induced Atp6ap2 as a strong downstream marker, but direct Atp6ap2 perturbation did not phenocopy the Trps1 state: instead, Atp6ap2 loss lowered Atp6ap2 and Atp6v0a1 without changing Tnc or Pid1, and its transcriptome was neither a mimic nor an inverse of the Trps1 signature. This supports the ATP6AP2/V-ATPase/Wnt-adaptor branch as a readout of Trps1 rather than a sufficient driver of the Tnc/Pid1 branch, with the caveat that RNA-seq here cannot resolve protein-level or flux changes and only tests loss, not gain, of Atp6ap2.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nrg1 did not phenocopy other NRG/ERBB family perturbations in this screen. In matched cell types, Nrg1 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Nrg2, Nrg3, Erbb3, and Erbb4, and there was no robust Nrg1 transcriptional output or comparable self-depletion. By contrast, Nrg3 showed self-transcript depletion in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, with Erbb4 and Nrg3 comparator engagement largely limited to self-transcript effects. Some divergence may reflect transcript abundance, guide efficacy, and perturbed-cell counts.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnn2 showed a transcriptomic profile that was uncoupled from calmodulin and other neuronal ion-channel perturbations in 308 CB GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. Although Calm1, Calm3, Kcnq2, Hcn2, and Kcnma1 produced stronger, FDR-significant responses elsewhere, their score profiles were essentially uncorrelated with Kcnn2, arguing against interpreting the weak Kcnn2 signal as a generic calcium/K+ channel transcriptional cassette. In 308 CB GABA, Kcnn2 had the clearest nominal target depletion but no downstream row was FDR-significant; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the best downstream row had FDR 0.708. These comparisons reflect transcriptomic adaptation, and the comparator genes are pleiotropic rather than acute channel-physiology readouts.

Mmaa perturbation showed no significant transcriptional feedback across the measured cobalamin, propionate, or one-carbon pathway genes, with no detectable changes among Mmut, Mmab, Mmachc, Mmadhc, Lmbrd1, Abcd4, Pcca, Pccb, Mcee, Acsf3, Mtr, Mtrr, Mthfr, and Cd320. This pattern is consistent with MMAA acting at the mitochondrial MMAB–MMUT cofactor delivery and repair step rather than through an mRNA feedback program. However, single-cell mRNA measurements cannot assess adenosylcobalamin occupancy, MMUT activity, or methylmalonic-acid accumulation.

Tpm3 targeting did not produce a detectable transcriptional compensation program in this assay: across all tests, Tpm1, Tpm2, Tpm4, Actg1, Flna, and Tmod1 showed no corrected induction, and even the strongest nominal single-gene responses did not survive multiple-testing correction. In the pooled mouse-brain dataset, this lack of induction was seen across the 22 neuronal classes, arguing against a simple mRNA feedback response within the Tpm3-associated actin-filament, growth-cone, and AIS cytoskeletal pathway. However, only assayed transcripts were evaluated, so isoform relocalization, filament coating, protein turnover, growth-cone morphology, and AIS nanoscale structure were not measured.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Tcf3 showed an exploratory, CA3-restricted signature-neighbor pattern in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, where it had the largest count of nominal p<0.001 genes but no FDR-significant genes. In this cell class, Tcf3 had weak positive whole-transcriptome correlations with Neurog3, Fgfr2, and Dnm2, and weak negative correlations with Tiam1 and Zbtb21. The Neurog3 link is plausible at the broader E-protein/bHLH E-box network level, but the correlations were low, derived from a single cell class, and do not establish a resolved Tcf3 module.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hspa8 showed a mostly divergent transcriptional perturbation state in the responsive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, with only partial convergence to Hspa9 and Hspa5 and weak similarity to Hsp90ab1, Hspd1, Dnajb6, Dnajc13, and Dnajc6. This pattern fits a specialized HSP70/HSP90 chaperone and heat-shock compensation context, where related factors share interactors yet do not simply substitute for cytosolic Hspa8; however, the comparison is based on whole-transcriptome score correlations rather than matched double-perturbation or biochemical assays.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Nrg3 did not show an interpretable phenocopy with Nrg1, Nrg2, Erbb3, or Erbb4 in this dataset. In the three best Nrg3-engaged cell types—155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA—top-200 restricted Nrg3 signatures had near-zero correlations with signatures from those related perturbations. This negative result is limited by failed or unmeasurable on-target transcript depletion for Nrg1, Nrg2, and Erbb3, and by the signature analysis being restricted to the top 200 Nrg3-scored genes per cell type.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ppp2r1a loss produced a cell-type-restricted sterol response rather than a pan-neuronal one: 155 MB Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut upregulated cholesterol-biosynthesis genes including Insig1, Msmo1, Dhcr24, Dhcr7, Nsdhl, Sc5d, Sqle, Ldlr, Lss, Fdft1, Fdps, Cyp51, and Hmgcs1, whereas the largest thalamic and cortical signatures, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, repressed Srebf2 and Hmgcr. These directions are inferred from mRNA only, since sterol metabolites and SREBP processing were not measured.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Erbb4 perturbation in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 046 CTX-CGE GABA cells was not phenocopied by Erbb3, Nrg1, Nrg2, or Nrg3 perturbations: these comparators showed no adjusted-significant signatures in the two Erbb4-engaged classes and had near-zero score-vector correlation with Erbb4. In Pvalb cells, Erbb4 was the top and only FDR-significant row, while in CTX-CGE GABA cells Erbb4 depletion was weaker but still FDR-significant. This suggests that cell-autonomous ligand or Erbb3 knockdown is not interchangeable with Erbb4 loss in these interneurons, with the caveat that ligand effects could be non-cell-autonomous or expressed elsewhere.

Axl did not converge with the TAM-family context in this screen: Mertk was the only assayed TAM paralog comparator, while Tyro3 and the ligands Gas6 and Pros1 were absent. Across the measured cell types, Axl and Mertk signatures were essentially uncorrelated, and Mertk had no FDR-significant differentially expressed genes, so the dataset did not recover an engaged GAS6/AXL-MERTK efferocytosis module or coupled AXL-associated PI3K signaling with Pik3ca/Pik3r1. Because both Axl and Mertk signatures were weak, this should not be interpreted as antagonism.

Atl3 perturbation did not produce FDR-significant induction of canonical GABARAP-linked tubular ER-phagy or unfolded-protein-response transcripts: Gabarap, Gabarapl1, Gabarapl2, Ccpg1, Tex264, Retreg1, and UPR markers including Hspa5 and Ddit3 were not activated at the mRNA level under basal Perturb-seq conditions. This suggests the observed phenotype is better framed as weak membrane-network or trafficking-related changes rather than a canonical ER-phagy or stress program. However, the lack of transcript induction does not rule out GABARAP recruitment, ER-phagy flux, or ER morphology changes at the protein or organelle level.

Scn8a was not transcriptionally interchangeable with the sodium-channel alpha paralogs Scn1a, Scn2a, Scn3a, or Scn9a: mean score-vector correlations were effectively zero, indicating near-zero cross-paralog similarity in this assay. A weak positive relationship was seen with Ank3, most clearly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also noted in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and low-count 308 CB GABA, while Scn1b showed only neighbor-level proximity. Because most Scn8a signatures were small, this non-phenocopy should be interpreted as transcriptomic rather than electrophysiologic divergence.

Kcnma1 showed a weak, distinct transcriptomic response that did not converge with other neuronal potassium- and calcium-channel perturbations. Across the full transcriptome, Kcnma1 had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor, and its profile was near-orthogonal to Kcnh1, Kcnq2, Kcnc3, Kcnab2, Kcnn2, Kcnn3, and Cacna1c, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA cells where Kcnma1 itself was significantly reduced. In the same dataset, Kcnq2, Kcnc3, and Kcnab2 showed broader self-knockdown, so the weak Kcnma1 neighborhood was not a generic ion-channel feature; this lack of convergence is transcriptomic only and reflects correlations dominated by weak Kcnma1 signatures.

Adgrb3 perturbation did not recover the expected C1QL–ADGRB3–ELMO1/DOCK1/RAC1 axis as a transcriptional module: C1ql1–4, Elmo1–3, Dock1, Rac1, and Baiap2 were measured yet were not detectably changed as transcripts, indicating an mRNA-level uncoupling of both C1QL-ADGRB3 synaptic organizer signaling and ELMO1-DOCK1-RAC1 actin regulation. This is consistent with a pathway whose biology is largely mediated by membrane and synaptic protein interactions, with the caveat that the C1ql ligand genes were response genes rather than perturbation targets and mRNA abundance is only an indirect readout of this signaling.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hs6st2 in 155 MB Glut showed a self-depletion-only transcriptomic response, with no FDR-significant compensatory shifts in heparan-sulfate biosynthesis or 6-O-sulfation genes and no shared signature with HS-dependent FGF/FGFR or Slit/Robo signaling perturbations. In the same cell type, Agrn, Ext2, Fgfr1, and Robo2 each had robust self-knockdown as their only significant event, their score-vector correlations with Hs6st2 were near zero, and Glce lacked a robust on-target mRNA response. These comparisons are transcriptomic and limited to the Perturb-seq panel, which lacked Hs6st1, Hs6st3, Hs2st1, and Ndst perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gabrb2 showed its clearest, cell-type-restricted relationship in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where its transcriptomic signature was most similar to Gabra1, Gabrd, Slc12a5, and Atp2b1 perturbations and most opposed to Grin1, Dlgap4, Nalcn, Ank3, and Scn1b. This rank ordering is consistent with a local GABA-A receptor and chloride-homeostasis versus excitability/synaptic module in this cell class, rather than isolated beta2 autoregulation, although the underlying full-transcriptome correlations had small absolute r values and are useful mainly for neighbor discovery rather than mechanistic epistasis.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Atl3 showed scattered nominal ER and membrane-trafficking signals across several neuronal cell types rather than a coherent corrected program. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut cells, Arl6ip1 was down and Reep1 up; in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells, Rtn3 and Rtn4 were down; in 155 MB Glut cells, Vapa and Spcs1 were up; and in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA cells, Yipf5 was up. These genes are directionally compatible with ATL3-related ER network maintenance, but all rows were nominal only, with mixed directions and no recurrence across cell types.

Hsf1 perturbation did not collapse all measured HSP transcripts: Hspa5, Hspa9, and Hspd1 showed no FDR-supported change in any Hsf1 cell type, even though Hsph1 and Hsp90aa1 were recurrently downregulated. This narrows the basal HSF1 output to an HSPH1/HSP90 branch rather than a global chaperone response, with the strongest recurring chaperone signal centered on Hsph1. The result is transcript-specific and basal, and does not exclude regulation of these genes under heat shock or other stress conditions.

Itm2b knockdown was transcriptionally uncoupled from the APP/BRI2 secretase-access and intramembrane-proteolysis axis in this dataset: App, Adam10, Psen1, and Sppl2a mRNAs were unchanged, and the Itm2b perturbation score vector was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of App and these processing-axis neighbors. This suggests Itm2b knockdown is not an mRNA-level proxy for the known BRI2–APP processing module, although Adam10, Psen1, and Sppl2a had weak on-target depletion here, making App the strongest direct comparator, and the correlations reflect rank-test transcriptomic scores rather than APP-processing biochemistry.

Col25a1 showed no FDR-supported target engagement or downstream transcriptional response across all 22 profiled mouse-brain cell types, including no supported changes in APP/Aβ-related markers or Ptprs/Ptprd receptor-candidate genes. In the same dataset, App and the neuronal comparator Syp each showed strong on-target depletion in 20 of 22 cell types but no non-self FDR-significant genes, whereas Adam10, Psen1, and Ptprd were themselves weak and FDR-null. This pattern suggests the Col25a1 failure was perturbation-specific and that acute APP-family perturbation did not produce a broad AD-like RNA state.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Myef2 perturbation induced a positive Dzip3/Vbp1/Ist1 module in the strongest responsive neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with the thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic classes showing especially strong FDR-significant responses. In contrast, Pura knockdown, despite effective depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, did not phenocopy this Myef2 signature. This suggests the neuronal Dzip3/Vbp1/Ist1 output is uncoupled from the canonical PURA-MyEF2 MB1 promoter axis described for Mbp regulation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Myef2 perturbation repeatedly increased a compact Dzip3/Vbp1/Ist1 proteostasis-endosomal marker module in selected neuronal classes, most clearly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where all three genes were FDR-significant. Directionally matched but less complete responses were also seen in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, though some of these extensions relied on nominal or FDR<0.1 support and low perturbed-cell counts. Within responsive cell types, Myef2 was the strongest inducer of this module across perturbations.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Nek1 did not produce a robust ciliary transcriptional module in this Perturb-seq dataset. Across the library, same-family Nek9 and cilia-related perturbations including Ift88, Kif3b, Pkd1, and Bbs9 were largely uncoupled or nearly orthogonal to Nek1 signatures, with only weak positive hints toward Ttll5 and Bbs5, and only in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut. The largest ciliary-aligned correlation was modest (r=0.1757), suggesting that acute mouse-brain Nek1 RNA signatures do not faithfully capture canonical ciliary loss.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf9 showed a gene-specific transcriptional effect in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut that was not recapitulated by other assayed Klf paralogs. In this subclass, Klf7 had only one FDR-significant hit, while Klf1, Klf11, Klf12, and Klf13 had none, and full-signature correlations with Klf9 were near zero despite paralogy and broader KLF-family links to cAMP-linked axon-growth regulation. This divergence is signature-based rather than a definitive paralog loss-of-function comparison, because knockdown of Klf13 and other paralog transcripts was not clearly demonstrated.

Gp6 perturbation did not detectably engage the canonical GPVI-mediated activation cascade at the mRNA level: Fcer1g, Fyn, Lyn, Syk, Lat, Lcp2, and Plcg2 remained unchanged, indicating no transcriptional activation or repression of the platelet GPVI-FcRγ axis in this dataset. This suggests the pathway is transcriptionally uncoupled from neuronal Gp6 targeting under the measured conditions, with the important caveat that Perturb-seq reads mRNA, whereas acute GPVI signaling is largely driven by receptor complex assembly and tyrosine phosphorylation rather than transcriptional change.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chrna4 showed an asymmetric, nominal cross-subunit transcript response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: Chrnb2 perturbation was associated with a nominal increase in Chrna4 transcript, whereas Chrna4 perturbation did not significantly change Chrnb2. This pattern is consistent with a possible subunit-balancing response after beta-2 loss and may help explain why Chrnb2 loss did not reproduce the Chrna4–Cyp46a1 program, but both cross-effects failed FDR correction and should be considered exploratory within nicotinic acetylcholine receptor cation-channel signaling.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Tcf12 did not phenocopy the related E-protein perturbations Tcf3 or Tcf4: across the 22 assayed cell types, Tcf12 genome-wide rank signatures were essentially uncorrelated with both paralogs, and in 052 Pvalb Gaba the focused Tcf4 response, with Oprd1 and Tmem44 down, was absent after Tcf12 perturbation. This divergence within E-box/class I bHLH transcriptional regulation suggests paralog membership alone did not predict the sampled neuronal transcriptomic response, although the comparison is limited by weak Tcf12 mRNA reduction and weak overall target engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Atp6ap2 did not phenocopy core Atp6v0c loss across the V-ATPase network. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Atp6ap2 showed a small, target-dominated response with FDR-significant Atp6v0a1 down-regulation, while Atp6v0c produced much broader transcriptional programs, including 537 FDR genes in 151 TH and 158 in 052 Pvalb Gaba. Similar buffering was seen for Atp6ap1, and in 191 MB P MY GABA Atp6ap2 caused strong self-depletion without non-target FDR genes. Because knockdown magnitudes and perturbed-cell counts differed between Atp6v0c and accessory-subunit guides, effect sizes are not directly normalized.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tfrc in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut converged transcriptionally with Ireb2 rather than with the ferritin subunit Fth1. In this cell class, Ireb2 was the strongest positive neighbor of the top 300 Tfrc-responsive genes, and Ireb2 knockdown nominally lowered Tfrc while increasing Vegfa, Kdm3a, Pfkl, and Ldha, consistent with a shared iron-starvation/IRP-IRE and glycolysis-associated program. By contrast, Fth1 knockdown showed strong on-target mRNA depletion but no genome-wide FDR-supported secondary response. This comparison is limited by the restricted top-300-gene signature and only nominal reduction of the Ireb2 self-transcript.

Tbx3 did not phenocopy its close T-box relatives in this postmitotic brain Perturb-seq screen: same-cell whole-genome score correlations between Tbx3 and Tbx2, Tbx4, or Tbx5 were nearly orthogonal, never exceeding |r|=0.0969. The comparator perturbations were themselves FDR-null, so the result is correlation-based and limited by weak signatures in these cells. Overall, the data do not support a convergent or interchangeable TBX2-subfamily module for T-box transcriptional regulation in the assayed postmitotic neurons.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Tcf3 did not share an interchangeable whole-transcriptome signature with the E-protein paralogs Tcf4 and Tcf12 in the profiled neuronal states. In 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, Tcf3 and Tcf12 had no FDR-significant genes, whereas Tcf4 had only two, with decreases in Oprd1 and Tmem44, and Tcf3 score correlations with Tcf4 or Tcf12 were near zero across classes. These results fit a weak, redundant, or context-dependent role for the E-protein/bHLH E-box network, with the caveat that transcriptomic summaries and available perturbations may miss incomplete protein loss or buffered effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rhot1 was transcriptomically quiet in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, showing no FDR-significant genes despite nominal target reduction, whereas other mitochondrial dynamics and quality-control perturbations in the same cell class were clearly detectable. In particular, Dnm1l, Opa1, Vps35, Kif5a, and Kif5c each showed FDR-significant on-target loss or broader significant responses, arguing that the negative Rhot1 result is target- or guide-strength-specific rather than a general inability to detect mitochondrial biology. A caveat is that these comparators sample adjacent mitochondrial fission/fusion and quality-control processes rather than an obligate RHOT1-containing complex, and guide efficacy differed by gene.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ap1s2 showed a largely buffered transcriptional phenotype compared with neighboring clathrin-linked trafficking perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Ap1s2 produced no FDR-significant downstream rows, and in 191 MB P MY GABA it produced only one, Btbd8, despite nominal target depletion. By contrast, Ap2s1, Ap2m1, and Rab7 generated many significant changes in these same neuronal classes, indicating stronger transcriptome coupling in synaptic vesicle recycling. This comparison is informative but caveated because Ap2s1, Ap2m1, and Rab7 are not AP-1 sigma paralogs.

Cd14 showed no convergence with its innate-signaling neighbors Tlr2, Tlr4, and Nfkb1: in matched cell types, genome-wide score correlations were near zero, and none of these perturbations produced FDR-significant rows. Across the assayed neuronal cell classes, the available receptor/pathway neighbors also failed to generate robust transcriptional programs, so the data did not reveal a hidden recurrent CD14-like module. This should be read as a context-specific null result, since Ly96, Lbp, and Myd88 were not perturbed and the comparison reflects weak basal signatures rather than ligand-driven signaling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf13 did not phenocopy its paralog Klf9 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class: whereas Klf9 produced a clear transcriptional signature with 20 FDR-significant genes, Klf13 had no FDR-significant downstream genes and an almost zero full-score correlation with Klf9 (0.0266). This argues against assuming interchangeable KLF9/KLF13 activity in these mature thalamic neurons, despite paralogy and prior reports of shared functions. The contrast is tempered by weak Klf13 guide engagement, and published comparators come from HT22 cells, hippocampal neurons, oligodendrocytes, and cancer-focused contexts rather than this thalamic class.

Adgrg1 showed no transcriptomic propagation into the expected adhesion-GPCR COL3A1/GNA12-GNA13/RhoA module: Col3a1, Tgm2, Gna12, Gna13, Rhoa, Cd81, and G-protein subunit transcripts such as Gnb1, Gng2, and Gnaq were FDR-null after perturbation, and Adgrg1 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Adgrg2, Adgrg6, Cd81, or Gnb1 perturbations. In the neuronal cell types assayed, including 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, this suggests weak or uncoupled mRNA-level signaling, while receptor-proximal RhoA activation could still occur without steady-state transcript changes.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Adcy5 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut showed an exploratory, restricted top-gene pattern in which the Adcy5 top-200 absolute-score signature was anti-correlated with cAMP/G-protein perturbations including Adora2a, Gnb1, Gnal, and Gnas, but this contrast was weak across the whole transcriptome. Safe-target controls such as Safe_target_70 and Safe_target_24 were also among the strongest neighbors, and nominal Adcy5 response genes did not recur across cell types, so the result is better viewed as a guide-signature caveat than as clear GPCR-cAMP/PKA/CREB pathway inversion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Trrap perturbation repeatedly downregulated an imprinted and snoRNA-host negative module, with Snrpn, Peg3, Mest, Nap1l5, and recurrent Snhg11 repression across post-mitotic neuronal classes, most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. This suggests imprinted and noncoding RNA biology as a dominant neuronal output of Trrap loss, but the data measure total expression only and cannot establish allele-specific imprinting, imprint-control methylation, or direct TRRAP binding.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grm7 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only cell type with significant Grm7 target depletion, yet related class-C metabotropic glutamate receptor and G alpha(i/o) signaling perturbations were not interchangeable with it. In this same cell type, Grm1 and Gnao1 were on target in their own perturbations, but their transcriptome signatures were nearly orthogonal to Grm7, with near-zero correlations also for Grm8, Grm3, and Adcy3. Most downstream effects were weak after multiple-testing correction, so this supports absence of a robust shared steady-state mRNA program rather than excluding shared acute signaling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf7 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class showed no strong phenocopy from other perturbations; notably, Klf9 was not similar to Klf7 but instead gave a much stronger yet only weakly inverse transcriptional program within the KLF-family axon-growth regulatory context. The contrast was restricted rather than strongly anti-correlated, with small genome-wide correlation and limited top-gene overlap, and involved genes such as Wsb1, Rasgrp2, Pld3, Tuba1a, and Tubb3, indicating non-interchangeable KLF paralog effects in this thalamic setting.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lemd3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a weak restricted top-gene signature that preserved TGF-beta/activin/BMP receptor-SMAD pathway directionality: among the 300 genes with the smallest Lemd3 p values, Ski was the nearest positive perturbation neighbor, whereas Smad2 was the strongest negative neighbor and Acvr2a the second-most negative. This pattern is mechanistically coherent with LEMD3 and SKI acting as SMAD repressors and SMAD2/ACVR2A as pathway-positive nodes, but the analysis was limited to a restricted gene set and the absolute correlations were modest.

Egr2 showed weak, largely null transcriptional signatures across 21 tested neuronal classes, with no strong same-file signature neighbor and no non-Egr2 perturbation exceeding abs(r)>0.2 in same-cell-type correlation scans. In selected neuronal activity and neurotrophin pathway comparators, Egr2 was essentially uncorrelated with Mef2c, Ntrk2, Mef2a, Ntrk3, Jund, Mapk1, and Mef2d, even though some of these perturbations produced detectable FDR-level effects in the same atlas. This pathway-uncoupling is exploratory because the Egr2 signature itself was weak, and direct comparisons to Egr paralogs or NAB cofactors were unavailable.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ache perturbation produced RNA signatures that were nearly orthogonal to nicotinic and muscarinic acetylcholine receptor perturbations, including Chrnb2, Chrna4, Chrna7, Chrm2, and Chrm3, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells. Chrnb2 was robustly engaged in the same three Ache-responsive classes yet showed near-zero full-signature correlation and mostly a self-transcript effect, while Chrna4 behaved similarly where engaged. In this assay, reducing the degrading enzyme and reducing receptor subunits were therefore not transcriptomically interchangeable, although this conclusion is limited to RNA signatures and most other receptor-subunit guides lacked clear on-target engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Esrrg was essentially flat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, with no target-transcript engagement or FDR-significant downstream genes, while Esrra and Rora produced strong signatures in the same stratum; Esrra also recovered mitochondrial genes. This contrast argues against generic interchangeability across nuclear-receptor perturbations in this screen, despite Esrrg lying near Esrra, Ppargc1a, and Ppargc1b in the ERR/PGC-1 co-regulator network. A caveat is that Rora target-transcript depletion was not itself FDR-significant, and the comparisons span different guide sets and cell counts.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Psmb4 perturbation in responsive neurons was associated with a recurrent down-regulation of synaptic transmission and neuronal excitability transcripts, including Atp1a3, Gria2, Syt1, Syp, Nsg1, Slc17a6, and Slc17a7, rather than only increased proteasome gene expression. This pattern was strongest in 155 MB Glut and also evident in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, with stress-associated transcripts induced alongside loss of neuronal identity markers. These findings are transcriptomic; electrophysiology, synapse number, and neuronal survival were not measured.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Bsg knockdown in eight neuronal contexts—052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut—produced robust on-target depletion but no detectable mRNA coupling to canonical BSG pathways: monocarboxylate/lactate genes Slc16a1, Slc16a3, Slc16a8, Slc16a11, Slc16a12, Ldha, and Ldhb, plus Mmp2, Mmp9, Vegfa, Kdr, Hif1a, Itgb1, Itga3, Itga6, and Cav1, all failed conventional FDR thresholds. This suggests the neuronal phenotype is uncoupled from canonical BSG transcript programs, with the caveat that many BSG effects may be post-translational or context-specific.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Huwe1 reduction recurrently induced a predominantly upregulated Rsrp1-centered RNA-processing module, with nuclear-speck/spliceosome-associated genes Srrm1, Srrm2, Sf3b1, Srsf1, and Dzip1, plus Tcea2 and Ankrd24. This was the most reproducible downstream signature in responsive neurons, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also seen in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and a smaller 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut response. The pattern suggests an RNA-processing state distinct from the developmental MYCN/Notch cascade, while RNA-seq supports induction of RNA-processing transcripts rather than direct changes in splicing or nuclear-speck morphology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cog4 showed a near-null phenotype in this atlas, unlike related Golgi trafficking perturbations. In the largest Cog4 perturbed-cell block, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Cog4 produced no FDR-significant hits, whereas Vps54 produced 31 significant genes in the same cell type; across the atlas, Cog5, Stx16, and Vps53 also yielded sparse significant hits. This pattern suggests the lack of a Cog4 signal is target-specific or reflects limited engagement/biological buffering rather than a general failure to detect COG/Golgi vesicle tethering or Golgi-to-ER retrograde transport effects, although the comparators are not all in the same complex and had different cell counts.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Magel2 did not yield a robust transcriptional module matching its canonical WASH-retromer or neurosecretory biology. In 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, only nominal changes in Snx27, Rab5b, and Cpe pointed toward endosomal or secretory trafficking, and these signals were not FDR-supported, with adjusted P values ranging from 0.3667 to 1.0. The least-null context was 155 MB Glut, while 191 MB P MY GABA showed a nominal response but no FDR-supported Magel2 genes, consistent with an acute protein-trafficking mechanism being poorly captured by steady-state single-cell mRNA differential expression.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tbce converged with the related cofactor Tbcd on an inducible post-chaperonin tubulin-folding transcriptional module, most clearly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where both perturbations increased Tuba1a and overlapping positive-response genes including Tuba1b and Ypel4. Similar Tuba1a-centered responses recurred in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 155 MB Glut, with Tubb5 also part of the broader pathway context. However, whole-transcriptome Tbce–Tbcd similarity was only modest, so the convergence is strongest for the tubulin response, especially in the 151 class.

Robo4 perturbation in neuronal profiles did not mobilize the canonical Slit/Robo4 endothelial-barrier or angiogenesis program: Slit2, Slit3, and vascular or endothelial genes Cldn5, Cdh5, Pecam1, Emcn, Kdr, Tek, Flt4, and Pxn were unchanged, with FDR=1.0 in every Robo4 neuronal contrast. Consistent with this, Slit-ROBO signaling components and angiogenesis/endothelial barrier organization pathways were effectively uncoupled or near zero in these data. A key caveat is that most of these markers are endothelial or vascular, so they may be uninformative in purified neuronal transcriptomes.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Dcx perturbation did not coherently rewire the expected doublecortin/tubulin RNA program across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. In the best-engaged contrasts, Dclk1 and Dclk2 transcripts were measured but not induced, so the genetically described Dcx/Dclk compensation was not evident as simple transcriptional compensation here. The only aligned downstream signal was in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, where Dcx, Tuba1a, and Tubb3 showed a weak same-direction decrease that remained nominal, with all FDR values at 1.0.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Avpr1a showed a transcriptomic pattern that did not converge with related AVP/OXT receptor-family perturbations or the Gq effector Plcb1 in this mouse-brain screen. Across shared cell classes, Avpr1a full-transcriptome signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Avpr1b, Avpr2, Oxtr, and Plcb1, arguing against treating these perturbations as interchangeable proxies. Most comparators were weak, with Avpr1b and Avpr2 showing no FDR-significant genes in 23 and 22 contexts, and Oxtr showing only an isolated Acly increase in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. No receptor protein or ligand-response assay was measured.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Abcc9 showed no multiple-testing-corrected downstream transcriptional response across the 22 assayed neuronal classes, and the nominal high-score genes did not define a recurrent ABCC9 program. The strongest single rows—Ly6e in Sst GABA, Arid2 in L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and Rufy3 in CB GABA—failed FDR correction, while recurrent same-direction nominal hits such as Med14 and Cttn appeared in only 5 of 22 cell types. Thus these rows should be treated as isolated nominal signals rather than ABCC9 biomarkers, with nominal p<0.05 used only descriptively.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Trappc6b showed no FDR-significant transcriptional hits, and this negative result was selective rather than a general failure to detect vesicle-trafficking perturbations. In the same matrix, Vps37a, Sec31a, Vps54, and Vps35 produced corrected signatures, including in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Trappc6b, Trappc9, and Trappc10 did not. In 155 MB Glut, Trappc6b had recurrent nominal Jun/Stmn4 positivity despite strong Vps37a/Sec31a signals, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut it showed only weak nominal target reduction while Vps54/Vps35 were strongly detected, consistent with TRAPP-specific buffering or weak engagement; however, these comparators are distinct trafficking complexes and serve as assay controls rather than mechanistic phenocopies.

Prkn perturbation did not recover a canonical PINK1-PRKN mitophagy RNA module: across 20 profiled Prkn cell types, neither Prkn nor key pathway and autophagy candidates such as Pink1, Becn1, Sqstm1, Tbk1, Mapk1, Afg3l2, Uchl1, and Atp13a2 reached FDR significance, and the strongest nominal hits were mostly one-cell-type events rather than a recurrent cross-cell program. This suggests that basal single-cell differential expression is a poor standalone biomarker for PRKN pathway activity, since candidate-gene DE cannot measure Parkin recruitment, mitochondrial ubiquitination, or mitophagy flux.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Avpr1b showed no FDR-significant transcriptional effects in this neuronal assay, including in hypothalamic extended-amygdala classes such as 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, where related receptor perturbations yielded only isolated hits. Avpr2 was likewise fully null, whereas Avpr1a and Oxtr each produced a single weak FDR row, including an Avpr1a-associated Srsf6 hit, and Avpr1b score signatures had near-zero correlations with Avpr1a, Avpr2, Oxtr, Crhr1, and Cckbr. Thus, despite pathway proximity in arginine vasopressin/V1b GPCR signaling, the family appears transcriptomically weak here, and the contrast is only a family-level observation rather than mechanistic proof of receptor divergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Klhl7 did not phenocopy Cul3 in the BCR(KLHL7)/CUL3-RING ubiquitin ligase context: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Klhl7 knockdown showed nominal target depletion but no FDR-resolved transcriptomic signature, whereas Cul3 produced small FDR-significant signatures, including one resolved row in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and six FDR<0.05 rows in 155 MB Glut. The Klhl7 and Cul3 signatures in these classes were nearly uncorrelated, although the Cul3 effects were also small, Cul3 had fewer perturbed cells than Klhl7 in 155 MB Glut, and this comparison is transcriptomic rather than proteomic.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cul3 perturbation in the two responsive glutamatergic classes, 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, was associated with a small down-regulated nuclear RNA-processing and splicing module centered on Pnisr, Rsrp1, Snhg11, and Srsf5. This recurring signal was strongest in 155 MB Glut, the only context with significant Cul3 knockdown and a multi-gene FDR-resolved response, while the thalamic class showed a strong but only partly FDR-resolved pattern. The module did not resemble canonical NRF2 output, and only Srsf5, Rsrp1, and Snhg11 were significant or near-significant in both cell types, so direct CUL3 regulation remains unproven.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Pnkd showed near-zero similarity to other perturbations across four informative contexts, with score vectors nearly orthogonal to top global neighbors and to movement-disorder or synaptic comparators including Sgce, Atp1a3, Gad1, Unc13a/Unc13b/Unc13c, Slc2a1, Thap1, and Ano3. In 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Pnkd depletion was FDR-validated but largely restricted to the target transcript, with no FDR trans program and unchanged active-zone genes such as Rims1, Rims2, Snap25, and Stx1b; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut was only nominal. This negative result is tempered because one context was nominal-only and comparator selection included STRING links that are not all physical interactions.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp536 was largely uncoupled from related zinc-finger and STRING-neighbor perturbations in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Zfp423 produced a strong thalamic transcriptional program with 150 FDR-significant genes, whereas Zfp536 had none and its score vector was uncorrelated with Zfp423. Across 22 shared cell types, Zfp536 also remained near zero correlation with Nkx6-2, Sox10, and Zfp521, including in an oligodendrocyte differentiation and myelination-associated network. Because these STRING links are functional associations rather than a defined Zfp536 complex, the lack of correlation does not by itself prove biochemical independence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Rbm28 showed a weak but repeated positive signature neighborhood with Uba5, Ufc1, Rrn3, and Nop56 in glutamatergic classes, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, repeated at lower amplitude in 155 MB Glut, and weaker still in 217 P MY Pineal Glut. This was the only recurring cross-perturbation organization around Rbm28, and the presence of Rrn3 and Nop56 is directionally compatible with rRNA processing/ribosome biogenesis, although full-signature correlations were small (up to r=0.270) and Uba5/Ufc1 are not established direct RBM28 partners.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Rhot1 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut showed only a weak restricted transcriptional signature, with weak positive and negative neighbors such as Tcf12 (r=0.283) and Grin2d (r=-0.230), and similarly weak correlations or anticorrelations with Rab27a plus mitochondrial transport and quality-control/dynamics perturbations including Trak1, Kif5a, Kif5c, Prkn, Dnm1l, Opa1, and Vps35. In this cell type, Rhot1 perturbation did not significantly regulate selected pathway-neighbor transcripts, so these exploratory top-500-gene comparisons do not support a canonical Miro1/TRAK/kinesin or PINK1/Parkin pathway-level signature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ddx3x in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was not interchangeable with major Wnt or eIF4F pathway neighbors: it partially overlapped Ctnnb1 on selected downregulated genes, but the whole-signature correlation with Ctnnb1 was weak, and alignment with Eif4e, Eif4a2, and Eif4g1 was even weaker. Consistent with this, Ddx3x did not significantly change canonical β-catenin readouts such as Axin2, Lef1, or Tcf7l2, and no perturbation produced a close full-transcriptome phenocopy or inverse phenocopy. These comparisons are based on transcriptomic score correlations, so DDX3X-dependent translational targets could change without matching mRNA abundance shifts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Tuba1a depletion elicited a tubulin-isotype compensation program in only two neuronal classes, most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Tuba1a decreased while Tubb3, Tubb2a, Tuba4a, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, and Tubb5 increased; 052 Pvalb Gaba showed the same direction but with a smaller significant module, including Tubb2a, Tuba4a, and Tubb3. This pattern is consistent with alpha/beta tubulin heterodimer stoichiometry and autoregulation, appears one-way relative to related tubulin perturbations, and is based on mRNA ranks rather than tubulin protein or polymer measurements.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa
full_finding_text: Oxtr was not transcriptomically interchangeable with its vasopressin-receptor paralogs Avpr1a, Avpr1b, and Avpr2 across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 215 MB Dopa. The only FDR<0.05 Oxtr response was in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, while Avpr1a showed a single FDR<0.10 hit in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and Avpr1b/Avpr2 had none; AVPR signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Oxtr in Oxtr-responsive classes. Because most family-member signatures were weak, this supports non-convergence rather than proof of distinct physiology.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Pde1c showed a restricted, weak convergence with the cyclic-nucleotide phosphodiesterase family in 308 CB GABA and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, where its score vectors correlated modestly with Pde10a more than with other assayed PDEs such as Pde4b or Pde4d. This pattern was most concentrated in the cerebellar GABA class and suggests a possible hindbrain/cerebellar follow-up module rather than a pan-neuronal signature, but the correlations were based on uncorrected score vectors and Pde1c had no FDR-significant genes in either cell type.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Uba5 perturbation, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons, was associated with broad up-regulation of a mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation module, including genes such as Ndufa2, Atp5j2, and Cox5a, whereas direct knockdown of the complex III subunits Uqcrc1 or Uqcrc2 strongly depleted their own transcripts but produced nearly self-only signatures and correlated weakly with the Uba5 state. Thus, the OXPHOS-up program appears uncoupled from generic respiratory-chain mRNA loss, although only complex III subunits were tested and scRNA-seq buffering does not exclude metabolic phenotypes.

Dnajc19 showed low signature correlation with the available mitochondrial import, chaperone, and metabolic perturbations: gene-score correlations with Hspa9, Hspd1, Tomm40, Ndufa13, Ndufs8, Got2, Lrpprc, Aco2, and Abcb7 were all near zero. This lack of convergence was also noted in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA for the mitochondrial protein import/TIM23-PAM context, where no robust Dnajc19 response was seen. Interpretation is limited because many direct TIM23-PAM partners were absent, Dnajc19 itself was weakly engaged, and Hspa9 was not cleanly mRNA-depleted.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Glce showed weak target engagement: its transcript was not significantly decreased in any measured Glce perturbation profile, and in 155 MB Glut the clearest contrast was that related HS/HSPG-neighbor perturbations Hs6st2, Ext2, and Agrn each showed strong self-transcript depletion while Glce did not. This argues against a generic inability to detect HS-related target rows in this dataset and instead suggests a weak Glce guide/readout. The negative result should therefore be read as no observed transcriptional effect under this assay, not proof that GLCE protein or HS structure is dispensable; moreover, self-transcript depletion is only an RNA proxy, and key HS genes such as HS2ST1, HS6ST1, and NDST family members were not targeted.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Hnf4g showed weak or absent convergence in the sampled mouse-brain Perturb-seq classes, with signatures essentially uncorrelated with Hnf4a and with HNF-network perturbations Hnf1a, Hnf1b, and Foxa2, despite prior gut and beta-cell relationships. In 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, the strongest nominal Hnf4g contrast still had only weak whole-signature neighbors, and in 001 L5-6 IT Glut there were just 32 perturbed cells and no FDR-significant gene; 308 CB GABA also did not reveal convergence. Most compared signatures were weak, so correlation-based comparisons cannot exclude pathway membership in cells that express HNF4G.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Baiap2 showed an uncoupled or only weakly correlated relationship to the ADGRB1/RAC1/CDC42 actin-adaptor branch in cortical glutamatergic cells, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut. In these groups, Adgrb1, Rac1, and Srgap3 signatures were near-zero or negative relative to Baiap2, while Cdc42 was only weakly positive, arguing that the Baiap2 state was not simply recapitulated by perturbing a physical actin interactor. This interpretation is tempered because several canonical actin effectors or Baiap2 paralogs, including Wasf1, Wasf2, Eps8, Abi1, and Abi2, were not assayed, and the comparator guides themselves showed weak on-target transcript depletion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lrp5 did not phenocopy the Lrp6/Ctnnb1-aligned canonical WNT/beta-catenin response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. In this cell type, Lrp6 produced a small signature with reduced Atrnl1, Nsmf, and Nrbp2 and a nominal decrease in Axin2, while Ctnnb1 drove a much stronger program including Lef1, Axin2, Nsmf, Nrbp2, and Atrnl1. Despite having more matched perturbed cells in the same group, Lrp5 left these loci unchanged, preserving an informative divergence between LRP5 and LRP6; notably, the Lrp6 signature was weaker than Ctnnb1, and Lrp6 itself was not significantly depleted.

Igf1r perturbation did not recover a conserved IGF1R pathway module in these data. Using only the 30 strongest nominal Igf1r genes per cell type, because no FDR-significant Igf1r signature was available, restricted correlations with Insr, Igf2r, Irs1, Pik3ca, Mtor, Pten, Tsc1, Tsc2, and Mapk1 were near zero on average. Nominal Igf1r hits were also poorly recurrent across cell types, so the expected IRS–PI3K–AKT and SHC–RAS–MAPK neighborhood was not stably observed.

Dzip1 showed no detectable convergence with available Hedgehog or ciliogenesis perturbations in this assay: whole-signature correlations with Gli1, Smo, Ptch1/Ptch2, Ift88, Ttc8, Bbs5, Cdon, and Cep290 were all near zero, and even the top positive or negative neighbors had absolute correlations below 0.03. This argues that nominal Dzip1 hits do not recover a cilium/Hedgehog transcriptomic module here, although the inference is limited because related ciliary perturbations were sparse and Dzip1 engagement itself may have been weak. Exploratory Dzip1l upregulation appeared in 046 CTX-CGE GABA and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, but no FDR-supported module was detected.

Prkca was largely uncoupled from related DAG/Ca2+-dependent PKC signaling signatures: despite pathway proximity to Prkcg, Plcb1, Dgke, Dgkd, Grm1, Grm5, and Camk2 genes, it produced no corrected transcriptional hits, and restricted within-cell-type correlations to 22 selected neighbors stayed near zero, roughly -0.088 to 0.097. This divergence persisted even where related perturbations were productive, including 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, although the Prkca signature was weak and the correlation analysis covered a selected related-target panel rather than all perturbations.

Hmgb1 perturbation in neurons did not engage canonical extracellular HMGB1–TLR/RAGE innate inflammatory signaling. Across neuronal classes, Ager, Tlr2, Tlr4, Cd14, Tnf, Il1b, Il6, Ccl2, and Ccl3 did not approach nominal or FDR significance, and the Hmgb1 transcriptional signature was not similar to perturbations of assayed HMGB1 receptors or downstream pathway neighbors. This negative result is specific to cell-autonomous neuronal Hmgb1 transcript perturbation and does not test extracellular, oxidized, or vesicular HMGB1 acting on astrocytes, microglia, or macrophages.

Ttc8 perturbation did not produce a broad transcriptional Hedgehog or BBSome response in this neuronal dataset. Canonical Smoothened-Gli-Ptch readouts, including Smo, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, and Ptch2, were not significantly shifted, and measured BBSome-subunit transcripts such as Bbip1, Bbs5, and Bbs9 also lacked a consistent compensatory or co-depletion pattern. The clearest target-engagement signal was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where the only FDR-positive contrast was Ttc8 itself, while cross-perturbation neighbors were weak. Low expression of some Hedgehog genes and the lack of protein-trafficking readouts limit how fully pathway activity can be excluded.

Ptch1 perturbation did not produce a measurable canonical Hedgehog/GLI transcriptional response. Across all Ptch1 strata, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch2, Smo, Gpr161, Cdon, Adcy3, and Sufu remained non-significant, and the nominal p<0.01 genes were mostly non-recurrent rather than a shared multi-cell-type module. This argues against interpreting the ranked genes as SMO–GLI output, although Hedgehog activity could still shift through protein localization or ciliary trafficking without detectable changes in these pathway transcripts.

Gli3 showed near-zero same-cell-type correlations with related Hedgehog/GLI perturbations, including Gli1, Gli2, Glis2, Glis3, Smo, Ptch1, Ptch2, Cdon, and Gpr161, with average Pearson correlations only about -0.0015 to 0.0181 and a full related-target range of -0.0506 to 0.1003. In these assayed neuronal populations, even within the same cell classes, those perturbations did not recreate the weak Gli3 score vector, arguing against a shared linear Hedgehog module here. This comparison is limited because most comparator perturbations were also weak by FDR; in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, Gli3 had the smallest nominal p value, but no result passed FDR.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nsmf in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not phenocopy core NMDA-receptor or synaptic-neighbor perturbations despite this being the cell type with the best Nsmf engagement. In this thalamic glutamatergic class, Grin1 produced a broad FDR-supported response, with 89 significant genes, whereas Nsmf produced no secondary FDR-supported genes, and its score vector was essentially uncorrelated with Grin1, Grin2b, Grin2a, Grin2d, Syn1, Camk2b, and Dlg4. These basal signatures therefore suggest weak coupling of Nsmf to postsynapse-to-nucleus NMDA/CREB signaling under steady-state conditions, with the caveat that NSMF/Jacob may act mainly after patterned synaptic or extrasynaptic NMDA stimulation.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pak3 showed no transcriptome-level convergence with the canonical RAC1/CDC42-activated group-I PAK module: in 155 MB Glut, 308 CB GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Pak3 signatures had near-zero correlation with Pak1, Pak2, Rac1, Cdc42, Limk1, Map2k1, and Mapk1 perturbations, and canonical RAC/CDC42-PAK pathway transcripts were not reproducibly changed. The Pak3 signal was weak—midbrain glutamatergic cells had nominal self-depletion that did not survive FDR, cerebellar GABA cells showed only Ccm2 up near FDR, and stronger knockdown or phosphoproteomics might reveal coupling missed by steady-state mRNA.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Bmpr2 perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed Bmpr2 self-depletion but did not produce an FDR-significant transcriptional response in the BMPRII-LIMK/Rho dendrite remodeling branch: Limk1, Limk2, Cdc42, Pak1, Pak2, Rhoa, Rac1, Cfl1, and Cfl2 were not significant. This does not recapitulate prior neuronal BMPRII dendritogenesis findings at the RNA level and suggests that any BMPRII-LIMK/Rho effect here may be post-translational, morphological, ligand/activity-dependent, or developmentally restricted rather than detectable in this steady-state scRNA-seq assay.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Max perturbation was associated with induction of the circadian repressors Per2 and Cry1 across four responsive neuronal subclasses—066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—forming a recurrent clock-related module in the direction up in Max-perturbed cells. This pattern is consistent with a circadian E-box transcriptional repression program and aligns with Mnt as a comparator, suggesting release of a clock-repressor circuit rather than only generic growth genes, although the supporting mechanism was defined mainly in human cell lines and this mouse brain dataset lacks time-series sampling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfx in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a distinct neuronal signature, with a 15-gene FDR pattern dominated by downregulated Inha, Arhgef25, Zmynd11, Prrg3, Begain, Npr2, Pcca, and Ssh3, that did not phenocopy the expected ZFX/Myc-E2f self-renewal network. Across all genes, correlations between Zfx and Myc, Mycn, E2f1, E2f4, Esrrb, or Sox2 were near zero, and no perturbation among 2,045 comparators exceeded |r|=0.102. These comparisons used Wilcoxon score vectors rather than raw single-cell expression, and direct Zfy/Zfp711-family paralog comparisons were unavailable.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Ankrd12 showed a buffered, paralog-specific brain transcriptional phenotype rather than an interchangeable ANCO-family cofactor pattern with Ankrd11. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the clearest FDR-corrected effect of Ankrd12 was self-knockdown, while Ankrd11 in the same class produced strong neuronal receptor and excitability responses, including genes such as Grin2b, Grm1, and Gabbr2. Across matched high-information cell types, including 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Ankrd12–Ankrd11 signature correlations were near zero; Ankrd11 yielded FDR-level Atp1a3, Kcnc1, and Snap25-related responses, whereas Ankrd12 had only one non-target FDR gene, U2surp, in 155 MB Glut. This supports shared ANCO-family co-regulator logic but not identical adult neuronal activity for ANKRD12 and ANKRD11.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Sec63 perturbation most consistently elicited an ER chaperone and UPR-like compensation program, with mostly increased Hspa5, Hyou1, Canx, Chac1, Pdia4, Hsp90b1 and related ER quality-control genes such as Herpud1, Sel1l, Sdf2l1, Pdia6, Rpn1, Ddost, Stt3b, Dnajb9, and Ssr1. The strongest support was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Hspa5, Canx, Hyou1, and Chac1 were FDR-significant and Pdia4/Hsp90b1 were nominally positive; 155 MB Glut showed Hspa5-only FDR support, while other listed cell types showed mostly nominal recurrence.

Mnx1 did not phenocopy its embryonic motor-neuron network neighbors in this brain-wide perturbation panel. Although Mnx1 is linked to Isl1, Lhx3, Foxa2, Neurog3, and Neurod1 in embryonic spinal motor-neuron specification and V2-interneuron repression, the sampled brain classes did not recapitulate that module: Lhx3, Isl1, Foxa2, and Neurod1 showed no FDR-significant genes, Neurog3 had only one, and correlations with the Mnx1 signature for represented direct partners never exceeded |r|=0.105. This negative result should be read with the caveat that STRING edges are functional associations, not proof of a stoichiometric complex, and the dataset lacks embryonic spinal motor neurons.

Nfx1 perturbation in basal mouse neuronal cells did not reproduce canonical NFX1 immune or telomerase outputs: across all 18 Nfx1-tested cell types, there was no FDR-supported derepression of the MHC class II X-box/antigen-presentation module genes H2-Aa, H2-Ab1, H2-Eb1, Cd74, and Ciita, and no FDR-supported response of the TERT/poly(A)-binding protein axis genes Tert, Pabpc1, and Pabpc4. This is a context-specific negative result, as these transcripts may be lowly expressed in neurons, and it refines prior immune or HPV-epithelial findings to more permissive settings rather than basal mouse neurons.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Tbx6 perturbation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA cells did not reconstitute the canonical WNT/NOTCH/MESP2 somitogenesis program: Dll1, Mesp2, Hes7, Notch1, Tcf7l2, and Sox2 were not FDR-supported responses, and genome-wide score comparisons found no meaningful Tbx6-aligned signature among perturbations of Mesp2, Dll1, Notch1, Tcf7l2, or related Tbx factors. Thus, the weak CTX-CGE signal appears uncoupled from the known paraxial-mesoderm network, though this contrast is tempered by the embryonic mesoderm literature and the brain GABA context with weak target engagement.
