cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Oprm1 perturbation was transcriptionally silent in this screen, and the broader opioid receptor family behaved similarly: Oprd1, Oprk1, and Oprl1 showed no FDR-significant hits across 22–23 cell types, with pathway-neighbor correlations near zero in μ-opioid Gi/Go GPCR signaling. In contrast, the shared Gi/Go components Gnao1 and Gnb1 produced sparse FDR-supported effects, including on-target depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, and Gnb1 also in 191 MB P MY GABA. These sparse core-pathway effects do not show that opioid receptors drive the same transcriptional changes in those cells.

Frrs1l depletion showed no simple transcriptional compensation within the FRRS1L-CPT1C ER AMPAR biogenesis pathway: across assayed cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Cpt1c, Gria1-Gria4, Cacng2/Cacng3/Cacng8, and Dlg4 mRNAs did not change at FDR-significant levels, and no secondary gene-level response survived correction. This suggests buffered downstream mRNA rather than receptor-subunit transcript rescue, while leaving open post-transcriptional effects on AMPAR processing, surface delivery, or synaptic abundance.

Ahrr perturbation showed no detectable derepression of the measured AHR/xenobiotic-response program in this basal mouse brain screen: Cyp1a1, Cyp1b1, Nqo1, Tiparp, and Aldh3a1 remained flat, and no FDR-significant AHR signaling axis response was seen. Ahrr RNA itself was also not significantly changed in any tested cell type where it was measured, which, together with reportedly low Ahrr expression in mouse brain and the lack of added AHR ligands, suggests low target engagement is a more parsimonious explanation than a strongly buffered knockout phenotype.

Epm2a perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from the expected laforin glycogen phosphatase/Lafora disease pathway: no multiple-testing-corrected downstream hit or recurrent nominal hit was detected, and measured neighbor transcripts including Nhlrc1, Ppp1r3c, Gys1, Gys2, Agl, Stbd1, Pygb, Gsk3b, and Epm2aip1 all remained nonsignificant. This suggests that, despite curated biochemical links between EPM2A, glycogen dephosphorylation, and NHLRC1/malin biology, the perturbation did not evoke a detectable mRNA glycogen or stress-response module, with the caveat that much of the known mechanism is post-translational/metabolic and several neighbors were assayed only as response genes, not as perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Trim2 perturbation in the responsive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class did not transcriptionally induce the canonical neurofilament axis: Nefl, Nefm, and Nefh mRNAs were unchanged, while App and Cntn1 were the main down-regulated genes. This suggests the TRIM2-NEFL ubiquitin proteostasis pathway is uncoupled at the mRNA-signature level in this cell type. Notably, Nefl knockdown and perturbation of the strongest Trim2 output genes did not phenocopy the Trim2 program, and NEFL protein accumulation was not measured, so the result is more consistent with mRNA/protein uncoupling than a contradiction of prior disease mechanisms.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Esrrg did not recover the expected ERRγ oxidative-metabolism module in 155 MB Glut or 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: canonical mitochondrial and energy-metabolism genes such as Atp5b, Cyc1, Ndufb10, Ndufa8, Mdh1, Got1, and Mpc1 were not significant Esrrg responses, even though related Esrra or Ppargc1b perturbations detected mitochondrial genes in the same screen. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Esrra but not Esrrg recovered mitochondrial genes, and in 155 MB Glut the strongest Esrrg nominal signal was not transcriptome-wide significant, so this apparent pathway uncoupling may reflect weak Esrrg engagement rather than true independence.

Il31ra showed no hidden IL-6-family receptor program when compared with nearby receptor perturbations: Osmr, its direct IL-31RA co-receptor, as well as Il6ra and Il6st, did not phenocopy the Il31ra transcriptomic signature. Osmr had no genes passing FDR < 0.05, and same-cell-type score vectors were only weakly correlated with Il31ra. This supports a cell-context-specific absence of an engaged IL-31 receptor/OSMR branch rather than a missed single-gene readout, although the comparator perturbations were themselves weak, so the contrast is informative mainly as a lack of phenocopy rather than a directional mechanistic split.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp423 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a large bidirectional thalamic expression signature concentrated on synaptic and membrane-excitability genes rather than a generic stress response. The strongest changes included increased Ntsr1, Kcnab3, and Nptxr with decreased Grid2ip, Cd47, and Grin2c, alongside broader remodeling of Grik3, Kcnq3, and Cacng7. The affected gene set was overrepresented for synapse, postsynapse, membrane-potential, and ion-transport annotations, although this post hoc enrichment does not by itself establish direct regulation by Zfp423.

Gp1ba showed no significant neural response in this assay, and several functionally adjacent hemostatic or hematopoietic perturbations behaved similarly: Gata1, Itga2, Itga2b, Itgb1, Klf1, Meis1, Mpl, and Thbd each remained FDR-silent across the brain cell types tested. This pattern is consistent with the GPIb-IX-V/VWF platelet adhesion and broader megakaryocyte or platelet biogenesis programs being buffered or not engaged in a neural context, rather than indicating a Gp1ba-specific anomaly. However, direct within-complex comparison was not possible because Gp1bb, Gp9, Gp5, and Vwf were not available as perturbation comparators.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sgce did not phenocopy the measured dystrophin-glycoprotein/sarcoglycan complex perturbations Sgcd, Dag1, or Dmd: in the two strongest Sgce cell types, 191 MB P MY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, same-cell-type score-vector correlations with these comparators were near zero. This argues against simple interchangeability of Sgce with other complex members at the acute transcriptomic level, although the interpretation is tempered because Sgcd and Dmd were weakly engaged or sparsely measured, so the lack of convergence could partly reflect comparator perturbation quality rather than biology alone.

Tbx4 showed no convergence with other T-box perturbations in this neuronal assay: same-cell signed Wilcoxon-score correlations with Tbx5, Tbx3, Tbx2, and Tbr1 were all small, with maximum absolute r values of 0.099, 0.086, 0.045, and 0.065. This argues against Tbx4 exposing a generic T-box transcriptional module here, especially because Tbr1 was active in the same dataset, with corrected effects in deep cortical excitatory classes such as L5-6 IT Glut. Interpretation remains limited because correlations were computed only within this dataset and Tbx4 engagement itself appeared weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Prkn was largely inert in this assay: across overlapping TH/MB-related classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, it showed no FDR-significant signal, and its signatures were essentially uncorrelated with related mitochondrial-autophagy perturbations (median |Spearman ρ| = 0.016; only 1/279 comparisons with |ρ| > 0.1). In contrast, Uchl1, Atp13a2, Dnm1l, Sqstm1, Vps35, and Park7 produced detectable target engagement or downstream differential expression in the same framework, although comparator guide counts and knockdown strengths differed, and some comparator signals reflected on-target transcript loss rather than broader programs.

Tecr showed no robust recurrent transcriptomic neighbor in the available perturbation panel: after excluding Tecr itself, the strongest Tecr-versus-other perturbation correlation in any assayed cell type was weak (|r|=0.193), and no target appeared among the top positive or negative 10 neighbors in more than 3 of 22 Tecr-assayed cell types. Weak, nonrecurrent similarities were seen with broader lipid-regulatory genes Hmgcr, Mecr, Srebf1, and Srebf2, but direct very-long-chain fatty-acyl-CoA synthesis and fatty acid elongation comparators such as ELOVL, HACD, PECR, and TECRL were not perturbed, limiting interpretation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Slc17a5 perturbation produced its strongest glutamatergic signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where lysosomal export/acidification transcripts increased rather than showing only Slc17a5 suppression. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Lamp2, Dpp7, Grn, and Neu1 were up, and in 155 MB Glut, Lamp2 and the V-ATPase gene Atp6v0b increased; the midbrain class also showed sterol induction with Snap25 and Eef1a2 decreases. This pattern is consistent with an adaptive lysosomal membrane flux response, although no lysosomal pH, sialic-acid storage, or protein-level measurements were available.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Reep1 showed weak or nonconvergent Perturb-seq signatures relative to related HSP/ER-shaping genes, with no reproducible transcriptional convergence with Reep2, Atl1, Spast, Arl6ip1, Kif1a, Tmem106b, or Vcp across shared cell types. In the tubular ER shaping/HSP structural module, Reep1, Reep2, Atl1, and Spast also lacked corrected non-self DEGs in this comparison, even though other neurodegeneration-associated perturbations in the same subset did yield downstream DEGs. The lone high Reep1–Reep2 match occurred in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, where both targets were only weakly depleted, so that apparent convergence is exploratory and limited by the restricted-signature analysis.

Ptpro perturbation did not transcriptionally phenocopy obvious pathway neighbors or receptor-type PTP relatives in matched cell classes: score correlations with Epha4, Epha5, Epha6, Plxna4, Ntrk3, Ptprd, Ptprf, and even robustly engaged Ptprn2 were near zero on average. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Ptpro showed only a limited response, with Grik5 as the sole FDR-significant downstream gene and an exploratory nominal Eph/Src/FAK-associated module, but restricted signature neighbors were modest and non-specific. These contrasts are tempered by weak Ptpro response amplitudes and mixed target engagement among several comparators.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnb1 perturbation produced its only FDR-significant transcriptomic response in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons, where a five-gene program was entirely upregulated and centered on an activity-dependent neurotrophin/secretory plasticity module rather than a broad stress or cell-death state. In this class, Bdnf, Vgf, Scg2, and Nptx2, along with Zbtb16, were induced; the Bdnf/Vgf/Nptx2/Scg2 axis also recurred nominally in additional cortical glutamatergic classes, but FDR support was confined to 005. These data are transcriptomic only and did not directly measure firing, Kv2.1 gating, or BDNF secretion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rbfox1 perturbation showed its strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where a mostly down-regulated synaptic membrane and axon excitability module was observed, including Adgrb1, Grin1, Vamp1, Scn1a, Scn1b, Kcnc3, Cntnap1, and related neuronal membrane genes such as Nptn, Sptan1, Slc6a7, and Prkcg. The abundance signature was dominated by reduced neuronal membrane, ion-channel, vesicle, and adhesion transcripts, with synaptic membrane emerging as the top grouped term among 28 significant genes. This pattern is consistent with RBFOX1 involvement in synaptic signaling and excitability programs, although the present assay measures abundance rather than the splicing or 3′ UTR regulation emphasized in prior mouse studies.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Sec31a showed a distinct, stronger transcriptional phenotype than assayed COPII and early secretory neighbors in two dominant contexts, 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. In 155 MB Glut, Sec31a perturbation produced 60 FDR genes with repression of Atp1a3, Atp1b1, Stmn3, Sparcl1, Nefl, and Vamp1 and induction of early secretory/ER-to-Golgi genes including Sec23a, Copa, Copb1, Srpr, and Golgb1, whereas Sec23a perturbation reduced Sec23a mRNA but was transcriptionally buffered, and Sec23a, Sar1b, Copa, Stx5a, and Ssr4 signatures were weak or uncorrelated with Sec31a in both cell types. This divergence is limited to assayed targets and could reflect paralog compensation or protein stability after guide targeting.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp106 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a transcriptional response that was distinct from acute perturbations of RNA-binding/ALS-neighbor genes Tardbp, Fus, Srsf1, and Matr3. Although these comparator perturbations were strongly active in the same thalamic class, with 130–2765 FDR-significant genes, their whole-transcriptome signed DE score correlations with Zfp106 were near zero, and a target-wide scan found no high-correlation positive or negative neighbor for Zfp106. This suggests acute Zfp106 knockdown did not phenocopy TDP-43/FUS-like states here, with the caveat that comparator perturbations had more cells and the analysis reflects transcriptome correlations rather than protein interaction assays.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|053 Sst Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Psmb4 perturbation in multiple neuronal classes, including 155 MB Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, repeatedly upregulated a proteasome-compensation program with Psme4, Psmc6, Psmd4, Psmc4, Psmd11, and Psmb2, with related induction of Pomp, Psmc1, and Psmc5 in several responsive populations. The strongest responses paired this module with stress-associated transcripts and loss of neuronal or synaptic markers, such as Slc17a6 downregulation in glutamatergic cells. Because the dataset measures mRNA only, it does not establish restoration of 26S proteasome abundance or proteolytic activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tnik was uncoupled from canonical Wnt/β-catenin behavior in this mouse brain Perturb-seq screen. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Apc, Ctnnb1, and Tcf7l2 produced clear FDR-significant signatures, whereas Tnik, sampled with 179 perturbed cells, produced no FDR-significant genes and showed near-zero full-signature correlations with those perturbations. Thus, the lack of Tnik response was not a general failure of Wnt-pathway perturbations here, although the comparison maps Wnt/TCF4 nomenclature to mouse Tcf7l2 and uses pooled whole-cell RNA rather than TCF/β-catenin chromatin output.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nr5a2 showed a weak, largely uncoupled brain perturbation signature relative to Wnt/beta-catenin neighbors. In the clearest case, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Ctnnb1, Apc, Tcf7l2, and Rora generated strong signatures with 106–383 FDR-significant rows, whereas Nr5a2 produced none and had near-zero correlations to those perturbations. Preselected paralog, Wnt-neighbor, RXR, and PPAR nuclear-receptor signatures also did not converge with Nr5a2, so despite known LRH-1/beta-catenin binding in other systems, these data are best read as context-dependent absence of an endogenous LRH-1/Wnt module in these brain cells.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Kmt2b perturbation was associated with a recurrent downregulated marker panel across several neuron classes, most consistently Stxbp2 and Csf2ra, with additional partial support from Rasgrp2, Ebf4, Fah, Col11a1, and Agbl4. The signal appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, among others; Stxbp2 showed broad nominal recurrence, while Csf2ra was the most FDR-recurrent gene. This module is best treated as a transcriptomic biomarker set rather than a proven direct KMT2B program, because recurrence was partly nominal outside the leading cell types and no curated pathway was evident.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Atp6v1b2 in 052 Pvalb Gaba neurons showed only weak convergence with the V-ATPase subunit Atp6v0c: among 2,040 perturbations, Atp6v0c was the closest score-vector neighbor but with a modest Pearson r of 0.305, while Atp6v1e1 and Atp6v1a were also only weakly positive and the strongest anticorrelation, Pitx3, was negligible. Although Atp6v1b2 and Atp6v0c were both depleted in cis, Atp6v0c produced a much larger Pvalb signature than Atp6v1b2, with 158 versus 9 FDR genes, suggesting related V-ATPase members were not transcriptional phenocopies in this cell class. This comparison comes from one responsive cell class, and Atp6v1b2 had fewer perturbed cells, so whole-transcriptome correlations may be diluted by many nonresponsive genes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gnb1 showed a buffered, divergent mRNA phenotype in 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: although Gnb1 itself was strongly depleted, its score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Gnao1, Gnb5, and Gnas, and no strong positive or inverse neighbor emerged in a cell-type-matched scan of the full perturbation library. This suggests that available heterotrimeric GPCR/G-protein beta-gamma signaling perturbations did not phenocopy Gnb1, with the caveat that comparisons were limited to mRNA correlations, Gnas target engagement was weak, and direct GNB1 gamma partners were not perturbed.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Hnf1a showed a concordant null or very sparse transcriptional response across 23 brain cell classes, including multiple glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, pineal, and cerebellar populations. Its paralog Hnf1b was similarly buffered across the same panel, with no FDR<0.05 genes detected, and related HNF/pancreatic transcription-factor perturbations such as Foxa2, Hnf4g, Nr5a2, Hnf4a, Gata6, and Mafa did not define a recurrent brain module. This pattern favors an off-context interpretation for HNF1-family factors in this brain atlas, although the comparator survey relied on DE tables and did not verify guide editing strength for every comparator.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ddx3x knockdown in the strongest neuronal signatures, specifically 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, did not detectably induce a type-I-interferon/TBK1 antiviral program. In these cells, transcripts such as Ifit1, Ifit2, Ifit3, Isg15, Stat1, Stat2, Irf7, Irf9, Mavs, Tbk1, and Ikbke lacked strong differential expression, despite DDX3X being linked to TBK1/IKKε-to-IRF3 antiviral signaling and relevant comparators including Tbk1, Ifnar1, Ifnar2, and Irf3. Because the dataset was basal rather than viral or pattern-recognition-receptor stimulated, this absence does not argue against inducible DDX3X antiviral functions.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Dhx9 in neurons did not phenocopy Dicer1, Ago1, Ago2, Adar, or Adarb1 perturbations in the main responsive cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, even though DHX9 has reported links to RISC loading and ADAR-related dsRNA resolution. Instead, the Dhx9 signature was closer to nuclear RNP, spliceosome, and nuclear-transport perturbations such as Tpr, Tnpo3, Srsf1, Ddx23, Prpf6, U2af2, and Xpo1. This negative comparison is suggestive rather than definitive because Dicer1, Ago1, and Ago2 showed weak target-transcript engagement in this dataset.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grm3 showed no target-transcript depletion in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, despite 139 perturbed cells and a near-null effect on Grm3 mRNA, whereas Grm1 and Grm7 were robustly depleted in the same cell type. Across matched cell types, Grm3 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with other metabotropic glutamate receptor perturbations, including Grm1, Grm5, Grm7, and Grm8. This suggests a target-specific null within this thalamic glutamatergic class rather than a general failure of the cell-type contrast, with the caveat that the comparison is based on mRNA signatures, not receptor activity, and that these genes are paralogous GPCRs rather than identical pathway nodes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Selenoi perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons produced a robust SREBP/cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptional response rather than simple induction of the CDP-ethanolamine enzyme set: Insig1, Msmo1, and Fdft1 increased strongly, with nominal increases in Hmgcr, Mvd, and Srebf2, and related sterol genes such as Hmgcs1 and Cyp51 tracking the same pathway. The same sterol-gene direction was seen more weakly in 155 MB Glut cells. In this dataset, the program was stronger after Pcyt2 perturbation and reversed after Srebf2 perturbation, but measurements were limited to mRNA, not lipid levels or SREBP2 activation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Dscam knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons produced a best-engaged signature that did not converge genome-wide with Dcc, Unc5c, Pak1, Ncam1, Robo1, or Cntnap2 perturbations, even though several of those comparators showed strong self-knockdown. Thus, within this thalamic cell class, the Dscam state appeared transcriptionally uncoupled from NTN1-DCC-UNC5C axon-guidance and related adhesion-receptor perturbations. This inference is limited to steady-state mRNA signatures after guide perturbation in one neuronal class, and Dcc itself was not strongly self-depleted in 151.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Esrra perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced the only FDR-significant on-target Esrra depletion and was accompanied by down-regulation of an ERRα-linked mitochondrial energy-metabolism module, including Mdh1, Got1, Mpc1, Dlat, Idh3b, Aco1, and Ndufs2. The affected program spans central carbon metabolism, pyruvate/TCA, and OXPHOS-linked genes, consistent with a neuronal PGC-1α/ERRα metabolic axis, although the corrected signal is a compact metabolic subset rather than a wholesale electron-transport-chain collapse.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sry did not phenocopy the small Sox2 and Sox5 transcriptomic signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: despite 227 perturbed cells, Sry produced no genes at FDR < 0.05 and did not reproduce the Tnnt1, Stam, or Dgkh changes, whereas Sox2 and Sox5 each showed two FDR-significant genes in the same cell class. This suggests the Sry null is not simply a universal failure of Sox-family perturbations in that cell type, although the comparator signatures were small and the contrast is transcriptomic rather than a direct measure of protein depletion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zbtb11 showed a distinct perturbation program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than a generic response shared by other assayed ZBTB factors. In this cell type, Zbtb7a produced 841 FDR hits but was essentially uncorrelated with the 48 Zbtb11 hits (correlation −0.04), while Zbtb18 and Zbtb38 had only weak similarity, indicating divergent rather than interchangeable effects. A key caveat is that Gabpa, Gabpb1, Gabpb2, and Zfp131 were not included in the panel, so the most mechanistically relevant related-target comparisons could not be tested.

Casr was transcriptionally uncoupled from represented family-C GPCR and calcium-signaling perturbations in this Perturb-seq dataset. Although related targets such as Gabbr2, Calm1, Gnao1, Grm1, Pde1c, Pth1r, and Gabbr1 showed stronger signatures elsewhere in the same table, full-vector comparisons between Casr and 26 curated CaSR-proximal perturbations remained small, with correlations from -0.198 to 0.233. A restricted top-100 analysis briefly suggested an inverse Casr-Grm1 relationship in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and 155 MB Glut cells, but transcriptome-wide correlations there were only -0.046 and -0.017, so Casr loss remains unresolved rather than clearly phenocopying nearby GPCR/calcium targets.

Nfs1 showed no meaningful positive or negative convergence with assayed Fe-S pathway or global transcriptomic neighbors in this dataset. Across comparisons with Lyrm4, Hspa9, Isca2, Abcb7, Aco2, Ireb2, Clpp, Clpx, and Tfrc, correlations were negligible (median |r| 0.0188, max |r| 0.117), and even in the best-engaged cell type, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the top genome-wide neighbors were tiny (Aff2 r=0.054, Phactr2 r=-0.058). Lyrm4 itself was weakly perturbed, so the absent Nfs1-Lyrm4 relationship likely reflects limited RNA-signature engagement rather than a definitive lack of underlying biochemistry.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tgif1 showed weak engagement in this dataset and was not phenocopied by related SMAD-corepressor perturbations. In 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Ski produced a cell-restricted signature with 14 FDR-significant genes, whereas Tgif1 had none and the shared-signature correlation was weak and negative (r = -0.079); in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ctbp1 had five FDR-significant genes while the Tgif1-Ctbp1 correlation was near zero (r = 0.026). Thus, within TGFβ/SMAD2-SMAD3-SMAD4 transcriptional regulation, Ski and Ctbp1 showed stronger, cell-type-specific outputs than Tgif1, with the caveat that Ski and CtBP1 also have TGIF-independent roles and the comparison is expression-signature based.

Dnajb4 showed no FDR-significant transcriptomic signal in this dataset, and Dnajb6 behaved similarly, whereas related chaperone perturbations produced stronger but still restricted readouts: Hsp90ab1 and Stub1 mainly showed strong on-target self-transcript depletion, and Hsf1 or Hspa8 altered limited chaperone-module genes without adjusted Dnajb4 regulation. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Dnajb4 had one of the larger perturbed-cell counts and a target decrease, yet still did not enter the adjusted Hsf1/Hspa8-responsive modules, cautioning against treating linked chaperone genes as interchangeable.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Mapt knockdown was robustly engaged in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Mapt was the top FDR hit yet showed no downstream FDR response, but its transcriptional profile did not resemble Gsk3b perturbation. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Gsk3b produced a small six-gene FDR signature involving Nrbp2, Rock2, Bhlhe40, Cck, and Rsrp1, while the whole-signature correlation with Mapt was near zero (r=0.023; also 0.015 in 155 MB Glut), indicating an uncoupled GSK3B–tau phosphorylation axis at the RNA level; tau phosphorylation itself was not measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Setd1a perturbation produced a recurrent predominantly down-regulated organelle and mitochondrial module across responsive classes, including 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, several GABAergic classes, and a low-cell-count pineal glutamatergic class. Recurrent decreases included Fbxw5, Itfg1, Coq2, Letm2, Pigq, Ufl1, Nprl3, Rmnd1, and Ttc8, with 155 MB Glut also showing enrichment for mitochondrion and mitochondrial inner membrane genes such as Ndufs2, Foxred1, and Tafazzin. This recurrence suggests a stronger Setd1a-loss output than any single cell-class hit, although organelle enrichment does not establish direct SETD1A-bound targets.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Acp1 did not converge with RTK/PTP or phosphatase-neighbor perturbations in this brain Perturb-seq dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Acp1 remained FDR-null, whereas Pten and Ptpa showed FDR-supported responses in the same cell classes. Across same-cell-type whole-transcriptome score correlations, Acp1 matched no strong non-self signature, with selected RTK/PTP/RAS/ERK neighbors such as Ptpn1, Ptpn11, Ntrk2, and Mapk1 reaching only weak correlations. This suggests the Acp1 mRNA signature was neither a generic phosphatase-damage nor a Ras/ERK/RTK-like signature, although weak target engagement could have attenuated correlations.

Ephb1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional feedback in the measured EphB ligands or selected EPH–Ephrin pathway neighbors: Efnb1, Efnb2, Efnb3, Ngef, Rasa1, Abl1, Tiam1, and Sos2 were unchanged, with adjusted p values of 1.0 in every Ephb1 contrast. In this assay, these ligand and immediate-neighbor mRNA levels therefore did not serve as readouts of Ephb1 engagement. This null result is limited to transcript abundance, since phosphorylation, receptor clustering, cytoskeletal remodeling, and cell-cell-contact geometry were not assayed.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: B9d1 in 308 CB GABA showed strong non-ciliary signature neighbors: its whole-transcriptome differential-expression pattern correlated positively with Ranbp2, Fbxo11, Atp6v1e1, P2ry14, and Eef2, and inversely with Wdr26, Dstyk, and Cckar. This was the only class with a robust B9d1 FDR-significant response and the strongest signature-neighbor relationships, suggesting that the CB response lies on a shared cerebellar perturbation-state axis that includes Ranbp2, Eef2, and Wdr26 rather than only ciliary transition-zone genes. This pattern is exploratory and reflects correlation of DE scores within one cell class, not direct physical or pathway relationships.

Il2rg did not converge with perturbations of related common-gamma-chain receptor components or STAT5B in neuronal classes: Il2ra, Il2rb, Il4ra, Il21r, and Stat5b showed no significant transcriptomic hits and their matched signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Il2rg, with Pearson r ranging from -0.057 to 0.096. This argues against an interchangeable neuronal module for common-gamma-chain interleukin receptor signaling in this dataset, while remaining limited to loss-of-function transcriptomic comparisons in neurons rather than ligand-stimulated immune cells where these receptors are normally active.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Vps35 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type showed only weak genome-wide signature correlations, but Rab7 was a modest positive neighbor and Dnm1l also trended concordantly, whereas Ap2s1 and Ap2m1 were among the strongest negative neighbors. This pattern is consistent with a Rab7-associated endosomal perturbation signature in this neuronal state, while suggesting that AP-2 adaptor loss shifts cells away from the Vps35-loss program. The comparison is exploratory because absolute correlations were small and direct VPS26/VPS29 and WASH-complex perturbations were not available.

Sphk1 perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from the profiled sphingosine-to-sphingosine-1-phosphate and adjacent sphingolipid metabolism neighborhood. Across the dataset, Sphk1 did not significantly regulate 20 measured S1P-receptor, S1P-turnover, sphingosine-kinase, or ceramide-metabolism transcripts, and its signature did not converge with S1pr2, Sptlc2, Asah1, or Smpd3 perturbations. This pattern was also seen in the exploratory 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA class, where no FDR-supported genes emerged, even though related-target effects such as Sptlc2 self-transcript depletion were detectable in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; the comparison is transcriptomic and signature-based, and most nearby sphingolipid genes were measured but not perturbed.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Zbtb42 showed only a weak, limited perturbation profile in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, the only cell type with an FDR-significant Zbtb42-associated gene. In that context, the Zbtb42 signature did not strongly converge with or oppose perturbations of Zbtb18, Zbtb20, or Zbtb7a, and similarly showed no notable match to Grm8 or Flvcr1. Because the Zbtb42 signature was weak and based on a single corrected gene, these data mainly exclude a large transcriptome-wide resemblance rather than proving interchangeability with other Zbtb-family repressors.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Caly depletion was not transcriptionally interchangeable with core clathrin-mediated endocytosis perturbations such as Ap2m1, Cltc, or Dnm1. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Caly showed strong target engagement but mainly a self-hit, whereas Ap2m1 or Cltc produced broader multi-gene signatures; score-vector correlations between Caly and these comparators were near zero. Similar buffered, non-phenocopying Caly profiles appeared in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, though this comparison is based on whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon score correlations and Cltc had low cell counts in several classes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Synj1, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, showed a transcriptomic profile that was largely self-dominated rather than interchangeable with nearby endocytic perturbations in clathrin-mediated endocytosis and synaptic-vesicle recycling. Although Synj1 is connected to Ap2m1, Cltc, and Dnm1 in the endocytic network, the dataset split these linked genes into divergent regimes: Ap2m1 and Cltc produced many non-target differentially expressed genes, whereas Synj1 and Dnm1 were almost entirely self-dominated. This comparison is transcriptomic only, pooled across targets with varying guide efficacy and cell counts, and did not measure protein-level endocytic phenotypes.

Fosl2 did not phenocopy the assayed AP-1/MAPK neighbors in this RNA readout. Across 22 shared cell classes, Fosl2–Jund correlations were near zero, Jund showed detectable self-depletion where Fosl2 did not, and Mapk8/Mapk9 were likewise non-convergent, arguing against a shared AP-1/JNK signature in this assay. In 308 CB GABA, the highest Fosl2–Jund correlation was still only 0.134; in 155 MB Glut, Fosl2 had only a weak Rnf34 signal while Jund self-depleted strongly; and in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, Jund but not Fosl2 showed corrected self-transcript decrease. Because most Fos-family partners were not perturbed and the Fosl2 signature itself was weak, this argues against a detected phenocopy rather than against biochemical interaction.

Hif1a perturbation did not produce coordinated repression of canonical HIF output genes, suggesting the assayed brain-cell state lacked an active HIF1A-dependent transcriptional program. Across curated targets including Vegfa, Slc2a1, Ldha, Aldoa, Pkm, Tfrc, Epo, and Car9, no rows reached nominal p < 0.01 or FDR < 0.05, and there was no convergence with Arnt or Arnt2 pathway partners. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Vegfa showed only a nominal decrease, while lowly expressed targets such as Epo and Car9 were difficult to interpret by logFC.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ptcd3 showed weak and inconsistent on-target depletion across measured neuronal classes and remained non-significant in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, even though Dap3, a related mitochondrial small-subunit gene, and respiratory-chain targets Uqcrc1, Cox5a, Ndufs2, and Ndufa4 were strongly self-depleted in overlapping classes. This suggests the Ptcd3 null result is target-specific, likely reflecting guide or engagement limitations rather than a global failure to perturb mitochondrial transcripts; however, comparator signals were partly structural or downstream of mitochondrial translation and were dominated by each target’s own transcript rather than a broad downstream state.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rorb showed little transcriptional impact in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: despite 162 perturbed cells and a modest Rorb logFC of -0.37, it yielded no FDR-significant genes, and its all-gene signature was nearly uncorrelated with Rora in the same cell class (r≈0.037). By contrast, Rora produced a strong ROR-family signature there, with 278 significant genes including Prkcg, Adgrb1, Rasa4, Tnnt1, and Plekhd1, while Rorc was also weak with no significant hits across tested classes. This comparison comes from one strongly Rora-responsive cell class and does not exclude Rorb activity at other developmental stages.

Mfsd6 depletion did not recapitulate a coherent energy-metabolism transcriptional program. Across cell types, recurrent signal was dominated by Mfsd6 itself, with no conventionally significant non-target differential-expression hits; the closest near-misses were Tmtc1 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and Ppm1b in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, both below FDR significance. This refines prior mouse observations linking Mfsd6 and Mfsd10 expression to altered brain energy consumption: here, lowering Mfsd6 alone was insufficient to produce a detectable downstream energy-response RNA state, although no metabolite or transporter-flux assay was performed.

Fmn1 perturbation showed no FDR-supported transcriptional response among expected actin-network and adhesion-partner transcripts, including Spire1, Spire2, Pfn1–Pfn4, Ctnna1, Actg1, Actn4, Fnbp1, Fnbp4, Eps8, Fhdc1, Fmnl1, Palld, and Diaph3. This suggests that canonical formin-mediated actin nucleation/cable assembly and adherens-junction or focal-adhesion cytoskeletal organization were transcriptionally uncoupled from Fmn1 guide assignment in this dataset. The analysis was limited to mRNA abundance, so it does not address actin filament assembly, focal adhesions, dendritic spines, morphology, or protein activity.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|053 Sst Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Spast shows only a weak, mixed nominal signal for organelle-membrane and trafficking biology, detectable only after pooling nominal P<0.001 genes across cell types rather than as a coherent per-cell ESCRT/ER program. Scattered nominal hits included Chmp3, Scarb2, Atf6b, Rer1, Caml, Ap2m1, and Kif1a across 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 053 Sst Gaba, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, nominal target engagement and Kif1a were seen, but no individual genes or pathways were FDR-significant, so the ER, ESCRT, and endosomal interpretation remains exploratory.

Klf1 in brain neurons did not phenocopy assayed KLF paralogs or the erythroid KLF1-associated regulatory axis across all shared assayed cell classes. Same-cell-type transcriptomic correlations with Klf7, Klf9, Klf11, Klf12, and Klf13 were near zero, and correlations with Bcl11a, Bcl11b, Gata1, and Ep300 were similarly minimal, indicating that weak Klf1 score vectors are largely uncoupled from KLF-family programs and from erythroid transcription/globin-switching pathways in these non-erythroid cells. This is a correlation-based result, and Tal1 was not tested as a comparator.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Atp6v0a1 showed an asymmetric V-ATPase transcriptional response: perturbing Atp6v0c, Atp6ap1, or Atp6ap2 recurrently reduced Atp6v0a1 mRNA, whereas direct Atp6v0a1 perturbation did not significantly induce or repress other measured V-ATPase subunit transcripts at FDR<0.05. This pattern was seen across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, suggesting Atp6v0a1 acts more as a downstream collateral transcript than a reciprocal feedback driver, with transcript-level caveats about misassembly, cell state, or guide strength.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ryk was not interchangeable with nearby Wnt/planar cell polarity receptors in the matched neuronal contexts. In 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, Ryk and Ror1 had no FDR<0.10 hits, while Fzd3, Prickle1, and Ror2 showed only isolated corrected signatures; Ryk score vectors were near-zero correlated with these comparators. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Ryk was nominally strongest but still FDR>0.31. A caveat is that Ror2’s corrected response occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, not a Ryk-measured match.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Atl1 perturbation produced mainly self-transcript depletion rather than a shared downstream RNA program across ER-shaping/HSP genes. In high-engagement contexts, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also 155 MB Glut, Atl1 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Reep1 or Reep2, even though Reep1 and Reep2, like Atl1, showed corrected self-knockdown in selected groups. This suggests the tubular ER network shaping and ER membrane fusion module did not collapse to an interchangeable transcriptional state; however, Reep2 is only a family comparator here, and Atl3 and Spast had weak on-target FDR support in this dataset.

Itga2b perturbation in assayed mouse brain nuclei did not transcriptionally recruit the canonical platelet αIIbβ3/integrin program: Itgb3, fibrinogen and von Willebrand ligands (Fga, Fgb, Fgg, Vwf), Fn1, Runx1, Tln1, and MAPK/RAF sentinels (Mapk1, Mapk3, Braf) all remained unchanged, with minimum FDR reported as 1.0. This suggests platelet adhesion, degranulation, and integrin signaling genes stayed uncoupled from Itga2b in this RNA readout, although the result is a targeted sentinel-gene check rather than formal pathway enrichment, and many platelet ligands were nearly absent from the matrix.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Fus knockdown produced a recurrent RNA-processing and nuclear-speckle-associated response centered on Rsrp1 and Atxn2l, with Luc7l2 and Snrnp70 recurring in the strongest signatures. The dominant response was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Clk1, Clk4, and Srsf6 were down, while 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA reproduced the Rsrp1/Atxn2l head with fewer downstream genes. Across other responsive classes, the pattern was heterogeneous and driven by a compact gene set; the data are gene-level and do not measure exon inclusion.

Pak2 perturbation did not reveal the expected PAK2–LIMK/cofilin actin-cytoskeleton axis at the mRNA level: Limk1, Limk2, Cfl1, Cfl2, and Actg1 showed no FDR-supported transcriptional response, and on-target Pak2 transcript depletion was not significant in any quantified cell type. This suggests that the disease-relevant Pak2 biology may lie in phosphorylation and F-actin polymerization rather than an acute steady-state transcript module, although the absence of phosphoproteomic or cytoskeletal measurements and the possibility of weak Pak2 knockdown limit interpretation.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Lonp1 perturbation up-regulated a Ddit3-centered integrated stress response/ATF4-like amino-acid module in a subset of neuronal classes, most clearly in 155 MB Glut and 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells. Ddit3 was the most recurrent anchor, with Shmt2, Aldh1l2, Chac1, Slc7a5, Slc7a1, and Herpud1 contributing to a coherent upward module; the pineal/peri-mesencephalic glutamatergic subset showed the highest-amplitude response. However, only Ddit3 in 155/217 and two additional genes in 217 reached FDR significance, while signals in 191 MB P MY GABA, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA were nominal and weak in cerebellar GABA cells.

Atl3 produced transcriptional signatures that were nearly orthogonal to Atl1, Reep1, Spast, and Vapb across the same 15 matched cell types, with mean Pearson correlations near zero, rather than phenocopying a shared GTP-dependent tubular ER fusion and ER network maintenance state. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, the largest Atl3 context had 82 perturbed cells but no FDR-significant response, with Vapb only a weak top-200 positive neighbor. Because similarity was computed from noisy mRNA score vectors and Atl3 engagement appeared weaker than some related perturbations, true protein-level convergence could still have been missed.

Bsn perturbation did not reveal an Atg5-dependent presynaptic autophagy mRNA program: no queried autophagy transcripts, including Atg5, Rheb, Atg16l1, Ulk2, or Map1lc3b, reached FDR, and Bsn signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Atg5 perturbation. Atg5 itself produced only a small, midbrain-restricted FDR signature not shared with Bsn, including in 155 MB Glut. In 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, Bsn effects were weak or nominal and did not converge with presynaptic interactors. These data are transcript-level only and do not measure autophagic flux or synaptic-vesicle turnover.

Mest did not show signature convergence with seven targeted imprinted-gene network neighbors—Gnas, Kcnq1, Magel2, Ndn, Peg3, Sgce, and Snrpn—whose perturbation signatures had low correlations with Mest, indicating that these imprinted-gene members were not acutely interchangeable with Mest at the neuronal transcriptomic level. This argues against a common acute perturbation module despite their functional association in STRING, with the caveat that only seven partners were tested and the STRING links here reflect functional associations, largely text-mining based, rather than a physical complex.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Sec31a perturbation in 155 MB Glut cells produced a strong response marked by repression of neuronal and synaptic transcripts such as Atp1a3, Nefh, Thy1, and Vamp1, alongside increased early secretory and ER-to-Golgi trafficking transcripts including Sec23a, Copa, Copb1, Srpr, Arfgap1, and Golgb1. This pattern is consistent with a compensatory secretory program after outer COPII-coat disruption rather than only generic transcriptional collapse, although only a subset of COPII/ERGIC genes increased and the data measure mRNA rather than vesicle budding or cargo export.

Srsf1 loss produced a recurrent nuclear RNA-processing and mRNA-splicing response rather than an arbitrary stress signature, with increased Ptbp2, Rbm28, Dazap1, and Psip1 alongside decreased Srsf2, Hnrnpdl, Clk4, and Clk1, plus changes in Hnrnpm and Celf3. The strongest responses were seen in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with large effects also in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, and the signature converged with Tnpo3 in these cell types. A caveat is that the assay measured steady-state transcript abundance, not exon inclusion or splice-junction usage.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Vps41 depletion was associated with a lysosomal compensation program in engaged 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, where Mcoln1, Atp6v0b, Atp6v1b2, Lamp2, Gba, Dpp7, and Gm2a increased, consistent with HOPS-dependent endosome/autophagosome-to-lysosome fusion disruption and lysosomal acidification/catabolism responses. The strongest on-target signals were FDR-significant Mcoln1 in 155 MB Glut and Dpp7 in 191 MB P MY GABA, while most other module genes were nominal only, and the dataset measures RNA abundance rather than lysosomal fusion or autophagic flux directly.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tfdp1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed weak positive convergence with Rb1 and E2f4: these were the top two positive signature neighbors among non-Tfdp1 perturbations, but the absolute correlations were small. This was the only cell type with FDR-significant Tfdp1 downstream genes, and the similarity was distributed across the ranked signature rather than driven by the two strongest Tfdp1 hits. In contrast, Tfdp2, E2f1, and E2f5 had flat profiles with no global FDR-significant responses, indicating that assayed E2F/DP-family perturbations were not interchangeable. Interpretation is tempered by different cell counts across perturbations and by Rb1 being assayed in only a subset of cell types.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Il17ra showed its strongest, but weak, signal in 308 CB GABA cells, where the expected IL-17RA to Act1/TRAF6, NF-kappaB, and MAPK inflammatory program was not induced at 5% FDR. In this cell class, Nfkbiz, Map3k7, and Mapk8 were only nominal, while Ccl2, Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Il6, Lcn2, Csf2, and Mmp3 were essentially neutral, and Il17ra did not align with broad inflammatory neighbor perturbations; Aatk and Dexi also missed 5% FDR, and Il17rd did not phenocopy Il17ra. This dataset reflects receptor perturbation without IL-17A/IL-17F ligand challenge, and Il17rc was not available as a comparator.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Six3 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons did not mobilize the canonical SIX3–Wnt/SHH developmental program: Wnt1, Wnt8b, Shh, Ptch1, Axin2, Tcf7l2, Pax6, Ccnd1, and Ccnd2 showed no FDR-significant response after Six3 perturbation. In the same dataset, direct perturbation of the Wnt effectors Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 produced strong signatures that were not recapitulated or correlated with Six3. This suggests a context mismatch with embryonic anterior neuroectoderm and rostral diencephalon circuitry, and Six3 target engagement was not confirmed.

Zbtb7a did not simply phenocopy other assayed Zbtb-family or NuRD-associated perturbations in this adult mouse neuronal loss-of-function dataset. Across the restricted top-100-gene signature comparison, mean cosine similarity was near zero for nine other Zbtb perturbations, only modestly positive for Gatad2b and Chd4, and recurrently inverse for Yy1, Huwe1, Trrap, and Chd8, suggesting a context-specific chromatin-regulatory balance rather than a canonical ZBTB7A–NuRD/corepressor state. These comparisons are screening statistics based only on the top 100 absolute Zbtb7a score genes per cell type.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Fgd4 showed a weak, non-convergent transcriptomic signature across many glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where it was the largest targeted group yet still lacked Fgd4 self-depletion while Pak1 showed clear on-target depletion in the same class. Consistent with this weak engagement, Fgd4 targeting did not nominally alter Fgd4, Cdc42, Rac1, Pak1, Pak2, Pak3, Akt3, or PI3K genes and had near-zero whole-transcriptome similarity to Cdc42, Rac1, or Pak perturbations, so the dataset does not detect a CDC42/RAC/PAK transcriptional response downstream of Fgd4; this should be read as pathway non-detection rather than biochemical proof, since the assay measures transcriptomes rather than CDC42-GTP and ineffective knockdown could explain the uncoupling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Camta1 showed no close full-transcriptome signature match across perturbations, with the strongest non-Camta1 correlation reaching only Pearson r=0.252. The modest nearest neighbors were concentrated in caudal responder cell types: in 191 MB P MY GABA, Trrap was the top positive neighbor and Wdr26 was also positively aligned, while Mecp2, Pogz, and Ankrd11 were modest negative neighbors; 155 MB Glut showed modest positive convergence with Rbfox1; and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut included negative neighbors such as Celf2, Calm1, and Pten. These patterns are best treated as hypothesis-generating contrasts rather than functional equivalence.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Itga2 showed its clearest, near-threshold transcriptional effect in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG glutamatergic cells, where Bcar1 was nominally induced, but this was not accompanied by coordinated movement of focal-adhion or integrin-pathway transcripts including Ptk2, Src, Itgb1, Col4a1, Ddr2, Mapk1, Pik3ca, Rac1, and Cdc42. Thus, the dataset supports only an isolated Bcar1 hint within alpha2-beta1 integrin/ECM adhesion signaling rather than broad pathway activation, and RNA-level data do not address integrin phosphorylation, adhesion, or subcellular localization.

Txndc15 perturbation in this mature-brain Perturb-seq dataset did not produce detectable differential expression in a ciliary transition-zone/Hedgehog marker panel, including Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Smo, and Ift88, and its transcriptional signature was nearly orthogonal to the available Meckel syndrome–related perturbations Ahi1, B9d1, Cep290, and Rpgrip1l. These results suggest that, in the assayed neuronal classes, Txndc15 loss does not map onto a simple ciliary RNA program, with the caveat that ciliary effects may be structural, post-transcriptional, developmental, or obscured by weak target-transcript engagement in some comparators.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tcf7l2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a strong thalamic Wnt/beta-catenin-TCF transcriptional signature, similar to Ctnnb1 and contrasting with Apc, whereas perturbing upstream components such as Lrp5, Lrp6, Fzd2, Fzd3, Fzd4, Fzd6, Fzd9, or Gsk3b was buffered and yielded little to no comparable response, despite substantial matched cell numbers. This suggests that the program is most sensitive at the nuclear beta-catenin/TCF node, although receptor redundancy, guide efficiency, ligand context, or insufficient pathway tone could also explain the weak upstream signatures.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gpr161 showed an orthogonal, weak signature that did not converge with Hedgehog, ciliary transport, or adenylate-cyclase pathway neighbors: across matched cell types including 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, score correlations with Smo, Ptch1, Ptch2, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ift88, Adcy3, Adcy5, and Cdon never exceeded |r| = 0.088. In contrast, Adcy3 showed detectable self-knockdown in several of these cell types, so this is a failure to see convergence rather than evidence of antagonism, especially given the generally weak engagement of several comparator perturbations.

Cdon showed essentially uncorrelated whole-transcriptome perturbation signatures relative to matched Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Lrp2, Neo1, Dcc, and Unc5c perturbations, so in this postmitotic brain assay it did not phenocopy measured Hedgehog receptor/transducer or netrin-receptor neighbors despite being a curated SHH coreceptor. This suggests the assay did not expose an interchangeable canonical Hedgehog-receptor phenotype for Cdon, although key partners such as Boc, Gas1, and Hedgehog ligands were not directly perturbed and the correlations summarize weak signatures.

Tacr3 perturbation was uncoupled from the canonical tachykinin/Gq immediate transcriptional program in this basal dataset: no adjusted-significant changes were detected in Fos, Jun, Egr1, Arc, Npas4, Nr4a1, Dusp1, or in Tac2, Pdyn, and Gnrh1, and no returned cell type showed statistically supported on-target depletion of Tacr3. These results suggest no sustained mRNA signature of tachykinin receptor/G alpha(q) signaling or the KNDy/GnRH neuroendocrine axis under the assayed state, while still leaving open acute ligand-dependent NK3R calcium signaling, peptide release, and circuit dynamics that were not measured.

Ptch2 perturbation did not produce a canonical Hedgehog/PTCH-SMO-GLI transcriptional response across all 23 profiled mouse-brain classes: Ptch1, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Smo, Hhip, Cdon, Boc, Gas1, and Gpr161 remained unchanged, and the Ptch2 transcript itself was not significantly perturbed. Thus, despite PTCH2 being a Hedgehog receptor and GLI-responsive gene, this dataset shows absent canonical readouts, consistent with pathway buffering, low ligand tone, or insufficient Ptch2 perturbation, with related Hedgehog perturbations appearing largely orthogonal rather than converging on GLI feedback.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Insr showed a muted transcriptional phenotype, similar to Igf1r, Irs1, Pik3ca, Pik3cb, and Pik3r1, while the negative mTOR regulators Pten, Tsc1, and Tsc2 produced large, cell-restricted programs in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, including several classes where Insr itself remained FDR-silent. Mtor and Rptor were also mostly silent, and Insr did not show strong positive or reciprocal signatures with these neighbors. This contrast localizes transcriptome-sensitive responses to the TSC/PTEN branch rather than to receptor/PI3K entry nodes, although sgRNA cutting, transcript stability, baseline expression, and the lack of proof for mTORC1 activation temper the interpretation.

Ffar1 showed no clear convergence with available GPCR, cAMP, PLC, or Pparg-related perturbations: whole-transcriptome Pearson correlations with Pparg, P2ry14, Gnas, Gnal, Gnao1, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Plcb1, and Prkaca were weak, and nearest-neighbor lists often included non-gene controls. In 308 CB GABA, a second cell class containing an Ffar1 row, there was likewise no mRNA-level target response, although it had the largest still-weak cross-perturbation correlations. These results do not support a canonical FFAR1/free-fatty-acid receptor, Gq/PLC, or insulin-secretion-like module, but interpretation is limited because key comparators such as Ffar4, Gnaq, and Gna11 were not perturbed and the analysis used transcriptome correlations rather than biochemical readouts.

Wrn perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the canonical WRN DNA-damage axis: no detectable ATR-p53, homologous-recombination, or proliferation module was induced, with Trp53, Cdkn1a, Bbc3, Pmaip1, Gadd45a/b/g, Rad51, Pcna, and Mki67 not showing significant or recurrent changes. Nominal Wrn hits were sparse and failed to form a reproducible cross-cell-type module, with no convergence with Atr or Trp53-associated programs. This negative call is tempered by weak Wrn mRNA engagement and by the likelihood that many WRN repair functions are primarily post-translational rather than transcriptional.

Ror1 perturbation was transcriptomically inert in the tested adult mouse brain cell types, clustering with a largely inactive WNT5A/FZD/ROR surface-receptor cohort rather than with responsive intracellular canonical Wnt nodes. In the main Ror1-tested classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Ror1 produced no FDR-significant differential-expression calls; similarly, Ror2, Ryk, Fzd2, Fzd3, Fzd4, Fzd6, and Fzd9 showed no corrected hits. By contrast, Apc and Ctnnb1 yielded hundreds of corrected hits, with Axin2 among canonical Wnt readouts. This contrast is limited to transcriptomic phenotypes, and Ror1 and most receptor comparators also lacked direct target-transcript engagement.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Map2k6 perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from the canonical p38/AP-1 stress-response module across many neuronal and glial classes, including multiple cortical IT glutamatergic populations, hippocampal and ET glutamatergic cells, several GABAergic classes, hypothalamic and midbrain glutamatergic cells, pineal glutamatergic cells, and cerebellar GABA cells. Expected markers such as Dusp1, Dusp5, Dusp6, Fos, Jun, Jund, Fosl2, Atf2, Mapk14, and Map2k3 showed no FDR-supported changes. In the lowest-p-value class, 001 L5-6 IT Glut, the signal was driven by Polr3a rather than a corrected Map2k6 response, and Map2k6 itself was only nominally depleted. This null result is limited to steady-state mRNA, whereas p38 pathway activity depends on phosphorylation and may require stress or cytokine stimulation.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Cntnap2 knockdown uncoupled the known Caspr2/contactin/Kv1 neighborhood at the mRNA level across 052 Pvalb Gaba, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Despite strong on-target depletion in several contexts, there was no secondary induction or repression of Cntn2, Kcna1, Kcna2, Cntn1, Cntnap1, Adam22, Lgi1, or Dpp6, and full-signature correlations with Cntn1 or Cntnap1 perturbations were near zero. This supports a protein-localization relationship without clear mRNA feedback, with interpretation tempered because Cntn2 was assessed only as an expressed transcript, not as a perturbation, and some cell-type analyses had low perturbed-cell counts.

Slitrk1 did not show a detectable convergent transcriptomic module with LAR-RPTP or broader synaptic-adhesion perturbations in matched cell subclasses. Its score vectors were nearly orthogonal to Ptprd, Ptprf, Nrxn1/2/3, Nlgn1/2/3, Lrrtm1/3/4, Cntnap1/2, and Ntrk2, and global neighbor scans found only weak nearest neighbors. This null pattern is notable because several other adhesion genes produced FDR-significant effects, but the readout is indirect, Ptprs was not perturbed here, and Ptprd/Ptprf themselves were weak in differential-expression tables.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Madd showed no convergence with related Rab, TNFR, MAPK, or synaptic-vesicle perturbations. In four informative cell classes—052 Pvalb Gaba, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut—Madd score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Rab27a, Rab3gap1, Rab3gap2, Dennd5a, Tnfrsf1a, Snap25, Stxbp1, and Map2k1, with maximum absolute Pearson r about 0.06, and all-target neighbor searches were also weak (|r|<0.09). These exploratory negative results argue against a robust shared Madd module, though low correlation could reflect post-transcriptional action or weak perturbation, and only selected informative cell classes were evaluated.

Nr1h2 perturbation in the 23 assayed neuronal classes did not recover the canonical NR1H2/NR1H3-RXR cholesterol-efflux program: Abca1, Abcg1, Apoe, Mylip, and Srebf1 showed no FDR-supported regulation, even though these genes are central to the curated LXR/RXR efflux pathway. The broad null across Glut, GABA, and Dopa neurons contrasts with a robust Srebf2 sterol signature seen in many of the same classes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, several lipid genes trended downward nominally, but none survived correction, and guide-editing or baseline-expression data were unavailable.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnh1 showed weak EAG-family behavior rather than a general failure to detect voltage-gated potassium-channel perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: Kcnh1 was unchanged and Kcnh5 remained FDR-negative, while Kcnq2, Kcnq3, Kcnab2, and Kcnc3 were each strongly self-depleted in the same cell type. This contrast, within potassium ion transmembrane transport and voltage-gated potassium-channel activity pathways, is strongest in this thalamic population and does not resolve whether guide efficiency, transcript detectability, or biological compensation underlies the EAG-family weakness.

Prdm5 showed a selectively weak perturbation profile in this adult-brain screen: across all 23 Prdm5-tested neuronal subclasses, it produced no FDR-supported genes, no self-transcript change, no ECM program, and no strong cross-target neighbor. This flat result was not uniform across the PRDM family, because Prdm10 generated a robust multi-cell-type signature with 182 FDR-significant rows across 10 cell types, whereas Prdm12 and Prdm16 had none and Prdm2 had only one hit. However, the stronger Prdm10 response should not be taken to imply interchangeable PRDM-family behavior or equivalent guide efficacy, expression, or protein turnover for Prdm5.

Prdm16 showed little detectable transcriptional impact in this neuronal perturbation library: unlike Prdm10, which produced 182 FDR-significant responses, Prdm16 was nearly silent, as were Prdm5 and Prdm12, while Prdm2 yielded only one significant response. Prdm16 also did not correlate strongly with the other assayed PRDM-family perturbations, indicating that PRDM-family perturbations were divergent rather than interchangeable here. This negative result is qualified by the absence of MECOM/Prdm3, the closest known H3K9me1 partner, so the comparison is broad across PRDM factors rather than a close-paralog test.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ahr perturbation did not elicit the canonical AHR-XRE detoxification or feedback program across all 21 assayed neuronal classes, including glutamatergic and GABAergic populations such as L5-6 IT Glut, L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Pvalb GABA, Sst GABA, and CB GABA. Ahr, Ahrr, Arnt, Aip, Cyp1a1, Cyp1a2, Cyp1b1, Nqo1, and Tiparp were all non-significant, indicating no detectable induction or repression of the expected ARNT-dependent xenobiotic-response arm. This likely reflects an assay state without active ligand-AHR transcription, and canonical targets may sit near neuronal detection limits, so extreme Cyp logFC values with p≈1 are not interpretable as regulation.

Gphn perturbation did not produce transcriptomic convergence with several known inhibitory-postsynaptic protein partners: Arhgef9, Glrb, and Nlgn2 were not strong same-cell signature neighbors of Gphn across matched cell types, never reaching |r| ≥ 0.10, and their own transcripts were not FDR-regulated after Gphn perturbation. In the GABAergic and glycinergic inhibitory receptor clustering context, core transcripts appeared buffered, with the Gabrg2 signature relationship varying by cell type. Comparisons were limited to matched cell types, and Gabarap, Mocs1, and Mocs2 were measured as transcripts but unavailable as Gphn signature comparators.

Ireb2 partial perturbation did not produce a coordinated iron-stress, hypoxia, or ferroptosis-like mRNA program in the measured cells. Aside from nominal Tfrc decreases in selected populations such as 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, canonical neighbors including Aco1, Fbxl5, Ncoa4, Slc11a2, Slc40a1, Cisd2, Hif1a, Hmox1, and Slc7a11 showed no coherent FDR-supported movement, so the Tfrc signal should not be overread as global iron-homeostasis collapse; however, many IRP outputs are translational or post-translational, and scRNA-seq alone cannot exclude altered iron flux.

Prdm2 showed a weak, largely uncorrelated transcriptional signature that did not phenocopy PRDM-family paralogs or predicted chromatin-network partners in this Perturb-seq dataset. Whole-transcriptome correlations were approximately zero versus Prdm5, Prdm10, Prdm12, Prdm16, and comparators including Ctbp1, Setdb1, Kat6a, Foxg1, Camkmt, Nsd1, Gata3, and Rb1, while the strongest neighbors were cell-type-idiosyncratic rather than a recurrent Prdm2-like module. In the assayed glutamatergic populations, PRDM/chromatin regulation signals were buffered or nominal, so the lack of convergence may reflect weak engagement rather than biological insulation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chn1 showed no detectable target depletion in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class, even though this was the highest-count Chn1 context, with 204 perturbed cells and essentially no RNA knockdown signal. In the same cell type, Epha4, Cdc42, Trio, Pak1, Tubb3, and Kif21a were robustly depleted, indicating that the class was not globally refractory to perturbation. Given the EphA4/alpha2-chimaerin relationship in EphA4/ephrinB3 axon-guidance signaling, the contrast is most consistent with Chn1-specific non-engagement, although comparators are not all direct Chn1 complex members and engagement was judged only at the transcript level.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
full_finding_text: Jund behaved as a weak, context-specific node rather than an interchangeable AP-1/JNK module member: in the best-engaged neuronal contexts, including 155 MB Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, Jund loss showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signature correlation with Fosl2, Atf2, Map2k1, Mapk8, and Mapk9, and no high-correlation positive or negative neighbors among assayed perturbations. In 155 MB Glut and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, target depletion was significant but downstream responses were buffered, while 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut were only nominal contexts. These comparisons are limited to whole-signature correlations, and Jun, Junb, Fos, Fosb, Fosl1, and Jdp2 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Usp9x showed a weak signature neighborhood with UFMylation and proteostasis regulators rather than a generic deubiquitinase, ubiquitin-ligase, FMR1, or mTOR-like response. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, the closest same-cell neighbors were Uba5, Ufc1, Ufsp2, and Nfe2l1, while Usp48, Mib1, Ube3a, Fmr1, and Mtor were near zero or uncoupled. The strongest on-target signal was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but genome-wide correlations were small, so this remains a signature-neighbor hypothesis rather than a pathway-activation call.

Zfp950 did not phenocopy Setdb1 in this brain Perturb-seq dataset: no Zfp950 contrast passed a 5% FDR threshold, including the highest-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, while Setdb1 showed 37 FDR-significant responses across 8 cell types. Across 21 shared cell types, Zfp950 and Setdb1 score signatures were essentially uncorrelated, indicating no shared gene-level response. This divergence is pathway-proximal within KRAB-ZFP/KAP1-SETDB1 retroelement and transcriptional repression, but Setdb1 is a broad chromatin effector rather than a Zfp950 complex member.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Inpp5k showed a weak, exploratory sterol/SREBP transcriptional tail, with nominal up-regulation of Cyp51, Insig1, Fdft1, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Dhcr24, Hmgcr, Sqle, and Srebf2 in selected contexts including 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 308 CB GABA. The effect recurred with the same sign across several Inpp5k signatures and aligned directionally with the much stronger sterol module seen after Tsc1 or Tsc2 loss, but no Inpp5k sterol gene passed FDR correction, so the signal remained far weaker than the Tsc1/Tsc2 comparators.

Slc22a17 knockdown reduced Slc22a17 transcripts in most measured cell types but did not transcriptionally engage a canonical LCN2 or iron-homeostasis response: Lcn2, the alternate receptor Lrp2, and the sampled iron-related genes Bdh2, Tfrc, Fth1, Hmox1, and Ncoa4 were unchanged at FDR<0.05. In this basal neuronal context, the LCN2-SLC22A17 siderophore/iron endocytosis program therefore appears buffered or uncoupled at the mRNA level. However, the dataset did not measure ligand state, iron levels, receptor internalization, or inflammatory stimulation, so unchanged RNA does not exclude protein-level pathway activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Sp4 showed a factor-specific, divergent transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: the restricted top-500-gene Sp4 signature was not reproduced by assayed SP/KLF family perturbations, including Sp7, Klf1, Klf7, Klf9, Klf11, Klf12, and Klf13, and its nearest positive or negative atlas-wide neighbors were only weakly correlated. This held even in 151, where Klf9 was itself active, arguing against a generic SP/KLF zinc-finger stress program. A caveat is that the comparison used top-500 absolute Sp4 genes rather than full-transcriptome correlations, and Sp1 and Sp3 were not assayed.

Adgrb1 showed no transcriptional engagement of canonical BAI1 pathways in this dataset: the BAI1-Par3/Tiam1-Rac synaptogenesis axis, the ELMO/DOCK/Rac engulfment module, and Rho/ERK or Bcr/RhoA signaling were not detected, and measured effector or disease-axis genes such as Pard3, Tiam1, Elmo1, Elmo2, Dock1, Dock3, Rac1, Bcr, Rhoa, Dlg4, Mdm2, and Trp53 were not significant hits. Adgrb1 signatures were essentially orthogonal to Adgrb3, Baiap2, Dock3, Dock7, Rac1, Tiam1, and Trio perturbations, but because Adgrb1 mRNA was not depleted in any assayed cell class, this cannot distinguish true absence of pathway biology from perturbation failure.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ache knockdown in three neuronal classes—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—produced strong on-target reduction of Ache but no detectable mRNA changes in cholinergic partner genes, including Chat, Slc18a3, Slc5a7, Bche, Prima1, Colq, and receptor genes such as Chrna4, Chrnb2, Chrna7, Chrm2, and Chrm3. In each class, Ache was essentially the only significant transcript, and receptor-subunit perturbation signatures were engaged yet largely uncorrelated with Ache. This is a negative mRNA-level result in three targeted neuronal classes, with many pathway transcripts low or sparsely detected.

Sacs showed a weak, largely uncoupled transcriptomic phenotype: in 308 CB GABA cells and across the screen, acute Sacs guides did not phenocopy Hsp70/proteasome protein-quality-control or Atxn1-neighbor perturbations. Curated chaperone genes were not significantly changed, no strong positive or negative Sacs signature neighbors emerged, and signatures from Hspa8, Hsp90ab1, Hspa9, Hsf1, Stub1, Vcp, and Atxn1 were stronger and poorly correlated with Sacs. This comparison is transcriptome- and score-correlation-based, so sacsin could still affect client folding post-transcriptionally without altering chaperone mRNAs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atg5 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a weaker thalamic echo of ER and endomembrane protein-handling biology: Atg5 itself was nominally decreased, with near-FDR downregulation of Pdia6 and nominal decreases in Xbp1 and Hspa5. This pattern converges with the 155 MB Glut response and suggests cell-type-restricted proteostasis sensitivity across selected glutamatergic classes, but the thalamic signal is modest, as no TH gene reached FDR < 0.10 and the inference depends on nominal Pdia6/Xbp1/Hspa5 behavior.

Ppp3r1 loss did not produce an FDR-significant mRNA response in the canonical calcineurin–NFAT–RCAN transcript layer, with Rcan1, Rcan2, Rcan3, Nfatc1, Nfatc2, Nfatc3, Nfatc4, Nfat5, and Nfatc2ip unchanged across the dataset, including the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut context where the main Ppp3r1 response module was otherwise clearest. Instead, the dominant non-target response involved Pcsk1n, Ptprs, Atp2a2, Coro6, Tle2, Ndrg2, Septin4, and Slc6a17. Because NFAT signaling is largely controlled by dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation, unchanged pathway-component mRNAs do not exclude altered NFAT activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Thap1 loss of function increased the Thap1 transcript in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells rather than depleting it, with the only FDR-significant self-transcript signal observed in this class (logFC 1.287, FDR 0.00573). This direction is consistent with release of THAP1 autoregulatory transcriptional repression, but the result could also reflect persistence of edited 3-prime RNA rather than restored protein. Outside this cell type, Thap1 target-transcript engagement was nominal or unresolved after multiple-testing correction, and single-cell 3-prime RNA counts do not measure THAP1 protein or allele editing.

Satb1 showed little overlap with its paralog Satb2 in this screen: across 22 shared cell types, their perturbation score vectors were nearly uncorrelated, with r ranging from -0.052 to 0.035, and they did not produce same-direction transcriptome signatures in any shared class. This argues against interchangeability of SATB-family chromatin regulators here, although interpretation is limited because Satb1 itself was weak: its target transcript was never significantly reduced after multiple testing, so the lack of convergence could reflect poor Satb1 engagement rather than true functional orthogonality in every cell type.

Irf7 perturbation did not reveal a strong shared basal neuronal IRF program: across 23 profiled glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, and pineal neuronal classes, it lacked detectable target-transcript depletion, a canonical IFN/ISG signature, and strong convergence or anticorrelation with Irf3, Irf5, or Irf9. In 22–23 overlapping cell types, Irf3, Irf5, and Irf9 yielded zero FDR<0.05 rows, and the closest Irf7 signature neighbor reached only a weak Pearson r of 0.207. A cell-type-specific exception was a Grb10 decrease in 054 CNU-MGE GABA after Irf7 but not queried pathway neighbors. These comparisons used final score vectors rather than guide-level replicates, and all IRF-family perturbations had weak on-target mRNA evidence.

St3gal5 perturbation did not yield a shared acute RNA module with available sphingolipid or ganglioside-related comparators in this screen.
