Across St3gal3, Sptlc2, Asah1, Smpd3, and Sphk1, no coherent FDR-significant convergent program emerged, and a restricted signature-neighbor scan found only modest, exploratory correlations rather than a robust St3gal5 neighbor. This was most evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, where St3gal5 knockdown was strongest yet non-target signals remained absent or weak. Interpretation is limited because most comparators, except Sptlc2, had weak on-target support, and key ganglioside enzymes such as Ugcg and B4galnt1 were not included.

Mc1r showed divergent perturbation behavior from other melanocortin-family members in this neuronal dataset: its signature had low correlation with Agrp, Mc3r, and Mc4r, rather than converging with them despite shared melanocortin ligand-receptor biology. The contrast is qualified by generally weak signatures across family members, with Mc3r and Mc4r each yielding only isolated FDR-supported genes in distinct subclasses. In 145 MH-LH TH Glut, Mc1r’s best adjusted signal was an exploratory Septin8 hit, while Mc4r showed a distinct Smox hit, reinforcing non-interchangeability in this setting.

Copa showed a weak, largely uncoupled transcriptional signature that did not converge with measured early secretory neighbors in the COPI/COPII trafficking pathway. Across the dataset, Copa score vectors were near zero in correlation with Copg1, Sec23a, and Sar1b, even though Copg1 and Sec23a were more clearly knocked down and mainly produced only self-gene hits. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Copa had the largest perturbation cell count but essentially no Copa mRNA repression, whereas Copg1 was strongly self-depleted without non-self FDR hits. Because most COPI subunits were not perturbed and Copa itself was weakly engaged, this is best read as a caution against assuming complex-level interchangeability from these data.

Sorbs1 showed weak, largely uncoupled transcriptional signatures across 22 Sorbs1-profiled neuronal classes. Its perturbation did not phenocopy available CAP/CBL/Rho/adhesion or synaptic-adaptor neighbors, with near-zero correlations to Cblb, Cdc42, Sh3kbp1, Baiap2, Bin1, Dlg4, and Syngap1, and core partner transcripts including Cbl, Flot1, Vcl, Pxn, Tln1, and Afdn were not robustly regulated. This argues against a coherent transcriptional CAP-adhesion module in this screen, but the result is exploratory because Sorbs1 engagement was weak and key biochemical nodes such as Cbl, Flot1, Vcl, Pxn, Tln1, Afdn, Sorbs2, and Sorbs3 were not perturbed.

Timmdc1 perturbation did not yield a coherent complex-I or OXPHOS transcriptional response: genome-wide testing found no FDR-significant downstream transcripts, and mitochondrial genes appeared only as isolated nominal, mixed-direction changes with FDR = 1.0, including Ndufa2, Ndufs3, Uqcrc1, Atp5c1, and Timm17a. In 155 MB Glut, only nominal OXPHOS rows were seen, such as Ndufa2 up, while 052 Pvalb Gaba showed a nominal Ndufs3 down row without any FDR-supported Timmdc1 response. The target transcript itself showed no reproducible knockdown, so these mRNA findings may reflect weak perturbation or assay buffering; complex-I activity, respiration, and ROS were not measured.

Stat3 perturbation produced RNA signatures that were largely independent of other STAT-family perturbations: Stat1, Stat2, Stat4, and Stat5b showed pooled correlations with the Stat3 signature of only r=0.0008–0.0127, suggesting little interchangeability despite shared STAT architecture and reported STAT1–STAT3 heterodimer capability. In 191 MB P MY GABA cells, Stat3 showed nominal depletion without an FDR-level trans response, and a more clearly on-target Stat1 perturbation still did not become Stat3-like. This contrast is based on transcriptomic signatures rather than direct measurements of STAT phosphorylation or DNA binding, and several STAT paralogs also had weak on-target engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fzd9 showed a much weaker transcriptional effect than several other Williams-region perturbations in the same library, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. In this cell type, Gtf2i, Baz1b, Gtf2ird1, and Eif4h each produced FDR-significant signatures with their strongest signal there, whereas Fzd9, along with Clip2 and Limk1, produced none. Because this is a locus-based comparison within the multigene Williams-Beuren interval, the difference should not be taken to mean a shared transcriptional class, and may also reflect guide performance or target expression.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Neurog3 in the 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut class showed an FDR-significant effect driven by Mest down-regulation, but its score vector was near-uncorrelated with screened pancreatic endocrine network neighbors Pax4, Pax6, Neurod1, Pdx1, Sox9, Foxa2, and Isl1, as well as with available Notch and proneural comparators such as Notch1, Notch4, Sox2, and Atoh1. In this brain dataset, these endocrine regulators were themselves FDR-silent or weak, suggesting the canonical NEUROG3 endocrine program is uncoupled here, with the caveat that several endocrine comparators were not screened.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Fgfrl1 showed no convergence with the available FGF/FGFR-related perturbations: across overlaps, its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Fgfr1, Fgfr2, Fgfr3, Fgf13, Fgf14, Flrt3, and Sos1. In 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Fgfrl1 comparisons remained FDR-null and lacked on-target depletion, whereas related perturbations such as Fgfr1 and Fgf13 showed detectable self-transcript depletion; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Rell2 downregulation was also detectable. This constrained contrast is limited because secreted FGFRL1-binding ligands were not assayed.

Itga7 perturbation in 22 assayed non-dopaminergic neuronal classes did not transcriptionally engage the expected integrin–laminin/ECM neighborhood. Although ITGA7 is positioned with ITGB1 and laminin- and dystrophin-associated components, measured transcripts such as Itgb1, Dag1, Lamc1, Dmd, Sgce, and related paralogs showed only a few nominal changes and no FDR-significant feedback, with near-zero related signature correlations. Perturbations of Itgb1, Dag1, Itga6, Dmd, or Sgce likewise did not converge with the Itga7 signature. This negative result is limited to measured transcript-level responses, as ECM signaling may be post-transcriptional.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Stk39 perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from the WNK-SPAK/OSR1-SLC12 cation-chloride pathway in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In these nominally engaged cell types, Wnk1/2/3/4, Oxsr1, Slc12a2, and Slc12a5 showed no significant or compensatory RNA shifts, and Stk39 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Wnk1, Wnk3, Slc12a2, or Slc12a5 perturbations. The 054 CNU-MGE GABA class had only 37 Stk39 cells and a near-signal at Dars, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, direct Slc12a5 perturbation elicited a significant immediate-early response despite Stk39 remaining FDR-silent; these RNA-level data do not test cotransporter phosphorylation or chloride flux directly.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Dlx5 showed no multiple-testing-significant downstream expression response in this dataset, even in GABAergic contexts where a same-dataset comparator was detectable: Arx produced FDR-significant outputs concentrated in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, whereas Dlx5 produced none. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Dlx5 had only the strongest nominal self-decrease without significant Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, or Slc6a1 changes, and there was no clear Dlx6 convergence, suggesting a target-specific mild Dlx5 phenotype rather than general refractoriness of GABAergic homeobox perturbations, with the caveat that Arx was only a biological comparator, not a biochemical positive control for Dlx5 editing.

Lrp2 showed near-zero similarity to related LDL-receptor-family and SHH/BMP-node perturbations, with score-vector correlations almost orthogonal to available comparators (maximum |r|=0.116), even though Sorl1, Lrpap1, Lrp1, and Bmpr2 produced robust signals in the same analysis. This weak, nonconvergent pattern was seen across assayed neuronal transcriptomes, including 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA, where Lrp2 engagement remained undetectable or only nominal. These comparisons rely on weak Lrp2 signatures, and some physical partners such as Cubn and Dab2 were not perturbed.

Slc25a26 showed a flat, comparatively weak perturbation profile: its intended transcript was measured but did not reach FDR-significant self-depletion in any assayed cell type. This contrast was target-specific rather than a generic failure of mitochondrial SLC25-family guides, because Slc25a12, Slc25a4, and Slc25a46 each showed clear self-transcript depletion in multiple matched classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with otherwise sparse downstream mRNA changes in this mitochondrial solute-carrier response context. These comparators are related carriers with distinct substrates, so the contrast does not imply paralog interchangeability.

Slc25a27 showed a distinct, largely uncorrelated perturbation profile rather than phenocopying other measured mitochondrial carrier or oxidative-stress genes. Across the experiment, transcriptome-wide Slc25a27 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Slc25a4, Slc25a12, Slc25a46, Ndufa4, and Park7, even though several of these comparators showed stronger self-depletion. In 155 MB Glut cells, Slc25a27 formed a high-cell group without nominal target knockdown, contrasting with FDR-significant self-depletion for other mitochondrial targets. Interpretation is limited because canonical UCP paralogs such as Ucp1, Ucp2, Ucp3, and Slc25a14 were not perturbed, and the measured SLC25 comparators transport different substrates and generally achieved stronger knockdown.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc25a36 showed broad but weak on-target depletion with no multiple-testing-supported self knockdown across the tested classes, including 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In contrast, other mitochondrial carrier-family perturbations in the same assay—Slc25a4, Slc25a12, and Slc25a46—showed FDR-supported self knockdown in caudal/midbrain populations, including the same cell types where Slc25a36 remained weak. This argues against a general failure to perturb SLC25 carriers, though the comparators transport different substrates and the closest paralog, Slc25a33, was not assayed.

Sil1 perturbation produced transcriptional signatures that were largely orthogonal to ER-chaperone and ER-stress comparators, with a maximum absolute correlation of only 0.144 across matched comparisons to Atf6, Hsp90ab1, Hspa5, Hspa8, Hspd1, and Manf. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Sil1 showed no FDR-significant response and did not resemble strongly engaged Hsp90ab1 perturbations in the same cell types. This argues against a shared acute BiP/UPR-like transcriptomic state under partial Sil1 perturbation, although some comparators, especially Hspa5 and Atf6, also had weak or inconsistent on-target RNA depletion, and these correlations do not measure chaperone activity.

Trpv4 showed little detectable engagement in this neuronal CRISPRi screen: its transcriptomic signature was nearly orthogonal to active Ca2+/TRP-neighbor perturbations, including Calm3, Prkca, Prkcg, Camk2 genes, Trpv1, Trpa1, Trpm3, Trpm7, Pkd1, and Stim1. In contrast, related calcium-channel signaling perturbations produced stronger signatures, and Trpv4 lacked a stable genome-wide signature neighbor across cell types. This restricted-signature result is more consistent with absent Trpv4 engagement in the assay than with a true disconnection from annotated Ca2+:calmodulin, PKC, TRP, or PKD2-linked biology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zeb1 showed its strongest downstream response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Ctbp1 was the top positive transcriptomic neighbor and partially matched the Zeb1 perturbation by upregulating Stxbp2, F11r, and Ap1m2. This pattern is mechanistically coherent with a ZEB1–CTBP corepressor relationship, but the overall genome-wide correlation was weak (Pearson 0.103). The interpretation is therefore suggestive rather than definitive, and it is limited by the absence of Ctbp2 as a direct comparator in the analyzed gene-target set.

Dcx lacked a robust perturbation-signature neighbor: whole-signature score correlations with Pafah1b1, Reln, Tuba1a, Tubb3, and Map1b were near zero, and even the strongest global neighbors such as Npy5r and Fbxo11 were weak. This absence of convergence suggests the Dcx transcriptional effect may be small, cell-state-restricted, or primarily post-transcriptional rather than part of a shared pan-neuronal migration module. Because correlations were computed on Wilcoxon scores across matched genes and cell types, a subtle or morphologic Dcx state would not necessarily be captured by bulk transcriptome similarity.

Zbtb7a perturbation repeatedly produced a conserved mixed neuronal, synapse-linked transcriptional state rather than a rare cell-type-specific effect, with recurrent up-regulation of Gpc1, Pnma3, Pnck, Usp11, and Atp1b2 and down-regulation of Stx16, Ppip5k1, Cacng7, and Gpr108. The strongest responses appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where additional genes such as Akap5, Vgf, Efnb3, Marcksl1, and Rasgrp2 contributed to the pattern. Synapse enrichment was database-derived, and these recurrent genes were not shown to be direct ZBTB7A targets in neurons.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Aimp1 perturbation did not produce a coherent transcriptional response across the cytosolic multi-tRNA synthetase complex in 155 MB Glut neurons: measured MSC member transcripts, including Aimp2, Eef1e1, Eprs, Iars, Lars, Kars, Qars, Rars, Dars, and Wars1, were FDR-negative, with Mars1 showing only an isolated nominal increase in this cell type. This pattern suggests uncoupling at the mRNA readout rather than complex-wide transcript feedback, although only transcript levels were assayed and most core cytosolic MSC genes were not perturbed as separate targets.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Coq5 showed a weak own-transcript response relative to related mitochondrial electron transport perturbations, indicating that the negative result is target-specific rather than a general failure of the dataset to detect mitochondrial knockdown. In 155 MB Glut, Coq5 was only nominally depleted and ranked seventh, while Uqcrc1 was robustly depleted in a comparator perturbation. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Coq5, Pdss1, and Pdss2 were nominally depleted with near-zero cross-perturbation correlations, whereas Ndufa13 and Cox5a were strongly depleted. These comparisons occur within mitochondrial electron transport and OXPHOS linkage, but the targets differ in basal expression and guide efficiency.

Cert1 produced transcriptomic signatures that were nearly orthogonal to related lipid-transfer and sphingolipid perturbations rather than phenocopying adjacent pathway nodes. Across comparable cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, correlations between Cert1 score vectors and Vapb, Sptlc2, Smpd3, Asah1, Sphk1, Stard7, or Osbpl2 were near zero, with maximum absolute related-gene correlation no greater than 0.079, arguing that these perturbations are not interchangeable surrogates for ER-to-Golgi ceramide transfer and sphingomyelin biosynthesis. This interpretation is tempered by the weakness of Cert1 signatures and incomplete coverage of related targets such as Vapa, Ppm1l, Osbp, and sphingomyelin synthases.

Ago2 did not phenocopy other measured AGO/RISC small-RNA pathway perturbations in this adult mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across shared cell types, Ago2 score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Ago1, Dicer1, Tnrc6a, and Tnrc6b, indicating weak and uncoupled RNA signatures despite their curated membership in RISC loading and miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional silencing. This means these related perturbations should not be treated as interchangeable pathway replicates here, although most comparators were also weak, so the contrast is limited to observed transcriptomic signatures rather than proven protein loss-of-function states.

Kctd8 perturbation did not produce detectable transcriptional compensation within the assayed GABAB receptor auxiliary KCTD-GIRK signaling module: Gabbr1, Gabbr2, Kctd16, Gnb1, and Kcnj6 showed no FDR-supported changes in any measured cell class. This argues against receptor-level homeostatic feedback at the mRNA level under these conditions, but the inference is limited to assayed transcripts, since Kctd12 and Kctd12b were not targeted and receptor localization or GIRK currents were not measured.

Kctd8 showed transcriptomic signatures that were nearly orthogonal to related perturbations in the GABAB receptor auxiliary KCTD-GIRK signaling axis: same-cell-type correlations with Kctd16, Kctd1, Gabbr1, Gabbr2, Gnb1, and Kcnj6 never exceeded |r|=0.081, and no strong positive or negative neighbors emerged across the panel. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Kctd8 target decrease was only nominal or lacked FDR support, whereas Gabbr1, Gabbr2, and Gnb1 showed clearer direct depletion, so Kctd8 transcriptomic neighbors do not appear to proxy acute GABAB signaling.

Abca1 was transcriptionally quiet in this dataset, and the same null pattern was seen for the ABCA paralog Abca7, with neither showing FDR-significant responses or a strong shared score-level signature. In contrast, several comparator disease-gene perturbations in the same screen were clearly active, with App, Pld3, Sorl1, and Lrp1 producing robust FDR-level signatures. This suggests the Abca1 null is selective rather than a general failure to detect perturbation effects, although the comparison is based on transcriptomic strength and the active comparators are not all direct ABCA1 pathway members.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Max showed a stronger and broader perturbation signature than related MYC/MAX-network or E-box factors in this dataset, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where the dominant Max-responsive class had 109 FDR-significant genes; similar Max-associated responses were also seen in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. By contrast, Myc and Mycn had no FDR-significant genes despite large cell counts in the strongest Max-responsive class, and Mnt, Mlxip, Tfap4, and Usf1 were also sparse, though these negative comparisons are tempered because their own target transcripts also lacked FDR-significant depletion.

Six5 perturbation did not transcriptionally mobilize known SIX5 cofactors or DM1-locus neighborhood genes in this assay: Eya1–Eya4, Dach1/2, Six2/4, Dmpk, Dmwd, Mbnl1, and Clcn1 showed no FDR-controlled shifts in any assayed brain cell type. This pattern argues against a detectable feed-forward or compensatory response from Six5 to the SIX/EYA/DACH program or the DM1-linked Dmpk-Six5 neighborhood at the transcript level here, while leaving open physical interactions and repeat-expansion chromatin effects that were not tested.

Tnik did not recover a Traf/NCK–JNK/MAPK-like RNA program in this dataset: across matched cell classes, Tnik showed approximately zero transcriptomic similarity to Mapk8, Mapk9, Map3k7, and Traf3 perturbations, so JNK/MAPK-side neighbors and the available TRAF-family perturbation did not phenocopy Tnik at transcriptome scale. This contrasts with non-neuronal reports linking TNIK to JNK and Reactome placement in ROS-MAP3K5 signaling, but the result is qualified because JNK/MAPK activity is phosphorylation-driven and the JNK-side perturbations themselves lacked FDR-significant RNA signatures.

Pnpt1 perturbation did not detectably engage the expected mitochondrial RNA/OXPHOS program in this dataset: none of 273 mitochondrial-encoded transcript tests, including mt-Nd2, mt-Nd3, mt-Atp8, and mt-Cytb, showed a significant response, and the indirect comparator Lrpprc was not correlated with the Pnpt1 score vector. In the largest perturbed-cell class, 155 MB Glut, Pnpt1 target engagement was not evident and mitochondrial or interferon sentinel signals were only nominal. This negative result is qualified by the assay’s limited capture of mitochondrial antisense RNAs or imported tRNAs and by the fact that Pnpt1 itself was not detectably depleted.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mlxip did not behave like the tested Max/Myc branch in this screen: in the nominally target-engaged cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and 308 CB GABA, Mlxip signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Max, Mnt, Myc, and Mycn, even though Max showed many FDR-significant genes in overlapping cell classes. The Mlxip phenotype remained globally weak, with sparse FDR-null downstream changes such as Trim28, Bdnf, Psmd1, and Slc4a10, and the dataset could not directly test interchangeability with Mlx or Mlxipl because those perturbations were absent.

Drd2 perturbation produced weak, nonconvergent transcriptional effects across the 23 assayed neuronal cell classes: score correlations with Drd3, Drd4, Drd5, and Adora2a were near zero, and these related receptor perturbations also lacked measurable self-transcript depletion. In the 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA class, the D2/A2A striatal medium spiny neuron module, including Drd2, Adora2a, Adcy5, Ppp1r1b, Drd3, Drd4, and Drd5, appeared flat and uncoupled. Thus dopamine-family membership or D2/A2A network proximity was not sufficient to yield interchangeable receptor-level Perturb-seq signatures here, although the result is mainly negative rather than definitive mechanistic divergence.

Wnk1 perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from the canonical WNK-SPAK/OSR1-cation-chloride cotransporter axis: Stk39, Oxsr1, Slc12a2, Slc12a5, Wnk3, and Klhl3 showed no nominally significant changes anywhere, while Slc12a6 and Cul3 appeared in only two nominal cell types each and remained non-significant overall. Across all 22 tested cell types, Wnk1 RNA trended downward but produced no FDR-significant genome-wide response, including in 155 MB Glut and 308 CB GABA, and Wnk1 signatures were near-zero correlated with Stk39, Slc12a2, Slc12a5, and Cul3 perturbations, consistent with a pathway effect that may be better reflected by phosphorylation or ion-flux readouts than transcript abundance.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Agrn perturbation in five engaged brain cell types—066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—showed a transcriptional signature that was essentially uncoupled from canonical Agrn pathway and ECM neighbors. In these cells, Agrn score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Lrp4, Musk, Dag1, Large1, Ext1, Ext2, Robo1/2, and Nrxn1/2 perturbations, with all related correlations |r|<=0.095, and even the nearest whole-panel positive or negative neighbors were weak. This indicates signature-level nonconvergence rather than receptor independence, especially because Lrp4 and Musk perturbations were often weakly or not measurably engaged.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Dpm1 knockdown showed its only sub-FDR<0.10 response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Dpm1 and Ttyh3 were down and Pdia6 was up, with Hspa5, Pdia3, Rft1, and Ddit3 increasing only nominally. This pattern suggests a narrow ER folding and lipid-linked-glycan compensation signal, but it is best treated as an exploratory biomarker hypothesis rather than a robust unfolded-protein-response call, since only Ttyh3 and Pdia6 passed FDR<0.10. In the same cell-type context, Manf produced a much stronger Hspa5/Pdia6/Sdf2l1/Dnajb9/Hyou1 response.

Osmr did not phenocopy related IL-6-family receptor perturbations or downstream STAT nodes in the assayed cells. Across 14 Osmr-tested glutamatergic classes and 8 GABA classes, Osmr, Il6st, Il31ra, Il6ra, and Crlf1 receptor signatures were largely silent after FDR correction, and same-cell correlations between Osmr and Il6st, Il31ra, Il6ra, Crlf1, Stat1, Stat3, or Stat5b were near zero, arguing against detectable convergence of OSM-OSMRβ-IL6ST/gp130 signaling or broader JAK/STAT, MAPK, and PI3K/AKT cytokine-response programs. This interpretation is tempered because most receptor-family signatures were weak, and Lifr, Osm, Il31, Jak1, Jak2, and Tyk2 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Kansl1 perturbation produced a recurrent, cell-type-selective signature across 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, marked by downregulation of Ttc4, Nsmce2, Ccdc39, Ppox, Commd4, Ctsa, and Man2b2 with recurrent Dgkz upregulation. A downregulated subset including Becn1, Pik3c3, Stx8, Vti1a, Snf8, M6pr, Tpp1, Ctsa, and Man2b2 mapped to endosomal, vacuolar, lysosomal, and autophagy-transport annotations, although several strongest recurrent genes were not canonical autophagy genes and Stx17/Snap29 were not FDR significant.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Eif4e in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a restricted top-300-gene signature whose strongest positive perturbation neighbors were Uba5, Ufc1, Rrn3, Hspa9, and Psmc5, while no strong negative neighbor emerged. This pattern suggests a chaperone/proteasome-associated proteostasis neighborhood, consistent with Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Stip1, Psmc6, Uba5, Ufc1, and Psmc5 appearing in the Eif4e-positive signature context, and indicates divergence from simple canonical mTOR-pathway comparisons. The result is exploratory because it used only high-scoring Eif4e genes and some neighbor perturbations had uneven own-transcript knockdown.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Trip12 showed reproducible but weak positive signature convergence with the 26S proteasome ATPase perturbations Psmc1 and Psmc5 across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. In these Trip12-responsive cell types, Psmc1/Psmc5 were recurrent top neighbors and shared down-regulation of Trip12-responsive genes including Amy1, Pabpn1, and in 155 MB Glut also Rnpc3, placing the phenotype on a ubiquitin-proteasome protein-homeostasis axis. However, whole-transcriptome correlations were small, one safe-target control appeared among top neighbors in 155 MB Glut, and the comparison remains hypothesis-generating.

Wnk3 perturbation did not produce a transcriptional induction or repression of the WNK-SPAK/OSR1–cation-chloride cotransporter axis: Slc12a2, Slc12a5, Stk39, Oxsr1, and Wnk1 RNA were not measurably changed in any tested cell type, including 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This pattern is more consistent with post-translational WNK3 biology than with an induced SLC12 transcriptional program, but the null RNA result does not establish normal cotransporter activity, which would require phosphoproteomics, surface KCC2, and chloride-flux assays.

Spast did not phenocopy the tubular ER-shaping HSP module in this assay: across matched cell types, its whole-transcriptome score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Atl1, Reep1, Reep2, and Atl3, even though these proteins are linked in tubular ER shaping and ER–microtubule coupling. This lack of convergence suggests that physical or disease-module proximity did not translate into transcriptomic interchangeability here. The comparison is tempered by generally weak Spast signatures, and Atl3 was co-measured in only 15 of the 22 Spast cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sox17 showed no FDR-significant response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, even though this was the largest Sox17 stratum (n=276), suggesting the null was not simply due to sampling. In the same thalamic glutamatergic class, Sox2 and Sox5 perturbations with fewer cells produced detectable corrected changes, including Tnnt1/Stam and Dgkh/Tnnt1, indicating that sparse SOX-family effects were detectable in this dataset. However, Sox2 and Sox5 are not SOXF paralogs of Sox17, and the shared Tnnt1 readout is only a dataset contrast rather than an established shared direct target.

Sacs showed an uncoupled transcriptomic profile from mitochondrial fission and mitochondrial quality-control perturbations: unlike Dnm1l and Opa1, which produced many significant expression changes, Sacs did not significantly alter Dnm1l, Opa1, or Mff transcripts and its signature did not correlate with those perturbations. This null pattern was also explicit in 308 CB GABA cells, where broader chaperone, mitochondrial, and cytoskeletal neighbor contrasts failed to reveal a Sacs-like program. A key caveat is that prior SACS-related transcriptomic and mitochondrial phenotypes came largely from knockdown cells or patient fibroblasts, whereas these Perturb-seq cells differed in species and timescale, and Sacs transcript reduction was weak.

Gdap1 was not transcriptomically interchangeable with direct mitochondrial-dynamics perturbations in this atlas: its score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Dnm1l, Opa1, and Mff, and unlike Dnm1l and Opa1, Gdap1 did not produce an FDR-level transcriptome-wide signature. In the best-supported glutamatergic context, 155 MB Glut, Opa1 and Dnm1l showed detectable signatures in related midbrain cells whereas Gdap1 was largely silent, suggesting the weak Gdap1 result is not simply because neuronal mitochondrial-dynamics stress is invisible here. This comparison is based on transcriptome correlations rather than mitochondrial morphology or biochemical readouts, and Gdap1 itself showed weak on-target engagement.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Lmbr1 showed weak, target-specific perturbation effects that were largely uncoupled from SHH/Hedgehog outputs across 052 Pvalb Gaba, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. In contrast, Cdon, Gli1, and Smo perturbations produced stronger FDR-level signatures in overlapping cell types, yet their transcriptome-wide score vectors were nearly orthogonal to Lmbr1, with tiny pairwise correlations to Cdon/Ptch/Smo/Gli signatures. Notably, 052 Pvalb Gaba showed only a near-threshold Lmbr1 biomarker signal, Htatsf1 up-regulation, while comparators were stronger; however, comparator signals came from separate guides and Lmbr1 itself was only weakly engaged.

Six5 did not converge with available SIX-family perturbations or with any strong screen-wide signature neighbor in these brain cell types. Across cell types, Six5 versus Six1, Six3, and Six6 score correlations never exceeded |r| = 0.064, and even in the strongest Six5 contexts—such as 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut—the best neighbors remained tiny, consistent with no detectable correlated response in the SIX/EYA/DACH transcriptional regulation module. This interpretation is tempered because Six2, Six4, and Eya1–Eya4 were not perturbed, and the Six5 signatures themselves were weak.

Mast1 showed an uncoupled transcriptomic signature from the available syntrophin/dystrophin/PTEN-neighborhood perturbations: despite reported links to Sntb2, dystrophin/utrophin, and PTEN, the Pten and Dmd perturbations were essentially uncorrelated with Mast1, and its strongest positive or negative signature neighbors were weak, including among the two cell types with the lowest Mast1 FDR values. This suggests that known MAST1 network membership did not predict its acute Perturb-seq RNA state, with the caveat that Sntb2 and MAST-family paralogs were not perturbed and correlations were assessed only from transcriptome-wide Wilcoxon score vectors.

Fmn1 showed no shared transcriptome-wide signature with the related formin perturbations Fmn2 or Diaph2: across the 22 shared cell classes, the Fmn1 and Fmn2 signatures were essentially orthogonal, and the two available Diaph2 profiles were also uncorrelated with Fmn1. This suggests that paralog redundancy cannot be inferred from the transcriptome alone in this panel, but the interpretation is limited because Fmn1 lacked validated target engagement and the Diaph2 comparisons came from only two low-count, non-engaged classes.

Pknox2 showed no strong whole-screen signature neighbor: excluding Pknox2 itself, the largest absolute correlation with any other perturbation was only 0.206, and in 20 of 21 cell types the maximum absolute correlation was 0.122 or less. The largest correlation occurred in 308 CB GABA, where the Pknox2 target row was not nominally significant. In 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, the smallest adjusted P value was driven by nominal Jag2 and Adamts10 up-regulation, but all rows were FDR-nonsignificant and the top positive neighbor was the safe-target perturbation Safe_target_91, arguing against a hidden convergent module involving comparators such as Gabra3 or Msx2.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Fbxo11 showed a nonconvergent perturbation pattern across matched neuronal cell types, with near-zero transcriptomic correlations to the ubiquitin-ligase relatives Fbxo38, Fbxw7, and Cul3 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA. This suggests that the canonical protein-degradation pathway was not recovered as a shared mRNA signature and that these perturbations were not surrogates for Fbxo11, although the comparison was limited to a small set of relatives and Fbxo11 signatures were weak.

Pum1 perturbation produced a transcriptomic signature that was nearly orthogonal to Cnot1, Fmr1, and Ddx3x, with only very small mean cosine similarities even among its strongest positive or negative global signature neighbors. This argues that, in this mouse-brain readout, Pum1 did not converge with related RNA-regulatory perturbations and was not simply reflecting a generic RNA-regulatory stress state. The inference is limited because the comparison used weak full-gene Pum1 signatures, and Pum2, Cnot7, and Cnot8 were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Chn1 showed little transcriptional signal in this assay: in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Chn1 had no target depletion or FDR-significant hits, even though several comparator perturbations in the same class were successfully depleted. Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 053 Sst Gaba cells, Epha4 knockdown usually yielded a corrected signature dominated by Epha4 RNA depletion itself, with no broad EphA4/ephrinB3 axon-guidance program and no Chn1-correlated neighbor; this is consistent with a largely non-transcriptional CHN1–EphA4–Rac1 process, though the inference is indirect because the profiled brain classes are not embryonic growth cones.

Set showed a weak transcriptional signature that was uncoupled from the PP2A-axis comparator Ppp2r1a. In the same 22 Set-profiled cell types, Ppp2r1a perturbation was highly active, with 3,147 FDR<0.05 genes, yet full Set-versus-Ppp2r1a score-vector correlations were near zero, despite the SET-PP2A context involving Anp32a, Ppp2cb, and Setbp1. Genome-wide differential expression after Set was dominated by nominal effects, and transcript-level on-target engagement for Set was not detected, consistent with failure to engage the SET-PP2A module at the transcriptome level, while noting that Ppp2r1a loss is not the mechanistic inverse of Set loss.

Klf13 was uncoupled from the SIN3A-associated transcriptional repression phenotype: although KLF13 is connected to SIN3A, CREBBP, and HDAC1-linked regulation, Sin3a perturbation was highly active in the same atlas while Klf13 produced no FDR-significant downstream genes and showed little score-level similarity to Sin3a. This argues that Klf13 is not a dominant or rate-limiting neuronal entry point into the broad Sin3a program in these cell classes. Even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Klf13 had its nearest hit, Klf13 itself remained inactive; given Sin3a’s pleiotropy, this non-phenocopy is not a strict contradiction.

Tcf3 in this dataset behaved as official Tcf3/E2A rather than the Wnt “TCF3” node: its perturbation signature was essentially uncorrelated with the beta-catenin–TCF/LEF Wnt comparators Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2, despite robust Wnt-like responses from those comparators across the same 22 cell classes. Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 showed 493 and 141 FDR-significant rows, respectively, whereas Tcf3 showed none, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. Because Tcf7l1 was not perturbed here, the contrast relies on Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 as Wnt pathway references.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Herc2 did not phenocopy related perturbations in matched neuronal contexts: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ube3a and Herc1 showed nominal self-depletion yet their whole-transcriptome signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Herc2, and Igf1r was also uncorrelated. The same lack of convergence was seen across 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, where Herc2 itself was weak and only Rack1 was significantly up-regulated downstream. These comparisons were based on weak signatures, with Ube3a and Herc1 self-depletion in 151 nominal or sub-FDR rather than FDR significant.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Minpp1 did not phenocopy nearby inositol or phosphoinositide perturbations: in the six cell types where Minpp1 was most strongly depleted—005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 053 Sst Gaba, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—its same-cell-type signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Inpp5k, Plcb1, and Itpr1, with maximum |Pearson r| of 0.044. This argues against a generic PI-cycle or IP3-receptor transcriptional program as the immediate output of Minpp1 knockdown, although the comparison is limited to same-cell-type scalar score correlations and some comparator perturbations had weaker on-target knockdown.

Lrch1 did not recover the expected LRCH1–DOCK8–CDC42/PAK cytoskeletal signaling module at steady-state RNA level: across shared cell-type groups, Lrch1 signatures correlated only weakly with Cdc42 or Pak1, and Cdc42/Pak1 perturbations were largely self-contained. This was evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Lrch1 had its strongest nominal self-score yet Cdc42 and Pak1 showed the strongest self-knockdowns without downstream FDR-significant genes; similar Pak1-only self-depletion without downstream response appeared in 191 MB P MY GABA, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. Because Dock8 and LRCH paralogs were not perturbed, and no CDC42-GTP, actin, morphology, or migration assays were measured, the axis may be buffered, non-transcriptional, or not engaged in these cell types.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
full_finding_text: Slf2 showed a distinct transcriptional pattern that Nsmce2 and Atr did not phenocopy. In the 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut cell type, Slf2 was associated with Ppp5c upregulation—the only FDR-significant Slf2 differential signal—and this Ppp5c response was not reproduced by Nsmce2 or Atr, which also had near-zero genome-wide score correlations with Slf2. Thus, within the RAD18-SLF1/2-SMC5/6 DNA damage response and ATR checkpoint/PPP5C context, the data indicate a lack of observed transcriptional convergence, although Nsmce2 and Atr perturbations were weak overall, limiting mechanistic interpretation.

Smchd1 did not recapitulate the expected LRIF1-linked heterochromatin module in this mouse brain Perturb-seq screen: across 22 matched cell types, Smchd1 and Lrif1 signatures were nearly uncorrelated (median Pearson r = 0.0076), and Lrif1 itself had no corrected hits. This argues that the neuronal assay did not engage the SMCHD1-LRIF1/D4Z4 repression context, though poor Lrif1 engagement remains a caveat. Notably, the dataset still detected corrected effects for the related SMC-family perturbation Smc1a, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells where Smchd1 was null.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Trhr showed a null result in the high-cell neuronal classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: despite 105 and 86 perturbed cells, respectively, there was no detectable on-target engagement or FDR-level downstream response. In these same broad classes, comparator perturbations Thra, Adcy3, and Camk2b showed measurable to strong target-transcript depletion, suggesting the Trhr null is target- or engagement-specific rather than a universal failure of the DE pipeline. This comparison is qualified by the comparators having larger perturbed-cell counts and not being one-to-one TRHR pathway members.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarcc2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a predominantly depleted synaptic receptor, adhesion, and postsynaptic membrane transcriptomic program, with downregulation of Ptprz1, Grin2b, Gabra4, Gabbr1, Grid1, Nlgn2, and Lrrtm1, alongside depletion of Ptpn3, Reep2, Tiam1, C1qtnf4, and the label gene Prkcd. A smaller set of synaptic genes, including Clstn1, Grin3a, and Grm5, was induced, indicating a mixed rather than unidirectional response. These data link Smarcc2 to maintenance of a mature synaptic transcriptome, although the pathway assignment is based on gene-expression patterns and does not measure synapse number or electrophysiology.

Kcnt2 showed essentially no transcriptomic convergence with Kcnt1 or other neuronal potassium-channel perturbations in this dataset: across the 22 shared cell types, Kcnt2–Kcnt1 Wilcoxon-score correlations were near zero, and correlations with Kcnma1, Kcnc1, Kcnn2, Kcnn3, Kcnq2, Kcnq3, Kcnh1, and Kctd16 were similarly weak. This suggests Kcnt2 should not be collapsed into the same module as related KNa or broader potassium-channel genes here, although the inference is tempered by weak Kcnt2 score profiles and lack of clear target-transcript depletion, which could reflect ineffective perturbation rather than true biological uncoupling.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Gphn perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut cells produced a nominal synaptic/postsynaptic transcriptional cloud, including Bdnf, Lrrc4c, Cplx1, Dscam, Lrrtm3, Grik5, Mapk8ip2, Slc1a2, Nos1ap, and Dlgap2, but only Cbarp was FDR-significant. In contrast, canonical inhibitory receptor-clustering and molybdenum-cofactor genes such as Gabrg2, Arhgef9, Glrb, Nlgn2, Slc12a5, Mocs1, Mocs2, and Gabarap were not FDR-regulated in any Gphn contrast. This suggests a broad synaptic remodeling signature rather than a simple transcriptional readout of gephyrin’s known scaffold or cofactor-related functions.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Mecp2 showed a divergent transcriptomic signature from nearby chromatin/corepressor and Rett-family perturbations across 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Even where Mecp2 responses were clearest, Sin3a produced many FDR-significant genes yet had near-zero full-score correlation with Mecp2, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut the best related-target matches were only weak, such as Tbl1xr1 at r=0.0958. This suggests that acute loss of Mecp2 is not interchangeable with Sin3a, Tbl1x/Tbl1xr1, Mbd2/Mbd5, Dnmt3a, Hdac4/5/8, Cdkl5, or Foxg1 at the whole-transcriptome level, with the caveat that editing efficiency, expression, and essentiality may differ across perturbations.

Mef2d showed a restricted, weak transcriptional signature that was largely uncorrelated with perturbations of Mef2a, Mef2c, Hdac4, Hdac5, Hdac8, Camk2a, Camk2b, Camk4, Creb1, Nfatc3, and Myod1, with whole-panel correlations never exceeding |r| = 0.177 and no strong positive or negative signature neighbor. In 155 MB Glut cells, where on-target Mef2d depletion was best, the response was limited to target-dominated nominal hits without FDR-supported downstream pathway coupling, arguing that this acute knockdown did not resolve a CaMK/MAPK/CREB/HDAC-linked MEF2 module, while leaving open protein-level MEF2 activity not captured by the weak RNA signature.

Add1 did not show mRNA convergence with measured perturbations in the actin-spectrin membrane skeleton and ankyrin-linked cytoskeleton: across the available targets, including Actb, Actg1, Ank1, Ank2, Ank3, Cdc42, Pak1, Prkca, Rac1, Sptan1, and Sptb, Add1 signature correlations were near zero overall, with a reported median same-cell-type correlation of about 0.007. This suggests the broader Add1 cytoskeletal neighborhood was not recovered as a transcriptomic module in this dataset, although only measured targets were tested and the Add1 signature itself was weak.

Msi1 was FDR-null in this atlas and did not phenocopy nearby Notch/PTEN perturbations: although Pten and Mib1 produced FDR-scale signatures elsewhere in the same dataset, Msi1, along with Notch3, Dll1, Psen1, Notch2, Adam10, and Pum1, was FDR-null, and restricted correlations between the top 200 Msi1 features and these neighbors were near zero. This argues that the weak Msi1 signal is specific in these profiled neurons rather than a global failure to detect PI3K/Notch-neighbor phenotypes, but the comparison is exploratory because it used only the top Msi1 features per cell type.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ndn knockdown was largely uncoupled from an E2F/cell-cycle module across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In this dataset, Ndn typically showed only self-transcript depletion, with no FDR-significant downstream mRNA changes, whereas E2f4 produced a detectable cell-cycle-like program including Aaas, Rad18, Tacc3, Tube1, and Blm. Ndn also showed little whole-signature similarity to Trp53, E2f1, E2f4, Dlx5, or Dlx6 perturbations, arguing against an acute Cdk1-like stress response, although the comparison is indirect because E2f4 serves only as an E2F-family proxy and some comparator perturbations had weak target depletion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnn3 showed a weak, nominally engaged signature only in the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class, where its transcriptional state was nearly orthogonal to related membrane-excitability perturbations. In this cell type, Kcnn2, Calm1, Calm3, Kcnma1, Kcnq2, Cacna1g, Atp2b1, Uba5, and Stub1 did not phenocopy Kcnn3, and even the strongest genome-wide same-cell-type neighbor was only r = 0.075. This suggests that, in this assay, Kcnn3 was not embedded in a shared Ca2+-activated K+ channel/calmodulin-gated excitability signature, although the weak query and single-cell-class context leave insufficient target engagement as a caveat.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Trp53 showed no conventionally significant transcriptomic response in this cell-type-resolved brain Perturb-seq dataset, suggesting a target-specific null rather than a global lack of power. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Trp53 remained FDR-null despite 251 perturbed cells and no clear on-target knockdown, while Pten and E2f4 produced strong significant programs; similar contrasts were seen in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, where comparator tumor-suppressor and E2F cell-cycle perturbations, including Crebbp in the same dataset, yielded detectable signatures with comparable or fewer cells. These comparators are same-dataset benchmarks, not linear Trp53 complex members, so they support a buffered Trp53 response rather than a p53-specific neighbor effect.

Itgb2 was uncoupled from the assayed integrin- and immune-adjacent perturbations across matched Itgb2 cell types, with whole-transcriptome correlations near zero for Itgb1, Itga4, Itga6, C3, Cd14, Csf1r, Ptprc, Rac1, and Cdc42. Across all 22 profiled Itgb2 neuronal subclasses, this argues against a robust shared beta-2 integrin leukocyte adhesion or ICAM/C3/fibrinogen receptor signaling axis in the assayed neurons. A key caveat is that direct CD18 alpha partners Itgal, Itgam, Itgax, and Itgad were not perturbed, and the available RNA-based comparator signatures were often weak; the only nominal integrin-family change was a non-significant Itgb1 decrease in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Tcf20 perturbation did not significantly recover the reported TCF20–TDG–TCF4 neurogenesis axis or the associated synaptic-marker response in this dataset: Tdg, Tcf4, Bdnf, Dlg4, Fos, Gabra1, Gabra5, Gria2, and Grin2b were all FDR-negative. This held even in the highest-count contrast in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, where Tcf4 showed only the strongest nominal response and weak neighbor correlation. Given weak target engagement and the mature single-cell assay context, these results refine rather than contradict prior embryonic or cultured-neuron studies.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Thbd showed no convergence with coagulation, complement, TAM, Toll-like, or endothelial pathway neighbors in the strongest tested neuronal cell types, including 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA. Across these contexts, score-vector correlations between Thbd and F2, C3, Cd46, Serpine2, Axl, Mertk, Kdr, Tek, Tlr2, and Tlr4 stayed near zero (|r| ≤ 0.057). In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Serpine2 knockdown was detectable whereas Thbd showed no significant downstream response, suggesting this lack of convergence was Thbd-specific; these comparisons reflect DE score-vector correlations among pathway neighbors rather than obligatory complex partners.

Adgrl3 did not phenocopy engaged latrophilin paralogs or its Tenm3/FLRT ligand neighborhood at the whole-transcriptome level. In 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and also 052 Pvalb Gaba, Adgrl3 showed self-knockdown, but no non-target genes were FDR-significant in the glutamatergic contexts, and score-vector correlations with Adgrl1, Adgrl2, Tenm3, Flrt3, and Tenm4 were near zero. This comparison is limited because Flrt3 and Tenm4 had weak or absent self-knockdown, and it reflects transcriptomic correlation rather than a direct synaptic phenotype.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Mafb perturbation in mature Pvalb interneurons did not produce a convergent large-Maf/AP-1 transcription-factor signature: the Mafb singleton signature was nearly uncorrelated with Maf and Mafa, and even its strongest positive or negative genome-wide neighbor was very weak (|r|<0.07). In the only class with any Mafb FDR hit, 052 Pvalb Gaba, there was a Ccdc88a decrease but no detectable Mafb knockdown and no change in reported Maf/Mafb interneuron markers; in 053 Sst Gaba, there were no Mafb FDR genes. These comparisons rely on weak signatures, with Maf, Mafa, and Mafb rows all having FDR=1 in PV/SST classes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grin2b loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed strong target depletion but an almost absent secondary transcriptomic response, with only Grin2b and Pianp reaching FDR, whereas Grin1 perturbation in the same thalamic glutamatergic state produced a much broader response with 89 FDR genes. This divergence suggests that the obligatory NMDAR subunit Grin1 and the GluN2B subunit are not interchangeable proxies in this cell type, although the larger Grin1 effect may partly reflect stronger knockdown potency rather than subunit biology alone.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Cox7b showed a divergent, mostly self-transcript-only Perturb-seq profile rather than the shared RNA response seen for some other Complex IV subunits. Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and 053 Sst Gaba, Cox7b had no corrected downstream genes and near-zero score-vector correlations with Cox5a, Ndufa4, and Cox4i1, even though those comparators showed stronger exact-target depletion. The only FDR-significant Cox7b-associated signal was Eepd1 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, while exploratory mt-Cytb and mt-Nd5 increases were nominal. These comparisons are based on RNA correlations and FDR counts, not protein knockdown or respiratory-complex activity.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Trip11 showed a selective null in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset: unlike the broader intracellular-transport perturbations Dctn1 and Dync1h1, which produced strong microtubule-associated transport response signatures, especially in midbrain populations, Trip11 remained FDR-null and nearly uncorrelated with those signatures across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. In 155 MB Glut, the largest Trip11 sample, Dctn1/Dync1h1 were active while Trip11 stayed silent; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Trip11 had nominal target-transcript signal without downstream response. This supports a specific Trip11 null rather than a general neuronal inability to mount transport-stress signatures, although direct golgin or TRIP11-complex comparators were largely unavailable.

Ppp3ca knockdown did not produce a canonical calcineurin-NFAT transcriptional feedback signature: Nfatc1/2/3/4/5, Nfatc2ip, and Rcan1/2/3 transcripts were not FDR-significant in any cell class. The strongest non-target response appeared in the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic class, where Ppp3ca, Iyd, Ptpn3, and Pik3r1 changed and Pcsk1n increased, while Ppp3r1 partially converged. This pattern is consistent with an RNA-only readout capturing a noncanonical module while missing calcineurin’s canonical post-translational NFAT activation, including phosphorylation state, nuclear import, or transient activity-dependent transcripts.

P2ry12 was largely buffered across the 21 assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, showing no target-transcript depletion and no FDR-significant downstream differential-expression event, and similar buffering was seen for related purinergic or microglia-associated receptors including P2ry14, P2rx2, Adora2a, Cx3cr1, Csf1r, and Trem2. In contrast, the generic GPCR beta subunit Gnb1 showed clear on-target depletion and downstream signals in several neuron classes, suggesting that the P2ry12 null is limited by receptor and cell context rather than a general inability to detect GPCR-associated perturbations; however, Gnb1 is not P2ry12-specific, and closer partners such as P2ry13 and Gnai1/2/3 were not testable here.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nkx6-2 showed a weak, largely noise-dominated phenotype: in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 308 CB GABA, its signatures were nearly orthogonal to screened oligodendrocyte-lineage, SOX-family, and NKX-family perturbations, including Myrf, Sox10, Sox9, Tcf7l2, Cspg4, Nkx2-1, Nkx2-5, Nkx3-1, and Zfp536. Unbiased nearest neighbors were weak, skewed toward 308 CB GABA, and partly included safe-target-like controls, so related-signature rescue did not work. These comparisons rely on weak restricted signatures, and overexpression literature for SOX10/OLIG2/NKX6.2 is not directly comparable to neuronal Nkx6-2 loss.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Foxp3 showed no hidden FOXP-family or signature-neighbor convergence across the profiled neuronal and glial cell types, including cortical IT and ET glutamatergic populations, multiple GABAergic classes, hypothalamic and thalamic glutamatergic cells, midbrain populations, dopaminergic cells, pineal glutamatergic cells, and cerebellar GABA cells. Foxp3 score correlations with Foxp1 and Foxp2 were near zero globally, and the best global signature neighbor was only weakly correlated (r=0.036), arguing against a shared forkhead-family response; however, this analysis may be noise-dominated because Foxp3 lacked a robust FDR-significant signature.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Kcnab1 knockdown did not produce a simple mRNA compensation program in the strongest on-target contexts, including 052 Pvalb Gaba and 046 CTX-CGE GABA. In these cells, Kcnab2 was not reproducibly induced, and the reciprocal perturbation likewise did not induce Kcnab1; Kcna1 and Kcna2 also were not detectably induced, indicating no coherent Kv1/Shaker auxiliary- or alpha-subunit transcript response. This argues against straightforward transcriptional replacement of lost Kvβ1, while leaving open post-translational trafficking, channel assembly, or other physiologic compensation not measured by mRNA abundance.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Xylt1 showed weaker Perturb-seq effects than related proteoglycan/glycosaminoglycan perturbations. In 155 MB Glut, Agrn, Ext2, and Hs6st2 had FDR-supported on-target depletion while Xylt1 remained non-significant and its checked signature neighbors were weak; in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, B3gat3 produced two FDR-significant downstream rows whereas Xylt1 had none. This argues that these cell classes could register GAG-axis perturbations, although the comparison is tempered because most stronger signals reflect target-RNA depletion rather than a shared downstream module, and the genes occupy different parts of proteoglycan biology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nkain2 showed no detected Perturb-seq effect: across tested cell types, including the highest-cell-count 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population, Nkain2 had no FDR-supported downstream differential expression and no detectable transcript depletion or enrichment. In the same dataset, Na,K-ATPase alpha-subunit perturbations provided a clear comparator, with Atp1a3 knockdown producing a strong mixed ion-channel/synaptic response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut involving genes such as Atp2a2, Ache, Prkcg, Ptpn5, Grin2a, Slc17a6, Kcnj9, Kcnj3, and Scn1b, while Atp1a2 was also silent. Because ATPase beta subunits and Nkain paralogs were not assayed, this contrast reflects both pathway divergence and uncertain guide engagement for Nkain2.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Arid2 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class produced a mixed synaptic and cell-junction response rather than a generic chromatin signature: Kcnj9, L1cam, Cntn1, Cdh11, Adam9, Nrxn1 and related neuronal adhesion or membrane genes were up-regulated, while Prkcd, Stxbp2, Rsrp1 and other cytoskeletal or signaling genes were down-regulated. The 56-gene response was enriched for cell junction, synapse, synaptic membrane and presynaptic membrane terms, but this enrichment in one responsive cell class does not by itself show direct ARID2 binding at these loci.

Dab1 did not show a detectable shared transcriptional module with the canonical Reelin-pathway perturbations Reln, Vldlr, Lrp8, and Fyn. Across the 20 Dab1-shared cell classes, these perturbations also lacked FDR-significant target-transcript depletion, and their score-vector correlations with Dab1 were weak (all |r|≤0.108), indicating no convergent FDR mRNA signature for Reelin-DAB1 tyrosine-phosphorylation signaling in this assay. In the best-powered cell type, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Dab1 itself showed no self-knockdown and no significant genes, so the result is best read as assay/pathway uncoupling rather than a mechanistic contradiction.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Sh3kbp1 showed no strong transcriptional convergence with CIN85-adjacent perturbations in 145 MH-LH TH Glut cells, the main cell type where Sh3kbp1 had a detectable downstream hit. In this cell type, Cblb, Cd2ap, Dab1, Dnm1, Dnm2, Drd2, Reln, Sos1, and Vldlr signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Sh3kbp1, despite pathway links to Cbl/Cblb-dependent receptor endocytosis, Reelin-Dab1 signaling, and dopamine receptor endocytosis. This suggests a transcriptionally buffered or uncoupled module, with the caveat that the Sh3kbp1 signature was small, several related perturbations had weak own-transcript knockdown, and genes such as Cbl, Egfr, Sh3gl, and Arap were not assayed.

Psen1 showed near-zero restricted-signature similarity to APP-processing and Alzheimer-family perturbations, including App, Sorl1, Adam10, Bin1, Mapt, Abca7, and Trem2, and it also lacked a strong positive or negative signature neighbor across the library. In this acute mouse neuronal CRISPR dataset, no perturbation strongly reproduced or opposed the Psen1 transcriptional state, so Psen1 should not be grouped with those disease- or pathway-proximal genes on the basis of this RNA signature. This conclusion is mainly a negative result because correlations were limited to the top 50 Psen1 genes per cell type and Psen1 itself was weak.

Mnt showed a sparse response in these mouse-brain cell types and was not globally interchangeable with other MYC/MAX/MNT E-box network perturbations: full-transcriptome signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Max, Myc, Mycn, Mga, Sin3a, Tcf4, and Usf1, despite known MNT-MAX and MNT-SIN3A interaction context. The data therefore support only limited module-level convergence, including small clock-gene signals involving Per1, Per2, Cry1, and Cry2, rather than a high-dimensional phenocopy. This apparent orthogonality may partly reflect weak Mnt engagement and the insensitivity of whole-signature Pearson correlations to small coordinated modules.

Reln perturbation produced transcriptome-wide signatures that were essentially orthogonal to perturbations of nearby Reelin-network genes, including Dab1, Lrp8, Vldlr, Fyn, Itgb1, and Sh3kbp1, with same-cell-type Pearson correlations near zero. Thus, despite these genes belonging to Reelin-mediated VLDLR/LRP8–DAB1–Fyn signaling, the measured RNA signatures should not be interpreted as a canonical Reelin cascade activity score. A key caveat is that weak Reln target engagement could obscure a true ligand phenotype, and these data reflect RNA correlations rather than biochemical readouts such as phospho-DAB1 or receptor occupancy.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rorc did not phenocopy the ROR-family paralog Rora in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. In this thalamic glutamatergic class, Rora perturbation produced a strong transcriptional program, including Nr1d1 and neuronal genes, with 278 FDR-significant genes, whereas Rorc and Rorb produced none, and the Rora–Rorc score correlation was essentially zero (r=0.007). Rorc signatures were also uncorrelated with other assayed ROR paralogs and REV-ERB neighbors, arguing for strong cell-context specificity in RORA/B/C and NR1D1 RORE-dependent circadian transcription, although poor Rorc target engagement could contribute.

Mchr1 showed no clear transcriptional convergence with the assayed ciliary-trafficking or ciliary-GPCR perturbations Ahi1, Bbs5, Bbs9, Npy2r, and Sstr5, and its signature-neighbor screen did not yield a strong recurrent positive or negative neighbor. This uncoupling suggests that, in this dataset, the known BBSome-dependent ciliary trafficking of MCHR1 protein was not captured as an Mchr1-like RNA-state signature. Interpretation is limited because the comparison relied on weak perturbational score correlations, and Bbs1, Bbs2, Bbs4, Sstr3, and the ligand Pmch were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Nr1i3 showed no multiple-testing-significant downstream transcriptional changes in any assayed neuronal class, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where the largest perturbed-cell count was obtained. This does not appear to reflect a global failure to detect nuclear-receptor biology in the matrix, because Nr1d1 produced a 116-gene FDR-significant response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Nr1d2 significantly induced Nr1d1 across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with genes including Erc2, Pdgfa, and Cacna2d3. These comparators are same-family nuclear receptors rather than direct CAR-complex controls, so the contrast supports a target- and context-specific null for Nr1i3 rather than a mechanistic CAR inference.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Vsx1 perturbation showed a significant response only in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells, but this response was uncoupled from the retinal cone-bipolar and OFF-bipolar program associated with Vsx1 in retina. In this brain cell class, Rcvrn, Tacr3, Neto1, Cabp5, Irx5, Grm6, Gpr179, Nyx, Trpm1, Vsx2, Otx2, Crx, Neurod1, and Ptf1a showed no effect, and there was no convergence with Vsx2 or other retinal-neighbor perturbations. Because the assay profiled mouse brain rather than retina, the absent marker response does not contradict retinal knockout phenotypes.

Zfp266 showed no strong same-cell transcriptional convergence with assayed chromatin regulators in this dataset: correlations with Setdb1, Dnmt3a, Chd4, Smarca2, and Smarca4 were weak, and full-signature comparisons did not reveal any recurrent positive or negative neighbor. Thus, despite ZFP266 being a KRAB-ZFP, the measured brain-cell mRNA response did not collapse onto a generic chromatin-repression program. This interpretation is limited by the weak Zfp266 signature and by comparing against broad chromatin regulators rather than a biochemically matched ZFP266 cofactor series.

Kcna1 perturbation produced RNA signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with Kcna2, Kcnab1, Kcnab2, Kcnq2, and Kcnq3, indicating no recurrent mRNA compensation or cross-perturbation transcriptomic convergence within the Kv1 voltage-gated potassium-channel complex in this atlas. This lack of correlation was observed despite stronger detectable on-target depletion for some other channel genes, including Kcnab2 and Kcnq2. Because the Kcna1 RNA signature was weak, the result refines rather than excludes related channel-level or electrophysiological convergence.

Dyrk1a did not converge transcriptomically with App, Psen1, Mapt, Gsk3b, or other disease-neighbor perturbations in this assay: genome-wide score correlations were near zero, and Dyrk1a lacked any strong positive or negative non-self neighbor, with the strongest across all classes reaching only |r|=0.192. This pattern suggests that Dyrk1a does not simply phenocopy APP/tau/GSK3B or the broader Down-syndrome and Alzheimer APP/tau/NFAT neighborhood at the mRNA level, although most Dyrk1a signatures were weak, so low correlations could also reflect limited perturbation engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Esrra showed exploratory positive restricted-signature convergence with Ppargc1a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, consistent with a possible shared PGC-1α/ERRα coactivator module. Across the 56 non-target FDR genes in the Esrra thalamic signature, the Ppargc1a-targeted perturbation ranked 3rd of 2,045 non-Esrra perturbations by Pearson correlation. However, this remains a signature-neighbor hypothesis because Ppargc1a mRNA was not depleted and the Ppargc1a perturbation had no FDR genes in the same class.

Dnajb6 showed no robust signature neighbor or detectable convergence pattern in this dataset. Across full-transcriptome comparisons, the nearest perturbation had only a near-zero correlation and the strongest anticorrelation was similarly minimal; even analyses restricted to nominal Dnajb6 signature rows yielded only weak positive and negative maxima. The assayed DNAJB-family comparator Dnajb4 likewise showed no FDR-level responses across classes, suggesting practical weakness rather than a shared DNAJB-family response. Because the Dnajb6 signature itself is intrinsically weak, these near-zero correlations should not be interpreted as mechanistic links.

Ago1 perturbation was largely uncoupled from the assayed miRNA-silencing axis across 20 shared Ago1 cell types: its transcriptomic signature was nearly uncorrelated with Ago2, Dicer1, Tnrc6a, and Tnrc6b perturbations, and it did not produce FDR-level feedback on measured RISC/miRNA machinery transcripts including Ago1, Ago2, Ago3, Ago4, Dicer1, Drosha, Dgcr8, Tnrc6a, Tnrc6b, and Xpo5. Because the related perturbations also showed weak FDR-level outputs, this lack of convergence may reflect perturbation weakness rather than a definitive absence of shared AGO1/miRNA RISC pathway effects.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ndufaf5 showed only a weak signature-neighbor pattern in 308 CB GABA cells: its perturbation signature was positively correlated with Lonp1, Ptcd3, and Ndufb9, but Safe_target_81 and Safe_target_15 controls appeared in the same correlation tail at similar magnitudes. Thus, 308 CB GABA is the only cell type with a suggestive Ndufaf5 pattern, and even there the observation remains exploratory because target engagement was weak and the signal was not strong enough to support confident pathway convergence.

Cd3g did not phenocopy the related TCR-CD3 complex genes Cd3d, Cd3e, or Cd247: all assayed CD3 subunit perturbations were weak at transcriptome-wide FDR control, and Cd3g showed near-zero genome-wide correlation with the Cd3d/Cd3e/Cd247 signatures rather than forming a coherent transcriptional module. In neurons, this nonconvergence across the TCR-CD3 receptor complex and signaling partners such as Lck, Lat, and Zap70 is most consistent with loss of biological context or a low-amplitude, out-of-context signal, rather than distinct neuronal functions for individual CD3 subunits.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ddx39b showed its dominant, FDR-resolved transcriptional response in 191 MB P MY GABA, where its whole-signature profile converged most strongly with Thoc1 and a nuclear RNA-processing module consistent with TREX-linked mRNP maturation and mRNA export. Top positive neighbors included Tpr, U2af2, Snrnp70, Prpf6, Ddx23, Hnrnpu, and Cdc40, with weaker convergence to several splicing perturbations than to Thoc1. This signal is correlation-based and restricted to the Perturb-seq signature, and proteasome neighbors such as Psmc1, Psmc5, and Psmb4 suggest some shared essential-gene stress component.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ppp2r1a, in an exploratory top-200-gene signature screen restricted to 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons, showed Stxbp1, Tsc1, and Tsc2 as the strongest positive signature neighbors, while Limk1 and Dnajb6 were among the strongest negative neighbors. This suggests that, within this vulnerable excitatory cortical class, the transcriptomic effects of these perturbations may converge with or oppose PP2A-Aα loss. The result is limited because the correlations are noncausal, based on a restricted signature, and computed in a single cell type.

Cd247 showed a convergent absence with the broader CD3 receptor subunit family rather than a hidden Cd247-specific program: across the pan-panel of 22 assayed neuronal groups, Cd247, Cd3d, Cd3e, and Cd3g all lacked FDR<0.05 transcriptomic responses in the TCR-CD3 signal initiation context, and Cd247 did not share a coherent signed transcriptional signature or strong score correlations with the other CD3-family perturbations. This comparison is limited to neuronal RNA measurements, with Cd3d absent from one low-count group and no protein editing or TCR-complex abundance data available.

Tbc1d23 showed no detectable convergence with the measured WASH/TBC comparators, suggesting an uninformative perturbation rather than a specific endosome-to-Golgi or WASH phenotype. Across the panel, Tbc1d23 had only weak correlations, with the strongest neighbors in 308 CB GABA being Ranbp2 (r=0.191) and Msx2 (r=-0.180), while Washc4, Tbc1d24, and Tbc1d32 had no FDR-supported genes and max |r|≤0.077 versus Tbc1d23. This null was not due to a general inability to detect trafficking genes, since Ap2s1, Rab7, Vps35, and Vps54 were detectable in the same analysis; however, direct partners such as Wdr11, Fam91a1, Golga1, and Golga4 were not tested, and the Tbc1d23 profiles were weak and subthreshold.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sdccag8 showed a modest inverse full-signature relationship with B9d1 in 308 CB GABA, where B9d1 ranked as the 6th most anti-correlated neighbor among 2,023 perturbations, but this finding is exploratory rather than mechanistic. In this cerebellar GABA context, the Sdccag8 signature had no FDR-significant genes, and B9d1 itself was not detectably depleted despite a stronger corrected B9d1 signature with 9 FDR genes. This ciliary-looking contrast, alongside Gas8 and other comparators, therefore lacks cis validation and should be interpreted cautiously.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Tek showed an inert phenotype that fit a broader expression-gated vascular RTK pattern in the neuronal screen: related endothelial receptors Kdr, Flt4, Notch4, Robo4, Eng, Acvrl1, and Pdgfrb were also mostly weak, and restricted-signature correlations did not reveal a stable Tek neighbor or related-target phenocopy. In 046 CTX-CGE GABA, the RTK comparator Kit could be knocked down with strong target-RNA depletion but only a one-gene response, suggesting that when receptor transcripts are present, downstream transcription can still be buffered rather than yielding broad differential expression.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Rgs6 showed a weak and noncoherent transcriptomic signature: in 052 Pvalb Gaba, the only FDR-supported feature was Wdfy3 down-regulation, yet the Pvalb Rgs6 score vector was essentially uncorrelated with Gnb5, Gnao1, Gabbr1, and Gabbr2 perturbations and had no close global neighbor, with Ufc1 the nearest at only r=0.083. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, related inhibitory-GPCR perturbations had clear on-target effects while Rgs6 itself showed no supported output, so within the measured transcriptomes the weak Rgs6 signal did not recapitulate the canonical RGS/Gbeta5/Galpha-i/o or GABAB receptor axis; receptor knockouts also need not phenocopy Rgs6 loss.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Smad9 did not yield a stable all-library perturbation module. Across 23 cell types, 22 had no signature neighbor with |r| > 0.164, and the only exception, 308 CB GABA, showed only modest correlations with Wdr26 and Dstyk and anti-correlation with Ranbp2, with Atp6v1e1 among nominal neighbors. Even in 308 CB GABA, the Smad9 signature had a minimum FDR of 0.840, no FDR-significant genes, and no on-target Smad9 depletion, so these correlations are exploratory and should not be interpreted as a robust hidden SMAD9 program.

Zbtb20 showed a target-specific null signature: across the Zbtb20-tested cell types, no downstream transcript reached conventional FDR significance, even in the best-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group, where Zbtb20 had only weak global signature neighbors. In the same matrix, other transcriptional regulators and context genes produced robust signatures, including Zbtb7a, Wac, Zfp423, Zbtb11, Prox1, and Tbr1, arguing that the assay could detect transcription-factor-like responses. Because these comparators differ in expression, guide efficiency, cell numbers, and biology, the contrast localizes the issue to Zbtb20 without explaining why.

Ica1 appeared transcriptionally uncoupled in this basal Perturb-seq dataset: assayed vesicle or synaptic comparators including Syn1, Rab27a, Snap25, and Gria1 showed only weak signature correlations, available pathway-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy the Ica1 score signature, and genome-wide matching found no close positive or negative whole-signature neighbor. Thus, the expected PICK1/ICA69 BAR-domain secretory-vesicle and AMPAR-trafficking biology did not emerge as a basal mRNA module here, with the caveat that Pick1 and Ica1l were not included and the observed correlations were weak signature-level measures.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ank1 did not elicit a broad transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells; in the same thalamic glutamatergic class, Ank3, but not Ank1 or Ank2, produced a large program with 121 FDR-significant genes, including Atp2a2, Opn3, Atp2b1, and Pcsk1n. This indicates that the ankyrin family was not transcriptionally interchangeable here, despite shared L1-ankyrin scaffold pathway context. A key caveat is that Ank1 and Ank2 lacked FDR-level target knockdown in this cell type, so the contrast reflects both paralog specialization and weaker guide engagement.

Six1 showed a near-null transcriptomic signature in this screen: across all 23 Six1-tested cell classes, no profiled perturbation meaningfully phenocopied or opposed its global Wilcoxon score pattern. Correlations with 2,045 other perturbations were near zero, including related factors Six3, Six5, Six6, Dach1, and Pax6 (r=0.008–0.019), arguing against detectable engagement of a PAX-SIX-EYA-DACH developmental transcriptional network in the profiled brain classes. This null-like result may still miss rare cell-state effects or protein-level phenotypes not captured by RNA.

Dlx6 showed no robust convergence or divergence with the available Dlx-family comparators or with whole-signature neighbors. Dlx5 and Dlx3 perturbations were themselves FDR-null, and Dlx6–Dlx5 and Dlx6–Dlx3 full-score correlations stayed near zero, while the strongest all-target Dlx6 signature neighbors were weak, with maximum |r| = 0.254, arising from a cell type with no corrected Dlx6 genes. Because Dlx1 and Dlx2 were not perturbation targets, direct comparison within the Dlx homeobox module was limited, and the weak neighbors are best treated as exploratory artifacts of a null Dlx6 vector.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
