full_finding_text: Ptprt knockdown in 155 MB Glut, the only cell class with FDR-significant depletion of the target transcript, produced a buffered, isolated scRNA signature that was nearly uncorrelated with Stat3, Il6ra, or Il6st perturbations, indicating no clear STAT3-like transcriptomic coupling and an mRNA-level uncoupling from JAK/STAT signaling in this neuronal context. This interpretation is limited because single-cell RNA does not measure STAT3 phosphorylation, and in the same cell type Stat3 and Il6st perturbations were only nominally engaged while Il6ra was not engaged.

Il12rb1 showed no detectable convergent transcriptomic module in the Il12rb1-tested neuronal cell classes: correlations with the expected IL-12/IL-23-family comparators Il12b, Il23r, Stat3, and Stat4 were approximately zero, and across 1,989 well-covered perturbations the nearest positive and negative neighbors were still negligible, with Klf7 at r=0.0304 and Marchf6 at r=-0.0143. Across 22 represented classes, Il12rb1 RNA and pathway transcripts lacked FDR-significant changes, and the strongest nominal effects did not recur across cell classes. Given weak Il12rb1 target engagement, this restricted-signature analysis supports no detectable convergence in this assay rather than a broader biochemical contradiction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Hbs1l showed only weak, score-based signature convergence with Uba5, Ufc1, and Rrn3, most clearly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and recurring in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with Ufsp2 and Eif4e also appearing as neighbors in some contexts. This pattern points to UFMylation and ER ribosome-associated quality control as the most interpretable signal, but it is hypothesis-generating because the result is limited to score-vector correlations: Hbs1l had no FDR<0.05 genes and no significant on-target knockdown in the implicated cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hnf1b showed no corrected downstream transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, even in the largest Hnf1b cell-type samples, whereas in the same dataset and cell type Tcf7l2 produced a strong thalamic signature with 106 FDR-significant genes, including Ramp3 down and Cck up, despite fewer perturbed cells. This suggests the Hnf1b null result is target- and context-specific rather than a general inability to detect transcription-factor perturbations, although the comparison is indirect because TCF7L2 is a Wnt-associated diabetes locus, not an HNF1B paralog or complex member.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Lman2l in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut showed a weak signature that did not phenocopy assayed ER-Golgi/COPII neighbors: despite much stronger self-depletion for Ergic1, Copg1, and Sec23a in the same broad cell classes, top-200 restricted-signature similarities between Lman2l and Ergic1, Copg1, Sec23a, Sec31a, or Copa were low, with the highest listed cosine only 0.207 in 155 MB Glut. No FDR-supported secondary pathway output was detected, suggesting the captured Lman2l state is not a generic early-secretory-pathway failure state; however, the Lman2l signature itself was weak and LMAN1/LMAN2 were not assayed.

Sptb perturbation showed no FDR-significant mRNA compensation by measured spectrin-associated membrane cytoskeleton genes, including Sptan1, Sptbn1, Sptbn2, Sptbn5, Ank3, Add2, and Epb41l1. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, the Sptb response was weak and nonconvergent relative to stronger Sptan1 and Ank3 responses. This negative result is limited because Sptbn4 was not measured, and possible isoform-specific, protein-level, or relocalization-based compensation was not tested.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ifngr1 showed only restricted convergence with the IFNγ receptor–JAK–STAT1 axis rather than a global phenocopy of Ifngr2 or Stat1. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ifngr2 nominally lowered Ifngr2 and Stat1, and Stat1 guides significantly lowered Stat1; in 191 MB P MY GABA, Stat1 guides significantly lowered Stat1 and nominally lowered B2m, while Ifngr1 nominally ranked Stat1 and B2m among its top negative genes. Yet whole-signature correlations between Ifngr1 and Ifngr2 or Stat1 were weak, with the largest absolute related-target correlation only r = -0.219 in 308 CB GABA, and Ifngr1 itself lacked confirmed knockdown.

Pdx1 perturbation in brain cells did not transcriptionally engage the canonical pancreatic PDX1 regulon or the PDX1-PBX-MEIS complex: Pbx1, Meis2, Foxa2, Mafa, Mafb, Neurod1, Neurog3, Hnf1a, Hnf1b, Gck, and Sst showed no FDR-significant response. This remained true even in the 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cell type, where Pdx1 had its lowest adjusted p value, driven by Vsnl1, but without canonical network changes. The result should be interpreted with the caveat that some endocrine hormone genes were sparse or outside the feature universe, and the assay measured RNA rather than chromatin occupancy.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pdx1 did not show strong cross-perturbation convergence with curated PDX1-associated genes or with unbiased transcriptomic neighbors. In 308 CB GABA cells, perturbations of Mafa, Pbx1, Neurod1, Hnf1a, Hnf1b, Foxa2, Neurog3, and Ptf1a were all weakly correlated with Pdx1, and the best library-wide positive and negative neighbors, Msx2 and Ranbp2, reached only modest correlations of about |r|≈0.23. This argues against a hidden interchangeable factor, with the caveat that correlations were based on transcriptomic score vectors and the top data-driven neighbors were not established direct PDX1 partners; the PDX1-PBX1-MEIS2 pancreatic enhancer complex was also not detected.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Klrk1 showed an uncoupled, essentially null transcriptional signature in 155 MB Glut and 053 Sst Gaba, not phenocopying broad immunoreceptor/MAPK/PI3K/Rac perturbations and remaining largely uncorrelated with Cd247, Fyn, Mapk1, Pik3r1, or Rac1. This was not due to a general inability to respond, because in the same analysis Mapk1 produced an on-target effect in 155 MB Glut and Rac1 yielded an FDR-resolved Ranbp1 response in 053 Sst Gaba. Interpretation is limited because Mapk1, Rac1, Fyn, Pik3r1, and Cd247 are broad signaling genes, and the core NKG2D adaptors Hcst and Tyrobp were not targeted.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Becn1 in 155 MB Glut showed its strongest cross-perturbation convergence with Rb1cc1/FIP200, the top positive neighbor of the Becn1 restricted signature, whereas Atg5 was only weakly concordant and its own transcript was not nominally depleted in this cell type. This places the Becn1 effect near macroautophagy initiation, linking ULK-complex entry with Beclin-PI3KC3 nucleation more than downstream Atg5 conjugation, but the comparison was based on the 200 largest absolute Becn1-score genes and several canonical PI3KC3-complex members were not directly perturbed.

Brinp1 showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to the assayed BMP/neurodevelopmental comparators Bmpr1b, Chd8, Cntnap2, Fmr1, Grin2a, Nf1, Pten, Shank3, and Tsc1, suggesting its weak signature is not a generic BMP-receptor, mTOR, CHD8, CNTNAP2, SHANK3, or NF1-like response. This interpretation is tentative because the Brinp1 perturbation itself produced only a weak signature, and the most direct BRINP/ASTN neighborhood contrasts—Brinp2, Brinp3, Astn1, and Astn2—were not available as perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fgf14 showed an exploratory, restricted positive-signature similarity in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where its top neighbors were Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Ank3, Dlgap4, and Grip1, with Ank3 linking the signal to an AIS/channel-organizing module. This comparison used only the top 100 absolute Fgf14 score genes, and the Fgf14 thalamic signature itself did not pass FDR < 0.05, so the result is tentative. In the same cell class, Scn and Kcnab comparator knockdowns were more strongly engaged than Fgf14.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Adgrg6 perturbation in the sampled neuronal classes showed no detectable engagement of canonical ADGRG6 programs: across 22 assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types, Schwann/myelin markers including Mbp, Mpz, Mag, Pmp22, Pou3f1, Egr2, Gjb1, Prx, Sox10, and Pllp, as well as BBB/ECM-associated genes such as Lrp1, Itgb1, Prnp, Col4a1, and Col4a2, remained flat. This likely reflects that the dataset lacked Schwann cells and brain endothelium, where these pathways were established, and that Adgrg6 target engagement was weak in these neurons.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Unc13a in 308 CB GABA cells showed a correlated whole-signature neighbor structure despite no detectable depletion of the Unc13a transcript, suggesting the apparent signal is not interpretable as Unc13a target engagement. In this cell type, the signature correlated with unrelated perturbations such as Wdr26, Dstyk, Ranbp2, and Fbxo11, and even anti-correlated with safe-target controls, while the strongest apparent target logFC was seen instead in a low-count cell type. Overall, this pattern is more consistent with an artifact-prone or off-target effect than with presynaptic Unc13a biology, although the analysis is correlational and does not identify the artifact source.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cacna1c knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a mainly self-only transcriptomic signature, and related voltage-gated calcium-channel perturbations in the same class were largely orthogonal rather than shared. In this context, Cacna1g knockdown produced a broader multi-gene response, including genes such as Ptprn, Stmn4, and Cpne7, whereas Cacna2d1, Cacnb4, and Cacna1c each were significant mainly for their own target transcript. Thus, pathway or network proximity within the voltage-gated calcium-channel complex did not predict a common scRNA-seq signature, although these were partial knockdowns and biophysical convergence could still exist.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Marchf6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons showed a sterol-gene module whose restricted 15-gene neighbor analysis placed Dctn1, Mib1, Chp1, Rab7, Tsc1, and Tsc2 as stronger positive neighbors than Marchf6 itself, with Pcyt2 also converging on the same readout. This suggests endolysosomal and TSC-associated perturbations can converge on neuronal sterol-module induction, but the result is hypothesis-generating because it was computed only on 15 sterol genes rather than whole-transcriptome similarity and needs targeted validation.

Ogfrl1 was transcriptionally uncoupled from canonical opioid receptor perturbations in the shared neuronal cell types: perturbation signatures for Oprd1, Oprk1, Oprl1, and Oprm1 showed same-cell correlations near zero with Ogfrl1 and neither phenocopied nor opposed it. This suggests that, despite the name, Ogfrl1 does not behave like a canonical OPR-family GPCR in these data. A key caveat is that the closest paralog, Ogfr, was not assayed, so the comparison addresses canonical opioid receptors rather than the strict growth-factor receptor paralog.

Ift43 perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported compensatory transcriptional program in the measured ciliary transport or ciliary signaling panel: transcripts such as Ift52, Ift22, Ift74, Traf3ip1, Ift88, Wdr35, Ttc21b, Adcy3, Tulp3, and Smo remained non-significant overall, with only isolated nominal shifts for Ift52, Ift22, Ift74, and Traf3ip1 that did not survive correction. This suggests weak or absent convergence with intraflagellar transport and Hedgehog/GPCR feedback at the mRNA level in this readout, while leaving open effects on ciliary localization or protein transport that transcript measurements would miss.

Dicer1 showed a non-convergent transcriptomic signature relative to the available miRNA-effector perturbations Ago1, Ago2, Tnrc6a, and Tnrc6b: correlations were essentially near zero, with the largest absolute related-target score correlation only r=0.117. Thus, despite their shared placement in microRNA biogenesis and RISC/TNRC6-mediated silencing, this screen did not capture a coherent RISC-loss state. Interpretation is limited because the comparator perturbations were themselves weak, and several core miRNA-pathway genes were not perturbed, including Drosha, Dgcr8, Tarbp2, Prkra, Xpo5, Ago3, and Ago4.

Mapk8 showed a weak and largely uncoupled basal Perturb-seq signature: across matched cell types, its full-gene correlations with Mapk9, Mapk8ip1, Map3k7, Atf2, Jund, Bcl2, and Trp53 were centered near zero, and a global neighbor scan did not yield a reproducible high-correlation partner apart from one exploratory CB GABA case. In 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, these results suggest that genes placed near stress-activated JNK/AP-1 MAPK signaling do not behave as an interchangeable basal transcriptomic module, with the caveat that several canonical upstream kinases or AP-1 components were not directly perturbed.

Dicer1 perturbation did not produce a consistent mRNA-level compensatory response in the measured miRNA-effector machinery: Ago1, Ago2, Tnrc6a, and Tnrc6b showed no coherent transcriptional change, with mixed nominal directions and no pathway-level signal across the assessed cells. This suggests that weak Dicer1 engagement is uncoupled from transcription of Argonaute/TNRC6 components in the microRNA biogenesis and RISC/TNRC6-mediated silencing pathway, while leaving open compensation through protein abundance, localization, activity, or miRNA loading that was not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Uqcc2 showed a weak, divergent perturbation profile in mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III assembly/CYTB biogenesis, rather than converging with measured core complex-III genes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells, Cyc1, Uqcrc1, and Uqcrfs1 had strong FDR-significant self-depletion, but Uqcc2 did not, and genome-wide correlations with Uqcc2 were near zero. This divergence may partly reflect weak Uqcc2 target depletion, and Uqcc1/Uqcc3 were not directly compared.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cacnb2 showed weaker engagement than related CaV-complex subunits in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: it did not reach self-knockdown FDR, whereas Cacnb4, Cacna1c, and Cacna2d1 each achieved significant self-depletion in the same cell type. This same-cell contrast argues against a generic failure of the thalamic comparison and suggests that beta paralogs are not interchangeable transcriptomic perturbations. A similar pattern was seen in 155 MB Glut, where Cacnb4 and Atp2a2 reached transcript-level FDR but Cacnb2 showed no significant target or downstream response. The comparators had more perturbed cells, and these results establish transcript knockdown rather than matched calcium-current phenotypes.

Slit2 showed no consistent convergence with its direct receptors Robo1 and Robo2, or with other assayed axon-guidance comparators including Dcc, Ryk, Unc5c, and Unc5d. Across the sampled mouse-brain cell types, genome-wide Slit2 correlations with Robo1, Robo2, Dcc, and Ryk were near zero, despite curated SLIT2-ROBO pathway membership. These results suggest that the weak cell-autonomous Slit2 RNA signature is not a reliable proxy for ROBO signaling state here, while also noting that the analysis measures transcriptome similarity rather than acute ligand-receptor or RHOA signaling activity.

Zfp341 showed no reproducible convergent transcriptional signature in the genome-wide neighbor scan: whole-signature correlations with Stat1, Stat3, and Il6st were essentially zero, and the strongest non-Zfp341 global neighbor was only r=0.0298. The nominal Zfp341 tail was not organized into a recurrent multi-cell-type module, so this perturbation behaves like a near-null signature and should not be used to infer related-target convergence or divergence. This conclusion is limited to Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon score profiles and could miss effects restricted to unmeasured genes or non-transcriptional phenotypes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Grhl2 showed no corrected transcriptomic response in brain, including the high-count neuronal populations 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, and the GRHL2-associated comparators Ovol2 and Gata3 were likewise flat. In contrast, Zeb1 and Cdh2 had detectable effects in selected thalamic and midbrain populations, indicating that neuronal Zeb1 or cadherin responses were uncoupled from the GRHL2/OVOL2/ZEB1 epithelial-state axis in this dataset. This interpretation is tempered because the library lacked several canonical epithelial perturbations, and Zeb1 transcript depletion itself was not significant in the Wilcoxon output.

Foxc2 showed a weak, largely orthogonal brain Perturb-seq signature that did not converge with Foxc1 or with assayed FOXC2-linked lymphatic-endothelial and ZEB-SNAI neighbors, including Sox18, Flt4, Prox1, Zeb1, and Snai2. Across overlapping genes and cell types, no related perturbation closely tracked Foxc2; notably, Zeb1 produced a robust independent signature that remained uncorrelated with Foxc2, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 155 MB Glut showed only mixed nominal Foxc2 effects. These transcriptome-level correlations are dominated by Foxc2’s weak signature and may not recapitulate relationships defined mainly in embryonic mesoderm, lymphatic endothelium, or human network data.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Epha3 was much weaker than the related Eph receptors Epha4, Epha5, and Epha7 in this Perturb-seq dataset, indicating that shared ephrin-pathway membership did not translate into interchangeability. Across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Epha3 showed no FDR-significant self-transcript response, whereas Epha4 had clearer self-knockdown in multiple cell types and Epha5/Epha7 each had one hit. The contrast is tempered by weaker Epha3 target engagement, so it should not be read as a clean receptor-specific downstream difference.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atxn1 showed its clearest and most specific Perturb-seq convergence with Cic in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons: Cic was the top positive Atxn1 signature neighbor among 2,045 perturbations, and all 130 genes significant in both signatures changed concordantly. This overlap, including genes such as Ankrd55, Lrrc7, Tecr, Aldh1l2, Trim9, and Grin2c, points to the ATXN1-CIC transcriptional-repressor complex rather than a broad stress or ataxia-gene program. Weaker similarities with Celf2 and Srrm2 were exploratory, and the RNA readout does not measure ATXN1-CIC protein occupancy.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Nr1h3 showed no robust transcriptomic signature neighbor in this dataset. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, the strongest related-target anti-neighbor was Rxrg, but the full-signature correlation was weak (r = -0.173), and no strong positive or negative neighbor emerged. This RXR nuclear-receptor partnership context makes Rxrg a plausible comparator, yet the relationship remains exploratory because the Nr1h3 CA3 signature itself had no FDR < 0.10 genes, with even the nominally strongest context remaining non-significant.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grm1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut defined the only cell group with FDR-significant Grm1 self-transcript reduction, yet the downstream transcriptional response was buffered, and perturbing canonical group-I mGluR pathway neighbors did not phenocopy it. Specifically, Grm5, Homer2, Itpr1, Plcb1, and Prkca showed near-zero correlation with the 333-gene nominal Grm1 signature. This apparent pathway uncoupling is limited to that nominal gene set, and interpretation is tempered because Plcb1 and Prkca lacked transcript engagement while Grm5, Homer2, and Itpr1 showed only nominal or sub-FDR self-effects.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Esr1 in 155 MB Glut showed an isolated response centered on Nfic upregulation rather than a coordinated ESR-mediated signaling module. In this cell type, perturbing Pgr, Ar, Gper1, Esrra, Rora, Ncoa1, Ncoa3, Crebbp, or Ep300 produced zero FDR<0.05 genes and near-zero correlation to the Esr1 score vector, so the Esr1/Nfic hit did not co-cluster with assayed steroid receptors, estrogen-related receptors, or receptor coactivators. By contrast, Rora and Esrra had strong signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, arguing against a generic failure to detect nuclear-receptor biology, although guide efficiency and pathway-family differences remain caveats.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Stard7 did not show a robust cross-perturbation RNA module: in 308 CB GABA and 191 MB P MY GABA, curated mitochondrial/cristae and lipid-transfer comparators such as Chchd10, Micos13, Mboat7, Pitpnm3, Tomm40, and Yme1l1 had Stard7 score correlations near zero overall, and the unbiased scan in 191 MB P MY GABA reached only weak extremes around |r| = 0.10. The few larger correlations in 308 CB GABA were exploratory because the comparator signatures were FDR-negative, so nominal Stard7 DE genes should not be overinterpreted as a generic mitochondrial lipid-transfer/cristae program.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Tbx22 showed no Benjamini-Hochberg significant differential-expression signal across assayed mouse brain cell classes, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, where the related T-box factor Tbr1 produced FDR-supported cortical signatures. In these matching glutamatergic populations, Tbx22 had zero FDR hits, with only nominal effects such as Vapa and Lsm7 decreases in 005 and Sort1 and Prrt3 changes in 027, whereas Tbr1 showed 7 and 4 FDR-supported genes, including Cpne6 and Cacna1g. This family-level contrast suggests Tbx22 is separable from brain-active T-box transcriptional regulation, although the comparison is not a paralog-rescue experiment and Tbr1 had higher perturbed-cell counts.

Cxcr2 showed a near-zero, largely orthogonal transcriptomic signature relative to related chemokine and inflammatory signaling perturbations across the assayed neuronal classes. In basal neurons, it did not phenocopy Cxcr4, Ccr2, Ccr5, Cx3cr1, Tlr9, Il6ra, Il1rap, or proximal MAPK/PI3K/Akt/NF-kB nodes such as Mapk1, Akt3, Nfkb1, and Nfkb2, including in 155 MB Glut and 308 CB GABA. However, several comparator receptors also had weak self-transcript engagement, so this mainly indicates no shared basal transcriptomic program in this dataset rather than strong pathway exclusion.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Lrrc3b showed its strongest, but still weak and FDR-negative, signature-neighbor structure in 308 CB GABA cells: across 16,945 genes, the subthreshold Lrrc3b score vector was most similar to B9d1 and Ranbp2 perturbations and most opposed to Wdr26, Cckar, and Nr4a1. This cell-type-restricted 308 CB GABA signature-neighbor module is hypothesis-generating because the comparator perturbations produced robust CB GABA signatures whereas the Lrrc3b arm was much weaker, and the modest correlations do not establish direct molecular interaction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Aifm1 was buffered relative to mitochondrial neighbors in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA: despite nominal downregulation of Aifm1 itself in the thalamic class, Aifm1 showed no FDR-significant genes, whereas Hspa9, Dnm1l, and Opa1 produced broad differential-expression programs linked to mitochondrial proteostasis and dynamics. This argues that the Aifm1 null was not a generic failure to detect mitochondrial perturbations in the atlas, although these comparators are pathway neighbors rather than obligate AIFM1 complex members and may differ in guide efficiency or loss-of-function mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Washc4 showed no detectable signature in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class, with 76 perturbed cells, weak on-target depletion and no FDR genes, even though vesicle-trafficking comparators in the same stratum, including Dnajc13, Vps35, Rab7, Ap2m1, and also Cltc and Atp6v0a1, produced on-target or multi-gene FDR responses. This contrast suggests the dataset can score WASH/retromer-associated endosomal trafficking perturbations, so the Washc4 null is unlikely to reflect a generic assay failure, although comparator targets often had stronger engagement and more perturbed cells.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Scn2a showed an exploratory, weak cortical signature in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut in which Kcnq2 aligned positively with the Scn2a restricted signature, whereas Ank3 was the top negative neighbor, despite all three mapping to the axon initial segment KCNQ-Ankyrin-NaV module. Because Scn2a target depletion in this cell type was not supported after multiple testing, this Kcnq2-versus-Ank3 contrast should be treated as a restricted-signature, hypothesis-generating observation rather than a definitive effect.

Tenm4 did not show a coherent transcriptomic signature shared with Tenm3, Adgrl1, Adgrl2, Adgrl3, or Flrt3 in this neuronal assay: score-vector correlations were near zero across this TENM4-latrophilin-FLRT adhesion axis, and non-self responses were generally weak. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons, Tenm4 showed only nominal self-depletion, while related perturbations often had stronger self-depletion without converging on a Tenm4-like program. These results suggest that known adhesion relationships here do not imply acute transcriptional interchangeability, with the caveat that the comparisons rely on restricted-signature summaries.

Tpm1 showed weak, near-zero transcriptional convergence with Tpm3 and with actin/tropomyosin cytoskeleton perturbations, with same-cell-type score-vector correlations to Tpm3, Actb, Actg1, Actn4, Cfl2, Limk1, and Mrtfa ranging from about -0.072 to +0.113. Core actin perturbations could generate robust signatures in the dataset, but Tpm1 did not transcriptionally induce the measured paralogs Tpm2 or Tpm4. Nominal, cell-type-specific responses were seen in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 053 Sst Gaba, yet these did not show meaningful convergence, and weak Tpm1 signatures plus missing Tpm3 and Actb target-transcript rows limit how definitively shared function can be excluded.

Il23r showed an uncoupled pattern in the assayed neuronal cells: related IL-23 receptor/JAK-STAT perturbations, including Il12rb1, Il12b, Stat3, Stat4, Rorc, and Nfkb1, also produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic hits in their tested panels, and their whole-transcriptome signatures were only weakly correlated with Il23r (all |r| ≤ 0.070). Thus the canonical IL-23 receptor/JAK-STAT module was not reconstructed in these unstimulated neuronal contexts, a result that should be interpreted with the caveat that ligand-competent receptor-positive conditions were not present and Jak2, Tyk2, Il23a, and Il12rb2 were not assayed.

Pcsk2 loss did not produce detectable mRNA-level compensation in the secretory-granule peptide and neuropeptide precursor processing pathway: Scg5/7B2, Cpe, Pcsk1, granins such as Chga, Chgb, and Scg2, and selected precursor genes including Cck, Npy, Sst, Pomc, Penk, Pdyn, Tac1, Tac2, Nts, and Vgf were not significantly induced or suppressed, with none of 320 tested candidates crossing FDR 0.1. This analysis was limited to a hand-curated gene list and does not measure peptide processing products directly, so mature peptide depletion remains a plausible hidden phenotype despite buffered pathway mRNAs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Prdm12 showed little evidence of a shared brain Perturb-seq program with other PRDM-family or chromatin-regulator perturbations in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Prdm10, and to a lesser extent Ehmt1, produced clearer FDR-significant signatures where Prdm12 was largely flat, and Prdm12 score vectors were only weakly correlated with Prdm10, Prdm2, Prdm5, Prdm16, and Ehmt1. A near-threshold Prdm12 hit was seen for Shprh in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, but no FDR-significant response emerged; this comparison is limited to the dataset, and Ehmt1 here is not the reported PRDM12 interactor EHMT2.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hspa5 perturbation did not measurably deplete Hspa5 mRNA: across 19 tested cell types, including the strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 155 MB Glut, Hspa5 never reached FDR-significant decrease and could even be positive while downstream ER-stress and ERAD genes such as Hsp90b1, Pdia4, and Derl3 were induced. This suggests Hspa5 transcript is a poor engagement readout for this perturbation, consistent with buffered UPR autoregulation; however, guide editing could still alter protein sequence without lowering mRNA, so the exact engagement mechanism remains unresolved without protein or genotype measurements.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ddx23 showed recurrent positive signature convergence with proteasome-associated perturbations, specifically Psmc1, Psmc5, Psmb4, and Pomp, in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, notably in the same cell types where Prpf6 also converged with Ddx23. This pattern suggests that the Ddx23 signature may include a broader essential-gene or protein-homeostasis component in addition to spliceosome-related features, so correlated neighbors should not all be interpreted as spliceosome-specific. The observation is based on perturbation-signature correlation and does not itself show altered proteasome activity after Ddx23 perturbation.

Gata2 showed a weak, largely orthogonal perturbation signature across all 23 assayed neuronal cell classes: neither Gata1, Gata3, Gata4, Gata6, nor the FOG-family cofactor Zfpm2 phenocopied it, with score-vector correlations near zero. The whole-library scan was also effectively null, with only minimal neighbors such as Dip2b (r=0.0270) and Nhs (r=-0.0191). Under these assay conditions, the data do not support a shared terminal-neuron GATA-family transcription-factor/cofactor module, although these near-zero correlations are more consistent with lack of convergence than active antagonism.

Gata1 showed essentially no transcriptomic convergence with assayed GATA-family paralogs or erythroid-network neighbors in the screened brain contexts: across matched cell types, perturbations of Gata2, Gata3, Gata4, Gata6, Gfi1b, Kit, Klf1, Spi1, Tcf3, Zfpm2, and Epor had near-zero correlation with the Gata1 signature, with scores ranging from -0.0596 to 0.146 and a median of 0.009 over 245 comparisons. This argues against an active latent GATA/FOG/TAL1-like hematopoietic circuit in these cells, although the comparison is transcriptomic and limited to perturbations represented in the screen, with several canonical GATA1 cofactors measured only as transcripts rather than perturbed.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mmaa showed its strongest signature-neighbor structure in 308 CB GABA cells, where correlations were positive with Atp6v1e1, B9d1, Ranbp2, and P2ry14 and negative with Wdr26, Cckar, and Dstyk. This pattern was exploratory and off-canonical rather than a known cobalamin-pathway response, and the largest absolute Mmaa correlations in the dataset were concentrated in this cerebellar GABAergic group. Because the Mmaa self-row there was weak and non-significant, and Mmaa itself was not knocked down in 308 CB GABA, this should be treated as a restricted-signature hypothesis requiring validation.

Gata3 did not phenocopy related GATA-family perturbations in this dataset: its score signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Gata1, Gata2, Gata4, Gata6, and Zfpm2, with correlations ranging from -0.100 to 0.075. Across GATA-family transcriptional regulation, these comparator perturbations were themselves weak overall, produced only sparse non-shared corrected hits, and a whole-library neighbor search did not identify a strong Gata3-like or anti-Gata3-like program. Thus, despite shared family biology, Gata3 appeared nonconvergent with other GATA factors and Zfpm2 here, with the caveat that the comparison is signature-based and most related perturbations were weak.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Ngfr showed no detectable RNA engagement in this Perturb-seq assay and did not phenocopy p75NTR-associated partners: its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Ntrk2, Lingo1, Sort1, and other related-target signatures, even though Ntrk2, Lingo1, and Sort1 each showed on-target RNA depletion in selected cell types. This was seen across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Ngfr remained FDR-null while Ntrk2 or Sort1 were measurably engaged; however, these comparisons are limited to RNA signatures and do not establish protein absence or loss of receptor complexes in every cell.

Pi4kb showed no strong transcriptomic convergence with assayed phosphoinositide, PI4K-paralog, ARF/Golgi-proximal, PTEN, or 14-3-3 perturbations: Pi4ka, Gbf1, Ocrl, Pten, Pik3r1, Pik3r2, Ywhae, Ywhag, and Ywhaz all matched weakly, with the largest absolute same-cell correlation only 0.13, and genome-wide positive and negative signature neighbors were likewise weak. Across cell types, no robust Pi4kb signature neighbor emerged, so none of the assayed perturbations serves as a simple transcriptomic surrogate for Pi4kb here. This should be read cautiously, because key PI4KB partners such as Acbd3 and Rab11a were not in the panel and weak Pi4kb engagement may have flattened correlations.

Pou2f1 showed no robust convergence with other assayed POU-family perturbations: the closest comparator, Pou2f2, had no FDR-significant rows, and the Pou2f1–Pou2f2 score correlation was near zero (r = 0.012856), with similarly minimal correlations to Pou3f3, Pou3f4, Pou4f3, Pou5f1, Pou6f1, and Pou6f2. Although prior Oct1/Oct2 biology could suggest paralog convergence, these data are more consistent with weak, unevaluable Pou2f1 and Pou2f2 engagement than with true pathway divergence. The panel also lacked key cofactors such as Hcfc1 and Pou2af1, so this does not argue against overlapping Oct1/Oct2 DNA binding.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atl3 showed only modest, context-specific restricted-signature similarity to ER-network genes. In isolated cell types including 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Arl6ip1, Reep2, and Vapb appeared among the top positive neighbors of the Atl3 top-200 restricted signature, but correlations were small (0.234–0.276) and safe-target perturbations appeared in similar neighbor lists. This provides only weak support for convergence in GTP-dependent tubular ER fusion and ER network maintenance, and suggests the Atl3 signature is low amplitude.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Tbr1 perturbation in cortical glutamatergic cells produced a small, membrane/synapse-biased response across 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. Cpne6 was repeatedly upregulated in all three responsive classes, Gaa was also up in some contexts, while Dkk3 was down in both IT classes and Epb41/Nptx1 were repeatedly down. Enrichment among q<0.10 genes pointed to neuron projection, cell junction, synapse, and dendrite terms, but most recurrent genes beyond Cpne6 were significant in only one or two classes, so the pathway interpretation rests on a small gene set.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Map2k6 showed no corrected perturbation response across the assayed cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut where perturbed-cell counts were relatively high, while several neighboring MAPK or stress-transcription-factor perturbations in the same dataset were detectable, including Map2k1, Mapk1, Mef2c, Atf2, Mapk8ip1, and Jund. The available upstream p38 neighbor Map3k7 was also silent, suggesting a branch-specific absence rather than a general failure to recover kinase programs, although this contrast is indirect because Map2k3 and Mapk14 were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarce1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a BAF-core-like signature that converged strongly with Smarcb1 and Smarcc2, anchored by the Ptpn3/Reep2/Prkcd module, but several related SWI/SNF perturbations did not phenocopy it. In this cell type, Smarca2, Smarca4, Smarcc1, Arid1b, Smarcd1, Bcl11a, and Bcl11b were only weakly correlated with Smarce1, with few or no shared significant hits, and no strong anti-correlated neighbor was detected. This suggests non-interchangeable, combinatorial BAF outputs in neurons, while differences in guide efficiency or mRNA engagement remain an important caveat.

Lhx3 showed little convergence with developmentally related transcription factors in the assayed adult brain cell classes: perturbation signatures for Lhx4 and Isl1, as well as Pou1f1, Prop1, Gata2, Pax6, Pax7, Foxa2, Pitx3, and En1, were nearly orthogonal to Lhx3, and a full neighbor scan found no strong positive or negative Lhx3 correlate. The largest related-factor correlations appeared in 217 P MY Pineal Glut and weak top neighbors in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, but these remained small and did not support an active LIM-homeodomain pituitary/spinal fate module; most individual signatures, including Lhx3, were weak.

B3gat3 did not show a coherent transcriptional signature with other glycosaminoglycan linker-region and heparan-sulfate biosynthesis perturbations: its Wilcoxon-score signature was essentially uncorrelated with Xylt1, Ext1, Ext2, Glce, and Hs6st2. This suggests that, in this screen, related enzymes in the same proteoglycan-linker/heparan-sulfate pathway did not converge on a common acute mRNA module. In 155 MB Glut, the cell type with the strongest nominal B3gat3 transcript decrease, strong Ext2 and Hs6st2 target knockdown was also observed without convergence to the B3gat3 state, although these comparisons are transcriptomic and B3gat3 knockdown was incomplete.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Chrna2 signatures did not phenocopy related cholinergic perturbations: across 17 nicotinic, muscarinic, and cholinergic comparators, score-vector correlations with Chrna2 stayed near zero (r=-0.074 to 0.091). The contrast was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Chrnb2, Chrna4, or Ache perturbations showed clear on-target mRNA depletion, but Chrna2 remained unchanged and uncorrelated. Because this is a restricted signature-correlation analysis with limited Chrna2 target engagement, the lack of convergence cannot be assigned to alpha2-specific biology alone.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chrna7 did not phenocopy cholinergic receptor-family perturbations in this dataset: although related guides were active in overlapping midbrain-region classes, Chrna7 score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Chrnb2, Ache, Chrna4, and other acetylcholine receptor-family genes. In 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Chrna7 showed nominal depletion but largely target-dominated responses, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Chrnb2, Ache, and Chrna4 had FDR-significant self-knockdown and Chrna7 did not. Because Chrna7 itself had weak FDR support, this is best read as lack of a strong shared transcriptomic signature, not proof of no shared physiology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Chrna6 remained unengaged in this assay, with no differential-expression hit reaching 10% FDR and score vectors uncorrelated with the engaged Chrnb2 and Chrna4 signatures, even in overlapping thalamic and midbrain-associated classes such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In the same dataset, Chrnb2, Chrna4, and Ache showed detectable, FDR-supported target or response rows in related classes, suggesting the null was selective to the Chrna6 perturbation or alpha6-restricted cell states rather than a universal cholinergic-assay failure; however, related perturbations had larger matched-cell counts, and the comparison relies on mRNA signatures rather than receptor currents or dopamine release.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Chrnb3 showed no significant target engagement in overlapping cholinergic contexts where related perturbations did engage: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, Chrnb2, Chrna4, and/or Ache had FDR-significant on-target knockdown, while Chrnb3 remained non-significant despite 120 or 96 perturbed cells in some cases. This contrast suggests the lack of a Chrnb3 response is more consistent with guide or target-engagement limitations than with a general failure of nicotinic acetylcholine receptor or cholinergic signaling perturbations, although related hits were often mainly on-target and cell numbers varied.

Bicc1 perturbation did not produce FDR-significant transcriptional changes in the expected Wnt, cAMP, miRNA, or PKD-axis readouts in the profiled neuronal classes: Adcy6, Pkd2, Axin2, Ctnnb1, Dicer1, Ago1, Ago2, Cnot3, Cnot7, Cnot10, Pkd1, Tmem67, Rpgrip1l, and Ttc21b were not detectably engaged, with minimum FDR values of 1.0 for key literature-axis transcripts. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Bicc1 appeared uncoupled from canonical Wnt readouts while Ctnnb1 remained active, suggesting these published renal epithelial and embryonic laterality mechanisms may not translate to the brain cell types tested here.

Nkx6-2 perturbation in the 22 sampled neuronal Glut/GABA classes did not detectably induce or repress a central nervous system myelination/oligodendrocyte differentiation module: Mbp, Plp1, Myrf, Sox10, Olig1, Olig2, Sox9, and Tcf7l2 showed no adjusted-significant changes, including in the best-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, where Olig2 and Tcf7l2 remained unchanged. Although NKX6-2 has been linked to myelination and MBP/PLP1 promoter regulation, these genes are often low or absent in neuronal classes, which limits sensitivity to detect myelin-program repression or induction.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Snrnp70 showed positive signature similarity to other RNA-processing and proteostasis perturbations across the main responder cell types, especially 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut. Its nearest restricted-signature neighbors included spliceosome/RNA-export genes Prpf6, U2af2, Thoc1, Tpr, and Ddx39b, along with proteasome genes Psmc1, Psmc5, Psmb4, and Pomp, suggesting a broader RNA-processing/proteostasis stress module rather than an isolated single-gene response, although these correlations were restricted-signature comparisons and do not establish direct biochemical coupling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc52a2 showed a flat, target-specific Perturb-seq signature rather than a general failure to detect mitochondrial metabolic perturbations. In overlapping neuronal classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, direct perturbation of OXPHOS genes such as Ndufa13, Cox5a, Uqcrc1, and Ndufb10 produced strong own-transcript depletion, whereas Slc52a2 did not. This contrast suggests Slc52a2 was uncoupled from the FAD/FMN-linked mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation readout, with the caveat that these comparators are downstream flavin users or mitochondrial genes, not RFVT paralogs.

Itga9 perturbation showed no compensatory transcriptional feedback onto the canonical alpha9-beta1 axis: Itgb1 remained unchanged, and the measured ligands/neurotrophins Fn1, Tnc, Spp1, Vcam1, Ngf, Bdnf, and Ntf3 were also flat, with no multiple-testing-supported response in any tested cell class. Thus, the dataset provides no evidence for an autocrine ECM or neurotrophin transcriptional program downstream of Itga9 loss, while leaving open effects on integrin activity, localization, extracellular ligand abundance, or phosphosignaling that were not measured.

Pex1 showed a divergent, near-zero-correlation pattern relative to available peroxisome-related perturbations: its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Pex14, Pex13, Abcd3, and Acox1. In 155 MB Glut neurons, Pex1 had only a nominal transcript decrease and no downstream FDR-supported hits, while Pex14 was strongly self-depleted in several neuronal classes yet produced almost no non-target adjusted mRNA response. Thus, peroxisomal protein import and metabolism perturbations did not behave as an interchangeable acute RNA module here, with the caveat that Pex6 and Pex26 were not targeted and Pex1 itself was weakly engaged.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cntnap1 showed a largely buffered transcriptional phenotype: across tested cell types, the only FDR<0.1 effect was reduced Cntnap1 itself, with no significant downstream transcripts. In the same thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, however, Ank3 perturbation produced 164 FDR<0.1 genes, indicating that the weak Cntnap1 response is not simply due to assay failure or low sensitivity in this cell type. This contrast reflects divergence within an axonal-domain scaffold neighborhood rather than direct antagonism within a shared obligate Caspr-contactin cis-complex.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf7 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class showed a downshift of a neuronal projection and cytoskeletal module, with negative signals for Tuba1a, Coro1a, Sptan1, Stmn2, Map1b, Map6, and Dctn1; the top negative genes were enriched for cytoskeleton organization and cell-projection organization. This was the only Klf7 context with FDR-supported genes, and only Tuba1a individually reached FDR < 0.05, so the result is best interpreted as a module-level decrease rather than broad single-gene significance.

Epha3 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the canonical Eph-ephrin cytoskeletal module in this Perturb-seq dataset: across assayed cell types, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, there were no FDR-significant mRNA changes, including for Rhoa, Rock1, Rock2, Nck1, Crk, Ngef, Adam10, and Efna5. This likely reflects that the assay measures steady-state mRNA after genetic perturbation, whereas published EPHA3 biology emphasizes acute ephrin-A5-triggered phosphorylation, RhoA/ROCK activity, and morphology; Epha4, Epha5, and Epha7 showed stronger target engagement.

Nsun2 showed only a weak standalone mRNA signature in this perturbation compendium, with no robust positive or negative signature neighbor emerging. The strongest whole-signature correlation reached only |r| = 0.282 in 308 CB GABA, while the available methylation-enzyme comparators Dnmt3a and Alkbh8 were essentially uncorrelated with matched Nsun2 signatures; other comparators such as Wdr26 and Dnajb4 likewise did not provide a clear phenocopy or opposing pattern. These comparisons are based on weak mRNA-score correlations, and informative direct NOL1/NOP2/SUN paralogs were not present.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fus showed a distinct acute knockdown signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons and did not phenocopy other strongly engaged RNA-binding or spliceosome-associated perturbations in that same responsive cell type. In this dominant Fus-responsive class, Tardbp, Matr3, Srsf1, and Snrnp70 were strongly engaged yet had near-zero whole-transcriptome correlations with the Fus gene-level Wilcoxon score vector, indicating divergence despite shared mRNA splicing and nuclear-speckle context. By contrast, Atxn2 and Hnrnpa1 were too weakly engaged to interpret as clean negative phenocopies.

Atrn did not have an engaged melanocortin/Agouti comparator in this dataset. Although Atrn is connected in the literature to the Agouti–MGRN1–melanocortin receptor neighborhood, key members were not testable here: Mgrn1, Atrnl1, and Agouti were not perturbed, while Agrp, Mc1r, Mc3r, and Mc4r perturbations showed no detectable target-transcript knockdown and near-zero correlation with the Atrn signature. This therefore reflects limited coverage and target engagement in the assay, not a contradiction of the canonical melanocortin literature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnpa2b1 produced a transcriptomic signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells that was not interchangeable with other hnRNP-family or RNA-processing perturbations. Whole-transcriptome correlations to Hnrnpa1, Hnrnpc, Hnrnpdl, Hnrnph2, Hnrnpu, and Syncrip were near zero in both high-response classes, and genome-scale neighbor analysis found only weakly similar or even opposed signatures, even when splicing factors such as Srsf1 and Snrnp70 were among the nearest positives. This distinction is notable because Hnrnpa1 was induced in the Hnrnpa2b1 response, especially in 155 MB Glut, but several comparator perturbations showed weak or atypical target engagement and the similarities were assessed using steady-state whole-transcriptome scores.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Sncb perturbation produced a transcriptomic signature that was not interchangeable with Snca in this dataset. Across 10 Sncb-engaged cell classes, including 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, Sncb and Snca Wilcoxon score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, with Snca Pearson r from -0.008 to 0.048, and no strong positive or negative CRISPR-signature neighbor. A cortical class, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, showed Snca FDR depletion while Sncb remained only nominal. This analysis was dominated by weak non-target ranks, and synuclein pathway genes were not transcriptionally activated or repressed at FDR.

Cnksr2 showed a divergent, transcriptionally buffered profile rather than phenocopying other postsynaptic or neurodevelopmental disease perturbations: across pan-subclass comparisons spanning the 19 Cnksr2-evaluable neuronal subclasses, correlations with Dlg4, Shank3, Syngap1, Pten, Fmr1, Mecp2, Nbea, and Ube3a were all near zero, with the largest absolute correlation only 0.0732 for Syngap1. This suggests these perturbations are not simple transcriptomic proxies for Cnksr2 in this screen, although the comparator set mixes direct synaptic-context genes with broader NDD genes and the result reflects signature-space contrast rather than proof of distinct disease biology.

Bckdhb perturbation did not produce a coherent transcriptional compensation signature within the mitochondrial branched-chain amino acid catabolism/BCKDH complex network: Bckdha, Dbt, Dld, Bckdk, Ppm1k, Bcat1, Bcat2, and Ivd showed mixed nominal directions and no consistent induction or repression in RNA abundance. This suggests that, despite their biochemical proximity to BCKDHB, related BCAA-catabolic transcripts were buffered at the mRNA level after partial Bckdhb depletion, with the caveat that these data do not assess BCKDH enzymatic flux or BCKDHA phosphorylation.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pou2f2 showed near-zero similarity to the assayed POU-family perturbations across 22 broad mouse-brain cell groups, including glutamatergic and GABAergic classes such as L5-6 IT Glut, Pvalb Gaba, Sst Gaba, and CB GABA. Its closest assayed comparator, Pou2f1, also lacked FDR-level hits, and no coherent Pou2f2-like transcriptomic neighborhood emerged among Pou1f1, Pou3f3, Pou3f4, Pou4f3, Pou5f1, Pou6f1, Pou6f2, or Pou2af1-related comparisons. This negative result refines rather than contradicts the known Oct2/Oct1/OBF1 module, because the sampled neuronal panel showed weak engagement of POU-family perturbations, Pou2af1 was not perturbed, and Pou2f3 was absent.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Slc9a9 showed only isolated nominal RNA hits rather than a coherent endosomal pH or trafficking program across 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. Nominal signals included Tm9sf3, Eif4e2, Lrrc8b, Atp6ap1, Atp6v1h, Slc11a2, and Slc30a4, but all were FDR-null, and expected outputs such as Tfrc, Slc1a3/GLAST, Gria1/2, and Grin2a/2b were also unchanged at FDR. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, leading rows were only nominal with no supported on-target depletion; this RNA readout therefore may miss NHE9-dependent effects on lumenal pH, surface abundance, glutamate uptake, or presynaptic calcium.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Phactr1 knockdown was uncoupled from the expected G-actin/PP1/MRTF-SRF RNA output in mouse-brain neurons: across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and 155 MB Glut, canonical pathway genes including Mrtfa, Mrtfb, Srf, Actg1, Flna, and Ppp1ca/b/c remained FDR-null, and Phactr1’s nearest perturbation neighbors were very weak. Even in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut, where nominal Phactr1 depletion was strongest, no downstream signature emerged, unlike the clear actin-compensation signatures seen with Actb or Actg1 perturbation; however, this comparison relies on transcriptomic differential expression rather than direct assays of actin polymerization, PP1 activity, or nuclear localization.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Apc perturbation showed its strongest effect in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where a 303-gene corrected signature prominently induced the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin negative-feedback genes Axin2, Nkd1, and Notum, consistent with pathway activation rather than a nonspecific stress response. In the same cells, selected thalamic glutamatergic and peptide/neurosecretory markers, including Grin2c, Grin2d, Gls, Cck, and Chgb, were reduced. This Wnt readout was opposed by Ctnnb1 loss, only partly overlapped Tcf7l2 perturbation, and was not phenocopied by Gsk3b or proximal receptor perturbations. The assay was RNA-only, so nuclear beta-catenin, APC protein, and Wnt reporter activity were not measured directly.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Edem3 was comparatively quiet in the ER proteostasis and ER trafficking comparator module, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, where Hspa5, Manf, Sec31a, Sec63, and in some comparisons Sec23a showed FDR-level signatures but Edem3 did not; Atf6 was similarly quiet. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the largest nominal Edem3-associated change was Xbp1 up-regulation, yet Edem3 still lacked a strong whole-signature neighbor. These contrasts should be interpreted cautiously because comparator guide strengths and cell counts differed, and Edem1/Edem2 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Mnt perturbation was associated with a small, hypothesis-generating core circadian clock module, with nominal up-shifts of Per2, Cry1, and sometimes Per1/Cry2 in several neuronal classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, as well as 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. The same Period/Cryptochrome pattern was more strongly recapitulated by Max and Sin3a perturbations in overlapping cell types, linking Mnt to a MAX/SIN3A-associated E-box repression axis, while the Mnt signal itself remained nominal after FDR correction and circadian phase or activity state was not measured.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Vps53 in 191 MB P MY GABA showed a modest positive signature correlation pattern in which the nearest neighbors were not a tight GARP-only cluster, but instead included proteasome, vacuolar-ATPase, clathrin, ESCRT, and Vps54 perturbations, such as Psmb4, Psmc1, Atp6v1a, Atp6v0c, Vps37a, Cltc, and Vps54. This suggests a broader endomembrane/proteostasis convergence in this hindbrain GABAergic context, consistent with but not specific to vesicle trafficking. The effect was exploratory and weak, with the largest neighbor correlation only r=0.261, and it came from restricted-signature correlation rather than pathway-level FDR across many genes.

Pou5f1 showed an uncoupled signature in the sampled neuronal populations: score correlations with canonical OCT4-network partners Sox2, Ctnnb1, Sall4, Esrrb, and Sox17 stayed near zero, and correlations with other POU-family perturbations, including Pou1f1, Pou2f1, Pou2f2, Pou3f3, Pou3f4, Pou4f3, Pou6f1, and Pou6f2, were likewise near zero. A broader neighbor scan found no stable high-correlation biological neighbor, suggesting the POU5F1/OCT4 pluripotency program was not engaged in these neuronal signatures. In 308 CB GABA cells, exploratory neighbors and a nominal Arid1b increase were seen, but differential expression was FDR-null and included Safe_target-labeled neighbors, so interpretation remains limited, especially because Pou5f1 itself appeared transcriptionally absent.

Afg3l2 showed a divergent, generally weak transcriptomic response that did not phenocopy Opa1 or the available mitochondrial protease/import perturbations Yme1l1, Clpp, Clpx, Lonp1, and Tomm40. Across sampled cell types, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Afg3l2 had nominal engagement but no FDR-significant trans-response, whereas direct Opa1 perturbation was much stronger. This argues against a simple acute Afg3l2-to-Opa1 phenocopy in mitochondrial m-AAA proteolysis and fission/fusion transcript programs, with the caveat that weak Afg3l2 engagement and missing Spg7, Afg3l1, and Oma1 perturbations could mask convergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Wdfy3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed an exploratory neighbor pattern in which Dctn1, Sema6a, Herc2, and Pten were positive neighbors on a Wdfy3-defined restricted signature, while Grin1 was the strongest negative neighbor. However, these relationships were signature-defined and likely inflated by restricting to Wdfy3 p<0.01 genes; across the full transcriptome, correlations were only modest, about 0.204 to -0.269. Thus, the pattern suggests candidate convergence and antagonism for follow-up rather than a pathway identity call.

Cd3e showed no convergence with other CD3/TCR complex perturbations across the 22 tested Cd3e brain cell classes: Cd3d, Cd3g, Cd247, and Cd4 had no robust differential-expression signals, their own target transcripts were not detectably affected, and their signatures correlated only weakly with Cd3e, with no coherent CD3/TCR-like neighbor emerging even in restricted analyses. In 308 CB GABA cells, Cd3e had the weakest global signature-neighbor extrema, but these correlations were small. Overall, this pattern is more consistent with an inactive or unmeasured TCR-CD3 module in these neuronal classes than with a Cd3e-specific downstream pathway.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Sox10 showed no conventionally significant differential-expression genes in this dataset, yet related perturbations did produce detectable signatures, indicating a target- and context-specific null rather than a general pipeline or guide-cell failure. In neuronal classes, Sox2 and Sox5 yielded FDR-significant rows in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and Myrf yielded one significant row in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, within a SOX-family and MYRF transcription-factor response context that included Tnnt1, Stam, Dgkh, and Mapk8. These contrasts were observed in neurons and therefore need not reproduce oligodendrocyte SOX10 relationships.

Epor showed an isolated, low-amplitude perturbation profile rather than a convergent module: across all 22 Epor-profiled neuronal classes, no strong positive or negative signature neighbor was detected among 43,663 non-Epor target/cell-type signatures. The largest all-gene Pearson correlation to an Epor signature was only 0.143 overall, and in the Pvalb cell class the largest absolute correlation was 0.077, with comparators including Nr2c2, Fgfr2, Abca1, Myo5a, Thbd, and Irf6. This absence of neighbors argues against assigning the weak Epor profile to another module, although small nonlinear overlap could be missed and the weak signature reduces power.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hsf1 was not phenocopied by the tested paralog Hsf4 in the assayed brain cell types. In the strongest Hsf1-response groups, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Hsf1 showed a chaperone-like signature including Hsph1, Hsp90aa1, and Hsp90ab1, whereas Hsf4 perturbation produced no FDR-significant genes across 23 groups and Hsf1–Hsf4 signature correlations were near zero. This contrast remains exploratory because Hsf4 target-transcript knockdown was weak and not FDR-significant, so limited Hsf4 engagement cannot be excluded.

Pafah1b1 did not show an acute transcriptomic phenocopy of Reelin-pathway or Dcx perturbations: in shared cell types, Reln, Vldlr, Lrp8, Dab1, and Dcx perturbations were FDR-negative and had mean Wilcoxon-score correlations near zero with Pafah1b1. Thus, although these genes are developmentally linked in neuronal positioning, this dataset does not support treating PAFAH1B1 and Reelin/VLDLR-Dab1 or DCX as interchangeable acute transcriptional modules in the measured brain cell classes. This is a failure to detect convergence here, not proof that convergence cannot appear in other developmental or morphologic assays.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cert1 perturbation in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type showed the strongest nominal Cert1 signature, but the canonical ER-to-Golgi ceramide transfer and sphingomyelin biosynthesis pathway did not display coordinated transcriptional compensation: Sgms1, Sgms2, Vapa, Vapb, Smpd3, Sptlc1, Sptlc2, Asah1, and Sphk1 were not coherently induced or repressed. This suggests transcriptional uncoupling in the most engaged cell type, while important caveats remain because only transcript abundance was assessed, not lipid flux, CERT phosphorylation, ER-Golgi contact-site localization, or sphingomyelin mass.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Tbx6 showed no convergent perturbation signature with other T-box family members or with its canonical neighbors Mesp2, Dll1, Notch1, and Tcf7l2. In 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where adjusted p values were smallest, correlations between the full Tbx6 score vector and other Tbx perturbations were near zero, with |r|≤0.031, and similarly weak for Mesp2/Dll1/Notch1/Tcf7l2; the same lack of a close positive or negative neighbor was also seen in 191 MB P MY GABA, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut. Because these comparisons used weak full-signature vectors, this supports absence of a nearby signature rather than active antagonism.

Nt5c2 showed no full-signature convergence with nearby purine or adenosine genes: across matched cell classes, its transcriptomic perturbation signature was essentially uncorrelated with Adk, Adora2a, Guk1, and Nme7. Although NT5C2 sits in purine metabolism and IMP/GMP catabolism, that pathway adjacency did not translate into an interchangeable cell-state RNA signature, suggesting that any shared biology may be buffered at steady state. This comparison is transcriptomic, so metabolite changes or sparse effects on a few enzymatic genes could have been missed.

Snta1 showed an uncoupled neuronal transcriptomic state relative to other assayed members of the dystrophin-associated glycoprotein and syntrophin scaffold complex: restricted top-signature correlations with Dmd, Dag1, and Sgcd were small and inconsistent, and Snta1 did not produce FDR-significant feedback on assayed DAPC or syntrophin-family transcripts such as Utrn, Dtna, Dtnb, Sntb1, and Sntb2. This comparison is transcriptome-only and should be interpreted cautiously, because Dmd overlapped Snta1 in only 13 shared cell classes, all DAPC perturbations were weak at FDR<0.05, and some apparent nearest neighbors were safe-target controls.

Cd3d perturbation showed convergent inactivity with other screened CD3/TCR-complex components: Cd3e, Cd3g, Cd247, and Cd4 also produced no FDR-significant genes across the tested neuronal classes, indicating an absent or uncoupled TCR-CD3 signaling module rather than a Cd3d-specific neuronal signature. This pattern was seen across the Cd3d-profiled neuronal classes in the brain dataset, and the comparison is limited to the subunits and CD4 included as perturbations; Lck, Zap70, Cd8a, and Cd8b1 were measured as transcripts but not tested as Cd3d comparator perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Setdb1 perturbation most consistently derepressed clustered protocadherin-gamma genes rather than producing a generic stress signature, with upregulation of Pcdhga7, Pcdhga8, Pcdhga9, Pcdhga11, Pcdhga12, Pcdhgb4, and Pcdhgb5 across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA neurons. The strongest recurrence was a SETDB1/HUSH-linked program including Atf7ip and Tasor in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, while other classes showed narrower protocadherin-only responses. These data are mRNA readouts, not direct measurements of H3K9me3 or 3D contacts, and the effect was strongest in only a subset of neuronal classes.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ufsp2 showed positive signature convergence with the UFMylation enzymes Uba5 and Ufc1 in both 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where Uba5 and Ufc1 were the top positive transcriptomic neighbors of Ufsp2. In 155 MB Glut, Ufsp2 had the stronger direct response, with leading genes including Atp6v0c, Syt11, Ndufa2, Rtn3, Srsf5, Ddit3, and C1qtnf4, forming a mixed Atp6v0c-down/electron-transport-up module rather than a corrected pan-UPR response. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the Ufsp2 signature was much shallower despite the same alignment. These associations were derived from mRNA Wilcoxon scores and do not measure UFM1 conjugates or UFSP2 protease activity.

Crbn was transcriptionally isolated in this dataset: Dcaf8, Dcaf17, Ddb2, and Ikzf3 all showed near-zero full-signature correlations with Crbn, and no nonself perturbation, including weak neighbors such as Or51e2 or Zswim6, provided a strong global positive or inverse match. Thus, the mouse Crbn loss-of-function signature did not converge with the assayed CRL4-DDB1/DCAF ubiquitin-ligase network or with an IKZF3-like program. This interpretation is limited because core DDB1, CUL4A, CUL4B, and RBX1 perturbations were absent, and the all-library neighbor analysis used a restricted 440-feature vector.

Esr2 perturbation signatures were not phenocopied by Esr1, Gper1, estrogen-related receptors, or the tested steroid-receptor coregulators across matched cell types. Esr2 score-vector correlations with Esr1, Gper1, Esrra, Esrrb, Esrrg, Ncoa1, Ncoa3, Hsp90ab1, Pgr, and Ar were on average near zero, with the largest listed comparator reaching only rho=0.122, indicating these perturbations were not interchangeable with Esr2 in this dataset. This interpretation is tempered by the weak Esr2 signatures and by the absence of Ncoa2 as a comparator.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tfrc perturbation produced a restricted HIF-compatible VEGFA/glycolysis response rather than a generic neuronal program, with Vegfa and glycolytic genes including Pfkp, Pfkl, Pgam1, Ldha, Pkm, and Aldoa increasing together in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and more weakly in 191 MB P MY GABA. The densest nominal module was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the only FDR-significant Vegfa increase was in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and most other genes were nominal; HIF protein activity and iron levels were not assayed.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Lhx4 perturbation did not detectably engage the canonical ISL1:LHX4:LDB1 to Slit2 axon-guidance program in the assayed brain cell classes. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, Lhx4, Isl1, Ldb1, Slit1, Slit2, Slit3, Robo1, and Robo2 all remained FDR-negative, with the strongest nominal Slit2 and Robo2 signals appearing only in 052 Pvalb Gaba. The target transcript itself showed no measurable rank shift, and no transcriptome-wide significant downstream genes were detected, indicating contextual absence in these postmitotic cell types rather than contradiction of embryonic motor-neuron findings.

Ddhd1 perturbation did not produce a coherent mRNA module in the expected phosphatidic-acid/phosphatidylinositol or mitochondrial-dynamics programs: selected PA-producing phospholipases (Pld1, Pld2, Pld6) and fission/fusion genes (Dnm1l, Mff, Fis1, Mfn1, Mfn2, Opa1) showed no consistent FDR-supported transcriptional change, and the strongest nominal effects did not recur. This pattern is more consistent with a buffered or orthogonal DDHD lipid-remodeling response than a canonical transcriptional pathway at the assayed time point, with the caveat that only selected transcripts were checked and the dataset cannot measure PA, PI, lysophospholipids, mitochondrial morphology, or protein activity.

Gdap1 perturbation did not produce an FDR-significant mRNA response in the expected mitochondrial fission/fusion and GDAP1L1 redox-compensation module: Gdap1l1, Dnm1l, Mff, Fis1, Mfn1, Mfn2, and Opa1 were present in signatures but not robustly regulated. This pattern held even in nominally engaged inhibitory populations such as 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where downstream programs remained weak or absent. Because the dataset measures steady-state mRNA, any compensation may instead occur through localization, redox state, or protein-level mitochondrial recruitment.

Mif knockdown produced a weak on-target RNA effect, most evident in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, but it did not trigger a significant downstream MIF receptor or inflammatory transcriptional program. Transcripts for Ddt, Cd74, Cd44, Ackr3, Cxcr2, Cxcr4, Tlr4, Nfkb1, Mapk1, Mapk8, and Pik3ca were not measurably changed at FDR level, and perturbation signatures for Cxcr2, Cxcr4, Tlr4, Hmgb1, Nfkb1, Mapk1, Mapk8, Pik3ca, and Itgb1 showed near-zero same-cell-type correlation with Mif. Interpretation is limited because Cd74, Cd44, Ackr3, and Ddt were not perturbed, Cxcr2 was sparsely measured, and phospho-ERK, NF-kB localization, secretion, and paracrine recruitment were not assayed.

Mbd5 showed a selective null result rather than a general failure to detect chromatin-regulator perturbations: in the same Wilcoxon analysis, Kansl1, Kmt2d, Chd8, Chd2, Chd4, Setdb1, Adnp, and Mecp2 produced FDR-resolved signatures, whereas Mbd5 produced none. This pattern was also seen in the highest-count Mbd5 group, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where there was no target engagement even though the same cell type was a major FDR-positive context for several comparator perturbations. Because guide efficiency and cell counts differed across targets, this comparison is best read as an assay-capability benchmark, with weak Mbd5 guide or transcript detectability a more plausible explanation than global insensitivity to chromatin genes.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Med13l in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed a specific downregulation of Arpp21 that did not look like a generic Mediator-complex signature. Arpp21 was the only FDR-significant gene after Med13l perturbation in this cortical glutamatergic class, and related perturbations in Med12, Med13, Med15, Med23, and Cdk8 had near-zero full-signature correlations with Med13l and did not reproduce the Arpp21 effect. Thus, although Med13l sits near CDK8-module neighbors, its cortical output here was not interchangeable, with the caveat that this conclusion rests on one cell class and one significant gene.

cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Pi4ka showed context-restricted positive signature neighbors rather than a universal phosphoinositide-gene program. In 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells, Pitpna and Atp6v0c were the top positive neighbors, with the Pi4ka–Pitpna match plausibly aligning with phosphatidylinositol transfer, although this comparison was based on fewer than 30 cells per perturbation. In 191 MB P MY GABA cells, the leading neighbors were Psmb4, Vps37a, Atp6v0c, and Cltc, suggesting a broader endomembrane stress or proteostasis axis. Across contexts, correlations were modest (r≈0.206–0.273), exploratory, and most neighbors were not direct PI4KA complex members.

Zfp329 showed a nonconvergent, weak Perturb-seq signature across 22 assayed Zfp329 cell groups and did not phenocopy broad zinc-finger-family perturbations or its restricted-signature neighbors. Full-transcriptome correlations to 50 Zfp/Zbtb/Zic/Zkscan perturbations were near zero, and the top positive and negative restricted-signature neighbors, including Zfp644, Zic3, Zfp280d, Pitpnm3, and Drd2, were low-confidence and unstable across cell types. Across the panel, Zfp329 also lacked FDR-supported target knockdown, recurrent downstream genes, and a Bcl2 disease-axis response, so the neighbor analysis should be viewed as hypothesis-generating only.

Camta1 perturbation repeatedly produced a strongly down-regulated neuronal gene core rather than a broad bidirectional program, with recurrent negative effects on Snhg11, Snrpn, Peg3, Coro6, Tecr, Aifm3, Cntnap1, Nefh, Vamp1, Haghl, and Vwa5b2 across many neuronal classes. The pattern was especially evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, where responses were dominated by negative changes. This supports CAMTA1-dependent neuronal transcriptional maintenance, although the Camta1 transcript itself was not FDR-depleted and the data cannot separate direct from downstream targets.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Mboat7 showed a largely target-only transcriptional signature that did not converge with Acsl4, an engaged arachidonoyl-CoA pathway comparator, in overlapping neuronal classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut. Full-gene score correlations between Mboat7 and Acsl4 were approximately zero in those classes and globally, and a restricted scan of Mboat7 top features found no strong positive or negative signature neighbors. This exploratory, transcriptional result suggests PUFA/acyl-chain supply and phosphatidylinositol reacylation perturbations are not interchangeable at the mRNA-signature level, with the caveat that both signatures were dominated by their own target transcript and direct MBOAT7 partners or other LPLATs were mostly not perturbed.

Nr1h5 perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptional response in the assayed panel, and the expected NR1H5/RXR sterol-responsive program was not detected. Canonical sterol, bile-acid, and cholesterol-efflux genes, including Abca1, Abcg1, Apoe, Srebf1, Nr0b2, and Cyp46a1, remained unchanged, with no convergence across related receptors Nr1h2, Nr1h3, Nr1h4 or RXR partners Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg. This null result was observed in the Glut/GABA neuronal Nr1h5 contexts and should be interpreted with caveats: detectable Nr1h5 mRNA engagement was absent, the queried genes mix FXRbeta-linked and broader NR1H-family lipid targets, and glial cells were not included.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Epha7 knockdown in the best-engaged thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced strong on-target Epha7 depletion but no FDR-supported transcriptional feedback in the canonical EphA7 neighborhood: Efna5, other ephrin-A ligands, Efnb2/Efnb3, and effectors such as Abl1, Ngef, and Rasa1 were not detectably induced or repressed, and genome-wide downstream changes were not supported across Epha7 perturbations. This points to mRNA-level uncoupling rather than a self-amplifying Eph module, with the caveat that protein phosphorylation or ligand presentation was not measured and low-expression partners can yield unstable logFC estimates.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Hspa9 showed a restricted-signature pattern most similar to Hspa5 and Hspa8, with repeated neighbors including Gfpt1, Atp2a2, Dnm1l, Opa1, and Psmb4, rather than the expected mitochondrial matrix chaperone/TIM23-import neighbors Hspd1 or Dnajc19.
