This convergence was clearest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and was weaker in 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where no perturbation strongly mirrored the Hspa9 state. Because comparisons used only the top 400 Hspa9-responsive genes and related perturbations were often weak, the result suggests a shared stress endpoint rather than a simple phenocopy of every mitochondrial chaperone/import perturbation.

En1 perturbation did not change the mRNA levels of complex-I subunits Ndufs1, Ndufs3, Ndufs8, or Ndufb9 in any En1-tested class, so the Engrailed-linked mitochondrial complex-I protection pathway was unchanged at the transcript level in this screen. This does not directly contradict prior En1/2 neuroprotection work, because that mechanism is described as translational and protein-level, particularly in injured midbrain dopaminergic neurons, whereas this assay measured baseline single-cell mRNA and did not test protein synthesis, complex-I activity, mitochondrial physiology, or MPP+/MPTP challenge.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Setd1a was not interchangeable with other assayed KMT2/H3K4 writers in this panel. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Setd1a and Kmt2d each produced strong signatures with hundreds of FDR hits but shared only 10 significant genes, indicating a nearly non-overlapping response. In 155 MB Glut, Setd1a showed a large signature with 465 FDR hits, whereas Kmt2a, Kmt2b, Kmt2d, and Kmt2e were weak, with only 0–4 hits. Because core SET1A/COMPASS subunits were not perturbed, this comparison is limited to the assayed KMT2 paralogs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Bdp1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a weak but coherent thalamic stress signature marked by up-regulation of Ddit3, Chac1, Asns, Shmt2, and several cytosolic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases including Cars and Mars1, with Kcnc2 down-regulated. This signature was a weaker member of the same ISR/tRNA-aminoacylation state seen more strongly after Elp1 or Elp2 perturbation, linking Pol III-dependent tRNA production to Elongator-related tRNA modification at the transcriptome-signature level, although the correlations were modest and do not demonstrate a direct BDP1-Elongator mechanism.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Mafa in 052 Pvalb Gaba neurons showed no detectable downstream response despite good cell coverage, with 178 Pvalb cells and no gene significant even at p<0.001. In the same cell class, other Maf-family perturbations were active: Maf, Mafb, and Mafg produced FDR-significant changes, including Mafg→Hmox1 and Maf→Cacnb3, Lifr, and Tmem108. Full-signature correlations between Mafa and Maf, Mafb, Mafg, or Nrl were near zero, suggesting target-specific silence in this Pvalb context, although absent Mafa target engagement cannot be excluded.

Gnrhr showed an essentially uncorrelated perturbation signature, with all-library score-vector correlations near zero across reproductive-axis receptors and canonical G alpha q/PLC/PKC/MAPK neighbors, including Kiss1r, Tacr3, Plcb1, Prkcg, Mapk1, Adcy3, Calm1, and Gnb5. In the surveyed brain cell classes, this pathway was therefore not detected as a coherent Gnrhr response, and Gnrhr had no meaningful positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor. This interpretation is tempered by the weak Gnrhr signature, the lack of Gnaq and Gna11 perturbations, and cell-type observations in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where Gnrhr depletion was not evident despite stronger on-target effects for some comparator perturbations.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Gipr in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons did not show a coherent incretin or Gs/cAMP transcriptional neighborhood: whole-transcriptome correlations with Glp1r, Gcgr, Gnas, Adcy1, and Adcy5 were near zero, and no non-self signature neighbor exceeded |r| = 0.109, with even safe-target controls among the top weak positives. This was the only cell type with a corrected Gipr downstream hit, where Prkci decreased, but cAMP/CREB markers remained mostly unchanged. Because related receptor perturbations were themselves weak, these results suggest a sparse Gipr signature rather than a generic class-B GPCR or cAMP program.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Tshz2 showed no transcriptome-wide significant downstream genes in cortical glutamatergic classes 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, whereas the same differential-expression pipeline detected a clear transcription-factor response for the positive comparator Tbr1 in these classes. Tbr1 produced 21 FDR-significant rows, including Cacna1g in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, indicating the Tshz2 null was not simply a universal failure of the Wilcoxon pipeline or of these cell classes to respond to transcription-factor perturbation. This contrast should be interpreted cautiously because Tbr1 is a comparator rather than a pathway neighbor of Tshz2, and guide efficiency or target expression differences may still contribute.

Rtn4r targeting did not produce a coherent transcript-level feedback signature for the canonical Nogo receptor/RHOA anti-axon-growth pathway: queried ligands, coreceptors, and effectors including Rtn4, Mag, Omg, Lingo1, Ngfr, Tnfrsf19, Rhoa, Rock1, Rock2, and Rtn4rl1 were not significantly changed, and the pathway appeared transcriptionally uncoupled after Rtn4r perturbation. This suggests that steady-state mRNA readouts may miss NgR1 pathway engagement, which is largely post-translational, so productive interrogation may require ligand, injury, protein-localization, or RHOA-activity assays rather than DE alone.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Setd5 perturbation in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class produced its strongest signature as an upregulated postsynaptic/synaptic-membrane module, with positive shifts in Lrrc7, Ntng1, Cacna1g, Grm1, Rgs8, Camk2a, Cacng5, Dagla, and Ap2b1. This 18-gene program was enriched for synapse, postsynapse, glutamatergic-synapse, synaptic-membrane, and dendritic-spine terms, providing a compact downstream readout of Setd5 disruption in this thalamic class. Several shared genes also increased after Ankrd11, whereas a restricted subset showed opposing behavior after Med15, Cic, or Rora. Some component genes were supported at FDR 0.1-0.25 rather than FDR<0.05.

Rxrb CRISPRi in profiled neurons did not recover the retinoic-acid/RXR, LXR/PPAR lipid, or bexarotene-associated Wnt/Rho outputs expected from RXR literature: across neuronal clusters, no downstream gene reached conventional FDR significance, and Lrp1, Lrp5, Sfrp5, Sema3f, Abca1, Abca7, Cyp46a1, Trem2, Dvl3, and Vangl2 remained nonresponsive. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, nominal Rxrb self-depletion occurred without an FDR-significant response, while Rora and Thra showed clear comparator signatures. Related perturbations of Rxra, Rxrg, Rara, Nr1h2, Nr1h3, Ppara, and Ppard did not phenocopy the Rxrb score vector, suggesting that partial neuronal Rxrb repression was insufficient to drive these modules under this CRISPRi context.

Etfa showed a restricted nominal signature that was nearly uncorrelated with Bckdhb, Ivd, Dld, Pcca, and Acox1 perturbations, arguing that the observed response was not simply a generic organic-acid or fatty-acid catabolism stress signature. In this dataset, the 90 Etfa features passing nominal p<0.001 had restricted Pearson correlations near zero with those comparators, even though Etfa sits in an electron-transfer flavoprotein and fatty-acid beta-oxidation functional neighborhood with Etfb, Etfdh, and acyl-CoA dehydrogenase genes. This interpretation is exploratory, because the signature was nominal and low similarity could reflect weak target engagement or cell-count differences.

Irf8 was part of a silent microglial/innate module in this neuronal atlas: across 111 target-by-cell-type neuronal contrasts, perturbing Irf8 or the related genes Spi1, Csf1r, Trem2, Cx3cr1, and C3 produced no FDR-supported transcriptional signatures. This shared neuronal silence suggests the lack of response was not unique to Irf8 and is consistent with the profiled cell-type universe omitting the lineage where Irf8 is most established. The comparator set was pathway-informed rather than exhaustive, and Cx3cr1 was not itself a measured transcript row.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chrna3 showed no FDR-significant on-target response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, even in its best-powered stratum with 148 cells, where only several nominal tail genes were seen and the perturbation did not phenocopy engaged cholinergic perturbations. This null appears target-specific rather than a universal cholinergic failure in this thalamic glutamatergic class, because Chrnb2, Chrna4, and Ache each produced detectable on-target responses in the same cells. Within neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptor signaling, related subunits are not identical obligate members of one pentamer, which tempers direct cross-target interpretation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp609 was not transcriptionally interchangeable with Nipbl in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Nipbl perturbation produced a strong response with 188 FDR-significant genes, including Pcp4, Grin2c, Spon1, Atp2b1, Rims2, and Grm1, whereas Zfp609 showed no FDR-significant genes in the same class despite more perturbed cells. Across 20 shared cell types, Zfp609 and Nipbl transcriptomic signatures were essentially uncorrelated, arguing against simple functional equivalence in sampled neuronal contexts; however, this comparison is transcriptomic only, and Nipbl was the only assayed member of the published Zfp609/Nipbl/Integrator axis.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Ryr2 was not broadly interchangeable with its paralog Ryr3 at the transcriptome-signature level. Across 21 shared cell types, Ryr2–Ryr3 score correlations were near zero in 19, with the only visible convergence being weak in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA (r=0.106). This comparison is limited because both signatures were weak and Ryr3 showed no FDR-level gene changes, so the result is signature-based rather than mechanistic. In the broader context of RYR-mediated endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic-reticulum Ca2+ release, Ryr2 appeared buffered and uncoupled from stronger calcium neighbors such as Atp2a2, Calm1, Cacna1g, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Tbx2 was transcriptionally silent in the brain screen, and the closely related Tbx3 showed the same inactive behavior, whereas Tbr1 produced a reproducible cortical glutamatergic signature with 21 FDR-significant genes across 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. This separates an inactive Tbx2/Tbx3 developmental-repressor branch from an active neural T-box program rather than treating T-box factors as interchangeable. The comparison is transcriptomic, limited to guide targets represented in enough cells, and Tbr1 was not used as a mechanistic substitute for TBX2.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Satb2 showed little detectable transcriptomic response in cortical glutamatergic groups, whereas the related projection-neuron factor Tbr1 was clearly active in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. In these same strata, Satb2/Tbr1 signature correlations were weak, and Satb2 did not produce adjusted-significant downstream changes or move cortical marker genes in the Bcl11b-Fezf2-Tbr1/Satb2 network, while Tbr1 perturbation yielded significant genes including Cacna1g and Cpne6. This contrast is perturbation-level only, and Satb2 guide activity was weaker than ideal.

Pik3ca did not share a robust transcriptomic phenotype with other assayed class IA PI3K subunits in this dataset: Pik3cb, Pik3r1, and Pik3r2 showed no FDR-significant rows in the assayed cell types and had near-zero median score correlations to Pik3ca. Within the class IA PI3K/PIP3-AKT signaling context, these single-subunit perturbations therefore were not interchangeable transcriptomic proxies for Pik3ca, although this lack of convergence is tempered by the fact that the comparator perturbations were themselves weak, so low target engagement rather than true biochemical divergence could explain the result.

Cd47 did not converge with available phagocytic-checkpoint family perturbations in the neuronal classes examined: across 19 shared Cd47 cell types, score correlations with Axl, Cd36, Csf1r, Fcgr2b, Itga2b, Itgb1, Mertk, Ptpn11, and Trem2 were essentially null, with median r values from -0.008 to 0.011. This argues against substituting those signatures for the CD47-SIRPα anti-phagocytic axis or related thrombospondin/integrin contexts, but the comparison is limited because direct Sirpa/Sirpg/Sirpb1a and Thbs1-4 perturbations were not available and many indirect neighbors showed weak own-transcript engagement.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Agrp showed no measurable on-target transcript depletion after sgRNA assignment in this DE resource, and several related melanocortin or appetite-pathway perturbations, including Mc3r, Mc4r, Lepr, Ghsr, Npy1r, Npy2r, Npy5r, and Insr, were likewise mostly unengaged or yielded only isolated secondary hits. In contrast, the related intracellular cAMP effector Adcy3 showed clear self-transcript depletion in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, suggesting the dataset can detect knockdown and that Agrp and its lowly expressed neuropeptide-GPCR neighbors form a context-limited subnetwork in this screen.

Pax8 showed nonconvergent and generally weak transcriptomic effects across the 22 assayed brain subclasses: it had no strong positive or negative signature neighbors, and its score-vector correlations with Pax2, Pax5, Pax6, and Nkx2-1 were near zero, while related perturbations in the broader PAX/NKX neighborhood were themselves largely FDR-negative. These data argue against an active shared paired-box PAX/Nkx2-1 transcription-factor module, despite known Pax8–Nkx2-1 proximity in thyroid contexts. This inference is tempered because correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors and weak on-target readout may dampen all comparisons.

Ndufb10 perturbation did not produce a shared Complex I or broader OXPHOS transcriptomic signature: across many mouse brain cell types, including glutamatergic and GABAergic populations, Ndufb10, Ndufa13, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, Ndufs4, Uqcrc1, Cox5a, and Sdha knockdowns were largely dominated by depletion of their own target transcript rather than a common stress program. Whole-signature correlations with Ndufb10 were near zero, including Ndufa13 (r=0.0247) and Ndufs2 (r=-0.0116), although this bulk Wilcoxon correlation approach could miss subtler protein-level or metabolic convergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Wdfy3 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons produced a synaptic/neurosecretory and AP-1/JNK transcript response rather than a generic bulk-autophagy program: Stmn4, Gpm6a, Kcnc2, Tspan7, Scg2, Syt11, Syt1, Chgb, Jun, and nominal-FDR Jund were mostly decreased, while Gls and Mapk8 increased. Enrichment recovered presynaptic/synaptic membrane and AP-1 terms, and this was the principal Wdfy3-responsive cell context, with recurrent Stmn4 down also seen in 155 MB Glut. These RNA changes do not by themselves establish altered synaptic release, JNK/AP-1 activity, or protein abundance.

Hdac4 showed an essentially uncorrelated Perturb-seq signature relative to other represented members of the HDAC4–MEF2/class-IIa transcriptional repression axis, including Hdac5, Hdac8, Mef2a, Mef2c, Mef2d, Camk2a, Camk2b, Camk4, Ywhae, Ywhag, Ywhaz, and Runx2. In the assayed states, this suggests that acute Hdac4 perturbation did not produce a detectable shared module-level response, even though the analysis could recover MEF2-factor transcriptional responses in cortical glutamatergic populations. In 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut neurons, nominal Hdac4-associated changes included Grin2a and reduced Shank2, but Hdac4 mRNA engagement was weak, so the near-zero correlations indicate lack of a detectable shared signature rather than biochemical independence.

Dync2i1 perturbation did not produce a canonical intraflagellar transport or primary-cilium Hedgehog transcriptional response. Across the measured dataset, curated IFT, BBS, transition-zone, and Hedgehog markers showed no adjusted changes, including Ift80, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Ift122, Ttc21b, Bbs9, Ptch1, Smo, Gli1, Gli2, and Gli3, and no related signature convergence was detected. This suggests the Perturb-seq readout was uncoupled from the expected pathway module, with the caveat that the check relied on transcript abundance and Hedgehog transcription factors were often lowly detected.

Itga2 showed a weak, largely isolated transcriptomic signature that did not phenocopy Itgb1 or nearby integrin/collagen-pathway perturbations. Across shared cell types, the Itga2 score vector was almost orthogonal to Itgb1, with Pearson r from -0.044 to +0.044, and no queried integrin, collagen, Src/FAK, MAPK, PI3K, Rac1, or Cdc42 perturbation exceeded |r| = 0.128. In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, this appeared as exploratory Bcar1 up without a coordinated core alpha2-beta1 integrin/ECM adhesion/focal-adhesion shift. Because the Itga2 signatures were themselves weak, this supports non-interchangeability rather than inverted alpha2-beta1 biology.

Sox17 perturbation showed no multiple-testing-corrected transcriptional response in any of the 23 assayed cell types, and a focused check of canonical SOX17-linked programs was likewise negative. WNT/CTNNB1 genes Ctnnb1, Lef1, Tcf7l2, and Axin2, arterial/endothelial Notch-vascular genes Notch1 and Dll4, endothelial markers Cdh5, Pecam1, Kdr, and Flt1, and SOXF genes Sox7 and Sox18 all had minimum FDR=1.0, suggesting these vascular, Wnt, and SOXF axes were uncoupled from the neuronal response. This was a targeted transcript check rather than a powered pathway-enrichment test, and endothelial or OPC compartments were not assayed.

Pnpt1 showed a largely null perturbation profile, and available RNA-processing, mitochondrial-RNA, and innate-immune comparators did not converge on it: Adar, Adarb1, Ddx3x, Dhx9, Ifih1, Irf3, Irf7, Lrpprc, Stat1, and Tlr3 all had near-zero score-vector correlations. In the PNPT1/SUPV3L1 mitochondrial RNA homeostasis context, no detectable mitochondrial RNA response was seen, including for mt-Nd2, mt-Nd3, mt-Atp8, and mt-Cytb. The strongest genome-wide neighbors appeared in 308 CB GABA cells, but correlations remained weak and no differential-expression row was FDR-significant. Interpretation is limited because direct mtEXO comparators, especially Supv3l1 and exosome genes such as Dis3, were not perturbed.

Ift81 perturbation did not produce a detectable transcriptomic response in canonical ciliary or Hedgehog-Smoothened-GLI readouts in this dataset: Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, and Smo were unchanged, and measured intraciliary transport and BBSome-related genes including Ift43, Ift88, Ttc21b, Kif3b, Bbs5, and Bbs9 also failed to show a compensatory module. This suggests that, in mostly neuronal classes from mature mouse brain, the transcriptome did not report canonical IFT81 pathway failure, with the caveat that ciliary trafficking, axoneme length, receptor localization, and Hedgehog responsiveness were not measured.

Dzip1 perturbation showed no FDR-supported transcriptional response in canonical Hedgehog or ciliary sentinel genes, including Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Hhip, Gpr161, Ift88, Bbs5, and Cep290, indicating that the expected Hedgehog/ciliary readout was silent at the mRNA level in these mouse-brain Perturb-seq profiles. In 046 CTX-CGE GABA and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut cells, there was likewise no FDR-supported cilium assembly or basal-body trafficking module, although Dzip1l was exploratorily increased in two classes. Because Dzip1 target engagement was weak and basal Hedgehog activity in the assayed neuronal classes is unknown, these data do not strongly contradict embryonic mouse findings of reduced Gli1 and Ptch1 after Dzip1 loss.

Ift81 showed no meaningful convergence with other ciliary perturbations in this dataset: across comparisons with Ift88, Ift43, Ttc21b, Kif3b, Dync2h1, Bbs5, Bbs9, Smo, Ptch1, and Gli1/2/3, transcriptome-wide score-vector correlations were weak, and even the best global non-self neighbor remained small. This argues against treating the weak Ift81 profile as a generic primary-cilium state. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, nominal on-target depletion and downstream signal were strongest yet still lacked FDR-significant genes, and canonical Hedgehog transcripts were unchanged after Ift81; related perturbations also had weak own-transcript depletion, and these correlations do not measure protein or ciliary phenotypes.

Gprasp2 perturbation in mouse brain neurons did not reproduce the Hedgehog or apoptosis transcriptional response reported for Gprasp2-null HEI-OC1 auditory cells. Across brain Perturb-seq profiles, including the two target-engaged neuronal classes, Smo, Ptch1, Ptch2, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Shh, Bcl2, Bax, and Casp3, Casp8, Casp9 were not FDR-significant, and in the engaged classes they were not even nominally shifted. This suggests the auditory-cell Hedgehog/apoptosis mechanism is strongly context dependent, with the caveat that the literature used full knockout and direct apoptosis assays, whereas the screen measured mRNA changes after partial perturbation in mouse brain neurons.

Foxa2 perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Lmx1a, Lmx1b, Nr4a2, En1, En2, Otx2, Pitx3, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Foxp1, and Foxp2 across shared assayed mouse-brain cell types, with full-transcriptome Pearson correlations near zero (extrema r = 0.0953 and r = -0.0878). This argues against treating Foxa2 as interchangeable with these dopaminergic developmental partners in the tested classes, but the comparison is limited by weak Foxa2 signatures and by assayed cell types that were mostly outside embryonic Foxa2-positive ventral midbrain progenitors, including MB Dopa where the expected loss was not tested.

Camk4 showed a weak basal transcriptomic response that was nearly orthogonal to perturbations of related Ca2+/calmodulin-CaMKK-CaMKIV-CREB signaling nodes, including Calm1/2/3, Camk2a/b/g, Creb1, Mef2a/c, Ppp3ca/cc, and Prkaca. Across same-cell full-transcriptome comparisons, all 262 Camk4 correlations with these pathway-adjacent perturbations had |r| < 0.10, even though several of those perturbations produced more genome-wide significant differential-expression rows than Camk4. This comparison is limited to steady-state RNA signatures, whereas curated pathway links are largely calcium-activation and phosphorylation relationships.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mesp2 showed restricted signatures in two brain glutamatergic cell types, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but perturbations of Tbx6, Dll1, Hes7, Notch1-4, and Fgfr1/2 did not phenocopy those signatures. In these two Mesp2 FDR-positive classes, correlations based on the top 100 Mesp2-ranked genes were only weak, and Tbx6, Dll1, and Hes7 had no FDR-significant genes across assayed brain contrasts. This divergence from the Mesp2-Tbx6-Notch-Ripply-Lfng somitogenesis circuit is consistent with a non-PSM, brain-specific context, with the caveat that several direct feedback genes were not included in the perturbation panel.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pax3 did not phenocopy Pax7 or any other Pax-family perturbation across the profiled adult brain cell types, including multiple cortical glutamatergic classes, hippocampal glutamatergic neurons, diverse GABAergic populations, hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, pineal, and cerebellar cells. Pax3-versus-other-Pax score correlations across matched comparisons were centered near zero, and rank-based statistics showed no detectable on-target transcript depletion. Because nearly all Pax-family perturbations were themselves largely null, these paralog relationships are difficult to interpret mechanistically, but the overall pattern is consistent with a paired-box developmental module that is absent or weakly engaged in this setting.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Dmd perturbation did not detectably mobilize a shared dystrophin-glycoprotein or agrin/dystroglycan RNA module across multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic classes, including L4-5 IT CTX Glut, CA3/CA2-FC DG Glut, Pvalb Gaba, and MB Glut. Transcripts such as Utrn, Grin1, Gabra1, and Gabrg2, along with comparator genes Dag1, Snta1, and Sgcd, showed weak or no FDR-level downstream changes. Agrn knockdown was on-target in five classes, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but yielded no additional significant genes, consistent with weak target engagement or transcriptional buffering rather than a shared DGC response.

Stx5a showed signatures that were largely uncoupled from measured ER-Golgi trafficking neighbors: perturbations of Cog4, Cog5, Copa, Copg1, Sar1b, and Sec23a, despite sometimes stronger on-target knockdown than Stx5a, had score-vector correlations with Stx5a centered near zero, including in the two strongest Stx5a cell classes. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, there was no high-correlation whole-screen or ER-Golgi-neighbor signature, and in 308 CB GABA, Copg1-down was observed but related perturbations still did not robustly phenocopy Stx5a. This argues against simply transferring bulk secretory-pathway annotations to Stx5a here, while leaving open weak Stx5a editing, alternative STX5 SNARE wiring, or cell-state-specific buffering; notably, direct partners Bet1, Gosr1, Gosr2, Sec22b, Ykt6, and Scfd1 were not available for matched comparison.

Otx2 showed no detectable convergence with Crx, Rax, Six3, Pax6, Vsx2, Six6, Pitx2, or any other profiled target: across 22 Otx2-tested neuronal subclasses, score-vector correlations were near zero, with the best positive correlation in any cell type only r = 0.1368. In this adult neuronal screen, including 217 P MY Pineal Glut where the Otx2-Crx retinal and pineal fate program was not detected, the weak Otx2 profile therefore resembles sparse noise rather than a buffered or redundant OTX/CRX-family module, while the lack of target engagement means these null correlations should not be interpreted as biochemical independence.

Six1 perturbation did not detectably engage the canonical PAX-SIX-EYA-DACH developmental transcriptional network in this brain dataset. Across all 23 Six1-tested cell classes, transcripts and readouts linked to kidney, myogenic, proliferative, and adipocyte-associated programs, including Pax2, Six2, Sall1, Grem1, Myod1, Myog, Ccnd1, Myc, Igfbp5, Cidea, Eya1, Eya2, and Dach1, were not detectably altered. Available perturbations of related factors such as Six3, Six5, Six6, and Dach1 were also weak overall, and because Eya1-Eya4 and Six2 were measured but not directly perturbed, only part of the canonical complex was sampled.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Tcf4 in 052 Pvalb Gaba showed a signature that measured E-protein paralogs and neural bHLH neighbors did not recapitulate: Tcf3 and Tcf12 perturbations did not lower Oprd1 or Tmem44, and all-gene Pearson correlations to the Tcf4 signature were near zero for Tcf3, Tcf12, Neurod1, and Neurod2, with the strongest non-Tcf4 neighbor only r=0.0667. This nonconvergence within the E-box/bHLH transcription-factor network suggests shared bHLH/E-box annotation was not sufficient to predict interchangeable acute single-cell phenotypes here, although comparator perturbations also had weak conventional signal and the correlation scan reflects sparse transcriptomic structure rather than direct protein interaction data.

Pax1 did not phenocopy the screened PAX paralogs or available developmental neighbors in this adult-brain dataset. Across Pax2–Pax8, score-vector correlations with Pax1 were uniformly weak, with a maximum absolute Pearson r of 0.177, and canonical partners such as Meox1, Hoxa3, Foxn1, and Pbx1 were likewise nonconvergent. The only notable resemblance was a modest, CA3-restricted similarity to Fgfr2 within 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, where all |r| > 0.2 relationships occurred, but this remained exploratory because the minimum Pax1 FDR there was 0.5072. Pax9, the most relevant reported paralog, was not tested.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Manf, in the strongest 155 MB Glut context, showed positive signature convergence with perturbations of ER/secretory and proteostasis-adjacent genes, including Gfpt1, Dhdds, Sec31a, Atp2a2, Pomp, Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, and Hspa5, while no strong anti-correlated neighbor was detected. This pattern suggests a broader proteostasis liability network rather than a single linear UPR factor, but it is based on moderate correlations across the top 200 Manf-score genes in one cell type, so it should be treated as a restricted-signature hypothesis; Hspa5 was informative but weakly sampled.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Tbx21 was largely silent in this atlas, whereas the brain T-box factor Tbr1 produced a reproducible cortical-glutamatergic response, indicating that the negative result is Tbx21-specific rather than a generic failure to perturb T-box transcription factors. Tbr1 yielded 21 FDR-significant hits concentrated in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, while Tbx21 and most other profiled non-brain T-box factors showed none. This comparison is based on counts of FDR-significant genes and does not establish equal guide efficiency across all T-box targets.

Dcc was a target-engagement outlier among neuronal surface-receptor perturbations: its guides showed weak transcript-level on-target effects that failed multiple-testing correction in every tested class, with Dcc self-depletion seen in 0 of 21 classes. This was not a general failure to detect long receptor-transcript knockdown in the dataset, because Cntn1, Nrcam, Ncam1, Epha4, Cntnap1, and Cntnap2 often showed strong self-transcript depletion across the same class universe, including high-depth classes such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. These comparators control detectability, not pathway equivalence or an obligatory DCC complex.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Bicc1 was essentially null in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: unlike Ctnnb1 perturbation in the same cell class, which reduced its own transcript and produced 383 FDR-significant genes, Bicc1 showed no on-target or downstream FDR signal. Its mRNA differential-expression score vector had negligible correlation with curated ciliary, miRNA, and Wnt-neighbor perturbations, including Ago1, Ago2, Ahi1, Dicer1, Pkd1, Prickle1, Rpgrip1l, and Ttc21b, indicating that the Bicc1 null is not interchangeable with a generic β-catenin/Wnt response, though this contrast is limited by weak Bicc1 engagement and correlation being restricted to mRNA DE vectors.

Pax6 showed no hidden Pax-family transcriptomic phenotype in this neuronal panel. Across 22 Pax6-assayed neuronal classes, the Pax6 transcript row was non-significant and no downstream gene reached standard multiple-testing significance, and a scan across the Pax paired-box paralog family (Pax1–Pax8) found no robust Pax6-specific convergence or divergence. Within matched cell types, Pax6-versus-other-Pax correlations were near zero, consistent with the broader lack of robust responses among Pax1–Pax8 perturbations; because paralog signatures were themselves weak, this absence of correlation should not be overread as functional antagonism.

Gpr12 did not show the expected convergence with adenylate cyclase/cAMP/PKA-CREB pathway perturbations in this dataset: its ranked scRNA signature was nearly uncorrelated with Gnas, Prkaca, and Creb1, and even its strongest restricted signature neighbors were only modest and cell-type-localized. This argues against treating the Gpr12 signature as an adult cell-autonomous Gs/PKA surrogate here, although the comparison is exploratory, the direct Gnas perturbation was itself weak, and close paralogs Gpr3 and Gpr6 were not assayed for a direct test.

Glra2 did not transcriptionally converge with glycinergic receptor neighbors: whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon score correlations between Glra2 and Glra1, Glra3, Glrb, Gphn, or Slc6a5 were near zero, and no perturbation in the full library showed a strong positive or negative match to any Glra2 cell-type signature. This buffered or absent RNA response was seen in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, suggesting that within glycine-gated chloride-channel signaling, Glra2 may be coupled more electrophysiologically than transcriptionally.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Col2a1 showed nonconvergent brain signatures relative to related collagen-family and collagen-receptor perturbations: Col11a1, Col25a1, Col4a1, Ddr2, Itga2, and Itgb1 each had zero FDR<0.05 rows across 21–23 assayed cell types, and in the four Col2a1-visible populations—017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 308 CB GABA—the signed-score correlations with Col2a1 were only -0.069 to 0.114. Thus, the collagen extracellular-matrix and receptor neighborhood did not phenocopy Col2a1; however, only related genes present in the library were tested and the correlations were based on weak signatures.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Setd1a loss produced a modest but coherent mTORC1-neighbor transcriptomic pattern: Nprl3 was repeatedly down, and Setd1a signatures showed modest positive similarity to Tsc1 and Tsc2 perturbations in MB Glut, TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and MB P MY GABA. The strongest Setd1a responses were largely down-regulated modules, with high-count thalamic glutamatergic cells showing strong downstream repression despite only nominal Setd1a transcript reduction. Because this signal is restricted-signature-based and transcriptomic, it suggests, rather than proves, mTORC1 activation, and no phospho-mTORC1 substrate was measured.

Ivd perturbation produced RNA signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of assayed BCAA-pathway and adjacent acyl-CoA genes, including Acat1, Auh, Bckdhb, Bckdk, Dld, Etfa, and Pcca. This lack of interchangeability persisted even though Acat1 and Auh achieved target-transcript knockdown at FDR level in at least one cell type, suggesting the pathway did not collapse into a single shared transcriptional program. A caveat is that these correlations were computed on weak restricted signatures, and many comparator target transcripts were sub-FDR in many cell types.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Vsx1 showed a sparse, cell-type-specific signature in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and nearby retinal transcription-factor perturbations did not converge on it. In this non-retinal class, Vsx2 did not phenocopy Vsx1: it produced no FDR-significant genes and its score vector correlated only weakly with the Vsx1 signature (r=0.054). Other retinal-neighbor perturbations, including Otx2, Crx, Rax, Neurod1, Ptf1a, Grm6, Nyx, and Gpr179, were likewise near zero, with no strong convergent or opposing Vsx1-like pattern; weak target engagement may have dampened correlations.

Col11a1 was uncoupled from the type XI collagen and collagen-interaction module in this neuronal Perturb-seq map: its signature showed near-zero correlation with Col2a1, Col25a1, Col4a1, Ddr2, Itga2, and Itgb1, and these related perturbations were largely FDR-negative across assayed neuronal cell types. The one FDR-level Col2a1 hit occurred in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, while 308 CB GABA showed some nominal Col11a1-versus-Col4a1 alignment, but neither supported a coherent ECM program. Because the comparator perturbations were themselves mostly weak, this is best interpreted as absence of convergence rather than an opposing effect.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Epha5 showed a divergent Perturb-seq profile rather than a generic Eph receptor effect. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, the only class with FDR-significant Epha5 target loss, the RNA response was buffered and nearly uncorrelated with Epha4 or Epha7; similarly low correlations were seen in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, where Epha5 was nominal and lacked a canonical Grin/Dlg4 synaptogenic response. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Epha4 and Epha7 knocked down strongly while Epha5 did not. Whole-library neighbors for Epha5 were also weak, although these correlations reflect restricted scRNA-seq signatures and do not exclude shared phosphorylation or morphology phenotypes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pex13 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic cells showed a distinctive corrected response centered on Insig1 and a cholesterol/sterol module, but this pattern was not broadly recapitulated by other assayed peroxisome-family perturbations. Pex1, Abcd3, Acox1, and Hsd17b4 did not reproduce a corrected Pex13-like TH phenotype, and although Pex14 achieved strong target-transcript knockdown, it showed only buffered downstream effects. These results suggest peroxisomal import or lipid-metabolism genes were not interchangeable in this assay, while noting that most non-Pex14 comparators had weak target engagement, limiting power to infer true pathway separation.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Klc1 knockdown showed no strong transcriptional convergence with the engaged kinesin-1 neighbors Klc2, Kif5a, or Kif5c across 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In these shared cell types, each perturbation mostly reported its own target transcript rather than a common kinesin-1 or microtubule cargo-transport RNA module; for example, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed strong Klc1 depletion with only Klc1 significant, and APP/Mapt responses were negative. Interpretation is limited by sparse secondary differential expression, and Kif5b, Klc3, and Klc4 were not informative here.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Celsr2 showed little transcriptomic coupling to the available noncanonical Wnt/planar cell polarity neighbors in this dataset. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Fzd3 was the top positive whole-signature neighbor of Celsr2, but the similarity was weak and exploratory, and Fzd3 itself had no FDR-significant response in that cell type. Other assayed PCP-related comparators, including Fzd6, Prickle1, Ror1, and Ror2, likewise did not phenocopy a broad Celsr2-like program, suggesting that any shared Celsr2–Fzd3 biology may be developmental, structural, or cell-contact dependent rather than a robust acute mRNA module.

Phf6 did not phenocopy core NuRD perturbation in this dataset: genome-wide tests found no conventionally significant downstream transcript changes after Phf6 perturbation, whereas Chd4 showed a large corrected signature and other related perturbations varied from sparse to strong, including null or weak effects for Gatad2b, Mbd2, Mbd5, and Phf8 and stronger effects for Phf12. These results suggest short-term transcriptomic uncoupling between PHF6 and generic NuRD chromatin regulation in these brain cell classes, rather than proving that PHF6 never acts through NuRD in brain.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tbx2 showed only weak, uncoupled signatures in mouse brain neurons, with no cell type yielding a multiple-testing-significant downstream response to Tbx2 perturbation. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, despite a large Chd4 signature, the Tbx2–Chd4 correlation was only r=0.022, and across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA, correlations between Tbx2 and Chd4, Mbd2, Gatad2b, Pbx1, Adam10, or Mitf never exceeded |r|=0.095. These data argue against Tbx2 scores reflecting TBX2-associated NuRD, MITF, or ADAM10 regulatory axes, although only a subset of TBX2 partners was perturbed and score-vector correlation cannot test physical complex formation.

Casz1 was weak and largely uncoupled from active NuRD-associated chromatin and neurodevelopmental perturbations in this adult brain Perturb-seq matrix. Compared with Casz1, Chd4, Gatad2b, Mbd2, Camta1, Tbr1, Kif1b, and Zic1 produced stronger FDR-supported signatures, and Casz1 was essentially uncorrelated with Camta1 and NuRD-linked perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Casz1 showed only nominal changes without FDR hits, while Camta1 or Chd4 were significant. Because prior CASZ1b-NuRD support comes from biochemical or tumor contexts, STRING links are associative, and Casz1 transcript knockdown was not observed, these data do not support using Casz1 as a proxy for NuRD or Camta1 activity in these adult brain classes.

Ncoa3 showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signature correlations with Ncoa1, Crebbp, Ep300, and measured nuclear-receptor perturbations including Esr1, Esr2, Nr3c1, Ar, Thra, and Thrb, so it did not phenocopy its expected SRC/p160 nuclear-receptor coactivation partners in this assay. Even in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, the only class with an adjusted Ncoa3-responsive gene, Anapc4, neighbor analysis found no strong convergent or anti-correlated perturbation. This lack of convergence is hard to interpret because Ncoa3 itself was not significantly depleted, and Ncoa2 was not in the library.

Cox6b1 did not phenocopy other complex IV perturbations in this experiment: unlike Cox5a, Ndufa4, and Cox4i1, it showed only weak or nominal own-transcript reduction without FDR-level downstream responses, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, where Cox5a and others reached clearer on-target depletion. Cox6b1 whole-transcriptome signatures were also nearly uncorrelated with Cox5a, Cox4i1, Ndufa4, Cox6a1, Cox11, Cox7b, and Cox8a, so same-complex membership in respiratory electron transport and complex IV assembly did not substitute for direct Cox6b1 validation here.

Cd3g perturbation in this neuronal dataset appeared uncoupled from canonical TCR-CD3 signaling: Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd247, Lck, Lat, and Zap70 remained nonsignificant in every tested cell type, so the neuronal signatures did not show measurable induction or repression of proximal TCR-CD3 pathway genes. This suggests the observed Cd3g-related transcriptional effects are disconnected from the known immune signaling circuit in neurons, with the caveat that the assay captured steady-state RNA rather than receptor phosphorylation or calcium/NFAT signaling.

Antxr2 showed an essentially uncorrelated transcriptional signature across 23 profiled mouse-brain neuronal classes, including excitatory, inhibitory, and dopaminergic neurons: Antxr1 did not phenocopy Antxr2, and assayed ECM, collagen/integrin, or reported entry-neighbor perturbations such as Lrp6, Col4a1, Itga2, Itga6, and Itgb1 showed near-zero transcriptome-scale convergence with Antxr2. In these cells, Antxr2 also had weak self-knockdown and no collagen-VI mRNA induction, although interpretation is limited because weak signatures can be noise-dominated and the native ANTXR2 ligand complex was not fully represented among perturbations.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Rho showed a broader retinal/opsin-null pattern in brain cell classes, with no FDR-significant transcriptome response across 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and no shared phototransduction-like signature with comparator perturbations Crx, Gucy2e, Nr2e3, Opn1mw, Opn1sw, Gnb5, or Nrl. Most comparators were likewise inert; Gnb5 showed detectable on-target depletion only in 052 Pvalb Gaba, and Nrl produced sparse isolated hits in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and low-cell-count 217 P MY Pineal Glut, where Rho had only 28 perturbed cells and no target engagement. Because comparators were chosen by retinal biology and library availability rather than exhaustive signature matching, these rare isolated hits could be stochastic or cell-type-specific.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Trak1 showed a notably sparse transcriptional response, appearing uncoupled from the strong mitochondrial dynamics and motor-adjacent stress modules seen in the same neuronal classes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, Trak1 yielded 0, 1, and 0 adjusted DE genes, whereas Dctn1, Dnm1l, Dync1h1, Hspa9, Ogt, and Opa1 produced tens to hundreds. This contrast suggests Trak1 was weaker than these pathway neighbors here, although the comparators are functionally adjacent rather than one stoichiometric complex, and some may have had stronger knockdown than Trak1.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atxn10 showed recurrent positive signature similarity to Gfpt1-targeted perturbations in both 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, which is directionally compatible with an ATXN10–OGT theme, but this remained exploratory rather than pathway proof. In Pvalb, the strongest neighbors were broader proteostasis and organelle-homeostasis states, including Hspa9, Vcp, Atp6v0c, Atp6v1b2, Pomp, and Psmb4. Important caveats are that Gfpt1-targeting guides did not measurably reduce Gfpt1 mRNA in the compared cell types, Ogt perturbation was a weak or absent Atxn10 neighbor despite robust Ogt knockdown, and the comparison used restricted Atxn10 FDR signatures.

Zkscan3 showed no shared detectable transcriptomic signature with the in-library Zkscan1 or Zkscan16 perturbations: their full signatures were nearly orthogonal to Zkscan3, and genome-wide positive or negative signature neighbors were extremely weak, with no correlation exceeding |r|=0.028 and the strongest at r=0.027. This argues that the null Zkscan3 result is not simply embedded in a broader KRAB/SCAN zinc-finger transcriptional regulation module in this screen, although the comparison is limited to transcriptomic readouts and to homologous mouse targets present in the library.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Scn2a perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced a transcriptomic signature that related Nav-channel and SCN2A-disease-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy. In this best-powered Scn2a cell type, effective perturbations of Scn1a, Scn1b, Ank3, Fgf13, Kcnq2, and Stxbp1 showed only weak to divergent similarity to the top 200 Scn2a-ranked genes, with Pearson r values from -0.184 to 0.166. This suggests the RNA response was target-specific rather than interchangeable across the SCN2A STRING/Nav interaction neighborhood, although direct channel physiology could still reveal relationships not captured by mRNA differential expression.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Abcd3 produced transcriptomic signatures that were nearly orthogonal to other assayed peroxisome-related perturbations, including Acox1, Hsd17b4, Pex1, Pex13, and Pex14, arguing that peroxisomal lipid transport, beta-oxidation, and matrix-import genes were not interchangeable perturbations in these neurons. This contrast was most evident in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, where Pex14 showed effective target knockdown yet still did not converge with Abcd3. Most comparator perturbations were otherwise weak, so the strongest support comes from the shared Pex14-engaged cell classes.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hsd17b4 perturbation did not converge with assayed peroxisomal neighbors, despite these genes sharing curated peroxisomal network annotations. Across same-cell comparisons with Abcd3, Acox1, Pex1, Pex13, and Pex14, Hsd17b4 profiles were nearly uncorrelated, with a maximum absolute Spearman rho of 0.096, arguing against using Hsd17b4 top genes as a generic peroxisomal beta-oxidation module. This contrast was evident in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, where Pex14 showed robust self-depletion, while most Hsd17b4 signatures were weak, leaving open that low target engagement rather than true pathway divergence explains the lack of convergence.

Rsrc1 showed a weak, uncoupled perturbation signature in this atlas despite its annotation as an SR-related pre-mRNA splicing and nuclear-speckle RNA-processing factor. Unlike pathway-neighbor perturbations such as Srsf1, U2af2, Srrm2, Cdc40, Fus, and Ddx39b, which produced strong transcriptomic signatures, Rsrc1 had no FDR-significant gene-by-cell-type rows and its whole-transcriptome score vectors were only weakly correlated with those perturbations, generally with |r| below 0.07. This contrast is expression-signature based, and the comparator genes are pathway neighbors rather than direct one-to-one substitutes for Rsrc1.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Hesx1 showed weak engagement and was not interchangeable with congenital hypopituitarism or forebrain-development neighbors in mature brain cell classes. Across 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA, perturbation signatures for Sox2, Six3, Chd7, Prop1, Pou1f1, Lhx3, Lhx4, Otx2, Pax6, Gli2, Prokr2, Nsmf, Sox3, and Tbx19 were centered near zero correlation with Hesx1; even when Sox2, Six3, or Chd7 had FDR-significant rows such as Slc6a6, Tnnt1, Stam, or Nfyb, their matched-cell signatures remained essentially orthogonal to Hesx1.

Spi1 showed a shared null pattern across the 22 measured glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal subclasses: its downstream scan was FDR-null, with only rare nominal hits that did not recur across cell types. The same neuronal null extended to PU.1-associated myeloid network genes Irf8 and Csf1r and to the microglial/Alzheimer-related genes Abca7, Cx3cr1, P2ry12, Tlr4, and Trem2, indicating that the canonical PU.1 myeloid axis was not detected in these neuronal states. This cautions against inferring a neuronal cell-autonomous response from disease-gene membership alone, although the pathway-informed comparator set was incomplete.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grik5 showed a distinct perturbation signature in the two cell classes where it was FDR-depleted, 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: perturbations of the related kainate receptor genes Grik1, Grik2, Grik3, and Grik4 did not phenocopy Grik5, had no FDR-significant DE programs in these classes, and their transcriptome-wide DE-score correlations with the Grik5 vector were near zero (about -0.011 to 0.056). This separates a GluK5-specific readout from a generic kainate-subunit signature, although some Grik1-Grik4 perturbations showed weak on-target mRNA depletion and may have been under-engaged.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
full_finding_text: Grik5 perturbation did not produce coordinated mRNA compensation by other kainate receptor subunits. Across contrasts examining Grik1, Grik2, Grik3, and Grik4 after Grik5 loss, no recurrent induction survived multiple testing, arguing against a general transcriptional replacement program for GluK5-containing kainate receptors. The only same-family signal was an exploratory Grik4 increase in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, but this occurred in a low-cell comparison where Grik5 itself was not detectably depleted, so it should be treated as a hypothesis rather than evidence of consistent compensation.

Gstm5 perturbation did not produce detectable transcriptional compensation in the measured glutathione transferase and xenobiotic catabolic process module: assayed Mu-class paralogs Gstm1, Gstm2, Gstm3, Gstm6, and Gstm7, as well as the Nfe2l2-Gclc-Gclm glutathione-synthesis axis, showed no adjusted induction. This argues against a strong mRNA feedback buffer in these neurons despite the local Mu-GST paralog family context, although only mRNA-level compensation was tested and protein abundance or enzyme activity could still compensate.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nalcn loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut showed weak or no transcriptomic convergence with GPCR and ion-channel neighbor signatures. In the most responsive thalamic class, the largest full-signature correlation to any perturbation was still weak, and Chrm3, Tacr1, Ntsr1, Hcn2, Kcnq2, Scn1a, Scn8a, Cacna1a, and Cacna1c were near zero, even though several channel perturbations were efficiently depleted in the same cells. This makes the uncoupling stronger for Hcn2, Kcnq2, Scn1a, and Scn8a than for the receptor perturbations, whose self-transcript engagement was weak in these cell types.

Gclm showed no robust convergent perturbation module: the assayed Gclc complex-member perturbation did not phenocopy the Gclm transcriptomic signature, and transcriptome-wide signature neighbors such as Rgma and Sphk1 were only very weakly related. In this dataset, Gclc and Gclm score vectors were nearly uncorrelated, with weak Gclm mRNA decrease but no canonical glutathione biosynthetic process activation or Gclc convergence, so neither weak signature can be treated as a clean readout of glutamate-cysteine ligase loss. A key caveat is that Gclc itself had poor measurable target engagement, and the neighbor scan used simple within-cell Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon scores.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Atxn10 loss in glutamatergic neurons produced a convergent but modest neuronal homeostasis signature: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, Atp1a3, Eef1a2, Snap25, Kifc2, Macf1, and multiple tubulin genes including Tuba4a, Tubb4a, and Tubb4b were mostly reduced, pointing to ion-pump, translation, and tubulin/cytoskeletal pathways. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, target engagement was strong but the significant response was narrow, centered on Atxn10, Tubb3, and Tubb4a. Shared genes were few in the 17-gene MB signature, and the cortical response had only three FDR-significant genes.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ehmt1 in 308 CB GABA cells showed an exploratory cerebellar signature-neighbor pattern rather than clear same-cell differential expression: Wdr26 was the top positive signature neighbor of the Ehmt1 perturbation (r=0.358) and Eef2 was the top negative neighbor (r=-0.329). This pattern was stronger than global Ehmt1 correlations, but Ehmt1 itself had no FDR<0.05 genes in 308 CB GABA, and the relationship was based only on correlations of ranked DE scores, so it should not be overread as mechanistic convergence.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Plpbp perturbation did not produce a coherent transcriptional compensation program in pyridoxal phosphate/vitamin B6 homeostasis or GABA metabolism. In 308 CB GABA, the only class with nominal Plpbp mRNA depletion near the top of the signature, Pnpo was only nominally increased, while Pdxk, Pdxp, Aldh7a1, Gad1, Gad2, and Abat were not FDR-regulated. Nominal Pdxk increases instead appeared in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 053 Sst Gaba without measurable Plpbp depletion, and all highlighted transcript-level tests had FDR=1.0, with no metabolite or PLP-dependent enzyme activity data available.

Mbd5 perturbation did not show a measurable canonical methyl-CpG-reader or NuRD-like signature in this dataset: its mean score-vector correlations with Mbd2, Mecp2, Chd4, and Gatad2b were near zero, indicating that Mbd5 was not interchangeable with these perturbations in the methyl-CpG-reader and NuRD-associated chromatin repression space. This pattern is consistent with the broader view that MBD5/MBD6 are divergent chromatin proteins rather than members of the classical MBD2-NuRD axis, although the inference here comes from weak Mbd5 profiles and cross-perturbation signature comparison rather than a direct biochemical test in the assayed cells.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nr4a1 showed its only notable signature-neighbor structure in 308 CB GABA, where a weak, non-FDR signature aligned positively with Wdr26, Dstyk, and Cckar and negatively with Ranbp2, B9d1, and Fbxo11. This cell type had the densest nominal Nr4a1 tail, but the strongest neighbors were non-NR4A perturbations; Nr4a2 and Nr4a3 were only weaker neighbors. Overall, this CB GABA axis is an exploratory rescreening hypothesis rather than a mechanistic NR4A pathway claim.

Bin1 showed a buffered transcriptional phenotype in this clathrin-mediated endocytosis context: despite confirmed Bin1 depletion, no non-target FDR-significant differentially expressed genes were detected after excluding the target transcript itself, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA cells. In contrast, pathway neighbors Ap2s1, Ap2m1, and Cltc produced broad downstream transcriptomic responses, with 1,319, 142, and 92 non-target FDR hits, respectively. This suggests Bin1 was not interchangeable with core AP2/clathrin perturbations, although cross-perturbation comparisons are limited by guide efficiency, perturbed-cell counts, and the transcriptomic, non-biochemical nature of the assay.

Pex1 perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported peroxisomal protein-import or peroxisomal cargo mRNA module. Despite PEX1’s role in PEX5 receptor recycling, transcripts for peroxisomal import components and related genes, including Pex5, Pex6, Pex13, Pex14, Pex26, Abcd3, Acox1, Hsd17b4, and Cat, did not show coordinated changes, indicating transcriptional uncoupling or buffering of this pathway under the tested perturbation. This null result should be interpreted cautiously because mRNA measurements do not directly assay peroxisomal protein import, PEX5 recycling, organelle abundance, or peroxisomal metabolites.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp397 in 155 MB Glut cells showed no strong convergence or anti-convergence with other perturbations in a restricted neighbor scan: using only the top 500 Zfp397-ranked genes, the strongest positive and negative correlations were weak, with Tlr4 at r = 0.192 and Slc17a5 at r = -0.196. This partially engaged MB Glut signature therefore did not reveal a clear phenocopy, anti-phenocopy, or convergent module elsewhere in the screen. Interpretation is limited because the Zfp397 seed signature itself was not FDR-significant.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gabbr1 showed a divergent, cell-type-specific Perturb-seq profile relative to Gabbr2 rather than an interchangeable GABA(B) subunit pattern. Gabbr2 was robustly depleted in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 145 MH-LH TH Glut where Gabbr1 was weak, whereas Gabbr1 had stronger corrected engagement in 308 CB GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Gabbr1 depletion occurred without corrected downstream genes. Across restricted-signature comparisons, Gabbr1-Gabbr2 correlations were near-zero to negative, and these exploratory comparisons were limited to each Gabbr1 signature’s top 250 nominal non-target genes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Fkbp1a depletion did not phenocopy calcineurin loss. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Fkbp1a showed the strongest on-target depletion yet no adjusted downstream genes, while Ppp3ca, Ppp3r1, and Calm1 were robustly depleted and produced downstream transcriptional changes; the Fkbp1a top-200 restricted signature was essentially orthogonal to Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1. Similar weak or absent convergence was seen in 155 MB Glut and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, although those pathway-neighbor signals were exploratory, and calmodulins regulate processes beyond calcineurin.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Atp13a2 produced a transcriptomic state that did not align with related perturbations: across seven cell types with significant Atp13a2 depletion, including 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, score-vector correlations with Atp13a3, Atp6v0c, Tsc1, Tsc2, Park7, Snca, Vps35, and Prkn were near zero. This suggests the Atp13a2 state is not a generic lysosomal, mTOR-axis, or Parkinsonism-family module, although interpretation is limited because Atp13a2 trans effects were very weak and Atp13a3 target engagement was also weak.

Stxbp1 produced a broader transcriptomic response than several presynaptic SNARE-associated partners, despite strong curated pathway connectivity. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Stxbp1 showed the broadest downstream response and poor score correlation with Snap25, Cplx1, and Syn1, while those comparators were strongly knocked down across many cells yet generated almost no non-target FDR calls, versus 88 for Stxbp1. A similar uncoupling was seen in 052 Pvalb Gaba, where Stxbp1 had a narrow Slc6a1-centered response but Snap25 and Cplx1 remained buffered. This contrast is transcriptomic and may reflect differences in residual protein, isoform coverage, or post-transcriptional phenotypic strength.

Hk1 showed whole-transcriptome signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of profiled glycolysis and glucose-transport neighbors, including Pfkm, Gpi1, Pgk1, Gapdh, Eno1, and Slc2a1, even though Pfkm, Pgk1, and Gpi1 displayed detectable on-target mRNA depletion in their own perturbations. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, the only class with FDR-significant Hk1 depletion, Hk1 ranked first by absolute score but no non-Hk1 gene reached FDR<0.05, and glycolytic-neighbor correlations remained near zero. These data suggest that shared Reactome/STRING glycolysis context does not imply a shared transcriptional state here, while metabolic phenocopying without correlated mRNA signatures remains possible.

Fth1 showed nonconvergent or effectively untested relationships with ferritin/iron and ferroptosis-adjacent perturbations in this screen. The most direct comparators were missing or incomplete: Ftl1 was absent as both a measured feature and perturbation, and Ncoa4 and Slc40a1 were measured but not perturbed, leaving the ferritin complex and ferritinophagy axis only partially testable. Available Acsl4, Cisd2, Ireb2, Tfrc, Abcb7, Gpx4, and Nfe2l2 perturbations were self-only or weak, with no correlation above |r|=0.098 and even the strongest genome-wide Fth1 neighbor remaining weak in 054 CNU-MGE GABA; despite strong Fth1 depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the screen did not support a convincing complex-member interpretation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp423 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic neurons showed only weak positive signature-neighbor convergence, with UFM1-system genes Uba5, Ufc1, and Ufsp2 and nuclear-transport genes Xpo1, Tnpo3, and Tpr among the top positive genome-wide neighbors. This pattern suggests an exploratory UFM1/nuclear-transport axis in the dominant Zfp423-responsive class, but all correlations were small, with the strongest Pearson r only 0.144, and no strong anti-correlated perturbation was observed, so the result is hypothesis-generating rather than mechanistic.

Lhx3 perturbation did not produce coherent activation or repression of the ISL1/LHX/LDB regulation of SLIT/ROBO axon-guidance transcription program in the measured adult brain cell types. Across the tested genes, Isl1, Lhx4, Ldb1, Ldb2, Slit1, Slit2, Slit3, Robo1, Robo2, and Robo4 showed no FDR-significant changes, so the ISL1-LHX3/LHX4-to-SLIT/ROBO cassette described in motor-neuron biology appeared uncoupled here. This interpretation is limited because not every possible enhancer target was assayed and the experiment was not performed in developing motor neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Tfg showed a weak, divergent Perturb-seq profile rather than phenocopying nearby ER-to-Golgi perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Tfg had no FDR-significant target depletion or comparable downstream response, while Copg1, Ergic1, Sec23a, and especially Sec31a showed stronger on-target loss or broader transcriptomic effects in the same dataset. Score-space comparisons likewise found no strong same-cell positive or negative Tfg neighbor across 42,153 profiles, including Sar1b, Sec23a, Sec31a, Ergic1, Copa, and Copg1, with related-comparator correlations remaining low; this suggests Tfg was underengaged here rather than simply recapitulating another secretory-pathway perturbation.

Htr6 showed essentially no convergence with serotonin-family receptors, G alpha(s) pathway neighbors, or Mtor in this dataset: across matched cell classes, Wilcoxon-score correlations between Htr6 and Htr4, Htr7, Htr1a, Htr2a, Htr3a, Adora2a, Gnas, Gnal, or Mtor stayed near zero, spanning r=-0.0795 to 0.0882 over 202 target-cell comparisons. This argues against interchangeable broad transcriptomic outputs among these perturbations here, although interpretation is limited by the weak Htr6 query signature and broad cell-class averaging; even in 308 CB GABA, the strongest Htr6 row, overlap remained weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Clock perturbation showed strongest convergence with Bmal1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where both perturbations repressed a shared circadian output program centered on Dbp, Nr1d2, Nr1d1, and Tef; in these glutamatergic classes, Clock also repressed Per3 and could increase Cry1. By contrast, in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Clock responses were largely limited to Nr1d2 and whole-signature Clock–Bmal1 correlations were weak or negative, so Bmal1 was not a universal proxy for Clock across cell types; these drop-off comparisons are based on correlations across Clock’s top 200 genes and do not establish different direct DNA targets.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Auh in 155 MB Glut showed an acute transcriptional signature that was not phenocopied by measured branched-chain amino acid/leucine catabolism neighbors: score-vector correlations with Acat1, Bckdhb, Bckdk, Dld, and Ivd were all near zero, arguing against a shared acute module for this pathway in the main Auh-engaged cell class. A notable caveat is that only five pathway-neighbor perturbations were available, several had weak self-knockdown in 155 MB Glut, and Acat1 was detectably knocked down only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Il4ra showed no detectable transcriptional output across 21–23 assayed neuronal cell groups, and the available related cytokine-receptor perturbations were likewise largely silent or nonconvergent. In this panel, Il2rg, Il6ra, Il21r, Ifngr1, Ifngr2, Stat3, and Gata3 produced no FDR<0.05 genes and correlated only weakly with Il4ra signatures, arguing against a distinct convergent IL-4/IL-13 receptor–JAK/STAT response here. Interpretation is limited because Il13ra1, Il13ra2, Jak1/2/3, Stat6, Il4, and Il13 were not perturbed, and several receptor comparators lacked corrected on-target knockdown.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rpgrip1l showed a divergent, generally weak pattern relative to related ciliary transition-zone/MKS complex perturbations. In 308 CB GABA, B9d1 had 9 corrected hits while Rpgrip1l had none, and within the restricted top-200 Rpgrip1l signature, B9d1, Cep290, and Ahi1 were anti-correlated with Rpgrip1l. In 155 MB Glut, Ahi1 and Ift88 each produced a corrected response where Rpgrip1l did not. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Rpgrip1l remained flat despite the best nominal gene, Dennd4b. These contrasts are exploratory because the Rpgrip1l signature was weak and guide efficacy or cell number may differ across perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gbf1 did not phenocopy the available ER–Golgi pathway neighbors in this dataset. Across overlapping cell types, its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Copa, Copg1, Ergic1, Sar1b, and Sec23a, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where correlations ranged from about -0.012 with Ergic1 to 0.142 with Copa. In that same class, Copg1 and Ergic1 showed efficient transcript depletion, yet Gbf1 retained a distinct Nsg1/Cck/Stmn2-like signature rather than a shared COPI, COPII, or ERGIC pattern. Interpretation is limited because only five related perturbations were available, several neighbors were transcriptionally quiet beyond self-knockdown, and direct ARF substrates plus ARFGEF1/2 were not targeted.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Abcb7, in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class where target depletion was strongest, showed no convergence with perturbations of Fe-S assembly or respiratory-chain neighbors including Nfs1, Isca2, Lyrm4, Aco2, Sdha, and Sdhb, and Fe-S/heme module transcripts were not coordinately induced or repressed; Fech and Abcb10 were also unchanged. This suggests the Abcb7 Perturb-seq signature is uncoupled from the expected cytosolic Fe-S and ABCB7-FECH-ABCB10 heme/iron modules at the mRNA level, although the comparators are pathway neighbors rather than ABCB7 complex members and transcriptomic similarity is only an indirect expectation for a metabolite transporter.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Adra2a showed near-zero signature similarity to the adrenergic receptor comparators Adra2b and Adra1a in the two cell classes with Adra2a FDR hits, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 053 Sst Gaba. In Pvalb cells, the Adra2a-associated effect included a Ppp2r2b increase, while in Sst cells it included a Zdhhc21 decrease, but alpha-adrenergic family signatures did not converge into a shared transcriptomic pattern. These comparisons should be interpreted cautiously because the Adra2a and Adra2b signatures were themselves weak, making the near-zero correlations a restricted-signature result.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Htr2a in 054 CNU-MGE GABA showed a mixed relationship to receptor and pathway neighbors rather than a simple shared-GPCR or Gq/PLC pattern. Over the 153 Htr2a nominal genes, Htr2a aligned with Adra2b, Adra1a, Htr1b, Adrb1, and Grm5, but was opposed by Grm1, Chrm2, Adrb2, and Plcb1; selected neighbors overall included both Htr2a-like and Htr2a-opposed signatures. This suggests chronic transcriptional output depends on receptor identity and cell context, with the caveat that several comparator perturbations had small cell counts.

Mapk9 showed weak, restricted Perturb-seq signatures that did not robustly converge in the same cells with assayed JNK/AP-1 neighbors, including Mapk8, Mapk8ip1, Map2k1, Map2k2, Map3k7, Atf2, and Jund. In the top-200 absolute-gene comparisons, Mapk8 was not near the Mapk9 signature, with Pearson correlations ranging from -0.354 to 0.106 across 21 shared cell types. This argues against simple interchangeability of nearby JNK nodes, but interpretation is limited because Mapk9 had no FDR-significant genes, nearest-neighbor lists included safe-target guides, and Map2k1/Map2k2 are ERK rather than canonical JNK MAP2Ks.

Robo4 did not phenocopy the neuronal Robo paralogs: its perturbation signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Robo1, Robo2, Slit2, and nearby guidance perturbations such as Plxna2 and Pak2, with no strong positive or negative transcriptome neighbor. In selected neuronal classes, Robo1 and Robo2 showed clear on-target transcript decreases, whereas Robo4 did not, suggesting Robo4 was uncoupled or near zero within Slit-ROBO signaling profiles in these data. This comparison used full Wilcoxon score vectors and could miss rare cell states or non-transcriptional guidance effects.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Atp6v1a showed a modest, subthreshold signature in 191 MB P MY GABA cells that converged positively with an endolysosomal/proteostasis neighborhood, with nearest neighbors including Psmb4, Vps37a, Psmc5, Psmc1, Atp2a2, Cltc, Vps53, and Atp6v0c. This pattern aligned with proteasome, ESCRT/vesicle-trafficking, calcium-pump, clathrin, and V-ATPase perturbations, but the contrast had only 39 perturbed cells and no genes at 5% FDR, so the result is restricted-signature and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Opn1mw perturbation in central brain glutamatergic neurons did not induce a canonical opsin, cone phototransduction, or cone retinoid-cycle program. In 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, the top nominal signal was Stx3, and in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Timm9, Gnpda2, and Ttc9b were the leading rows, but all remained FDR-negative and the whole-signature neighbors were only weakly correlated. Measured photoreceptor markers Opn1sw, Rho, Crx, Nrl, Nr2e3, and Gucy2e were unchanged, though this conclusion is limited to the assayed markers and no formal pathway enrichment was significant.

Opn1mw showed a largely null transcriptomic profile in the profiled central-brain subclasses, consistent with a broader absence or uncoupling of opsins, cone phototransduction, and cone retinoid cycle programs in these cells. Across related photoreceptor-associated perturbations, Opn1sw, Rho, Crx, Nr2e3, and Gucy2e had no q<0.05 responses in their tested cell types, while Nrl yielded only two isolated significant rows that were not mechanistically explored. In 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, even the closest Opn1mw whole-signature neighbors were weak, with |Pearson r|≤0.116.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tpi1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed its closest positive signature neighbor as Pgk1, with Gapdh also nearby, and all three perturbations converged on a lower-glycolysis pattern marked by downregulation of Pnisr, Rsrp1, Ttc14, and Ogt. The shared decrease was strongest and FDR-supported for Pgk1, also seen for Gapdh despite unquantified Gapdh mRNA knockdown, whereas Tpi1 itself showed only nominal non-target decreases and low overall score-vector correlations, suggesting a buffered global response but cell-type-specific convergence on a lower-glycolysis stress module.

Chrnb1 did not show a coordinated perturbation signature with the canonical muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunits Chrna1, Chrnd, Chrne, and Chrng in this mouse brain dataset. Across matched brain cell types, Chrnb1 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with those comparators, and restricted signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal stable receptor-family neighbors, indicating no detectable convergence for the acetylcholine-gated cation channel complex in this assay. Because the comparison was limited to transcriptomic readouts with mostly weak cis perturbations, this should be interpreted as absence of detectable convergence in brain, not evidence against shared protein complex membership.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mdh1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a transcriptional signature that converged with Got1 rather than with the broader malate-aspartate shuttle: on a 91-gene Mdh1 nominal module, the Got1 perturbation was strongly similar, whereas Mdh2 was near neutral and Got2 and Slc25a12 were weakly anti-correlated. Although these genes are all placed in the same malate-aspartate shuttle, the data support a cytosolic-arm-specific state for Mdh1/Got1 rather than interchangeable phenotypes across all shuttle components, with the caveat that this comparison comes from a single cell type and restricted module.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sele did not define a recurrent module in this dataset: available adhesion-pathway comparators Itgb2, Itgb1, and Itga4 were FDR-negative in all overlapping cell classes and showed near-zero correlation with Sele signatures, with Itgb2 ranging from r = -0.147 to 0.053. The largest whole-transcriptome neighbors appeared only in 308 CB GABA, where Wdr26 correlated positively and Eef2 negatively, but the underlying Sele contrast had no corrected hits in that cell type, so these CB GABA correlations remain weak follow-up candidates rather than evidence for a hidden adhesion program.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ccdc50 was transcriptionally uncoupled from stronger endolysosomal and autophagy perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: in this thalamic glutamatergic class, Rab7 yielded 501 FDR-significant genes and Vps35 yielded 17, whereas Ccdc50 yielded none, and Ccdc50 score vectors were nearly orthogonal to Rab7, Vps35, Sqstm1, Atg5, and Tbk1. This contrast is based on transcriptomic signatures rather than autophagic flux, LC3 lipidation, or lysosomal damage assays, and Atg5 and Tbk1 were not strongly active in this dataset.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Ndufs8 perturbation produced RNA signatures that were poor matches to other Complex I subunits or assembly factors in four best-engaged mouse-brain cell types—155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. Across 100 Ndufs8-versus-Nduf/Ndufaf comparisons, the mean signed-Wilcoxon correlation was 0.010, the highest was Ndufb10 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut at r=0.0816, and 36 correlations were negative. Even where Ndufs8 knockdown was strong, downstream respiratory-chain mRNAs were largely buffered and no high-correlation genome-wide neighbor emerged, arguing against shared RNA phenocopy rather than against shared protein-complex membership.

Sall4 perturbation left the curated SALL4-PTEN, SALL-family, SOX2/NANOG, and available NuRD-associated transcripts unchanged across all measured cell types: Pten, Nanog, Sox2, Sall1, Sall2, Sall3, Chd4, Gatad2b, and Mbd2 all showed no significant shift, and the on-target Sall4 RNA readout itself showed no rank shift.
