Thus, the canonical SALL4-NuRD/PTEN repression and SALL4/OCT4-SOX2-NANOG pluripotency axes appear transcriptomically uncoupled in this mouse brain screen, although promoter occupancy or protein-level NuRD recruitment were not assayed and subtle chromatin effects in rare SALL4-expressing cells cannot be excluded.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gata4 showed a largely uncorrelated perturbation signature across the assayed brain cell classes, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic populations, with near-zero same-cell correlations to Gata1, Gata2, Gata3, Gata6, Zfpm2, Nkx2-5, Tbx5, Mef2c, Smad2, Smad3, and Foxa2. In this dataset, Gata4 therefore did not converge with GATA-family paralogs or the cardiogenic/endodermal GATA4 network, and signature-neighbor searches found only very weak positive or negative neighbors. Because the Gata4 score vectors were weak, the main inference is absence of correlation rather than antagonism.

Chrna1 showed a near-null phenotype across the sampled brain cell classes: its transcript was not detectably depleted, it had no meaningful whole-signature neighbors, and no FDR-significant downstream genes were observed. The same near-null pattern was seen for the assayed muscle-type receptor partners Chrnb1, Chrnd, Chrne, and Chrng, which also lacked on-target knockdown and any significant downstream genes. Together, these transcriptomic data suggest a complex-wide absence of the muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor module in this brain atlas, while not directly testing receptor assembly or ion currents.

C3 showed a nonconvergent, largely inert transcriptional signature in this neuronal Perturb-seq atlas: across 23 tested neuronal classes, its profile was almost uncorrelated with biochemical neighbors and innate-immune comparators including Cr2, Cd46, Itgb2, Cx3cr1, Csf1r, Trem2, and Cd14 (r≈0.003–0.016), and no glutamatergic, GABAergic, or dopaminergic class showed FDR-supported C3 target engagement, downstream DE, or a convergent complement-neighborhood module. This suggests the assayed neuronal complement neighborhood was inactive rather than weakly shared, although the inference is limited to weak transcriptomic correlations and several canonical partners, such as Itgam, were not assayed.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Alk showed a weak, target-specific perturbation phenotype rather than a general failure of the assay to detect neuronal RTK/MAPK-axis signaling. In 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ntrk2 was clearly depleted, and in 155 MB Glut, Mapk1 was depleted, with cell counts comparable to Alk; by contrast, Alk in paired classes retained FDR=1 for its own transcript and lacked FDR-significant downstream genes. In 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Alk produced only nominal signals, so the stronger Ntrk2 and Mapk1 responses suggest Alk-specific guide expression, target-expression, or state/context limitations, although these comparators do not identify the precise cause.

Ophn1 showed no transcriptional convergence with related Rho-family or synaptic perturbations in this dataset: whole-signature correlations with Cdc42, Rac1, Pak1/2/3, Trio, Arhgap18/32, Arhgef9, Syngap1, Shank2/3, Fmr1, and AMPA/NMDA receptor genes including Gria1/2 and Grin1/2d were near zero, and even the top positive and negative signature neighbors were very weak. Thus, despite curated links to Rho-family GTPase and synaptic AMPA/endophilin biology, the steady-state RNA phenotype was transcriptomically uncoupled from those comparators; this may reflect a weak Ophn1 signature, and lack of mRNA convergence does not exclude shared protein-level RhoGTPase signaling.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Comt showed a largely self-only transcriptomic phenotype and did not phenocopy assayed dopamine or adrenergic receptor perturbations or Ache in the Comt-engaged classes, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In these cell types, Drd2, Drd3, Drd4, Drd5, Adra1a, Adra2a, Adra2b, and Ache were essentially uncorrelated or orthogonal to the Comt signature, while closer catecholamine-metabolism neighbors such as Maoa, Maob, Ddc, Dbh, Pnmt, and Aldh3a1 were not available, limiting pathway reconstruction; receptor and Ache comparisons were exploratory and some receptor perturbations had weak target-transcript engagement.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Tbx1 was largely transcriptomically silent in these neuronal states, especially relative to the neuronal T-box factor Tbr1. Across 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Tbr1 produced 21 FDR-significant rows across three glutamatergic groups, including strong effects such as Cacna1g and Cpne6 up-regulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, whereas Tbx1 showed only one isolated hit, Polr2a down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, with near-zero correlation to Tbr1 and no broad T-box-family response. This family-level contrast indicates that Tbx1 and Tbr1 should not be treated as interchangeable perturbations in these cells.

Vps13c perturbation did not produce a detectable constitutive RNA program for canonical PINK1/PRKN mitophagy or lysosome markers: Pink1, Prkn, Park7, Rab7, Lamp1, Lamp2, Sqstm1, and Optn were all FDR non-significant, with a global absence of significant downstream transcriptional responses. This was seen across sampled brain cells, including 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, although NP-CT showed only nominal Tbk1 and Ctsd increases. These data separate reported damage-induced VPS13C-linked mitophagy from a constitutive transcript-level response, while not excluding pathway activation through phosphorylation, ubiquitination, protein relocalization, or stress-conditioned states.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Epha6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed only nominal target-transcript reduction, whereas matched Epha4 and Epha7 perturbations in the same thalamic glutamatergic class produced much stronger corrected target depletion. Across all-gene signatures, Epha6 was essentially uncorrelated with Epha4, Epha5, Epha7, Epha2, Fyn, and Rac1, suggesting that shared Eph receptor family membership did not make Epha6 an interchangeable transcriptomic proxy here. This contrast may reflect guide or transcript-detection efficiency as well as receptor biology, and many related perturbations had sparse corrected downstream effects.

Nfe2l2 showed a transcriptional signature that was largely orthogonal to available NRF2-pathway perturbations and to its CNC-bZIP paralog Nfe2l1: mean score-vector correlations with Cul3, Mafg, Nfe2l1, Gclc, Gclm, Sqstm1, and Prdx1 were near zero, and a genome-wide neighbor search found no strong phenocopy or inverse. Despite the expected KEAP1-CUL3-NFE2L2 and Nfe2l2-Mafg neighborhood, this pattern suggests weak Nfe2l2 engagement or substantial pathway buffering, with the caveat that these are transcriptome correlations, Cul3 is pleiotropic, and Keap1 was not perturbed.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Pomp perturbation in 155 MB Glut produced a prominent program marked by reduced synaptic and mature neuronal transcripts together with increased stress and damage-response genes. Down-regulated markers included Atp1a3, Sncb, Gpm6a, Nsg1, Tspan7, Gabrg2, Syp, Slc17a6, Grin1, and Gria2, while induced genes included Mafg, P4ha2, Bax, Optn, Hsp90ab1, Hsph1, Zfand2a, and Ddit3. This vulnerable glutamatergic population also showed proteasome-subunit compensation and strong convergence with Psmb4, Psmc1, and Psmc5 perturbations, although the RNA signature does not directly measure proteasome activity, neuronal firing, or viability.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Plxnd1 did not show strong on-target mRNA depletion in this atlas, whereas related axon-guidance perturbations did in selected cell types, suggesting the negative result is not a general failure of the Wilcoxon pipeline or of guidance genes as a class. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Robo2 and Plxna2 reached FDR-significant depletion, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Sema5a and Robo1 did as well; additional comparator signals were seen in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. These cross-gene, cross-cell-type comparisons benchmark perturbation efficacy but do not show that PLXND1 was expressed or required in every Plxnd1-assayed cell type.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Sstr5 restricted signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a reproducible SSTR5-like or Gi/o-coupled module. Using only the top 200 Sstr5 genes per cell type, correlations were small and inconsistent across classes, with no consistent recovery of Gnao1, Adcy1, or Adcy5; in 053 Sst Gaba, the strongest related-looking result was an anti-correlation with Pik3ca, but this was exploratory because neither Sstr5 nor Pik3ca showed an FDR-significant response there. Overall, these data argue against inferring hidden PI3K or GPCR convergence from the weak restricted-signature matches.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Slc25a12 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a much narrower mRNA signature than Mdh1 within the same malate-aspartate shuttle: Mdh1 produced 29 FDR-significant genes, including up-regulated Cars and Gls, whereas Slc25a12, Got1, Got2, and Mdh2 were largely dominated by self-transcript loss. This indicates that curated pathway membership did not translate into interchangeable transcriptional perturbations in this cell type, with the contrast strongest here and based on mRNA signatures rather than shuttle flux.

Cox11 did not phenocopy structural complex-IV subunit perturbations: across same-cell whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon score correlations with Cox4i1, Cox5a, Cox6a1, Cox6b1, Cox7b, and Cox8a, correlations were near zero, indicating that this complex-IV assembly factor and structural subunits were not interchangeable at the scRNA-seq signature level. Even the strongest genome-wide Cox11 neighbors were weak, and in selected GABA cell types the signal appeared weak or buffered, with nominal mitochondrial RNA increases, so the result may reflect weak Cox11 signatures and differing knockdown efficiencies rather than absence of pathway relatedness.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Alx3 showed an orthogonal or disjoint perturbation profile relative to its paralogs Alx1 and Alx4 in this adult neuronal Perturb-seq panel. The only FDR-significant Alx3-associated change was Serinc3 downregulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and genome-wide signature correlations with Alx1 and Alx4 were near zero, with no strong signature-neighbor module detected. In contrast, Alx1 produced a single distinct hit, Lztr1 upregulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, while Alx4 had no FDR-significant transcriptional signature; these summary correlations are exploratory, and Alx1 had low perturbed-cell counts in several classes.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Chmp4b showed weak direct differential expression, but in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut its restricted transcriptomic signature converged with ESCRT pathway neighbors, with Snf8 and Vps37a among the top positive signature correlates. This was the clearest pathway-consistent signal, recovering ESCRT-II/ESCRT-I relationships rather than a generic neuronal response. The effect was modest and based on signature correlations only, and Vps37a itself had weak on-target transcript depletion in these strata; available cross-perturbation comparisons were largely limited to ESCRT-I/II neighbors rather than paralogs or VPS4 perturbations.

Mc3r did not phenocopy other melanocortin-family or proximal cAMP perturbations in this dataset. Across shared cell types, Mc3r score vectors were near-zero correlated with Mc4r, Agrp, Gnas, and Adcy3, while related perturbations were generally weak: Mc1r, Mc2r, Agrp, and Gnas had no FDR-significant genes and Mc4r showed only one isolated hit. These data therefore argue against treating MC3R, MC4R, AGRP, or Gs/adenylyl-cyclase perturbations as interchangeable transcriptomic readouts here, while remaining consistent with weak or buffered signatures rather than opposed biochemical signaling.

Kcnt1 was a weak outlier among assayed neuronal ion-channel perturbations: under the same analysis pipeline, Kcnt1 and Kcnt2 showed corrected self-transcript depletion less often than Kcnq2, Scn1a, Hcn2, Kcnc3, Scn8a, and Kcnma1. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, a well-sampled Kcnt1 contrast showed no target engagement or downstream FDR signal, whereas several comparator channels showed robust corrected self-depletion. This suggests the weak Kcnt1 result reflects this target/context/assay combination rather than a general inability to detect ion-channel knockdown, noting that the comparison is limited to assayed channels and mainly captures direct self-depletion rather than broad downstream programs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Thra showed a cell-type-restricted signature that was not phenocopied by related thyroid-receptor nodes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these two contexts, Thrb, Rxra, Rxrb, Rxrg, Ncoa1, and Ncoa3 produced no genes at FDR < 0.1, whereas Thra produced 5 and 1 genes, respectively; no comparator also showed a strong genome-wide score correlation with the Thra signature. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the Thra-associated program included decreased Hr, Adgrb1, and Hcn2, but this contrast remains exploratory because comparator guides showed weak own-transcript depletion in the same assay.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ar showed weak perturbation behavior in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where nominal Ar transcript lowering did not yield an FDR-significant downstream response. This quiet pattern extended to nearby steroid receptors: Pgr and Nr3c2 had no adjusted hits, and Esr1, Esr2, and Nr3c1 showed only isolated adjusted genes across matched brain classes. In contrast, selected non-steroid nuclear receptors, including Rora, Nr1d1, and Esrra, produced strong adjusted signatures in the same cell type, suggesting a broader ligand-dependent steroid-receptor detection limitation rather than an Ar-specific failure; however, this is an exploratory cross-perturbation comparison, not a matched ligand-activation experiment.

Zfp846 showed a weak and largely orthogonal transcriptional signature across the 22 modeled Zfp846 cell classes, with restricted-signature cosine similarities near zero relative to Setdb1, Chd4, and other Zfp-family perturbations, including Zfp644 and Zfp692. This argues against treating Zfp846 as a generic surrogate for the KAP1-SETDB1/NuRD heterochromatin-repression neighborhood or broader KRAB/C2H2 DNA-binding regulation. A key caveat is that these comparisons relied on a restricted nominal Zfp846 gene set because the full Zfp846 signature was weak, with sparse differential expression and no confirmed Zfp846 transcript depletion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nsd1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a small but FDR-supported acute RNA response, biased toward up-regulated transcripts, with significant depletion of the Nsd1 target transcript and a marker context including Ddo, Pygm, Capn3, Ptgds, and Myo5c. This response did not look like a generic H3K36-writer signature: Ash1l showed effective self-knockdown but no FDR-supported non-self module, and Nsd2 and Setd2 did not phenocopy Nsd1, with near-zero genome-wide correlations to Nsd1. Because Nsd2 lacked detectable target knockdown and Setd2 was tested in fewer cells, the safest interpretation is lack of acute signature convergence rather than proven biological non-equivalence.

Grik3 perturbation produced transcriptomic signatures that were nearly orthogonal to those from other kainate receptor subunits, arguing against treating Grik1, Grik2, Grik4, and Grik5 loss as interchangeable with Grik3 at this Perturb-seq endpoint. Across 86 same-cell correlations between Grik3 and Grik1/2/4/5 score vectors, the mean absolute correlation was 0.0213 and the maximum was 0.1107. In kainate receptor synaptic signaling contexts, including 053 Sst Gaba, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 001 L5-6 IT Glut, Grik3 knockdown appeared buffered and orthogonal, though these correlations assess downstream RNA-state similarity rather than biochemical coassembly or electrophysiological interchangeability.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cox7b targeting showed a weak, cell-type-restricted pattern of nominally increased mtDNA-encoded respiratory-chain transcripts: mt-Co2 and mt-Nd4 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and mt-Cytb and mt-Nd5 in 155 MB Glut. This is consistent with a possible OXPHOS or mtDNA-encoded respiratory-chain compensation response, but all signals were exploratory because none passed FDR, and the 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut context also lacked detectable Cox7b transcript engagement.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cplane1 showed a transcriptomic response that was largely near-orthogonal to other assayed ciliary-family perturbations, even in matched MB/TH contexts with on-target knockdown. In 155 MB Glut, Cplane1 mRNA was significantly depleted without downstream FDR-significant non-target changes, and Ahi1, Ttc8, Ift88, Adcy3, Cep290, and Rpgrip1l had near-zero score-vector correlations; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Cplane1 was only nominally engaged but still remained near-zero relative to strongly perturbed Ttc8 and other neighbors. This suggests the acute transcriptome does not collapse Joubert, BBS/IFT, and ciliary signaling perturbations into one interchangeable neuronal state, although core CPLANE comparators Fuz, Intu, and Wdpcp were not in the library.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Vapb showed a single exploratory signature-neighbor pattern that was localized to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where its top positive neighbors were Psmc1, Psmb4, Atp6v0c, Psmc5, Sec31a, and Pomp, suggesting weak convergence with a proteostasis/ER-export module. The correlations were modest, with restricted top-500 signature Pearson r values around 0.37–0.39, and Vapb knockdown in this cell type was only nominal rather than FDR-significant. Although Vapb ranked highly in two additional cell types, target depletion there also did not pass FDR correction.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Lhcgr perturbation was largely silent across neuronal subclasses, including 053 Sst Gaba, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, and the related receptors Fshr and Tshr were similarly inert or isolated. In contrast, downstream cAMP/PKA/CREB-axis perturbations were detectable in overlapping classes: Adcy3 and Prkar1a showed significant on-target transcript loss, while Creb1 and Crebbp produced broader responses including a strong Creb1-to-Crem signal, with Crem/Camk2b/Mmab modules in 155 MB Glut. These comparisons suggest receptor-level uncoupling rather than a general inability to detect pathway perturbation, although comparator guides differed in cell counts and target-expression levels.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Epha10 did not phenocopy other perturbed Eph-family receptors in this brain assay: across matched cell types including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Epha10 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Epha4, Epha5, Epha7, and Ephb2, within the broader EPH-Ephrin signaling context. In several of these same classes, Epha4, Epha7, or Epha5 showed stronger, sometimes FDR-significant self-transcript depletion, whereas Epha10 remained weaker, so the contrast is partly attributable to lower guide engagement for Epha10.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pgr in 308 CB GABA showed a divergent perturbation signature that was nearly uncorrelated with Ar, Esr1, Esr2, Nr3c1, Nr3c2, Pgrmc1, Ncoa1, Ncoa3, and Ep300, indicating that these steroid-receptor-family and receptor-coregulator perturbations did not phenocopy Pgr in this baseline cerebellar GABA state. This argues against treating Pgr and these related receptors or coactivators as simple substitutes here, although the low correlations do not rule out shared direct target genes after hormone stimulation.

Nefm showed a self-dominated, nonconvergent Perturb-seq response: despite detectable self-knockdowns for Nefl, Nefh, Kif5a, Kif5c, Klc1, and Klc2, these related neurofilament and kinesin-associated perturbations did not share a strong Nefm-like transcriptional signature. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells, Nefm depletion was confirmed but remained largely self-only, while 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was near threshold. Correlation testing was limited to the strongest Nefm-score genes because the full Nefm signature lacked secondary FDR hits.

Nsf showed an almost absent FDR-resolved transcriptional response, consistent with a buffered or uncoupled NSF/SNAP-dependent cis-SNARE disassembly node in this assay. The related cofactor Napb phenocopied this pattern: despite strong self-depletion in several cell types, including 155 MB Glut, it produced no non-self FDR hits. In contrast, trafficking neighbors Ap2s1, Ap2m1, Cltc, and Stxbp1 generated broad downstream signatures, indicating that strong transcriptional consequences were detectable here. Cross-perturbation counts alone do not prove biochemical buffering, because guide efficiency and protein depletion may differ by target.

Lgr4 showed no convergence with direct Wnt-receptor perturbations: in same-cell signature comparisons, its profile was nearly uncorrelated with Fzd2, Fzd3, Fzd4, Fzd6, Fzd9, Lrp5, Lrp6, Ctnnb1, and Apc, with Pearson correlations ranging from -0.140 to 0.080. This separates Lgr4 from a generic canonical RSPO-LGR4-Wnt receptor potentiation signature in these data, although the available library lacked the closest LGR paralogs and RSPO/ZNRF3/RNF43 module members, and signature-level contrasts alone do not demonstrate receptor inactivity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tbl1x was silent in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: in 129 perturbed cells, genome-wide differential expression did not pass a 5% FDR threshold, even though the same thalamic glutamatergic class showed strong signatures for the circadian/nuclear-receptor regulators Rora, Nr1d1, and Bmal1, with 278, 116, and 103 significant genes, respectively. Because TBL1X is placed in RORA/REV-ERB and BMAL/CLOCK/NPAS2 transcriptional regulation, this pattern suggests pathway-level uncoupling rather than a general inability to detect transcriptional programs, while not implying biochemical dispensability of TBL1X.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Dnm1 showed strong target knockdown but remained transcriptionally silent beyond the target in multiple neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. In those same or overlapping classes, Ap2s1, Ap2m1, Cltc, Dnm1l, and Grin1 produced substantial non-target differential expression, from dozens to more than 1000 significant genes. This contrast suggests a pathway-position- or function-specific buffering of Dnm1 rather than a general inability of thalamic or midbrain neurons to mount transcriptional responses, though the mixed comparator set mainly demonstrates assay competence rather than a single linear pathway relationship.

Rxylt1 did not phenocopy Fktn, Large1, Dag1, or Dpm1 at the scRNA-seq signature level, even though these genes lie in the same matriglycan biosynthesis pathway on DAG1. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class, where the clearest on-target Rxylt1 depletion was seen and related Large1/Fktn perturbations were also engaged, Rxylt1 showed no FDR-significant downstream genes, no strong whole-signature neighbor, and score vectors that were essentially uncorrelated with those comparators. This apparent uncoupling is tempered by weak Rxylt1 knockdown and reliance on scRNA correlations rather than matriglycan abundance.

Bbip1 showed transcriptionally non-interchangeable behavior with nearby BBSome and ciliary trafficking perturbations in this assay: whole-transcriptome signatures for Bbip1 were essentially uncorrelated with Ttc8, Bbs5, Bbs9, and the BBSome regulator Lztfl1, despite their shared BBSome and cilium assembly neighborhood. This pattern suggests that BBSome subunit perturbations should not be treated as interchangeable proxies here, although the contrast is signature-based and could reflect weaker Bbip1 target engagement rather than a true mechanistic difference among BBSome components.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kmt2b in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a distinctive RNA signature that was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of related chromatin writers, including Kmt2a, Kmt2c, Kmt2d, Setd1a, Nsd1, Kmt2e, and Setdb1, even when several of those perturbations produced sizeable signatures. In this primary Kmt2b-responsive class, the broad output was mostly downregulated, and related writers shared few significant genes with Kmt2b, suggesting Kmt2b is not simply reporting a generic KMT2B/WDR5 H3K4 methyltransferase-complex or chromatin-writer response. This comparison is based on RNA signature rank/score similarity and may be affected by differences in guide potency or protein turnover.

Tnrc6b did not phenocopy the assayed miRNA-effector neighbors Tnrc6a, Ago1, Ago2, Dicer1, or Cnot1: across shared cell classes, its score vector showed near-zero correlation with each comparator, with mean Pearson r values of 0.011 for Tnrc6a, 0.024 for Dicer1, 0.0066 for Ago1, 0.0016 for Ago2, and 0.0065 for Cnot1, and no pair exceeding r = 0.107. In the miRNA/small-RNA silencing pathway, where some convergence might be expected, this instead suggests transcriptomic buffering and non-convergence, although the comparison is caveated because the comparator perturbations had weak or absent on-target FDR support.

Cd79a perturbation did not detectably move the proximal BCR second-messenger and NF-kB-linked transcript program in the profiled mouse brain cells: Cd79b, Blnk, Btk, Syk, Lyn, Pik3r1, Nfkb1, and Nfkb2 were measurable yet unchanged across Cd79a contrasts, and the Cd79a transcript itself was not significantly depleted in any cell type. This pattern is consistent with the absence of a B-cell receptor apparatus in these cells, although transcript abundance is only an indirect readout of BCR signaling, which is typically phosphorylation driven.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Ovol2 showed a weaker perturbation response than related developmental regulators in several high-cell-count neuronal classes, arguing that its null result is not simply due to low power. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Ovol2 had no corrected hits while Zeb1 and Ctnnb1 produced corrected signatures, and in 052 Pvalb Gaba, Ovol2 remained null whereas Zeb2 showed a corrected response. This contrast indicates differential signature strength across perturbations, although guide efficiency and cell-count differences mean it should not be read as a direct mechanistic ranking among these genes.

Grik1 showed no biologically interpretable transcriptomic signature neighbor: whole-signature correlations with kainate-receptor paralogs Grik2, Grik3, Grik4, and Grik5, as well as other ionotropic glutamate receptor perturbations including Gria2, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b, were all near zero, and the most extreme screen-wide correlations to Grik1 were only 0.030 and -0.018. Thus neither kainate-receptor family convergence nor broader disease-gene convergence was supported, and weak nominal neighbors such as Diaph2, Dll1, or Nme7 are too small to assign pathway meaning. This null result is conservative because weak-signature correlation is limited and does not test functional epistasis.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tek perturbation did not produce a canonical angiopoietin/Tie2 endothelial-like output across 23 assayed neuronal classes, including multiple Glut, GABA, Dopa, and Pineal populations. The nominal Tek-associated changes were weak and did not survive multiple testing, while Angpt1, Angpt2, Tie1, Kdr, Flt1, Flt4, Pecam1, Ptprb, Cdh5, Robo4, Eng, Acvrl1, Klf2, Klf4, Efnb2, Dll4, Notch1, and Vegfa were all FDR-null, arguing against interpretation as Tie2 pathway transduction. This pathway readout is based on pathway identity rather than direct mouse endothelial positive controls in the dataset.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Kif5a showed partial target-engagement convergence with the related heavy-chain paralog Kif5c, but not transcriptome-wide convergence. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Kif5c also showed significant target depletion, yet Kif5a–Kif5c genome-wide DE-score correlations were near zero across the four on-target Kif5a classes: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. Across these classes, Kif5a was down without a coordinated Kinesin-1 transcriptional response involving Klc1 or Klc2, and because both perturbations had almost no significant non-target genes, this is a restricted-signature negative result rather than a pathway-level activity readout.

Nfx1 showed no coherent transcriptional phenocopying with nearby perturbations in this dataset. Across the 18 Nfx1-tested cell types, there was no FDR-supported Nfx1 response and no strong same-cell signature neighbor; the best unbiased match reached only |r| = 0.148. In matched cell types, perturbations of curated neighbors Ube3a, Sin3a, Psen1, Syncrip, and H2-Eb1 were essentially uncorrelated with Nfx1, arguing against functional interchangeability here. This comparison is exploratory because it relies on full-signature correlations, and the Nfx1 anchor signatures themselves were weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Eno1 was an outlier among glycolytic perturbations in the high-cell-count neuronal classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: while Pgk1, Tpi1, Gpi1, and Hk1 showed strong on-target depletion, Eno1 remained FDR-silent. This argues against a general failure to recover glycolysis-related perturbations in these contexts and is more consistent with weak or missing Eno1 engagement, or target-specific buffering. A caveat is that the comparator signal mainly reflects direct target depletion rather than broad pathway remodeling, and Eno1 itself was unmeasured.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tas2r118 showed only weak, context-specific signature neighbors, with no FDR-controlled downstream genes in the pooled differential-expression scan. In audited cell types, the strongest whole-signature correlations were modest, peaking in 308 CB GABA at about r=0.266 and r=-0.265, and involved unrelated genes such as Lonp1, Wdr26, Gfra1, Tsga10, Gapdh, Reep2, and Lrp6 rather than known taste-receptor partners. Signals in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 001 L5-6 IT Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA were similarly weak, and the restricted cell-type audit plus whole-score correlations warrant caution.

Tnrc6a did not phenocopy its expected miRISC partners or paralog: within-cell-type whole-transcriptome correlations between Tnrc6a and Tnrc6b, Ago1, Ago2, Dicer1, or Cnot1 were essentially zero, despite their expected convergence in the miRNA-induced silencing/GW182-AGO-CCR4-NOT deadenylation network. In 155 MB Glut cells, where Tnrc6a showed the only sub-10% FDR hits and weak self-knockdown, Cnot1 produced a stronger but distinct signature. These data favor under-engagement or redundancy over a clean canonical miRISC phenotype, while leaving open that small sets of direct miRNA targets could be missed by whole-transcriptome correlations.

Itgb1 knockdown did not transcriptionally phenocopy perturbations of beta1-compatible alpha-integrin subunits or Itgb2: signatures for Itga2, Itga4, Itga6, Itga8, Itga9, and Itgb2 showed mean cosine similarities near zero to Itgb1, and isolated significant effects among related alpha-integrins did not form a shared Itgb1 module in the beta1-integrin extracellular-matrix adhesion pathway. This comparison is limited to transcriptomic scores, most Itgb1 effects were weak, Itga5 and Itgav were not tested, and the assayed neurons may not coexpress the relevant receptor pairs or assembled complexes.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Nr6a1 in 052 Pvalb Gaba showed no evident convergent module: the Pvalb Nr6a1 signature was weak and had only tiny correlations with all other perturbations, with top non-self neighbors Ctnna3 (r=0.0659) and Mecp2 (r=-0.0661). Measured nuclear receptor and transcriptional-coregulator network comparators, including Rarg, Dnmt3a, Nr5a2, Nr4a3, Arnt, Arnt2, and Crebbp, were essentially uncorrelated, arguing against interpreting the single Trim23 signal as part of a latent NR6A1-corepressor module in Pvalb cells, though this analysis is limited to one cell class and a weak seed signature.

Gucy2e was broadly inert in the assayed brain cell classes, and this was not unique to one guide set: other available receptor-guanylyl-cyclase and inherited retinal disease perturbations, including Gucy2c, Npr2, Rho, Crx, Nr2e3, Cep290, and Nrl, were also mostly silent. The relevant RetGC/GCAP cGMP synthesis pathway for visual phototransduction was largely absent or untested here, because key neighbors such as Guca1a, Guca1b, Gucy2f, and Pde6b were not assayed. A caveat is that the comparator set was manually chosen and incomplete, and the two Nrl FDR hits were isolated single genes rather than a coherent phototransduction program.

Il12rb1 perturbation in the Il12rb1-tested neuronal cell classes did not transcriptionally engage the canonical IL-12/IL-23 receptor–JAK/STAT module: Il12b, Il23r, Stat1, Stat3, Stat4, and Ifng were unchanged, and across the 22 represented classes the aggregate transcriptome showed no strong related or data-driven signature neighbor. Likewise, perturbing IL-12/IL-23-family or nearby STAT genes did not produce a transcriptome similar to the Il12rb1 signature. This interpretation is limited to mRNA, as phospho-STAT signaling, secreted cytokines, and several pathway components were not measured here.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Large1 showed no convincing shared transcriptomic module with other dystroglycan-axis perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Large1 had FDR-confirmed self-knockdown but no additional FDR genes and no compensatory changes in Dag1, Fktn, Crppa, Pomk, Pomt1, Pomgnt1, Pomgnt2, B3galnt2, B4gat1, Rxylt1, Large2, or Agrn; in 155 MB Glut, Large1 depletion was strong only nominally. Agrn instead showed strong on-target-only depletion across five neuronal classes, whereas Fktn, Dag1, Crppa, and Dmd lacked FDR-confirmed self-knockdown, so the main signal is buffered lack of convergence rather than interchangeability.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Cep112 showed a weak, cell-type-specific signature correlation only in 308 CB GABA, where its score vector aligned modestly with B9d1, Cep290, and Kif5a. This was the sole exploratory convergence among 21 Cep112-profiled neuronal classes and suggests a possible cerebellar GABA cilium-related module involving transition-zone biology. However, the Cep112 signature in 308 CB GABA had no FDR-significant genes, and the top nominal genes for B9d1, Cep290, and Kif5a largely did not overlap with Cep112, so the pattern is hypothesis-generating rather than a validated pathway hit.

Ttc21b showed little transcriptional convergence with related ciliary perturbations: on the 1,127 nominal Ttc21b rows, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Ttc8, Ahi1, and Rpgrip1l had near-zero cosine similarity to the Ttc21b restricted signature, ranging from about -0.048 to 0.043, despite their shared primary cilium/intraflagellar transport network context. This suggests the dataset should not be summarized as a coherent neuronal IFT module, although the comparison is exploratory because the Ttc21b signature itself is weak and these cosine estimates may be influenced by noisy genes.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc12a2/NKCC1 showed little transcriptomic response in this screen, in clear contrast to the related chloride exporter Slc12a5/KCC2. Whereas Slc12a5 had FDR-significant own-transcript loss in five cell types, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, and drove a cell-type-restricted program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut marked by Nr4a1, Dusp1, Fos, Syngap1, and Chml, Slc12a2 remained largely flat and its score vector was essentially uncorrelated with Slc12a5. This separation is transcriptional rather than a direct ion-flux readout, and weaker Slc12a2 guide efficacy could have contributed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Stk39 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was largely transcriptomically silent, showing only nominal self-depletion and no FDR-significant genes, whereas direct Slc12a5/KCC2 perturbation in the same cell class produced a clear immediate-early response with Slc12a5 down and Nr4a1, Dusp1, and Fos up. This cross-perturbation contrast suggests the assay could detect a downstream cotransporter response in these thalamic glutamatergic cells, so the Stk39-negative result is not simply a universal detection failure, although Slc12a5 had more perturbed cells and the comparison is transcriptomic rather than phosphoproteomic.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Wac showed transcriptomic responses that were not recapitulated by acute Mtor or Rptor perturbation in its two strongest responding cell classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these populations, Wac–Mtor and Wac–Rptor score correlations were near zero, and direct Mtor or Rptor perturbations yielded few or no FDR-significant genes, so the comparison is mainly a negative signature result rather than a definitive readout of mTORC1 activity. Thus, despite prior links between WAC and the mTOR/autophagy axis, the neuronal Wac RNA signature here is not well explained as acute Mtor or Rptor loss.

Glra1 showed near-zero transcriptome-wide score correlations with related glycinergic synapse perturbations, including Glra2, Glra3, Glrb, Slc6a5, Gphn, and Arhgef9, indicating that expected pathway membership did not translate into interchangeable Perturb-seq signatures. Across 129 matched cell-type comparisons, related perturbations such as Glrb and Arhgef9 displayed clear self-transcript reduction in several classes, whereas Glra1 generally did not; in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Glra1 had only nominal target decrease and no FDR-significant downstream response. These comparisons are limited to transcriptome-wide score correlations, and several comparator perturbations also showed sparse responses.

Lrrtm3 perturbation produced an RNA signature that was essentially orthogonal to perturbations of the neurexin and LAR-RPTP adhesion-neighborhood genes Nrxn1, Nrxn2, Nrxn3, Ptprd, and Ptprf, rather than phenocopying them. This pattern was seen by whole-transcriptome correlation or rank score across multiple classes, including 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, where Lrrtm3 knockdown showed nominal target-transcript decreases but no FDR-significant downstream response and only weak related-target correlations. Ptprs, a known partner, was not perturbed, and all comparisons are based on RNA signatures rather than synaptic binding or morphology assays.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Crebbp in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed no strong non-self signature match; instead, Kmt2d, Kdm6a, and Trrap sat in the weak positive tail of its signature-neighbor ranking, consistent with a shallow enhancer and histone-acetyltransferase chromatin-neighbor module. Kmt2d and Trrap were only modestly correlated with Crebbp (r=0.174 and 0.160; largest non-self correlation 0.194), and Trrap shared some specific Crebbp-directional genes despite weak whole-signature similarity. This pattern is exploratory and does not imply direct perturbation of the same complexes.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mkx showed no stable convergence or divergence with related TALE-homeobox or TGFβ perturbations across the 21 assayed neuronal subclasses, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic populations. Comparator perturbations involving Meis1/2, Pbx1/3, Smad2/3/4, Tgfbr1/2/3, and Tgif1 were mostly FDR-silent, and a restricted 40-gene signature-neighbor scan found no perturbation recurring in more than two top-neighbor slots. Thus, no reproducible Mkx-like or Mkx-opposing program was detected, although comparator coverage was indirect and the Mkx signatures themselves were weak and FDR-null.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pdcd10 perturbation in this neuronal dataset was uncoupled from the canonical endothelial CCM program: across diverse glutamatergic and GABAergic clusters, Klf2, Klf4, Map3k3, Mef2a/Mef2c, Rhoa, Rock1, Rock2, and Cdc42 showed no coherent FDR-supported response, and canonical CCM, MEKK3-KLF, RhoA-ROCK, Rap1, and Cdc42 transcripts did not form a supported signature. The strongest nominal target engagement appeared in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 052 Pvalb Gaba, yet downstream markers remained nonsignificant, cautioning against using neuronal Klf2/Klf4, Map3k3, Rhoa, Rock1, or Rock2 RNA as biomarkers of Pdcd10 engagement here.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pth1r showed its strongest apparent signature-neighbor relationships in 308 CB GABA, where Wdr26, Cckar, and Ranbp2 were the top correlated or anti-correlated perturbations, but this pattern was not biologically secure. In that cell type, all local Pth1r differential-expression signals had FDR=1, and negative-control safe-target perturbations such as Safe_target_15 and Safe_target_81 appeared among the top anti-neighbors. Because these neighbor calls were based on full-transcriptome score correlations without independent batch correction, the observed Pth1r module is better treated as a quality-control caution than a confident network inference.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Dlx3 perturbation was uncoupled from the canonical forebrain GABAergic DLX effector program: across 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 053 Sst Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA, Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, and Nrp2 showed no significant change. In 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, the strongest nominal Dlx3-associated row was Cadm3, but it corrected only to FDR 0.213 and did not extend to a broader DLX or GABA-effector response, consistent with a mature cell-context distinction from embryonic Dlx1/Dlx2 activity.

Micos13 showed a weak, largely uncoupled transcriptional signature in this screen: it produced no FDR<0.05 rows, whereas Opa1 and Dnm1l produced 184 and 204 significant rows, and Micos13 full-vector correlations with Opa1, Dnm1l, and Mff were near zero. Micos13 was also weaker than several respiratory-chain perturbations, including Cox5a, Uqcrc1, Ndufb8, and Uqcrfs1, suggesting that partial Micos13 depletion did not collapse onto a generic mitochondrial cristae, dynamics, or OXPHOS-stress transcriptome. A caveat is that these comparators are pathway neighbors rather than MICOS13 paralogs, and differences in target engagement could contribute to the contrast.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gpr158 knockdown produced transcriptomic signatures that were not interchangeable with assayed members or neighbors of its proposed signaling axis. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, where both Gpr158 and Gnb5 were measurably knocked down, their genome-wide Wilcoxon-score vectors were essentially uncorrelated across 16,762 genes (r=-0.0033). Across the best Gpr158-engaged cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, correlations with Gnb5, Gnao1, Gabbr1, and Gabbr2 stayed near zero, while Gpr179 showed no interpretable on-target engagement; caveats include the absence of Rgs7 from the library and that Gnb5 has partners beyond GPR158.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Matr3 showed a recurrent 10-gene core that was not reproduced by other ALS-linked RNA-binding-protein perturbations, even in shared responsive cell types. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Tardbp and Fus could produce sizeable transcriptomic signatures, yet Fus, Tardbp, Hnrnpa1, Hnrnpa2b1, and Son failed to recapitulate the Matr3 core, including genes such as Ddhd1, Atp9b, E2f4, Gpt2, and Rsrp1. This dataset-level contrast is based on post-knockdown transcriptome similarity, with guide efficiency and target engagement varying across perturbations.

Pcdh15 showed near-zero signature similarity to the available related perturbations Pcdh19, Adgrv1, and Cdh2 across the same 22 brain cell types, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where Pcdh15 had the largest nominal burden yet still no robust alignment with those comparators. This pattern argues against a generic cadherin-family or Usher-family perturbation signature, although interpretation is limited because Pcdh15 itself and the Pcdh19 and Adgrv1 comparators lacked FDR-supported on-target knockdown, so the apparent orthogonality could partly reflect weak perturbations rather than distinct biology.

Sema4d did not show interchangeable transcriptomic effects with the available semaphorin-family, plexin-family, neuropilin, Met, or small-GTPase-neighbor perturbations: across 13 tested comparators, whole-signature correlations with Sema4d were only -0.094 to +0.096, so related perturbations neither reproduced nor inverted the Sema4d signature. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, only Ablim1 was Sema4d-associated despite only nominal Sema4d knockdown, while Plxna2 showed a stronger corrected self-knockdown; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Sema5a achieved stronger self-knockdown than Sema4d. Direct B-plexin and CD72 receptor perturbations were not represented, and some related signatures had weak downstream FDR support.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Dstyk in 308 CB GABA neurons did not phenocopy a simple FGF/RAS/ERK loss-of-function state. Instead, the Dstyk signature anti-correlated with several MAPK-pathway perturbations, including Braf, Hras, Mapk1, Kras, and Fgf1, and it did not produce an FDR-grade ERK-output response in marker genes such as Dusp6, Etv4, Etv5, Spry4, or Egr1. This suggests pathway uncoupling in this mature cerebellar GABA context, with the caveat that prior literature comes from kidney/HEK FGF stimulation and several comparator MAPK signatures were themselves weak in 308 CB GABA.

Kremen1 showed a weak, noninterchangeable transcriptional signature across all 23 profiled cell classes: compared with available Wnt-related perturbations in Lrp5, Lrp6, Fzd2/4/6/9, Ctnnb1, Apc, Gsk3b, Lgr4, Ror1, Ror2, and Lrp4, score-vector correlations were near zero, with a largest absolute Pearson correlation of only 0.124. In the comparator-rich 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population, Ctnnb1 or Lrp6 loss suppressed Wnt-response genes, whereas Apc loss activated Axin2 and Nkd1, but Kremen1 remained neutral, consistent with an accessory or ligand-gated role rather than a transcriptomic phenocopy of core WNT/TCF components; however, Kremen2 and DKK ligands were not perturbed, and interpretation is limited by the weak Kremen1 signature itself.

Ripor2 loss did not phenocopy available RHO-family or STRING-neighbor perturbations in this brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across all 21 analyzed Ripor2 cell classes, Ripor2 score vectors showed only very small correlations with Rac1, Cdc42, Pak1/2/3, Arhgap18, Arhgap32, Arhgef9, Rdx, Epb41l1, and Ywhae, with the largest absolute correlation only 0.096, and no strong target-level signature neighbor or broad RHO-polarity transcriptional state emerged. This uncoupling is tempered by weak Ripor2 mRNA engagement and the absence of direct perturbations for key partners including Rhoa, Rhoc, Rock1/2, Ripor1, and Ripor3.

Alk perturbation did not project onto the canonical RTK/RAS/PI3K signaling neighborhood in this dataset: its transcriptomic signatures were largely orthogonal to Insr, Igf1r, Ret, Met, Ntrk1/2/3, Mapk1, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Ptpn11, Sos1, and Kras, so canonical pathway directionality was not interpretable here. The nominal leading genes were mostly cell-type-private rather than a shared Alk module. In 308 CB GABA, Alk showed no target engagement and no FDR-significant genes. This signature-level result does not exclude ALK signaling in unmeasured states, with poor Alk guide activity, or along the unassayed Ltk/ALKAL ligand axis.

Gpr68 perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported basal Gq/PLC/MAPK/NFκB or immediate-early transcriptional program, despite its canonical annotation to G alpha(q) and phospholipase-C signaling. Across tested neuronal classes, Gnaq, Gna11, Plcb1, Mapk1, Mapk3, Nfkb1, Rela, Fos, Jun, Egr1, Nr4a1, Arc, and Npas4 were not significantly changed; in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut there was no target knockdown or immediate-early response, and in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut the best associated gene, Zbtb18, reached only q=0.096. Direct Plcb1 and Mapk1 perturbations showed detectable self-knockdown in one cell type each, but no broader FDR-supported transcriptome, suggesting the expected pathway was unengaged, post-transcriptional, stimulus-dependent, or below power under these basal transcriptomic conditions.

Il1r1 perturbation did not mobilize a canonical IL-1 to NF-kappaB/MAPK/AP-1 inflammatory transcriptional program in these assayed neurons: measured response genes including Nfkbia, Nfkbiz, Tnfaip3, Ptgs2, Il6, Cxcl1, Ccl2, Fos, Jun, Junb, Dusp6, Myd88, and Traf6 were not significantly altered after correction. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons, there were more nominal signals and a nominal Junb decrease, but neither the bulk effect nor the canonical AP-1 signal survived correction. Because this was a basal CRISPR perturbation rather than acute IL-1 stimulation, weak Il1r1 engagement could mask true receptor-dependent responses.

Twist1 did not engage the canonical EMT/CDH1 transcriptional program in the profiled mature brain cell classes, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. Across Twist1 contrasts, selected EMT and CDH1-regulatory markers remained unchanged, including Cdh1, Cdh2, Vim, Fn1, Snai1, Snai2, Zeb1, Zeb2, Twist2, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Notch1, and Notch2. This suggests the EMT/CDH1 axis was uncoupled from Twist1 in these neuronal contexts, although this was a selected marker check rather than a formal pathway-enrichment test and neurons are an indirect context for EMT.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp1a3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a thalamic transcriptional program that was not reproduced by related Na,K-ATPase alpha paralogs: Atp1a1 knockdown was detectable but produced only itself as an FDR hit, and Atp1a2 was not detectably engaged in this neuronal class. The Atp1a3 signature showed only weak-to-moderate restricted similarity to Atp2a2 and Atp2b1, supporting alpha-3-specific, nonredundant effects in neurons that can co-express alpha-1. This comparison is tempered by more modest Atp1a1 knockdown and by correlations being computed only across 79 preselected Atp1a3-responsive genes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Vps13d showed a weak positive signature convergence in the best-engaged cell types, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, where top score-correlation neighbors included Rab7, Dnm1l, Opa1, and Hspa9, consistent with a mitochondrial fission, mitophagy, and endolysosomal trafficking neighborhood. However, the signal was exploratory rather than a strong module: the maximum relevant correlation was only 0.131, top negative neighbors were not coherent, and Vps13d responses appeared buffered relative to broader signatures from neighbors such as Dctn1 and Vps37a.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Suclg1 showed weak or buffered target engagement in this screen: in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, matched Suclg1 self rows were FDR-negative, while Sucla2 reached robust self-depletion in the same classes, and other TCA or mitochondrial neighbors such as Mdh1, Mdh2, Sdha, Idh3a, and Ogdh were also strongly depleted, especially in 155 MB Glut. Because SUCLG1 and SUCLA2 are partner subunits of succinate-CoA ligase, this contrast suggests a perturbation-specific weakness for Suclg1 rather than a general inability of these neuronal classes to report mitochondrial-gene knockdown, although the comparison reflects transcript depletion rather than identical metabolic phenotypes and could be influenced by guide efficiency or isoform-specific expression.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Neo1 perturbation was not broadly recapitulated by related DCC/RGM/BMP/UNC5-family perturbations in this dataset. Across full transcriptomes, Dcc, Rgma, Unc5c, Unc5d, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, and Hjv were near-uncorrelated with the Neo1 signature, suggesting the NEO1 netrin/RGM and BMP/SMAD-HJV networks are buffered rather than interchangeable here. An apparent opposing signal in 308 CB GABA for Unc5c, Bmpr1b, and Hjv was exploratory, because the same restricted signature-neighbor pattern also matched many unrelated perturbations, including safe-target controls.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Cacna1a showed a weak and non-interchangeable transcriptomic response relative to related calcium-channel perturbations. Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Cacna1a did not cluster with CaV2.1 auxiliary-subunit complex genes or nearby channel genes, even when comparators such as Cacnb4, Cacna2d1, and Cacna1g had stronger corrected on-target knockdown. In thalamic cells, correlations to Cacna1a were very small, including r=0.055 for Cacnb4 and r=0.066 for Cacna2d1, indicating that partial Cacna1a loss produced a buffered or divergent mRNA response rather than a shared presynaptic calcium-channel program.

Rel showed no detectable convergence with assayed NF-kappaB family members or pathway neighbors in the neuronal Perturb-seq panel. Its weak transcriptomic signature was essentially uncorrelated with Relb, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Chuk, Traf3, Tlr3, Tlr4, Tlr8, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, and Tnfrsf13c, and no perturbation in the full dataset emerged as a meaningful positive or negative Rel neighbor, with the strongest correlation only r = 0.0309. This argues against a coherent hidden NF-kappaB module or compensatory paralog signature here, while noting that weak response vectors could miss protein-level or stimulus-gated NF-kappaB activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Got1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a transcriptomic program that was not reproduced by mitochondrial malate-aspartate shuttle neighbors. Despite target engagement, Got2 was among the most anti-correlated perturbations to the restricted Got1 signature, while engaged Mdh2, Slc25a12, Gls, Glud1, and Sdha were near zero or weakly negative rather than phenocopying Got1. This suggests cytosolic Got1-Mdh1 convergence with mitochondrial-neighbor divergence in this cell type, although the result is based on transcriptomic contrast rather than direct flux, and some members such as Slc25a13 and Aco2 were not interpretable here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Eno1 perturbation showed no detectable enolase-isozyme compensation at the RNA level: across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells, Eno2 and Eno3 were not FDR-significantly induced, and core glycolysis genes including Hk1, Gpi1, Tpi1, Pgk1, Pkm, Ldha, and Ldhb also lacked compensatory upregulation. Eno2 instead trended weakly downward in these classes, but only nominally. Interpretation is limited because Eno1 knockdown was unmeasured and Eno2, Eno3, and Eno4 were not themselves perturbed for direct comparison.

Hnrnpa1 was largely silent across the 21 profiled neuronal classes, with no FDR-level self-knockdown and only a single FDR-level downstream row, while its paralog Hnrnpa2b1 was also weak. In the same cell-type contexts, other RNA-binding and splicing perturbations—Srsf1, Snrnp70, Tardbp, and Fus—produced hundreds to thousands of differential-expression rows and stronger self-transcript decreases, including in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Hnrnpa1 showed little RNA-processing signal aside from Rbm5 down in one cell type. This contrast suggests the Hnrnpa1 negative result is target-specific rather than a general failure to detect RNA-processing perturbations, although the comparison is based on gene-abundance DE burdens and self-transcript rows rather than matched protein depletion or isoform-splicing measurements.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Acbd5 showed no convergence with Vapb, Pex14, or other peroxisomal neighbor perturbations in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. Across restricted Wilcoxon score correlations, Acbd5 signatures were near zero versus Abcd3, Acox1, Acsl4, Agps, Hsd17b4, Pex1, Pex13, Pex14, and Vapb, with the largest absolute correlation only |r|=0.1075. In midbrain glutamatergic contexts, Vapb and Pex14 showed robust self-knockdown, but no Acbd5-like downstream program emerged, suggesting the non-convergence likely reflects weak Acbd5 target engagement rather than clear pathway independence.

Ptpn11 loss was not a simple Ntrk2-loss phenocopy: across the top-500 Ptpn11 restricted signatures, correlations with Ntrk2 signatures stayed near zero, even where Ntrk2 showed strong self-knockdown. This uncoupling was seen in neuronal contexts including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; in 052 Pvalb Gaba, Vgf was nominally decreased after Ptpn11 perturbation, yet the Ntrk2 signature still did not become Ptpn11-like. Although PTPN11 is placed in NTRK2/FRS2/FRS3 and BDNF/TrkB signaling, these mature in-vivo mRNA responses did not collapse into a single TrkB-SHP2 signature, and the comparison is limited to restricted transcriptomic signatures rather than acute phospho-signaling.

Kdm5b showed an all-gene signature that was largely uncoupled from assayed H3K4 chromatin neighbors and from every other top positive or negative perturbation signature. Across 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Kdm5b mRNA was reduced, but the downstream RNA program appeared buffered: correlations with Kdm5c, Kmt2a, Kmt2b, Kmt2d, Setd1a, Phf8, Dnmt3a, and Myc ranged from -0.073 to 0.123, and no assayed perturbation exceeded |r|=0.20. This suggests no strong pathway-neighbor or compensatory perturbation, although the comparison is limited to assayed targets and may be damped by Kdm5b’s weak scalar response.

Sp110 showed no meaningful convergence with related IFN-pathway perturbations or any data-driven signature neighbor. Across the available comparisons, IFN receptor, IRF, STAT, and Nod2 perturbations, including Irf2, Ifngr1, Irf9, Ifnar1, Stat1, Stat2, Irf7, Nod2, and Ifngr2, all had near-zero similarity to Sp110, and the strongest non-self cosine was only 0.0357. Consistently, the interferon and antigen-presentation effector module, including Stat1, Stat2, Irf1, Irf7, Irf9, Isg15, Ifit1-3, Oas1a, Oas2, Psmb8/9, Tap1/2, B2m, H2-K1, H2-D1, H2-Ab1, and H2-Eb1, showed no FDR-significant change. Because the Sp110 signature itself was weak, the absence of convergence is more reliable than any weak positive or negative neighbor; related complex-family perturbations such as Sp100, Sp140, and Pml were not available.

Ergic1 perturbation did not trigger detectable transcriptional compensation within the measured ERGIC and early ER-Golgi vesicle-trafficking neighborhood: Ergic2, Ergic3, Lman1, Lman2, Surf4, Sec22b, Copg1, Sec23a, Sec31a, Sar1b, and Stx5a all remained below significance, with no shared perturbation signature despite being close pathway neighbors. This suggests the buffered state is not explained by simple mRNA-level replacement of ERGIC1 by these measured genes, although compensation through protein stability, localization, trafficking flux, or unmeasured cargo receptors would not have been detected.

Ndufs1 showed a weak perturbation profile that did not phenocopy better-engaged mitochondrial respiratory chain Complex I assembly perturbations such as Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, Ndufs8, and Ndufb8. In the same dataset, several of these related genes displayed much stronger on-target depletion, whereas Ndufs1 lacked a coherent positive or negative transcriptional signature relationship with other NDUF perturbations. This pattern argues against a generic inability to measure mitochondrial transcripts and instead points to weak Ndufs1 target engagement, with restricted-signature score correlations limiting interpretation and not supporting claims of biological antagonism among Complex I subunits.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Scarb2 showed a largely self-contained transcriptional response: across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 155 MB Glut, signatures for Psap, Atp13a2, Lamp2, Ctsb, and Grn were near-zero correlated with Scarb2, even when those comparator knockdowns were strong. This argues against a shared lysosomal or GCase-adjacent RNA module and narrows the signal to SCARB2 rather than generic lysosomal impairment, though Gba1 was not perturbed and transcriptome-wide correlations may miss shared lipid or enzyme-activity phenotypes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hspa5 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a whole-transcriptome signature that converged most strongly with Hspa9, and also with Hspa8, Uba5, and Ufc1, whereas Atf6, Manf, Hsp90ab1, and Hspd1 were only weakly correlated and the strongest negative neighbor was negligible. This places the Hspa5 state with selected Hsp70 and UFMylation/proteostasis stresses, not broadly with all UPR-adjacent perturbations. The responsive class included corrected ER chaperone/ERAD genes, an ISR-like tail, and non-depleted Hspa5 mRNA, but these similarities are correlative, and the Uba5/Ufc1 link reflects transcriptome similarity rather than direct epistasis.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Grm5 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed the clearest nominal self-depletion yet still did not converge transcriptionally with metabotropic receptor paralogs or proximal postsynaptic partners: Grm1, Grm3, Grm7, Grm8, Homer2, Shank3, Plcb1, and Itpr1 all had near-zero score-vector correlations with Grm5, and Plcb1, Itpr1, and Shank3 showed only their own self rows at FDR<0.05 rather than a shared Grm5-like module. Grin2b, by contrast, did produce FDR-level hits in this cell type, suggesting the weak Grm5 response reflects mRNA-level buffering or uncoupling rather than a globally unresponsive cell state.

Prdx1 was uncoupled from antioxidant-pathway perturbations in this screen: across matched cell types, perturbing Nfe2l2, Nfe2l1, Gclc, Gclm, or Gpx4 produced near-zero correlations with the Prdx1 score vector (median |r|=0.0188; maximum |r|=0.124), and no other perturbation strongly mimicked or opposed the Prdx1 signature. The largest observed neighbor correlation was still weak in 308 CB GABA cells for Gclc versus Prdx1 (r=0.124). This contrasts with curated pathway links, but several neighbor perturbations showed weak target-transcript engagement, and direct thioredoxin-cycle partners such as Srxn1, Txn1, Txnrd1, and other Prdx genes were not targeted here.

Pparg perturbation did not reveal a canonical PPARG:RXRA adipogenic or lipid-transcription program in the assayed neurons. Across all Pparg-assayed neuronal classes, interpretable PPARG-linked genes including Cd36, Fabp4, Fabp5, Lpl, Plin2, Abca1, Abcg1, Acox1, Angptl4, Srebf1, and Srebf2 were not even nominally significant, arguing that the module was absent rather than weakly present. This negative result is qualified by the experimental context: the tested cells were unstimulated neurons, whereas much canonical PPARG biology is ligand-induced and described in adipocytes or macrophage-lineage cells.

Sclt1 showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signature similarity to Cep83, Cep164, Ahi1, Adcy3, Cplane1, and Ift88 across the same brain cell classes, despite SCLT1 being part of the distal-appendage/ciliopathy network involved in basal-body anchoring and ciliogenesis. In 155 MB Glut, Sclt1 had only nominal target-transcript reduction, whereas Ahi1, Adcy3, and Cplane1 showed strong target-transcript depletion. This divergence suggests related ciliary perturbations are not interchangeable surrogates for Sclt1 in short-term brain RNA phenotypes, although the weak Sclt1 signature itself could have suppressed correlations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cox6a1 showed weak acute transcriptomic effects: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, the strongest response was mainly depletion of Cox6a1 itself, with no FDR-resolved OXPHOS or broader respiratory-chain module and no clear Cox6a2 or other subunit compensation. Related complex-IV perturbations, especially Cox5a and Ndufa4, often had stronger on-target FDRs than Cox6a1, yet their significant signatures were also almost exclusively the edited transcript and did not phenocopy Cox6a1. These comparisons are based on transcriptome correlations, not complex-IV activity, and only a subset of COX6A1 partners was assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Srsf1 perturbation showed its strongest signature similarity to Tnpo3, which was the dominant positive comparator in responsive cell types and ranked top in 13 of 21 matched classes. This convergence was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and also evident in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Srsf1 loss converged with Tnpo3 and reduced Clk transcripts within an SR-protein phosphorylation and nuclear import axis. A key caveat is that Tnpo3 mRNA was not significantly reduced in Tnpo3-guide cells, so this is a signature-neighbor relationship rather than a clean matched knockdown comparison.

Hecw2 perturbation did not recover the p73 or GDNF/RET/AKT/NEDD8 axes as coordinated mRNA modules in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset: Trp73, Ret, Gdnf, Akt1, Akt2, Akt3, and Nedd8 were all not FDR-significant, and no assayed brain cell class showed an FDR-controlled differential-expression hit. This suggests the readout is distinct from prior HECW2/NEDL2 literature centered on protein-level regulation, p73 assays, and enteric or kidney developmental contexts, so lack of these transcriptional changes should not be taken as absence of biochemical HECW2 activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Pik3cb did not produce corrected neuronal signatures in this wild-type mouse brain single-cell RNA dataset, whereas Pten, and more weakly Mtor, did in the same PI3K/AKT/PTEN signaling context. In particular, Pten yielded 45 FDR-supported calls concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, while Pik3cb yielded none in those strata; the same pipeline also detected corrected Pten and Mtor-neighbor responses where Pik3cb remained uncorrected. These results argue that Pten-responsive brain transcriptomes are not simply phenocopied by acute Pik3cb loss, with the caveat that prior PTEN–p110β links largely come from tumor or prostate epithelium and Pik3cb target-transcript engagement here was weak.

Snca showed a nonconvergent acute transcriptomic profile: across Snca-tested matched cell types, its all-gene signature was essentially uncorrelated with Sncb and with curated synaptic/Parkinson-related perturbations including Syn1, Syp, Stxbp1, App, Atp13a2, Park7, Vps35, and Nsf, with Snca–Sncb correlations ranging from -0.051 to 0.048. In the best-engaged context, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Snca was significantly reduced yet no robust downstream program emerged, and similarly weak or buffered behavior was seen in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. Because most Snca downstream signatures were weak, these small correlations are negative evidence only, not proof of pathway independence.

Htr2c did not phenocopy the assayed Gq/PLC/Ca2+ effector perturbations in this dataset: across shared cell classes, its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Plcb1, Itpr1, Prkca, and Prkcg, with mean r values of 0.0046–0.0169. This uncoupling appeared despite measurable engagement of some comparator perturbations, especially Itpr1, Plcb1, and Prkcg, indicating a receptor-context separation in basal transcriptomes rather than a global failure to detect the pathway. In 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, the largest Htr2c-related correlations were still small. Because similarity was computed from weak score vectors, the near-zero correlations do not rule out Htr2c using these effectors after serotonin stimulation.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Pnkd knockdown in the three FDR-engaged cell types—155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba—showed strong target depletion but no FDR-validated trans program, and the expected active-zone/neurotransmitter-release sentinel mRNAs remained unchanged. In particular, Rims1, Rims2, Unc13a, Snap25, Stx1b, Gad1, Slc6a1, and Atp1a3 were not FDR-regulated, indicating that acute Pnkd loss was transcriptionally uncoupled from the RIM/Munc13/SNARE and transmitter-marker axis in resting single cells. This is limited to selected sentinel transcripts, as RIM1/2 protein abundance and vesicle exocytosis were not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp644 did not phenocopy a detectable chromatin-regulator response in the assayed brain cells, including the G9a/GLP-H3K9me2 repression neighbor Ehmt1. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Zfp644 had no FDR-significant genes, whereas Ehmt1, Setdb1, Kmt2a, Kmt2b, Kmt2d, and Chd4 showed detectable phenotypes in the same cell class. Restricted Zfp644 signatures in 155 MB Glut and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut also did not align with Ehmt1, although comparator guide counts and target engagement were not matched and the Zfp644 correlation signatures themselves were not FDR-supported.

Sox10 perturbation did not detectably alter the canonical SOX10–MYRF oligodendrocyte myelination module in this neuronal assay. Across assayed neurons, oligodendrocyte precursor and myelin genes including Myrf, Pdgfra, Cspg4, Olig1, Olig2, Mbp, Plp1, Mag, Mog, Mobp, Cldn11, Pllp, Mal, and Gpr17 were not significantly shifted, indicating that the expected SOX10-linked program was neither activated nor repressed. This likely reflects assay context, since these markers are low or absent in many neuronal classes and the experiment did not target OPCs or oligodendrocytes.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Stx5a showed weak signature-neighbor transfer rather than a clear surrogate perturbation. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, no whole-screen perturbation correlated with the Stx5a signature above |r|=0.09 after excluding Stx5a itself, despite the Sidt2-up signal. In 308 CB GABA, which showed Copg1-down, the strongest neighbors were only modest, with positive Fbxo11, Atp6v1e1, and Eef2 and negative Frrs1l, Cckar, and Bcap31, around |r|≈0.23. These Pearson correlations from Wilcoxon score vectors are exploratory audit controls, not mechanistic substitutes or direct pathway partners.

Prickle1 was transcriptionally uncoupled from the measured Wnt/planar cell polarity network in this dataset: its perturbation did not coordinately change mRNA abundance of Prickle2, Celsr2, Fzd3, Fzd6, Ror1, Ror2, Ryk, Smurf1, or Smurf2, and matched-cell-type transcriptome correlations with Celsr2, Fzd3, Fzd6, Ror1, Ror2, and Ryk were near zero, with the largest absolute all-gene Pearson correlation only 0.109. Even Celsr2, despite stronger on-target knockdown, did not resemble the Prickle1 signature, so pathway membership alone should not be taken as evidence of a Prickle1 phenocopy here; this conclusion is limited to transcriptome correlations and available pathway neighbors, as matched Vangl and Prickle paralog perturbations were not available.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Smad1 showed only weak positive and negative signature correlations, insufficient to define a stable module. The strongest neighbors were confined to 308 CB GABA cells, with modest positive correlations to Cckar, Frrs1l, and Wdr26 (r up to 0.275) and similarly weak negative correlations to Eef2, Fbxo11, and Gabrb1, while even a negative-control target appeared in the local neighborhood. Because these score-vector neighbors may reflect cell-class-specific noise or shared technical structure, the restricted Smad1 signature should not be interpreted as a coherent BMP pathway program.

Opn1sw targeting in brain cell types did not transcriptionally engage the canonical visual phototransduction/11-cis-retinal opsin signaling module: measured genes including Opn1mw, Rho, Arr3, Gnat1, Gnat2, Gnb3, Gngt2, Grk1, Rcvrn, and multiple Pde6 family members showed no detectable change, with no nominally significant responses reported across 19 opsin/phototransduction genes. This suggests that outside retinal context, Opn1sw perturbation does not recruit the broader phototransduction gene program, although the assay did not test light responses, chromophore availability, or photoreceptor-specific compartments.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cox5a showed sparse corrected transcriptomic signatures in the two largest glutamatergic contexts, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where on-target depletion was seen but downstream OXPHOS, mtDNA, and ISR markers were largely silent. This pattern resembled other complex-IV structural or assembly-related perturbations, including Cox4i1, Cox6a1, Cox6b1, Cox7b, Cox8a, Ndufa4, Cox11, and Coa8, rather than Opa1, which in the same dataset elicited a broad ATF4/ISR-like program with genes such as Asns, Ddit3, Chac1, and Slc7a5. Because this comparison is transcriptomic and some neighbor perturbations had weak on-target FDR, the absence of downstream genes should not be taken as equivalent protein knockdown.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Marcks in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed its clearest on-target response, yet its transcriptomic signature was largely uncoupled from the MARCKS Ca2+-PKC-actin-PIP2 membrane module: correlations with curated neighbors Actb, Actg1, Calm1, Calm3, Camk2a, Camk2b, and Prkcg were very small, and even the strongest whole-library neighbors were weak (Syp positive, Reln negative). Thus, in this dataset, a MARCKS loss signature should not be read as a generic PKC, calmodulin, CaMK, or actin-cytoskeleton perturbation, although this conclusion is limited to this single cell type and the scan emphasized only weak or absent relationships.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarcb1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a broad transcriptional response that was not reproduced by all SWI/SNF perturbations. Smarcc2 converged strongly with Smarcb1, and Smarce1/Arid2/Arid1a/Arid1b were also convergent within the BAF chromatin-remodeling pathway, whereas Smarca2, Smarca4, Smarcc1, and Smarcd1 were weak or divergent. Notably, Smarca2 knockdown strongly reduced its own mRNA yet produced little downstream response, while some other negative comparators also had weak target-transcript depletion, cautioning that BAF subunits were not equivalent nodes in this cell type.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Gnb5 showed a distinct acute transcriptional state that assayed G-protein/R7-neighbor perturbations did not recapitulate: Gnb1, Rgs6, Gnao1, and Adcy1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Gnb5 globally and within 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, including the Pvalb context where Gnb5 itself was significantly depleted. In that Pvalb population, the Gnb5 response was largely limited to target-transcript loss, with only exploratory nominal changes such as Hcn1 and Atp2b3.
