This interpretation is tempered because Rgs7, Rgs9, and Rgs11 were not perturbed, and the assayed Rgs6 Pvalb perturbation showed weak target engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cry2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a distinct circadian transcription-translation feedback loop effect that Cry1 did not phenocopy: Cry2 perturbation lowered the Nr1d1/Dbp clock-output branch, whereas Cry1 produced only an isolated Per2 increase, did not reduce Dbp or Nr1d1, and had near-zero genome-wide correlation with Cry2. This responsive thalamic class also showed convergence of Bmal1 and Clock perturbations on Dbp/Nr1d genes. A caveat is that Cry1 guide efficacy at the Cry1 transcript was not FDR-significant here, so the paralog contrast may underestimate complete Cry1 loss.

Myod1 showed no convergent neuronal Perturb-seq signature with its assayed E-protein partners or neural bHLH factors: transcriptome-wide Wilcoxon score-vector correlations with Tcf3, Tcf4, Tcf12, Neurod1, Neurod2, and Neurog3 were all near zero, with the largest only r=0.016 for Tcf3. This suggests that known MyoD:E-protein biochemical relationships in myogenic contexts do not translate into an interchangeable MYOD/TCF transcriptional phenotype in differentiated neurons, where Myod1 is silent. Because these comparisons rely on weak RNA-level signatures, shared mechanisms not reflected in neuronal RNA abundance could have been missed.

cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Hoxc13 was largely silent in this adult-brain Perturb-seq dataset, and related posterior HOX perturbations did not uncover a hidden HOX module: Hoxa13, Hoxd13, Hoxb8, and Hoxd10 were also nearly silent and their score-vector DE summaries did not converge with Hoxc13. Across 113 HOX target-by-cell-type tests, the only corrected signal was a single Hoxd10–Tut1 association in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, where Hoxc13 itself had 43 perturbed cells and no significant genes; that Hoxd10/Tut1 result was based on only 25 perturbed cells.

Stub1 showed a buffered transcriptomic response that was not interchangeable with other assayed protein-quality-control perturbations. Its whole-transcriptome signature was near-zero correlated with Hsp90ab1, Hspa8, Hspa9, Hsf1, and proteasome subunits such as Psmb4, Psmc1, and Psmc5, even though some of those proteasome perturbations produced thousands of downstream transcript changes. Thus, physical proximity of CHIP/Stub1 to chaperone and proteasome machinery did not translate into acute RNA-signature equivalence in this screen, although the very broad proteasome signatures warrant caution because some subunits showed weak measured on-target transcript depletion.

Rfx3 showed no reproducible convergence with the only screened RFX-family comparator, Rfx7, or with nearby ciliary perturbations across the 22 Rfx3-tested Glut/GABA groups. In restricted analyses using only the top 100 absolute Rfx3 genes per cell type, correlations with Rfx7 and canonical ciliary genes such as Foxj1, Ift43, Ift88, and Ttc8 were near zero, and a global neighbor scan found no stable positive or negative partner. This weak pattern should not be read as a generic RFX-family or ciliary module, especially because both Rfx3 and Rfx7 lacked corrected hits and true RFX3 heterodimer partners were not perturbed.

Ust showed near-zero correlation with other Golgi glycosaminoglycan/proteoglycan perturbations, including Ext1, Ext2, Glce, Hs6st2, Gpc6, B3gat3, and Xylt1, across matched cell types despite their shared extracellular-matrix/GAG biosynthetic context. In the 155 MB Glut class, related perturbations such as Hs6st2 and Ext2 had strong on-target transcript depletion whereas Ust did not, arguing that Ust should not be collapsed with heparan-sulfate or common proteoglycan-linker genes when interpreting neuronal Perturb-seq signatures. A caveat is that the comparator set spans a broader GAG/proteoglycan group, and Ust knockdown was weak, so the lack of correlation may partly reflect limited target engagement.

Nrp2 produced a transcriptomic signature that was essentially uncorrelated with Nrp1 and with the plexin perturbations Plxna1, Plxna2, and Plxna4, rather than forming a shared semaphorin/neuropilin/plexin receptor signature. In 308 CB GABA cells, the informative contrast was strongest: Plxnd1 and Unc5c were Nrp2 anti-neighbors, while Nrp1 was only mildly positive. This inference is limited to transcriptome correlations, and measured Nrp2 knockdown was weak; because Nrp1 target engagement was also weak, the cleaner comparison is to the better-engaged Plxna1 and Plxna2 perturbations.

Csmd1 perturbation was not accompanied by a detectable classical-complement transcriptional response in the assayed neuronal subclasses: across 22 groups, C1qa, C1qb, C1qc, C3, C4b, Cd46, Cfb, Cfh, Cfi, Cfp, and Cr2 mRNAs were essentially unchanged, with no induced or repressed complement-gene program. This suggests that, in these neurons, CSMD1’s known role as a synaptic and astrocytic inhibitor of classical-pathway activation is uncoupled from bulk complement-component mRNA induction, although incomplete synaptic protein depletion and the lack of direct readouts of C3/C4b deposition, factor-I cofactor activity, microglial engulfment, or astrocyte responses remain important caveats.

Rab3gap2 showed no robust mRNA-signature convergence with the curated RAB3GAP1:RAB3GAP2–RAB18 trafficking axis. Across 21 shared cell types, Rab3gap2 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Rab3gap1 and Rab18, with Pearson score-vector correlations near zero, and no cell type showed a high-correlation global-signature neighbor for Rab3gap2. This suggests the axis is not visibly engaged at the transcriptome level in this screen, although the inference is limited because Rab3gap1 and Rab18 perturbations themselves lacked FDR-level own-transcript knockdown.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Glrb perturbation produced transcriptomic signatures that were nearly uncorrelated with Glra1, Glra2, Glra3, Gphn, Arhgef9, and Slc6a5 perturbations in the Glrb-engaged cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, arguing against a strong phenocopy within glycine-gated chloride-channel signaling and gephyrin-linked postsynaptic GlyR localization. This nonconvergence is most convincing for Arhgef9, which showed strong self-depletion in two matching contexts, whereas the lack of convergence with Glra1/2/3 remains less definitive because those comparator perturbations had weak target engagement in the same cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Glrb depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA showed clear on-target knockdown but no FDR-detectable compensatory induction of the assayed glycinergic synapse transcript module: Glra1, Glra2, Glra3, Gphn, Arhgef9, Slc6a5, and Slc6a9 remained unchanged. The strongest target engagement was in the thalamic glutamatergic group, while the midbrain-pons-medulla GABA group had the largest Glrb logFC yet no non-target transcript reached significance. Related-target signatures were weak or nonconvergent, suggesting no simple transcriptional replacement program, though compensation could be transient, protein-level, or limited to finer subclasses.

Il21r did not show a coherent IL21R–common-γ/JAK-STAT transcriptional module in the profiled basal neurons. Across all 21 Il21r-profiled glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, Il21r had no target-transcript knockdown, no FDR-significant downstream response, and only weak restricted-signature similarity to Il2rg or Stat3; related receptor perturbations including Il2rg, Il2ra, Il2rb, and Il4ra, as well as Stat1, Stat3, and Stat5b, were likewise FDR-silent. This pattern is most consistent with an inactive or unmeasured common-γ cytokine circuit in these unstimulated neurons, with the caveat that Jak1 and Jak3 were not tested and the comparison is transcriptomic and restricted-signature based.

Cd36 showed no detectable engagement of canonical innate-immunity circuitry in this dataset: Cd36, Tlr2, Tlr4, Tlr9, and Trem2 had floor-level self-transcript rows, Tlr6 was not assayed, and Cd36 signatures did not reproducibly correlate with assayed TLR, integrin/tetraspanin, or class-B scavenger-receptor neighbors such as Itgb1, Itgb2, and Cd81. In the assayed neuronal classes, this leaves the CD36-TLR4/TLR6-NLRP3 inflammatory pathway unsupported under unstimulated transcriptomic perturbations and does not test ligand-driven receptor clustering by amyloid-beta, oxLDL, or microbial ligands.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Csf3r showed weak or absent convergence with related cytokine, chemokine, colony-stimulating factor, and STAT perturbations across diverse neuronal and glial cell types, including multiple cortical glutamatergic classes, GABAergic populations, hypothalamic, midbrain, pineal, and cerebellar cells. Correlations between the near-null Csf3r signature and all perturbations were very small (max r=0.184, min r=-0.194), and within a focused set including Csf1r, Il6ra, Il6st, Osmr, Epor, and Stat1/2/3/4/5b the maximum absolute correlation was 0.146, arguing against a detectable CSF3/G-CSF receptor JAK-STAT module in this dataset.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Plxnd1 showed nominal target depletion in two L2/3 IT glutamatergic cell types, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, but its transcriptional signature was essentially uncoupled from semaphorin-plexin signaling and adjacent axon-guidance perturbations: correlations with Nrp1, Nrp2, Sema4d, Sema5a, Sema6a, Kdr, Rac1, Rapgef2, Rapgef4, Plxna1/2/4, Plxnc1, Robo1, and Robo2 were near zero, with no FDR-significant downstream activation. Although stronger correlations appeared in 308 CB GABA, they are treated cautiously because neither Plxnd1 nor the closest neighbor targets were on-target depleted there.

Trpm7 did not phenocopy a generic cation-channel, glutamate/Ca2+ signaling, or PI3K-mTOR perturbation in this screen. Across 18 shared cell types, the only other assayed TRPM-family member, Trpm3, showed at most a very weak correlation with Trpm7 (r≤0.032), and calcium pumps/channels and synaptic signaling nodes including Atp2b1, Atp2b2, Cacna1d, Camk2a, Gnb1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Mtor, Pik3ca, and Plcb1 also had near-zero mean correlations. This supports a specific Cnnm2-related hint rather than a shared cation-channel transcriptomic state, with the caveat that Trpm6 was not assayed.

Ncam1 showed a buffered transcriptional phenotype in which the downstream trans response was weak and not unique to this perturbation: after excluding the directly targeted Ncam1 transcript, related neuronal immunoglobulin-superfamily adhesion perturbations behaved similarly, with L1cam, Chl1, Cntn1, and Cntnap1 showing no trans FDR hits and Nrcam and Cntnap2 showing only two and one hits, respectively. This pattern supports a broader neural cell-adhesion/neuron-projection module that is poorly read out by steady-state nuclear RNA, although comparator perturbations differed in on-target strength and the few Nrcam/Cntnap2 hits did not form a recurrent adhesion-gene module.

Myo5a did not permit a meaningful test of the canonical RAB27A-MLPH/MYRIP-MYO5A cargo-adaptor module in this dataset. Rab27a was the only directly targeted comparator, but it showed no on-target FDR-significant knockdown in overlapping cell types, while Mlph, Myrip, Myo5b, and Myo5c were not targeted. Accordingly, near-zero Myo5a-Rab27a signature correlations should be interpreted as lack of comparator engagement rather than evidence against module relevance. The only transcript-level hint was a nominal, FDR-insignificant Myrip decrease in a weakly engaged L2/3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut signature.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Nobox showed only a weak, restricted-signature similarity to Lhx3 that did not hold up in full-transcriptome comparisons. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, the only class with a q<0.1 Nobox outlier, Lhx3 was the top restricted neighbor, and in 054 CNU-MGE GABA it was again a top-10 neighbor, yet full-transcriptome Pearson correlations were just 0.165 and 0.119. Because safe-target perturbations also appeared among top-10 restricted neighbors in 12 of 22 Nobox cell types, and the correlations were computed post hoc from the top 100 Nobox genes per cell type, these data suggest an extremely weak, nonreproducible Nobox signature rather than homeobox interchangeability.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kmt2d in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed its strongest positive signature neighbor with Kdm6a, consistent with an MLL3/4-KDM6A enhancer-regulation axis in this neuronal context, whereas the paralog Kmt2c was weakly correlated and had no corrected hits. The agreement was strongest on the restricted 314-gene Kmt2d-responsive signature rather than the whole transcriptome. This argues against simple Kmt2c-Kmt2d interchangeability here, although interpretation is limited because Kdm6a itself had only one FDR-level gene and Kmt2c had only 55 perturbed cells in 151 TH.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Slc12a5 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class showed a selective multigene response characterized by Slc12a5 downregulation and induction of immediate-early/activity-regulated genes including Fos, Nr4a1, and Dusp1. In the same cell type, strongly engaged Gabra1, Gabrg2, Kcnq2, and Kcnq3 perturbations reduced their own transcripts but largely produced only self-target effects and did not phenocopy the Slc12a5 signature; whole-signature correlation likewise found no strong phenocopy. This suggests the response is not a generic consequence of receptor or ion-channel knockdown, although guide strength, baseline expression, and protein half-life differ across genes.

Gnptab showed a selectively weak perturbation signal rather than a general failure to detect endolysosomal genes: in the same dataset, Atp6v0c produced 813 FDR-significant rows, and Ctsb, Gaa, Psap, Ppt1, Atp6v0a1, and the related complex member Gnptg also yielded at least some FDR-level signatures, with several showing stronger on-target transcript depletion than Gnptab. This pattern argues that the Gnptab null is gene-specific, with likely caveats around guide efficacy, transcript dynamics, or enzyme turnover; however, not all comparators are in the M6P-tagging complex, and some contrasts reflect transcript depletion rather than a shared pathway-response score.

Kcnh5 perturbation showed no multiple-testing-significant mRNA response in this screen: Kcnh5 itself did not reach FDR-level target depletion, and measured voltage-gated potassium-channel neighborhood transcripts, including Kcnab1/2/3, Camk2a/b/d, Cask, and related channel genes, were unchanged. This null was not a generic inability to detect ion-channel knockdown, because Kcnq2 and several KCNC-family perturbations in the same dataset did show target-transcript loss. The comparison is limited to transcript engagement rather than identical downstream phenotypes, and paralog expression and guide performance may differ.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Hlcs showed no reproducible convergence with Pcca or with top positive or negative signature neighbors across 22 shared cell types, including diverse glutamatergic and GABAergic populations. Both Hlcs and the related Pcca perturbation were transcriptionally weak: Pcca had no FDR-significant genes and its median correlation with the Hlcs top-100 score vector was only 0.0179. Because the neighbor analysis was limited to the 100 largest absolute Hlcs scores per cell type, these sparse nominal genes should not be interpreted as a stable biotin transport and biotin-dependent carboxylase activation state.

Neurod2 showed no clear transcriptomic convergence with related neuronal bHLH perturbations or functional neighbors: its score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Neurod1, Atoh1, Neurog3, Tcf3, Tcf4, Tcf12, Tbr1, Myt1l, and Cplx2, and an unbiased neighbor search found no strong partner, with the best match only weakly positive in 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells (Fntb, r=0.210). This argues against inferring a shared Neurod2 pathway from top signature similarity here, although the null pattern likely reflects weak Neurod2 engagement and sparse responses rather than proving these factors are unrelated.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nr2f1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a distinctive signature with Sorl1 up-regulation and Sema7a repression. The close paralog Nr2f2 only partially converged, nominally reproducing Sorl1 induction in this cell class but not Sema7a repression, Astn1 changes, or the broader Nr2f1 score vector, whereas Nr2f6 did not converge on Sorl1 at all. This suggests limited interchangeability within NR2F/nuclear receptor transcription in this neuronal state, although Nr2f2 and Nr2f6 did not show significant self-transcript knockdown here and the comparison is signature-based rather than a definitive epistasis test.

Pdss2 perturbation did not produce a coherent compensatory coenzyme Q or mitochondrial electron-transport transcriptional program in the assayed brain cells. Across cell types, no multiple-testing-significant differential-expression call was detected, and CoQ-pathway genes including Pdss1, Coq2–Coq9 as well as respiratory-chain genes such as Ndufs1, Ndufs3, and Uqcrfs1 showed only nominal, FDR-null changes, with no Pdss1/Coq5 convergence. This separates the single-cell mRNA readout from PDSS2’s expected biochemical role, while leaving CoQ abundance, respiratory flux, and ROS unmeasured here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gdi1 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not transcriptionally phenocopy Rab7 or other assayed Rab-pathway perturbations. In this cell type, Rab7 knockdown produced a high-magnitude module including Atp6v1b2, Ptgds, Dpp7, Scpep1, Insig1, Atp6v0b, Dusp1, and Ccdc136, but these genes remained non-significant after strong Gdi1 depletion, and correlations between Gdi1 and Rab7, Rab18, Rab27a, Rab28, Rab3gap1, Rab3gap2, or Gdap1 signatures were weak. This result comes from score-vector comparisons of RNA signatures, not direct measurements of Rab localization or trafficking flux.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Rb1cc1 showed a distinct macroautophagy-related perturbation pattern that was not interchangeable with other autophagy genes across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Map1lc3a was dominated by self-knockdown, Atg5 was weak, and Becn1 only partially converged with Rb1cc1 in 155 MB Glut, where the Rb1cc1 signature was largest. In 151, related perturbations did not reproduce the Rb1cc1 profile, and in 191 the sparse signature centered on Rb1cc1, Atp1a3, and Nrxn1. Some divergence may reflect weak Atg5 engagement, and the comparisons relied on a restricted Rb1cc1 signature rather than an independent pathway assay.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp322a perturbation did not produce a robust, reproducible phenocopy with literature neighbors, STRING neighbors, or top score-vector neighbors in this adult mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across cell types, signatures were largely orthogonal to Pou5f1, Sox2, Myc, Mapk1, Add1, and Pde1c, arguing against recovery of a hidden pluripotency or MAPK/AP-1 module. The only notable neighbors were confined to 308 CB GABA, where correlations reached about |r|≈0.3, but Zfp322a target engagement was weak and no FDR-significant genes were detected, so these relationships remain exploratory rather than mechanistic.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cep120 did not phenocopy related ciliary perturbations or any strong signature neighbor in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Ttc8 showed strong self-depletion, yet Cep120 remained weakly engaged and its signature was uncorrelated with Ttc8 (r=-0.0147); globally, correlations with Cep290, Ift81, Ift88, Cep164, and other neighbors were all near zero, so the candidate cilium and centrosome program showed no recurrent transcript change or signature convergence. This interpretation is limited because correlations were computed from summary Wilcoxon scores rather than raw single-cell expression, and many structural interactors were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Osbpl2, in the best nominally engaged 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, did not transcriptionally track available presynaptic exocytosis perturbations: Osbpl2 perturbation did not significantly change Snap25, Stxbp1, or Syn1 mRNAs, and its genome-wide signature was essentially uncorrelated with the strongly on-target Snap25, Stxbp1, and Syn1 knockdowns. This suggests that any ORP2 role in presynaptic neurotransmitter release is not organized here as a broad core-SNARE mRNA program, though Stx1a, the syntaxin isoform emphasized elsewhere, was not assayed.

Fzd2 showed a nonconvergent, weak transcriptomic signature that did not resemble interchangeable perturbations of other Frizzled receptors, ROR/RYK, LRP5/6, or canonical β-catenin/APC pathway genes. Across Fzd2-versus-Wnt comparisons, correlations were near zero overall, and even the nearest whole-library neighbors were weak. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Fzd2 had the largest matched cell count but no FDR response, while Ctnnb1, Apc, Gsk3b, and Lrp6 were active with near-zero correlation to Fzd2. Because the Fzd2 signature itself was weak, this mainly supports a lack of captured response rather than mechanistic anti-correlation.

Pax5 showed a largely null, non-convergent pattern in this neuronal atlas, and that silence extended to related Pax-family paralogs and B-lineage PAX5-network genes. Across sampled neuronal classes, including 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and 308 CB GABA, Pax2/Pax5 midbrain-cerebellum pathway genes showed no detected sampled neuronal response, while Ebf1, Ebf2, Ebf3, Ets1, Bach2, Cd79a, and Cd79b did not form a coherent neuronal module. A few isolated hits in Bach2, Ebf2, and Pax7, including nominal signals in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, did not reproduce a shared Pax5-like program, consistent with missing lineage context rather than a single failed guide set.

Gata6 showed transcriptome-wide perturbation signatures that were largely uncoupled from expected GATA-family and TGF/BMP-SMAD neighbors in the sampled neurons: correlations with Gata1, Gata2, Gata3, Gata4, Zfpm2, Smad2, Smad4, Tgfbr2, Tgfbr1, Bmpr2, and Acvr1 were all weak or near zero, and Gata6 did not phenocopy other assayed GATA factors. In 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, Nsun2 was the only adjusted-significant downstream gene for Gata6, but the broader local signature and whole-signature neighborhood remained weak. These comparisons used whole-signature Wilcoxon scores rather than validated pathway readouts, and some comparator perturbations had weak target engagement.

Il17rd did not yield a coherent transcriptomic module in this dataset: its score vector was essentially uncorrelated with Il17ra, Fgfr1, Fgfr2, Fgfr3, Braf, Mapk1, Nfkb1, and Tlr8, so the expected FGF/Ras/MAPK, IL-17, and TLR signaling relationships were not recovered in the basal neuronal assay. The Il17rd signature itself was weak, with no detectable depletion or enrichment of the targeted transcript, and pathway-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy it. These near-zero correlations are best interpreted as negative evidence in this context, not proof that IL17RD lacks roles in ligand-stimulated or non-neuronal cells.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Otud7a showed a weak positive signature similarity to Ank3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Ank3 was the top positive neighbor of the Otud7a score vector among other perturbations. This convergence fits an OTUD7A-Ankyrin signature neighborhood, but the effect was small: Pearson r was 0.143, Otud7a had no FDR-significant genes in this cell class, and its vector was much weaker than direct Ank3 perturbation, which was strongly engaged with Ank3 logFC -0.256 and 121 FDR-significant genes.

Dnajc6 showed a transcriptomic signature that was essentially orthogonal to perturbations of nearby clathrin-endocytic and synaptic-vesicle genes, including Ap2s1, Ap2m1, Cltc, Dnm1, Dnm2, Synj1, Syp, Snap25, and Bin1, even when several of those comparators had FDR-significant signatures. In this assay, Dnajc6 therefore was not interchangeable with related endocytic perturbations, and its knockdown appeared less transcriptionally penetrant. This interpretation is tempered because correlations were computed on differential-expression scores rather than raw cell profiles, and Dnajc6 itself had no FDR-significant downstream signature; correspondingly, Dnajc6 downregulation did not induce Gak or a coherent HSPA8/auxilin clathrin-coated-vesicle uncoating or synaptic-vesicle recycling core-module mRNA response.

Ncoa1 showed a null-like transcriptomic response in this experiment: a global scan after Ncoa1 perturbation found no multiple-testing-significant changes, including in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut populations where nuclear receptor transcriptional coactivation appeared buffered or uncoupled. In contrast, related perturbations such as Thra, Nr3c1, Rara, Esr1, Esr2, and Ncoa3 produced at least one FDR-significant hit, whereas Rxra and Pparg also did not. This pattern suggests target- or context-specific buffering rather than a blanket failure to detect nuclear-receptor biology, although most related positives were sparse and these perturbations are not interchangeable loss-of-functions.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Dmbt1 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut showed the only FDR-significant downstream hit, with Epb41 down, but the overall signature did not converge with the expected DMBT1 secreted mucosal/pattern-recognition or surfactant-associated network. In this cell class, the strongest whole-signature neighbors were weak (Smarcb1 r = 0.162, Pex1 r = -0.180), while Dmbt1-network comparators present in the library—Hmgb1, Lgals3, and Reg1—had near-zero correlations and no adjusted hits. Because comparator analysis was restricted to the 027 class and STRING edges reflect functional associations rather than a physical complex, this is better treated as an isolated neuronal response than a recovered DMBT1 network program.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Glud1 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed no coherent transcriptional induction of a TCA-cycle, aminotransferase, or glutamate-receptor module: in the best-engaged cell class, Glud1 itself was the only FDR-significant gene, and related perturbations such as Got2, Got1, Gls, Slc25a12, Ogdh, and Dld were only weakly concordant without broad pathway convergence. The thalamic Glud1 signature had no high-correlation positive or negative all-target neighbor, and secondary changes were nominal, so the main effects may lie in metabolic flux or electrophysiology rather than steady-state mRNA, which cannot directly assess alpha-ketoglutarate production, ammonia handling, NAD(P)H, or TCA flux.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Srrm2 knockdown produced a recurrent mixed signature across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and low-cell-count 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells, with repeated decreases in a nuclear-speckle/RNA-processing branch including Leng8, Pnisr, Rsrp1, Atxn2l, Akap8l, Snrnp70, Prpf4b, Srsf5, Srsf11, and Sf3a2, alongside increases in Nxf1, Dgkz, Ap1g2, Bicd2, Arhgef1, and Zfp598. The strongest signatures were enriched for the nuclear-speckle component, although some recurrence used nominal p<1e-3 and the assay did not directly measure alternative splicing.

Rxrg showed near-zero Perturb-seq signature similarity to its expected nuclear-receptor partners, including Rxra, Rxrb, Rara, Rarb, Rarg, Ppara, Ppard, Pparg, and Ppargc1b, so curated RAR/RXR retinoic-acid and RXR/PPAR module proximity did not translate into a shared transcriptomic neighborhood. In a whole-screen search, no positive or negative neighbor exceeded |r|=0.0357 outside the self-correlation. This weak convergence should be interpreted cautiously because the Rxrg query signature itself was weak, potentially reflecting dropout or guide inefficiency, and several RXR paralog perturbations were also near-null.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Adgrv1 was distinct from other adhesion GPCR perturbations: across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, Adgrl1, Adgrl2, and Adgrl3 showed clean self-transcript loss, whereas Adgrv1 did not, and correlations using the restricted Adgrv1 top/bottom genes were near zero. This suggests the Adgrv1 null transcriptional result was not a generic failure to detect adhesion-GPCR perturbations, though the comparison is limited to paralogous family members rather than the same protein complex.

Lrrc3b did not phenocopy its STRING-predicted functional neighbors Adgrl1, Adgrl2, or Adgrl3 across the measured central brain cell types: across 22 matched cell types, all 66 Adgrl–Lrrc3b within-cell-type correlations were very small (|r| ≤ 0.164). In 308 CB GABA, where subthreshold Lrrc3b showed its strongest signature-neighbor relationships, Adgrl2 and Adgrl3 still remained weakly correlated. These results argue against treating the predicted Lrrc3b–latrophilin neighborhood as interchangeable perturbation biology, while noting that STRING edges are predictive associations and Lrrc3b itself was only weakly engaged.

Lrrn2 showed a flat, FDR-null transcriptional phenotype that did not converge with a related leucine-rich-repeat neuronal adhesion/receptor context in the sampled mouse neurons. Across matched cell types, the closest NLRR paralog Lrrn3 was also transcriptionally flat, and Lrrn2 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Lrrn3, Lrrtm1/3/4, Lingo1/2, and STRING-nominated Adgrl1/2/3 comparators, with Pearson r ranging from -0.073 to 0.058. Most comparator signatures were themselves weak, so these data argue against only a large shared RNA program, not physical interaction or redundant synaptic phenotypes.

Cckbr showed a weak signature, and perturbations of related CCK/gastrin GPCR pathway components did not converge on a Cckbr-like transcriptional state. Cck knockdown was robust in several classes, yet even there its correlation with the Cckbr score signature remained very small; likewise, Plcb1 and Itpr1 had significant on-target effects but their Cckbr-score correlations never exceeded |r| = 0.070, and Cckar lacked useful target engagement. These data argue that ligand loss, receptor loss, and proximal Gq/PLC-calcium node perturbation are not interchangeable cell-autonomous signatures in this dataset.

Gclc showed a transcriptional signature that was nearly orthogonal to matched perturbations of antioxidant-network neighbors, including Gclm, Gpx4, Nfe2l2, Prdx1, Sod2, and Fth1, rather than acting as a phenocopy of them. This suggests that acute single-gene perturbations within the GCLC-GCLM glutamate-cysteine ligase complex and related oxidative-stress pathway were not interchangeable in this dataset. The contrast is tempered by weak on-target transcript knockdown for Gclc and Gclm and by the use of transcriptome-only endpoint comparisons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grn in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a buffered, self-dominated signature: knockdown of nearby endolysosomal genes Tmem106b, Psap, Ctsb, and Scarb2 mainly depleted their own transcripts and did not phenocopy Grn or feed back on Grn. By contrast, Rab7 knockdown triggered a large late endosome-lysosome stress program, with 501 FDR-significant genes and Grn up-regulation (logFC 0.719), alongside lysosomal markers including Atp6v1b2, Dpp7, Lamp2, Atp6v1a, Sqstm1, and Gaa. However, the Rab7-Grn link was supported mainly by rank with small score correlation, so it is better viewed as a restricted-signature relationship than a strong phenocopy.

Dip2b produced a weak adult mouse-brain perturbation signature that did not phenocopy tubulin-component or fragile-site/neurodevelopmental perturbations: across shared cell types, correlations with Tuba1a, Tubb3, Fmr1, and Aff2 were essentially nil (|r|≤0.0685), and even the top whole-signature neighbors remained weak in the three most target-engaged classes, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. In 110, Camsap2 was the strongest nominal response, hinting at neuronal microtubule biology, but no downstream gene reached FDR significance. Because Dip2a, Dip2c, Dmap1, Atat1, and Hdac6 were not perturbed, this reads as pathway uncoupling rather than definitive separation from all DIP2B partners.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pdhb in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed significant self-knockdown, but no FDR-significant downstream genes, and its genome-wide Perturb-seq signature was essentially uncorrelated with those of the coupled PDH-complex components Pdha1 and Dlat, which also showed only self-depletion in the same cell type. Thus, within the PDH complex and pyruvate-to-acetyl-CoA conversion pathway, acute single-gene perturbation produced shared on-target mRNA loss without a shared broader transcriptomic program; nearest Pdhb signature neighbors were weak, and the analysis was limited to largely null DE-score vectors with several regulatory comparators absent.

Nrcam knockdown was transcriptionally uncoupled from the canonical Sema3F/Neuropilin/Plexin pathway in this Perturb-seq dataset: across 22 cell types, Sema3f, Nrp2, Plxna3, Plxna1, Plxna2, Ank3, Cntn1, Cntn2, Dlg1, Dlg3, Dlg4, and Nfasc did not show significant corrected mRNA changes, and known adhesion or cytoskeletal neighbors did not phenocopy the Nrcam knockdown transcriptome. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Ank3 was transcriptomically divergent from Nrcam despite pathway proximity. This suggests the adult readout mainly captures loss of Nrcam transcript rather than induction of a receptor-complex feedback program, with the caveat that the assay does not match embryonic or postnatal circuit phenotypes reported in mouse studies.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mkx perturbation in 21 assayed brain neuronal subclasses, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic types, did not move the canonical tendon extracellular-matrix/TGFβ program. Across 378 tests of 18 markers, including Scx, Tnmd, Col1a1, Col1a2, Fmod, Dcn, Bgn, Thbs4, Tgfb1-3, Egr1, and Egr2, no nominally significant changes were detected, and no downstream gene reached multiple-testing significance in any comparison. This likely reflects both weak, inconsistent Mkx target-RNA engagement and the fact that these tendon/ECM genes are not expected to be strongly active in neurons.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Dcaf17 did not show a shared transcriptional signature with the available CRL4-DCAF–adjacent perturbations Ddb2 and Dcaf8 across the profiled brain cell types, including multiple cortical glutamatergic classes, GABAergic populations, hypothalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, pineal glutamatergic cells, and cerebellar GABA cells; in 155 MB Glut, which had a relatively large Dcaf17 cohort, the profile also remained buffered and contributed to this nonconvergence. Although Dcaf17 sits near DDB1/CUL4 network components, the dataset lacked Ddb1 or Cul4a/b perturbations, and Ddb2 and Dcaf8 are related DCAF-family nodes rather than Dcaf17 paralogs, so the data do not support a generic CUL4-DDB1/DCAF module signature shared by Dcaf17, Ddb2, and Dcaf8.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cic loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons only partially phenocopied Ras/MAPK perturbations. Although a small MAPK/CIC-consistent subset was present, with Dusp4 and Ptpn5 up and nominal increases in Etv5 and Spry4, the transcriptome-wide Cic signature was almost uncorrelated with Nf1, Braf, Map2k1, and Map2k2 perturbations in the same cell type. This suggests a thalamic Cic program beyond the classic RTK/Ras/ERK-to-ETV1/4/5 axis, while comparisons remain limited because upstream kinase perturbations need not match acute ERK-mediated CIC phosphorylation and were not time-resolved.

Cx3cr1 showed a largely null transcriptomic phenotype in this assay, resembling other weak innate or microglia-associated receptor perturbations such as Trem2, Csf1r, Axl, P2ry12, Ccr5, Ccr2, Tlr4, and C3, while App displayed robust self-transcript depletion in 20 of 22 assayed cell types. In high-count neuronal contexts including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Cx3cr1 had no FDR-supported downstream response even though App was strongly self-suppressed in the same data, suggesting a target-context-specific null rather than a general failure of detection, with the caveat that transcriptomic comparison alone does not prove comparator guides failed mechanistically.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Six6 showed no detectable convergence in mouse-brain Perturb-seq: across 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, the weak Six6 signatures did not align with Six-family paralogs, eye-field genes, STRING neighbors, or top positive/negative signature neighbors. In the strongest nominal context, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, the largest same-cell correlation outside Six6 was only with Ski (r=0.139), while 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba also lacked FDR-significant responses or a supported module. Thus, despite reported developmental links to Six3, Pax6, Rax, Otx2, Dach1, and Vsx2 within a SIX/Six3 retinal and Wnt-beta-catenin network, this atlas reconstructed only an absence of detectable convergence from weak Six6 profiles.

Slc25a13 perturbation showed no coordinated RNA compensation across all 21 assayed neuronal classes: transcripts in the malate-aspartate shuttle and aspartate/glutamate carrier set, including Got1, Got2, Mdh1, Mdh2, Slc25a11, Slc25a12, Slc25a18, and Slc25a22, as well as urea-cycle genes Ass1, Asl, Arg1, Cps1, Otc, and Nags, were not FDR-significantly changed. The only noted cross-perturbation nuance was detectable Slc25a12 depletion in some caudal classes, while Slc25a13 itself showed no robust transcript-level response; interpretation is limited because the assay was RNA-only and several hepatic urea-cycle genes were weakly represented or absent in some neuronal groups.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Htr2a showed a distinct perturbation signature in the 054 CNU-MGE GABA class: compared across Htr2a nominal genes, Htr2b was anti-correlated with Htr2a, whereas Htr2c was weakly aligned to near-neutral. This suggests that within 5-HT2 and broader GPCR/Gq signaling, close receptor paralogs were not interchangeable in the Htr2a-responsive class. The comparison is limited by restricted-signature correlation, and Htr2b and Htr2c each had only 39 perturbed cells in this class.

Fmn2 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the measured FMN2/SPIRE actin-nucleation and actin-compensatory network: Spire1, Spire2, Fmn1, Pfn1, Pfn2, Cdc42, Actg1, and Flna were all nonsignificant after correction, indicating that the canonical actin neighborhood was uncoupled from the Fmn2 transcriptome in this dataset. In the same analysis framework, Actb perturbation strongly and repeatedly upregulated Actg1 and Flna, arguing this was not a generic failure to detect actin compensation. This comparison is limited to mRNA and does not directly test FMN2-dependent actin polymerization, protein localization, or filament morphology.

Slc20a2 did not show a convergent neuronal Perturb-seq signature with the tested PFBC-neighborhood comparators Xpr1 and Pdgfrb. Across overlapping neuronal subclasses, score correlations to Slc20a2 were near zero, with Xpr1 only weakly engaged and Pdgfrb showing no measurable engagement or FDR-significant response. Although XPR1 and SLC20A2 are linked in phosphate homeostasis, this assay did not capture a shared neuronal signature for that module, and Slc20a1 and several disease-family genes were not available as exact perturbation comparators.

Bscl2 showed an acute RNA signature that did not converge with curated lipid-organelle or ER-shaping perturbations in the same cell-type contrasts: correlations with Rab18, Cpt1c, Atl1/Atl3, Reep1/Reep2, Spast, Ddhd1/Ddhd2, Vapb, Vps13a/Vps13c/Vps13d, and Vps35 were near zero, and an unbiased neighbor search found no strong positive or inverse match, with only weak similarity to Cfl2. This argues against a shared scRNA-seq injury module for this neighbor set, although many comparators had weaker self-knockdown than Bscl2, LDAF1/TMEM159 was not directly tested, and the correlation analysis relied on weak Bscl2 secondary genes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Calm1 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a selective transcriptional signature rather than broad remodeling of canonical CaM-pathway mRNAs: Calm2/3, Camk2a/b/g, Camk4, Ppp3ca/Ppp3cc, and Grin1/2a/2b were largely unchanged, and although Atp2b1 transcript fell, Atp2b1 knockdown did not phenocopy Calm1. Across 2,046 perturbation signatures, no strong global neighbor matched the Calm1 151 signature; a restricted 151-class scan instead nominated Camta1 as the most negative neighbor. These RNA-level results do not assess protein phosphorylation, Ca2+ flux, or channel gating.

Glce perturbation showed little acute transcriptional coupling to the measured heparan-sulfate pathway: Ext1, Ext2, B3gat3, Agrn, Xylt1, Hs6st2, and Gpc6 were not FDR-significant, and whole-signature comparisons found no strong phenocopy or anti-phenocopy among related HS/HSPG perturbations, with maximum related score-correlation |r| = 0.093. In 155 MB Glut neurons, Glce appeared weaker than related self-depletions in the extracellular HSPG neighborhood. These data suggest that GLCE function may be buffered or reflected in extracellular HS structure rather than an acute cell-autonomous RNA feedback program, although only a subset of HS enzymes/core proteins was tested and RNA cannot read out HS sulfation or epimerization.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ndufb11 in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed FDR-supported on-target RNA depletion, but its transcriptomic signature was otherwise buffered: among 25 other assayed NDUF-family perturbations in the same engaged subclasses, correlations with Ndufb11 were near zero and there was no robust positive or negative transcriptome-wide signature neighbor. Related Complex-I perturbations were likewise dominated by self-transcript depletion rather than shared downstream programs, so the lack of convergence reflects the RNA readout and could also arise from buffering, dose, or scRNA sensitivity rather than true biochemical independence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tpi1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a node-specific glycolysis response: despite pathway membership, Hk1, Gpi1, and Slc2a1 knockdowns engaged their own transcripts but did not phenocopy the broader Tpi1/Pgk1/Gapdh pattern, and Tpi1 score-vector correlations with these perturbations were low. Global similarity modestly favored Pgk1 and Gapdh, concentrating the signature around the TPI1-GAPDH-PGK1 interval rather than upstream glycolysis. Tpi1 knockdown also lacked FDR-supported compensatory changes in assayed glycolysis genes or Slc2a1, although Hk1/Gpi1 lesions may have been weaker and Gapdh/Eno1 on-target rows were not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cacna2d2 showed a weak, target-specific result in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: despite 177 perturbed cells, it had no detectable self-depletion and no FDR-significant transcriptomic hits, whereas related voltage-gated calcium-channel genes Cacna1g, Cacna1c, Cacna2d1, and Cacnb4 were significantly self-depleted in the same cell class. This contrast argues against an assay-wide failure to detect calcium-channel perturbations and instead points to limited target engagement or RNA-level detectability for Cacna2d2 in this thalamic context, without implying biochemical dispensability.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Eif5a showed an exploratory concordant signal with Eef2 specifically in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut: within a restricted signature of 102 nominal Eif5a genes, Eef2 was the top positive neighbor, suggesting a possible elongation-factor-like state in this cortical excitatory context. However, this convergence was not seen as a strong whole-genome correlation, and Eif5a target engagement in this cell type was weak, with the Eif5a transcript not nominally significant after adjustment, so the observation is hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

Glp1r showed weak score vectors that did not converge with related incretin-receptor or cAMP-pathway perturbations, with only small correlations to Gipr, Gcgr, Gnas, Adcy3, and Prkaca. In the same analysis framework, Adcy3 and Prkaca guides still reduced their own transcripts, indicating the platform could detect on-target effects. Thus, this basal screen did not recover a shared GLP1R–Gαs–adenylyl cyclase–PKA transcriptomic module, so pathway-level interpretation of nominal Glp1r genes is not supported here, while low Glp1r engagement remains an important caveat.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Agps in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal class is associated with a Dhcr24-centered, SREBP2-linked sterol program, and Far1, Pex14, and Pex13 show partial concordant induction of the same module, including genes such as Insig1, Dhcr24, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, and Stard4. In whole-signature comparisons within this class, Pex14, Abcd3, Acbd5, and Far1 rank among the most positive Agps neighbors, but the correlations are very small, Pex13 mRNA depletion was weak, and most shared sterol-gene effects were only nominal, so the convergence is best viewed as exploratory support for a broader peroxisome/ether-lipid axis rather than a strong Agps-specific signature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kdm6b did not behave like an interchangeable KDM6-family or H3K4/MLL-family chromatin perturbation in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Kdm6b showed no adjusted transcriptomic hits, whereas Kdm6a had sparse detectable effects and Kmt2d, Kmt2b, Setd1a, and Kdm5c produced strong signatures at similar cell counts; Kdm6b–Kdm6a whole-signature correlations were near zero. This suggests weak engagement or buffering of Kdm6b in this context, with the caveat that the contrast is transcriptomic and guide pools differed in target efficiency, and the chromatin-regulator comparators are positive controls rather than exact complex matches.

Ndufaf2 perturbation lowered the Ndufaf2 transcript itself, but it did not produce a coordinated mRNA response in mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I assembly genes or a broader OXPHOS transcript panel, including nearby peripheral-arm flavoprotein module genes such as Ndufa12, Ndufs1, Ndufs3, Ndufs4, Ndufs6, Ndufv1, and Ndufv2. No individual cell type passed per-signature FDR correction for the on-target row. This suggests an RNA-level uncoupling between acute Ndufaf2 knockdown and adjacent OXPHOS transcriptional programs, with the caveat that the assay did not measure protein abundance, assembly intermediates, oxygen consumption, or ROS.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Hspa8 depletion produced a recurrent compensatory heat-shock/chaperone response rather than a cell-type-specific idiosyncratic signature, with up-regulation of HSP70/HSP90-network genes including Dnaja1, Hspa4l, Hsp90aa1, Hsph1, Stip1, Dnajb1, Cct6a, and in one cortical class Mars1. FDR-supported induction was seen in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; the thalamic class showed the strongest response with a small set of neuronal down-regulated genes, while broader recurrence outside these cell types was nominal only. Hsf1 activity was not directly assayed.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Lepr perturbation showed a detectable signature only in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells, but this signature did not resemble a canonical leptin receptor JAK/STAT-IRS-melanocortin program: Jak2, Stat3, Stat5b, Socs3, Irs1, Sh2b1, Pomc, Agrp, and Mc4r were not significant after FDR correction, and the Lepr profile was only weakly correlated with measured pathway neighbors and related cytokine or insulin-family receptors such as Il6st, Il6ra, Insr, Ptpn1, Prlr, Ghr, Mc4r, Agrp, and Fto. This suggests pathway uncoupling rather than an acute LEPR readout, with the caveat that Lep, Jak2, Socs3, Sh2b1, and Pomc perturbations were unavailable and CRISPR loss does not mimic acute leptin stimulation.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Prpf6 showed a convergent positive signature with other splicing perturbations, especially Ddx23 and U2af2, in the most responsive glutamatergic classes: 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and more weakly 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. In restricted 150-gene signatures, Ddx23 was the top positive neighbor in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with U2af2 also among the top neighbors, while anti-correlated neighbors were not comparably strong. This convergence was seen alongside broader spliceosome-related genes such as Snrnp70, Cdc40, Son, Ddx39b, and Srsf1, but correlations were based only on the top 150 Prpf6 genes per class and the comparator perturbations had heterogeneous DE strength.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gsdme did not show a stable transcriptional convergence pattern in this dataset: across 22 profiled neuronal cell types, including 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 308 CB GABA, there was no FDR-significant downstream signature, no recurrent nominal p<0.001 gene, and no stable restricted signature neighbour. The strongest top-200 neighbours were weak, cell-type-specific, and sometimes Safe_target controls, with the largest correlations arising in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA despite only two nominally significant rows and no FDR support. Because key comparators in the CASP3/GSDME and granzyme-B/GSDME pathway, including Casp3, Gsdmd, Gsdma, Gsdmc, Nlrp3, and Pycard, were mostly not assayed, absent genes cannot be interpreted as negative tests for compensatory convergence.

Zbtb16 showed a weak and largely orthogonal Perturb-seq signature: across all 22 tested cell types it had no FDR-significant differentially expressed gene, no recurrent nominal gene module, no autophagy module, and no high-correlation positive or negative neighbor in a genome-wide signature search. Other assayed ZBTB factors, including Zbtb10, Zbtb11, Zbtb18, Zbtb20, Zbtb21, Zbtb24, Zbtb38, Zbtb42, and Zbtb7a, also did not phenocopy Zbtb16, nor did assayed Rara, Hdac4, Hdac5, Sin3a, or Cul3 perturbations, despite reported links to HDAC/corepressor, RARA, and CUL3 biology. Because the observed correlations were dominated by a weak Zbtb16 signature, and Ncor1, Ncor2, and Hdac1 were not assayed, no shared module can be inferred from related perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Trps1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a thalamic signature that was not reproduced by perturbing Gata1, Gata2, Gata3, Gata4, Gata6, Sox9, Runx2, Stat3, Maf, or Mafb: related perturbation correlations to Trps1 ranged only from -0.041 to 0.071, with no close positive or inverse signature neighbor. This argues that the neuronal Tnc/Atp6ap2/Pid1 response is not an interchangeable readout of nearby GATA- or osteochondral transcription-factor programs, although some comparator target transcripts were not significantly reduced, so variable guide engagement may contribute to the contrast.

Crx perturbation in the sampled mouse brain classes did not recruit the expected CRX-centered photoreceptor transcriptional program: across 18 assayed photoreceptor or phototransduction genes, including Rho, Gnat1, Gnat2, Opn1mw, Opn1sw, Cnga1, Cngb1, Pde6b, Pde6g, Prph2, Rcvrn, Rbp3, Rom1, Arr3, Pdc, Gnb3, Gngt1, and Guca1a, none reached even nominal significance, and the genome-wide scan found no FDR-significant downstream genes in any evaluated brain cell type. This null result should be interpreted with the caveat that the marker set was hand selected and many photoreceptor genes were sparsely represented in the differential-expression rows.

Lrrtm3 showed an orthogonal RNA-signature pattern relative to the assayed LRRTM paralogs Lrrtm1 and Lrrtm4, with near-zero correlations across shared cell types rather than a coherent paralog-wide response. In 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Lrrtm3 knockdown produced nominal target-transcript decreases but no FDR-significant downstream response, no App, neurexin, or LAR-RPTP phenocopy, and only weak whole-transcriptome neighbors. This comparison is limited because it relies on mostly non-FDR perturbations and did not include Lrrtm2.

Dync2i1 showed an essentially uncorrelated perturbation signature relative to other ciliary and Hedgehog genes, including Dync2h1, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Ttc21b, Bbs5, Bbs9, Cep290, Nek1, Smo, Ptch1, Ptch2, and Gli1/2/3. Across 323 same-cell-type comparisons, the maximum absolute Pearson correlation of Wilcoxon scores was only 0.095, indicating no clear convergence on intraflagellar transport or primary-cilium Hedgehog signaling transcriptional readouts. This lack of similarity is tempered by the weak, non-significant Dync2i1 signature, which limits interpretation.

Cd2ap showed a target-specific null in this assay: unlike several Alzheimer or endocytic perturbations such as App, Dnm1, Sorl1, Synj1, Tmem106b, Mef2c, Bin1, and Cltc, which each had at least some FDR-significant on-target transcript depletion, Cd2ap had no significant target-transcript engagement, similar to Abca7. Nearby adaptor or actin-neighborhood genes were also mostly unengaged at the RNA level, so the result does not support convergence with a shared disease-family signature. This comparison is based on on-target depletion counts rather than full-signature correlations, and guide efficacy and baseline expression likely differed across targets.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Atoh1 showed near-zero global transcriptomic correlation with its tested partners and pathway neighbors across all Atoh1-tested cell types, indicating that developmental or biochemical proximity did not translate into an interchangeable mature-neuron perturbation signature when the Atoh1 program was quiescent. Comparators including Tcf3, Tcf4, Gfi1, Pou4f3, Notch2, Smo, Gli1/2/3, Neurod1/2, Zic1/2, and Tcf12 were almost orthogonal to Atoh1 globally, with only weak, inconsistent local positive similarity in 308 CB GABA that did not survive FDR correction; canonical regulators such as Hes1 and Ascl1 were not screened.

Fam149b perturbation signatures were uncoupled from the expected primary-cilium and SHH-Smoothened transcriptional neighborhood: across 14 assayed comparators, including Tbc1d32, Ift88, B9d1, Cep290, Ahi1, Cplane1, Dync2h1, Pibf1, Rpgrip1l, Smo, Ptch1, and Gli1/2/3, the largest absolute correlation was only 0.197, and the direct literature neighbor Tbc1d32 reached only |r|=0.135. Thus, this dataset did not resolve a shared neuronal transcriptional module for canonical ciliary trafficking or SHH signaling, although the analysis was based on post-perturbation mRNA ranks rather than ciliary protein localization or morphology, and several cilium-gene perturbations had weak target-transcript readouts.

Inpp5k showed pathway-neighbor uncoupling at the whole-transcriptome level: its acute neuronal signatures did not phenocopy nearby phosphoinositide, PI3K-Akt-mTOR, or congenital-muscular-dystrophy perturbations, with same-cell-type correlations to Tsc1, Tsc2, Pten, Mtor, Pik3ca/Pik3cb/Pik3r1, Akt3, Ocrl, Synj1, Plcb1, Fktn, Dag1, and Dpm1 near zero. In 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Cyp51 was nominally positive, but the largest related-target correlation was only Inpp5k:Tsc1 r=0.0995. Because correlations were based on rank-gene scores and the Inpp5k signatures were themselves weak, low similarity may partly reflect limited target engagement; accordingly, the weak sterol module should not be overread as a full mTOR-like state.

Fzd3 produced transcriptomic signatures that were largely uncoupled from other Wnt/planar-cell-polarity and canonical-Wnt perturbations in these mouse-brain data: across matched cell-class correlations, its profile was nearly orthogonal to Fzd2, Fzd4, Fzd6, Fzd9, Ryk, Ror1, Ror2, Lrp5, Lrp6, Celsr2, Prickle1, Apc, Ctnnb1, and Gsk3b, with all Pearson |r| below 0.20. This argues against treating loss of different Wnt receptors or downstream β-catenin regulators as interchangeable here, although the analysis used single-cell-class Wilcoxon score vectors and the comparator perturbations varied in effect size; in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Fzd3 was only nominally depleted without FDR-significant single-gene changes.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Casr showed only a weak, restricted signature in 308 CB GABA cells: among the top 100 Casr scores, its profile converged with Gpr68, Cckar, and Zic3 perturbations and inversely related to Ranbp2, Fbxo11, and Msl2. This suggests an exploratory extracellular proton and calcium GPCR crosstalk signal, with Gpr68 the most biologically plausible neighbor, but the result is limited to one low-response cell class and Casr itself had no FDR<0.05 differential expression in 308 CB GABA.

Zbtb10 did not phenocopy available Sp4, Myc, or other captured ZBTB-family perturbations in these neuronal populations. Across matched cell types, full-transcriptome correlations with Sp4 were essentially zero, and correlations with Sp7, Myc, Zbtb7a, Zbtb11, Zbtb16, Zbtb18, Zbtb20, Zbtb24, Zbtb38, and Zbtb42 were similarly weak. In 145 MH-LH TH Glut, the strongest nominal Zbtb10 burden coincided with a weak negative correlation to Zbtb7a rather than related-factor convergence. Because signatures were weak and restricted-signature neighbors included Safe-target controls, this argues against interchangeability but remains a cautious transcriptomic comparison.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sec63 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed positive signature convergence with proteostasis perturbations, most notably Hspa5, when analysis was restricted to the top 200 absolute Sec63 genes; across all genes, correlations were small. In this cell type, the Sec63 response included ER stress and ER quality-control markers such as Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Nfe2l1, and Chac1, and Hspa5 perturbation induced overlapping genes, nominating Hspa5/BiP as a functional marker and nearest interpretable neighbor of the Sec63 response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tcf7l2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a bidirectional but mostly decreased thalamic glutamatergic transcriptional signature consistent with a terminal differentiation, synaptic/excitability, and axon-guidance program rather than a generic Wnt-feedback response. Among 106 altered genes, Ramp3, Spock3, Kcnc2, and Pcsk2 decreased, Cck increased, and Grin2b, Gabbr2, Prkcd, Snap25, Robo1, and Lef1 also changed. This was the only cell class with a large Tcf7l2 program, and the dataset is transcriptomic only, so electrophysiological consequences were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Glud1, in the best-engaged thalamic class 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, showed only weak convergence with Got2 and not with Gls, Got1, or glutamate-receptor subunit perturbations such as Grin1 and Grin2b. Got2 was the nearest assayed biochemical neighbor but still matched weakly (r=0.0929), while several comparators had detectable own-target knockdown yet were nearly uncorrelated. Although STRING places Glud1 near Got2, Got1, Gls, Gad1, and Gad2, these small correlations suggest a context-restricted signature rather than pathway-wide interchangeability, and should be treated as a hypothesis about pathway topology rather than proof of shared mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Bmal1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut shows a clock-network signature that converges with Nr1d1, Clock, and Nr1d2, while opposing Rora by whole-transcriptome score correlation. In this dominant Bmal1-responsive thalamic class, Nr1d1, Clock, and Nr1d2 are the top positive signature neighbors and Rora is the top negative neighbor, indicating that related clock-loop factors are not interchangeable in this neuronal state. This pattern is cell-type-specific, and despite the overall negative correlation, Rora still shares some individual FDR genes with Bmal1.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Galr1 was transcriptionally silent in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, with only isolated nominal deviations that did not survive multiple testing and no meaningful signature neighbors. Its ligand Gal phenocopied this null pattern, whereas shared Gi/o and adenylate-cyclase pathway genes Gnao1, Gnb1, and Adcy3 showed detectable on-target transcript loss when directly perturbed, especially in the glutamatergic classes. Together this suggests an inactive or buffered Gal/Galr1 upstream node rather than a general failure to detect GPCR second-messenger perturbations, although these downstream genes are not GALR1-specific and Galr2/Galr3 were not tested.

Pah showed no close same-cell positive or negative perturbation neighbor by whole-signature correlation: across 43,663 same-cell comparisons, the strongest positive match was only to Syne1 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells (r=0.1495) and the strongest negative match was shallow in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut cells (r=-0.1329), with no comparator reaching |r|>=0.2. This weak Pah phenotype therefore was not rescued by related-target signature comparison, and mechanistic inference was limited because direct PAH pathway partners and aromatic amino-acid hydroxylase paralogs were not included as perturbation targets.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Smo showed no convincing convergent module in an all-target signature-neighbor scan: the strongest correlations were only modest and were restricted to 308 CB GABA cells, with positive neighbors including Cckar (r=0.297), Frrs1l (r=0.289), and Msx2, and negative neighbors including Fbxo11, Dnajb4, and Eef2, with Fbxo11 reaching r=-0.274. Because these neighbors fell outside Hedgehog pathway context and reflect weak signature correlations only, they are best treated as exploratory, cell-type-specific QC context rather than mechanistic SMO partners.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Pcdh19 showed a weak, largely null-like transcriptional signature that did not phenocopy Cdh2 knockdown, even in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 054 CNU-MGE GABA where Cdh2 strongly engaged and depleted its own transcript. In these cell types, the Pcdh19 and Cdh2 score vectors were nearly uncorrelated, so within the PCDH19–N-cadherin cell-adhesion context, partial Pcdh19 loss and Cdh2 loss were transcriptionally uncoupled rather than interchangeable. This comparison is limited by the weaker Pcdh19 RNA signature and does not directly test the PCDH19/N-cadherin protein complex.

Ephb4 was sharply uncoupled from Epha4 and other Eph-family perturbations in this neuronal Perturb-seq screen: while Epha4 showed strong on-target depletion with genome-wide significance in six cell classes, Ephb4 produced no FDR-significant rows, and its whole-signature correlation with Epha4 was essentially zero (r = 0.0029). This null pattern was also seen in large strata such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Epha4 self-depletion was detectable. These data suggest that EPH-Ephrin signaling should not be treated as an interchangeable transcriptional module across Eph receptors here, although the contrast is confounded by weak Ephb4 on-target signal and differing receptor expression programs.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: En2 showed its largest aggregate signature-neighbor structure in 308 CB GABA, where 28 of the 30 strongest absolute correlations to non-safe perturbations were concentrated; Wdr26 was the top positive neighbor and Ranbp2 the top negative neighbor, with Dstyk, Nr4a1, B9d1, and P2ry14 also among the comparators. However, this pattern did not resemble a canonical Engrailed developmental network and remained a restricted, exploratory state effect, because En2 had no corrected single-gene response in 308 CB GABA and the test did not cover the dopaminergic class.

Pdss1 perturbation did not trigger a transcriptional coenzyme Q biosynthesis feedback program: Pdss2 and the other measured canonical Coq pathway transcripts, including Coq2, Coq3, Coq4, Coq5, Coq6, Coq7, Coq8a, Coq8b, Coq9, Coq10a, and Coq10b, showed no significant induction or repression after correction, with all adjusted p values reported as 1.0 across 252 tests. This argues against simple mRNA-level compensation for partial Pdss1 knockdown in these neurons, while leaving open effects on CoQ intermediates or enzyme activity that were not assayed.

Pou1f1 perturbation in all 22 Pou1f1-tested brain cell classes was largely uncoupled from the anterior-pituitary lineage transcription program: signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Prop1, Lhx3, Lhx4, Sox3, Pitx2, Zfhx3, and assayed POU paralogs including Pou2f1, Pou2f2, Pou3f3, Pou3f4, Pou4f3, Pou5f1, Pou6f1, and Pou6f2, with combined all-gene correlations ranging only from -0.0648 to 0.1072. Related developmental transcription-factor perturbations neither phenocopied nor opposed the weak Pou1f1 signatures, suggesting this program is absent rather than redundantly encoded in these brain classes, although correlations were computed from per-cell-type differential-expression scores rather than single-cell embeddings or a pituitary perturbation experiment.

Otud7a perturbation produced no robust mRNA changes in the OTUD7A-Ankyrin/spectrin proteostasis pathway: Ank1, Ank2, Ank3, Sptan1, Sptb, Sptbn1, and Sptbn2 were unchanged across assayed cell classes, with all reported at FDR = 1.0. This null transcriptional result is consistent with a mechanism acting primarily at the protein ubiquitination, stability, or localization layer rather than at transcript abundance. However, no protein ubiquitination, Ankyrin-G localization, or spine morphology was measured, and weak Otud7a knockdown could also explain the absence of secondary mRNA effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Chrne showed no detectable self-transcript depletion across the assayed brain cell signatures, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, even though the transcript was measured in every Chrne perturbation signature. In contrast, Agrn, Pak1, Cdc42, and Chrnb2 showed clear self-depletion in selected cell types, with strong effects in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. Other muscle AChR subunits, including Chrna1, Chrnb1, Chrnd, and Chrng, behaved like Chrne, suggesting a target-context-specific null within the Agrn-Musk-Lrp4 and neuromuscular-junction AChR organization neighborhood rather than a universal assay failure.

Sbf2 did not phenocopy the available phosphoinositide or autophagy neighbors Becn1 and Synj1: in matched cell classes, whole-signature correlations with Sbf2 were near zero, including in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells where only exploratory mixed nominal signal was seen in autophagy and endolysosomal trafficking genes such as Ctps2, Vps37a, and Park7. Because MTMR2 and SBF1 were not perturbed and the Sbf2 signature itself was weak, these data argue against a broad shared endosomal/autophagy transcriptomic module and do not support using Becn1 or Synj1 as substitutes for the specific SBF2-MTMR2 branch.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ppargc1b knockdown was not transcriptomically interchangeable with Ppargc1a or the assayed PPAR receptors Ppara, Ppard, and Pparg in the main responder classes, notably 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In 155 MB Glut, where Ppargc1b showed the only FDR-significant response, Atp5b was down and the negative tail was enriched for mitochondrial genes, a signature not reproduced by the paralog or receptor perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ppargc1b had no FDR-significant genes but showed a nominal Idh3b/Uqcrc1/Ndufa10 negative tail. Because all compared perturbations had weak target-transcript depletion, the near-uncorrelated signatures may reflect perturbation strength as well as biology.

Ocrl did not phenocopy the core AP-2/clathrin endocytic machinery in this dataset: unlike Ap2s1, Ap2m1, and Cltc, which produced large corrected transcriptional changes, Ocrl generated no corrected DE rows and its whole-transcriptome score vectors were near-zero correlated with Ap2s1, Ap2m1, Cltc, Appl1, and Synj1. This divergence was also seen in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Ocrl showed only nominal target depletion while AP2/CLTC comparators were strong. The result separates OCRL as a catalytic/regulatory node from structural coat machinery, with the caveat that correlations were transcriptome-wide rather than pathway-specific lipid-flux measures, and Cltc was assayed in 18 of 21 Ocrl cell classes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Twist2 was inactive across assayed cell types in this screen, including higher-count strata such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where no corrected Twist2 hits were detected. In contrast, network-neighbor EMT/mesenchymal transcription factors showed selected responses in the same general context: Zeb1 was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also active in 155 MB Glut, while Zeb2 produced corrected hits in 052 Pvalb Gaba and one in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. This contrast is exploratory and based on corrected DE counts rather than matched target engagement, and Zeb1/Zeb2 are network neighbors rather than obligatory members of a TWIST2 complex.

Arl2bp did not phenocopy related ciliary perturbations in this brain dataset: signatures for Arl3, Bbs5, Cep290, and Ift88 were globally near-orthogonal to the Arl2bp signature within the ARL2/ARL3 ciliary basal-body interaction module. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where Arl2bp had the largest cell count and a nominal decrease, Arl3 was measurably knocked down yet remained nearly uncorrelated with Arl2bp (r = 0.016). These comparisons are transcriptomic, Arl2bp engagement was weak, and several related-gene perturbations had low cell counts.

Fgfr1 showed a transcriptomic signature that Fgfr2 and Fgfr3 did not recapitulate, arguing against a shared pan-FGFR state. Across Fgfr1-shared cell classes, Fgfr2 correlations with the Fgfr1 score vector ranged from -0.029 to 0.097 and Fgfr3 from -0.043 to 0.031; in 155 MB Glut, the correlations were 0.028 and 0.013. This nonconvergence is exploratory because Fgfr2 and Fgfr3 self-transcripts were not FDR-depleted, indicating weak measurable receptor engagement and limiting interpretation of family or downstream convergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Snai2 showed a notably weak signature relative to related EMT, TGFβ, Notch, and cadherin perturbations: across the same table, Snai2 had no FDR-significant genes, whereas Zeb1, Cdh2, Zeb2, Smad2, Tgfbr2, and Notch1 each had at least one corrected response. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Snai2 was FDR-null despite 105 perturbed cells, while Zeb1, Cdh2, and Smad2 were significant; similarly, Snai2 remained FDR-null in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, where Zeb2 and Tgfbr2 showed corrected genes such as Rasd2 and Ssbp4. This argues against a dataset-wide failure to detect EMT-neighbor biology, although comparator cell counts were often higher and measured transcriptional targets were not identical.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sox5 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class showed a sparse, target-private signature rather than a convergent module. In a 2,046-perturbation score-correlation scan, no strong Sox5-like or Sox5-opposing neighbor was detected; the best Pearson correlations across whole Wilcoxon score vectors were weak, at +0.0968 with Chp1 and -0.1045 with Nfe2l1. This was the only Sox5-responsive cell class at FDR<0.05, with limited upregulation of Dgkh and Tnnt1, though whole-vector Pearson correlations may miss nonlinear or pathway-specific relationships.

Adgrb1 was a null outlier in this screen: its perturbation did not measurably deplete Adgrb1 transcript in any assayed cell class and produced no FDR-significant downstream hits, even where the strongest apparent signal was only nominal Rufy3 up-regulation in 155 MB Glut cells (FDR=0.181592). In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Adgrb1 was nominally increased rather than depleted. By contrast, nearby adhesion-GPCR/Rho-synaptic genes Celsr2, Adgrl1-3, Baiap2, and Trio showed FDR-significant target depletion or downstream rows in the same matrix, though these comparators are pathway neighbors rather than ADGRB1 complex members and guide or expression differences were not controlled.

Clcn5 did not show transcriptome-wide convergence with the intracellular CLC genes Clcn3 or Clcn4, nor with an endosomal CLC/v-ATPase ion-homeostasis set including Atp6v0a1, Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2, Atp6v1e1, Atp6v0e2, Tmem9, and Tmem9b. In the screen, complete-signature correlations with Clcn3 and Clcn4 were essentially zero, and targeted pathway genes were not FDR-significant downstream of Clcn5. This lack of a coherent module is correlation-based and limited by weak Clcn5 knockdown; in 308 CB GABA, the strongest whole-signature neighbors were only modest and did not recover the expected CLCN5 pathway family.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nfe2l1 showed a weakly convergent UFMylation-related signature, most clearly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Uba5 was the top positive all-gene neighbor and Ufc1 ranked third, while strong similarity to direct proteasome perturbations was absent. The pattern recurred only weakly in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, with correlations near 0.1 and low counts in the latter class. Overall, these data suggest an ER proteostasis stress integration link between Nfe2l1 and UFMylation machinery, but not a proven direct NFE2L1-to-UFMylation mechanism.

Il2rb did not recover the expected IL-2/IL-15 receptor–JAK/STAT neighborhood in this assay: its score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with perturbations of Il2ra, Il2rg, Stat1, Stat3, and Stat5b, and no other perturbation showed a strong whole-transcriptome match or anti-match to Il2rb. This uncoupling was observed in basal brain classes rather than a specific cell type. Because most upstream cytokine machinery is immune-cell biased and Il2rb showed weak target-transcript engagement, these data do not support strong claims of true pathway divergence.

Zbtb24 showed a weak, buffered perturbation signature that did not phenocopy available Dnmt3a, Mecp2, or other ZBTB-family perturbations in the assayed neurons. Its score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Dnmt3a, Mecp2, Zbtb7a, Zbtb10, Zbtb11, Zbtb16, Zbtb18, Zbtb20, Zbtb21, Zbtb38, and Zbtb42; notably, Zbtb7a yielded 2,002 FDR hits across the same 22 class labels, whereas Zbtb24 yielded one. This argues against a generic methylation-regulator or BTB/zinc-finger response, although comparator choice was indirect because Cdca7, Hells, and Dnmt3b were measured only as transcripts, and guide efficacy and perturbed-cell counts could affect effect sizes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp2b2 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not produce an FDR-significant downstream transcriptional module, even though Atp2b2 loss was stronger there, and Atp2b3 loss was also significant but similarly buffered. In contrast, Atp2b1 knockdown in the same cell type induced an immediate-early/neuropeptide program with 21 non-target genes, including Fos, Nr4a1, Cck, Vgf, Chml, and Necab2. This suggests that plasma-membrane Ca2+ pump paralogs are not interchangeable in this thalamic glutamatergic context, although the Atp2b1-linked module was concentrated in one cell type and transcriptomics cannot identify the immediate Ca2+ signal responsible.

Gper1 behaved as a null-like perturbation across the 22 measured Gper1 cell classes, with almost no corrected scRNA-seq response and no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor. It did not converge with Esr1, Esr2, Pgr, or downstream cAMP/MAPK-related perturbations including Gnas, Adcy3, Mapk1, and Creb1; in a genome-wide search, every non-self perturbation had |r|<0.030.
