This argues against rescuing the weak Gper1 profile by borrowing related steroid-receptor or cAMP-pathway signatures, although the conclusion is limited by the weakness of the underlying signatures.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Adgra1 showed poor target engagement in this Perturb-seq design: its transcript was not detectably depleted in any assayed cell class, and its genome-wide signature remained uncorrelated with other available adhesion-GPCR perturbations. This contrasts with Adgrl1, Adgrl2, and Adgrl3, which each showed significant self-transcript depletion in lower-brain classes including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. The comparison is family-level rather than a true ADGRA paralog test, since Adgra2 and Adgra3 were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Arih1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed its nearest positive signature neighbor as Cul3, consistent with a weak positive convergence in the Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligase pathway, but the relationship was only partial rather than a phenocopy. The overlapping high-rank genes were directionally concordant, yet the overall correlation was small, and Cul3 had weaker on-target depletion than Arih1 in this cell type. Thus, the responsive thalamic cells support an ARIH1–CRL connection while arguing against simple interchangeability of Arih1 and Cul3 loss in this transcriptomic assay.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tnpo3 perturbation most closely matched Srsf1, Tpr, Prpf6, and Ddx23, while Kpna3 and Xpo7 were largely buffered and Xpo1 showed only partial overlap, arguing against a generic importin/exportin failure state and instead pointing to SR/splicing and the nuclear-pore-basket RNA-export interface. This pattern was seen across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with the largest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and recurrent Col20a1 induction. These correlations were restricted to Tnpo3-significant genes and do not establish direct ordering among TNPO3, TPR, and spliceosome factors.

Dpm1 showed a transcriptomic pattern that was uncoupled from the STT3B N-linked glycosylation perturbation and from any strong recurrent neighbor in the screen. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Dpm1 was the only context with FDR<0.10 genes and the main site for a nominal Pdia6/Hspa5/Rft1 response, while in 155 MB Glut there was no FDR<0.10 Dpm1 response despite strong Dhdds/Manf ER-chaperone signals. Although Stt3b knockdown was strong in 151 and 191 MB P MY GABA, it remained essentially uncorrelated with the Dpm1 top-100 signature; comparisons to Dpm2/Dpm3 were not possible because those guides were absent.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Drd2 showed no FDR-resolved self-transcript loss in this dataset, even though nearby Gi/o signaling components were detectably knocked down in selected cell classes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Gnao1 and Gnb1 showed strong self-depletion; Gnb1 was also depleted in 191 MB P MY GABA, and Gnb5 in 052 Pvalb Gaba. This pattern suggests receptor-specific under-engagement for Drd2 rather than a general inability to assay dopamine receptor Gi/o-cAMP pathway genes, although Gnao1, Gnb1, and Gnb5 are shared, broadly expressed transducers rather than direct Drd2 phenocopies.

Slc6a5 showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to related inhibitory-synapse perturbations, including Slc6a1, Glra1, Glra2, Glra3, Glrb, Gphn, and Arhgef9. In the only responding class, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, the narrow Slc6a5 signature marked by Ppat, Foxg1, and Ltk did not track these comparators, and across 151 matched target-by-cell-class comparisons the absolute correlation never exceeded 0.075. This pattern argues that glycinergic inhibitory neurotransmission genes were not interchangeable at the signature level here, although the analysis used restricted Wilcoxon-score signatures and several related perturbations were inactive in L2/3 itself.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Zeb2 did not phenocopy the strong thalamic Stxbp2/Ap1m2/Patj/F11r module seen with Zeb1 and Ctbp1, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where the response appeared buffered despite many Zeb2-assigned cells. Across matched summaries, Zeb2 also showed low restricted-signature correlations with Zeb1/Ctbp1 in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, arguing that the ZEB paralogs were not interchangeable and that the shared CtBP-linked junction/polarity readout was not a generic corepressor effect. This comparison is based on signature similarity, not protein occupancy or guide-level epistasis.

Cd79a showed no convergent BCR-module transcriptome in this brain-cell Perturb-seq screen: its expected partner Cd79b was likewise null, and Cd79a-versus-Cd79b genome-wide score correlations were near zero. Other lymphocyte receptor or B-cell-lineage comparators, including Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd3g, Pax5, Fyn, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, and Ptpn11, also had no detectable hits, consistent with B-cell receptor complex assembly and surface expression not being detectably perturbed here. Because these immune perturbations were themselves weak or unengaged, the result fits a context failure in non-B-cell brain populations rather than a mechanistic separation of CD79A from CD79B.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Xpo7 showed a weak or buffered transcriptional response across the 21-cell-type panel and did not phenocopy the related exportin Xpo1. In the XPO7/XPO1 nucleocytoplasmic protein transport context, Xpo1 produced a robust corrected signature whereas Xpo7 produced none and Kpna3 was similarly weak; residual signature correlations also left Xpo1 and Kpna3 near zero rather than among close Xpo7 neighbors. This divergence was evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, although Xpo1 self-transcript increases in some contrasts mean the comparison is not a matched knockdown experiment.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Gp1ba showed no coherent neural signature in this dataset. In 053 Sst Gaba, the strongest nominal effect was Auh down, but it remained near-threshold and isolated, and a restricted search using the top 40 Gp1ba-associated genes per cell type found only weak global neighbors such as Mpc1, Plxnd1, Lepr, and Chrna3, with no convergence on VWF/GPIb-IX-V signaling, hemostasis, or a compensatory pathway. Because this neighbor analysis was intentionally restricted, it serves as a falsification or triage check rather than a full-transcriptome correlation.

Shank2 did not transcriptomically converge with Shank3 or Dlg4, even though all three are closely linked within the SHANK-Homer-GKAP postsynaptic scaffold. In the same cell type, whole-signature correlations were essentially null, with median r=0.011 for both Shank2–Shank3 and Shank2–Dlg4, and the Shank2 profile did not resemble either comparator at the all-gene level. This argues against treating SHANK paralogs or PSD95/Dlg4 as interchangeable in global mRNA output, although the weak Shank2 signature may underestimate protein-level or longer-term convergence.

Unc5d produced an acute transcriptomic signature that did not converge with assayed Netrin/UNC5/FLRT/latrophilin pathway neighbors: whole-signature cosine similarities with Dcc, Neo1, Unc5c, Flrt3, Adgrl1, Adgrl2, Adgrl3, and Slit2 were near zero. Thus, in this assay, these perturbations did not phenocopy Unc5d despite known extracellular coupling among these molecules. This separation should be interpreted with caveats, as Flrt2 and Ntn1 were not targeted and weak Unc5d target engagement could reduce cross-perturbation similarity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gria4 did not phenocopy the other AMPA receptor pore-forming subunits: across 21 matched cell types, its aggregated score vectors were essentially orthogonal to Gria1, Gria2, and Gria3, despite all four belonging to the AMPA receptor activation and trafficking pathway. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Gria4 showed clear target depletion but no FDR-significant downstream genes and no alignment with Gria1/2/3, Dlg4, or Grin1 perturbations. The only exception was a moderate Gria4–Gria3 correlation in 308 CB GABA, where the correlated state was exploratory and mixed with mostly non-AMPAR perturbations; individual Gria4 cell-type signatures were generally weak after multiple testing.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
full_finding_text: Tbr1 showed only an exploratory, restricted-signature convergence in 001 L5-6 IT Glut: among the top 200 Tbr1-ranked genes, Sema5a, Gpr161, and Srgap3 were the closest neighbors and matched this restricted signature better than the curated TBR1 partner set. However, the similarity dropped substantially at whole-transcriptome scale, and these neighbor perturbations had only 29 to 55 perturbed cells with no FDR-significant full signatures, so the result should be viewed as hypothesis-generating rather than a robust convergence pattern.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Got2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed strong on-target depletion but essentially no broader transcriptional response: it had no non-self FDR genes, and its score correlations with Mdh1, Got1, Mdh2, Slc25a12, Gls, and Glud1 were all near zero. In the same cell type, Mdh1 was clearly divergent, producing 28 non-Mdh1 FDR genes, including induction of Gls. Thus, within this thalamic glutamatergic class, malate-aspartate shuttle and related aspartate/glutamate metabolism perturbations were not transcriptionally interchangeable, although this contrast is strongest in one cell type and reflects mRNA signatures rather than direct flux or enzyme activity.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Stat1 perturbation was associated with a nominal downregulation of an MHC-I antigen-presentation program, with lower B2m, H2-K1, H2-D1, and Nlrc5, most clearly in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA. A similar nominal module recurred after Ifngr1 and Ifngr2 perturbation, linking the Stat1 signature to type-II interferon receptor tone and the IFN-gamma–STAT1–NLRC5 pathway. The effect was weak and did not pass FDR, and interpretation in 191 MB P MY GABA is limited because Ifngr1 had only 39 perturbed cells.

U2af2 most consistently produced a down-shift of Rsrp1 together with an RNA-processing/nuclear-speck module, including Tial1, Srrm2, Luc7l2, Srsf5, Srsf11, Hnrnpu, Rnpc3, and Pnisr; a smaller subset, including Map7d1 and Iffo1, increased. Rsrp1 was lower in 11 of 23 cell types, and 120 genes recurred in at least four U2af2 signatures, making this module a more reliable readout of U2af2 pathway engagement than the U2af2 mRNA row itself. The strongest responses occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, while 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA showed downstream changes despite no measured U2af2 mRNA decrease. Enrichment was based on a recurrence-filtered list and does not directly measure alternative splicing.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ctnnb1 reduction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced the strongest response, with suppression of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin feedback genes including Lef1, Axin2, Notum, Wnt9b, and Fzd8, alongside remodeling of cadherin/catenin genes such as Cdh2, Ctnnd1, and Tiam1 and mixed synaptic receptor and excitability genes including Gabra4, Gabrb2, Grin2b, Gria2, Chgb, and Dagla. Apc showed an opposing pattern, while Lrp6 and Tcf7l2 partially converged, although cadherin/catenin comparators did not phenocopy the full signature. These pathway inferences are transcriptomic only, without beta-catenin localization, TCF reporter, or synaptic morphology measurements.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Tuba4a knockdown did not phenocopy related alpha/beta-tubulin or microtubule-associated perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut cells. Across Tuba1a, Tubb2a, Tubb3, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, Tubb5, Map1b, Map6, Mapt, Stmn2, Dcx, and Kif2a, whole-signature correlations were very low, with no same-cell-type neighbor showing |Pearson r| above 0.103. The pattern was largely Tuba4a self-depletion without a broad microtubule transcriptome, although this conclusion is limited to DE score-vector correlations and may be damped by weak downstream Tuba4a signal.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nlgn1 showed weaker apparent target engagement than related neurexin-neuroligin synaptic adhesion perturbations in the same cell-type panel: self-transcript depletion occurred in 0/22 Nlgn1 comparisons, versus 12/22 for Nlgn2, 5/22 for Nlgn3, and 8/22 for Nrxn1. Matched examples in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut showed strong Nlgn2/Nlgn3 depletion where Nlgn1 had no depletion. This contrast supports a perturbation-engagement caveat, not the absence of Nlgn1 biology, because guides and perturbed-cell counts differed across targets.

Scn3a showed limited engagement in this screen: its transcript was measured across all tested cell classes but was not robustly depleted after multiple-testing correction, whereas related voltage-gated sodium-channel genes Scn1a, Scn2a, Scn8a, and the beta subunit Scn1b achieved strong self-depletion in multiple matched cell classes yet produced few FDR-significant non-target changes. Together, these comparisons suggest a largely self-only Nav RNA response rather than a hidden shared transcriptional module, with the caveat that these data reflect RNA signatures, not sodium currents or excitability, and family members differ in expression domains and disease mechanisms.

Meox1 perturbation in the 22 tested mouse brain cell classes showed little convergence with its assayed developmental neighbors Tbx6, Pax1, Sox17, and Mesp2: their signature correlations with the Meox1 score vector were all weak, with Pearson r values from -0.069 to 0.107, and whole-library similarity search likewise found no strong recurrent Meox1 neighbor. This pattern suggests that the embryonic MEOX1 somitogenesis/sclerotome neighborhood was not engaged by the neuronal Meox1 perturbation, although the comparison is signature-based, Meox2 and Tcf15 were not perturbed, and the assayed brain cells do not match embryonic sclerotome.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Eif4g1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed its strongest biological convergence with Eif4e, the top positive whole-transcriptome signature neighbor among 2,045 perturbations in that cell type. Both perturbations induced Vgf, linking the result to the cap-dependent translation initiation eIF4F complex, but the overall similarity was modest: the correlation was only r=0.182 and just 8 of the top 100 nominal genes overlapped. Thus, Eif4e reduction appears to produce a stronger and partly distinct RNA response than Eif4g1 reduction, rather than an interchangeable mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Dmxl2 depletion was transcriptionally uncoupled from expected Rabconnectin-3/RAVE and V-ATPase acidification neighbors across matched cell classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. Although Atp6v0a1, Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2, and Atp6v0c showed detectable on-target perturbation effects, their score-vector correlations with Dmxl2 were near zero, and Madd and Rab3gap1 were similarly nonconvergent. In Pvalb interneurons, Dmxl2 appeared buffered while V-ATPase subunits remained detectable. These comparisons rely on weak transcriptomic signatures and do not directly measure vesicle pH, V-ATPase assembly, or Rab3 activity.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Ano3 in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA showed an Emc3-centered, low-cell-count transcriptomic response that did not phenocopy Kcnt1, Stim1, Gnal, Adcy3, Adcy5, Gnas, or Gnao1. Same-cell score correlations with these KCNT1/Slack, SOCE, and GNAL/cAMP-related perturbations were near zero, and a genome-wide scan found only weak positive or negative Ano3 signature neighbors. Thus, the small Ano3 mRNA signature appears uncoupled from these pathway neighborhoods in this stratum, with the caveat that the comparisons are noisy transcriptomic correlations whereas the cited mechanisms are protein, calcium, or electrophysiology based.

Gnb1 knockdown did not produce detectable transcriptional compensation by measured heterotrimeric G-protein subunits: Gnb2/3/4/5, Gnao1, Gnai1/2/3, Gnas, and several Gng genes remained not significantly upregulated, arguing against simple mRNA-level replacement of the lost beta subunit. This pattern was seen across the profiled neuronal contexts, including 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, within heterotrimeric GPCR/G-protein beta-gamma signaling. Some gamma subunits were not perturbed or may be lowly expressed, and any compensation via protein stability or complex assembly would not be detected here.

Ogfrl1 showed no strong recurrent positive or negative signature neighbor in an unbiased search, arguing against a clear assignment to any assayed transcriptional module under these conditions. Across same-cell comparisons to all other perturbations, the median maximum absolute non-self correlation was only 0.0869, and no cell type exceeded |r| = 0.2197; comparators such as Dnm2 and Wdr26 did not emerge as convincing neighbors. Because these correlations were computed on weak Ogfrl1 signatures, the low similarity could reflect query noise as well as biological disconnection.

Cd3d perturbation in all 21 Cd3d-profiled neuronal classes did not produce a proximal TCR/CD3 transcriptional response: Cd3e, Cd3g, Cd247, Cd4, Cd8a, Cd8b1, Lck, Fyn, Zap70, Lat, Ptpn6, Skap1, and Cd6 remained unchanged, so the canonical TCR-CD3 complex and T cell receptor signaling program appeared absent or uncoupled in this neuronal context. This result is limited to steady-state transcript measurements and does not test ITAM phosphorylation or other acute protein-level signaling events.

Eef1a2 showed a transcriptional signature that was not reproduced by perturbing Eef2, despite their shared placement in the eukaryotic translation elongation pathway. In this dataset, Eef2 had weak measured target engagement, with no significant Eef2 RNA depletion in assayed cell types, and its profile had almost no overlap with Eef1a2 FDR<0.1 genes and tiny full-vector correlation. Thus, the Eef1a2 phenotype should not be collapsed into a generic elongation-factor program, although this divergence is a dataset-level contrast rather than proof that EEF2 protein loss is biologically orthogonal.

Ndufaf5 did not share a convergent transcriptomic signature with related complex I biogenesis perturbations in this mouse-brain scRNA dataset. Ndufaf2, Ndufaf4, and Ndufaf5 each showed no FDR-significant genes across the tested target-by-cell signatures, and broader Nduf-family perturbations such as Ndufs2, Ndufs8, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufv2, Ndufs7, Ndufb8, and Ndufb11 were mostly limited to self-transcript knockdown rather than a shared downstream RNA program. Whole-signature similarity likewise failed to place Ndufaf5 with complex I or assembly-factor neighbors, although comparator coverage was limited because Ndufaf8 and Pyurf were not perturbed.

Ctnnbl1 showed near-zero transcriptomic signature correlations with the available spliceosome perturbations Cdc40, Prpf6, Srrm2, and U2af2, and it was likewise essentially uncorrelated with catenin-family perturbations including Ctnnb1, Ctnna2, Ctnna3, and Ctnnd2; global signature-neighbor analysis also did not reveal any strong or specific match. These data argue against a shared transcriptional endpoint with the tested spliceosome or Wnt/catenin perturbations, although interpretation is limited because key PRP19 core interactors were not present in the perturbation panel.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pdha1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a notable case where PDH complex membership did not translate into a shared Perturb-seq program: although Pdha1, Pdhb, and Dlat each had strong on-target depletion, the genome-wide score correlations between Pdha1 and Pdhb or Dlat were near zero. This suggests nonconvergent transcriptional responses within the PDH complex / pyruvate decarboxylation to acetyl-CoA pathway after partial perturbation. The comparison is strongest for Pdha1 versus Pdhb and Dlat, because Pdhx and Dld were not FDR-significant at their own transcripts in this cell type.

Pbx1 perturbation did not phenocopy its TALE/HOX network neighbors: mRNA score signatures were near zero in correlation with Pbx3, Meis1, Meis2, Pknox2/Prep, Hoxa1, and Hoxa3, both globally and within the assayed cell classes, and no hidden cell-type-specific high-correlation pattern was detected. In the context of PBX-MEIS/PREP-HOX TALE-homeodomain complexes, these data do not support simple interchangeability or a shared acute transcriptional output among the tested inputs, although this conclusion is limited because Pbx1 target engagement/knockdown was weak.

Gpr45 perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated with related class-A GPCR and cAMP-module perturbations, including Gnas, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Mc3r, and Mc4r. The largest related all-gene Pearson correlation was only 0.129, and even the best top-500 restricted neighbor, Mc3r in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, was no stronger than safe-target null correlations. These exploratory summary-signature analyses therefore do not support interpreting the weak Gpr45 signal as a latent cAMP or melanocortin transcriptional program, especially because the Gpr45 query signature itself is not FDR-supported.

cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Nr4a2 did not show a robust convergent NR4A-family transcriptional response when compared with paralog perturbations. Across 22 shared Nr4a2-Nr4a1/Nr4a3 subclasses, whole-signature correlations with Nr4a2 were nearly zero, with median within-subclass Spearman correlations of 0.016 for Nr4a1 and 0.017 for Nr4a3. Nr4a1 had no significant genes, and Nr4a3 showed only a single corrected Xpo6 hit in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, which was not replicated by Nr4a2 in Pineal cells, so a paralog-based rescue of the weak Nr4a2 signal is not justified.

Tnfrsf1b showed no convergence with Tnfrsf1a or other assayed TNFRSF/NF-kB perturbations in this dataset: signature-neighbor searches found no robust shared or opposing module, Tnfrsf1b–Tnfrsf1a score correlations were near zero, and Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf4, Tnfrsf9, Tnfrsf11a, Chuk, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, and Traf3 all had weak, uniformly nonsignificant signatures. This supports absence of a robust latent TNF-receptor-family module rather than mechanistic antagonism, with the caveat that these comparisons were computed on noisy weak signatures.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Tnrc6a showed a weak, mixed whole-library signature neighborhood in 155 MB Glut rather than the expected convergence with the miRNA-induced silencing/GW182-AGO-CCR4-NOT deadenylation pathway. The strongest positive neighbor was Crebrf and the strongest negative neighbor was Wdr26 in the same cell class, while other noted neighbors included Camta1, Smad1, Notch1, Fzd6, and even a safe-target control. Across 42,153 target-by-cell correlations, all absolute r values were below 0.168, indicating a low-amplitude, off-pathway pattern; these correlations came from Wilcoxon score vectors and do not constitute a direct interaction assay.

Ranbp2 showed only limited convergence with other nuclear-transport perturbations: across overlapping cell types, its signature was weakly similar to Tpr and Tnpo3, but near neutral relative to Nup93, Xpo1, Xpo7, and Kpna3. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, the pattern was mixed and fit a weak SUMOylation/nuclear-pore RanGTPase plus RNA-processing response involving Rbm15, Srrm2, Snrnp200, Rbm8a, Pcbp1, and Utp3. The closest neighbors also included proteasome and splicing perturbations such as Psmb4 and Prpf6, but these cosine similarities were modest and based on summary signatures rather than replicated perturbation-level covariance.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gapdh in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a thalamic signature that partially converged with Pgk1, but not with most assayed glycolytic or pyruvate-dehydrogenase neighbors. Pgk1 reproduced part of the Gapdh-linked program, including changes in Pnisr, Rsrp1, Ogt, Grm1, and the broader Pnisr/Rsrp1-centered RNA-processing signature with Ttc14 and Leng8, whereas Tpi1, Hk1, Pfkm, Gpi1, and Dlat were dominated by on-target self-reduction with little secondary differential expression. The whole-transcriptome Gapdh-Pgk1 correlation was only modest, and direct target engagement for Gapdh could not be measured.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mc1r showed a weak, cell-type-specific signature in 308 CB GABA in which its transcriptomic pattern aligned with B9d1 and opposed Wdr26, consistent with a primary-cilium GPCR trafficking and Gβγ scaffold signaling axis. In this cell type, B9d1 was the top positive Mc1r signature neighbor and Wdr26 the top negative neighbor, whereas other Mc1r profiles had very weak global neighbors. This interpretation remains exploratory because the Mc1r differential expression was weak and the mechanistic context for B9D1 and WDR26 comes from non-cerebellar systems.

Magi2 was not transcriptomically equivalent to its canonical postsynaptic partners in this dataset: its RNA signature showed only weak maximum matched-perturbation correlations with Pten, NMDA-receptor subunits including Grin2b and other available Grin genes, Dlg4, Nlgn1/2/3, and Cacng2 across the postsynaptic MAGI2-PTEN/NMDA receptor/neuroligin scaffold. This suggests that Pten or receptor-subunit knockdown was not a good RNA-signature proxy for Magi2 here, although Magi2 target engagement was weak and shared protein-localized synaptic phenotypes cannot be excluded.

Prkcg showed no robust transcriptomic convergence with its close conventional PKC paralog Prkca or with any other global signature neighbor. In the Ca2+/diacylglycerol-activated conventional PKC signaling context, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut cells, Prkcg signatures were very small, top positive and negative whole-transcriptome neighbors were weak, and no non-self perturbation produced a strong score-vector correlation. Interpretation is limited because Prkca itself had no FDR-significant knockdown, with near-zero Prkca/Prkcg correlations across matched classes, preventing a clean paralog phenocopy test.

Tacr1 showed a weak and largely near-orthogonal scRNA-seq loss-of-function signature that did not converge with the measured tachykinin paralog Tacr3 or with nearby GPCR signaling perturbations, including Plcb1, Prkca, Prkcg, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Gnal, Gnao1, Gnas, and Sstr5. Within matched cell classes, the maximum absolute Pearson correlation between Tacr1 and Tacr3 signatures was only 0.0786, suggesting that, in this Perturb-seq matrix, tachykinin-family receptors and proximal NK1R-pathway neighbors are not transcriptomically interchangeable; this inference is limited to scRNA-seq score vectors, and the Tacr1 anchor signature itself is weak.

Plxnc1 showed a distinct perturbation signature that did not phenocopy nearby semaphorin, plexin, or neuropilin perturbations in this dataset. Across available comparators—Plxna1, Plxna2, Plxna4, Plxnd1, Sema4d, Sema5a, Sema6a, Nrp1, and Nrp2—signature correlations with Plxnc1 were near zero, including in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class where strongly engaged Sema5a and Plxna2 perturbations still had minimal correlation to Plxnc1. This argues against treating class A/D plexins or neuropilins as PLXNC1-equivalent here, although the canonical ligand Sema7a was not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ogt showed a distinct perturbation signature from Gfpt1 across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. Gfpt1 perturbation secondarily lowered Ogt while strongly inducing an unfolded-protein/integrated-stress module including Ddit3, Asns, Herpud1, Hspa5, Sdf2l1, and Cyb5r1, but direct Ogt perturbation in the same major contexts did not reproduce that module. Because Gfpt1 itself was not significantly depleted, this supports pathway-level divergence rather than a clean GFPT1 loss-of-function equivalence test.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Map3k7 showed only a weak phenotype in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: although the Map3k7 transcript itself was nominally reduced, it did not reproduce the small FDR-significant Map2k1-responsive neuronal module seen in the same cell class. In contrast, Map2k1 loss was associated with decreased Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, and Unc13a, whereas Map3k7 had no shared effect on those genes. This suggests the limited Map3k7 signal was not simply a generic MAPK detectability issue, with the caveat that the Map2k1 signature itself comprised only four FDR-significant genes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gatad1 showed signature convergence with Phf12, but not with Kdm5b, Kdm5c, Sin3a, or Gatad2b, in the two informative cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. Phf12 was the top positive whole-signature neighbor of Gatad1 in both classes, and many Gatad1 FDR genes were also significant with the same sign after Phf12 perturbation, whereas the other chromatin comparators were near zero. This points to a PHF12/GATAD1-linked EMSY/KDM5A/SIN3-associated chromatin neighborhood, with the caveat that the comparison relies on restricted score correlations from DE summaries and Kdm5a itself was not assayed.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Hcrtr2 did not show a robust same-pathway or shared-signature neighborhood across cell types: its perturbation scores were not reproducible as a common transcriptional signature, and the strongest cross-perturbation neighbors were weak, often no stronger than safe-target controls. In 145 MH-LH TH Glut, the nominally strongest Hcrtr2 stratum had 15 nominal p<0.001 genes but no FDR-significant genes, with only weak Xiap and Adcy5 correlations. In 217 P MY Pineal Glut, the largest absolute neighbor was Fntb at r=-0.213, but this 25-cell stratum is especially noisy, so the signal is better treated as instability than a module assignment.

Il6ra showed no convergent basal Perturb-seq signature with the related gp130 signaling components Il6st, Osmr, or Stat3 across shared Glut/GABA neuronal classes. In this dataset, Il6ra, Il6st, and Osmr perturbations were all transcriptionally weak, and Il6ra score-vector correlations with Il6st, Osmr, and Stat3 were near zero, with no FDR-supported Il6ra response across 22 tested neuronal classes. The only near-hit was in 308 CB GABA, still below FDR<0.05, and most receptor-subunit target transcripts were not robustly depleted, limiting interpretation of these weak, restricted signatures.

Zbtb21 did not show a strong full-transcriptome convergence with other assayed Zbtb-family perturbations in these mouse brain cell types. Across 189 matched comparisons with Zbtb10, Zbtb11, Zbtb16, Zbtb18, Zbtb20, Zbtb24, Zbtb38, Zbtb42, and Zbtb7a, the median Pearson correlation was 0.006, with only 5 of 189 having |r|>0.1, indicating essentially uncorrelated whole-signature effects in the BTB-ZF transcriptional repression and chromatin regulation context. This comparison is caveated because these genes are family members, not proven ZBTB21 complex subunits, and the Zbtb21 signatures themselves were weak across all 21 measured cell-type contrasts.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Slc24a5 showed a sparse, cell-type-specific response in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, where Lpcat4 was the only conventionally significant downstream transcript and was increased. Beneath that hit, a small nominal up-signature of eight genes included Lpcat4, Mgll, and Stard10, which converge on glycerophospholipid biosynthesis, suggesting an exploratory lipid-metabolism context in this one responsive cell type. Because only Lpcat4 survives per-gene multiple-testing correction and pigmentation-gene or broader signature-neighbor comparisons were weak, this pathway signal should be viewed as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

Foxp2 did not yield a recurrent downstream module across cell classes. The smallest nominal Foxp2 rows were mostly cell-class-specific singletons rather than recurrent cross-cell-class markers: no transcript reached nominal p<0.001 in more than one class, and only Reep5 and Sike1 appeared at p<0.01 in three of 22 classes. Transcriptome-wide signature matching also found only very weak neighbors, with the strongest whole-signature match to Slc7a14 or Dnajc19 at |r|=0.152, so there was no FDR-supported pathway-level propagation in this analysis.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gtf2h5 showed only weak, nonconvergent perturbation effects, most clearly in 191 MB P MY GABA, the only cell class with any FDR<0.1 genes after perturbation. In that class, the strongest signature neighbors were essentially uncorrelated with Gtf2h5 (r=0.066 and r=-0.054), and assayed transcription-associated comparators including Cdk13, Med12, Med13, and Taf1 also showed little similarity, with no strong positive or negative correlation. This argues that the weak Gtf2h5 output does not conceal a strong shared transcriptional module, although true TFIIH core and CAK subunits were not assayed, limiting direct complex-member interpretation.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gad1 perturbation did not define a shared transcriptional module with its GABA pathway neighbors across 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. Knockdown of Gad2, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, or Abat showed little cross-correlation with the Gad1 signature, and single-node disruption of GABA vesicular transport, reuptake, or catabolism did not shift Gad1/Gad2 mRNA; conversely, Gad1 knockdown did not significantly alter Slc32a1 or Slc6a1. This uncoupling persisted even where on-target depletion was strong, although Abat and Slc6a1 had incomplete engagement in some cell types and pathway activity was inferred from mRNA rather than metabolite flux.

Kdm4c did not show a shared detectable KDM4-family neuronal signature in this experiment: the assayed paralog Kdm4b was likewise FDR-silent, and its matched score correlation with Kdm4c was essentially zero (r=-0.0028). No perturbation emerged as a strong positive or negative signature neighbor of Kdm4c, consistent with no FDR-detectable Kdm4c or Kdm4b mRNA program within the KDM4-family H3K9/H3K36 histone demethylation and chromatin-regulation context. This interpretation is tempered by weak target-transcript statistics for both genes and the fact that Kdm4a, a potentially redundant enzyme, was not assayed.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pbx3 in 308 CB GABA showed its closest signature neighbors among non-PBX perturbations: Wdr26, Dstyk, and Cckar were the strongest positive neighbors, while B9d1, Fbxo11, and Ranbp2 were the strongest negative neighbors. This within-cell geometry suggests an unexpected local module rather than obvious TALE/HOX or paralog organization, with a nominal signature-neighbor module that includes Nol6, Pink1, Rab2a, Psd2, and Kcng4. These patterns were computed only from 308 CB GABA score vectors, so the correlations are exploratory and do not imply direct regulation or physical interaction.

Il4ra targeting in 23 assayed neuronal cell groups showed no detectable canonical IL-4/IL-13 receptor–JAK/STAT transcriptional output: genome-wide testing found no downstream genes at FDR < 0.05, and Il2rg, Il13ra1, Il13ra2, Jak1/2/3, Stat3, Stat6, Tyk2, Socs1, and Socs5 remained unchanged. The target transcript itself also showed no detectable on-target RNA reduction. Because the readout was basal mRNA abundance rather than receptor protein or phospho-JAK/STAT6, and many pathway genes were observed but not perturbed, these data suggest the neuronal assay did not engage a canonical IL-4/IL-13 response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Matr3 showed restricted-signature similarity to RNA splicing and mRNA nuclear export perturbations—U2af2, Ascc3, Cdc40, Prpf6, Tpr, and Thoc1—rather than to disease-family RBP comparators, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In these strongest classes, U2af2 or Ascc3 were top neighbors, consistent with nuclear RNA-processing biology. However, this support is limited to the top 300 Matr3-ranked genes in each cell type, and full-transcriptome correlations were weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ank3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed its strongest opposing full-rank signatures with Gabrb2 and Atp2b1. Direct perturbation of Gabrb2 or Atp2b1 increased Vgf, Nr4a1, and Opn3, whereas Ank3 perturbation decreased these genes, consistent with a counter-signature involving an inhibitory receptor subunit and a plasma-membrane calcium pump; Fos also falls within this opposing context. This pattern suggests a testable calcium-extrusion and GABA-A receptor counter-response to the Ank3 thalamic program, although the mechanistic coupling to Ank3 remains indirect in this cell type.

Pitpnm3 perturbation did not produce a recurrent, multiple-testing-corrected mRNA program consistent with the known PITPNM/NIR PI-PA exchange and PIP2-homeostasis pathway. Across assayed cells, there were no FDR-supported changes in PITP-family genes, PIP2-cycle or PLC/DAG/PA components, calcium/PYK2-adjacent transcripts such as Ptk2b, or related candidates including Pitpna, Pitpnb, Pitpnc1, Pitpnm1, Pitpnm2, Plcb1, Dgkd, Dgke, Itpr1, Prkca, and Prkcg; the strongest adjacent signal was a nominal, single-cell-type Pip5k1c row in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA. This pattern fits a buffered, weakly engaged, or post-transcriptional effect rather than evidence against local lipid-transfer activity, especially because the assay measures mRNA rather than PI, PA, DAG, calcium, or PIP2 turnover.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Gphn showed a cell-type-dependent relationship with Gabrg2 rather than an invariant surrogate pattern. Gabrg2 was a positive Gphn neighbor in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA cells, but in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut it flipped negative, where Dlg4 and Gria3 instead were positive Gphn neighbors. In L2-3 IT cells, the Gphn-positive set included Grin2a and the negative set included Grin2b, Syngap1, and Camk2a. This signature-based contrast concerns inhibitory receptor clustering genes and does not measure inhibitory synapse physiology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Med13 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed Nipbl as its top positive non-self whole-signature neighbor, but only weakly, with a modest correlation across 17,259 genes (r=0.191); the strongest inverse neighbor was likewise weak, Setd5 (r=-0.104). The overlapping thalamic program included Med13-sensitive genes such as Pcp4, Grm1, Atp2a2, and Prkcd, supporting an exploratory mediator–cohesin enhancer–promoter architecture hypothesis. However, this is a rank-based association with low absolute correlation and does not show that MED13 and NIPBL co-occupy these genes in thalamic neurons.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Prkaa2 showed only a weak, exploratory same-cell transcriptomic neighborhood in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut: its top positive signature correlations were with Trpm7, Kcnj6, and Ppara, and top negative correlations were with Btbd9 and Camsap1, with a maximum absolute correlation of just 0.219. These neighbors were outside the annotated AMPK core, and neither they nor Prkaa2 had FDR<0.05 genes in this cell type. Together with the lack of convergent signal with Prkag2, this argues against a robust hidden AMPK-module interpretation here.

Cox8a showed little to no transcriptional phenocopy with neighboring complex IV perturbations: across 152 matched comparisons, Cox8a signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Cox11, Cox4i1, Cox5a, Cox6a1, Cox6b1, Cox7b, and Ndufa4, with median |r| = 0.021 and maximum |r| = 0.137. In nominally target-engaged cell types such as 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, even the nearest genome-wide signature neighbors did not approach |r| = 0.2, suggesting that complex IV membership did not translate into interchangeable single-cell RNA signatures, although low Cox8a target engagement and target-only related perturbations make these correlations sensitive to noise.

Aopep showed essentially no transcriptional resemblance to the renin-angiotensin receptor-adjacent perturbations Agtr1a, Agtr2, or Agtrap in this mouse brain dataset, with maximum absolute same-cell signature correlations of only 0.075, 0.067, and 0.060. This limited cross-perturbation comparison argues against treating Aopep as equivalent to those receptor-pathway programs here, despite indirect database and prior vascular/RAS rationale for examining that neighborhood. Because the Aopep signature itself was weak and the RAS link is indirect, this is best interpreted as a failure to find similarity rather than evidence against any biochemical substrate relationship.

Litaf did not phenocopy the active endolysosomal trafficking and acidification perturbations in this dataset: it produced no multiple-testing-corrected downstream transcriptional response, had no strong same-cell signature neighbors, and showed only weak correlations to selected comparators such as Atp6v0c, Rab7, Vps37a, Vps35, Tmem106b, Grn, and Lamp2 (max |r| ≤ 0.147). In contrast, Atp6v0c and Rab7 generated hundreds of FDR-significant genes. This separation from core neuronal lysosome acidification and Rab7-like programs may reflect specialization, redundancy, or simply weak Litaf target engagement, so causal interpretation is limited.

Pde4d showed a sparse mRNA signature that did not phenocopy Pde4b or other cAMP-pathway perturbations in this Perturb-seq dataset. Across 238 cell-type/target comparisons with Pde4b, Pde1c, Pde3a, Pde10a, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Gnas, Prkaca, Prkar1a, and Creb1, genome-wide correlations were essentially zero, with median |r|=0.019 and maximum |r|=0.124; for Pde4b specifically, r ranged from -0.033 to 0.059. Thus, despite shared cAMP hydrolysis and GPCR-cAMP-PKA pathway membership, these perturbations did not yield a large shared transcriptional program, although the weak Pde4d signature itself may depress correlations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gabra4 showed a weak, cell-type-specific signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where its score vector was most similar to several GABA(A) receptor subunit perturbations, with Gabrb2, Gabrd, and Gabra1 ranking among the nearest positive neighbors and fitting an alpha-4-containing GABA(A) receptor / GABA-gated chloride channel context. However, the Pearson correlations were small, unrelated perturbations such as Uba5 and Atp2b1 also ranked near Gabra4, and this convergence was not seen across the other 20 cell types; even in this thalamic class, strong Gabrb2, Gabrd, Gabra1, and Gabrg2 knockdowns produced sparse downstream FDR effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Syncrip showed a notably weaker perturbational response than several related RNA-binding proteins in the same neuronal populations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Syncrip had no FDR-significant genes, including cases with nominal target-transcript reduction, whereas Hnrnpu, Snrnp70, Celf2, Srrm2, Hnrnpc, and Fus produced tens to hundreds of FDR genes. This argues against a generic failure of RBP perturbations and suggests non-equivalent hnRNP outputs, though the comparators are network neighbors rather than exact paralogs and Hnrnpr was not targeted.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Alk showed only an exploratory signature-neighbor pattern, centered in 308 CB GABA rather than a clear ALK-pathway module. In this cerebellar GABA class, Alk was most similar to Wdr26 and also correlated with Dstyk, Cckar, Msx2, and Sp7, while opposing Fbxo11, Eef2, Dnajb4, Ranbp2, and B9d1. However, Alk itself showed no target engagement and no FDR-significant genes in 308 CB GABA, so the observation is weak and appears to reflect a cell-restricted transcriptional state comparison rather than canonical Alk partners.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Tenm3 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut classes showed a largely target-only Perturb-seq response and did not share a transcriptomic signature with the latrophilin-teneurin module or related wiring genes. In 151 TH, Adgrl1, Adgrl2, Adgrl3, Robo1, and Epha7 each showed significant self-knockdown, yet their score-vector correlations with Tenm3 were near zero; in 155 MB, Tenm3 was likewise uncorrelated with Adgrl genes and the Tenm4 paralog. This lack of correlation reflects single-gene perturbation score similarity and does not argue against physical protein interactions.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Grid2 showed only an exploratory, cerebellar-restricted convergence signal: in 308 CB GABA, its weak perturbation signature correlated positively with Gria4 and Neo1, suggesting a possible cerebellar postsynaptic receptor signature neighborhood. This was modest and hypothesis-generating rather than validated, because neither Grid2 nor the comparator perturbations produced FDR-significant differential expression in that cell class. The caveats are that 308 CB GABA is a broad class, the comparator target transcripts were not FDR-confirmed, and Neo1 is not a canonical Cbln1-GluD2 core component.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sgcd did not phenocopy related dystrophin-glycoprotein complex or dystroglycan-glycosylation perturbations in this neuronal dataset. Across 21 measured neuronal classes, including multiple cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic types and GABAergic classes, Sgcd score-vector correlations with Dag1, Sgce, Large1, Fktn, Dmd, and Snta1 were near zero, and even unrestricted nearest neighbors were weak overall (strongest positive r=0.206, strongest negative r=-0.176). Large1 provided the only notable local comparator, but interpretation is limited by weak Sgcd engagement; in the largest sampled class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the signature remained sub-threshold with no genes reaching FDR<0.05.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gad2 knockdown reduced the Gad2 transcript in five engaged inhibitory classes—046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 053 Sst Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with especially strong on-target decreases in Pvalb, hypothalamic, and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA cells—but did not produce compensatory mRNA changes in neighboring GABA-axis genes. Across these classes, Gad1, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, and Abat remained non-significant, indicating no simple transcriptional feedback within GABA synthesis, vesicular transport, reuptake, or degradation, although compensation at protein or metabolite levels was not tested.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gad2 perturbation showed overlapping but non-identical target-engagement patterns relative to Gad1 and Slc32a1 across inhibitory subclasses. In 053 Sst Gaba, Gad2 reached FDR-significant target-transcript depletion, whereas Gad1 and Slc32a1 were only nominal; in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Slc32a1 was significant while Gad2 was not FDR-significant; and in 308 CB GABA, Gad1 and Slc32a1 were significant where Gad2 was not. These contrasts concern on-target transcript detection rather than shared downstream biology, and may reflect guide efficiency and baseline expression; no clear Gad1, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, or Abat compensation was detected after Gad2 knockdown.

Btbd9 was uncoupled from dopamine/adenosine, iron-handling, and core circadian-clock perturbation signatures: its score vectors showed near-zero mean correlations with Adora2a, Drd2, Drd3, Ireb2, Fth1, Tfrc, Bmal1, Clock, Cry1, and Cry2. Although Btbd9 models and annotations implicate dopamine, iron, rest-phase sleep, circadian, locomotor, and synaptic biology, these data suggest any Btbd9 effects on those modules may be indirect, protein-level, chronic, or limited to cell states not effectively perturbed here. This correlation analysis used restricted score vectors and did not directly assay dopamine, iron, ubiquitination, or clock physiology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nalcn knockdown did not produce a clear RNA-level feedback response in NALCN channelosome components in the two most engaged cell classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these blocks, Unc79, Unc80, Nalf1, Nalf2, Calm1, Calm2, Calm3, and Src all failed to reach FDR-significant change, arguing against simple transcriptional compensation of the channelosome after Nalcn depletion. This inference is limited because these complex members were measured only as transcripts, and their own perturbation signatures were not available in the library.

Tubb3 showed a cell-type engagement pattern closely matching the β-tubulin paralogs Tubb2a, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, and Tubb5, but it did not produce a robust genome-wide signature neighbor. In the two engaged, well-powered cell types examined—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba—Tubb3 knockdown was significant yet yielded no non-target FDR genes, and the strongest non-self transcriptomic correlations were small. These data suggest co-assay in similar neuronal contexts, likely reflecting shared tubulin expression or guide-detection constraints rather than interchangeable downstream mRNA states.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chd2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed signature neighbors that were confined to its 34-gene high-confidence module rather than the full transcriptome: within this restricted set, Elp1 and Xpo1 were positively correlated with Chd2 and Nalcn was negatively correlated. Across all 17,259 measured genes, however, correlations were weak, ranging from -0.064 to 0.117, so these relationships are best viewed as exploratory module-level convergence rather than evidence that Elp1, Xpo1, or Nalcn globally mimic or rescue Chd2.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Cdk8 showed a corrected-null perturbation profile in this mouse neuron screen, unlike its Mediator kinase-module partners Med13 and Med13l, which produced sparse but corrected, cell-type-restricted signatures despite shared complex connectivity. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Med13 exposed a thalamic module absent from Cdk8; in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Med13l showed Arpp21 down-regulation while Cdk8 had no corrected gene; and in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, Med13 increased Fam168b. Med12 was also corrected-null, and Ccnc, Cdk19, and kinase-inhibitor perturbations were not included in this comparison.

Nrg2 showed a divergent, near-zero-correlation Perturb-seq signature relative to the neuregulin paralogs Nrg1 and Nrg3 across matched cell classes, indicating that these ligands were not interchangeable at the full-transcriptome level. This pattern fits with distinct outputs in NRG2-ErbB receptor signaling, even though related ligands, receptors, and ERK-pathway neighbors in the same resource showed clear on-target or downstream signals. The comparison is limited to RNA signatures rather than ligand binding or receptor phosphorylation, and Nrg1 was missing from two Nrg2-positive cell-class contrasts.

Atg16l1 showed an RNA-signature profile that was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of closely related autophagy genes, including Atg5, Map1lc3a, Sqstm1, Becn1, and Rb1cc1, as well as Lamp2, Mtor, Rptor, Rubcn, and Tbk1, in the same assay. This lack of alignment extended across macroautophagy and autophagosome assembly, including the ATG12-ATG5-ATG16L1 LC3-lipidation module, and also failed to match lysosomal, mTORC1, negative-autophagy-regulator, or mitophagy-neighbor perturbations. The divergence comes from a restricted signature comparison and may be technical, because Atg16l1 target-transcript engagement was weaker than for several comparator perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Chp1 loss produced a sterol/SREBP-associated transcriptional program that opposed Srebf2 perturbation: in the dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Chp1 upregulated Srebf2 and cholesterol-biosynthetic targets, whereas Srebf2 knockdown reduced Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, and Cyp51 and was the strongest negative restricted-signature neighbor of Chp1. Similar lipid-module induction appeared in 155 MB Glut and, despite weaker Chp1 transcript detection, in 191 MB P MY GABA. These comparisons rely on mRNA signatures and restricted-neighbor analysis rather than direct nuclear SREBP2 activity measurements.

Cnksr2 perturbation was largely uncoupled from a canonical RAS/RAF/MAPK transcriptional signature in this assay: across the 19 Cnksr2-evaluable neuronal subclasses, its whole-transcriptome signatures were nearly orthogonal to matched Braf, Raf1, Hras, Kras, Map2k1, Map2k2, and Mapk1 perturbations, with the largest absolute Cnksr2–Braf correlation only 0.0897. This refines the pathway label, suggesting Cnksr2 loss is not equivalent to knocking down MAPK-core genes here, although the weak Cnksr2 signature limits power to detect subtle similarities.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gfpt1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a signature that converged with ER/proteostasis perturbations rather than displaying a strong inverse neighbor: Atp2a2 and Hspa9 were the top positive genome-wide neighbors (both Pearson r≈0.493), with weaker positive similarity to Dhdds, Elp1, and Hspa5, while the most negative neighbor was minimal (r=-0.054). This state was marked by the Ddit3, Chac1, Hspa5, Herpud1, and Asns module, supporting a bona fide proteostasis-stress/UPR-ISR-like program, although the analysis is correlative, moderate in strength, and strongest in this one cell type.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Rab7 perturbation defined a lysosome-biogenesis-like state that was closer to Tsc1/Tsc2 than to core mTORC1 loss. In the responsive MB-associated cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Tsc1, Tsc2, and Vps41 were positive Rab7 restricted-signature neighbors, whereas Mtor and Rptor were among the most anti-correlated neighbors. This argues against treating all lysosomal mTORC1 perturbations as interchangeable, although the restricted-signature correlations do not identify whether TFEB, RagC, or another transcription factor drives the Rab7 program.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Rb1cc1 perturbation produced a recurrent, mostly downregulated ER chaperone and lysosomal proteostasis signature rather than broad transcriptional induction of autophagy genes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Calr, Hspa5, and Pdia6 decreased with significant target knockdown; in 155 MB Glut, Calr and Psap decreased, and this class showed the largest downstream signature despite only nominal Rb1cc1 transcript depletion. The compact ER signal included only nominal Xbp1 and Hyou1 changes, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells showed target engagement but only two significant non-target transcripts.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Manf perturbation most consistently derepressed an Hspa5-centered ER chaperone and unfolded-protein-response module rather than a broad neuronal identity shift. Across 23 measured comparisons, Hspa5 increased in all and reached significance in eight cell types, including 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, often alongside Sdf2l1, Dnajb9, Hyou1, Pdia6, Snd1, Sec11c, Rpn1, Copa, and Mia3. Effects were mostly up across cell types, with a buffered 308 CB GABA exception; however, only 30 Manf gene-by-cell-type rows were significant, and Manf itself was significantly reduced in just one cell type.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnq3 was not transcriptomically interchangeable with Kcnq2 or Kcnq5 in this dataset, despite their known Kv7/KCNQ M-current partnership. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Kcnq3 showed the best on-target engagement, with target mRNA passing FDR, yet downstream transcripts remained below FDR, consistent with a buffered or weak mRNA response. Across shared cell types, Kcnq3 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Kcnq2 and Kcnq5, and its top positive and negative signature neighbors were weak. Because these are signature-based comparisons and Kcnq3 knockdown itself was limited, the lack of correlation does not by itself establish functional divergence of the channels.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ascc3 showed positive signature similarity to spliceosome- and proteasome-centered perturbations in the most responsive neurons. In 155 MB Glut, U2af2, Prpf6, Ddx23, Cdc40, Psmc5, and Psmb4 were among the closest positive neighbors, and Prpf6 was again the top neighbor in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 191 MB P MY GABA. These correlations were top-ranked but modest in absolute value, and the neighboring perturbations were not ASCC complex members, so the result is suggestive rather than definitive.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Arhgef9 showed a restricted, target-dominated transcriptomic signature in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, but known inhibitory-synapse neighbors and receptor subunits—Cdc42, Nlgn2, Nlgn3, Gabra1, Gabrb2, Gabrb3, Gabrg2, and Glrb—although often effectively depleted in the same classes, had near-zero correlation with the Arhgef9 top-200 non-target signature. This suggests that participation in the ARHGEF9-collybistin/gephyrin inhibitory postsynaptic network was not sufficient to predict a shared steady-state RNA program here; notably, Gphn itself was not FDR-engaged in the 110/151/155 comparisons.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Igf2r knockdown in 052 Pvalb Gaba cells showed a sparse RNA response that was transcriptionally uncoupled from profiled endolysosomal trafficking and IGF-growth pathway perturbations. Despite IGF2R’s curated links to mannose-6-phosphate, clathrin/GGA, retromer, and IGF2-related biology, the Pvalb Igf2r signature did not phenocopy or correlate meaningfully with Sort1, Cltc, Ap1b1, Ap2m1, Lamp2, Lrp1, Vps35, Igf1r, Insr, Mtor, Tsc1, Tsc2, Mapk1, Pik3ca, or Pik3r1; a genome-wide same-cell-type scan also found no meaningful neighbors. This comparison is strongest as a lack of RNA-signature similarity in Pvalb, and several pathway-neighbor perturbations in that cell type also showed weak target-transcript engagement.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Macf1 in 155 MB Glut showed a buffered, largely self-contained transcriptomic response and did not phenocopy expected Wnt or cytoskeletal neighbors: whole-signature correlations with Apc, Ctnnb1, Gsk3b, Lrp6, Fzd3, Map1b, Actg1, Dctn1, and Dync1h1 were near zero, with no robust positive or negative neighbors detected. In the same cell class, Dctn1 and Dync1h1 instead triggered a strong sterol-biosynthesis module marked by Insig1, Msmo1, Fdps, Hmgcs1, and Hmgcr that was absent from Macf1. Several comparators, especially Dst, Apc, Gsk3b, Lrp6, and Fzd3, had weak self-knockdown, and these comparisons rely on mRNA signatures only.

Bbip1 did not show a detectable Hedgehog or ciliary-GPCR transcriptional output at the RNA level. Under Bbip1 perturbation, canonical pathway genes including Smo, Ptch1, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, and Gpr161 were at most isolated nominal hits, with Smo, Gli1, Gli2, and Gli3 all showing minimum nominal p-values greater than 0.63, and perturbation signatures for Ift88, Cep164, Cep290, Smo, Ptch1, and Gli2 were uncorrelated with Bbip1. This uncoupling may reflect that BBSome/LZTFL1-related effects are primarily ciliary trafficking or localization phenotypes rather than steady-state mRNA changes, and no direct ciliary receptor localization or Hedgehog signaling assay was performed.

Kif3b perturbation did not produce a detectable transcriptional program in the expected ciliary, Hedgehog, or NMDAR-transport pathways: Kif3a, Kifap3, Ift20, Ift88, Shh, Smo, Ptch1, Ptch2, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Grin2a, Grin2b, Apc, and Dlg4 all remained non-significant, with no related perturbation convergence noted for KIF3/Kinesin-2 intraflagellar transport. This absence of mRNA changes does not rule out effects on ciliary trafficking, cilium length, receptor localization, or other protein-level phenotypes.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Lmbr1 perturbation in adult mouse brain cells was uncoupled from canonical SHH/Hedgehog signaling: across neuronal and glial populations including Pvalb Gaba, CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, MB Glut, MB P MY GABA, and CB GABA, Shh, Ihh, Dhh, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Boc, Cdon, Gas1, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Sufu, Kif7, and Lrp2 showed no significant response, and Lmbr1 signatures were essentially orthogonal to Hedgehog-neighborhood perturbations such as Cdon, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, and Gli1/2/3. This separates adult neuronal Lmbr1 mRNA knockdown from the LMBR1/ZRS developmental regulatory architecture, with weak Lmbr1 engagement limiting inference.

Crhr1 perturbation showed no compensatory or immediate-early transcriptional response at steady-state RNA level. Across tests, canonical CRH receptor/Gs-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP-ERK output genes such as Fos, Jun, Egr1, Nr4a1, Crem, Dusp5, Rgs2, Npas4, Arc, and Sik1 were not detectably induced, and CRH-family transcripts Crh, Crhr2, Ucn, Ucn2, and Ucn3 were unchanged. This suggests basal Crhr1 editing was uncoupled from the expected ligand-activated pathway in this dataset, with the caveat that prior literature largely measures acute ligand stimulation and phosphorylation rather than steady-state transcript abundance after genetic perturbation.

Dyrk1a perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptional response in the immediate-early and glutamatergic postsynaptic program, including Arc, Camk2b, Dlg4, Egr1, Fos, Grin2a, Npas4, and Synj1, and likewise did not FDR-regulate the NFAT/RCAN1 and APP/tau neighborhood genes App, Psen1, Mapt, Gsk3b, Rcan1, Nfat5, and Nfatc3. Thus, canonical DYRK1A-linked synaptic and Down-syndrome/Alzheimer-related modules were buffered or not engaged at the RNA level in this screen, with the caveat that prior literature often assays protein phosphorylation, synaptic phenotypes, or long-term complete dosage changes rather than sparse single-nucleus transcriptional endpoints.

Ednra did not behave interchangeably with the paralogous endothelin receptor Ednrb in this neuronal Perturb-seq contrast: Ednrb produced no FDR-significant effects, and Ednra–Ednrb whole-signature correlations across 19 shared cell types were near zero. This weak correspondence was notable despite both receptors being annotated as endothelin GPCRs linked to phosphatidylinositol-calcium signaling, and in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut the expected Ednra/Ednrb–Plcb1 Gαq/phospholipase-C beta pathway signal was not recovered in endpoint transcriptomes. Interpretation is limited because neither receptor showed detectable transcript knockdown, and 053 Sst Gaba was unavailable for Ednrb.

Ghsr showed no concordance with perturbations of related ghrelin, Gq/cAMP, or appetite GPCR genes in the screen: full-transcriptome score correlations with 16 comparators, including Adcy1/3/5, Plcb1, Agrp, Drd2, Ghr, Gipr, Glp1r, Htr2c, Lepr, Mc3r, Mc4r, Npy1r, Npy5r, and Sstr5, were near zero across 330 matched cell-type pairs. Thus, despite network links to G alpha-q and GPCR signaling neighbors, related perturbations did not reveal a hidden Ghsr-like signature, although rapid electrophysiological or second-messenger convergence could have been missed by this weak steady-state transcriptomic signal.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Eef2 showed an idiosyncratic transcriptomic program in the main responsive cell types—007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut—with weak whole-transcriptome score correlations to assayed translation elongation or protein-synthesis regulators including Eef1a2, Eif5a, Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1, and Tsc2, and no close positive or negative genome-wide signature neighbor. The contrast was evident alongside cell-type-specific features such as Vgf/Bdnf/Inhba/Nptx2 and Cx3cl1 induction in 007, and the analysis notes that correlations were based on Wilcoxon score vectors, so weak or only partially engaged signatures could affect similarity estimates.

Abhd2 did not phenocopy Abhd12 at the neuronal transcriptome level: across 22 shared cell types, Abhd2–Abhd12 whole-signature correlations were essentially zero and never exceeded small absolute values, despite stronger Abhd12 target knockdown and FDR-significant Abhd12 effects in many cell types. Related lipid-hydrolase, cannabinoid, and progesterone-axis perturbations, including Pgrmc1, also failed to share the Abhd2 signature. These results support divergent ABHD lipid-hydrolase biology, with the caveat that the comparison was based on mRNA signature correlations and did not measure ABHD2 or ABHD12 lipid products.

Abhd2 perturbation in neurons produced a transcriptomic signature that was uncorrelated with perturbations of the progesterone- and cannabinoid-axis receptors Pgr, Pgrmc1, and Cnr1 across the matched Abhd2 cell types. This suggests that, in this mouse-brain CRISPRi dataset, the Abhd2 readout is not a simple transcriptional proxy for the canonical ABHD2 progesterone–2-AG–CatSper mechanism described in sperm. Related lipid-hydrolase, cannabinoid, and progesterone-axis perturbations also failed to share the Abhd2 signature, although CatSper subunits were not informative comparators and Cnr1/Pgr target engagement was weak.

Pank2 did not show a stable cross-perturbation signature neighborhood: in a restricted analysis using the top 200 Pank2 genes per cell type, the top positive and negative neighbors changed almost completely by cell type, and Pank2 correlated poorly with stronger Atp13a2, Fth1, and Cisd2 perturbations in the same panel. This means nearest-neighbor inference did not rescue a reproducible Pank2 program, although the interpretation is limited by weak Pank2 target engagement; other perturbations in the panel showed strong on-target depletion, arguing against a general workflow failure.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Prokr2 showed only weak transcriptomic convergence in this dataset, especially in 308 CB GABA cells where even the strongest whole-signature neighbors reached only about |r|=0.28. Among related neuroendocrine, Kallmann, and GPCR perturbations, the largest correlation was with Tacr1 at r=0.174, with similarly weak relationships to Sox10, Tubb3, Nsmf, Fgf12, Gnao1, Chd7, Fezf1, B9d1, and Wdr26. These results suggest that genes within the shared Kallmann syndrome and GnRH developmental axis are not interchangeable at this broad-cell transcriptomic endpoint, although this interpretation is limited because Prokr2 score vectors were weak and the cognate ligands Prok1/Prok2 and paralog Prokr1 were not perturbed.

Pou4f3 showed no strong signature neighbor in unbiased positive or negative scans across all 23 profiled brain cell classes. The strongest cell-type-restricted similarity was weak (r = 0.167), and the genome-wide maximum across shared features was only r = 0.033, so top positive and negative neighbors looked like background rather than an alternative POU4F3-like state. Perturbations of available STRING-adjacent genes and other POU-domain factors, including Ranbp2, Dstyk, Atoh1, Gfi1, Isl1, and Pax2, did not phenocopy the Pou4f3 signature, though weak FDR-negative signatures could mask relationships that might emerge with stronger on-target perturbation.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tnfrsf4 did not converge with a TNFR/NF-kappaB neighborhood in the neuronal panel: across 22 assayed neuronal subclasses, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic types, no related perturbation among Cd40, Cd80, Chuk, Edar, Fas, Icos, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Ngfr, Rel, Relb, Tbk1, Tnfrsf11a, Tnfrsf13c, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Tnfrsf9, and Traf3 phenocopied the Tnfrsf4 signature, and the pairwise signature correlations were essentially flat. This comparison was restricted to weak transcriptomic signatures, with no FDR-significant genes for Tnfrsf4 or most neighbors, and several canonical ligand or adaptor genes were not targeted.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarce1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed its strongest genome-wide signature convergence with Smarcb1 and Smarcc2, the top two positive neighbors among 2045 perturbations. These perturbations recapitulated down-regulation of Ptpn3, Reep2, Prkcd, Begain, and Abhd12b, often with larger effect sizes, while no strong anti-correlated neighbor was detected. Although the absolute correlations were modest and other related subunits showed weaker similarity, this pattern in the only Smarce1-responsive cell class is consistent with canonical BAF-core convergence rather than an isolated guide artifact.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarcb1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a transcriptomic signature that converged most strongly with other SWI/SNF BAF-complex perturbations, especially Smarcc2 and Smarce1, with Arid2, Arid1a, and Arid1b also among the closest positive neighbors. This convergence was strongest when correlations were computed on the 500 genes with the largest absolute Smarcb1 responses; whole-transcriptome correlations were lower but preserved the same BAF ordering. Not every SWI/SNF target phenocopied Smarcb1, as Smarca2, Smarca4, Smarcc1, and Smarcd1 were weak or more divergent, and inverse signatures were weak.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: F2 showed no strong convergence or anticorrelation with any screened perturbation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA cells. The closest available thrombin cofactor target, Thbd, had near-zero correlation with the F2 whole-transcriptome signature, and across all non-F2 perturbations the largest absolute Pearson correlation was only 0.173; nominal neighbors such as Ppib and Fmn1 were likewise near zero. Because F2 itself does not appear engaged in this dataset, this is best read as a quality-control negative result rather than evidence against the biochemical F2-THBD relationship.

Cstf2 showed no meaningful signature convergence or antagonism in the genome-wide neighbor scan: correlations with other perturbations were very small, with the strongest positive and negative values only about r=0.10 and -0.10, and one top positive match was the Safe_target_27 control-like perturbation. Thus the weak Cstf2 phenotype should not be turned into a pathway-neighbor claim. This screen also lacked direct perturbation comparators for CstF/CPSF and related 3′-end processing partners, including Cstf1, Cstf3, Cstf2t, SYMPK, and FIP1L1, limiting genetic-complex interpretation.

Itga7 perturbation produced signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with Itgb1, Itga6, Dag1, Dmd, Sgcd, Sgce, Snta1, and other assayed integrin paralogs across 22 non-dopaminergic neuronal classes, indicating no FDR-significant transcriptional feedback within integrin-laminin and ECM-proteoglycan interactions in this neuronal dataset. Even in 308 CB GABA, the closest positive and negative Itga7 signature neighbors were weak at about |r|≈0.25 and did not show an obvious integrin-laminin identity. This contrast with related basement-membrane linkages described in muscle is indirect and is tempered by poor Itga7 target-transcript engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nop56 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a partial convergence pattern: across its 24-gene downstream signature, perturbations of Srsf1 and Rbm28 were positively correlated with Nop56, whereas Las1l and Son were not. This suggests the 151 Nop56 program does not simply track every available rRNA-processing perturbation and may bridge nucleolar stress with splice-factor biology. Important caveats are that Rbm28 and Las1l had weak target-transcript engagement and no FDR genes in 151, and the canonical box C/D partners Fbl, Nop58, and Snu13 were not tested.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Mapkbp1 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed a transcriptional signature that did not converge with perturbations of JNK/MAPK scaffold signaling genes (Mapk8, Mapk9, Mapk8ip1, Map3k7, Map2k6), Nod2, or ciliary disease-family genes (Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Bbs5, Bbs9). A genome-scale neighbor scan likewise found no strong Mapkbp1 co-signature. Because these comparisons were based on scRNA-seq differential-expression score vectors and the comparator perturbations also had weak L4/5 FDR responses, the result excludes transcriptomic phenocopy in this neuronal context but not biochemical pathway coupling.

Bckdk perturbation did not transcriptionally mobilize the canonical branched-chain amino-acid catabolism module: across the tested transcripts, including Bckdha, Bckdhb, Dbt, Dld, Bcat1, Bcat2, Ivd, Mccc1, Mccc2, Pcca, Pccb, Ppm1k, and Acly, only nominal signals were seen and none were FDR-supported, with no coordinated mRNA response detected. This negative, exploratory result suggests that expected effects of BCKDK may be better reflected in BCKDH and ACLY phosphorylation or metabolic flux, which were not assayed here rather than in single-cell mRNA feedback.

Tbc1d24 showed a notably weak transcriptomic response: across 22 target rows, its own mRNA was not depleted at FDR<0.05, and signature-neighbor analysis found no meaningful positive or inverse correlation with other perturbation signatures. This contrasted with several neuronal vesicle-release comparators—Snap25, Stxbp1, Sv2a, Syn1, Dnm1, and Cplx1—which repeatedly showed FDR-supported depletion of their own transcripts. Thus, the Tbc1d24 null appears target-specific rather than a general failure to detect synaptic biology, although the comparison is based on transcript-level engagement and broad signature correlations rather than matched protein depletion.

Bbs5 did not phenocopy the assayed same-complex perturbations: across matched cell types, its transcriptomic score signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Bbs9 and Ttc8, arguing that this dataset does not reveal a shared BBSome transcriptional module. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Bbs5 showed the strongest nominal self-decrease and the largest perturbed-cell count, yet no corrected downstream genes, while Ttc8 showed strong self-depletion but still little similarity to Bbs5. This contrast is exploratory because Bbs5 engagement was weak, Bbs9 appeared buffered, and score-vector correlations may miss shared protein-trafficking phenotypes.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mttp showed no clear transcriptional convergence with available lipid-transfer or secretory-pathway perturbations across 22 assayed brain cell classes, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic types. Using top-200 restricted signatures, Mttp had only weak cosine similarity to Mboat7, Sar1b, Sec23a, Sec31a, Srebf1/2, Ppara/Ppard/Pparg, Mtor, and LRP-family perturbations. Because Apob and the PDI complex member P4hb were not perturbed, the weak brain RNA signature should not be taken as a complete MTTP/PDI/APOB lipoprotein-assembly response, and lack of convergence does not exclude protein-level lipid transport.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Adk showed a nonconvergent signature across six cell types with nominal target lowering, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut. Same-cell-type score correlations with other perturbations were near zero, and available purine/adenosine-adjacent comparators such as Nt5c2, Adora2a, Pde10a, Pde4b, and Pde4d did not converge with Adk. This argues against Adk being a hidden Nt5c2-, Adora2a-, or PDE-like state, but interpretation is limited because several canonical ADK partners, including Ada, Nt5e, Pnp, Ak1/Ak2, Ampd1-3, Adsl, and Aprt, were not perturbed.
