Phkb did not phenocopy assayed phosphorylase-kinase partners: its transcriptomic signatures were nearly orthogonal to Phka1 and to Calm1, Calm2, and Calm3, with correlations near zero in matched cell types. Although calmodulin perturbations were detectably engaged in many of the same cell types, their signatures did not resemble Phkb, and Phka1 was similarly silent. These results suggest that, in this assay, membership in the phosphorylase-kinase complex did not translate into a shared neuronal mRNA signature, with the caveat that both Phkb and Phka1 showed weak on-target effects and calmodulin has many PHK-independent Ca2+-signaling functions.

Twist2 showed no target-transcript depletion and no corrected downstream response across all 23 measured cell types, with no cytokine/NF-kappaB induction detected. The related paralog Twist1 behaved similarly, remaining FDR-null in all 23 cell types, and Twist1/Twist2 signed-score correlations were essentially zero in each cell type (rho -0.024 to 0.071). In this neuronal screen, these results argue against a detectable shared Twist-family bHLH/E-box transcriptional signature, although the weak, uncorrelated signatures are tempered by poor target engagement for both perturbations.

Vldlr showed a restricted transcriptional signature that did not converge with canonical Reelin-pathway perturbations: correlations of the top 200 Vldlr-scored genes with Lrp8, Dab1, Reln, and Fyn were centered near zero, and a broader neighbor scan also found no robust Vldlr-like perturbation, including among endocytic or neurodegeneration-adjacent genes such as Lrp1, Sorl1, Sort1, and App. This suggests that shared receptor-proximal pathway membership did not predict similar acute RNA phenotypes here, although the analysis was signature-restricted and on-target depletion for Dab1 and Lrp8 was weak.

Mpl showed weak, nonconvergent transcriptional signatures in this dataset: across same-cell-type perturbations, whole-signature correlations with Mpl were tiny, and restricting comparisons to cytokine receptor and STAT-family perturbations such as Csf3r, Epor, Ghr, Il6ra, Il6st, Lepr, Osmr, Prlr, Stat1, Stat3, and Stat5b kept correlations near zero. Thus, despite the canonical assignment of MPL to THPO/JAK-STAT signaling, no obvious cytokine/JAK-STAT-like or signature-neighbor module aligned with Mpl here. This interpretation is exploratory because Thpo and Jak2 perturbations were not available and the Mpl signatures themselves were weak.

Crlf1 was not transcriptomically interchangeable with the available cytokine-receptor or Stat3 perturbations: its signature was effectively uncorrelated with Il6st, Il6ra, Osmr, Csf3r, and Stat3, and even the best non-self whole-transcriptome neighbors were weak, with top positive and negative neighbors Tbr1 and Braf and |r|<0.137. This leaves the CRLF1-CLCF1/CNTFR/IL6ST/LIFR-JAK/STAT signaling context only partially tested, because the Crlf1 signature itself was weak and the more direct contrasts Clcf1, Cntfr, and Lifr were not perturbed.

Adgrb3 showed a nonconvergent transcriptomic profile in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset: within-cell correlations between Adgrb3 Wilcoxon-score vectors and related adhesion-GPCR comparators, including its paralog Adgrb1, Adgrl1/2/3, Adgra1, Adgrg1/2/6, Adgrv1, as well as Baiap2, Dock3, Dock7, and Rac1, were all near zero, with maximum absolute r = 0.079. It also lacked strong whole-signature neighbors, with only weak global correlations to Kat6a (r = 0.175) and Sec31a (r = -0.143). These comparisons are exploratory because sparse target engagement can obscure true protein-level pathway relationships in mRNA signatures.

Pde1c did not phenocopy its Ca2+/calmodulin and cAMP-pathway neighborhood in this assay: unlike Calm1, Calm3, Prkaca, Ppp3ca, and Ppp3r1, which showed clear target engagement and multiple significant downstream responses, Pde1c and most other assayed PDE genes were largely silent, with only isolated hits for Pde10a or Pde4b. This pattern was seen across cell types; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Pde1c showed only a nominal trend despite strong comparator responses, and weak positive correlation with Pde10a appeared in 308 CB GABA and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. The contrast does not imply biochemical disconnection, since calmodulin, PKA, and calcineurin perturbations are broader and more pleiotropic.

Pou3f4 was uncoupled from the otic mesenchyme Tbx1/Epha4 developmental program in the mouse brain restricted-signature comparison: across 22 brain cell classes, Tbx1 and Epha4 did not show correlated Perturb-seq signatures with Pou3f4, and even the top positive and negative Pou3f4 signature neighbors were only weakly correlated. This suggests the disease-relevant Pou3f4 network may be context-restricted, with brain-class perturbation not recovering the periotic mesenchyme program. Because the supporting Tbx1 and Epha4 mechanisms were established in otic tissue rather than these brain classes, this is best viewed as an indirect, exploratory negative result.

Chrna5 showed a transcriptomic signature that was largely decoupled from other cholinergic perturbations: across matched comparisons, its strongest transcriptome-wide correlation with nicotinic subunits or neighbors was only |r| = 0.1097. In matched cell classes, Chrna5 was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of Chrna3, Chrna4, Chrnb2, Chrnb4, Chrna7, Ache, Chrm2, Chrm3, and Ntrk2, even though α5 is a co-assembled nicotinic receptor accessory subunit. This null pattern reflects basal RNA signatures rather than electrophysiology or nicotine-evoked channel function.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Prnp loss showed near-zero score-vector correlations with perturbations of assayed PrP interactors and nearby surface-signaling genes, including App, Ncam1, Fyn, Lrp1, Hspa5, Adgrg6, Cacna1c, Cacna1d, Gsk3b, Psen1, Snca, Grm5, Csnk2b, and Adam10, across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In the strongest Prnp-engaged classes, Prnp knockdown often had no FDR-significant non-target genes, so curated PRNP pathway proximity did not imply a shared acute RNA signature in these neuronal classes.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Pcsk5 showed no coherent transcriptional module across the tested contexts and did not phenocopy Pcsk2 or downstream TGF/BMP receptor–SMAD perturbations. In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, the only FDR-significant Pcsk5 context, Ssb decreased but Pcsk5 itself remained FDR=1.0, annotated pathway genes were silent, and score-vector correlations with Pcsk2, Acvr1/2a/2b, Bmpr1a/1b/2, Tgfbr1/2/3, and Smad2/3/4/9 were near zero. In 217 P MY Pineal Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, only weak, idiosyncratic signals such as Ccdc90b appeared, with best neighbors all |r|<0.10; these exploratory transcript-level correlations do not exclude protein-level convergence.

Prkdc did not show a shared basal transcriptomic signature with the assayed Atr or Trp53 DNA-damage perturbations in the overlapping neuronal classes: Prkdc-versus-Atr and Prkdc-versus-Trp53 correlations stayed near zero, and the p53/DNA-damage transcriptional response genes, including Cdkn1a, Mdm2, Bbc3, Bax, Ddb2, Gadd45a, Rrm2b, and Phlda3, were not coherently induced. Because all three signatures were weak and the comparators lacked significant basal effects, this supports a negative result in unstressed cells rather than strong mechanistic divergence or interchangeability among these DDR perturbations.

Runx3 showed a weak, largely uncorrelated brain transcriptomic signature that did not resemble Runx2, TGF-beta/BMP receptor-SMAD perturbations, WNT-associated Ctnnb1, or available STRING neighbors such as Tbx21 and Zfhx3, with whole-transcriptome correlations all near zero (|r|≤0.097). In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Runx3 was FDR-null even where Smad2 or Tgfbr2 produced isolated significant effects, and Runx3 did not detectably engage Bcl2l11 or Cdkn1a. This argues against reading the observed profile as a weaker canonical RUNX3-SMAD/WNT response, though interpretation is limited by the weak Runx3 signal and the absence of Cbfb and Runx1 perturbations.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rusc2 perturbation in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a buffered, weak transcriptional response: Rusc2 itself was down most clearly in 155 MB Glut, but AP-4/RUSC2/ATG9A vesicle-trafficking genes such as Atg9a, Serinc1, Serinc3, Ap4s1, Rusc1, and Wdr47 did not reach FDR significance. Consistent with this, the Rusc2 signature had near-zero aggregate correlation with engaged kinesin-linked perturbations including Kif5a, Kif5c, Klc1, Klc2, Mapk8ip1, Trak1, and Dctn1. Ap4s1 was itself only weakly engaged, and these results suggest that acute mRNA covariation did not capture the known transport adaptor relationship.

Cacng8 did not show transcriptional convergence with AMPA receptor trafficking and regulation genes: its ranked scRNA differential-expression signature was essentially uncorrelated with TARP paralogs Cacng2 and Cacng3, AMPAR pore subunits Gria1 and Gria2, and nearby postsynaptic genes such as Dlg4 and Frrs1l, and even its strongest positive or negative neighbor across all perturbations was weak. In 191 MB P MY GABA cells, the nominal Cacng8 self-transcript signal and top neighbor were still weak and uncorrected, arguing against a robust Cacng8 mRNA module, while leaving open that post-translational AMPAR-complex convergence would be missed by scRNA DE-based correlations.

Dll1 showed no coherent convergence with Notch receptor perturbations: its full-signature correlations with Notch1, Notch2, Notch3, and Notch4 were only about r = 0.011–0.014, and a scan across all assayed perturbations found no strong positive or inverse signature neighbor. Thus, despite DLL1 being placed upstream of Notch receptor activation and transcriptional output, the single-cell RNA profiles did not support a shared autonomous state transition. A key caveat is that the receptor perturbations themselves had weak or absent self-transcript engagement, so the lack of correlation cannot be attributed uniquely to pathway divergence.

Nr1h5 showed a weak, FDR-negative transcriptional signature, and related perturbations did not uncover a hidden Nr1h5-like program: whole-panel restricted transcriptome-wide score correlations with Nr1h2, Nr1h3, Nr1h4, Rxra, Rxrb, Rxrg, Ncoa1, Abca1, and Srebf1 were all near zero, with the top genome-wide neighbor only r=0.0257. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA, there was likewise no interpretable related-target convergence beyond nominal Rbm26 and Phax outliers, supporting the absence of a detectable NR1H5/RXR sterol-responsive module in these data, while noting that weak signatures and differing perturbation roles limit the comparison.

Snx10, across 22 Snx10-assayed neuronal classes, showed weak target-transcript reduction, no FDR-significant differential expression, and did not phenocopy stronger endolysosomal or V-ATPase neighbor perturbations. In matched cell types, Atp6v0c produced a much stronger signature, and Rab7, Ctsb, Vps35, Atp6v0a1, and Lamp2 also generated stronger signatures whose mean all-gene correlations with Snx10 were near zero. Thus, within this neuronal dataset, Snx10 appears buffered and uncoupled from the SNX10/V-ATPase endosomal trafficking pathway, although the comparison is to pathway neighbors rather than direct complex members and Snx10 target engagement was weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Eif4a2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a sparse, largely self-only RNA signature: only 2 FDR-significant rows were detected, with the target transcript and Cadm4 passing FDR, whereas the cap-dependent translation initiation partner Eif4e produced a broad signature with 160 significant rows and Eif4g1 mainly affected its own target. Score-vector correlations between Eif4a2 and Eif4e, Eif4g1, Eif4h, or Ddx3x were weak, suggesting EIF4F-neighbor perturbations were not interchangeable in this neuronal context, although this comparison reflects RNA abundance signatures only and knockdown strength and guide performance differed across perturbations.

Pde3a showed a weak, near-zero signature that did not recapitulate the measured cAMP/cGMP phosphodiesterase and G alpha(s)-GPCR signaling perturbations: its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Pde10a, Pde4b, Pde4d, Pde1c, Prkaca, Gnas, Gnal, Adcy3, and Prkar1a. Selected immediate-early or cAMP-response genes and the Pde3b paralog were also not recurrent FDR-significant consequences of Pde3a perturbation, and some related phosphodiesterase perturbations produced stronger corrected signals. Because target engagement for Pde3a was weak, this lack of alignment should not be taken as proof that active PDE3A is disconnected from PKA biochemistry.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Adar in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells showed significant depletion of its target transcript, but its whole-transcriptome differential-expression signature did not converge with the paralog Adarb1: although Adarb1 was also significantly depleted in the same cell class, the two score vectors were essentially uncorrelated (r=-0.0076). This supports divergence within A-to-I RNA editing by ADAR-family enzymes rather than a single generic family effect. In this cell type, Adar also lacked an FDR-level off-target program or interferon response, while the Adarb1 signature was heavily Flnb-centered, so guide-specific or off-target contributions cannot be excluded.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Dld showed RNA score-vector signatures that were nearly orthogonal to Dlat, Dlst, Pdha1, Pdhb, Pdhx, Ogdh, and Bckdhb in the three best Dld-engaged cell types—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba—indicating no coherent PDH/OGDH/BCKDH or broader TCA partner-transcript response. This contrast was signature-based and arose despite stronger self-knockdown for several neighboring mitochondrial perturbations elsewhere in the screen; the Dld signal itself was weak, with no FDR-significant downstream genes, so these data refine rather than refute DLD’s shared biochemical E3 role.

Cog5 showed only a sparse, weak signature in this Perturb-seq dataset, and the only same-complex comparator, Cog4, did not display detectable convergence with it despite the direct COG4–COG5 assembly relationship. Across 19 shared cell types, Cog4 and Cog5 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, and Cog4 itself had low cell counts with no strong on-target or downstream signal. Thus, the weak Cog5 pattern, seen in contexts including 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, cannot be generalized to the full COG complex here, especially since COG1, COG2, COG3, COG6, COG7, and COG8 were not assayed.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Zic3 showed only a weak, near-threshold signature in 308 CB GABA cells, where its nominal cerebellar membrane/neuronal module was mostly up and aligned more with Wdr26 and Cckar than with other Zic-family structure, while opposing Ranbp2. Across the 30 nominal Zic3 CB genes, Wdr26 matched 28 of 30 directions and Ranbp2 inverted most, including markers within the small module such as Pkd2, Galnt16, Tspyl1, Vps50, Vsnl1, Agrn, and Psd2. This pattern is hypothesis-generating and may reflect a broader cerebellar perturbation state rather than a direct Zic3-specific mechanism.

Srr showed a transcriptional signature that was nearly orthogonal to NMDAR-subunit and adjacent amino-acid perturbations, rather than being interchangeable with them. Across matched cell classes, correlations between Srr and Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Grin2d, Grin3a, Gls, Glud1, Got1, Got2, Slc1a1, Slc1a2, and Slc32a1 were very small overall, despite several comparator perturbations showing strong on-target engagement. This suggests Srr RNA effects were uncoupled from NMDAR coagonist signaling signatures in this dataset, although the comparison is limited to measured perturbations and cell classes, and weak Srr target engagement may have compressed the Srr signature.

Zfp804a did not transcriptionally converge with psychiatric or synaptic neighbors in this Perturb-seq screen. Across perturbations, its strongest same-cell-type signature neighbor reached only r = 0.139, and dataset-present ZNF804A-associated targets including Nrxn1, Dtnbp1, Comt, Cacna1c, Nlgn2, Nlgn3, Atxn1, Ctnna2, and Myt1l all showed |r| ≤ 0.0886. In L5-6 IT glutamatergic cells, weak positive neighbors included Sema5a and Tbr1, with Nlgn2 nominally up but not FDR-significant. These comparisons reflect transcriptome-wide perturbation scores rather than protein interactions, and some reported partners were not perturbed here.

Ikzf3 showed no consistent convergence with an IKZF-family or CRBN-centered program in this Perturb-seq dataset. Across all 21 measured neuronal subclasses, Ikzf3 had no target-transcript engagement and no FDR-supported downstream program, so comparisons relied on a top-50 nominal Ikzf3 signature. Within that restricted analysis, Crbn cosine similarity to Ikzf3 was small and sign-mixed, and direct paralog tests were unavailable because Ikzf1, Ikzf2, Ikzf4, and Ikzf5 were not perturbed. Thus, neuronal Ikzf3 perturbation did not robustly phenocopy CRBN-mediated IKZF3 biology or recover stable neighbors such as Pax5, Ebf1, or Spi1.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Atrn showed its strongest whole-signature neighbors only in 308 CB GABA cells, where positive correlations were with Ranbp2, Fbxo11, and Dnajb4, and negative correlations were with Wdr26, Cckar, and Msx2, rather than with known ATRN partners. This pattern coincided with Cnnm2 up-regulation in the same cell type, but several neighbor perturbations had weak target engagement and some target transcripts were not FDR-engaged. Because the analysis used restricted transcriptome signatures in a low-cell-count cell type, these cerebellar relationships should be treated as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: B9d1 produced a stronger, non-interchangeable transcriptomic response in 308 CB GABA than other available ciliary or Joubert-family perturbations. In this cell class, Ahi1, Cep290, Ift43, Ttc8, Arl3, Bbs9, Ift88, Rpgrip1l, and Bbip1 did not yield FDR-significant genes, although Ahi1 and Cep290 showed weak partial positive score correlations with B9d1. Thus the observed state appears B9d1-skewed rather than a generic cilia-loss signature, with the caveat that most direct B9D1-B9D2-MKS1 complex members were not in the library and guide efficiencies may differ.

Csrnp3 showed no strong positive or negative convergence in this screen: across all 22 assayed cell classes, no perturbation correlated strongly with the Csrnp3 signature in matched cell types, with the most extreme same-cell Pearson correlations only 0.125 to Bsn and -0.107 to Pex1. Its scalar signature counts were on the scale of internal negative-control targets such as Safe_target_14 and Safe_target_92, and across the panel Csrnp3 also lacked mRNA knockdown, FDR-significant downstream genes, and paralog transcript compensation. These correlations came from Wilcoxon score vectors in the same dataset and were not replicated externally.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Acox1 in 308 CB GABA neurons showed an exploratory, weak signature that did not phenocopy peroxisome-import perturbation: Acbd5 was nominally down after Acox1 perturbation, and the Acox1 whole-transcriptome score vector was anti-correlated with Pex14, while Cpt1c and Ppargc1a were positively correlated. This suggests that, in this neuronal state, partial catalytic Acox1 loss may be separable from PEX14-dependent matrix import or ACBD5 tether biology, although no gene passed FDR<0.05 and the correlation metric is transcriptomic rather than a direct metabolic assay.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Kifbp showed a buffered, weakly correlated transcriptional output rather than phenocopying related perturbations. Across matched comparisons in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Kifbp-versus-Kif-family correlations stayed very small, and similarity to Dctn1, Stmn2, or RET-neighborhood genes such as Ret, Phox2b, Zeb2, and Elp1 also remained weak. Even in the strongest Kifbp classes, non-self neighbors were weak, with target-only or near-target-only FDR responses. These comparisons used bulk within-cell-type score-vector correlations, and limited guide counts or transcriptomic readout alone could miss local transport phenotypes.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnb1 showed a specific response in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut that Kcnb2 did not phenocopy: the only FDR-significant Kcnb1 program in the dataset was a five-gene upregulation including Bdnf, Vgf, Scg2, and Nptx2, with nominal Kcns2/Kcnma1 increases consistent with Kv2 delayed-rectifier potassium-channel remodeling. By contrast, Kcnb2 had zero FDR hits in this class and only weak similarity to the Kcnb1 top-100 signature, although this contrast is tempered by the lack of significant on-target Kcnb2 transcript depletion, which may underestimate true Kcnb2 biology.

Tbc1d32 showed no coordinated response with assayed ciliary, Hedgehog, or TBC-family neighbors in this restricted signature-neighbor analysis: correlations were near zero, with the strongest mean score-vector correlation only r=0.029 for Rpgrip1l, and nearby perturbations such as Ahi1, Arl3, Bbs5, Bbs9, Cep120, Cep164, Cep290, Cplane1, Dync2h1, Dync2i1, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Kif3b, Pkd1, Ptch1, Ptch2, Rpgr, Smo, Tbc1d23, and Tbc1d24 were themselves mostly sparse. No coordinated reporter-gene change was seen in Shh-Smoothened-GLI signaling genes including Gli1/2/3, Ptch1/2, and Smo. Interpretation is limited because several exact TBC1D32 partners, including CDK20 and FAM149B1, were not assayed.

Sar1b did not transcriptomically phenocopy the COPII coat-cycle genes Sec23a or Sec31a, even though these genes are close pathway neighbors. Across matched cell types, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, whole-signature correlations were near zero, indicating buffered and nonconvergent COPII-mediated vesicle transport signatures. In 155 MB Glut, Sec23a was strongly repressed by its own perturbation yet still showed essentially no correlation with the Sar1b signature; interpretation is cautious because Sar1b downstream effects were weak and Sec31a repression was inconsistent.

Phactr1 showed no detectable convergent Phactr-family signature with the assayed paralog Phactr2 in this dataset. Although Phactr proteins share RPEL/G-actin architecture, Phactr2 had weak on-target response and did not produce a robust Phactr1-like signature in shared cell classes, including L4-5 IT CTX Glut, L5 ET CTX Glut, CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and MB Glut, consistent with uncoupled RNA-level behavior in the G-actin/PHACTR1/PP1 RPEL signaling context. Top score-vector neighbors of Phactr1 were also very weak, and Phactr1 transcript decreases generally did not survive per-class FDR correction, so this negative comparison should not be taken as evidence that Phactr1 and Phactr2 proteins differ in function.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Actb did not show a close whole-transcriptome phenocopy among library perturbations. In the four strongest Actb contexts—005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut—the strongest positive or negative whole-signature correlations with other perturbations, including Xpo1, Tsc1, Calm2, Pex1, Tnrc6a, Sec31a, Nefl, and Atp6v0c, were only about +0.126 or -0.128. Across these cell types, Actb is better interpreted through its measured compensation genes, notably Flna and Actg1, rather than as convergence on another screened guide, although the weak similarity could partly reflect limited guide efficiency for some comparators.

Spred2 showed a weak whole-transcriptome perturbation signature that was essentially orthogonal to the expected SPRED/NF1/Ras/FGF neighborhood: across all cells, Pearson correlations were near zero with Spred1, Nf1, Braf, Raf1, and Mapk1, and the largest matched-cell correlation among 24 related perturbations was only 0.131. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, expected RAS/MAPK negative-regulation features were absent and signatures remained orthogonal to Spred1, Nf1, Fgfr1, and Fgfr2. Because Spred2 had no corrected hits, this divergence indicates lack of detectable convergence in this assay rather than proof of a distinct SPRED2 pathway.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Kif5c showed transcriptomic signatures that were essentially uncoupled from related motor-system perturbations in the two best-engaged cell types, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these cells, Kif5c signatures were nearly orthogonal to Kif5a, Klc1, Klc2, Kif1a, and Dync1h1, with full-signature Pearson correlations between -0.028 and 0.023, despite KIF5C belonging to the Kinesin-1 and microtubule cargo transport system. This apparent pathway uncoupling is caveated because the Kif5c signatures were weak, so buffering or assay noise could also explain the lack of similarity.

Map6 showed near-zero within-cell-type transcriptional signature correlations with assayed microtubule and transport perturbations, including Tubb3, Tubb4a, Stmn2, Mapt, Map1b, Dcx, Camsap1, Mark3, Dync1h1, Kif5a, and Kif5c, and likewise with glutamatergic perturbations spanning Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Dlg4, Gria1, and Gria2. This pattern was seen across same-cell-type comparisons, including 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, despite several comparator perturbations having FDR-significant genes. Because the analysis used RNA score vectors only, the lack of shared transcriptional similarity does not exclude cytoskeletal or electrophysiologic coupling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nlgn3 showed transcriptomic divergence in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: its signatures were nearly orthogonal, with all-gene correlations close to zero, to perturbations of related synaptic and neurodevelopmental genes including Nlgn2, Nrxn1, Nrxn2, Dlg4, Shank3, Grin2b, and Cntnap2 within the neurexin–neuroligin postsynaptic adhesion network. These comparators were measurably knocked down in the same cell classes, yet only modest, cell-type-specific neighbors emerged, arguing against a large shared mRNA program while remaining limited by the weak non-target Nlgn3 signature and not excluding shared synaptic function.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Prox1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a nonconvergent transcriptional profile with no close same-cell-type phenocopy among assayed perturbations. Although Prox1 up-regulated outputs including Mef2c and Auts2, direct perturbation of Mef2c or Auts2 in the same cell type produced only one FDR hit each, arguing that the Prox1 signature is not a broad Mef2c/Auts2 output state. A scan across other targets found only weak neighbors, and this exploratory result is caveated because gene-level Wilcoxon scores were used without correlation significance testing, so low-count or inefficient perturbations could appear falsely dissimilar.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp644 showed exploratory rather than mechanistic restricted signature neighbors: in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, the top-100 absolute-score neighbor search returned Sptb, Tnpo3, Wdr48, Safe_target_9, Chrna5, and Zfp609 rather than Ehmt1, and in 155 MB Glut the weakest-adjusted-p-value class, driven by nominal Stoml1 up-regulation, still had no FDR-significant gene and no Ehmt1-like neighbor structure. Across these cell types, correlations to Ehmt1 were weakly negative or near zero, so these restricted correlations should be treated as hypothesis-generating QC signals rather than genome-wide concordance with G9a/GLP-H3K9me2 repression biology.

Fgf12 produced a transcriptomic signature that was nearly orthogonal to Fgf13, Fgf14, and sodium-channel perturbations including Scn1a, Scn1b, Scn2a, and Scn8a, despite shared FHF/NaV excitability biology. Across the dataset, score correlations with these comparators were close to zero, and no strong positive or inverse perturbation neighbor emerged. In 155 MB Glut, Fgf12 showed its best nominal target engagement but no non-target adjusted response, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, stronger Fgf13 and Scn knockdowns were clearly not Fgf12-like. Because Fgf12 had weak per-cell-type engagement, this mainly argues against a robust RNA phenocopy rather than against electrophysiologic convergence.

Nexmif perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the N-cadherin/delta-catenin/integrin adhesion signaling module: Cdh2, Ctnnd2, Itgb1, and Rhoa did not pass FDR, and the Nexmif mRNA signature was essentially uncorrelated with Cdh2, Ctnnd2, or Itgb1 perturbation signatures. Related adhesion-pathway perturbations showed stronger on-target or downstream signals than Nexmif, although Itgb1 itself was transcriptionally weak. This contrasts with prior developmental cortex or cultured-neuron studies linking NEXMIF/KIDLIA to N-cadherin, delta-catenin, RhoA, actin dynamics, neuron migration, and dendritic growth, and may reflect the guide-based transcriptomic readout and weak Nexmif target suppression.

Alx4 showed no measurable engagement of its own transcript and did not participate in a strong positive or negative perturbation module across all 23 assayed mouse brain cell types; similarly, the paralogs Alx1 and Alx3 also lacked convincing on-target transcript shifts and produced only sparse, isolated corrected hits. Even where Ctnnb1 produced a robust signature, ALX-family perturbations did not form a recurrent brain signature, supporting absence of an ALX developmental transcription program in this screen rather than a paralog-specific Alx4 neural module, with the caveat that Alx1 was tested in fewer groups.

Wt1 showed a weak, non-convergent transcriptional signature in this dataset: same-cell-type correlations were small overall, with the largest positive and negative values both occurring in 308 CB GABA, and correlations with Ep300 and Crebbp were near zero. Thus, screened CBP/p300 coactivator perturbations did not recapitulate a Wt1-like neuronal state, and no strong same-cell-type signature neighbor emerged. This interpretation is cautious because Basp1 was not in the perturbation library, EP300/CREBBP are pleiotropic coactivators, and the analysis relies on weak Wt1 signatures rather than validated Wt1 loss-of-function signatures.

Syn2 did not form a convergent transcriptomic unit with synapsin paralogs or nearby synaptic vesicle cycle genes in this Perturb-seq dataset. Its signature was nearly uncorrelated with Syn1, Syn3, Syp, Snap25, Sv2a, Syt2, and Stx1b, while Syn1, Syp, Snap25, and Sv2a showed broader FDR-supported target engagement and Syn3 had no FDR-supported engagement. Even in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Syn2 mRNA knockdown was clearest, signature neighbors were weak, and Syn3 comparisons are limited by undetectable knockdown rather than a clean loss-of-function profile.

Cox6a1 knockdown did not produce detectable mRNA-level compensation by Cox6a2 or other assayed cytochrome-c-oxidase subunit transcripts, arguing against a simple COX6A paralog switch or complex IV subunit remodeling response in post-mitotic brain cells. In the best-engaged cell type, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Cox6a1 was depleted but no non-target changes passed multiple-testing correction, and related signatures were largely on-target only for Cox5a and Ndufa4. This null result should be interpreted with the caveat that Cox6a2 is expected to be low in brain, and lack of Wilcoxon-detected mRNA changes does not exclude translational, assembly-level, or metabolic compensation.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Chmp4b in 308 CB GABA showed the largest absolute signature correlations in the dataset, but its strongest positive and negative neighbors were mostly non-ESCRT genes rather than canonical ESCRT components: positive neighbors included Fbxo11, B9d1, Atp6v1e1, and Hmgcr, while negative neighbors included Wdr26, Cckar, Dstyk, and Nr4a1. This cerebellar GABAergic pattern is therefore biologically interesting but may reflect a local cell-state or stress-like axis rather than direct ESCRT pathway reconstruction, especially since only 44 Chmp4b-perturbed CB GABA cells contributed and no direct CHMP4B link is asserted for most neighbors.

Ebf2 showed a convergent near-null transcriptional response with the other assayed COE/EBF paralogs: Ebf1 and Ebf3 were also FDR-null or nearly so, and Ebf2 score vectors were only weakly correlated with Ebf1, Ebf3, or any non-self signature neighbor. In the only FDR-positive cell type, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, the isolated Tbc1d14 signal still did not yield strong positive or negative neighbors, with maximal absolute Pearson r of 0.131 across matched cell types. These comparisons are limited by poor apparent engagement of each EBF paralog and by transcriptional-score-based correlations only.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Msx2 in 308 CB GABA showed an exploratory, restricted convergence with the MSX2/BMP-homeobox developmental network: its all-gene signature aligned with Sp7 and partly with Bmpr1b, with some relation to Smad9 and Smad1, but Runx2, Dlx5, Bmpr1a, and Bmpr2 were weakly or negatively correlated. This was the only cell type with a strong Msx2 signature-neighbor structure and an FDR-significant downstream hit, while outside CB GABA Msx2 lacked strong neighbors. Because target engagement was weak and several strongest neighbors were not canonical MSX2 pathway genes, Msx2 should not be treated here as a simple proxy for canonical BMP-osteogenic signaling.

Syt2 was not interchangeable with core synaptic-vesicle perturbations in this RNA readout: Stxbp1 and Snap25 produced more FDR-level transcriptional output than Syt2, while canonical related perturbations such as Syp, Syn1, Dnm1, Cplx1, Stx1b, Vamp1, Syn2, Dlg4, Unc13a, and Cplx2 showed only weak convergence with the sparse Syt2 signature. In fast calcium-dependent synaptic vesicle exocytosis contexts, especially 155 MB Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Syt2 knockdown had little secondary FDR-significant response, consistent with transcriptional buffering. This contrast is exploratory because it relies on only 90 nominal Syt2 coordinates and related targets differ in expression, cell coverage, and on-target efficacy.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp160 did not show a stable positive or negative surrogate perturbation in restricted-signature neighbor analyses. Across 36,337 Zfp160-neighbor correlations, the strongest positive and negative correlations were only modest and were concentrated mainly in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, with neighbors including Cd3d, Rsrc1, Glra3, Klf9, Sec31a, and Npy1r. Safe_target_* perturbations also appeared among the most extreme neighbors across multiple cell types, so the pattern is exploratory rather than mechanistic. A key caveat is that comparisons used only the top 250 ranked Zfp160 genes per cell type, amplifying nominal, non-FDR signal.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Xrn1 showed neuronal signatures that were not phenocopied by available RNA-decay neighbors. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the strongest Xrn1-responsive class, a 29-gene FDR<0.10 mixed synaptic signature appeared despite no measurable Xrn1 transcript depletion, and Cnot1, Upf3b, and Ski did not mimic it. In 155 MB Glut, Xrn1 produced 21 FDR<0.10 genes with a small Slc17a6/V-ATPase vesicle signature, while Cnot1 showed a distinct response rather than a full copy. These comparisons were limited because only a few canonical 5′-3′ decay genes were perturbed and the neighbor scan used restricted Xrn1 gene sets rather than genome-wide correlation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Grin3a was uncoupled from core NMDA receptor perturbation signatures in this dataset: in matched cell types including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b showed clear self-knockdown, whereas Grin3a did not, and Grin3a score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, and Grin2d. This argues against reading Grin3a as a generic NMDA-receptor-loss signature, although the weak Grin3a vector leaves open that failed or buffered perturbation, rather than true pathway divergence, contributed to the lack of correlation.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Mef2c showed a cell-type-specific assay response in cortical IT neurons, with the strongest signatures in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, where shared features included Chgb, Stac2, Gria2, and Serinc2 up-regulation and Slit2 down-regulation. In contrast, Mef2a and Mef2d did not phenocopy this MEF2-family transcriptional regulation signature: each had zero FDR<0.05 genes in these two cell types and only near-zero to weak score correlations with Mef2c. Because Mef2a and Mef2d target transcripts were not significantly knocked down here, this supports an assay-level divergence rather than proof of biological non-redundancy.

Nbea did not converge strongly with related synaptic or kinase-pathway perturbations: its closest non-Nbea global neighbor was extremely weak, and restricted-signature comparisons were near zero for available PKA-adjacent, postsynaptic, and neurodevelopmental-disease perturbations including Kif1a, Syp, Prkar1a, Sv2a, Dlg4, Shank3, Fmr1, and Grin2b. Across several glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types, Nbea showed buffered target downregulation with mixed nominal trafficking genes rather than a shared downstream module. This interpretation is limited because SAP102/Dlg3 and KIF21B perturbations were absent, and similarities were computed from DE-result vectors rather than raw single-cell embeddings.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Arid2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a transcriptional signature most similar to the shared BAF/PBAF core subunits Smarcb1, Smarce1, and Smarcc2, while Arid1a, Arid1b, Smarca2, Smarca4, Bicra, and Smarcad1 had near-zero correlations and did not recapitulate the Arid2 pattern. This supports a PBAF/base-module interpretation of the Arid2 phenotype rather than interchangeability with cBAF ARID subunits, ncBAF, or all SWI/SNF ATPase perturbations, although the comparison was limited to a top-500-gene Pearson signature in one cell type and lacked PBRM1, BRD7, and PHF10 perturbations.

Bsn showed a transcriptional signature that was near-orthogonal to perturbations of assayed presynaptic or autophagy-linked interactors, including Snap25, Syp, Syn1, Unc13b, and Atg5, indicating that in this assay a scaffold perturbation did not phenocopy depletion of vesicle/exocytosis components within presynaptic active-zone organization. Comparator genes often showed direct self-transcript depletion, whereas Bsn had no measurable Bsn transcript in some of those cell types. This comparison was based on rank correlations of mRNA signatures, and some STRING partners such as Ctbp2, Erc2, and Rims1 were not assayed.

Ndufv2 showed a divergent, weakly correlated transcriptional response relative to other Complex I Nduf perturbations: despite biochemical relatedness to Ndufv1, Ndufs1, Ndufs2, Ndufs8, Ndufb10, and Ndufa13, its signature was essentially uncorrelated with these comparators and did not yield a clear phenocopy or anti-phenocopy. This suggests that complex membership alone was insufficient to produce a shared mRNA signature in the measured setting, with the strongest caveat being weaker Ndufv2 target knockdown than many neighboring Nduf perturbations, limiting subunit-specific interpretation and reflecting a transcriptomic analysis restricted in one audit to Ndufv2 top genes.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Sorl1 showed no strong convergence with the VPS10P paralog Sort1 or with genome-wide signature neighbors. In 155 MB Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, all-target Sorl1 score-vector correlations were near zero, and in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, although Sort1 had corrected target engagement, neither Sort1 nor Sorl1 produced corrected non-self hits. These results argue against a shared sortilin-family mRNA response or a large Sorl1 co-response module, though the correlations were computed across all measured genes and may be dominated by weak noisy ranks when Sorl1 lacks corrected downstream genes.

Tbx19 showed weak or absent convergence with both T-box-family transcriptional programs and the available pituitary transcription-factor neighborhood in this adult brain dataset. Its perturbation signature was nearly uncorrelated with Tbr1 and other T-box paralogs (Tbx1, Tbx2, Tbx3, Tbx4, Tbx5, Tbx6, Tbx21, Tbx22) and with pituitary-linked factors including Avpr1b, Gata2, Lhx3, Lhx4, Neurod1, Nr5a1, Pax7, Pou1f1, and Prop1; the largest absolute Pearson correlation was only 0.098. These signature-level comparisons therefore do not support a generic T-box, POMC-lineage, or pituitary-transcription-factor state, although many expected partners were not directly targeted and the comparison network is developmental/pituitary rather than adult neuronal.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ywhaz perturbation produced a near-null nontarget transcriptome rather than a shared 14-3-3 downstream signature. In the only cell type with FDR-significant Ywhaz self-depletion, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, there were no FDR-significant nontarget genes and no close transcriptome-wide neighbor, including Ywhag or Ywhae; Ywhaz–Ywhag and Ywhaz–Ywhae correlations were only about r≈0.05. Ywhag, despite stronger engagement, likewise showed no non-target FDR hits, consistent with buffering within the 14-3-3 isoform/adaptor network without paralog mRNA induction. These correlations may be damped by weak Ywhaz engagement and do not address protein-level redundancy.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Abat in 052 Pvalb Gaba neurons showed a distinct transcriptomic response rather than a generic GABAergic-loss signature: although Gad1, Gad2, Slc6a1, Gabra1, Gabrb2, and Gabrg2 each knocked down their own transcripts more strongly than Abat, their transcriptome-wide Wilcoxon score correlations with the Abat signature were near zero (about r = -0.0368 to 0.0352). In this cell type, Abat was down without FDR-supported compensatory pathway transcription, and Gls appeared only weakly engaged, so comparisons should be limited to Pvalb neurons and interpreted cautiously.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ahi1 showed an exploratory signature-neighbor pattern in 308 CB GABA cells: B9d1 and Cep290 were positively correlated with the Ahi1 perturbation by weak whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon-score vectors, consistent with a primary cilium transition zone and ciliary trafficking neighborhood. However, Ahi1 itself was not measurably depleted in this cell type, so this should not be treated as robust convergence or mechanistic proof. The broader context was mostly no FDR-significant transcriptional output, and the signal was weaker than comparators such as Ranbp2 and Wdr26.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grin1 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a dominant, bidirectional transcriptional response consistent with mixed synaptic and neuronal-system remodeling rather than uniform suppression of neuronal genes. Induced genes included Scg2, Stmn4, Kctd16, Gpm6a, Igf1, and Jun, whereas Erc2, Homer2, Kcnab2, Gabrd, and Prkcd decreased, with enrichment for synapse, post-synapse, pre-synapse, and neuronal-system annotations. These pathway labels are annotation-based and do not establish whether the response is protective, maladaptive, or secondary to altered firing.

Stra6 perturbation did not converge with nuclear retinoid-receptor perturbations on a common transcriptomic program. Across matched cell types, Stra6-vs-RAR/RXR score-vector correlations were near zero, with |r|max = 0.0945, and focused signature-neighbor scans did not identify strong positive or inverse neighbors. Rara, Rarb, Rarg, Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg perturbations were largely silent overall; the only significant receptor-target row was Rara→Arrb2 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut. In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, Stra6 showed its lowest adjusted p value, but Chfr remained non-significant and the strongest neighbor correlation was only r = 0.0674. These transcriptomic comparisons cannot distinguish low receptor expression from insufficient editing.

Bckdk showed essentially no transcriptomic convergence with related branched-chain amino acid or oxidative decarboxylation perturbations, including Bckdhb, Dld, Ivd, Pcca, Pdha1, Pdhb, Dlat, Dlst, Ogdh, and Auh; correlations were near zero overall, with Bckdhb at mean r = 0.0003 and Dld at mean r = 0.0024, and even the strongest average positive and negative neighbors were tiny. In this dataset, Bckdk also produced no FDR-significant mRNA response in the BCKDH phosphorylation/branched-chain amino acid catabolism pathway, so the weak Bckdk signature should not be used as a proxy for BCKDH-complex or adjacent mitochondrial dehydrogenase biology, while noting that near-zero correlations may reflect low signal rather than true independence.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut
full_finding_text: Irf3 did not show a convergent signature with connected PRR/IFN pathway perturbations in the assayed neuronal states, including 308 CB GABA and 001 L5-6 IT Glut. Across related targets such as Ifnar1, Ifngr2, Irf7, Tbk1, and Stat1, same-cell correlations with Irf3 were near zero, with a maximum all-gene related correlation of r=0.094; even the best Reactome/STRING-linked neighbor, Ifnar1 in 308 CB GABA, reached only r=0.306. Unrestricted top neighbors like Pank2 or Sema5a were also modest and exploratory, so Irf3, Irf7, TBK1-pathway, receptor, and STAT perturbations were not interchangeable here.

Stat5b produced a transcriptomic signature that was largely orthogonal to other STAT-family perturbations and to screened receptors linked to growth-hormone or cytokine signaling, with near-zero score-vector correlations versus Stat1, Stat2, Stat3, Stat4, Ghr, Epor, Prlr, Il2rg, Ifngr1, and Ifngr2 under basal in vivo mouse-brain conditions. This suggests that curated pathway membership did not translate into transcriptomic phenocopy here, so receptor perturbations such as Ghr, Epor, Prlr, and Il2rg are not suitable positive controls for the observed Stat5b signature. Comparisons were based on bulk cell-type score correlations, and the screen did not include Stat5a, Jak1, Jak2, Jak3, or Tyk2.

Chp1 showed an exploratory restricted-signature similarity to Dctn1, Mib1, Dync1h1, Marchf6, Rab7, Tsc1, and Tsc2, with Srebf2 as the strongest negative neighbor. Because these positive neighbors include genes with curated roles in dynein/dynactin and endolysosomal trafficking, ER lipid homeostasis, and mTORC1 regulation, the pattern suggests that membrane-trafficking and ER lipid-state perturbations can reproduce the Chp1 sterol-related module, including markers such as Insig1 and Hmgcr. This inference is hypothesis-generating because neighbors were computed from a Chp1-selected 332-gene feature set rather than the full transcriptome.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ifngr2 perturbation showed a weak, module-restricted IFN/MHC-I effect rather than a transcriptome-wide IFN-family signature: in subcortical classes including 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Ifngr2 loss nominally decreased a six-gene antigen-presentation module comprising Stat1, Nlrc5, B2m, H2-K1, H2-D1, and Tapbp. Stat1 perturbation reproduced this same module more strongly than Ifngr2, whereas whole-transcriptome Ifngr2 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Stat1, Ifngr1, Irf1, Irf9, Stat2, Ifnar1, or Ifnar2; this convergence was restricted to the selected six-gene module, and JAK1, JAK2, Tyk2, and Ifng perturbations were not available for comparison.

Cplx1 showed near-zero transcriptomic signature correlation with perturbations of connected presynaptic vesicle-release genes, including Cplx2, Snap25, Stx1b, Stxbp1, Vamp1, Syp, Sv2a, Dnm1, Syn1, Dnajc5, Syt2, and Unc13a. In this assay, no perturbation had a robust positive or negative correlation with Cplx1, even though several comparator genes had strong on-target knockdown. These results suggest that SNARE-associated synaptic vesicle exocytosis and neurotransmitter-release pathway membership did not translate into a shared mRNA state here, while the weak secondary Cplx1 signature means the finding argues against a robust shared transcriptional program rather than shared release biology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ifnar2 did not show a recognizable type-I-interferon IFNAR/JAK-STAT neuronal signature: across 22 shared Glut/GABA neuronal groups, the paired receptor subunit Ifnar1 was FDR-negative and essentially uncorrelated with Ifnar2, and the ISGF3-related perturbations Stat1, Stat2, and Irf9 were likewise only weakly aligned rather than convergent. This negative pattern also held in specific groups such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Stat1 had on-target comparator hits but Ifnar2 still did not match. These comparisons rely on whole-transcriptome score correlations from weak signatures, and key comparators such as Jak1 and Tyk2 were not assayed as perturbation targets in the queried table.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|215 MB Dopa|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pitx3 showed near-zero signature correlations with its dopaminergic developmental neighbors, including Pitx2, Nr4a1/2/3, En1/En2, Foxa2, Lmx1a/Lmx1b, Otx2, Ret, and Gfra1, across 215 MB Dopa, 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 308 CB GABA. In 215 MB Dopa, correlations to Ret, Nr4a1, and Lmx1b were 0.031, 0.012, and 0.001, and expected PITX3-NR4A2 terminal-differentiation markers such as Th, Slc6a3, and Ddc were not detected after FDR correction. Because these perturbations were generally weak, this argues against substituting related developmental-factor or Ret/Gfra1 signatures as proxies for Pitx3 here, but does not establish biological independence in embryonic mdDA neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zc3h14 perturbation produced its clearest glutamatergic RNA-processing signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Pabpn1 was down-regulated in both cell types, Cstf2 was additionally down-regulated in 155 MB Glut, and Tra2a was up-regulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The midbrain glutamatergic class also showed the clearest measured on-target Zc3h14 depletion, whereas the thalamic class had the strongest downstream signature despite only nominal target depletion. These transcript-level changes are consistent with a poly(A)-tail and pre-mRNA 3-prime processing response, but the dataset does not test poly(A)-tail length, cleavage activity, or whether Pabpn1/Cstf2 changes are causal.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Klc2 showed transcriptomic buffering rather than convergence with related motor-pathway perturbations: in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Klc2 was target-depleted but its whole-transcriptome signature remained essentially uncorrelated with Klc1, Kif5a, Kif5c, or Dync1h1, with the strongest non-self neighbor only |r|=0.113 and Klc1 reaching just r=0.0965 in 052 Pvalb Gaba. In overlapping cell types, Dync1h1 instead produced sizable non-self FDR responses, so biochemical pathway proximity did not predict a shared RNA state; however, these correlations are exploratory because Klc2 profiles contained almost no non-target FDR signal, and KLC2 and dynein are pathway neighbors rather than the same complex.

Cd4 did not transcriptionally engage the canonical CD4/TCR-CD3/MHC-II signaling program in the profiled neuronal strata. In the same dataset, perturbations of Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd3g, and Cd247 likewise showed no robust on-target or downstream FDR-significant effects, and their signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Cd4, consistent with an absent or inactive immune receptor complex in these cells, despite CD4’s usual cooperation with peptide-MHC-II, CD3 chains, and Lck. This inference is limited by incomplete coverage of proximal immune components and by reliance on transcriptomic rather than direct protein-complex readouts.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ank1 showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signature correlation with ankyrin-family, spectrin/adducin scaffold, channel, and adhesion perturbations in the two cell types with FDR-level Ank1 knockdown, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut. In these cells, Ank1 did not converge with Ank2, Ank3, Sptan1/Sptb, Add1/2/3, Kcnq2/3, Nrcam, Scn1a/2a/8a, Cntnap2, or Epb41l1, and unrestricted neighbor searches also failed to reveal a high-correlation module, consistent with RNA-level buffering rather than a shared excitability or L1-ankyrin transcriptional state; however, protein interactions or post-translational scaffold changes would not be detected by RNA signatures alone.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Rdx showed a sparse, cell-context-limited signature, most evident in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, where it ranked first nominally but its restricted neighbors were only modest. Across available cytoskeletal and membrane-associated comparators in the ERM membrane-cortex actin linkage context, including Nf2, Actb, Actg1, Actn4, Add1-3, Cdc42, Rac1, Apc, Cdh2, and Epb41l1, same-cell restricted correlations never exceeded r=0.298; the strongest genome-wide restricted neighbor was Syp in CNU-MGE GABA at r=0.447. Because only the top 200 nominal Rdx genes per cell type were used and true ERM paralogs Ezr and Msn were not perturbed, Rdx should not be interpreted here as a generic actin-disruption state.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Naa20 shows restricted-signature similarity not to other NAT genes such as Naa10 or Naa15, but to perturbations in nuclear transport, ubiquitin-like conjugation, O-GlcNAc/proteostasis, pre-mRNA splicing, and proteasome components. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the strongest neighbors include Tnpo3, Ufc1, Uba5, and Tpr; in 155 MB Glut, Prpf6, Psmc1, Tpr, and Ogt stand out; and in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, similarity includes Prpf6, Ogt, U2af2, and Psmc5. Bap1 is an opposing neighbor in two glutamatergic signatures. These exploratory correlations used only the 500 highest-magnitude Naa20 genes per cell type and do not establish direct pathway membership.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Atp1a1 showed a divergent Perturb-seq profile relative to the other Na+/K+-ATPase alpha paralogs across 22 shared neuronal classes, including L2-3 IT CTX Glut, CA3/CA2-FC DG Glut, multiple GABA classes, and MB Glut. Atp1a3 was efficiently knocked down, whereas Atp1a2 did not show reliable on-target engagement in these neuronal populations, and Atp1a1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with either paralog, with no strong positive or inverse signature neighbors elsewhere in the matrix. In 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Atp1a1 knockdown was strong and Atp1a3 induction was the only FDR-significant paralog change, suggesting limited, cell-type-specific compensation; these comparisons reflect RNA-level Wilcoxon signature correlations rather than pump activity.

Kcnh5 did not converge transcriptomically with its EAG paralog Kcnh1 in this dataset. Across 21 shared cell classes, Kcnh5–Kcnh1 full-signature correlations were near zero, and in the two cell types showing nominal Kcnh5 target depletion, no strong same-cell-type positive or negative signature neighbor emerged. Genes from the voltage-gated potassium-channel neighborhood, including Kcnh1, Kcnq2/3, Kcnc1/2, Kcna1, Kcnab1/2/3, Camk2a/b/d, Cask, and Kcnd1, were not significantly altered after Kcnh5 targeting, so these weak perturbations argue mainly against claiming interchangeability rather than proving divergent channel biology.

Adrb2 was uncoupled from the basal cAMP/PKA/CREB transcriptomic circuitry captured by this screen: Adrb2, like the beta-adrenergic paralogs Adrb1 and Adrb3, showed no corrected receptor-level mRNA response, and its score vectors correlated only weakly with intracellular pathway perturbations such as Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Gnas, Prkaca, Prkar1a, and Creb1 (all |r|max < 0.10). Although some downstream perturbations were detectable in at least some cell types, Adrb2 did not elicit an immediate-early neuronal program, with no corrected induction of Fos, Jun, Egr1, Nr4a1, Arc, Npas4, or Bdnf. These cross-perturbation comparisons are based on mRNA score vectors and involve different perturbed-cell counts across targets.

Kalrn knockdown did not transcriptionally induce a coordinated Rac/PAK/MAPK or postsynaptic NMDA-receptor program: Rac1, Rhoa, Cdc42, Pak1/2/3, Mapk1/3, Dlg4, Grin2a/b, Ntrk2, Trio, Tiam1, Arhgap32, and Dock7 all remained at FDR=1.0, even though some related postsynaptic and Rho-neighbor perturbations produced strong transcriptomic signatures in the same screen. The only hint of convergence was weak Kalrn–Trio overlap in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and the mRNA endpoint cannot assess Rac1-GTP or RhoA-GTP, kinase activity, receptor localization, spine morphology, or synaptic transmission directly.

Ywhaz perturbation did not detectably mobilize canonical 14-3-3 effector pathways at the mRNA level. Across a targeted set of RAF/MAPK, catenin/Rho/LIMK, apoptosis, and glutamatergic synaptic/NMDAR-related transcripts, including Araf, Braf, Raf1, Mapk1, Mapk3, Ctnnb1, Limk1, Limk2, Bad, Foxo3, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b, no genes reached the FDR threshold. The only cell type with significant Ywhaz self-depletion, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, had no significant nontarget genes, while 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut showed only borderline signals such as Pfn2 and nominal Mapk1. This targeted check, rather than formal enrichment, is consistent with many Ywhaz outputs being post-translational rather than transcriptional.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Robo2 knockdown, despite efficient on-target engagement, did not produce FDR-supported transcriptional feedback onto the canonical SLIT-ROBO neighborhood in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, or 155 MB Glut. In these best-engaged cell classes, Robo1, Robo4, Slit1/2/3, Srgap1/2/3, Abl1, Nck1/2, Pak1/2/3, Cdc42, and Rac1 remained unchanged, and genome-wide testing found no significant downstream transcripts after excluding the direct on-target effect. This absence of remodeling should be interpreted cautiously because the assayed mRNAs are proxies, whereas SLIT-ROBO signaling may be regulated post-translationally or subcellularly rather than at steady-state transcript levels.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Runx2 perturbation was transcriptionally inert in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut subclass: expected RUNX2-associated osteogenic and BMP/Wnt markers, including Sp7, Spp1, Ibsp, Alpl, Col1a1, Satb2, Sox9, Lef1, and Axin2, were not detectably regulated. This was not a general inability of the screen to capture Wnt-linked transcription, because Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 perturbations in the same subclass produced strong responses, including regulation of Lef1 and Axin2. Thus, in these assayed brain-neuronal and dopaminergic subclasses, canonical Wnt activity was recoverable but uncoupled from a latent Runx2 osteogenic module; Cbfb was not perturbed.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Nrxn2 was not a strong transcriptomic proxy for other synaptic-adhesion perturbations in 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. In MB Glut, where the strongest measured Nrxn2 knockdown was seen, the response was largely target-only, and whole-signature correlations with Nrxn1, Nrxn3, Nlgn2, and Nlgn3 were very small despite broader own-transcript depletion for some of those related targets. The CNU-HYa HY GABA Nrxn2 signature likewise lacked strong positive or negative transcriptome-wide neighbors, supporting non-interchangeability within the presynaptic neurexin/trans-synaptic adhesion pathway, though the inference is limited by noisy, weak target-only Nrxn2 signatures.

Nfix perturbation showed no detectable NFI paralog compensation or family-level signature convergence in this dataset: Nfia, Nfib, and Nfic transcripts did not measurably shift in the best Nfix-engaged strata, and whole-transcriptome score correlations between Nfix and Nfia/Nfib/Nfic perturbations were near zero (about -0.061 to 0.081). This pattern was seen across several mature mouse brain cell classes, including L4-5 IT CTX Glut, CTX-CGE GABA, CA3/CA2-FC/DG Glut, and L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, but the Nfix signature itself was weak, so these near-zero relationships are best treated as a negative control rather than proof of functional divergence.

Tlr2 showed convergent absence rather than a canonical inflammatory signature across all 22 Tlr2-tested neuronal classes: Tlr2 had zero FDR-significant genes, no target-transcript shift, and no high-correlation signature neighbor, while related perturbations in Cd14, Tlr4, Nod2, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Chuk, Map3k7, Mapk8, Mapk9, Rel, and Tlr3/5/7/8/9 were also almost entirely inactive. Only isolated exceptions appeared, with Tlr8 yielding Cnpy3 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and Tlr3 yielding Rgs4 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut. Because Tlr1, Tlr6, Myd88, Tirap, and IRAK genes were not assayed, silence cannot be tested for every proximal complex member.

Ifnar1 showed weakly engaged, idiosyncratic transcriptional effects rather than a clean type I interferon receptor signature. Across all 22 assayed brain cell classes, Ifnar1 lacked FDR-significant genes, showed no coherent basal ISG decrease, and its same-cell-type score vectors were near-zero correlated with Ifnar2, Stat1, Stat2, Irf9, Irf7, Ifngr1, Ifngr2, Il10ra, and Il10rb; the strongest genome-wide neighbor was only modest. This is best read as a lack of pathway convergence, especially since Ifnar2 itself also showed weak target engagement; CA3/CA2-FC DG glutamatergic neurons had the densest nominal, but still weak, signal.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Elp1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a dominant response that was closely phenocopied by Elp2, the top non-self neighbor of the Elp1 top-100 gene signature with cosine 0.974, whereas Alkbh8, Nsun2, and Eif2ak4 were much weaker matches. This supports an Elongator-complex phenotype rather than a generic RNA-modification or ISR-kinase knockdown signature, with convergence on stress-associated genes including Asns, Cars, Chac1, and Shmt2 in the context of Elongator-dependent tRNA anticodon modification. A caveat is that the neighbor analysis was computed from the top 100 Elp1 genes in one cell type, and Alkbh8/Nsun2 were nearby perturbation controls rather than biochemical paralogs of Elp1.

Gfi1 showed no coherent shared transcriptional module with its paralog Gfi1b or with other perturbations across all 23 profiled mouse-brain cell classes. Gfi1–Gfi1b score-vector correlations were near zero or weakly negative in 22 shared cell types, and the strongest non-self neighbors, including Nr2c2, Cit, Ranbp2, and Scn9a, remained low amplitude with absolute correlations below 0.20. In this brain dataset, the GFI1 SNAG/CoREST-LSD1/HDAC repression program and canonical partners such as Gata2, Meis1, and Pbx1 were not detectably aligned, although the weak Gfi1 signature makes this mainly a negative related-target result rather than evidence for an opposing mechanism.

Itga2b showed a weak phenotype with no detectable convergent or inverse signature relative to other targeted integrin-family perturbations or any genome-wide high-correlation neighbors. Other assayed integrin subunits, including Itga2, Itga4, Itga6, Itga7, Itga8, Itga9, Itgb1, and Itgb2, were themselves weak and had only tiny cell-matched correlations with Itga2b, while genome-wide score-vector neighbors ranged from r=-0.138 to 0.159. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, the nominal Tsc2 signal and largest cellwise correlation still remained below interpretable thresholds. Because Itgb3 was not perturbed and correlations were based on DE score vectors rather than a replicated similarity model, the most appropriate conclusion is absence of detectable convergence rather than mechanistic divergence.

Yme1l1 targeting did not phenocopy the Opa1 ATF4-like amino-acid stress program. Across shared cell types, including the 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut class where Yme1l1 transcript depletion was strongest, direct Opa1 perturbation repeatedly induced Asns, Chac1, Ddit3, Slc7a5, Shmt2, and related genes such as Aldh1l2, Mars1, Cars, Slc6a9, and Mthfd2, whereas Yme1l1 showed no FDR-supported induction of this module. This suggests partial Yme1l1 loss was uncoupled from the OPA1/OMA1 mitochondrial inner-membrane protein degradation and integrated stress-response axis, although Opa1 loss and Yme1l1 depletion are not equivalent lesions and stronger or chronic YME1L1 loss may be required.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Srrm2 showed a spliceosome-adjacent but not generic splicing-factor phenotype, most evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells. Its nearest positive signature neighbors were Snrnp70, U2af2, Prpf6, and Thoc1, but the correlations were modest, based on gene-level Wilcoxon scores, and some U2af2, Prpf6, and Thoc1 target-transcript rows were weak. In contrast, Srsf1 loss, despite a very strong perturbation with thousands of hits, was essentially uncorrelated with Srrm2, indicating that Srrm2 loss is not interchangeable with generic essential SR splicing-factor depletion.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp949 showed no robust same-cell signature neighbor across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA. Correlations to comparators such as Ranbp2, B9d1, Wdr26, and Dstyk were only weak, with the strongest at r=0.215, and no top-5 neighbor recurred across cell types; 308 CB GABA had the largest absolute correlations but they remained weak. These Wilcoxon score-vector correlations may miss nonlinear or target-subset relationships.

Sdccag8 perturbation produced almost no multiple-testing-corrected transcriptomic response, and the expected primary-cilium, basal-body, Hedgehog, and centrosomal programs were not detectably activated or repressed. Across the measured signatures, canonical ciliary and SDCCAG8-neighborhood transcripts such as Ofd1, Cep290, Pcm1, Rabep2, Erc1, Cep131, Bbs4, Ift88, Kif3a, and Rpgrip1l showed no FDR-significant changes, despite prior biology linking SDCCAG8 to these pathways. This null RNA signature may reflect weak perturbation engagement, post-transcriptional effects, or cell-state buffering, and it does not exclude altered cilium morphology, protein localization, or Hedgehog signaling because those were not assayed.

Zfp280c showed no convergence with the assayed zinc-finger comparator perturbations Zfp280d and Zfp292 across matched cell types. In 39 overlapping comparator–cell-type pairs, genome-wide Spearman correlations remained near zero, indicating that these related zinc-finger signatures were not interchangeable with the Zfp280c signature in this dataset. This interpretation is limited by the fact that Zfp280d and Zfp292 were only coarse comparators, and the correlation analysis was restricted to targets present in the atlas.

Tlr4 showed essentially no convergence with the available TLR-family or downstream NF-kappa-B-neighbor perturbations in the assayed Glut/GABA neuronal panel. Cd14, Tlr2, Tlr7, Tlr9, and Nfkb1 had no FDR-supported hits, Tlr3 showed only a single Rgs4 hit, genome-wide score correlations with Tlr4 were near zero on average, and even whole-library signature neighbors were weak. This suggests that, in this basal neuronal context, the TLR4-CD14/MD-2 innate immune signaling module is uncoupled rather than shared, although key nodes such as Ly96, Myd88, Ticam1, Tirap, and Traf6 were not directly perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cntn1 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class showed a strongly on-target yet transcriptionally buffered response, with no non-target FDR hits, whereas the related nodal architecture gene Ank3, despite weaker silencing, triggered a broad 120-gene state change. This cell-type-matched contrast in node of Ranvier and ankyrin-spectrin scaffolding genes indicates that not all node/paranode components are silent in the screen. The comparison is architectural rather than one-to-one, since Ank3 is a pathway neighbor rather than a direct CNTN1-complex member.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sptan1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed only an on-target transcriptomic hit, with no non-target FDR-significant genes, whereas the comparator Ank3 in the same cell type produced a broad 121-gene differential-expression program; the two signatures were only weakly correlated. This divergence suggests that, within the neuronal spectrin membrane skeleton/axon initial segment context, immediate mRNA consequences of αII-spectrin depletion are not interchangeable with ankyrin-G perturbation. The contrast is transcriptomic only and does not establish different effects on AIS assembly or electrophysiology.

Irf2 perturbation produced no coherent transcriptomic convergence with other IRF-family perturbations: across the IRF neighborhood and genome-wide, nearest Irf2 signature neighbors were uniformly weak, and related IRF targets largely lacked reliable self-transcript depletion. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA and the pan-neuronal tested set, Irf2 did not drive a coherent type I interferon/IFN-axis program involving Stat1, Stat2, Isg15, Usp18, Ifit1-3, Ifitm1-3, Oasl1/2, Rsad2, Ddx58, Ifih1, Bst2, Zbp1, Tlr3, or Tlr7. By contrast, Stat1 showed detectable self-transcript depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, indicating that the broad Irf2/IRF null was not simply assay blindness, although the Stat1 comparison reflects RNA-level target engagement rather than a large downstream STAT1 program.

Drd5 showed no strong convergence with any other perturbation signature in the all-perturbation search. Across 43,663 same-cell-type Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon score vectors, the strongest positive neighbor was Wdr26 in 308 CB GABA at only r=0.1349, and the strongest negative neighbor was Ank1 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut at r=-0.1030. This suggests the weak Drd5 response was not rescued by assignment to another transcriptional module, although these very small correlations may be noise-dominated under the analysis used.

Uqcrh showed weak detectable target-mRNA depletion, resembling the small mitochondrial complex III subunits Uqcrb and Uqcrq rather than the core/Rieske/cytochrome-c1 subunits Uqcrc1, Uqcrfs1, and Cyc1, which had stronger on-target transcript effects. Several respiratory-chain perturbations were strongly knocked down in one cell type, and a second high-powered cell class also showed robust respiratory-chain target depletion while Uqcrh remained unengaged. This pattern suggests a subunit-class or target-engagement limitation rather than functional interchangeability, with the caveat that Uqcrb and Uqcrq lacked protein-level validation and only the quantified low-molecular-weight perturbations were represented.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Dym showed only a weak perturbation signature in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic glutamatergic cell type, and its reported interactor Ppib did not phenocopy that signal even though Ppib itself was much more cleanly depleted. In this acute neuronal Perturb-seq context, the DYM–PPIB secretory interactor axis therefore appeared nonconvergent rather than interchangeable. This comparison is limited by the weak Dym perturbation, and the other reported interactor, Golm1, was not available for evaluation here.

Lmx1b showed essentially zero correlation with Lmx1a, Pitx3, Nr4a2, Foxa2, En1, En2, Otx2, and Tcf7l2 perturbation signatures in matched cell types, including 215 MB Dopa, so the expected midbrain dopaminergic transcription-factor network and maintenance program was not recovered; markers such as Th, Slc6a3, and Ddc were part of this context. These near-null relationships appear exploratory and are likely dominated by weak or non-engaged single-TF signatures in this dataset, and should not be interpreted as antagonism among these factors.

Mtor showed a weak, transcriptionally buffered RNA phenotype in this dataset, and the direct mTORC1 scaffold comparator Rptor behaved similarly rather than phenocopying loss of the upstream repressors Tsc1 or Tsc2. Across 23 cell types, Rptor produced zero FDR<0.05 genes, whereas Tsc1 and Tsc2 produced 1,162 and 423, respectively, consistent with much larger adjusted RNA programs after repressor perturbation than after direct Mtor/Rptor knockdown. This contrast is best interpreted as assay-level buffering or weak target engagement for Mtor/Rptor, not as evidence that the core mTORC1 complex is biologically dispensable.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pde10a showed an isolated signal in 308 CB GABA cells that appears uncoupled from the target-engaged striatal program: Ubac2 passed 5% FDR, but Pde10a itself was not significantly reduced, and the 308 score vector was essentially uncorrelated with the 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA signature. This argues against overinterpreting the single cerebellar hit as a coherent PDE10A-related transcriptomic response, although weak biology could still exist and might require protein-level knockdown or pathway assays to detect.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Kit perturbation was largely uncoupled from related receptor and downstream pathway perturbations in neuronal transcriptomic readouts. In 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where Kit knockdown was FDR-supported, the response largely stopped at Kit itself and correlations with Csf1r, Flt3, Pdgfrb, Mapk1, Ptpn11, Pik3r2, Fyn, Cblb, Stat3, and Stat5b were all near zero, with no strong same-cell-type transcriptomic neighbor. In 155 MB Glut, a robust Mapk1 knockdown was likewise uncorrelated with the nominal Kit signature. Because many comparator signatures were weak and correlations were computed over rank-score vectors, this supports transcriptomic, not biochemical, non-equivalence of KIT loss to generic RTK/MAPK/STAT loss.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Kmt2e showed near-zero transcriptome-wide correlation with Kmt2a, Kmt2b, Kmt2d, and Setd1a perturbation signatures in the glutamatergic classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, even though those active KMT2-family writer perturbations produced much larger differential-expression burdens. In the strongest Kmt2e cell type, this divergence was prominent alongside shared induction of Snhg11, Atp6v0b, and Eno2, and the same lack of alignment was seen in the second resolved glutamatergic class. These results argue that Kmt2e was not interchangeable with enzymatic H3K4 writer perturbations in this assay, although comparator perturbation strengths were unequal.

Pgrmc1 perturbation produced a transcriptional signature that was largely orthogonal to available steroid, P450, nuclear-receptor, and lipid-related perturbations across matched cell types: all-gene correlations with Por, Sigmar1, Pgr, Ar, Esr1, Esr2, Hmgcr, Srebf1, Srebf2, Stard7, Hsd17b4, Ppara, Nr3c1, and Nr3c2 ranged from -0.090 to 0.079 across 307 matched signatures. This suggests Pgrmc1 should not be treated as interchangeable with these pathway-adjacent perturbations in these neurons, while noting that closer paralog or complex members such as Pgrmc2, Tmem97, and Insig1 were not perturbed.

Brwd1 perturbation in neuronal cells did not phenocopy assayed BAF-complex subunit perturbations: across 153 same-cell-type comparisons, Brwd1 RNA signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Arid1a, Arid1b, Smarca2, Smarca4, Smarcb1, Smarcc1, or Stat5b perturbations, with mean absolute correlation 0.017 and maximum 0.098. This indicates that acute partial Brwd1 loss in euploid neurons is not equivalent to generic BAF loss of function, although the comparison is limited to steady-state RNA signatures and BRWD1 and BAF could still converge at chromatin loci without matching transcriptomic effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Phf21a perturbation is associated with Rreb1 upregulation in neuronal classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where the signal is among the strongest observed, but this response is not unique to PHF21A. Myt1l and Zbtb7a perturbations also increase Rreb1 in overlapping neuronal subclasses, supporting an Rreb1-centered cross-perturbation transcriptional module rather than a PHF21A-specific endpoint. In 155 MB Glut, Phf21a-linked Rreb1 upregulation also appears alongside L3mbtl3. This convergence is based on a single-marker pattern, not a full-signature correlation analysis.

Lrif1 did not phenocopy Smchd1 in this brain Perturb-seq dataset: across the 22 matched cell classes, their whole-transcriptome perturbation score vectors were essentially orthogonal, so the expected SMCHD1-HP1 heterochromatin and inactive-X compaction module, involving LRIF1 with SMCHD1 and HP1-family genes CBX1, CBX3, and CBX5, was not recovered as a shared transcriptomic signature.
