Because both Lrif1 and Smchd1 showed weak transcript-level engagement, this non-recovery is exploratory and does not argue that the proteins are functionally disconnected.

Nlgn2 perturbation produced a largely target-only corrected transcriptional signature, and related neurexin–neuroligin perturbations showed a similar sparse pattern rather than a shared mRNA module: Nlgn3 and Nrxn1 were also mostly dominated by their own target-transcript effects, whereas Nlgn1 and Nrxn2 showed weaker or less frequent target engagement. This was seen in 052 Pvalb Gaba, where Nlgn2 loss was strong but remained target-only, and in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, which had the largest Nlgn2 logFC yet no corrected non-target response, suggesting buffering despite robust engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Scn8a showed that intracellular FGF modulators did not transcriptionally phenocopy Nav1.6 loss: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, strong Fgf13 knockdown was uncorrelated with the Scn8a signature, despite occurring in the same glutamatergic contexts. This supports uncoupling of the intracellular-FGF arm from the Scn8a program, within a broader axon initial segment Ankyrin-G channel-clustering context that includes weak Ank3 convergence and a Scn1b neighbor signal. The negative result for Fgf14 is more tentative because target engagement was mostly weak.

Slc4a7 showed a weak, largely uncoupled transcriptional profile that did not converge with assayed acid-base or ion-transport perturbations in bicarbonate transport and intracellular pH regulation. Correlations with Slc9a7, Slc9a9, Slc12a2, Slc12a5, V-ATPase components, Clcn3/4/5, and Trpm7 were near zero, with the largest absolute pair only r=0.158, so within this target set the Slc4a7 signature was not a reusable shared module. This interpretation is limited because Slc4a7 was the only SLC4 perturbation represented and the correlation test relied on weak Slc4a7 score vectors.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Plxna1 showed sparse, context-specific transcriptomic effects and did not phenocopy assayed semaphorin/plexin pathway neighbors in the two cell types with FDR-level hits, 191 MB P MY GABA and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut. In same-cell comparisons, Plxna1 signatures were only weakly correlated with Nrp1, Nrp2, Sema6a, Plxna2, Plxna4, Rac1, and Kif21a; in CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, Kif21a was the sole FDR downstream hit. These low correlations were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors and may also reflect partial knockdown, weak neighbor engagement, and the limits of a transcriptomic rather than biochemical readout.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Eif4h showed a restricted, cell-type-specific signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where its 200 strongest genes converged most positively with Eif4e and Eif4a2, and Eif4h shared Hexim1 induction with Eif4e. This pattern links the only robust Eif4h response to cap-dependent translation initiation and the eIF4F-associated helicase axis rather than an unrelated stress program. However, the result is exploratory because full-transcriptome correlations were much weaker and Eif4h on-target depletion was not significant.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Vezf1 perturbation showed a narrow but recurrent cross-cell-type signal centered on Zcchc18 down-regulation. Zcchc18 was the only FDR-significant gene in both 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut, and it was also nominally down in the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, where the broader Vezf1 signature contained six FDR-significant genes. This recurrence across inhibitory and glutamatergic populations is the clearest convergence for Vezf1, although the signal is limited to a single gene and does not by itself define a pathway-level mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnpc showed a target-specific, divergent perturbation program in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class rather than a generic hnRNP or spliceosome-neighbor signature. In this primary response class, even the closest non-self perturbations were only weak global matches to the Hnrnpc score vector, with STRING-linked partners Hnrnpa2b1, Hnrnpu, Ddx39b, and Fus near zero to negative, and similarly weak relationships for Srsf1, Prpf6, and Ddx23. This comparison is based on score-vector correlation in one cell class and does not establish equal editing strength across perturbations.

Hoxd10 did not share a transcriptomic state with the other assayed clustered Hox perturbations in the mouse-brain screen, including Hoxd13, Hoxa1, Hoxa3, Hoxa13, Hoxb8, and Hoxc13. Across matched cell types, Hoxd10–Hoxd13 correlations were essentially zero, and the available Hox perturbations produced no FDR-significant genes, arguing against a common HOX-family artifact, rescue, or phenocopy signature in these brain cells. This interpretation is limited because the closest Hox10 paralogs, Hoxa10 and Hoxc10, were not assayed, and all available Hox signatures were weak, compressing correlation dynamic range.

Tfap4 showed a largely flat perturbation profile in this dataset, with no strong positive or negative signature neighbor across the panel and no convergence with related bHLH/E-box transcription-factor perturbations. In contrast, the comparator Max produced a robust active response, including 167 corrected rows, whereas Tfap4 produced none and, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, showed no on-target transcript effect despite 238 Tfap4-targeting cells. These data argue against grouping Tfap4 with the MAX/MYC-like bHLH/E-box response here, while noting that the comparison is within a broad family and does not imply direct TFAP4 partnership with Max or Myc in neurons.

Adipor2 loss produced a transcriptional signature that was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of Appl1, Ppara, Ppard, Pparg, Ppargc1a, Ppargc1b, Prkaa2, Prkag2, Asah1, Smpd3, and Cpt1c across matched neuronal cell classes, so available APPL, AMPK/PPAR, ceramidase, and fatty-acid pathway neighbors did not phenocopy Adipor2 in this basal assay. This suggests mRNA-level uncoupling of Adipor2 from adiponectin-linked pathway neighbors in basal neurons, while leaving open that lipid or kinase signaling outputs may not be captured; notably, Adipor1, Adipoq, Cdh13, and Appl2 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Wdfy3 showed low transcriptomic signature similarity to nearby autophagy, lysosomal, and SQSTM1-pathway perturbations in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic neuron class: correlations with Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Rb1cc1, Sqstm1, Tbk1, Lamp2, Ctsb, and Htt were all small. Thus, in this neuronal context, the Wdfy3 response did not phenocopy core selective macroautophagy or aggrephagy neighbors, although this inference is indirect because it relies on cross-perturbation differential-expression similarity and the comparator guides differed in efficiency and cell counts.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nme7 showed weak, largely orthogonal transcriptomic signatures relative to assayed cilia- and cytoskeleton-adjacent perturbations, so it was not interchangeable with IFT, BBS, RPGRIP1L, FOXJ, RFX, DNAL1, or tubulin perturbations in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Nme7 had its largest nominal transcript decrease but remained nonsignificant; in 308 CB GABA, Dnal1 versus Nme7 reached the strongest negative correlation, yet the absolute correlation was only 0.106. Interpretation is limited because the Nme7 signature itself was weak and direct γTuRC genes and NME paralogs were not in the panel.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mef2a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a signature that was largely uncoupled from single-transcript perturbations of canonical MEF2-associated regulators. In this responsive cell type, Hdac4, Hdac5, Ep300, Crebbp, Mapk1, Atf2, Camk4, Ppp3ca, and Creb1 had near-zero or only weak negative correlations with the Mef2a response, indicating that these available pathway perturbations were poor proxies for Mef2a depletion. This comparison is limited to transcript-abundance perturbations, and the p38 MAPK gene Mapk14, a STRING Mef2a neighbor, was not assayed.

Fktn perturbation produced RNA signatures that were essentially uncoupled from measured α-dystroglycan pathway, ligand, and disease-family perturbations. Across matched cell classes, score correlations between Fktn and Agrn, Crppa, Dag1, Dmd, Dpm1, Large1, and Rxylt1 centered near zero, with only a weak maximum for Dpm1 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut. This pattern persisted even where comparator knockdown was clearer, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, suggesting that different nodes of the DAG1 glycosylation and matrix-linkage axis were not transcriptomically interchangeable; caveats are weak target engagement for some comparators, no FKRP comparator, and use of RNA signatures rather than matriglycan abundance.

Cc2d1a produced transcriptomic signatures that were largely orthogonal to comparator perturbations, with only weak Pearson correlations to Chmp4b, Htr1a, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Crbn, Mef2d, and Deaf1. Thus, in this assay, ESCRT-III/endosomal-sorting, NF-kB, serotonin-receptor, transcription-factor, and intellectual-disability related perturbations did not phenocopy Cc2d1a, despite expected links such as the physical connection to CHMP4B. A caveat is that whole-signature correlations could miss similarity if Cc2d1a elicited only a weak or partially engaged response.

Zfp280d did not phenocopy its closest assayed ZNF280-family paralog, Zfp280c: across 18 shared cell types, their genome-wide perturbation score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, arguing that family membership alone does not predict interchangeable transcriptional outputs in these brain cell classes. This comparison is tempered by weak own-transcript depletion for both Zfp280d and Zfp280c, and by the lack of any stable screen-wide signature neighbor for Zfp280d among the best-inspected cell types.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Napb did not phenocopy nearby SNARE-cycle perturbations. Across shared cell types, Napb score signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Snap25, Stx1b, Stxbp1, and Nsf, indicating that functional proximity in the vesicle-fusion network was not sufficient to produce an interchangeable single-cell RNA signature. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Napb was essentially target-only, whereas Stxbp1 showed a broader transcriptional response, with 67 FDR<0.05 rows. This comparison is based on transcriptomic score correlations, and Nsf target engagement was weak; Napa and Napg were not perturbed.

Lrrtm4 showed no transcriptional substitution by its paralogs: across 21 shared cell types, Lrrtm1 and Lrrtm3 perturbations did not phenocopy the Lrrtm4 genome-wide score vector, with full-signature correlations all weak (|r|≤0.116) and several negative. This uncoupling was noted in the LRRTM4–HSPG/neurexin/RPTP trans-synaptic adhesion context, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. The result comes from weak restricted transcriptome signatures, not direct synapse-density or binding assays.

Fzd6 showed no transcript-level target depletion and no FDR-supported downstream transcriptomic response across all 22 measured Fzd6 cell classes, and this null pattern was not unique to Fzd6: single perturbations of Fzd2, Fzd3, Fzd4, Fzd6, and Fzd9 yielded only one FDR-significant gene across 1.86 million differential-expression rows, with no Frizzled self-transcript reaching significance. In the dataset, single-receptor or Celsr2 perturbations in Wnt/Frizzled planar-cell-polarity and Ca2+ signaling were broadly buffered or transcriptionally sparse, although this comparison reflects mRNA phenotypes only and sparse DE could also indicate weak transcript-level engagement or low receptor expression.

Tpr showed positive signature similarity to a recurrent neighborhood of RNA-processing, mRNA-export, proteasome, and UFMylation perturbations, with Prpf6, Psmc1, Psmc5, Psmb4, Cdc40, Ddx39b, Ufc1, Thoc1, Tnpo3, and Pomp repeatedly ranking among its closest positive neighbors, and Ranbp2 showing partial convergence. The strongest responses were seen in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, suggesting a broader post-transcriptional and proteostasis stress axis, although the score-vector correlations were modest and do not establish direct biochemical interaction.

Guk1 showed near-zero signature correlation with the available nucleotide-related perturbations Nt5c2 and Nme7 across matched cell types, arguing against a simple generic purine-enzyme knockdown program and suggesting that the muted RNA response to Guk1 is target-specific or strongly buffered. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, this fits a GMP/GDP and cGMP-linked nucleotide homeostasis context with buffered or uncoupled downstream transcription involving Pde1a and Uqcrc2. Interpretation is limited because most proximal STRING neighbors were not perturbed in the library and Nme7 target engagement was weak.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Adarb1 perturbation was associated with selective Flnb down-regulation, rather than a generic consequence of perturbing the related Adar enzyme or the AMPA-receptor substrate Gria2. In key comparator contexts including 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Adar or Gria2 showed on-target knockdown but did not reproduce the Adarb1→Flnb decrease, and transcriptome-wide signature correlations between Adarb1 and these comparators were near zero. This effect was observed at the level of mRNA abundance only; editing efficiencies of shared substrates were not compared.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lztfl1 perturbation did not transcriptomically phenocopy BBSome or IFT perturbations in this assay, even in the best-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class. In that thalamic population, Lztfl1 score vectors were nearly orthogonal to Ttc8, Bbs5, Bbs9, Bbip1, Ift88, Ift81, Ift43, Kif3b, Cep164, Cep83, and Cep290, with only weak correlations such as r=0.055 versus Ttc8 and r=0.104 versus Ift88. This suggests that, at the detectable bulk mRNA-signature level, Lztfl1 is not interchangeable with loss of BBSome subunits or related ciliary factors, although interpretation is limited by weak knockdown of several related targets.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Acvr2a, in 308 CB GABA cells, did not phenocopy Acvr2b or other queried TGF-beta-family receptor perturbations despite pathway diagrams that place ACVR2A and ACVR2B as alternative type-II activin receptors. The Acvr2a signature showed poor correlation with Acvr2b, Acvr1, Acvrl1, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, and Tgfbr3, with no receptor exceeding |r|=0.146. This contrast relies on weak, sparse transcriptomic signatures, so the lack of phenocopy could reflect incomplete knockdown, downstream buffering, or missing ligand stimulation.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Pcca showed only weak, biologically non-specific same-cell-type signature neighbors across 308 CB GABA, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut. The strongest non-self correlations were modest, peaking at |r|=0.267 in 308 CB GABA, where Ranbp2 was the top positive neighbor and Wdr26 the top negative; Sphk1 and Sin3a also appeared, alongside Safe_target controls. In 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, the lowest-FDR Pcca row was Acot7 at FDR 0.1846 and Sphk1 reached only r=0.1474, so these restricted correlations do not support a robust or convergent Pcca response module.

Rab28 was mostly uncoupled from available ciliary or retinal-disease-family perturbations in this mouse brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across Arl2bp, Arl3, Bbs5, Bbs9, Cep164, Cep290, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Lztfl1, Rpgrip1l, and Ttc21b, only three FDR hits were seen in 4.8 million tests, and these comparators were near zero in a Rab28-restricted signature-neighbor score. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Rab28 showed the most nominal p<0.001 rows but was itself weakly depleted, so this was not prioritized as a direct Rab28 program; the comparator set and nominal-feature restriction limit interpretation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sptb showed a weak, buffered perturbation response in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class and did not phenocopy stronger spectrin-associated membrane cytoskeleton perturbations. In this matched cell type, Sptb had 154 perturbed cells with zero FDR hits, whereas Sptan1 and Ank3 produced robust corrected effects, and genome-wide signature correlations were near zero with Sptan1, Ank1, Ank2, Ank3, Add1, Add2, Add3, and Epb41l1. This divergence may reflect biology, but the weak Sptb vector also leaves open the possibility of lower guide activity.

Rab18 showed little transcriptional convergence with its canonical activator complex: across the same 21 cell classes, all-gene score correlations between Rab18 and Rab3gap1 or Rab3gap2 were near zero, despite the RAB3GAP-RAB18 ER recruitment and nucleotide-exchange relationship. This argues against a simple model in which partial loss of the RAB3GAP-RAB18 module yields a shared transcriptional signature in these brain cell classes. A key caveat is that all compared perturbations had weak downstream signatures, and Tbc1d20 was not available as an exact comparator.

Ets1 showed no convergence with the screened ETS-family perturbations across all shared assayed neuronal classes: Elf2, Etv6, and Spi1 had very low correlations and did not phenocopy Ets1. This argues against interchangeability between Ets1 and these ETS-family genes in neurons, although the inference is limited by the weak neuronal Ets1 signature. The best documented comparator, Ets2, was not screened, and the endothelial/angiogenesis context in which Ets1/Ets2 buffering is most relevant was absent from this assay.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ctbp1 showed a restricted convergence with Zeb1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where both perturbations aligned on a Stxbp2/Ap1m2/F11r/Hook2/Usp43/St3gal4 module consistent with CTBP-ZEB transcriptional co-repression. Outside this thalamic state, Zeb1, Zeb2, and Chd4 were not broadly Ctbp1-like across matched cell types, so the relationship appears cell-state restricted rather than interchangeable across the brain panel. An apparent Ctbp1-Zeb2 anti-correlation in 308 CB GABA remained exploratory because Zeb2-targeted cells did not show reduced Zeb2 RNA, and correlation rankings may be influenced by weak effects across measured genes.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Iqsec1 depletion produced a target-only transcriptional effect in both 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut cells: despite strong knockdown of Iqsec1, Arf6, Gria1, Gria2, and Dlg4 mRNAs were unchanged, with no other FDR-significant downstream RNA response detected. In the midbrain glutamatergic class, neighboring Dlg4 and Gria2 perturbations were likewise target-only. Thus, the BRAG2/Iqsec1–Arf6 AMPA-receptor internalization module appeared transcriptionally uncoupled from Iqsec1 knockdown here, although protein abundance, receptor surface levels, Arf6-GTP, and electrophysiology were not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Pura showed a distinct perturbation signature in the two Pura-responsive classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, whereas Purb and Purg did not phenocopy it. In these cell types, Purb and especially Purg had near-zero correlation with the Pura response and no FDR-significant signatures, arguing that PUR-domain paralogs were not interchangeable under these guide conditions. The contrast is strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and is supported but sparser in 155 MB Glut, with the important caveat that Purb/Purg transcript knockdown was itself weak after FDR correction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tubb4b perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons did not reproduce the tubulin-paralog compensation seen with Tuba1a perturbation in the same cell type. In this thalamic class, Tuba1a significantly induced Tubb3, Tubb2a, Tuba4a, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, and Tubb5, whereas Tubb4b loss left other tubulin transcripts below FDR; the strongest Tubb4b-related trend was only a nominal, non-FDR increase in Tubb5. This suggests that neuronal tubulin perturbations are not interchangeable at the RNA-signature level, with the contrast strongest in this one cell type.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarcd1 showed a sparse, weak response that was detectable only in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic glutamatergic class, where Ptpn3 trended downward near the FDR threshold and Ankrd40 was increased. The key convergence was that Ptpn3 was also strongly decreased in the same thalamic class after Arid1a, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, and Smarce1 perturbation, linking the weak Smarcd1 signal to a stronger mSWI/SNF/BAF thalamic response module. However, Ptpn3 did not reach FDR<0.05 for Smarcd1 itself, and no direct SMARCD1-to-Ptpn3 mechanism was identified.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gpr68 showed no robust convergence with proton-sensing family members or signature neighbors in this dataset. The closest paralogs, Gpr4, Gpr65, and Gpr132, were not perturbed, so the proton-sensing GPCR family comparison was not directly testable. The strongest Gpr68 score-correlation neighbors were only modest, all confined to the 308 CB GABA cerebellar cell type, and the negative tail included Safe_target-labeled profiles such as Safe_target_70 and Safe_target_15, making the pattern exploratory rather than a confident hidden-module signal.

Hif1a showed no detectable convergence with its expected dimerization partners Arnt or Arnt2: Hif1a score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with both genes, and restricted-signature neighbor searches did not recover either partner or other HIF pathway members. In this basal perturbation setting, weak Hif1a nominal genes therefore should not be treated as a reconstituted hypoxia-response module, including canonical genes such as Vegfa, Slc2a1, Ldha, Epo, and Car9. This contrast comes from weak basal signatures and does not show that the HIF1A–ARNT complex is absent under hypoxia.

Adra2b did not phenocopy Adra2a or related adrenergic/cAMP pathway perturbations in this dataset: across 22 shared cell types, full-signature correlations with Adra2a were essentially zero, with max |r| = 0.033, and the strongest related correlation was still weak, |r| = 0.110 for Gnb1 in a thalamic class. No non-Adra2b perturbation strongly matched or opposed the Adra2b score vector. This lack of convergence is limited to transcriptomic guide-perturbation scores and may partly reflect weak Adra2b engagement, with no coherent FDR-supported Adra2b mRNA output.

Dtnbp1 produced a transcriptomic signature that was essentially orthogonal to the trafficking comparators Ap3b1 and Klc1 in this assay, with mean Dtnbp1–Ap3b1 and Dtnbp1–Klc1 score correlations of 0.0018 and 0.0095, respectively. This suggests that within the BLOC-1/AP-3 endosomal and lysosome-related organelle trafficking context, pathway adjacency did not translate into transcriptomic interchangeability here. A key caveat is that Ap3b1 showed weak on-target depletion, while Klc1 is an indirect comparator rather than a BLOC-1 subunit, even though Klc1 had strong self-knockdown.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fmr1 perturbation did not phenocopy the measured FMRP-CYFIP/eIF4E-AGO module: in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Fmr1 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Fxr1, Cyfip1, Cyfip2, Eif4e, and Ago2. This transcriptomic contrast suggests these post-perturbation scRNA signatures are not interchangeable, although the Fmr1 signature was weak, FXR2 was not targeted, Fxr1 coverage was limited, and this does not argue against biochemical coupling among the proteins.

Zfp654 showed a weak signature, and the assayed predicted STRING-neighborhood comparators Zbtb11, Zfp148, and Tbc1d23 did not phenocopy it. Although Zbtb11 and Zfp148 had FDR-significant perturbation signatures, their full-transcriptome correlations to Zfp654 were near zero in every matched cell type, while Tbc1d23, like Zfp654, had no FDR hits. Thus, STRING proximity here should not be taken as transcriptional interchangeability in the profiled neuronal classes, especially because these comparators were predicted neighbors rather than validated complex members and several higher-ranked STRING partners were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Zbtb11 loss produced an otherwise down-biased signature with a small induced branch in selected neurons. Dhx16 increased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Mtg1 increased in 151, and Ppargc1a increased only in 191 MB P MY GABA, while many mitochondrial and RNA-processing genes remained repressed. This pattern fits a limited, transcript-only homeostatic response within ZBTB11/NRF-2 control of mitochondrial complex I and nucleolar/RNA-processing output, but the induced genes were few and not consistently shared across cell types.

Ptprc showed no FDR-supported neuronal transcriptomic response in glutamatergic or GABAergic classes, including 308 CB GABA, and its correlations with related perturbations were small. Immune-receptor neighbors Cd247, Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd3g, Il2rg and the assayed Src-family neighbor Fyn likewise lacked robust neuronal signatures, whereas the neuronal receptor-PTP Ptprn2 showed direct on-target repression without a broad secondary program. This contrast is consistent with lineage-availability buffering rather than a general failure of receptor-phosphatase perturbations, although key CD45 partners such as Lck, Lyn, Csk, and PTPRCAP were not assayed and all comparisons are transcriptomic.

Cd79b showed no convergent transcriptomic relationship with its obligate partner Cd79a in the brain dataset: both perturbations were FDR-null, and Cd79b-versus-Cd79a score correlations across matched genes and cell classes were small, ranging from -0.032 to 0.117. This suggests that B-cell antigen receptor signaling, including the CD79A/CD79B heterodimer module, was not engaged in these off-lineage cells, and that the weak correlations likely reflect null-signature noise rather than meaningful antagonism or mechanistic separation of the two subunits.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Cfap69 did not behave as an interchangeable ciliary perturbation in this screen. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Cfap69 had 83 and 68 perturbed cells yet showed no target or downstream FDR-significant response, while ciliary-neighbor perturbations were detectable in the same classes, including Ttc8 self-knockdown, Adcy3 effects, and an Ift88→Pcsk1n row. Across 191 MB P MY GABA and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, the broader comparator set remained sparse and target-specific. This uncoupling is consistent with target- or context-specific nonengagement, with the caveat that Adcy3, Ttc8, Ift88, and Bbs5 are pathway neighbors rather than direct CFAP69 complex partners.

Cblb showed near-zero similarity to assayed pathway neighbors in neuronal RNA signatures, not phenocopying Fyn, Sh3kbp1, PI3K subunits (Pik3r1, Pik3r2, Pik3ca, Pik3cb), antigen-receptor genes such as Cd247 and Cd79a, or NF-κB-related neighbors including Tbk1 and Nfkb2. This suggests that the canonical CBL-B immune-receptor module is not recapitulated in these neuronal perturbations, with Cblb appearing buffered and uncorrelated across the tested ubiquitination and TCR/BCR/FCER1 signaling axes. These comparisons rely on restricted-signature correlations, and direct contrast with Cbl or Cblc paralogs was not possible.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zmynd8 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut most closely matched Kdm5c, making Kdm5c the top positive signature neighbor, while available NuRD-related perturbations Chd4, Gatad2b, Mbd2 and the same-family Zmynd11 did not phenocopy the Zmynd8 response. This supports a ZMYND8-associated KDM5C axis in the main responsive thalamic class, which also showed Zfp532 induction and synaptic effector changes, but the similarity was modest overall (Pearson 0.186), and Gatad2a was measured as a transcript rather than directly perturbed.

Chrne showed uncoupled, weak transcriptomic relationships in mouse brain cells: its perturbation signatures did not converge with skeletal-muscle nicotinic AChR subunits Chrna1, Chrnb1, Chrnd, or Chrng, nor with Agrn-Musk-Lrp4 neighborhood genes, even though these genes belong to the known neuromuscular receptor network. Across the dataset, same-cell-type Pearson correlations were weak, with a maximum absolute correlation of 0.121, and no Chrne signature had a close whole-transcriptome neighbor. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA, the nominal Chrne-associated signal was strongest, but no gene reached FDR<0.1; the lack of convergence may reflect little engagement of several lowly expressed muscle subunits in brain transcriptomes.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Atp6v1e1 showed a weak positive signature convergence in 052 Pvalb Gaba: despite no FDR-significant differentially expressed genes for Atp6v1e1 in this cell type, its whole-transcriptome profile was most similar to Atp6v0c and Atp6v1b2, the top two positive perturbation neighbors. This restricted convergence is consistent with a V-ATPase complex relationship in fast-spiking inhibitory neurons, but the correlations were modest and the shared nominal genes, including stress-associated signals such as Ddit3, Herpud1, Dusp1, and Cyp46a1, should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than a validated pathway.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Ptprf showed a restricted, weakly connected perturbation profile: in the two most engaged cell types, 155 MB Glut and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, perturbations of Ptprd, Ptprt, Ntrk3, Slitrk1, Il1rapl1, and Nrxn1 were essentially uncorrelated with Ptprf, and even the strongest whole-dataset neighbors had |r| ≤ 0.073. In MB Glut, Ptprt had a significant on-target hit and self-depletion but still did not phenocopy Ptprf. These correlations come from precomputed Wilcoxon signatures, are limited to two cell types, and Ptprs was not targeted.

Asah1 perturbation did not produce a corrected compensatory transcriptional response in a 28-gene lysosomal ceramide hydrolysis and sphingolipid metabolism panel. Across genes including Asah2, Acer1-3, Smpd1-4, Sphk1, Sphk2, Sgpl1, Ugcg, Gba, Gba2, Psap, Lamp2, Npc1, and Npc2, the dataset showed no corrected expression changes, suggesting no obvious acute transcriptional feedback through adjacent sphingolipid genes after Asah1 loss. This conclusion is limited to transcript measurements and does not address ceramide or sphingosine lipid abundance.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nsf showed weak, restricted transcriptomic similarity and no global convergence with canonical SNARE perturbations. Across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA cells, the strongest same-cell correlation was only r=0.189, with Atp6v0c as the top neighbor in 191 MB P MY GABA; other weak neighbors included Atp6v1a, Cltc, Psmb4, and Zic3. Global correlations with Napb, Snap25, Stx1b, and Vamp1 were near zero, suggesting buffered or uncoupled behavior for the NSF/SNAP-dependent cis-SNARE disassembly pathway, although this inference is limited by very small score vectors and almost no FDR-resolved genes.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Vps13d showed a sparse, paralog-specific transcriptional profile rather than a shared VPS13-family signature in acute mouse neurons. Across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Vps13a, Vps13b, Vps13c, and Vps13d each produced only a few FDR-level events, and those events occurred in different targets and cell types. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, the only FDR-significant non-target Vps13d hit was Tmx3, whereas in 155 MB Glut Vps13d remained nonsignificant even as Vps13c and several mitochondrial and trafficking neighbors showed signals; not all paralogs were assayed in all cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Serpini1 showed a sparse, cell-context-specific perturbation pattern that was not interchangeable with other assayed serpin-family genes. In the confidently engaged Serpini1 context, correlations between Serpini1 and either Serpine2 or Serpinb6a were near zero, indicating divergent transcriptomic effects. This was especially evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic neurons, where Serpine2 produced an FDR-level transcriptional signature that Serpini1 did not share. These comparisons are limited to the serpin perturbations present in the panel and do not address biochemical inhibitor specificity.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Tlr7 basal Perturb-seq signatures were uncoupled from annotated endosomal TLR pathway neighbors in Tlr7-overlapping neuronal classes, including 054 CNU-MGE GABA and 145 MH-LH TH Glut. Despite pathway proximity within TLR7/8–IRF7–NF-kappa-B innate signaling, perturbations of Tlr8, Tlr9, Irf7, Nfkb1, Tlr3, and Il17rd did not phenocopy Tlr7; instead, related targets produced only isolated singleton FDR hits, such as Tlr8, Irf7, and Il17rd in 054 CNU-MGE GABA. This comparison is limited to basal-state transcriptomic correlations, and key literature partners Myd88, Unc93b1, Irak1, and Irak4 were not measured here.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Gphn in superficial cortical IT glutamatergic neurons showed a restricted signature pattern in which Gabrg2 and Grin2a were positive same-cell neighbors, whereas Grin2b, Ap2s1, Shank2, Syngap1, and Camk2a tended to oppose it. This was seen in both 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where Grin2a was the top positive neighbor and Gabrg2 ranked ninth, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, which reproduced the Grin2a/Gabrg2-positive and Grin2b/Syngap1/Camk2a-negative pattern. Because absolute pairwise correlations were low, this supports only a rank-based synaptic receptor-neighbor relationship, not a deterministic pathway order.

Htr1f showed a weak, broadly sparse transcriptomic phenotype that fit a family-wide pattern across serotonin receptor perturbations rather than an Htr1f-specific anomaly. Across all 21 Htr1f-tested mouse-brain cell classes, robust Htr1f-dependent differential expression was generally absent, and among 241 Htr-family target-by-cell-type tests only two genes reached FDR < 0.05. Htr1f score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Htr1a, Htr1b, Htr2a, Htr2b, Htr2c, Htr3a, Htr3b, Htr4, Htr6, and Htr7 perturbations, with median |r| = 0.0136 and maximum |r| = 0.069, so shared serotonin-receptor pathway annotation did not predict a shared basal transcriptomic module; this comparison does not address acute serotonin- or drug-stimulated signaling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kdm5c showed a distinct neuronal perturbation profile that Kdm5b did not reproduce in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the only cell class with an FDR-resolved Kdm5c signature, Kdm5c loss produced an up-dominant TH response within a KDM5/H3K4 demethylation and transcriptional repression context, with genes such as Ptgds, Capn3, Zfp532, and Ache implicated, whereas Kdm5b was buffered and nearly uncorrelated with the Kdm5c TH signature. Across the same 22 shared cell classes, Kdm5b had no FDR-significant genes, although weak Kdm5b target-RNA depletion could have contributed to this negative result.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Bmpr1b showed its strongest cortical signal in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut cells as a near-threshold increase in Mrgbp, but this did not align with a broader BMP/TGF-beta receptor or SMAD signature. Correlations with related perturbations, including Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Bmpr1a, Bmpr2, Fkbp1a, Smad1, Smad4, Smad6, Smad9, Tgfbr1, and Tgfbr2, were essentially zero. Given that Mrgbp did not pass FDR<0.05 and the cell count was 32, this appears to be a weak isolated candidate rather than a coherent canonical BMP transcriptional program.

Grik2 showed near-zero transcriptome-wide signature similarity to other kainate-receptor subunits and nearby glutamate-receptor or PSD/TARP pathway perturbations. In this mRNA assay, perturbations of Grik1, Grik3, Grik4, Grik5, AMPA/NMDA subunits including Gria1 and Grin2d, as well as Dlg4 and Cacng8, did not phenocopy Grik2, despite their known complex or pathway relationships. Most Grik2 effects were weak, so this is best interpreted as a lack of detectable phenocopy rather than evidence for strong antagonism.

Lyrm4 showed a weak, nonconvergent Perturb-seq profile: in matched cell types, its score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with the same-pathway Fe-S biogenesis perturbations Nfs1 and Isca2, so the dataset did not show the expected signature convergence within mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis. This contrast is tempered by sparse target engagement, with both Lyrm4 and Nfs1 weakly represented and Isca2 significant only for its own transcript in one cell type, arguing against inferring ISC activity from the Lyrm4 profile alone.

Pkd1 showed a silent transcriptional signature in this mouse neuronal scRNA-seq screen: across the same 21 cell types, Pkd1 produced no FDR-significant differential-expression rows, whereas Tsc1 and Tsc2 produced strong signatures with 1,150 and 423 significant rows, respectively. This contrast suggests that the assay could detect neuronal TSC-mTOR vulnerability, but that program was not activated by Pkd1 loss here. A key caveat is that reported PKD1-TSC2-mTOR coupling comes mainly from kidney cystogenesis literature rather than neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ttc8 did not show a strong shared transcriptomic module with other available BBSome or cilium-pathway perturbations. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, the clearest Ttc8 target-engagement signal and only FDR-positive contrast was Ttc8 itself, while cross-perturbation neighbors were weak: Bbs5, Bbs9, and Bbip1 had weaker on-target mRNA depletion and were nearly uncorrelated with Ttc8, and even whole-transcriptome neighbors were small in magnitude, with Rora r=0.094 and Iqsec1 r=-0.059. This supports a negative module result rather than a unique TTC8 mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Hsf1 perturbation most strongly reduced a compact HSF1-linked heat-shock chaperone module, with recurrent decreases in Hsph1, Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Ahsa2, and Stip1. The clearest signal was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, with smaller but similar signatures in 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. This pattern supports a canonical HSF1 transcriptional output rather than a broad neuronal stress program, although direct Hsf1 mRNA knockdown was only nominal and the assay captured basal, not induced heat-shock, state.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Hsf1 perturbation produced a cell-type-specific heat-shock/chaperone transcriptional program that was not recapitulated by direct Hsp90ab1 knockdown. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Hsf1 loss generally decreased Hsph1, Hsp90aa1, Ahsa2, Stip1, and Rsrp1, with the strongest effects in glutamatergic groups, whereas Hsp90ab1 loss strongly reduced Hsp90ab1 mRNA but only weakly and often oppositely shifted several HSF1-responsive HSP transcripts. This contrast is transcriptomic rather than a direct HSF1-activity assay, and most Hsp90ab1 feedback-like increases were weak and not FDR-significant.

Taf1b showed no robust signature neighbor or convergent module in the assayed library. Across shared cell types, score correlations with the available Pol I/TAF comparators Rrn3, Myc, and Taf1 were near zero, and the largest absolute empirical correlation to any perturbation in any Taf1b cell type reached only 0.184. This is consistent with the absence of a stable downstream program for Taf1b in the RNA polymerase I/SL1 rDNA transcription initiation context, although interpretation is limited because direct SL1 comparators such as Tbp, Taf1a, Taf1c, Taf1d, and Polr1a were not assayed.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Taok1 showed its strongest signature-neighbor pattern specifically in 308 CB GABA cells, where it aligned positively with Wdr26, Cckar, and Msx2 and negatively with Ranbp2, Fbxo11, and B9d1. However, Taok1 self-knockdown in 308 CB GABA was weak and not nominally significant, while Wdr26 and Ranbp2 had much stronger cerebellar signatures, so this should be treated as an exploratory hypothesis about a shared cerebellar GABAergic cell state rather than a canonical TAOK pathway.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Ap1b1 perturbation produced only one FDR-significant non-target signal: Napa was decreased in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut cells. However, this same signature did not show detectable Ap1b1 transcript reduction, so the Napa decrease is best treated as a target-uncoupled, trafficking-adjacent exploratory marker rather than a secure AP1B1 transcriptional response. This interpretation is reinforced by the small number of perturbed cells in that cell type (55) and by the fact that Atp6v1a and other nominal partners did not survive FDR correction.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Iqsec2 showed weak target engagement in this dataset, and Iqsec1 did not rescue or mirror it. In 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut, Iqsec1 had clear on-target RNA depletion where Iqsec2 did not, while whole-signature Iqsec1–Iqsec2 score correlations were near zero in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In 151, the largest Iqsec2 signature included a nominal Cux1 row but no FDR<0.05 genes. These transcriptomic contrasts are confounded by different knockdown strengths and do not establish distinct protein mechanisms.

Mitf showed no strong similarity to any other perturbation across all 22 Mitf-tested cell classes: whole-transcriptome Mitf signatures lacked a clear correlated neighborhood, with only tiny correlations to other targets (|r| ≤ 0.174) and even a safe-target guide among the top absolute neighbors. Because Tfe3, Tfeb, and Tfec were not included in the perturbation set, the screen could not directly test redundancy within the MiT/TFE transcription-factor family, so functional compensation by these paralogs remains unresolved.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Npas3 showed no multiple-testing-corrected differential-expression hits across the dataset, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, even though the same DE table clearly detected bHLH-PAS transcription-factor output from the related circadian factors Bmal1 and Clock, with strong Dbp and Nr1d2 responses in those classes. This pattern suggests the Npas3 null is more consistent with target- or state-specific buffering than with a general inability of the assay to read out transcription-factor programs, while noting that CLOCK/BMAL1 are assay comparators rather than mechanistic substitutes for an NPAS3 complex.

Nkx3-1 showed a weak profile that was not rescued by related perturbations or by any signature-neighbor convergence in this dataset. A library-wide search found no non-self perturbation with correlation beyond |r|=0.125 to any Nkx3-1 cell-class score vector, and the assayed NKX-family perturbations were nearly orthogonal to Nkx3-1, with maximum |r| values of 0.069 for Nkx2-1, 0.054 for Nkx2-5, and 0.065 for Nkx6-2. These results argue against a shared NKX homeobox perturbation module here, although the correlations were computed from rank-like Wilcoxon score vectors dominated by a weak Nkx3-1 signal.

Ptchd1 showed no convergence with the postsynaptic-density synaptic perturbation module: its whole-transcriptome signature was essentially orthogonal to Dlg4, Shank2, Shank3, Nlgn3, and Nrxn1 in the matched cell types assayed. Thus, despite reported postsynaptic PTCHD1 interactions, the perturbation did not collapse onto a generic synaptic-ASD or postsynaptic scaffold transcriptional program. This separation should be interpreted cautiously, because physical protein interactions do not require shared differential-expression signatures and target engagement may differ across perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Scn8a shows a recurrent but weak positive signature convergence with Ank3 in engaged or near-engaged neuronal subclasses, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 308 CB GABA, where Ank3 ranks second or third among related perturbations; Scn1b is also a neighbor in some contexts. This links the signal to the axon initial segment Ankyrin-G channel-clustering module, but the shared module is much smaller than Ank3’s broader transcriptional effect, with low absolute correlations derived from Wilcoxon score vectors rather than validated molecular complexes.

Atxn7 did not yield a corrected perturbation signature consistent with the expected SAGA/STAGA histone acetyltransferase and deubiquitination module in this assay. Although ATXN7 is a SAGA component, measured SAGA-neighbor transcripts including Usp22, Atxn7l3, Eny2, Kat2a, Trrap, Supt3, Tada1, Supt7l, and Taf5l showed no FDR-significant change after Atxn7 perturbation. The strongest response was limited to two nominal, nonrecurrent hits in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 308 CB GABA likewise lacked corrected effects, so this result is best interpreted as pathway nonrecovery with weak Atxn7 knockdown rather than evidence that ATXN7 is dispensable.

Tfcp2 showed essentially no convergence with the related perturbations Ubp1 and Grhl2: same-cell Pearson correlations between the Tfcp2 score vector and Ubp1 or Grhl2 stayed near zero, providing no evidence here for a shared TFCP2-family RNA polymerase II transcriptional regulation signature across the measured mouse cell classes. This is notable given reported TFCP2/UBP1 family relationships and possible redundancy, but the result is mechanistically cautious because Tfcp2 knockdown was weak and the Grhl2 target transcript was largely uninformative in this dataset.

Dalrd3 partial knockdown did not show convergence with available RNA/tRNA-biogenesis neighbor perturbations. Across the 23 assayed cell classes, Rars2 and Polr3b, which are only indirect STRING-neighborhood comparators rather than METTL2 complex members, had near-zero genome-wide correlations with Dalrd3, and in the 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut class the strongest whole-signature neighbors were still very weak, with Kat6a at r=0.105 and Epha5 at r=-0.081. These data argue against a large shared transcriptional state downstream of Dalrd3, although interpretation is limited because Rars2 and Polr3b showed weak on-target engagement.

Htr2c showed essentially no transcriptomic convergence with other serotonin-receptor perturbations, including the closest 5-HT2 comparators Htr2a and Htr2b, whose mean same-cell correlations with Htr2c were only 0.0115 and 0.00669, while Htr1a, Htr1b, Htr1f, Htr3a, Htr3b, Htr4, Htr6, and Htr7 were similarly near zero. This indicates that the weak Htr2c profile does not define a shared serotonin-receptor or Gq-PLC-Ca2+ signaling module involving Plcb1, Itpr1, Prkca, or Prkcg. In 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, the largest Htr2c neighbor correlations were observed, but they still remained small, and most serotonin-receptor perturbations also had weak on-target rows, so the result is a lack of shared transcriptomic signal rather than a receptor-family hierarchy.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Gli1 showed a weak, exploratory positive restricted-signature convergence with Cdon in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells: Cdon was the top positive perturbation neighbor across the top 100 Gli1-responsive genes, but this relationship attenuated when expanded to the top 500 genes. This same-cell-type alignment is the only hint in the dataset that an SHH receptor-proximal component can track with Gli1 in a neuronal class, yet the broader SHH receptor and SMO-proximal signaling program remained mostly uncoupled, so the observation is suggestive rather than a robust pathway cascade.

Taok1 perturbation produced transcriptional signatures that were not interchangeable with the available TAO-MAPK stress and JNK pathway perturbations: across 20 Taok1-shared cell types, all-gene score correlations with Map2k6, Mapk8, Mapk9, Map3k7, Jund, and Atf2 were uniformly weak, with absolute maxima no greater than 0.207. In 308 CB GABA cells, the strongest Taok1 neighbors instead involved Wdr26/Cckar/Msx2 and Ranbp2/Fbxo11/B9d1 rather than these MAPK/JNK genes. This comparison is limited because Taok2, Taok3, and Map2k3 were not in the library, and steady-state transcriptome correlations may not track acute kinase-substrate relationships.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sall1 perturbation in neurons was largely uncoupled from SALL1-NuRD and related chromatin-remodeler signatures: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Chd4, Chd8, Chd2, Kdm5c, and Ctbp1 showed robust effects, Sall1 had 0 FDR hits despite 201 perturbed cells, and in 308 CB GABA the strongest unbiased Sall1 neighbors were still weak. Across all-gene Wilcoxon score vectors, Sall1 was near-uncorrelated with Chd4, Gatad2b, Mbd2, Hdac4, Hdac5, Chd2, Chd8, Kdm5c, and Ctbp1, although this analysis is dominated by the weak Sall1 signatures and several comparators are broad pathway neighbors rather than direct SALL1 cofactors.

Atl1 loss was uncoupled from canonical unfolded protein response induction in these neuronal transcriptomes: Hspa5, Ddit3, Xbp1, Atf4, Atf6, Hsp90b1, Calr, and related ER-stress markers were not detectably induced at FDR<0.05, and no secondary transcript-level hits survived multiple-testing correction. This suggests the ER-localized perturbation does not manifest as a simple Hspa5/Ddit3/Xbp1-type ER-stress signature here, although the readout was transcript-only, so mild, transient, isoform-specific, or protein-level UPR activity could have been missed.

Kcnt1 showed no support for using its Slo2 paralog Kcnt2 as a transcriptional proxy in this Perturb-seq assay. Kcnt2 perturbation was also weak, with no FDR-significant rows, and across matched cell types its signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Kcnt1 over the strongest Kcnt1 genes, consistent with only a weak and nonconcordant response in sodium-activated potassium channel activity/Slo2 Slack-Slick family programs. Because both perturbations had weak target engagement, this rules out only a strong shared RNA signature within this assay.

Taf1 showed near-zero transcriptomic correlation with the only queried general transcription factor neighbor, Gtf2h5, across overlapping cell types, so the screen did not reveal a Gtf2h5 phenocopy of Taf1 in the RNA polymerase II/TFIID transcription initiation context. However, this comparison was weak for evaluating core TFIID biology because the perturbation panel lacked Tbp and the core Taf2–Taf13 partners; since Gtf2h5 is a TFIIH subunit rather than a TFIID TAF, the absence of a related-target signature should not be overinterpreted as Taf1 specificity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Adgrl1 perturbation produced strong self-transcript depletion in several engaged cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, but little downstream RNA change. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Adgrl2 and Adgrl3 were also directly engaged, the whole-transcriptome signatures were nearly orthogonal to Adgrl1 (Adgrl1–Adgrl2 r=0.018; Adgrl1–Adgrl3 r=0.036), and Adgrl1 loss did not detectably increase Adgrl2 or Adgrl3 transcripts. Adgrl3 also engaged 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where Adgrl1 was not FDR-significant; these descriptive correlations are dominated by each paralog’s self-transcript row.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gucy2e showed only an exploratory, cerebellar-GABA-restricted signature pattern: in 308 CB GABA, its score vector aligned moderately with Wdr26 and Dstyk and opposed B9d1, Fbxo11, and Dnajb4, rather than tracking known RetGC pathway members. This was the only cell class with a sizeable nominal Gucy2e tail, yet no genes reached FDR significance, so the observed neighbor structure is weak, single-cell-type-specific, and may reflect a generic cerebellar GABA state or noise rather than Gucy2e biology.

Gstm5 showed a weak transcriptomic signature that did not converge with Gpx4, the only assayed comparator in the related glutathione-associated peroxide defense network. Across 22 shared cell groups, Gstm5–Gpx4 score-vector correlations were essentially zero (median r = 0.0169), with the most negative restricted comparison in 308 CB GABA, supporting orthogonality rather than a shared antioxidant or peroxide-detoxification response. This interpretation is limited because both signatures were weak in this dataset, most related antioxidant neighbors were not assayed, and Gpx4 transcript itself was not measured as a target-engagement row.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Dctn1 perturbation showed a convergent sterol-response program with Dync1h1, the cytoplasmic dynein heavy chain, which was the top non-Dctn1 signature neighbor in the strongest Dctn1-responsive classes and recapitulated a restricted version of the sterol module in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, including genes such as Insig1, Msmo1, Fdps, Hmgcr, and Srebf2. This supports a dynein-dynactin transport-axis origin rather than a Dctn1-only artifact, although overall correlations were modest, other dynactin subunits were not tested, and Dync1h1 did not reproduce every Dctn1-responsive cell type.

Htr7 showed a receptor-level null relative to detectable intracellular cAMP nodes: despite its curated placement in HTR7–G alpha(s)–adenylate cyclase signaling, Htr7 did not converge with Htr4, Htr6, Gnas, Prkaca, Adcy3, or Pde10a signatures by full-transcriptome correlation, and the assayed Gs-coupled serotonin receptors were FDR-negative at the mRNA signature level. In contrast, Prkaca, Adcy3, and to a lesser extent Pde10a showed detectable guide engagement in selected contexts, suggesting weak or buffered receptor-level transcriptional responses rather than absence of a measurable cAMP axis; this remains a pathway-level comparison rather than matched epistasis.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Hsf4 loss was not Hsf1-like in these brain cells: across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Hsf1 perturbation repressed an HSF1 heat-shock chaperone/proteostasis module comprising Hsph1, Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Ahsa2, Rsrp1, Stip1, and Mat2a, whereas the corresponding Hsf4 tests were flat with FDR=1.0 and Hsf4 signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Hsf1 or Hsp90ab1. The Hsf4 signal itself was weak, so this supports lack of an Hsf1-like output rather than a full map of HSF paralogs.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Reg1 showed no compelling signature neighbor in this brain Perturb-seq screen: across cell types, including 308 CB GABA and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, score-vector correlations with other perturbations remained weak, with a maximum absolute Pearson r of 0.206, and some top-ranked neighbors were even safe-target controls such as Safe_target_1 rather than disease genes like Cckar, Atp6v1e1, or Ednrb. Although 046 CTX-CGE GABA had the most nominal Reg1-associated genes and 308 CB GABA had the strongest positive neighbor correlation, neither produced corrected hits or pathway-level convergence, and weak signatures make neighbor ranks unstable.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnb2 showed a weak or null transcriptional effect in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut: unlike Kcnb1, its perturbation produced no FDR-significant genes and did not induce the Bdnf/Vgf/Zbtb16/Scg2/Nptx2 module seen after Kcnb1 perturbation in the same cell class. Genome-wide score vectors for the Kv2 paralogs were essentially uncorrelated, underscoring a paralog-specific divergence in delayed-rectifier potassium-channel biology. This contrast is transcriptomic, however, and Kcnb1 had more perturbed cells than Kcnb2; it does not test Kv2.2 protein localization or gating.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Atp6v0c showed a much stronger transcriptomic effect than other assayed V-ATPase subunits, indicating these perturbations were not interchangeable. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Atp6v0c yielded 537 FDR genes, with Atp6v0a1 repression and a stress-up, calcium- and synaptic-down program, whereas Atp6ap1, Atp6ap2, Atp6v0a1, Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2, and Atp6v1e1 produced only 2, 2, 1, 0, 0, and 0 despite strong own-transcript depletion for Atp6ap1, Atp6ap2, and Atp6v0a1. A major 052 Pvalb Gaba response also showed Atp6v0a1 co-down with Jun, Crem, Ecel1, and Ddit3 induction. Because the assay measures transcript knockdown, residual protein, gRNA potency, and subunit stoichiometry may explain part of this noninterchangeability within the V-ATPase organelle acidification pathway.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ift43 showed weak or absent convergence with related ciliary perturbations in this assay, particularly in 308 CB GABA cells. Although several ciliary genes such as Ttc8, Cplane1, Arl3, Sdccag8, B9d1, and Bbs5 produced at least one significant transcriptomic hit somewhere in the atlas, Ift43 and the same-IFT-A neighbor Ttc21b had none, and their full-signature correlation never exceeded r = 0.037. The strongest Ift43 match was only a weak correlation with B9d1 in 308 CB GABA (r = 0.208), suggesting that IFT-A physical proximity did not translate into interchangeable mRNA signatures here; this inference is limited to profiled perturbations and transcriptomic readouts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cdc40 showed a perturbation signature that converged most with core spliceosome perturbations, especially Prpf6, Ddx23, U2af2, and also Snrnp70, with Tpr as a positive neighbor, rather than with broader RNA-binding factors such as Srrm2 or Ddx39b. This pattern was seen in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, within a pre-mRNA splicing/activated spliceosome context. The convergence was strongest when analysis was restricted to Cdc40 FDR genes; genome-wide correlations were positive but modest, and Ppil1 was not present in the perturbation library.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sema5a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed the only FDR-significant on-target depletion, but after correction it produced little to no trans-mRNA response. In the same cell class, Plxna2 was likewise essentially on-target-only, and neighboring semaphorin/plexin perturbations including Plxnc1, Plxna4, Sema6a, Nrp1, and Nrp2 also lacked corrected trans signatures, suggesting that receptor proximity within Sema5A glycosaminoglycan and plexin guidance signaling does not predict an acute transcriptomic match here. This refines rather than contradicts prior Sema5A–Plexin biology, since PLXNB3 and Sema5b were not perturbed and PLXNA2 evidence comes from dentate granule cells, not this thalamic glutamatergic class.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Ndufs2 showed a weak, Pvalb interneuron–restricted convergence with Ndufs3: in 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, Ndufs3 ranked 4th of 2,039 perturbations by Pearson correlation across the 80 largest nominal nonself Ndufs2 genes, consistent with a biologically coherent Complex I neighborhood. This signal remained exploratory, however, because the comparison used a restricted signature, Ndufs3 depletion in Pvalb reached only FDR=0.0797, and Ndufs3 had no nonself FDR hits. Related Complex I perturbations were engaged in Pvalb but did not reproduce the Mllt10/Ppil4 response seen after Ndufs2 perturbation.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Rpgrip1l showed a weak perturbation whose transcriptional effects were largely undetected across many brain cell classes, including cortical glutamatergic neurons, multiple GABAergic groups, thalamic glutamatergic cells, midbrain, and cerebellar GABA neurons. Canonical ciliary transition-zone and Hedgehog/Gli markers remained uncoupled from the perturbation: Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Shh, Smo, and ciliary partners such as Ahi1, B9d1, Cep290, Ift88, Tctn1, and Tmem67 were not detectably shifted. Even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, no transcript reached corrected significance, consistent with the caveat that this was a weak RNA perturbation rather than a null developmental or ciliary-localization assay.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Rorb knockdown appeared uncoupled from the canonical ROR/RORE circadian module. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where Rorb target RNA was most clearly depleted, Arntl, Clock, Npas2, Nr1d1, Nr1d2, Cry1, Cry2, Per1-3, Dbp, Tef, Rora, and Rorc showed no detectable shift, and correlations between the Rorb signature and perturbations of Rora, Rorc, Nr1d1/2, Bmal1, Clock, Cry1/2, and Tef were near zero in L4-5 IT, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 308 CB GABA. This inference is limited by phase dependence and the restricted panel/correlation design rather than a synchronized clock assay.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Syn1 did not behave as a transcriptomic phenocopy of Syn2 or Syn3 across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. After removing on-target rows, Syn1–Syn2 and Syn1–Syn3 downstream score correlations were near zero in strongly engaged Syn1 contexts, including 155 MB Glut. Syn2 showed weaker target engagement than Syn1, and Syn3 showed none at FDR level, so these restricted-signature comparisons argue against interchangeable synapsin signatures but do not quantify biological redundancy.

Trappc10 showed a buffered transcriptomic response, and the other assayed TRAPP-related perturbations, Trappc9 and Trappc6b, were similarly FDR-null with near-zero whole-signature correlations to Trappc10. Thus, despite their shared annotation in the TRAPP II vesicle tethering/RAB-GEF module and known functional relatedness, these data did not recover a strong shared TRAPP loss-of-function mRNA program. Because all three perturbation signatures were weak, the target-target correlations are difficult to interpret and should be viewed cautiously.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Usp48 perturbation in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuron population showed a responsive transcriptional signature, but it did not detectably activate or repress the canonical TRAF2/RELA/NF-kappaB mRNA readout: Traf2, Traf6, Rela, Nfkb1, Nfkbia, and Tnfaip3 were not FDR-significant. Thus, despite USP48’s curated linkage to TRAF2/RELA-associated NF-kappaB biology, the mouse-neuron response at this endpoint should not be interpreted as a canonical NF-kappaB transcriptional output. A caveat is that NF-kappaB regulation can be post-translational or occur at genes or time points not captured here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Scarb2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons showed a narrow transcriptional effect, with the strongest supported on-target signal largely limited to Scarb2 itself, and it did not phenocopy broader Rab7/Vps35 endosomal-retromer trafficking perturbations. In this cell type, Rab7 and Vps35 produced much broader responses, with 501 and 17 FDR-significant genes, respectively, yet their score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Scarb2. This contrast appears strongest in this one cell type and is based on RNA signature correlation rather than direct trafficking assays, cautioning against treating lysosomal trafficking perturbations as interchangeable.

Mbl2 perturbation left the measured lectin-complement program transcriptionally unchanged: across 35 assayed genes, including Mbl2, Mbl1, Masp1, Masp2, C2, C3, C4b, C1qa/C1qb/C1qc, Cfb, Cfd, Cfh, Cfi, Cfp, Serping1, Cr2, Itgam, and Itgb2, no transcript showed significant induction or repression, with 699 tests yielding no FDR-significant hits and a maximum absolute score of 2.139. This suggests the lectin pathway was transcriptionally uncoupled from Mbl2 loss in this dataset, while noting that the readout is mRNA only and does not capture extracellular complement cleavage, C3 deposition, or opsonization.

Homer2 showed transcriptional uncoupling from canonical mGluR1/5-Homer-IP3R/Shank postsynaptic scaffold genes: genome-wide Perturb-seq correlations with Grm1, Grm5, Shank2, Shank3, Dlg4, and Itpr1 were essentially zero, including in 046 CTX-CGE GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Homer2 had nominal on-target signal. Thus, physical membership in the scaffold did not translate into interchangeable RNA signatures in this assay. A caveat is that several comparator knockdowns were stronger than Homer2 knockdown, so the near-zero correlations could partly reflect insufficient Homer2 perturbation rather than no shared biology.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Kalrn did not broadly phenocopy its paralog Trio in this Perturb-seq dataset. The only convergence was a weak, cell-type-restricted restricted-signature correlation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, where Trio was a weak positive neighbor of Kalrn (r=0.290 across the top 200 Kalrn genes); in all other cell types, correlations ranged from -0.128 to 0.171. Thus, despite their shared placement in Rho GTPase/actin-cytoskeleton signaling, Kalrn and Trio appeared transcriptionally uncoupled here, and this comparison does not represent an FDR-supported shared differential-expression program.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Gprc5b perturbation in 052 Pvalb Gaba cells produced a self-transcript-only signature: the targeted Gprc5b RNA was significantly reduced, but no other transcripts reached FDR significance. The same pattern was seen for Gpr158, Gabbr1, and Gabra1 in this cell class, suggesting a convergent neuronal receptor response with buffered downstream steady-state mRNA changes in mature inhibitory neurons. This comparison is limited to the profiled genes and this single cell type, and it does not address electrophysiological outputs.

Hoxa13 showed near-zero transcriptomic signature correlation with Hox13 paralogs and TALE cofactors in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq screen: its perturbation scores were nearly uncorrelated with Hoxd13, Hoxc13, Hoxa1, Hoxa3, Hoxb8, Hoxd10, Meis1, Meis2, Pbx1, and Pbx3. Thus, despite known Hox/TALE and Hoxa13–Hoxd13 relationships from other systems, Hoxa13 did not behave like these related perturbations here, arguing against treating them as interchangeable in adult brain cells. This comparison reflects transcriptomic output rather than direct binding, and prior literature is largely from embryonic limb or reproductive tissues rather than brain.

Hspa8 shows positive signature convergence with proteasome-subunit perturbations rather than with most annotated chaperone perturbations, placing Hspa8 loss in a broader ubiquitin-proteasome protein quality-control state. Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, or Pomp were top-5 positive Hspa8 neighbors in 17 of 21 cell types, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Psmc5, Psmb4, and Psmc1 correlated with Hspa8 at r=0.250–0.290. The signal was also notable in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, but correlations were modest overall, with a maximum non-self r of 0.334, so the convergence does not by itself establish direct epistasis.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Il1rap did not show the expected convergence with its receptor-pair partner Il1r1. Across 21 shared cell classes, the Il1rap and Il1r1 perturbation signatures were essentially orthogonal on average, with mean Pearson r near zero, and in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 308 CB GABA they were weakly anti-correlated rather than convergent. This contrast is limited by weak signatures: Il1r1 had no FDR-significant response or target-transcript signal, and no clear canonical IL-1/IL-33/IL-36 to MYD88-IRAK-TRAF6–NF-kappaB transcriptional module was detected.

Sox3 showed no FDR-supported recurrent pathway: nominal outliers such as Nenf, Armcx3, Syn2, and Rnf14 were sparse, did not form a cross-cell-type module, and the thalamic score vector lacked a high-correlation positive or negative neighbor signature. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the best-powered Sox3 class had no FDR hits and contrasted with Sox2 and Sox5 on Tnnt1, Stam, and Dgkh within SOXB1 / sequence-specific RNA polymerase II transcriptional regulation. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, nearest signals remained nominal, while 217 P MY Pineal Glut was underpowered. These recurrence and correlation screens used Wilcoxon score vectors rather than raw single-cell profiles.

Krit1 perturbation did not yield a recurrent response module across the 21 Krit1-tested neuronal classes. No gene recurred across cell types at nominal p<0.001, only 16 genes recurred twice at p<0.005, and the strongest positive and negative whole-signature neighbor correlations were weak (r=0.1429 and r=-0.1347), including in the cell type with the best nominal target-transcript decrease. Overall, there was no FDR-controlled Krit1 response or canonical CCM KLF2/KLF4 induction, so these recurrence and neighbor analyses are best read as quality-control checks rather than definitive network biology.

Htr3a did not show a convergent Perturb-seq signature with the receptor subunit Htr3b: their score vectors were essentially uncorrelated across shared cell types, and the putative 5-HT3 receptor subunit module was sparse overall in this dataset. The only adjusted Htr3b hit, Myadm, appeared in a single 40-cell hippocampal excitatory contrast (012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut), so it remains exploratory rather than a reproducible 5-HT3 transcriptomic program. This interpretation is further limited because neither Htr3a nor Htr3b showed measured target-transcript depletion.

Ppp3cc showed near-zero transcriptome-wide correlation with perturbations in the assayed Ca2+/calmodulin–calcineurin/NFAT neighborhood, including Calm1, Calm2, Calm3, Nfatc3, Camk2a, Camk2b, Camk2g, Camk4, and Ca2+-channel subunits such as Cacna1a, Cacna1c, Cacna1d, Cacna1e, Cacng2, Cacng3, and Cacng8, with no coherent coupling across the same cell types. Because the Ppp3cc signature itself was weak, this argues only that its steady-state transcriptome does not align with a canonical NFAT-like program, not that PPP3CC biology is independent of Ca2+/NFAT or acute protein dephosphorylation.

Tacr3 showed no detectable convergence with same-family or pathway-neighbor perturbations in this assay: genome-wide score correlations with Tacr1, Kiss1r, Gnrhr, and Plcb1 were near zero, and in the only cell type with an adjusted Tacr3-associated hit, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, the strongest library neighbors in the Dazap1-positive class were still extremely weak (|r| < 0.10). These results argue against a coordinated tachykinin receptor or G alpha(q) GPCR transcriptional module, although the compared signatures were generally weak, so the null should be read as lack of detectable convergence rather than definitive pathway independence.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Slc6a1 showed a weak, mixed, and cell-type-restricted signature rather than a reproducible GABA-network module. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Gabbr2 was only a modest neighbor (r=0.425), and in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, Gabbr1 was similarly weak (r=0.363); in 191 MB P MY GABA, the strongest contrast was an exploratory negative relationship with Scn1a (r=-0.543). Across 052 Pvalb Gaba, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and low-count 053 Sst Gaba, inhibitory synapse receptor and release genes remained uncoupled or weakly correlated, with most secondary genes not FDR-significant because correlations were computed from only 50 nominal Slc6a1-response genes per cell type.

Adcy3 showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to canonical melanocortin, G-protein, PKA, BBSome, and ciliary GPCR neighbors, including Gnas, Gnao1, Prkaca, Prkar1a, Mc4r, Lepr, Bbs5, Bbs9, and Gpr161, indicating these perturbations did not phenocopy the Adcy3 signature. In broad hypothalamic classes, including 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Adcy3 was down while downstream mRNA outputs appeared buffered, and only weak convergence was seen for some cilium/trafficking genes such as Ap2s1, Lztfl1, Pkd1, Ap2m1, and Ift88. This suggests the expected PVH MC4R→ADCY3 ciliary signaling module is not resolved in this steady-state Perturb-seq readout, potentially because the relevant PVH MC4R neurons are rare and pathway activity was not measured directly.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Atcay knockdown was largely uncoupled from core kinesin-1 perturbations: in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Atcay signatures showed near-zero same-cell-type correlation with Klc1, Klc2, Kif5a, and Kif5c knockdowns, despite clear reduction of Atcay transcript in these classes. The strongest Atcay class, 155 MB Glut, remained buffered at FDR and lacked meaningful signature neighbors, suggesting that cargo-specific Caytaxin disruption in kinesin-1 cargo transport and mitochondrion distribution may not phenocopy depletion of core motor subunits at the mRNA level; sparse signatures may also miss subcellular transport defects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pcyt2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut converged with perturbation of its downstream PE-pathway neighbor Selenoi on a shared upregulation of sterol/lipogenic genes, including Insig1, Msmo1, Fdft1, Hmgcr, Mvd, Srebf2, Sqle, Dhcr24, Idi1, Ldlr, and Hmgcs1. This convergence was strong within the sterol/SREBP gene panel and weaker across the whole transcriptome, suggesting a pathway-specific response consistent with PE-synthesis strain rather than a globally similar signature; other CDP-ethanolamine pathway transcripts were not detectably induced.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kdm6a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells aligned strongly with Kmt2d, but the related comparators Kdm6b and Kmt2c did not phenocopy this program: both showed near-zero restricted correlation to the Kdm6a signature and no FDR-significant genes, arguing that the thalamic response is not a generic H3K27-demethylase or MLL3/4 paralog effect. This divergence was observed in the MLL3/MLL4-ASCOM enhancer chromatin and H3K4/H3K27 crosstalk context, with genes such as Ntng1, Nell1, Ptpn5, Cyp46a1, Tspan33, and Mical2 implicated, although the Kmt2c comparison was lower powered because only 55 perturbed cells were available.

Kif11 showed a weak transcriptomic perturbation, weaker than most assayed KIF/KLC family genes and far weaker than structural tubulin perturbations such as Tuba1a, Tuba4a, Tubb2a, Tubb3, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, and Tubb5. Its signature had near-zero correlation with other kinesin-related perturbations, including Kif1a, Kif1b, Kif2a, Kif3b, Kif5a, Kif5c, Kif21a, Kifbp, Klc1, Klc2, and Mapre2, and a restricted top-gene neighbor search did not identify a biologically specific Kif11 neighbor. These comparisons are tempered by differing cell counts and guide efficacies, and the analysis relied on transcriptome scores only.

En1 did not show the expected convergence with En2 or the broader engrailed/homeobox midbrain dopaminergic-neuron maintenance neighborhood in this dataset. In 215 MB Dopa, En2, Foxa2, Lmx1a, Lmx1b, Nr4a2, Otx2, and Pitx3 were not recovered in the assayed transcriptome, with no FDR-significant responses across 156 perturbation-by-cell-type tests, and their score correlations with En1 were very small. Genome-wide signature-neighbor comparisons likewise failed to reveal a strong En1-related module, although interpretation is limited by weak target engagement and sparse dopaminergic coverage.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Rab7 loss recurrently upregulated a lysosomal/vacuolar acidification program, with Atp6v0b and Dpp7 most repeatedly induced, alongside Lamp2, Mcoln1, Insig1, Neu1, and Atp6v1b2, across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. The strongest responses were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, consistent with stress on endo-lysosomal trafficking and vacuolar acidification rather than unrelated neuronal activation, although the same mRNA signature could also reflect increased lysosome biogenesis, altered lysosome state, or survival selection because protein abundance and lysosomal pH were not measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Uqcrq did not phenocopy other mitochondrial respiratory-chain complex III or adjacent ETC perturbations in this Perturb-seq readout. In 155 MB Glut, Uqcrc1, Cox5a, Cyc1, and Uqcrfs1 showed much stronger own-transcript depletion than Uqcrq, and in 191 MB P MY GABA the Uqcrq Wilcoxon score vector was nearly uncorrelated with Uqcrc1, Cyc1, Uqcrfs1, and Uqcrh. Genome-wide signature neighbors were weak, with maxima around |r|≈0.1. This divergence may reflect weak Uqcrq knockdown as well as biological buffering; 217 P MY Pineal Glut had low cell counts, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed only Gpr180 as an FDR-significant associated gene.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
