full_finding_text: Wac showed a modest but reproducible positive signature similarity to spliceosome and proteasome perturbations, especially Prpf6, Ddx23, Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, and Pomp, across Wac-active cell classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. In these populations, Wac loss also aligned with a nuclear speckle and pre-mRNA processing response marked by Luc7l2, Luc7l3, Sf3b1, Rbm25, Rbm4, Srsf11, Clk1, and Jmjd1c, suggesting a broader RNA-processing/proteostasis state rather than an isolated Wac-specific program; however, these are correlation-based relationships and do not imply direct physical interaction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mapre2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed an engaged perturbation with on-target depletion, but it did not form a coherent microtubule plus-end or transport module with the available comparators. In this cell type, Apc, Clip2, Dctn1, Dync1h1, Kif5a, Map1b, Mapt, Spast, and Tubb3 all correlated only weakly with the Mapre2 score vector, with |r| ≤ 0.056, so these perturbations did not phenocopy Mapre2. Interpretation is limited because Mapre1, Mapre3, Clip1, Ckap5, Clasp1, and Clasp2 were not targeted, and Mapre2 signatures were weak in most cell types.

Cckar showed little transcriptomic coupling to canonical second-messenger neighbors: across matched cells, Cckar score vectors had very small same-cell correlations with Plcb1, Itpr1, Adcy1, Adcy3, and Adcy5, with maximal |r|≤0.179, even though perturbations of Plcb1, Itpr1, and Adcy3 achieved detectable self-depletion in some contexts. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, significant Plcb1 and Itpr1 self-depletion likewise lacked a matching Cckar response. This suggests the CCK1R Gq/PLC/IP3/calcium program was not transcriptionally engaged here, although the Cckar signature was weak and proximal Gnaq/Gna11 perturbations were not assayed.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Aco2 in 046 CTX-CGE GABA cells did not phenocopy neighboring mitochondrial enzyme perturbations: correlations of its differential-expression score vector with 16 pyruvate/TCA/OXPHOS perturbations were essentially zero, ranging from Ogdh r=-0.031 to Mdh1 r=+0.037, and no whole-transcriptome neighbor strongly matched or opposed it. Thus, despite ACO2 being a core TCA enzyme, the measured Aco2 signature appears weak or idiosyncratic rather than a local citrate-isocitrate blockade. A key caveat is that correlations were computed from DE score vectors, not raw single-cell states, and Aco2 itself was not detectably depleted.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnpu showed positive restricted-signature convergence primarily with spliceosome and proteasome perturbations, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, and also across 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. The strongest positive neighbors included U2af2, Snrnp70, Prpf6, Cdc40, and the proteasome-related Psmc1, Psmb4, Psmc5, and Pomp, while strong recurrent negative neighbors were not observed. This pattern fits HNRNPU’s RNA-processing role, but the proteasome convergence is exploratory and was derived only from correlations over the top 300 absolute Hnrnpu-scored genes in each cell type.

Reep1 perturbation did not detectably induce a canonical unfolded-protein response or ER-associated degradation transcriptional program in this dataset: selected markers including Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Xbp1, Herpud1, Hsp90b1, Manf, Edem1, Edem2, Sel1l, Syvn1, Calr, and Canx were not recurrently upregulated, and no consistent signal was seen across the tested signatures. This suggests that acute Reep1 loss lacked a clear bulk ER-stress transcript signature here, although only a selected UPR/ERAD marker panel was assayed and ER morphology and Xbp1 splicing were not measured.

Syp appeared buffered relative to related presynaptic perturbations in the presynaptic SNARE and vesicle-release neighborhood: across the same 22 broad cell types, Syp produced no non-self genes passing FDR < 0.05, whereas Snap25 and especially Stxbp1 produced 5 and 88 such hits, respectively. This contrast, alongside related genes such as Sv2a, Cplx1, and Syn1, suggests that network proximity does not imply transcriptomic interchangeability. The comparison is based on aggregate FDR-hit counts rather than matched guide efficiencies or a full signature-correlation analysis.

Prop1 showed no robust positive or negative transcriptomic signature neighbor across the perturbation panel. Across 43,663 within-cell-type Prop1 correlations, the strongest positive and negative neighbors were both weak, with Bcap31 at r=0.171 and Hmgcr at r=-0.161, and a Safe_target control among the top weak positives; both extremes occurred in 308 CB GABA cells. The scalar burden of Prop1 low-p rows stayed within the empirical safe-target range, and no recurrent or FDR-significant Prop1 module was detected, consistent with a vector near the empirical null rather than a distinct pathway state.

Tbck showed an uncoupled, weak signature that was essentially uncorrelated with represented perturbations across the mTORC1–autophagy–lysosome axis, including Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1, Tsc2, Akt3, Atg5, Becn1, Lamp2, Atp6v1e1, and Vps13d. In this dataset, at least one pathway neighbor such as Tsc1 produced strong differential expression, suggesting the Tbck null result was target-specific rather than a general lack of pathway sensitivity. Because the Tbck signature itself was weak, this should not be taken to disprove prior TBCK links to mTOR regulation and autophagic-lysosomal phenotypes.

Satb1 showed no strong positive or negative signature neighbor in this dataset-wide scan: available functional neighbors and cortical neurodevelopmental regulators, including Foxp1, Yy1, Ep300, Tcf3, Tbr1, Satb2, Bcl11b, Mafb, Ndufb9, and Kcnd3, all had weak correlations with the Satb1 score profile, with the largest all-target correlation only r = 0.146. Thus, the nominal Satb1 genes did not define a reproducible shared module, and broad pathway enrichment would likely overfit noise. A caveat is that these correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors rather than independent replicate-level expression profiles.

Ddhd2 did not phenocopy Ddhd1 at the mRNA-signature level: across all 22 shared cell types, Ddhd2 and Ddhd1 transcriptome score vectors were essentially uncorrelated and centered near zero, despite both genes being grouped in Reactome phosphatidic-acid hydrolysis within phosphatidic-acid metabolism. No phosphatidic-acid pathway transcript module was evident. Because target engagement for both Ddhd2 and Ddhd1 was weak, this lack of correlation is exploratory and may reflect inadequate knockdown rather than true mechanistic divergence, so they should not be treated as interchangeable transcriptomic controls in this assay.

Phf21a is not a simple Rest phenocopy in this neuronal atlas: Phf21a targeting robustly upregulated Rreb1 in five subclasses, and Rreb1 was the only gene repeatedly significant across more than two cell types, whereas Rest perturbation produced no FDR-significant genes across 23 subclasses and did not induce Rreb1. In the context of BHC/CoREST histone-deacetylase and LSD1 chromatin repression, this pattern suggests REST-independent, REST-low, or buffered CoREST biology in these neurons, although weak Rest perturbation, low Rest expression, or compensation cannot be excluded.

Pparg showed no convergence with the expected PPAR-family and RXR nuclear-receptor module in neurons: across all Pparg-assayed neuronal classes, its signature was weak, lacked FDR-controlled differentially expressed genes and canonical lipid-response markers, and had essentially no meaningful correlation with Ppara, Ppard, Rxra, Rxrb, Rxrg, Ppargc1a, Ppargc1b, Ncoa1, Ncoa3, Nr1h2, or Nr1h3. The strongest nominal Pparg cell class also lacked a close perturbational neighbor, so these data do not recover an expected PPARG:RXRA/cofactor module rather than proving its absence.

Grip1 perturbation did not transcriptionally phenocopy the AMPAR/postsynaptic-density network. In this dataset, no FDR-significant mRNA changes were detected for Gria1, Gria2, Gria3, Gria4, Pick1, Dlg4, or Ephb2 after Grip1 perturbation, and full-vector correlations with related perturbations such as Gria1/2/3/4, Kif5a, Dlg4, Shank2, and Shank3 were near zero. The Grip1 signature itself was weak, so these results argue against a simple receptor-subunit mRNA program while leaving open post-transcriptional effects on AMPAR trafficking, localization, phosphorylation, or synaptic currents.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Setd5 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a restricted, partly opposing cross-perturbation pattern rather than a strong global correlation structure: Ankrd11 was its top positive all-gene neighbor, while Med15, Rora, and Cic were top negative neighbors. The informative overlap was concentrated in a synaptic/cell-state module including Prkcd, Lrrc7, Plekhg1, Ntng1, and Grm1, with several shared increases after Setd5 and Ankrd11 but opposing changes after Med15, Rora, or Cic. Absolute correlations were weak overall, and Kmt2e, Setd2, and Chd8 did not globally phenocopy Setd5 in this class.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Kcnab1 and Kcnab2 were not interchangeable in this dataset: although Kcnab2 knockdown showed FDR-confirmed self-depletion in five cell classes—052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—its signatures were only weakly correlated with Kcnab1 in those same classes (r=0.037–0.133). In matched classes, Kcnab2 was knocked down more robustly than Kcnab1, and restricted signature-neighbor scans did not recover Kv-family perturbations as dominant Kcnab1 neighbors, arguing against Kcnab2 as a direct phenotypic surrogate for failed or buffered Kcnab1 perturbation; these correlations were computed on restricted Kcnab1 top-gene sets, not full-atlas embedding distances.

Lrrtm1 showed weak or absent transcriptional convergence with related synaptic adhesion and postsynaptic scaffold perturbations, including Lrrtm3, Lrrtm4, Nrxn1/2/3, Nlgn1/2/3, Dlg4, Grid1/2, Adam22, Shank2/3, and Slitrk1; across 22 profiled classes, the largest absolute Pearson correlation was only 0.164. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, the only FDR-significant downstream gene was R3hdm2, yet convergence remained weak. This pattern likely reflects weak Lrrtm1 signatures and is compatible with shared protein-level synapse biology that does not appear as a shared acute scRNA-seq program.

cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
full_finding_text: Nr4a2 perturbation did not detectably shift the expected Nurr1/PITX3 dopaminergic terminal-differentiation program in the assayed broad subclasses. Across 22 Nr4a2-assayed subclasses, canonical dopamine-neuron and adjacent markers including Th, Slc6a3, Drd2, Pitx3, Lmx1a, Lmx1b, En1, En2, Rcor2, Egr1, Nr4a1, and Nr4a3 showed no FDR-supported response, and the disease-relevant 215 MB Dopa subclass had no Nr4a2 differential-expression result. Thus this dataset refines rather than contradicts canonical midbrain dopaminergic pathway expectations, because most assayed classes were non-dopaminergic and the key dopaminergic subclass was effectively untested.

Wdr37 did not show a shared brain Perturb-seq RNA signature with its PACS-axis comparators Pacs1 or Pacs2: across matched brain cell types, the perturbation score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, and all three perturbations lacked FDR < 0.05 hits. This argues against a simple “same complex, same neuronal RNA signature” interpretation for the PACS1–WDR37 ER-calcium/protein-traffic module in this dataset, while remaining compatible with context dependence, including lymphocyte-specific biology, assay differences, or weak perturbation strength rather than definitive biochemical independence.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Srebf1 showed no detectable SREBP-family loss-of-function signature in this dataset: its transcript was measured in every Srebf1 perturbation contrast but never reached nominal or adjusted significance, and its perturbation signature did not resemble Srebf2. In contrast, Srebf2 knockdown was significant in 17 of 22 shared neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, and recurrently downregulated the sterol/cholesterol module Dhcr24, Insig1, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Cyp51, Hmgcr, Sqle, Fdft1, Fdps, Ldlr, Lss, and Acaca; the Srebf1 arm is therefore limited by weak target engagement rather than a global assay failure.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Xiap showed no strong phenocopy or anti-phenocopy in the whole-library neighbor screen. In 308 CB GABA cells, the largest same-cell-type correlation was weak, with Cckar at r=0.2499, while the strongest negative neighbor was Fbxo11 at r=-0.2273; other nearby weak correlations included Wdr26 and Eef2. These modest associations, together with weak Xiap target-transcript evidence in the cell class where the highest absolute correlations appeared, argue against interpreting the Xiap signature here as converging on a hidden receptor, NF-kB, or neuronal-development perturbation, and correlation alone does not establish mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Camta1 did not simply phenocopy calcium/calmodulin signaling perturbations in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class. In this strongest thalamic responder, Calm1 was weakly anti-correlated with the Camta1 signature, while Camk2a, Camk2b, and Camk2g were near zero to only weakly correlated. Camta2 and Camta3 were not assayed, so true CAMTA paralog comparisons were unavailable. Overall, the measured calcium/calmodulin neighbors were weak or opposing rather than mimetic, suggesting the Camta1 state should not be read as generic loss of calmodulin or CaMK signaling.

Lrfn2 showed transcriptomic signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of Dlg4, Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Nrxn1, Nrxn2, Nrxn3, Ptprd, and Ptprf across shared cell types, indicating that in this dataset it did not phenocopy the PSD-95/NMDAR/neurexin synaptic-adhesion neighborhood despite belonging to the SALM1 scaffold. In the only noted Lrfn2 cell type, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, the detectable signal was Slc12a5 up-regulation, yet the overall signature remained distinct. This comparison reflects whole-transcriptome similarity rather than local synaptic assembly or protein trafficking, and Lrfn2 itself showed weak measured engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Mapk8ip1 perturbation did not transcriptionally converge with JNK, ERK, kinesin, APP, or Mapkbp1 perturbations in the three cell types with corrected Mapk8ip1 knockdown—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Correlations with App, Jund, Kif5a, Kif5c, Klc1, Klc2, Map2k1, Mapk1, Mapk8, Mapk9, and Mapkbp1 were negligible, and a screen-wide neighbor search found only weak correlations. This suggests transcriptional uncoupling from JNK scaffold signaling, kinesin/APP cargo coupling, and MAPK kinase responses, while not excluding shared protein phosphorylation, axonal transport, or stress phenotypes.

Hivep2 showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signature correlation with the assayed HIVEP-family paralogs Hivep1 and Hivep3, and a genome-wide search did not identify any strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor. In the five nominally engaged contexts, the top non-safe nearest-neighbor signature had absolute correlation no greater than 0.122, so Hivep2 did not phenocopy Hivep1, Hivep3, or any other assayed perturbation. Because Hivep1 and Hivep3 were themselves only weakly engaged, this should be interpreted as dataset-level non-convergence rather than a definitive test of paralog function.

Il6st showed only weak transcriptomic similarity to related IL-6 family/gp130 signaling perturbations in this screen: correlations with Il6ra, Osmr, Crlf1, Stat3, Ptpn11, Mapk1, and Akt3 were all low, and its strongest global signature neighbor reached only r=0.188. This argues against treating these receptor subunits or pathway nodes as interchangeable surrogates for Il6st in basal neurons. The comparison is tempered by generally weak signatures overall, lack of target-transcript depletion for Il6ra and Osmr, and correlation estimates derived from score vectors rather than replicated stimulation assays.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Mib1 clustered with Dctn1, Dync1h1, Chp1, Rab7, Tsc1/Tsc2, and Marchf6 perturbations in a shared transcriptomic neighborhood marked by convergent up-regulation of sterol genes such as Insig1, Hmgcr, Msmo1, and Ldlr across several neuronal classes, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. The strongest glutamatergic response was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 155 MB Glut uniquely showed FDR-significant Mib1 depletion. This pattern supports a broader vesicle/ER/nutrient-state sterol module rather than a Mib1-only or Notch-only effect, although the relationship is transcriptomic, panel-restricted, and not biochemically tested.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gria2 showed a divergent Perturb-seq RNA signature from other AMPA receptor subunits and TARPs: in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Gria2 depletion was FDR-significant yet produced little downstream RNA change, and the transcriptome-wide signatures of Gria1, Gria3, Gria4, Cacng2, Cacng3, and Cacng8 were essentially uncorrelated rather than phenocopying Gria2. This argues against treating these related targets as transcriptionally interchangeable, although the comparison is limited by transcriptome-wide correlations and incomplete FDR validation of all comparator perturbations in the same cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Phf12 perturbation produced a transcriptional signature that converged with Gatad1 rather than Sin3a: Gatad1 was the top correlated perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, while Phf12–Sin3a correlations were near zero or weakly negative across 21 shared cell types. In the dominant responsive class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Phf12 affected RNA-processing genes and repressed synaptic/glutamatergic genes. This supports a cell-context-specific SIN3-associated chromatin repression relationship, with Gatad1 backed by transcriptomic convergence and STRING association rather than a demonstrated PHF12–GATAD1 complex in these neurons.

Npsr1 did not yield a reproducible transcriptional module in this dataset. The direct ligand perturbation, Nps, was absent from the library, and a global signature-neighbor scan showed only weak similarities, with Bsn the top positive neighbor (r = 0.179) and Atp6v1e1 the most negative (r = -0.156); in 308 CB GABA, the related receptor Cckar reached only r = 0.176. In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, the response was similarly weak, arguing against rescuing the Npsr1 phenotype by nearby perturbations, while noting that correlation may miss nonlinear or cell-state-restricted effects and low cell numbers can distort similarity estimates.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Supt16 showed its strongest positive transcriptomic signature neighbors in proteasome-related perturbations rather than annotated FACT partners: Psmc1, Psmc5, Psmb4, and Pomp repeatedly ranked near the top across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, consistent with convergence on a 26S proteasome/proteasome maturation stress state. These correlations were reproducible but modest and purely transcriptomic, and direct comparisons to Ssrp1, Polr2a, or core PAF1 elongation components were not possible because those perturbations were absent from the library.

Krit1 did not show CCM-complex-like convergence with Pdcd10 in this screen: across the 21 shared cell types, whole-signature correlations between Krit1 and Pdcd10 were near zero, and Pdcd10 had no FDR-significant rows. This argues that the assay did not recover an interchangeable KRIT1/CCM2/PDCD10 module, and CCM complex with MEKK3-KLF2-KLF4 signaling was not induced in the neuronal Krit1 data. However, Ccm2 was not assayed, and both perturbations were weak, so the lack of convergence may reflect limited guide activity rather than true biology.

Il1rapl1 perturbation did not show strong transcriptomic convergence with its reported synaptic partners or related pathways: signatures were near-orthogonal to Ptprd, Il1rapl2, Il1rap, Il1r1, and Nrxn1/2/3, and even whole-library nearest neighbors were weak. Il1rapl1 knockdown also did not elicit a consistent FDR-level compensatory response among closely related IL-1 receptor-family transcripts, while Mcf2l, Rhoa, Rock1, and Rock2 remained FDR-negative. These results suggest that the IL1RAPL1-PTPRD and Mcf2l-RhoA-ROCK synaptogenic axis was not convergent at the RNA readout here, with the caveat that the assay captures scRNA differential expression rather than splice-, phosphorylation-, compartment-, or cell-contact-dependent protein biology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rora showed a specific dependency in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class: unlike its ROR-family paralogs Rorb and Rorc, Rora produced a broad signature in this responsive cell type, while Rorb and Rorc perturbations had zero FDR-significant genes and near-zero correlation with the Rora program. This suggests the effect is Rora-specific rather than a generic consequence of perturbing any ROR nuclear receptor, although the comparison is tempered by caveats that Rorb target engagement was only nominal and Rorc target engagement was not detected.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Psmb4 showed strongest signature convergence with the proteasome-linked perturbations Pomp, Psmc1, and Psmc5 in the three highest-response cell types—155 MB Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—supporting a proteasome assembly/particle-linked program. In contrast, Nfe2l1, Nfe2l2, and Vcp were weak and did not phenocopy Psmb4 in this screen, so upstream proteostasis regulators were not interchangeable with disturbing the proteasome particle itself; however, these negative comparisons remain uncertain because those perturbations had few significant genes.

Il10ra showed no detectable loss-of-function response across the 22 assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes: there was no on-target RNA depletion, no FDR-significant downstream gene, and no evident Stat3-linked IL-10 receptor/JAK-STAT signaling. Il10rb behaved similarly, with a weak, FDR-silent signature that was essentially uncorrelated with Il10ra across the matched neuronal classes. Although IL10RA and IL10RB are receptor partners, these weak signatures suggest the assayed neurons were outside an active IL-10-responsive state rather than indicating an opposing mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mdh2 repression in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons showed robust on-target transcript reduction but no FDR-significant changes beyond Mdh2 itself, indicating a target-only response in this cell class. In the same neurons, the cytosolic paralog Mdh1 was not interchangeable with Mdh2: Mdh1 perturbation produced a broader 29-gene signature that included Gls up-regulation and Nrxn1 and Grin2b down-regulation, within malate-aspartate shuttle context. This comparison is limited to one cell type and could also reflect differences in knockdown depth, protein half-life, or compartment-specific metabolic bottlenecks.

Gtf2ird1 perturbation did not measurably deplete Gtf2ird1 mRNA, making the self transcript a poor engagement readout in this dataset. Across all 22 tested cell types, the self row had FDR=1.0, with only a small nominal decrease in the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class (logFC -0.170, p=0.011), even though this thalamic class showed the dominant downstream response with seven FDR<0.1 genes, including candidate markers F11r, Sparcl1, Rab30, and Abca3. Thus, a downstream signature should not be dismissed solely for lack of self-mRNA signal, but the RNA data alone also cannot establish loss of GTF2IRD1 protein; transcriptional buffering or protein-level editing remain plausible caveats.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hap1 in 155 MB Glut was largely uncoupled from the sterol transcriptional program seen after perturbing Htt, Dctn1, and Dync1h1: those knockdowns increased an SREBP/cholesterol module including Insig1, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Fdps, Ldlr, Hmgcr, Nsdhl, Fdft1, Srebf2, Fasn, Dhcr24, and Cyp51, whereas Hap1 and kinesin-family perturbations (Kif5a, Kif5c, Klc1, Klc2) did not. This contrast was strongest in 155 MB Glut, based on a signature-level comparison, and Htt mRNA itself was only nominally reduced in that cell type.

Exoc6b showed low or absent transcriptomic convergence with measured trafficking neighbors in this screen: across 22 available vesicle, SNARE, Rab, Sec, and Ral perturbations, including Cdc42, Rala, Rab18, Rab27a, Rab7, Sec23a, Sec31a, Snap25, Stx5a, Stxbp1, and Vamp1, correlations with the Exoc6b signature were uniformly weak, with maximum |r|=0.0949. Thus, indirect perturbations in exocyst-mediated exocytosis and Golgi-to-plasma-membrane transport did not phenocopy Exoc6b, although no other EXOC core subunit or the Exoc6 paralog was directly targeted, limiting comparison to pathway neighbors rather than interchangeable complex members.

Tnfrsf1a showed near-zero signature similarity to Tnfrsf1b and other measured TNF-receptor or NF-kappaB-adjacent perturbations, including Tnfrsf11a, Cd40, Fas, Il1r1/Il1rap, Tlr4, Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, Chuk, Map3k7, and Tnfrsf13c. In this assay, these related perturbations were also largely transcriptionally quiet, with no detectable canonical TNFR1-induced NF-kappaB or cytokine response, so the main cross-perturbation observation is lack of convergence rather than an opposing program. Because these are weak-signal correlation comparisons, the near-zero similarity could also reflect technical noise or absent target engagement in comparator perturbations.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tsc1 showed Perturb-seq signatures that generally aligned with Tsc2 and Rab7 and opposed Mtor/Rptor, consistent with the expected TSC-RHEB-mTORC1 pathway sign, but Tsc1 and Tsc2 were not interchangeable across cell types. The clearest positive Tsc2/Rab7 and negative Mtor/Rptor neighbors appeared in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, while 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut showed 94 significant genes for Tsc1 versus 2 for Tsc2, and 308 CB GABA showed 0 for Tsc1 versus 37 for Tsc2. These were genome-wide score correlations with modest absolute values, so some differences could reflect guide potency or transcript detectability rather than true complex-member divergence.

Add2 showed a weak and largely unique scRNA-seq signature that did not phenocopy nearby spectrin–actin/adducin membrane-skeleton perturbations. Across shared cell types, Add2-score correlations with Add1 and Add3 were near zero, and correlations with Sptan1, Sptb, Ank1/2/3, and Epb41l1 remained very small; in the strongest Add2 contexts, the nearest all-library neighbors still had |r|≤0.123. This pattern was seen in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, but the contrast is limited by weak Add2, Add1, and Add3 signatures and applies only to this scRNA-seq readout.

Slc4a7 showed no convincing positive or negative signature neighbor in a same-cell genome-wide correlation search. The strongest non-self similarities were very weak, with maximum |r| below 0.18, and top-ranked neighbors included Pax1, Tsc1, Cadm2, and multiple safe-target controls such as Safe_target_6, Safe_target_51, and Safe_target_100. Across cell types, this pattern suggests the Slc4a7 perturbation is near-null or control-like rather than converging on a latent neuronal program, although a slight true response cannot be excluded because weak seed profiles are difficult to distinguish from residual noise.

Ube3a showed no strong transcriptomic neighbor in this dataset: the largest full-transcriptome correlation with any perturbation was only r=0.140, and sampled 15q11-q13 genes and GABA-related comparators, including Herc2, Snrpn, Ndn, Gabra5, Gabrb1, Gabrb2, Gabrb3, Gphn, and Magi2, were essentially uncorrelated. Across several GABA cell classes, the pattern was heterogeneous and did not converge across perturbations. Even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where the strongest Ube3a target-transcript signal appeared, the signature remained weak, so these small correlations mainly support the absence of a robust proxy rather than mechanistic divergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Lmbrd1 showed no detected convergence with the lysosomal cobalamin export module in the assayed cells, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA. The screen could not directly reconstruct the established ABCD4–LMBRD1–MMACHC pathway because Abcd4 and Mmachc perturbations were absent, and the only intracellular cobalamin-related comparator, Mmaa, was weakly engaged, showed no corrected response, and did not phenocopy or match Lmbrd1. This lack of co-signature reflects pathway coverage and engagement limitations rather than evidence against Lmbrd1’s known lysosomal cobalamin role.

Arih1 knockdown in unstimulated mouse brain did not produce a detectable ISG15/EIF4E2 antiviral transcriptional response: across 22 cell-type tests, Isg15, Ube2l6, Herc6, Trim25, Ifit2, Stat1, and Eif4e2 showed no FDR-level change. This refines, rather than contradicts, curated ARIH1 involvement in ISG15 biology, suggesting that under basal conditions the perturbation did not induce an interferon-like transcriptional state. The null mRNA result is indirect, however, and does not test ISGylation activity itself.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ndufa4, in the engaged cell types 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, showed a self-dominated knockdown response without a shared respiratory-chain RNA program: although Cox5a, Cox4i1, Ndufs8, Ndufa13, Ndufc2, Ndufb10, Uqcrc1, Uqcrfs1, and Sdha were also strongly engaged in these same classes and each produced precise self knockdown, the genome-wide Ndufa4 score vector had near-zero correlation with them and no strong recurrent positive or negative signature neighbor. This suggests convergence on target-transcript depletion rather than an interchangeable COX/ETC transcriptional module, while not implying the protein complexes are functionally unrelated.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Map2k2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells did not reproduce the transcript module repressed by Braf and Map2k1 in the RAF-MEK-ERK pathway: Braf and Map2k1 converged on repression of Vgf, Ptpn5, and Unc13a, with Etv5 additionally significant after Map2k1 perturbation, whereas Map2k2 showed a weaker, buffered signature with low neighbor correlations in this cell type. Because Map2k2 target depletion was weaker than Map2k1 depletion, this divergence may reflect a MEK dosage threshold rather than MEK2-specific wiring.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Hectd4 showed an isolated perturbation signature rather than a shared module. Across roughly 1,500–2,000 perturbations per assayed class, no whole-transcriptome neighbor exceeded |r|=0.151, and in the best-engaged 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class the correlations with Huwe1, Ube3a, and Grin2b were near zero. In 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Hectd4 was nominally depleted but produced no FDR-significant downstream genes, whereas overlapping Huwe1 perturbations yielded clear multi-gene responses, arguing against a simple lack-of-power explanation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Rubcn showed a buffered or silent transcriptional response relative to autophagy/endolysosomal and mTOR-neighbor perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. Despite 192 and 174 perturbed cells in these strata, Rubcn had 0 FDR-significant genes, whereas Rab7, Tsc1, Tsc2, Vps35, Becn1, and Rb1cc1 produced many significant changes in the same cell types. This argues that the Rubcn null is not simply due to insensitive cell types or absent pathway biology in the screen, although the comparators are pathway neighbors rather than interchangeable Rubicon-complex subunits and guide efficiency differences may contribute.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Rax in 308 CB GABA showed an exploratory signature-neighbor axis rather than a single-gene effect: although no Rax-associated genes reached FDR<0.1 in this cell class, its whole-transcriptome score vector positively aligned with Msx2, Dstyk, Cckar, Plxnd1, Wdr26, Zic3, and Zic1, and opposed Ranbp2, Fbxo11, and Lhx4-like signatures. Because this pattern was restricted to one cell class and two Safe_target controls also appeared among the negative neighbors, it should be treated as a validation hypothesis, not a mechanistic claim.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Pten perturbation produced feedback-like remodeling within PTEN-TSC-PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling rather than a simple RNA proxy for increased pathway output: in the strongest corrected response, the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Akt3 was significantly downregulated, whereas in the weaker 191 MB P MY GABA response, Pik3r1 was the only corrected gene and was upregulated. These transcript changes occurred in cell types where Pten/Tsc1/Tsc2 loss converged and Mtor/Pik3ca loss opposed Pten, but the dataset measured steady-state RNA, not PIP3, AKT phosphorylation, or mTORC1 activity.

Trappc9 perturbation did not produce a coherent NF-kappaB transcriptional feedback response in this mouse brain neuronal dataset. Across a 13-gene NF-kappaB and upstream adaptor panel, including Nfkbia, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, Rela, Map3k14, Chuk, Ikbkb, Traf2, Traf3, Tbk1, and Ikbkg, transcript abundance showed no recurrent or FDR-significant mRNA-level changes. Thus, despite TRAPPC9/NIBP being linked to NIK-IKKbeta-NF-kappaB signaling, these data indicate no immediate unstimulated NF-kappaB mRNA signature, while still allowing post-translational or stimulus-dependent effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Dlg4 knockdown in the two FDR-confirmed midbrain classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, did not transcriptionally phenocopy NMDAR/CaMKII perturbations: score correlations with Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, and Camk2b were near zero even when those comparator transcripts were strongly depleted. Within the PSD-95/NMDA-receptor postsynaptic scaffold context, this suggests that removing the Dlg4 scaffold transcript is not interchangeable with reducing receptor-subunit or CaMKII transcripts at the whole-mRNA-signature level, although electrophysiologic phenotypes could still converge despite uncorrelated transcriptomic signatures.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Gipr perturbation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, the only cell type with a corrected downstream hit, did not induce a canonical cAMP/CREB immediate-early transcriptional program: Fos, Egr1, Arc, Bdnf, Nr4a1, Nr4a2, Sik1, and related markers were unchanged after correction, with only Jund showing a small nominal signal. Thus, the basal L5 ET Gipr signature does not appear to be a simple transcriptional copy of ligand-stimulated GIPR signaling, and related GPCR perturbations did not converge on this program; this should be interpreted in the context of basal neuronal perturbation rather than endocrine ligand-stimulation literature.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ifngr2 perturbation produced an exploratory, nominal decrease of a STAT1/NLRC5/MHC-I antigen-presentation module in a subset of subcortical neurons, including 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. The affected genes were Stat1, Nlrc5, B2m, H2-K1, H2-D1, and Tapbp, with a similar but stronger pattern after Stat1 perturbation. This signal is directionally consistent with IFN-gamma receptor/JAK-STAT1 and MHC-I presentation pathways, but it is restricted and exploratory, with all individual Ifngr2-derived module rows having FDR=1.0.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Dcc showed no reproducible convergence with DCC-family or other axon-guidance perturbation signatures. Across same-cell-type comparisons, transcriptome-wide correlations were tiny and largely driven by an FDR-null Dcc signature: in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, the strongest global neighbors were Adam22 (r=0.204) and Sec31a (r=-0.185), while in 308 CB GABA the strongest curated guidance comparator was a small anti-correlation with Plxnd1 (r=-0.173). Thus, despite overlap with Netrin-1/DCC attractive signaling genes such as Unc5c, Unc5d, Dscam, and Neo1, the data did not support a convergent transcriptional response.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Iqsec1 showed no robust transcriptional convergence with its paralog or synaptic neighbors in the two engaged cell types, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut. In both contexts, Iqsec1 itself was significantly depleted, yet Dlg4, Gria2, and Iqsec2 had near-zero score correlations with Iqsec1, and restricted-signature searches found no convergent or anti-correlated perturbation. This negative result is informative for the IQSEC/BRAG Arf-GEF module, but the Iqsec2 comparison is engagement-confounded because the assayed Iqsec2 perturbation never achieved significant self-knockdown; correlations also used full Wilcoxon score vectors dominated by non-significant genes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cox5a perturbation was transcriptionally buffered in several neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA: unlike the mitochondrial comparator Opa1, Cox5a did not induce the ATF4/integrated stress response amino-acid module marked by Asns, Cars, Mars1, Ddit3, Chac1, Slc7a5, Shmt2, and Aldh1l2, and it did not show the Opa1-associated repression of selected mtDNA transcripts such as mt-Co2 and mt-Cytb. This contrast suggests that, in these cells, complex-IV subunit depletion by Cox5a lacks the broad stress signature seen with the inner-membrane/cristae regulator Opa1.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Itga4 perturbation did not produce a convergent integrin-like neuronal transcriptional state across diverse glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types. Canonical α4-integrin partners and ligands, including Itgb1, Itgb7, Vcam1, Madcam1, and Fn1, were transcriptionally silent in Itga4 contrasts, and related subunit perturbations such as Itga9, Itga6, Itga8, Itga7, Itga2, Itga2b, Itgb1, and Itgb2 showed no close positive or negative phenocopy. The few nominal signals were weak and cell-type-limited, and this restricted-signature comparison is further tempered by weak target engagement among related integrin perturbations in this neuronal screen.

Cask knockdown did not transcriptionally phenocopy Grin1/NMDA-receptor perturbation, even though CASK is curated in NMDA receptor assembly and trafficking pathways that include Grin2b and Dlg4. In this Perturb-seq dataset, Grin1 produced adjusted transcriptomic effects, including many hits in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and detectable hits in several other classes, whereas Cask produced none and showed near-zero correlation with Grin1 signatures. This uncoupling should be interpreted cautiously because Grin1 perturbations generally achieved stronger knockdown and often affected more cells.

Grin3a perturbation did not recover a corrected transcriptional module for the GIT1-Rac1/PAK spine-maturation pathway: Git1, Arhgef7, Rac1, Pak1, Pak2, Pak3, and Limk1 were measured, but none reached FDR<0.05. This negative RNA signature refines rather than contradicts prior GluN3A models, because the reported mechanism emphasizes postsynaptic receptor localization and protein-complex signaling through Rac1/PAK actin regulation, which may not produce rapid steady-state mRNA changes. A caveat is that only a small hand-curated gene set was examined, and mRNA abundance is an indirect readout of actin regulatory signaling.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Esr1 showed a weak, cell-type-specific and non-interchangeable signature with Esr2 in 155 MB Glut, the only Esr1-responsive class. Esr1 perturbation produced a single FDR-level hit, Nfic up-regulation, while Esr2 had a different single hit, Jmjd6, and their full score vectors were only weakly correlated (r=0.0606). There was no coordinated ESR-mediated signaling module across ESR2, co-regulators, steroid-receptor genes, or all perturbations, and neither perturbation showed detectable depletion of its receptor transcript, so the contrast is qualitative and hypothesis-generating.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cul3 loss in the responsive neuronal classes 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not significantly induce the canonical KEAP1–NFE2L2 oxidative-stress transcriptional program: Nfe2l2, Keap1, Sqstm1, Hmox1, Nqo1, Gclc, Gclm, Txnrd1, Slc7a11, and Srxn1 were not detectably induced, and Nfe2l2 perturbation did not resemble the Cul3 transcriptome. This separates the measured Cul3 response from the best-known KEAP1-CUL3-RBX1 substrate pathway at the mRNA level, although NRF2 activation could still occur post-transcriptionally and the Nfe2l2 guide signature itself was weak in this dataset.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf9 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut subclass showed a thalamic module that was uncoupled from simple thyroid-hormone receptor perturbation: although Thra perturbation engaged a canonical receptor program and reduced Hr and Thra, Klf9 itself was only nominally reduced, and Thra, Thrb, Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg signatures had near-zero correlation with the Klf9 program and did not reproduce the Wsb1, Hcn3, Pld3, and Plxna3 response. This suggests the Klf9 downstream module is not a clean proxy for the whole THRA/RXR branch, with the caveat that CRISPR receptor loss is not equivalent to timed T3 exposure.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Mc4r in 145 MH-LH TH Glut showed a transcriptional signature that was nearly orthogonal to melanocortin-family, obesity-pathway, neuropeptide-processing, and cAMP-effector perturbations in the same dataset, including Mc1r, Mc2r, Mc3r, Agrp, Gnas, Adcy3, Lepr, Sim1, Pcsk2, Cpe, Prkaca, and Prkar1a; even strongly engaged Cpe and Prkaca knockdowns had approximately zero correlation with Mc4r. In this only FDR-positive Mc4r cell type, the signal was limited and did not recover the expected melanocortin receptor to GNAS/adenylyl-cyclase/cAMP neighborhood, although score-vector correlations may miss effects confined to subpopulations or non-transcriptional signaling.

Foxi1 perturbation did not engage the canonical epithelial SLC26A4/V-ATPase acid-base program in any of the 20 tested mouse brain classes: genome-wide Wilcoxon analyses found no transcriptome-wide significant responses, and Slc26a4, Atp6v1b1, Atp6v0a4, Slc4a9, plus measured V-ATPase subunits including Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2, Atp6v1e1, Atp6v0a1, and Atp6v0c were statistically flat, with several key targets at FDR=1.0. This suggests the known Foxi1 disease cassette is not portable into assayed neuronal glutamatergic or GABAergic brain populations, although the relevant kidney, inner-ear, epididymal, and ionocyte states were not sampled.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Xrn1 perturbation showed its strongest differential-expression signature in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, where a 29-gene FDR<0.10 response emphasized synaptic and postsynaptic programs rather than a bulk buildup of decay substrates. The mixed signature included increased Adgrb1, Rims2, Adcy1, Ppp1r9b, and Shank1, with App, Clstn1, and Atp6v0c decreased, and was enriched for dendritic-spine, postsynaptic-density, glutamatergic-synapse, and chemical-synaptic-transmission terms. This pattern was not mimicked by Cnot1, Upf3b, or Ski, and the module should not be taken as proof that these mRNAs are direct XRN1 substrates.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Wdr26 showed a neuronal signature that was not phenocopied by Gnb1 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA cells. Although Gnb1 achieved strong self-depletion, it produced almost no downstream differential expression, and its score vector, like Dyrk1a, was near-orthogonal to Wdr26, uncoupling Wdr26 from G beta-gamma / PLCB2 signaling at the transcriptional level in these brain profiles. This divergence should be interpreted cautiously because prior WDR26–G beta-gamma work was done in leukocytes, and other G beta isoforms or acute signaling outputs may compensate here.

Itga8 showed no detectable acute transcriptional convergence with Itgb1 or other assayed integrin-family neighbors in this Perturb-seq dataset. Across 176 integrin perturbation-by-cell-type tests, only one gene reached FDR < 0.05, and the transcriptome-wide Itga8–Itgb1 score correlation was essentially zero (r = -0.008), arguing against a shared acute α8β1 / integrin cell-surface interaction signature involving genes such as Fn1, Tnc, Spp1, Vtn, Npnt, Ptk2, Ilk, Vcl, Pxn, Tln1, Tln2, and Fermt2. However, all integrin-family perturbations were weak, and because Itgb1 is a broadly shared β subunit, the lack of an Itga8-only phenocopy is not definitive.

Oprm1 showed no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor in the matched perturbation matrix: its Wilcoxon score vector was essentially orthogonal to opioid receptor paralogs Oprd1, Oprk1, and Oprl1, as well as to Gi/Go–cAMP pathway neighbors Gnao1, Gnb1, Adcy1, and Adcy5. The strongest non-Oprm1 correlation was only with Sec31a (r=0.036), indicating that family or pathway annotation did not yield interchangeable loss-of-function signatures here. Because correlations were computed on score vectors rather than raw single-cell expression, and Oprm1 engagement was weak, mechanistic interpretation is limited.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Eng did not show an interchangeable Perturb-seq phenotype with related TGF/BMP/vascular receptors in the assayed neuronal classes. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut, Acvrl1, Tgfbr3, and Acvr2b resembled Eng in lacking FDR-supported depletion of their own transcripts, while Bmpr2 showed clear direct transcript knockdown, strongest in 155 MB Glut, yet its score vectors still did not converge with Eng. Thus, within the BMP9/10-ENG-ALK1-SMAD endothelial signaling neighborhood, receptor-complex membership alone did not predict a shared neuronal signature, although this screen was limited and many comparator signatures were weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kmt5b, in the responsive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class, did not phenocopy Chd8, Arid1b, or any other assayed perturbation: whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon-score correlations showed only a very weak top neighbor, Kansl1 (r=0.1407), a minimal anti-neighbor, E2f4 (r=-0.0567), and essentially no correlation with Chd8 or Arid1b. Thus, the mouse thalamic Kmt5b signature appeared isolated, contrasting with human cortical organoid reports of shared KMT5B-ARID1B-CHD8 convergence, a difference that may reflect species, developmental stage, cell-type, and endpoint context.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Vps13d showed a buffered, weak transcriptomic response relative to neighboring mitochondrial fission, mitophagy, and endolysosomal trafficking perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 155 MB Glut cells, Vps13d often produced only target engagement or no FDR-significant genes, whereas Dnm1l, Opa1, Rab7, Hspa9, Dctn1, Dync1h1, and also Vps35 or Vps37a generated much broader signatures. Thus, Vps13d was not an acute RNA-level phenocopy of these neighbors, although guide efficiency, target essentiality, and the transcriptomic rather than morphological readout limit direct comparison.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gls did not share a transcriptomic signature with perturbations of other glutamate-cycle or mitochondrial glutamate-metabolism genes in the two best-powered contexts, 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In these cell types, score-vector correlations between Gls and Abat, Gad1, Gad2, Glud1, Got1, Got2, Slc1a1, Slc1a2, Slc25a12, and Slc25a13 stayed near zero, while related pathway genes were largely unchanged after Gls knockdown. The observed profiles were dominated by on-target transcript loss, so pathway membership did not predict convergent same-cell signatures here.

Lgals3 showed no convincing neuronal transcriptomic response, and this absence extended to Galectin-3-linked innate and receptor neighbors rather than reflecting a uniquely failed Lgals3 signature. In the neuronal panel, perturbations of Trem2, Tlr2, Tlr4, Csf1r, Axl, Mertk, C3, Cd36, Itgb2, and Cx3cr1 were also largely unengaged, did not converge with Lgals3 by signature similarity, and mostly lacked target-transcript engagement. The strongest restricted neighbor signal was in 308 CB GABA for Cd36, but even there no Lgals3 on-target engagement was detected; this conclusion is limited to the restricted transcriptomic signatures assayed and does not exhaust the full Galectin-3 interactome.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zeb1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a distinct downstream signature that was not interchangeable with Zeb2 or nearby canonical EMT/TGFβ-SMAD perturbations: Zeb2, Snai2, Twist1, Twist2, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Smad2, and Smad3 all had near-zero correlation with the Zeb1 signature in this dominant Zeb1-responsive cell type. This suggests that, in this adult brain context, the relevant CDH1/EMT-linked module is selectively wired to a narrow Zeb1/CtBP-associated regulon rather than generically shared across EMT-like regulators, although comparator target engagement was not independently validated and the assay did not use ligand-stimulated epithelial EMT conditions.

Vcp showed its closest positive signature neighbors among proteasome and proteasome-biogenesis perturbations, specifically Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, and Pomp, consistent with the ubiquitin-proteasome and VCP segregase module. However, the convergence was weak and not interchangeable: absolute Vcp-neighbor correlations were small, no robust inverse neighbor was detected, and these comparator perturbations produced far larger transcriptomic responses in the same panel, with 1,409–9,951 FDR<0.05 genes versus only 2 for Vcp. Direct comparison to canonical VCP adaptors NPLOC4 and UFD1 was not possible because those perturbations were unavailable.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Or51e2 did not phenocopy the available olfactory/cAMP pathway neighbors: across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and other profiled cell types, its perturbation signature was essentially uncorrelated with Gnal, Adcy3, Gnb1, Gnb5, Adcy1, and Adcy5. The Or51e2 signal was itself weak, with no clear self-depletion or downstream hits even in the largest contrasts, whereas comparator perturbations sometimes showed measurable self-depletion. This comparison is limited to pathway neighbors because no other Olfr-family perturbation was available.

Rapgef2 showed no detectable phenocopy with the related RapGEF Rapgef4 in this dataset: across 20 shared cell classes, Rapgef2–Rapgef4 whole-signature correlations were near zero, ranging from -0.042 to 0.035, indicating no interchangeable basal program within cAMP/Rap guanine-nucleotide exchange signaling. This comparison is informative mainly as a negative phenocopy test, however, because both Rapgef2 and Rapgef4 perturbations were weak, lacked FDR-significant downstream genes, and had only extremely weak positive or negative signature neighbors.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Huwe1 showed weak, recurrent signature convergence with Trip12 and selected proteasome perturbations, especially Psmc1, Psmb4, and Pomp, across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells. In contrast, similarity to other HECT-family ligases, including Ube3a, Hectd4, Herc1, and Herc2, was near zero or negative. The strongest positive proteasome-neighbor correlations appeared in 191 MB P MY GABA, but all Pearson correlations were small, so this pattern is best viewed as exploratory and useful for nominating follow-up perturbation pairs rather than inferring a shared complex.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Atp6ap1 showed a narrow, non-interchangeable transcriptomic response relative to other V-ATPase perturbations, especially Atp6v0c. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Atp6v0c produced a much broader FDR signature than Atp6ap1 (537 versus 2 genes), and weak transcriptome-score correlations were seen between Atp6ap1 and all tested V-ATPase members, including Atp6ap2, Atp6v0a1, Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2, and Atp6v1e1. This pattern also appeared in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, although comparator guide efficiency, cell counts, and subunit biology may contribute, and the similarities are transcriptomic rather than biochemical.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Oprd1 in 052 Pvalb Gaba showed a transcriptomic signature that was nearly orthogonal to perturbations of Prkaca, Gnao1, Gnb1, Adcy1, and Adcy5, despite these genes lying in the delta opioid receptor/Gi-o/adenylyl-cyclase-cAMP pathway. In this cell type, Prkaca was a strong perturbation, yet its correlation with Oprd1 was near zero, and the same was true for Gnao1, Gnb1, Adcy1, and Adcy5. This suggests that receptor knockdown did not phenocopy core cAMP effector perturbations in this single-cell RNA assay, with the caveat that transcript knockdown is not equivalent to acute ligand-dependent GPCR signaling and several downstream targets showed weaker engagement than Prkaca.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Gabbr1 perturbation did not yield a reproducible positive transcriptomic phenocopy with canonical GABA(B)-associated partners or Gi/o-effectors. Across 308 CB GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, restricted Gabbr1 signatures showed no consistent positive relationship to Gabbr2, Gnao1, Gnb1, Gnb5, Adcy3, Kctd8, Kctd16, Kcnj6, or Cacna1g; in 308 CB GABA, the exploratory Gabbr1 signature was inversely related to Cacna1g, Gnao1, Kcnj6, Gnb1, and Gabbr2. Interpretation is limited because several KCTD/GIRK perturbations lacked significant self-knockdown and the Gabbr1 response genes used for these correlations were non-FDR.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Fam149b in 155 MB Glut showed only weak self-depletion, and stronger knockdown of other ciliogenesis genes did not phenocopy its transcriptional signature. In the same cell class, Ahi1 and Cplane1 achieved FDR-significant self-depletion, yet their signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Fam149b, indicating divergent responses despite shared primary cilium assembly/protein localization to cilium biology. This comparison is limited to mRNA endpoints, and the shared literature context reflects ciliary biology rather than a direct FAM149B1-AHI1-CPLANE1 complex.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Bach2 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed a sparse signature that was uncoupled from the canonical BACH2–small-Maf/Maf-recognition-element antioxidant program: Hmox1, Nqo1, Gclm, Gclc, Mafg, Mafk, Nfe2l1, and Nfe2l2 were not significantly changed, and the Bach2 L4/5 score vector was nearly uncorrelated with Maf, Mafg, Nfe2l1, and Nfe2l2 perturbations. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Mafg perturbation strongly induced Hmox1, whereas Bach2 did not, although this mismatch could reflect weak Bach2 perturbation rather than true biological independence.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mpc1 was not interchangeable with downstream mitochondrial pyruvate-oxidation perturbations in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Dlat, Pdha1, Pdhb, and Mdh2 showed clear self-depletion, whereas Mpc1 did not, and in both 052 Pvalb Gaba and thalamic neurons the genome-wide Mpc1 signature was nearly uncorrelated with Dlat, Dld, Pdha1, Pdhb, and Mdh2. Similar contrasts appeared in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Mdh2 self-depletion exceeded weak nominal Mpc1 effects. These comparisons are transcriptomic and do not measure pyruvate flux, acetyl-CoA, lactate, or respiration.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Lyst showed an exploratory positive convergence with Vps35l in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut: when analysis was restricted to the top 200 Lyst-scored genes, Vps35l ranked 9th of 2022 targets, consistent with a plausible Retriever-associated endosomal-recycling link. However, this signal was weak and cell-type-specific, because the corresponding all-gene correlation was only 0.098 and Lyst target engagement was nominal. Thus, the Lyst–Vps35l connection is best treated as a hypothesis rather than a robust screen-wide module.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Epha7 did not produce a recognizable Eph-family transcriptomic signature in the assayed neurons. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Epha7 showed strong or nominal self-depletion but no FDR-supported downstream program, no ligand or effector feedback, and only near-zero similarity to other Eph receptor perturbations, with the strongest all-perturbation correlations just 0.0759 and 0.0717, the latter to Epha4. These weak score vectors suggest either a weak RNA phenotype or non-interchangeable transcriptional consequences relative to Epha2/3/4/5/6/10 and Ephb1/2/4, while leaving open shared non-transcriptional signaling.

H2-Eb1 perturbation in the assayed neuronal cells did not engage the MHC class II antigen-presentation or IFN-gamma–STAT1–CIITA transcriptional module: across 23 glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic classes, H2-Aa, H2-Ab1, H2-Eb2, H2-DMa, H2-DMb1/2, H2-Oa, H2-Ob, Cd74, Ciita, Rfx5, Rfxank, Rfxap, Stat1, Ifngr1, Ifngr2, and Il6ra remained nonsignificant, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 155 MB Glut. This argues against a coordinated antigen-presentation state, although only mRNA was tested and peptide loading or surface MHC-II protein was not measured.

Meis2 did not share a strong perturbation signature with expected MEIS/PBX/HOX-family partners in this screen: Meis1, Pbx1, Pbx3, Pknox2, Hoxa1, Hoxa3, Hoxa13, Hoxb8, Hoxc13, Hoxd10, Hoxd13, and Tgif1 were largely uncorrelated or buffered relative to Meis2, with a related-panel maximum of only |r|=0.121 and just two corrected DE genes across the queried TALE/HOX panel. In the 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA class, Meis2 itself showed no corrected response and no strong partner-family neighbor, suggesting weak engagement or missing developmental context rather than clear pathway divergence.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Kif1a perturbation produced a modest recurrent up-regulation of a sterol/cholesterol-biosynthetic program rather than an annotated KIF1A kinesin/vesicle pathway signal. Hmgcs1 was the clearest induced transcript in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Dhcr24 was FDR-significant in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and Insig1 and Msmo1 were near-FDR in 191 MB P MY GABA; a broader 14-gene panel including Hmgcr, Fdft1, Sqle, Srebf2, and Ldlr was repeatedly positive at nominal p<0.05 across several cell types. This pattern suggests a compensatory lipid-state response, with the caveat that only Hmgcs1 and Dhcr24 met FDR<0.05 individually and the broader module was identified by recurrence and nominal significance after inspection of the Kif1a signature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Mapt knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons did not phenocopy related cytoskeletal, synaptic, or neurodegeneration-linked perturbations. Although comparator perturbations such as Map1b, Map6, Mapre2, Map1lc3a, Tuba1a, Tubb3, App, Bin1, Dlg4, Syn1, Nefl, Nefm, Nefh, and Grn showed good self-engagement, their whole-transcriptome signatures were nearly orthogonal to Mapt, with Mapt itself strongly down but no coherent downstream microtubule RNA module. This null RNA similarity may still miss smaller shared modules or protein-level and morphological convergence.

Thrb did not show the expected TR–RXR receptor-subunit transcriptional coupling in this screen: Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg perturbations produced no FDR-significant genes and were essentially uncorrelated with Thrb signatures, so a shared canonical receptor program was not recovered. This uncoupling was noted in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut within the thyroid hormone receptor transcriptional response context, while Thra-specific Hr downregulation appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The result is exploratory because RXR knockdown and RXR target-transcript effects were also weak, and transcriptomic data cannot localize the missing ligand or cofactor step.

Pbx3 showed near-zero transcriptome-level similarity to assayed PBX/MEIS/HOX-family perturbations, with Pbx3 score signatures essentially uncorrelated with Pbx1, Meis1, Meis2, Pknox2, and Hox genes including Hoxa1, Hoxa3, Hoxb8, Hoxd10, and Hoxd13. In 308 CB GABA, several PBX-family and MEIS comparisons were even weakly negative. These results do not recover a common PBX-HOX-MEIS TALE-homeodomain network signature in this dataset, although most family-member perturbations were themselves weak, so the lack of correlation may reflect under-engagement rather than true independence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Prox1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons appears uncoupled from the canonical VEGFC-FLT4-PROX1 lymphatic axis: perturbing Flt4, Nr2f2, Sox18, or Nr5a2 produced no FDR-significant genes in this responsive thalamic class, and Flt4, Nr2f2, Sox18, Nr5a2, and Vegfc transcripts were unchanged within the Prox1 signature. Thus these canonical endothelial-network members neither phenocopied nor moved inside the thalamic Prox1 program, although this negative result may reflect inactivity or weak editing of those partners in adult neurons rather than falsifying the pathway in its proper endothelial context.

Tubb2a perturbation did not converge on a shared transcriptional signature with other assayed microtubule genes in this mouse-brain screen. Across same-cell comparisons with Tubb3, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, Tubb5, Tuba1a, Tuba4a, Dcx, Dync1h1, Mapt, Kif5a, and Kif5c, correlations were near zero, with the largest absolute Pearson r only 0.089; in the highest-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, the best non-self neighbor was still weak, Ift88 at r=0.148. This pattern suggests protein or pathway proximity did not yield a common mRNA state, although restricted DE score vectors may miss protein-level, morphological, or time-window-limited phenotypes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ptprm showed no convergent downstream mRNA signature with the assayed type-IIB paralog Ptprt. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the only context with corrected Ptprm target depletion, Ptprm produced a self-transcript response without a cadherin/catenin, type-IIB-paralog, or high-correlation neighbor signature, while Ptprt lacked on-target depletion there. Ptprt’s only corrected hit was its own transcript in 155 MB Glut, so the family-level comparison is negative and power-limited, especially because Ptprk and Ptpru were not perturbation targets.

Chrm3 showed a near-null, uncoupled pattern in this dataset: same-dataset muscarinic and GPCR-pathway comparators did not reveal a hidden Chrm3-like program. Chrm2, the only other muscarinic receptor perturbation in overlapping cell types, was FDR-null and nearly uncorrelated with Chrm3 at both differential-expression and signature levels. By contrast, Gnao1, Plcb1, and Mapk1 showed detectable on-target depletion in overlapping classes, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, although these comparators are imperfect because they are downstream or branch-specific pathway neighbors rather than an immediate M3 Gq alpha subunit.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Idh3a showed no convergence with other mitochondrial TCA perturbations across seven engaged cell types, including 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. Genome-wide signature correlations with Aco2, Dld, Dlst, Mdh2, Ogdh, Sdha, Sdhb, and Suclg1 stayed near zero, even in same-cell comparisons where Sdha, Mdh2, or Ogdh were efficiently repressed, indicating pathway membership did not imply interchangeable Perturb-seq signatures. Several comparator knockdowns were weak, so this rules out only a large shared RNA program.

Oprl1 showed near-zero concordance with canonical Gi/o–cAMP and calcium-linked GPCR signaling neighbors in this assay. Across 151 matched comparisons, Oprl1 score vectors correlated only weakly with Gnao1, Gnb1, Prkaca, Adcy1, Adcy5, Cacna1a, and Creb1, with Pearson values from -0.096 to 0.081, and it did not phenocopy the better-engaged Gnao1, Gnb1, or Prkaca perturbations. These data suggest the Oprl1 CRISPR signature did not propagate through the expected inhibitory G-protein/cAMP axis here, although weak Oprl1 target engagement and the limits of correlation leave acute second-messenger signaling unresolved.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Myc showed a weak or null perturbation signature that was uncoupled from strong Max and Trrap responses across the same MYC-network cell contexts, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In the best-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Myc had zero FDR-significant genes, whereas Max and especially Trrap had strong signatures, with 109 and 455 significant genes, and Myc correlated near zero with both. Recurrent Trrap-linked decreases included Snrpn and Snhg11, but interpretation is tempered because Max and Trrap have MYC-independent functions and the Myc guides did not measurably deplete Myc mRNA.

Stat5b perturbation in basal mouse brain cells did not produce a coherent canonical JAK/STAT or GH/cytokine-response transcriptional signature. Across 22 cell types, a 32-gene panel showed no FDR-supported changes, including classic feedback targets Cish and Socs1, Socs2, and Socs3, and no adjusted support among Bcl2l1, Bcl2, Pim1-3, Igf1, Ghr, Prlr, Il2rg, or Epor. Even in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where Stat5b mRNA depletion was strongest, downstream canonical targets were not detected, although this transcript-based basal snapshot does not exclude ligand-evoked STAT5B activity.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Bmal1 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut produced a compact four-gene Perturb-seq signature, with significant changes in Nr1d2, Nr1d1, Npas2, and Camkv, but this module was not phenocopied by other assayed clock-loop perturbations in the same cell type. Clock, Cry1, Cry2, Nr1d1, Nr1d2, Rora, Rorb, Rorc, and Tef each showed zero FDR-significant genes and near-zero correlation with the Bmal1 vector, suggesting a Bmal1-specific response here, while differing editing efficiencies and the lack of FDR genes limit inference about protein-level perturbation.

Purg did not phenocopy Pura, or even the limited Purb signal, in this dataset. Pura showed strong on-target depletion with 61 FDR<0.10 rows in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, whereas Purb had only one FDR-level row and Purg had none. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Purg remained weak despite high counts; in 052 Pvalb Gaba its lowest adjusted-p row was Vps39 but only nominal. A neighbor search found only weak correlations, arguing against a coherent Purg-like perturbation signature, though the comparison is asymmetric because Pura achieved stronger on-target depletion than Purg.

Serpinb6a showed a divergent perturbation profile from the other assayed serpin-superfamily targets, with score correlations to Serpini1 and Serpine2 essentially zero across shared cell types. In contrast, Serpini1 and Serpine2 displayed more FDR-level transcriptional responses, indicating that the weak Serpinb6a response is not a generic property of all serpin-family guides in this dataset and arguing against a single interchangeable inhibitory-serpin signature. This comparison is limited because Serpini1 and Serpine2 are broad superfamily comparators rather than direct Serpinb6a paralogs, and closer mouse paralogs such as Serpinb6b/c/e were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zfhx4 loss did not recapitulate Chd4 loss in these mouse brain perturbation signatures, indicating an uncoupled ZFHX4-CHD4/NuRD axis in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Chd4 produced stronger, FDR-resolved expression programs, whereas Zfhx4 remained weak; even where 155 MB Glut showed the strongest Zfhx4 transcript depletion, downstream response was minimal and Chd4-Zfhx4 signature correlations stayed near zero, with genes such as Begain and Tro contributing to the contrast. This cautions that the GBM tumor-initiating cell ZFHX4-CHD4 relationship may be context dependent and not transferable to broad mouse postmitotic brain classes.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ptpro perturbation showed its only genome-wide corrected response in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons, where Grik5 was downregulated. In the same L4/5 signature, a small set of synaptic and Eph/Src/FAK-adjacent genes, including Nptx1, Epha5, Ptk2, Srcin1, and Rasal1, were also nominally decreased, suggesting a weak synaptic-adhesion or Eph/Src/FAK-related module. However, these accompanying genes did not survive per-signature correction, with FDR=1.0, so they should be treated as rank-level support rather than a proven pathway-level response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Dnajc5 showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to selected presynaptic vesicle, SNARE, cognate-Hsp70, and DnaJ perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells. Despite biochemical proximity to the presynaptic SNAP-25/SNARE chaperone module, Dnajc5 score vectors were nearly orthogonal to Snap25, Hspa8, Stxbp1, Stx1b, Syp, Sv2a, Vamp1, and Dnajc13, and genome-wide searches found no strong positive or negative neighbors. In 155 MB Glut, Dnajc5 depletion was strongest yet produced no FDR-significant downstream transcript, so the tiny correlations could reflect a weak Dnajc5 signature as well as real pathway divergence.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Klhl20 showed near-zero basal mRNA signature correlation with Cul3, Becn1, and Hif1a perturbations, indicating that in mouse brain it did not phenocopy the available CUL3-KLHL20 ubiquitin ligase, autophagy, or hypoxia-related programs. In 155 MB Glut cells, Cul3 and Becn1 produced FDR-level responses, with 6 and 5 significant genes respectively, whereas Klhl20 produced none, and matched full-signature correlations were essentially zero overall. These data are limited to basal single-cell RNA and do not assess protein-level substrate stabilization or stress conditions such as starvation, interferon, or hypoxia.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Tbl1x did not phenocopy its NCoR/SMRT-associated paralog Tbl1xr1. In the matched neuronal classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, Tbl1xr1 showed FDR-level expression signatures, whereas Tbl1x had no genome-wide differential-expression hits, no measurable depletion of its own RNA, and near-zero score correlations to Tbl1xr1. This suggests divergent or unrecovered TBL1-family responses in the NCoR/SMRT/HDAC3 cofactor-exchange machinery, although the comparison is caveated because Tbl1xr1 also lacked a corrected decrease in its own transcript, making the contrast signature-based rather than a fully target-engaged paralog titration.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Camk2a in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut showed an exploratory, cell-type-restricted Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent CaMKII and NMDA receptor postsynaptic signaling pattern that aligned more with Grin2b than with Grin2a. Its signature weakly converged with Grin2b and opposed Grin2a, with nominal decreases in the activity-regulated Bdnf/Nptx2 module, including Bdnf, Nptx2, Scg2, Homer1, and Ptpn5, whereas Grin2a drove several of these genes upward. This signal was sub-FDR, and the comparison reflects Wilcoxon score signature similarity rather than direct causal pathway activity.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Smad3 did not phenocopy nearby TGF/BMP/SMAD perturbations in this dataset: across matched cell types its all-gene signature was essentially uncorrelated with Smad2 and Smad4, and it showed no FDR-significant DE genes, even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut where perturbed-cell counts were highest. By contrast, pathway neighbors had cell-type-restricted hits, including Ski in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Bmpr2 across several classes, and Smad2 in two classes, with related Tgfbr2/Bmpr1b effects also seen without Smad3 convergence. This is a restricted transcriptomic contrast, and weak Smad3 target engagement limits clean paralog or receptor-epistasis inference.

Vapb perturbation did not transcriptionally co-perturb the expected ER membrane-contact and FFAT lipid-transfer machinery: perturbation signatures for Cert1, Osbpl2, Acbd5, and Dnm1l showed low similarity to the Vapb signature, and Vapb loss did not robustly induce measured partner or receptor transcripts including Vapa, Mospd2, Mospd3, Rmdn3, Stard3, Stard3nl, Wdr44, or Vps13a. This suggests that physical contact-site membership was uncoupled from shared mRNA outputs in this assay, although redundancy among ER receptors could not be directly tested because Vapa, Mospd2, Mospd3, and Rmdn3 were measured but not perturbed.

Zfp160 did not phenocopy the screened chromatin neighbors Setdb1 or Chd4: across all 18 matched cell types, the restricted 250-gene Zfp160 signature showed near-zero correlations with Setdb1 and Chd4 perturbations. Although KRAB-ZFP repression is often linked to KAP1-associated SETDB1-dependent H3K9 methylation and NuRD/HDAC pathways, these weak Zfp160 signatures in mouse brain neurons were uncoupled from those chromatin effector arms. This interpretation is limited because Setdb1 and Chd4 are pathway neighbors rather than proven Zfp160 cofactors in neurons, and Zfp160 engagement was weak.

Camsap1 showed an unusually weak Perturb-seq signal in this screen: compared with related cytoskeletal and motor perturbations including Dctn1, Dync1h1, Tuba1a, Tubb2a, Tubb3, and Kif5a, it had weaker on-target transcript depletion and lacked downstream differential-expression signals at FDR thresholds. This contrast suggests the near-null Camsap1 readout is not a general property of cytoskeletal genes in the panel, although differences in guide efficiency, transcript half-life, essentiality, and baseline expression mean this is a same-screen activity contrast rather than an equal-potency comparison.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lemd3 was largely transcriptionally quiet in this in vivo neuronal screen, similar to most assayed TGF/BMP receptor and SMAD-family perturbations, which usually produced no genes at FDR<0.05. A limited, cell-type-specific pattern appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where the strongest Lemd3 depletion yielded a restricted signature that aligned with Ski and opposed Smad2 and Acvr2a, within a globally buffered TGF-beta/activin/BMP receptor-SMAD repression context. These comparisons are transcriptomic only, as receptor expression, editing, ligand availability, and protein signaling were not measured.

Ager showed a shared no-effect pattern in the assayed neuronal classes: there was no measurable Ager mRNA depletion, no adjusted-significant downstream transcriptomic response, and its behavior matched several glial or innate immune receptor perturbations, including Axl, Cd14, Tlr2, Tlr4, Trem2, Tnfrsf1a, and Tnfrsf1b.
