Across these comparators, target-transcript rows were uniformly non-significant and no FDR-significant neuronal signatures were detected, suggesting a broader cell-context limitation rather than an Ager-specific guide anomaly, with conclusions restricted to the neuronal strata tested.

Htr1b showed near-zero transcriptional similarity to other assayed serotonin receptors and Gi/o signaling neighbors, including Htr1a, Htr1f, Gnao1, and Gnb1. Across the broader Htr receptor family, perturbations produced almost no corrected transcriptomic effects in this dataset, with only two corrected non-target rows across 241 target-cell tests, so the screen did not recover a shared Htr-family or Gi/o perturbation state. This signature-based contrast suggests receptor paralogs and pathway neighbors were not interchangeable in this readout, while not proving that the underlying proteins lack related signaling.

Dtnbp1 showed a weak transcriptional perturbation whose signature was orthogonal to Ntrk2 and Snap25 perturbations, despite literature links among dysbindin, BDNF secretion, and SNARE biology. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Dtnbp1 had the strongest nominal self-reduction but no FDR-supported downstream response, while Ntrk2 and Snap25 were clearly engaged yet remained uncorrelated with Dtnbp1; similarly, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut showed nominal Dtnbp1 target reduction without downstream Dtnbp1 genes. These indirect comparators suggest that known Dtnbp1 synaptic phenotypes were not recapitulated as an Ntrk2- or Snap25-like whole-transcriptome program here.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Unc5d showed no robust shared downstream transcriptional module in genome-wide nearest-neighbor searches: excluding the self-match, the median strongest absolute cosine similarity per cell type was only 0.079, and the only notable non-self outlier occurred in 308 CB GABA, where Unc5d paired with non-guidance targets such as Wdr26, Dnajb4, Pax7, and Klf7 rather than a coherent Netrin/FLRT-related program. This pattern suggests the Unc5d profile is largely weak, cell-private, or noisy at the present depth, especially since cosine similarity is a limited signature metric and the CB GABA outlier had only nominal Unc5d knockdown.

Setd2 showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to other H3K36/chromatin disease-family perturbations in the same Perturb-seq contexts: across 15 matched cell-type contexts, score correlations between Setd2 and Ash1l, Nsd1, or Setd5 averaged only r=0.004, 0.003, and 0.016, indicating that these related perturbations did not reproduce the assayed Setd2 signature in the SETD2-H3K36/RNA polymerase II chromatin neighborhood. This argues against substituting NSD1, ASH1L, or SETD5 signatures for SETD2, although the comparison relied on score correlations rather than matched effect-size models, and restricted signature-neighbor analysis was exploratory because some top neighbors were safe-target controls.

Tlr5 showed no convergence with the available TLR-family or innate-pathway perturbations in the neuronal classes assayed: Tlr2, Tlr3, Tlr4, Tlr7, Tlr8, Tlr9, Cd14, Map3k7, and Nfkb1 were almost entirely FDR-silent, and whole-transcriptome score correlations with Tlr5 were near zero. Thus, within this dataset, there was no detected shared TLR5-flagellin/MyD88/NF-kappaB activation or loss signature, and the negative Tlr5 result was not rescued by paralogs, co-receptors, or downstream neighbors. This comparison was limited to assayed related targets, with proximal adaptors such as Myd88 and Traf6 not available.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Wwox showed its only sizable signature-neighbor structure in 308 CB GABA cells, where Wdr26, Dstyk, Cckar, B9d1, Ranbp2, and Fbxo11 ranked among the stronger correlations, but Safe_target_70, Safe_target_15, and Safe_target_81 also appeared among the strongest anti-correlations. Because the Wwox transcript itself was unchanged in this cell type and nominal responses were not concentrated into FDR-significant cell-type programs, this cerebellar GABA axis is better treated as exploratory nuisance structure than as a Wwox biomarker module.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Trem2 showed little detectable activity in these neuronal datasets, whereas Plxna1, the only assayed member of the Reactome SEMA6D-PLXNA1:TREM2:DAP12 semaphorin signaling complex, was perturbable in neurons but remained uncorrelated with Trem2. In 191 MB P MY GABA, Plxna1 showed significant on-target depletion without convergence with Trem2, and in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, a Plxna1-associated Kif21a increase likewise did not produce a shared Trem2 pathway signature. These transcriptomic, cell-type-restricted results argue that neuronal Plxna1 phenotypes should not be interpreted as active neuronal TREM2-DAP12 signaling, especially since key immune adapters such as Tyrobp and Syk were not directly perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Vps41 showed pathway-specific rather than generic VPS-family transcriptomic neighbors across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA: Rab7 was a top non-self neighbor in all three classes, with additional convergence to Tsc1/Tsc2, Dctn1/Dync1h1, and Slc17a5, while Vps35, Vps35l, Vps53, and Vps54 were only weakly correlated. The pattern fits HOPS-dependent endosome/autophagosome-to-lysosome fusion and lysosome-centered mTOR/TSC signature convergence, but all correlations were modest, and other canonical HOPS subunits were not assayed.

Slc25a36 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the expected mitochondrial pyrimidine-nucleotide/mitochondrial-genome axis across all tested cell classes. Across 21 neuronal groups, Slc25a36 showed broad but weak self-depletion without multiple-testing-supported target knockdown, and the 13 mitochondrial-encoded RNAs, including mt-Atp6, mt-Co1, mt-Cytb, and mt-Nd1 through mt-Nd6, had 0/273 FDR-significant tests with mixed nominal directions. This suggests the Perturb-seq signature did not reach a mitochondrial-genome failure state, although mt-RNAs are only a proxy and do not directly report mtDNA copy number, nucleotide pools, respiration, or membrane potential.

Hras showed a convergent silent transcriptional outcome with Kras rather than a shared Ras-pathway signature: Hras produced no multiple-testing-corrected differentially expressed genes in any profiled cell type, and the closest available paralog, Kras, likewise had no FDR-significant genes, with weak signed Hras–Kras score correlations and no strong restricted transcriptome-wide phenocopy. This pattern is consistent with Ras GTPase paralog buffering, but it should be interpreted cautiously because Kras had low per-cell-type counts and weak target-transcript support, and Nras was not perturbed for a complete paralog comparison.

Cep164 showed little expression-space convergence with related ciliary and centrosomal perturbations, with near-zero or only weak correlations to Cep83, Cep290, Ift88, Ift81, Ift43, Bbs5, Bbs9, Arl3, Kif3b, and Cep120 despite its known linkage to the centriole distal appendage and cilium-initiation pathway. The Cep164 signature itself was weak, and many comparator perturbations were also shallow. In 191 MB P MY GABA, the only q<0.10 Cep164-associated gene was Ypel4; in 155 MB Glut and 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, only nominal decreases such as Cox17, Eps15, and Ccnl1 were seen, so the lack of correlation here does not argue against the established pathway.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gapdh perturbation produced a small, coherent, predominantly negative signature only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where the response appeared restricted to a Pnisr/Rsrp1/Grin1/Ogt/Leng8 module with partial Gapdh-Pgk1 convergence rather than broad glycolytic feedback. In this cell type, neighboring glycolysis and central-carbon genes including Hk1, Pgk1, Tpi1, Gpi1, Pfkm, Ldha, and Slc2a1, as well as canonical ER-stress and apoptosis markers Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Bax, Bbc3, and Casp3, did not pass FDR. Because only mRNA abundance was assayed, post-translational GAPDH functions could still change without transcript-level shifts.

Fshr did not show a shared brain transcriptomic signature with its glycoprotein-hormone receptor relatives Lhcgr and Tshr. In this basal mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset, Fshr and Lhcgr had no FDR-significant genes across matched cell classes, while Tshr yielded only one significant gene, Stxbp1, and Fshr genome-wide score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with either comparator. This non-convergence is transcriptomic and unstimulated, and related receptors may align only under ligand or endocrine-state conditions not tested here.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Atp6v1b2 perturbation showed its clearest transcriptional response in 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, where Atp6v1b2 was depleted but the downstream signature was not a simple lysosome-biogenesis program. In this class, other measured V-ATPase subunits and related genes, including Atp6v1a, Atp6v1e1, Atp6v0a1, Atp6v0c, Atp6ap1, and Atp6ap2, as well as Ragulator–mTORC1 and TFEB/MITF-layer transcripts such as Mtor, Lamtor1-5, Tfeb, Tfe3, Mitf, Lamp1, and Lamp2, were mostly unchanged at FDR level, with only weak positive convergence noted with Atp6v0c across perturbations. This absence of mRNA induction does not address V-ATPase assembly or activity, lysosomal pH, autophagic flux, mTORC1 phosphorylation, or TFEB localization.

Atp6v0c knockdown repeatedly reduced Atp6v0a1, which was the most recurrent non-target transcript and was down in 12 cell types, while the nearest positive transcriptomic neighbors were modest correlations to endomembrane, proteasome, calcium, and trafficking perturbations including Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, Pomp, Cltc, Sec31a, Caml, Hspa9, Vps37a, Vps53, and Snf8. The strongest response occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, with additional responses in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut, supporting a broader V-ATPase/endomembrane proteostasis module rather than a single neurotransmission gene, although these neighbor relationships do not establish physical interaction.

Ets1 was uncoupled from Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK pathway neighbors in all shared assayed neuronal classes: perturbing Braf, Hras, Kras, Map2k1, Map2k2, Mapk1, or Raf1 did not phenocopy the Ets1 transcriptomic state, with a maximum absolute whole-transcriptome correlation of only 0.105. Although ETS1 is a curated MAPK effector, these neuronal loss-of-function data suggest that the MAPK-to-ETS axis is inactive, indirect, or context-restricted here. This inference is limited because transcriptome correlation is an indirect pathway readout, MAPK perturbations can have ETS1-independent effects, and Ets1 itself showed no strong signature to match.

Aff3 showed no convergence with its profiled paralog Aff2 in this dataset: neither perturbation achieved FDR-significant self-knockdown, and their cell-matched score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, with Pearson r ranging from about -0.066 to 0.065. In the context of RNA polymerase II elongation and super elongation complex–related genes such as Mllt3, Cdk9, Mllt1, Ccnt1, Aff4, Ell, Eaf1, Ccnt2, Ell3, and Ell2, no shared Aff2/Aff3 signature was detected. Because both perturbations had weak target-transcript engagement, this null comparison does not strongly argue against broader AFF-family relatedness.

Grik4 showed a weak, essentially uncorrelated transcriptomic signature that did not converge with perturbations of kainate receptor genes Grik1, Grik2, Grik3, or Grik5, AMPA genes Gria1-4, NMDA genes Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, or Grin2d, metabotropic glutamate genes Grm1, Grm3, Grm5, or Grm7, or the synaptic scaffold genes Dlg4, Shank2, and Shank3. Nearest positive and negative neighbors were weak and partly included negative-control targets, so no informative glutamatergic module emerged; however, this lack of convergence is underpowered and may reflect poor Grik4 engagement rather than true biological independence.

Acvr2b showed a weak transcriptional signature across the 23 profiled neuronal classes and did not phenocopy related TGF-beta-family perturbations in matched cell types. Whole-transcriptome score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Acvr2a, Bmpr2, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Acvr1, and Smad2, Smad3, or Smad4, with the strongest non-self neighbor only weakly correlated, and no gene passing FDR correction. In these basal neuronal states, this argues against treating these receptor and SMAD perturbations as interchangeable, while not excluding biochemical convergence under ligand-stimulated conditions.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cep85l did not reproduce the recurrent cholesterol/SREBF2 sterol-biosynthesis program seen after Dync1h1 perturbation. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Dync1h1 upregulated sterol genes including Insig1, Fdps, Fdft1, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Srebf2, Hmgcs1, Cyp51, and Sqle, whereas Cep85l showed a much weaker or absent signature in matched groups. This divergence cautions against treating CEP85L-complex members as transcriptomically interchangeable, although Dync1h1 also had stronger on-target depletion and larger perturbed-cell counts than Cep85l.

Nectin1 showed a quiet, largely uncorrelated transcriptional profile: across the best-engaged cell types—005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA—its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with available adhesion and synaptic perturbations including Cadm2, Cdh2, Ctnna2, Ctnnb1, Dlg4, Epha4, Ephb2, Nlgn1-3, and Nrxn1-3, and no strong positive or negative genome-wide neighbor emerged, with maximum |r| only 0.108. This is notable because other adhesion or synaptic targets produced strong signatures in the same dataset, although true Nectin paralogs plus Afdn, Pard3, Cadm1, and Cadm3 were not assayed and the weak Nectin1 signal is therefore noise-sensitive.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Nos1ap showed near-zero signature correlation with Dlg4, Dlgap4, Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Grin2d, Grin3a, Shank2, Shank3, Nlgn1, Nlgn2, Kcnq1, and Kcnq2 perturbations, so in this adult mouse brain screen its transcriptional effects did not phenocopy NMDA-receptor, PSD, neuroligin, Shank, or Kcnq neighbors despite NOS1AP’s adaptor proximity to nNOS/PSD95 signaling. This non-convergence was seen in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Nos1ap had no response while Grin1, Grin2b, and Dlg4 scored strongly. Because Nos1ap engagement was weak, the lack of correlation is more reliable as non-convergence than as proof of a distinct downstream mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Pdhx did not phenocopy core pyruvate dehydrogenase complex subunits in this Perturb-seq dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Pdhx showed its strongest measured mRNA decrease, but this reduction was not FDR-significant, whereas Pdha1, Pdhb, and Dlat each had significant self-depletion; in the same cell class, the Pdhx score vector was essentially uncorrelated with Pdha1, Pdhb, Dlat, and Dld and had no meaningful genome-wide signature neighbor. A second class, 191 MB P MY GABA, similarly showed nominal Pdhx reduction while Pdha1 reached significant self-depletion, suggesting non-equivalent signatures, although this contrast is confounded by weaker Pdhx engagement rather than proving a biological exception within the complex.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Gnptg showed a technically inconclusive same-complex comparison with Gnptab in this screen. Although a nominal anti-correlation appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut using an 80-gene restricted signature, Gnptab perturbation never achieved FDR-significant on-target depletion or any downstream profile, so the pattern is better treated as a low-confidence artifact candidate than evidence of GNPTAB-GNPTG antagonism. In 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Gnptg target mRNA passed FDR, but lysosomal hydrolase trafficking genes such as Idua, Lamp1, Lamp2, Ctsd, Gaa, Igf2r, and M6pr were largely buffered.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gpr162 showed no strong convergence with other perturbations in its three best-engaged neuronal classes—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—where the largest absolute full-signature correlations after excluding the self row were all below 0.08. In these contexts, Gpr162 was essentially the only FDR-significant row, with no STING proxy activation, and available comparators such as Adgra1, Pak1, Trp63, and Gabrg2 did not yield a convergent signature; however, correlations from score vectors do not prove mechanistic independence, and key receptor relatives including Gpr153 were not engaged in the screen.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ppp3ca showed a partly shared transcriptomic response with the calcineurin regulatory subunit Ppp3r1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Ppp3r1 was the top positive Ppp3ca signature neighbor, but the absolute genome-wide correlation was low. In this same thalamic class, Ppp3cc was only weakly engaged, and Nfatc3, Calm1, Calm3, and Camk2b did not phenocopy Ppp3ca. This calcium/calmodulin-dependent calcineurin complex pattern suggests partial convergence of catalytic and regulatory subunits rather than interchangeability of related pathway perturbations, with Pcsk1n increased and canonical NFAT/RCAN transcripts remaining silent.

Fzd4 did not show a strong generic Frizzled-family or Norrin-receptor transcriptional signature in these neuronal Perturb-seq data. Across assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, restricted correlations between the top 200 Fzd4-scored genes and perturbations of Fzd2, Fzd3, Fzd6, Fzd9, Lrp5, Lrp6, Tspan12, Lgr4, or Ctnnb1 were weak; even in 308 CB GABA, which showed the largest nominal related-target correlations, no gene passed FDR and Fzd4 mRNA was only nominally decreased. These exploratory comparisons are limited because the seed Fzd4 signatures were themselves weak and did not include Ndp or Wnt ligand perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Agk showed a much weaker mitochondrial stress transcriptomic signature than Opa1 or Dnm1l in the same analysis, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells. Whereas Opa1 and Dnm1l produced many significant stress-response genes such as Asns, Ddit3, Chac1, and Cars, Agk yielded no adjusted hits in the global Wilcoxon summary. This suggests the dataset was capable of detecting mitochondrial transcriptional stress, but AGK perturbation engaged weakly or remained largely biochemical rather than transcriptional in these acute neuronal contexts; notably, the comparison is to mitochondrial-dynamics genes, not the same pathway as TIM22 carrier import.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Elp2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a strong positive-neighbor pattern in restricted signature-neighbor analysis, with Elp1 as the top correlate and Hspa9, Gfpt1, and Atp2a2 as second-tier neighbors converging on the same 151 FDR genes, while the best inverse neighbor, Pten, was weak. The associated program included ATF4 amino-acid starvation/integrated-stress-response output genes such as Atf4, Ddit3, Asns, Chac1, Slc7a5, and Trib3, suggesting a convergent stress/proteostasis module rather than a clean bidirectional axis, although these correlations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish pathway membership.

Scn9a showed a target-specific loss of signal rather than a generic failure to recover sodium-channel perturbations: across 20 Scn9a-profiled neuronal classes, the target transcript and downstream transcriptome stayed below nominal on-target and FDR-significant thresholds, and Scn9a signatures were nearly uncorrelated with related Nav1.7/action-potential module perturbations. In the same dataset, Scn1b, Scn1a, Scn2a, Scn8a, and the FHF regulator Fgf13 repeatedly showed self-transcript knockdown, indicating that family membership alone did not overcome cell-context specificity. This comparison is transcriptomic, not electrophysiological, and weak Scn9a signatures may suppress correlations.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Retreg1 knockdown showed weak or absent convergence with available autophagy and ER-shaping perturbations in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. Using only the top 200 Retreg1 non-target genes because the all-gene signature was weak, correlations with Atg5, Becn1, Rb1cc1, Vcp, Atl3, and Map1lc3a remained weak, and comparator perturbations produced Calr, Hspa5, Pdia6, and Rtn1 responses that Retreg1 did not. This supports a selective ER-phagy interpretation rather than Retreg1 acting as a simple transcriptomic surrogate for core macroautophagy loss, although key ER-phagy receptors were not perturbed.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ufsp2 showed its principal transcriptional response in 155 MB Glut cells, where the corrected program was a mixed oxidative-phosphorylation/V-ATPase module rather than a canonical unfolded-protein-response signature. The leading changes included Atp6v0c down with Cox5a, Ndufa2, and Timm8b up, and the broader set also included Rtn3, Srebf2, and Insig1. Although this pattern is compatible with UFMylation biology, only three leading genes drove the oxidative-phosphorylation enrichment, and canonical UPR markers Ddit3, Hspa5, and Xbp1 were nominal or absent after multiple-testing correction.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tgfbr1 did not yield a convergent perturbation module in this dataset: across many glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types, its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Tgfbr2, Smad2, Smad3, and Smad4, and unrestricted global nearest-neighbor searches produced only very weak correlations, with strongest neighbors around |r|≈0.10 and even negative-control targets among them. Cell-type-specific signals were also weak, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where no canonical TGF-beta signature or FDR-significant downstream gene emerged; this may reflect weak Tgfbr1 target engagement, making uncorrelated noise expected.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Ppard perturbation produced transcriptomic signatures that were nearly orthogonal to Ppara, Pparg, Rxra/Rxrb/Rxrg, Ppargc1a/Ppargc1b, and Ncoa1/Ncoa3 across matched cell types, and also did not align with the robust Srebf2 lipid-transcription-factor response. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, the largest positive neighbors were Dnm2 and Ppargc1a, while in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA the strongest negative and positive neighbors were Sec31a and Fzd3, but all non-self correlations remained weak, with |r| below 0.2. Because Ppard signatures were weak in this screen, the lack of correlation is more reliable than the identity of any weak neighbor.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tardbp showed weak-to-moderate positive signature similarity to spliceosome or splicing-regulator perturbations, most notably Srsf1, Prpf6, Ddx23, U2af2, and Snrnp70, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. The pattern was weak across all genes but stronger in top-200-gene restricted comparisons, linking the recurrent Tardbp module to RNA splicing/RNA processing; in this context, Tardbp and Snrnp70 were down and Unc13a was up. However, some comparator perturbations, especially Prpf6, Ddx23, and U2af2, had weak self-knockdown, so this remains hypothesis-generating.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Otulin in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut neurons showed a transcriptional signature that was largely uncoupled from available linear-ubiquitin and innate-immune pathway neighbors. Correlations with Cyld, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Nod2, Tlr2, TNFR-related perturbations, Traf3, Tlr3, and Tlr8 were low or opposing; the nearest positive comparator was Il1rap at only r=0.146, while Nod2 was the strongest negative at r=-0.113. This sole genome-wide Otulin response included Gpm6a induction without canonical inflammatory sentinels, but core LUBAC genes Rnf31, Rbck1, and Sharpin were not perturbed, and these correlations reflect transcriptomic similarity rather than biochemical epistasis.

Il1r1 did not show a convergent perturbation signature with its required co-receptor Il1rap: across the assayed neuronal classes, Il1r1–Il1rap same-cell transcriptome correlations were weak and slightly negative on average, and Il1rap also lacked corrected self-depletion. In the 308 CB GABA class, the strongest Il1rap anti-correlation and top Il1r1 neighbors were still weak and unsupported by corrected Il1r1 hits, while targeted comparisons to nearby inflammatory signaling perturbations, including Tlr9, found no strong Il1r1-like signature. This is best treated as a negative control on pathway-level interpretation of basal single-cell transcriptomes rather than evidence for an IL1R1-independent Il1rap mechanism.

Crhr1 showed weak, uncoupled transcriptional effects relative to downstream cAMP/PKA/CREB perturbations: in the same cell-type panel, Prkaca, Adcy3, Prkar1a, and Creb1 produced corrected transcriptional hits, whereas Crhr1 produced none, and its score vectors were poorly correlated with these neighbors. This contrast was also seen in overlapping neuronal classes, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Crhr1 transcript reduction was nominal but no corrected downstream markers were detected, while Prkaca was readily detected. These comparisons are signature-level and may reflect differences in guide efficiency or transcript detectability rather than biochemical cAMP output.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnc2 showed isoform- and cell-type-specific Perturb-seq effects rather than a shared Kv3 loss signature: in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Kcnc2 mRNA was depleted with buffered secondary responses in voltage-gated potassium transport/action-potential repolarization genes, yet Kcnc1 and Kcnc3 signatures were near-zero correlated with Kcnc2 in these engaged contexts. Kcnc3 had broader target engagement than Kcnc2, including 191 MB P MY GABA where Kcnc2 was not engaged, while 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut showed nominal Kcnc2 decrease but significant Kcnc3 decrease. These comparisons are limited to mRNA readouts and unequal perturbed-cell counts across paralogs.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Dlst showed a buffered, weakly engaged transcriptomic response that was largely uncoupled from Ogdh, Dld, and nearby tricarboxylic acid cycle perturbations. In 155 MB Glut, where Dlst engagement was best, the signature had near-zero correlation with Ogdh, Dld, Dlat, Pdha1, Pdhb, Idh3a, Mdh2, Sucla2, and Sdha, and no non-target gene reached adjusted significance despite Dlst adjusted p≈0.056. A similar pattern appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where nominal Dlst depletion lacked an adjusted downstream program, while related TCA perturbations showed much stronger on-target transcript knockdown; these comparisons are transcriptome-based, and OGDHC effects could differ at protein or metabolite levels.

Cacna1d perturbation produced transcriptome signatures that were largely uncoupled from related calcium-signaling perturbations, including Cacna1c, Cacna1g, Cacna2d1, Cacna2d2, Cacnb2, Cacnb4, Calm1/2/3, Camk2a/b/g, and Ryr2/3; in matched cell types, the strongest same-cell correlation reached only |r| = 0.143, and unbiased neighbor search found no strong match. This was seen despite network proximity within calcium-channel pathways, implying that molecular adjacency did not translate into interchangeable RNA phenotypes here. The Cacna1d signature itself was weak, however, so near-zero correlations may partly reflect limited target engagement or low signal-to-noise; among the few supported cell-type effects, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut showed a Vps28 decrease and 053 Sst Gaba showed Ddx24 upregulation.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Dync1h1 loss converged most strongly with Dctn1, not with weaker dynein-family comparators, through a shared sterol program involving Insig1, Msmo1, Fdps, Hmgcr, and Srebf2. This convergence appeared across responsive neuronal classes including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with the largest sterol induction and strongest Dctn1 alignment in 155 MB Glut. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Dync1h1 depletion was strong but sterol movement was only nominal, while Dctn1 and Rab7-like restricted signatures remained close. Pafah1b1 showed few cells and no FDR-positive direct signature, and Dync2h1/Dync2i1 did not yield interpretable on-target contrasts here.

Notch2 perturbation showed no detectable canonical NOTCH2 transcriptional output: across all tested signatures, Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Hey2, Heyl, and Nrarp remained unchanged, with every test reported at FDR=1.0. Because these HES/HEY-family and Nrarp genes are expected readouts of NICD–RBPJ–MAML signaling, their lack of response argues that active canonical Notch signaling was not reached in this experiment. However, since on-target Notch2 RNA was not reduced, this result indicates an absent pathway readout rather than genetically proven pathway inactivity.

Col4a1 did not show convergence with perturbations of related collagen-family genes, Ddr2, beta1/alpha integrins, or TGF-beta/SMAD neighbors, and even the strongest positive or negative whole-library signature neighbors were only weakly correlated. This pattern argues for a buffered or unengaged Col4a1 perturbation rather than a hidden canonical ECM-receptor transcriptional state. In 308 CB GABA cells, the largest nominal neighbor correlations still lacked FDR-significant genes, with Col4a1 p=0.823 and FDR=1.0. These comparisons used per-cell-type Wilcoxon score vectors, engagement strengths may differ across perturbations, and Col4a2 was not perturbed.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sox9 showed little coupling to its canonical Wnt/BMP/chondrogenic partner network across the 23 tested neuronal subclasses, including glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, and pineal populations. After Sox9 perturbation, Ctnnb1, Runx2, Col2a1, Fgf9, Fgfr3, Tcf7l2, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, Smad1/2/3/4, and Sox5 did not show coherent corrected responses, and Sox9 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Bmpr2, Col2a1, and Sox5 perturbation signatures. This weak neuronal signature should therefore not be read as partial activation of canonical chondrogenic or Wnt programs, while noting that the expected SOX9 network is largely defined in skeletal and developmental contexts.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zbtb7a perturbation in adult neurons was largely uncoupled at the mRNA level from canonical Notch, TGF-beta/SMAD, and fetal-globin-repressor pathway readouts: among queried genes including Dtx1, Smad4, Notch1-3, Hes1, Hes5, Hdac1, Ncor1, Ncor2, and Bcl11a, only Chd4 reached significance, and only in 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 155 MB Glut. This suggests that canonical ZBTB7A mechanisms described in other systems do not map one-to-one onto the adult neuronal signature, while leaving open regulation through binding, chromatin remodeling, or pathway activity changes without mRNA shifts.

Rara perturbation was not interchangeable with paralogous Rarb, Rarg, or Rxr-subunit perturbations under basal mouse-brain conditions. Across 21 shared cell types, Rarb, Rarg, Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg showed near-zero whole-signature correlations with Rara and collectively yielded no FDR-significant genes, indicating no detectable convergence in retinoic-acid/RAR-RXR transcriptional programs. In 145 MH-LH TH Glut cells, the only FDR-significant Rara response was Arrb2 up-regulation, and this was not reproduced by perturbing the related receptors; however, all family-member signatures were weak, so the result indicates lack of detectable convergence rather than opposing functions.

Tomm40 suppression, most clearly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells where Tomm40 itself was FDR-significantly reduced, did not produce an FDR-supported RNA signature of mitochondrial protein import, integrated stress, mitophagy, or respiratory-chain change. Atf4 and Ddit3, chaperonins Hspa9, Hspd1, and Hspe1, mitophagy genes Pink1 and Park7, TOM-complex receptors Tomm20, Tomm22, and Tomm70a, and selected OXPHOS or mtDNA transcripts including Ndufs1, Cox4i1, Atp5f1a, mt-Atp6, and mt-Atp8 all remained below significance. This negative RNA result does not exclude compartment-specific import defects, proteostatic compensation, or protein-level respiratory effects.

Erbb3 did not yield a coherent transcriptomic signature of the canonical neuregulin–ERBB3–PI3K/AKT–MAPK axis in this Perturb-seq dataset. Across 234 related comparisons, Erbb3 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Nrg1, Nrg2, Nrg3, Erbb4, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Akt3, Mapk1, and other RTK perturbations, with only weak same-cell-type correlations and no multiple-testing-significant differential expression in any assayed cell class. In 052 Pvalb Gaba and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, target engagement appeared Erbb4-biased rather than Erbb3-biased. This interpretation is limited by absent Erbb2 and Egfr perturbations, predominantly post-translational PI3K/MAPK activity, and lack of observed Erbb3 target engagement.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Homer2 showed a faint, exploratory SAPAP/PSD scaffold signal: Dlgap4 was a recurrent positive neighbor when similarity was restricted to the top 100 Homer2 genes, most notably in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and also in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This pattern suggests limited capture of SAPAP/DLGAP postsynaptic-density scaffold biology, but it is tempered by weak Homer2 transcript engagement in four of five contributing cell types, occasional low perturbed-cell counts, near-zero genome-wide canonical-partner correlations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and the fact that safe-target controls also reached extreme restricted-neighbor scores.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gigyf2 showed exploratory positive restricted-signature similarity to proteasome and TSC perturbations in the two main glutamatergic response cell types, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these cells, Psmb4, Psmc1, Pomp, Tsc1, and Tsc2 were among the strongest positive Gigyf2 neighbors in a top-300 gene comparison, suggesting convergence on a broader translation/proteostasis stress axis rather than only a narrow RQC module. This pattern is hypothesis-generating, however, because the correlations were computed only on the 300 most nominal Gigyf2 genes per cell type and were much smaller across the full transcriptome.

Satb2 showed no strong positive or negative convergence across all 23 assayed cell types: the assayed paralog Satb1 had no adjusted-significant genes and its correlation with Satb2 averaged 0.006 across the 22 shared Satb1/Satb2 cell types, while literature-connected comparators Cux1, Ski, and Runx2 and unbiased nearest neighbors all remained weak, with the strongest positive and negative correlations only r=0.196 and r=-0.186. This suggests no convincing SATB-family or SATB2-connected chromatin-regulatory module in the tested perturbation space, with the caveat that correlations were limited to assayed genes and cell types and that Lonp1 and Wdr26 are only mathematical neighbors, not validated Satb2 interactors.

Rab3gap2 does not phenocopy stronger synaptic-vesicle exocytosis perturbations at the mRNA-signature level. Although Snap25 and Stxbp1 knockdowns were robustly detected across many cell types, their transcriptional signatures were not correlated with Rab3gap2, so the historical Rab3-linked exocytosis context is not recovered here as a shared steady-state neuronal mRNA program. Rab3gap2 itself showed little multiple-testing-corrected transcriptional output beyond one on-target RNA measurement and one isolated off-target-locus response. This comparison tests transcriptomic similarity rather than vesicle release physiology, and Snap25 and Stxbp1 are pathway neighbors, not Rab3gap complex subunits.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarcb1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a strong bidirectional postsynaptic/glutamatergic rewiring program rather than a simple loss of synaptic identity: Grin1, Grin2b, Grin2c, Camk2a, Grm1, Gabra4, and Shank1 were downregulated, while Clstn1, Clstn2, Clstn3, Syt4, Grm5, Adam23, Dagla, and Rims3 were upregulated. This pattern is consistent with a remodeled synaptic state, but the pathway label is based on gene annotations and differential-expression enrichment, and the assay measured mRNA rather than receptor abundance or synaptic physiology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarcc2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed strongest convergence with the BAF/SWI-SNF core assembly partners Smarcb1, Smarce1, and Arid1a/Arid1b, with Smarcb1 reaching r=0.899 across the 185 Smarcc2 FDR genes. In contrast, Smarca2 self-depletion did not reproduce the Smarcc2 program: although Smarca2 mRNA was reduced, it yielded only its own row at FDR<0.05 and was essentially uncorrelated with the Smarcc2 signature. These comparisons are limited to the Smarcc2 FDR gene set, and several comparator perturbations had weak mRNA self-depletion.

Copg1 showed no reliable phenocopy from the only other assayed core COPI subunit, Copa, but this contrast appears to reflect weak Copa target engagement rather than a true biological separation. In this dataset, Copa had fewer perturbed cells, never achieved FDR-significant self-transcript depletion, and did not produce a Copg1-like signature, so the lack of α-COP/γ1-COP convergence is best treated as a comparator-quality warning. This caveat applies across the COPI-dependent ER/Golgi vesicle traffic context, including several glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal populations.

Crlf1 perturbation did not produce a detectable mRNA-level response in the canonical CRLF1–CLCF1/CNTFR/IL6ST/LIFR–JAK/STAT pathway: Crlf1 itself showed no measurable depletion across retained cell classes, and Clcf1, Cntfr, Lifr, Il6st, Jak1, Jak2, Tyk2, Stat3, and the feedback gene Socs3 were not significantly activated or repressed. This suggests that a cell-autonomous JAK/STAT transcriptional endpoint was not captured in this neuronal scRNA dataset, with the caveat that prior literature emphasized receptor-competent assays and phosphorylation readouts rather than steady-state transcriptomic changes.

Nrg2 showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signature correlation with Erbb3, Erbb4, and assayed RAF-MEK-ERK and PI3K pathway perturbations, including Braf, Raf1, Map2k1, Map2k2, Mapk1, Pik3ca, Pik3cb, Pik3r1, Akt3, and Pten, despite curated placement of NRG2 in ErbB signaling. In this dataset, Nrg2 therefore did not phenocopy ErbB receptor or intracellular signaling-node perturbations, and the ligand perturbation appeared transcriptomically uncoupled from those comparators. This interpretation is tempered by weak Nrg2 target engagement, missing Erbb2, Egfr, and Nrg4 assay rows, and the indirect nature of whole-transcriptome CRISPR signature correlations as pathway readouts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cacna2d1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a buffered, divergent transcriptional response that was not transcriptomically interchangeable with other voltage-gated calcium-channel perturbations, including Cacna1a, Cacna1c, Cacna1d, Cacna1e, Cacna1g, Cacna2d2, Cacnb2, Cacnb4, Cacng2, Cacng3, and Cacng8. Even when Cacna1c, Cacna1g, and Cacnb4 achieved corrected on-target knockdown in the same thalamic class, their signed differential-expression profiles were nearly uncorrelated with Cacna2d1. Because the Cacna2d1 signature contained few corrected downstream genes, this supports a lack of a strong shared transcriptional program rather than arguing against biochemical interaction.

Gabrb3 did not appear transcriptionally interchangeable with other GABA-A receptor subunits or inhibitory postsynaptic neighbors: perturbing Gabrb1, Gabrb2, Gabra1, Gabrg2, Gphn, Nlgn2, or Arhgef9 yielded mean full-transcriptome Pearson correlations near zero with the Gabrb3 signature. After Gabrb3 targeting, core GABA synthesis, transporter, metabotropic receptor, and gephyrin-scaffold transcripts were not FDR-altered, and the closest matched subunit response was only a nominal Gabra1 decrease rather than a corrected hit or compensatory upregulation. This contrast is transcriptomic, and several comparator signatures were themselves weak, so convergence at electrophysiology or receptor-surface levels remains possible.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Gabra1 knockdown was not interchangeable with the related GABA-A subunits Gabrb2 or Gabrg2: despite strong on-target depletion in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Gabra1 largely showed a sparse target-only signature with no broad compensatory receptor-subunit mRNA response. In contrast, Gabrb2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut induced activity-linked genes including Nr4a1, Vgf, and Nalf1, and Gabrg2 in 155 MB Glut induced Vgf. Gabra1-Gabrb2 convergence in 151 was real but weak, and these small, cell-type-restricted differences do not by themselves establish distinct channel biophysics.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: E2f4 showed a distinct, non-interchangeable perturbation profile in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic neurons: it produced 32 FDR genes, all up, consistent with selective partial derepression of an E2F4/DREAM cell-cycle repression module that included Mybl2, Cdk1, Ccna2, Mcm2, and Pcna. In the same cell type, E2f1 and E2f5 produced no FDR genes and Tfdp1 produced only two, with near-zero whole-signature correlation to E2f4 except for a weak Tfdp1 similarity. These negative related-perturbation results could also reflect guide efficiency, protein half-life, or basal expression, not biology alone.

Htr2b showed essentially no transcriptomic phenocopy across 21 sampled Htr2b neuronal classes: full-signature correlations with Htr2a and Htr2c were near zero, and other serotonin receptors (Htr1a, Htr1b, Htr1f, Htr3a, Htr3b, Htr4, Htr6, Htr7) as well as sampled Gq-pathway neighbors and related receptors (Adra1a, Chrm3, Grm1, Grm5, Plcb1, Mapk1, Prkca, Prkcg) also did not converge with Htr2b. In this dataset, canonical G alpha(q)-PLC-IP3-DAG-Ca2+/ERK signaling was not transduced into a robust FDR-supported mRNA response, so the near-zero correlations indicate lack of transcriptomic phenocopy rather than definitive functional antagonism, especially because Htr2b itself was weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grid2 showed a relatively weak, Grid2-specific signature rather than a general failure of synaptic or glutamate-receptor perturbations in this screen. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Grid2 scored poorly, whereas matched comparator perturbations for Grid1, Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Nrxn1, and Nlgn2 produced corrected differential-expression signal, and Grin1/Grin2/Grid1 showed strong direct target-transcript knockdown. Because these comparators used different guides and often had more perturbed cells, the contrast points to weak Grid2 reagent performance or expression rather than proving a unique biological buffering of Grid2.

Nr1i3 did not recover the expected CAR/PXR/RXR xenobiotic nuclear-receptor module in assayed mouse brain neurons. Across the 22 neuronal classes tested, Nr1i3 produced no multiple-testing-significant downstream transcriptional changes, and perturbations of Nr1i2 and the RXR partners Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg were likewise weak and poorly correlated with the Nr1i3 signature, indicating little convergent transcriptional behavior. Even in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, the only class with FDR-level Nr1i2 hits, similarity to Nr1i3 remained low. This differs from liver-focused, ligand-activation literature and may reflect the brain loss-of-function Perturb-seq context.

Wrn did not converge with the available DNA-damage perturbation signatures in this screen: Atr and Trp53, the only nearby pathway neighbors present, showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signed-score correlations with Wrn in shared cell types. Most direct WRN/RecQ resection partners, including Blm, Dna2, Exo1, Fen1, and Rpa genes, were not included as perturbation targets, so the dataset offers no robust related-target support for the weak Wrn phenotype. This negative signature-neighbor result is a limited check and does not imply that ATR or TP53 perturbation should phenocopy WRN loss.

Smad2 loss did not phenocopy nearby canonical TGF-beta/activin SMAD2-SMAD4 signaling perturbations in these neuronal data. Across 21 matched cell types, Smad2 score vectors were nearly orthogonal to Smad3, Smad4, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Ski, and Tgif1, and in the two cell classes where Smad2 had FDR-significant hits, the top unbiased positive or negative neighbors were still very weak (|r| ≤ 0.122; including Xpo1, Chp1, Ywhae, and Esrrg). This argues that pathway proximity did not yield exchangeable CRISPR transcriptomes here, although the Smad2 signature itself was weak and the comparisons were transcriptomic rather than phospho-SMAD assays.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gper1 perturbation did not yield a transcriptional signature of the expected GPER1 cAMP, EGFR-MAPK, or PI3K/Akt pathways: across 22 measured Gper1 cell classes, including 155 MB Glut, proximal signaling and immediate-early genes such as Gnas, Adcy1/3/5, Braf, Raf1, Mapk1/3, Creb1, Crem, Fos, Fosb, Fosl2, Jun, Jund, Pik3ca/b, Akt1/2/3, Egfr, Shc1, Src, and Ptk2 were not detectably altered, with inspected rows at FDR=1.0. In the same MB Glut class, Adcy3 and Mapk1 perturbations showed direct transcript loss, whereas Gper1 did not, suggesting assay or engagement uncoupling rather than absence of GPER signaling, especially given the weak receptor knockdown and the ligand-evoked, mainly human pathway context.

Gli1 perturbation in this neuronal Perturb-seq dataset did not produce a canonical Hedgehog/GLI transcriptional response: across all 23 profiled neuronal classes, Hh ligands, receptors, and effectors such as Shh, Dhh, Ihh, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Sufu, Kif7, Hhip, Boc, and Gas1 remained non-significant, and the whole-transcriptome Gli1 signature was nearly uncorrelated with perturbations of Smo, Ptch1, Ptch2, Gli2, Gli3, Gpr161, and Cdon. This suggests the observed neuronal response was largely uncoupled from canonical Hh feedback under these assay conditions, although weak neighbor perturbations and possible partial perturbation leave buffering versus technical failure unresolved.

L1cam perturbation produced transcriptional signatures that were not recapitulated by related adhesion and axon-guidance genes: in matched cells, score-vector correlations with Chl1, Nrcam, Cntn1, Nrp1, Nrp2, Plxna1, Plxna2, Plxna4, Fgfr1, Epb41l1, and Ank1/2/3 were near zero on average. This held in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA within the Reactome L1CAM interaction/axon-guidance module. The two FDR-confirmed on-target L1cam signatures also lacked strong positive or negative signature neighbors, although most L1cam signatures were weak and transcriptomic non-phenocopy does not rule out shared protein-level or morphological functions.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Med15 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons produced a thalamic down-signature centered on a synaptic and dendritic membrane module, including genes such as Grm1, Atp2a2, Pcp4, and Prkcd. Among assayed Mediator-family perturbations, Med13 and Med23 partially converged with this Med15 program, whereas Med12, Med13l, and Cdk8 showed weak or absent responses, with Med12 and Cdk8 lacking FDR-significant genes despite larger cell counts. Genome-wide score correlations were weak, so the overlap reflects a restricted down-gene set rather than a global phenocopy.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ndufb8 showed mostly non-convergent transcriptomic effects relative to other respiratory-chain perturbations: across 30 related targets, responses were largely dominated by loss of each targeted transcript, with 89 target-by-cell-type tests showing self-knockdown but only 4 also yielding any non-self significant gene. In six Ndufb8-sensitive contexts, including 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 308 CB GABA, correlations with Ndufs1, Ndufs2, Ndufs8, Ndufb9, Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Sdha, Uqcrc1, Cox5a, and Cox4i1 were near zero to modest, peaking at Ndufs8 in 308 CB GABA (r=0.196), so shared complex-I membership did not predict a common acute neuronal scRNA signature.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Thap1 showed partial concordance with the THAP1-complex neighbor Ogt: both perturbations decreased Prepl in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, consistent with a THAP1-HCFC1-OGT-linked transcriptional output. In 155 MB Glut, Prepl was part of a significant Prepl/Cuedc2/Fam117a triad, and in 191 MB P MY GABA it was part of a complete Thap1 triad. However, this overlap was narrow rather than interchangeable, as the Ogt comparison came from a restricted 16-feature scan in which Ogt ranked 16th, while Yy1 and Slc1a2 were stronger scalar neighbors without a direct curated THAP1-complex interpretation.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Cd40 showed no convergent transcriptional signature with assayed CD40/TNFRSF/NF-kappaB neighbors in 053 Sst Gaba or 308 CB GABA cells. Across Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Relb, Tnfrsf13c, Cd27, Tnfrsf4, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Tnfrsf9, and Tnfrsf11a perturbations, profiles were largely transcriptionally silent at FDR 0.05, and Cd40 was not strongly similar to any related target. The only FDR-significant event in this panel was Nav2 after Tnfrsf13c perturbation in Sst GABA cells. In 308 CB GABA, weak Cd40 neighbor correlations and nominal Fcor and Sfxn5 outliers did not resolve into a significant module, consistent with an inactive noncanonical NF-kappaB program in these measured states; interpretation is limited because Cd40lg, Traf2, and Traf6 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ndufb3 showed a divergent transcriptomic pattern in 191 MB P MY GABA, the only cell type with FDR-supported downstream Ndufb3 hits: unlike related complex I perturbations Ndufa13, Ndufb8, Ndufb10, and Ndufs8, which displayed much stronger self-transcript depletion, the Ndufb3 score vector had near-zero correlations with the measured Nduf/Ndufaf signatures and no strong signature neighbors. This suggests the Ogdh/Pcbp3-associated Ndufb3 signal should not be treated as an interchangeable mitochondrial respiratory-chain complex I module, although the contrast is transcriptomic, cell-type-restricted, and could reflect weak Ndufb3 target engagement rather than subunit-specific biology.

Nfkb2 showed no transcriptomic convergence with the available NF-κB-family or upstream receptor/kinase perturbations in this brain Perturb-seq assay: Nfkb1, Rel, Relb, Chuk, Tlr4, Tnfrsf11a, Tnfrsf1a, and Tnfrsf1b were all FDR-silent and had near-zero score-vector correlations with Nfkb2. This suggests that noncanonical NF-κB/p100-p52-RelB signaling and canonical NF-κB/TNF-TLR feedback were buffered or too weak to detect here, with the caveat that correlations were dominated by a weak Nfkb2 signature and several relevant targets, including Rela, Map3k14, Bcl3, Nfkbia, and Nfkbib, were not perturbed.

Jarid2 showed weak, largely uncoupled signatures that did not converge with or strongly oppose the available H3K27 demethylase, Trithorax, or SWI/SNF-family chromatin perturbations. Across the assayed pathway neighbors, Jarid2 score vectors were near zero against Kdm6a, Kdm6b, Arid1b, Smarca4, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Kmt2a, Kmt2d, Setd1a, and Kdm5b, arguing against a generic chromatin-regulator or H3K27-axis response. In 308 CB GABA, Jarid2 had a nominal multi-gene module but still lacked FDR-supported genes and only weak coupling to these comparators; direct PRC2 subunit perturbations were not available.

Sucla2 showed no robust phenocopy with its expected complex partner Suclg1 in the ADP-forming succinate-CoA ligase/TCA cycle, but this negative comparison is technically limited. Suclg1 perturbation never achieved corrected self-knockdown, and Sucla2–Suclg1 signature correlations were essentially zero, so the contrast is better explained by weak Suclg1 target engagement than by a confident alpha-versus-beta subunit divergence. Across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Sucla2 transcript decreased without corrected downstream or compensatory Suclg1/Suclg2 responses.

Rarb did not show a stable transcriptomic signature shared with Rara, Rarg, or the Rxr-family perturbations (Rxra, Rxrb, Rxrg) in the observed retinoic acid/RAR-RXR nuclear receptor signaling context. Across matched cell-type score vectors, Rarb signatures were near-zero correlated with these comparator perturbations, so the observed Rarb effect should not be treated as a canonical retinoid-receptor module in this dataset. This interpretation is tempered by weak or undetected on-target Rarb knockdown in every matched cell type tested and by similarly modest target engagement for the receptor comparators, which separates the observed signatures but does not establish mechanistic independence.

Ndufa9 showed a notably weak RNA-level perturbation response compared with related mitochondrial complex I targets in the same screen. Unlike Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, Ndufb8, and Ndufs8, Ndufa9 had no significant self-transcript depletion or downstream FDR-significant rows, and it remained near the bottom of the response distribution, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells where other complex-I perturbations were active. This argues against interpreting the Ndufa9 rows as a generic complex-I failure signature, while remaining consistent with weak guide engagement or RNA-level buffering; comparisons are limited by guide efficiency, cell numbers, and the mix of assembly factors and structural subunits.

Ndufa10 perturbation, like many related Nduf/Ndufaf complex I biogenesis perturbations, was dominated by depletion of the target transcript itself rather than a recurrent downstream FDR expression program. Across 25 related perturbations other than Ndufa4, 61 of 70 FDR hits were the perturbed transcript, with only 9 non-target genes, and an exploratory restricted-signature search found only weak non-self neighbors for Ndufa10. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, target transcripts were reduced while downstream nuclear expression appeared buffered; however, comparisons mixed structural subunits and assembly factors and were not normalized for guide efficiency.

Hoxa3 showed a weak, nonconvergent signature in the assayed brain classes: available Hox-family perturbations, anterior-HOX/retinoic-acid chromatin neighbors including Pbx1, Mafb, Rara, Rxra, Kdm6a, Kmt2c, and Kmt2d, and even the strongest positive or negative transcriptome-wide neighbors were all only weakly correlated. This pattern was seen across classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and 308 CB GABA, where Hoxa3 was measurable but unchanged. Because the Hoxa3 vector had no FDR hits and the closest group-3 paralogs Hoxb3 and Hoxd3 were not screened, the result is exploratory but argues against a coherent active HOX-patterning module around Hoxa3 in these cell classes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cacnb2 showed a sparse transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with CaV structural subunit perturbations overall largely limited to self-only or no FDR-significant effects under the same Wilcoxon pipeline. This contrasted with broad, multi-cell-type FDR-supported signatures for the calcium-linked excitability comparators Atp2a2 and Grin1. The pattern suggests acute disruption of the high-voltage calcium-channel complex is transcriptionally buffered in these cells, although only a subset of CaV-family genes was assayed, excluding Cacnb1, Cacnb3, and Cacna1b.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Prox1 showed an unusual on-target transcript pattern: in the only FDR-positive context, the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, measured Prox1 mRNA increased rather than decreased (logFC +0.440, FDR 0.00446), whereas 21 other Prox1-assayed cell types were not significant. This suggests the active thalamic signature is best interpreted as a guide-associated Prox1 loss-of-function phenotype with edited or feedback-altered transcript levels, not a conventional mRNA knockdown. The dataset does not report indels or protein loss, so the Prox1 mRNA increase could reflect feedback, altered transcript stability, guide-selection bias, or transcript preservation after coding disruption.

Stat1 perturbation showed nominal convergence with Ifngr1 and Ifngr2 on an MHC-I-related module, including markers such as B2m, H2-K1, and Nlrc5, whereas Ifnar1, Ifnar2, Stat2, and Irf9 perturbations did not phenocopy this pattern across 23 cell types under basal neuronal conditions. The separation was also reflected by tiny whole-transcriptome correlations between Stat1 and these canonical type-I IFN/ISGF3 neighbors. This suggests a basal IFNGR-biased MHC-I branch rather than a full IFNAR/ISGF3 signature, although weak self-transcript depletion for several comparator perturbations could mask true type-I relationships.

Rfx7 showed an orthogonal transcriptional profile in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq screen: it did not phenocopy the assayed Rfx3 paralog, Trp53, Ep300, Crebbp, or PI3K/mTOR-pathway perturbations including Pten, Mtor, Tsc1, Tsc2, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, and Pik3r2. Rfx7-versus-Rfx3 correlations were essentially zero across all 22 shared cell classes, and even its top whole-signature neighbors were weak, including in the four classes with the largest nominal Rfx7 effects. This interpretation is limited because correlations were computed from bulk score vectors within annotated cell classes, and weak Rfx7 engagement could dampen true pathway similarity.

Agtr2 showed a weak, nonconvergent renin-angiotensin perturbation profile: the closest assayed receptor/regulator neighbors, Agtr1a and Agtrap, were also target-negative with no FDR-significant genes, while Atp6ap2 was efficiently depleted in 11 of 21 broad cell types yet remained nearly uncorrelated with Agtr2. This pattern was seen even in high-count groups such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Agtr2 lacked FDR-supported responses but Atp6ap2 showed strong engagement. Because Atp6ap2 is also a V-ATPase accessory protein, these broad-class all-gene correlations argue that related renin-angiotensin perturbations are either uninformative or biologically divergent from the weak Agtr2 signature.

Actb perturbation showed a nonreciprocal relationship with Actg1 in this screen: Actb guides induced Actg1 and Flna, whereas Actg1 perturbation mostly caused Actg1 self-depletion and did not reproduce the Actb-induced program, with Actb-versus-Actg1 signature correlations near zero across 22 matched cell types. In 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, Actb produced a broader response including Flna, Actg1, Rsu1, Fads1, and Fads2, and this was the only context where Actg1 perturbation also significantly induced Flna. A caveat is that Actb-versus-Actg1 comparisons relied on downstream signatures because Actb itself was absent from response-gene rows, and Actg1 self-depletion reached FDR significance in only 8 of 22 shared cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Sin3a did not behave like a generic HDAC/chromatin perturbation in these neurons. Across the six largest responder cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, available recruiters or HDAC/chromatin comparators such as Mecp2, Rest, Chd4, Gatad2b, Mbd2, Hdac4, Hdac5, and Hdac8 were mostly uncorrelated with or opposed to the Sin3a signature, while Kansl1, Bap1, and Kdm5c were recurrent negative neighbors. This contrast is qualified by the absence of canonical SIN3-HDAC core subunit perturbations including Sin3b, Hdac1, Hdac2, Rbbp4, and Rbbp7.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Trhr showed transcriptomic signatures that were largely uncoupled from assayed Gq/phosphoinositide pathway perturbations across many glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types, with score correlations near zero versus Plcb1, Itpr1, and Prkca, and similarly little alignment with other sampled Gq-coupled receptors such as Htr2a, Htr2c, Grm1, Grm5, Adra1a, and Chrm3. Although TRHR is curated in Gαq signaling, this dataset did not include Trh, Trhr2, Gnaq, or Gna11, so weak Trhr engagement or missing proximal nodes could explain why canonical pathway loss was not captured.

Nup93 showed a weak, uncoupled CRISPRi transcriptional readout compared with the other assayed nucleoporins Tpr and Ranbp2: Nup93 had zero FDR hits and near-zero whole-transcriptome correlations with both, whereas Tpr and Ranbp2 produced FDR-supported signatures in nuclear pore complex assembly and nucleocytoplasmic transport contexts. This contrast appeared across cell classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA, arguing against a generic shared NPC-stress signature here. However, direct Nup93 inner-ring partners such as Nup155, Nup205, Nup188, Nup35, Ndc1, and Pom121 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Atp6v1a in 052 Pvalb Gaba recovered a V-ATPase/lysosomal acidification neighborhood, with Atp6v0c as the second-nearest non-self signature and Atp6v1e1 and Atp6v1b2 also among the closest neighbors, yet its transcriptional impact was weak: the strongest on-target depletion occurred in Pvalb interneurons, but no non-target gene passed 5% FDR. By contrast, Atp6v0c triggered a broad synaptic, ion-channel, and stress-response program, including reduced Kcnc1, Gabrd, Gria2, Gria3, Pvalb, and Scg2, while Atp6v1b2 produced a smaller significant module. This contrast may partly reflect differences in perturbation efficiency and cell counts, and Atp6v0c could also reveal V0-sector functions not captured by Atp6v1a depletion.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Hoxa1 showed a weak, largely uninformative same-cell transcriptional signature across 23 targeted cell types, including cortical glutamatergic neurons, multiple GABAergic classes, midbrain dopamine, pineal glutamatergic cells, and cerebellar GABA, and it was essentially orthogonal to available Hox-family, Pbx/Meis/Pknox, and retinoic-acid receptor perturbations such as Pbx1, Meis2, and Rarb. Across these comparisons, absolute Pearson correlations were at most 0.115, with no detectable convergence despite expected pathway relatedness; interpretation is limited because Hoxa1 engagement was not measurable, no gene reached FDR < 0.10, Hoxb1 was unavailable as a comparator, and correlations were computed from restricted same-cell signatures rather than raw counts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Celf2 is not interchangeable with other neuronal RNA-binding or RNA-processing perturbations in this expression readout. In the dominant Celf2-responsive classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Rbfox1, Fmr1, Adar, Adarb1, Hnrnpu, and Srsf1 showed near-zero or negative correlations with the Celf2 signature, while the closest neighbors such as Cic, Dctn1, Dync1h1, and Tsc2 were only modestly similar (r about 0.20-0.26). This panel reflects gene-abundance scores rather than isoform changes, so shared regulation of unmeasured splice events may still be missed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cul3 showed only weak, cell-type-restricted transcriptomic similarity to other assayed perturbations: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Arih1 was the top whole-signature neighbor, and in 155 MB Glut, Tpr was the top neighbor, but all non-self correlations were small. In these responsive populations, available NRF2- and CRL-related comparators, including Nfe2l2, Klhl7, Fbxw7, and Akap11, were near zero, so no assayed pathway neighbor phenocopied the Cul3 mRNA state. This remains exploratory because score-vector correlations were computed one cell type at a time and key complex members such as Rbx1 and Keap1 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Unc13b did not phenocopy related presynaptic perturbations across 12 matched cell types, including cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic neurons, Pvalb GABA, hypothalamic GABA, midbrain glutamatergic, and cerebellar GABA populations. In this panel, Snap25, Stxbp1, and Stx1b often showed detectable repression of their own transcripts, whereas Unc13a, Unc13b, and Unc13c did not at the transcript level, and Unc13b’s transcriptome-wide signature correlations with Unc13a, Unc13c, Stxbp1, Stx1b, Snap25, and Cacna1a were near zero. These comparisons rely on transcriptome-wide Wilcoxon scores, some comparator perturbations also had limited downstream signatures, and mRNA knockdown does not fully measure protein engagement.

Wnk1 did not behave as transcriptomically interchangeable with its paralog Wnk3 in this Perturb-seq screen. Across the 22 cell types tested for both genes, Wnk1-versus-Wnk3 score-vector correlations were near zero, ranging from r=-0.0266 to 0.1604, despite both being discussed in the WNK-SPAK/OSR1–cation-chloride cotransporter signaling axis with Stk39, Oxsr1, Slc12a2, Slc12a5, Cul3, and Klhl3. In the same pan-cell-type view, Wnk1 showed no FDR-significant genome-wide mRNA shift and no recurrent correlated WNK-axis comparator signature; however, Wnk3 target engagement was weak, so this supports a failure to observe interchangeability rather than proving mechanistic divergence.

Gli2 perturbation did not mobilize the canonical Hedgehog/GLI feedback program in this neuronal Perturb-seq dataset: Gli1, Ptch1, Ptch2, Hhip, Boc, Sufu, and Kif7 remained unchanged, with weak overall Gli2 signature support and no reproducible movement of the GLI/SUFU/KIF7 module. This absence was also seen in the largest sampled neuronal subclasses, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where many perturbed cells still yielded min FDR=1.0, arguing against a simple low-power explanation. The finding suggests these mature neurons were not running an acute detectable canonical Smoothened-to-GLI transcriptional output, while not excluding ciliary or protein-level GLI regulation, developmental progenitor responses, or responses in glia and tumors.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cfl2 showed weak or absent convergence with nearby actin-pathway perturbations in the two cell types where Cfl2 knockdown reached FDR, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA. In 155 MB Glut, restricted top-100 Cfl2 signature correlations were modest for Pak1 and near zero for Actg1 and Cyfip2, while in 191 MB P MY GABA all available comparators were small in magnitude. This cautions against treating the Cfl2 profile as a simple transcriptional readout of ADF/cofilin actin-filament turnover, with the caveat that only top-100 Cfl2 genes were compared, Tpm3 was not itself FDR-significant, and transcriptome similarity is an indirect proxy for actin dynamics.

Tanc2 was not transcriptionally interchangeable with nearby postsynaptic or neurodevelopmental perturbations: across the 21 cell types where Tanc2 was assayed, it produced no FDR-significant signatures and showed only weak cosine-score convergence with a curated comparator set. In contrast, many related perturbations, including Dlg4, Shank2, Shank3, Nrxn1, Nlgn3, Ctnnb1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Mapk8ip1, and Camk2a, had at least one significant cell-type signature, suggesting that within postsynaptic density and dendritic-spine scaffold biology, Tanc2 appears more buffered than several neighboring synaptic perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Tmem63a showed weak engagement in this mouse brain Perturb-seq dataset and did not phenocopy related channel perturbations: unlike Tmem63b, which displayed clear self-transcript depletion across 10 neuronal classes, Tmem63a and Tmem63c showed no FDR-significant self-depletion, and whole-signature correlations of Tmem63a with Tmem63b, Tmem63c, Trpv4, and Trpm7 were near zero across the assayed neuronal classes. The contrast was especially evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Tmem63b self-depletion was strongest, arguing against simple TMEM63 paralog interchangeability here, while remaining mainly an internal assay-control observation because Tmem63a itself was only weakly engaged.

Sos2 showed no coherent convergent transcriptional module in this Perturb-seq dataset: across 40,279 signature-neighbor comparisons, the strongest positive or negative correlations were weak (maximum absolute Pearson r = 0.204), and the nominal p<0.001 neighbors were mostly one-off genes such as Zbtb21, Caly, Mc3r, and Fktn rather than GRB2/SOS/RAS pathway members. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, the largest Sos2 correlations were still weak and not SOS/RAS neighbors. These data argue against assigning a Ras, RAC1, or PI3K module from this dataset alone, while noting that noise may dilute correlations and that acute post-translational SOS2 signaling could be missed by steady-state scRNA-seq.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc17a5 showed a reproducible transcriptomic neighborhood that aligned more strongly with endolysosomal trafficking, acidification, and nutrient-sensing perturbations than with several other lysosomal disease genes. Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, Vps41, Rab7, Tsc1, Tsc2, Atp6v0a1, and Atp6v1a were recurrent positive neighbors, while Gns, Lamp2, and Ppt1 were weak or inconsistent matches; Uba5, Ufc1, and Ufsp2 were recurrent anti-neighbors. This signature-restricted analysis used the top 200 Slc17a5-scoring genes per cell type and reflects correlation rather than physical interaction or epistasis.

Sos1 showed weak or absent whole-transcriptome similarity to other perturbations, including the RAS/MAPK neighbors Nf1, Map2k1, Braf, and Ntrk2, even though those genes produced detectable, often FDR-significant phenotypes in the same dataset. Across the dataset, no strong positive or negative Sos1 transcriptional neighbor was found; instead, Sos1 loss was only locally connected to the Vgf axis, with a nominal Vgf decrease in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA that matched Braf and opposed Nf1, while 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed stronger neighbor responses but Sos1 remained weak. These correlations were based on Wilcoxon-score vectors rather than raw expression, and low target engagement could reduce apparent similarity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Stat2 showed near-null on-target effects in this neuronal Perturb-seq dataset: its own-transcript decrease was only nominal and never FDR-significant, including in 155 MB Glut, and transcriptome-wide signatures did not reveal a convincing Stat2-specific convergent or opposing perturbation. In contrast, the ISGF3 partner Stat1 achieved corrected self-depletion in caudal neuronal populations, notably 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, while Irf9 resembled Stat2 in lacking a robust corrected signature. This dataset-specific contrast, based on mRNA rather than matched protein knockdown and with weak-signature correlations dominated by broad positive structure, cautions against treating Stat2 and Irf9 guides as interchangeable with Stat1 for type-I interferon/ISGF3 signaling here.

Por knockdown did not produce an FDR-significant basal induction of curated oxidative-stress, ER-stress, ferroptosis, cholesterol, or retinoic-acid sentinel transcripts, including Slc7a11, Hmox1, Nqo1, Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Xbp1, Sqle, Cyp26a1/1b/1c, Aldh1a1/1a2, and Rarb. This was also true in the clearest Por-responsive class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, which showed no significant sentinel stress or retinoid induction and only weak signature-neighbor convergence. Because the assay used a small mRNA sentinel panel rather than metabolomic or lipid-peroxidation readouts, the absence of transcriptional induction does not exclude enzymatic pathway defects after partial CRISPRi knockdown.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Dhx9 showed positive signature convergence with a nuclear-pore/spliceosome/nuclear-transport axis, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where recurrent neighbors included Tpr, Tnpo3, Srsf1, Ddx23, Prpf6, U2af2, and Xpo1. This pattern suggests a neuronal response closer to nuclear RNP disruption than to a generic helicase-family effect, while remaining uncoupled from RISC/ADAR comparators such as Dicer1, Ago1, Ago2, Adar, and Adarb1. An exploratory proteasome-like component, including Psmc1, Psmc5, Psmb4, and Pomp, was also seen in some stronger classes, but these correlations were limited to the top 500 Dhx9 genes and do not establish direct physical interaction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ndufs4 showed a notably weaker perturbation signature than many other complex I Nduf genes in this atlas. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Ndufs4 had its largest cell count and a nominal self-hit, it lacked downstream FDR-significant genes, while many related subunits, including Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, Ndufb8, and Ndufs8, showed strong on-target depletion. This suggests Ndufs4 should not be treated as interchangeable with stronger complex I signatures here, although the contrast is based on target-transcript differential expression and FDR hit counts rather than matched guide cutting efficiency or respiratory-chain activity.

Sucla2 fit a broader TCA/OXPHOS perturbation pattern in which mitochondrial enzymes showed strong self-knockdown but very sparse non-self transcriptomic effects. Across 16 related perturbations, including Aco2, Cox4i1, Dld, Dlst, Idh3a, Ndufs4, Ndufs8, Ogdh, Pdha1, Pdhb, Sdha, Sdhb, Suclg1, Uqcrc1, and Uqcrfs1, downstream FDR calls were limited, and Sucla2 had no strong positive or negative genome-wide signature neighbor in the three FDR-engaged cell types. This suggests weak coupling to whole-transcriptome DE in this dataset, though the comparator set was manually curated and assessed only at the transcript DE-summary level.

Lpar6 showed near-zero within-cell restricted-signature correlations with the available related GPCR perturbations S1pr2, P2ry12, P2ry14, and Cnr1, indicating that these lipid/P2Y-family receptor perturbations were not useful surrogates for Lpar6 in this screen. Across all 21 Lpar6-tested neuronal cell groups, no glutamatergic or GABAergic group showed Lpar6 target-transcript depletion or FDR-supported downstream differential expression, so the related-GPCR comparisons remained restricted and exploratory. Interpretation is further limited because the correlations used the top 200 uncorrected Lpar6 genes, and canonical Lpar1-Lpar5 and immediate GNA12/GNA13/Rho pathway nodes were not perturbed.

Htr4 did not form a detectable transcriptional module with the shared 5-HT4/5-HT6/5-HT7 serotonin receptor to G alpha(s)-cAMP-PKA pathway in this CRISPR transcriptomic dataset. Whole-signature correlations between Htr4 and Htr6 or Htr7 were near zero, and Htr4 also showed negligible correlation with assayed Gs/cAMP neighbors including Gnas, Adcy3, Adcy5, Prkaca, and Pde4d; all three receptor perturbations had zero FDR-significant hits. Because receptor mRNAs showed weak self-depletion, this is best interpreted as no detectable convergence at the signature level rather than proof that these receptors cannot converge biochemically.
