cell_types: 308 CB GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Pik3cb showed mostly uncorrelated RNA signatures relative to class-IA PI3K-related perturbations, including Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Pik3r2, Pten, Mtor, Rptor, and Akt3, across 308 CB GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut cells. Same-cell-type correlations were generally near zero; even the strongest related-target matches were weak, such as Pik3cb–Pik3ca in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut (r=0.128), and the largest related-target correlation overall was only r=0.169. Because the Pik3cb signature itself was weak and global neighbor searches also showed low absolute correlations, these pathway-near perturbations were not interchangeable at the transcriptome level and should be interpreted isoform-by-isoform and cell-type-by-cell-type.

Ptprn showed a self-only mRNA phenotype that was mirrored by its closest paralog Ptprn2, but the two perturbations did not share a downstream transcriptomic signature. Ptprn2 knockdown was stronger, with on-target depletion significant in 16 of 22 cell types, yet all significant Ptprn2 rows were Ptprn2 itself; similarly, Ptprn in strongly engaged glutamatergic contexts such as 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut yielded no non-target FDR hits. Across 21 matched cell types, Ptprn and Ptprn2 ranked signatures were essentially uncorrelated after excluding the two target transcripts, suggesting convergent self-only differential expression without a shared nonself mRNA module in dense-core secretory vesicle biology involving Cpe and Pcsk2.

Icos showed no convergent signature with assayed immune-costimulation, TCR, IL-2 receptor, PI3K, Src, or NF-kB perturbations in mouse brain: across 251 shared cell-type comparisons with Cd40, Cd80, Pik3r1, Il2ra, Il2rb, Il2rg, Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd3g, Cd247, Fyn, and Nfkb1, the maximum absolute Pearson correlation to the Icos score vector was only 0.156. Across 21 Icos-sampled brain classes, Icos also lacked target-transcript engagement, produced no FDR-significant DE, and did not induce canonical ICOS-pathway transcripts; its strongest genome-wide neighbors were weak and even included safe-target controls, with 308 CB GABA showing only modest correlations to Wdr26, Hmgcr, and P2ry14. Only perturbations present in the screen could be compared, and ICOSL was measured as a transcript but not perturbed.

Nr1h2 showed a broad null in this Perturb-seq dataset: across 23 assayed neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, it produced no FDR-supported target or downstream transcriptional effects, with only exploratory nominal decreases in Abca1, Abcg1, Acox1, and Srebf2 in that one class. This was not a general failure to detect sterol programs, because Srebf2 perturbation gave a strong multi-cell-type cholesterol-biosynthesis and uptake signature, with recurrent decreases in Insig1, Cyp51, Dhcr24, and Msmo1 in 16/22 cell types, whereas Nr1h3, Rxra/Rxrb/Rxrg, Abca1, and Srebf1 likewise had zero FDR hits; the contrast reflects branch-specific pathway responsiveness rather than a direct complex-member comparison.

Icos perturbation in 21 Icos-sampled mouse brain classes showed no detectable canonical downstream RNA response: Icosl, PI3K/AKT components Pik3r1, Pik3cd, Akt1, Akt2, and Akt3, NF-kB/Src-related genes Nfkb1, Fyn, and Lck, and Tfh-effector markers Bcl6, Cxcr5, and Il21 were all nonsignificant, with no FDR-significant differential expression and no resemblance to assayed immune-neighbor programs. This suggests the ICOSL, PI3K/AKT, NF-kB/Src, and Tfh transcript sets are uncoupled from Icos perturbation in this brain-cell context, although the assay measures steady-state RNA rather than acute phosphorylation or PI3K lipid signaling.

Cd4 showed a weak perturbational signature with no convergent module in this dataset: curated immune or MHC neighbors available in the library, including Ccr5, Cxcr4, and H2-Eb1, had essentially zero transcriptomic correlation with Cd4, and an unbiased scan across 2,045 targets found a largest non-self positive correlation of only r=0.0268. Thus, neither curated CD4-associated neighbors nor whole-library signatures reproduced the Cd4 profile. This near-zero correlation does not rule out shared protein-level biology in true immune cells, and several STRING partners, including Lck, Zap70, Cd8a, and H2-Ab1, were not assayed here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cisd2 depletion did not phenocopy the Opa1-linked integrated-stress transcriptional program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these same midbrain classes, Opa1 perturbation induced Asns, Chac1, and Ddit3 with dozens of differentially expressed genes, whereas Cisd2 showed strong on-target knockdown but sparse or no FDR-significant non-target changes; in 155 MB Glut, the strongest Cisd2 knockdown was not accompanied by any FDR-significant non-target transcript. This suggests that, in this assay, CISD2-related ER-mitochondrial biology was not read out as a generic mitochondrial amino-acid stress signature, with the caveat that the comparison relies on mRNA signatures and the 155 Opa1 signal was only nominal.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Hmgb1 did not phenocopy its assayed receptor or MAPK/NF-kappaB/IRF pathway neighbors in neuronal groups. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, same-cell-type transcriptome-wide score correlations between Hmgb1 and Ager, Cd14, Tlr2, Tlr4, Nfkb1/2, Rel/Relb, Irf3/7, Tbk1, Traf3, Map2k1/2/6, and Mapk8/9 were near zero. This argues that the Hmgb1 signature was not simply a weak extracellular HMGB1-TLR/RAGE inflammatory response; notably, Map2k1 produced FDR-significant responses in overlapping neuronal groups, including genes such as Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, and Unc13a. These comparisons are based on transcriptome-wide correlations, and many receptor perturbations also lacked strong on-target expression in these neurons.

Chuk showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to nearby NF-κB/TLR/TNFR perturbations and to all unbiased same-cell signature neighbors: across 535 correlations to curated pathway neighbors, the maximum absolute correlation was only 0.132, and across all 43,663 non-self same-cell comparisons the strongest positive and negative neighbors remained weak at 0.182 and -0.161. Thus, although network resources place CHUK near Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Relb, Traf3, Map3k7, Tlr7, and Tnfrsf11a, these perturbations did not phenocopy Chuk, consistent with context-dependent pathway deployment rather than a strong basal linear module. This interpretation is tempered by the weak Chuk signatures and by the absence of Ikbkb, Ikbkg, Rela, and Nfkbia perturbations, with no receptor stimulus provided.

Itga9 did not show a convergent transcriptomic signature with its canonical partner Itgb1 or with other integrin alpha/beta subunits. Across shared cell classes, Itga9 and Itgb1 score-vector correlations were centered near zero, and among nine integrin-subunit perturbations only two single-gene FDR hits were seen outside Itga9, including isolated hits for Itga8 in 052 Pvalb Gaba and Itga6 in 191 MB P MY GABA. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Itga9 showed no FDR response despite a nominal Araf decrease. Because many related integrin perturbations had weak on-target transcript depletion, these results argue against a detectable ITGA9:ITGB1 ECM-adhesion transcriptional module, not against alpha9-beta1 signaling per se.

Prdm5 did not align with a detectable chromatin- or matrix-neighbor module in this dataset. Although Ctcf and Ehmt1 were active perturbations, their same-cell transcriptomic signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Prdm5, and Nsd2 and Col11a1 were likewise uncorrelated; across a genome-wide target-neighbor scan, no non-Prdm5 target showed a strong positive or negative correlation with the Prdm5 signature. Across all 23 Prdm5-tested neuronal subclasses, there were no FDR-supported Prdm5 genes, no self-transcript change, and no ECM program, with the caveat that only same-cell correlations were tested and several reported interactors were not exact perturbation targets.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Prepl showed a nonconvergent transcriptional profile relative to Snap25, Ache, Ide, Prep, Cltc, and Nsf: in the high-engagement 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut populations, correlations between the Prepl-restricted top-200-gene signature and these synaptic-vesicle, cholinergic, clathrin, or paralogous endopeptidase perturbations stayed near zero, even where both perturbations had clear target knockdown. This pattern is consistent with a PREPL-specific AP-1/trans-Golgi trafficking or vesicle-filling liability rather than a generic synaptic failure program, although the comparison relied on a restricted signature, some Nsf and Cltc/Prep knockdowns were only nominal, and direct AP-1 subunits were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfhx3 perturbation in the responsive thalamic class 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not engage the curated RUNX3-SMAD-CDKN1A transcription module: Runx3, Smad2, Smad3, and Smad4 signatures were uncorrelated with Zfhx3, and Cdkn1a was unchanged after Zfhx3 perturbation. Thus, the RUNX3-ZFHX3-TGF-beta mechanism described in human gastric systems appears non-dominant in these mouse neuronal Perturb-seq data, with pathway neighbors showing no broad convergence with the Zfhx3 response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Glmn in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a neuronal RNA response that FKBP1A knockdown did not phenocopy: Fkbp1a was strongly depleted by its own perturbation, yet the Glmn–Fkbp1a signature correlation in that same cell type was essentially zero (r=0.0007). This divergence suggests that, in this dataset, the FKBP-associated GLMN physical-interaction branch is not the main route to the Glmn phenotype, although the contrast is limited because only one FKBP family perturbation with clear on-target detection was available.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfhx3 perturbation in the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, the only cell class with an FDR-supported Zfhx3 response, induced Zfhx4 but not Zfhx2. However, direct perturbation of Zfhx2 or Zfhx4 produced transcriptomic signatures that were nearly uncorrelated with the Zfhx3 signature, indicating nonconvergent ZFHX-family transcriptional responses. This pattern is consistent with possible compensation or a secondary marker role for Zfhx4 rather than functional interchangeability with Zfhx3, although a small shared regulatory submodule cannot be excluded.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ank3 showed a thalamus-specific response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells that was not reproduced by the ankyrin paralogs Ank1 or Ank2. In this Ank3-responsive class, Ank1 and Ank2 had more perturbed cells than Ank3 yet yielded no FDR-significant genes, and their full transcriptional signatures were near-orthogonal to the Ank3 signature, consistent with a buffered or orthogonal rather than shared effect. This supports ankyrin paralog specificity, although differences in guide efficacy, measured transcript abundance, and isoform composition remain caveats.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Dalrd3 perturbation produced a single near-FDR downstream signal: in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut cells, Mcl1 was upregulated (logFC +0.755, adjusted p=0.0928). This was the only adjusted p<0.1 event and occurred despite only weak reduction of the Dalrd3 transcript in the same cells. The pattern is consistent with an exploratory anti-apoptotic survival candidate response involving Mcl1, but no strong whole-signature neighbor was detected, and direct DALRD3-to-MCL1 regulation was not shown.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Marchf6 perturbation reduced Marchf6 mRNA and selectively induced a compact SREBP2/cholesterol-biosynthesis transcript module in two glutamatergic classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with increased Insig1, Msmo1, Cyp51, Hmgcr, Fdft1, Fdps, Dhcr24, Hmgcs1, Ldlr, Sqle, Sc5d, Lss, Idi1, and Srebf2. The pattern was strongest in 151 and reproduced in 155, was opposed by Srebf2 knockdown, was not phenocopied by Amfr, and lacked a canonical UPR-marker wave. The assay measures mRNA, not MARCHF6 substrate protein stability or sterol flux.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp2b1 showed a distinct transcriptional response in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class that Atp2b2 and Atp2b3 knockdowns did not phenocopy. In this Atp2b1-responsive class, Atp2b2 and Atp2b3 were efficiently reduced yet each yielded only its own target as an FDR-significant gene, with genome-wide correlations to the Atp2b1 signature of just r=0.085 and r=0.0002. This suggests PMCA paralogs were not functionally interchangeable in this single-cell mRNA assay, although protein isoform abundance and pump activity were not measured.

Erf showed no recovered convergence with the available ETS-family perturbations: Ets1, Elf2, and Etv6 had near-zero score correlations with the Erf signature and only 0–2 FDR-significant downstream hits, indicating these comparators were weak and largely uninformative in this screen. Thus, the dataset does not support interchangeability between Erf and the assayed ETS factors, but it also cannot directly evaluate proposed ERF antagonism of ETS activators in neurons because ETS2, the most relevant comparator, was not informatively present.

Fas perturbation showed no detectable transcriptional activation of canonical Fas/CD95 signaling in the captured baseline cells: across Fas-covered glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, DISC/extrinsic apoptosis, NF-kappaB, JNK, and necroptosis transcripts including Fadd, Casp8, Cflar, Ripk1, Ripk3, Casp3, Casp7, Chuk, Ikbkb, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Tnfaip3, Jun, Jund, Mapk8, and Mapk9 were not FDR-significant, and there was no convergence with related TNFR or NF-kappaB perturbations. This null mRNA result does not test DISC assembly, caspase cleavage, or NF-kappaB nuclear translocation, and Faslg was not present in the tested rows.

Ntsr1 perturbation was not transcriptionally interchangeable with Sort1 in this adult mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset: across 21 shared cell types, the Ntsr1-versus-Sort1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated, with Pearson r ranging from -0.115 to 0.038. In the neurotensin receptor and sortilin axis, this lack of signature convergence argues against treating Sort1/NTSR3 as an Ntsr1 surrogate and is more consistent with distinct receptor versus cargo-related functions. A key caveat is that Sort1 was the only related comparator available; Nts and Ntsr2 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Vps54 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a phenotype that was clearly separated from the retromer comparator Vps35: although Vps35 was well engaged in the same cell class and produced 17 FDR genes, its score correlation with Vps54 was near zero, with only Atp2a2 shared at FDR significance. This divergent retrograde-trafficking-neighbor pattern suggests the Vps54 response is not simply a generic consequence of perturbing endosome-to-Golgi trafficking genes, though the comparison is limited to signatures and does not directly measure cargo flow or retromer/GARP complexes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Eif4e showed a distinct transcriptomic response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells that was not reproduced by perturbing the assayed eIF4F partners Eif4a2 or Eif4g1. Although Eif4a2 and Eif4g1 each had stronger depletion of their own transcripts than Eif4e, they produced only 2 and 1 FDR genes, respectively, and had low whole-transcriptome correlation with the Eif4e signature. This suggests the cap-binding node is not interchangeable with scaffold or helicase knockdown in this assay, while leaving open isoform redundancy and post-transcriptional regulation as caveats.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chd4 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed perturbation signatures most similar to Adnp and Gatad2b, but not to Mbd2. This restricted convergence is consistent with CHD4-associated ChAHP and NuRD signatures in this neuronal state and argues against treating all assayed NuRD-associated DNA-binding subunits as interchangeable here. The pattern was observed in single-cell differential-expression signature correlations, which were modest and do not directly measure physical complex formation.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Smpd3 showed an internal consistency warning: the strongest nominal downstream signatures were decoupled from Smpd3 mRNA engagement. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Timm8b gave the smallest adjusted p value in the Smpd3 matrix even though Smpd3 itself was not nominally depleted, and 308 CB GABA showed a similar pattern for Plekhn1 with essentially absent target engagement. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, the highest Smpd3 signature-neighbor correlation was still low, and the top Cox19 response did not pass FDR, so these genes are not reliable Smpd3 biomarkers without orthogonal validation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nfat5 targeting most consistently reduced Slc38a2, which was down in 18 of 20 signatures, top-ranked negative in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 155 MB Glut, and reached FDR<0.05 only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In that class, Nfat5, Slc38a2, and Slc6a6 were the three most negative rows. Across the broader osmolyte pathway, Slc6a6 fell only nominally while Slc5a3, Slc6a12, and Akr1b3 were largely unchanged, so the signal points to Slc38a2 rather than a generic transcriptional collapse.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Igsf8 perturbation did not produce a transcriptional program interchangeable with the related tetraspanins Cd81 or Tspan7. Across seven neuronal classes—052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—Cd81 and Tspan7 were effectively perturbed, yet Igsf8–Cd81 and Igsf8–Tspan7 full-transcriptome correlations stayed near zero, with Igsf8 responses often limited to self-depletion and little downstream RNA signal. This uncoupling is based on RNA signatures only, and Cd9, the strongest known Igsf8 partner, was not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atxn2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed that other ataxin-family perturbations were not good substitutes: Atxn1 and Atxn10 produced many more differentially expressed genes than Atxn2, whereas Atxn7 produced none at 5% FDR, and all three signatures were only weakly correlated with Atxn2. This divergence suggests that acute transcriptomic responses within the ataxin disease-gene family are not interchangeable in this cell type, although the comparison is tempered by differing perturbed-cell counts and target-engagement depths across perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Dlgap4 showed exploratory Perturb-seq similarity to NMDA receptor perturbations rather than to direct PSD95-SAPAP-SHANK scaffold partners. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Grin1 was a nearer positive Dlgap4 signature neighbor than Dlg4, Shank3, or Grid1; in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Grin2b was the second positive neighbor and remained top-five in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. This pattern included Vgf decreases in L5 ET neurons aligning more with Grin2b, but absolute score correlations were small and should be viewed as hypothesis-generating.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Marchf6 perturbation in the two strongest responsive neuronal classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, produced a cholesterol/SREBP-linked transcriptional response without a canonical unfolded protein response or ER-stress transcript wave. In these cells, Hspa5, Xbp1, Atf4, Ddit3, Herpud1, Eif2ak3, Ern1, Dnajb9, Derl1, Sel1l, and Syvn1 were not significantly induced, even as a sterol module emerged. This suggests a relatively narrow, branch-specific response in these neuronal types, while not excluding transient or protein-level ER stress.

Mc1r did not recapitulate the canonical MC1R→Gs→adenylyl-cyclase/cAMP program in this dataset: across shared neuronal cell types, Mc1r score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Gnas, Adcy1, Adcy3, or Adcy5 perturbations, and no shared Mc1r-like neuronal signature was recovered. The Mc1r transcript was measured but was not detectably perturbed in any sampled cell type, so the contrast is best interpreted as weak or failed receptor engagement in this assay rather than strong evidence against canonical MC1R biochemistry.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Dlgap4 perturbation showed its main signal in the 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA inhibitory class, where Scn1b and Tacc1 were strongly decreased, yet measured Dlgap4 mRNA was not detectably depleted. The downstream changes were FDR-significant, but Dlgap4 logFC was positive and nonsignificant, so this pattern is best treated as an on-target-caveated, noncanonical result. In this screen, the only inhibitory-class FDR response occurred without measurable Dlgap4 transcript knockdown, raising the possibility of post-transcriptional, guide-composition-driven, or off-target effects until replicated.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tnpo3 perturbation repeatedly down-regulated Srrm2, but direct Srrm2 perturbation only weakly or partially phenocopied the restricted Tnpo3 signatures, indicating that Srrm2 is better interpreted as one component of a broader SR-protein nuclear import and mRNA splicing/nuclear-speckle module rather than the sole driver. This pattern was seen across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Srrm2, Srsf1/2/5/7, Akap8l, and Tcea2 were mostly down after Tnpo3 perturbation, with Srrm2 effects varying by cell type.

Bbs9 perturbation did not produce a coordinated ciliary transcriptional module in this dataset. Instead, cilium-associated transcripts such as Intu, Dync2i1, Cluap1, Ccdc28a, and Bbs5 appeared only as isolated nominal hits with mixed directions, and all had FDR=1.0, arguing against a robust BBSome or intraflagellar-transport expression program. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, which had the most perturbed cells, Bbs9 itself was not reduced and Cluap1 changed only nominally, consistent with a low-engagement or buffered Bbs9 profile.

Lrig2 perturbation did not produce a coherent transcriptional response in the better-known LRIG2-associated receptor and signaling axes in this mouse brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across mature neuronal and GABAergic cell types, EGFR/PDGFRB/ERBB/RET/FGFR-related genes, the NEO1–ADAM17/RGMA axon-guidance module, HPSE2, and BMP/SMAD sentinels such as Bmp4, Bmp6, Smad1, Smad5, Id1, Id2, and Id3 were FDR-negative, with only isolated nominal signals, including weak Neo1 and Smad5 rows in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. These results suggest the assay may not robustly read out LRIG2 mechanisms that depend on receptor cleavage, phosphorylation, protein stability, or surface localization rather than mRNA abundance.

Etv6 did not resemble a scaled SIN3A/corepressor or generic ETS-family perturbation in these mouse-brain cells. Although ETV6 has been linked to SIN3A/HDAC transcriptional repression, the dataset showed only a weak Etv6 signature, with 2 FDR-significant rows versus 2,653 for Sin3a, and near-zero score correlations between Etv6 and Sin3a. Etv6 was also essentially uncorrelated with Ets1, Elf2, and Spi1, including in the two Etv6-responsive glutamatergic classes, so weak target engagement limits any definitive mechanistic uncoupling claim.

Mc2r showed no convergence with melanocortin receptor and cAMP comparator signatures in this brain Perturb-seq dataset: its transcriptional signature was essentially uncorrelated with Mc1r, Mc3r, Mc4r, Agrp, Gnas, Adcy3, and Adcy5 perturbations, with near-zero global correlations. This argues against pooling Mc2r with central melanocortin or generic cAMP perturbations here, although the comparison is limited because the receptor perturbations themselves were weak at the FDR level and Mrap, Mrap2, and Pomc were not included.

Bcl11b showed essentially no alignment with the paralog Bcl11a in this atlas: across all 22 matched classes, their perturbation score signatures were uncorrelated, with Pearson correlations ranging from -0.066 to 0.045. This contrast argues against assuming paralog interchangeability or a shared BCL11A/B cortical projection-neuron transcriptional program here. However, both perturbations were weak by FDR, and developmental literature on combined Bcl11a/Bcl11b loss does not require acute adult single-gene signatures to correlate positively.

Grik2 showed only exploratory neighborhood structure in a restricted unadjusted 75-feature scan: Pde1c and Cacng8 were weakly concordant, whereas Grm1, Syn2, Slc1a1, and Cacng3 were weakly opposing. The pattern suggests possible glutamate-receptor and excitability-adjacent relationships, but the correlations were modest and did not reveal a robust mechanistic neighbor. Important caveats are that the Grik2 seed genes were not FDR-significant and the comparison relied on nominal p<0.001 features only.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Sort1 showed a buffered transcriptomic phenotype: across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Sort1 perturbation was sparse, with only on-target knockdown reaching significance in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and no significant non-target changes. Sorl1, App, Psap, and Grn were similarly sparse, whereas Ap2s1, Ap2m1, Rab7, Vps35, and Vps54 produced many significant changes, most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, indicating that VPS10P cargo-receptor loss is not phenotypically equivalent to disrupting core clathrin/endosomal machinery; this contrast is transcriptomic rather than a direct trafficking readout.

Trpv1 showed a sparse and weak whole-transcriptome signature that was not phenocopied by related TRP channels or canonical regulatory partners across the 22 Trpv1-tested neuronal classes. Perturbations of Trpa1, Trpv4, Trpm3, Calm1/2/3, Prkaca, Prkcg, Cnr1, Ntrk1, and Ngfr were essentially uncorrelated with Trpv1, and related TRP-channel or endocannabinoid-receptor perturbations were themselves sparse and did not reproduce the Trpv1 singleton hits. This contrast is limited to transcriptomic signatures, and weak Trpv1 target engagement plus sparse comparator responses reduce mechanistic interpretability.

Pou3f3 showed no clear convergence with other assayed POU-family perturbations in this dataset: Pou3f4 and Pou2f1 each had zero FDR < 0.05 genes at the target-wide level, and Pou3f3-versus-Pou3f4 or Pou3f3-versus-Pou2f1 signature correlations remained near zero across shared cell classes. However, the most relevant paralog, Pou3f2, was not present among the perturbation targets, so these results do not directly test the established Brn1/Brn2 redundancy, and Pou3f4 or Pou2f1 should not be treated as substitutes for a direct Pou3f2 perturbation.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kif1a showed a largely private, weak transcriptomic state rather than converging with related transport or synaptic-vesicle perturbations. In 155 MB Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, correlations to kinesin paralogs and partners, dynein, and Rab3/synaptic-vesicle genes such as Kif1b, Kif5a, Kif5c, Klc1, Klc2, Dync1h1, Rab3gap1/2, Snap25, Syp, Syn1, and Stxbp1 were near zero overall. Even where Kif1a knockdown was engaged, downstream changes were sparse, and transcriptome-level comparisons are limited by variable target engagement in some comparators.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Pomp showed its strongest positive whole-transcriptome neighbors among proteasome perturbations, especially in 155 MB Glut where Psmb4, Psmc1, and Psmc5 were the top three correlated signatures (Pearson 0.801, 0.774, and 0.740). The same three comparators repeatedly emerged in other Pomp-responsive populations, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, with weaker responders still showing the same pattern. This convergence supports an on-axis proteasome-related response, although transcriptome-wide correlations cannot distinguish primary proteasome dysfunction from shared downstream stress.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Psmc5 showed a proteasome-component expression program: in responsive classes including 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, its whole-transcriptome signatures were most positively similar to Psmc1, Psmb4, and/or Pomp, with no strong anti-correlated perturbation. This convergence, together with up-regulation of a 26S proteasome and ubiquitin-proteostasis rebound module, supports an on-pathway proteasome-insufficiency signal, although direct Psmc5 mRNA depletion was not measurable and similarity was based on DE score vectors, with generally smaller FDR burden than Psmc1 or Psmb4.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Atxn1 was not interchangeable with the ataxia-family perturbations Atxn2, Atxn7, and Atxn10: in the dominant Atxn1-responsive thalamic population, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, these perturbations showed weak correlations to the Atxn1 transcriptomic signature, and Atxn10 was notably engaged yet essentially uncorrelated with Atxn1. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Atxn10 instead showed a strong 180-gene response, reinforcing divergence across perturbations. These comparisons are based on transcriptome correlations in the assayed cell types and do not test protein aggregation, repeat-expansion toxicity, or noncoding-repeat mechanisms.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Bptf perturbation showed a recurrent upregulated Zcwpw2/Grk4 module across 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Zcwpw2 was the most recurrent positive marker, significant in seven classes, while Grk4 formed a second positive arm, strongest in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The largest signature occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas 052 Pvalb Gaba showed only a small three-gene FDR-significant set. This module is defined by recurrence in this dataset rather than a known BPTF-bound pathway.

Epb41l1 showed near-zero transcriptomic correlation with synaptic comparator perturbations including Cask, Gria1, Gria2, Grin2b, Nlgn2, Nlgn3, Nrxn1, Nrxn3, and Rdx across shared cell types, including 155 MB Glut, despite pathway placement in protein 4.1 membrane-cytoskeleton, AMPA receptor trafficking, and neurexin-neuroligin/CASK networks. These weak RNA signatures suggest that Epb41l1 does not phenocopy nearby synaptic perturbations at the scRNA-seq level, although the lack of similarity does not address receptor trafficking, protein localization, or synaptic physiology.

Adgrv1 did not show convergence with the available Usher-network comparator Pcdh15 in this neuronal Perturb-seq panel. Although ADGRV1 is close to WHRN, PDZD7, USH2A, and PCDH15 in the USH2 ankle-link/Usher protein network, only Pcdh15 was perturbable here, and both Adgrv1 and Pcdh15 lacked FDR-significant genes. Across the 22 shared tested cell types, Pcdh15 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Adgrv1, so the result is best read as absence of a shared transcriptomic program rather than a strong opposing phenotype.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnb1 perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut showed only nominal upregulation of Kcns2 and Kcnma1, suggesting exploratory Kv2 delayed-rectifier potassium-channel remodeling in this Kcnb1-specific downstream response relative to Kcnb2. Because KCNS2/Kv9.2 is a regulatory subunit that can assemble with KCNB1/KCNB2, the weak Kcns2 increase is consistent with possible homeostatic channel-composition compensation after Kv2.1 perturbation, but this remains tentative: neither Kcns2 nor Kcnma1 passed FDR correction, and channel-complex stoichiometry was not assayed.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Psmc1 perturbation in responsive neurons induces a compensatory proteostasis program rather than simply reducing proteasome transcripts, with up-regulation of proteasome subunits and regulators including Psmc3, Psmc4, Psmc6, Psmd1-4, Psme4, Psma5, Ubc, and Uchl1, alongside chaperone and stress-apoptosis genes such as Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Hsph1, Dnajb4, Ddit3, and Bax. This pattern is prominent in 155 MB Glut and also seen in 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with convergence across related proteasome perturbations, although proteasome activity, polyubiquitin load, and cell death were not directly measured.

Pdss2 did not phenocopy its expected coenzyme Q/ubiquinol biosynthesis neighbors Pdss1 or Coq5 in this screen. Pdss2, Pdss1, and Coq5 were all FDR-null, and Pdss2 showed near-zero concatenated Wilcoxon-score correlations with Pdss1 (r=0.0111) and Coq5 (r=0.00250), with no strong positive or inverse signature neighbors overall. Although PDSS1 is the obligate enzymatic partner of PDSS2 and COQ5 is in the same pathway, these contrasts were dominated by weak signatures, so the result should not be taken as evidence that the enzymes are biologically independent.

Camkmt showed a null transcriptional response in this dataset: unlike same-assay Calm1 and Calm3 perturbations, which displayed strong on-target transcript depletion in 10/22 and 13/22 matching subclasses, Camkmt showed 0/22 and its whole-transcriptome signature was nearly uncorrelated with Calm1, Calm2, Calm3, Camk2a, Camk2b, Camk2g, or Camk4 perturbations. This divergence suggests the Camkmt null is not due to a general inability to detect calmodulin-axis perturbations here, although the comparison is based on transcript-wide score correlations rather than shared protein methylation measurements.

Adcy1 showed no coherent convergence with nearby cAMP-pathway perturbations in this screen: its score vector was essentially uncorrelated with Adcy3, Adcy5, Prkaca, Gnas, Calm1, and Calm3, and whole-library neighbors had |r|<0.03. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Adcy1 was only nominally engaged while Prkaca was strongly depleted in overlapping cells; in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Adcy3 and Prkaca showed on-target depletion but Adcy1 remained non-significant. These weak correlations are best read as failure to detect convergence, not proof of biological independence.

Gpr12 perturbation did not recover the expected adenylate cyclase/cAMP/PKA-CREB transcriptional program: sentinel cAMP/CREB response genes such as Fos, Junb, Arc, Nr4a1, Crem, Bdnf, Rgs2, and Pde4b were not FDR-significant, and the Gpr12 ranked signature was nearly uncorrelated with Gnas, Prkaca, or Creb1 perturbations. This separates the scRNA endpoint from canonical biochemical descriptions of GPR12 activity, although the conclusion is exploratory because cAMP outputs can be acute or post-transcriptional and Gpr12 transcript engagement was weak.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gnas did not phenocopy other heterotrimeric G-protein perturbations in this screen. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Gnao1 showed strong on-target depletion, and Gnb1 was also strongly depleted in those classes plus 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas Gnas was silent in the same contexts and its targeted transcript was not significantly depleted. This divergence in heterotrimeric G-protein signaling argues against treating Gnas as interchangeable with Gnao1 or Gnb1, although differences in guide performance, regional expression, and subunit biology may contribute.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Snrnp70 showed strong, target-specific effects that were not phenocopied by the related snRNP perturbations Snrpb or Snrpn in the five strongest responder cell types—155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut. In these contexts, Snrnp70 produced large signatures with roughly 90–386 FDR-significant genes and a mixed U1 snRNP/spliceosome and RNA-processing response, whereas Snrpb was nearly silent and Snrpn was weak. This contrast is potency-qualified because Snrpb target RNA was not significantly depleted and Snrpn depletion was smaller than Snrnp70.

Smpd3 showed near-zero whole-transcriptome Pearson correlation with the two measured pathway-neighbor perturbations, Asah1 and Tnfrsf1a, in matched cell types, indicating that these targets were not signature-equivalent in this assay. Thus, despite Reactome proximity within sphingomyelin and ceramide metabolism and TNFR1-mediated ceramide production, the perturbations did not form an interchangeable transcriptional module. This comparison is limited because only two neighbors were available, the signatures were weak, and lack of mRNA similarity does not exclude shared lipid-level outputs.

Pknox2 showed weak engagement in this dataset and did not phenocopy the TALE-PBX-HOX neighborhood: its Perturb-seq signature was nearly uncorrelated with assayed Pbx1, Pbx3, Meis1, Meis2, and Hox perturbations, including Hoxa1, Hoxa3, Hoxa13, Hoxb8, Hoxc13, Hoxd10, and Hoxd13. This suggests that membership in the broader TALE-PBX-HOX transcriptional regulation neighborhood was not sufficient to yield interchangeable transcriptomic signatures here, with the caveat that Pknox1, Pbx2, Pbx4, and Meis3 were not assayed and the comparisons are transcriptomic rather than biochemical.

Avpr2 showed weak or absent convergence with other vasopressin/oxytocin receptor family perturbations in this baseline neuronal transcriptomic dataset. Its perturbation signature was not strongly correlated with Avpr1a, Avpr1b, or Oxtr, with restricted top-500-gene comparisons yielding maximum absolute correlations of 0.269, 0.228, and 0.150, respectively, and no strong Avpr2-like state among related cAMP pathway perturbations. These results suggest Avpr2 is not interchangeable with these receptor paralogs here, although the comparison is transcriptomic and baseline rather than an assay of acute vasopressin or oxytocin ligand responses.

Nek1 showed no strong same-cell-type transcriptional neighbors in the library: across 43,663 comparator signatures, the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations were only r=0.176 and r=-0.160, with Ttll5, Unc5c, and Bbs5 appearing only as very weak exploratory neighbors rather than convergent or opposing phenocopies. This full-library scan therefore argues against an obvious transcriptional substitute for Nek1, while also leaving open the caveat that these weak differential-expression correlations do not establish functional independence at the protein or organelle level.

Glra3 showed near-zero RNA-signature correlations with inhibitory-synapse neighbors including Glra1, Glra2, Glrb, Gphn, Arhgef9, Slc6a5, Slc32a1, Gabra1, Gabrb1, and Gabrg2, so in this dataset it was not interchangeable with glycinergic, GABAergic, transporter, or scaffold perturbations despite their shared biology. The signatures were weak overall: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Glra3 appeared RNA-buffered or unengaged while Glrb and Arhgef9 showed mainly self-down effects, and even the nominal peak in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA remained exploratory.

Hivep1 perturbation in unstimulated brain cell classes did not detectably engage the κB/NF-κB-responsive transcriptional program: no FDR-significant genes were observed in any assayed cell type, and the signature did not converge with Nfkb1, Nfkb2, or Relb, nor with HIVEP paralogs. Related HIVEP and NF-κB-family perturbations were also mostly weak in this dataset. Thus, the inflammatory expectation from HIVEP1 loss in stimulated monocytes/macrophages does not directly transfer to this neural Perturb-seq context without a defined inflammatory challenge.

Pou6f2 showed no convergence with its closest in-screen class-VI paralog, Pou6f1: their signature correlations were nearly zero across profiled classes, and neither perturbation produced an FDR-significant downstream response. In the same analysis matrix, a more distant POU-family factor, Pou3f3, showed a small but detectable response with two FDR-significant downstream genes, including Dync1h1 and Pithd1, indicating that the weak Pou6f2 signal is not a universal property of POU-family perturbations. A caveat is that Pou6f1 itself may have been under-engaged.

Ephb2 did not show strong transcriptomic convergence with other EPH receptor paralogs in this dataset: across Epha10, Epha2, Epha3, Epha4, Epha5, Epha6, Epha7, Ephb1, and Ephb4, same-cell-type score-vector correlations to Ephb2 ranged only from about -0.120 to +0.111, and no top positive or negative signature neighbor closely matched Ephb2. In the EPH-ephrin signaling context, most family perturbations were weak or FDR-null, with Epha4 only slightly less buffered, so the lack of transcript correlation does not exclude shared ligand binding or protein-level pathway activity.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Wnk3 did not transcriptionally phenocopy Wnk1, Stk39, Slc12a2/NKCC1, or Slc12a5/KCC2 in the two Wnk3-responsive classes, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In both cell types, whole-transcriptome score correlations with these comparators were essentially zero and no FDR genes were shared; in 052 Pvalb Gaba the Wnk3 response was only two genes, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut it was limited to a Ppp2cb decrease. A direct Slc12a5 perturbation produced on-target and immediate-early responses absent from the Wnk3 signature, and these contrasts are based on transcriptome correlations rather than OXSR1/STK39 or KCC2 phosphorylation assays.

Zfpm2 showed near-zero whole-transcriptome signature correlation with Gata4 and Gata6 perturbations across 21 shared mouse brain cell classes, so the expected canonical GATA/FOG transcriptional regulation module was not reproduced in these neurons. This refines, rather than contradicts, prior developmental and biochemical contexts in which ZFPM2 is a GATA-family cofactor. Interpretation is limited because the Zfpm2 perturbation itself was weak at the mRNA level, and Gata5 and Ctbp2 were not available as comparator perturbations.

Rara perturbation did not produce a canonical retinoic-acid/RAR-RXR transcriptional response: sentinel receptor-family and retinoid-metabolism transcripts including Rarb, Rarg, Rxra, Rxrb, Rxrg, Dhrs3, and Cyp26b1 showed no FDR-level differential expression. In this dataset, the Rara signature therefore does not resemble either strong RARA loss-of-function or ligand-like pathway activation. This interpretation is limited because only transcript-level sentinel genes were tested, and many RARA outputs are ligand-, enhancer-, and cell-state-dependent.

Ammecr1 was transcriptionally decoupled from its AMME-locus neighbor Acsl4 in the Perturb-seq data: although Acsl4 showed stronger, uniformly negative target-RNA depletion, the Ammecr1 and Acsl4 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated (r=0.0036), and Acsl4 did not share the Ammecr1 transcriptomic signature. This argues against treating contiguous Xq22.3–Xq23 deletion neighbors as interchangeable neuronal perturbations, with the caveat that Acsl4 serves here as a genomic and disease-neighborhood comparator rather than a known stoichiometric AMMECR1 complex member.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnph2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells was marked by strong Rsrp1 repression, and this same sentinel transcript split related RNA-binding perturbations: Snrnp70, Srrm2, and Srsf1 also drove Rsrp1 downward, whereas Celf2, Fus, and Tardbp drove it upward. This opposing pattern suggests the recurrent Hnrnph2–Rsrp1 effect is not a generic RNA-binding-protein stress response, but the comparison is limited to one cell type and one sentinel gene, with weak whole-transcriptome similarity across perturbations.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Kif5a knockdown produced no significant transcript-level compensation across the measured motor/adaptor network in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut: Kif5c, Klc1, Klc2, Kif5b, Kif1a, Dync1h1, Dctn1, Trak1, Trak2, Rhot1, and Nefh remained unchanged, indicating no coordinated Kinesin-1 transcriptional response despite close network relationships. Cell-type context suggested only weak Kif5c similarity, and by contrast Dctn1/Dync1h1 often showed stronger responses in the same classes. This lack of mRNA change does not exclude protein relocalization, altered cargo loading, or activity compensation.

Ivd perturbation did not produce an FDR-significant compensatory transcriptional response in the canonical BCAA/leucine-catabolic program. Across assayed cell types, including 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, transcripts for Bcat1/Bcat2, Bckdha/Bckdhb, Dbt, Dld, Bckdk, Ppm1k, Etfa/Etfb/Etfdh, Mccc1/Mccc2, Auh, Hmgcl, Acat1, and Pcca/Pccb did not pass FDR, indicating no acute RNA-level pathway feedback; metabolite accumulation, enzyme inhibition, and flux changes were not measured.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Add2 reduction, in the five cell types with the clearest on-target depletion—110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—was not accompanied by FDR-supported induction of Add1, Add3, or spectrin–ankyrin/adducin membrane-skeleton genes including Dmtn, Sptan1, Sptb, Ank1, Ank2, Ank3, Epb41l1, Sptbn1, and Sptbn2. This suggests no acute transcript-level compensatory module, while leaving open compensation through protein stability, phosphorylation, developmental effects, or longer-term adaptation.

Tnfrsf11a showed weak or absent convergence with assayed TNFR/NF-kappaB neighbors in this basal neuronal Perturb-seq dataset: related perturbations such as Tnfrsf13c, Cd40, Tnfrsf1b, Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Relb, Map3k7, and Tbk1 did not phenocopy the Tnfrsf11a transcriptomic signature, with the strongest same-cell similarity only r=0.092 for Traf3. This lack of recovery was also seen across cell contexts, including 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, but interpretation is limited because key pathway nodes including Tnfsf11, Traf6, Tnfrsf11b, and Traf2 were not perturbed.

Stat2 perturbation in unstimulated neuronal populations did not suppress the canonical interferon/ISGF3 program: across measured GABAergic and glutamatergic classes, a 21-gene ISG panel showed no FDR-significant response, including Stat1, Irf9, Irf7, Ifit1/2/3, Isg15, Oas1a, Oas2, Rtp4, and Usp18, and no class showed a significant differential-expression signature. This suggests these basal neuronal states lacked a detectable STAT2-dependent antiviral program, although the cells were not exposed to type-I or type-III interferon and Stat2 depletion itself was only nominal.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nr2c2 showed transcriptomic responses in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, and 155 MB Glut cells that were not phenocopied by Nr2c1. Across these Nr2c2-responsive classes, Nr2c1 had no FDR < 0.05 genes and near-zero correlation with Nr2c2 signatures, despite the known NR2C1–NR2C2 orphan nuclear-receptor relationship. The Nr2c2 pattern included Ccdc84 across all three classes, plus Stxbp2 and Miga1 in 151 and Ralgps1 in 017, while 155 showed only Ccdc84 down-regulation. This comparison is limited to transcriptome signatures and does not test DNA binding or protein-level receptor availability.

Tshz3 did not show a convergent perturbation signature with the related genes Tshz2 or Set in the assayed neurons. Across cell types, Tshz2 had no detectable FDR<0.10 signal, and Tshz2-versus-Tshz3 score-vector correlations remained near zero, ranging from -0.0497 to 0.0469; Set was likewise uncorrelated with Tshz3, arguing against a shared Tshz3 transcriptional-repression module being recovered here. Because both Tshz2 and Tshz3 effects were weak, these near-zero correlations should not be overinterpreted as definitive mechanistic divergence.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Mecr perturbation showed only weak, non-recurrent mitochondrial complex-I/OXPHOS-adjacent RNA changes rather than a robust OXPHOS module. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Ndufaf5 was the top nominal downregulated gene, and in 052 Pvalb Gaba, Ndufc1 was nominally down; Ndufs2 also appeared as an isolated nominal hit in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. However, all three changes were nominal only, each occurred in just one cell type, and there was no cross-cell-type recurrence or curated signature convergence, indicating pathway-level uncoupling at the mRNA level.

Pou3f4 showed little transcriptomic similarity to related class-III POU factors or a reported interactor: across 22 shared cell classes, perturbation score-vector correlations with Pou3f3, Pou4f3, and Hnrnpu were near zero, and even the top positive or negative Pou3f4 signature neighbors were weak. Thus, in this dataset, sequence-family membership or reported physical interaction did not recover a shared POU3/interactor module. Because the Pou3f4 signatures themselves were weak, this lack of correlation is less definitive than a strong anti-correlated response.

Agrp perturbation produced a largely null, uncoupled transcriptomic response: no multiple-testing-significant differential-expression hit appeared in any measured class, and nominal Agrp-associated genes were scattered rather than forming a recurrent cross-cell-type melanocortin, cAMP, or neuropeptide module. This contrasts with the canonical AGRP→MC3R/MC4R signaling axis, as Mc3r and Mc4r neighbors were only sparsely engaged and other appetite-pathway neighbors showed at most isolated secondary hits. The absence of transcriptomic recurrence does not exclude acute electrophysiologic or paracrine peptide effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cdkl5 knockdown in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic cell class was not phenocopied by Mapre2 perturbation, even though both transcripts were significantly depleted in that same population. The Cdkl5 and Mapre2 RNA signatures were essentially uncoupled, and available perturbations of CDKL5 pathway neighbors also did not mimic the Cdkl5 signature; Hdac4 was only weakly engaged and not significantly depleted. This remains exploratory because CDKL5 regulates EB2/MAPRE2 through phosphorylation, so reducing Mapre2 mRNA does not directly test the CDKL5-to-EB2 kinase-substrate relationship.

Pou6f2 showed no convergent transcriptomic module in this screen: across 2,045 other perturbations, no strong positive or negative signature neighbor emerged, and in 16 of 23 cell classes the best absolute Pearson correlation was below 0.10. The closest in-screen comparators, including Mcph1, Atp6ap1, and Agtrap, were only weakly similar, arguing against an obvious compensatory receptor, ligand, or complex-member module in these cells. This sparse landscape is consistent with limited curated context, although incomplete databases cannot exclude uncurated or cell-state-specific POU6F2 cofactors.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ywhae perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not phenocopy the Braf-linked transcriptomic program: whereas Braf perturbation significantly reduced Vgf, Ptpn5, Atp2a2, and Unc13a in this same class, Ywhae depletion left these genes unchanged (FDR=1.0) and showed only a weak, restricted correlation with the Braf signature. Thus, despite Braf being a curated Ywhae network neighbor, partial Ywhae mRNA loss should not be interpreted as broad inhibition of BRAF-linked signaling; this conclusion is limited to the strongest Ywhae-engaged cell class, and the Ywhae signal itself was FDR-marginal.

Nfat5 produced transcriptomic perturbations that were not interchangeable with the related NFAT-family factor Nfatc3: in matched cell types, Nfat5–Nfatc3 signature correlations were very small (|r|<0.08), indicating divergent perturbation signatures within the NFAT/Rel family. The dataset did not show strong transcriptomic convergence or a robust recurrent positive or negative comparator for Nfat5. A caveat is that these comparisons used whole-transcriptome score vectors, and the only notable Nfatc3 change was a nominal response in 308 CB GABA, where Nfatc3 transcript increased, Slc38a2 decreased, and the largest positive Nfat5–Nfatc3 correlation still remained below 0.08.

Peg3 perturbation in the basal in-brain setting did not detectably induce sentinel RNAs for the reported p53-Bax, Siah1a apoptosis, TNF–NF-kappaB, or autophagy axes: Trp53, Bax, Siah1a, Traf2, Nfkb1, Rela, Atg5, Becn1, and Map1lc3a showed no FDR-significant change. This null pattern held even in strong Peg3-depletion contexts such as 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, where responses were largely self-only. The result suggests Peg3 dose alone is insufficient in this basal state, while leaving open post-transcriptional regulation or stimulus-dependent effects after DNA damage, TNF, or other challenges.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Nkx2-1 showed a divergent, not shared, transcriptomic profile relative to the other assayed Nkx-family perturbations in this screen. In hippocampal excitatory classes 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, Nkx2-5 had sparse FDR-significant hits at B4galnt1 and Fmnl1, respectively, whereas Nkx2-1 had no FDR<0.05 genes in those classes and near-zero correlations with Nkx2-5; correlations with Nkx3-1 and Nkx6-2 were also weak across matched classes. These comparisons are limited to the screened Nkx genes, and the Nkx2-5 effects were themselves sparse and idiosyncratic.

Gfra1 perturbation did not produce a coordinated RNA-level response in canonical GFRA1/RET or alternative NCAM/Fyn signaling components: Ret, Ncam1, Fyn, Mapk1, Mapk3, Akt1, Akt3, Pik3ca, and Pik3r1 were not FDR-significantly induced or repressed, and the weak Gfra1 signature did not covary with NCAM1, RET, or Fyn perturbation signatures. This negative result is limited to steady-state transcripts rather than ligand-evoked RET phosphorylation, and weak Gfra1 depletion is the most parsimonious explanation for the apparent uncoupling.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnh1 showed a weak Perturb-seq signature, and the related KCNH/EAG paralog Kcnh5 was not transcriptomically interchangeable with it. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Kcnh1 and Kcnh5 had nearly uncorrelated score vectors, despite both belonging to the KCNH/EAG delayed-rectifier channel family. Both perturbations lacked FDR-significant genes, so this comparison is limited to weak score-vector structure; in thalamus, Kcnh1 itself was unchanged even where its largest nominal downstream statistic was observed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Clcn3 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a small, asymmetric acidification-compensation signal: Clcn3 loss only nominally increased Atp6v0b and Herpud1, whereas the reciprocal Atp6v0c perturbation in the same cell type robustly induced Clcn3 and Herpud1 while reducing Atp6v0c. Restricted-signature comparisons also weakly linked Clcn3 to Rab7 and V-ATPase perturbations, but not Clcn4 or Clcn5. This pattern is consistent with endolysosomal Cl-/H+ exchange and acidification, although only the Atp6v0c-to-Clcn3 arm was FDR-supported and the Rab7/Atp6v0c convergence relied on top-gene-restricted correlation.

cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Trak1 perturbation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells showed only a nominal, low-power induction of a Rhot2/Pink1-centered mitochondrial transport signature, with Rhot2 the top nominal gene and Pink1 eighth, alongside genes such as Ndufs5 and Dctn6. This pattern is mechanistically suggestive because Rhot2 is a TRAK partner in the TRAK1/RHOT mitochondrial microtubule transport pathway, but it should be treated as an exploratory compensation hypothesis only: there were just 24 perturbed cells, Trak1 itself was not decreased, and all genes had FDR=1.0.

Pou6f1 showed no corrected transcriptomic response across all 23 assayed mouse-brain cell classes, and the only assayed class-6 paralog, Pou6f2, likewise had zero corrected hits. Their matched-class perturbation scores were essentially uncorrelated, indicating no convergent signature for class-6 POU-homeobox transcriptional regulation in this dataset. As a result, these data provide no evidence that Pou6f1 and Pou6f2 are interchangeable drivers of the surveyed brain-cell states, although this comparison relies on weak bulk-of-cell-class signatures rather than high-confidence differentially expressed genes.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tgfbr2 showed a sparse perturbation profile: across the assayed cell types, the only FDR-significant Tgfbr2-associated gene was Ssbp4 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and this signature did not converge with proximal Tgfbr1/Tgfbr3/SMAD perturbations. In contrast, related TGF-beta/BMP-family perturbations produced significant calls in other neuronal classes, including Bmpr2 on-target depletion in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut, and Smad2 or Bmpr1b hits in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA. Because these comparator effects occur in different cell types, they should not be read as direct epistasis, but they do indicate that the sparse Tgfbr2 result is target-specific rather than a universal failure of this pathway subset in the screen.

Col2a1 perturbation in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq atlas did not recapitulate the chondrocyte COL2A1-ITGB1-SMAD1/BMP axis: Col2a1 produced almost no multiple-testing-adjusted transcriptional response across measured cell types, and Itgb1 or other collagen-family/collagen-receptor perturbations showed little shared full-signature similarity or robust adjusted differential expression. These data therefore suggest the cartilage mechanism is uncoupled from the brain-cell signatures here, with the important caveat that the dataset did not assay chondrocytes, cartilage ECM deposition, SMAD1 phosphorylation, or extracellular collagen protein.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnpdl perturbation produced a modest but significant increase in Hnrnpu specifically in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, and this was the only genome-wide FDR-significant downstream transcript detected for Hnrnpdl. Other hnRNP-family transcripts, including Hnrnpa1, Hnrnpa2b1, Hnrnpc, and Hnrnph2, were not significantly changed, arguing against a broad stress-like hnRNP response. Given the hnRNP/RNA-binding-protein network context, the Hnrnpu signal is consistent with a possible compensatory marker, but it remains indirect, cell-type-restricted, and the Hnrnpdl self-transcript was only nominally decreased in the same class.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gabrr2 was notably discordant from canonical GABA-A receptor subunits in this screen: unlike Gabra1, Gabrb2, Gabrb3, Gabrd, Gabrg2, and Gabrb1, it showed no clear on-target depletion and no strong signature neighbor, with a maximum same-cell-type correlation of only |r|=0.154. This null persisted across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, while 308 CB GABA showed only a subthreshold nominal signal. The contrast suggests a Gabrr2-specific null or missing Gabrr2-expressing contexts, with the caveat that rho paralogs Gabrr1 and Gabrr3 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc7a6os showed restricted signature similarity that repeatedly converged on spliceosome and proteostasis perturbations rather than on direct Son, Srrm2, or Pld3 perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, top positive neighbors included Prpf6, Ddx23, U2af2, Psmc1, Psmc5, and Psmb4; 155 MB Glut similarly aligned with Ddx23, Prpf6, and U2af2, while 191 MB P MY GABA aligned with Prpf6, Cdc40, Hnrnpu, and Ddx23. These correlations used only the top 500 Slc7a6os genes, so they indicate RNA-processing and protein-homeostasis stress convergence, not genome-wide phenocopy or epistasis.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Smad6 showed weaker responses than nearby BMP/TGF-beta pathway nodes in this Perturb-seq screen: across sampled cell types including 155 MB Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 308 CB GABA, Smad6 had no multiple-testing-corrected differential expression, while related perturbations such as Bmpr2, Ski, Smad2, Tgfbr2, and Bmpr1b produced corrected signatures. This suggests the pathway neighborhood was recoverable, although comparator effects were cell-type-specific and differed in cell counts, target engagement, and expected signature relative to derepressing an inhibitory SMAD.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Slc7a14 in 052 Pvalb Gaba neurons showed a buffered, self-contained transcriptomic response rather than convergence with related perturbations: residualized logFC signatures were near zero versus the only other SLC7-named perturbation, Slc7a6os, and versus assayed STRING neighbors including Gabbr2, Frrs1l, Pcsk2, Rp9, and Dmxl2. In this dataset, that argues against treating Slc7a14 as interchangeable with nearby amino-acid-transporter-family biology, although most true SLC7 paralogues were not present in the library and the correlation analysis is exploratory.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Slc24a5 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut neurons showed a distinct response that did not phenocopy the pigmentation-related perturbations Kit or Mitf: this was the only class with a Slc24a5 FDR hit, marked by increased Lpcat4 and a nominal glycerophospholipid signature, while Kit and Mitf in the same cell type did not reproduce the Lpcat4 increase and had near-zero transcriptomic score-vector correlation with Slc24a5. This contrast is limited by generally weak comparator signatures, only 38 Mitf cells in this class, and the fact that the comparison is transcriptomic rather than a melanocyte functional assay.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc17a5 perturbation repeatedly increased a cholesterol biosynthesis/sterol regulatory response in neurons, most clearly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, and more weakly but concordantly in 191 MB P MY GABA. Insig1, Msmo1, and Dhcr24 were FDR-significant in active cell types, with nominal support for Hmgcr, Sc5d, and Ldlr in the GABA signature. In 155 MB Glut, this sterol induction co-occurred with lysosomal genes and decreased Snap25/Eef1a2, while the overall sterol signal was distributed across small gene sets.

Mt3 partial loss did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptional compensation signature under basal conditions. In the measured Mt3 STRING neighborhood and related stress programs, metallothionein and metal-ion homeostasis genes such as Mt1, Mt2, Mt4, Mtf1, Slc30a1, Slc30a3, Slc30a4, Slc39a1, Atox1, Ccs, Sod1, and Gpx8 showed no significant changes, and canonical antioxidant or NRF2/glutathione genes including Hmox1, Gclc, Gclm, Nfe2l2, Sod2, and Fth1 were likewise not induced. This transcript-level check was done in basal profiles, and many STRING partners were not themselves perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cacna1c in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not phenocopy perturbations of downstream CaV1.2-calmodulin-CaMK-calcineurin signaling genes. Although Calm1 and Ppp3r1 showed multi-gene signatures and Calm3, Camk2b, and Ppp3ca showed robust self-knockdown, their score correlations with the Cacna1c signature were near zero or negative, indicating that partial Cacna1c depletion was uncoupled from stronger downstream Ca2+/calmodulin, CaMKII, and calcineurin-node loss. This divergence may reflect channel-independent roles of the downstream genes, and the mRNA-level mismatch does not rule out acute Ca2+ signaling changes.

Bmpr2 showed a transcriptomic signature that was not reproduced by perturbing related BMP/TGFβ receptor-family genes, including Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Acvrl1, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Smad1, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, Smad6, Smad9, and Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, and Tgfbr3. Across these comparators, all-gene score correlations with Bmpr2 were near zero, with maximum |r| = 0.092, and a restricted top-gene neighbor scan found no strong phenocopy. Because most comparators did not show FDR-significant depletion of their own transcripts, this is best interpreted as a negative observability result rather than proof of biological divergence.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Atr showed little cross-perturbation convergence in 308 CB GABA cells: its transcriptomic signature was essentially uncorrelated with the available Prkdc, Mtor, Trp53, and Mapk8 perturbations, and an all-target neighbor search found no strong recurrent Atr-like perturbation, with the largest correlation still weak (r=0.1919) to Dnajb4. These weak Atr vectors therefore do not support a shared generic DNA-damage or stress module in the PI3K-related DNA-damage kinase network, although the inference is limited because Atr itself was weak and key comparators such as Atm, Atrip, and Chek1 were not available.

Irf9 perturbation produced a full-transcriptome signature that was essentially uncorrelated with Stat1, Stat2, Ifnar1, Ifnar2, Ifngr1, Ifngr2, Adar, Ifih1, and measured IRF-family perturbations including Irf1, Irf2, Irf3, Irf5, Irf6, Irf7, and Irf8. This suggests that, in these brain cell classes under basal conditions, IRF9 does not participate in a shared loss-of-ISGF3 or type-I-interferon transcriptional module, with ISG markers such as Isg15, Ifit1, Ifit3, Rtp4, and Usp18 not detectably suppressed after Irf9 perturbation. Correlations were derived from DE score vectors and mostly compare weak perturbations.

Mbl2 showed a transcriptional profile that was largely decoupled from the available complement and innate-immune perturbations in the library: whole-transcriptome scores were essentially uncorrelated with C3, Cr2, Itgb2, Clec16a, Tlr2, Tlr4, and Tlr9, with the largest same-cell-type absolute correlation only |r|=0.1316. However, the most direct lectin-pathway comparators were not present, including Mbl1, Masp1, Masp2, C2, and C4b, so this should not be interpreted as a full phenocopy test of the MBL complex or total lectin-pathway activity.

Lrif1 perturbation produced a neuronal signature that was largely orthogonal to Rara rather than Rara-like, despite the reported LRIF1/RIF1 interaction with RARα in retinoic-acid receptor transcriptional repression. Across 21 matched brain cell classes, Lrif1-versus-Rara score correlations were very small, ranging from −0.032 to 0.119, and supporting observations noted that their perturbation signatures were not detectably aligned in matched cell types. This suggests the RARA link alone does not explain the Lrif1 pattern, with ligand state and assay context likely important because the screen did not include defined retinoic-acid stimulation or RARA reporter activity.

Sptlc2 showed near-zero transcriptional signature correlation with the available sphingolipid pathway-neighbor perturbations Asah1 and Smpd3 across 21 shared cell types, indicating that these related enzymes were transcriptionally uncoupled in this neuronal CRISPRi dataset. Thus, despite their biochemical links within broader sphingolipid ceramide and sphingomyelin metabolism, the screen did not resolve a common sphingolipid-stress module. This interpretation is tempered by weak target engagement for Asah1 and Smpd3, so the lack of convergence could reflect incomplete knockdown as well as true pathway separation.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Tbx22 did not produce a coherent brain transcriptional module in this dataset, and the craniofacial or cleft-palate network around Tbx22 appeared uncoupled from a shared neuronal response. Across all assayed mouse brain cell classes, Tbx22 perturbation had no Benjamini-Hochberg significant differential-expression call. The only assayed STRING neighbor, Irf6, also lacked a broad brain signature, showing just one FDR hit, Sgcb, in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut among the Tbx22-overlapping classes, although this single-gene result could be idiosyncratic.

Zkscan1 was not transcriptionally interchangeable with the assayed ZKSCAN relatives: in matched cell types, its score-vector signatures were essentially orthogonal to those of Zkscan3 and Zkscan16, and perturbing those two family members did not reproduce the Zkscan1 signature. This argues against a shared neuronal program for these KRAB/SCAN zinc-finger factors in the mouse brain, despite the SCAN domain’s capacity for selective oligomerization. However, Zkscan3 and Zkscan16 were themselves weak perturbations, so the lack of convergence does not by itself prove biochemical independence.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tmem165 is mirrored by a related Golgi glycan perturbation in which St3gal5 knockdown showed strong self-depletion but mostly self-only transcriptional effects across ten neuronal classes, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Only Pggt1b and Eif4e3 reached exploratory significance in 155 MB Glut, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut St3gal5 had corrected self-knockdown without a broad downstream signature, despite ST3GAL5 acting in ganglioside sialylation rather than the Ca2+/Mn2+ antiport reaction of TMEM165.

Nrp1 was transcriptionally silent in this analysis, and its close paralog Nrp2 was likewise FDR-null, even though the same dataset detected clear self-transcript depletion for several related guidance receptors, including Plxna2, Robo1, Robo2, Sema5a, and Unc5c, in selected cell types. In 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, for example, related receptors showed on-target mRNA loss while Nrp1 remained null, indicating that Nrp1 inactivity is not explained by a general inability to detect receptor knockdown and that these perturbations are not interchangeable; however, these effects were mostly limited to the targeted transcript and did not establish broader pathway activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Timp2 produced a transcriptomic perturbation pattern that did not converge with the TIMP paralog Timp3: across 22 shared cell types, whole-signature Timp2–Timp3 correlations stayed near zero, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where both perturbations reduced their own transcripts and Timp2 showed strong self-depletion. In this atlas, the data therefore argue against treating Timp2 and Timp3 as interchangeable perturbations. This comparison is transcriptomic, however, and because Timp3 had few FDR-significant rows, it rules out strong RNA-level convergence rather than shared protein-level substrates.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Syt14 showed only a weak, mixed nominal transcriptional response rather than a recurrent synaptotagmin, SNARE, or vesicle-trafficking module. Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and 308 CB GABA, there were no conventionally significant genes; the strongest signal was Tbc1d14 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but it remained below FDR support (q=0.123631). Other nominal hits, including Hyou1, Taf1b, Arhgef9, Gria4, Minar2, Vgf, Tgfbr2, Ndufb8, and Wdr26, were mostly isolated single-class events, and whole-signature neighbors were only weakly correlated, arguing against a robust module call.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Srebf1 showed only scattered, cell-type-specific nominal differential-expression candidates rather than a coordinated SREBP lipid or sterol program. The best rows were Slc38a2 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Lrrc57 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and Acat1 and Pi4ka in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, with Pigq and Hspa5 also among the top hits, but all were below conventional adjusted-significance thresholds (FDR 0.100–0.287). Consistently, the full Srebf1 slice lacked any gene with FDR <0.1, signature-neighbor support was weak, and the expected SREBF sterol-output module was absent under Srebf1 despite being down under Srebf2 in comparator analyses.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Bap1 showed a neuronal signature that was not interchangeable with PR-DUB-associated perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba. In these Bap1-responsive cell types, Asxl3 and Foxk2 had no FDR-significant genes, and Ogt produced unrelated transcriptomic signatures despite strong Ogt knockdown; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, even measurable Foxk2 knockdown did not phenocopy Bap1. Shared Scg2 down-regulation marked the Bap1 response, but comparisons are based on transcriptomic signatures only, Asxl3 engagement was limited, and Ogt has broad non-PR-DUB functions.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Caskin1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut showed a target-centric RNA signature that did not converge with perturbations in the CASK–Caskin1–neurexin/neuroligin synaptic scaffold neighborhood. In these two best-engaged Caskin1 contexts, whole-transcriptome Pearson correlations between Caskin1 and Cask, Nrxn1, Nrxn2, Nlgn2, or Nlgn3 were near zero, and even the best-matched or most inverse neighbors had only very small correlations. This uncoupling should be interpreted conservatively because Cask itself lacked FDR-significant on-target depletion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Nfs1 did not phenocopy the strong Hspa9-associated mitochondrial stress program in shared cell types. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Nfs1 showed its best target-RNA engagement, Nfs1 scores were essentially uncorrelated with Hspa9 scores and key Hspa9-induced markers such as Shmt2, Cyb5r1, Chac1, and Slc7a5 were not significant. This contrast also held in 155 MB Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, where Hspa9 drove recurrent stress-like responses but Nfs1 showed little or no downstream signal, consistent with Hspa9 perturbation being stronger and biologically broader than Nfs1 loss.

Sacs showed an acute RNA signature that was uncoupled from neurofilament and microtubule cytoskeleton perturbations: although Nefl, Nefm, Nefh, Map1b, Kif5a, Tubb3, Tubb4a, and Tubb5 produced measurable signatures, Sacs was FDR-null and only weakly correlated with them. In the sampled 308 CB GABA cells, Sacs was explicitly null, and broader chaperone, mitochondrial, and cytoskeletal neighbor contrasts also did not reveal a Sacs-like program. This pattern is consistent with a structural, post-transcriptional intermediate-filament defect rather than a primary reduction of cytoskeletal mRNAs, with single-cell RNA being an indirect and potentially insensitive readout.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Nrcam did not phenocopy Ank3 or other curated L1/contactin/axon-guidance neighbors in the profiled transcriptomes across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, several cortical glutamatergic classes, and selected GABAergic and midbrain populations. Same-cell-type RNA score correlations with Ank3, Cntn1, Nrp2, Ank2, Cntnap1/2, L1cam, Chl1, Ncam1, Cdh2, Robo1/2, Dscam, and Plxna1/2 were near zero, with the largest absolute correlation only 0.091. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ank3 showed 121 FDR hits whereas Nrcam had 2, with Nrcam–Ank3 r=-0.026. This comparison may miss shared nontranscriptional or subcellular phenotypes.

H2ac8 showed transcriptomic signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with the core-histone perturbations H3f3a and H4c11 across matched brain cell classes, indicating that these histone-gene guides did not converge on a shared nucleosome or core-histone module state in this dataset. This pattern was mostly absent or uncorrelated overall, with only nominal H2ac25 down signal noted, and it should be interpreted cautiously because the comparison reflects weakly engaged single-gene perturbations rather than biochemical independence among H2A, H3, and H4 proteins.

Npy2r showed no detectable convergence with the other available NPY-family receptor perturbations in this dataset: Npy1r and Npy5r did not phenocopy the Npy2r transcriptional signature, with score-vector correlations near zero in overlapping cell types. More broadly, scans for nearest positive and negative perturbation signatures found only weak similarities to Npy2r. Because all three receptor perturbations were weak, this result argues against a shared transcriptional phenotype here within the neuropeptide Y-family receptor ligand-binding pathway, rather than against overlapping ligand biology.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cnot1 did not phenocopy the assayed TNRC6 miRNA-effector neighbors Tnrc6a and Tnrc6b.
