In 155 MB Glut, the main responsive class, Cnot1 showed a small four-gene downregulated response led by Pcsk1n, whereas Tnrc6a and Tnrc6b had more perturbed cells but no FDR-significant genes, and their Wilcoxon score correlations with Cnot1 were approximately zero. Thus, despite the TNRC6-CCR4-NOT miRNA repression link, the dataset does not support a generic TNRC6-dependent miRNA-silencing phenotype for Cnot1; this comparison is pathway-neighbor based and all effects were small.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Lonp1 showed convergent upregulation with a mitochondrial-stress signature-neighbor set, especially in 155 MB Glut and 217 P MY Pineal Glut cells. In a restricted six-gene score built around Ddit3, Shmt2, Aldh1l2, Chac1, Slc7a5, and Slc7a1, Opa1, Hspa9, Dnm1l, and Srsf1 ranked with or above Lonp1, indicating a shared stress output rather than a Lonp1-only marker. In 155 MB Glut, Lonp1 had the best-powered ISR-like response, whereas in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, Lonp1 ranked third; this restricted analysis does not imply full-transcriptome equivalence across these perturbations.

Lrrtm4 perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptional response in the canonical HSPG/glypican–neurexin/RPTP–LRRTM–AMPAR adhesion axis. Across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, partner transcripts such as Gpc4, Gpc6, Nrxn1, Nrxn2, Ptprd, Ptprf, Ptprs, Lrrtm1, and Lrrtm3 were nominal at best, and related perturbations including neurexins, neuroligins, RPTPs, and Gpc6 showed only weak similarity to the Lrrtm4 signature. In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, on-target Lrrtm4 mRNA depletion was not detected, further limiting interpretation.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Dgkd showed weak depletion, while the only assayed paralog, Dgke, separated sharply with strong target-only knockdown and near-zero matched-cell-type score correlations to Dgkd. In 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Dgke had strong self-depletion without a matching Dgkd signature, and across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut the isoform signatures remained essentially uncorrelated. Neither perturbation induced FDR-significant transcriptional changes in the other isoform, consistent with divergence within diacylglycerol phosphorylation/phosphatidic acid biosynthesis rather than interchangeability.

Camk2g did not produce a transcriptional signature resembling nearby calcium/CaMKII/NMDA perturbations: whole-transcriptome score correlations with Camk2a, Camk2b, Camk4, Calm1, Calm2, Calm3, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b stayed near zero across 22 matched cell types. Thus, in this basal Perturb-seq readout, Camk2g loss was not transcriptionally interchangeable with these related perturbations, and there was no robust shared downstream response in the Ca2+/calmodulin-CaMKII-CREB signaling neighborhood. This negative comparison is tempered by weak Camk2g on-target engagement and by the score-based, bulked cell-type analysis.

Phactr2 showed near-zero transcriptional signature similarity to the available comparators Phactr1 and Mrtfa, and likewise did not phenocopy Actb or Actg1 across shared cell types, arguing against a reusable PHACTR-family or broader actin-axis module in this experiment. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, the Phactr2 response was weak and appeared uncoupled from stronger core-actin perturbations in PP1/actin cytoskeleton regulation. Consistently, the Lrfn4 increase after Phactr2 perturbation was not FDR-supported for Phactr1, Mrtfa, Actb, or Actg1. A caveat is that Phactr3 and Phactr4 were not assayed, and Phactr1 itself had weak target engagement with no FDR-significant hits.

Yeats2 perturbation showed no coordinated transcriptional feedback of canonical ATAC-complex subunits across all 21 Yeats2-profiled cell types. Transcripts for Kat2a, Kat2b, Kat14, Tada2a, Tada2b, Tada3, Zzz3, Mbip, Wdr5, Sgf29, Dr1, and Drap1 showed no nominal p<0.01 signal and no FDR-supported response, consistent with an overall weak Perturb-seq signature lacking recurrent shared modules or strong nearest-neighbor perturbation matches. This negative result is limited to mRNA readouts; complex occupancy and histone-acylation marks were not measured.

Hes7 perturbation in mouse brain cell classes did not activate the canonical HES7-LFNG/Notch somitogenesis module. Lfng, Dll1, Dll3, Notch1, Notch2, Notch3, Mesp2, Tbx6, Rbpj, Dusp4, and Hes1 were measured but not detectably FDR-regulated, and the Hes7 expression signature was nearly uncorrelated with Dll1, Notch1-4, Psen1, and Mesp2 perturbations. Thus, despite literature links between HES7 and segmentation-clock circuitry, the brain dataset suggests this pathway is uncoupled here, likely because these genes are not in their native presomitic mesoderm regulatory state.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gabra3 was not a transcriptomic phenocopy of other GABA-A receptor subunit perturbations. In 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Gabra3 showed self-depletion but weak correlation with related perturbations such as Gabrg2, Gabrb2, Gabrb3, Gabra1, and Gabra5, and in 155 MB Glut, Gabrg2 produced a corrected Vgf response that was absent after Gabra3 perturbation. In 308 CB GABA, several GABA-pathway genes, including Gabrg2, Gabrb2, Slc32a1, Gad1, and Gabbr1, showed strong on-target effects while Gabra3 did not engage. These weak transcriptomic signatures do not address shared effects on GABA currents.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gabbr2 did not phenocopy Gabbr1 at the mRNA-signature level: despite their shared role in GABA_B receptor Gi/o signaling, Gabbr2-versus-Gabbr1 score-vector correlations were essentially zero globally and within 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. In these cell types, Gabbr2 depletion was significant, but downstream transcriptional output was sparse after FDR correction—often with no non-target genes passing FDR—so the contrast rests on correlation of perturbation scores rather than a resolved shared gene program.

Smarcad1 was transcriptionally inert across the assayed panels: in the same 20 cell-type panels where Brd4, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Chd4, Chd8, Arid2, Setdb1, and Arid1a produced corrected transcriptional signatures, Smarcad1 did not, and its signatures were nearly uncorrelated with related SWI/SNF-family, BAF, CHD, bromodomain, HDAC, and heterochromatin perturbations, including Smarca2 and Brd1. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the largest Smarcad1 group still lacked target depletion or a corrected downstream signature, although guide efficiency and cell-count differences mean this contrast does not prove SMARCAD1 protein was depleted.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Idh3a knockdown showed no compensatory mRNA induction of Idh3b, Idh3g, the Idh1/Idh2 isoenzymes, or nearby TCA-cycle genes including Aco2, Dld, Dlst, Mdh2, Ogdh, Sdha, and Sdhb across engaged cell classes such as 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. In several classes, Idh3a was significantly depleted but the non-target transcriptome remained buffered, arguing against a simple mRNA-level replacement program, while leaving open post-translational changes in IDH3 assembly or activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp292 showed no corrected transcriptional signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, even though STRING-listed Zfp292 network neighbors Ctcf, Arid2, and Kdm6a produced corrected signatures in the same stratum. This suggests the assay could detect transcriptional and chromatin-regulator perturbations in that cell type, making the Zfp292 null more consistent with Zfp292-specific engagement or context limits than with a universal lack of sensitivity. STRING links here are functional predictions rather than proof of a single obligatory Zfp292 complex, and downstream gene overlap was not required for the contrast.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Dach1 showed an isolated signal in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut: Ppdpf was the only FDR-significant Dach1-associated gene, but this CA3 signature was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of Six1, Six3, Six5, Six6, Ski, Tgif1, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Sin3a, Pax3, and Pax6, and Ppdpf did not become significant after those related perturbations. This suggests the CA3 Dach1/Ppdpf signal was uncoupled from the assayed DACH1/SIX/EYA and SMAD-associated network in this dataset, although the observation is limited to one cell type and could reflect weak engagement of Dach1 or comparator perturbations.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Dhdds in the responsive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut populations showed positive signature convergence with a broader secretory proteostasis module, with nearest positive neighbors including Gfpt1, Hspa9, Atp2a2, Atp6v0c, Hspa5, proteasome genes such as Psmb4, Psmc5, Pomp, and Psmc1, and the ER trafficking gene Sec31a. These correlations became stronger when analysis was restricted to the 500 most Dhdds-affected genes, whereas the strongest full-transcriptome negative neighbors were weak and exploratory, so the pattern suggests a shared ER/secretory homeostasis state rather than an isolated single-enzyme effect.

Nrxn1 perturbation showed a mostly self-only, low-output transcriptional pattern, and related perturbations of Nrxn2, Nlgn1, Nlgn2, and Nlgn3 across the same 22 Nrxn1 cell types likewise did not reveal a broad reciprocal RNA cascade within the neurexin–neuroligin trans-synaptic adhesion pathway; Nrxn3 was not evaluable because its self-transcript row was absent. In target-engaged cell types, multiple-testing-significant downstream responses to Nrxn1 were essentially absent, with caveats that guide efficiencies and cell counts differed across comparators and that absence of soma RNA effects does not directly test trans-synaptic adhesion.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Atad1 showed strong on-target knockdown but no FDR-supported downstream transcript changes, yielding a narrow self-only signature. This pattern converged with Pex14, which in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut also showed strong target depletion with exactly one FDR hit, Pex14 itself. Together these perturbations point to buffered mitochondrial/peroxisomal membrane protein quality-control or import biology that is transcriptionally quiet, although the comparison is limited to transcriptomic output and PEX14 and ATAD1 act at related but distinct membrane-homeostasis steps.

Irf8 showed a nonconvergent pattern in these neuronal data: across IRF-family perturbations, signatures were sparse and largely FDR-negative, with only two of 203 IRF-family contrasts reaching q<0.05. Irf8 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with related immune and interferon perturbations, including Irf1, Irf2, Irf3, Irf5, Irf6, Irf7, Irf9, Stat1, and Spi1, with mean |r|=0.0197 and max |r|=0.0968. This buffered or nonconvergent behavior was observed in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 155 MB Glut, but the weak signatures leave open convergence under cytokine or myeloid differentiation cues.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Lrpprc in 155 MB Glut showed a shared down-mitochondrial-mRNA endpoint with Opa1 and Lonp1, including reduced mitochondrially encoded transcripts such as mt-Nd1, mt-Co3, and mt-Nd4, but this convergence did not extend to Pnpt1, Ptcd3, Gfm2, or Dap3. The pattern suggests a convergent mitochondrial RNA-abundance phenotype rather than a generic signature of all assayed mitochondrial RNA or translation perturbations, with weak whole-transcriptome similarity across perturbations. A caveat is that SLIRP, the direct LRPPRC complex partner, was not perturbed, and comparisons here are limited to transcript abundance.

Hcn2 showed measurable target engagement in this dataset, but the closest paralog comparator, Hcn1, was not an interpretable phenocopy: Hcn1 perturbation never achieved adjusted on-target depletion in any of the 22 matched cell classes, and Hcn2 perturbation left Hcn1 RNA unchanged. Consistent with this, no adjusted compensatory RNA induction was detected for core HCN-family genes or the TRIP8b/Pex5l regulator set, including Hcn1, Hcn3, Hcn4, and Pex5l. These results reflect a perturbation-quality limitation rather than a definitive biological divergence between HCN1 and HCN2.

Clip2 showed an orthogonal transcriptomic signature relative to the assayed microtubule plus-end and dynein-adjacent perturbations Mapre2, Dctn1, and Pafah1b1, rather than phenocopying them. This separates physical membership in the CAP-Gly microtubule plus-end/dynactin-adjacent network from a shared scRNA-seq differential-expression state and is consistent with a largely post-transcriptional cytoskeletal role for CLIP proteins. Important caveats are that Clip1, Clasp1, Clasp2, Mapre1, and Mapre3 were not assayed, and the Wilcoxon-score correlation approach may miss non-transcriptional phenocopy.

Sox2 showed little convergence with the SOX2 developmental transcriptional network in this screen: across all 22 Sox2-assayed cell-type groups, its perturbation signature was essentially uncorrelated with Sox3, Pax6, Pou5f1, Sall4, Ctnnb1, and Mecp2, and even the nearest whole-screen neighbors were weak and concentrated in a cell type without FDR-resolved Sox2 effects. This weak-score contrast suggests the assayed differentiated neuronal classes did not capture a canonical SOXB1 neural-progenitor program, but the lack of correlation alone does not rule out SOXB1 biology in progenitors or under stronger perturbation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zic1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed the only clear target engagement, with significant Zic1 down-regulation, Slc29a1 up-regulation, nominal synaptic gene changes, and no detectable Hedgehog/GLI signature. In this same cell type, Zic2, Zic3, and Zic4 did not reproduce the Zic1 transcriptome: whole-transcriptome correlations with Zic1 were near zero, and only Zic2 appeared as a weak neighbor when analysis was restricted to the top 200 Zic1-responsive genes. Because Zic2/3/4 lacked significant self-transcript suppression here, this divergence could reflect either true paralog non-interchangeability or failed perturbation engagement.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ahi1, in 155 MB Glut cells, did not phenocopy its ciliary neighbors Cplane1, Ift88, B9d1, Cep290, Rpgrip1l, or Ttc8 at the transcriptomic level. Cplane1 showed a self-FDR signal and Ift88 had a single Pcsk1n FDR hit, yet their score correlations with Ahi1 were only 0.021 and 0.016, while B9d1, Cep290, and Rpgrip1l were likewise near zero and had no FDR-level response. This suggests that, in the one robustly engaged Ahi1 context, primary-cilium transition-zone and IFT perturbations are not transcriptionally interchangeable, although comparator target engagement varied and shared ciliary morphology phenotypes cannot be excluded.

Cacng3 produced transcriptomic signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with the related TARP perturbations Cacng2 and Cacng8 across all 22 matched neuronal classes, with whole-signature Pearson correlations near zero in both comparisons. In the same dataset, related AMPAR or postsynaptic perturbations such as Gria2, Frrs1l, Dlg4, and Shank2 showed strong target-transcript rows, suggesting the Cacng3 result was not simply an AMPAR-analysis blind spot. However, because Cacng2 and Cacng8 themselves also had weak target-transcript rows, the lack of convergence may reflect both biology and incomplete perturbation engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cdc42 in the engaged 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class showed a transcriptomic signature that was not shared with Rac1, Pak1, Pak2, Pak3, or Dock7. Although PAK1-3 are direct CDC42/RAC effectors in the curated RHO GTPases activate PAKs pathway, score-vector correlations with Cdc42 were near zero, and the nominal P<0.001 hits for these related perturbations did not overlap the eight Cdc42 hits. This argues against a simple linear CDC42-to-PAK transcriptional reporter in this readout, with the caveat that the comparison reflects mRNA-based DE summaries rather than direct PAK activity and knockdown strength was not uniform across targets.

Foxj1 did not recover the canonical motile-cilium/FOXJ1 multiciliogenesis network in the 22 Foxj1-sampled neuronal cell types. Across these classes, Foxj1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Rfx3, Trp73, Cep164, Ift88, Ift43, Ift81, Cep83, Foxj3, and Rfx7, with pairwise correlations only about -0.121 to 0.088, and no strong positive or negative signature neighbor emerged. This suggests the neuronal dataset is not reading out multiciliogenesis; however, the comparison is limited to transcriptional score vectors in mouse neuronal classes, and Rfx2, Mcidas, and Gmnc were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Gnao1 knockdown did not produce a simple cAMP-axis transcriptomic signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, or 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons: perturbations of Gnas, Adcy1, Adcy5, Pde10a, Pde4b, Adora2a, Gnb5, and the nearby phospholipase gene Plcb1 were essentially uncorrelated with Gnao1, and Plcb1 was cleanly disrupted in L4/5 IT cortex without phenocopying Gnao1. This suggests absence of Gnao1-like transcriptomic convergence rather than unchanged second-messenger signaling, because several cAMP-effector perturbations showed weak direct target engagement.

Smad9 perturbation did not produce a recognizable canonical BMP/SMAD transcriptional response in the neuronal panel: the sentinel BMP/TGF target genes Id1, Id2, Id3, Bambi, and Smad7 showed no detectable induction or repression, with no nominal or FDR-supported changes. This pathway-specific silence suggests the perturbation was uncoupled from the expected BMP-SMAD early-response axis in these cells, although the interpretation is tempered by the lack of an FDR-level decrease in Smad9 itself, leaving ineffective mRNA knockdown as an alternative explanation.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Pde10a showed a cell-type-specific transcriptional program in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA that was not recapitulated by other assayed cyclic-nucleotide PDE or GPCR/PKA perturbations. In this cell group, Pde1c, Pde3a, Pde4b, Pde4d, Adcy5, Drd2, Gnas, Gnal, Prkaca, Prkar1a, and Creb1 lacked FDR-significant signatures, and their score-vector correlations with the Pde10a signature were near zero to weak, arguing that the Pde10a state is not a generic cAMP-pathway effect. A key caveat is that several comparator perturbations also showed weak target-transcript reduction, so the contrast rests on observed transcriptional signatures rather than fully validated pathway perturbation.

Ttc21b showed only a weak positive neighbor pattern with a small ciliary trace rather than a robust module. Arl3 and B9d1 appeared among the top 16 positive Ttc21b neighbors, consistent with primary cilium/intraflagellar transport network membership, but their cosine similarities were low at about 0.11 and the strongest cosine overall was only 0.147. Safe_target-labelled perturbations ranked similarly, and the nearest-neighbor list was low-amplitude and not specific for ciliary biology, so this signal is best viewed as hypothesis-generating rather than a biomarker set.

Tsga10 showed no detectable convergence with Hif1a or centrosome/ciliogenesis-adjacent perturbations across comparable Glut/GABA neuronal contrasts. Its mRNA signature was weak, same-cell correlations with Hif1a, Cep112, Cep83, Cep120, Cep164, Cep290, Cep85l, Foxj1, Foxj3, Rfx3, and Rfx7 stayed near zero, and these comparators also lacked FDR-significant signatures. Thus, despite annotated TSGA10–HIF1A and cilia/centriole links, this dataset does not support a shared neuronal transcriptional module, with the caveat that only mRNA was assayed and HIF1A nuclear localization and ciliary ultrastructure were not measured.

Zbtb16 perturbation did not recapitulate the reported ZBTB16–CUL3–ATG14L autophagy axis at the mRNA level: across all 22 tested cell types, no transcript passed FDR 0.05, and targeted checks found no FDR-significant changes in Atg14, Cul3, or core autophagy genes including Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Map1lc3a, and Gabarapl1. Thus, these scRNA data do not support a transcriptional autophagy module response to Zbtb16 perturbation, with the caveat that only steady-state mRNA was measured, not ATG14L protein stability, ubiquitination, autophagy flux, or GPCR stimulation.

Ddr2 showed essentially no convergence with assayed collagen/ECM, integrin, Src-family, SOS, MEK, ERK, or RTK perturbations in this neuronal Perturb-seq screen: whole-transcriptome correlations with Col4a1, Itga2, Itgb1, Fyn, Sos1, Sos2, Map2k1, Map2k2, Mapk1, Pdgfrb, Met, and Ntrk2 were all near zero, with absolute maximum r=0.103 in matched cell types. This suggests the dataset did not engage a canonical DDR2 neighborhood, although Ddr1 was not assayed, Col4a1 is not a Reactome-listed fibrillar DDR2 ligand, and several comparator perturbations were themselves weak; in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Ddr2 appeared buffered while selected kinase controls were detectable.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Rax did not recapitulate the canonical RAX eye-field and retinal-progenitor transcriptional network in the profiled brain neurons: in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, the Rax signatures were nearly orthogonal to perturbations of Otx2, Pax6, Six3, Six6, Crx, Vsx2, Nr2e3, Nrl, and Hesx1. The only multiple-testing-corrected Rax responses were singleton down-regulated genes, including Gosr2 in L5/6 IT glutamatergic neurons and Myl12b in L2/3 IT CTX glutamatergic neurons, so the conclusion is limited to absence of a detectable mature-neuron module in this dataset.

Cd36 showed no multiple-testing-significant differential-expression response in any assayed cell type, and even the measured Cd36 transcript was not significantly changed in Cd36-annotated cells. In the same analysis framework, however, App was directly suppressed at FDR<0.05 in 20 of 22 tested cell types, and Lrp1 and Scarb2 also produced FDR-level signals. This pattern suggests that the missing Cd36 signature is target- and expression-context-specific rather than a general failure to detect lipid- or amyloid-related perturbations, while noting that these comparator genes are related but not functionally interchangeable with Cd36.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Scamp5 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic cells showed a strongly buffered transcriptional response, with only 3 FDR<0.05 genes despite target depletion, resembling the similarly buffered Syp, Snap25, and Stxbp1 perturbations rather than the broad AP-2/RAB7 trafficking responses seen with Ap2s1, Ap2m1, and Rab7. In this class, Fyttd1 and Gabra1 were the only clear non-target hits and sterol genes trended weakly upward. This contrast suggests acute Scamp5 loss is not transcriptionally equivalent to core AP-2/RAB7 disruption, although different pathway steps, guide efficiency, and essentiality may contribute.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Ghr targeting did not recover the expected GH–GHR–JAK/STAT5–SOCS transcriptional module in this assay: Socs2, Cish, Jak2, Stat5b, Igf1, Socs1, and Socs3 were not adjusted-significant outputs, and the weak Ghr signature was essentially uncorrelated with Prlr, Epor, Lepr, or Stat5b perturbation signatures across many glutamatergic and GABAergic classes. Even the strongest nominal classes, such as 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, lacked adjusted responses, including in tested hypothalamic classes, so this reflects pathway uncoupling under weak Ghr engagement rather than proof that neuronal GHR cannot signal via JAK2/STAT5.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Lrp4 did not recapitulate a canonical AGRN-LRP4-MUSK neuronal transcriptional module in this Perturb-seq dataset. Across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Agrn perturbation could show depletion, but Lrp4 and Musk were not measurably engaged, and the Lrp4 signature was not correlated with Agrn or Musk. In 191 MB P MY GABA, the only FDR-significant Lrp4 row, an exploratory Arglu1 increase appeared without strong canonical neighbors; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Lrp4 gave only a nominal Axin2 increase rather than a corrected Wnt response, so interpretation is context- and efficacy-sensitive.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gli2 showed signatures that were largely not interchangeable with other Hedgehog pathway perturbations, including Gli1, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Cdon, Gpr161, and Smo, across the profiled neuronal classes. In 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, Smo was the top positive genome-wide neighbor of Gli2, but the alignment was weak (r=0.134) and restricted, with small correlations overall and Smo not significant in that class. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Smo and Gli2 were weakly anti-correlated, and there was no confident Gli2-driven Hedgehog feedback or detectable SUFU-KIF7-related transcriptional response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ash1l was not transcriptionally interchangeable with related chromatin and lysine-methylation perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons. In this thalamic class, Ash1l showed only one FDR-validated effect, essentially limited to its own transcript, whereas Setd1a and Kmt2d produced 368 and 314 FDR hits, and Kmt2b, Kmt2a, and Nsd1 were also much stronger. Across the full transcriptome, Ash1l had near-zero correlation with all other perturbations, with no |r| above 0.04, arguing against a common generic KMT-loss program. This comparison is limited because the matched genes are pathway neighbors or STRING-associated chromatin regulators rather than obligate ASH1L complex subunits, and some comparator guides showed weak self-transcript depletion.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Napb depletion did not elicit transcriptional compensation of the measured SNAP/SNARE machinery in the five target-engaged cell types—001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In these contexts, Napa, Napg, Nsf, Snap25, Stx1a, Stx1b, Stxbp1, and Vamp2 showed no corrected mRNA change, arguing against an RNA-level feedback loop replacing β-SNAP with α/γ-SNAP or core vesicle-fusion genes. This inference is limited to assayed transcripts and does not address protein-level compensation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hectd4 knockdown in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, where the target effect was strongest, did not produce a basal mRNA signature of the reported HECTD4–GluN2B/MALT1 excitotoxicity axis: Grin2b and Malt1 were not significantly changed, Ptpn5 was never FDR-significant in any Hectd4 class, and a direct Grin2b perturbation was essentially uncorrelated with Hectd4. These data suggest the published HECTD4-GluN2B/MALT1 injury mechanism is uncoupled from resting transcription and is more likely protein-level or injury-context-dependent in this basal mouse-brain Perturb-seq setting.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: U2af2 showed positive convergence with spliceosome-related perturbations, especially Prpf6, Cdc40, and Snrnp70, but its largest signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA also aligned with proteasome perturbations such as Psmc1, Psmb4, Psmc5, and Pomp, suggesting a mixed spliceosome-neighbor and proteostasis or essential-stress component rather than a pure U2AF complex fingerprint. No robust inverse neighbor emerged, and the correlations were modest, based on gene-level Wilcoxon scores; U2af1 and Prpf19 were not assayed.

Tas2r118 showed an orthogonal signature to the available GPCR and calcium-signaling perturbations in this dataset, with broad pathway neighbors such as Gnal, Gnao1, Gnas, Gnb1, Gnb5, Plcb1, Itpr1, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Calm1-3, and Rgs6 not resembling the Tas2r118 profile. This does not refute annotated bitter-taste T2R biology; rather, the library lacked the key gustatory comparators, including Gnat3, Plcb2, Itpr3, Trpm5, and other Tas2r receptors, so only broad pathway-neighbor orthogonality could be assessed in brain cell classes.

Adamts17 perturbation in the assayed neurons did not produce an FDR-level transcriptional response in the fibrillin microfibril or BMP/TGFβ-SMAD axes: Fbn1, Fbn2, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Tgfbr3, and Smad1/5/9 were not significantly regulated, and the Adamts17 signature was nearly uncorrelated with assayed Fbn1 and BMP/TGFβ receptor perturbations. This suggests the established ADAMTS17–fibrillin/BMP-SMAD connection is uncoupled from acute neuronal mRNA signatures here, with the caveat that several related comparators were not targeted and the assay measures transcripts rather than extracellular matrix assembly.

Ddhd1 produced a transcriptomic perturbation signature that was not interchangeable with Ddhd2: across 22 matched cell types, their score-vector correlations were essentially zero, indicating nearly orthogonal responses despite both being DDHD-family, HSP-linked lipid enzymes placed together in Reactome PA-hydrolysis and broader DDHD phosphatidic-acid/phosphatidylinositol lipid metabolism context with Pld1, Pld2, and Pld6. This contrast should be interpreted cautiously because both paralogs showed weak scRNA target engagement, so the result reflects observed mRNA signatures rather than definitive lipid-function differences.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ppt1 was transcriptionally buffered in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons, where acute knockdown produced no significant downstream program, even though these same cell types were competent to mount a broad endolysosomal response to Rab7 perturbation. In contrast, Rab7 induced large lysosomal/vacuolar signatures, including genes such as Atp6v1b2, Atp6v0b, Dpp7, Lamp2, Grn, and Mcoln1, with especially strong thalamic and detectable midbrain responses. This contrast suggests that acute Ppt1 loss is not equivalent to disrupting core late-endosome/lysosome trafficking, while noting that Rab7 is only a pathway-neighborhood comparator rather than a Ppt1 paralog or CLN enzyme.

Alms1 did not converge with BBSome, IFT, basal-body, transition-zone, or other ciliopathy-neighbor perturbations in this acute mouse-brain Perturb-seq atlas. Across 20 comparators, including Bbs5, Bbs9, Ttc8, Ift88, Cplane1, Ahi1, and Cep290, Alms1 whole-transcriptome score correlations across 421 shared target/cell-type pairs were uniformly small, from -0.117 to 0.110. This nonconvergence was seen in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, although the comparison relies on weak Alms1 signatures and transcriptome correlations rather than matched cilium imaging.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Kcnd3 did not phenocopy Dpp6 in this screen: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Kcnd3 showed its best nominal on-target signal, Dpp6 was strongly detected, yet the Kcnd3 and Dpp6 whole-transcriptome score vectors were essentially uncorrelated there and across 22 shared classes. This argues against a shared steady-state mRNA module for Kv4/A-type voltage-gated potassium channel activity in these data. A caveat is that Kcnd3 knockdown was weak and did not reach 5% FDR, and DPP6 may influence compartmentalized electrophysiology without a matched whole-cell transcriptomic response.

cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Nr2e3 perturbation did not mobilize the canonical rod/cone phototransduction program in the assayed brain dataset, including in 217 P MY Pineal Glut. Across an explicit retinal marker panel—Crx, Nrl, Rho, Opn1sw, Opn1mw, Arr3, Gnat1, Gnat2, Gnb3, Gngt2, Pde6b, Pde6c, Cnga1, Cnga3, Prph2, Rom1, Rcvrn, Esrrb, Rorb, and Thrb—no measurable response was detected, and the pineal subgroup with 39 perturbed cells showed only nominal non-retinal hits such as Endod1. This absence call is limited by the non-retinal context and small pineal cell count.

Myrf showed a near-null perturbation signature across all 23 assayed neuronal classes, with no detectable decrease or increase of Myrf transcripts and an extremely sparse genome-wide response after multiple-testing correction. In the same differential-expression table, the comparator perturbation Srebf2 showed strong on-target depletion and a coherent cholesterol-homeostasis response involving Dhcr24, Insig1, Hmgcs1, and Fdps. This contrast suggests the Myrf near-null phenotype is not simply a generic failure to recover membrane-associated transcription-factor biology, although Srebf2 controls assay responsiveness rather than pathway equivalence with MYRF.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gria1 perturbation produced transcriptomic signatures that were mostly divergent or uncorrelated with other AMPA receptor components, including Gria2, Gria3, Gria4, Cacng2, Cacng3, Dlg4, and Grip1, despite their shared pathway context in AMPA receptor assembly, trafficking, and synaptic plasticity. The main exception was a modest convergence with Cacng8 in 191 MB P MY GABA cells, where Gria1 was the only FDR<0.05 gene and Cacng8 was the top positive signature neighbor. This convergence was small in absolute value and based on score-vector similarity rather than replicated electrophysiology.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Pgrmc1 knockdown did not behave like an upstream SREBP2/cholesterol perturbation in neurons: across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Srebf2 knockdown reproducibly reduced a sterol-biosynthetic program including Dhcr24, Insig1, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Fdft1, Hmgcs1, Sqle, Ldlr, Acaca, and Fdps, whereas Pgrmc1 showed no FDR sterol-module response and was nearly uncorrelated with Srebf2. This divergence may reflect transcription-factor versus post-transcriptional regulation, and several direct partners such as Cyp51 and Insig1 were not themselves perturbed.

Gclm perturbation showed a weak, consistent decrease in Gclm mRNA across cell types, but the expected glutathione/KEAP1-NFE2L2 antioxidant transcriptional program was not detectably induced. No curated readout genes, including Gclc, Nfe2l2, Nqo1, Hmox1, Slc7a11, Gss, or Sod2, reached FDR significance in any measured cell type, and the few FDR-level downstream changes were isolated to two different cell types rather than recurring. Because this check used a manually curated gene panel rather than formal pathway enrichment, and target engagement may have been partial, weak pathway output could have been missed.

Rhobtb2 perturbation in neurons produced transcriptome signatures that were largely uncoupled from Cul3, Hsp90ab1, Rho-family genes, and screened BTB/CUL3-neighbor perturbations such as Rhot1, Kctd1, Klhl7, and Klhl20, despite the known RHOBTB2–CUL3 biochemical relationship. In 155 MB Glut cells, Rhobtb2 showed only a nominal target-mRNA decrease without FDR-significant downstream genes, and this was also the cell type where Cul3 was significantly depleted yet still did not phenocopy Rhobtb2. These comparisons are transcriptome-level and may miss ubiquitination events, and some comparator perturbations had small cell counts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Uqcrh showed a specific null transcriptomic response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells: unlike related respiratory electron transport and complex III genes, Uqcrh stayed flat, did not yield a genome-wide expression vector resembling major complex III or other respiratory-chain perturbations, and had only very weak nearest-neighbor relationships. In the same dataset and cell types, Uqcrc1, Uqcrc2, Uqcrfs1, Cyc1, Ttc19, Cox5a, and Sdha showed strong target-mRNA depletion, indicating this was not a generic failure to perturb OXPHOS genes. This contrast is transcriptomic and based on on-target mRNA, so it does not establish whether UQCRH protein was depleted.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ptprt in 155 MB Glut showed the only cell class with FDR-significant depletion of the target transcript, yet its perturbation produced a buffered, isolated mRNA signature rather than a synaptic cell-adhesion phenocopy. In this class, Cdh2, Nlgn1, Nlgn2, Nlgn3, Nrxn1, Nrxn2, and Nrxn3 perturbations had strong signatures but were near-orthogonal to Ptprt loss, indicating no Cdh2/Nlgn/Nrxn transcriptional phenocopy. This is consistent with the caveat that known PTPRT effects are local synapse and Fyn-dependent phosphorylation phenotypes that may leave little steady-state transcriptomic footprint.

Setbp1 showed no FDR-significant differential-expression hits in this Perturb-seq matrix, but this appears to be a target-specific null rather than a global assay or Wilcoxon failure, because other regulatory perturbations in the same dataset produced strong responses, including Ppp2r1a with 3,147 significant rows and Setd1a with 1,245. Related perturbations such as Setdb1, Setd5, Ski, and Nf1 also did not phenocopy a Setbp1 transcriptomic signature in matched cell types. Direct effect-size comparisons remain caveated by differences in guides, expression levels, and cell counts across targets.

Nr4a3 showed no robust convergence or divergence with its NR4A paralogs Nr4a1 and Nr4a2 in this dataset. Across the NR4A paralog module, perturbations were transcriptionally weak, with only 1 FDR-significant row among 1,131,682 tests and no adjusted self-transcript depletion for any of the three genes. A restricted top-200-gene signature neighbor scan likewise found no strong positive or negative correlation between Nr4a3 and Nr4a1 or Nr4a2. Thus, the result does not support paralog interchangeability or antagonism, and is better interpreted as insufficient family-wide engagement or temporal buffering rather than true biological divergence.

Ndufv1 perturbation was characterized mainly by self-transcript depletion rather than a convergent oxidative phosphorylation RNA signature: in a curated comparison of 41 NDUF/COX/UQCR/SDH perturbations, most significant rows were the perturbed gene itself, with Ndufv1 showing one self-only hit, Ndufs8 four self-only hits, and Ndufs2 seven hits of which five were self. In 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, Ndufv1 transcript decreased while downstream OXPHOS RNA appeared buffered. This comparison was targeted, not genome-wide, and limited to NDUF/COX/UQCR/SDH-named perturbations.

Avpr2 showed weak, nonconvergent transcriptomic relationships with canonical Gs/cAMP neighbors in this brain Perturb-seq dataset: restricted top-gene correlations between Avpr2 and Gnas, Adcy1/3/5, or Pde1c/3a/4b/4d/10a perturbations were all modest, with maximum |r| of 0.276. This lack of convergence stood out because Adcy3 and Pde10a displayed detectable on-target depletion elsewhere in the same matrix, including Pde10a in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA. Vasopressin ligand genes and the canonical renal water-channel effector also did not respond detectably, although these comparisons were limited to the top 500 Avpr2-ranked genes per cell type.

Klhl7 did not converge with other measured BTB/Kelch-related perturbations in mouse neurons: Klhl20, Btbd9, and Rhobtb2 showed only weak maximum score-vector correlations with Klhl7 of 0.165, 0.068, and 0.153, respectively, indicating little or no robust shared expression signature. This weakens a model in which reducing any CUL3/BTB adaptor produces a common neuronal stress state detectable by Perturb-seq, although these were pathway-neighbor rather than obligate same-complex comparisons and each related perturbation had weak FDR support.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Dhdds showed a gene-specific signature within the assayed glycosylation set: in the two responsive glutamatergic classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, perturbations of Dpm1, Stt3b, Fktn, St3gal3, and St3gal5 did not phenocopy the Dhdds downstream program, with near-zero correlation to Dhdds and significant effects absent or largely limited to each target transcript. This supports a restricted-library uncoupling result in which DHDDS was uniquely visible among tested glycosylation genes, while interpretation is limited because Nus1, Dolk, and Srd5a3 were not assayed and comparator self-knockdown differed from Dhdds.

Atg16l1 perturbation was uncoupled from a canonical autophagy/lysosome RNA signature in these brain cells: across the measured panel, Atg5, Map1lc3a, Sqstm1, Becn1, Rb1cc1, Lamp2, Mtor, Rptor, Rubcn, and Tbk1 did not show recurrent FDR-significant regulation, and the few nominal changes were sparse, directionally mixed, and not recurrent across cell types. Thus, despite ATG16L1’s pathway membership in LC3-family lipidation and autophagosome assembly, this dataset detected no coherent basal transcript response, with the caveat that the autophagy panel was small.

Il6st perturbation in unstimulated neurons did not produce a canonical gp130 JAK/STAT/SOCS feedback signature: Socs3, Socs1, Stat3, Jak1, Jak2, Mapk1, Akt3, Egr1, Fos, and Junb were not significantly changed, and the expected acute IL-6-family pathway output was not induced. This pattern suggests basal-state uncoupling, consistent with either little tonic gp130 signaling or buffering of receptor loss at the sampled time point, and it should not be taken to mean that IL6ST cannot drive JAK/STAT signaling when ligand is present.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ank2 did not emerge as a shared acute transcriptional module with the ankyrin/spectrin/adducin membrane-cytoskeleton scaffold: in 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Sptan1 and Add1 perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Ank2 in the Ank2-responsive classes. This contrast was seen even where related perturbations such as Sptan1, Ank1, or Ank3 showed stronger self-transcript depletion, while Ank2 responses were weak or buffered with no FDR-significant secondary genes. Near-zero correlations here are driven by weak Ank2 signatures, and lack of RNA convergence does not address physical complex formation.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Adrb3 did not recapitulate the canonical adrenoceptor–Gαs–adenylyl-cyclase branch in this screen. In 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, Adcy3 knockdown was clearly detected, yet Adrb3 remained FDR-silent and its overall signature was essentially uncorrelated with Adcy3, as well as with beta-adrenergic paralogs and nearby cAMP-pathway genes such as Gnas, Adcy1, and Adcy5. Because Adcy3 is a downstream pathway neighbor rather than a receptor paralog, and Adrb3 expression was low, this points to limited perturbation engagement rather than disproving ADRB3-to-cAMP signaling in neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Dnmt3a showed a weak and largely distinct perturbation profile: in matched thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic cells, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Kmt2a and Kmt2b produced corrected transcriptomic signatures whereas Dnmt3a did not, and Dnmt3a score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Kmt2a, Kmt2b, Mbd2, Mecp2, Tcf4, or Zbtb18. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Dnmt3a depletion was only nominal, with nominal Gls decrease, no broad corrected GABAergic response, and no Mecp2-like convergence along the neuronal mCH/methyl-DNA reader axis.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Kcnc3 showed broader CRISPRi engagement than the other Kv3 alpha-subunits, but its transcriptomic signature was not interchangeable with Kcnc1 or Kcnc2. In shared FDR-engaged contexts such as 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Kcnc3–Kcnc1/Kcnc2 score-vector correlations were near zero, and responses were largely limited to target depletion with buffered or uncorrelated downstream RNA in the voltage-gated potassium channel context. These comparisons involve weak, target-only signatures, and Kcnc4 was not assessed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Asxl3 was null in the assayed cell types and did not phenocopy Bap1: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the largest Asxl3 stratum remained FDR-null, while a corrected Bap1-labeled PR-DUB/H2AK119ub1 chromatin-regulation signature was detected, and in 052 Pvalb Gaba a second Bap1-labeled response appeared without Asxl3/Bap1 score-vector convergence. Across examined contexts, including 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Asxl3 and Bap1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated. Because Asxl1/Asxl2 were not in the library and Asxl3 mRNA engagement was weak, the divergence is mechanistically indeterminate rather than a clean contradiction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Med15 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type shows a coordinated down-regulation of a synaptic and dendritic membrane module, rather than mixed activation and repression. The 19-gene response includes neuronal structural and signaling transcripts such as Atp2b1, Ptpn3, Lrrc7, Ntng1, Atp2a2, Grm1, Gabra4, Kcnc2, Pcp4, Prkcd, and Trim9, and this was the only cell class with a conventional Med15 differential-expression signature. The pattern is partly shared by Med13 and Med23, but is distinct from the local Srebf2 sterol program; enrichment is based on a small compartmental gene set and does not demonstrate direct MED15 binding.

Actg1 perturbation showed a limited and asymmetric RNA response relative to Actb. Across the dataset, Actb perturbation repeatedly induced Actg1 and Flna, but Actg1 perturbation yielded only one non-target FDR-significant hit, Flna, in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and whole-transcriptome Actg1-versus-Actb signature correlations were near zero. Several cell types with strong Actg1 self-depletion, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, showed no corrected downstream Actg1 response. Because Actb itself was not measured as a response feature, reciprocal beta-actin induction after Actg1 perturbation could not be directly tested.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Sv2a was not interchangeable with all presynaptic perturbations: across matched neuronal classes including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 155 MB Glut, Sv2a, Syp, Cplx1, and Gad1 were largely target-dominant, whereas Stxbp1 was the clear outlier with many FDR-significant non-target genes, including a broad L4/5 IT cortical response. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Sv2a showed strong depletion without downstream DE, but Stxbp1 produced downstream changes. These gene-level summaries indicate pathway-neighbor divergence rather than a unified synaptic-vesicle knockdown program and do not prove a direct vesicle-fusion consequence.

Uqcrfs1 knockdown did not trigger detectable stoichiometric mRNA feedback within the measured mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III module: transcripts for Uqcrc1, Uqcrc2, Uqcrb, Uqcrh, Uqcrq, Cyc1, and the neighboring genes Ttc19 and Uqcc2 were not significantly changed, and in 155 MB Glut cells Ttc19 was likewise not induced, yielding only weak Uqcrfs1–Ttc19 signature convergence. This pattern is consistent with Uqcrfs1 acting through protein-level assembly and maturation steps, but the panel was limited and does not directly assess complex III assembly or proteostasis.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Flrt3 did not show a recurrent downstream transcriptional module or a strong perturbation neighbor. In the two cell types with the largest nominal effects, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, the leading signals were isolated rather than shared, with top genes including Klhl7, App, Ski, and Eef2, and the nearest non-self signatures had only about |r|~0.1 genome-wide correlation. Thus, lowering thresholds is unlikely to rescue a coherent Flrt3 program, although this does not exclude post-transcriptional roles within the FLRT3-latrophilin/UNC5/ROBO adhesion network.

Ndufs7 perturbation did not recover a recurrent mitochondrial integrated stress response program: Atf4, Ddit3, Chac1, Trib3, Xbp1, Lonp1, Hspa9, Hspd1, Hspe1, and Atf5 were not activated, with adjusted support absent across the dataset. This negative result held in the largest nominally engaged cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where downstream rows remained non-significant and Xbp1 was only nominally changed. The result should be interpreted cautiously, because weak Ndufs7 engagement may have produced a false negative rather than a true absence of Complex I stress signaling.

Dync2h1 showed near-zero transcriptional convergence with the available ciliary comparators in the screen, including the dynein-2 partner Dync2i1/Wdr60 and the IFT, kinesin, and BBS genes Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Kif3b, Ttc21b, Bbs5, Bbs9, and Ttc8. Across these ten perturbations, transcriptomic effects were globally weak, with only a few significant pairwise similarities, suggesting that the primary cilium/retrograde intraflagellar transport module was largely buffered or poorly captured by basal scRNA-seq. This inference is limited to the assayed ciliary genes and RNA signatures, not broader dynein-2 subunits or nontranscriptional ciliary phenotypes.

Psen1 knockdown left the canonical APP/Notch gamma-secretase substrate axis largely uncoupled at the RNA level: Notch receptors and targets such as Notch1, Notch2, Notch3, Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Hey2, Dll1, and Jag1, as well as App, Bace1, Bace2, Adam10, Aplp1, and Aplp2, showed no coherent FDR-level transcriptional response. This suggests the Perturb-seq readout is not directly reporting PSEN1-dependent proteolytic flux, with the caveat that A-beta peptides, NICD cleavage, and Notch protein activation were not assayed and postmitotic neurons may have low ligand-dependent Notch signaling.

Zfp1, despite its annotation as a nuclear KRAB/C2H2 transcription factor linked to generic transcriptional regulation, showed little detectable RNA-program impact in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq assay. Across all 23 profiled mouse-brain cell types, Zfp1 perturbation produced mixed, nonsignificant on-target RNA changes, no q<0.10 downstream differentially expressed genes, and no strong perturbation-signature neighbor. This nearly null response suggests that the expected KRAB-ZFP transcriptional effects were not observed here, although weak target-transcript engagement means the result cannot distinguish biological buffering from an inefficient perturbation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Tmem165 showed weak engagement in the assayed neurons: its mRNA trended downward but was not significantly depleted after correction in any cell type, and Tmem165 perturbation produced no multiple-testing-corrected differential-expression hits. In contrast, the Golgi Ca2+/Mn2+ transporter neighbor Atp2c1 achieved corrected self-knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, yet Atp2c1 itself was the only corrected hit in both classes. Together, this points to a transcriptionally buffered or silent Golgi calcium/manganese homeostasis module in these neurons, while leaving the Tmem165 silence plausible but unproven.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc25a46 knockdown was transcriptionally uncoupled from the Opa1/Dnm1l amino-acid or integrated-stress-like module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells: unlike Opa1 and Dnm1l perturbation in these same classes, Slc25a46 did not measurably induce Asns, Chac1, Ddit3, Cars, or Slc7a5, and whole-signature correlations to Opa1 or Dnm1l were weak. This contrast should be interpreted cautiously because Slc25a46 engagement was partial and the comparison is based on target-neighbor logic rather than matched biochemical epistasis.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Zc3h14 did not collapse into a generic RNA-binding or mRNA-processing factor loss program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these two best Zc3h14 contexts, whole-transcriptome signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Cstf2, Srsf1, and Celf2 perturbations, with score vectors near zero or only weakly negative; Cstf2 perturbation itself produced no FDR-significant downstream genes. Thus the Pabpn1/Cstf2 decrease is better viewed as a readout or partial compensatory arm than a proven single mediator, although Cstf2 depletion was weak and Pabpn1 was not directly perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Trmt1 did not reproduce the amino-acid-stress or ISR-like transcriptional program seen with Elongator loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. In this same cell type, Elp1 and Elp2 strongly upregulated Asns, Atf4, Ddit3, Cars, Herpud1, Mars1, Shmt2, Slc3a2, Slc7a5, and Slc38a2, whereas the Trmt1 signature was absent or weak, with the highest-cell-count Trmt1 contrast lacking FDR<0.05 hits. This suggests that the cell type can mount a tRNA-perturbation-associated stress program, but that response is coupled to Elongator rather than Trmt1 loss; the ISR assignment is transcriptomic and pathway-inferred, without phospho-eIF2α or ATF4 protein measurements.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Edem3 perturbation produced only a weak, thalamus-restricted UPR-like signal: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Xbp1 was the top nominally increased transcript after perturbation (logFC +0.487, nominal p=1.39e-5), consistent with possible IRE1-XBP1 feedback. However, this effect did not survive multiple-testing correction (FDR 0.239), was not seen broadly across cell types, and the assay measured total Xbp1 RNA rather than IRE1-dependent Xbp1 splicing or XBP1s protein, so it is best viewed as a hypothesis-generating compensatory marker rather than evidence of a robust unfolded-protein response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Arl3 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class showed significant target transcript reduction, but the resulting signature did not converge with available ciliary perturbations. Ttc8 was efficiently self-depleted and Ift88 was nominally self-depleted, yet their correlations with Arl3 were only 0.0277 and 0.0329, and unrestricted nearest-neighbor correlations for Arl3 were also very small. This argues against a shared IFT/BBSome-like transcriptional module here, while remaining limited by missing direct ARL3-related perturbations such as Arl13b, Rp2, Pde6d, and Unc119 and by weak engagement for several ciliary targets.

Map3k7 showed no strong whole-transcriptome signature neighbor in this dataset, and assayed TAK1-pathway relatives—including Chuk, Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Map2k6, Mapk8, Mapk9, Tgfbr1/2/3, Tlr3, Tlr8, Il1r1, Il1rap, and Tnfrsf1a/b—were sparse or essentially uncorrelated with Map3k7 rather than forming a shared TNF/IL-1/TLR to NF-kB and JNK-p38 MAPK module in resting neurons. This apparent uncoupling should be interpreted cautiously because TAB1/2/3, TRAF6, IKBKG, IKBKB, MAP2K4, and MAP2K7 were not perturbed, and the comparisons are limited to RNA phenotypes.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Hdx showed weak or absent convergence with other perturbations, including homeobox-related factors, and the scanned signatures did not define a robust Hdx module. Across cell types such as 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, the strongest Hdx neighbors remained small, with Mafb r=0.149 and Plxna2 r=-0.123 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, while Pitx3 and Pbx3 were only weak neighbors elsewhere. Safe-target perturbations also appeared among nominal nearest neighbors, suggesting noise rather than biology; these weak signatures rule out a large shared module but do not exclude subtle context-specific effects.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gad1 knockdown showed that Gad1 and the paralog Gad2 were not interchangeable at the transcriptome level across overlapping inhibitory classes, including 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. In the GABA synthesis and GABA shunt context, Gad1 depletion was not accompanied by Gad2 mRNA upregulation, and Gad1–Gad2 differential-expression signatures stayed close to zero similarity. Notably, even where Gad1 on-target depletion was strongest, secondary transcriptomic responses were weak or absent; however, this comparison was transcriptomic only, without measurements of Gad2 protein, enzyme activity, or GABA pools.

Gaa knockdown showed a self-only transcriptomic response: after strong depletion of the Gaa transcript, no additional conventionally significant differentially expressed genes were detected, including in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA where on-target knockdown was strongest. This same architecture recurred for the lysosomal enzyme comparators Ctsb and Ppt1, indicating that the muted Gaa RNA signature reflects a broader pattern of individual lysosomal enzyme knockdowns rather than an isolated case. Because only RNA readouts were compared, and these enzymes act on different substrates, the shared target-only behavior should not be taken to imply shared metabolic phenotypes.

Fcgr4 showed no reproducible convergence with Fcgr2b or other assayed myeloid/neuroimmune receptor perturbations in the tested neuronal classes. Same-cell correlations between the Fcgr4 score vector and Fcgr2b, Cd14, Csf1r, Cx3cr1, Itgb2, Tlr2, Tlr4, and Trem2 were near zero overall (r = -0.078 to 0.088), and the strongest genome-wide Fcgr4 neighbor in any cell class reached only |r| = 0.161. This pattern is more consistent with globally weak or unengaged immune-receptor programs in the screen than with a specific divergence of Fcγ receptors, although key Fcgr4 signaling partners such as Fcer1g and Syk were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Ttll5 showed sparse or self-only transcriptional effects across a cilium-associated retinal-degeneration comparator panel in mouse brain neurons, with no shared Ttll5-like neuronal module emerging across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA. In the thalamic glutamatergic class, Ttc8 and Arl3 showed significant self-knockdown, whereas Ttll5 did not, and Rpgr plus other neighbors such as Ift88 and Bbs5 were also largely transcriptionally silent. This interpretation is limited by variable target engagement, a hand-curated comparator panel, and the absence of direct TTLL paralog perturbations.

Taar1 showed a transcriptomic signature that was largely uncoupled from the expected amine-GPCR and G-protein/cAMP signaling neighborhood: whole-transcriptome scores correlated only weakly with Adcy1, Adcy5, Gnas, Gnao1, Pde1c, Comt, dopamine receptors Drd2/3/4/5, adrenergic receptors Adra1a/Adrb1/Adrb2, and serotonin receptors Htr1a/Htr1b/Htr1f. This was also true in the two highlighted cell types, including 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut. These correlations reflect chronic CRISPRi transcriptomes rather than direct pathway-activity readouts, so acute agonism and knockdown may diverge.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Vps37a showed robust, cell-type-specific Perturb-seq signatures in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas the related ESCRT-III perturbation Chmp4b did not phenocopy it in those same mushroom body classes. In 155 MB Glut, Vps37a had a large FDR signature with stress and lysosomal-acidification/V-ATPase induction and reduced synaptic or neuronal membrane genes; in 191 MB P MY GABA, it showed a smaller but similar program including Atp6v1h, Atp6v0b, and Tnfrsf12a induction. Chmp4b had no FDR genes in either class despite substantial cell numbers, although this divergence is tempered by the lack of FDR-verified Chmp4b target knockdown, which may indicate weaker Chmp4b engagement rather than a fully distinct biology.

Thap11 showed a specific recurrent perturbation signature that was not reproduced by the related THAP-domain factor Thap1 across the same 23 cell types. Thap1 yielded only 16 FDR-significant gene-by-cell-type calls overall and none within the 20-gene Thap11 core, whereas Thap11 produced 1,543 total significant calls and 274 within that core. This divergence argues against treating THAP-domain factors as interchangeable and instead supports THAP-family transcription-factor specificity, while noting that perturbed-cell counts differed and the comparison rests on mRNA differential expression rather than matched protein depletion.

Sipa1l3 showed little to no detectable transcriptomic effect in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset: guide assignment was not accompanied by significant loss of Sipa1l3 RNA in any measured class, and no Sipa1l3 perturbation effect survived 10% FDR in any assayed cell class. In contrast, Epha4, a reported Sipa1l3 pathway neighbor from Xenopus eye development, showed clear on-target depletion, including very strong depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, yet its global signatures did not resemble Sipa1l3. Thus, the Epha4/Sipa1l3/Wnt eye-development relationship was not recapitulated in these mouse-brain transcriptomes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Paqr7 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed only target self-depletion as an FDR-significant effect, and its perturbation signature did not converge with Pgrmc1. Although Pgrmc1 knockdown in the same class was much stronger, with robust self-depletion, its ranked transcriptomic response was uncorrelated and orthogonal to Paqr7, consistent with separation of PAQR mPR and PGRMC branches of nonclassical progesterone signaling rather than interchangeable receptor subunits. This comparator is pathway-adjacent, however, and lack of shared mRNA response does not exclude shared rapid signaling.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cspp1 did not behave like an interchangeable ciliary perturbation in this dataset. Across same-cell comparisons, its strongest absolute correlation was only 0.305, and in the primary cilium/Joubert ciliary module its signatures were at most weakly correlated with B9d1, Ahi1, Cplane1, Cep290, Rpgrip1l, Ift88, Bbs5, and Ttc8. In 308 CB GABA, B9d1 showed nine FDR-significant genes not reproduced by Cspp1, while in 155 MB Glut, Ahi1 and Cplane1 showed transcript-level target depletion but Cspp1 did not. This contrast is tempered by weak Cspp1 engagement and generally small comparator signatures.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Tubb5 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut produced strong on-target transcript depletion but an otherwise sparse RNA phenotype, with no statistically resolved secondary genes in the strongest contrasts and no p53/apoptosis marker induction. In these same high-power glutamatergic classes, Tubb2a, Tubb3, Tubb4a, and Tubb4b showed the same self-limited pattern, each with only 1–2 FDR-significant genes, arguing that Tubb5 was not uniquely associated with a shared microtubule-repair or paralog-compensation transcriptional program. This comparison is based on FDR hit counts rather than matched protein-level perturbation strength.

Scn1b showed a sparse RNA output and did not transcriptionally phenocopy voltage-gated sodium-channel alpha-subunit or related epilepsy ion-channel perturbations. Across comparisons with Scn1a, Scn2a, Scn3a, Scn8a, Scn9a, Cacna1a, Kcnq2, and Kcnq3, transcriptome-wide score-vector correlations were near zero, ranging from -0.100 to 0.137, and no other perturbation produced a strongly convergent or strongly opposing signature. Some comparator perturbations had weak on-target knockdown, and the lack of RNA correlation does not exclude shared electrophysiologic effects.

Slc1a1 perturbation did not phenocopy neuronal glutamate receptor-subunit perturbations at the transcriptional level. Compared with Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, and Gria2, Slc1a1 showed a much weaker signature, with only 4 total FDR differential-expression rows versus 103, 23, and 62 for Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b, respectively. Across the three Slc1a1-engaged cell classes, it lacked a recurrent non-target module and score-vector scans found no strong positive or negative neighbors, suggesting glutamatergic receptor-coupled transcription was largely uncoupled from Slc1a1 in this dataset. This comparison is based on DEG burden and score-vector correlations rather than direct glutamate receptor activity measurements.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Psmc1 showed a cell-type-specific proteasome-subunit contrast in cortical projection neurons: 001 L5-6 IT Glut and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut responded to Psmc1, while showing weak or no FDR-significant responses to Psmc5 or Pomp, whereas 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut was near-negative for Psmc1 despite 79 perturbed cells but responded strongly to Psmb4, with 842 FDR-significant genes. In 001, the Psmc1 signature included reduced Slc17a7 and paradoxically increased Psmc1 transcript; in 008 it included Dnm1 and Camk2a repression. These contrasts come from restricted single-cell signatures, and some missing responses could reflect guide efficiency rather than true subunit-specific biology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Yy1 perturbation showed a restricted transcriptomic signature that converged with Brd4, Chd8, and Trrap, but not with Jarid2, across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 308 CB GABA, consistent with enhancer-promoter and chromatin-cofactor regulation rather than the assayed Jarid2 PRC2 state. In the strongest Yy1-responsive classes, Brd4 ranked among the top positive neighbors, Chd8 was especially prominent in 151 TH and 155 MB, and Trrap was recurrently positive, whereas Jarid2 was weak to negative and had no FDR-significant response; these comparisons were limited to the top 250 Yy1 genes per cell type and Jarid2 target engagement was not measurable.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Atp6v0a1 was not phenotypically interchangeable with Atp6v0c in this dataset: despite both being V-ATPase V0 subunits, Atp6v0a1 perturbation was largely target-only, with no genome-wide downstream differential expression surviving multiple-testing correction and little correlation with the Atp6v0c signature. This buffered pattern appeared even in strong target-engagement populations such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, whereas Atp6v0c caused broad effects, including recurrent secondary loss of Atp6v0a1 mRNA. The divergence may reflect both subunit biology and stronger Atp6v0c knockdown.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hspd1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed the clearest nominal on-target transcript decrease, with Hspd1 ranking third by nominal p value, yet it did not produce a corrected mitochondrial unfolded-protein-response or compensatory chaperone/protease program. Dnaja3 and Ddit3 shifted only nominally, while Atf5, Hspa9, Hspe1, Lonp1, and Clpp were uncorrected and non-significant, with adjusted p values of 1.0. Thus, in this cell type, nominal Hspd1 depletion was uncoupled from a robust UPRmt-positive HSP60-loss signature, and this inference remains transcriptomic and cell-type-restricted.

Klrk1 showed only a weak, non-recurrent nominal transcriptional tail rather than a reproducible module. Across cell types, the largest nominal effects were scattered among unrelated genes such as Gabrg2, Arfgef1, Abi2, and Emc2, failed FDR correction, and did not recur across cell types; for example, in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, Gabrg2 was the strongest nominal row but had FDR 0.944, while in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, a near-top Arfgef1 decrease had FDR 1.0. Restricted neighbor analysis based on the top 50 Klrk1 genes per cell type was unstable and repeatedly included Safe_target-labeled perturbations, so these nominal genes should not be treated as pathway biomarkers without independent validation.

Nrxn3 showed no robust perturbation signature across the 21 Nrxn3-assayed neuronal classes: its cell-wide gene-level vectors were nearly uncorrelated with neurexin paralogs Nrxn1 and Nrxn2, neuroligins Nlgn1, Nlgn2, and Nlgn3, and other synaptic-adhesion neighbors including Dlg4, Lrrtm1, Lrrtm4, and Ncam1. Top positive and negative neighbors were likewise close to zero, so Nrxn3 did not converge within the NRXN3/neurexin trans-synaptic adhesion pathway in this readout. Because Nrxn3 target mRNA was not robustly detected, biological divergence and technical failure cannot be cleanly separated, and these data should not be over-interpreted as an informative neurexin-family RNA phenotype.

Pou6f1 did not participate in a coordinated Emb/POU6F1–MEF2D–p300 enhancer-complex module in the brain Perturb-seq data. Across all 23 assayed mouse-brain cell classes, Mef2d and Ep300 perturbations showed no corrected hits and almost no signature correlation with Pou6f1, and they did not phenocopy the Pou6f1 profile. These matched null contrasts suggest that the skeletal-muscle Emb/POU6F1–MEF2D–p300 complex is not the dominant POU6F1 wiring diagram in the assayed neurons, while remaining a context-specific mechanism rather than a contradiction of the original muscle finding.

Ulk4 was uncoupled from Rb1cc1/FIP200, the available comparator for canonical ULK1-FIP200 autophagy initiation, in matched neuronal classes: across 21 shared classes, Ulk4 and Rb1cc1 transcriptomic signatures were near-zero correlated rather than phenocopying each other. Rb1cc1 showed clear on-target depletion and broader downstream effects, including significant knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas the largest Ulk4 test showed only a nominal Jak1 decrease. In this dataset, this supports interpreting ULK4 as a distinct pseudokinase scaffold rather than a proxy for the canonical autophagy-initiation complex, although direct comparison to Ulk1, Ulk2, Ulk3, Atg13, and Atg101 was not available.

Tshz2 showed a null phenotype in this adult-brain Perturb-seq assay, and its paralog Tshz3 behaved similarly rather than as a compensating or interchangeable module. Across 22 Tshz2-covered brain cell classes, neither perturbation produced FDR-significant downstream effects or target-mRNA depletion, and their nominal signatures were essentially uncorrelated, with matched-class score correlations near zero. This argues against an interchangeable Tshz2/Tshz3 module under these assay conditions, but the contrast is limited by weak engagement of both perturbations and does not contradict established Tshz3 roles in cortical projection neurons.

Dlx5 did not show detectable convergence with its linked paralog Dlx6: across the shared Dlx5 cell types, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, Dlx5–Dlx6 score-vector correlations were near zero, and neither perturbation produced FDR-significant output genes. In these contexts, Dlx5 showed only nominal target decreases within a Dlx5/Dlx6 GABAergic interneuron and PV-differentiation module, without significant repression of GABA-effector markers such as Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, or Slc6a1, so the apparent divergence from Dlx6 remains exploratory and may reflect weak engagement or noise.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Brsk2 showed no detectable transcriptional convergence with the available related perturbations Strada, Mark3, Prkaa2, or Mapt in the two cell types with the clearest Brsk2 hints, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. In these cells, full-score correlations were near zero, with the strongest non-self neighbor only r = 0.102 in Pvalb GABAergic cells and r = 0.159 in L4-5 IT glutamatergic cells, despite those cell types producing strong differential-expression signals for other perturbations. This suggests the measured RNA response did not capture the canonical STK11/LKB1-SAD kinase and MAPT phosphorylation axis, although Brsk1 and Stk11 were not included and the Brsk2 signatures themselves were weak.

Irf1 showed little detectable basal transcriptomic response across all 23 profiled neuronal cell classes, with no target-transcript depletion and no FDR<0.05 downstream hit in Glut, GABA, Dopa, or Pineal cells. This null sat within a broadly quiet interferon/TLR/IRF module: across 399 target-by-cell-type contrasts for Adar, Ifnar1/2, Ifngr1/2, Irf2/3/5/7/8/9, Nfkb1, Rel, Stat1/2, and Tlr3/4, only six corrected rows were significant. Restricted signature-neighbor analysis likewise found no strong Irf1-like perturbation, though these cross-perturbation comparisons are transcriptomic and several related targets lacked on-target validation.

Ndufc2 showed a pattern shared across many mitochondrial Complex I perturbations: transcriptomes were dominated by loss of the targeted subunit mRNA, with only sparse secondary differential expression rather than a broad nuclear OXPHOS-stress program. Across 26 Nduf subunit or assembly-factor perturbations, there were 64 FDR-significant direct target-transcript results but only nine non-target results across 572 target-by-cell-class tests, including cell types such as L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, Pvalb Gaba, and MB P MY GABA. This comparison is limited by variable guide performance and cell coverage and reflects transcriptomes, not Complex I assembly or enzymatic activity.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mtnr1b in 308 CB GABA, the only positive cell type, was transcriptionally uncoupled from the canonical melatonin receptor / G alpha i inhibition of adenylyl cyclase pathway: its perturbation showed only weak correlations with Gnao1, Gnb1, Gnb5, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Prkaca, Prkar1a, Creb1, and Pde1c, and its closest whole-transcriptome neighbors were only moderate and did not include core Gi/o effectors. This suggests that although an MTNR1B biochemical pathway exists, no coherent downstream transcriptional module was recovered here, with the caveat that G-protein and cAMP signaling are often post-translational and may not produce matched mRNA signatures after CRISPR perturbation.

Csrnp3 showed a largely null profile across all 22 assayed cell classes: its perturbation lacked mRNA knockdown, produced no FDR-significant downstream genes, and did not transcriptionally induce the related family members Csrnp1 or Csrnp2, with no strong signature neighbors detected. This refines, rather than proves, a CSRNP-family redundancy model in DNA-binding transcriptional regulation, because Csrnp1 and Csrnp2 were measured only as transcripts and not perturbed; any buffering could therefore be constitutive, protein-level, or developmental rather than an acute paralog mRNA switch-on.

Cpe did not transcriptionally converge with the related prohormone-processing perturbation Pcsk2 in the screened brain cells: across shared classes, the aggregate Cpe–Pcsk2 signature correlation was near zero (r=0.004). This was evident even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Cpe knockdown was strong and Pcsk2 showed engagement but did not produce a Cpe-like mRNA program. Pcsk2 itself was FDR-engaged in only 4 of 20 shared cell classes, and Pcsk5 was not interpretable as a comparator because its transcript was not depleted.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Iqcb1 showed little transcriptomic coupling to related ciliary disease genes in this mouse brain dataset. Across available perturbations of Cep290, Ahi1, Bbs5, Bbs9, Cep164, Glis2, Ift88, Rpgrip1l, Sdccag8, and Ttc21b, same-cell Pearson correlations with Iqcb1 stayed near zero, from -0.119 to 0.176, including in 308 CB GABA and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut. This argues against a shared immediate transcriptional module for ciliogenesis, transition-zone trafficking, or BBSome-associated cargo trafficking here, although several comparator perturbations were themselves weak and the analysis is limited to represented genes.

Lmx1a showed no detectable convergence with Lmx1b or nearby midbrain developmental transcription-factor perturbations in this adult neuronal Perturb-seq dataset. Across 22 matched classes, Lmx1a score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Lmx1b, Foxa2, Otx2, Nr4a2, Pitx3, En1, Isl1, Lhx3, Sox11, Sox2, and Pitx2, so the expected Wnt1-Lmx1a and SHH-Foxa2 midbrain dopaminergic program, including in 215 MB Dopa cells, was not recovered. This apparent uncoupling is most consistent with weak Lmx1a engagement and noncanonical adult cell types rather than a true separation from the developmental network.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Shank3 repression in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not produce a shared acute transcriptomic module with postsynaptic-density or NMDA-receptor neighbors: Dlg4, Dlgap4, Homer2, Grin1, and Grin2b signatures were weakly correlated with Shank3, often with different differential-expression burdens.
