In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Shank3 itself was the only FDR-significant gene, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut the strongest sampled Shank3 class showed Uba5 as the only downstream FDR-significant marker. These comparisons reflect transcriptomic score correlations rather than protein-complex occupancy or electrophysiology.

Chrng did not phenocopy other acetylcholine receptor partners in the brain dataset: its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Chrna1, Chrnb1, Chrnd, and Chrne, and all five skeletal-muscle AChR subunits showed weak or non-significant auto-target rows across matched brain cell classes. By contrast, neuronal cholinergic genes Chrnb2, Chrna4, and Ache showed significant self-transcript decreases, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. These comparisons reflect transcriptomic signatures, not receptor assembly or electrophysiology, and suggest the muscle nicotinic AChR complex was not measurably engaged in the profiled brain cells.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Ebf3 showed essentially no shared transcriptomic response with its paralogs Ebf1 or Ebf2 across the 21 shared cell types, with mean full-signature Pearson correlations near zero, and Ebf4 was not perturbed. In the 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut cell type, there was a single noticeable but weak and exploratory Ebf3–Ebf2 anticorrelation. Thus, despite the COE-family relationship and expected shared EBF/COE RNA polymerase II transcriptional regulation, the assay did not reveal a reproducible common paralog program, although all three EBF perturbations had weak on-target transcript effects, limiting any strong conclusion about nonredundancy.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Ppp3cc was transcriptomically uncoupled from the calcineurin core complex perturbations Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1 across overlapping neuronal populations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1 showed FDR-significant on-target knockdown and downstream responses, whereas Ppp3cc did not; similar Ppp3ca-positive/Ppp3cc-null and Ppp3r1-positive/Ppp3cc-null contrasts were seen in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA. Whole-transcriptome correlations were near zero, and weaker on-target RNA evidence plus fewer perturbed cells for Ppp3cc caution against treating it as a faithful calcineurin-loss surrogate.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ndufa6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed the only FDR-significant on-target knockdown for this gene, yet its whole-transcriptome signature was essentially uncorrelated with the other 2,045 perturbations, including complex-I neighbors Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, Ndufs8, and Ndufb8. Although several of these same-complex perturbations had stronger target-transcript depletion than Ndufa6, they still did not produce a shared downstream mitochondrial complex-I or respiratory electron transport RNA program, suggesting the screen primarily captured variable CRISPRi engagement rather than a convergent OXPHOS state.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Atp8a2 showed weak, nonconvergent transcriptional signatures across the measured neurons, with genome-wide score correlations near zero versus the related P4-ATPase perturbations Atp9a and Atp11c across shared cell classes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Atp8a2 depletion was largely self-dominated, lacking a significant downstream module or non-target genes at FDR < 0.25; in 308 CB GABA, non-target hits appeared but Atp8a2 itself was not significantly reduced and nearest-neighbor correlations were only modest. Overall, these data do not support interchangeable acute RNA phenotypes for shared P4-ATPase annotation, though interpretation is limited by weak Atp8a2 signatures and nearest-neighbor examples drawn from only a subset of cell types.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Arsb showed a divergent pattern rather than a generic lysosomal-stress response. Across shared cell types including 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, restricted transcriptome-wide correlations found no strong positive or negative Arsb neighbor, and after excluding the target transcript Arsb had no FDR-supported downstream mRNA response. The related sulfatase Gns was weak, with only one FDR-level on-target row in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and a nearly orthogonal signature, whereas Atp6v0c produced a broad response with 813 FDR-significant rows, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; these comparators are lysosomal but differ from ARSB in substrate and complex membership.

Nr1d2 perturbation in mouse brain cell groups did not produce FDR-supported changes in a selected set of REV-ERB lipid-output genes, including Srebf1, Srebf2, Hmgcr, Insig2, Por, Apoe, and Abca1, and selected clock-output genes also lacked FDR-corrected responses. The only significant hits in the Nr1d2 perturbation slice were Nr1d1 rows in three cell groups, suggesting that neuronal Nr1d2 perturbation preferentially exposes a clock-paralog node rather than robust lipid-output regulation. This was a selected-gene negative check rather than an unbiased lipid-pathway enrichment test.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Sstr5 showed no FDR-controlled transcriptional response across the Perturb-seq matrix, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where it had many perturbed cells, while the proximal Gi/o node Gnao1 was strongly depleted in those same classes. This contrast suggests the Sstr5 silence is more likely due to an upstream receptor limitation, such as receptor expression or guide engagement, rather than a general failure to detect GPCR/Gi/o biology. Consistent with this, neighboring Gi/o-coupled adenylyl-cyclase and ion-channel components Kcnj6, Adcy1, and Adcy5 were also transcriptionally buffered.

Nfkb1 was transcriptomically uncoupled from the broader NF-kappaB neighborhood in this basal brain screen: across all 22 Nfkb1-sampled cell classes, its steady-state signature showed near-zero similarity to Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, Chuk, Map3k7, and Traf3, and likewise to inflammatory receptor perturbations including Il1r1, Il1rap, Il17ra, Tlr2/3/4/5/7/8/9, and Tnfrsf1a/b. The broader canonical NF-kappaB/IKK subset was transcriptionally quiet at this FDR threshold, although these Wilcoxon-based correlations would miss post-translational NF-kappaB activity or transient stimulus responses.

Cyc1 perturbation did not produce an interchangeable acute transcriptional phenotype with other complex III genes: across the dataset, genome-wide score-vector correlations between Cyc1 and Uqcrc1, Uqcrc2, Uqcrfs1, Uqcrb, Uqcrh, Uqcrq, or Ttc19 stayed near zero, despite their shared respiratory-chain assembly. This nonconvergence was seen in classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Cyc1 often showed strong self-knockdown but few corrected downstream hits. A caveat is that several small subunits, especially Uqcrb, Uqcrh, and Uqcrq, had weak RNA self-knockdown, making them poor tests of mechanistic equivalence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ogdh knockdown did not transcriptionally phenocopy OGDH-complex partners or neighboring TCA perturbations: DE-score correlations with Dld, Dlst, Suclg1, Sucla2, Idh3a, Pdha1, Pdhb, Dlat, Aco2, and Mdh2 were near zero overall and within the main engaged neuronal classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Ogdh was significantly depleted but showed little downstream RNA change, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut depletion was nominal. These comparisons reflect Wilcoxon DE-score correlations rather than matched metabolic phenotypes, and Dld/Dlst engagement was often weak.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ap1s2 did not converge transcriptionally with the only assayed AP-1 core comparator, Ap1b1, despite their expected partnership in AP-1/clathrin-coated Golgi-endosomal vesicle biogenesis. Across 22 cell types, Ap1b1 showed only three significant rows, mostly self-gene dominated, and its score-vector correlations with Ap1s2 were near zero. In 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, Ap1b1 but not Ap1s2 had a significant Napa row; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Ap1s2 effects were weak or nonsignificant. This contrast is limited because most other AP-1 subunits were not assayed.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Crebrf perturbation in adult mouse brain did not resemble canonical CREB3/UPR/autophagy or mTOR/TSC transcriptional programs. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, curated UPR/autophagy genes such as Atf4, Atf6, Atg5, Becn1, Hspa5, Map1lc3b, Mtor, Sqstm1, and Xbp1 showed no FDR-significant response, and Crebrf score vectors correlated only weakly with Atf6, Creb1, Crebbp, Akt3, Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1, and Tsc2 perturbations. Instead, the neuronal signature was narrow and Ddx5-dominated, with additional changes mostly nominal; this transcriptomic comparison is limited to adult mouse brain cells and may not match prior overexpression or goat endometrial systems.

Kif2a showed near-zero whole-transcriptome correlation with Dync1h1, Kif5c, Kif1a, Kif5a, Tuba1a, Tubb4a, Dctn1, Dcx, and Pafah1b1 perturbations assayed in the same subclasses, so it did not phenocopy the microtubule-motor or cortical-malformation gene family in this dataset. This refines rather than negates the disease-genetic grouping of KIF2A with genes such as DYNC1H1 and KIF5C, because the contrast is weakened by poor Kif2a target-transcript engagement and by missing comparisons to Kif2b, Kif2c, and Tubg1.

Lrmda showed no convergence with Vps35l or other selected pigmentation comparators in this mouse neuronal Perturb-seq dataset: the exact Vps35l comparator never exceeded |r| = 0.067 with Lrmda, and the strongest whole-perturbation neighbors were still weak (max r = 0.172, min r = -0.147). Thus, the Lrmda signature did not phenocopy the reported melanosome biogenesis or RAB32-LRMDA-Commander trafficking context, arguing against treating Lrmda as equivalent to Vps35l here. This contrast should be interpreted cautiously because the literature is largely from human melanocytes or biochemical assays, RAB32 and RAB38 were not assayed, and Lrmda target engagement was weak.

Ptprn2 did not transcriptionally phenocopy its IA-2 paralog Ptprn or the secretory-granule neighbors Cpe, Pcsk2, and Syp: in matched cell types, the Ptprn2 perturbation signature was essentially uncorrelated with these perturbations, even when other secretory-vesicle genes showed stronger self-knockdown. This argues against a shared acute RNA-feedback module in dense-core and synaptic-vesicle secretion downstream of Ptprn2 loss. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Ptprn2 was robustly depleted, but nearby Sh2b1 and Lonp1 signals were only exploratory, and the comparison relies on Wilcoxon score vectors rather than direct vesicle phenotypes.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Bpnt2 in 155 MB Glut showed no hidden BPNT2-like transcriptional module when compared with the available Golgi GAG-sulfation pathway neighbors Hs6st2 and Ust. In the only matched robust context, Bpnt2 and Hs6st2 both had FDR-significant target knockdown, yet their non-target score profiles were essentially uncorrelated and lacked FDR-scale secondary genes. Ust was not detectably engaged. Because Hs6st2 and Ust are upstream PAPS-consuming comparators to BPNT2 PAP clearance, this reads as pathway buffering rather than a strong epistasis result.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Tlr8 perturbation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA produced a selective Cnpy3 up-regulation that was not reproduced by Tlr7, Tlr9, or proximal TLR/NF-kappaB comparators including Tbk1, Chuk, Traf3, Stat1/2, Rel/Relb, Cd14, and Tlr2–5. In this neuronal class, Cnpy3 was the only FDR-significant gene-level effect after Tlr8, despite weak engagement of the comparator perturbations at their own target transcripts; the closest nominal related signal was Tbk1 to Cnpy3, but it lost FDR support. This pattern diverges from a simple interchangeable endosomal TLR7/8/9 MyD88-module expectation.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ski knockdown in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut neurons, and more sparsely in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, produced a transcriptional response that was uncoupled from canonical TGF-beta/BMP/SMAD output. In these responsive classes, representative SMAD-responsive genes Smad7, Id1, Id2, Id3, Junb, and Serpine1 were not adjusted-significant, and perturbations of pathway neighbors Bmpr2, Acvr2a, Smad4, Smad2, and Sin3a showed only weak correlation with the Ski signature. This comparison is acute and transcriptomic, several comparator perturbations had fewer cells, and canonical SMAD targets may be weakly expressed in neurons.

Fcgr4 perturbation in the tested neuronal classes did not elicit a detectable transcriptional response in the proximal Fcγ receptor signaling module: Fcer1g, Syk, Lyn, Hck, and Tyrobp were unchanged wherever measured, with no FDR-supported downstream effects, and broader myeloid or immune-state genes such as Trem2, Csf1r, Cd14, Tlr2, Tlr4, and Itgb2 were also not detectably altered. This suggests that, in this unstimulated neuronal assay, Fcgr4 should not be interpreted as activating or repressing the FcRγ/Syk/Tyrobp pathway, while leaving open non-transcriptional signaling such as FcRγ phosphorylation or Syk activity and not contradicting myeloid-cell biology.

Set showed a weak neuronal Perturb-seq response, and the related factor Setbp1 also produced an FDR-level null signature with no detectable convergence to Set. In this dataset, Setbp1 had 0 FDR<0.05 downstream genes, signatures were uncorrelated with Set, and restricted nearest-neighbor analysis did not reveal a stable perturbation that consistently phenocopied or opposed Set. These results suggest that the reported SETBP1–SET–PP2A relationship from leukemia overexpression contexts did not translate into a shared mouse neuronal loss-of-function RNA phenotype here, with the caveat that target-transcript measurements for both genes were weak.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Smad4 showed weak or absent convergence with nearby TGF/BMP/SMAD/SKI pathway perturbations across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA. Although Bmpr2, Ski, Smad2, Tgfbr2, and Bmpr1b each produced at least one sparse significant signature somewhere in the screen, Smad4 produced none, and full-transcriptome score correlations to 16 comparators remained near zero. This lack of interchangeability is tempered by the caveat that the Smad4 vector itself was weak, so limited target engagement may partly explain the weak correlations.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Lhx4 showed no detectable convergence with its assayed paralog Lhx3 across 22 shared cell classes, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic populations, but this appears to reflect unresolved perturbation engagement rather than true divergence. Both Lhx4 and Lhx3 lacked FDR-supported target-transcript or downstream effects, and their Wilcoxon score vectors were nearly uncorrelated across matched cell types (mean |Pearson r| = 0.033). Even in classes such as 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 155 MB Glut, the lowest adjusted rows remained nonsignificant, so the dataset does not support a coherent shared LIM-homeodomain signature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Clec16a showed a buffered or unresolved transcriptional effect in this Perturb-seq assay: across assayed cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, it produced no transcriptome-wide FDR-significant differential-expression calls and no close signature neighbor, even though core endolysosomal/autophagy perturbations such as Rab7, Rb1cc1, Becn1, Sqstm1, Lamp2, Mtor, and Atg5 generated clear FDR-level responses, with Rab7 especially strong. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut there was only a subthreshold Sod2/Lrrtm1 pattern. Because RNF41 and USP8 were not perturbed, this contrast is to broader pathway neighbors rather than direct CLEC16A complex partners.

Dag1 perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from its expected dystroglycan extracellular-matrix and glycosylation network: its whole-transcriptome signature showed near-zero correlations with Agrn, Lrp4, Musk, Dmd, Snta1, Plec, Sgcd, Sgce, integrins Itga6/Itga7/Itgb1, and glycosylation genes Large1, Fktn, Crppa, Dpm1, and Rxylt1, and Dag1 did not significantly alter these related transcripts. This near-null pattern was observed despite curated physical and pathway links, with the caveat that only mRNA-level score correlations and compensation were assayed, not protein complexes, glycosylation state, or adhesion phenotypes.

Actn4 showed no recurrent downstream RNA program in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq survey: on-target suppression was only weakly detectable and did not survive multiple-testing correction, no transcript reached the reported FDR threshold in any Actn4 contrast, and nominal hits were mostly cell-type singletons rather than a repeated module. Thus, known ACTN4 structural and nuclear functions, including NF-kappaB-related coactivation, were not recapitulated as a steady-state neuronal RNA signature here. Because the dataset lacks morphology, protein localization, synaptic stimulation, and podocytes, non-transcriptional ACTN4 activity cannot be excluded.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Foxg1 showed low signature similarity to SMAD/TGF-beta targets, Kdm5b, and other forkhead-family perturbations in the three cortical glutamatergic classes where its signal was clearest: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut. The best non-self Pearson correlations were only 0.120, 0.083, and 0.070, and in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut the strongest SMAD/Fox/Kdm5b correlation was |r|=0.072. In these classes, Foxg1 responses were weak overall, with only Gtf2ird1 up-regulated at FDR significance in 005, so the low similarity could reflect inadequate Foxg1 perturbation as well as pathway specificity.

Dpysl5 was largely silent in this Perturb-seq dataset: across all 22 Dpysl5-tested cell classes it produced no FDR-supported on-target or downstream RNA effects, and its signed transcriptomic profile showed near-zero correlation with semaphorin/plexin and Gsk3b pathway neighbors including Plxna1, Plxna2, Plxna4, Nrp1, Nrp2, and Plxnd1. In contrast, several of those neighbors had occasional validated hits, including in 191 MB P MY GABA and within the broad 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class. This suggests that CRMP/Sema3A pathway membership did not yield a Dpysl5-like transcriptional signature here, though direct perturbations of other CRMP-family paralogs were not available.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Dnm1l loss produced a cell-type-specific amino-acid/ISR transcriptional program that was not reproduced by knockdown of the related dynamin-family GTPase Dnm1. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Dnm1l depletion was strongest and accompanied by induction of Asns, Ddit3, and Chac1; 155 MB Glut cells showed a smaller but coherent version of the same program, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells shared the stress signature despite only nominal Dnm1l transcript depletion. By contrast, Dnm1 was efficiently depleted, including in these same classes, but yielded no FDR-significant downstream genes, although this transcriptomic comparison may miss acute synaptic-vesicle phenotypes from Dnm1 protein loss.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Dlat perturbation did not produce a shared single-cell transcriptional program with other pyruvate dehydrogenase complex or adjacent mitochondrial carbon-entry genes, despite their functional relatedness. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Dlat knockdown was clearest, median full-signature correlations between Dlat and Pdha1, Pdhb, Pdhx, Dld, Dlst, Ogdh, or Mpc1 were near zero, and only Dlat passed FDR<0.05. In 191 MB P MY GABA, Pdha1 and Ogdh showed FDR-scale self-knockdown whereas Dlat was only nominal, suggesting that weak or sparse downstream differential expression and guide strength may partly explain the low cross-perturbation concordance.

Il1rap perturbation did not detectably engage the annotated IL-1/IL-33/IL-36 receptor to MYD88-IRAK-TRAF6 and NF-kappaB transcriptional program in basal glutamatergic or GABAergic neuronal classes. Canonical inflammatory feedback and cytokine genes, including Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Socs3, Il1a, Il1b, Il6, Tnf, Ccl2, Ccl3, Ccl4, and Cxcl10, were unchanged after multiple-testing correction, indicating that IL1RAP-associated signaling is not constitutively reflected in neuronal mRNA in this assay. The strongest nominal effect was in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, but it was not significant, and the null result could reflect absent ligand stimulation, neuronal context, or weak perturbation.

Mbd5 showed near-zero signature correlation with measured PR-DUB-associated perturbations, including Bap1, Asxl3, and Foxk2, even though biochemical work has linked MBD5 to the BAP1/ASXL complex. In the same perturbation framework, Bap1 produced detectable hits whereas Mbd5 did not, so the expected complex-level convergence in the BAP1/ASXL PR-DUB chromatin deubiquitination pathway was not observed. However, this contrast should be interpreted cautiously because the supporting literature comes largely from human chromatin and cancer-cell systems, and Mbd5 knockdown was weak in mouse neurons.

Ovol2 showed weak and largely uncoupled transcriptomic effects in mature mouse brain Perturb-seq, with no strong nearest neighbor across the library and only very small whole-signature correlations to Zeb1, Zeb2, Ctnnb1, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, Notch1, Notch2, Sec31a, or Fzd3. This pattern was also seen in the measured brain classes, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA where the strongest positive and negative neighbors were still weak, so the canonical OVOL2-ZEB/TGF-β/Notch epithelial-plasticity circuitry was not detected in these mature neurons; however, weak Ovol2 engagement limits how strongly negative pathway inferences can be made.

Nyx showed no transcriptomic convergence in the adult brain screen with the retinal ON-bipolar pathway neighbors Grm6 and Gpr179: all three perturbations were weak, and Nyx versus Grm6 or Gpr179 full-signature correlations remained near zero. This pattern suggests that the canonical retinal ON-bipolar mGluR6-TRPM1 signalplex was uncoupled from adult-brain expression signatures in this dataset, likely because the relevant retinal cell type was absent and the assay did not measure TRPM1 localization or light responses, rather than contradicting retinal literature.

Rgma was transcriptionally uncoupled from canonical RGMA pathway neighbors in this Perturb-seq dataset: its signature was nearly uncorrelated with perturbations of Neo1, Hjv, and BMP-receptor genes including Bmpr2, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Acvr1, Acvr2a, and Acvr2b. This lack of convergence persisted even in cell types where Bmpr2 knockdown was effective, arguing against simple interchangeability with the expected RGMA-NEO1 or BMP/SMAD coreceptor signaling programs. In the nominally most responsive class, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, changes were driven by Pde1b, Scn4b, Ano3, Rasd2, Tbc1d8, and Rgs9, but remained FDR-negative; limited transcriptomic correlation and possibly weak Rgma target engagement remain important caveats.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zbtb11 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced a broad transcriptomic state that did not phenocopy direct complex-I knockdown: across 26 individual Nduf/Ndufaf perturbations, including Ndufc2 and Ndufaf1, each perturbation yielded at most one significant gene, whereas Zbtb11 showed 48. This argues that the Zbtb11 program is not simply a generic response to loss of a single complex-I subunit, but may reflect a Zbtb11-specific regulatory collapse or multi-gene threshold effect, with the caveat that this comparison is limited to one cell class, transcriptomic readouts, and possibly variable protein depletion efficiency.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atf2 showed a selective, non-interchangeable transcriptional effect in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where it produced the strongest supported program with 12 FDR<0.05 genes. In the same class, related AP-1 and JNK/p38-axis perturbations including Jund, Fosl2, Mapk8, Mapk9, Map2k6, and Map3k7 were buffered, and broader CRE/MAPK perturbations such as Creb1, Braf, and Map2k1 were essentially uncorrelated with the Atf2 signature. This same-assay differential-expression contrast is not an epistasis test, and differing knockdown efficiencies of upstream kinases remain a caveat.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Adora2a was largely silent in the 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA class: despite 162 perturbed cells, it showed no significant target engagement and no movement of Scg2, Crem, Pde10a, Bdnf, or Creb1. In the same cells, however, Pde10a perturbation knocked down Pde10a and induced Scg2, with nominal Crem induction, indicating that the adenosine A2A/Golf-cAMP signaling neighborhood was still reportable downstream. Receptor-proximal comparators Drd2, Gnas, and Gnal were also weak or uninformative here, with caveats including only 71 Pde10a cells, Crem at FDR 0.064, and no on-target Gnal row.

Lars2 showed a muted Perturb-seq response, with no transcriptome-wide significant downstream genes across the 23 tested cell types, and this negative profile matched the other screened mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases Fars2 and Rars2. In contrast, stronger mitochondrial perturbations such as Opa1 and Dnm1l produced robust stress responses, including an ISR-like mitochondrial-stress signature, indicating that the Lars2 result reflects buffering within mitochondrial tRNA aminoacylation or weak aaRS target engagement rather than a general inability of the assay to detect mitochondrial dysfunction.

Prlr did not resemble related cytokine-receptor or downstream signaling perturbations: across matched cell types, Prlr signature correlations with available neighbors such as Ghr, Epor, Il6st, Osmr, Stat1, Stat3, Stat5b, Pik3ca, Pik3cb, Mapk1, Mapk9, Ptpn1, and Ptpn11 were essentially near zero, with Pearson r spanning about -0.0937 to 0.1226 and never exceeding |r| = 0.1519 in any cell type. This lack of convergence suggests little active PRLR biology was captured, although many related perturbations were themselves transcriptionally weak, and key pathway partners including Jak2, Stat5a, Cish, Socs1, Socs2, and Socs3 were not perturbation targets.

Nr1h3 perturbation was essentially flat in this dataset, with no transcriptome-wide significant downstream differential-expression hits, and the same lack of response extended to Nr1h2, Rxra, Rxrb, Rxrg, Abca1, and Srebf1. In contrast, Srebf2 knockdown produced a robust sterol signature, with 45 significant hits including reduced Dhcr24, Insig1, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Hmgcr, Cyp51, Sqle, Fdps, Fdft1, and Ldlr. The flat Nr1h3 result therefore does not reflect a global inability to detect lipid transcriptional responses, although guide potency differed and Srebf2 is a pathway neighbor rather than a direct LXR complex member.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pgk1 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons produced a compact, mostly negative transcriptomic program that was not interchangeable with other canonical glycolysis perturbations. In this cell type, Hk1, Gpi1, Pfkm, and Tpi1 knockdowns were on-target but showed no FDR<0.05 overlap with the 22-gene Pgk1 module, whereas Gapdh partially converged on Pnisr, Rsrp1, Ogt, and Ttc14. This suggests a lower-glycolysis or target-specific state rather than a generic glycolysis-loss program, with the caveat that Gapdh depletion itself could not be evaluated because its transcript was not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Scn2a knockdown showed no detectable transcriptional compensation in the two best-engaged cell types, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 145 MH-LH TH Glut. Despite strong depletion of Scn2a, nearby sodium-channel, AIS, and synaptic disease-neighbor genes—including Scn1a, Scn1b, Scn3a, Scn8a, Scn9a, Ank3, Fgf12, Fgf13, Kcnq2, Kcnq3, Dnm1, Snap25, and Stxbp1—were not compensatorily induced, and the signature remained largely target-only rather than converging with related Nav/AIS perturbations. Any compensation may instead occur through protein localization, channel gating, firing changes, or later time points rather than these mRNAs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Ttc19 showed near-zero transcriptomic signature correlation with available complex III and OXPHOS-neighbor perturbations, including Cyc1, Uqcc2, Uqcrfs1, Uqcrc1, Uqcrc2, Uqcrb, Uqcrh, Uqcrq, Coq5, Ndufb10, and Ndufs8, in the strongest responding cell types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. In these contexts, Ttc19 depletion was often the main significant effect, with buffered downstream complex-III transcription and weak or target-only nearest neighbors, arguing that these complex-III perturbations are not interchangeable in this mouse-brain assay; interpretation is limited because library coverage of assembly factors was partial, with Bcs1l, Lyrm7, Uqcc1, and Uqcc3 absent.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Fbn1 showed weak, largely uncoupled transcriptional signatures, with almost no correlation to assayed TGF-beta/BMP receptor or SMAD perturbations, including Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Tgfbr3, Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Acvrl1, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, and Smad1/2/3/4/6/9. Across same-cell comparisons, correlations were near zero overall, and whole-library neighbors were only modest, with all |r|>0.2 confined to 308 CB GABA. This suggests that, in these neurons, Fbn1-linked extracellular TGF-beta/BMP bioavailability did not translate into a canonical cell-intrinsic receptor-SMAD transcriptional response; notably, Fbn1 itself was weak and no Fbn1 genes reached FDR 0.05.

Lrrn3 perturbation did not produce a coherent transcriptional signature for the proposed clathrin-adaptor/endocytosis–EGF/MAPK connection in these adult mouse brain contrasts. Across matched cell-type contrasts, Lrrn3 showed no transcriptome-wide FDR-level differential expression, and predicted partners such as Ap3s1, Vps33a, Ap2a2, Sgip1, Btbd8, Sclt1, Ap2b1, Aak1, Synj1, and Kcnq5 were not significantly induced or repressed. Consistently, perturbing Synj1, Kcnq5, or Sclt1 did not phenocopy Lrrn3. This should be interpreted cautiously because EGF-MAPK activity was not directly assayed and RNA changes may not reflect adaptor activity.

Ndufs7 was an outlier among mitochondrial respiratory-chain Complex I and IP subcomplex perturbations, showing much weaker transcriptomic effects than related NDUF targets such as Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, Ndufs8, and Ndufb8. In this dataset, many other NDUF perturbations achieved significant on-target knockdown in at least one cell type, whereas Ndufs7 had none, and signature-neighbor analysis found no strong positive or negative neighbor. The largest nominally engaged groups, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, still lacked convincing FDR support, and this comparison is based on mRNA recovery and DE-score correlations rather than direct protein depletion or Complex I activity.

Drd5 perturbation was not transcriptionally coupled to canonical dopamine receptor or Gs/olf–adenylyl-cyclase pathway neighbors in this basal single-cell RNA-seq assay. After Drd5 perturbation, measured pathway transcripts including Adcy5, Gnas, Pde10a, Adora2a, and Drd2/3/4 were not significantly changed, and the Drd5 signature was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of Adcy5, Gnal, Gnas, Pde10a, Adora2a, Drd2, Drd3, or Drd4, with the largest absolute correlation only 0.0939 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut for Drd5 versus Adora2a. This null transcriptomic result is indirect for fast GPCR second-messenger biology, and Drd1 plus several downstream dopaminergic markers were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ap2s1 perturbation repeatedly produced a non-target transcriptional module in which Tfrc increased while Srebf2 and SREBP-linked sterol/cholesterol biosynthesis genes, including Insig1, Cyp51, Dhcr24, Fdft1, Hmgcr, and Ldlr, were mostly decreased. This pattern recurred across several neuronal classes, notably 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. The readout is consistent with a slower iron/endosomal-sterol compensation state rather than direct cargo uptake, although no iron uptake, cholesterol, LDLR protein, or surface Tfrc measurements were available.

Tacr1 perturbation showed no adjusted transcriptomic response in the steady-state assay: measured tachykinin-family receptor and ligand transcripts (Tacr2, Tacr3, Tac1, Tac2, Tac4), NK1R-proximal GPCR components (Gnaq, Gna11, Gnas, Arrb1, Arrb2, Plcb1, Prkca, Prkcg), and immediate-early readouts such as Fos, Fosl2, Egr1-3, Jun, Arc, and Npas4 remained FDR-flat. The Tacr1 and Tacr3 signatures were near-orthogonal. This suggests the assayed cells did not capture acute substance-P/NK1R signaling, with the caveat that the readout was steady-state scRNA-seq rather than phospho-PLC, calcium, cAMP, ERK, or receptor-internalization measurements.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Ppargc1a showed no FDR-significant transcriptional signature in this assay, whereas the same mitochondrial-biogenesis neighborhood was robustly accessible through Esrra and Nrf1. Esrra yielded 57 significant genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and Nrf1 yielded 303 significant genes across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA. By contrast, Ppargc1b had only one corrected hit and Ppara, Ppard, Pparg, Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg were silent, indicating a pathway-neighborhood contrast rather than proof of a single linear cascade, especially since Esrra and Nrf1 signatures were not identical and Nrf1 lacked transcript-level knockdown.

Atp6v1e1 showed a much weaker perturbation signature than other V-ATPase complex members in the same dataset, particularly Atp6v0c, Atp6ap1, and Atp6ap2, and also compared with Atp6v0a1, Atp6v1a, and Atp6v1b2. Whereas Atp6v0c had 813 FDR-significant rows and significant on-target depletion in 22 of 23 cell types, Atp6v1e1 had zero FDR-significant rows and zero FDR-significant target-transcript rows. This divergence, in a pathway context of V-ATPase, endolysosomal acidification, and lysosomal mTORC1 sensing, suggests guide efficacy or subunit-specific buffering may dominate the transcriptomic signal; it reflects differential-expression strength rather than matched biochemical measurements of V-ATPase activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rasa2 was largely uncoupled from detectable RAS/MAPK transcriptional outputs in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, despite this being the best-powered thalamic context. With 134 perturbed cells, Rasa2 produced only one nominal, non-FDR hit and did not shift the key response genes Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, or Unc13a. By contrast, Nf1, Braf, Map2k1, and Pten all showed FDR-level responses here; Braf and Map2k1 loss repressed genes that Nf1 loss induced, indicating pathway competence and localizing the negative result to Rasa2 rather than the cell state. This conclusion is limited to transcriptome endpoints, Pten is only PI3K-adjacent, and Rasa2 protein loss was not verified.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Syngap1 showed no FDR-significant transcriptional response in the glutamatergic classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, even though these same cell types were clearly Perturb-seq responsive: NMDAR/PSD neighbors Grin1, Grin2b, and Dlg4, and Ras-mTOR disease-pathway genes Tsc1, Tsc2, Pten, Nf1, and Chd8 produced significant target and/or downstream signatures, in some cases with comparable or fewer cells. Thus, Syngap1 appeared buffered or uncoupled from robust mRNA signatures in these contexts, although this transcriptomic comparison does not directly test electrophysiology, AMPA/NMDA receptor trafficking, or Ras/ERK phosphorylation.

Rel targeting showed no detectable NF-kappaB output in this dataset: measured feedback, inflammatory, and pro-survival transcripts, including Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Bcl2l1, Sod2, Il6, Tnf, and Birc3, remained FDR-silent, and a curated NF-kappaB response set also showed no significant response. This included no detectable c-Rel-associated neuronal survival output in 215 MB Dopa cells. The result suggests no basal c-Rel program was captured here, but interpretation is limited because only a marker-gene panel was inspected, Rel mRNA engagement was weak, and no explicit IL-1beta, glutamate, or inflammatory stimulus was applied.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tnfrsf1b perturbation did not reveal a basal neuronal TNF/NF-kB feedback program across the tested glutamatergic and GABAergic classes, including L5-6 IT, L4-5 IT CTX, L2-3 IT CTX, CA3/CA2-FC DG, L5 ET CTX, Pvalb, Sst, and CNU-HYa HY neurons. Canonical inflammatory/NF-kB transcripts such as Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Tnf, Il6, Traf1, and Birc3 were not regulated, and no downstream gene reached FDR significance. This argues against a hidden inflammatory TNFR2 state in these neurons, although most pathway readouts were RNA-level only and nominal Birc2 or Map3k7 signals were not FDR-significant.

Grm8 perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptional response in the canonical Gi/o–adenylate cyclase–cAMP pathway: transcripts such as Gnai1, Gnao1, Adcy1, Adcy5, Pde4b, Plcb1, Prkcg, and Itpr1 were not FDR-regulated, despite nominal signals including Gnai1 in 046 CTX-CGE GABA and Adcy1 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. This contrasts with other metabotropic-glutamate pathway neighbors that did yield FDR-level rows in the same file, and may reflect weak Grm8 knockdown plus rapid, non-transcriptional second-messenger GPCR signaling.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa
full_finding_text: Oxtr perturbation did not produce adjusted transcriptional changes in canonical oxytocin receptor second-messenger pathway genes in the candidate-responsive classes 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 215 MB Dopa: Gnao1, Gnaq, Plcb1, Itpr1, Prkca, Prkcg, Arrb1, and Arrb2 all remained nonsignificant after correction. This held even in 066, the only FDR<0.05 Oxtr response class, and near-threshold classes also lacked corrected pathway-transcript shifts. The result is limited to steady-state RNA, not ligand-evoked calcium, IP3, PKC activity, ion-channel state, or receptor desensitization.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gucy2c perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from the expected guanylin/GUCY2C/cGMP neighborhood across 22 assayed neuronal classes, with scattered nominal changes only and no FDR-level downstream response. In particular, the endogenous ligand genes Guca2a and Guca2b were essentially null, and other cGMP-related genes such as Gucy1a1, Gucy1b1, Pde9a, Npr2, Pde1a, and the trafficking interactor Lman2 did not show corrected changes. This suggests the screen largely sampled cells without an active ligand-receptor transcriptional circuit, although the cGMP panel was hand-curated and transcriptomics could miss acute cGMP signaling that does not alter mRNA.

Ubr1 showed no reproducible convergence with the available ubiquitin-ligase/proteostasis neighborhood in this dataset. Across assayed cell types, the closest positive and inverse neighbors of the nominal Ubr1 signatures were not recurrent, and the available comparators Trip12, Amfr, and Ube2e2 had near-zero median correlations with Ubr1. Most direct N-recognin or N-end-rule comparators, including Ubr2, Ubr4, Ubr5, Ubr7, and Ate1, were not in the perturbation library, so weak Ubr1 scalar hits cannot be assigned to an N-end-rule module; this is further limited because correlations used only the top 200 Ubr1-ranked genes per cell type and the Ubr1 signatures themselves were not FDR-supported.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ubp1 perturbation showed a cell-type-restricted on-target effect in 155 MB Glut, where Ubp1 mRNA was significantly depleted, but no coherent downstream RNA polymerase II transcriptional program was detected. The strongest non-self nominal changes in this cell type included Ppfia1, Eif4a2, Mccc2, Slc16a11, Luc7l, and Crim1, yet all remained non-significant after correction with FDR=1.0. No non-self gene recurred consistently across cell types, indicating self-knockdown without an FDR-supported non-self cascade in these mature neurons.

Il12b showed near-zero signature correlations in matched neuronal classes and did not phenocopy the expected IL-12/IL-23 receptor neighborhood or nearby JAK/STAT and NF-kB perturbations. Across 22 Il12b-profiled glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, Il12rb1 and Il23r had weak on-target transcript effects, and same-cell-type correlations between Il12b and 18 related perturbations—including Stat1, Stat2, Stat3, Stat4, Stat5b, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, Irf1, and Irf8—remained close to zero, with the largest absolute correlation only r=0.162. This likely reflects the tested neuronal context rather than a contradiction of the known IL12B–IL12RB1 interface.

Ankfy1 did not phenocopy Vps35 or stronger endolysosomal comparator perturbations in this matrix: Ankfy1 showed no FDR-significant hits, and its score-vector correlations with Vps35 never exceeded |r| = 0.068, while Vps35, Ap2s1, Atp6v0c, and Tsc1/Tsc2 produced significant responses. This places partial Ankfy1 loss far from Rab5/PI3P early-endosome trafficking and retromer sorting signatures, and from broader endolysosomal or autophagy-adjacent perturbation space including Wdfy3 and Becn1, though only Vps35 is a direct documented retromer comparator here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Isca2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a self-limited transcriptomic response that was nearly uncorrelated with related mitochondrial perturbations and with its top dataset neighbors: correlations with Aco2, Nfs1, Hspa9, Hspd1, Ndufs1, Ndufs2, Ndufv1, Sdhb, and Uqcrfs1 ranged from about -0.014 to 0.033, and the top positive genome-wide neighbor was only 0.053. This argues that partial Isca2 loss did not recapitulate a generic mitochondrial program in this class, especially since Hspa9 in the same class produced a broad response, although direct ISCA1 and IBA57 comparators were unavailable and the weak Isca2 signature limits dynamic range.

Mphosph9 showed near-zero transcriptomic correlation with the ciliary-neighborhood perturbations available in the library, including Cep83, Cep164, Cep290, Ift88, Tbc1d32, and Kif3b. Because the direct CP110-CEP97-KIF24 branch, including Ccp110, Cep97, Kif24, and Ttbk2, was not perturbed, these comparisons are indirect, and all of the signatures were weak. Overall, the data do not reveal a shared cilium-assembly state with Mphosph9 and suggest that any MPHOSPH9/CP110-CEP97-related signal may be buffered or not detected at the mRNA level.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Uqcrc2 knockdown in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA produced strong on-target depletion but did not yield an FDR-significant non-target oxidative-phosphorylation or mitochondrial complex III mRNA program: transcripts such as Uqcrc1, Uqcrfs1, Uqcrb, Uqcrq, Uqcrh, Uqcc2, Ttc19, Cyc1, Cox7c, Sdha, and Sdhb were not significantly co-regulated, aside from a nominal Uqcrfs1 increase in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA that did not survive FDR correction. Genome-wide Uqcrc2 signatures were also nearly uncorrelated with perturbations of other complex III subunits or assembly factors, although these estimates were based on weak, mostly self-transcript signatures and on mRNA rather than protein or activity readouts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gria3 showed weaker, non-convergent perturbation effects than related excitatory postsynaptic genes, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where it had the strongest nominal on-target signal yet no adjusted downstream differential expression and no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbors. In the same thalamic glutamatergic class, Grin1, Dlg4, and Dlgap4 were more robustly engaged, while Gria1 and Gria2 achieved adjusted target knockdown in other classes where Gria3 did not. This suggests AMPA receptor complex membership did not make Gria3 interchangeable, although guide efficiency, cell counts, and the indirect transcriptomic readout limit the comparison.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Syn3 showed weak engagement in 155 MB Glut: despite the strongest nominal self-depletion in this class, Syn3 had no corrected RNA response, while related presynaptic perturbations Syn1, Syn2, Syp, Snap25, Stx1b, and Syt2 all showed strong self-transcript depletion with equal or fewer perturbed cells. Syn3 also did not show measurable convergence with Syn1 or Syn2 RNA signatures across shared cell types. This suggests a Syn3-specific null within the synaptic vesicle cycle/neurotransmitter release context, although the result could reflect guide inefficiency or low, variable Syn3 expression rather than true biological absence of effect.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lgi1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered at the mRNA level: in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, it did not FDR-significantly change Adam22, Dlg4, Kv1-channel genes (Kcna1, Kcna2, Kcnab1), AMPAR-related genes (Cacng2, Gria1, Gria2), or Grin1. Direct Adam22 depletion was also largely buffered beyond loss of the Adam22 transcript itself, despite significant Adam22 knockdown in two cell types, whereas Grin1 showed a stronger downstream RNA response. This weak Lgi1 effect should be interpreted with the caveat that the perturbation was modest and the assay did not measure extracellular LGI1, synaptic localization, or electrophysiology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Bicra showed a flat perturbation profile in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where several mSWI/SNF/BAF neighbors produced strong signatures. In this same thalamic class, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Smarce1, and Arid1a yielded many differentially expressed genes, with Ptpn3, Reep2, and Prkcd strongly decreased by Smarcb1/Smarcc2/Smarce1 but not by Bicra. This target-specific contrast argues that thalamic neurons were responsive to chromatin-remodeler perturbation, although direct ncBAF partners and the closest paralog, including Brd9, Bicral, and Ss18, were not available for comparison.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nlgn2 loss was largely transcriptionally buffered in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, with almost no FDR-significant downstream mRNA changes beyond the target and, in 155 MB Glut, a lone Pcsk1n hit. By contrast, perturbing the coupled GABA_A receptor subunits Gabra1, Gabrb2, or Gabrg2 was also mostly target-only but occasionally produced sparse secondary responses, including rare Nr4a1, Vgf, or Nalf1 changes, that were absent after Nlgn2 perturbation. This comparison is limited to three receptor subunits and FDR-significant transcript endpoints.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Phf8 showed no reproducible transcriptome-wide differential-expression signal in any assayed neuronal class, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. This was weaker than several same-screen chromatin regulators—Setd1a, Brd4, Kmt2d, Chd8, Kmt2b, Kmt2a, and Kdm5c—which yielded FDR-significant genes, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The contrast argues against a global failure to detect chromatin perturbations, although the comparison is based on counts of FDR-significant targets rather than matched effect sizes, and related genes such as Kdm5b, Kdm6b, and Phf6 were also relatively buffered.

Chrm2 showed a receptor-level null signature, with no significant depletion of its target transcript in any measured cell class, and the paralog Chrm3 was similarly inert. In contrast, several related perturbations in the muscarinic acetylcholine receptor / G alpha (i) signaling neighborhood, including Gnao1, Gnb1, Gnb5, Adcy3, Ache, Gabbr1, and Gabbr2, displayed significant own-transcript depletion in one or more cell classes. This pattern suggests the silence was specific to the assayed muscarinic receptor perturbations rather than a global inability to perturb Gi/o-related pathways, although the comparison is based mainly on own-transcript depletion and may reflect differences in basal expression or guide quality.

Cep83 did not form a shared transcriptomic module with tested distal-appendage or ciliopathy genes in this dataset, despite expected structural links in centriole distal appendage and primary cilium initiation. Its score profiles were nearly uncorrelated with Sclt1, Cep164, Ift88, Ift43, Cplane1, and Bbs5; across 199 comparator signatures, only four isolated FDR hits appeared as singletons. The strongest correlations were still weak, including in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, and in 155 MB Glut Cplane1 and Ift88 showed singleton hits while Cep83 remained flat. These comparisons are limited to guides present in the dataset, and the signatures were generally weak at the FDR level.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ryr2 was buffered and uncoupled from stronger calcium-pathway perturbation responses in this dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ryr2 remained negative despite strong target-engaged signatures for Atp2a2, Grin1, Calm1, and Cacna1g, and in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Ryr2 showed nominal mRNA reduction but no FDR-level downstream genes, whereas Grin2b, Grin2a, Atp2a2, and Calm1 produced stronger responses. This argues against a general failure to read out calcium biology, although the comparators are pathway neighbors rather than RYR2 complex members and their stronger effects coincided with stronger on-target depletion.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Acsl4 perturbation produced a forebrain-enriched SREBP/cholesterol-biosynthesis response, most clearly in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, where Srebf2 was FDR-significantly induced alongside nominal increases in Hmgcs1, Hmgcr, Insig1, Sqle, Msmo1, Dhcr24, Cyp51, Fdft1, and Ldlr. Similar nominal upregulation recurred in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, consistent with lipid-sterol compensation, although most individual sterol genes were only nominal and the panel was interpreted post hoc.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pcyt2 perturbation produced its strongest phenotype in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where a coherent cholesterol/SREBP-like program was induced, including Insig1, Cyp51, Nsdhl, Msmo1, Fdft1, Ldlr, Hmgcr, Idi1, Hmgcs1, Sqle, Dhcr24, Pmvk, Mvd, Dhcr7, and Srebf2. This response appeared more membrane-lipid specific than a generic stress state and links PE-pathway perturbation to a neuron-intrinsic sterol transcriptional module. A weaker upregulation was also seen in 145 MH-LH TH Glut. However, Pcyt2 transcript itself was not depleted in 151, so the data support pathway engagement without quantifying residual PCYT2 activity.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Txndc15 depletion most clearly revealed a sterol/SREBP transcriptional module rather than a ciliary marker program. In 155 MB Glut cells, where Txndc15 was strongly reduced, the non-target FDR-significant genes were cholesterol/SREBP-related: Hmgcs1, Insig1, Ldlr, Srebf2, Fdft1, and Dhcr24. A similar but weaker, directionally coherent response appeared in 191 MB P MY GABA cells, where Insig1 was the only non-target gene reaching FDR significance and other cholesterol genes such as Msmo1, Fdps, Cyp51, Hmgcr, and Sqle were only nominally up.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Pex13 perturbation most clearly elicited an Insig1/SREBF2 cholesterol-biosynthesis response, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where Insig1 was the only downstream gene passing correction and the broader sterol module was most coherent. Across 155 MB Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, the same panel showed nominal upshifts, including Dhcr7, Ldlr, Cyp51, Dhcr24, Fdft1, Lss, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Hmgcr, Srebf2, Sqle, and Sc5d. However, all genes besides Insig1 were nominal, and the sterol panel reflects a literature-guided post hoc view.

Tbc1d32 perturbation did not produce a coordinated transcriptional response in this single-cell RNA readout: canonical Hedgehog/GLI markers including Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Shh, Ihh, Dhh, Hhip, Gpr161, Sufu, Stk36, Kif7, and Cdk20, as well as a ciliary-gene panel including Ahi1, Arl3, Arl13b, Bbs5, Bbs9, Cep290, Cplane1, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, and Rpgrip1l, showed no coordinated or FDR-significant changes. This lack of mRNA response does not exclude structural cilium defects, and target-transcript engagement was weak.

Tbk1 perturbation in basal neuronal cells did not detectably change canonical TBK1–IRF/type-I-interferon or NF-kB transcripts, with Ifit1/2/3, Isg15, Ifnb1, Irf3, Irf7, Stat1, Nfkbia, Cxcl10, Tnf, and Oas1a remaining FDR-silent. In overlapping neuronal cell types, related perturbations of Chuk, Traf3, Irf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Ifnar1, Ifnar2, Map3k7, Tlr4, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Relb, and Stat2 were likewise silent. These data suggest the curated TBK1 antiviral module is stimulation-dependent rather than a standing basal program here, noting this was not a TLR, cGAS-STING, or viral-stimulation assay.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Chp1 knockdown recurrently upregulated an SREBP2/cholesterol-biosynthetic transcriptional module across neuronal classes, with the strongest signal in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and aligned but narrower responses in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and several other glutamatergic and GABAergic types. Induced genes included Insig1, Msmo1, Cyp51, Fdft1, Hmgcr, Dhcr24, Hmgcs1, Ldlr, Srebf2, Sc5d, and Sqle. This sterol program appeared without Gpat4 or Gnpat mRNA induction, and SREBP2 cleavage, lipid pools, and cholesterol flux were not measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Htt perturbation repeatedly upregulated a cholesterol/SREBP-associated sterol module, most clearly in 155 MB Glut, where seven positive genes passed FDR<0.05, including Insig1, Hmgcs1, Fdps, Srebf2, Ldlr, Sqle, and Fdft1. Directionally matching but weaker signals appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, with Msmo1, Dhcr24, Cyp51, and Fasn also contributing. The induced set mapped to cholesterol metabolic and sterol biosynthetic processes, and the module was stronger after Dctn1 or Dync1h1 perturbation; however, only 155 MB Glut showed a broad sterol program at FDR<0.05, while the other classes had small Htt-perturbed counts or only nominal module-level support.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Dync2h1 was essentially inert in this screen: across all Dync2h1-tested cell-type blocks, including 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, it produced no FDR-significant downstream genes. In the same neuronal classes, the paralog Dync1h1 showed a strong recurrent sterol/cholesterol biosynthetic response, with induction of Insig1, Fdps, Fdft1, Msmo1, Cyp51, Hmgcr, Srebf2, Ldlr, Sqle, and Dhcr24. This contrast is used as an internal positive control and does not imply a Dync2h1 sterol mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Srebf2 knockdown collapses a coherent sterol/cholesterol transcriptional module across several neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. Downregulated transcripts include Dhcr24, Insig1, Msmo1, Cyp51, Hmgcs1, Fdft1, Fdps, Hmgcr, Sqle, and Ldlr, with Insig1, Dhcr24, Cyp51, and Msmo1 recurring most strongly. The response is broad in 191 MB P MY GABA, strong in 155 MB Glut, narrower in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and all measurements are mRNA only, without SREBF2 protein, nuclear SREBF2, or cholesterol abundance readouts.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sigmar1 knockdown did not detectably recruit the canonical ER-stress or ER-mitochondria calcium-transfer neighborhood at the RNA level. Across the strongest on-target cell types—005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and 308 CB GABA—UPR and ER-proteostasis transcripts were not coordinately induced, with 0/414 FDR-significant tests, and Hspa5, Atf6, Itpr1, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b perturbation signatures were nearly orthogonal to Sigmar1. This refines rather than disproves the HSPA5/BiP–IP3R–MAM model, given the steady-state CRISPRi assay and missing ITPR3 and TMEM97 perturbations.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Atf6 showed near-null transcriptional effects in basal mouse-brain cells: no downstream transcript reached FDR significance in any profiled cell type, including 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with only nominal signals such as Herpud1 in some contexts. In contrast, the regulated-intramembrane-proteolysis neighbor Srebf2 was significantly depleted in 17/22 shared cell types and repeatedly downregulated a sterol/cholesterol program including Dhcr24, Insig1, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Fdft1, Ldlr, and Acaca. Thus, despite shared S1P/S2P protease logic, Atf6 appeared buffered relative to Srebf2; however, Mbtps1, Mbtps2, and Scap were not perturbed, so the comparison is between the terminal transcription factors rather than the shared proteases.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Dll1 perturbation produced no conventionally significant transcriptome-wide hits after multiple-testing correction and did not share a transcriptomic program with assayed Notch-pathway neighbors. In contrast, Mib1, a Notch-ligand trafficking neighbor, induced a strong sterol/cholesterol module across several neuronal populations, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with genes such as Insig1, Dhcr24, Fdft1, Msmo1, Ldlr, Hmgcs1, Hmgcr, Srebf2, Fdps, and Nsdhl. This divergence suggests Mib1 has a robust neuronally restricted output that Dll1 does not phenocopy here, although the sterol module should not be assumed to be canonical Notch output without direct rescue or pathway assays.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Far1 knockdown repeatedly produced a nominal SREBP2/cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptional response, with Far1 down and sterol genes up, most clearly in 155 MB Glut and also in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. Recurrently induced genes included Insig1, Srebf2, Hmgcs1, Dhcr24, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Fdft1, Cyp51, Ldlr, and Tecr. The pattern aligned with Marchf6 loss and opposed Srebf2 loss, whereas Agps and Pex14 were not equivalent in this assay. Most sterol-gene changes were nominal rather than FDR-significant, and plasmalogens and cholesterol were not measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Tubb3 knockdown was largely buffered and remained almost self-only across 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, with a highly restricted FDR-level response; in 191 MB P MY GABA, Rnf31 was the only non-target hit despite strong Tubb3 depletion. In contrast, the microtubule-pathway neighbor Dync1h1 induced a broad sterol/SREBF program, including Insig1, Fdps, Msmo1, Cyp51, Hmgcr, Srebf2, Ldlr, Sqle, and Dhcr24, and in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut this sterol response appeared despite subthreshold Dync1h1 self-knockdown.

Acvr2b perturbation in 23 profiled neuronal classes produced no FDR-supported canonical activin/NODAL/BMP receptor-SMAD transcriptional response. Although Acvr2b transcripts trended downward in most cell types, no multiple-testing-supported on-target knockdown was detected, and curated pathway genes spanning receptors, SMADs, inhibitory SMADs, IDs, ligands, and regulators, including Acvr2a, Acvr1b, Acvr1c, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, Smad6, Smad7, Id1-Id4, Nodal, Ski, Skil, and Tgif1, were unchanged. This suggests no detectable basal pathway readout in this assay, while incomplete knockdown and the lack of phospho-SMAD or ligand-secretion measurements remain important caveats.

Ndufs4 perturbation did not induce a canonical mitochondrial integrated-stress, UPRmt, mtDNA-encoded complex-I, reactive-glial, or inflammatory marker program: manually selected markers such as Atf4, Ddit3, Ddit4, Trib3, Asns, Hspd1, Hspe1, Clpp, Lonp1, Fgf21, Gdf15, Lcn2, Gfap, C1qa, Aif1, Tnf, Il1b, and mt-Nd1/2/4/5/6 showed no FDR-significant induction, and genome-wide differential expression found no multiple-testing-significant genes in any tested cell type. This contrasts directionally with chronic Ndufs4-null Leigh models dominated by regional inflammation, but the negative result is limited by partial target engagement, manual marker selection, and the difficulty of interpreting glial transcripts in neuronal nuclei.

Lrp2 perturbation was uncoupled from the expected SHH/BMP/retinoid and LDL-receptor-family transcript readouts in this dataset: core markers including Gli1/2/3, Ptch1/2, Smo, Shh, Bmp4/7, Bmpr1a/b/2, Smad1/4/9, Rarb, Stra6, Apoe, Lrp1, Lrp8, Vldlr, Sorl1, and Lrpap1 showed no adjusted response. Cell-type-specific signals were also weak: in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut the nominal patterns remained non-significant, and in 308 CB GABA Apoe was only nominal. This is limited to transcript measurements; ligand trafficking, SMAD phosphorylation, GLI activity, and SHH localization were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Rab7 perturbation induced a sterol and lysosomal cholesterol response, with upregulation of Insig1, Msmo1, Cyp51, Fdft1, Hmgcs1, Sqle, Dhcr24, and Ldlr in the most responsive neurons, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, and more sparsely in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. This sterol-associated module accompanied the Rab7 lysosomal response and suggests cholesterol trafficking stress in responsive neurons, although the dataset measured biosynthetic transcripts rather than LDL uptake, NPC1 flux, or free cholesterol.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tsc2 perturbation in non-cerebellar neurons converged on an up-regulated sterol/cholesterol and lysosomal transcriptional module, most strongly in 155 MB Glut and also in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Recurrent induced genes included Cyp51, Msmo1, Ldlr, Insig1, Fdft1, Nsdhl, Hmgcr, Dhcr7, Sqle, Atp6v0b, Dpp7, Lamp2, Grn, and Pik3r1/Pik3r3. The 155 MB Glut response was largest and also contained a smaller down-regulated neuronal gene set, while the other classes reused the same positive module at smaller scale. This pattern is consistent with an mTORC1-linked metabolic transcriptional arm, but cholesterol abundance and mTORC1 phosphorylation were not measured.

Nr1h3 perturbation in neuronal Glut/GABA classes did not engage canonical LXRα/RXR transcriptional output: Abca1, Abcg1, Apoe and sterol or lipogenic genes including Srebf1, Srebf2, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Dhcr24, Msmo1, Sqle, Fdps, and Fdft1 were detectable but not significantly regulated. This uncoupling also extended to LXR-linked lipogenesis, with no significant output after Nr1h3 or Srebf1 perturbation. A key caveat is that the experiment used genetic perturbation without exogenous LXR ligand, and all assayed Nr1h3 cell classes were neuronal rather than astrocytic or microglial.

Rfx3 targeting did not detectably induce or repress the canonical RFX3 cilium program in the assayed neuronal signatures. Across all 22 Rfx3-tested Glut/GABA groups, the on-target transcript was not significantly depleted, no gene reached FDR < 0.10, and measured ciliary and Hedgehog-linked markers including Foxj1, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Dync2i1, Kif3b, Bbs5, Bbs9, Cep164, Cep290, Ttc21b, Ttc8, Smo, Ptch1, Gli2, and Gli3 remained unchanged after correction, with no strong Rfx7 phenocopy or convergence with nearby ciliary perturbations. A caveat is that these were brain, not ependymal, cell groups, target engagement was weak, and the analysis relied on measured transcripts rather than direct cilia phenotypes.

Zfp398 showed no convergence with the TGF/BMP-SMAD and EP300/CBP module in adult mouse brain Perturb-seq: its score vectors were nearly orthogonal to Smad1/2/3/4/6/9, TGF/BMP receptors including Acvr1, Acvr2a/b, Acvrl1, Tgfbr1/2/3, Bmpr1a/1b/2, and Ep300/Crebbp, with the largest Smad-family |r| 0.0956 and largest Ep300/Crebbp |r| 0.0532. This contrasts with human PSC reports linking ZNF398 to SMAD3/EP300 at active TGF-beta targets, but here the module may have been absent, inactive, or missed because Zfp398 perturbation was weak and comparator transcripts were not strongly depleted in every cell type, including 054 CNU-MGE GABA.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Med15 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons did not phenocopy Srebf2, even though MED15 is a known SREBP cofactor. In the same cells, Srebf2 perturbation robustly lowered the SREBP2 sterol-biosynthesis program, including Dhcr24, Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Cyp51, and Sqle, whereas these genes were not significant after Med15 perturbation and the overall signatures were nearly uncorrelated. This suggests the neuronal Med15 program is not simply the canonical SREBP2 cholesterol module, although weak Med15 transcript-level engagement could have masked a lipid effect and does not exclude MED15-SREBP coupling in other cells or states.

Chuk perturbation showed no coherent basal NF-κB or inflammatory transcript response: across a manually selected panel including Nfkbia, Nfkbib, Tnfaip3, Birc2, Birc3, Ccl2, Ccl5, Cxcl10, Il6, Tnf, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Relb, Jun, Fos, Egr1, and Ifit1/Isg15, there was no coordinated suppression or induction, and no detectable basal Nfkb2/Relb-axis signal. This suggests that in this unstimulated neuronal dataset, CHUK depletion is insufficient to reveal the canonical cytokine/TLR/TNFR NF-κB program, while activity-dependent or cytokine-induced outputs could have been missed.

Smad1 showed weak or absent transcriptional convergence with canonical BMP/TGF-family neighbors, including Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, Smad6, Smad9, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Acvrl1, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Tgfbr3, and the corepressor Ski. Most comparator perturbations were themselves sparse, with few or no FDR-significant genes, and Smad1 score correlations were small, peaking at Bmpr1b in 308 CB GABA (r=0.202) and Smad9 (r=0.138). In 052 Pvalb Gaba, there was no robust Smad1-dependent basal RNA response, and the absence of convergence could reflect weak guide efficacy; Smad5 was not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Elp1 perturbation induced an ATF4-like amino-acid-starvation program in selected neuronal classes, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Atf4, Ddit3, Chac1, Sesn2, Asns, Cars, Mars1, Lars, Aars, Slc7a5, Slc1a4, Slc3a2, Slc38a2, Shmt2, Mthfd2, Aldh1l2, and Herpud1 were upregulated, with recurrent Srsf5 and Ddx17 downregulation. Smaller but directionally similar responses appeared in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, consistent with Elongator-dependent tRNA anticodon modification stress, although tRNA U34 modification, translation speed, ATF4 protein, and ELP1 protein loss were not directly measured.

Tgfbr3 perturbation produced transcriptomic signatures that were essentially orthogonal to Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Bmpr2, activin/BMP receptor, and Smad perturbations in matched neuronal cell types, with across-cell-type mean correlations of 0.015 to Tgfbr1, 0.014 to Tgfbr2, and 0.007 to Bmpr2, and no related comparator exceeding |r| = 0.168 in any Tgfbr3 cell type. This argues against treating Tgfbr3 as an interchangeable proxy for catalytic TGF-beta/BMP receptors or SMAD nodes here, although several related perturbations had weak on-target rows, so the contrast is strongest for Bmpr2 and for the absence of any family-wide convergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Marchf6 knockdown elicited a predominantly upregulated sterol/SREBP transcriptional module, most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, with weaker but directionally coherent responses in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. Increased transcripts included Hmgcr, Cyp51, Dhcr24, Sqle, Msmo1, Insig1, and Srebf2-pathway genes, while Srebf2 perturbation opposed this module, Amfr did not phenocopy it, and canonical UPR markers such as Hspa5, Xbp1, and Herpud1 were not induced. Overall, the pattern fits homeostatic feedback remodeling of cholesterol biosynthesis after loss of an ER ubiquitin ligase rather than a direct transcription-factor role for Marchf6, although sterol intermediates and substrate proteins were not measured.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Acvr1 loss in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons was not transcriptomically interchangeable with Bmpr2 loss or with perturbation of nearby BMP/TGF-beta receptor-SMAD genes. Although Bmpr2 showed strong self-depletion in both glutamatergic cell types, the Acvr1–Bmpr2 differential-expression score correlations were near zero (r=0.026 and r=0.024), and correlations with Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Acvrl1, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Smad1/2/3/4/6/9, and Tgfbr1/2/3 also remained near zero. This divergence was measured from mRNA differential-expression scores rather than receptor phosphorylation or ligand-response assays.

Bmpr1a showed weak or absent convergence with related BMP/TGF receptor and SMAD perturbations in this dataset. Across Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Acvrl1, Tgfbr1/2/3, and Smad1/2/3/4/6/9, transcriptomic score correlations with Bmpr1a were near zero, with the largest reported correlation only r = 0.093, despite these genes forming a strongly connected BMP receptor–SMAD module. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut, Bmpr1a also lacked on-target depletion or downstream FDR hits, whereas Bmpr2 showed self-depletion; however, most related perturbations were themselves weak and these comparisons reflect score correlations rather than direct receptor activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Micu1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a buffered, largely null transcriptional phenotype: although Micu1 itself was the top nominal hit, no downstream genes reached FDR significance, and its full-transcriptome profile was near-zero correlated with Atp2a2, Itpr1, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b perturbations (Pearson about -0.052 to 0.047). In the same cells, Atp2a2 produced a strong ER calcium/stress-like response with genes including Ddit3, Chac1, Xbp1, Hspa5, Herpud1, and Asns, while Grin1/Grin2a/Grin2b also showed stronger detectable responses. This contrast suggests the assay could detect calcium-associated programs, but Micu1’s mitochondrial uniporter gating effect remained compartmentally distinct, with the caveat that these comparators affect different Ca2+ compartments and had different knockdown strengths.

Afg3l2 perturbation did not induce a detectable mRNA-level mitochondrial stress, UPR-like, OPA1-processing, or fission/fusion program. Canonical stress markers including Atf4, Ddit3, Ddit4, Trib3, Chac1, Dele1, Hspa9, Hspd1, Hspe1, Lonp1, Clpp, and Hspa5, as well as Opa1, Oma1, Yme1l1, Dnm1l, Mff, Fis1, Mfn1, Mfn2, Tomm20, and Tomm40, showed no FDR-significant response. This suggests the transcriptome did not report a compensatory module, while not ruling out altered cleavage or abundance of OPA1, EMRE, or other mitochondrial substrates.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Npy1r perturbation showed no FDR-supported transcriptional response in the canonical Gi/o-cAMP pathway or immediate-early reporters across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. Genes spanning Gnai1/2/3, Gnao1, Adcy1/3/5/6/8, Prkaca, Prkacb, Creb1, Fos, Egr1, Arc, and Junb were not corrected differentially expressed, suggesting a transcript-level readout mismatch rather than absence of receptor signaling, since cAMP, calcium, phosphorylation, and synaptic outputs were not measured.

Ager perturbation showed no adjusted-significant downstream transcriptomic response, with canonical RAGE inflammatory effector programs remaining uncoupled: NF-kappaB/MAPK components such as Nfkbia, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rela, Rel, Relb, Mapk1, Mapk3, and Traf6, as well as cytokine and Toll-like receptor genes including Tnf, Il1b, Il6, Ccl2, Cxcl10, Myd88, Tlr2, Tlr4, and Tlr9, were not detectably activated or repressed. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Nfkb1 was the strongest nominal NF-kappaB-family signal, but it remained non-significant after adjustment, consistent with the caveat that RAGE signaling is typically ligand induced and this unstimulated dataset did not assay AGE, S100, HMGB1, or amyloid-beta stimulation or show Ager target engagement.

Il6ra perturbation in 22 tested Glut/GABA neuronal classes did not recruit a detectable IL-6 receptor/IL6ST-JAK-STAT-MAPK transcriptional program: genome-wide summaries showed no multiple-testing-significant response, and a curated 23-gene set including Il6ra, Il6st, Osmr, Jak1/2, Tyk2, Stat1/3, Socs1/3, Nfkb1, Mapk1, Akt3, Ptpn11, Irf1/9, Fos, Jun, Jund, and Pik3c/r genes had no FDR-supported changes. This pattern is consistent with a low-receptor, unstimulated state rather than active IL-6 signaling, although only RNA-level changes were assessed and phosphorylation or ligand-induced activity was not measured.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Pex13 shows a buffered transcriptomic relationship with its docking-complex partner Pex14: in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Pex14 achieved strong FDR-level target knockdown, yet Pex14 itself was the only FDR-significant gene and there was no corrected non-target response. Across these neurons, the main shared downstream pattern with Pex13 was only a nominal cholesterol/SREBF-associated upshift, including genes such as Dhcr24, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Insig1, Cyp51, and Srebf2, with the strongest corrected Pex13 signal centered on Insig1 in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp2a2 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced the strongest transcriptional response, marked by induction of ER-stress/UPR genes including Ddit3, Xbp1, Herpud1, Hspa5, Chac1, Asns, and Creld2 together with integrated-stress and amino-acid transport/metabolism genes such as Shmt2, Slc38a2, Slc38a1, Slc1a4, Slc7a5, and tRNA-synthetase programs, while selected neuronal transcripts including Slc17a7 and Prkcd were reduced. Similar stress-pathway induction appeared in some other responsive classes, but this thalamic class showed the dominant footprint; the data are mRNA-only and do not directly measure ER calcium, XBP1 splicing, CHOP protein, or cell death.
