Irf5 perturbation across all matched Irf5-assayed neuronal groups was uncoupled from canonical TLR-MyD88, cytokine, type-I-interferon, and IRF8-Irf5 reactive microglial programs: representative genes including Irf1, Irf7, Irf8, Irf9, Stat1, Stat2, Isg15, Ifit1-3, Ccl2, Ccl5, Cxcl10, Tnf, Il1b, Il6, Il12b, and Nfkbia did not move as a corrected set, with only Stat2 and Irf9 nominally significant and both FDR 1.0. Across the 22 shared Glut/GABA groups, transcriptome-wide score correlations with related perturbations such as Irf7, Irf8, Stat1, Ifnar2, Tlr3, Tlr7, Tlr8, and Nfkb1 were near zero, although these comparator perturbations may also be weak in these neuronal groups.

Irf2 perturbation did not produce a coherent interferon-stimulated gene response in this basal neuronal Perturb-seq dataset: across a hand-curated 29-gene IFN/ISG panel and 22 Irf2 signatures, 0 of 637 rows reached FDR < 0.05, with only 3 nominal p < 0.05. The expected IFN/ISG module, including Stat1, Stat2, Irf1, Irf7, Irf9, Isg15, Usp18, Ifit1-3, Ifitm1-3, Oasl1/2, Rsad2, Ddx58, Ifih1, Bst2, Zbp1, Tlr3, and Tlr7, stayed flat, including in 054 CNU-MGE GABA. Because on-target Irf2 RNA depletion was not demonstrated and the test was limited to basal neuronal signatures, this should be interpreted as a buffered or uncoupled response rather than evidence against IRF2 biology in neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp1a3 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons lowered Atp2a2 mRNA, but it did not phenocopy direct Atp2a2 perturbation: the Atp2a2-linked stress module, including Xbp1, Hspa5, Ddit3, Chac1, Cars, Asns, Herpud1, Shmt2, and Vegfa, was induced only when Atp2a2 itself was targeted. Instead, the Atp1a3 response showed broader Na,K-ATPase and cation-homeostasis remodeling, with Atp2b1, Kcnj9, Kcnj3, Kcna4, and Cacna1d down and Grin2a and Scn1b up. This comparison is limited to mRNA in one thalamic cell class, without protein or ER Ca2+ measurements.

Smad9 showed buffered or uncoupled effects relative to BMP/TGF-beta pathway neighbors in this neuronal Perturb-seq dataset. Compared with Bmpr2, Smad2, Tgfbr2, Bmpr1b, Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Bmpr1a, Smad1, Smad3, Smad4, Smad6, and Tgfbr1, Smad9 signatures were essentially uncorrelated, with near-zero score-vector correlations, while several neighbors produced stronger readouts and Bmpr2 showed significant on-target depletion in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut. In 155 MB Glut, Smad9 had the strongest nominal on-target decrease yet no FDR-significant on-target or downstream genes; in 308 CB GABA, a modest module appeared without FDR-significant genes or on-target depletion. These divergences may reflect guide efficacy or knockdown differences, and Smad5 and Smad7 were not assayed as comparators.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Atp2c1 loss did not reproduce the ER-stress and unfolded protein response program seen with Atp2a2 depletion in the same glutamatergic cell types, notably 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In thalamic glutamatergic cells, Atp2a2 knockdown induced UPR markers including Ddit3, Chac1, Xbp1, Herpud1, Hspa5, Cars, and Asns, whereas Atp2c1 left these markers unchanged; midbrain glutamatergic cells showed a smaller but still significant Atp2a2 stress response that was likewise absent after Atp2c1 perturbation. This contrast is tempered by stronger Atp2a2 than Atp2c1 knockdown, so the difference may reflect both target identity and depletion depth.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Stim1 did not phenocopy Atp2a2 in the two neuronal classes where Stim1 was best engaged, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these same cells, Atp2a2 loss produced a strong ER-stress-like and unfolded protein response program, with induction of Ddit3, Chac1, Xbp1, Hspa5, Asns, Herpud1, Cars, and Shmt2, whereas Stim1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Atp2a2 and lacked those markers. This contrast is transcriptional and does not address whether STIM1 and ATP2A2 share acute calcium-flux phenotypes after stimulation.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Hmgcr knockdown in 191 MB P MY GABA did not phenocopy Srebf2 loss: despite nominal Hmgcr depletion, it did not produce the strong repression of sterol genes seen with Srebf2 knockdown, including Msmo1, Fdft1, Fdps, Hmgcs1, Sqle, Lss, and Ldlr. This divergent result indicates that the assay could measure an SREBP-regulated cholesterol biosynthesis module in this cell class, so the weak Hmgcr phenotype is unlikely to reflect simple failure to capture cholesterol transcripts, although Srebf2 perturbation was more strongly engaged than Hmgcr perturbation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nfic in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class showed a prominent Bambi up-regulation that did not resemble a generic BMP/TGF-beta receptor-Smad knockdown state. In this same cell type, perturbations of Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, Smad1, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, Tgfbr1, and Tgfbr2 had near-zero whole-signature correlations with the Nfic response, ranging from -0.043 to 0.045, and none induced Bambi. This supports an Nfic-specific Bambi signal, with the caveat that comparator knockdown strength was not verified at the protein level and receptor-Smad perturbations may act on different ligand arms or time scales.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Elp2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells preferentially activated an ATF4/Ddit3-skewed integrated stress response rather than a uniform ER-chaperone UPR transcriptome. Atf4, Ddit3, Trib3, Asns, Chac1, and amino-acid transporter genes including Slc7a5, Slc3a2, Slc38a2, Slc1a4, and Slc7a1 were significantly induced, whereas Hspa5, Dnajb9, and Xbp1 were not significantly induced in the same cells. This stress call is tempered because Xbp1 splicing and ATF4 translation are not captured by these mRNA measurements, and single-cell dropout may weaken chaperone-gene detection.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ryr3 perturbation was transcriptionally null across the assayed glutamatergic classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, with no FDR-significant response genes despite detectable on-target depletion in related calcium-signaling perturbations. In the same dataset, the ER Ca2+ release comparators Ryr2 and Itpr1 were also sparse or nearly null, whereas Atp2a2, an ER Ca2+ pump rather than a RYR paralog, triggered a strong ER-stress/UPR-like program marked by Ddit3, Xbp1, Herpud1, Hspa5, Asns, and Chac1, indicating pathway-level non-equivalence rather than interchangeable ER calcium regulation.

Cd14 perturbation in these basal neuronal cultures did not engage the expected CD14/TLR inflammatory program: canonical cytokine and chemokine genes such as Tnf, Il1b, Il6, Ccl2, Cxcl10, and Ifnb1 were not detectably induced, and NF-kappaB feedback and interferon-response transcripts including Nfkbia, Nfkbib, Stat1, Irf1, Irf7, Ifit1, Ifit2, Ifit3, Isg15, and Oas1a remained largely flat, with only weak nominal fluctuations. This is consistent with no basal Cd14/Tlr2/Tlr4/Nfkb1 convergence in an unstimulated setting, with the caveat that the experiment tested loss of function under basal conditions rather than acute LPS or lipoteichoic-acid stimulation of immune cells.

Pcsk5 perturbation showed no FDR-significant transcriptional output for annotated PCSK5-linked pathways in this screen: neurotrophin genes and receptors such as Bdnf, Ngf, Ntf3, Ngfr, Ntrk1, Ntrk2, Ntrk3, and Sort1, TGF/BMP-SMAD genes including Gdf11, Bmp2/4/7, Tgfb1/2/3, Acvr1, Bmpr1a/b, Bmpr2, and Smad1/2/3/4/5/9, and lipase-processing genes Lpl, Lipc, Gpihbp1, and Lmf1 were unchanged. In the only responsive cell type, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, Ssb decreased while Pcsk5 itself remained nonsignificant and pathway signatures were uncorrelated. These transcript sets are proxies and do not measure immature versus mature substrate proteins.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp2b2 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not reproduce the ER Ca2+ depletion/integrated stress-like program seen with Atp2a2 knockdown in the same class. Whereas Atp2a2 loss was associated with increased Ddit3, Hspa5, Xbp1, Chac1, Asns, Slc7a5, Sesn2, and Trib3, Atp2b2 knockdown left these stress markers far from significance. This separates plasma-membrane PMCA2 perturbation from ER SERCA2 depletion at the scRNA phenotype level, although the stress designation is inferred from marker genes rather than protein or ER-calcium measurements.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Opa1 knockdown in neurons repeatedly induced an amino-acid, one-carbon, and stress-response program, with upregulation of Asns, Mars1, Cars, Shmt2, Chac1, Ddit3, Aldh1l2, Slc7a5, Aars, Herpud1, Mthfd2, Eprs, Slc3a2, Xpot, and Gpt2 across 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. The pattern resembles mitochondrial integrated-stress signaling and showed nearest-neighbor convergence with Hspa9 and Lonp1 perturbations, but Atf4, Dele1, and Hri activity were not measured directly, so the ISR assignment is inferred from transcript identity; some classes also showed weak or non-significant on-target engagement or only partial mt-RNA involvement.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Il10rb perturbation showed no detectable JAK/STAT or interferon-stimulated RNA response across all 22 assayed neuronal subclasses, including glutamatergic and GABAergic types such as L5-6 IT Glut, Pvalb Gaba, Sst Gaba, and CB GABA. Canonical readouts remained unchanged, with Stat1, Stat2, Stat3, Socs3, Irf1/7/9, Ifit1/2/3, Isg15, Usp18, Oas1a, Oasl2, Gbp2, Gbp7, and Cxcl10 all not significant. This null result reflects steady-state RNA in guide-bearing cells and does not test acute IL-10 or IFN-lambda stimulation.

Ifnar2 loss in 22 Glut/GABA neuronal groups did not collapse the canonical type-I-interferon IFNAR/JAK-STAT/ISG module: across 462 Ifnar2 measurements for 21 interferon-response markers, none reached FDR significance, and only Stat2 in 053 Sst Gaba was nominally significant with FDR 1.0. Genes expected to track IFNAR signaling, including Stat1, Stat2, Irf7, Irf9, Isg15, Ifit1/2/3, Oas1a/Oas1g/Oasl2, Usp18, Rsad2, Cxcl10, Ifi44/Ifi44l, and Bst2, remained statistically flat, although the marker set was targeted and low basal ISG expression in neuronal nuclei may have limited power.

Sp110 perturbation showed no FDR-significant transcriptional change in an interferon and antigen-presentation effector module, with near-zero similarity to related perturbations. Across basal brain neuronal classes, including 052 Pvalb Gaba where Stat1 had the largest absolute panel score, the IFN/MHC panel remained silent: Stat1/2, Irf1/7/9, Isg15, Ifit1/2/3, Oas1a/Oas2, Psmb8/9, Tap1/2, B2m, and H2-K1/H2-D1/H2-Ab1/H2-Eb1 were not detectably remodeled. This negative result was obtained under unchallenged conditions with weak Sp110 engagement and does not test IFN- or pathogen-stimulated macrophages.

Tlr9 perturbation in the neuronal screen did not engage the canonical TLR9/MyD88/NF-kB/IRF innate-signaling module: across 22 profiled glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal contrasts, transcripts representing proximal adaptors and downstream branches, including Myd88, Traf6, Nfkb1, Nfkbia, Rela, Irf3, Irf7, Stat1, Isg15, Oas1a, Cxcl10, Ifnb1, Tnf, Il6, Il1b, Tbk1, and Unc93b1, were not significantly responsive. This pattern suggests pathway silence rather than a muted inflammatory program, although several cytokines were likely near the neuronal detection floor, so their non-response is best interpreted alongside the absent Tlr9 target-transcript effect and generally weak related TLR perturbation signals.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tmem126a did not elicit the mitochondrial integrated-stress-response-like amino-acid/CHOP program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, or 191 MB P MY GABA cells: markers such as Asns, Ddit3, Chac1, Mars1, Shmt2, Slc7a5, and Cars were silent after Tmem126a perturbation, whereas Opa1, Dnm1l, and Hspa9 induced them in the same assay. This suggests the flat Tmem126a profile is not a dataset-wide inability to detect mitochondrial phenotypes, although weak on-target Tmem126a mRNA reduction limits inference about its intrinsic stress potency relative to those comparators.

Lrrfip1 perturbation did not produce a coherent IFN/TNF/NF-kappaB marker response in these mostly neuronal basal profiles: no multiple-testing-significant gene-level changes were detected, and representative interferon-stimulated, TNF, and NF-kappaB-responsive transcripts such as Ifit1/2/3, Ifitm3, Isg15, Irf7, Irf9, Stat1, Stat2, Ccl5, Cxcl10, Tnf, Il6, and Nfkbia were not coherently altered across the surveyed mouse-brain cell classes. This suggests LRRFIP1-linked inflammatory signaling was uncoupled or not detected here, with the caveat that the assay lacked dsDNA, dsRNA, LPS, or infection challenge, target depletion was weak, and cytokine secretion and phospho-signaling were not measured.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Irf7 perturbation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA neurons produced a specific decrease in Grb10, and this response was not reproduced in the same cell type by related IFNAR, IRF, STAT, TLR, NF-kappaB, or Traf3 perturbations, including Ifnar1/2, Irf1/2/3/5/8/9, Stat1/2/3, Tlr3/7/9, Nfkb1, Rel, and Relb. The strongest comparator was only nominal, with Tlr9 showing a weak negative effect, so the contrast is best read as no detected convergence rather than proof of pathway exclusion, especially given small sample sizes and generally weak target-transcript engagement.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sqstm1 perturbation in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced transcriptomic signatures that were not interchangeable with related autophagy, lysosomal, mTORC1/TSC, Nrf2/NF-kB, or ALS/FTD perturbations, including Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Lamp2, Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1, Tsc2, Tbk1, Vcp, and Camta1. In these three strongest on-target cell types, same-cell Wilcoxon score correlations never exceeded |r|=0.073, and nearest-neighbor searches found no strong match or inverse match. This contrast suggests partial p62 loss is a weak proxy for those modules here, although many comparator perturbations had weaker on-target support than Sqstm1.

Tlr3 did not phenocopy TLR receptor paralogs or proximal IRF/NF-kB pathway neighbors in these basal Perturb-seq profiles: across 310 matched same-cell-type comparisons, correlations with Tlr4, Tlr7, Tlr8, Tlr9, Traf3, Tbk1, Irf3, Irf7, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, Chuk, Map3k7, and Ifih1 stayed near zero. This uncoupling persisted in 054 CNU-MGE GABA interneurons, where Tlr8 and Irf7 each showed a one-gene FDR signal but Tlr3 remained weak and uncorrelated. Because many pathway-neighbor perturbations also had weak or zero-gene FDR signatures, these results reflect similarity of weak basal transcriptional effects rather than ligand-induced signaling capacity.

Uqcc2, a mitochondrial complex III/CYTB biogenesis factor, showed a weak and divergent response in the measured mouse-brain neuron classes and did not trigger a coherent mitochondrial integrated stress response program. Across a 17-gene ATF4/ISR and mitochondrial chaperone/protease panel, transcripts including Atf4, Asns, Ddit3, Ddit4, Trib3, Mthfd2, Gdf15, Fgf21, Hspd1, Hspe1, Hspa5, Hspa9, Clpp, Lonp1, Dele1, Oma1, and Yme1l1 were not consistently induced. Even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, which had the strongest nominal Uqcc2 self-depletion, there were no FDR-significant hits, although this comparison is indirect because prior literature used stronger mitochondrial stressors and cultured cells rather than partial acute perturbation in postmitotic mouse brain neurons.

Trappc6b perturbation showed a weak, directionally consistent upregulation of a sterol/SREBP-associated module rather than a canonical vesicle-tethering program, with recurrent signals involving Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Fdft1, and Srebf2 across nominal signatures. This pattern suggests cholesterol homeostasis as an exploratory follow-up readout after TRAPP perturbation, but the effect was buffered overall: most member genes did not survive cross-gene meta-analysis FDR, and no single cell type showed a corrected sterol response.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Qrich1 perturbation in unstressed mouse brain cells was uncoupled from a simple canonical ER-stress or integrated stress response transcriptome: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, it did not FDR-induce Atf4, Atf6, Ddit3, Xbp1, Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Herpud1, Pdia4, Ppp1r15a, Trib3, or related marker RNAs. Atf6 and Nfe2l2 perturbations also showed no FDR-significant genes in this panel, and weaker stress-proteostasis comparators did not reproduce the breadth of the Qrich1 response, so epistasis conclusions are limited by weak target engagement and the basal, non-ER-stressed context.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Chchd10 loss did not phenocopy the mitochondrial integrated stress response seen with Opa1 or Dnm1l perturbation in the same dataset. Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, strong Chchd10 target depletion was largely transcriptionally buffered, without induction of the ISR-like Asns, Chac1, Ddit3, Slc7a5, Shmt2, Mars1, Cars, or Aldh1l2 module that Opa1/Dnm1l activated. This suggests the guide-driven Chchd10 perturbation was buffered or incomplete rather than a generic cristae-collapse lesion, although Opa1 and Dnm1l are pathway neighbors and their own target-transcript significance varied across cell types.

Lamp2 did not phenocopy its available lysosomal, chaperone-mediated autophagy, macroautophagy, or mTOR-pathway neighbors: across 257 same-cell-type comparisons with Hspa8, Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Map1lc3a, Sqstm1, Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1, Tsc2, Ppt1, and Ctsb, Lamp2 signature correlations were near zero. In 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Tsc1/Tsc2 produced much stronger corrected signatures than Lamp2, indicating detectable responses were possible in the same classes. Caveats are that several ideal comparators, including Lamp1, Cd63, Tfeb, and Tfe3, were not tested, and some autophagy perturbations had weak on-target repression.

Ifnar1 perturbation did not detectably repress the canonical type I interferon receptor/JAK-STAT/ISGF3 antiviral program at baseline. Across all 22 Ifnar1-assayed brain cell classes, there was no coherent downregulation of core ISG and ISGF3-associated transcripts, including Stat1, Stat2, Irf9, Irf7, Bst2, Isg15, Ifit1, Oas1a, Oasl2, Rsad2, Usp18, Ccl5, and Cxcl10, and the effect was weak overall, lacking FDR-significant genes and not aligning with IFNAR or STAT/IRF comparator perturbations. Because this was a manually selected transcript set and a basal transcriptomic readout, the absence of decreased ISGs does not exclude acute phospho-STAT defects after IFN-alpha or IFN-beta stimulation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cox5a perturbation produced robust on-target transcript depletion but, in the strongest neuronal contexts—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA—did not yield FDR-significant induction of mitochondrial-encoded OXPHOS transcripts such as mt-Co1, mt-Co2, mt-Co3, or mt-Cytb, nor an ATF4/integrated stress response amino-acid module marked by Asns, Cars, Mars1, Ddit3, Chac1, Slc7a5, and Shmt2. In these same cell types, Opa1 perturbation induced the ISR-like module, highlighting a cross-perturbation contrast, although only transcript abundance was measured and weak coordinated shifts could be missed after multiple-testing correction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Elp2 knockdown produced a broad, FDR-significant response specifically in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, where amino-acid starvation and integrated-stress-response genes were induced, including Atf4, Ddit3, Asns, Chac1, Slc7a5, Slc3a2, Slc38a2, Slc1a4, Slc7a1, Shmt2, Mthfd2, and Stc2, while synaptic, dendritic, glutamatergic, and cytoskeletal transcripts such as Adgrb1, Cacna1g, Camk2a, Slc17a7, Syt7, Tuba1a, and Tubb3 were reduced. This pattern is consistent with impaired Elongator-dependent tRNA wobble-uridine modification and proteostasis, although the dataset measures mRNA endpoints rather than tRNA modifications, translation speed, ATF4 protein, or electrophysiology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Clpx perturbation in mouse brain cells did not activate the mitochondrial integrated stress response/ATF4-like amino-acid module that was induced by Opa1 and Dnm1l in the same dataset. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells, Clpx showed no FDR-supported induction of Asns, Ddit3, Chac1, Cars, Mars1, Shmt2, Aldh1l2, or Herpud1, suggesting partial Clpx perturbation was buffered or below threshold; however, the dataset measured transcriptional similarity only and did not assess OMA1, DELE1, HRI, eIF2α phosphorylation, or ATF4 protein.

Rnf216 was uncoupled from curated innate-immune and autophagy pathway neighbors in this transcriptome-based dataset: across in-library perturbations spanning Becn1, Atg5, Atg16l1, Traf3, Tlr2/3/4/5/7/8/9, Il1r1, Il1rap, Nod2, Map3k7, Nfkb1/2, Tbk1, Irf3, Cyld, Otulin, Rnf13, and Rnf220, same-cell correlations with the Rnf216 signature were near zero, and canonical transcripts such as Arc, Becn1, Traf3, Tbk1, Irf3, and Nfkb1 were not FDR significant. This argues against a broad neuronal TLR/IL-1/NF-kappaB/IRF or BECN1-autophagy module driven by Rnf216 at the mRNA level, while noting that RNF216 effects may instead act through ubiquitination and degradation, and several relevant adaptor genes were not perturbed in the library.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Rapgef2 was uncoupled from the basal Rap/Ras to RAF-MEK-ERK transcriptional output in this Perturb-seq dataset: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Rapgef2 perturbation did not significantly shift the ERK/immediate-early markers Vgf, Egr1, or Ptpn5, and whole-transcriptome signatures did not converge with Ras/MAPK-neighbor perturbations. In contrast, Nf1, Braf, and Map2k1 produced robust, directionally coherent Vgf/Ptpn5-like outputs in the same cells. A caveat is that Rapgef2 on-target engagement was weak in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and prior ERK effects were reported under GPCR, dopamine, or learning stimulation rather than basal conditions.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Dctn1 showed partial convergence with Rab7: in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Rab7 perturbation partially phenocopied the Dctn1 cholesterol program and induced sterol genes including Insig1, Msmo1, Cyp51, Ldlr, and Fdps. This pattern places the response near a Rab7 late-endosome positioning and cholesterol-sensing module, consistent with late endosome positioning or cholesterol export rather than generic cytoskeletal stress, although Rab7 was only a modest whole-transcriptome neighbor and late-endosome localization or ORP1L cholesterol state were not directly measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Ndufs8 depletion reduced Ndufs8 itself but did not trigger a coordinated transcriptional response across other OXPHOS subunits. In the strongest-engaged cell types—155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA—non-target respiratory-chain transcripts such as Ndufa10/11/12/13, Ndufs1/2/3/4/7, Ndufv1/2, Ndufb7/8/9/10/11, Ndufc2, Cox5a, Uqcrfs1, Sdha, and Sdhb were not FDR-shifted. Related Complex I biogenesis perturbations also did not phenocopy Ndufs8 signatures, although only tested transcripts were assessable and post-transcriptional pathway changes remain possible.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lars2 did not trigger a canonical ATF4/integrated stress response mitochondrial-stress program in 155 MB Glut or 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: Atf4, Ddit3, Asns, Chac1, Mthfd2, Slc7a5, and related markers were not detectably induced, and the best-powered Lars2 groups were FDR-silent. In the same dataset, Opa1 and Dnm1l perturbations produced strong ISR-like signatures, including Asns, Cars, Ddit3, Chac1, and Mars1, with reduced mitochondrial transcripts such as mt-Co2. This suggests the missing Lars2 ISR is unlikely to reflect assay insensitivity, although these mitochondrial comparators do not imply mechanistic equivalence and Lars2 target engagement is unknown.

Ndufb7, like other complex-I subunits in this screen, showed a largely buffered RNA phenotype in which the dominant signal was self-depletion rather than downstream transcriptional change. Across 572 NDUF perturbation-by-cell signatures spanning subunits such as Ndufa10, Ndufb10, Ndufs1, and Ndufv2, only 8 signatures had any non-self FDR hit, totaling 9 non-target genes. This sparse, often uncorrelated response was seen in cell types including 191 MB P MY GABA and 155 MB Glut, though the aggregate mixes many guides and cell classes and does not establish reduced complex-I protein activity in every perturbation.

Ndufa8 knockdown produced a relatively weak Complex I perturbation compared with several neighboring Nduf/Ndufaf targets, but across the broader Complex I panel the dominant signal was still on-target transcript reduction with sparse non-target differential expression. In 155 MB Glut, Ndufa8 was solidly reduced yet weaker than several related perturbations, and in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA the target decreased without non-target genes even at FDR<0.2. Across 550 target-by-cell-class tests, 61 on-target versus only 9 non-target genes passed FDR<0.05, consistent with a buffered nuclear mRNA response to partial Complex I depletion rather than Ndufa8-specific dispensability; however, guide potency varied and comparisons are based on transcript-level knockdown, not matched protein or respiratory phenotyping.

Gabrg3 perturbation showed no detectable transcriptional compensation within the GABA receptor activation module: alternative GABA-A receptor subunits such as Gabra1-5, Gabrb1-3, Gabrd, and Gabrg2, along with GABAergic synapse and transport genes including Gad1, Gad2, Slc6a1, Slc32a1, Arhgef9, and Gphn, were not significantly induced or repressed at FDR-supported levels. This suggests that receptor replacement or inhibitory-synapse compensation was not detectable under the tested perturbation, although the conclusion is limited by weak on-target Gabrg3 knockdown rather than full genetic loss.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Marchf6 showed a cell-type-specific sterol-transcription response that Amfr/gp78 did not phenocopy in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons. In these two glutamatergic classes, Marchf6 perturbation was associated with increased SREBP-regulated cholesterol-biosynthesis transcripts, including Insig1, Hmgcr, Cyp51, Msmo1, and Fdps, whereas Amfr was efficiently reduced yet ranked near the bottom of the sterol-module score distribution and did not induce this program. This divergence argues for a Marchf6-specific ERAD-E3 branch rather than a generic ERAD effect, although the comparison is based on transcriptomic output rather than direct measurement of HMGCR ERAD activity, and canonical UPR markers were not induced.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gabra1 perturbation did not produce a detectable transcriptional replacement program across five contexts—005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Other GABA-A receptor subunits (Gabra2-5, Gabrb1-3, Gabrd, Gabrg2-3, Gabrr2) and related GABAergic genes including Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, Gphn, Arhgef9, Nlgn2, and Abat showed no FDR-significant compensatory induction. The strongest on-target depletion was in Pvalb Gaba, while weak Gabra1-Gabrb2 convergence appeared only in thalamic glutamatergic cells; low-expression instability and nontranscriptional compensation remain caveats.

Gabrr2 perturbation was largely uncoupled from the expected GABAergic marker program: across the measured transcripts, there were no FDR-significant changes in GABA synthesis, vesicular transport, transporter, or receptor-subunit genes, including Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, Abat, and multiple GABA-A subunits. In 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, Gabrr2 was also essentially null, with Gabrb2 only a nominal hit (FDR=1.0), and nominal effects did not form a repeated cross-cell-type module. This marker test was limited to selected transcripts and does not address acute electrophysiological compensation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Dnm1l loss induced a recurrent ATF4-like amino-acid stress program across five subcortical neuronal classes, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where target depletion coincided with broad upregulation of Asns, Cars, Ddit3, Chac1, Mars1, Shmt2, and Slc7a5. Related but smaller signatures recurred in 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, emphasizing amino-acid biosynthesis, transport, one-carbon metabolism, and tRNA charging rather than generic mitochondrial transcript loss. The state is inferred from marker genes; ATF4 protein, eIF2 phosphorylation, mitochondrial morphology, and function were not measured.

Rubcn perturbation did not produce a detectable transcriptional module for canonical autophagy, PI3KC3, Rab7/HOPS, Rag, TSC, or MTOR pathways: across 621 tested transcripts, none reached FDR<0.05, including Becn1, Pik3c3, Pik3r4, Atg14, Uvrag, Vps16, Vps41, Rab7, Stx17, Snap29, Sqstm1, Tfeb, Tfe3, Mtor, Tsc1, Tsc2, Atg5, and Atg16l1. This argues against using neighboring autophagy-gene mRNA as a Rubcn pharmacodynamic readout in these neuronal classes, while leaving open the caveat that pathway flux could still change without differential expression.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Stat4 perturbation in 22 assayed brain neuronal classes, spanning multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic types, did not detectably engage the canonical IL-12/IL-23/JAK-STAT or Th1 immune-differentiation program. Transcripts such as Stat1, Stat2, Stat3, Stat5b, Irf1, Irf7, Irf9, Il12b, Il12rb1, Il21r, Il23r, Tbx21, Rorc, and Foxp3 were unchanged, and related perturbations of Ifnar1/2, Ifngr1/2, Il6ra, Il6st, IRFs, and other STATs were likewise largely inert. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA and 052 Pvalb Gaba, the strongest nominal hits remained below FDR significance and did not support a JAK-STAT response. This negative evidence is limited to mRNA differential expression; upstream cytokines, phospho-STAT4, and immune cell types were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hspd1 was not interchangeable with the related mitochondrial chaperone Hspa9 in this neuronal screen. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Hspd1 remained FDR-silent and nearly orthogonal to Hspa9 (Pearson r = -0.0368), whereas Hspa9 produced 649 significant genes, including Shmt2, Chac1, Lonp1, Asns, Atf5, and Ddit3; in 155 MB Glut, Hspa9 again showed an 87-gene mitochondrial chaperone stress response while Hspd1 had no corrected hits despite nominal transcript depletion. This separation is inferred from mRNA signatures, with Hspa9 but not Hspe1 serving as the strong same-network comparator.

Gabrb1 depletion did not produce a coordinated transcriptional compensation program among the assayed GABAergic components: across selected GABA-A receptor subunits, anchoring factors, and GABA synthesis or transport genes, the nominal hit rate was near background, with no FDR-significant increases in Gabra1-5, Gabrb2, Gabrb3, Gabrd, Gabrg2, Gabrg3, Gphn, Arhgef9, Slc6a1, Slc32a1, Gad1, or Gad2. In the best-sampled 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Gabrb1 showed only nominal self-depletion without an FDR-level response, whereas Gabrb2 in the same class showed a stronger on-target and activity-gene signature. This analysis was limited to detectable transcripts, so compensation through protein trafficking or receptor assembly would not be captured.

Tnfrsf13c perturbation in 23 profiled brain neuronal classes produced an extremely sparse transcriptional response and was transcriptionally uncoupled from the curated BAFF/BAFF-R to TRAF/non-canonical NF-κB signaling pathway. Across neurons, a 26-gene BAFF/TNFR/NF-κB/survival panel remained unchanged, including Tnfsf13b, Traf3, Map3k14, Nfkb2, Relb, Chuk, Bcl2, Bcl2l1, Birc2, and Birc3, with no convergence to related TNFR/NF-κB perturbations. This negative neuronal result should not be generalized to B cells or CNS macrophages, and the target itself was not detectably engaged.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Csf3r perturbation in unstimulated mouse brain cells showed no coherent activation or repression of canonical CSF3/G-CSF receptor signaling across the profiled glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types. In particular, sentinel transcripts for JAK-STAT and related outputs, including Cish, Socs3, Stat1, Stat3, Stat5b, Jak1, Jak2, Tyk2, MAPK, PI3K/AKT, and AP-1 genes such as Fos, Jun, and Jund, did not shift with multiple-testing correction, and no genome-wide corrected hit was detected. This null result is tempered by the use of mRNA rather than phospho-signaling readouts, the lack of Csf3 or Jak1/Jak2 perturbations, and the possibility of weak Csf3r engagement.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nipa1 showed mostly weak or absent transcriptomic similarity to BMP-receptor/SMAD and HSP-associated trafficking perturbations across 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. Correlations with Bmpr2, Acvr1/2a/2b, Bmpr1a/1b, Smad1/4/9, Map3k7, and with Spast, Atl1/3, Reep1, Kif5a/Kif1a, Vps37a, and Epb41l1 were weak, and even unrestricted neighbor searches did not reveal a close phenocopy. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Nipa1 knockdown was strongest but FDR-silent and lacked BMP-feedback induction, while the CA3 signal was exploratory because Nipa1 itself was not knocked down; these comparisons were further limited by noisy whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon scores and variable target engagement.

Gabra2 did not show detectable convergence with a restricted panel of GABAergic pathway perturbations. Across shared cell types, correlations between Gabra2 Wilcoxon-score signatures and 16 perturbations spanning GABA synthesis, vesicular loading, reuptake, metabolism, receptor subunits, and inhibitory-synapse scaffolding were near zero, even though neighbors such as Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, Arhgef9, Gphn, Abat, Gls, and Glud1 showed detectable target knockdown elsewhere in the dataset. This weak, transcriptomic-only result suggests Gabra2 should not be aggregated into a GABA module without stronger knockdown or broader pathway testing.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Hspa9 perturbation recurrently induced an ATF4-like amino-acid/integrated-stress response across responsive neuronal classes, marked by upregulation of Shmt2, Asns, Chac1, Ddit3, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases such as Nars, Eprs, and Cars, amino-acid transporters Slc7a1 and Slc7a5, and Cyb5r1. The strongest transcriptomic response occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, with smaller but supported signatures in 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. This pattern points to a general mitochondrial-to-nuclear stress state rather than a single respiratory-chain or synaptic program, although ATF4 itself was only nominally increased, so the module is inferred from established ISR target genes rather than direct ATF4 detection.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Gria4 showed an uncoupled Perturb-seq phenotype rather than a shared glutamate-receptor or postsynaptic-density transcriptomic response. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, despite clear Gria4 depletion and efficient depletion of Dlg4 and Grin1, correlations with Gria4 were negligible, and across non-cerebellar contexts including 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 053 Sst Gaba, correlations to Cacng2/3/8, Dlg4, Grid1/2, Grik1-5, and Grin1/2a/2b/2d/3a stayed below |r|=0.10. This suggests the measured Gria4 response is not a generic AMPA, NMDA, kainate, delta receptor, or postsynaptic-pathway average, although only assayed perturbation neighbors were comparable and Cnih2/3 and Shisa6/9 were unavailable.

Atf6 perturbation did not coordinately change canonical unfolded protein response or ERAD transcripts in this basal brain screen: across 22 profiles, Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Manf, Xbp1, Ddit3, Herpud1, Dnajb9, Hyou1, Pdia4, Pdia6, and Sel1l showed mixed signs without FDR-significant regulation. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Atf6 produced only nominal Herpud1 induction, whereas Manf and Hspa5 perturbations revealed stronger ER quality-control responses. Because only mRNA was measured and no acute tunicamycin/thapsigargin stress challenge was applied, weak target engagement could mask a true dependency.

Bcas3 was mostly uncoupled from assayed autophagy, mitophagy, Notch, and angiogenic receptor perturbations in this neuronal Perturb-seq dataset. In a restricted comparison using the top 200 Bcas3-ranked genes per cell type, signatures showed low similarity to Prkn, Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Rb1cc1, Rubcn, Mtor, Map1lc3a, Tsc1, Tsc2, Kdr, Flt4, Tek, Acvrl1, Nrp1, Nrp2, Notch1, and Dll1, with only a single Trim23 induction in L4-5 IT CTX Glut and no engagement of endothelial migration programs in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut or MB Glut. This limited convergence may reflect that only the top 200 genes were scanned and comparator perturbations varied in strength.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Dhdds perturbation induced an ER unfolded-protein and chaperone program most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and also in 155 MB Glut, with recurrent upregulation of Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Sdf2l1, Pdia4, Pdia6, Creld2, Herpud1, Manf, Hyou1, Dnajb11, Ddit3, and Xbp1. The thalamic population showed the largest response, while the midbrain glutamatergic class also showed ER chaperone induction and reduced Slc17a6 and Atp1a3. This pattern is consistent with dolichol-phosphate/ER N-glycosylation stress, although the dataset measured mRNA rather than Dol-P, N-glycans, or DHDDS protein, and Dhdds self-transcript knockdown was only nominal after multiple testing.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ywhag knockdown in 155 MB Glut does not phenocopy the Tsc2/TORC1 sterol-lysosomal transcriptional program. In this cell type, Tsc2 perturbation altered 202 genes, including positive sterol/TORC1-associated genes such as Cyp51, Insig1, Ldlr, and Pik3r3, whereas these genes were unchanged after Ywhag knockdown and the Ywhag–Tsc2 score correlation was near zero (r=0.0155). Thus, despite curated links between YWHAG and phosphorylated TSC2/TORC1, Ywhag loss is not equivalent to Tsc2 loss at the mRNA level here, with the caveat that this is a transcriptional comparison rather than a direct readout of phospho-TSC2 binding or acute TORC1 activity.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Map1lc3a knockdown in four validated mouse-brain neuronal classes—052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—produced a self-only transcriptional response and did not elicit significant mRNA compensation among measured ATG8 paralogs or core macroautophagy genes, including Map1lc3b, Gabarap, Gabarapl1/2, Sqstm1, Atg5, Becn1, Rb1cc1, Lamp2, Mtor, and Rptor. This suggests that any LC3/GABARAP buffering here is not an acute transcriptional feedback program, although paralogs were not directly perturbed and mRNA levels do not capture LC3 lipidation or paralog protein activity.

Tango2 reduction did not measurably induce the prespecified transcriptional sentinels for ER stress, oxidative stress, fatty-acid oxidation, OXPHOS, or mitochondrial dynamics in this mouse-brain atlas: a 53-gene panel, including Hspa5, Ddit3, Atf4, Xbp1, Sod2, Acadvl, Ndufs4, Cox5a, Sdha, Uqcrc1, Tomm40, Hspa9, and Pdha1, showed no FDR-supported changes. This absence held even in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, where Tango2 knockdown was nominally strongest, while comparator perturbations such as Hspa9, Sdha, Cox5a, Uqcrc1, Ndufs2, Ndufb8, Ttc19, and Pdha1 produced detectable signatures. These data refine rather than refute mitochondrial and lipid models, because the screen was transcript-based and did not directly assay metabolic flux, respiration, lipid species, or Golgi traffic.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mapk1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a notable divergence from neighboring Ras/MAPK perturbations: although Mapk1 was nominally depleted, it did not significantly change the Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 output module that was clearly modulated by upstream pathway nodes. In the same cell type, Braf, Map2k1, and Ntrk2 perturbations repressed Vgf/Ptpn5-family genes, whereas Nf1 perturbation induced Vgf, Ptpn5, and Etv5, consistent with opposing Ras/MAPK inputs. This suggests downstream buffering or compensation at the ERK2 node, with the caveat that Mapk1 had fewer perturbed cells and only nominal target-transcript evidence here.

Ndufa13 knockdown showed no detectable transcriptional feedback across mitochondrial Complex I genes: other nuclear Nduf subunits and mitochondrially encoded mt-Nd transcripts were not transcriptionally remodeled, with measured non-target Nduf and mt-Nd genes all unchanged at the mRNA level. This indicates that despite Ndufa13’s role in Complex I biogenesis and respiratory electron transport, the broader respiratory-chain module remained transcriptionally buffered rather than coordinately induced or suppressed. The absence of mRNA changes does not exclude post-transcriptional Complex I assembly defects or respiratory dysfunction.

Drd3 perturbation showed no significant transcript-level response in the canonical D2-like dopamine receptor/Gi-Go/adenylate-cyclase axis or immediate-early GPCR response program: Drd1, Drd2, Drd3, Drd4, Drd5, Adcy1, Adcy5, Gnao1, Gnas, Pde10a, Fos, Egr1, Dusp1, Arc, and Homer1 were unchanged at the sampled endpoint. Thus, expected dopamine receptor, cAMP, and immediate-early mRNA readouts were uncoupled from Drd3 perturbation, with no meaningful Drd3-family convergence detected; this likely reflects that mRNA is an indirect, potentially late readout of acute GPCR outputs such as cAMP flux, receptor phosphorylation, trafficking, and calcium signaling.

Dnal1 showed little transcriptional convergence with the screened ciliary-neighbor perturbations: across Foxj1, Rfx3, Rfx7, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Bbs5, Bbs9, Ttc8, Ttc21b, Cep164, Cep290, and Cfap69, the best absolute correlation was only 0.194, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where Dnal1 had its strongest nominal decrease, the largest correlation was with Ift88 at r=0.091. This suggests that partial neuronal Dnal1 suppression did not reproduce a general ciliary transcriptional program, although the analysis was limited to available perturbations and closer outer-dynein-arm partners such as Dnah5, Dnai1, Dnai2, Dnali1, Lrrc6, Zmynd10, and Ccdc114 were not directly tested.

Tnfrsf9 perturbation in unstimulated neurons did not produce a coherent TNFSF9–TNFRSF9 signaling transcript response: transcripts for Tnfsf9, related receptors such as Tnfrsf1a and Tnfrsf1b, TRAF adaptors including Traf1, Traf2, and Traf3, and NF-kB neighborhood genes such as Chuk, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, and Relb were not reproducibly changed, with FDR-supported effects absent wherever measured. This held across surveyed neuronal classes; even in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and 191 MB P MY GABA, only nominal signals appeared and did not support pathway activation. Because the assay captured mRNA in unstimulated neurons, it does not address acute ligand binding or NF-kB/MAPK phosphorylation.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ifih1 targeting showed no detectable induction or suppression of canonical interferon-stimulated genes in the neuronal classes examined, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. This matched comparator perturbations: Adar and Stat1 guides reduced their own transcripts in selected classes, yet markers such as Ifit1, Ifit2, Ifit3, Isg15, Oas1a, Oasl1, Oasl2, Rsad2, Usp18, Ifnb1, and Cxcl10 remained flat, consistent with a weak basal ADAR1-MDA5 and type I interferon JAK-STAT transcriptional state in this unchallenged assay; however, only mRNA output was measured, without acute dsRNA stimulation or complete protein loss.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lztr1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed strong on-target depletion but only a weak, nominal downstream module; within that restricted gene set, the Lztr1 response aligned with Nf1 loss and opposed loss of Braf, Kras, Map2k1, and Shoc2, consistent with de-repression of RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK signaling in this neuronal class. The contrasted genes included Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, Atp2a2, and Unc13a, with Vgf and Ptpn5 tending to increase with Lztr1 or Nf1 loss and decrease with Braf or Map2k1 loss. Full-transcriptome correlations were small, so this is a directionally interpretable but modest signal.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Pibf1 was transcriptionally nonconvergent with a ciliary/Joubert comparator panel despite shared centrosome/cilium membership: across 278 target-cell signatures, Ahi1, Cep290, Cplane1, Ift88, Kif3b, Bbs5, Bbs9, Rpgrip1l, and Cep83/Cep112/Cep120/Cep164 yielded only four FDR-significant rows, and Pibf1-to-comparator correlations were near zero in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut. In these cell types, Pibf1 showed nominal on-target reduction but no FDR response or restricted-signature similarity, although most comparator perturbations were also transcriptionally weak, so the lack of convergence does not rule out related ciliary functions.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Htt showed its strongest response in 155 MB Glut cells, where a coordinated sterol-regulatory program including Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, and Srebf2 was upregulated. In the same cell type, Hap1 was target-engaged but did not phenocopy Htt: its 16-gene sterol panel shifted slightly downward on average rather than upward. This divergence suggests the Htt sterol response is not interchangeable with simple HAP1 loss and is more aligned with dynein/dynactin-linked transport perturbations such as Dctn1 and Dync1h1, although the contrast is strongest in one cell type and the assay measures mRNA rather than cargo motility.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Oprk1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any assayed cell class, including glutamatergic and GABAergic populations such as 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, where only near-miss signals were seen. Canonical opioid-receptor signaling transcripts, including Oprd1, Oprm1, Oprl1, Pdyn, Penk, Pomc, Pnoc, Gnao1, Gnb1, Adcy1/3/5, Pde4b, Pde10a, Mapk1/3/8/9, Arrb1/2, and Grk2/3, did not form a significant module. This null RNA readout likely reflects mismatch with acute Gi/o GPCR signaling, since phosphorylation, cAMP, ion-channel, peptide-release, and ligand-evoked states were not assayed.

Irf9 perturbation did not detectably suppress the canonical ISGF3/type-I-interferon transcriptional response in this basal mouse-brain Perturb-seq experiment: Stat1, Stat2, Irf7, Adar, Ifih1, Isg15, Ifit1, Ifit3, Ifi44, Usp18, Rtp4, Rsad2, Oas1a, Oas2, Bst2, Ifitm3, and Ifi27l2a/b were FDR-null, and related perturbations were near-zero correlated. Cell-type-specific signals were weak, with nominal but non-significant rows in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. Because only abundant transcripts were assayed and cells were not challenged with IFN or virus, this result indicates that the stimulated antiviral pathway was not engaged rather than proving IRF9 has no role.

Kiz perturbation in these brain cells did not converge with a retinal cilium/centrosome transcriptomic module: candidate ciliary-family transcripts including Bbs5, Bbs9, Cep83, Cep290, Ift88, Ift43, Ift81, Cep164, Cep120, Cep112, Cep85l, Nek1, Nek9, and Kif3b were not FDR-supported downstream markers, and Kiz signatures were essentially uncorrelated with the matched BBS, IFT, CEP, KIF3B, and NEK perturbations. This argues against a shared brain whole-transcriptome ciliopathy program here, although the conclusion is acute and transcriptomic, Kiz engagement was weak, and relevant ciliary biology may be structural or compartmental rather than reflected in steady-state mRNA.

Ccr5 perturbation showed no significant transcriptional response, with no genome-wide differential-expression hits and no directional knockdown signature for the target transcript itself. Canonical CCR5-neighborhood genes, including ligands Ccl3, Ccl4, and Ccl5, Gi components Gnao1, Gnb1, and Gnb5, and MAPK/CREB or immediate-early genes Mapk1, Mapk3, Creb1, Fos, Jun, Egr1, and Arc, were not coherently regulated, including in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 155 MB Glut. This suggests basal neuronal Ccr5 perturbation is transcriptionally uncoupled from canonical CCR5 signaling, although target engagement was weak and single-cell mRNA cannot assess ERK/CREB phosphorylation, calcium flux, receptor trafficking, or dendritic remodeling.

Eif2ak4 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the canonical GCN2-mediated integrated stress response in this dataset: Atf4, Ddit3, Asns, Ppp1r15a, Trib3, Chac1, and amino-acid transporter markers such as Slc7a11 and Slc7a5 were not induced or reproducibly repressed, with all reported as non-significant. This separates the knockout from an amino-acid-starvation-like ISR at the steady-state mRNA level, although the single-cell assay cannot capture EIF2S1 phosphorylation, ATF4-biased translation, or acute starvation dynamics.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Spred1 was transcriptomically uncoupled from the neuronal NF1/Raf/MEK module recoverable in the same dataset: across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Nf1 loss increased a Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5-containing program, while Braf or Map2k1 loss decreased overlapping genes such as Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, and Unc13a, yet Spred1 showed no FDR-significant response and near-zero correlation with Nf1, Braf, or Map2k1 signatures. This contrast is limited to matched cell-class transcriptomic readouts, and weak Spred1 guide engagement could contribute to the apparent pathway uncoupling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Raf1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells did not reproduce the thalamic RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK response module seen with neighboring perturbations: Braf and Map2k1 loss repressed, and Nf1 loss activated, a bidirectional Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 program, with related ERK feedback markers such as Dusp4/5/6, Spry1/2, Fos, and Egr1 also absent after Raf1 perturbation. Despite a similar perturbed cell count, Raf1 left these markers largely uncorrected, although Raf1 itself was only weakly reduced in this cell type, so this supports nonresponse of the specific perturbation rather than a definitive epistasis order.

Cep120 perturbation did not produce a recurrent transcriptional shift in the measured candidate cilium and centrosome program, including Cep290, Cep164, Cep83, Ift81, Ift88, Ttc8, Ttc21b, Rpgr, Rpgrip1l, and related genes. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, this pattern suggested transcriptional uncoupling from the expected ciliogenesis/centriole biology rather than convergence with other ciliary perturbations. This negative result is limited to a pragmatic subset of measured, targeted genes, and structural cilium defects could still occur without detectable mRNA changes.

Sil1 perturbation did not consistently induce the canonical ER HSPA5/BiP unfolded-protein-response program: transcripts such as Hspa5, Hyou1, Xbp1, Atf4, Ddit3, Atf6, Ern1, Eif2ak3, and Manf were not significantly upregulated, and HYOU1 compensation was likewise absent. This is notable because SIL1 is a HSPA5 nucleotide-exchange factor in the ER lumen, yet the single-cell RNA readout appeared uncoupled from the expected stress program implicated by complete Sil1 deficiency. Interpretation is limited because the RNA perturbation was weak and scRNA cannot capture BiP ATPase cycling, Xbp1 splicing, or protein-level ER stress.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Trip12 perturbation did not significantly induce a canonical ARF-p53 or DNA-damage transcriptional program in resting mouse brain cells: across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, a 15-gene p53-response panel including Trp53, Cdkn1a, Mdm2, Bax, Bbc3, Pmaip1, Ccng1, Gadd45a, Phlda3, Aen, Rrm2b, Sesn1/2, Zmat3, and Ddit4 showed no multiple-testing-significant induction. Instead, Trip12 produced sparse, cell-type-specific signatures with Pabpn1/Amy1 down-regulation, limited proteasome-neighbor convergence, and partial Huwe1 similarity; the assay did not measure ARF or RNF168 protein, histone ubiquitination, DNA damage, or longer-term cell-cycle outcomes.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tlr9 did not show transcriptional convergence with assayed endosomal TLR-family or NF-kB/IRF pathway perturbations in this screen. Across neuronal cell types, correlations with Tlr2, Tlr3, Tlr4, Tlr7, Tlr8, Chuk, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Irf3, Irf5, Irf7, Stat1, and Tbk1 were mostly weak or near zero, and the only notable pattern was an exploratory signal in 308 CB GABA, where Tbk1 was weakly positive and Nfkb2 weakly negative. Because Tlr9 itself had no FDR-significant genes, this should be treated as a screen-level negative comparison rather than evidence against shared mechanisms in responsive cells.

Cdkn2a perturbation did not detectably change canonical CDKN2A effector circuits: across tested cells, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, candidate RB/E2F and ARF-MDM2-p53 genes such as Rb1, E2f1/2/3/4/5, Cdk4/6, Ccnd1/2/3, Trp53, Mdm2, Mdm4, Cdkn1a, Bax, Bbc3, Pmaip1, and Gadd45a/b/g were not significant, with direct candidate inspection yielding adjusted p values of 1.0. This supports pathway inactivity or buffering in basal neuronal states, although the result is based on candidate inspection rather than formal enrichment and absent Cdkn2a RNA engagement weakens mechanistic inference.

Cnr1 showed weak, unstable transcriptional signatures that were not phenocopied by available CB1-associated perturbations: across matched cell types, correlations between the Cnr1 top-signature genes and perturbations of Drd2, Gnao1, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, and other GPCR/cAMP/synaptic neighbors were near zero, with maximum |r| only 0.328 and no stable nearest-neighbor or inverse-neighbor pattern. This suggests little coherent projection of the curated CB1/Gi-o/adenylyl-cyclase axis or endocannabinoid synaptic modulation onto steady-state mRNA in this assay, although the analysis used only the top 200 Cnr1 score genes per cell type and several direct partners, including Cnr2, Gnai1/2/3, Gpr55, and Adcy8, were not tested.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Zeb2 showed its strongest signatures in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, but these responses were uncoupled from assayed TGFβ/BMP-SMAD signaling perturbations. In Pvalb cells, Zeb2 had a primary response with four 5%-FDR genes plus a 10%-FDR Dlx6/Patj extension despite weak measured Zeb2 knockdown, and no close phenocopy with Zeb1, Ctbp1, Smad1/2/3/4, Tgfbr1/2, or Bmpr2. In L4-5 IT neurons, Patj was the single 5%-FDR Zeb2-induced gene, and the signature likewise did not align with Bmpr2 or SMAD perturbations. These data suggest context-specific ZEB2 outputs rather than simple canonical SMAD loss-of-function phenocopies, although incomplete knockdown or low pathway activity in the assayed cells means the lack of correlation does not prove Smad independence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sos2 was FDR-null in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, with 114 cells and no significant hits, even though the same dataset detected nearby RTK-SOS-RAS/MAPK pathway perturbations in this cell type: Nf1, Map2k1, Braf, and Ntrk2 each produced FDR-level responses centered on Vgf, Ptpn5, and Atp2a2. This contrast suggests the Sos2-negative result is not simply a global failure to recover Ras/MAPK biology, but may reflect Sos2-specific buffering, weak guide engagement, or both; comparator perturbations also differed in guide counts and target engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ntrk1 appeared uncoupled from neurotrophin-family and RAF-MEK/MAPK transcriptional responses in high-count 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells: despite 177 perturbed cells, Ntrk1 left Vgf, Ptpn5, Atp2a2, Etv5, and Unc13a unchanged at FDR=1, whereas Ntrk2, Map2k1, and Braf perturbations decreased overlapping members of this module. In the same dataset, Ntrk2 also showed cell-type-restricted engagement, including strong on-target depletion with reduced Akap5 in 052 Pvalb Gaba and significant on-target depletion in 155 MB Glut, supporting receptor- and context-specific uncoupling rather than a general assay failure; however, only transcriptomic readouts were measured, without NGF stimulation, ERK phosphorylation, or receptor protein abundance.

Tnfrsf9 showed no significant response in this screen, and this lack of signal was mirrored across a broader TNF receptor superfamily and NF-kB neighborhood, including Tnfrsf4, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Tnfrsf11a, Fas, Cd40, Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, and Chuk, all of which were FDR-null across the gene-level tests. In this neuronal screen, the convergent absence of hits suggests pathway-level inactivity or poor engagement rather than an isolated Tnfrsf9-specific effect, although several comparator perturbations also lacked proven target RNA depletion, so the result reflects observed screen behavior rather than definitive protein inactivity.

Tlr5 perturbation in the neuronal panel did not transcriptionally engage canonical flagellin–TLR5 programs: NF-kappaB cytokines and chemokines such as Tnf, Il6, Il1b, Ccl2, Cxcl10, and Nos2, along with proximal MyD88-IRAK-TRAF6 components including Myd88, Traf6, Irak1, Irak4, Map3k7, Nfkbia, Rela, and Nfkb1, showed no detectable response, and the PI3K-Akt-mTOR branch genes Akt1, Akt2, Akt3, and Mtor also lacked support. Because this dataset used Tlr5 loss of function without exogenous flagellin, the absence of these genes should not be interpreted as an antagonist-like result in microglia.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Stt3b depletion did not yield a resolved canonical unfolded-protein-response or ER-stress transcriptional program in the two best-engaged mouse brain cell classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA. In both contexts, canonical markers including Hspa5, Xbp1, Ddit3, Atf4, Atf6, Ern1, Hyou1, Dnajc3, Eif2ak3, and Pdia3 were not FDR-induced; the MB P MY GABA class showed only nominal up-scores for Hyou1, Eif2ak3, and Pdia3. This suggests no strong bulk UPR state at the mRNA level, although only selected RNA markers were examined and Xbp1 splicing, client glycosylation, and acute protein stress were not measured.

Gabra5 perturbation did not produce detectable transcriptional remodeling of the measured GABA pathway genes: across selected GABA_A receptor subunits, including Gabra1-6, Gabrb1-3, Gabrg1-3, Gabrd, Gabre, Gabrq, Gabrp, Gabrr1-3, as well as Gad1, Gad2, and Slc6a1, no rows passed FDR < 0.05. Thus, in the measured cell classes, there was no FDR-supported mRNA compensation by alternate GABA_A subunits or core GABA synthesis and transport genes, although target engagement was weak, so this absence should not be taken as proof that alpha5 function was lost without feedback.

Tnfrsf13c showed no convergence with related TNFR/NF-κB perturbations across the 23 profiled brain neuronal classes. In the same cell classes, Bcl2, Cd40, Chuk, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, Tnfrsf11a, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Tnfrsf9, and Traf3 had weak transcriptional effects, with no genes at FDR<0.10, and their same-cell score correlations with Tnfrsf13c were near zero. This suggests BAFF/BAFF-R to non-canonical NF-κB signaling was not detectably engaged in these neuronal classes, although BAFF/APRIL receptors or ligands were not available as perturbation targets here.

Minar2 did not phenocopy measured Notch receptor or mTORC1/TSC/RAPTOR/Akt3 perturbations in these brain cell groups: across 195 full-transcriptome Minar2-versus-related comparisons, the median absolute correlation was 0.018, and only one pair exceeded |r|>0.2, the largest being with Notch2 in 308 CB GABA (|r|=0.216). This uncoupling persisted even though the matrix detected strong Tsc1/Tsc2 effects, suggesting that published MINAR2 links to NOTCH2 or RAPTOR/mTORC1 do not translate into an acute transcriptional phenocopy here; interpretation is limited by weak Minar2 signatures and missing perturbations such as Minar1 and several mTORC1 components.

Polr3b perturbation in this unstimulated neuronal screen did not show a detectable basal RIG-I/interferon response. Across sampled neuronal subclasses, sentinel genes for Pol III cytosolic DNA sensing and interferon signaling, including Ifnb1, Ifit1, Ifit2, Ifit3, Isg15, Irf7, Stat1, Nfkb1, Mavs, Rsad2, Oas1a, and Oasl2, were not significantly changed, arguing against an innate-immune interpretation of the observed neuronal effects. This negative result should be interpreted with the caveat that the experiment lacked a viral-DNA challenge and several interferon genes were lowly expressed or unmeasured.

Irf6 did not show transcriptomic convergence with the assayed IRF, type-I-interferon, STAT, or NF-kB perturbations across the 23 measured brain cell groups. Across 356 same-cell comparisons to Irf1, Irf2, Irf3, Irf5, Irf7, Irf8, Irf9, Ifnar1, Ifnar2, Ifih1, Stat1, Stat2, Nfkb1, Chuk, Tfap2a, and Trp63, the largest absolute Pearson correlation was only 0.106, and Irf6 also lacked target-transcript depletion and a reproducible signed module. These transcriptomic correlations could be muted by weak Irf6 engagement and do not test acute interferon stimulation.

Irf1 perturbation did not produce a coordinated loss of canonical IFN/IRF1 effector genes across the 23 profiled neuronal cell classes. In basal Glut, GABA, Dopa, and Pineal populations, expected host-defense, antigen-presentation, JAK/STAT, and apoptosis genes such as Ly6e, B2m, Ifit1/2/3, Isg15, Oas-family genes, Psmb8/9, Stat1, Stat2, Tap1, Zbp1, and Casp genes all remained non-significant, with FDR=1.0 throughout; the only near-outlier was 308 CB GABA, where Ly6e moved nominally upward rather than downward. This directional uncoupling is tempered by the caveat that Irf1 itself was not significantly depleted, indicating weak perturbation engagement rather than a clean mechanistic contradiction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|053 Sst Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Prkar1a depletion did not produce an FDR-supported PKA/CREB immediate-early transcriptional program across the profiled cells, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 053 Sst Gaba, and 155 MB Glut. A 19-gene panel containing Fos, Egr1, Crem, Nr4a1, Jund, Dusp1, Arc, Npas4, and Creb1 showed no significant module-level activation; the only interpretable signal was a weak nominal Fos-centered tail in 155 MB Glut, where Fos itself had FDR=0.458. This suggests canonical activity-regulated transcription was largely uncoupled from Prkar1a loss, although spatial, post-translational, compensatory, or sensitivity-limited effects remain possible.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fgfr2 showed a weaker or absent FGFR/RAS-module transcriptional response than related perturbations in this atlas. In 155 MB Glut, Fgfr1 perturbation significantly reduced Fgfr1 RNA itself, whereas Fgfr3 and Fgfrl1 resembled the weak Fgfr2 self-signal. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Braf or Map2k1 perturbation yielded adjusted hits including Vgf, Ptpn5, Unc13a, and Etv5, indicating detectable downstream MAPK-node responses. These comparisons suggest the Fgfr2 null was not simply a global detection failure, although guides, cell counts, targets, and cell types differ and are not quantitative potency controls.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sqstm1 knockdown produced strong on-target depletion but little broader transcriptional response in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. Canonical p62-associated Keap1-Nrf2, selective autophagy/LC3, lysosome, and mTOR pathway transcripts, including Keap1, Nfe2l2, Nqo1, Hmox1, Gclc, Gclm, Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Map1lc3a, Map1lc3b, Lamp2, Tbk1, Mtor, and Rptor, stayed below FDR detection, with only nominal Nbr1 increase in one cell type. This suggests that, in this basal mouse-brain assay, expected p62-linked programs were not detectably rewired at the mRNA level, while protein or post-translational pathway activity remains possible.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Opa1 perturbation induced an amino-acid stress program marked by Asns, Chac1, and Ddit3 across several brain cell types, but broad loss of mitochondrial-encoded respiratory-chain RNAs was restricted to a subset. In 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, mt-Co2, mt-Cytb, mt-Nd1/4/5, mt-Atp6/8, and mt-Co3 decreased broadly, whereas 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut showed the stress module without any mt-RNA reaching FDR<0.05. 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA showed intermediate patterns. Because mitochondrial scRNA-seq counts can reflect RNA abundance, mitochondrial mass, stress, or capture effects, these data do not directly assay respiratory complex activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grm7 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not produce an FDR-resolved transcriptomic footprint in the expected class-C metabotropic glutamate receptor and G alpha(i/o) signaling readouts: Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Prkaca, Creb1, Pde4a, Cacna1a, Cacna1b, Kcnj3, Kcnj6, Fos, Arc, and Npas4 showed no resolved induction or repression. Although curated pathway context places GRM7 in group-III mGlu and G alpha(i/o) signaling, these mRNA features were not mobilized here, cautioning against using them as pharmacodynamic biomarkers in this dataset; the assay also does not test second messengers, ion currents, CREB phosphorylation, or presynaptic release probability.

Lrrc7 perturbation did not produce detectable acute mRNA changes in the mGluR5/DISC1/CaV1.2 postsynaptic localization axis: Grm5, Disc1, Cacna1c, Cacna1d, Camk2a, Camk2b, Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Dlg4, Actn4, Ctnnd2, and Shank3 were unchanged across all Lrrc7 cell classes. This suggests that short-term LRRC7 loss is more consistent with altered PSD organization, receptor trafficking, or localization than with immediate receptor-gene transcription, and it cautions that Grm5 transcript abundance is unlikely to be a useful acute biomarker. The assay cannot assess mGluR5 or CaV1.2 localization, phosphorylation, or rescue by CDPPB.

Camk2g perturbation in the basal Perturb-seq state did not robustly suppress the Ca2+/calmodulin–CaMKII–CREB immediate-early gene program. Canonical activity-regulated markers including Fos, Arc, Bdnf, Egr1, Npas4, and Creb1 showed only scattered nominal changes, with no FDR-supported downregulation, indicating an uncoupled or weak basal downstream response. This result is compatible with an activity-gated γCaMKII nuclear-shuttle model but does not demonstrate it as a resting single-cell transcriptomic output, especially since the assay was not an evoked Ca2+ or neuronal-activity condition and the marker check was targeted rather than a full CREB regulon analysis.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Xiap perturbation in 22 tested mouse brain cell classes, including diverse glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, showed no significant induction of the canonical XIAP-associated apoptosis or inflammatory modules at baseline: curated Birc/caspase transcripts such as Birc2, Birc3, Birc5, Casp3, Casp7, Casp8, and Casp9, and NOD/RIPK/NF-kB genes including Nod1, Nod2, Ripk1, Ripk2, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rela, Rel, and Relb remained nonsignificant. Xiap signatures also correlated only weakly with Fas, Tnfrsf1a/b, Tlr2/3/4/5/7/8/9, Nfkb1/2, Cyld, Map3k7, Tbk1, Rel, Relb, Traf3, or Bcl2 perturbations, consistent with stimulus- and protein-state-dependent XIAP functions; only transcripts were measured, the panel was manually selected, and no SMAC, cytochrome-c, NOD, TNF, or TLR stimulation was applied.

Fyn showed no convergent mRNA signature with available perturbations in its expected postsynaptic and disease-adjacent network: same-cell-type single-cell DE correlations were near zero versus Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Dlg4, Ncam1, App, Mapt, Prnp, Reln, Dab1, and PI3K components Pik3ca, Pik3cb, and Pik3r1. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Pik3ca was nominally down with Fyn perturbation, but pathway-neighbor signatures remained globally uncorrelated. This null pattern is tempered by noisy all-gene Pearson comparisons, stronger on-target repression for several comparators than for Fyn, and the absence of close Src-family paralog perturbations.

Lyst perturbation did not produce a recurrent canonical lysosome or autophagy transcriptional response: across a curated 26-gene panel, no FDR-significant changes were detected, and genes such as Tfeb, Rab27a, and Ap3b1 were especially weak. This uncoupling was seen despite nominal Lyst decreases in several neuronal cell types, including 155 MB Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. The result suggests that steady-state mRNA for Lamp1/2, cathepsins, Rab effectors, AP-3 components, and autophagy markers may not report the primary LYST defect, although the small mRNA-based panel cannot assess organelle size, lysosomal pH, protease activity, or secretory-granule exocytosis.

Cplx2 perturbation did not expose a SNARE-dependent synaptic vesicle exocytosis transcript module in this dataset. Across nuclei, Cplx2 signatures did not significantly change Cplx1, Snap25, Stx1a/Stx1b, Vamp1/Vamp2, Syp, Syn1/Syn2, Stxbp1, Syt1/Syt2, or Unc13a/Unc13b, and Cplx2 showed no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor, including among presynaptic comparators such as Cplx1, Snap25, Stx1b, Stxbp1, Syn1/2, Syp, Syt2, Unc13a/b, and Vamp1. This null pattern was seen in L4-5 IT CTX glutamatergic, Pvalb GABAergic, and TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic cells, although Stxbp1 itself was responsive in L4-5 IT. Because the readout is nuclear mRNA abundance, acute presynaptic release defects or local synaptic protein changes could have been missed.

Sv2a loss did not produce a coordinated transcript-level response in a curated synaptic-vesicle/SNARE-neighbor panel under the sampled conditions. Representative vesicle, release, calcium-sensor, complexin, and GABA-synthesis genes, including Syp, Snap25, Stx1b, Vamp1, Syn1/2/3, Cplx1/2, Syt2, Unc13a, Stxbp1, and Gad1, were not significantly changed after Sv2a perturbation, arguing against a simple compensatory mRNA program for the vesicle-release apparatus. This negative result is limited to transcript measurements and does not test the paralogs SV2B or SV2C.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Snca knockdown, including in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and across all Snca-tested cell types, did not significantly change measured transcripts in the canonical SNARE/synaptic-vesicle program or Parkinson-neighbor genes at FDR 0.05. Genes such as Syn1, Syn2, Syn3, Syp, Snap25, Stx1b, Stxbp1, Cplx1, Cplx2, Nsf, Vamp1, Dnajc5, Rab3a, Vps35, Atp13a2, Park7, App, and Prkn remained essentially unchanged, even where Snca itself was strongly reduced. This negative transcriptional result does not exclude effects on protein abundance, localization, vesicle cycling, or unmeasured genes.

Trp53 perturbation did not detectably engage a canonical p53 stress-response transcriptional program in these basal brain cells. Across signatures, no conventionally significant transcriptome response was observed, and classic p53 effector transcripts for cell-cycle arrest, DNA damage, apoptosis, and feedback control—including Cdkn1a, Mdm2, Bax, Bbc3, Pmaip1, Gadd45a, Ddb2, Ccng1, Zmat3, and Perp—were unchanged, so the few nominal hits should not be interpreted as active p53 signaling. This result is limited to transcript abundance, as p53 can also act through protein stabilization, post-translational regulation, and stimulus-dependent enhancers.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rora loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells selectively engaged a narrow slice of the RORE-governed circadian transcription program: Nr1d1 and Cry2 were significantly reduced, while Arntl/Bmal1, Dbp, Clock, Nr1d2, Tef, Hlf, Cry1, Per2, and Per3 did not pass FDR. Thus, the visible clock response was a partial downstream downregulation rather than a wholesale BMAL1-CLOCK oscillator collapse. Because this was not a circadian time course, the lack of FDR signal for Arntl or Dbp in this sampling context does not exclude rhythmic regulation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gabrd depletion in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class produced strong on-target knockdown but no significant compensatory mRNA change in other assayed GABA-A receptor subunits, including Gabra1/2/3/4/5, Gabrb1/2/3, Gabrg2/3, and Gabrr2, nor in Gad1, Gad2, or Slc6a1. This pattern is consistent with effects on GABA-A receptor composition, localization, or conductance rather than broad inhibitory-pathway transcriptional remodeling over the sampled interval, although only the named transcripts were tested and compensation could be post-transcriptional or occur outside the assay window.

Relb perturbation showed no detectable NF-kB output in this basal neuronal Perturb-seq dataset: across all 23 assayed neuronal cell classes, NF-kB feedback and inflammatory effector genes including Nfkbia, Nfkbib, Nfkbiz, Tnfaip3, Birc2, Birc3, Traf1, Ccl2, Cxcl10, Il6, and Tnf remained unchanged, and there was likewise no evident Relb-dependent signal in the noncanonical NF-kB p100/p52-RelB pathway context involving Nfkb2, Chuk, Traf3, Nfkb1, and Rel. This fits a caveat that the experiment appears unstimulated and neuronal, whereas RelB biology is often described in receptor-stimulated settings.

Nin showed a transcriptional response that was largely orthogonal to the available ciliogenesis and centrosome disease-family perturbations, rather than converging on a general centrosome- or cilium-loss state. Across 232 correlations with Cep83, Cep164, Cep290, Cep120, Dzip1, Bbs5, Ift88, Kif3b, Rpgrip1l, Ttc8, and Tuba1a, the mean absolute correlation was only 0.0226 and the maximum was 0.145. This suggests Nin was transcriptionally uncoupled from distal-appendage, transition-zone, IFT, BBSome, and tubulin-associated perturbations in this dataset, although direct paralog or subdistal-appendage comparators were not included and the readout was RNA signatures rather than centrosome imaging.

Stra6 perturbation showed no detectable transcriptomic engagement of the expected retinoid-transport, RAR/RXR, or STRA6-coupled JAK/STAT programs: Rbp4, Rbp1, Ttr, Lrat, Rdh10, Cyp26a1, Aldh1a2, Aldh1a3, Crabp1/2, Rara/Rarb/Rarg, Rxra/Rxrb/Rxrg, Stat1/3/5a/5b, Socs3, Fos, and Jun all lacked a corrected response. In the 145 MH-LH TH Glut comparator context, Stra6 also did not converge with RAR/RXR perturbations or any strong all-target neighbor.
