This null result is limited to steady-state mRNA, without retinol, retinoic acid, receptor phosphorylation, or STAT phosphorylation measurements.

Epha6 knockdown did not produce a coordinated transcriptional shift in the measured Eph/ephrin receptor signaling and axon guidance neighborhood: across 31 assayed ligands, receptors, and canonical downstream genes, including Efna1/2/3/4/5, Efnb1/2/3, Epha1/2/3/4/5/7/8/10, Ephb1/2/3/4/6, Fyn, Nck1/2, Rac1, Rhoa, Pak1/2/3, Mapk1, and Mapk3, no row reached FDR < 0.05. This leaves the curated module indistinguishable from background, consistent with contact-dependent or post-translational Eph signaling, while noting that phosphorylation, receptor clustering, axonal localization, and cell-cell contact outputs were not measured.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Unc13c perturbation showed no coherent transcriptional compensation in a candidate presynaptic vesicle-priming and exocytosis panel across the assayed neuronal strata, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types. Genomewide differential expression found no FDR-significant response in any stratum, and the panel spanning Unc13a/b/c, Rims1/2, Stxbp1, Stx1a/b, Snap25, Syt1/2, Cplx1/2, Syp, Rab3a, and Ca2+ channel subunits remained transcriptionally uncoupled from Unc13c, with no convergence across Unc13 paralogs. This negative result is limited by weak target engagement and the use of a candidate-gene panel rather than formal pathway enrichment.

Ndufa10 depletion did not produce an FDR-significant ATF4-integrated mitochondrial stress/ISR transcriptional program in this screen: Atf4, Atf5, Ddit3, Asns, Chac1, Slc2a3, Sod2, and the rest of a 27-gene marker check remained below correction. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, a few stress-related or mitochondrial genes were only nominal and isolated, including nominal Timm44 and Ndufb10 decreases in 155 MB Glut. Because ISR genes can be sparse in single-cell data and ATF4 protein was not measured, these results favor no immediate canonical neuronal ISR rather than excluding later, post-transcriptional, metabolic, or threshold effects.

Dnajc6 CRISPRi did not produce a coherent mRNA response in the canonical HSPA8/auxilin clathrin-coated-vesicle uncoating or synaptic-vesicle recycling machinery: across 22 tested cell classes, no genome-wide effects survived multiple-testing correction, and direct checks found Dnajc6, Gak, Hspa8, Cltc, Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Dnm1, Dnm2, Synj1, Syp, Snap25, Sv2a, Syn1/2/3, Bin1, Dnajc5, Vamp1, and Unc13a all FDR-negative downstream of Dnajc6. This suggests the pathway readout here was not transcriptional, with the caveat that the panel was manually curated and transcript-only, so vesicle uncoating, clathrin cages, and synaptic-vesicle proteins were not measured directly.

Prkaca depletion showed no detected mRNA response in the canonical PKA–CREB/MECP2 activity-regulated transcription axis: Creb1, Crem, Mecp2, and activity-linked genes Bdnf, Fos, Egr1, Arc, Npas4, and Nr4a1 were not FDR-significant, even with strong Prkaca knockdown in several cell classes. This suggests that, in this unstimulated steady-state assay, loss of Prkaca transcript was uncoupled from an immediate transcript-level readout of basal PKA signaling, while leaving open regulation through phosphorylation or responses that would require cAMP stimulation or neuronal depolarization.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Erf perturbation did not phenocopy ERK/MAPK pathway perturbation in this dataset: across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Erf signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Braf, Mapk1, Map2k1, and Map2k2, even though Braf and Map2k1 produced corrected Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5-centered responses and other MAPK comparators showed significant engagement. This suggests that the measured RAF/MEK/ERK phenotypes were not detectably routed through ERF here, although weak Erf target engagement could also explain the apparent uncoupling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Fgfr3 loss was neutral in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where a neuronal MAPK-output module marked by Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, and Atp2a2 was readily detected and down-regulated after Map2k1, Braf, and Ntrk2 perturbation. This suggests the null Fgfr3 result was pathway-selective rather than an assay-wide failure to capture ERK/MAPK-linked transcription, although the convergent module was observed in only this neuronal subclass, and Ntrk2 is not an FGFR-family member.

Osmr perturbation did not detectably engage canonical OSMR or IL-31 signaling in 14 tested glutamatergic classes and 8 tested GABA classes: genome-wide summaries found no FDR-significant differentially expressed genes, and expected downstream SOCS/JAK/STAT, MAPK, PI3K/AKT, and inflammatory markers including Stat1, Stat3, Socs3, Fos, Jun, Jak1, Jak2, Tyk2, Mapk1, Mapk3, Akt1, Bcl3, Ccl2, Cxcl1, Vegfa, Il6st, and Il31ra showed no supported response. This suggests the perturbation was uncoupled from an active cytokine pathway in these basal neuronal contexts, although transcript readouts are indirect and the negative result could reflect absent ligand stimulation or ineffective Osmr perturbation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Adrb1 did not behave like a canonical upstream ADRB1→Gs→cAMP/MAPK perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons: whole-transcriptome correlations with Gnas, Adcy1/3/5, Prkaca, Creb1, Map2k1, and the paralogs Adrb2 and Adrb3 were near zero. In this thalamic class, downstream Prkaca, Creb1, and Map2k1 perturbations produced corrected signatures while Adrb1 did not, indicating an uncoupled or buffered response rather than a simple loss-of-upstream-cAMP transcriptome. Because Adrb1 itself was weakly engaged and Adrb2/Adrb3 were also unengaged, the lack of correlation cannot cleanly separate biological divergence from insufficient receptor knockdown.

Edem3 perturbation did not produce coherent transcriptional remodeling of the measured glycoprotein ER-associated degradation and unfolded protein response module: across 21 Edem3 tests, Edem1, Edem2, Os9, Sel1l, Derl1, Derl2, Derl3, Syvn1, Dnajb9, Hspa5, Xbp1, Atf4, and Ddit3 showed no FDR-level response. This leaves the ERAD/UPR transcript module effectively uncoupled from partial Edem3 knockdown at the mRNA level, although paralog-level comparisons were limited because Edem1 and Edem2 were not perturbed, and glycan intermediates, ERAD flux, and Xbp1 splicing were not measured.

Ifih1 showed near-zero full-transcriptome correlation with available antiviral RNA-sensing and type I interferon pathway perturbations, including Adar, Ifnar1, Ifnar2, Irf3, Irf7, Nfkb1, Stat1, Stat2, Tbk1, Tlr3, and Traf3, in matched neuronal cell types. Across all 22 Ifih1-sampled neuronal classes, there was no detectable target depletion, FDR-controlled downstream expression, recurrent nominal genes, or convergence with these comparators, suggesting that basal neuronal Ifih1 does not behave as an interchangeable IFIH1 pathway module. This comparison is limited because Ddx58, Dhx58, and Mavs were not available, and most signatures were weak.

Nefl knockdown did not produce a detectable transcript-level response in the curated NMDA receptor postsynaptic anchoring and long-term potentiation neighborhood: representative genes including Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Grin2c, Dlg4, Camk2a, Camk2b, Rasgrp1, Raf1, Mapk1, and Mapk3 were not significantly changed, with minimum FDR reported as 1.0 across Nefl perturbations. This negative result narrows interpretation of NEFL-related Reactome links to GRIN1/PSD biology, but it is based on a targeted gene check and steady-state mRNA, so effects on receptor anchoring, phosphorylation, currents, or synaptic physiology could still be present.

Strada perturbation produced transcriptomic signatures that were largely orthogonal to mTORopathy and AMPK-family perturbations, with near-zero all-gene correlations to Tsc1, Tsc2, Mtor, Rptor, Pten, Depdc5, Brsk2, Prkaa2, Prkag2, and Mark3 across matched cell types. In 155 MB Glut and 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, even the most engaged Strada signatures showed no detectable transcriptional feedback in canonical mTORC1 or AMPK pathway transcripts, suggesting the expected LKB1-STRAD-MO25/AMPK-mTOR axis was buffered or uncoupled at the RNA level; however, most Strada signatures were weak, and these comparisons rely on RNA scores rather than p-S6, kinase activity, cell size, or migration phenotypes.

Nfkb2 perturbation was uncoupled from canonical and noncanonical NF-κB sentinel RNAs: across 22 Nfkb2 cell classes, transcripts including Nfkbia, Nfkbib, Nfkbid, Nfkbie, Tnfaip3, Birc3, Relb, Nfkb1, Rel, Bcl3, Map3k14, Chuk, and Traf-family genes showed no detectable induction or repression. This absence of Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Birc3, Relb, Map3k14, Traf, and Chuk responses argues against a downstream inflammatory NF-κB program in these cells, although the readout was limited to a small RNA panel and did not assess p100 processing, RelB:p52 nuclear localization, or stimulus responsiveness.

Grik4 showed weak target engagement in this dataset: across the same 22 cell classes, its self-transcript was measured but not reproducibly depleted, whereas several related glutamate-receptor and postsynaptic perturbations showed stronger on-target depletion, including Grin1, Grin2b, Gria2, Grik5, Grik3, Dlg4, and Shank3. This suggests the weak Grik4 response is not simply a general inability to knock down synaptic membrane receptors here, although the comparison is based on RNA self-knockdown rather than matched protein or electrophysiology, and Grik1 and Grik2 were also weakly engaged.

Syt2 perturbation reduced Syt2 itself but did not produce FDR-significant transcriptional changes in measured presynaptic partner genes, including synaptic-vesicle, SNARE, active-zone, and excitability genes such as Snap25, Stx1b, Vamp1, Cplx1/2, Syn1/2/3, Syp, Unc13a/b/c, Cadps2, Dnm1, Dlg4, and Syt14. This was most evident in 155 MB Glut and also in 052 Pvalb Gaba, where knockdown was secure yet secondary responses were absent or weak, suggesting pathway membership reflects biochemical vesicle trafficking or fast calcium-dependent exocytosis rather than a coordinated mRNA module. Only assayed transcripts were evaluated, and Syt1, Vamp2, and Stx1a were not included as perturbation comparators here.

Med12 did not transcriptionally converge with TGF-β receptor–SMAD perturbations in the mouse brain atlas: across matched brain cell classes, Med12 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Smad2, Smad3, Acvr1, Acvr2a, and Acvr2b, with all-gene correlations near zero and top-200 restricted correlations remaining weak. Thus, TGF-β/BMP receptor and downstream SMAD perturbations did not phenocopy Med12 transcriptomes in the assayed mature mouse brain cells, although these weak signatures and the correlative nature of the analysis do not directly measure pathway activity.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Lonp1 showed a stronger Ddit3-centered stress response than related mitochondrial proteostasis targets in 155 MB Glut and 217 P MY Pineal Glut: perturbing Clpp, Clpx, Afg3l2, Hspd1, or Yme1l1 did not phenocopy the Lonp1-associated Ddit3/Shmt2/Aldh1l2 module, which also included markers such as Chac1, Slc7a5, and Slc7a1. This suggests the response was not a generic consequence of disrupting any mitochondrial proteostasis gene in these cells, although the comparison relied on a six-gene restricted stress score and comparator counts in 217 P MY Pineal Glut were sometimes only 20–33 cells.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ext1 did not transcriptionally phenocopy Ext2 or related heparan-sulfate perturbations: across 22 matched cell types, Ext1-versus-Ext2 score correlations were near zero, and in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut, Ext2 showed corrected self-knockdown with little broader program, whereas Ext1 was only nominally down in some contexts. Candidate HS biosynthesis genes B3gat3, Glce, Hs6st2, Xylt1, proteoglycans Agrn and Gpc6, and HS-dependent Hedgehog/Wnt receptors such as Smo, Ptch1/2, Fzd2/3/4/6/9, and Cspg4 did not phenocopy the Ext1 profile; this contrast is transcriptomic, cell-type-specific, and likely influenced by unequal target engagement rather than biochemical independence of EXT1 and EXT2.

Rdx perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptional response in the queried GABAA receptor anchoring or L1/CAM recycling modules: Gabra1, Gabra2, Gabra3, Gabra4, Gabra5, Gabrb3, Gabrg2, Gabrd, Gphn, and the adhesion-related genes L1cam, Ank2, Ank3, Chl1, Cntn1, Ncam1, and Nrcam all remained unchanged, with reported FDR = 1.0. This negative result suggests RDX-linked neuronal membrane functions may be transcriptionally uncoupled and more consistent with trafficking or surface organization, although these mRNAs are only proxies and protein surface pools were not assayed.

Gaa knockdown did not phenocopy related glycogen, mannose-6-phosphate trafficking, lysosomal, or mTOR-autophagy perturbations: curated neighbors such as Epm2a, Lamp2, Gnptab, Gnptg, Manba, Ppt1, Ctsb, Tsc1, Tsc2, Mtor, Atg5, and Atg16l1 were only weakly or not correlated with Gaa, and broader TFEB/autophagy-lysosome compensation markers including Tfeb, Tfe3, Mcoln1, Lamp1, Sqstm1, and Map1lc3b were not induced. This was seen in Gaa-engaged cell types such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, although several close comparators, especially Epm2a and Gnptab, had poor self-knockdown, so the result is strongest as a lack of phenocopy among available signatures rather than proof the pathways never intersect.

Epor perturbation in all 22 Epor-profiled neuronal classes did not produce the expected canonical EPOR transcriptional program: steady-state mRNAs in JAK/STAT, PI3K/AKT, MAPK, and feedback branches, including Jak2, Stat5b, Stat3, Socs1/2/3, Cish, Pim1/2, Bcl2, Bcl2l1, Akt1/2/3, and Mapk1/3, were not FDR-significant, and Epor score vectors were not similar to perturbations of Stat1/2/3/4/5b or cytokine-family receptors such as Mpl, Csf1r, Csf3r, Il21r, and Il23r. This argues against reading the neuronal Epor signatures as a standard JAK2/STAT5 output, although acute phosphorylation or ligand-dependent signaling could have been missed by the steady-state mRNA assay.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lrrc7 showed a weaker, largely uncorrelated transcriptional response than PSD/NMDAR/CaMKII neighbor perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. While Grin1, Nrxn1, Grin2b, Camk2b, Adam22, Dlg4, Ctnnd2, Grin2a, and Shank3 produced strong self-knockdown in the same dataset, Lrrc7 was only nominal and remained non-significant after adjustment, and neither unbiased nor related-gene searches identified a robust transcriptomic neighbor. Score-vector correlations with other perturbations were weak, with direct PSD-neighbor correlations near zero, although this contrast may partly reflect weaker Lrrc7 knockdown; Adam22 is included as a synaptic comparator rather than an established direct LRRC7 interactor.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Prkag2 was transcriptionally muted in this Perturb-seq assay and did not resemble the TSC branch of mTORC1 signaling: unlike Tsc1/Tsc2, which produced hundreds of significant changes, especially in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Prkag2, Prkaa2, Rptor, and most Mtor perturbations were largely quiet. In 155 MB Glut, Tsc1/Tsc2 induced signatures including Cpeb1, Stmn4, Atp6v0b, Pik3r3, Cyp51, and Insig1, while Prkag2 showed no FDR-significant response; similar contrast was seen in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. Weak nominal Prkag2 effects did not directionally align with AMPK or mTOR comparators, although absent Prkag2 engagement or guide efficacy differences could explain the contrast.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Camk2b knockdown was largely uncoupled from the NMDA receptor transcriptional programs seen after Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b perturbation. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Camk2b showed strong or FDR-level target engagement but essentially target-only signatures, whereas GRIN perturbations produced tens of non-self hits, including genes such as Scg2, Stmn4, Kctd16, Gpm6a, Erc2, Nptx2, Cckbr, Bdnf, Kcnv1, and Vgf. This comparison is transcriptomic rather than a biochemical test, and GRIN perturbations differed in target gene, cell number, and knockdown magnitude; notably, Grin2a in 007 showed downstream hits without FDR-level self-knockdown.

Lrrtm1 perturbation did not reveal a broad transcriptional homeostatic response: Cadm1/SynCAM1, Lrrtm2-4, neurexins (Nrxn1-3), neuroligins (Nlgn1-3), and PSD-related genes including Dlg4, Grid1, Grid2, Shank2, and Shank3 showed no adjusted-significant induction or repression in the profiled classes. This suggests that reported buffering by SynCAM1 or LRRTM2 may not appear as a pan-cell-class mRNA feedback loop here, but the interpretation is limited because the matched dataset showed weak Lrrtm1 target-transcript engagement and prior SynCAM1 results came from a non-matched mouse PFC time point.

Fas showed no meaningful transcriptomic similarity to assayed TNF receptor superfamily members or downstream NF-kappaB/MAPK pathway perturbations in this unstimulated mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset. Correlations between Fas and Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Tnfrsf4, Tnfrsf9, Tnfrsf11a, Tnfrsf13c, Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Chuk, Mapk8, and Mapk9 were all near zero, and the best global neighbors were trivial, with Hras at r=0.037 and Wdr26 at r=-0.036. Across Fas-covered glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, there was also no statistically supported on-target depletion, FDR<0.05 downstream effect, or DISC/NF-kappaB/JNK transcriptional activation; because many signatures were weak and correlations used signed Wilcoxon scores, the main conclusion is lack of detectable convergence rather than mechanistic antagonism.

Trp73 perturbation did not detectably regulate canonical p73 outputs in this assay: no transcriptome-wide FDR-significant genes were found in any assayed cell type, and targeted checks showed no adjusted-significant changes in TP53-family apoptotic transcription genes such as Cdkn1a, Bax, Bbc3, Pmaip1, Mdm2, Fas, Apaf1, Casp1, Casp3, Casp9, or Perp, no Ngfr response in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut or 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut neurons, and no Foxj1/Rfx2/3/4 multiciliogenesis program. Because target engagement was weak, this argues against a pathway readout in the assay rather than against pathway dependence under true p73 loss.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Katnip perturbation did not engage the expected ciliary, CILK1, or katanin transcriptional neighborhood across 22 tested neuronal classes, including glutamatergic and GABAergic populations such as L5-6 IT Glut, CA3/CA2-FC DG Glut, Pvalb Gaba, Sst Gaba, and CB GABA. Among 18 measured readouts including Ahi1, Arl13b, Cep164, Cilk1, Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Katna1, and Katnb1, there were no recurrent FDR-supported shifts, and related CEP/IFT perturbations were also largely silent. This negative result is consistent with biology that is structural or post-translational rather than reflected in neuronal mRNA, since the assay does not capture cilia number, ultrastructure, CILK1 phosphorylation, or protein localization.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Uba5 perturbation produced a selective ER-stress output centered on Ddit3, with Atf4 significant in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, rather than a broad canonical Hspa5/Xbp1 unfolded-protein-response program. This pattern was seen across responsive classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Ddit3 induction recurred, while Hspa5 and Xbp1 were mostly not significant and Calr decreased in 151. Because this is a 3-prime scRNA differential-expression readout, Xbp1 splicing and acute ER stress were not directly measured.

Mib1 showed a transcriptomic phenotype that was largely uncoupled from canonical Delta/Jagged-Notch transcriptional output in this adult neuronal Perturb-seq assay. Measured Notch pathway components and targets, including Dll1, Jag1, Notch1-3, Rbpj, Maml1, Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Hey2, Heyl, Dtx1-4, and Nrarp, were not detectably remodeled by Mib1 perturbation, and available Dll1, Notch1-4, Adam10, and App perturbations did not reproduce the Mib1 sterol-panel signature. This refines rather than rules out the usual MIB1-Notch interpretation, because adult neuronal classes, weak target-transcript depletion, and an mRNA-centric monoculture-like readout could miss ligand-sending effects or lowly expressed Notch transcripts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Map1lc3a showed a buffered, self-only transcriptomic response despite strong on-target depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where the only FDR-significant gene was Map1lc3a itself. In overlapping thalamic or midbrain classes, autophagy-neighbor perturbations Rb1cc1, Becn1, Atg5, and Depdc5 produced secondary FDR-level genes, including Calr, Hspa5, Pdia6, Psma5, Dnm1, Ctsb, Rtn1, Pik3r1, Ldlr, Insig1, and Hmgcs1, suggesting the null Map1lc3a transcriptome is specific to the LC3A/ATG8 layer rather than a general feature of neuronal macroautophagy perturbation, although guide efficiency, target expression, and downstream biology differ across perturbations.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Slc6a1 knockdown in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 053 Sst Gaba showed no detectable compensatory mRNA changes in GABA synthesis and vesicular loading genes or the inhibitory synapse receptor and release network: Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Abat, Stx1a, Snap25, Syt1, Gabra1, Gabrb2, Gabrg2, Gabbr1, Gabbr2, and Gphn were not altered at FDR. Direct Gad1, Gad2, or Slc32a1 perturbations were likewise mostly self-only, suggesting pathway adjacency did not yield interchangeable transcriptomic signatures, although this comparison is limited to mRNA and not metabolic flux or receptor function.

Drd3 showed near-zero global score correlations with related D2-like dopamine receptor and Gi-Go/adenylate-cyclase signaling perturbations in this dataset, rather than forming a meaningful shared transcriptional neighborhood. Drd2 was only weakly positive globally, while Drd4 and Gnao1 were essentially uncorrelated, and the full Drd3-versus-target correlation range was only -0.022 to 0.036 across comparators including Drd5, Adcy1, Adcy5, Adora2a, Gnas, Pde10a, Safe_target_22, and Ephb1. This is a transcriptomic-score contrast, so weak Drd3 engagement could mask true receptor-family relationships.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp2b1 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type showed only weak convergence with Atp2a2/SERCA2: Atp2a2 knockdown produced a much larger 187-gene signature, with overlap limited to five FDR genes, including Chml, Fos, Vgf, Gpr88, and Xylt2. In contrast, Atp2a2 uniquely induced ER-stress and unfolded-protein-response markers Ddit3, Xbp1, Hspa5, and Chac1, a program absent from the smaller Atp2b1 response. This comparison is limited to one cell type and is based on transcript signatures rather than direct ER calcium or unfolded-protein-response assays.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp2b3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut appeared transcriptionally uncoupled from related calcium pumps: despite significant on-target depletion, Atp2b3 produced no nonself FDR<0.05 genes, like Atp2b2, whereas Atp2b1 produced 21 and Atp2a2 produced 186. Score-vector correlations between Atp2b3 and Atp2b1, Atp2b2, or Atp2a2 were near zero, and markers seen with Atp2a2 or Atp2b1 responses, including Ddit3, Xbp1, Hspa5, Chac1, Fos, and Chml, were not induced by Atp2b3. This divergence is strongest in this shared cell type and is based on transcriptomic, not direct calcium-transport, readouts.

Traf3 showed essentially no transcriptomic convergence with available TNFR/NF-kappa-B/TBK1 pathway-neighbor perturbations: score-vector correlations with Cd40, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Relb, Chuk, Tbk1, and Cyld were near zero globally and never exceeded |r|=0.0878 within any cell type. Thus, despite pathway annotations placing TRAF3 in TNFR/NIK/TBK1 interaction space, no shared Traf3-like state or detectable non-canonical NF-kappa-B/NIK signal was seen. This remains a negative screen result, because the comparator perturbations also lacked transcriptome-wide significant hits.

Tnfrsf1a perturbation did not produce a detectable canonical TNFR1 transcriptional response in this unstimulated dataset: NF-kappaB and cytokine-associated genes such as Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Nfkb1, Rela, Ikbkg, Tab2, Tab3, Ccl2, Cxcl10, and Il6, as well as death-domain and apoptotic markers including Casp8, Birc2, and Birc3, were not significantly induced or repressed. Thus, expected TRADD-RIPK1-TRAF-IKK and caspase-8-linked outputs appeared uncoupled at the transcript level here, although TNF ligand challenge or protein, phosphorylation, secretion, or cell-death assays could still reveal pathway competence.

Cacng3 perturbation did not produce a coordinated transcriptional AMPAR/TARP/postsynaptic response across the 22 tested neuronal classes: in a 12-gene panel spanning Cacng2, Cacng3, Cacng8, Gria1–4, Dlg4, Grip1, Shank2, Shank3, and Frrs1l, no rows were FDR-significant and only a small minority were nominal. The weakest cell-type-specific hints were in L5-6 IT Glut and Sst Gaba, where nominal outliers lacked FDR support. Thus, despite Cacng3’s curated role in AMPAR trafficking and gating, this dataset shows no compensatory Gria/Cacng/Dlg4/Shank mRNA module; however, this is a panel-based negative result and post-translational receptor trafficking was not measured.

Flt3 perturbation did not produce a coordinated mRNA response in canonical FLT3 signaling components: transcripts in the GRB2/SOS, PTPN11/GAB2/STAT5, and PI3K/MTOR arms, including Grb2, Sos1, Ptpn11, Stat5a, Stat5b, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Mtor, Mapk1, and Mapk3, all showed no significant or directionally coherent change, with the proximal effector set uniformly at FDR=1.0. This pattern is consistent with pathway inactivity or transcriptional uncoupling rather than a missed downstream module, although the assay measured mRNA only, so weak phosphorylation-dependent signaling could have occurred without detectable transcriptional changes.

Bbs9 did not transcriptionally phenocopy related BBSome or ciliary transport perturbations in these neurons: whole-signature correlations with Ttc8, Bbs5, Bbip1, Lztfl1, Ift88, Ift81, Kif3b, and Cep290 stayed near zero, with the largest absolute related-target correlation only 0.152, despite their close physical and pathway coupling in the BBSome-mediated cargo targeting to cilium network. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, Bbs9 had the highest perturbed-cell count, yet Bbs9 itself was not reduced and Cluap1 changed only nominally, consistent with a low-engagement or buffered negative profile. Because these related perturbations were themselves weak at the corrected differential-expression level, the nonconvergence could reflect technical limits or post-transcriptional biology rather than true divergence among complex members.

Zfp451 showed no robust pathway activation or repression in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset: the expected SUMO2/3–PML, TGF-beta/SMAD, and SATB2-linked programs were not recovered as transcriptional modules, with little or no change in Pml, Sumo1/2/3, Smad2/3/4/7, Tgfbr1/2, or Satb2. Compared directly with Smad2, Smad4, Tgfbr2, and Bmpr2 perturbations, Zfp451 had weak signatures and no high-correlation neighbor. This null result is qualified by a weak guide response, RNA-only readout, and the absence of TGF-beta, proteotoxic, or DNA-damage stimulation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Itpr1 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic cells did not phenocopy Atp2a2 loss: despite a larger perturbed-cell count and nominal on-target depletion, Itpr1 produced no FDR-significant transcriptional changes, whereas Atp2a2 knockdown triggered 187 FDR-significant genes, including Ddit3, Xbp1, Hspa5, and Chac1, consistent with a strong ER calcium homeostasis/stress-response signature. This suggests that ER Ca2+ refilling by SERCA2 and IP3-gated ER Ca2+ release were not interchangeable in this assay, although the two perturbations differed in knockdown magnitude and cell counts.

Irf3 knockdown did not detectably mobilize the canonical type-I-interferon/antiviral program in the assayed neurons: Ifnb1, Ifit1, Ifit2, Ifit3, Isg15, Rsad2, Usp18, and Cxcl10 showed no significant induction or repression, even in the highest-cell-count 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contrast where Irf3 transcript reduction was strongest and no FDR-significant genes were found. This suggests the sampled neuronal states were not dependent on the canonical antiviral module in this assay, although the inference is limited by weak Irf3 knockdown and the absence of viral, dsRNA, DNA, or LPS stimulation.

Ntrk3 perturbation produced no FDR-significant mRNA changes in a curated canonical NTF3-NTRK3 signaling panel, including Ntf3, Shc1, Grb2, Plcg1, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Akt1/2/3, Mapk1/3, Braf, and Raf1, with only sparse cell-type responses noted in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA. This suggests the Perturb-seq RNA readout was poorly coupled to immediate TrkC signaling and should not be taken as evidence that RAS, PI3K/AKT, or PLC pathways were shut down, since the assay was marker-based and these pathways are primarily reflected in phosphorylation and localization rather than steady-state mRNA.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Eda did not phenocopy Edar or intracellular NF-kappaB-neighborhood perturbations in the assayed brain cell classes. Across 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 155 MB Glut, Eda whole-transcriptome response vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Edar, Chuk, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Rel, Relb, and TNF-receptor controls Tnfrsf1a/b. The only receptor-level FDR hits in this neighborhood were Edar-specific—Zmym3 in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and Rptor in 155 MB Glut—and were absent from Eda, consistent with dataset uncoupling and possibly weak Eda target engagement rather than biochemical disproof.

Prkaa2 did not show a convergent transcriptomic signature with the canonical AMPK heterotrimer or the LKB1–AMPK–mTORC1/autophagy axis in these perturbation data. Same-cell score correlations with Prkag2, Strada, Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1, and Tsc2 were near zero, and Prkag2, Mtor, Tsc1, Tsc2, Rptor, Ulk1, Tfeb, and Fnip1 were not corrected downstream hits; this lack of recovery was also evident across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA. The result is best read as weak pathway engagement at basal mRNA level, possible isoform redundancy, or post-translational signaling, not pathway absence.

Adrb3 was not an interchangeable transcriptional perturbation with the other β-adrenergic receptors in this assay: like Adrb1 and Adrb2, Adrb3 produced no FDR-significant gene expression changes, and across whole-transcriptome signatures it remained nearly uncorrelated with adrenergic and cAMP-pathway neighbors including Adra1a, Adra2a, Adra2b, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, and Gnas, with correlations never exceeding |r| = 0.101. In 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA cells, Adcy3 appeared engaged while Adrb3 stayed uncoupled, consistent with weak on-target engagement and the caveat that shared receptor class does not require matched loss-of-function transcriptomes.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ntrk3 did not phenocopy nearby Trk/RAS perturbations in these data. In 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, the only FDR-significant Ntrk3 response was Arhgap12 up-regulation, with only weak depletion of Ntrk3 itself, whereas Ntrk2 depleted its own transcript and reduced Akap5. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Ntrk2 and Braf converged on repression of a Vgf/Atp2a2 module, while Ntrk3 was silent. This cross-perturbation contrast, not a direct epistasis test, argues for cell-type- and paralog-specific Ntrk2/Braf coupling rather than interchangeable Trk-family effects.

Ppard perturbation did not produce a coherent PPARD/RXR nuclear-receptor or fatty-acid/lipid-metabolism signature in this dataset. Across an a priori 35-gene panel spanning Rxra/Rxrb/Rxrg, Ncoa/Ncor regulators, and canonical lipid genes such as Acox1, Cpt1a, Fabp5, Angptl4, Pdk4, Lpl, and Srebf1, there were no FDR-significant Ppard responses, and nominal hits were not recurrent enough to define a robust downstream module. This suggests the assayed basal neuronal state did not expose the expected lipid program, although low expression of some lipid genes and weak Ppard knockdown could have masked regulation.

Tuba4a knockdown did not reveal FDR-level mRNA compensation among major tubulin paralogs or selected neuronal microtubule-associated genes: Tuba1a, Tubb2a, Tubb3, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, Tubb5, Mapt, Map1b, Map6, and Stmn2 showed no significant transcriptional upregulation. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut cells, Tuba4a was reduced without a broad microtubule transcriptome response, suggesting that any alpha/beta-tubulin stoichiometry buffering was not detectable at the mRNA level in this inspected gene set and could instead involve translational, degradation, or tubulin PTM mechanisms.

Ndufaf4 showed much weaker on-target transcript depletion than many mitochondrial complex I structural subunit perturbations in this dataset: although 15 of 25 complex-I subunit or assembly-factor perturbations reduced their own transcript at FDR < 0.05, Ndufaf4 had a minimum on-target p = 0.190 with FDR = 1.0. Ndufaf2 and Ndufaf5, the other represented assembly-factor perturbations, were also transcriptome-wide FDR-silent, suggesting a target-specific or assembly-factor-related limitation rather than a global inability to detect mitochondrial gene perturbations; however, these comparators are not all at the same assembly step, and protein-level knockdown was not measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Kdr was flat in kinase-responsive neuronal cell classes, indicating no detectable VEGFR2-linked PI3K/MAPK transcriptional output from Kdr in this dataset. In 155 MB Glut, Fgfr1 and Mapk1 showed significant self-depletion while Kdr remained inactive; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Braf had four FDR-significant genes whereas Kdr had zero hits and no target depletion; and in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Braf significantly down-regulated Vgf but Kdr again showed no FDR-significant response. This null is context-specific, since other RTK/MAPK-neighbor perturbations scored, although Fgfr1, Mapk1, and Braf are not obligate KDR-complex members.

Uqcrb perturbation did not elicit a coordinated RNA-level response in mitochondrial respiratory electron transport or complex III genes in this dataset. Despite direct measurement of the target transcript, nearby complex-III and adjacent respiratory-chain genes including Cyc1, Uqcrc1, Uqcrc2, Uqcrfs1, Uqcrh, Uqcrq, Ttc19, Uqcc2, Uqcr10, Uqcr11, Ndufs1, Ndufs2, Sdha, Sdhb, Cox5a, and Cox6a1 remained FDR-null across Uqcrb contrasts, arguing against detectable ETC remodeling here, although this negative result is conditional on RNA differential expression and could also reflect ineffective Uqcrb perturbation.

Apbb2 perturbation did not coherently rewire APP/FE65 adaptor, APP-processing, sortilin, or tau-neighborhood transcripts across the profiled brain cell types. In a curated 29-gene set including App, Aplp1/2, Apbb1/3, Adam10, Bace1/2, Ncstn, Psen1/2, Psenen, Aph1a/c, Sorl1, Sort1, and Mapt, there were nominal changes but no FDR-supported gene-set signal; in 308 CB GABA cells, Ncstn and Psen1 showed only exploratory downshifts. This negative mRNA result from single-gene Perturb-seq does not exclude effects on APP cleavage, AICD/Aβ flux, or synaptic phenotypes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pik3ca showed a weak transcriptomic effect in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons: despite being the largest Pik3ca-perturbed stratum and showing the strongest nominal target-transcript depletion, it had no FDR-significant differentially expressed genes, whereas Pten, Tsc1, Tsc2, and Mtor in the same cell type had 33, 321, 86, and 2 significant genes, respectively. This pattern suggests stronger RNA-level sensitivity to the PTEN/TSC/mTOR branch than to upstream Pik3ca depletion in this thalamic class, although the between-perturbation contrast is tempered by differing guide counts and target-engagement strengths and does not imply biochemical inactivity of PIK3CA.

Syp knockdown did not show detectable mRNA compensation by synaptophysin/synaptogyrin family members or core vesicle partners in this dataset. Transcripts for Synpr, Syngr1, Syngr2, Syngr3, Vamp2, Snap25, Stxbp1, Sv2a, Syt1, Syn1, Syn2, Syn3, Cplx1, and Vamp1 remained without significant induction, arguing that any buffering of Syp in these cells is not mediated by transcriptional upregulation within the synaptic vesicle endocytosis and presynaptic SNARE neighborhood. This does not exclude constitutive redundancy, protein-level compensation, or compensation by paralogs not effectively measured here.

Chmp4b signatures were more consistently positively correlated with proteasome and V-ATPase perturbations than with most ESCRT targets, with Psmb4, Psmc5, Psmc1, Pomp, Atp6v1e1, and Atp6v1b2 ranking among the strongest recurrent neighbors, alongside ESCRT genes such as Snf8 and Vps37a. This pattern suggests a broader proteostasis and acidification-skewed endolysosomal state, not an ESCRT-only signal, and in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells it coincided with ESCRT-neighbor convergence and nominal Ptpn23 up-regulation. However, the global correlations were small and support only module-level association, not direct regulation by Chmp4b.

Nav3 did not behave like a generic axon-guidance or neuronal-adhion perturbation in this dataset: across 19 assayed comparators, including Cntn1, Dcc, L1cam, Ncam1, Robo1/2/4, Slit2, Sema/Plexin genes, and Unc5c/Unc5d, Nav3 all-gene signatures were nearly orthogonal, despite strong self-knockdown for several comparators such as Cntn1, L1cam, Ncam1, and Robo2. This suggests the Nav3 readout should not be interpreted as phenocopying those receptor or adhesion perturbations, although the Nav3 signatures were weak, Nav1/Nav2 were not assayed, and not every comparator showed strong guide engagement.

Grin2d perturbation did not produce detectable mRNA-level compensation within the NMDA receptor assembly and postsynaptic anchoring module: across 23 Grin2d signatures, Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Grin2c, Grin3a, and Dlg4 never reached FDR significance. This was most evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Grin1 appeared responsive but Grin2d remained buffered, and in 052 Pvalb Gaba, where the perturbation was essentially target-only. The result argues against transcript-level rescue by receptor stoichiometry rewiring, while leaving open compensation through trafficking, phosphorylation, protein abundance, or activity-dependent synaptic localization.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cry2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produces a narrow downstream clock response centered on Nr1d1 and Dbp rather than a full circadian transcription-translation feedback loop rewrite. In this responsive thalamic class, the only multi-gene FDR-significant signal is a downregulated clock-output module, while Nr1d2, Per1, Cry1, Per2, Arntl, Npas2, and Clock do not pass FDR; small phase-dependent changes may still be missed by the design. Bmal1 and Clock perturbations converge on Dbp/Nr1d downregulation here, whereas Cry1 diverges.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Uqcrc1 knockdown, despite significant depletion of the target transcript, did not produce an FDR-detectable mitochondrial quality-control RNA state in the best-engaged classes, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. Pink1, Prkn, Park7, integrated-stress and UPRmt markers such as Atf4, Atf5, Ddit3, Hspa9, Hspd1, Clpp, Lonp1, and mitochondrial-dynamics genes Opa1 and Yme1l1 were not FDR-modulated; complex-III partner convergence was weak, and a dopaminergic row was underpowered. This transcript-only assay may have captured a partial or early perturbation that did not reproduce pathogenic UQCRC1-variant phenotypes.

Htr1a showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to serotonin-receptor paralogs and selected Gi/o–cAMP pathway neighbors, with all-gene correlations close to zero for Htr1b, Htr1f, Htr2a, Htr2c, Htr3b, Htr7, Gnao1, Gnb1, Gnb5, Adcy3, and Adcy5, and the largest observed magnitude only around 0.12 for Adcy5. Although HTR1A is canonically placed in a 5-HT1A Gi/o adenylyl-cyclase inhibition neighborhood, these data did not show robust convergence across receptor perturbations. This interpretation is tempered by weak Htr1a signatures, unstable neighbors, and lack of validated on-target Htr1a mRNA depletion, so absent convergence may reflect failed target engagement rather than pathway insulation.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Edar showed an uncoupled pattern in this brain Perturb-seq screen: in 155 MB Glut and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, the only FDR-passing Edar-associated signals were isolated singletons, Rptor up and a weaker Zmym3 hit, and these did not recur after perturbing the ligand Eda or available NF-kB-neighbor genes Chuk, Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, and Relb, which were themselves FDR-silent. Thus the canonical EDA-EDAR TNF-receptor to NF-kB/JNK pathway was not detectably engaged in these neuronal classes, although EDARADD, TRAF6, and IKBKG were not directly targeted and ligand-receptor effects may be paracrine rather than cell-autonomous.

Mecr did not phenocopy curated mitochondrial perturbations in this screen: across 306 same-cell-type comparisons with Bckdhb, Dlat, Dld, Dlst, Etfa, Ivd, Ndufa12, Ndufaf5, Ndufs1, Ndufs2, Ndufv1, Ogdh, Pdha1, and Pdhb, the strongest transcriptome correlation was only |r|=0.121, and in the two cell types with nominal Mecr target knockdown—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba—the maximum was |r|=0.061. This argues that partial acute Mecr CRISPRi did not converge on those downstream lipoate, dehydrogenase, fatty-acid-oxidation, or complex-I states, although the comparison was limited to transcriptome correlations and did not include canonical mtFAS neighbors such as Mcat, Oxsm, Lipt1, Lipt2, or Lias.

Cox6b1 perturbation did not produce a coherent oxidative-phosphorylation transcriptional compensation program. Across all Cox6b1 tests, only 103 rows reached nominal p<0.001, representing 102 unique genes, and these nominal hits were mostly private to single cell types rather than recurring across cell types. The measured 21-gene OXPHOS panel, including Cox4i1, Cox5a, Cox5b, Cox6a1, Cox6c, Cox7a2, Cox7b, Cox7c, Cox8a, Ndufa4, Uqcrb, Uqcrc1, Uqcrc2, mt-Co1, mt-Co2, mt-Co3, mt-Cytb, mt-Atp6, mt-Atp8, and Atp5o, showed no FDR-significant changes; even in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, where adjusted p values were smallest, Cfdp1 and Pde8b remained above FDR thresholds. This was a targeted transcript check rather than a protein-complex or metabolite measurement.

Cntn1 knockdown in neuronal cells was transcriptionally uncoupled from canonical Contactin-Notch signaling: curated Notch receptors, ligands, cofactors, and targets, including Notch1, Notch2, Dtx1/2/3, Rbpj, Maml1, Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Hey2, Heyl, Nrarp, Dll1, Jag1, and Jag2, showed no FDR-supported RNA changes, with all adjusted p values reported as 1. This negative result is cell-autonomous and neuronal, so it does not test CNTN1 as a ligand acting in trans on oligodendrocytes or in mixed axon-glia contexts.

Ap4s1 did not phenocopy neighboring adaptor, clathrin, retromer, or autophagy perturbations in this Perturb-seq dataset. Unlike AP-2-related genes and Cltc, which produced corrected signatures, Ap4s1 produced none, and its score-vector correlations with Ap1b1, Ap1s2, Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Ap3b1, Ap3b2, Cltc, Vps35, Becn1, Atg5, Atg16l1, and Sqstm1 were near zero. These comparisons suggest Ap4s1 is buffered relative to AP-2 and Cltc rather than reflecting a generic clathrin/adaptor stress state, although direct same-complex inference is limited because Ap4b1, Ap4e1, and Ap4m1 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ndufb9 showed a nonconvergent transcriptomic response relative to other mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I perturbations: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, its whole-transcriptome score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with the better-engaged Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, Ndufs8, and Ndufb8 perturbations. Across these cell types, Ndufb9 depletion was largely cis-only, with the target passing FDR while trans genes and selected stress markers did not, though this comparison is based on weak, restricted single-cell Wilcoxon signatures rather than respiratory phenotypes.

Ndufa12 showed a pattern of self-transcript knockdown with little to no FDR-significant spread to other genes, consistent with a broader Nduf-family buffering pattern in mitochondrial complex I/respiratory electron transport. Across 26 Nduf-family perturbations, only 73 of 9,662,574 rows reached FDR<0.05, and 64 of those were the targeted Nduf transcript itself; even stronger knockdowns of Ndufa13, Ndufb10, and Ndufc2 rarely produced secondary mRNA changes. This same self-only pattern appeared in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, although the readout is limited to mRNA and does not exclude protein-complex, metabolic, membrane-potential, or respiration effects.

Ndufb7 showed a weaker guide-engaged transcript phenotype than several other assayed complex I subunits: its target transcript reached FDR-level depletion in fewer cell classes than Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufb8, Ndufs2, and Ndufs8. The clearest Ndufb7-engaged classes were 191 MB P MY GABA and 155 MB Glut, where Ndufb7 itself was significantly depleted but downstream RNA responses were sparse, with no correlated complex-I or stress signatures at FDR. This pattern likely reflects guide efficiency and cell-count differences, so it should not be taken to mean NDUFB7 is intrinsically less important than neighboring complex-I subunits.

Itga8 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcript changes in a targeted 23-gene panel spanning α8β1 partners and ligands, focal-adhesion components, the nephronectin–Gdnf axis, and TGFβ/SMAD signaling across 21 neuronal cell classes. The FDR-silent set included Itgb1, Fn1, Tnc, Spp1, Vtn, Npnt, Ptk2, Ilk, Vcl, Pxn, Tln1, Tln2, Fermt2, Gdnf, Gfra1, Ret, Tgfb1, Tgfb2, Tgfb3, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, and Smad7. This panel-level negative result does not address matrix binding, receptor activation, kinase phosphorylation, or developmental kidney mesenchyme contexts.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Tgfbr2 perturbation did not phenocopy Tgfbr1, Tgfbr3, Smad2, Smad3, or Smad4 in its best observed contexts, arguing against a simple canonical TGF-beta receptor–SMAD2/3 interpretation for the nominal CNU-MGE and glutamatergic responses. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA, the 500 strongest Tgfbr2 genes showed very low correlations with Tgfbr1, Tgfbr3, Smad2, Smad3, and Smad4, and this was the only class with an FDR<0.05 Tgfbr2-induced gene, Ssbp4. Two weaker glutamatergic contexts, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, also lacked tight Tgfbr1/SMAD phenocopy; these signatures were subthreshold, with Nipal3 or Cct7 leads but no FDR<0.05 Tgfbr2 genes, and several comparator perturbations had low cell counts in CNU-MGE GABA.

Rxra showed near-zero transcriptional correlations with Rxrb, Rxrg, and canonical heterodimer partners including Rara, Rarb, Rarg, Ppara, Ppard, Pparg, Nr1h2, Nr1h3, Vdr, and Thra, indicating that these expected nuclear-receptor relationships were not transcriptionally engaged in this dataset. The global neighbor search found only weak Rxra neighbors, roughly at safe-target-control levels, and even in 308 CB GABA cells, where the weakest extrema appeared, Rxra correlated only modestly with any perturbation. This pattern is consistent with buffered or uncoupled retinoic-acid and lipid-transcription programs, with no Apoe/Abca1 response, although weak signatures or low Rxra target engagement could mask true complex membership.

Rorc perturbation produced no coordinated clock or metabolic transcriptional response across the 22 assayed brain cell types: RORE-linked circadian genes such as Nr1d1, Nr1d2, Arntl, Clock, Cry1, Cry2, and Per1/2/3, along with lipid/steroid genes including Srebf1, Srebf2, Cyp51, Apoe, Sult4a1, and Cyp46a1, showed only nominal, uncoordinated tails. Rorc signatures were effectively uncorrelated with Rora, Rorb, and Nr1d1/Nr1d2 comparators, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Rora was active while Rorc remained transcriptionally silent. This acute, broad-brain assay may not capture peripheral or synchronized contexts where RORC biology has been defined.

Abat knockdown, most clearly in 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, did not elicit an FDR-supported compensatory transcriptional response in the GABA degradation/GABA shunt or broader GABAergic signaling module: across 23 Abat signatures, Aldh5a1, Gad1, Gad2, Slc6a1, Slc32a1, Gabra1, Gabrb2, and Gabrg2 all remained non-significant, with no robust correlation to pathway-neighbor or whole-transcriptome signatures. Thus, despite known functional links among these genes, the perturbation showed no detectable mRNA feedback, with the caveat that the dataset measures transcripts rather than metabolites, release probability, or receptor currents.

Ap4s1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant mRNA response in known AP-4 cargo, accessory, AP-4-subunit, or autophagy genes, including App, Atg9a, Daglb, Serinc1, Serinc3, Rusc1, Rusc2, Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Sqstm1, Map1lc3a, Map1lc3b, Gabarap, Ap4b1, Ap4e1, and Ap4m1. In mixed mouse neuronal classes, this suggests that acute single-cell transcript abundance is uncoupled from the AP-4 protein-sorting phenotypes, especially ATG9A trafficking, and the indirect nature of mRNA readouts plus potentially weak Ap4s1 knockdown may have muted pathway detection.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Ndufa11 showed weaker target engagement and weak convergence than several other assayed Complex I subunits, so it did not behave as an interchangeable proxy for Complex I loss in this dataset. In 155 MB Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Ndufa11 was significantly down where engaged, but secondary transcriptome effects were absent or weak. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, and Ndufs8 showed stronger own-transcript depletion while Ndufa11 was not FDR-significant. This comparison reflects measured transcript-level engagement and signatures, not protein-level Complex I loss.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atp1a3 perturbation produced its strongest, cell-type-specific signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where cation-homeostasis transcripts were repressed while synaptic and secretory programs were induced. The response included downregulation of Atp2a2, Atp2b1, Kcnj9, Kcnj3, Kcna4, Cacna1d, Prkcg, and Rgs16, alongside induction of Ache, Vgf, Pcsk1n, Scg2, Ptpn5, Grin2a, Slc17a6, Srxn1, and Scn1b, consistent with selective Na,K-ATPase/cation remodeling rather than generic silencing. This module was distinct from Atp1a1/Atp1a2 responses and from Atp2a2 stress-module coupling, but intracellular ions, acetylcholine, and peptide secretion were not measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tef behaved more like a CLOCK/BMAL1 output than a reciprocal core-clock driver in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Across these contexts, Clock or Bmal1 perturbation shifted Tef and other PAR-BZIP/D-box circadian-output genes such as Dbp and Nr1d2 much more strongly than Tef perturbation shifted Clock, and single-gene Tef knockdown did not produce FDR-level changes in Clock, Dbp, Hlf, Per3, Nr1d2, or related panel genes. The contrast was clearest in 155 MB Glut, weaker or buffered in the other classes, and should be interpreted with caution because guide targets and cell counts differed and Clock/Bmal1 self-knockdown was not always FDR-significant.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Retreg1 knockdown did not induce a canonical ER-stress or autophagy transcript program in the assayed brain neuron classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. In the best-powered engaged classes, Retreg1 itself was FDR-repressed, but no non-target transcript reached FDR significance, and targeted markers such as Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Map1lc3b, Ddit3, and Xbp1 were not induced; the clearest nominal shifts were decreases, including Hspa5 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Hsp90b1 in 052 Pvalb Gaba. This suggests acute Retreg1 depletion was uncoupled from a detectable Hspa5/Ddit3/Xbp1-type mRNA alarm, although the readout was marker-based and cannot assess ER expansion or flux.

Rpgr showed buffered transcriptional effects across the 21 assayed neuronal subclasses, and its direct interactor Rpgrip1l did not phenocopy it: Rpgrip1l also had no FDR-significant rows in the shared subclasses, and their ranked signatures were essentially uncorrelated, indicating no shared neuronal transcriptional signature in the RPGR-RPGRIP1L ciliary interaction network. This held even in high-count strata such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Rpgr lacked significant downstream or target-transcript changes; other cilium-related perturbations sometimes showed sparse FDR signals, though several were limited to target-mRNA effects and the comparator panel was restricted to screened ciliary genes.

Tgif1 perturbation did not significantly shift the expected TGIF1-associated TGFβ/SMAD, CtBP/HDAC, or retinoid transcripts, with Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, Smad7, Ctbp1, Ctbp2, Hdac1, Hdac2, Ski, Skil, Rara, Rxra, Serpine1, and Tgif2 remaining unchanged across the assayed signatures. In 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the TGFβ/SMAD2-SMAD3-SMAD4 module was mostly uncoupled, although Ski and Ctbp1 showed clearer divergent contrast. Perturbations of Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Smad2, Smad3, and Smad4 were also largely weak, arguing against a dominant canonical TGFβ/activin or retinoid transcriptional axis here, while leaving open that the pathway may have been inactive because ligand signaling or the relevant developmental state was absent.

Relb showed no detectable basal neuronal transcriptional output across 23 assayed neuronal classes: Relb, together with Rel, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Chuk, and Traf3, converged on a corrected null, with zero FDR-significant genes across core NF-kB signatures and near-zero score-vector correlations to Relb. This pattern argues against a hidden Relb-like neuronal module in the noncanonical NF-kB p100/p52-RelB pathway and is more consistent with pathway quiescence or failed engagement, although all comparator signatures were weak and the result should not be interpreted as genetic epistasis.

Tubb4a showed a buffered, target-dominated response: its perturbation mainly depleted Tubb4a mRNA with little broader shared differential expression, and this pattern was also seen for related microtubule cytoskeleton genes including Tubb2a, Tubb3, Tubb4b, Tubb5, Tuba1a, Tuba4a, Map1b, and Mapt. Across comparable cell types, these single tubulin or MAP knockdowns were mostly self-transcript-only or near-target-only signatures, suggesting pathway-level mRNA buffering within the alpha-beta tubulin heterodimer context. A caveat is that this comes from aggregate FDR-count comparisons rather than full correlation or morphology analyses, and Tuba1a showed somewhat more non-self hits in two cell types.

Tbce perturbation produced a recurrent Tuba1a-centered tubulin-transcript rebound rather than tubulin mRNA repression. Tuba1a increased in all 21 profiled Tbce cell-type tests, with FDR-significant effects in five, and the strongest signature was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Tubb5 also increased and broader tubulin-isoform compensation was seen, including Tubb3, Tubb2a, Tuba4a, Tubb4a, and Tubb4b. Similar Tuba1a responses also recurred after Tbcd perturbation in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 155 MB Glut, consistent with post-chaperonin tubulin-folding and tubulin mRNA homeostasis; however, compensation is inferred from mRNA because soluble tubulin, TTC5 activity, and microtubule polymer mass were not measured.

Prdm16 perturbation did not recapitulate the reported neural-stem and ependymal outputs linked to BMP/TGF signaling, Vcam1, and Foxj1 in the assayed brain cell classes. Across all 23 assayed cell classes, Prdm16 showed no multiple-testing-corrected transcriptional hit, and sentinel genes for these programs, including Bmpr2, Smad1, Smad2, Smad4, Foxj1, and Vcam1, were not robustly shifted. This suggests the dataset samples a different compartment than the radial-glial, neural-stem, choroid-plexus, or ependymal contexts where Prdm16 has been reported to act, and effects in unassayed progenitors or epithelial cells could have been missed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Adam22 loss showed no transcriptional compensation of its synaptic partner module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut cells. In the strongest knockdown context, Adam22 was the only FDR-significant depleted transcript, while Lgi1, Dlg4, Gria1-4, Grin1, Kcna1, Kcna2, and Cacng2 remained unchanged; across the full Adam22 panel, none of 210 tested partner-gene rows reached FDR significance. These data argue against a simple mRNA feedback response in the LGI1-ADAM22-MAGUK and AMPA/NMDA/Kv-channel organization pathways, while leaving altered receptor trafficking, nanodomain organization, or complex assembly unresolved.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Prkaa2 showed no FDR-significant transcriptional response in this Perturb-seq dataset, even in cell types with large Prkaa2 sample sizes such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, whereas the pathway-neighbor perturbations Tsc1 and Tsc2 produced strong signals, with 1,162 and 423 corrected rows and repeated effects in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Prkag2 was likewise silent, indicating that detectable mTOR/TSC outputs were recovered in the atlas while AMPKα2/γ2 perturbations were not; however, Tsc1/Tsc2 are downstream mTOR regulators rather than AMPK subunits, so this is a pathway-neighbor contrast, not a same-complex comparison.

Il2rg perturbation showed no canonical common-γ-chain interleukin receptor or JAK/STAT feedback transcriptional response across all 22 Il2rg-tested neuronal cell classes. Transcripts for Jak1, Jak3, Stat1, Stat3, Stat5a, Stat5b, Socs1, Socs2, Socs3, Cish, and nearby receptor genes including Il2ra, Il2rb, Il4ra, Il7r, Il9r, Il15ra, and Il21r were not detectably shifted, consistent with neuronal signatures lacking an engaged cytokine-receptor circuit. This null result does not exclude phosphorylation-only signaling changes, and microglia or infiltrating lymphocytes were not among the assayed neuronal groups.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Nfe2l1 perturbation was largely uncoupled from the canonical proteasome bounce-back program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba: about 50 measured Psm*/Pomp genes did not reach FDR significance, and the all-gene profiles matched Psmc1, Psmb4, Psmc5, or Pomp only weakly. In the same neuronal classes, direct proteasome-core or assembly perturbations produced large signatures, indicating these cells could mount proteasome-stress transcriptomes that weak basal Nfe2l1 depletion, measured without proteasome inhibitor challenge, did not trigger or mimic.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Wdr26 showed repeated positive score-vector similarity to proteasome or proteasome-assembly perturbations, particularly Psmc1, Psmc5, Psmb4, and Pomp, across several responsive cell types including 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. The convergence was modest but recurrent, consistent with placement of WDR26 in a CTLH E3 ubiquitin-proteasome/proteostasis axis rather than a single receptor pathway. Important caveats are that direct CTLH core members were not targeted here and WDR26 substrates were not measured at the protein level.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Sod2 knockdown produced clear on-target transcript depletion but did not elicit a coordinated FDR-significant oxidative- or mitochondrial-stress mRNA program across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA neurons. Canonical markers including Nqo1, Hmox1, Atf4, Ddit3, Sqstm1, Prdx3, Hspe1, and Gclm were not FDR-induced; only a nominal Hspa5 signal appeared in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells. This manually selected stress panel therefore suggests little transcript-level remodeling, while not excluding transient, translational, or metabolite-level stress responses.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Unc13b perturbation showed no coordinated mRNA response in the canonical presynaptic vesicle-release neighborhood across multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types, including L4-5 IT CTX Glut, L2-3 IT CTX Glut, MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, Pvalb Gaba, MB Glut, and CB GABA. A 15-gene panel spanning Unc13 paralogs and RIM/Rab3/SNARE/active-zone partners such as Unc13a, Unc13c, Rims1, Rab3a, Snap25, Stxbp1, Stx1b, Vamp2, Syt1, Bsn, and Cacna1a had 0 of 168 tests significant after correction. This negative result occurred under weak Unc13b target engagement, so presynaptic release changes could still occur without altered transcript abundance.

Grik1 showed no corrected transcriptional response in this dataset family, and this null was not a universal failure to detect glutamate-receptor perturbations: under the same analysis, Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Gria2, Grik3, and Grik5 each produced at least one significant gene, whereas Grik1, Grik2, and Grik4 produced none. The contrast was most evident in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Grik5 had significant on-target depletion but Grik1 did not. This pattern suggests a Grik1-biased lack of signal, although guide performance and partially different assayed cell-class sets remain caveats.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Mitf showed no multiple-testing-supported downstream transcriptomic response, including in high-cell-count neuronal classes such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Tsc1 and Tsc2 produced tens to hundreds of significant genes; in 155 MB Glut, Sqstm1 and Map1lc3a were also detectable. This contrast indicates that mTOR/lysosome-adjacent perturbations can be read out in these neurons, so the Mitf-negative result is more specific than a general assay failure, although TSC1/TSC2 affect many processes beyond MITF/TFEB and the comparison is pathway-adjacent rather than direct epistasis.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Srebf2 knockdown was clear in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, yet these classes showed weak or absent downstream sterol-gene propagation: no 12-gene sterol-module member reached FDR<0.2, and genes such as Hmgcs1, Insig1, and Dhcr24 showed only nominal or directionally flat changes. These buffered or uncoupled transcriptomic responses suggest that on-target Srebf2 depletion alone does not demonstrate functional perturbation of the SREBP2 regulon in every neuronal subclass, while also leaving open caveats of limited power, dropout, or low baseline module activity.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Pik3r1 was FDR-silent in this Perturb-seq dataset, and the same was true for the assayed class IA PI3K subunits Pik3r2, Pik3ca, and Pik3cb, even in nominal hotspot cell types such as 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. In contrast, Tsc1, Tsc2, and Pten perturbations produced robust transcriptomic responses, with hundreds to thousands of significant genes across matched neuronal classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. This suggests that the weak Pik3r1 phenotype is local to the upstream PI3K subunit layer rather than a general failure to read out PI3K/PTEN/TSC/mTOR biology, while noting that Tsc1/Tsc2/Pten are downstream negative regulators rather than direct Pik3r1 paralogs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Frmpd4 was weak in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class, with no Frmpd4 FDR response even in its best self-depletion context. In the same thalamic class, related postsynaptic and synaptic perturbations including Dlg4, Dlgap4, Grin1, Grin2b, Nrxn1, Syn1, Nlgn2, Cyfip2, and Shank3 showed strong self-depletion and/or significant signatures. This suggests the Frmpd4 negative result is not a universal lack of sensitivity in this cell class, although the stronger comparator effects could reflect both biology and guide efficacy differences.

Nr2e1 showed a transcriptomic perturbation profile that did not phenocopy available TLX-neighbor or nuclear-receptor perturbations in neurons: across within-cell-type comparisons, full-signature correlations with Hdac5, Foxg1, Nr2e3, Nr2f1, Nr2f2, Nr2c1, retinoic-acid receptors, retinoid-X receptors, and Nr4a receptors were uniformly low, with all Pearson |r| below 0.272 and mean correlations near zero for Hdac5, Foxg1, Nr2e3, and the Nr2f family. This suggests Nr2e1 is largely orthogonal to these related perturbations at the whole-transcriptome level, although the analysis was based on score correlations and could not test direct protein interactions or unprofiled partners such as Atn1, Kdm1a, Ncor1, or Ncor2.

Tmem106b knockdown was largely buffered at the transcript level, with no FDR-significant regulation of Grn, Sort1, Psap, Ctsb, Lamp2, or v-ATPase genes, even in cell types where on-target depletion was clear, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. In the same atlas, Atp6v0c perturbation produced a broad downstream program, highlighting a cross-perturbation contrast that suggests Tmem106b is not an acute transcriptional phenocopy of lysosomal acidification failure; however, this comparison is limited to transcriptomic readouts and may reflect differing guide efficiencies and cell counts.

Ndufaf2 showed a near-null downstream transcriptomic response that fits a broader buffering pattern across related complex-I perturbations rather than a unique exception. Across 26 tested Nduf-family targets and 572 cell-type signatures, only 9 FDR-significant non-self differential-expression rows were detected, with other complex-I subunits and assembly factors such as Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs2, Ndufb8, and Ndufv2 also largely buffered. In pathway terms, the target transcript could be depleted without a coordinated complex-I or OXPHOS mRNA cascade, although this count-based comparison reflects significant non-self mRNA changes, not direct respiratory-chain activity.

Ndufs3 did not phenocopy other complex I perturbations at the whole-transcriptome level: across 25 in-library NDUF/NDUFAF targets, its score vectors showed near-zero correlations, with a maximum Pearson r of 0.095, even though NDUFS3 shares the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I and assembly module with genes such as Ndufa9, Ndufa13, Ndufb10, Ndufs8, Ndufc2, and Ndufs2. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Ndufs3 was down while the broader transcriptomic OXPHOS state appeared buffered. This uncoupling was based on weak Ndufs3 RNA signatures and does not test complex I protein assembly directly.

Zkscan3 loss did not measurably derepress the canonical ZKSCAN3/TFEB autophagy-lysosome transcriptional program in this mouse brain dataset under basal conditions. Across measured cell types, expected targets and pathway genes including Map1lc3b, Wipi2, Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Sqstm1, Lamp1, Tfeb, and Gsk3b showed no FDR-significant differential expression after perturbation. This contrasts with acute knockdown models in published systems but is more consistent with later chronic knockout results, suggesting strong cell-context dependence and a caveat that only transcript-level responses in basal in vivo neurons were tested.

Nod2 perturbation in unstimulated neurons did not detectably activate or repress a coherent canonical NOD2 program: transcripts in NOD2/NF-kB/MAPK signaling and NOD2-ATG16L1 autophagy, including Tab1, Irf3, Il6st, Chuk, Map3k7, Tbk1, Irf9, Nfkb1, Rel, Xiap, Atg16l1, and Sqstm1, were not significantly changed where measured, and genome-wide signature correlations with Rel, Irf5, Csf1r, Mif, Chuk, Irf3, Map3k7, Tlr9, Atg16l1, and Xiap were only weak. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons, even the nominal Arrb2 decrease did not support a robust canonical program. This likely reflects context rather than contradiction, since no bacterial ligand was present and key nodes such as RIPK2, CARD9, and NOD1 were not perturbed, while NF-kappaB/MAPK activity can be post-translational.

Unc13a showed only partial self-transcript reduction across matched neuronal subclasses, with no robust downstream transcriptional activation across the presynaptic active-zone synaptic-vesicle priming/exocytosis program. In the same dataset, other vesicle-release genes including Snap25, Stxbp1, Cplx1, Syn1, and Stx1b displayed strong, significant self-transcript depletion in multiple matched cell types, while the related Unc13b and Unc13c perturbations were also weakly engaged and showed no acute mRNA compensation. This pattern suggests a target-specific engagement limitation rather than general buffering of vesicle-fusion genes, although guide design, expression level, transcript detectability, and cell-type sampling could also explain the differences.

Timmdc1 showed a weak, perturbation-family-specific profile across the same brain cell classes where structural respiratory-chain targets behaved differently: Uqcrc1, Ndufb10, Ndufc2, Ndufs8, Ndufb8, and Ndufa10 showed strong self-transcript depletion, whereas Timmdc1 and assayed Ndufaf assembly-factor targets such as Ndufaf2, Ndufaf4, and Ndufaf5 remained weak. This pattern was seen in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, with only nominal Timmdc1 signals like Ndufa2 up or Ndufs3 down. The main cross-perturbation difference was target-transcript depletion rather than broad downstream differential expression, and key MCIA core genes Acad9, Ecsit, and Tmem126b were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ssr4 knockdown was uncoupled from a canonical ER-stress and folding transcriptional program, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with similar separation also seen in 155 MB Glut. In the thalamic class with strongest Ssr4 engagement, Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Hyou1, Canx, and Chac1 were not significantly induced after Ssr4 perturbation, whereas Sec63 or Hspa5 perturbation in the same class induced multiple FDR-significant UPR/folding genes. Thus, within the ER protein translocation through Sec61/TRAP context, Ssr4 should not be treated here as a generic ER-stress perturbation; this comparison is transcriptomic and did not measure glycosylation-client abundance.

Rac1 showed a largely buffered, near-null transcriptomic response across the 22 tested cell-type groups, with no target-transcript FDR signal and no convergence with curated RAC1/Rho-GTPase neighbors. In matched cell types, Rac1 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Cdc42, Pak1, Pak2, Pak3, Trio, Tiam1, Dock3, Dock7, Arhgef9, Arhgap18, Arhgap32, Kalrn, and Limk1, even though several of these perturbations produced detectable FDR-level effects in the same assay. This supports transcriptomic uncoupling rather than implying that RAC1 is mechanistically unrelated to those pathway-adjacent genes.

Gfm2 targeting did not produce a coherent or significant change in mtDNA-encoded oxidative phosphorylation transcript abundance: the 13 mitochondrial mRNAs, including mt-Atp6, mt-Co1, mt-Cytb, and mt-Nd1 through mt-Nd6, showed mixed directions with no significant hits. This is consistent with GFM2 acting at mitochondrial translation termination/recycling rather than directly determining mt-mRNA levels, but the inference is limited because the assay measures RNA, not nascent mitochondrial translation, OXPHOS protein abundance, or respiration, and Gfm2 mRNA depletion was weak.

Ptcd3 perturbation showed no FDR-corrected change in mitochondrial genome-encoded OXPHOS mRNAs, including mt-Atp6, mt-Atp8, mt-Co1, mt-Co2, mt-Co3, mt-Cytb, and mt-Nd1 through mt-Nd6, and no Ptcd3 cell-type signature produced a conventionally significant differential transcript after multiple-testing correction. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, the mitochondrial translation signal was weak or absent, while comparator profiles detected Dap3 depletion. Across several neuronal classes, comparator self-knockdowns were detectable, suggesting the null Ptcd3 result reflects a steady-state mRNA readout limitation rather than absence of mitochondrial translation or respiratory-chain involvement.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Huwe1 perturbation in mature brain cell types, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, did not produce FDR-significant mRNA induction of the canonical MYCN–DLL–Notch or p53 axes: Mycn, Dll1, Dll3, Hes1, Notch1, Notch2, Trp53, Cdkn1a, Mdm2, and Mcl1 all remained below FDR<0.05. This suggests a mature-neuron response distinct from progenitor-like programs, although the null mRNA result does not exclude post-translational changes in MYCN, p53, or MCL1 protein abundance.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grin2d was not transcriptionally interchangeable with Grin1 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class: Grin1 knockdown produced 89 FDR-significant genes, whereas Grin2d perturbation produced none despite more perturbed cells and nominal target depletion. Other NMDA receptor subunit perturbations were also much smaller than Grin1, with Grin2b modest and Grin2a largely target-only, consistent with a Grin1-responsive but Grin2d-buffered pattern in NMDA receptor assembly and postsynaptic anchoring genes. This dataset did not perturb Grin2c, and the contrast is transcriptional within the same cell class rather than electrophysiological.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Calm2 knockdown in 155 MB Glut, the only context with FDR-significant Calm2 depletion, was uncoupled from canonical calmodulin effector mRNAs: Camk2a was only nominal, and Camk2b, Camk2g, Ppp3ca, Ppp3r1, Itpr1, Ryr2, Cacna1a, Cacna1c, Adcy1, Adcy8, as well as Calm1 and Calm3, all failed FDR. Thus, despite pathway expectations for Ca2+/calmodulin signaling to CaMK, calcineurin, calcium-channel, calcium-release, and adenylyl-cyclase regulation, this perturbation showed no matched RNA response, with the caveat that the assay captures steady-state mRNA rather than protein activity and partial Calm2 depletion may preserve residual signaling.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Flt3 did not behave as a shared FLT-family or downstream RTK module in these neurons: across representative contexts including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Flt3 showed no FDR-level response and no strong positive or negative signature neighbor, with correlations to Kit, Kdr, Flt4, Csf1r, Pdgfrb, Mapk1, Mtor, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Ptpn11, Raf1, Sos1, and Stat5b remaining weak. Isolated FDR hits occurred instead in related targets such as Kit, Kdr, Flt4, Mapk1, or Mtor, but these sparse events may reflect self-transcript or other idiosyncratic effects, and correlation was assessed in four representative Flt3 contexts rather than every cell class.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Kiss1r perturbation showed no FDR-supported transcriptional activation of the canonical KISS1R/Gq/PLC/MAPK program across the surveyed brain classes, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic populations such as L2/3 IT CTX Glut, CA3/CA2-FC DG Glut, Pvalb Gaba, Sst Gaba, and CB GABA.
