Transcripts for Plcb1, Gnaq, Gna11, Arrb2, Mapk1, Mapk3, Fos, Egr1, and Nr4a1 remained nonresponsive, and direct receptor-neighbor comparisons were largely unavailable. This steady-state mRNA result does not rule out rapid post-translational Ca2+, phosphoinositide, or phospho-ERK signaling downstream of ligand-bound KISS1R.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Dpm1 showed a much weaker transcriptional phenotype than related ER-glycosylation stressors in overlapping neuronal classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these cells, Dpm1 induced no FDR<0.05 genes and only nominal increases in an ER protein folding/unfolded-protein-response-like module, whereas Manf strongly induced Hspa5, Pdia6, Sdf2l1, Dnajb9, Hyou1, and Hsp90b1, and Dhdds produced broader ER-stress signatures. This contrast suggests the screen could detect chaperone induction, but partial Dpm1 knockdown did not phenocopy stronger disruption of ER glycoprotein homeostasis; however, Dhdds target knockdown itself was not FDR-significant, leaving room for perturbation- or guide-specific effects.

Rai1 perturbation did not recapitulate the canonical CLOCK/core circadian transcriptional program in the assayed brain cell classes. Across matched cell types, none of the core circadian transcripts Arntl, Clock, Cry1, Cry2, Nr1d1, Nr1d2, Per1, Per2, or Per3 showed an FDR-significant response, and Rai1 perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of Clock, Cry1, Cry2, Nr1d1, and Nr1d2. This suggests acute Rai1 loss did not simply replay a cell-autonomous core-clock program, although circadian outputs are time-of-day and cell-state sensitive and weak Rai1 target-transcript engagement limits the strength of this negative conclusion.

Cd27 perturbation in neuronal classes did not phenocopy nearby TNFR/NF-kB family perturbations: its whole-transcriptome signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Cd40, Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Chuk, Tnfrsf4, and Tnfrsf9, and the nearest-neighbor landscape did not reveal a coherent Cd27 pathway signature. This is consistent with uncoupling of CD27 from TRAF to NF-kB/JNK signaling in this neuronal loss-of-function dataset rather than hidden CD27-CD70 activity. A caveat is that the signatures were weak, Cd70 was not perturbed, and the 308 CB GABA outlier had zero FDR-significant genes and no corrected on-target Cd27 effect.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarca4 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed nominal on-target reduction but no FDR-significant transcriptional response, while Smarca2 was likewise self-only or FDR-silent. In the same thalamic cell type, core and accessory BAF perturbations including Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Arid2, Arid1a, and Smarce1 produced strong, partially convergent programs, with Smarcb1 and Smarcc2 sharing a prominent signature. Thus, this cell class can report a BAF transcriptional phenotype, and the Smarca4-negative result is not simply explained by cell type or assay, though weaker Smarca4 RNA knockdown could account for some or all of the contrast.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Cst3 knockdown in diverse neuronal and interneuron populations, including cortical IT/ET glutamatergic neurons, hippocampal glutamatergic neurons, multiple GABAergic classes, thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, and cerebellar cells, did not produce detectable mRNA feedback in the cysteine protease inhibition/cathepsin B axis or related lysosomal, autophagy, and APP-associated markers: Ctsb, Ctsl, Cstb, App, Grn, Lamp2, Psap, Cd63, Lgmn, Becn1, Sqstm1, and Lamp1 all remained unchanged. Cst3 signatures also did not converge with Ctsb, App, Grn, Psap, Lamp2, or Trem2 perturbations, though only selected transcripts were assayed and post-translational cathepsin activity changes would not be captured.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Oprd1 depletion in 052 Pvalb Gaba did not produce a coordinated PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 transcriptional response: Akt1, Akt2, Mtor, Pik3ca, Pik3cb, Pik3cd, Pik3r1, Rptor, and Eif4ebp1 were not adjustably changed, and canonical PI3K-mTOR pathway mRNAs were not coordinately regulated in the only class showing nominal Oprd1 target depletion. This flat mRNA pattern contrasts with reported agonist-evoked PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-p70S6K phospho-signaling in mouse IL-PFC PV interneurons, suggesting the receptor effect may be post-translational, ligand-state dependent, or diluted in pooled steady-state Perturb-seq data.

Gclc targeting did not coordinately remodel the expected glutathione biosynthesis and cellular redox homeostasis program: across a 22-gene panel spanning glutathione, NRF-family detoxification, thioredoxin, and ROS-buffering genes, canonical transcripts such as Gclm, Gss, Gsr, Gpx1, Nfe2l2, Keap1, Nqo1, Hmox1, Txnrd1, Prdx1, Sod1, Sod2, Cat, Slc7a11, and Srxn1 were neither consistently induced nor repressed, with 0/484 panel tests passing FDR<0.1. This transcriptional uncoupling is tempered by the caveat that the perturbation appeared weak, as Gclc itself showed no FDR-supported transcript depletion, so GCLC protein or glutathione may not have fallen enough to trigger NRF-family compensation.

Gabra5 showed weaker on-target transcriptional engagement than several other GABA_A receptor subunit perturbations in the same screen. While Gabra1, Gabrb2, Gabrb3, Gabrd, and Gabrg2 each showed FDR-supported depletion of their own transcripts in at least two cell types, Gabra5 showed none, so it should not be assumed to behave interchangeably with these related subunits despite belonging to the same receptor family. This contrast comes from differential-expression readouts and does not address receptor assembly or electrophysiology.

Foxk2 perturbation did not phenocopy available chromatin- or mTOR-axis neighbors in this neuronal Perturb-seq atlas: across matched neuronal cell types, FOXK2-score correlations with Sin3a, Bap1, Smarca4, Mtor, Tsc1, and Tsc2 were all near zero, indicating no detectable transcriptome-wide convergence with the SIN3A/BAP1 chromatin module or the mTORC1/TSC-FoxK regulatory axis under the assayed conditions. This inference is tempered by generally weak single-perturbation signatures, and the closest paralog, Foxk1, was not included in the screen.

Mdh2 knockdown showed no FDR-level compensatory RNA response in the assayed malate-aspartate shuttle, nearby TCA-cycle, or mitochondrial-stress genes. Across neurons, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, transcripts such as Mdh1, Got1, Got2, Slc25a12, Slc25a13, Aco2, Idh3a, Ogdh, Sdha, Sdhb, Mpc1, Atf4, Ddit3, and Clpp did not pass FDR thresholds; in 052 Pvalb Gaba, Tcaf1 was the only non-target FDR hit. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Mdh1 produced a broader Gls/Nrxn1/Grin2b-containing response than Mdh2. These results are transcript-level only, so metabolic flux changes could still occur without detectable mRNA shifts.

Bbs5 perturbation left the canonical BBSome-mediated cargo-targeting to cilium pathway transcriptionally quiet: there was no corrected change in mRNAs for BBSome components and related machinery, including Bbs9, Ttc8, Bbip1, Arl6, Lztfl1, Rab3ip, Ift81, and Ift88, nor for representative ciliary cargo/signaling genes such as Smo, Mchr1, and Sstr3. This uncoupling was observed without a specified cell-type restriction and is consistent with the caveat that BBSome biology primarily reflects subcellular protein trafficking rather than transcriptional regulation of pathway components.

Lrp8 was part of a Reelin/ApoER2-Dab1 signaling branch that appeared FDR-null or only weakly engaged in this Perturb-seq RNA readout: Lrp8, Vldlr, Reln, Dab1, and Fyn showed neither detectable self-transcript depletion nor any FDR-significant genome-wide target-cell contrast, whereas neighboring perturbations such as App, Grin1, Grin2b, Lrpap1, Gsk3b, Dlg4, and Lrp1 did show self-transcript depletion in at least some cell types. This branch-specific contrast argues against a global inability to detect neuronal receptor or synaptic perturbations, although the comparison relies on transcript depletion and DE counts rather than matched protein knockdown for every target.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Fcgr2b showed signatures that were nearly orthogonal to related immune-receptor perturbations across many neuronal cell types, including glutamatergic and GABAergic classes. In the same panel, Fcgr4, Trem2, Fyn, BCR subunits Cd79a/Cd79b, and PI3K/SHP neighbors Pik3ca, Pik3cb, Pik3r1, Pik3r2, and Ptpn11 were FDR-silent, with Fcgr2b transcriptome-score correlations remaining very low for Fcgr4 and Trem2. Even well-sampled groups such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut were FDR-silent, arguing against a shared latent neuronal Fcγ/myeloid receptor program, though this comparison is transcriptomic and limited to the perturbed genes in the library.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atf6 loss did not produce a coordinated ER-chaperone, ERAD, or integrated-stress transcriptional program, even in better-powered profiles such as 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where only nominal signals like Herpud1 were seen. In contrast, the same screen recovered an ER quality-control module through comparator perturbations: Manf knockdown increased Hspa5 and other folding genes including Hyou1, Sdf2l1, Dnajb9, and Pdia6 across several cell types, and Hspa5 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut increased Hsp90b1, Pdia4, and Derl3. This supports assay sensitivity for UPR-adjacent genes, while noting that Manf loss is not equivalent to direct ATF6 activation or inhibition.

Pclo showed essentially nonconvergent RNA signatures relative to Bsn and other presynaptic active-zone or synaptic-release perturbations in this dataset. Across 22 Pclo cell contexts, ranked transcriptome correlations were tiny, with Bsn max |r| = 0.095 and Bsn/Unc13a/Unc13b/Unc13c/Snap25/Syn1/Syn2/Syn3/Stxbp1 max |r| = 0.131, indicating that Pclo cannot be treated here as a proxy for Bassoon or generic release machinery. This weak coupling was observed despite related synaptic genes showing FDR-significant signatures, and although the network was largely uncoupled from Pclo RNA, nominal Erc2 downregulation appeared in 191_MB_P_MY_GABA. Because the Pclo signatures themselves were weak, the lack of RNA correlation does not exclude shared structural or electrophysiologic phenotypes.

Egr2 perturbation in 21 Egr2-tested neuronal classes did not produce detectable transcriptional compensation through the measured Egr paralogs, NAB corepressors, or AP-1/immediate-early genes: Egr1, Egr3, Egr4, Nab1, Nab2, Fos, Jun, Junb, and Jund all remained at FDR=1.0 across Egr2 signatures. This suggests no detectable EGR/NAB immediate-early feedback state in this neuronal Perturb-seq context, while noting that Egr paralogs and NAB cofactors were measured but not directly perturbed here, and prior feedback reports came from other cell models rather than these mouse neuronal classes.

Syn2 knockdown did not produce detectable mRNA compensation in the synapsin paralog module or the synaptic vesicle cycle/neurotransmitter secretion pathway: Syn1, Syn3, Snap25, Syp, Sv2a, Syt2, Stx1b, and Dlg4 showed no measurable regulation, including in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells. Thus, despite Syn2’s functional connection to presynaptic vesicle-cycle proteins, the perturbation appeared uncoupled from transcriptional rewiring of these partner transcripts. This conclusion is limited because only selected partner mRNAs were examined, not protein abundance, phosphorylation, vesicle localization, or release probability.

Myt1l loss did not detectably de-repress the canonical Notch-HES neurogenesis axis in this mature mouse-brain Perturb-seq screen. Across tested neuronal classes, Hes1, Hes5, Notch1, Notch2, Notch3, Dll1, Dll3, Dll4, Jag1, and Jag2 showed no significant response, refining prior MYT-family annotations that emphasize repression of neurogenesis inhibitors rather than overturning them. This null result should be interpreted cautiously because several Notch-pathway transcripts are lowly expressed in differentiated neurons, and incomplete RNA-level guide engagement could have obscured small effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tuba1a knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced the strongest response, with reduced Tuba1a accompanied by coordinated induction of multiple alpha- and beta-tubulin isotypes, including Tuba4a, Tubb2a, Tubb3, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, and Tubb5, consistent with one-way compensation in alpha/beta tubulin heterodimer stoichiometry and autoregulation. In the same cell class, strong Tuba4a or individual beta-tubulin knockdowns showed target engagement but did not reciprocally induce the broad tubulin module, indicating Tuba1a is not transcriptionally interchangeable with these related isotypes; this contrast was strongest in this one class, and the data do not show whether induced isotypes enter polymerized microtubules.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Vamp1 showed only a weak transcriptomic response and did not phenocopy related presynaptic vesicle/SNARE perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. Although these cell types showed Vamp1 self-depletion, score-vector correlations with Snap25, Stx1b, Stxbp1, and Syp were near zero, and even the strongest positive or negative whole-signature neighbors were weak (|r|≤0.0755). In 155 MB Glut, the strongest Vamp1 knockdown still produced no off-target FDR genes or coordinated SNARE-neighbor compensation, so the result indicates no detectable shared RNA state rather than absence of biochemical interaction.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarcc1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not induce the strong BAF-sensitive Ptpn3/Reep2/Prkcd/Tiam1 module seen with Smarcc2 and Smarcb1, and unlike Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Arid2, Arid1a, Smarce1, and Smarcd1, it showed no genome-wide corrected transcriptomic response in this cell type. This contrast suggests that the 151 TH mSWI/SNF or BAF-related program is not a universal consequence of perturbing every core complex member, although the interpretation is limited because Smarcc1 mRNA knockdown was not detected here.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Med13l perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells was marked primarily by downregulation of Grm1, which was the only high-confidence Med13l hit in this thalamic class. Grm1 repression also recurred with Med13, Med15, and Med23 perturbations, whereas Cdk8 and Med12 did not show FDR-significant Grm1 responses. Compared with Med13l, Med13, Med15, and Med23 revealed a broader downregulated thalamic neuronal module including Prkcd, Pcp4, Plekhg1, and Grin2b, with weaker genome-wide correlations and no combinatorial rescue tested.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gfpt1 perturbation showed a branch-specific stress program rather than a generic response to reduced fructose-6-phosphate supply: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, knockdown of the upstream glycolytic neighbor Gpi1 significantly reduced Gpi1 itself but did not induce the Gfpt1-associated UPR/ISR genes Ddit3, Hspa5, Asns, Herpud1, or Sdf2l1, and was essentially uncorrelated with Gfpt1. This contrasts with the stronger Gfpt1 response, which combined Ogt/Oga downregulation with ER-stress signaling, although only one upstream neighbor was tested and metabolites were not measured.

Camkmt perturbation showed no supported transcriptional compensation in the calmodulin/CaMK axis: Calm1, Calm2, Calm3, Camk2a, Camk2b, Camk2g, and Camk4 remained FDR-negative, and Camkmt mRNA itself was not significantly altered in any Camkmt-targeted cell type. This fits a case where the expected primary consequence is loss of CAMKMT-dependent trimethyl-calmodulin rather than an RNA program, so the transcriptomic null may reflect pathway buffering or a readout mismatch, with the important caveat that neither CAMKMT protein nor methylated calmodulin was assayed.

Notch4 perturbation was uncoupled from canonical Notch transcriptional readouts in the measured neuronal signatures: Notch1, Notch2, Notch3, Dll1, Adam10, Psen1, Mib1, Hes7, and Hesx1 did not show coordinated differential expression, and the dataset therefore did not reveal the expected receptor-to-NICD-to-transcription module. A key caveat is that direct Notch4 transcript knockdown could not be assessed because Notch4 was absent from the differential-expression feature table, and the measured genes are only pathway sentinels rather than a full HES/HEY nuclear reporter panel.

Srr perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from a hand-curated D-serine/serine-metabolism and NMDAR-neighborhood gene set: despite Srr’s role in D-serine synthesis, knockdown did not yield FDR-supported changes in nearby metabolic genes (Psph, Phgdh, Psat1, Shmt1/2, Dao, Ddo), transporters (Slc1a1, Slc1a2, Slc1a4, Slc1a5), DISC1, or Grin receptor transcripts. The clearest target depletion was in 155 MB Glut, but downstream and neighborhood effects there remained nominal only. This RNA-only test was hand-curated, and some genes were lowly expressed, with unstable extreme logFC values in rarely detected genes.

Dld perturbation did not produce a coherent partner-transcript response in this assay. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba cells, expected PDH, OGDH, BCKDH, and TCA-associated genes, including Dlat, Dlst, Ogdh, Pdha1, Pdhb, Pdhx, Bckdhb, Sdha, Mdh2, Idh3a, and Aco2, showed mixed directions with no significant coordinated induction or repression. This uncoupling was also orthogonal across related perturbations, suggesting that Dld loss here did not elicit a matching compensatory mRNA program, with the caveat that only transcript abundance was measured and the relevant defect may be enzymatic flux or redox based.

Clpp knockdown did not produce a detectable mitochondrial unfolded-protein or integrated-stress transcriptional program: Ddit3, Atf4, Atf5, Hspd1, Hspe1, Hspa9, Lonp1, and Clpx were not induced at FDR<0.05 in any assayed Clpp contrast, and in the 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cell type the only corrected hit was Rbm45 up-regulation despite weak measured Clpp depletion. This uncouples partial Clpp loss from canonical UPRmt/ISR readouts in this dataset, especially since the same pathway was present after Lonp1 perturbation, while transcript-only measurements could have missed transient, translational, or proteolytic stress responses.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Syn1 perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut was largely on-target only, with no non-Syn1 FDR genes despite successful knockdown, and a similarly self-dominated pattern was seen for Syn2, Syp, Stx1b, Syt2, Camk2b, and other presynaptic comparators. In the same cell type, Stxbp1 contrasted sharply by producing a broad non-self response, with 66 non-self FDR genes there and 88 overall. These results suggest that downstream transcriptional breadth is uncoupled from the presynaptic vesicle pathway, although the comparators are presynaptic genes from different molecular complexes and all counts come from the same transcriptomic endpoint.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Adam10 perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from canonical APP/Notch pathway output across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. App, Psen1, Dll1, Mib1, and Notch1-4 were not differentially expressed, and Adam10 signatures did not align with APP, Notch, gamma-secretase, ADAM-family, TIMP3, or tetraspanin perturbations. This likely reflects proteolytic regulation rather than acute mRNA feedback, but direct shedding and cleavage products such as sAPPα, Aβ, NEXT, and NICD were not measured.

Cadm2 showed a target-centric, buffered transcriptomic response that was not unique among neuronal-adhesion perturbations. In this Perturb-seq library, Cadm2 depletion produced no FDR-significant non-target transcripts, and a related-target audit across Cntn1, Ncam1, Nrcam, Nlgn2, Nrxn1, Nlgn3, Nrxn2, Dlg4, Cask, and Nectin1 found only four off-target FDR hits among 4,881,774 tested rows, suggesting that scRNA differential expression under-resolves adhesion biology as a class. This comparison did not directly perturb Cadm1, Cadm3, or Cadm4, and the sparse RNA effects should not be taken as absence of synaptic phenotypes.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Rarg did not behave as an interchangeable RAR/RXR-family perturbation in this adult brain atlas: its loss-of-function signatures were generally weak and broadly uncorrelated with Rara, Rarb, Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg, arguing against treating these guides as equivalent readouts of retinoic acid / RAR:RXR signaling. Only modest, restricted similarity appeared in selected cell types, including 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where Stra6, Rara, and Rarb showed limited convergence, and 308 CB GABA, where Rarg showed modest restricted similarity to Rara despite no FDR-supported Rarg response and a top non-retinoid neighbor. These correlations were computed on weak signatures, including a restricted top-200 view, and should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Agtr2 perturbation did not produce detectable transcriptional readouts of canonical AT2R-associated pathways in this screen: Fos, Jun, Egr1, Mapk1, Mapk3, Mtus1, Nos1, Nfkb1, and Ptpn6 all showed no FDR-supported change, so MAPK, immediate-early, MTUS1, nitric-oxide, NF-kappaB, and Ptpn6/SHP-1 signatures were effectively uncoupled. A key caveat is target engagement: Agtr2 transcript was measured but not detectably depleted in any cell type, and extreme logFC values with near-zero scores were treated as low-expression artifacts, so these null results should not be taken as evidence against ligand-stimulated AT2R biology.

Cacng2 did not phenocopy AMPA receptor trafficking and synaptic targeting perturbations: across 155 MB Glut, 053 Sst Gaba, and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, Cacng2 showed no robust RNA-state propagation and lacked detectable self-transcript depletion, whereas comparator perturbations such as Dlg4, Gria2, Frrs1l, and Cpt1c did. Consistent with this, Cacng2 Wilcoxon-score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Gria1-4, Dlg4, and other postsynaptic neighbors, although this comparison relied on weak genome-wide score vectors and Cacng2 itself had weak self-transcript engagement.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Notch4 did not act like an interchangeable Notch-family or ligand-pathway perturbation in this dataset. Across matched cell types, including 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA, whole-transcriptome correlations with Notch1/2/3, Dll1, Adam10, Psen1, and Mib1 were all small, with the strongest related-target correlation only r=0.1008. Mib1 nevertheless produced much stronger responses in several matched classes, while the Notch4 transcript itself was not quantified.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Tubb3 showed an asymmetric tubulin-compensation pattern: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, acute Tubb3 knockdown did not induce other measured α/β-tubulin paralogs at FDR-significant levels, even in the strongest knockdown contexts. In the same dataset, by contrast, Tuba1a loss induced a tubulin-isotype module, including Tubb3, Tubb2a, Tubb4a/Tubb4b, Tuba4a, and Tubb5 depending on cell type. This suggests Tubb3’s acute response is buffered rather than reflecting a universal tubulin-isotype feedback program, with the caveat that the comparison is limited to two highlighted cell types and contrasts acute Perturb-seq with developmental Tubb3 knockout compensation.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tm2d1 did not produce an APP- or Notch-like transcriptional state in its two responsive mouse neuronal cell types, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In both cell types, Tm2d1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with App, Psen1, Adam10, and Notch1–4 perturbations, despite APP being effectively engaged in the same comparison context. The L5 ET cortical glutamatergic neurons showed the only multi-gene adjusted Tm2d1 response, whereas the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons showed a single adjusted hit, R3hdm2. This uncoupling is limited to transcriptomic signatures, and Psen1 and Adam10 perturbations were also weak; Tm2d2 and Tm2d3 were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Braf showed a cell-type-specific transcriptional effect that Raf1 did not reproduce in the tested thalamic and hypothalamic populations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Raf1 perturbation had 140 cells but no FDR-significant genes and did not reduce the Braf-associated markers Vgf or Ptpn5; in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Raf1 likewise left Vgf unchanged. These results suggest a Braf-biased, non-interchangeable RAF paralog contribution to RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK transcriptional output in these neurons, although Raf1 mRNA engagement was weak and Araf was not assayed.

Cep112 perturbation in 21 profiled neuronal classes was mostly uncorrelated with available centrosomal, ciliary, and kinesin perturbations, so its centrosomal or basal-foot annotation did not translate into interchangeable neuronal signatures. Across 323 same-cell comparisons with Cep120, Cep164, Cep290, Cep83, Cep85l, Cfap69, Ttll5, and Kif family perturbations, 317 showed |Pearson r|≤0.11, with only a weak convergence cluster in cerebellar GABA cells, including 308 CB GABA. These correlations were based on genome-wide Wilcoxon scores from weak Cep112 signatures, and most comparator genes were pathway neighbors rather than confirmed CEP112 complex members.

Lrp8 perturbation did not detectably remodel steady-state mRNA in the canonical Reelin/ApoER2-Dab1 pathway or the ApoER2 postsynaptic NMDA/synaptic module: Reln, Vldlr, Dab1, Fyn, Lrpap1, Lrp1, Grin1, Grin2b, and Dlg4 were not FDR-significantly changed, and Lrp8 signatures were only weakly correlated with related perturbations. In this dataset, upstream receptor, ligand, adaptor, and kinase perturbations also lacked robust transcriptomic signatures, suggesting that relevant ApoER2 biology here may lie in phosphorylation, receptor processing, localization, isoforms, or Reelin secretion rather than bulk RNA output.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tpk1 did not phenocopy perturbations of TPP-dependent mitochondrial dehydrogenase genes in this dataset: its whole-transcriptome score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Pdha1, Pdhb, Pdhx, Dlat, Dld, Ogdh, Dlst, Bckdhb, and Bckdk, even though direct Pdha1, Pdhb, and Dlat perturbations showed corrected self-transcript decreases in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Ogdh showed a corrected self-transcript decrease in 155 MB Glut. This separation may reflect weak measured Tpk1 engagement, and the comparison is limited to transcriptomic scores because several proximal thiamine transporters and transketolase were not included.

Fnip1 perturbation did not detectably induce the canonical FLCN–FNIP/Rag–mTORC1/MiT-TFE lysosomal transcriptional program: Tfeb, Tfe3, Sqstm1, Lamp2, cathepsins, and v-ATPase genes showed no FDR-significant response. This was seen even in 155 MB Glut cells, where on-target Fnip1 depletion was strongest, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where related pathway perturbations such as Tsc1, Tsc2, Depdc5, Mtor, Sqstm1, and Atp6v0a1 were active. The negative result may reflect weak Fnip1 engagement, state dependence, or buffering by Fnip2, and interpretation is limited because Flcn and Fnip2 comparators were not perturbed and the screen measured basal RNA rather than TFEB localization, Rag nucleotide state, or autophagic flux.

Sox18 perturbation produced no detectable transcriptional response in the assayed brain neuronal groups: across all Glut/GABA/Dopa classes, the canonical SOX18–PROX1/VEGF/Notch lymphangiogenic program remained silent, with no significant regulation of Prox1, Flt4, Kdr, Foxc1, Foxc2, Nr2f2, Ccbe1, Ctnnb1, Mef2c, or Notch1-4, and no panel tests reaching FDR<0.10. This refines rather than contradicts endothelial literature, because the dataset was restricted to neuronal classes and Sox18 itself was not significantly depleted, so the result does not establish whether neurons could respond to forced SOX18 loss or gain.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grid1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed measurable self-knockdown but a buffered downstream RNA response, and it did not phenocopy Grid2 or canonical glutamate-receptor perturbations. Transcriptome similarity to related receptors was near zero, including Grid2 (r=0.022) and Grin1 (r=-0.0059); Grin1 produced 89 FDR-significant genes whereas Grid1 produced only itself. This separates Grid1 from NMDA, kainate, metabotropic, and Grid2 loss-of-function signatures in this thalamic cell type, while noting that Grid2 on-target depletion was weak and Cbln/Nrxn bridge components were not directly perturbed.

Atp13a2 knockdown did not reproduce the published SYT11- and HDAC6/autophagosome-fusion effector models at the mRNA level: Syt11, Hdac6, Cttn, lysosomal markers Lamp2, Ctsb, and Ctsd, v-ATPase genes Atp6v0c and Atp6v1a, and autophagy or related genes Tsc2, Snca, Tfeb, Sqstm1, and Map1lc3b all showed no FDR-significant response, with Syt11 only nominal in 155 MB Glut despite strong target knockdown. This transcript-level uncoupling is consistent with prior studies using different systems and primarily measuring autophagic flux, protein recruitment, or deacetylation rather than single-cell neuronal mRNA under basal conditions.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Ndufs2 perturbation in 052 Pvalb Gaba interneurons produced a distinctive, small nonself transcriptional response, with induction of Mllt10 and Ppil4, whereas perturbing other engaged Complex I transcripts—Ndufa13, Ndufb8, Ndufc2, Ndufb10, and Ndufa10—depleted their own transcripts but did not yield FDR-significant nonself hits. Thus, in this Pvalb assay, Complex I co-membership did not make these perturbations interchangeable with Ndufs2, although there was weak, restricted convergence with Ndufs3. This contrast is transcriptomic and may reflect differences in guides, knockdown magnitude, transcript abundance, and exact subunit targeted.

Stat3 perturbation did not detectably engage the canonical JAK/gp130-STAT3-SOCS module in these neuronal transcriptomes: Socs3 and Socs1 were not nominally altered, and related pathway components including Jak1, Jak2, Tyk2, Il6st, Il6ra, Osmr, Lifr, Lepr, and Kit did not form a clear downstream module. Consistent with this, perturbing upstream cytokine receptors or Kit failed to phenocopy Stat3, with Il6st, Il6ra, Osmr, Lepr, Kit, Ifngr1, and Ifngr2 showing only near-zero correlation to the Stat3 signature. A weak exception appeared in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, where Stat3 target depletion and receptor correlations were borderline but still small, suggesting stimulus-dependent rather than constitutively wired signaling in these steady-state cell-class averages.

Abca1 showed no FDR-significant downstream RNA response in this neuronal panel, and perturbations of the LXR/RXR regulators Nr1h2, Nr1h3, Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg were likewise null, suggesting the NR1H2/NR1H3 cholesterol-efflux transcriptional program was not detectably engaged here. Abca1 RNA was measured across assayed Abca1 cell types, but knockdown was not significant after multiple-testing correction. This interpretation is limited because the dataset did not test LXR ligand state or basal pathway activity, and target engagement for each nuclear receptor was not independently validated.

Nr1h4 showed no gene-level FDR-significant transcriptomic response, and related perturbations of Nr1h2, Nr1h3, Nr1h5, Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg were likewise jointly silent across 133 target–cell-type combinations, with no corrected convergence or divergence in the NR1H/RXR lipid nuclear receptor module. This shared null suggests the sampled mouse brain states were not running a robust FXR/RXR-like bile-acid/LXR program at baseline, although the scan was transcriptomic only and limited by uncertain engagement of each paralog or RXR isoform.

Cacnb4 was unexpectedly uncoupled from other voltage-gated calcium-channel subunit perturbations in this assay. Across 238 Cacnb4 comparisons with Cacnb2 and alpha1, alpha2delta, and gamma subunits such as Cacna1a, Cacna1c, Cacna1d, Cacna1e, Cacna1g, Cacna2d1, Cacna2d2, Cacng2, Cacng3, and Cacng8, the median absolute score-correlation was only 0.0208; for Cacnb2 specifically, median |r| was 0.0192 and maximum |r| was 0.0938. Other synaptic calcium signaling perturbations produced broader transcriptional signatures, suggesting Cacnb4 loss was molecularly buffered or otherwise not transcriptionally interchangeable here, although comparator target engagement varied and electrophysiological or protein-level similarity was not measured.

Champ1 loss did not produce an FDR-supported Mcl1-linked apoptosis or stress-survival mRNA response in the assayed mouse neuronal classes. Mcl1 was measured across all 22 Champ1 cell types, with a minimum p value of 0.064 and FDR of 1.0 throughout, and Trp53, Cdkn1a, Bbc3, Bax, Sqstm1, and Fam162a likewise showed no FDR-significant changes. This suggests the cancer-cell CHAMP1–Mcl-1 survival axis was not recapitulated here at the transcript level, with the caveat that only mRNA was assayed and prior results came from proliferative cancer cells under antimitotic stress rather than mouse neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Med12 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not phenocopy other Mediator perturbations: despite a larger cell count, it showed no FDR-significant genes and was nearly uncorrelated with Med13, Med15, and Med23 transcriptomic signatures (Pearson 0.011–0.062). In the same cell type, Med13, Med15, and Med23 produced robust repression of genes including Prkcd, Grm1, Pcp4, Atp2b1, and Plekhg1, whereas Cdk8 was also FDR-silent. This contrast is transcriptomic and cell-type-specific, and target-transcript depletion was not validated for each comparator.

Dap3 knockdown in unstimulated mouse neurons was transcriptionally uncoupled from the expected IFN/Fas/TNF apoptosis program: it did not FDR-regulate sentinel transcripts including Bax, Bcl2, Casp3, Casp8, Casp9, Dapk1, Fas, Ifngr1, Ifngr2, Irf1, Stat1, Tnfrsf10b, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Trp53, and Xiap. In 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, the target itself was the main significant signal, with only weak restricted neighbors and Dapk1 merely nominal in the strongest cell type. This refines rather than refutes prior stress-conditioned apoptosis literature, since the assay used partial CRISPRi in unstimulated mouse brain cells and several death-receptor comparators were themselves weakly engaged.

Atp6v1e1 perturbation did not trigger a broad transcriptional V-ATPase replacement program: across 26 measured V-ATPase-family transcripts, only Atp6v1e1 and a weak Atp6ap1l signal reached subthreshold significance, while other subunits such as Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2, Atp6v0c, Atp6ap1, and Atp6ap2 were largely unchanged. Its whole-signature profile also did not closely converge with Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1/Tsc2, Atg5, Becn1, or Mitf perturbations. The clearest weak response was in 308 CB GABA cells, whereas 052 Pvalb Gaba cells had no FDR-significant genes and only weak proximity to Atp6v0c and Atp6v1b2; because knockdown was weak, stronger ATP6V1E1 depletion could still reveal CLEAR, mTOR, or autophagy responses.

Cd2ap perturbation did not produce a detectable transcriptional response in this mouse neuronal scRNA-seq dataset: genome-wide testing found no multiple-testing-corrected Cd2ap-dependent transcripts, and direct on-target Cd2ap depletion was weak and non-significant across profiled neuronal classes. Consistent with that, the annotated CD2AP actin/endocytic adaptor network showed no RNA-level reprogramming, including Sh3kbp1, Cblb, Fyn, Rac1, Cdc42, Cltc, Dnm1, Dnm2, Synj1, Bin1, Abca7, App, Psen1, Sorl1, Picalm, Cttn, Tjp1, Actn4, and Nphs2. Because this panel was literature-derived rather than a prespecified enrichment set, the null RNA result does not exclude CD2AP protein-complex or subcellular phenotypes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rxrb did not phenocopy RXR paralogs or nearby nuclear-receptor perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons. In this cell class, nominal Rxrb self-depletion produced no FDR-significant downstream program, whereas Rora and Thra generated significant comparator signatures, including markers such as Prkcg, Adgrb1, and Hr. Across 24 related perturbations spanning RXR/RAR/LXR/PPAR/thyroid and lipid-disease neighbors, Rxrb score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, arguing that partial Rxrb loss did not collapse retinoic acid/RXR transcription here, with the caveat that several comparators had weak self-knockdown and Rora is a family comparator rather than a direct RXRB heterodimer.

Cadps2 showed weak transcriptomic engagement relative to selected synaptic and vesicle-release perturbations: unlike Snap25, which had corrected hits in 19 of 22 tested cell types, and Cplx1, which had hits in 9 of 22, Cadps2 had none, similar to Cplx2, Unc13a, and Unc13c. This contrast was evident even in cell types with the most Cadps2-perturbed cells, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where no corrected Cadps2 signal was detected. The comparison set was hand selected, and many significant comparator effects reflected the perturbed transcript itself rather than broad downstream modules.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Cacna1e showed near-zero or opposing transcriptomic correlations with other voltage-gated calcium-channel network members, including α1 paralogs Cacna1a, Cacna1c, Cacna1d, and Cacna1g and auxiliary subunits Cacna2d1, Cacna2d2, Cacnb2, Cacnb4, and Cacng2/3/8, across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA. The strongest related-gene correlation was only weakly negative with Cacna1g in 308 CB GABA, where Cacna1e itself was not detectably depleted. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Cacna1g, Cacna2d1, and Cacnb4 self-depleted while Cacna1e did not, arguing against a single interchangeable Cav-channel perturbation module, although Cacna1e was only weakly engaged in many cell types.

Mrtfa perturbation did not produce a coherent actin–MRTF–SRF or immediate-early transcriptional response in this dataset. Across a 17-gene panel including Mrtfb, Srf, Actg1, Actn4, Cfl1, Cfl2, Arc, Egr1, Fos, Tagln, Acta2, Tpm1, Tpm2, Myh9, and Myh10, there were no FDR-significant rows and only scattered nominal changes, with no related perturbation convergence. This interpretation is limited to measured transcripts: Actb was not a DE gene here, SRF/MRTFB protein activity was not assayed, and weak Mrtfa engagement could mask a canonical program.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Large1 depletion showed a largely transcriptionally buffered response across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut cells. In the main FDR-confirmed context, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Large1 itself was the only FDR-significant hit, while curated alpha-dystroglycan matriglycan and dystroglycan-complex transcripts, including Dag1, Fktn, Crppa, Pomk, Pomt1, B4gat1, Large2, and Agrn, were unchanged by FDR. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Wwox increased despite only nominal Large1 depletion. These data are limited to mRNA and do not measure alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation, matriglycan length, or extracellular-matrix binding.

Bcl11a showed no multiple-testing-significant differential expression in this screen, making its null result target-specific rather than a general failure to detect chromatin-regulator phenotypes. In the same table, several BAF/SWI/SNF or CHD4-related perturbations had strong significant signatures, including Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Chd4, Arid1a, Smarce1, Arid1b, Smarca2, and Smarcc1; in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell class, Bcl11a remained null despite 203 perturbed cells while Chd4 was strongly significant. This uncoupling suggests Bcl11a and Bcl11b were weaker than core BAF-associated remodelers, although these comparators are not equivalent subunits and may have broader essential functions.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp804a perturbation did not reproduce a robust synaptic-adhesion or neuroligin-neurexin transcriptomic response in adult mouse cells. In 001 L5-6 IT Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, expected genes including Nlgn1-3, Nrxn1-2, Cadm1-4, Cntnap2, and Pcdh10 were only nominally changed, with isolated signals such as nominal Nlgn2 up in L5-6 IT Glut and nominal Nlgn3 down in CNU-HYa HY GABA, all remaining FDR = 1.0. Mouse Nlgn4 was not a prominent measured signal, suggesting the adhesion/neuroligin biology reported previously may be developmental, activity-dependent, or not captured by this adult mRNA readout.

Traf3 CRISPRi did not transcriptionally engage canonical TRAF3 output modules under basal neuronal conditions: Nfkb2, Relb, Map3k14 and other non-canonical NF-kappa-B/NIK genes, as well as Tlr3, Ifnb1, Isg15, Cxcl10, and Stat1 from the TLR/RLR type-I-interferon program, remained FDR negative across assayed brain cell types. Even in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, which showed the smallest genome-wide Traf3 adjusted p value, there was no FDR-significant Traf3 response. This likely reflects unstimulated, low-engagement cells, and the basal transcriptomic assay did not test receptor stimulation or protein-level events such as NIK stability, RELB nuclear localization, or phosphorylation.

Fgf14 perturbation did not produce FDR-significant mRNA changes in the canonical AIS NaV/Kv module across any of the 22 tested cell classes, including Scn1a, Scn1b, Scn2a, Scn8a, Kcnq2, Kcnq3, Ank3, Kcnab1, and Kcnab2. In measured classes such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 308 CB GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, the pattern supports a protein-channel mechanism with no adjusted core mRNA response, indicating that transcript abundance is a poor proxy for the immediate Fgf14 loss-of-function phenotype, which is thought to involve channel gating, protein targeting, and AIS localization.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Stat4 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut neurons showed signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with assayed STAT paralogs and IL-receptor neighbors, arguing against interpreting the weak Stat4 signal as a generic STAT-family module. Across cell types, mean signed-score correlations were near zero for Stat1, Stat2, Stat3, Stat5b, Il12b, and Il12rb1, with the largest absolute related-target correlation only 0.175. This is exploratory because the signatures were largely nonsignificant, and key network neighbors such as Tyk2, Jak2, and Il12rb2 were not assayed as comparators.

Raf1 perturbation did not produce a reproducible canonical ERK-feedback transcriptional response. Across pooled single-cell transcriptomes, ERK-output and immediate-early genes including Dusp4/5/6, Spry1/2, Etv1/4/5, Fos/Fosb, and Egr1-4 were not detectably altered, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic neurons Raf1 also failed to reproduce the Braf/Map2k1/Nf1-responsive Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 module. These results argue against a strong RAF-MEK-ERK state change under Raf1 knockdown, while leaving open transient phospho-ERK or very early mRNA pulses that steady-state single-cell RNA measurements could miss.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Cpt1c perturbation produced a largely target-only transcriptomic response across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. Known AMPAR/SAC1/ATL1 and lipid/AMPK-adjacent genes, including Gria1-4, Sacm1l, Atl1, Cacng2, Cacng3, Acacb, Cpt2, Prkaa2, and Prkag2, were not significantly changed, and perturbations of Gria, Cacng, Atl1, Prkaa2, or Prkag2 did not phenocopy the Cpt1c score vector; however, these comparisons rely on mostly weak DE score vectors and some partner perturbations had limited on-target engagement.

Cacna1a partial loss showed no FDR-supported transcriptional compensation among the measured calcium-channel genes: Cacna1c, Cacna1d, Cacna1e, Cacna1g, Cacna2d1, Cacna2d2, Cacnb2, Cacnb4, Cacng2, Cacng3, and Cacng8 were not induced. This argues against a simple mRNA-level feedback program in the presynaptic depolarization and calcium channel opening pathway, although responses across the CaV2.1 auxiliary-subunit complex were only weakly correlated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut. Cacna1b was not assessed, so functional buffering may still occur through translational, trafficking-based, circuit-level, or N-type substitution mechanisms.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ergic1 depletion was uncoupled from a canonical ER-stress/unfolded protein response in the two strongest knockdown cell types, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: UPR and ER quality-control transcripts including Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Canx, Hyou1, Nfe2l1, and Chac1 were not significantly induced. In contrast, Sec63 and Hspa5 perturbations induced ER chaperone and quality-control genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, suggesting that in this assay the ER-stress-positive secretory-pathway perturbations were Sec63 and Hspa5 rather than Ergic1; however, the positive comparator was strongest in one thalamic glutamatergic class and unfolded-protein load was inferred from transcripts rather than measured biochemically.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Aifm1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed only a nominal self-transcript decrease, ranking among the negative genes but not reaching FDR significance, and no downstream genes were FDR-significant. By contrast, respiratory-chain and intermembrane-space comparators such as Ndufa13, Uqcrc1, Cox5a, Ndufs2, and Ndufs8 often had strong self-transcript loss yet still yielded only the targeted transcript at FDR<0.05. This suggests the AIFM1/CHCHD4 respiratory-chain biogenesis axis is weakly captured by steady-state mRNA here, with CHCHD4 absent from the library and likely protein-complex or metabolic effects not guaranteed to produce an mRNA program.

Grid2 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage its expected synaptic-organizer neighborhood across the pan-assayed Grid2 cell types: no gene reached FDR<0.10, on-target Grid2 transcript knockdown was weak, and canonical NRXN-CBLN-GRID2 excitatory synapse organization genes including Cbln1/2, Nrxn1/2, Grm1, Shank1/2, Grid2ip, Gopc, Gria1-4, Dcc, and Neo1 were not significantly regulated. This argues against inferring downstream Grid2 signaling from these DE profiles, while leaving open non-transcriptomic effects on ligand secretion, receptor localization, channel gating, LTD, or dendritic competition.

Sema6a perturbation showed transcriptome-wide uncoupling from semaphorin-plexin cell-surface signaling neighbors, with at most weak full-vector similarity to Plxna1, Plxna2, Plxna4, Nrp1, Nrp2, Plxnd1, Plxnc1, Sema4d, and Sema5a despite curated SEMA6A–plexin proximity. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Sema6a mRNA reduction was only nominal and lacked FDR-significant downstream genes, while in 191 MB P MY GABA the only FDR-significant downstream gene was Camk2n1 without measured Sema6a depletion. These results suggest neighbor perturbations are not interchangeable transcriptomic proxies for Sema6a here, although weak Sema6a engagement limits power to detect true convergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Dnajb6 did not transcriptionally mobilize the HSP40–HSP70–HSF1 heat-shock response in basal neuronal Perturb-seq across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. Canonical chaperone/stress readouts such as Hsf1, Hspa8, Hspa9, Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Dnaja1, Hsph1, Hspa4l, Ahsa2, and Stip1 showed no FDR-significant Dnajb6 responses, whereas Hsf1, Hspa8, and especially Hspa9 perturbations produced non-self stress-related DE signals in the same dataset. This contrast is tempered by differing guide efficacies and cell counts, and Hspa9 showed many non-self DE genes despite lacking FDR-significant self-depletion.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Slc1a2 knockdown in matched excitatory neurons was largely transcriptionally uncoupled from NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Slc1a2 showed significant on-target depletion but no FDR-significant secondary response, and in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut it was only nominal, whereas Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced strong downstream programs. Across engaged classes, Slc1a2 correlations with Grin1/Grin2a/Grin2b and Slc1a1 were near zero, suggesting EAAT2 uptake perturbation did not phenocopy or oppose postsynaptic receptor loss in this assay; these are transcriptomic contrasts, not direct electrophysiology or extracellular-glutamate measurements.

Litaf showed no multiple-testing-corrected downstream transcriptional response in this neuron-rich brain Perturb-seq panel, and the related LPS/TLR/TNF inflammatory axis also appeared largely unengaged: Tlr2, Tlr3, Tlr4, Tlr5, Tlr7, Tlr8, Tlr9, Tnfrsf1a, and Tnfrsf1b were nearly inert, yielding only two FDR-significant genes across 188 target-cell profiles. In unstimulated Glut, GABA, and Dopa classes, these data therefore do not support interpreting Litaf as an innate-cytokine node, with the caveat that stimulated macrophages or microglia were not assayed and many TLR targets were sparsely detected.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pomp showed a more buffered, weaker perturbation pattern than direct proteasome-subunit targets such as Psmb4, Psmc1, and Psmc5 across the brain. In several cell types with adequate Pomp cell counts, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 053 Sst Gaba, and 308 CB GABA, Pomp produced no FDR-significant differential expression, whereas Psmb4 or Psmc1 yielded detectable signatures in the same classes. This suggests assembly-chaperone perturbation was not interchangeable with 20S or 19S subunit perturbation here, although sgRNA potency or mRNA/protein stability could also explain the contrast.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Uchl1 depletion did not phenocopy core proteasome-subunit perturbations. After excluding the target transcript, Uchl1 produced no cell-type-level differentially expressed genes at 5% FDR and no closely matching or inverted signature, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Psmb4, Psmc1, and Psmc5 each drove hundreds to thousands of significant genes. This separates Uchl1 loss from immediate proteasome-mediated ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic stress in this assay, although the proteasome-subunit guides often lacked FDR-significant loss of their own mRNAs and therefore serve as pathway-neighbor contrasts rather than matched knockdown controls.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Plxna4 did not phenocopy related semaphorin-system perturbations in this dataset: across 198 same-cell-type comparisons, its transcriptome-score signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Plxna1, Plxna2, Plxnc1, Plxnd1, Nrp1, Nrp2, Sema4d, Sema5a, and Sema6a, with the largest absolute Pearson correlation only 0.0939. This held in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Plxna2 and Plxna4 were both detectably knocked down yet produced essentially unrelated signatures; however, these are score-based correlations, and Plxna4 target engagement was weaker than Plxna2 in the shared cell types.

Pacs2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant RNA response, including at Pacs2 itself, and did not shift canonical ER-mitochondria contact, autophagy, UPR, or apoptotic markers such as Bcap31, Atg14, Stx17, Becn1, Itpr1, Mfn2, Xbp1, Atf4, Ddit3, Bid, or Bcl2l11. This pathway-negative pattern was also seen across several neuronal cell types, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, but interpretation is limited by weak Pacs2 knockdown and an RNA-only readout of largely post-transcriptional organelle biology.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Shank2 knockdown was largely uncoupled from NMDA receptor subunit transcriptional phenotypes in cortical IT glutamatergic neurons. Across 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b perturbations produced many more FDR-significant mRNA changes than Shank2, with 103, 23, and 62 significant rows versus only one on-target row for Shank2 and no non-target FDR hits. The nearest same-cell-type Shank2 neighbors were only weakly Grin2b-like, with nominal Nptxr/Lingo1-type candidates, so receptor-subunit loss and Shank2 loss were not equivalent in this mRNA assay, which does not directly measure NMDAR currents.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Msi1 perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from canonical NUMB/Notch and PTEN/p21 readouts across many neuronal classes, with Numb, Numbl, Pten, Cdkn1a, Hes1, Hes5, and Notch1/2/3 mRNAs unchanged at the FDR threshold. This held across diverse glutamatergic and GABAergic populations, including large strata such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 053 Sst Gaba showed the strongest nominal response but only 39 Msi1 cells and no FDR-significant genes. Because the assay measured RNA abundance rather than NUMB, PTEN, HES, or phospho-AKT protein activity, and several genes were lowly detected in some groups, these null mRNA results do not exclude MSI1 effects at translation or protein output.

Klf13 perturbation did not produce FDR-significant changes in a 12-gene panel of published KLF13-linked cAMP and growth-hormone JAK/STAT output genes, including Prkaca, Calm3, Jak1/2/3, Stat3, Stat5a/5b, Socs1, Socs3, Igf1, and Bdnf, in any assayed class. This suggests no detectable release of these pathways in the mature neuronal states profiled, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Klf13 still had no FDR-significant downstream genes. The result is limited by weak Klf13 target-transcript engagement and by the gene-level panel check rather than a full pathway enrichment test.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Smarca2 showed a buffered perturbation profile in glutamatergic neurons, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Arid2, Arid1a, and Smarce1 each produced 11–286 FDR-significant genes, while Smarca2 affected only its own transcript. In 155 MB Glut, Smarca2 was also engaged without an FDR-level downstream program, and related BAF subunits likewise showed weaker off-target responses than in 151 TH. This refines expectations for mSWI/SNF ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling, although differing cell counts and weak Smarca4 target engagement limit a direct SMARCA2–SMARCA4 paralog comparison.

Pld3 knockdown in the assayed neuronal populations produced widespread on-target Pld3 mRNA reduction but did not induce APP/TLR/interferon sentinel transcripts: App, Sorl1, Tlr7, Tlr9, Ifit1, Ifnb1, Irf7, and Isg15 remained non-significant. Thus, in this Perturb-seq setting, reduced Pld3 was transcriptionally uncoupled from lysosomal nucleic-acid catabolism/endosomal TLR control and from APP/endosomal sorting signatures. This does not exclude signaling through Mb21d1/cGAS or Tmem173/STING, which were not tested here, or post-transcriptional activation of TLR or cGAS-STING pathways.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Oprk1 showed no reproducible target-transcript decrease and no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any assayed cell class, even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In contrast, perturbations of Grin2b, Grin2a, Gnao1, Gnb1, Pde10a, Chrnb2, Chrna4, Adcy3, Pde4b, and Mapk1 produced significant on-target or downstream signatures across neuronal receptor and intracellular signaling pathways in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and related classes. This contrast indicates assay headroom and suggests the Oprk1 null is target-specific, although comparator expression, guide number, cell counts, and biology were not matched.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ddr2 remained FDR-null in higher-powered neuronal contexts, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, despite 101–163 perturbed cells and no detectable Ddr2 transcript depletion or downstream FDR-level effects. In overlapping cell classes, Ntrk2, Map2k1, and Mapk1 produced detectable on-target or pathway-level signals, indicating that the Ddr2 null is not simply due to poor assay sensitivity for kinase or RTK-pathway phenotypes. This contrast serves as an assay-sensitivity control rather than evidence of shared mechanism, since the comparator kinases are not DDR2 paralogs and differ in expression and wiring.

Il31ra perturbation showed no detectable baseline transcriptional output of its expected downstream pathways in the central brain panel. Across all Il31ra conditions tested, canonical JAK/STAT, MAPK, and cytokine-feedback genes including Socs3, Cish, Stat3, Stat5b, Mapk1, Fos, and Jun remained nonsignificant, indicating that these transcripts were uncoupled from Il31ra loss at the transcript level. This null result should be interpreted with the caveat that the assay lacked an explicit IL-31 ligand challenge and measured transcript abundance rather than phospho-STAT or phospho-ERK signaling.

Fgf14 showed divergent or near-zero whole-transcriptome correlations with Fgf12, Fgf13, Fgf1, Fgfr1, Fgfr2, Fgfr3, Fgfrl1, and NaV/Kcnab perturbations across overlapping cell classes, rather than globally phenocopying those signatures; the strongest absolute Pearson correlations for these comparator families were only about 0.094 to 0.105. In the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, Scn and Kcnab knockdowns were strongly engaged while Fgf14 remained weak, with an exploratory restricted signature converging on Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Ank3, Dlgap4, and Grip1. This lack of phenocopy should be interpreted cautiously because correlation is blunt for weak Fgf14 signatures and the Fgf14 knockdown may have been weaker than some Scn or Kcnab comparators.

Cacng8 showed a weak, no-FDR-significant transcriptomic response, a pattern shared by the screened TARP paralogs Cacng2 and Cacng3 across 22 cell types, even in high-count strata such as 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. In contrast, AMPA receptor trafficking and postsynaptic neighbors including Gria2, Frrs1l, Dlg4, and Camk2b displayed corrected self-knockdown hits in selected classes, arguing for a TARP-specific guide or assay limitation rather than a general failure to perturb synaptic genes, although target-level DE summaries without matched guide efficiency or protein measurements limit interpretation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Ppib depletion in seven target-engaged neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, did not induce a canonical ER/unfolded-protein response transcript program: Atf6, Hspa5, Xbp1, Calr, Canx, Sec63, and Stt3b were not FDR-responsive, and Ppib signatures were nearly uncorrelated with assayed ER-neighbor perturbations. This argues against a bulk ER stress transcriptional response, although weak engagement of most comparator perturbations and possible noncanonical or proteomic stress remain caveats.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Clock perturbation most clearly suppresses a canonical CLOCK:BMAL1 circadian-output module in two neuronal classes, 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In both, Dbp, Nr1d2, and Tef are downregulated, with Per3 additionally significant in 155 MB Glut; Per1, Hlf, and Bhlhe41 also track this output pattern, while Cry1 can show nominal or significant induction in the highest-response contexts. Bmal1 shows convergent signatures, but multi-gene FDR support is concentrated in these two cell types, and the Clock transcript itself is not FDR-depleted.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Med13 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a transcriptional response that partially converged with Med15 and Med23, with shared significant genes including Prkcd, Grm1, Pcp4, Plekhg1, and Atp2a2, whereas the more immediate CDK8-module neighbors Cdk8 and Med12 had larger perturbed cell counts but no FDR-significant genes in the same class. This suggests Mediator subunits were not interchangeable in this thalamic population, although the correlations were modest, guide efficacy may differ across perturbations, and the panel lacked Ccnc and Cdk19.

Myo6 perturbation did not produce a coordinated mRNA response in its known trafficking network across the profiled brain cells. In particular, AP-2/clathrin endocytosis genes such as Ap2a1, Ap2a2, Ap2b1, Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Clta, Cltb, and Cltc, and TOM1/OPTN-linked autophagy genes including Tom1, Optn, Tax1bp1, Calcoco2, Atg5, Atg7, Map1lc3b, Sqstm1, and Tbk1 showed no FDR-supported changes; weak nominal Myo6-associated signals were not recurrent across cell classes. This negative result is transcriptional and does not exclude altered partner recruitment, vesicle movement, or autophagic flux without detectable mRNA shifts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Arid1b in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a weak, self-limited transcriptomic response within the canonical BAF/SWI-SNF context: Arid1b itself was the only FDR-significant hit, whereas Arid1a, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, and Smarce1 perturbations in the same cell class yielded 22, 286, 185, and 11 FDR-significant genes, respectively. Although Arid1b weakly aligned with signatures of other cBAF-member perturbations, most overlap fell below the Arid1b FDR threshold, so its acute effect should not be treated as generic cBAF collapse; comparator guide-cell counts and knockdown strengths were not identical, and these are transcriptomic rather than biochemical readouts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Chrnd was unchanged in brain-cell Perturb-seq, even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where Agrn, Chrnb2, Ache, and Chrna4 showed significant self-transcript knockdown; Agrn, Chrnb2, and Ache also had significant self-knockdown in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, with additional signal in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 145 MH-LH TH Glut. This suggests the matrix can detect expressed cholinergic or NMJ-neighbor genes, whereas Chrnd and most muscle-type AChR/NMJ module genes, including Chrna1, Chrnb1, Chrne, Chrng, Musk, and Lrp4, are largely silent, though the strongest comparators include neuronal and secreted cholinergic genes rather than only strict CHRND-complex members.

Crppa reduction showed no significant transcriptional feedback in the measured alpha-dystroglycan O-mannosylation and extracellular-matrix module: across monitored genes including Dag1, Fkrp, Fktn, Large1, Rxylt1, Pomk, Pomt1, Pomt2, Pomgnt1, Pomgnt2, B4gat1, B3galnt2, Gmppb, Agrn, Dmd, Lama2, and Lrp4, transcript levels remained essentially flat after perturbation. This suggests that mild neuronal Crppa perturbation was not reported back through steady-state RNA in the CDP-ribitol/alpha-dystroglycan pathway, with the caveat that the knockdown was weak and the assay measured RNA rather than alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation.

Kcna1 perturbation did not produce a recurrent transcriptional compensation program among measured ion-channel genes: Kcna2, Kcna4, Kcnab1, Kcnab2, Kcnq2, Kcnq3, Scn1a, Scn2a, and Scn8a were never FDR-significant, and nominal p<0.001 downstream rows were unique to single broad cell classes rather than recurring across them. This included 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, where the smallest adjusted p values still remained non-significant, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where many nominal rows coincided with weak Kcna1 depletion, limiting on-target interpretation. The negative result is further limited to mRNA measurements, not channel localization or activity.

Coq5 partial knockdown did not trigger a coordinated transcriptional compensation program in the measured ubiquinol/coenzyme Q biosynthesis or OXPHOS modules. Across 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Coq5 was nominally reduced, but neighboring CoQ genes such as Pdss1, Pdss2, Coq3, Coq4, Coq6, Coq7, Coq9, Coq10a, and Coq10b showed mixed nominal directions and remained FDR-null; no gene in the full Coq5 table crossed FDR 0.05. OXPHOS sentinels including Ndufa13, Uqcrc1, Cox5a, Cyc1, and Sdha also showed only weak, non-coherent responses, with the caveat that only transcript levels were tested and some metabolon genes were not perturbed or strongly expressed in every cell type.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Foxl2 was largely uncoupled from related perturbation signatures in this brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across cell types including 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, pathway neighbors such as Ctnnb1, Sox2, Bmpr2, Smad2, Tgfbr2, Foxg1, and Nr5a1 each showed at least one FDR-significant context, whereas Foxl2 and its paralog Foxl1 showed none. Correlations between Foxl2 score vectors and Forkhead, TGF/BMP/SMAD, Wnt, and ovarian-fate comparators were weak, with a maximum curated-neighbor |r| of 0.133; most comparator hits were single-gene FDR events, and the expected FOXL2-SMAD relationship is drawn from ovarian or gonadotrope cells rather than neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp423 showed a distinct transcriptomic response in the adult thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class that was not reproduced by perturbing Zfp521, Ebf1, Ebf2, Ebf3, Acvr2b, Bmpr2, Smad1, Smad4, or Smad9. In this responsive class, these EBF and BMP/SMAD pathway neighbor perturbations were largely weak or FDR-silent, so the Zfp423 state was not interchangeable with canonical BMP/SMAD or EBF partner loss. This contrast is based on transcriptomic phenotypes rather than direct measurements of editing, protein abundance, BMP ligand tone, or SMAD phosphorylation.

Nfe2l2 perturbation did not produce a coherent reduction of the canonical NRF2 antioxidant and detoxification program in these neuronal contrasts. Curated NRF2 output genes including Gclc, Gclm, Gsr, Hmox1, Nqo1, Prdx1, Prdx6, Slc7a11, Sqstm1, Srxn1, Txn1, and Fth1 were essentially flat with mixed directions, so the expected KEAP1-CUL3-NFE2L2 stress-response regulon was not captured. This reflects a curated-gene inspection rather than a positive enrichment result, and NRF2 target induction is stress- and context-dependent under basal single-cell conditions.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Bmpr2 knockdown in 155 MB Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut produced strong on-target RNA depletion, with Bmpr2 as the only FDR-significant gene in these contexts, yet it did not elicit an FDR-significant canonical BMP receptor-SMAD-ID transcriptional response. In particular, Id1–Id4, Smad1/5/9, and feedback/readout genes Hey1, Hes1, and Bambi were not detectably changed. This suggests buffered downstream transcription in these neuronal states, while remaining consistent with caveats that the assay measured RNA only and did not assess BMP ligand exposure or SMAD phosphorylation.

Kif21a did not behave like a generic kinesin knockdown in this assay: its full-transcriptome signature was largely orthogonal to available perturbations of Kif1a, Kif1b, Kif2a, Kif3b, Kif5a, Kif5c, Kif11, Klc1, and Klc2, with all matched correlations very small (|r|<0.087). This argues against treating microtubule-based movement and plus-end kinesin motor activity as a single interchangeable transcriptomic class here. A caveat is that the closest paralog Kif21b and KANK/CMSC partners were not perturbed, so comparisons were limited to broader motor neighbors rather than the exact KIF21A complex.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Cdkal1 perturbation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut was associated with an isolated increase in Ggps1, the only FDR-significant gene in this contrast, rising by 0.84 logFC across 44 perturbed cells. Other measured mevalonate and prenylation genes, including Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Mvk, Fdps, Idi1, Fnta, and Fntb, did not show coordinated induction. This pattern links Cdkal1 to a geranylgeranyl-diphosphate synthase readout in this hypothalamic/thalamic glutamatergic class, but it does not support a broad canonical mevalonate-pathway response.

Cd79b perturbation was uncoupled from the measured B-cell antigen receptor signaling transcript readout: Cd79a, Ptprc, H2-Eb1, Nfkb2, and assayed Tlr genes showed no corrected changes, while Nfkb1 and Pik3ca/Pik3cb/Pik3r1/Pik3r2 reached only weak nominal p values with FDR 1.0. In this mouse-brain transcriptomic endpoint, the result supports an off-lineage null rather than recruitment of BCR-, PI3K-, immune-marker-, or NF-kappaB-associated transcripts, with the caveat that only transcript abundances were tested and acute phosphorylation or calcium flux were not measured.

Smad4 loss did not recover a canonical TGF/BMP/SMAD feedback program in the assayed neuronal states: across cell types, literature-curated sentinel genes including Id1-Id4, Smad7, Ski, Skil, Jun, Fos, Zeb1, and Zeb2 showed no FDR-significant response. This argues against strong tonic canonical SMAD signaling in these homeostatic cells, although the inference is limited because the panel was hand-curated rather than enrichment-derived. In 145 MH-LH TH Glut, Jun induction and Kctd3 loss were only nominal and remained non-significant after correction.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Mafg knockdown in 052 Pvalb Gaba cells produced a selective Hmox1 burst rather than a broad canonical Nrf2/small-Maf antioxidant program. In this context, Hmox1 was the strongest Pvalb signal, while other ARE-related genes such as Gclc, Gclm, Sqstm1, Fth1, and Sod2 were not FDR-significant, and related perturbations including Nfe2l1, Nfe2l2, Gclm, Sqstm1, Fth1, Sod2, and Psmb4 did not reproduce the Hmox1 response. The contrast is strongest for Hmox1 rank specificity, because some comparator perturbations showed weak or absent on-target transcript reduction, notably Nfe2l2.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grm6 was uncoupled from related metabotropic glutamate receptor and retinal-cascade perturbations in this brain dataset, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. Grm6 signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Grm1, Grm3, Grm5, Grm7, Grm8, Gnao1, Gnb1, Gnb5, Nyx, Gpr179, and Rho, with the largest absolute correlation only about 0.14, and unlike Grm1, Grm7, Gnao1, and Gnb1, Grm6 showed no detectable self-repression. These weak, nonconvergent signals suggest the canonical retinal mGluR6-Go-TRPM1 pathway was not engaged here, though several core retinal partners were not perturbed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gabrg2 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was largely target-only, with strong depletion of Gabrg2 but no non-target genes reaching FDR<0.10, whereas the comparator Gabrb2 perturbation in the same thalamic glutamatergic class induced a broad Nr4a1/Vgf/Fos/Npas4/Homer2 program. Thus, despite both encoding GABA_A receptor subunits, Gabrg2 and Gabrb2 were not interchangeable here, consistent with subunit- and cell-context-specific receptor biology. This contrast is transcriptomic only and reflects different guides and cell counts rather than matched receptor-composition or chloride-current assays.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Drd4 silencing appeared selectively silent at the receptor layer: in matched brain cell classes including 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Drd4 showed no detectable target RNA reduction and no FDR-significant differential-expression signal, similar to Drd2, Drd3, Drd5, and Adora2a. In contrast, Comt and the intracellular GPCR/cAMP nodes Gnao1, Gnb1, and Adcy3 showed clear on-target decreases in selected cell types, suggesting limited receptor accessibility or expression rather than total assay failure, although these intracellular perturbations produced only sparse downstream transcriptional effects.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nectin1 showed its clearest nominal on-target depletion in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA, but these engaged cell types remained transcriptionally quiet: no adherens-junction, Nectin-family, or synaptic-adhesion transcripts reached FDR significance. Across Afdn, Nectin2/3/4, Cdh2, Ctnna2, Ctnnb1, Pard3, Cadm1/2/3, Dlg4, Ephb2, Nrxn1/2, and Nlgn2, changes were at most nominal; in CB GABA, Ephb2 was nominally decreased. These data argue against a rapid mRNA-level feedback module after acute Nectin1 loss, while leaving protein localization, junction morphology, and Afdn function unresolved.

Myo6 showed very low transcriptomic similarity to related cytoskeletal and vesicle-trafficking perturbations in the assayed cell classes: full-score-vector correlations with same-cell-type perturbations were tiny, and selected comparators including Myo5a, Myo9a, Actb, Actg1, Cltc, Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Dnm1, Dnm2, Dync1h1, Kif5a, Vps35, Vps41, Washc4, Tmem63c, and Sec31a never exceeded |r|=0.080. Thus, Myo6 did not phenocopy clathrin-mediated endocytosis/AMPA receptor internalization or broader actin-based motor and vesicle-trafficking signatures, although weak Myo6 score vectors may understate pathway similarity and this same-cell-type comparison is transcriptomic rather than a direct protein-interaction assay.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Dnm2 was transcriptionally uncoupled from other endocytic network perturbations, including Dnm1, Bin1, Cltc, Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Synj1, and Vps35, across several shared cell classes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, AP-2, clathrin, Synj1, and Vps35 perturbations produced FDR-supported signatures where Dnm2 was weak, singleton-only, or FDR-negative, and full-signature correlations were small. The only broader Dnm2 nominal module appeared in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, but target reduction there was only nominal, so this contrast more securely reflects observed transcriptomic divergence than protein-level endocytic requirements.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sele perturbation in the neuronal dataset did not induce the canonical endothelial leukocyte-rolling or vascular adhesion module across diverse glutamatergic and GABAergic classes, including L5-6 IT Glut, L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Pvalb Gaba, Sst Gaba, MB Dopa, and CB GABA. Where measured, Selplg, Icam1, Vcam1, Itgb2, Itgb1, Itga4, Pecam1, Cdh5, Tnf, Il1b, Ccl2, and Cxcl10 were unchanged, indicating that vascular-wall and inflammatory marker genes were uncoupled from neuronal Sele perturbation; some markers such as Selp and Sell were absent in subsets of cell classes, consistent with low expression or filtering.

Vdr perturbation was uncoupled from its expected RXR partners in this basal screen: whole-transcriptome signatures for Vdr showed nearly zero same-cell correlations with Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg, so the expected ligand-dependent VDR/RXR transcriptional module was not recovered. This should be interpreted cautiously, however, because the RXR perturbations themselves also lacked FDR-supported own-transcript knockdown, raising the possibility that weak perturbation engagement or absence of ligand, rather than true independence, explains the lack of coupling.
