cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sgcd perturbation produced a transcriptional non-response across 21 neuronal classes, including multiple cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic types and GABAergic classes such as Pvalb and Sst Gaba. Despite SGCD being a core dystrophin-glycoprotein complex component, no coordinated remodeling was detected for DGC and related genes including Dag1, Sgca/Sgcb/Sgcg/Sgce, Sspn, Dmd, Utrn, Snta1, Sntg1/2, Dtnb, Dtna, Large1, Fktn, Pomt1/2, Pomgnt1, Nos1, and Cav3; all remained non-significant. The largest sampled class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, showed only a sub-threshold signature. The on-target transcript was measured but did not show a reproducible decrease, and these data do not address protein assembly, localization, membrane mechanics, or calcium handling.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Notch1 did not behave interchangeably with available Notch-pathway neighbors in this screen. Across cell types, perturbations of Notch2, Notch3, Notch4, Dll1, Psen1, and Adam10 showed weak, mostly isolated signatures that were nearly uncorrelated with Notch1, and unbiased matching found no robust positive or inverse transcriptomic neighbor. In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons, Notch1 uniquely increased Camk2g, whereas related perturbations did not reproduce this response, and canonical HES/HEY/DTX targets remained unchanged. Interpretation is tempered by lower cell counts for some comparators and by correlations computed on ranked differential-expression score vectors rather than raw single-cell profiles.

Notch2 showed a muted transcriptional phenotype that was not an isolated outlier within the assayed Notch receptor-ligand-protease module: perturbations of Notch1, Notch3, Notch4, Dll1, Adam10, Psen1, and Fbxw7 together produced only three FDR<0.05 genes across 140 target-by-cell-type signatures in the annotated neuronal classes. The few related hits were isolated single-gene signatures, including Camk2g, Mpc2, and Trp53inp2, rather than recurrent HES/HEY-type outputs. This sparse pattern should be interpreted cautiously because Fbxw7 is pleiotropic, Adam10 and Psen1 had fewer and lower-count signatures, and the isolated hits do not establish direct Notch regulation.

Phka1 perturbation showed no coordinated transcriptional response in a targeted glycogen metabolism and phosphorylase-kinase panel: across the assayed genes, including Agl, Gaa, Gbe1, Gyg, Gys1, Gys2, Pygb, Pygl, Pygm, Ugp2, and the PhK components Phkb, Phkg2, Calm1, Calm2, and Calm3, no FDR-supported changes were detected. Thus, measured glycogenolysis transcripts were uncoupled from Phka1 perturbation, with Phka1 and Phkb near-null and nonconvergent at the mRNA level; this caveat is important because the phenotype assayed was transcript abundance, whereas PhK mainly regulates glycogen breakdown through phosphorylation and allostery.

Gpx4 perturbation did not produce a detectable transcriptional response in the measured GPX4-glutathione lipid hydroperoxide detoxification and ferroptosis-suppression axis: Slc7a11, Acsl4, Tfrc, Aifm2, Gclc, Gclm, Fth1, Nfe2l2, and GPX-family transcripts remained unchanged, with no FDR-significant effects in any Gpx4 comparison. This was also true in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, even though comparator perturbations such as Fth1 and Acsl4 showed clear on-target knockdown in the same screen, suggesting the lack of response may reflect limited GPX4 depletion or absent Gpx4 expression rather than true buffering.

Madd perturbation did not produce significant transcript-level changes in its expected RAB/synaptic-vesicle or TNFR-MAPK-apoptosis pathways: Rab27a, Rab3a, Rab3gap1, Rab3gap2, Kif1a, Kif1b, Snap25, Stxbp1, Tnf, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf1b, Mapk1, Mapk3, Mapk8, Mapk9, Casp3, Casp8, and Fadd were present but remained unchanged at the FDR threshold. This held across tested cell classes, including 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, where Madd itself showed the strongest nominal decreases yet downstream signatures and related-perturbation convergence were weak. The result is a negative steady-state scRNA finding and does not assess Rab activation, vesicle transport, ERK phosphorylation, TNF stimulation, or caspase activity.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gata2 perturbation did not reproduce the published developmental neurotransmitter-fate programs in this mouse brain screen. Across 145 MH-LH TH Glut and eight GABA-labeled classes, canonical GABAergic, glutamatergic, serotonergic, and Nkx2-2/Skor2 markers—including Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, Slc17a6, Slc17a7, Tph2, Slc6a4, Gata3, Lmx1b, Nkx2-2, and Skor2—remained nonsignificant, and the inhibitory classes had no FDR<0.05 downstream genes. The sole significant hit was an Mlec decrease in 145 MH-LH TH Glut without a fate-marker switch, consistent with the caveat that prior Gata2 effects were embryonic and lineage-specific rather than evident in these later neuronal classes.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Rmnd1 perturbation did not produce a coordinated loss of mitochondrial-encoded RNAs; instead, the few mtDNA transcript changes were sporadic nominal increases, most notably mt-Co2 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 155 MB Glut, with a small cluster of nominal increases in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut. Across mt-Co1, mt-Nd4, mt-Atp6, mt-Nd1, mt-Nd5, and mt-Cytb, none passed FDR correction, and genome-wide testing yielded no corrected hit, suggesting that mtDNA transcript abundance is a weak RNA readout for RMND1 loss in this assay.

Hoxb8 showed a buffered, nonconvergent pattern: across the assayed neurons, related HOX-family perturbations and the HOX cofactors Pbx1 and Meis1 were largely devoid of robust differential-expression phenotypes and did not align with Hoxb8 signatures. Six additional HOX perturbations yielded only one FDR-significant gene across 136 target-cell-type signatures, and Hoxb8 correlations with Pbx1 and Meis1 were near zero. Weak nearest-neighbor relationships did not define a strong perturbational neighborhood, although key comparators were missing, including Hoxa8, Hoxc8, Hoxd8, and several Hoxb-cluster STRING partners.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Spata7 showed no detectable significant transcriptional response in this brain Perturb-seq dataset, unlike several related ciliary or retinal-ciliopathy perturbations that produced sparse FDR-supported signals in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 308 CB GABA, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA. In particular, Ahi1, Adcy3, Cplane1, Ift88, B9d1, and Bbs5 had limited hits, and in 155 MB Glut some showed self-transcript depletion, whereas Spata7 lacked an on-target readout. This suggests Spata7 was not interchangeable with broader BBSome, IFT, transition-zone, or ciliary-cAMP perturbations in the assayed neurons, although related-target effects were generally small and guide efficiency and expression were not matched to Spata7.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Il10rb was broadly assayed across 22 glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal subclasses and appeared transcriptionally neutral: it showed no RNA-level target depletion, no corrected downstream hits, no JAK/STAT or ISG shift, and no robust cytokine- or receptor-family signature neighbors. Il10ra was likewise neutral, and Il10rb signatures were only weakly correlated with Il10ra, Ifnar1, Ifnar2, Ifngr1, Ifngr2, Stat1, or Stat3, so Il10rb did not phenocopy IFN/STAT-family receptor perturbations. This pattern is consistent with a silent IL-10 receptor module in these assayed neuronal states, while limited target engagement and unavailable comparators such as IFNLR1 and IL22RA1 remain caveats.

Fth1 knockdown did not transcriptionally recruit a corrected iron-homeostasis, ferritinophagy, or ferroptosis RNA module: Aco1, Ireb2, Tfrc, Slc11a2, Slc40a1, Hfe, Hmox1, Hmox2, Ncoa4, Gpx4, Slc7a11, Acsl4, Cisd2, Nfe2l2, and Keap1 were not induced at corrected significance, with only isolated nominal signals. This pattern was seen despite strong on-target Fth1 depletion in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, suggesting that partial Fth1 loss in these acute cultures did not create a broad RNA-level iron-starvation or ferroptotic state, while leaving open post-transcriptional IRP/IRE regulation through translation or mRNA stability.

Phkb perturbation showed no significant transcriptional feedback across the assayed dataset, with no conventionally significant downstream transcripts in any cell type and 0/374 significant tests within the curated glycogenolysis neighborhood. Genes in the phosphorylase-kinase complex and glycogen-control module, including Phka1, Phka2, Phkg2, Calm1/2/3, Pygb/Pygm/Pygl, Ppp1ca/b/c, Ppp1r3a/b, Gys1/2, and Gsk3b, were unchanged. One cerebellar class, 308 CB GABA, showed slight Phkb mRNA increase and weak nominal Ppp1cb engagement, but no row reached FDR<0.05. Interpretation is limited by weak Phkb knockdown and by mRNA being an indirect readout of a largely post-translational metabolic pathway.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Flrt3 was transcriptionally unengaged in the measured perturbation contexts, with no FDR-supported reduction of the Flrt3 target transcript in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut or 155 MB Glut, even though related adhesion/guidance perturbations in the same broad neuronal classes showed clear self-depletion, including Adgrl1, Adgrl2, Adgrl3, Tenm3, Robo1, Robo2, Ncam1, Unc5c, and Fgfr1. This contrast is driven mainly by target-transcript rows rather than downstream pathway output, and direct comparison was limited because Flrt1/Flrt2 and Unc5a/Unc5b were not available as perturbation targets.

Stard7 perturbation produced no coherent transcriptional change in a 34-gene sentinel panel spanning mitochondrial phosphatidylcholine, CoQ, cristae, and lipid-transfer pathways: expected transcripts such as Parl, Yme1l1, Pcyt1a, Pcyt2, Chpt1, Cept1, Coq2-Coq10b, Pdss1, Pdss2, Micos13, Tomm40, Afg3l2, Dnajc19, Slc25a46, Cert1, Pitpna, Pitpnm3, Osbpl2, Mboat7, Selenoi, and Agk remained FDR-negative, with 0 of 748 tests below 0.10 and a minimum FDR of 0.972. This suggests the canonical STARD7 lipid-transfer axis was not accompanied by a compensatory mRNA program here, with the caveat that the panel captures steady-state RNA and STARD7 may act post-transcriptionally.

Mphosph9 perturbation did not produce a reproducible ciliary transcriptional response, so the curated MPHOSPH9–CP110–CEP97 ciliogenesis mechanism was not read out as an mRNA program in this assay. Transcripts for Ccp110, Cep97, Kif24, Ttbk2, and other ciliary-neighborhood genes including Cep83, Cep164, Cep290, Ift88, Tbc1d32, and Kif3b were measured but remained unchanged. This suggests the MPHOSPH9/CP110-CEP97 negative regulation of cilium assembly was buffered or not detected at the RNA level, although weak target depletion and the RNA endpoint cannot exclude altered centriole localization, ciliogenesis, or ciliary morphology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Hnrnpu perturbation produced a recurrent mixed downstream module rather than a single canonical pathway, with Dmtf1, Atxn2l, Macf1, Gpr180, Hdac3, Depdc5, and amino acid/protein-biosynthesis genes including Asns, Cars, Lars, Mars1, and Guf1 induced, while Ahi1, Rsrp1, and Trim9 were repressed. This pattern recurred across responsive neuronal classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, and was also seen in 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. The recurrence is robust in this dataset, but the genes span multiple processes, and the HNRNPU-to-DEPDC5 link remains indirect.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Psmc1 showed transcriptomic convergence with other proteasome perturbations: in the two largest response classes, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, its nearest positive neighbors were Psmb4, Psmc5, and Pomp, and these positive correlations also persisted in other strong classes including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This supports a proteasome-related interpretation of the large Psmc1 programs despite weak Psmc1 mRNA knockdown, although only library-included proteasome perturbations were compared and the similarities are transcriptomic rather than biochemical.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Nipa1 knockdown in the 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA class, which showed the strongest measured reduction of Nipa1 transcript, did not produce a detectable BMP-like RNA response: there were no FDR-significant downstream genes and no induction of BMP-SMAD feedback markers including Id1, Id2, Id3, Id4, Smad7, Bambi, or Bmpr2. Thus, despite expectations from BMP receptor trafficking models, released BMP signaling was not evident at the single-cell RNA endpoint, though this inference is limited by a small RNA marker panel, low detection of several BMP targets, and absence of phospho-SMAD or receptor protein measurements.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Slc32a1 perturbation in GABAergic classes did not transcriptionally phenocopy other inhibitory-transmission genes: across 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 053 Sst Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA, genome-wide rank-based DE score correlations with Gad1, Gad2, Slc6a1, Gabrg2, Gphn, Nlgn2, and Slc12a5 were near zero, with the largest same-pathway correlation only r=0.105 for Gabrg2 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA. These results suggest a sparse, cell-intrinsic Slc32a1 signature rather than a shared GABAergic module, although some receptor-subunit comparisons had fewer than 60 perturbed cells and synaptic function was not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Fgf13 loss showed an uncoupled mRNA response from voltage-gated sodium-channel and axon-initial-segment excitability programs. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the strongest Fgf13-responsive context, Fgf13 was the top depleted transcript, Rell2 was the only non-target FDR hit, and Scn1a, Scn1b, Scn2a, Scn8a, Kcnq2, Kcnq3, Ank3, and Nfasc remained unregulated; well-engaged sodium-channel subunit perturbations also had near-zero transcriptomic correlation with Fgf13. The same lack of FDR-level Nav/AIS regulation was seen in 155 MB Glut and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, although these data do not address channel biophysics or protein trafficking.

Tspan7 knockdown left the canonical PICK1–AMPAR/β1-integrin branch uncoupled from transcript abundance: Gria1, Gria2, Gria3, Gria4, Pick1, and Itgb1 showed no FDR-supported mRNA changes, and no AMPAR/PICK1/β1-integrin pathway activation or repression was detected. This matters because the established TSPAN7 biology is centered on PICK1–GluA2/3 trafficking and synaptic function, so in this dataset the relevant readouts are likely receptor localization or electrophysiology rather than bulk mRNA, with the caveat that only transcript abundance was assayed.

Dll1 perturbation showed no detectable cell-autonomous canonical Notch transcriptional output in the assayed guide-carrying neurons. Transcriptome-wide, there were no genes passing multiple-testing correction, and canonical readouts including Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Hey2, Nrarp, Rbpj, as well as measured processing components such as Dtx1, Dtx3, Psen1, Aph1a, and Adam10, were not significantly regulated. In 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut cells, Ext2 was the strongest nominal signal but remained above FDR significance. This negative result is tempered by weak Dll1 target engagement and by the possibility that ligand knockdown is read out mainly in adjacent receiver cells rather than within the sender cell.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Dlx5 depletion in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA cells showed nominal target engagement but did not significantly repress the canonical GABAergic effector program: Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, and Arx were not FDR-significant, and Lhx6 was only nominally lower in Pvalb cells. Thus, the expected Dlx5/Dlx6 interneuron and PV-differentiation module was not coupled to acute single-gene Dlx5 perturbation here, with the caveat that the assay reflects weak target mRNA evidence and differs from embryonic or double-Dlx developmental perturbations.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Iqsec2 showed sparse and transcriptionally separable effects from excitatory postsynaptic receptor trafficking/PSD signaling perturbations in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In the same cell classes, Grin1, Nrxn1, Dlg4, Dlgap4, Grin2b, and Tsc1 produced readily detectable signatures, whereas Iqsec2 had 0 and 1 FDR<0.05 genes, respectively; the only genome-wide significant Iqsec2 hit was Arfgap1 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut included only a nominal Cux1 row. However, comparator perturbations often had stronger on-target RNA depletion than Iqsec2, so apparent pathway uncoupling is confounded by weaker Iqsec2 engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Chd7 showed a divergent and notably weak Perturb-seq profile, not phenocopying Chd8 or other ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling factors such as Chd4, Chd2, Kmt2d, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Kmt2a, and Arid1a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA neurons. Across the panel, Chd7 produced only one FDR-significant gene, with Nfyb up in 191 MB P MY GABA, while Chd8, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, and Kmt2d generated far larger DE burdens; Chd7 score vectors were near-zero correlated with Chd8 in the Chd8-responsive classes. This contrast may reflect weaker Chd7 target engagement rather than a true downstream wiring difference.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Adgrg6 showed a broadly null response across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, and this was not a generic failure of membrane-signaling perturbations. In the same dataset, related adhesion GPCRs and cAMP/PKA neighbor nodes—Adgrl1, Adgrl2, Adgrl3, Prkaca, Prkar1a, Adcy3, Prnp, and Lrp1—showed significant self-transcript depletion, whereas Adgrg6, Adgrg1, and Adgrg2 did not. This comparison mainly reflects direct target-transcript effects rather than matched downstream signatures, and target expression and guide efficacy differed by gene.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pfkm in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons showed a buffered Perturb-seq profile relative to the same glycolytic pathway neighbor Pgk1: although Pfkm was strongly depleted, it produced no non-target FDR genes, whereas Pgk1 in the same cell class produced 21 non-target FDR genes, led by Pnisr, Rsrp1, and Srrm2. This suggests that same-pathway membership did not translate to interchangeable transcriptomic outputs in these thalamic neurons, though Pgk1 had stronger target repression, more perturbed cells, and direct PFK1 paralog comparators were not available.

Rlf perturbation in this brain dataset did not produce a detectable Notch/Jagged transcriptional response: across assayed brain cell types, including the other 21 Rlf-assayed cell types, canonical Notch signaling transcripts such as Jag1, Jag2, Notch1, Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Rbpj, and Maml1 were not FDR-shifted in any Rlf contrast. This argues that the reported Jag1/Notch consequence of Rlf loss in embryonic heart development does not generalize to these brain signatures, while noting that the assay measured only mRNA and could miss subtle, noncanonical, or transient Notch effects.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smarcd1 showed a notably weak transcriptional effect in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with only 1 gene at FDR<0.05, whereas related mSWI/SNF/BAF perturbations in the same class were much stronger, including Smarcb1 with 286 genes, Smarcc2 with 185, and Arid2, Arid1a, and Smarce1 with 56, 22, and 11. The sparse Smarcd1 response included Ankrd40 up and a Ptpn3 down trend, suggesting that BAF subunits were not interchangeable here, although unequal guide efficacy or knockdown efficiency could partly explain the difference.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Grin1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a broad transcriptomic state that was not accompanied by compensatory induction of GluN2/GluN3 subunit or Dlg4 mRNAs, including Grin2a, Grin2b, Grin2c, Grin2d, Grin3a, Grin3b, and Dlg4, within the NMDA receptor/glutamatergic synapse pathway. In the same cells, perturbations of Grin2a, Grin2b, Grin2d, Grin3a, Dlg4, Syngap1, and Shank3 were nearly orthogonal and did not phenocopy Grin1, although some comparators showed weak self-transcript engagement. This contrast is transcriptomic only; receptor assembly, synaptic localization, and current amplitudes were not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Snrpb showed a notably weak perturbation signature relative to other splicing-factor targets in the same dataset: although Srsf1, U2af2, Prpf6, Snrnp70, Ddx23, and Hnrnpc produced broad total-expression programs with 218–9,588 FDR-significant rows, Snrpb generated only 1 overall and was effectively silent in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where 179 and 183 perturbed cells still yielded zero FDR genes. This suggests the null signal is specific to Snrpb or the SmB/SmN branch captured here, not a generic limitation of perturbing mRNA splicing and snRNP assembly genes, though canonical Sm-core partners were largely unassayed and Snrpb mRNA engagement was weak.

Notch1 perturbation was uncoupled from the canonical NOTCH transcriptional arm: across the 22 assayed Notch1 cell types, Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Hey2, Heyl, Nrarp, Dtx1, Dtx2, and Dtx3 were unchanged, so the expected RBPJ/MAML-dependent HES/HEY/NRARP/DTX response was not detected. The only FDR-significant hit was an increase in Camk2g in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and this Camk2g response was absent under related Notch-pathway perturbations. These markers are canonical but do not exhaust the full Notch regulon in every neuronal context.

Bmpr1a perturbation showed no detectable canonical BMP-SMAD transcriptional output in the assayed neurons: representative response and feedback genes Id1, Id2, Id3, Id4, Junb, Klf10, and Smad7 were not FDR-shifted, with only a nominal signal for Id2 in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut (p = 0.0483, FDR = 1.0). This argues against a hidden tonic BMPR1A-SMAD state in these neurons, although the readouts were RNA rather than phospho-SMAD measurements and baseline expression may be sparse in some neuronal groups.

Hivep1 did not phenocopy its HIVEP paralogs or nearby NF-κB-family perturbations in this mouse brain dataset: across shared cell types, whole-transcriptome score-vector correlations between Hivep1 and Hivep2, Hivep3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, or Relb were near zero. This indicates no detectable convergence with the HIVEP zinc-finger paralog module or κB/NF-κB-responsive transcription, so Hivep1 should not be treated here as an interchangeable proxy for Hivep2/Hivep3 or for Nfkb1/Nfkb2/Relb. A caveat is that the comparator signatures were themselves mostly weak, making the result most informative as absence of detectable convergence.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Nrxn1 appeared buffered in cortical IT glutamatergic neurons, particularly 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, where comparable numbers of perturbed cells nonetheless yielded no non-self FDR genes for Nrxn1, while Grin2a and Grin2b produced broad cortical NMDA receptor perturbation modules. In 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Grin2a produced 20 and Grin2b 46 non-self FDR genes, including markers such as Nptx2, Bdnf, Ptgs2, Kcnv1, Vgf, and Rph3a, indicating that synaptic perturbations can couple strongly to soma RNA in these classes even when Nrxn1 does not; this contrast is strongest in these two IT subclasses and should not be generalized to all Nrxn1-expressing neurons.

Prlr perturbation did not produce the expected prolactin receptor–JAK2–STAT5 transcriptional program: across 21 Prlr signatures, Cish, Socs1, Socs2, Socs3, Jak2, Sh2b1, Stat5a, and Stat5b were not significantly activated or suppressed, and Prlr did not converge with Ghr, Epor, Il6st, Osmr, Stat1, Stat3, Stat5b, Mapk1, Pik3ca, or Pik3cb neighbors. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA cells, the only significant Prlr-associated transcript was Spcs1, remaining a single-gene effect without canonical PRLR-JAK/STAT output. Because the assay measured steady-state RNA rather than acute phospho-STAT5, AKT, MAPK, or Src activity, this is best read as pathway uncoupling under the assayed conditions, not proof that PRLR cannot signal.

Frmpd4 perturbation showed no FDR-significant transcriptomic response across all 22 assayed cell classes and did not transcriptionally remodel known partner machinery, including PSD-95-family genes Dlg1, Dlg2, Dlg3, and Dlg4, the mGluR/Homer module Grm1, Grm5, Homer1, Homer2, and Homer3, or related scaffold genes Arhgef7, Tnik, Dlgap4, Shank2, and Shank3. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, a postsynaptic comparator panel also lacked significant Frmpd4-related engagement. These null mRNA findings are consistent with FRMPD4 acting mainly as a protein-domain scaffold, while mRNA abundance remains an indirect proxy for synaptic localization and function.

Tspoap1 was transcriptionally uncoupled from the available presynaptic active-zone and calcium-channel perturbations across all 23 assayed neuronal cell classes, including 308 CB GABA: same-cell correlations with Cacna1a, Cacna1d, Kcnma1, Unc13a, Unc13c, Stxbp1, Syn1, Syn2, and Cplx2 were near zero, even though several of those perturbations showed detectable signatures in the same dataset. This negative comparison is informative but incomplete, because direct partners such as Tspo, Rims1, Rims2, Acbd3, and Rimbp2 were not targeted, and weak Tspoap1 target engagement may have reduced sensitivity to detect convergence.

Psap knockdown did not transcriptionally engage the expected PSAP-related axes in this dataset: transcripts for Gpr37 and Gpr37l1, lysosomal and sphingolipid catabolism genes including Gba, Galc, Arsa, Asah1, Smpd1, Smpd3, Lamp1, Lamp2, and Ctsb, and progranulin-trafficking genes Grn, Igf2r, M6pr, Lrp1, and Sort1 were all unchanged by FDR. The recurrent nominal signals were exploratory only, and because this 16-gene panel was literature-prioritized, protein trafficking or lysosomal lipid changes could still occur without mRNA changes.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Lrpap1 showed a largely self-only, uncoupled transcriptomic response in the strongest subclasses—155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—where full ranked RNA signatures had near-zero correlations with perturbations of LDLR-family receptors and related neighbors including Lrp1, Lrp2, Lrp4, Lrp5, Lrp6, Lrp8, Vldlr, Sorl1, Sort1, Reln, Dab1, App, and Agrn. Across the full library, no strong positive or inverse transcriptomic neighbor was detected, suggesting that physical interaction in LDLR-family chaperone and receptor-trafficking pathways did not translate into a shared neuronal mRNA program here, although shared protein-trafficking phenotypes without correlated RNA changes could have been missed.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Acvrl1 perturbation showed no detectable canonical BMP/SMAD transcriptional footprint across the sampled neuronal cell types, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic classes such as L5-6 IT Glut, L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Pvalb Gaba, Sst Gaba, and CB GABA. The expected response genes Id1, Id2, Id3, Smad6, Smad7, Serpine1, Hey1, and Hey2 were not significantly changed in any contrast, and Acvrl1 itself was measured but did not show significant depletion or induction. This absence is based on transcript readouts only and could reflect weak target engagement rather than a definitive lack of SMAD signaling.

Gns showed little to no transcriptomic convergence with available lysosomal and glycosaminoglycan-related perturbations in this assay. In 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, Gns was downregulated, but downstream signatures were buffered and correlations with Ctsb, Psap, Ppt1, Atp6v0a1, Arsb, Atp6v1a, Lamp2, Gnptg, Ext2, and Hs6st2 were near zero, even though several comparators had stronger on-target knockdown. Many comparator perturbations were themselves sparse at FDR, and the closest Sanfilippo genes were not screened, so these indirect lysosomal neighbors should not be treated as interchangeable with Gns.

Kcnj6 showed weak transcript engagement across the Perturb-seq panel and never reached multiple-testing-corrected significance, even though canonical GABAB/G-protein/GIRK pathway neighbors such as Gabbr1, Gabbr2, Gnao1, Gnb1, and Gnb5 had measurable, sometimes cell-type-specific on-target depletion. This contrast was evident in classes including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, where comparator perturbations were significant while Kcnj6 was not. The result is best read as assay-level pathway uncoupling rather than contradiction of GIRK biology, since transcriptomic differential expression is an indirect readout for a rapidly gated ion channel and direct Kir3 paralogs Kcnj3, Kcnj5, and Kcnj9 were not perturbed.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Uqcrc1 perturbation showed near-zero score-vector correlations with other complex III or maintenance genes, including Uqcrc2, Uqcrfs1, Uqcrq, Uqcrb, Uqcrh, Cyc1, Uqcc2, and Ttc19, across engaged classes such as 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. This indicates that physical complex III membership did not translate into acute transcriptomic interchangeability here, although most comparator signatures were shallow and Uqcrq, Uqcrb, and Uqcrh lacked FDR-significant own-target depletion.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Stx1b showed a nonconvergent transcriptomic profile relative to nearby presynaptic release genes in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. In these classes, Stx1b knockdown was on target, but Pearson correlations between Stx1b and Snap25, Stxbp1, Vamp1, Cplx1, or Syt2 differential-expression score vectors were near zero, and Stx1b had no strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor. This suggests that within SNARE-associated synaptic vesicle exocytosis, Stx1b did not phenocopy these pathway neighbors, although downstream signal was weak and key comparators such as Stx1a, Vamp2, and Syt1 were not tested.

Notch3 targeting did not produce a detectable canonical NOTCH3/RBPJ/MAML transcriptional response in any sampled neuronal class: Hes/Hey/Nrarp readouts, including Hes1, Hes5, Hes7, Hesx1, Hey1, Hey2, Heyl, and Nrarp, remained unchanged, and transcripts for Rbpj and Maml1/2/3 also showed no detectable activation or repression. This argues that these guide cells did not enter a canonical Notch3 transcriptional state, although the inference is limited because most MAML paralogs were not directly perturbed and the dataset measures downstream transcripts rather than NICD3 protein or reporter activity.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Neo1 in this brain Perturb-seq dataset was transcriptionally uncoupled from BMP/SMAD-HJV signaling: in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut, Neo1 signatures were weakly correlated with Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, and Hjv perturbations, and the clearest Bmpr2 knockdowns showed strong target-transcript reduction with almost no downstream FDR-significant RNA changes. Thus, a Neo1 perturbation here is not a reliable proxy for BMP-SMAD or HJV-hepcidin pathway activity, with the caveat that the assay measures mRNA rather than SMAD phosphorylation, RhoA activation, HJV secretion, hepcidin, or iron handling.

Lrrn3 showed weak on-target depletion, and its paralog Lrrn2 was similarly weak, whereas several queried comparators in the same analysis framework, including Lingo1, Nrxn1, Nrxn2, Nlgn2, Nlgn3, and the STRING neighbor Synj1, showed strong on-target effects. This contrast argues against a global inability to perturb neuronal comparator genes and instead suggests an Lrrn-specific limitation in guide performance, target expression, or capture. However, the comparator set is not a single protein complex, and this finding summarizes target engagement rather than downstream phenocopy.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Isca2 knockdown in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class produced the only FDR-significant on-target reduction of Isca2, but the expected mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis and OXPHOS client mRNA panel remained neutral. In this engaged state, transcripts including Isca1, Iba57, Nfs1, Iscu, Glrx5, Fdx1/2, Fxn, Nfu1, Bola3, Aco2, Lias, Ndufs1, Ndufs2, Ndufv1, Sdhb, Slc25a3, Uqcrfs1, Hspa9, and Hspd1 showed no coherent response, suggesting a likely post-transcriptional biochemical lesion rather than transcriptional compensation, with the caveat that the readout is transcript-based rather than direct Fe-S insertion, enzyme activity, lipoate synthesis, or respiration.

Crppa perturbation did not phenocopy other dystroglycan-network genes in this Perturb-seq dataset. Although Agrn and Large1 showed clearer on-target signatures, Crppa score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Agrn, Dag1, Dpm1, Fktn, Large1, Lrp4, and Rxylt1, with the strongest related-pair correlation only about |r|=0.192. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Crppa contrasts were flat or lacked FDR-significant genes while related perturbations showed self-transcript depletion; even in 308 CB GABA, nominal Crppa decreases did not yield a robust transcriptomic phenotype. Because these correlations were computed from weak Crppa signatures, the result is best interpreted as a non-phenocopy rather than mechanistic antagonism.

Musk perturbation left the canonical AGRN–LRP4–MUSK/AChR clustering transcript set unchanged in the assayed brain-cell mRNA data, including Agrn, Lrp4, Dok7, Rapsn, Chrna1, Chrnb1, Chrnd, Chrne, Chrng, Ache, Dvl1-3, Pak1, Abl1, Src, Fnta, and Rac1. Similar to Agrn and Lrp4 perturbations, canonical receptor-complex, AChR-clustering, and cholinergic effector transcripts were not detectably remodeled, suggesting this NMJ postsynaptic program was buffered or uncoupled at the transcript level in these brain cell classes. This caveat is important because MuSK signaling is largely mediated by phosphorylation and receptor clustering, which Perturb-seq would not capture.

Ccr5 showed a sparse perturbational signature concentrated at the chemokine-receptor layer rather than a general failure to perturb GPCR signaling genes. Across shared cell types, Ccr2, Cx3cr1, Cxcr2, and Cxcr4 behaved similarly, with near-zero correlations to Ccr5 and almost no adjusted hits, including neuronal contrasts such as 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Ccr5 remained FDR-negative and lacked target-transcript depletion. In the same screen, expressed signaling genes including Gnao1, Gnb1, Gnb5, Mapk1, and Stat1 showed adjusted on-target depletion, suggesting context- or expression-limited CCR-family responses; comparator searches did not include every CCR5 ligand or all G-protein subunits.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cstf2 perturbation in the two most engaged strata, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, did not transcriptionally induce the paralog Cstf2t or the core CstF partner transcripts Cstf1 and Cstf3, consistent with a buffered or minimal total-gene response in mRNA 3'-end processing and polyadenylation. In 155 MB Glut, the clearest Cstf2 target-transcript decrease was observed but remained FDR-insignificant, and 191 MB P MY GABA showed a nominal, also FDR-insignificant, decrease. This argues against an acute mRNA-level handoff to Cstf2t/CstF subunits, while leaving open effects on CSTF2T protein abundance, localization, or poly(A)-site usage.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Chrnb4 showed no statistically supported on-target mRNA change in any assayed cell type, even though its transcript was measured, whereas comparator cholinergic perturbations Chrnb2 and Ache were strongly depleted in midbrain/thalamic populations including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. This pattern suggests the negative result is specific to the Chrnb4/Chrna3/Chrna5 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor cluster rather than a universal failure of cholinergic-axis perturbation, with the caveat that Chrnb2-containing receptors are not interchangeable with α3β4α5 receptors and downstream effects of Chrnb2 or Ache were not analyzed here.

Cx3cr1 perturbation showed no transcriptional feedback onto its canonical ligand Cx3cl1: across all Cx3cr1 contrasts, Cx3cl1 was measured but never changed with FDR-adjusted support in the assayed neuronal classes. This leaves the CX3CL1–CX3CR1 fractalkine pathway transcriptionally flat in this dataset, suggesting the relevant circuit was absent or not perturbed here. The result is limited to transcript-level feedback, as receptor activity, ligand shedding, and microglial responses were not assayed.

Dnajc6 knockdown did not induce Gak mRNA, contrary to the chronic compensatory increase in GAK reported in germline auxilin-null mouse brain. Across 22 Dnajc6-perturbed cell classes, Gak showed no significant mRNA increase, and there was no coherent core-module transcript response in the HSPA8/auxilin clathrin-coated-vesicle uncoating pathway, including genes such as Hspa8, Cltc, Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Synj1, and Dnm1. This suggests that acute Dnajc6 perturbation lacks the chronic transcriptional compensation seen in germline loss, although only Gak transcript was measured, not GAK protein, activity, later time points, or non-neuronal compartments.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: B9d1 showed a transcriptomic phenotype that was uncoupled from measured B9d1 cis-transcript reduction. Across 21 tested classes, the B9d1 row never reached FDR significance: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the smallest nominal B9d1 decrease but no FDR-significant downstream genes, whereas 308 CB GABA had the strongest downstream response, including a genome-wide significant differential-expression tail, despite a non-significant B9d1 RNA change. This pattern suggests a B9d1-specific cerebellar GABA response within the ciliary transition-zone/Joubert-Meckel network, but interpretation is limited because CRISPR coding perturbation may disrupt protein without lowering RNA and B9d1 may be sparsely detected.

Nefh perturbation showed limited self-transcript engagement breadth compared with related neurofilament subunits, yet like Nefl and Nefm it produced essentially no corrected non-self transcriptional response. Across strata, Nefh reached self-transcript significance in 2/22 strata versus 11/22 for Nefl and 3/23 for Nefm, while all three had zero non-self genes at FDR < 0.05. In 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Nefh target transcripts were reduced without broader remodeling, though this comparison may reflect guide design, on-target cutting, and baseline transcript detectability.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cdkal1 perturbation most reproducibly increased Eef1a2, with the only FDR-significant effect seen in 155 MB Glut; across 22 contrasts, Eef1a2 shifted upward in 19, including 7 nominal positives. This recurrent signal is directionally consistent with tRNA(Lys) A37 methylthiolation and translation elongation pathway context, but in 155 MB Glut it remained largely uncorrelated with Elp1 and Elp2 perturbations and occurred without nominal Cdkal1 transcript depletion. The interpretation is therefore hypothesis-generating and based on RNA abundance rather than direct measurements of elongation activity or codon-specific translation.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Cdkal1 did not phenocopy Elp1 or Elp2 perturbations in neuronal Perturb-seq: in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Cdkal1 signatures were weak and nearly uncorrelated with the robust Elp1/Elp2 outputs. In 155 MB Glut, the strongest Cdkal1 hit included Eef1a2 upregulation despite little nominal Cdkal1 transcript depletion, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Cdkal1 had zero FDR-significant genes. These data separate Cdkal1 tRNA(Lys) A37 methylthiolation from Elongator-dependent wobble U34 modification, with the caveat that the genes act at different tRNA positions rather than as paralogous subunits.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Aff2 produced a signature that was essentially orthogonal to Aff3 and Fmr1, despite their family relationships. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, the cell type with the only significant Aff2 response, Aff2 downregulated Susd4, whereas matched Aff3 and Fmr1 perturbations showed near-zero genome-wide correlation with Aff2 and did not appreciably change Susd4. Across shared cell types, Aff3 and Fmr1 remained within |r|<0.07 of Aff2, suggesting paralog- and cell-type-specific outputs, with the caveat that these are score correlations rather than matched protein-depletion comparisons.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Aff2 showed weak target engagement and mostly sparse or subthreshold downstream expression changes across 22 assayed cell types. The Aff2 transcript itself never passed FDR correction, and only 1 of 371,818 Aff2 differential-expression tests reached FDR<0.05, despite annotated AFF-family RNA processing and transcription-elongation context. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Aff2 had the strongest nominal mRNA decrease but no corrected downstream genes, while 155 MB Glut showed a nominal Aff2 decrease with only subthreshold Tef/Pcsk2 signals. This weak readout could reflect biological buffering, low knockdown efficiency, low Aff2 expression, or gene-level scRNA-seq missing isoform or splicing consequences.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Cckar showed no adjusted on-target knockdown anywhere in this Perturb-seq dataset, similar to Cckbr, even though the ligand Cck was directly and significantly depleted in three neuronal populations: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. In the cholecystokinin receptor signaling axis, this asymmetry suggests ligand accessibility but receptor-limited perturbability in these broad matched cell classes. This comparison is limited to transcript knockdown and does not address secreted CCK peptide release or receptor activity.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gpr179 was not interchangeable with its paralog Gpr158 in this brain Perturb-seq panel: across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, the Gpr179 perturbation showed no measurable on-target transcript shift and its score profile was uncorrelated with Gpr158 or retinal-pathway/nearby GPCR signatures. By contrast, Gpr158 showed clear self-depletion in several of these classes, although downstream FDR hits beyond the target row were sparse, so the paralog contrast rests mainly on target-transcript depletion.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Clcn5 showed much weaker neuronal transcriptional effects than its intracellular CLC paralog Clcn4 across 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut cells. In these classes, Clcn4 was significantly self-depleted, consistent with endosomal chloride/proton exchange by intracellular CLCs, whereas Clcn5 showed no corrected self or downstream response; in Pvalb the smallest Clcn5 signal involved Man1a2 but remained non-significant, in thalamic cells Clcn5 self-depletion was only nominal, and in midbrain glutamatergic cells there was no Clcn5 self-effect. This contrast is tempered by higher matched perturbed-cell counts for Clcn4, and most corrected Clcn4 hits were the target transcript itself.

Adcy3 was transcriptionally distinct from the assayed adenylyl cyclase paralogs Adcy1 and Adcy5, rather than behaving as a generic adenylyl cyclase knockdown. Across the dataset, Adcy1 and Adcy5 were not close transcriptomic neighbors of Adcy3, and their restricted signatures were nearly orthogonal to Adcy3, consistent with paralog and context specificity, including within ADCY3-mediated GPCR/cAMP signaling in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA cells. A caveat is that Adcy1 and Adcy5 showed weaker self-transcript depletion, so some divergence may reflect perturbation strength rather than pure paralog biology.

Adcy3 showed a weak but biologically coherent positive-neighbor signal toward primary cilium and receptor-trafficking perturbations: Ap2s1 was its top positive neighbor, and Pkd1, Lztfl1, Ift88, and Ap2m1 also ranked among the strongest positive transcriptomic neighbors. These genes map to cilium assembly and receptor/internalization pathways, consistent with the same subcellular context as ADCY3 and MC4R, but the effect was modest, with the largest restricted cosine only 0.126, so this should be treated as a hypothesis for follow-up rather than a definitive pathway readout.

Atp1a2, although curated as a plasma-membrane P-type ATPase within the ATP1A:ATP1B:FXYD Na+/K+ exchange complex, did not produce a detectable neuronal transcriptional ion-homeostasis program in this assay. Across the assayed neuronal classes, including 22 Glut/GABA/Pineal/GABA-labeled classes, Atp1a2 mRNA was not significantly depleted and no genes reached 5% FDR differential expression, with no downstream P-type ATPase module detected. In pathway context, Atp1a2 was absent while Atp1a1 and Atp1a3 were engaged. This null transcriptional readout may reflect weak target engagement and does not exclude acute electrophysiologic or metabolic phenotypes.

Atp1a2 was not interchangeable with the Na+/K+-ATPase alpha paralogs Atp1a1 and Atp1a3 in this screen: across assayed neuronal classes, Atp1a2 showed no detectable mRNA depletion, no 5% FDR-significant differential-expression genes, and genome-wide score vectors that remained near zero in correlation with either paralog perturbation. By contrast, Atp1a1, and especially Atp1a3, showed detectable on-target depletion and significant transcriptomic responses in the same analysis framework. This comparison is transcriptomic and depends on guide sets achieving knockdown, a caveat underscored by the lack of measurable Atp1a2 depletion itself.

Add1 did not show transcriptional convergence with its adducin-family partners Add2 and Add3: in 21 shared cell types, same-cell-type Add1-versus-Add2 and Add1-versus-Add3 score correlations were centered near zero, even though these genes are known members of the adducin alpha/beta and alpha/gamma spectrin-actin complex. This suggests that physical complex membership did not translate into interchangeable whole-cell mRNA phenotypes here. A key caveat is that all three perturbations produced weak FDR-level responses, so the comparison rests on restricted signatures rather than strong differential-expression programs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Lztr1 perturbation was not phenocopied by Cul3 in the two main Lztr1-engaged cell classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where the Lztr1-Cul3 signatures showed low concordance despite the known LZTR1-CUL3 ubiquitin-adaptor axis. In 151, Lztr1 had strong on-target depletion with a nominal Vgf/Ptpn5 module and the clearest same-cell RAS/MAPK contrast against Nf1, Braf, Map2k1, and Shoc2; in 005, Lztr1 depletion was strong with only a near-threshold Cacna1b decrease. This contrast is tempered by weak Cul3 target engagement, lower matched-cell counts, and the possibility that broader CUL3 biology obscures LZTR1-adaptor-specific effects.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ap3b2 depletion showed no transcriptional compensation within the AP-3/BLOC-1 pathway across four engaged cell types—L4-5 IT CTX glutamatergic, CNU-HYa HY GABA, TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic, and MB glutamatergic cells. In these contexts, Ap3b2 was reduced at FDR, but other adaptor subunits and linked genes, including Ap3b1, Ap3d1, Ap3m1, Ap3m2, Ap3s1, Ap3s2, Bloc1s1, Atp8a1, Stx12, and Syt1, remained FDR-unchanged. Even where Ap3b2 knockdown was strongest, the response largely stopped at the target transcript, and this candidate-gene analysis did not measure AP-3 complex abundance or cargo localization.

Ahrr perturbation showed no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any tested cell class, and the canonical AHR xenobiotic module was not derepressed: Cyp1a1, Cyp1b1, Nqo1, Tiparp, and Aldh3a1 all had FDR = 1.0 in Ahrr tests. This null pattern converged with Ahr and Arnt perturbations, which likewise lacked transcriptome-wide significant differential expression and any significant target-transcript change, suggesting weak or absent aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling in this basal neuronal screen. A caveat is that Ahr was observed in 21 rather than 22 cell classes, and lack of DE cannot distinguish pathway inactivity from ineffective editing.

Fezf1 perturbation did not engage the expected FEZF1/FEZF2-Hes5-Neurog2 forebrain neurogenesis axis in this dataset: across profiled classes, Hes5, Neurog2, Ascl1, and Fezf2 were not detectably altered after multiple testing, and the Fezf1 transcript itself showed no measurable depletion or induction. This pattern is most consistent with cell-state mismatch and weak Fezf1 target engagement rather than reversal of the embryonic progenitor mechanism, with the additional caveat that Fezf2 was available only as a readout and not as a matched perturbation comparator.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Gpr162 depletion in unstimulated neurons did not activate or repress a STING-TBK1-CXCL10 transcriptional proxy: Sting1, Tbk1, and Cxcl10 were unchanged, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA cells with strong Gpr162 self-depletion, while 052 Pvalb Gaba showed only near-threshold on-target depletion. Across these classes, Gpr162 was often the only significant transcript and no strong cross-perturbation neighbor emerged. This refines, rather than contradicts, cancer-cell reports, since the screen lacked irradiation or cGAS-STING stimulation and did not assay IRF3 phosphorylation or secreted interferon.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Foxj3 perturbation in mouse brain did not reproduce the myogenic FOXJ3→Mef2c relationship: Mef2c mRNA was unchanged, with no nominally significant response across 21 brain cell types spanning cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic neurons, multiple GABAergic classes, hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, pineal, and cerebellar populations. This refines rather than contradicts prior muscle-based work, because the earlier FOXJ3–Mef2c link came from skeletal muscle/myoblast enhancer assays, and Foxj3 target engagement in this brain dataset was weak.

Foxj3 was not phenocopied by related forkhead-family or STRING-nominated neighboring perturbations in this dataset. Across same-cell transcriptome signatures, Foxj3 correlations were near null overall, with the strongest positive and negative values only about r=0.12 and r=-0.12, and assayed neighbors including Foxk2, Foxj1, Dicer1, Nf1, Pax6, Zbtb18, and Phf8 also remained near zero. In 308 CB GABA cells, Foxj3 showed a nominal self-decrease without FDR-level downstream genes. This conclusion is limited to assayed perturbations in shared cell types, with low Foxj3 signal and no Foxj2 comparator.

Kcnb2 perturbation did not robustly induce Kcnb1 mRNA, and the reciprocal Kcnb1 perturbation likewise did not robustly induce Kcnb2 mRNA, with no FDR-significant cross-induction detected across 22 matched cell types. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, this contrasted with a strong Kcnb1-associated Bdnf/Vgf/Zbtb16/Scg2/Nptx2 program while Kcnb2 remained transcriptionally null, underscoring Kv2 paralog divergence rather than a simple reciprocal mRNA-compensation loop. This inference is limited to mRNA; compensation through protein abundance, tetramer stoichiometry, localization, or phosphorylation remains possible.

Ddhd2 knockdown did not produce a coherent transcriptional compensation program for lipid storage or lipolysis. Across the measured 34-gene lipid/lipase panel, no genes reached FDR<0.1, including Dgat1, Dgat2, Plin2, Pnpla2, Ldlr, Insig1, and Ddhd1, and this pattern was seen in 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut neurons. Thus, despite DDHD2’s placement in TAG/DAG and phosphatidic-acid hydrolysis pathways, the Perturb-seq readout appeared transcriptionally uncoupled from the expected lipid-storage phenotype; this interpretation is limited because the panel was hypothesis driven and transcript levels may not track acylglycerol accumulation.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Lingo1 showed a nonconvergent transcriptional profile relative to its paralog Lingo2 and the assayed Nogo-receptor partners Rtn4r and Ngfr in the Lingo1-engaged cell types 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In these classes, Lingo1 knockdown was validated, yet score correlations to Lingo2, Rtn4r, and Ngfr were near zero, with no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbors; in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Becn1 was the sole downstream FDR hit. This suggests buffered, nonconvergent RNA-level behavior in the Nogo receptor/myelin-inhibitory RhoA signaling context, although weak comparator target engagement means true pathway phenocopy could have been missed.

Ep300 perturbation did not yield a coherent single-cell RNA expression module: no cell type showed an FDR-significant downstream response, and nominal Ep300 hits were not recurrent across cell types, with no gene recurring at p < 0.001 in more than one Ep300 cell type. Thus, the broad Reactome EP300/CREBBP transcription-factor pathway annotations, including RUNX, TP53, NOTCH, and FOXO contexts, were not recovered as corrected scRNA-seq targets here. This mismatch is consistent with weak target engagement and context restriction rather than a biochemical disproof of those curated pathways.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Erbb3 showed no detectable target-transcript depletion in 052 Pvalb Gaba or 046 CTX-CGE GABA interneurons, whereas the matched Erbb4 perturbation significantly depleted Erbb4 mRNA in both classes. This pattern indicates an Erbb4-biased, rather than Erbb3-like, signal within NRG/ErbB receptor signaling in these inhibitory neurons, and Erbb3 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with assayed ErbB, NRG, PI3K, MAPK, and related RTK perturbations. The caveat is that the significant Erbb4 effects were on-target RNA depletion, without a broad FDR-significant downstream Erbb4 program in these contrasts.

Fras1 showed no convergent neuronal transcriptomic signature with Grip1 or the basement-membrane/integrin-adjacent comparators Itga8, Itgb1, and Agrn: across shared cell types, these perturbation signatures were nearly orthogonal or uncorrelated. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the largest Fras1 cell-count bin showed only a nominal Lef1 decrease and no detectable Fras1 depletion, whereas Agrn showed clear on-target depletion in the same broad class. Because Fras1 engagement was weak and Frem1/Frem2 were not available as direct comparators, this should not be read as a biochemical contradiction of the Fraser complex.

Lrba perturbation in the neuronal screen did not recapitulate the canonical LRBA CTLA4-recycling or ATG9A-trafficking biology as an mRNA program: across brain-cell contrasts, Ctla4, Atg9a, Tom1, Tollip, Rab11a, and Rab11b showed no significant transcript changes versus matched non-target cells. This suggests transcriptional uncoupling of the LRBA-CTLA4 endosomal recycling and ATG9A-associated trafficking pathways in this assay, with the important caveat that the screen measures steady-state brain-cell transcripts, whereas key LRBA mechanisms are protein-trafficking and immune-cell CTLA4 turnover.

Ndufaf4 showed no coordinated FDR-significant downstream program: there were no transcriptome-wide significant differential-expression hits, and oxidative phosphorylation, complex I, mitochondrial import, or mitochondrial stress-response genes such as Sdha, Ndufb1, Tomm22, Ndufv3, and Ndufaf8 did not form a significant module. The strongest signals were isolated nominal genes, including Pex13, Gls, and Pmm1; in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Pex13 remained non-significant at FDR 0.149 and the Ndufaf4 target row was not significantly reduced, while 022 L5 ET CTX Glut contributed nominal rows like Pmm1 without passing FDR. Because the mitochondrial scan was exploratory and target knockdown was not evident, the pathway-level silence should be interpreted cautiously.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Paqr7 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed only on-target self-depletion at FDR significance, and the matched PAQR-family comparator Paqr8 in the same class likewise showed only self-depletion. Despite this family relationship within PAQR membrane progesterone receptor signaling, their ranked transcriptomic responses were essentially uncorrelated in these unstimulated thalamic cells, with Pearson r=0.009 and no overlap among the top 50 positive or negative genes, indicating that Paqr7 and Paqr8 were not transcriptomically interchangeable under these conditions.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pign did not phenocopy the only assayed GPI-adjacent comparator, Dpm1: across 21 matched cell types, their transcriptomic Wilcoxon score-vector correlations were centered near zero, ranging from -0.132 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut to 0.0757 in 308 CB GABA. This suggests that pathway membership alone did not yield a shared acute transcriptional state in this dataset, although the comparison is limited to transcriptomic score correlations, Dpm1 showed weak own-transcript engagement, and most direct PIG/PGAP genes were not represented in the library.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gcgr showed weaker on-target detectability than several other perturbations in the same Wilcoxon analysis: although the Gcgr transcript was measured, Gcgr-perturbed cells versus matched non-target controls never showed self-transcript depletion across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In contrast, Cck, Adcy3, and Adra1a did show detectable on-target depletion in some classes, suggesting a target-context limitation for Gcgr, such as very low receptor expression in the assayed neurons, rather than a dataset-wide failure; these comparators are positive controls, not GCGR paralogs.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Antxr1 was not interchangeable with its paralog Antxr2 in this screen. Across matched cell types, Antxr1–Antxr2 genome-wide score-vector correlations were near zero (r = -0.0589 to 0.0777), indicating divergent transcriptional signatures despite their shared ANTXR receptor and collagen-homeostasis family context. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, the only sparse FDR-level event was Antxr2-associated Mga, with no Antxr1 counterpart. Both receptor signatures were weak overall, so these RNA-level data do not exclude shared protein-level collagen handling outside the measured endpoint.

Cr2 perturbation did not reveal a coherent neuronal CR2/CD21 B-cell coreceptor or complement-regulation module. In the neuronal classes assayed, the related perturbations C3, Cd27, Cd4, Cd79a, Cd79b, and Ptprc were largely FDR-silent, while Cd81 was the only recurrently engaged comparator and appeared broadly active rather than Cr2-matched. This negative result is limited by panel coverage and cell context: only a subset of Cr2-associated immune genes was tested, and the absence of lymphocytes or follicular dendritic cells likely explains why several canonical lymphocyte markers showed no significant response.

Hoxc13 perturbation in adult brain did not detect the canonical HOXC13 hair-follicle/keratin transcriptional program: although Foxq1 and many Krt/Krtap-family genes, including Krt31, Krt33a, and Krt86, were present in the differential-expression table, none showed multiple-testing-corrected changes in any cell type. This suggests the epithelial HOXC13 pathway is uncoupled from the brain signatures here, while also leaving open the key caveat that the screen assayed adult brain only and therefore does not test hair-follicle cells where HOXC13 is normally active.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Fbxo11 perturbation showed on-target Fbxo11 mRNA changes, but canonical FBXO11 substrate biology was not recovered as substrate mRNA responses: Bcl6, Dtl, Snai1, and Prdm1 transcripts were not FDR-significant in any Fbxo11-perturbed brain cell type examined, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA. This negative result is consistent with FBXO11 acting mainly through ubiquitination and protein degradation, so steady-state mRNA is only an indirect readout of the canonical protein-turnover pathway.

Cask showed no detectable transcriptomic convergence with its curated synaptic partners: across matched cell-type/gene vectors, Cask knockdown signatures had near-zero Pearson correlation with Caskin1, Dlg4, and Nrxn1, and no perturbation in the library emerged as a tight Cask transcriptome neighbor. This suggests that membership in the CASK–neurexin–CASKIN1–Mint1/APBA1–LIN7 scaffolding complex does not imply interchangeable acute mRNA Perturb-seq signatures, while remaining a restricted transcriptional contrast that does not test protein localization, binding, or synaptic physiology.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Cst3 perturbation showed near-zero transcriptomic correlation with its measured protease partner Ctsb across 22 matched neuronal cell types, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic classes. Although Ctsb is the strongest measured STRING-linked Cst3 partner and was efficiently knocked down in many of the same neurons, neither perturbation produced opposing or phenocopying global mRNA signatures; both were largely self-knockdown patterns. This suggests the Cst3–Ctsb relationship is uncoupled at the transcript level in the cysteine protease inhibition/cathepsin B axis, with caveats that Wilcoxon score correlations may miss activity-level, secreted CysC, or disease-state effects.

Gfi1b showed no convergence with its paralog Gfi1 in the mouse-brain perturbation panel: Gfi1 itself had no genes at FDR < 0.05, and Gfi1b-versus-Gfi1 score correlations across 22 overlapping cell classes never exceeded |r| = 0.093. This negative audit argues against a hidden shared GFI-family neuronal module or recapitulation of the canonical GFI-family SNAG/RCOR-KDM1A-HDAC hematopoietic repression program in mouse brain, although both perturbation signatures were weak, so the comparison should not be read as a strong epistasis test.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Creb1 perturbation was dominated by recurrent induction of the paralog-family gene Crem, which was the top positive gene in five neuronal classes—066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—with FDR-significant logFC of 1.09–1.57, consistent with CREB-family compensation. In several classes the response was sparse and largely Crem-only, while 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed the largest program. The data measure total Crem transcripts, so activating CREM versus ICER repressor isoforms cannot be distinguished, and no direct Crem or Atf1 perturbation was available for reciprocity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Hsp90ab1 did not show a strong transcriptomic neighbor or clear phenocopy of available heat-shock/chaperone perturbations. In four scanned, best-engaged cell types—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA—genome-wide correlations to other perturbations were very small, and correlations with Hsf1, Hspa8, and Hspd1 were near zero. These cells showed target downregulation without a coherent downstream HSP90 proteostasis program, with only nominal Hsp90aa1 or Hspa8 increases and no FDR-significant non-target response; interpretation is limited because only four contexts were scanned and the comparator perturbations were weakly engaged.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Fgf13 showed no detectable convergence with its FHF paralogs Fgf12 or Fgf14 in the Fgf13-engaged cell classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, but this comparison is exploratory because Fgf12 and Fgf14 self-depletion was weak and did not reach FDR-level target knockdown in these contexts. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Fgf13 was the top depleted transcript and Rell2 was the only non-target FDR hit, while expected Nav/AIS and channel-subunit signatures still did not converge.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cox4i1 showed a buffered, target-only RNA phenotype in several midbrain classes, and the related complex-IV subunit Cox5a converged on the same pattern. In 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Cox4i1 depletion was FDR-significant yet produced no corrected non-target response, no HIF/COX4I2 induction, and only weak whole-transcriptome neighbors; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed near- or nominal Cox4i1 depletion. Cox5a had much stronger self-transcript depletion in overlapping classes but still zero non-target FDR hits, arguing that the buffered complex-IV RNA response is not simply a weak-guide artifact, although only RNA endpoints were assessed and score correlations were near zero because both signatures were dominated by their own transcripts.

Atp11c showed mixed, non-significant target-mRNA changes across all 20 assayed neuronal cell types, with no FDR-supported differential expression in either glutamatergic or GABAergic subclasses and no stable nearest-neighbor convergence within the P4-ATPase/aminophospholipid flippase complex. In the same neuronal contexts, the related P4-ATPase Atp9a displayed strong recurrent self-depletion in 18 of 20 tests, whereas Atp8a2 more closely resembled Atp11c with weak engagement. This transcript-level comparison suggests the Atp11c null result is unlikely to reflect a general inability to perturb membrane P4-ATPases in this experiment.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gtf2h5 perturbation showed a recurring but weak nominal increase of Polr2a across four cell classes—054 CNU-MGE GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—without broader pathway convergence beyond the RNA polymerase II transcription initiation axis. This pattern was never nominally decreased, but it remained statistically fragile: only 191 MB P MY GABA had any genes with FDR<0.1, where Clu and Polr2a both reached q=0.071, while the other three classes had Polr2a FDR=1.0.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Kctd16 did not show a coherent same-cell transcriptomic phenocopy of Kctd8, Gabbr1, or Gabbr2 across 20 overlapping cell classes, including multiple cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic populations as well as CTX-CGE, Pvalb, CNU-MGE, and other GABAergic groups. Its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with these GABA_B complex neighbors, indicating that physical or pathway proximity did not translate into interchangeable Perturb-seq signatures. This interpretation is tempered by the weak Kctd16 signatures, and the lack of an mRNA phenocopy does not address possible shared GIRK physiology.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Cacna1d perturbation showed an exploratory voltage-gated calcium-channel family compensation pattern, most evident in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where nominal Cacna1d reduction coincided with nominal induction of Cacna1c, the strongest positive gene in that cell type. Weaker nominal increases of Cacna1i in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Cacna1e in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut were also seen. However, no gene reached FDR significance, all paralog rows had adjusted p values of 1.0, and Cacna1e/Cacna1i are family members rather than narrow L-type Cav1.3 paralogs.

Mff did not phenocopy the related mitochondrial-dynamics perturbations Dnm1l or Opa1 in this dataset: its all-gene score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with both neighbors, while Dnm1l and Opa1 showed clear, FDR-significant cell-type-specific differential-expression signatures in the same Wilcoxon framework. Mff itself produced no FDR-resolved differentially expressed gene in any profiled cell type, so within the mitochondrial fission/fusion network, adaptor knockdown was transcriptomically separable from perturbing the core fission GTPase or a fusion gene. This comparison comes from acute transcriptomic profiles, and the weak Mff perturbation could have reduced apparent similarity.

Hoxd10 perturbation in the assayed mouse-brain cell classes did not detectably activate the literature-defined Hox10 lumbar motor-neuron identity program associated with Hoxa10 and Hoxc10. Across the dataset, Hoxd10 signatures were globally weak, showed no recurrent cross-cell-type transcriptional response, and the Hoxd10 transcript itself was not observed as a differential-expression feature, preventing direct quantification of on-target RNA effects. Because these profiles exclude embryonic lumbar spinal motor neurons and lack Hoxa10 or Hoxc10 perturbations, this result refines the developmental spinal literature rather than directly contradicting it.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Adam10 showed weaker on-target transcript depletion than the comparator perturbations App and Tspan7 across shared cell classes, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. In these classes, App and Tspan7 often produced strong self-transcript hits, sometimes as the only significant signal, whereas Adam10 was only directionally consistent and weak, with no clear APP/Notch transcript output. Because App and Tspan7 generally had more perturbed cells, differences in effect size and cell count cannot be fully separated.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atrx most strongly downregulated Resp18 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic class, where Resp18 appears to be the dominant Atrx-responsive gene and a small shared module rather than a broad transcriptional program. In the same cell type, Bptf and Trrap perturbations also decreased Resp18, indicating convergence on a secretory-vesicle-associated readout. This convergence is centered on Resp18 and should not be taken to mean that Bptf or Trrap broadly phenocopy Atrx in this thalamic population.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Coq5 showed near-zero transcriptomic correlation with the same-pathway perturbations Pdss1 and Pdss2 in neuronal cell types where Coq5 was better engaged, including 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. In these contexts, Coq5 was nominally down without coordinated ubiquinol/coenzyme Q biosynthesis pathway changes, and in one thalamic class all three perturbations had nominal own-transcript depletion yet still did not converge. This restricted single-cell RNA contrast suggests same-pathway assignment did not predict an interchangeable state, although PDSS knockdown was modest and no core COQ3/4/6/7/9 perturbations were available.

Epha10 perturbation aligned with its receptor-level annotation in EPH-ephrin signaling and axon guidance, but the Perturb-seq readout did not show a recurrent downstream transcriptional module. Across cell types, nominal effects were dominated by the Epha10 self-transcript, with no genome-wide FDR-significant differential-expression hit and no recurring axon-guidance or ephrin gene set. Related Eph receptors appeared buffered and uncorrelated with Epha10 loss. Interpretation is limited because no Efna/Efnb ligands were perturbed, and steady-state mRNA may not capture Eph receptor signaling.

Pah targeting did not detectably regulate the measured phenylalanine-catabolism, BH4-regeneration, or monoamine-synthesis transcript panel: Pah, Qdpr, Pcbd1, Pts, Gch1, Gchfr, Spr, Th, Tph1, Tph2, Il4i1, Kyat1, Kyat3, Asrgl1, Got1, Got2, Tat, Hpd, Fah, Hgd, Aadat, and Ddc all remained nonsignificant after correction. In 145 MH-LH TH Glut cells, Kyat1 showed the smallest nominal decrease, but this still had FDR=1. This negative result suggests transcriptional uncoupling from PAH’s annotated metabolic role, with the caveat that most direct pathway neighbors were assayed only as response genes, not as separate perturbations.

Atp8a2 perturbation is consistent with a buffered P4-ATPase transcriptomic response in this assay: among available family comparators, Atp9a was robustly depleted in 18 of 22 profiled cell types yet produced no non-target genes at FDR < 0.05, whereas Atp11c showed no measurable own-transcript knockdown and likewise no downstream adjusted response. This pattern was seen in contexts including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA, within aminophospholipid flippase/phospholipid-asymmetry biology, but the closest ATP8A2 complex members, Tmem30a and Atp8a1, were not screened.

Caskin1 perturbation showed no FDR-detectable induction of Caskin2 or other measured CASK/neurexin-neighborhood transcripts, including Cask, Abi2, Apba1, Nck1, Ppfia2, Lin7b, and Nlgn3. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, this Caskin postsynaptic-density and spine scaffold module appeared transcriptionally buffered after acute Caskin1 knockdown, with 0 of 414 tested rows significant. These data suggest that the reported Caskin1/Caskin2 redundancy is unlikely to reflect rapid Caskin2 mRNA induction here, although compensation could still occur at protein, localization, developmental, or circuit levels.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Crebbp showed a cell-type-specific transcriptomic response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons that Ep300 did not phenocopy, despite being the closest KAT3 paralog. In this class, the Crebbp–Ep300 genome-wide score correlation was low (r=0.090), Ep300 had no FDR <0.1 genes, and other broad coactivator perturbations such as Brd4, Creb1, and Chd8 were even less similar. This suggests CBP and p300 are not interchangeable here, although the comparison is limited by absent Ep300 target-transcript depletion and by reliance on transcriptomic score correlations rather than chromatin or protein readouts.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
