full_finding_text: Avpr1b was uncoupled from detectable canonical Gq/PLC/PKC transcriptional signaling in this assay: across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 001 L5-6 IT Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Avpr1b showed no FDR-significant downstream response, with the lowest row in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut still non-significant (FDR 0.103 for Mink1). In contrast, pathway-neighbor perturbations such as Plcb1 and Prkcg were detectable in the same dataset, suggesting the null is more consistent with absent receptor engagement or ineffective upstream perturbation than with a general inability to detect calcium/PKC-associated signaling, while noting these comparators are not direct measurements of AVPR1B-mediated calcium flux in the same cells.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Actb perturbation recurrently induced a compact actin-cytoskeleton compensation program centered on Actg1 and Flna, rather than a mixed stress or toxicity signature. Across the tested cell types, all FDR-significant transcript changes were up-regulated, with Flna the broadest recurrent response and Actg1 the most recurrent paralogous response. The strongest program appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, where Actg1/Flna co-occurred with Myh10, Vcl, Wdr1, and Rsu1; paired Actg1 and Flna induction also appeared in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. Notably, Actg1 perturbation was not generally reciprocal, although in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut it also induced Flna. Because the Actb transcript itself was not measured, recurrence is inferred from downstream responses rather than quantified knockdown.

Chp1 showed a sterol-compensation transcriptional program that was not phenocopied by related calcineurin/NHE-side perturbations at the mRNA level: Ppp3r1, Slc9a7, and Slc9a9 had near-zero correlation with the Chp1 signature and little or no downstream FDR signal. Chp1 loss also did not induce Slc9a1–Slc9a9, Gpat4, Gnpat, Srebf1, or Scap transcripts, arguing that the response is not a simple mimic of calcineurin-subunit or NHE-transcript knockdown. This comparison is limited to perturbations present in the screen, and SLC9A1 and post-transcriptional NHE function were not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Brd4 showed a decoupling between measured target-transcript depletion and downstream transcriptional impact across neuronal cell types. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the strongest response occurred despite weak, non-significant Brd4 mRNA reduction, with 311 FDR-significant genes, synaptic remodeling, recurrent Pabpn1 and Leng8 induction, and convergence with Trrap/Yy1-like signatures; 155 MB Glut showed a smaller related program with Pabpn1/Leng8 induction and Mt3 repression. By contrast, 001 L5-6 IT Glut and 053 Sst Gaba had nominal Brd4 decreases but no FDR-significant downstream genes, so Brd4 mRNA logFC alone was not a reliable engagement metric in this transcript-only dataset.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Cux1 perturbation did not recover the expected upper-layer cortical CUX1/CUX2 dendrite-and-synapse transcriptional program in cortical IT glutamatergic cells. Across 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, there were no FDR-controlled downstream transcriptomic hits, and even the layer II/III context closest to prior upper-layer biology showed essentially no Cux1 self-depletion. Because all upper-layer groups also lacked significant Cux1 reduction, these data cannot separate biological buffering from failed perturbation, and may not capture the developmental CUX1-dependent RNA polymerase II transcription and dendrite morphogenesis program.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gatad1 perturbation was associated with increased transcripts for connected chromatin factors, most notably Phf12, in responsive neuronal populations. In 155 MB Glut, Phf12 was the strongest Gatad1-induced transcript and the only one passing FDR 0.05, while in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Phf12 induction was nominal; Kdm5a was nominally induced in both classes. This pattern fits a possible feedback or stoichiometry-adjustment response within an EMSY/KDM5A/SIN3-associated chromatin-reader neighborhood, but Kdm5b, Kdm5c, Sin3a, and Gatad2b were uncoupled and no protein-complex abundance was measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Cry1 perturbation produced sparse genome-wide responses after multiple-testing correction, but isolated nominal increases in other clock genes appeared in specific glutamatergic classes. In 155 MB Glut, Cry2 was the top positive nominal hit, and in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Bhlhe40 was the fourth positive nominal hit, suggesting possible CRY-paralog replacement or weak secondary CLOCK:BMAL1/PER:CRY engagement outside 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. However, both signals had FDR=1.0 after testing more than 17,000 genes, so they remain hypothesis-generating rather than validated compensatory programs.

Clpx did not produce a coherent transcriptomic loss state with its CLPXP partner Clpp in this Perturb-seq dataset. Although both genes belong to the mitochondrial CLPXP protein degradation module, Clpx had no FDR-significant hits, Clpp had only one, and their same-cell-type score correlations were near zero, indicating nonconvergent, buffered signatures rather than interchangeable perturbations. Because both signatures were very weak, the low correlation could reflect poor perturbation strength rather than true biological divergence between CLPX and CLPP.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: E2f1 perturbation was associated with a nominal increase in E2f6 in two neuronal subclasses, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, consistent with a possible E2F6-mediated transcriptional repression feedback signal. However, this pattern was limited to 2 of 23 cell classes, both E2f6 observations had FDR=1.0, and the affected subclasses otherwise showed weak E2f1 downstream responses, so the finding is best viewed as exploratory rather than a validated compensatory program.

Adarb1 perturbation did not detectably change the total mRNA abundance of classical ADAR2-edited receptor and channel transcripts, including Gria2, Grik2, Htr2c, Gabra3, and Kcna1, in any observed cell type. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cell type, Adarb1 itself was partly depleted and Flnb, Flna, and Zfp941 responded, yet these canonical recoding substrates remained abundance-uncoupled. This suggests the Perturb-seq readout is not directly capturing the classic A-to-I recoding mechanism; unchanged total mRNA does not exclude substantial effects on editing, splice isoforms, channel composition, or excitability.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Atad1 showed a buffered, self-only transcriptional response in neuronal classes where mitochondrial dynamics perturbations were clearly detectable: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 191 MB P MY GABA, validated Atad1 knockdown yielded no FDR-supported non-target transcripts, with unchanged AMPAR transcripts in the highlighted glutamatergic and GABAergic classes, whereas Opa1 and Dnm1l produced broad signatures ranging from tens to 155 significant genes. This contrast suggests the Atad1 result is not due to screen insensitivity in these classes, although OPA1 and DNM1L serve only as functional mitochondrial benchmarks rather than direct ATAD1-complex comparators.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nsd1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed a small but FDR-supported acute RNA phenotype, biased toward up-regulated transcripts, with significant depletion of the Nsd1 target transcript and a Ddo/Pygm/Capn3/Ptgds/Myo5c-positive marker signature. However, this response did not converge with Dnmt3a: Dnmt3a knockdown was only nominal at the target transcript, produced no FDR-supported acute RNA module, and its genome-wide score vector was uncorrelated with Nsd1. Thus, within the PKMT/H3K36 chromatin regulation context, the neuronal NSD1-H3K36me2-DNMT3A axis was not captured as an immediate Dnmt3a-like transcriptome, noting that the dataset measures RNA only and cannot assess H3K36me2, H3K27me3, non-CG methylation, or delayed methylome-dependent effects.

Btbd9 did not show acute transcriptional convergence with the RLS genetic-neighbor perturbations Meis1 or Ptprd in this mouse Perturb-seq assay. Across shared cell types, score-vector correlations between Btbd9 and either Meis1 or Ptprd were essentially zero, arguing that these restless-legs genetic risk loci do not meet in a shared immediate mRNA module here. However, Meis1 and Ptprd were themselves weak in the dataset, with no FDR<0.05 gene rows, so this does not rule out chronic developmental or circuit-level convergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Elf2 showed a divergent ETS-family transcriptional pattern rather than being interchangeable with Ets1, Etv6, or Spi1 in this screen. Across matched cell types, Ets1, Etv6, and Spi1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Elf2, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut the same-cell comparison was especially distinct: Etv6 induced Adora1 whereas Elf2 induced Stxbp2, with a near-zero full-transcriptome correlation. These data are transcriptomic only, and most Elf2 responses were weak, but they argue against treating ETS-family perturbations as equivalent here.

Elf2 perturbation in the assayed neuronal brain classes did not reactivate the canonical ELF2 programs reported in other contexts: genes from the RUNX1/LMO2-linked B-cell receptor program, including Runx1, Lmo2, Lyn, and Blk, and from the Tie2 endothelial program, including Tek and Cdh5, were not significantly or FDR-responsively regulated. Consistent with this, perturbations of available related genes such as Vcp, Tek, and the Stxbp2 paralog Stxbp1 did not phenocopy Elf2, suggesting that these immune and endothelial annotations do not transfer to these neuronal phenotypes.

P2ry12 perturbation did not reveal a transcriptional ADP–P2Y12–Gi footprint in the assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes: across 21 P2ry12-assayed Glut/GABA groups, there was no detectable depletion of the targeted P2ry12 transcript and no FDR<0.05 downstream differential-expression event, even though ADP–P2Y12–Gi signaling is a curated canonical pathway. In contrast, the comparator Gnb1 showed CRISPR-associated transcript loss and downstream effects. This null neuronal result does not rule out acute P2Y12 signaling, because the endpoint is transcriptomic and may miss rapid second-messenger or motility phenotypes, and no microglial group was represented in the P2ry12 result set.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Fam120a did not phenocopy Pura in the Purα-containing neuronal mRNP context across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 308 CB GABA. Fam120a produced no transcriptome-wide FDR-significant downstream genes and showed only small score correlations with Pura, whereas Pura produced 37 significant rows, concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut, Fam120a showed only near-threshold signals such as Hgs and Luc7l3, and stronger Pura target engagement remains an important caveat.

Fam120a was largely uncoupled from the strong Srsf1 perturbation response in basal post-mitotic mouse brain cells. Across all 23 cell types, Srsf1 produced a broad signature with 9,588 FDR-significant rows, whereas Fam120a produced none, despite on-target Fam120a transcript effects and only weak correlation with Srsf1, Srebf1, and related RNA-binding or Ago2/Src-PI3K perturbations. In 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Fam120a showed nominal knockdown without downstream significant hits, while Pura and Srsf1 were clearly responsive, suggesting any FAM120A–SRSF1–SREBP1 role may be context-specific and depend on mTORC1/SRPK2 activation absent here.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Atxn10 loss did not phenocopy other spinocerebellar-ataxia disease-network perturbations in the two cell types with sufficiently large Atxn10 signatures, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In these Atxn10 FDR-gene sets, perturbations of Atxn1, Atxn2, Atxn7, Cacna1a, Kcnc3, Ppp2r2b, Nop56, Afg3l2, Iqcb1, Dab1, and Prkcg were only weakly correlated, despite STRING linking ATXN10 to many of these genes. This divergence suggests the disease label or network proximity poorly predicts the acute cell-autonomous transcriptional state here, with the caveat that STRING relationships partly reflect disease/text co-membership and the comparison was limited to two Atxn10 signatures.

Atxn2 perturbation showed no detectable transcriptional induction of the paralog Atxn2l in any tested cell type, with all 21 Atxn2l measurements under Atxn2 perturbation reported at adjusted p=1.0, arguing against simple mRNA-level paralog compensation in this dataset. In the ATXN2 RNA-granule and TDP-43 interaction context, this was described as weak convergence with Tardbp but no Atxn2l induction. A caveat is that ATXN2L protein abundance or relocalization could still buffer ATXN2 loss without a change in Atxn2l mRNA.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Klf7 in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic glutamatergic class produced the only FDR-supported response, and it was characterized by an axon-cytoskeletal module rather than reconstitution of the classical TrkA-CDKN-Rac3 developmental KLF7 target axis. In this cell type, Ntrk1, Cdkn1a, Cdkn1b, and Rac3 were not measurably altered, while cytoskeletal genes such as Tuba1a changed. This interpretation is tempered by very low or absent Ntrk1 in this thalamic class and by the fact that the comparison spans embryonic sensory or cortical systems versus a differentiated thalamic Perturb-seq cell class.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Klf11 perturbation in this unstimulated neuronal Perturb-seq screen did not mobilize the published KLF11-linked TGF-beta/SMAD7, apoptotic, or monoamine-oxidase stress programs: across many glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types, Smad7, Maoa, Maob, Casp3, and Bcl2 showed no FDR-supported differential expression, and the full Klf11 differential-expression table lacked significant downstream responses. No cell type showed a reliable shift of Klf11 transcript itself after assignment to the Klf11 perturbation, so these null results are best interpreted as poor target engagement and strong context dependence rather than contradiction of stimulus-, ethanol-, glucocorticoid-, oligodendroglial-, epithelial-, or injury-based models.

Dpyd perturbation showed no detectable transcriptional feedback onto pyrimidine catabolism, beta-alanine biosynthesis, or nearby nucleotide-metabolism transcripts: across all 22 tested cell types, Dpys, Upb1, Abat, Aldh6a1, Aldh9a1, Bcat2, Cad, Umps, Tyms, Dhfr, Nt5c, and Upp1 remained unchanged, with weak top positive, top negative, and adjacent-neighbor signatures. This suggests the perturbation did not propagate through mRNA-level pathway regulation, although only transcript changes were assayed and metabolites such as uracil, thymine, dihydrouracil, beta-alanine, and 5-fluorouracil metabolism were not measured.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Acvrl1 was silent in neuronal contrasts, and its HHT co-receptor Eng was likewise not transcriptionally engaged, whereas the related type-II BMP receptor Bmpr2 showed significant self-transcript depletion in matched 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut classes. This suggests the assay could engage BMP receptor transcripts in these neurons, but the ACVRL1/ENG pair was poorly accessible or biologically inactive in these cell classes. A caveat is that Bmpr2 and Acvrl1 are different receptor subunits with different basal expression, and the comparison relies on self-transcript engagement rather than matched vascular phenotypes.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Map2k1 perturbation in 191 MB P MY GABA cells produced a small but statistically supported, off-canonical response: Las1l decreased and Uso1 increased, while the TH-associated Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 MAPK module seen in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells was absent. Across most Map2k1 contexts, no FDR-supported downstream transcriptome was detected, and here Map2k1 self-knockdown was only nominal, so this signal should be treated cautiously rather than annotated as a canonical RAF–MEK–ERK transcriptional program.

Nf1 showed a clear transcriptional phenotype in this dataset, with 25 FDR-supported differential-expression rows, whereas Spred1 and Spred2 did not phenocopy Nf1 and produced no FDR<0.05 or FDR<0.1 rows across the tested cell types. In the SPRED-neurofibromin RasGAP recruitment context, this contrast suggests the SPRED arms were effectively silent relative to Nf1 here, but the interpretation is limited because Spred1 and Spred2 also lacked FDR-level target-transcript knockdown, so the result does not show that SPRED biology is dispensable in these neurons.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Clcn4 loss did not resemble a generic endolysosomal acidification failure: in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Clcn4 was self-only or FDR-negative, with strong self-knockdown in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c and midbrain glutamatergic cells but no robust trans FDR genes, and in Pvalb interneurons Clcn4 itself was the sole FDR-significant gene. By contrast, Atp6v0c perturbation in the same broad cell classes produced broad transcriptional output, with 24–537 FDR-significant genes including Atp6v0c, indicating divergence between these vesicular ion-homeostasis modules rather than a one-to-one mechanistic substitute.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Cox7b showed a single corrected association: Eepd1 was upregulated in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, but Cox7b itself was essentially unchanged in that same cell type. This pattern, based on 49 perturbed cells, argues against interpreting the result as a coherent mitochondrial Complex IV program and instead suggests Eepd1 is a fragile, cell-restricted, hypothesis-generating marker. The broader mitochondrial context was mostly buffered and divergent across subunit perturbations, with no direct support linking Eepd1 to COX7B or Complex IV assembly.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Chrnb2 perturbation showed convergent self-knockdown only, matching Ache in the same three neuronal classes: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In each class, Chrnb2 was significantly depleted without FDR-significant non-target transcriptional changes; in 191 MB P MY GABA, non-target rows such as Ppfia2 and Flvcr1 were only subthreshold. Ache perturbation likewise reduced Ache in these same classes but produced no non-Ache FDR genes, suggesting that acetylcholine clearance and nicotinic receptor response components were both targetable yet buffered in the resting transcriptome, with the caveat that Ache loss is not equivalent to receptor-subunit loss and extracellular acetylcholine was not assayed.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Lingo2 did not phenocopy related LINGO/NgR receptor perturbations in this screen: its signature correlations with Lingo1, Rtn4r, and Ngfr were near zero, with no meaningful correlated or anti-correlated profile among related receptors or across full-overlap targets. By contrast, Lingo1 showed target-transcript depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, with Becn1 upregulation significant in 007, and Rtn4r showed a downstream Drp2 hit in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut. This contrast is transcriptomic and tempered by uneven guide cell counts; Rtn4r itself had only one FDR-significant downstream gene, and most related-target comparisons used rank-like score vectors rather than validated phenotypes.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Ank2 showed weaker and less penetrant on-target transcript depletion than its ankyrin paralogs in shared cell classes. In 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Ank1 or Ank3 reached FDR-significant self-transcript depletion where Ank2 did not, even though Ank2 had its strongest nominal depletion in 155 MB Glut and its largest perturbed-cell count in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This suggests the weak Ank2 result was not a universal guide- or cell-type failure, although the comparison is based on self-transcript readouts rather than matched protein depletion or guide efficiency.

Camk2b knockdown did not produce FDR-significant transcriptional compensation by the measured CaMKII family members or endogenous inhibitors: Camk2a, Camk2d, Camk2g, Camk2n1, and Camk2n2 were all nonresponders in the assayed window, including across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. This argues against an obvious mRNA-level paralog or inhibitor feedback loop, while leaving open buffering through protein turnover, localization, phosphorylation, or unmeasured isoforms.

Ascc3 perturbation did not transcriptionally co-induce the known ASCC/ALKBH/RQT components Ascc1, Ascc2, Trip4, Alkbh3, or Zfp598; these core pathway transcripts were not FDR-significantly changed, even though hundreds of downstream genes changed overall. The most penetrant response was in midbrain glutamatergic neurons, where 130 genes met FDR<0.1 and the program was dominated by decreases in neuronal and endomembrane genes, including App, Atp1a3, Psap, Srrm2, and Rtn1. This argues against a simple mRNA feedback loop on the core repair/ribosome-rescue machinery, with the caveat that only mRNA abundance was assayed, not activity, localization, ubiquitination, or ribosome-collision phenotypes.

Atp13a3 showed weak but consistent RNA depletion across all 22 mouse-brain cell classes, yet no cell class had a genome-wide significant downstream response after multiple-testing correction. This null was not explained by an assay blind spot for P5B ATPases: the paralog Atp13a2 achieved FDR-significant self-depletion in seven cell types, including 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but still produced no FDR-significant non-target genes, and Atp13a2 and Atp13a3 signatures were essentially uncorrelated. These transcriptome-only data do not test polyamine flux, lysosomal physiology, or protein abundance.

Epm2a showed a weak, target-specific result in this file: although the Epm2a transcript was present in each Epm2a perturbation result table, it was not significantly depleted in any cell type. This null is less likely to reflect a globally underpowered dataset because other neuronal-disease perturbations in the same matched framework, including Dnm1, Ppt1, and Scarb2, showed corrected self-depletion at overlapping neuronal cell counts. The comparison is based on on-target transcript behavior rather than matched biology, and these comparator genes are not laforin complex members.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
full_finding_text: Hdac5 perturbation showed no strong non-self correlates across the main interpreted cell types, and the only multiple-testing-significant non-target event was a Chd5 induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut. In that same cell type, however, Hdac5 transcript was not detectably reduced, so the Chd5 increase is uncoupled from verified target engagement. This chromatin-remodeling singleton response, observed in 79 perturbed cells without guide-level replication, should be treated as an isolated outlier that could reflect indirect or guide-associated effects rather than a canonical HDAC5-loss program.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Ptprf knockdown showed clear self-depletion in 155 MB Glut and weaker but still evident self-depletion in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, yet across all Ptprf target-by-cell-type contrasts no downstream gene passed multiple-testing correction. In these two cell types, the restricted Ptprf signatures did not converge with related LAR-RPTP or synaptic-adhesion perturbations such as Ptprd and Nrxn1, indicating that synaptic-adhesion and NMDA-receptor biology was uncoupled from the mRNA readout. This negative transcriptional result is limited to RNA abundance after a single perturbation modality, not electrophysiology or ultrastructure.

Add3 did not phenocopy Add1 or Add2 at the transcriptome level: across shared cell types, Add3-versus-Add1 and Add3-versus-Add2 score-vector correlations were centered near zero, so Add3 showed no detectable whole-transcriptome signature overlap with the other adducin perturbations. This is notable because ADD3 is annotated in an ADD1:ADD3 membrane-skeleton complex, yet in these neuronal Perturb-seq data physical complex membership did not translate into interchangeable signatures. A key caveat is that all three adducin perturbations were weak by FDR, so the near-zero correlations may reflect weak engagement rather than true biochemical divergence.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Plcb1 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX glutamatergic neurons showed significant on-target self-transcript depletion, and Itpr1 was similarly depleted in the same cell class, yet their genome-wide perturbation scores were essentially uncorrelated and each perturbation produced only a self-transcript FDR hit. Thus, within the Gq/PLCβ/IP3-calcium signaling neighborhood that includes PRKCA/GNAQ-family components, the canonical PLCβ to IP3 receptor leg appeared uncoupled at the transcriptome level in this dataset, with the caveat that the comparison is limited to one cell class and RNA readouts, so coupling could be fast, post-translational, or spatially localized.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Chmp4b perturbation showed only nominal, cell-type-restricted increases in several ESCRT or ESCRT-adjacent transcripts, including Stam2, Ptpn23, Vps4a, Chmp3, Snf8, and Vta1, across 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. The pattern is consistent with a possible feedback attempt to restore endosomal scission or ESCRT-III recycling, with Ptpn23 and Vps4a emerging as exploratory state markers, but all signals were FDR-nonsignificant and several came from low-cell-count strata.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Nfyc perturbation was associated with a weak, recurrent increase in Nfya transcripts, while Nfyb and endogenous Nfyc did not show comparable transcript changes, consistent with only weak target engagement in NF-Y/CCAAT-box transcriptional regulation. This pattern appeared across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells, with the strongest nominal Nfya rise in 155 MB Glut and a nominal rise also in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. However, the Nfya increase did not pass FDR correction, and reciprocal testing was not possible because Nfya and Nfyb perturbations were unavailable.

Kcnn2 showed weak, low-amplitude Perturb-seq effects that did not phenocopy the related SK-channel paralog Kcnn3: across 23 matched brain cell types, their whole-transcriptome score vectors were near-zero correlated rather than convergent. This exploratory contrast is limited because neither perturbation produced FDR-significant genes. In 308 CB GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Kcnn2 had nominal target depletion, but downstream rows remained nonsignificant, and small-conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channel signaling components, including Calm1, Calm3, Kcnq2, Hcn2, and Kcnma1, appeared buffered and uncoupled at the transcriptome level.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mpc1 perturbation did not produce detectable Mpc2 mRNA induction in any measured cell type, including 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Mpc1 showed its clearest nominal decrease. In these classes, the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier complex therefore showed partial Mpc1 loss without a transcriptional partner-rescue response, and there was no FDR-level bulk RNA response. This argues against simple Mpc2 transcript compensation after partial Mpc1 perturbation, although only RNA was measured, so MPC2 protein stability or carrier activity could still change.

Flt4 showed transcriptional signatures that were essentially orthogonal to related VEGFR3-network perturbations, including Kdr, Nrp2, Prox1, and Mapk1, with no non-self absolute Pearson correlation above 0.165 and only very weak pairwise correlations for these neighbors. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Prox1 produced a strong program with 50 FDR<0.05 genes, whereas Flt4 had none and the two were uncorrelated; in 155 MB Glut, Mapk1 showed direct depletion without Flt4-like correlation. Because correlations were computed from signed Wilcoxon scores, undetected Flt4 target engagement could itself make related perturbations appear divergent.

Alx1 did not converge with ALX paralogs or the p300/CBP coactivator axis in the assayed brain cell signatures: perturbations of Alx3, Alx4, Ep300, and Crebbp were essentially uncorrelated with Alx1, and these genes were not transcriptomic neighbors in the measured neuronal populations. This suggests the paired-type homeobox craniofacial transcription program was buffered or not detected in these neurons. A key caveat is that the comparator signatures were themselves weak, so the result reflects transcriptomic similarity in neuronal cells rather than biochemical interactions in craniofacial mesenchyme.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Kmt2e showed responsive transcriptomic effects in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, but Ogt perturbation, although strongly engaged—especially in 155 MB Glut—did not phenocopy Kmt2e; their signatures were essentially uncorrelated in both classes. This suggests that within the OGT-linked KMT2E protein-stability neighborhood, Ogt loss is not a simple transcriptomic surrogate for Kmt2e loss in these neurons. The interpretation is tempered by Ogt pleiotropy, weak Kmt2e mRNA engagement, and the absence of matched Usp7 and Hcfc1 comparators.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Il10ra showed a flat on-target result: across assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, including 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Il10ra perturbation never detectably reduced or induced its own transcript, even though the transcript was measured in every contrast. By comparison, the JAK-STAT pathway neighbor Stat1 produced clear on-target RNA depletion in those same neuronal classes, strongest in 191 MB P MY GABA. This internal contrast argues against a blanket assay failure, while noting that Stat1 and Il10ra differ in baseline expression, guide cutting, and transcript stability.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mef2d did not behave interchangeably with Mef2c across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons. In these classes, Mef2c knockdown produced FDR-supported transcriptional signatures and direct Mef2c depletion, consistent with active MEF2 transcriptional activation, whereas Mef2d showed no FDR hits, near-zero score correlations with Mef2c, and in some high-cell-count strata only nominal self-depletion without adjusted downstream differential expression. This contrast is tempered by weaker Mef2d guide activity, so the result refines rather than fully settles paralog non-interchangeability.

Mef2d knockdown did not produce FDR-supported induction of the measured paralogs Mef2a or Mef2c, indicating that MEF2 paralog compensation was not visible as transcript up-regulation in this single-cell mRNA readout. In the 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut class, where nominal Mef2d depletion was observed, the strongest Mef2a response under Mef2d perturbation was instead a nominal down-regulation. This negative result is limited to mRNA abundance, so compensatory changes could still occur through phosphorylation, localization, or dimer usage without altered Mef2a/Mef2c transcript levels.

Pax2 showed no convergent acute adult-brain transcriptomic response with the related Pax5 or Pax8 perturbations. In the assayed adult brain classes, Pax5 and Pax8 were as FDR-null as Pax2, and their mean within-cell score correlations with Pax2 were only 0.011 and 0.015, respectively. Thus, despite known developmental cooperation and redundancy among PAX2/5/8, these data do not support a shared adult-brain Pax2-Pax5-Pax8 module here; importantly, all three perturbations were weak or null, so the result reflects absence of convergence rather than opposing biology.

Kiss1r showed a largely null, nonconvergent profile: its score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with available neuropeptide and reproductive-axis perturbations including Tacr3, Gnrhr, Npy1r, Npy2r, and Agrp, arguing against a shared transcriptional program among these comparators. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Tacr3 produced a single Dazap1 hit while Kiss1r remained FDR-null, which supports only an exploratory related-receptor contrast rather than a Kiss1r-specific module. This interpretation is limited because several closest pathway neighbors were not perturbed and most comparator signatures were weak.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Far1 did not behave like a generic peroxisome-loss perturbation. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Pex14 was strongly knocked down at the transcript level, yet no sterol genes reached FDR significance, whereas Far1 knockdown linked to sterol-gene induction including Dhcr24 in relevant contexts. Agps showed only a thalamic sterol overlap and lacked FDR-level self-knockdown, so interchangeability with Far1 is not established. This comparison is limited because only transcript-level target engagement was measured, and residual protein, timing, or viability could differ across perturbations.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Dzip1 showed an exploratory, nominal increase of Dzip1l in two cell classes, 046 CTX-CGE GABA and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, suggesting a possible weak paralog-compensation signal within cilium assembly and basal-body trafficking genes. However, this pattern did not survive multiple-testing correction: every Dzip1l adjusted p value was 1.0 across Dzip1 contrasts, no FDR-supported module was detected, and Dzip1l was not available as a perturbation comparator in this dataset. Given that DZIP1L is a basal-body/transition-zone protein, the nominal response is biologically coherent but remains tentative.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|215 MB Dopa
full_finding_text: Foxp1 showed only nominal, mixed downstream hotspots that were not coupled to measurable Foxp1 knockdown in several cell types, so these signals should be treated as tentative follow-up markers rather than direct FOXP1-regulated outputs. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Hook3 and a nominal up Kcnk3 excitability signal were the lowest adjusted hits despite no Foxp1 transcript depletion; 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had a Slc6a8 outlier; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut showed Mfap3 and Pik3c2a; and 215 MB Dopa had large nominal Med25 and Ap1g1 logFC values from only 31 perturbed cells. Across these contexts, all adjusted p values were at least 0.123.

Foxp1 showed little transcriptional convergence with Foxp2 in this screen: their full-score signatures had near-zero correlation across 22 shared cell types, despite the expected biochemical relatedness of FOXP-family factors. In 001 L5-6 IT Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Foxp1 knockdown was weak and did not produce an FDR-significant downstream FOXP-family transcriptional repression program. This limits treating FOXP1 as interchangeable with the measured Foxp2 perturbation here, especially since Foxp2 itself was only weakly engaged and Foxp4 was not perturbed.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Foxp1 was largely silent across cortical glutamatergic and Pvalb GABA classes, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Mef2c showed clear within-screen transcription-factor responses in the same classes. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Foxp1 had only a nominal self-transcript decrease with no FDR-significant DE; in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, nominal synaptic outliers such as Nlgn3 and Dlg2 lacked corrected hits. This contrast suggests a target- or guide-specific Foxp1 failure rather than a global assay inability, not a mechanistic FOXP1-MEF2C relationship.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Mef2a showed a limited, cell-type-skewed transcriptomic response compared with the other assayed MEF2 paralogs: across the cross-perturbation comparison, Mef2c was broader and stronger, with 71 FDR-significant hits spanning 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Mef2a had only four hits and Mef2d had none. The main Mef2a-responsive class was 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where there was weak Mef2a-Mef2c-Celf2-Cic convergence within a MEF2 paralog transcription-factor module that also included Gpr4, Ogt, and Prkcg. This isoform-specific pattern is transcriptomic and may depend on guide efficacy in each cell type.

Myrf was essentially silent across all 23 assayed neuronal classes, with no detectable transcript-level increase or decrease after Myrf-targeting guides, and the related myelin-axis factors Sox10, Nkx6-2, and Egr2 were similarly near-null in the GABAergic, glutamatergic, and dopaminergic panel. This shared lack of FDR-significant responses is consistent with the Sox10–Myrf oligodendroglial transcription module and CNS myelination program being restricted to oligodendroglial context rather than interchangeable with neuronal state, although the assay does not establish genetic ordering among these factors because the perturbations were not functionally active here.

Neurod2 perturbation did not robustly activate canonical NeuroD2-linked effector axes: Cplx2, Rest, Zeb1, and Dpysl3 all failed FDR correction, indicating no clear movement of the Cdc20-APC/NeuroD2/Cplx2 or REST-Zeb1 neuronal differentiation pathways in this screen. This absence of expected transcript-level changes is notable because prior studies place NeuroD2 upstream of presynaptic and neuronal-differentiation effectors, but the current assay also showed no detectable Neurod2 mRNA knockdown, so the negative result should be interpreted cautiously.

Bsn showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to its active-zone paralog Pclo across all 22 matched neuronal cell types, indicating that these homologous scaffolds were not transcriptionally interchangeable in the assayed cells. This weak, near-orthogonal pattern also extended to presynaptic and vesicle-gene perturbations such as Snap25, Syp, Syn1, Unc13b, and Atg5. Bsn itself had weak downstream signatures: only 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut yielded an FDR-significant gene, Mcts1, whereas 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed no robust convergence, and the comparison is based on rank correlations rather than synaptic physiology.

Hnrnph2 acute perturbation did not produce FDR-supported induction of the measured H/F-family paralogs Hnrnph1, Hnrnpf, Hnrnph3, or Grsf1, indicating that transcript-level paralog compensation was not a robust acute response across the screened neuronal populations. This contrasts with mouse Hnrnph2-null models reporting Hnrnph1 upregulation, suggesting the compensation seen in chronic loss may not generalize to acute pooled perturbation. The close H/F genes were measured but not perturbed here, and weak nominal Hnrnph1 increases in a few cell types could reflect subthreshold compensation.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gpr156 did not produce a recurrent neuronal transcriptional program in this Perturb-seq dataset: across 22 measured brain neuronal classes, including multiple glutamatergic and GABAergic populations, score vectors were weak, nominal high-scoring genes did not organize into a consistent cross-cell-type module, and signatures were near-uncorrelated with Gpr158 and Gpr179. The established GPR156-Gαi hair-cell polarity pathway therefore was not detected in these broad brain neuron classes, with the caveat that the sampled cells were not EMX2-positive auditory or vestibular hair cells and close pathway controls such as G proteins and GPSM2/GABAB subunits were not directly perturbed.

Gpr156 showed no FDR-significant transcriptional program and its weak signatures were near-uncorrelated with related receptor or deafness-family perturbations. In the same brain neuron classes, Gpr158 and Atp2b2 each caused strong depletion of their own target transcript, in 6 and 16 classes respectively, but no additional FDR-significant genes, while Gpr179 and Pcdh15 also yielded no FDR hits. This argues that the lack of a Gpr156 program is not simply a failure to detect receptor transcripts, although these comparators are only pathway-adjacent and differ in guide efficiency and expression level.

Chchd2 knockdown did not produce a coherent FDR-significant mitochondrial transcriptional response in this screen: COX/OXPHOS and mtDNA-encoded sentinels such as mt-Nd4, Cox16, Ndufb10, and Atp5d, along with MIA40 import genes Chchd4 and Gfer and cristae/shape regulators Micos13, Opa1, and Oma1, showed only nominal or null shifts, and Chchd2 itself was the only FDR-significant gene. This suggests that reported links of CHCHD2 to COX4I2 regulation, cytochrome-c/crista biology, and MIA40 import were not captured as an mRNA module here, with the caveat that the tested panel was a sentinel set from the DE table and protein-level mitochondrial phenotypes could occur without transcript changes.

Chchd2 showed a largely target-only response, and its paralog Chchd10 phenocopied this pattern: in overlapping classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, both perturbations achieved strong self-depletion yet produced no FDR-significant non-target genes. Within the CHCHD2-CHCHD10 mitochondrial intermembrane-space module, residual score correlations between Chchd2 and Chchd10 were weak, so the data support shared buffering and a lack of acute off-target transcriptional consequences rather than a robust common transcriptional module, with the caveat that these correlations were computed on weak, high-FDR signatures.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Brd1 showed a buffered, nonconvergent relationship with the BRPF-MYST histone acetyltransferase scaffolding context: in the two Brd1-responsive classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA, Kat6a and Kat6b did not phenocopy Brd1, with zero FDR-supported genes and near-zero Brd1 signature correlations, and across 22 shared Brd1 classes Brd1–Kat6a/Kat6b all-gene correlations remained between -0.099 and 0.075. Thus the Brd1 signal in this screen should not be treated as interchangeable with MOZ/MORF catalytic loss, especially because target engagement and loss-of-function strength were uncertain for all three genes.

Hnf1b showed essentially no concordance with Hnf1a across the profiled brain cell types, despite the known HNF1A/HNF1B DNA-binding dimer relationship: across 23 matched cell types, score correlations were near zero, ranging from -0.0396 to 0.1116, including r = 0.0025 in the L4/5 IT CTX Glut context where Hnf1b was closest to an effect. In this weak-Hnf1b setting, Hnf1a therefore did not phenocopy Hnf1b, cautioning against assuming rescue or interchangeability in these brain cells; the supporting biochemical literature is also kidney/pancreas-biased rather than brain-specific.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Hoxa1 perturbation did not mobilize the canonical embryonic Hoxa1/retinoic-acid program in the sampled brain cell classes. Across 23 targeted neuronal and glial classes, including cortical IT and ET glutamatergic neurons, multiple GABAergic classes, midbrain dopaminergic cells, pineal glutamatergic cells, and cerebellar GABA cells, Aldh1a2/Raldh2, Cyp26a1, and reported embryonic downstream genes such as Zic1, Hnf1b, Foxd3, Pax8, Fgfr3, and Lhx5 were statistically unchanged, with near-zero Hox/RA/Pbx/Meis signature correlations. This null result likely reflects a non-embryonic, non-permissive state rather than contradicting Hoxa1 requirements during early hindbrain development.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Adcy5 showed weak, non-significant self-repression in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas its paralog Adcy3 showed significant self-transcript reduction in those same midbrain classes. This contrast suggests the screen detected stronger engagement for Adcy3 and that Adcy5 and Adcy3 should not be treated as interchangeable perturbations within the membrane adenylyl-cyclase paralog module. The comparison is limited to self-transcript engagement, not matched cAMP activity or shared downstream FDR modules; in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Adcy2 was nominally up with Adcy5 down.

Nfia perturbation in 22 Glut/GABA neuronal classes did not phenocopy its NFI paralogs Nfib, Nfic, or Nfix: across 66 cross-perturbation comparisons, Pearson correlations remained near zero, from -0.061 to 0.0876, and Nfia did not FDR-induce any paralog transcript. This argues against a shared NFI-family transcriptional module or compensatory Nfib/Nfic/Nfix response in these neuronal signatures, although interpretation is limited by the weak Nfia own-gene response, so the near-orthogonal signatures could reflect true specialization, insufficient perturbation strength, or both. In 053 Sst GABA neurons, the largest nominal Nfia tail still lacked any FDR-confirmed gene and showed the most negative Nfia-versus-Nfix correlation.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Foxg1 perturbation showed a recurrent but weak downward shift of Tle2, consistent with a possible Groucho/TLE co-repressor-family response. Tle2 was down-ranked in 16 of 22 neuronal classes and appeared among the top 200 negative genes in eight classes, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 053 Sst Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but every adjusted p value was 1.0, so this remains an exploratory, nominal trend rather than a corrected Tle2-specific effect.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Lepr showed weak effects across obesity-linked energy-balance cell contexts where related perturbations were stronger, indicating these genes were not interchangeable in this dataset. In 145 MH-LH TH Glut, Mc4r produced a clearer, FDR-supported Smox response while Lepr had no FDR-supported gene. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Fto generated strong signatures, including an Rsrp1-led program with 15 genes at FDR<0.1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Lepr remained weak despite substantial perturbed-cell counts. This comparison is pathway- and disease-family level, not a same-complex test, since FTO is obesity-associated rather than a LEPR receptor subunit.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Chrnb1 showed no measurable cis transcript depletion in the differential-expression analysis, even though related nicotinic receptor subunit perturbations did: Chrnb2 and Chrna4 were knocked down at the transcript level in selected thalamic and midbrain groups, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. This contrast suggests the Chrnb1 null is specific to the β1/muscle-subunit context assayed here rather than a general failure of receptor-subunit guides or the Wilcoxon pipeline, while noting that the comparator signal is limited to cis depletion and not necessarily broader downstream responses.

Hcrtr2, although annotated as an orexin-A/orexin-B GPCR in orexin-receptor and G alpha q signaling, showed no detectable basal transcriptional module after perturbation: across 22 tested cell types, no FDR-significant downstream genes were found, and Hcrtr2 itself did not show statistically supported self-repression. The strongest nominal shifts appeared in the MH-LH/TH glutamatergic group, but none survived multiple-testing correction. This pattern suggests pathway uncoupling or failed target engagement rather than absence of pathway membership, with the caveat that the assay did not assess acute second messengers, calcium, ligand-evoked activity, or behavior.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Kif5a showed a muted secondary transcriptional phenotype in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut: beyond significant depletion of the Kif5a transcript, it produced few or no FDR-significant non-target genes, with only nominal secondary signals such as Kpnb1, Kcnn2, and Dnajc6 in 155. In the same cell classes, Dctn1 and Dync1h1 perturbations yielded dozens of FDR-significant genes, indicating these cells can mount broader responses to cytoskeletal transport perturbation; however, this contrast is mechanistically indirect because Dctn1 and Dync1h1 are dynein/dynactin, not Kinesin-1 heavy-chain, genes.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Il17ra did not show an Il17rd-like receptor-family perturbation pattern in the assayed cell classes. Across 21 shared cell classes, Il17ra and Il17rd signatures were essentially uncorrelated, with Spearman rho ranging from -0.0219 to 0.0446. In 308 CB GABA, where the strongest Il17ra nominal tail was concentrated, canonical IL-17 outputs were absent and Il17rd did not phenocopy Il17ra. Conversely, Il17rd had only one 5% FDR event, Cep70 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, so the contrast mainly supports absence of phenocopy rather than a specific Il17rd mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Npy5r was uncoupled from the broader Gi/o neighbor Gnao1. In the high-count glutamatergic classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Gnao1 perturbation clearly depleted Gnao1 RNA, whereas Npy5r showed no target-transcript depletion, no FDR-significant downstream genes, and near-zero score correlation with Gnao1. Within the G alpha i/adenylate-cyclase signaling context, this suggests that Npy5r perturbation is not a strong transcriptomic proxy for wholesale Gi/o loss, which is not unexpected because Gnao1 is a broad G-protein alpha subunit used by many receptors.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Pik3r1 did not behave interchangeably with the paralogous regulatory subunit Pik3r2 in this brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across 199 related perturbation–cell type comparisons, Pik3r1 showed no reproducible all-gene convergence with Pik3r2 or other assayed class IA PI3K subunits, and in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA an exploratory comparison of the top-200 nominal Pik3r1 genes suggested anticorrelation with Pik3r2. This signal was restricted and caveated, because the individual genes were not FDR-significant and the broader subunit set was largely FDR-silent.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Nf2 perturbation in mature mouse neurons did not measurably induce a Hippo/YAP-TEAD transcriptional program. In the two clearest target-engaged classes, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Ccn1, Ccn2, Ankrd1, Amotl2, Areg, and Ptgs2 were not coordinately upregulated, and even the strongest on-target Nf2 transcript depletion remained FDR-negative downstream. This negative result is limited to steady-state transcripts, since Hippo regulation can be post-translational and these neuronal classes differ from Schwann, meningeal, mesothelial, or liver contexts.

Mitf perturbation did not produce a coherent MITF-M/CLEAR lysosome-autophagy program across the 22 tested Mitf cell classes. In this neuronal dataset, genome-wide testing found no multiple-testing-supported downstream transcriptomic response, and canonical lysosomal or autophagy genes such as Atp6v0d1, Clcn7, Atp6v0e, Arsb, Atp6v1b2, Ctsf, Map1lc3a, Lamp1, and Hexb changed only nominally and in mixed directions. The audit was limited to measured transcripts, and weak target engagement is possible: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Mitf itself was unchanged, while in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut the lowest adjusted p values still remained non-significant.

Fgf1 showed a broadly buffered null phenotype across all 22 tested neuronal classes: the complete Wilcoxon analysis found no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response, the targeted Fgf1 transcript was measured but not detectably depleted after multiple-testing correction, and nominal raw-p tails were scattered rather than forming a recurrent gene module. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Fgf1 loss was uncoupled from canonical FGF-FGFR to RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT comparator perturbations. This aligns with reports that FGF1-null mice have essentially no isolated abnormalities, although organism-level developmental data do not establish the same compensation mechanism as these cell-autonomous transcriptomes.

Nr3c2 perturbation did not detectably shift canonical mineralocorticoid/corticosteroid effector genes in this screen, including Sgk1, Fkbp5, Scnn1a, Scnn1b, Scnn1g, Nedd4l, Hsd11b2, and the Atp1 pump subunits Atp1a1 and Atp1b1. A targeted check likewise found no hidden Nr3c2 mineralocorticoid/steroid-receptor transcriptional module, and MR–GR stress-axis crosstalk through Fkbp5 appeared uncoupled from Nr3c2 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. This null should be interpreted in the context of heterogeneous mouse-brain subclasses with weak Nr3c2 mRNA engagement and the fact that many canonical markers are peripheral epithelial or adult hippocampal MR genes.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Nr3c2 was not interchangeable with its corticosteroid-receptor paralog Nr3c1 in this dataset: across 21 matched cell types, their full Wilcoxon-score signatures were near-zero correlated, and in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Nr3c1 showed sparse FDR-significant hits while Nr3c2 showed none. The divergence was most evident as an Nr3c1 Mapk8ip1 hit in the glutamatergic class and a stronger Nr3c1 Nr2f1 hit in the GABAergic class, consistent with uncoupled MR-GR stress-axis crosstalk involving Fkbp5, though guide efficacy may also contribute.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Akap6 loss did not recapitulate direct calcineurin-subunit perturbations in this basal Perturb-seq screen. Across overlapping neuronal classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1 showed stronger self-depletion and limited downstream FDR hits, whereas no Akap6 stratum reached conventional or near-significant transcriptome-wide hits and its knockdown was weak after FDR correction despite target transcript measurement. These data suggest AKAP6-calcineurin/NFAT/MEF2 coupling is more context-specific, consistent with stimulated, developmental, or injury settings rather than a constitutive brain transcriptome module.

Nek9 showed no detectable convergence with related perturbations or unbiased transcriptomic neighbors. Among the available NIMA kinase and spindle/NPC-adjacent comparators, Nek1, Kif11, and Ranbp2 were essentially uncorrelated with Nek9 across overlapping cell types, and the top all-target neighbors in the two main cell types examined, including Pvalb GABA and 155 MB Glut, had absolute whole-transcriptome correlations below 0.066. This suggests no coordinated transcript-level propagation within the mitotic spindle cascade in this dataset, though the test was low-sensitivity and key comparators such as Nek6, Nek7, Plk1, and Cdk1 were absent.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: H2-Eb1 did not show significant on-target RNA depletion in neuronal classes where a related immune-adjacent perturbation was technically detectable: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, Stat1 perturbation significantly reduced Stat1 RNA, whereas H2-Eb1 perturbation left H2-Eb1 at FDR=1.0; 155 MB Glut was also part of the IFN-gamma–STAT1–CIITA–MHC-II pathway context. This suggests H2-Eb1 was uncoupled from that module in these neurons, although STAT1 is an upstream transcriptional hub rather than a one-to-one complex comparator.

Hnf4a showed an almost entirely nonsignificant transcriptome-wide response across the profiled mouse brain classes, and family comparisons stayed similarly quiet: Hnf4g, Hnf1a, and Hnf1b had no FDR<0.1 genes, while matched Hnf4a-Hnf4g score vectors were essentially uncorrelated. In the 191 MB P MY GABA class, Hnf4a had a single significant row with Cacybp down, but still lacked target-transcript depletion and did not reveal a broader HNF module. Together, the HNF4A/HNF4G and HNF1A-HNF4A relationships were not detected in these brain classes, although the weak perturbation engagement means this supports context restriction rather than dispensability.

Ager was unengaged in this unstimulated neuronal Perturb-seq dataset, with no measurable Ager mRNA depletion or downstream FDR signal even in the highest-powered strata such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In contrast, App was strongly depleted in 20 of 22 neuronal classes, including TH and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, and its adjusted signal was limited to the targeted transcript. Thus, within the amyloid-beta/APP/RAGE disease axis, App and the Aβ receptor Ager were not transcriptomically interchangeable here, and APP perturbation does not directly test AGER-ligand binding.

Apbb2 showed near-zero transcriptomic similarity to App and other assayed APP-processing, tau, and Alzheimer-related perturbations, rather than phenocopying them. Across 217 same-cell comparisons with App, Adam10, Psen1, Sorl1, Gsk3b, Mapt, Fyn, and related targets, the maximum absolute correlation was only 0.098, while App knockdown in the same resource was a strong positive control, significant in 19 of 21 shared cell types. This suggests the weak Apbb2 signatures are not simply diluted App-loss states, although full reciprocal testing was limited because Apbb1, Apbb3, Aplp1, Aplp2, Bace1, Psen2, Ncstn, and Psenen were not perturbed.

Ccr2 showed perturbation signatures that were essentially orthogonal to those of the related chemokine receptors Ccr5, Cxcr2, and Cxcr4 across 20–22 shared neuronal classes per comparator, rather than forming a shared CCR/CXCR chemokine receptor family module. Across all 64 receptor-class correlations, values ranged from -0.0368 to 0.0492, so the data did not reveal a conserved neuronal GPCR-response axis that could clarify the weak Ccr2 perturbation. This remains exploratory because the signatures were weak and restricted, and the comparator receptors may also be weakly expressed or unengaged in these neuronal classes.

Pitx2 showed a shared FDR-null pattern with related developmental comparator perturbations: Pitx3, Foxc1, and Tfap2a each had zero FDR-significant genes in the profiled neurons. This suggests that a PITX/FOXC/AP-2 developmental transcription-factor module was either weakly engaged or biologically quiescent in these neuronal states, rather than Pitx2 being an isolated miss. However, target engagement for these comparator transcription factors was not independently verified, and several related genes, including Pitx1, Lef1, Lefty1, Lefty2, Cited2, and Shox2, were not included in the perturbation panel.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Dpp6 showed clear target engagement in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with the largest log-fold reduction in the midbrain/pons/medulla GABA class, but no validated downstream mRNA program emerged in these cells. The available Kv4 pore-forming comparator, Kcnd3, was covered in the same cell types yet had weak or non-FDR-significant knockdown and near-zero whole-transcriptome correlation with Dpp6, indicating no shared Dpp6/Kcnd3 transcriptomic module in this dataset, while leaving open that the non-convergence may reflect weak Kcnd3 engagement rather than biological uncoupling.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut
full_finding_text: Myt1l perturbation showed a recurrent but narrower downregulated module marked by Kifc2 and Slc22a17, overlapping the broader Rreb1-up response across several responsive classes. Kifc2 was significantly decreased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 155 MB Glut, while Slc22a17 was significantly decreased in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 001 L5-6 IT Glut. This pattern was strongest in midbrain glutamatergic and thalamic cells, but only four cell types met FDR significance for each gene, and the overlap was inferred from differential RNA abundance.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Pitpna showed a specific phenotype in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells that was not reproduced by nearby phosphoinositide-pathway perturbations. In this Pitpna-sensitive thalamic class, Pi4ka was significantly mRNA-depleted but had zero non-target FDR genes and therefore did not phenocopy the Pitpna transcriptome, which included synaptic, PLC-PKC, and calcium-signaling remodeling with genes such as Prkcg, Atp2a2, and Pip5kl1. Pitpnm3 could not be evaluated as a negative control because it lacked FDR-level self knockdown, so that comparison is uninterpretable.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Col4a1 perturbation showed no robust neuronal Col4a1 response, but its collagen-IV partner Col4a2 was weakly and nominally increased in four cell types—001 L5-6 IT Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA—within basement membrane or extracellular matrix organization context. This pattern was absent in most cell types, every Col4a2 signal had FDR=1.0, and Col4a1 itself was not significantly depleted; in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, nominal Col4a1 depletion and Col4a2 up-regulation both had FDR=1.0.

Cntnap1 showed a largely target-only transcriptional phenotype: across tested cell types, the only FDR<0.1 effects were direct decreases of Cntnap1 itself, with no significant downstream transcripts. This pattern converged with Cntn1, its CASPR cis partner, and with the paralog Cntnap2, both of which were also dominated by self-transcript depletion and almost no reproducible non-target differential expression. The strongest on-target depletion appeared in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In the paranodal/juxtaparanodal axonal-domain organization context, these data support target downregulation without compensatory neighbor mRNA changes, though the comparison is limited to DE summaries rather than protein localization or electrophysiology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Chd4 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells produced a dominant response in which Chd4 RNA decreased, while the NuRD ATPase paralog Chd3 increased significantly and Chd5 increased only nominally. This pattern is consistent with attempted CHD-family compensation within the NuRD pathway rather than a response limited to distal effector genes, but it does not demonstrate formation of a rescuing NuRD complex. The signal was strongest in this cell type, where other CHD-family ATPase transcripts were also induced.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Frrs1l shows a buffered RNA phenotype that is closely mirrored by its ER AMPAR-biogenesis partner Cpt1c: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, both perturbations produce strong self-depletion but no non-self FDR-significant genes. This convergence is consistent with the FRRS1L-CPT1C assembly module affecting receptor maturation or trafficking rather than inducing a canonical transcriptional program, although the comparison relies on gene-level Wilcoxon summaries and sparse nominal secondary hits were not shared.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Gria2 showed a markedly buffered transcriptional program relative to the NMDA-receptor subunits Grin1 and Grin2b, particularly in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut. In that matched cortical glutamatergic class, Gria2 had only itself as an FDR-significant RNA with 53 perturbed cells, whereas Grin2b yielded 47 FDR genes with 55 perturbed cells, indicating that the weak Gria2 program was not simply a failure of glutamate-receptor genes to score. This contrast is based on RNA output rather than receptor currents, and Grin1 had a somewhat larger median perturbed-cell count than Gria2.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Prpf6 perturbation reproducibly upregulated a nuclear RNA-processing/spliceosome-adjacent program, with recurrent increases in Srsf10, Sart1, Ssb, Cherp, Ddx18, Ddx41, Prpf38a, and Prpf39 across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 191 MB P MY GABA. The largest response occurred in midbrain glutamatergic neurons, followed by thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells, suggesting a compensatory RNA-processing program rather than uniform loss of splicing-factor transcripts. This steady-state expression dataset does not directly measure spliceosome assembly, PRPF6 protein, or intron retention.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Dlx6 showed no measurable on-target depletion across the assayed GABAergic classes, including 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 053 Sst Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA, and no detected Dlx6-driven changes in the GABA synthesis/parvalbumin-interneuron program marked by Gad1, Gad2, Pvalb, Sst, and Slc6a1. In the same dataset, direct Gad1 or Gad2 perturbations produced strong on-target depletion in multiple inhibitory classes, suggesting the Dlx6 null reflects target-specific non-engagement, low expression, or guide inefficiency rather than a universal assay failure; however, Gad1/Gad2 are pathway comparators rather than Dlx paralogs, and matched guide design and expression levels were not available.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gatad2b loss in glutamatergic neurons most consistently pointed to Rasgrp2 upregulation as a candidate downstream output. The clearest FDR-significant non-target signal appeared in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, while additional Gatad2b signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 155 MB Glut showed mostly nominal Rasgrp2 increases. Notably, Chd4 perturbation also produced FDR-significant Rasgrp2 upregulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, suggesting a small shared NuRD-linked neuronal response, though most Gatad2b recurrences remained sub-FDR.

Ngfr showed no multiple-testing-significant transcriptomic response in any assayed cell class, and its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Rtn4r, Lingo1, Sort1, Rac1, or Ntrk2 perturbations. Thus, canonical p75NTR co-receptor pathways were not detected in this RNA assay, including RTN4R–LINGO1–RHOA/myelin-inhibitor signaling and Sortilin/pro-neurotrophin death signaling. In 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 308 CB GABA, the weakest nominal Ngfr signals still lacked pathway coupling; in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Ngfr was null while Sort1 was depleted when directly perturbed. This steady-state RNA readout does not assess acute RHOA activity, apoptosis, neurite collapse, or ligand-evoked p75NTR signaling.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Nrg3 perturbation showed a ligand–receptor split relative to Erbb4 rather than a same-cell-type phenocopy. Nrg3 was strongly depleted on target in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, while several inhibitory or cerebellar populations showed little measured Nrg3 repression despite moderate cell counts. In contrast, Erbb4 perturbation strongly reduced Erbb4 in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where Nrg3 itself was weak, consistent with distinct excitatory-to-GABAergic NRG3–ERBB4 contexts; receptor protein activity and synaptic connectivity were not measured.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Nkx2-5 in mouse brain appeared uncoupled from its canonical cardiogenesis cofactor network. Across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Gata4, Tbx5, Nkx2-1, and Nkx6-2 showed no FDR-significant rows and genome-wide signatures near-orthogonal to Nkx2-5. Mef2c was successfully perturbed and active, with cortical and Pvalb responses including strong target depletion and Chgb induction, but its transcriptomic effects were uncorrelated with Nkx2-5. This comparison is limited to brain transcriptomic effects, and other cardiac partners such as Tbx20 and Hand2 were not tested.

Gstm5 was transcriptionally uncoupled from its known mouse sperm partners Pfkm and Hk1 in neuronal perturbation signatures, with little to no convergence across neuronal cell groups. This pattern is consistent with the GSTM5–PFKM–HK1 relationship reflecting a specialized sperm fibrous-sheath glycolytic complex rather than a reusable neuronal transcriptomic module. A key caveat is that this comparison was based on whole-transcriptome score correlations from relatively weak perturbation profiles, not direct measurements of protein-complex formation or glycolytic activity.

Naa10 showed a null transcriptional response in this Perturb-seq dataset: genome-wide differential-expression testing found no statistically resolved downstream Naa10 effect in any cell type, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In contrast, the related perturbations Naa15 and Naa20 produced hundreds to thousands of significant genes in the same experiment, and their transcriptome-wide score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Naa10 rather than resembling or opposing it. This divergence from the expected NAA10–NAA15 NatA coupling likely reflects weak Naa10 engagement, and Naa20 is only a related family comparator, not a NatA core subunit.

Kdm4b did not share a clear transcriptomic module with the closest assayed KDM4-family comparator, Kdm4c: across 21 shared cell types, their full-score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, centered near zero, and neither showed FDR-supported signatures. This contrasts with Reactome grouping KDM4B and KDM4C in the same methylated-H3, including H3K9me2/H3K9me3, demethylation reactions, suggesting that shared substrate annotation did not translate into similar measured perturbation signatures in this mouse-brain dataset. Because both signals were weak and Kdm4c had fewer perturbed cells, the comparison is best used for module triage rather than enzyme-specific mechanistic ranking.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Drd2 perturbation in the broad 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA population was essentially flat and uncoupled: Drd2 itself was not detectably depleted, and no corrected downstream remodeling was seen in the dopamine receptor Gi/o-cAMP or D2/A2A striatal medium spiny neuron module, including Adcy5, Adora2a, and Ppp1r1b. This likely reflects weak expression or dilution within a broad LGE/LSX class rather than a definitive negative result for purified D2 medium spiny neurons, so the absence of a canonical D2 signal should be interpreted cautiously.

Chchd10 showed efficient self-transcript depletion yet no genome-wide significant non-target transcriptional response, and its paralog Chchd2 displayed the same buffered pattern: in several classes Chchd2 self-knockdown was even stronger than Chchd10, but it likewise yielded zero non-target FDR hits. This concordance in the mitochondrial intermembrane-space CHCHD10-CHCHD2/cristae module argues against interpreting the silent Chchd10 profile simply as target failure, while remaining consistent with redundancy, incomplete protein depletion, or stress-dependent effects. The single-cell assay measures mRNA responses, not complex abundance, respiration, or stress-challenge phenotypes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Adam22 showed weaker transcriptional consequences than other synaptic perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons: despite strong Adam22 knockdown, it remained the only FDR-significant transcript, with no non-target FDR genes and no detectable compensation among AMPA/NMDA/Kv-channel synaptic organization genes such as Gria1-4, Grin1, Cacng2, Kcna1/2, Camk2a, or Kcnb1. In the same cell classes, however, Grin1 produced 88 non-target FDR genes in thalamic neurons, while Kcnb1 and Camk2a produced 5 and 3 in L4/5 IT cortex, arguing against a global inability to report synaptic-gene responses; comparators differed in cell counts, on-target strength, and are not all direct ADAM22-complex members.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Atp9a was uncoupled from available endosomal-neighbor perturbations in thalamic glutamatergic cells. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Atp9a showed its strongest self-depletion, it had only its own transcript significant, while Rab7 produced 501 FDR<0.05 genes and Vps35 produced 17, with genome-wide score correlations to Atp9a near zero. A similarly strong Atp9a contrast in 155 MB Glut also remained self-only even though Rab7 elicited a multi-gene response there. This divergence is limited by the lack of direct comparators from the MON2-DOP1B-ATP9A/SNX3-Wls axis.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Otx2 repression was silent in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 053 Sst Gaba: neither class showed FDR-supported differential expression, and the target transcript did not show a detectable rank shift, with no downstream response involving genes such as Smap1 or Uchl1. This refines adult OTX2 biology toward a source-cell explanation, in which PV/GABA phenotypes depend on choroid-plexus OTX2 homeoprotein transfer rather than strong local interneuron Otx2 transcription. Caveats are that only bulk-like class-level contrasts were available, choroid plexus was not perturbed, and Otx2 mRNA was low, especially in Sst GABA.

Manf showed a transcriptomic pattern that Atf6 and Nfe2l2 did not phenocopy in this dataset: across the assayed cell types, Atf6 and Nfe2l2 perturbations produced zero FDR-significant genes, despite MANF’s curated connection to ATF6/ER-stress regulation. This negative result does not support a simple ordering in which Manf loss is interchangeable with perturbing those stress-pathway genes, but the inference is limited because neither comparator showed FDR-significant self knockdown, indicating weak perturbation engagement rather than strong mechanistic separation.

Kif2a perturbation did not produce a recurrent cytoskeletal or microtubule transcriptional module in this dataset. Across tested subclasses, there were no FDR-significant downstream genes, and the 65 nominal hits at p<0.001 were all singleton cell-type events; even at p<0.005, only Spock2, Smarcc2, and Snx27 recurred. This pattern is consistent with Kinesin-13 microtubule depolymerization being buffered at the mRNA level here, although the recurrence check was not a formal pathway-enrichment test and cannot exclude local cytoskeletal remodeling.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Atl1 knockdown showed a possible, weak compensation signal limited to 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons, where the atlastin paralog Atl3 was nominally increased. This fits the tubular ER network shaping and ER membrane fusion context, in which ATL3 is the closest assayed paralog, but the effect was modest: Atl3 was only an uncorrected positive hit, neither Atl3 nor the Atl1 self-transcript passed FDR in that cell type, and no shared downstream RNA program or recurrent signal was observed across other cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
