full_finding_text: Cd247 showed no multiple-testing-supported differentially expressed genes in the assayed neuronal groups, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, whereas neuronal calcium and synaptic perturbation controls in the same analysis were clearly detected. In particular, Calm1 produced 27 FDR<0.05 rows, and Cacnb4 showed self-depletion and downstream responses in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic populations, with Rasgrp2 included in this internal contrast. This pattern suggests the Cd247 null was gene-module specific rather than a global failure to detect neuronal signaling perturbations, while noting that Calm1 and Cacnb4 are not CD3 complex members and are used only as screen-performance comparators.

Ncam1 knockdown showed no detectable mRNA-level compensatory upregulation of the related adhesion gene Ncam2 or the polysialyltransferases St8sia2 and St8sia4: all three were unchanged at FDR 1.0 in every measured Ncam1 cell-type contrast. This suggests buffered transcriptional output within the Ncam1 neural cell adhesion and neuron-projection development context, but the comparison is limited because Ncam2, St8sia2, and St8sia4 were not themselves perturbed, and the assay would not capture compensation through altered NCAM protein glycosylation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Ctnnbl1 perturbation showed a sparse, mostly exploratory recurrent up-response centered on Arhgef1. Arhgef1 was the strongest and only FDR-significant signal in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and it was also nominally up in 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where no FDR-significant downstream Ctnnbl1 target was detected. This pattern nominates a modest RhoA guanine-nucleotide exchange signaling link, but two of the three Arhgef1-positive contexts were only nominal, and there is no direct validation connecting CTNNBL1 to RhoA regulation.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Bbx showed no FDR-supported perturbation program across the assayed forebrain glutamatergic neuronal classes, including 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut. Consistent with this, Nfix perturbation did not measurably de-repress Bbx, suggesting the reported developmental NFIX-Bbx forebrain regulation may be progenitor-biased or not engaged by the relatively weak perturbations in these named neuronal classes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cacna1e did not phenocopy its CDKL5 pathway neighbor in RNA space: across 22 shared cell types, Cacna1e and Cdkl5 perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Cdkl5 was strongly self-depleted, whereas the paired Cacna1e perturbation showed a wrong-way self logFC, even as related perturbations such as Cacna1g, Cacna2d1, and Cacnb4 self-depleted. This suggests the CDKL5–Cav2.3 phosphorylation axis may be invisible to steady-state transcriptomic readouts, since the dataset lacks phosphoprotein and current measurements.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Hnrnpa2b1 perturbation was accompanied by recurrent Hnrnpa1 induction in the two main responsive glutamatergic classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Hnrnpa1 increased while Hnrnpa2b1 was reduced. This was the clearest repeated transcript-level response, within a broader but weakly similar hnRNP/RNA-processing pattern involving genes such as Rbm25, Tcerg1, Hnrnpu, Srsf1, and Snrnp70. In 155 MB Glut, the target-transcript depletion was clearest, but co-regulation of core m6A/DGCR8 pathway transcripts was not FDR-supported, and protein induction or functional rescue was not measured.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Dyrk1a perturbation showed a recurrent but only nominal increase of Dcaf7 in caudal glutamatergic populations, specifically 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut. This was the clearest mechanistically suggestive pattern in an otherwise FDR-negative screen and is consistent with a DCAF7-DYRK1A scaffold context, but it remains exploratory because all Dcaf7 adjusted p values were 1.0. In 155 MB Glut, Dyrk1a itself also showed a nominal increase, and Dcaf7 was not perturbed directly for reciprocal testing.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Gprasp2 loss did not phenocopy Vps35 or Rab7 perturbations in the target-engaged glutamatergic classes 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Gprasp2 showed target depletion but much weaker downstream transcriptional signal than Vps35 or Rab7, with only 1 overlapping top-100 gene with Vps35 and 2 with Rab7, and mGluR/synaptic markers remained FDR-negative. In 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Gprasp2 and Vps35 also had disjoint leading signatures. This suggests Gprasp2 reduction is divergent from retromer and late-endosome trafficking loss, although Gprasp2 signatures were weak and the closest paralog comparators, Gprasp1 and Beclin2, were not in the library.

Hcn1 did not phenocopy Hcn2 in this transcriptomic readout, despite both being paralogous HCN-channel pore-forming subunits. Hcn2 showed FDR-supported self-knockdown in 9 of 22 cell types, whereas Hcn1 showed none, and their genome-wide perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated, with no reciprocal paralog transcript induction. In 155 MB Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Hcn1 was the top absolute feature but produced no FDR-significant downstream genes; in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Ctnnd2 was the only FDR-supported non-Hcn1 hit. This contrast is tempered by weaker Hcn1 target engagement and by the fact that the comparison is based on RNA signatures rather than Ih current.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Nrg1 perturbation showed no detectable self-transcript depletion in the inhibitory classes 052 Pvalb Gaba and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, whereas the comparator Erbb4 perturbation produced significant self-transcript depletion in those same two classes. In this dataset, the NRG1/ERBB receptor tyrosine kinase signaling signal was therefore more detectable on the receptor limb than the ligand limb, with little additional FDR-significant RNA output beyond Erbb4 self-depletion. This interpretation is limited by the use of broad taxonomy labels rather than purified PV subtypes.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Il6ra showed no detectable transcript depletion or induction across 22 Il6ra-tested glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, with no receptor-family convergence in the IL-6 receptor/IL6ST–JAK-STAT-MAPK signaling context. In the same differential-expression pipeline, intracellular pathway neighbors did show on-target depletion in selected classes: Mapk1 in 155 MB Glut, and Stat1 in 191 MB P MY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Il6ra remained unchanged in those same classes. This argues that the Il6ra null was target-specific rather than a universal DE failure, although Stat1 and Mapk1 differ from Il6ra in basal expression, guide performance, and intracellular versus receptor biology.

Cnnm2 perturbation did not produce a coherent RNA-level compensation program within the magnesium ion transport and homeostasis pathway: measured transcripts for Trpm7, Trpm6, Nipa1, Nipa2, Magt1, Slc41a1/2/3, Mmgt1/2, Mrs2, and Cnnm paralogs Cnnm1/3/4 showed no consistent FDR-supported induction or repression. This suggests that buffering of Cnnm2 loss is unlikely to occur through simple transcriptional replacement by another known magnesium transporter, although transport activity, membrane localization, magnesium concentration, or unmeasured regulators could still compensate.

Cnnm2 showed an uncoupled transcriptional profile in this Perturb-seq dataset: its full-transcriptome score vectors correlated only weakly with available Trpm7, Nipa1, Mt3, and Slc12a2 perturbations, and a search across all targets found no strong positive or inverse neighbor, with even the strongest all-target match remaining weak. Thus, despite reported CNNM–TRPM7 coupling at the protein and ion-transport level, the RNA readout did not support assigning Cnnm2 to a generic TRPM7-like divalent-cation program. This interpretation is limited because most comparator perturbations were themselves weak, and key CNNM2 complex partners or paralogs such as Ptp4a1, Ptp4a2, Ptp4a3, and other Cnnm genes were not perturbed.

Hnrnpu-perturbed cells showed higher, not lower, measured Hnrnpu RNA across all tested cell types relative to matched non-targeting controls, with a median logFC of 1.33 and significant increases in 18 of 22 cell types. This makes Hnrnpu self-expression a key engagement caveat in this nominal loss-of-function Perturb-seq setting, arguing against interpreting the transcriptional signatures as simple Hnrnpu mRNA depletion. Because the assay measures RNA rather than protein abundance or on-target indel outcomes, the increase could reflect stable mutant transcripts, transcriptional feedback, or edited-cell state changes.

Hspa8 perturbation did not produce an FDR-significant transcriptional induction of canonical chaperone-mediated autophagy or clathrin-uncoating components: Lamp2, Cltc, Picalm, and Dnajc6 showed no significant expression change in any measured cell type. Thus, the acute RNA response appears dominated by compensatory chaperones rather than a clear transcriptional module for these pathways. This transcript-level negative result does not exclude altered LAMP2A-specific CMA flux or clathrin-uncoating activity, which may be detectable only at the activity or protein level.

Nr5a2 did not show convergent transcriptomic effects with its paralog Nr5a1/SF-1 in the mouse brain screen. Across matched cell types, Nr5a1 signatures were almost uncorrelated with Nr5a2, with only one Nr5a1 FDR hit, and preselected paralog, Wnt-neighbor, RXR, and PPAR nuclear-receptor signatures likewise failed to converge with Nr5a2. Because Nr5a2 target engagement was weak, this remains exploratory, but it cautions against assuming that dual LRH-1/SF-1 agonist activity reflects a shared neuronal NR5A module; the contrast does not directly measure ligand pharmacology or SF-1 protein activity.

Abhd12 could not be evaluated against its expected lyso-PS/endocannabinoid neighborhood in this screen because the perturbation library lacked most cognate comparators. Although external work places ABHD12 near ABHD16A and serine-hydrolase genes including ABHD6, MGLL, FAAH, NAPEPLD, DAGLA, and DAGLB, these targets were not present here, and the only other Abhd-family perturbation, Abhd2, did not achieve FDR-level self knockdown. As a result, the absence of convergence is not interpretable as ABHD-family divergence, but mainly reflects sparse library coverage and weak comparator engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gnao1 knockdown did not phenocopy the related Gi/o signaling perturbations Gnb1 or Grm7 in the cell types where repression was effective, notably 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. Whole-transcriptome correlations with Gnao1 were near zero even though Gnb1 was efficiently repressed in the same two classes and Grm7 was efficiently repressed in thalamic glutamatergic cells. In 155 MB Glut, Gnao1 showed strong cis knockdown but no FDR-significant trans program and no Rho marker response. This contrast is transcriptomic only, Grm7 engagement was decisive mainly in the thalamic class, and GNB/Gα stoichiometry could be buffered post-transcriptionally.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Lgi1 showed a muted transcriptomic response across neuronal classes despite broad representation: no Lgi1 signature contained an FDR-significant DE gene, including in 155 MB Glut, and Adam22 could be significantly depleted yet remained nearly transcriptomically silent, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In contrast, the comparator Grin1 produced many significant responses across 14 cell types, with especially strong effects in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, separating buffered LGI1–ADAM22 synaptic adhesion/AMPA-Kv1 scaffold perturbation from core NMDAR subunit loss. This contrast is tempered by Grin1 being a downstream synaptic neighbor rather than a direct LGI1 receptor, and by somewhat larger cell counts and stronger target depletion for Grin1.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Calm1 showed a gene-specific downstream expansion in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class that was not reproduced by Calm3, even though Calm3 was efficiently depleted in that same responsive class and in multiple other cell types. The dominant Calm1 response was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 155 MB Glut showed strong on-target Calm1 depletion but no FDR-supported non-Calm1 program. Across the calc... pathway context, Calm1 transcript decreased whereas most canonical partner mRNAs remained unchanged. Calm2 was only weakly engaged in this screen, so the clearest paralog contrast is Calm1 versus Calm3.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Kansl1 did not phenocopy Ogt, the only other assayed NSL-complex gene, in neuronal Perturb-seq. In the overlapping responsive classes 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, whole-transcriptome similarity between Kansl1 and Ogt was near zero to weakly positive, even though Ogt often produced more significant genes. This weak cross-perturbation similarity within KAT8/NSL chromatin regulation suggests Ogt is not a reliable transcriptional proxy for Kansl1 here, with the caveat that other NSL members were not assayed and Ogt perturbation may not isolate the NSL-bound OGT pool.

Camsap1 targeting did not induce detectable transcript-level compensation by its paralogs Camsap2 or Camsap3: across all assayed Camsap1 signatures, both paralog mRNAs remained unchanged, with FDR=1.0 throughout. In this dataset, the relevant context is CAMSAP-family non-centrosomal microtubule minus-end organization, but there was no FDR-level Camsap1 transcriptomic output indicating a paralog switch in any assayed neuronal class. A key caveat is that Camsap2 and Camsap3 were not themselves perturbed, so only their transcript response to Camsap1 targeting could be evaluated.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Hnf1a perturbation was transcriptionally null in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class, despite this cell type clearly supporting strong transcription-factor responses in the same dataset. In that class, Prox1 and Tcf7l2 produced 50 and 106 FDR-significant genes, whereas the larger Hnf1a and Hnf1b contrasts had a minimum FDR of 1.0, indicating no genome-wide significant response. This supports a target-specific HNF1-family null rather than a failure of the cell type or differential-expression workflow, although it does not imply mechanistic proximity between Hnf1a and Prox1 or Tcf7l2.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Gigyf2-responsive glutamatergic populations showed clear divergence from Gigyf1 perturbation: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Gigyf1 knockdown, despite 244 perturbed cells per class and measurable but modest Gigyf1 mRNA reduction, yielded zero FDR<=0.05 downstream genes and near-zero full-score correlation to the Gigyf2 signatures. The strongest Gigyf2 effects occurred in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, with recurrent RNA-processing programs, a downregulated synaptic-gene tail in midbrain cells, and no induction of direct 4EHP-GIGYF2/ribosome-surveillance complex transcripts such as Eif4e2, Zfp598, Ddx6, or Tnrc6a; however, modest on-target depletion means post-transcriptional paralog differences remain inferential.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Fgfr1 perturbation in 155 MB Glut cells did not resemble a canonical MEK/ERK-loss transcriptional phenotype. Although Map2k1 and Mapk1 perturbations were engaged in the same cell class, their genome-wide Wilcoxon z-score signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Fgfr1 (r=0.023 for Map2k1 and r=-0.034 for Mapk1). In this dataset, 155 MB Glut was also the only class showing FDR-significant Fgfr1 self-depletion, and the response remained dominated by the Fgfr1 transcript, suggesting any FGFR1 signaling here may be post-transcriptional, ligand-dependent, or confined to a subset within the broad cluster.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Cyfip1 showed little acute transcriptional response in this scRNA assay, and the paralog comparator Cyfip2 behaved similarly despite cleaner knockdown: Cyfip2 was significantly self-depleted in six cell types, including 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, yet no significant non-self genes were detected. This pattern is consistent with CYFIP-family perturbations in the RAC1-WAVE actin-remodeling context being largely mRNA-silent or buffered, with the caveat that Cyfip2 is an alternative WAVE-complex subunit rather than a perfect Cyfip1 substitute and the assay captures RNA only.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gigyf1 showed its clearest transcript depletion in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, yet neither cell type had any downstream gene at FDR<0.05, so the response was target-dominated rather than pathway-dominated. This buffered pattern was also seen in another cell type with nominal on-target depletion, while related perturbations in the same translation-initiation/4EHP-GIGYF repression context, including Gigyf2, Eif4e, and Cnot1, produced FDR-positive signatures. The interpretation is limited because no protein, ribosome profiling, cap-binding, or IGF1R phosphorylation measurements were available.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Gigyf1 showed minimal RNA-level activity in this assay and did not track with related translation-initiation perturbations. Across tested cell types, Gigyf1 produced only one FDR-significant response, whereas Gigyf2 and Eif4e produced many more, and Gigyf1 score correlations with Gigyf2 or Eif4e were near zero. This contrast was clear in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where Gigyf1 had no downstream FDR-positive signature despite nominal on-target loss, while Gigyf2, Eif4e, and sometimes Cnot1 did. Interpretation is tempered because Eif4e, not Eif4e2, was assayed, and guide count or depletion differences may contribute.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Grik3 perturbation showed its strongest non-target response in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons, where the L5 ET Grik3-associated Gdpd5/Kcng3 response featured increased Gdpd5 and near-threshold Kcng3, with nominal decreases in Gpm6b and Htr1b, yet no detectable loss of Grik3 mRNA. This pattern was sparse overall and appears uncoupled from target-transcript depletion; only Gdpd5 met FDR<0.05, Kcng3 was FDR<0.10, so the signal may reflect productive protein-disrupting edits, DNA-damage or guide effects, or an indirect state shift rather than graded Grik3 RNA knockdown.

Cck perturbation was not phenocopied by knockdown of the peptide-processing genes Cpe or Pcsk2: despite stronger on-target knockdown for Cpe and Pcsk2 than for Cck itself, Cck transcript abundance was not detectably reduced and remained non-significant under both perturbations, and their genome-wide signatures were nearly uncorrelated with engaged Cck signatures. This is consistent with proCCK neuropeptide processing acting downstream of precursor transcription, so Cck mRNA is a poor proxy for mature active CCK in these enzyme perturbations; notably, mature CCK peptide forms were not measured, and Pcsk2 was assayed in fewer, often lower-cell-count strata than Cpe.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Cck perturbation was transcriptionally decoupled from Cckar and Cckbr perturbations in the engaged Cck cell types, notably 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In these cells, Cck showed strong self-depletion or the strongest on-target response, but receptor perturbations were weak, showed near-zero similarity to the Cck signatures, and did not reveal a strong Cck-like neighbor across the genome. A nominal Cck–Cckar anticorrelation in 308 CB GABA was not retained because neither perturbation showed its own transcript engagement there, so technical non-engagement remains a major alternative to receptor-pathway biology.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Il1rap did not robustly phenocopy the IL1RAP-family synaptic paralogs Il1rapl1 or Il1rapl2 in this Perturb-seq dataset. Across most shared cell classes, the perturbation states were nearly orthogonal, with only weak positive similarity in 308 CB GABA, where Pearson correlations to Il1rapl1 and Il1rapl2 were 0.154 and 0.161. Thus, the expected PTPdelta/IL1RAP-family trans-synaptic adhesion relationship did not translate into a clear shared mRNA module, and this interpretation is tempered because the paralog perturbations themselves were weak and two Il1rapl1 hits were isolated single-gene results rather than a module.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Hecw2 showed a weak and divergent perturbation profile rather than a generic HECT/E3-ligase effect: in overlapping cell classes including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Hecw2 produced no FDR-significant downstream response even where its transcript decrease was among the best nominally, while Huwe1 yielded robust FDR-controlled signatures, sometimes with fewer targeted cells. Hecw2 full-score signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Huwe1, Hectd4, and Ube3a, suggesting the weak Hecw2 response was not simply a detection limit of the pipeline or of ubiquitin-proteasome/E3-ligase perturbations, although these comparators are related by annotation rather than being HECW2 complex members or paralogs.

Calm2 knockdown did not trigger transcriptional compensation by its coding paralogs Calm1 or Calm3: across all measured contrasts, including the 155 MB Glut context where Calm2 itself showed significant on-target depletion, Calm1 and Calm3 remained unchanged at the mRNA level, with no transcriptome-wide secondary gene effects detected. This suggests that within the Calm1/Calm2/Calm3 calmodulin core, downstream RNA responses were buffered rather than replaced by paralog induction, although only mRNA was assayed, so compensation through protein stability, existing calmodulin pools, or translation cannot be excluded.

H4c11 showed a weak transcriptomic perturbation, and the only other clustered core-histone perturbation in the screen, H2ac8, was similarly weak and did not phenocopy H4c11. Across subclasses, H2ac8 had no significant differential-expression rows, its own transcript showed no resolved RNA-level engagement, and H4c11–H2ac8 score correlations were essentially zero. In this experimental context, the canonical histone/nucleosome assembly pathway therefore did not reveal a shared single-locus core-histone loss module, though this contrast is between two weak signatures and should not be taken as a biochemical difference between H4 and H2A proteins.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Fxr1 perturbation did not produce detectable Gria2 mRNA induction, including in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut where the published FXR1–GluA2 axis was specifically checked; Gria2 was unchanged and no FDR-controlled transcriptome-wide hit was seen in any assayed cell type. This includes a cortical glutamatergic class, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where Cyfip2 showed on-target signal but Fxr1 and Gria2 mRNA were not significant. These results suggest that the GluA2 synaptic translation effect reported after forebrain Fxr1 deletion may not be visible in single-cell mRNA and could reflect translational rather than transcriptional regulation.

Fxr1 did not phenocopy the assayed FMRP-family/CYFIP neighborhood in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout. Across the Fxr1-tested cell types, Fxr1 signatures were weakly correlated with Fmr1, Cyfip1, and Cyfip2, and did not align closely with translation, MAPK, mTOR, Pak2, or App perturbations. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Cyfip2 showed stronger on-target depletion, whereas Fmr1 and Cyfip1 were not significant; in 308 CB GABA, Fxr1 had only nominal signal without FDR support. Because Fxr1 target depletion was weak and Fxr2 was unavailable, the lack of convergence may reflect both perturbation strength and biology.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Eif4a2 knockdown in 052 Pvalb Gaba neurons showed strong target engagement, and the main exploratory non-target signal was a nominal increase in Eif4g2, an eIF4F/cap-dependent translation initiation network partner and the top STRING functional associate of Eif4a2. However, this Eif4g2 rise did not survive FDR correction and was prominent only in Pvalb cells; no non-target transcript passed genome-wide correction, so the pattern is best treated as a testable, cell-type-specific compensatory hypothesis rather than an established feedback loop.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Atp1a1 knockdown produced a very small FDR-controlled transcriptional response overall, but in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut it was associated with a modest, FDR-significant increase in Atp1a3 while Atp1a2 remained unchanged. This suggests a narrowly restricted, RNA-level candidate compensation within ATP1A-mediated Na+/K+ ion transport, limited to this upper-layer cortical glutamatergic class rather than broadly across neuronal classes. The observation is confined to transcript levels and has not been shown to restore pump protein abundance or ionic flux.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Pi4kb showed a quiet transcriptional phenotype, and this was not obviously just due to weak Pi4kb self-depletion: the paralog Pi4ka had clear FDR-level depletion of its own transcript in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, yet across 22 Pi4ka-overlap cell types there were only four FDR-significant rows. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the only FDR-significant Pi4kb downstream gene was Tmem50b, with near-threshold Rnf145. Together this suggests buffered PI4P-network responses with little steady-state mRNA output, although Pi4ka and Pi4kb occupy overlapping but nonidentical PI4P pools.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Gucy2c was quiet in this screen, with no comparable program detected for the related perturbations Gucy2e and Npr2, whereas the comparator Pde10a produced a detectable GABA-class response. In 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, Pde10a showed corrected self-downregulation with Scg2 upregulation, and across 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 308 CB GABA the comparator signal also included Ubac2. This cross-perturbation contrast suggests the assay could detect related second-messenger biology when consequential, but it does not establish that PDE10A and GUCY2C act in one linear pathway in these cells.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Max perturbation produced a small, cell-type-specific compensatory signal within the MAX/MYC/MNT/MGA transcription-factor network: Mga transcripts increased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, while Mnt increased in 191 MB P MY GABA. This pattern is compatible with a homeostatic attempt to rebalance MAX-network repressors, but the effect was limited, with only two Max-perturbed classes significantly inducing Mga and one inducing Mnt, and no protein or chromatin measurements testing whether added MGA or MNT compensated for edited MAX.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Lrig2 showed weak, nonconvergent transcriptomic signatures across 308 CB GABA, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut. Correlations to other perturbations were very small, including RTK/RAS/PI3K/mTOR neighbors such as Hras, Akt3, Tsc2, Fgfr2, Axl, and Met, with no high-correlation positive or negative neighbor and even the top related signal remaining small. Thus, Lrig2 did not phenocopy a single canonical receptor or effector from transcriptomics alone. Lrig1 and Lrig3 were not perturbed, so paralog buffering could not be tested.

Fbxo38 loss did not transcriptionally phenocopy the expected SCF/KLF7 coactivation axis in this Perturb-seq dataset. Across all 22 profiled glutamatergic and GABAergic classes, Fbxo38 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Klf7, Fbxw7, and Fbxo11 perturbation vectors, and the putative readouts Klf7 and Cdkn1a were not adjusted-significant after Fbxo38 perturbation. Because Klf7, Fbxw7, and Fbxo11 guide effects were themselves transcriptionally weak, these data argue against detectable convergence in this assay rather than excluding a biochemical interaction.

Npas3 did not show the expected convergence with its ARNT-family partners: Arnt and Arnt2 perturbations were also transcriptionally flat, with zero FDR-significant genes, and their score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Npas3, with maximum absolute Pearson correlations of 0.082 and 0.056. In the assayed states, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, this suggests no coherent ARNT-dependent NPAS3 module was exposed, although the weak phenotypes of Arnt and Arnt2 leave open redundancy, poor perturbation, or low expression as alternative explanations.

Pcca did not show convergence with the assayed PCCA-adjacent comparators in this dataset: across matched cell types, Mmaa, Hlcs, and Acox1 had only weak correlations with Pcca signatures, and Pccb, the obligate PCC beta subunit, was not screened. Because these available comparator perturbations also showed weak target-transcript engagement and were mostly negative or weak overall, the data do not provide a robust transcriptional model of PCC loss, and no assayed neighbor can serve as a surrogate for the missing Pcca–Pccb complex comparison.

Kat6b showed a distinct, largely quiet perturbation profile that did not converge with related chromatin coactivator perturbations in the MOZ/MORF histone acetyltransferase and transcription coactivation context. Kat6a and Ep300 were similarly FDR-quiet, while Trrap was much stronger, with many adjusted hits in 12 of 22 overlapping classes, yet remained nearly uncorrelated with Kat6b. This pattern was evident even in classes such as 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Trrap responses were large but Kat6b lacked FDR-significant effects. Interpretation is limited because only a few chromatin neighbors were assayed, BRPF1/2/3, ING5, and MEAF6 were not detected, and Trrap target mRNA did not show a clean knockdown pattern.

Nr2f6 did not act as an interchangeable NR2F paralog with Nr2f1 or Nr2f2 in these mouse-brain Perturb-seq signatures. Across shared cell classes, whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon-score correlations between Nr2f6 and the Nr2f1/Nr2f2 perturbations were approximately zero, and the signatures did not converge in score space, arguing against pooling these nuclear-receptor perturbations or substituting Nr2f1/Nr2f2 effects for Nr2f6. However, all three paralog perturbations showed weak on-target transcript suppression, so the near-zero correlations are better taken as a warning against interchangeability than as proof of distinct mechanisms.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Paqr8 shows a distinct steady-state transcriptomic effect rather than phenocopying related nonclassical progesterone-pathway receptors. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the only cell type with significant Paqr8 target-transcript reduction, Paqr7 and Pgrmc1 were also transcriptionally engaged, yet their genome-wide correlations with Paqr8 were nearly zero (r=0.009 and r=0.041, respectively). Across overlapping cell types, correlations between Paqr8 and Paqr7, Pgrmc1, Adipor2, Pgr, and Gper1 remained close to zero, supporting non-interchangeable, buffered cell-autonomous roles and arguing against a shared basal transcriptional module, while not excluding convergent ligand-evoked or phosphoproteomic signaling.

Nr2c1 perturbation did not transcriptionally mobilize the canonical TR2 PML/SUMO/corepressor axis in the neuronal Perturb-seq readout. Across Nr2c1 contrasts, curated partners and effectors including Pias1, Nr2c2, Sumo1, Ncor1, Nrip1, Pml, Hdac3, Hdac4, Kat2b, Med1, Rarb, and Esr1 showed no FDR-level response, indicating no detectable mRNA feedback in this module. This negative result is limited to transcript abundance, since PIAS1, SUMO, PML, HDAC, and NRIP1 regulation can occur through localization, coregulator exchange, or protein modification rather than steady-state RNA changes.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Cux2 showed weak perturbation effects in upper cortical glutamatergic classes, including 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut: despite nominal Cux2 self-repression, there were no corrected downstream DE genes in key classes, and whole-transcriptome Cux2 signatures had no strong positive or negative neighbor. In the same assay, Mef2c and Tbr1 produced corrected transcriptomic responses in overlapping cortical classes, whereas Cux1 and Satb2 were also weak, with especially limited Cux1 target-transcript engagement, arguing that these cortical identity factors were not interchangeable under these conditions.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Prep in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a self-limited response: Prep knockdown reduced its own transcript, but there was little broader differential expression at FDR. Its paralog Prepl, assessed in the same thalamic class, likewise mainly reduced its own transcript, yet the genome-wide score vectors for Prep and Prepl were essentially uncorrelated across 17,259 genes (r = 0.039), indicating that a paralogous serine-hydrolase label did not translate into interchangeable transcriptional consequences. This comparison is transcriptomic and limited to Prepl because several closer peptidase neighbors were not perturbation targets.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Phox2a showed weak, largely orthogonal Perturb-seq signatures in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, where the only near-threshold effect was an isolated decrease in Itfg1 and it did not converge with Phox2b, Rnf220, Lmx1b, or Ret. Across 22 shared classes, Phox2a–Phox2b score correlations were close to zero, Phox2b itself had no significant effects, and the assayed Rnf220 cofactor did not phenocopy Phox2a; the strongest CNU-MGE neighbor was only r = 0.154. This argues against a latent Phox2 developmental module in the assayed classes, though all signatures were weak, Zc4h2 was not assayed, and CNU-MGE is an indirect context for Phox2 biology.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Sms showed a sparse differential-expression profile in this screen. The only non-Sms FDR hit was Elfn2 up-regulation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA cells, but this contrast did not show detectable Sms knockdown, so the strongest apparent downstream signal is biologically uncoupled from target engagement. As a result, Elfn2 should not be treated as a confident SMS biomarker from this dataset alone, and guide-level off-target testing was not possible from the available summary.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Pacs2 showed weaker detectability than related ER-mitochondria and fission-neighborhood perturbations: across 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, no Pacs2 perturbation reached an FDR-significant gene-level effect, including the target transcript, whereas Bcap31 and Dnm1l produced stronger corrected self-knockdown or downstream signatures in overlapping classes. This suggests the weak Pacs2 result is target-specific rather than a general atlas failure to capture nearby organelle biology, although Bcap31 and Dnm1l are related comparators, not interchangeable with Pacs2 or a rescue/epistasis test.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Setx showed little acute transcriptomic impact compared with Tardbp and Fus in overlapping neuronal classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In these thalamic, midbrain, and pontine/medullary contexts, Setx had no FDR-significant genes overall, with only a subthreshold hit in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Tardbp and Fus produced tens to hundreds of corrected changes. This indicates that within ALS-linked RNA-homeostasis perturbations, Setx knockdown was not interchangeable with the stronger acute signatures from Tardbp or Fus, noting that these data compare knockdowns rather than disease-mutant alleles.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Nbea showed several nominal downstream signatures that were uncoupled from clear target engagement. In 053 Sst Gaba and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, many genes reached nominal P<0.01 despite weak, absent, or essentially unchanged Nbea, with examples including nominal Sv2a down-regulation in Sst cells and Syp down-regulation in CNU-MGE GABA. By contrast, 052 Pvalb Gaba had the strongest nominal Nbea self-knockdown but only a weak downstream signature. No cell type showed a transcriptome-wide significant Nbea response at conventional FDR thresholds, so these nominal tails are better treated cautiously, while noting that target mRNA is an imperfect engagement readout.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp397 showed its largest nominal non-target changes in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where Cadps, Stac2, and Sema3e appeared as tempting neuronal hits, but these signals were uncoupled from target repression. In these cell types, Zfp397 itself was not measurably decreased, with Stac2 occurring where Zfp397 even trended upward and Sema3e accompanied only weak target engagement. Given FDRs of 0.298-0.381 and just 37-54 perturbed cells, these are exploratory rather than Zfp397-controlled pathway readouts.

Mmaa produced whole-transcriptome signatures that were near-orthogonal to Lmbrd1 and Pcca in matched cell types, so these related pathway perturbations were not transcriptionally interchangeable in this dataset. This lack of convergence was seen despite pathway links connecting Mmaa with intracellular cobalamin trafficking and with propionate and methylmalonyl-CoA metabolism. The contrast should be interpreted cautiously, however, because Mmaa and Pcca both showed weak target engagement, whereas Lmbrd1 displayed clearer transcript knockdown, so the near-zero correlations may reflect under-perturbation as much as true biological divergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Nfatc3 was largely silent in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, showing no clear target depletion, no significant downstream genes, and near-zero score-vector correlation with the signatures from Ppp3ca or Ppp3r1 perturbation. In contrast, Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1 engaged calcineurin subunit transcripts and produced FDR-supported signals in these neurons, indicating that the assay could detect calcineurin-module perturbations. This same-pathway contrast warns about perturbation quality and pathway context rather than proving that calcineurin responses bypass NFATC3, since calcineurin also has NFAT-independent substrates.

Opn1sw showed no detectable brain transcriptional response in this experiment: like the related retinal opsins Opn1mw and Rho, it had zero FDR-significant differential-expression hits in the matched brain cell types, and its signatures were nearly uncorrelated with either comparator. This pattern suggests retinal opsin perturbations behaved as a family-level negative control rather than a coherent brain transcriptomic module, with visual phototransduction/11-cis-retinal opsin signaling genes remaining unchanged. A caveat is that only Opn1mw and Rho were available as family comparators, and the shared inaction likely reflects missing retinal cell biology.

Park7 perturbation did not produce an FDR-detectable mRNA program consistent with the PARK7-NFE2L2 oxidative-stress axis or PINK1/Parkin mitophagy: across the dataset, no antioxidant, mitophagy, or mitochondrial-quality-control downstream genes reached FDR significance, and nominal Park7 signals were sparse rather than a recurrent module. This suggests uncoupling at the basal transcriptome level, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells where Dnm1l/Opa1-linked mitochondrial programs remained active while Park7 appeared buffered, while still leaving open post-translational NRF2 regulation, acute mitophagy defects, or damage-triggered responses.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Park7 did not phenocopy the direct mitochondrial dynamics perturbations Dnm1l or Opa1 in the two Park7-engaged midbrain classes, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. In these cells, Park7 loss showed on-target depletion but little to no downstream FDR-significant non-target response, whereas Dnm1l and Opa1 produced many transcriptomic changes and near-zero full-transcriptome correlation with Park7. This suggests that, in this basal assay, PARK7 was more buffered and not interchangeable with core fission/fusion regulators, although comparator guide efficiency and cell counts differed, and Opa1 on-target signal in 155 MB Glut was nominal rather than FDR significant.

Pura perturbation in mouse neuronal cell classes did not produce an FDR-significant decrease in the processing-body factor transcripts Lsm14a or Ddx6, including in the strongest responding populations such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut. This contrasts with human PURA-depleted HeLa and fibroblast systems, where LSM14A and DDX6 decline and P-body biology is disrupted. The discrepancy is tempered by the readout difference: these data measure steady-state mRNA in mouse brain cells, whereas the literature also involves protein abundance and P-body formation.

Pdss1 perturbation did not transcriptomically converge with the related CoQ-pathway perturbations Pdss2 or Coq5: genome-wide score correlations were near zero across every shared cell class, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Pdss1 showed its strongest self-depletion and the only adjusted p below 0.2. In the ubiquinol/coenzyme Q biosynthesis context, Pdss1 target RNA was reduced where engaged, but there was no FDR-level compensatory induction of other CoQ genes and no strong positive or negative signature neighbor. Because all three perturbations had weak adjusted RNA signatures, the lack of correlation may largely reflect noise and incomplete target engagement rather than definitive biological separation.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ppara showed no corrected differentially expressed genes in this neuronal Perturb-seq matrix, whereas the same dataset contained a detectable comparator perturbation: Srebf2 yielded 45 FDR<0.05 genes across 16 neuronal groups. This contrast indicates that the assay could recover transcription-factor effects in neurons despite the lack of a Ppara signal. The difference was evident in groups including 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Srebf2 had 7–8 significant genes but Ppara had none; however, Srebf2 is not a PPAR complex member, so this is an assay-context contrast rather than a mechanistic Ppara comparator.

Trip11 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage a curated Golgi, ERGIC, or ciliary membrane-trafficking program in the assayed neurons: no FDR-level changes were detected for canonical partners such as Ift20, Arf1, Gcc2, Golga paralogs including Golga1, Rabs, or dynein/dynactin transcripts, and no transcript-level module of Golgi/ciliary machinery was induced or repressed. This suggests that GMAP-210/TRIP11’s vesicle-tether and IFT20-localization roles were not accompanied by a detectable steady-state mRNA compensation program here, with the caveat that only transcript abundance, not protein localization or vesicle-trafficking function, was measured.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Nr6a1 perturbation did not detectably mobilize the expected NR6A1 developmental transcriptional repression program in the profiled mature brain classes. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Nanog, Tdgf1, Bmp15, Gdf9, Sox2, and Hcrt were not detectably changed, so canonical pluripotency, germ-cell/oocyte, early neural-stem-cell, and hypocretin-linked targets were uncoupled from these signatures. This may reflect that developmental targets are silent in mature neurons, that Hcrt neurons were diluted within broad hypothalamic classes, and that Pou5f1 was absent from the differential-expression table.

Tmem63c did not transcriptionally converge with the related TMEM63/OSCA channel paralogs Tmem63a or Tmem63b in this in vivo screen: across 22 matched cell classes, Tmem63c genome-wide score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with both paralogs. Consistent with this divergence, the dataset detected strong FDR-significant depletion of the target transcript for Tmem63b in 10 classes, whereas comparable on-target depletion was not seen for Tmem63a or Tmem63c. This contrast is transcriptomic and may reflect guide efficiency and target-mRNA behavior rather than complete functional nonoverlap.

Sdha showed a self-knockdown without an FDR-validated trans-gene response, and selected comparisons within oxidative phosphorylation/electron transport chain perturbations suggested the same qualitative pattern: Uqcrc1, Cox5a, and Ndufa10 each had strong self-mRNA depletion in several measured cell classes but no FDR-validated trans genes. This makes the Sdha phenotype look like a broader OXPHOS buffering pattern at the sampled transcriptional time point rather than a uniquely silent complex-II effect, although the comparator set was limited and the lack of trans hits could reflect partial knockdown, mRNA stability, or limited power.

Sdha showed a detectable on-target mRNA decrease, but the only assayed same-complex structural comparator, Sdhb, did not achieve FDR-validated self-knockdown, so this dataset cannot test whether SDHA and SDHB perturbations converge on a shared complex II phenotype. Across the surveyed cell types, Sdha downregulation occurred without detectable mRNA compensation among other complex II genes, including Sdhb, Sdhc, Sdhd, and Sdhaf1-4. Thus, the result should not be interpreted as SDHA-SDHB antagonism, because Sdhb guides may have edited protein or targeted a lowly expressed transcript without measurable mRNA depletion.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut
full_finding_text: Pitpnm3 remained FDR-null across several broad brain classes, even where the related phosphatidylinositol-transfer perturbation Pitpna was strongly engaged. In matched cell types including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, Pitpna showed strong on-target depletion and 37 FDR-significant rows overall, whereas Pitpnm3 had comparable or larger cell counts but no adjusted response, and their score vectors were nearly uncorrelated. This suggests these PITP-network perturbations are not interchangeable in these neuronal transcriptomes, with the caveat that Pitpna is a network neighbor rather than a PITPNM paralog and Pitpnm1/2 were not tested.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Pou6f1 did not participate in a broad Crhr1/Pou6f1 transcriptomic program in the assayed classes. In the closest context, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, Crhr1 perturbation yielded zero FDR-significant genes and only weak correlation with Pou6f1, so the CRH/CRHR1-linked Pou6f1 olfactory-plasticity axis was not recovered in these broad contrasts. This refines rather than contradicts prior work, because the literature concerns adult-born CRHR1+ olfactory-bulb granule neurons, whereas the dataset label here is a broad glutamatergic class that may not include the responsive GABAergic granule-neuron population.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nrp1 perturbation did not produce an FDR-significant transcriptional response in any assayed GABAergic subclass, including 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 053 Sst Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA, despite the known Sema3A-NRP1-plexin axon-guidance context. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Nrp1 showed only nominal self-depletion with adjusted p=1.0 and no downstream FDR hits, while related receptors such as Plxna2, Robo2, and Robo1 showed self-transcript depletion in 052 Pvalb Gaba, underscoring that classical developmental guidance biology was not recapitulated as a steady-state mRNA program here.

Zfp182 showed weak or null transcriptional effects and did not resemble Setdb1- or Chd4-like chromatin repression: across 17 matched cell-type strata, its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Setdb1 and Chd4 perturbation signatures, and genome-wide differential expression did not yield an FDR-significant Zfp182 response. This was also true in the largest stratum, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Setdb1 and Chd4 produced significant phenotypes elsewhere in the dataset. These results suggest that the assayed Zfp182 perturbation did not detectably engage a broad KRAB/C2H2 repression axis, although Zfp182 engagement was weak, Trim28/Kap1 was not directly measured, and Chd4 is only a broad chromatin comparator.

Sry perturbation in brain cell classes did not engage the canonical SRY-SOX9 sex-determination axis: Sox9 was not measurably changed in any of the 23 assayed brain cell types, and direct Sox9 targeting was also FDR-null, with no corrected response genes detected. This uncoupling from the expected gonadal pathway should not be taken as contradictory to sex-determination literature, because the Perturb-seq data come from neuronal and other brain cell populations rather than fetal supporting-cell precursors such as pre-Sertoli cells.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Ptpn11 perturbation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA nominally lowered the target transcript and also showed nominal decreases in Nf1 and Vgf, suggesting a possible local compensatory relief of the RAS/MAPK brake NF1 when SHP2 signaling is reduced. This single-cell-type pattern may help explain the lack of a large downstream ERK transcriptional program, but it remains exploratory: the Nf1 effect was only nominal, cross-perturbation similarity was weak, and no RAS-GTP or ERK activity was measured.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sall1 showed a broadly negative perturbation profile across 22 assayed neuronal subclasses, including cortical glutamatergic and GABAergic types, hypothalamic, midbrain, pineal, and cerebellar neurons: the Sall1 transcript was measured in every contrast but was not detectably shifted, and genome-wide differential expression was largely null or subthreshold. Sall4 behaved similarly, with no detectable target-transcript engagement and no 5%-FDR genes, and cross-cell-type score correlations with Sall1 were minimal, indicating that in these assayed neurons the SALL-family comparison was negative rather than redundant, divergent, or coupled to SALL1-NuRD/chromatin perturbations.

Stub1 depletion did not induce a corrected HSF1 heat-shock or chaperone transcriptional program: across family-level tests, no Hsp, Dnaj, Bag, or Hsf1-related changes were FDR-significant, and after multiple-testing correction there were no downstream transcriptomic hits beyond Stub1 itself. This was seen in 155 MB Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells, where on-target Stub1 knockdown was evident but chaperone-family induction remained absent. Because the screen was performed under basal conditions without imposed heat shock or proteotoxic stress, rare nominal chaperone changes should be interpreted cautiously.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sox4 did not share a detectable transcriptional module with its SOXC paralog Sox11 in this dataset. Across the 22 Sox4-measured neuronal classes, including cortical glutamatergic and GABAergic types as well as hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, pineal, and cerebellar neurons, neither single-gene perturbation produced FDR-resolved downstream differential expression, and Sox4/Sox11 ranked transcriptome signatures were essentially uncorrelated across shared cell types, with mean Pearson r about 0.006. This argues against a detectable SoxC neuronal differentiation program after single Sox4 or Sox11 perturbation here, although both perturbations showed weak measured target engagement, so the lack of convergence is not definitive.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Nr5a1 showed no convergent broad-brain transcriptomic response with its closest assayed paralog Nr5a2. Across 22 neuronal subclasses—including cortical IT and ET glutamatergic types, hippocampal glutamatergic populations, multiple GABAergic classes such as Pvalb and Sst, and midbrain, thalamic, pineal, and cerebellar groups—neither perturbation produced any FDR-supported genes, and full-signature Nr5a1-versus-Nr5a2 correlations were near zero, ranging from -0.059 to 0.060. Because both perturbations were weak, this lack of convergence may reflect absent target expression or engagement rather than definitive biological divergence between NR5A family members.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc25a13 was largely inert in the assayed neuronal classes: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, its own transcript was unchanged and showed no downstream FDR-significant hits, even with many perturbed cells in 155 MB Glut. In the same caudal glutamatergic and GABAergic classes, the paralog Slc25a12 was strongly depleted, indicating that within the malate-aspartate shuttle/aspartate-glutamate carrier context, the direct neuronal RNA effect segregated to Slc25a12 rather than Slc25a13. This contrast is driven mainly by the target-transcript row, since Slc25a12 itself produced little additional downstream regulation.

Rala showed no FDR-significant RNA response in this dataset, and the measured neighboring perturbations Hras, Kras, and Exoc6b were likewise FDR-null, indicating shared absence of a detectable transcriptional effect across the Ral small-GTPase and exocyst signaling neighborhood. However, this silence cannot be cleanly attributed to RALA-specific buffering because these comparators were only pathway-adjacent, their knockdown efficiency was not FDR-confirmed, and several direct paralog or effector perturbations, including Ralb, Ralbp1, Ralgds, Exoc2, and Exoc8, were not available.

Rdx knockdown did not produce detectable transcriptional compensation by its ERM paralogs: Ezr and Msn transcripts were non-significant in every Rdx cell type measured, indicating no Ezr/Msn upregulation within the ERM membrane-cortex actin linkage context that also included Nf2 and actin-associated genes. This refines the idea of ERM family relatedness by showing no mRNA-level replacement of Rdx in this dataset, although Ezr and Msn were only measured as response genes and were not themselves perturbed, so functional redundancy cannot be tested directly.

Tead1 showed little convergence with the only informative Hippo-network comparator, Nf2: across matched gene and cell-type rows, the Tead1-versus-Nf2 scores were nearly zero, and Nf2 itself was weak in this dataset, with no FDR-significant differential-expression rows. In the Hippo/YAP-TAZ-TEAD transcription context, there was no corrected Tead1 output and no Nf2 convergence, including for genes such as Ccn1, Ccn2, Apoe, and Dab2. Because most TEAD paralogs and YAP/TAZ were not perturbed here, this contrast should be interpreted cautiously rather than as a mechanistic contradiction.

Sptlc2 knockdown showed no detectable mRNA-level compensation by other serine palmitoyltransferase components or ORMDL regulators: Sptlc1, Sptlc3, Sptssa, Sptssb, and Ormdl1-3 were all non-significant. This pattern was seen across the assayed neuronal classes, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut; in the thalamic glutamatergic class with the strongest Sptlc2 depletion, these feedback genes still failed 5% FDR. The caveat is that only transcripts were measured, whereas ORMDL- and ceramide-linked SPT homeostasis is expected to act largely post-transcriptionally.

Smarcc1 showed minimal activity in this Perturb-seq screen, whereas its closest assayed paralog Smarcc2 was far more engaged in matched contexts: Smarcc2 had 188 total FDR<0.05 differential-expression rows and significant target-transcript depletion in 4 cell types, while Smarcc1 had only 1 significant row and no significant target-transcript depletion. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, BAF-related perturbations were active but Smarcc1 was flat, so the Smarcc1 guide-set phenotype should not be treated as a proxy for SMARCC scaffold-dimer loss; however, Smarcc2 also achieved better target-transcript knockdown, limiting a clean protein-function comparison.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Sucla2 knockdown in the strongest Sucla2 self-hit classes showed no FDR-supported mRNA compensation by the shared alpha subunit Suclg1 or the alternative GDP-forming beta paralog Suclg2 across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, arguing against an obvious mRNA-level rescue of the ADP-forming succinate-CoA ligase/TCA-cycle module. Some additional classes had only nominal Sucla2 self-hits, and low basal Suclg2 expression or dropout could mask small effects; the assay addresses mRNA induction, not protein-level isoenzyme switching.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Rxrg showed a near-null program in this screen, particularly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, where corrected differential expression was essentially absent; in the thalamic class, Rxrg yielded only weak signals such as Raf1 and Ppp2r5d at FDR 0.4375. This was not a general failure to recover nuclear-receptor phenotypes, because Nr1d1 and Thra produced corrected hits in the same screen, whereas the RXR paralogs Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg were all near-null. However, this internal contrast does not explain why Rxrg failed, since Nr1d1 and Thra are not RXRG heterodimer partners.

Mlxip perturbation did not detectably engage the canonical MLXIP-MLX glucose-responsive transcription program in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq screen. Across cell types, Txnip and Arrdc4 were not even nominally changed, and a 14-gene glycolysis/lipogenesis panel, including Acly, Acaca, Fasn, and Hk2, showed no FDR-supported response. This remained true even in neuronal classes with the largest nominal Mlxip decreases, such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut. The null result may reflect basal conditions without high-glucose or lipid stress, and weak Mlxip transcript knockdown could also have masked canonical target-gene responses.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Snf8 did not define a uniformly coherent ESCRT transcriptional axis in this dataset: Chmp4b was essentially uncoupled from Snf8, while Vps37a showed only local positive convergence with Snf8 in selected non-cortical CNU/MB signatures, including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA. In 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Rap1gap down-regulation was the clearest corrected Snf8 hit. Interpretation is limited because most direct ESCRT-II/III neighbors were not perturbed, and Vps37a responding-cell counts were low.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Vps13c showed low convergence with its paralogs in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Vps13a, Vps13b, and Vps13d had near-zero score correlations with Vps13c and none produced downstream FDR-significant hits in these restricted cross-perturbation comparisons. This argues against treating VPS13 family members as interchangeable within ER-endolysosomal lipid-transfer biology in these neuronal Perturb-seq signatures, although the inference is limited to two emphasized cell types and is tempered by weak on-target engagement for some paralog perturbations.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
full_finding_text: Smarca2 perturbation showed a single FDR-significant non-target transcriptional change: Ppfia2 was decreased in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut cells. However, in that same comparison Smarca2 itself was not significantly depleted, and only 60 perturbed cells were available, so the Ppfia2 signal appears decoupled from measured target engagement. This makes Ppfia2 an isolated, hypothesis-generating marker in this cell type rather than a strong mechanistic anchor for SMARCA2 function.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Rapgef4 perturbation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA was associated with a nominal decrease in Rap1gap, the strongest Rapgef4-linked gene in that class and the only one directly touching the Rap GTPase circuit, making it a candidate compensatory Rap-cycle response within cAMP-EPAC-Rap signaling. However, this signal did not pass FDR correction, and Rapgef4 transcript reduction in the same cells was weak, so the finding is best viewed as buffered or suggestive rather than a confirmed response; related pathway context also included a stronger Pde10a response in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.

Kpna3 did not phenocopy the available Ran/karyopherin transport neighbors Ranbp2 and Xpo1: across overlapping mouse cell types, Kpna3 score-vector correlations with Ranbp2 and with Xpo1 were near zero, indicating essentially uncorrelated transcriptional signatures in the NLS-dependent nucleocytoplasmic import/Ran-karyopherin pathway. This lack of similarity was not due to a globally silent nuclear-transport program in the dataset. A caveat is that Ranbp2 and Xpo1 are pathway neighbors rather than Kpna3 paralogs, and Xpo1 perturbation often increased its own transcript, so the contrast is transcriptomic rather than a clean matched loss-of-function comparison.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Setdb1 perturbation most strongly upregulated Atf7ip and Tasor, encoding SETDB1/HUSH-associated repressors, suggesting a possible mRNA-level compensatory attempt to restore SETDB1/HUSH H3K9me3 silencing rather than a purely end-stage clustered protocadherin readout. This signal was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, also present in 155 MB Glut cells, and in 308 CB GABA appeared as isolated Atf7ip induction without an FDR-level protocadherin response. Tasor reached FDR<0.05 in two cell types and Atf7ip in three, so the induction does not by itself establish direct feedback regulation or increased protein activity.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Rp9 did not phenocopy the spliceosome-related perturbation Prpf6 in this neural assay. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, Rp9 produced a compact response, with a four-gene downregulated signature as its strongest effect, while in 155 MB Glut cells only exploratory recurrence of Ctps2 and Trim3 decreases was seen. By contrast, Prpf6 caused hundreds to more than 1000 FDR-significant transcript changes across these same contexts, indicating divergent transcriptomic breadth within an RP-PRPF pre-mRNA splicing context. This comparison is based on transcript abundance rather than direct splicing, and Prpf6 target-transcript knockdown was not itself demonstrated.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Pax3 perturbation in the assayed mouse brain cell classes did not engage the canonical PAX3–SOX10–MITF neural-crest module: Mitf and Sox10 were unchanged across all 22 sampled glutamatergic and GABAergic cell types, and perturbing Mitf or Sox10 produced signatures essentially uncorrelated with Pax3. More broadly, no Pax3 downstream gene reached multiple-testing significance, with the strongest single-gene effects remaining sub-FDR. This likely reflects context mismatch, since the dataset samples brain cells rather than premigratory neural crest, melanoblast, or Schwann-cell lineages where PAX3-SOX10-MITF biology is expected.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tubb2a knockdown produced a narrow, cell-restricted β-tubulin compensation pattern rather than a broad isotype program. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Tubb2a depletion was strongest, Tubb3 was significantly induced, providing the only FDR-supported secondary β-tubulin response. By contrast, Tubb4b showed recurrent positive but FDR-nonsignificant nominal effects in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA. These data are consistent with selective substitute β-tubulin isoforms after Tubb2a loss, but the signal is weak and not shared across related microtubule-neighbor perturbations.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Unc13c did not phenocopy Unc13a or Unc13b across the Perturb-seq transcriptome in the profiled neuronal populations, including multiple cortical glutamatergic and GABAergic classes as well as hippocampal, hypothalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, pineal, and cerebellar cells. Full-transcriptome correlations between Unc13c and either paralog were centered near zero, while Unc13a was largely FDR-silent and Unc13b showed only one isolated FDR hit, so the assay did not reveal a common Munc13-family active-zone priming module mRNA state. A shared electrophysiological effect could still be missed by steady-state mRNA readouts.

Samd12 perturbation was transcriptionally uncoupled from the proposed SAMD12-CNKSR2-MAP4K/TNIK scaffold mechanism: candidate pathway mRNAs Cnksr1, Cnksr2, Cnksr3, Tnik, Map4k4, and Mink1 were not FDR-significant, and Samd12 did not globally correlate with Cnksr2 or Tnik perturbations. No cell-type-specific signal was reported, and other FAME repeat-expansion host genes present in the dataset did not broadly phenocopy Samd12. These data therefore should not be read as a transcriptional reporter of the CNKSR2-TNIK mechanism, since only transcript abundance was measured and SAMD12 may still regulate CNKSR-MAP4K complexes at the protein level without changing their mRNAs.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Tfcp2 showed its largest nominal single-gene responses in cell types without clear on-target knockdown, so these signals should not be treated as TFCP2 biomarkers. Plxdc1 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Thyn1 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and Efr3a in 053 Sst Gaba were the top scalar hits in the Tfcp2 table, yet Tfcp2 itself was only weakly changed in the first two cases and was even directionally increased in 053 Sst Gaba. These are therefore best viewed as hypothesis-generating outliers, with the caveat that the dataset does not test responses to complete TFCP2 loss in another assay.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Sp7 did not phenocopy the available Sp-family comparator Sp4 in midbrain/thalamic glutamatergic classes. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Sp4 produced significant signatures, whereas Sp7 was silent in both, including 155 MB Glut where more matched Sp7-perturbed cells were available. This suggests that shared Sp1-family zinc-finger architecture was not sufficient to infer interchangeable neuronal responses in this dataset. A caveat is that Sp4 was the only close SP/KLF family comparator queried, so broader paralog comparisons were not tested.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Thra perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was associated with Hr downregulation, the strongest non-target decrease in this class, alongside reduced Adgrb1 and Hcn2. This cell-type-restricted pattern is consistent with reduced TRα-dependent activation of Hr and suggests, but does not prove, a local feedback-like relief of thyroid hormone receptor corepression because Hr is a thyroid-hormone-responsive gene and HR can repress thyroid hormone receptors. Related receptor or coactivator perturbations did not converge on this module, and receptor occupancy, HR protein, and rescue were not measured.

Vezf1 perturbation in the adult brain did not detectably engage the canonical Dnmt3b/Cited2/Stmn1 endothelial and DNA-methylation axis: Dnmt3b, Dnmt3a, Dnmt1, Cited2, and Stmn1 showed no FDR-supported RNA response in any of the 23 assayed cell types. This leaves the observed Vezf1 RNA signatures uncoupled from the published embryonic stem cell and endothelial programs, suggesting context-specific neuronal effects rather than a direct replay of those mechanisms. The main caveat is that this is a negative RNA result only, without direct methylation or chromatin measurements.

Phka1 did not converge with the only other assayed phosphorylase kinase regulatory subunit, Phkb. Across matched cell types, Phka1–Phkb transcriptomic correlations were close to zero, ranging from -0.0978 to 0.0492, and neither perturbation produced FDR-significant outputs. In this screen, the expected shared complex membership of Phka1 and Phkb therefore did not translate into similar neuronal expression signatures, but this contrast is best interpreted cautiously because both perturbations showed weak RNA-level target engagement and were effectively near-null.

Tmem63b was the only TMEM63-family perturbation that was interpretable in this dataset. Although Tmem63a and Tmem63c are paralog comparators, their guide cells showed no detectable self-depletion and did not produce significant downstream signatures, so they could not serve as loss-of-function phenocopies for Tmem63b. As a result, the TMEM63 paralog comparison is technically disarmed: the data do not show that Tmem63b has a unique downstream program, and they cannot distinguish true paralog divergence from inefficient knockdown of Tmem63a and Tmem63c.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ppp3r1 showed a distinct transcriptomic response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where calcineurin-related perturbations were not interchangeable despite shared holoenzyme membership. In this class, Ppp3ca was well knocked down but its response correlated only weakly with Ppp3r1, while Ppp3cc produced no FDR-significant rows, indicating divergent detectable outputs across related subunits. This comparison is transcriptomic rather than functional, and differences in target engagement and perturbation cell counts across subunits are important caveats when interpreting the contrast.

Ppip5k2 targeting did not produce a significant transcriptional compensation response within the PPIP5K/IP6K inositol-pyrophosphate network: Ppip5k1, Ip6k1, Ip6k2, Ip6k3, Ippk, Itpk1, Minpp1, and Xpr1 were not reproducibly induced, despite PPIP5K1 and the IP6Ks being the closest biochemical collaborators of PPIP5K2. In the 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cell type, the lowest adjusted p value in the screen still did not reflect clear on-target suppression of Ppip5k2, and a nominal Ip6k2 decrease was not FDR significant. These results concern transcript abundance only, not enzyme activity or InsP7/InsP8 levels.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zic4 did not phenocopy Zic1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells despite a comparable number of perturbed cells. In this thalamic glutamatergic context, Zic1 perturbation showed FDR-supported Slc29a1 up-regulation and reduction of Zic1 transcript, whereas Zic4 perturbation did not significantly change Slc29a1 or Zic4 and only nominally reduced Zic1. This divergence within the ZIC1/ZIC4 paralog module appears cell-type-specific, and interpretation is tempered by the lack of direct edit-rate information for the Zic4 perturbation.

Pcdh15 perturbation in brain cells left the canonical PCDH15/CDH23 tip-link and auditory mechanotransduction network transcriptionally silent. Across 21–22 cell-type contrasts, measurable partner genes including Cdh23, Lhfpl5, Myo7a, Ush1c, Ush1g, Tmie, Tmc1, Tmc2, and Cib2 showed no coordinated differential expression and none reached FDR<0.05, indicating no detectable brain transcriptional coupling to this sensory hair-cell module. This negative result is limited to RNA summaries in brain cells and does not assess tip-link mechanics or protein localization.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Tfdp1 showed nominal mRNA decreases in five cell types—most clearly in 155 MB Glut, and also in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 308 CB GABA—but none had FDR-significant downstream genes. This buffering was strongest where knockdown looked most apparent, arguing against a ubiquitous immediate transcriptional requirement for TFDP1 in the basal dataset. Within pRB/E2F-related context, responses were mostly buffered, with only weak positive convergence toward Rb1 and E2f4 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. Partial knockdown, low cycling-gene expression, or limited power could explain the null downstream signal.

Tbc1d23 showed no adjusted transcriptional signal in the basal single-cell mRNA readout: no downstream transcript reached significance in any analyzed cell-type contrast, the target mRNA itself was not detectably depleted, and the strongest nominal changes were isolated subthreshold events rather than coherent pathway anchors. This null result is consistent with TBC1D23 functions that center on trans-Golgi/endosomal vesicle tethering, Golgi-localized LKB1-AMPK signaling, and stimulus-dependent innate-immune maintenance, which are not resolved by unstimulated neuronal transcriptomes; weak knockdown and the lack of trafficking, Golgi phosphorylation, or LPS/TLR challenge assays are important caveats.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
full_finding_text: Trappc10 showed a buffered or null transcriptional response across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA, with no multiple-testing-corrected differential expression; in 155 MB Glut the strongest nominal signal involved Jund but still did not reach FDR significance. By contrast, vesicle-trafficking comparators in the same screen were detectable, including Vps35, Sec23a, and Sec31a, indicating that the Trappc10 null result was selective rather than a general failure to detect vesicle biology, although these comparators are endosomal/COPII genes rather than TRAPPC10 complex members.

Trim2 perturbation did not induce its paralog Trim3 at the mRNA level: Trim3 showed no significant increase in any measured class, with FDR 1.0 throughout and a slight decrease in 151 TH cells (logFC -0.060). Thus, despite the known TRIM2-TRIM3 physical and regulatory relationship, the acute response did not show a simple paralog-transcription feedback loop, suggesting any buffering by TRIM3 is post-transcriptional or absent in these contexts. This interpretation is limited because only Trim3 RNA abundance was assayed, not TRIM3 protein levels, heteromer stoichiometry, or E3 activity.

Pkd1 showed near-zero transcriptomic convergence with the assayed ciliary comparators Ift88 and Kif3b in this neuronal screen. Although PKD1, IFT88, and KIF3B are all associated with the primary cilium/polycystin channel context, no shared Pkd1-IFT module was recovered, and none of the three perturbations produced a broad FDR-significant response. This should be interpreted mainly as a negative screen result, because Pkd1, Ift88, and Kif3b each had weak signatures, and closer polycystin-family comparators were not assayed.

Scn1b depletion did not reveal a broad β1-regulated transcriptional module in this Perturb-seq assay: after excluding the Scn1b target-transcript rows, the FDR-resolved downstream response was extremely sparse, and no other perturbation showed a strongly convergent or opposing transcriptome-wide score vector relative to Scn1b.
