This refines prior suggestions that β1 regulated intramembrane proteolysis can influence gene expression, implying that any transcriptional output may be conditional on timing, stimulation, network state, or perturbation duration, or may consist of subtle coordinated shifts below single-gene FDR thresholds.

Pou4f3 was uncoupled from the canonical POU4F3 auditory hair-cell transcription and survival network in this brain Perturb-seq dataset. Across all 23 profiled brain cell classes, Pou4f3 showed no FDR-significant transcriptomic effect, no measurable target-transcript depletion, and no activation of measured hair-cell program genes; Gfi1, Bdnf, Ntf3, Myo7a, and Rbm24 remained FDR-negative. Perturbation signatures for Atoh1, Gfi1, Isl1, and Pax2 were essentially uncorrelated with Pou4f3, so the contrast with cochlear hair-cell biology should be interpreted cautiously because the comparison is indirect.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Robo1 did not behave as an interchangeable transcriptomic paralog with Robo2 in the profiled neuronal cell types. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, Robo1 showed the strongest engagement, while Robo2 knocked down strongly in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 155 MB Glut; across the shared Pvalb, midbrain glutamatergic, and thalamic contexts, their whole-transcriptome score vectors were near zero correlation. Both perturbations were largely target-only, and Robo2 was not significantly knocked down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, so this contrast is transcriptomic and limited by target engagement.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Pik3cb showed only mixed nominal, cell-type-restricted transcriptional effects rather than a coherent PI3K/AKT/mTOR module. The largest nominal island appeared in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, but it was not FDR supported and that cluster had only 38 perturbed cells; 053 Sst Gaba had the lowest adjusted p value yet only 24 perturbed cells and no corrected downstream genes. Akt3, Prkcb, Prkacb, and Ndufb9 were isolated nominal events, with a weak recurrent decrease of a single mitochondrial complex-I transcript across 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|053 Sst Gaba
full_finding_text: Psmc5 showed convergence with other 26S proteasome perturbations where it was responsive, but it was not interchangeable with Psmc1 or Psmb4 in several Psmc5-low cell types. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 001 L5-6 IT Glut, and 053 Sst Gaba, Psmc1 or especially Psmb4 produced much larger FDR-significant burdens even when Psmc5 had few or no significant genes; for example, in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Psmc5 had 3 FDR genes versus 842 for Psmb4. These magnitude differences may reflect guide potency or transcript detection as well as true subunit biology.

Suco showed no convergent comparator module in this neuronal Perturb-seq panel: whole-transcriptome correlations between Suco and every other co-profiled perturbation remained below |r| = 0.20, with the largest observed neighbor in 308 CB GABA cells being Ranbp2 at r = 0.190. Available related perturbations, including Col2a1, Col11a1, Fam120a, and Hif1a, were near zero correlated with Suco across overlapping classes, so the weak Suco profile did not align with an ER, collagen-family, Hif1a, or Fam120a module. A caveat is that many higher-scoring STRING Suco partners were not profiled here, and the available comparators were either low-scoring associations or collagen-family rather than canonical type I collagen comparators.

Suco showed no detectable neuronal transcriptional program linked to the rough endoplasmic reticulum or collagen biosynthetic process in this Perturb-seq screen. Across sampled classes, the Suco perturbation had no multiple-testing-significant differential expression, and available collagen-family or low-scoring STRING comparator perturbations, including Col2a1 and Col11a1, did not recapitulate the Suco transcriptome. This suggests a cell-context uncoupling rather than a contradiction of skeletal biology, since osteoblasts were not assayed and the panel lacked Col1a1 and Col1a2.

Sorl1 showed a target-only transcriptional response in this dataset: its knockdown produced no multiple-testing-corrected non-self hits, and the same was true for App despite much stronger App mRNA depletion across many cell types. Thus, the curated SORL1-APP cargo axis appeared transcriptionally quiet here, with no detectable APP-axis differential-expression module. This comparison is limited because it assays acute mRNA abundance, not APP processing, endosomal localization, or other trafficking-related phenotypes.

Stx5a showed a sparse, cell-type-idiosyncratic transcriptomic signature consistent with buffered or plastic Golgi trafficking rather than a uniform Stx5a-loss state. After multiple-testing correction, nominal hits were poorly recurrent across 21 cell classes, did not form a shared ER–Golgi stress program, and did not phenocopy COPII, COPI, or COG perturbations such as Cog4, Cog5, Copa, Copg1, Sar1b, or Sec23a; in 308 CB GABA, Copg1 was down but related target signatures were otherwise uncoupled, with related context in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut. This pattern is hypothesis-generating, because poor Stx5a guide activity could also explain the weak signal and should be tested with stronger guides or protein-level STX5 depletion.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Snap25 showed a comparatively sparse transcriptomic response relative to Stxbp1 in matched neuronal classes despite both acting in SNARE-mediated synaptic-vesicle exocytosis. In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut, stronger Snap25 knockdown produced no secondary FDR hits, whereas Stxbp1 yielded dozens, including 66 and 11 genes in those same classes. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Snap25 had only two non-target hits, with Septin4 down and Syt7 up. This comparison is transcriptomic and may reflect differences in guide potency, expression, or collateral roles.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Plxna2 showed FDR-significant on-target depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where Sema5a perturbation was even more strongly engaged and Plxna4 was only nominally engaged, yet none of these perturbations produced a shared FDR-level downstream transcriptomic program. In this thalamic class, semaphorin/plexin axon-guidance relationships therefore did not appear as simple ligand-paralog interchangeability, with the caveat that prior Sema5A-PlxnA2-Rap1 and Plxna2/Plxna4/Sema6A links were defined in developing hippocampal contexts rather than this profiled thalamic transcriptome.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Smad2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells showed the broadest nominal response among Smad2 cell types, with a small synaptic-output module in which Cpne7 was the only FDR-significant hit and was decreased. Seventeen genes reached nominal p<0.001, including synaptic genes Ache, Rims4, Slc17a6, Atp6ap2, Ywhah, Cck, Rasgrp2, and Vdac1, yielding a synapse-enriched interpretation. However, this pathway signal is based on a nominal gene set, so the clearest multi-gene neuronal Smad2 response remains restricted to this thalamic/hypothalamic glutamatergic class.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Pou3f3 perturbation did not recover the expected POU3F3/POU3F2 cortical neurogenesis and migration program in the assayed cortical glutamatergic classes. Across 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, no corrected downstream genes were detected, including in upper-layer classes. This should be interpreted cautiously because Pou3f2 was not assayed, Pou3f3 itself showed no strong transcript depletion, and the dataset does not model embryonic progenitors.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Slf2 perturbation showed mostly weak, nominally negative on-target transcript effects, and the strongest Slf2 mRNA decreases were uncoupled from downstream transcriptional response. In 191 MB P MY GABA, as well as 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut, Slf2 decreased nominally, including p<0.005 contexts, yet there were zero FDR-significant downstream genes. The only FDR-significant event across Slf2 results was Ppp5c upregulation in an upper-layer glutamatergic class where Slf2 itself was not nominally significant, suggesting buffering within the RAD18-SLF1/2-SMC5/6 DNA damage response; Slf2 depletion was not FDR-significant and protein abundance was not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Taf1b showed no multiple-testing-corrected downstream transcript changes in any assayed cell type, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, even where perturbed-cell counts were highest. In contrast, the Pol I initiation neighbor Rrn3 produced corrected signatures in shared cell types, with 76 FDR-significant genes overall, dominated by thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons. This supports recovery of RNA polymerase I/SL1 initiation-axis responses in the dataset, but does not establish mechanistic divergence because Taf1b guide efficacy and target engagement were weak; notably, Rrn3 is pathway-adjacent and its target-transcript FDR in 151 TH was 0.096.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp423 showed an increase in its own transcript in the strongest responsive cells, with significant positivity in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only nominal positivity in 308 CB GABA. This supports that the perturbation is linked to the intended locus, especially in the thalamic class with the dominant response, but it also means target mRNA abundance cannot be treated as a simple readout of Zfp423 loss of function. Outside the thalamic response, target-transcript changes were generally weak or absent, and the observed increase could reflect feedback, mutant-transcript stabilization, isoform effects, or editing efficiency rather than knockdown strength.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Trpa1 showed its strongest nominal response in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons, a layer-5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic class, but the signal did not survive multiple testing. The pattern was mixed, with nominal decreases led by Sstr4, while Trpa1 itself was unchanged; the minimum FDR was 0.217 and no gene reached FDR significance. Thus, in this broad L5 ET transcriptional class, the data do not support a large baseline transcriptional dependency on Trpa1, though this differs from prior acute pharmacology in somatosensory L5 pyramidal neurons.

Sdhb was not interchangeable with Sdha in this dataset: although both are components of mitochondrial succinate dehydrogenase/respiratory complex II, Sdha showed much stronger self-depletion than Sdhb, and their whole-transcriptome perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated across 22 matched cell classes. This divergence is therefore best interpreted with caution, as unequal target engagement and RNA-level buffering are a more likely explanation than confident subunit-specific biology. Additional caveats are that Sdhc, Sdhd, and Sdhaf1-4 were not perturbed here, and Sdhb engagement was weaker than Sdha.

Tshr perturbation was weak in this atlas, resembling the near-null behavior of the related glycoprotein-hormone receptors Fshr and Lhcgr, while downstream cAMP-pathway effectors were directly perturbable. In contrast to the receptor family, Prkaca and Adcy3 showed strong depletion when targeted, including in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, and Prkaca depletion was also recoverable in 052 Pvalb Gaba, where Tshr showed only a nominal Arfgef3 decrease. These cross-perturbation contrasts use different guide sets and perturbed-cell counts, and the Adcy3/Prkaca results show target knockdown rather than a full Tshr-dependent program.

Pax6 perturbation did not detectably engage the PAX6 neural-progenitor transcriptional network in the assayed neurons: across 22 Pax6-assayed neuronal classes, Pax6 RNA itself was not significantly reduced, no downstream gene reached standard multiple-testing significance, and proxy circuit genes Sox2, Pbx1, Smarca4, Eomes, and Tbr1 all remained non-significant, with selected rows at FDR=1.0. This refines rather than contradicts prior progenitor-focused literature, because the test was indirect in differentiated neuronal states and relied on proxy markers for progenitor biology.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Ret showed weak and nominal depletion without a coherent downstream transcriptional response, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas the comparator receptors Ncam1 and Epha4 were robustly depleted in multiple neuronal classes, including 155 MB Glut, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. Despite this stronger engagement, their transcriptomic score vectors were not Ret-like, and related RET/GDNF, RAS-MAPK, and developmental comparators likewise lacked a coherent Ret-like profile. This contrast argues against a general failure to deplete neuronal surface receptors, while remaining limited to transcriptomic similarity because NCAM1 and EPHA4 are broad adhesion or guidance receptors rather than stoichiometric RET subunits.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Ret showed near-zero or mixed similarity to perturbations of Gfra1, Mapk1, Braf, and Sos2 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, so the canonical GDNF-GFRA1-RET to RAS/MAPK/AKT neighborhood did not phenocopy the measured Ret signatures. In CA3, Ret had the strongest nominal non-Ret signature but lacked pathway-neighbor convergence, and in TH, nominal Ret depletion produced no FDR-significant downstream response. Because Gfra1 and several comparators, as well as Ret itself, showed weak or incomplete target-transcript depletion, this reflects pathway-level nonconvergence rather than proof that RET cannot signal through MAPK in these neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ptprd perturbation did not recover a reproducible transcriptional module for the expected synaptic-adhesion biology. Across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 155 MB Glut cells, no transcript reached FDR significance in Ptprd contrasts, and only isolated nominal decreases appeared in adhesion or receptor-associated genes such as Nrcam, Nrg3, Nfasc, and Ntrk2. These weak, cell-type-specific signals showed no strong cross-perturbation convergence and do not establish direct downstream regulation by PTPRD or its IL1RAP/IL1RAPL1/SLITRK-associated pathway.

Nfat5 targeting in basal mouse brain cell types did not reproduce a broad canonical NFAT5 osmolyte program: across 20 signatures, classic partners Slc5a3, Slc6a12, and Akr1b3 were largely unchanged in neuronal and GABAergic classes, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, 308 CB GABA, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA. Instead, Slc38a2 was the most recurrent negative downstream transcript, while Slc6a6 showed only nominal decreases in a subset of cell types. Low basal expression and the lack of a hyperosmotic challenge likely limited power for some osmolyte genes.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Tgfbr1 did not show significant self-depletion in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut or 155 MB Glut, even though its transcript was present in the differential-expression table for every tested group. In the same neuronal classes and with comparable perturbed-cell counts, the related receptor Bmpr2 was cleanly self-depleted, indicating that receptor transcripts were measurable in this matrix and that the Tgfbr1 null is more likely target- or guide-specific than a general failure to detect membrane-receptor knockdown. A caveat is that Bmpr2 is a BMP receptor rather than the TGFBR1:TGFBR2 complex partner, and even its significant knockdown yielded only one FDR-significant gene in those groups.

Pcsk2 showed a largely target-only Perturb-seq profile, and its pathway neighbor Cpe behaved similarly rather than producing a shared downstream mRNA program. Across the 20 shared cell types, Pcsk2–Cpe score-vector correlations were near zero, while Cpe was efficiently depleted in 17 of 22 contexts with only one non-target FDR hit. These data suggest that, in this assay, the common biology of these linked secretory-granule peptide-processing enzymes is buffered at the mRNA level and may be primarily post-translational, with the caveat that comparisons were based only on mRNA signatures and Cpe had larger perturbed-cell counts in many cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Purb did not produce corrected transcriptomic signatures in the midbrain glutamatergic populations 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, even though it had equal or higher matched-cell counts than Pura in those same classes. In contrast, Pura showed corrected signatures with FDR-significant Pura downregulation, whereas Purg showed no FDR-significant genes across its evaluated contexts. These results suggest PUR-family perturbations were not interchangeable in this screen, with downstream effects for Purb appearing buffered; however, Purb and Purg also had weak target-transcript FDR support, so the dataset shows divergence rather than a molecular explanation.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp462 showed whole-transcriptome perturbation signatures that were essentially orthogonal to Pbx1 and Ehmt1 across the main nominal-response classes, including 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut. Thus, in these neuronal cell types, Pbx1 or Ehmt1 perturbations did not act as interchangeable proxies for Zfp462 loss, and the ZFP462-PBX1 or ZFP462-G9A/GLP developmental transcription control relationship was not detected or appeared context dependent. This interpretation is tempered by the absence of Ehmt2 targeting, variable target-transcript engagement for Pbx1 and Ehmt1, and the possibility that whole-transcriptome correlations diluted small shared modules.

Setd2 perturbation did not produce the coherent down-regulation of clustered protocadherin transcription expected from developmental cortical-knockout literature. Across 840 measured Pcdha/Pcdhb/Pcdhg rows, effects were mixed in sign and none reached FDR significance, including genes such as Pcdhga7, Pcdhb9, Pcdhgc4, Pcdhgb4, Pcdha8, Pcdha12, Pcdhgc5, Pcdhb18, and Pcdha11. In neuronal subclasses including 046 CTX-CGE GABA and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, nominal changes included both positive and negative rows, suggesting any SETD2–Pcdh relationship here is context-specific; many protocadherins were also sparsely detected.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Sppl2a perturbation did not reveal substrate-transcript feedback for the known SPPL2A substrate genes Tmem106b and Itm2b across the assayed neuronal classes, including multiple cortical glutamatergic and GABAergic populations, hippocampal, thalamic, midbrain, pineal, and cerebellar neurons. Neither Tmem106b nor Itm2b reached FDR-significant mRNA changes, and selected substrate, lysosomal, and inflammatory pathway-neighbor perturbations did not produce a convergent Sppl2a-like transcriptomic program, although direct Itm2b targeting gave measurable guide-dependent depletion. These results are consistent with SPPL2A acting through post-translational intramembrane cleavage, while also underscoring that absence of Tmem106b or Itm2b mRNA change does not test lysosomal cleavage fragments directly.

Rtn4r perturbation was not a transcriptional phenocopy of the available NgR1 coreceptors Lingo1 or Ngfr in resting-brain single-cell profiles. Within the Nogo receptor/RHOA anti-axon-growth signaling context, same-cell-type Rtn4r–Lingo1 and Rtn4r–Ngfr signatures were essentially uncorrelated; Lingo1 showed stronger on-target transcript depletion with four FDR-significant rows, whereas Ngfr had none, and Rtn4r itself was weakly engaged and nearly FDR-silent. Direct comparisons were limited because Rtn4, Tnfrsf19, Rtn4rl1, and Rtn4rl2 were not perturbed.

Zic3 showed little engagement in the measured mouse-brain neuronal perturbations: across assayed genes and cell types, its perturbation produced no multiple-testing-significant downstream transcriptional change, and the Zic3 transcript itself was not credibly depleted in any cell-type contrast. Consistent with this weak signature, perturbations of developmental partners in the GLI/NODAL/Wnt/PCP axis, including Gli3, Acvr2b, Sox2, Pou5f1, and Rac1, did not phenocopy Zic3. This uncoupling should be interpreted cautiously because key left-right genes such as Nodal, Lefty2, and Cfc1 were not perturbed, and the relevant literature is largely embryonic rather than neuronal.

St3gal3 showed no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response across the 22 profiled Glut/GABA neuronal classes, and restricted whole-signature correlations did not identify a robust positive, negative, or St3gal5-like neighbor. The related Golgi sialyltransferase St3gal5, although reduced more robustly with FDR-significant target knockdown in 10 of 22 cell classes, likewise produced zero FDR-significant non-target genes. Together, these perturbations in Golgi sialylation and sialic-acid metabolism appear to behave as target- or product-level hits rather than broad transcriptional stressors, with the caveat that mRNA readouts do not directly test ganglioside or glycoprotein abundance.

St3gal3 perturbation showed no FDR-level transcriptional response among related sialyltransferases across all 22 profiled Glut/GABA neuronal classes: St3gal2, St3gal5, other measured St3gal-family genes, and the polysialyltransferases St8sia2 and St8sia4 were not induced or repressed, and the comparator perturbation St3gal5 likewise lacked non-target FDR hits. Thus, within Golgi sialylation and sialic-acid metabolism, any biochemical redundancy with St3gal2 is not visible as mRNA compensation here; only transcript abundance was assayed, not enzyme activity, substrate competition, or glycan-product flux.

Sox11 perturbation showed no robust differential-expression signature in this screen, and related SOXC or Sox11-network perturbations were similarly weak, so the data do not cleanly test Sox11 versus Sox4/Sox12 redundancy. Sox4 was likewise silent, Sox12 was not assayed, and prioritized neighbors such as Pou3f3, Klf7, Pax6, and Ednrb yielded at most isolated single-gene hits, leaving the expected SOXC neurogenesis and neuronal-differentiation module undetected. This convergence is further limited because most comparator perturbations, including Sox11, did not measurably deplete their own transcripts.

cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp280d perturbation showed a weak, exploratory HP1/CBX heterochromatin signal: Cbx5 was nominally decreased in four cell types—012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—while Cbx1 and Cbx3 were not nominally changed. This repeated Cbx5-down pattern partially echoes human ZNF280D partner annotations, but adjusted P values for Cbx5 were 1.0, no CBX proteins were perturbed here, and the cross-species interaction context does not establish CBX pathway regulation in mouse single-cell data.

Syn3 showed no FDR-supported transcriptional response: across the perturbation, no gene reached FDR<0.10 and the nominal tail was sparse and nonrecurrent, arguing against pathway enrichment from single-cell hits despite the expected synaptic-vesicle context. In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, Mapk1ip1 had the smallest nominal p value but remained nonsignificant after correction, and in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Ccdc28b and Psmc6 shared the lowest adjusted p value at FDR=0.353. This transcriptomic null does not exclude electrophysiological or vesicle-pool effects without large mRNA changes.

Reln perturbation did not resemble Grin1 or Grin2b perturbations, even though the NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations produced detectable single-cell RNA programs, indicating that Reln was effectively uncoupled from these NMDAR-subunit transcriptional signatures. In this dataset, the separation suggests that Reelin’s known modulation of NMDA-receptor and synaptic-plasticity signaling does not translate into the same transcriptomic response as loss of core NMDAR subunits. A key caveat is that prior work emphasizes receptor phosphorylation, calcium influx, and LTP, whereas this study measures single-cell RNA after genetic perturbation.

Trappc6b did not transcriptionally phenocopy the measured TRAPP II subunits Trappc9 or Trappc10 in this dataset. Although shared biology might be expected from TRAPP / ER-Golgi vesicle transport complex membership, all three perturbations were weak: Trappc9 and Trappc10 showed only nominal target reduction, had no FDR-significant genes, and their ranked signatures had near-zero Spearman correlation with Trappc6b, with little overlap among top genes. Interpretation is limited because other TRAPP components were not perturbed and Trappc9/10 knockdown was only nominal.

Smarcad1 targeting did not detectably engage the canonical SMARCAD1 heterochromatin maintenance or DNA double-strand-break repair transcriptional program in this assay. Across all 20 measured Smarcad1 cell types, no multiple-testing-corrected differentially expressed genes were found, and the Smarcad1 transcript itself was not significantly depleted in any cell type. The strongest nominal Smarcad1 mRNA decrease appeared in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, but with only 29 perturbed cells it remained non-significant and had no corrected downstream genes, so the result is a pan-assay weak-engagement null rather than a selective responder pattern.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Vps54 showed its only multiple-testing-significant response in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic cell type, whereas the GARP-complex partner Vps53 did not phenocopy this response there: the Vps54–Vps53 score correlation was low (0.155) and Vps53 had no FDR-significant genes. This separates Vps54 from Vps53 at the transcriptome level in this dataset, despite prior human-cell RNAi work suggesting similar effects of VPS52/VPS53/VPS54 on mannose-6-phosphate receptor-dependent lysosomal sorting. However, the Vps53 guides showed weak on-target mRNA engagement, so the apparent difference may reflect insufficient Vps53 perturbation rather than a true subunit-specific effect.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Ppargc1a did not behave interchangeably with its paralog Ppargc1b in this assay, particularly in 155 MB Glut cells. Across matched cell classes, Ppargc1a and Ppargc1b score vectors were nearly uncorrelated, and the only corrected Ppargc1b hit—Atp5b down in 155 MB Glut—was not reproduced by Ppargc1a in the same cell type. Although pathway context grouped these genes with Esrra/Nrf1 mitochondrial programs, both perturbations showed weak measured on-target mRNA effects, so the divergence could reflect perturbation quality rather than true paralog-specific biology.

Ubp1 did not show convergent Perturb-seq signatures with the assayed CP2/Grainyhead-family factors Tfcp2 or Grhl2. In cell-type-matched score-vector comparisons, Ubp1 signatures were near-zero correlated with both comparators, and Tfcp2 and Grhl2 perturbations produced zero FDR-positive downstream genes. Because these comparator perturbations also lacked robust self-knockdown or broader downstream signatures, the screen does not support functional interchangeability between Ubp1 and Tfcp2 or Grhl2, although this contrast is limited by weak target engagement and the absence of a TFCP2L1 perturbation.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc25a4 showed a largely target-only profile rather than a multi-gene downstream module across several neuronal classes, including 052 Pvalb Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. In the same dataset, and often in the same cell types, mitochondrial comparator perturbations of Opa1 and/or Dnm1l elicited broad FDR-level mitochondrial fusion/fission stress programs, such as in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. This contrast suggests the quiet Slc25a4 profile is unlikely to reflect a generic inability of these cells to mount mitochondrial transcriptional responses, while noting that Opa1 and Dnm1l are mitochondrial dynamics comparators rather than ANT1-complex members.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Nfix showed a sparse differential-expression pattern after multiple-testing correction, with the smallest adjusted p values outside L4/5 IT occurring in isolated, target-uncoupled genes rather than a recurrent NFIX program. In 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Cwc27 was the lowest-FDR row despite no measurable Nfix self-reduction; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ogfr was similarly isolated with essentially unchanged Nfix transcript; and in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Crat and Sntb2 had modest adjusted p values while Nfix was not nominally reduced. These rows are therefore better treated as validation candidates than as an NFIX pathway, especially since other Nfix isoforms or protein effects could have been missed and guide identities were unavailable.

Tfap2a perturbation did not elicit a detectable canonical AP-2 transcriptional response in the assayed adult-brain neurons: curated AP-2 cofactors and reported targets, including Cited2, Kctd1, Ep300, Pitx2, Hspd1, Nop2, and Mybl2, all remained FDR-null, indicating that the AP-2/TFAP2 transcriptional regulation program was not engaged or was uncoupled in these cells. This null result is notable because a productive TFAP2A perturbation might be expected to shift components of the Cited2/Ep300/Kctd1 and retinoic-acid-linked network, but many curated AP-2 targets derive from embryonic, cardiac, or other non-neuronal contexts and may not be expressed or wired in these neurons.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Tfap2a showed no significant downstream gene changes across its available cell-type signatures, and AP-2-associated neighbor perturbations did not converge on a TFAP2A-like program. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, only sparse exceptions were seen: Kctd1 and Crebbp produced a few significant rows, including a single Resp18 hit for Kctd1 in Pvalb, while Ep300, Gata3, Pax3, Pax6, Sox10, and Tfap2a were FDR-null. This exploratory pattern is limited by the absence of true AP-2 paralog perturbations and by weak self-transcript depletion for most comparators.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Sox5 perturbation produced FDR-significant expression changes only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where the response was limited to upregulated Dgkh and Tnnt1. These genes were uncoupled from canonical SoxD developmental transcriptional programs, as expected corticofugal or oligodendrocyte-related Sox5/Sox6 modules were not recovered and non-151 cell types showed only subthreshold outliers after correction. This argues against interpreting the TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Dgkh/Tnnt1 response as recovery of a known SOX5 developmental pathway, although Dgkh and Tnnt1 could still be indirect SOX5 targets and direct comparison to Sox6 or Sox13 was not possible.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Zkscan16 showed weak or discordant transcriptomic signatures that did not phenocopy Zkscan1, Zkscan3, Mecp2, or Zfp462 in adult mouse neurons, arguing against interchangeability of KRAB/SCAN zinc-finger regulation with the MeCP2/TRIM28 context here. Across 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, restricted top-gene correlations were small; Mkrn3 induction was most notable in subcortical classes, while cortical 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut instead showed near-threshold Zdhhc17 down-regulation. Trim28 was not perturbed in this dataset.

Unc13a perturbation showed no acute transcriptional paralog compensation across all 23 assayed neuronal subclasses: although Unc13a mRNA was partially reduced, Unc13b and Unc13c were neither nominally induced nor FDR-significant, and the broader presynaptic active-zone synaptic-vesicle priming/exocytosis program remained largely transcriptionally silent, including genes such as Snap25, Stxbp1, Cplx1, Syn1, Stx1b, and Dpp6. Thus, any functional redundancy among Munc13 isoforms in this system was not explained by rapid Unc13b/Unc13c mRNA upregulation, with the caveat that only mRNA was measured, not pre-existing protein, isoform localization, or synapse-type-specific buffering.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Srrm2 showed a high-response phenotype in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA that did not obviously converge with Son, suggesting the SON-SRRM2 nuclear-speckle scaffold axis was not interchangeable in this dataset. However, this comparison is engagement-limited: Son had no FDR<0.05 off-target genes in these three Srrm2-high groups, little correlation with Srrm2, and Son transcript FDR was 1.0, so the apparent non-equivalence should be treated as exploratory rather than a clean loss-of-function contrast.

Zfp609 perturbation did not coherently down-regulate the published Zfp609/Nipbl cortical-migration targets Sema3a, Nrp1, Plxnd1, and Gabbr2 in the sampled mouse-brain neuronal classes; across 88 gene-by-cell-type tests, all rows had FDR=1.0. This suggests that the Zfp609-Nipbl-Integrator, paused-RNA-polymerase-II promoter program described in embryonic cortical neural progenitors was not detectably active here and may diverge from Nipbl in these assayed states. Interpretation is limited because the dataset profiled neuronal cell classes rather than embryonic progenitors and showed weak, variable on-target Zfp609 knockdown.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Sdccag8 showed a negative result in 155 MB Glut cells: unlike Ahi1 and Cplane1 perturbations in the same cell type, which produced strong FDR-significant cis transcript loss of their target genes, Sdccag8 had no significant cis or trans row. This same-cell cross-perturbation contrast suggests that the null Sdccag8 result is not simply a property of 155 MB Glut cells and may reflect a target-engagement limitation specific to Sdccag8. The comparison is limited to cis transcript rows and does not imply that Ahi1 or Cplane1 downstream biology matches SDCCAG8 biology.

Washc4 perturbation showed no detectable transcriptional compensation among the other measured WASH core subunits: Washc1, Washc2, Washc3, and Washc5 mRNAs were measured but none changed significantly. This suggests that the weak Washc4 perturbation did not trigger a WASH-subunit mRNA feedback program, consistent with a setting where disease-related effects are thought to involve protein-complex destabilization rather than transcriptional regulation. Interpretation is limited, however, because Washc4 itself was not significantly depleted, and stronger neighboring responses were seen in endosomal trafficking genes in some glutamatergic cell types.

Zfp292 did not show detectable convergence with its predicted partners Zfp644 and Tcf20 in this dataset. Although Zfp644 was the top STRING partner and Tcf20 was also predicted to interact with Zfp292, both perturbations lacked corrected signatures, and Zfp644 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Zfp292 across common cell types. In the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut context, related chromatin-network neighbors were active, but Zfp292, Zfp644, and Tcf20 remained weak, so the putative Zfp292–Zfp644/Tcf20 transcription-factor module could neither be validated nor ruled out.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Vsx2 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut showed a nominal down-biased postsynaptic/dendritic-spine module, with synaptic genes such as Adgrb1, Homer1, Nptx1, Ephb2, Nos1ap, Gabbr1, Ppp3ca, Atp2b1, Dip2a, and Kcnn3 appearing in the downward tail. This module is biologically coherent, as top-tail genes were enriched for synapse and dendritic-spine terms, but it remains statistically exploratory because all named synaptic genes had FDR 0.94-1.0 and the signal depends on nominal ranks rather than adjusted significance.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Trim37 perturbation showed no detectable mRNA coupling to the peroxisomal matrix protein import/PEX5 stabilization pathway across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 308 CB GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba. None of 22 Pex/peroxisome marker transcripts met the dataset FDR threshold after Trim37 depletion, and available Pex1 perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Trim37. This negative result is caveated because Pex5 was not in the panel, Pex1 is only a pathway neighbor, and some direct TRIM37 substrates were absent; notably, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA showed a non-target module with Trim37, Fbxo3, and Senp5 down, yet peroxisome and PRC mRNA views remained negative.

Rab3gap1 did not yield a shared transcriptomic module with Rab3gap2 or Rab18 in this dataset, despite their curated biochemical relationship in the RAB3GAP/RAB18 vesicle-mediated transport axis. Rab3gap1 perturbation did not detectably alter Rab3gap2, Rab18, Rab3a/b/c/d, Rab5a, or Rab43 transcripts, and its all-gene signature was essentially uncorrelated with Rab3gap2 or Rab18 perturbations. In 052 Pvalb Gaba neurons, Rab3gap2 showed clear on-target depletion without a corrected downstream response, and in 155 MB Glut cells, nominal Rab3gap1 and Rab18 depletion still lacked FDR-significant downstream genes or convergence; only Rab3gap2 and Rab18 were available as related perturbations, while Rab3-family GTPases and Tbc1d20 were measured only as transcripts.

Tgif1 targeting showed no detectable acute transcriptional compensation by its paralog Tgif2: although Tgif2 was measurable across all 23 Tgif1 signatures, it was neither induced nor repressed after Tgif1 perturbation, with a maximum absolute score of 0.175 and uniformly nonsignificant values. This argues against TGIF paralog buffering through acute Tgif2 mRNA upregulation in the assayed cells, but the result is limited by the lack of a Tgif2 perturbation, unverified Tgif1 knockdown, and the possibility that compensation occurs at protein, chromatin, or developmental-selection levels.

Vps13a produced transcriptomic signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with Vps13b, Vps13c, and Vps13d across shared cell classes, indicating nonconvergent perturbation effects despite VPS13-family membership. In 155 MB Glut, Vps13a and Vps13c were both depleted yet correlated only weakly (r=0.009), and in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA Vps13a was the most negative transcript without any FDR-significant downstream genes. Overall, the dataset supports paralog-specific behavior in VPS13 phospholipid-transfer and membrane-contact biology, but this rests on weak whole-transcriptome signatures rather than strong response modules.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfhx4 showed little detectable transcriptional effect in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where its perturbation produced no FDR-resolved program, while the paralog Zfhx3 generated a significant thalamic program with five FDR < 0.05 genes that included Zfhx4 itself as a positive hit. Across ZFHX zinc-finger homeobox paralog perturbations, Zfhx3 and Zfhx4 score vectors were only weakly correlated (r = 0.062), arguing that Zfhx3 and Zfhx2 do not phenocopy Zfhx4 in this postmitotic class. This comparison is based on mRNA differential-expression correlations rather than direct redundancy or binding assays, and Zfhx2/Zfhx3 perturbation efficiency was not independently assessed.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Ocrl showed only isolated nominal endocytic and phosphoinositide-pathway transcript changes rather than a recurrent corrected module. In 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, Ap2m1 was nominally decreased, while in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Inpp5b and Ap2a2 were nominally increased. However, these cell types had weak measured Ocrl transcript knockdown, and all pathway-related rows remained nominal only, so the pattern appears buffered and divergent across related AP-2/clathrin-mediated endocytosis signals rather than a coherent transcriptional compensation program.

Slc25a27 perturbation under basal conditions showed weak target down with no multiple-testing-corrected downstream transcriptional module: no reproducible oxidative-stress, apoptosis, or oxidative-phosphorylation remodeling program was detected, and the strongest nominal genes were mostly cell-type singletons rather than a repeated response. This refines prior UCP4-related biology by suggesting that partial basal knockdown in these cells is not sufficient to produce a broad stress transcriptome, while still leaving open post-transcriptional effects on membrane potential, ROS, calcium, or ATP that would not be captured by mRNA readouts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp148 showed no strong transcriptomic surrogate in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal class, the clearest Zfp148-responsive population. In this class, the closest positive neighbor was Celf2 with only weak similarity (r=0.131) and the most negative was Esrra (r=-0.082), while Trp53 and Hdac8 were essentially uncorrelated, arguing against a simple p53-, HDAC-, KLF-family, or splicing-factor proxy for the Zfp148 program. Interpretation is limited because the paralog Zfp281 and cofactors Sp1, Sp3, and Hdac1 were not included in the perturbation library.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Vps53 showed mostly divergent, only weakly positive similarity to related trafficking perturbations in GARP/EARP and neighboring Golgi retrograde tether biology, including Vps54, Stx16, Tbc1d23, Cog4, and Cog5. In the two Vps53-responsive cell types, 191 MB P MY GABA and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, available comparators did not reproducibly phenocopy the Vps53 signature, and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Vps54 produced a 31-gene FDR response whereas Vps53 produced none. Given possible differences in guide efficiency, cell counts, and complex membership, this could reflect true subunit or context specificity, or a failure of the Vps53 perturbation to reach the same functional state.

Timp2 perturbation left the canonical TIMP/MMP transcriptional axis largely unchanged: across 22 Timp2 signatures, Mmp2, Mmp14, other measured MMPs (including Mmp9, Mmp15, Mmp16, and Mmp24), and Timp paralogs (Timp1, Timp3, Timp4) did not show detectable FDR-significant RNA responses, including in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut. This suggests acute Timp2 loss is transcriptionally uncoupled from the expected extracellular MMP biology, although sparse neuronal scRNA-seq may miss some MMP transcripts and unchanged mRNA does not test MMP2 activation or catalytic activity.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp949 showed signatures that were essentially uncoupled from Setdb1 and Chd4 across multiple neuronal cell types, including cortical glutamatergic, GABAergic, hypothalamic, midbrain, and cerebellar populations. Although KRAB-ZFP repression can use KAP1-SETDB1 and chromatin-corepressor machinery, Zfp949 did not phenocopy these pathway-adjacent perturbations: its score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Setdb1 or Chd4, and Zfp949 had no genome-wide significant downstream transcript at 10% FDR. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, despite the largest perturbed-cell count, no FDR-significant Zfp949 gene or Cdkn1b induction was detected, while matched Setdb1 and Chd4 effects were stronger.

Tbx19 perturbation did not activate or repress the canonical TBX19–POMC neuroendocrine axis in the assayed adult brain classes: Pomc and Pcsk1 were measured across Tbx19 cell classes and were not significantly changed, and the guide assignment also did not produce a measurable decrease of the Tbx19 transcript in any assayed class. These data therefore separate the pituitary POMC/ACTH differentiation pathway from broad adult neuronal contexts, with the caveat that Pomc and Pcsk1 are only proxies for the full corticotroph program and pituitary endocrine cells were not included.

Rxra showed only an exploratory synaptic signal after pooling weak nominal hits across cell types: the 105 genes with nominal p<0.001 were enriched for synapse/presynapse annotations, with mixed directions and genes such as Cacnb1, Stx6, Stx12, P2rx4, Brsk1, Rtn4r, Dnm1, Nlgn2, and Sv2b. This pattern is directionally consistent with published RXRA roles in dendritic spine and projection biology, but the signal was driven by cell-type-unique nominal hits, and no contributing gene was FDR-significant within its own cell type.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
full_finding_text: Mark3 perturbation did not produce a robust mRNA module for canonical MARK microtubule/Tau substrate genes in 308 CB GABA cells: Mapt, Map2, Map4, and Map1b were not FDR-significant, and even the strongest nominal pattern was only a weak Mark3 decrease accompanied by nominal Map1b loss in this cell type. The Mark3 transcriptome was largely orthogonal to tau/microtubule, AMPK-family, MAPK, and mTOR neighbor perturbations, suggesting that in these cells canonical MARK biology is transcriptionally uncoupled from MAP transcripts, with the caveat that the assay measures mRNA rather than Tau/MAP phosphorylation or microtubule state.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Rlf did not phenocopy its zinc-finger paralogs Zfp292 or Zfp654 in the assayed brain cells, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the only cell type with FDR-significant Rlf target-gene responses. In that thalamic class, all-gene score correlations between Rlf and the paralog perturbations were near zero (0.067 for Zfp292 and 0.039 for Zfp654), and neither paralog produced FDR-significant genes. Thus, within this Perturb-seq dataset, paralogy did not imply interchangeability, although the contrast is partly limited by the weak Zfp292 and Zfp654 signatures.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
full_finding_text: Slc1a1 showed a largely self-limited perturbation profile that differed from Slc1a2 across neuronal cell types, indicating that these EAAT-family perturbations were not interchangeable. Slc1a1 was most engaged in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where effects were mostly restricted to on-target repression; in L5 ET neurons, Ptpn23 was the lone significant non-target response. By contrast, Slc1a2 was strongest in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and neither perturbation induced compensatory Slc1a2, Slc1a3, or Slc6a1 transcripts. A caveat is that Slc1a6 and Slc1a7 were not available as comparator perturbations.

Trp73 did not phenocopy its p53-family paralogs in this dataset: same-cell Trp73 transcriptional signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Trp53 and Trp63, and p53-family perturbations did not produce shared same-cell signatures. Consistent with this, TP53-family apoptotic transcriptional markers such as Cdkn1a, Bax, Bbc3, Pmaip1, Mdm2, Fas, Apaf1, Casp1, Casp3, Casp9, and Perp were not detectably induced after Trp73 and were uncorrelated across the p53-family comparators. However, all three targets showed weak perturbational phenotypes without FDR-significant hits, so the contrast likely reflects limited readout rather than true antagonism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
full_finding_text: Zmynd8 perturbation recurrently increased Zfp532, a mouse ortholog of a ZMYND8-associated zinc-finger partner, most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and nominally across 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA. This pattern suggests a candidate compensatory response within a ZMYND8-associated KDM5C and GATAD2A/NuRD recruitment hub, with convergence noted for Kdm5c while available NuRD or Zmynd11 perturbations were divergent. Only Zfp532 showed a recurrent transcript increase; Zfp592 and Zfp687 were not co-induced, and partner protein abundance was not measured.

Trem2 showed a notably silent perturbation in this dataset: where the target transcript was measured, significant Trem2 RNA depletion was not detected after Trem2 guide assignment, and no transcriptome-wide downstream response was significant in any assayed cell class. This null was not a universal assay failure, because the same workflow detected strong on-target knockdown of Ctsb in 17 of 22 Trem2-assayed cell types and a narrower Grn effect in one thalamic class. However, Ctsb and Grn are not TREM2 complex members, so this contrast speaks to detectability rather than shared mechanism.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc25a46 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA most closely resembled Slc25a4 and Slc25a12 perturbations: strong depletion of the target transcript with little or no recurrent non-target differential expression. In these same cell classes, Opa1 and Dnm1l instead induced a recurrent amino-acid/integrated-stress-like program that was not measurably induced by Slc25a46. Thus, despite family relatedness, the atypical outer-membrane-associated Slc25a46 should not be assumed to phenocopy mitochondrial-dynamics hits at the RNA level.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Slc25a46 perturbation produced a buffered or absent broad RNA response: although Slc25a46 itself was significantly depleted in three subcortical cell classes—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA—no experiment-wide significant non-target transcripts were detected. In these same classes, Opa1 and Dnm1l, linked to mitochondrial outer-membrane dynamics and MICOS/cristae maintenance, induced recurrent stress modules, highlighting the contrast with Slc25a46. This muted profile is compatible with compensation or buffering, but remains exploratory because the dataset lacks longitudinal sampling, mutant-mRNA decay, protein measurements, and rescue experiments.

Zfp236 perturbation most reproducibly produced a down-regulated Ogt plus Eif4a2 module: Ogt decreased in all 22 cell-type signatures and was FDR-significant in 11, while Eif4a2 decreased in 19 of 22 and was FDR-significant in 9. The largest corrected response was in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells, with similar modules in midbrain glutamatergic, hindbrain/midbrain GABAergic, and hypothalamic/mammillary glutamatergic classes, sometimes alongside Cpt1c, Kmt5b, or Gdi1. This pattern is weakly similar to Gfpt1 and Ogt perturbations in O-GlcNAc/hexosamine signaling, but the data are mRNA-only and do not show reduced OGT or EIF4A2 protein, and Zfp236 target-transcript depletion itself was not observed.

Trappc9 showed transcriptomic signatures that were essentially uncorrelated with Trappc10 and Trappc6b across every shared cell type, even though all three proteins are annotated within the TRAPPII/RAB GEF vesicle-trafficking network. This argues that partial knockdown of individual TRAPP subunits was not transcriptionally interchangeable in this neuronal Perturb-seq setting. A key caveat is that all three perturbations were weak at FDR-corrected single-gene resolution, and the comparisons were based on mRNA-derived score vectors rather than direct protein-complex activity.

Pde4b was not transcriptionally interchangeable with the closest assayed PDE4 paralog, Pde4d: across the 22 shared cell types, their Perturb-seq differential-expression score vectors were essentially uncorrelated, and Pde4d produced no adjusted hits of its own. In the one highlighted context, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, this fit a weak target decrease with buffering and Pde4d divergence within cAMP catabolic process/PDE4 signaling. Pde4b signatures in the two adjusted-hit cell types also did not closely match selected cAMP, PKA, EPAC, RAF, or MAPK neighbor perturbations, though this comparison was based on mRNA DE rather than cAMP microdomains or phosphoproteomic outputs.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zic1 perturbation produced a small, cell-type-restricted response centered in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where an exploratory neuronal/synaptic pattern showed mixed nominal up- and down-shifts in Grm5, Nrg3, Stxbp1, Slc6a17, Scn1a, Rims2, Gap43, and Calb1. This suggests the acute Zic1 response may touch neuronal signaling genes in addition to developmental programs, but all of these module genes remained nominal after multiple-testing correction, so the pattern should be treated as a hypothesis for independent validation.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Sqstm1 depletion in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut was accompanied by a localized nominal increase in Nbr1, with the on-target Sqstm1 decrease itself only near significant. This pattern suggests a weak, cell-type-restricted compensation hypothesis between the p62/NBR1-family selective-autophagy receptors within the broader selective autophagy and mitophagy context. However, the Nbr1 signal did not survive multiple testing, this class had 104 perturbed cells, and no genes reached FDR < 0.05, so the observation should be treated as tentative.

Xpr1 perturbation did not transcriptionally phenocopy Slc20a2, Ppip5k2, or Pdgfrb in matched neuronal contexts: across 13 neuronal cell types, all-gene score-vector correlations were essentially zero. This suggests that, in the acute transcriptome, XPR1-dependent inorganic phosphate export and the broader PFBC phosphate-transporter network were uncoupled from these related perturbations. However, because Slc20a2, Ppip5k2, and Pdgfrb also lacked FDR-significant knockdown of their own transcripts in the same neuronal settings, the absent correlation could reflect weak target engagement rather than true biological separation.

Sipa1l3 showed no consistent transcriptomic alignment with the Rap pathway neighbors Rapgef2 and Rapgef4 across matched brain classes: their perturbation signatures were essentially uncorrelated, neither phenocopying nor opposing the Sipa1l3 profile. This suggests that, despite Sipa1l3 being RapGAP-class and Rapgef2/Rapgef4 being RapGEFs, the Perturb-seq data do not support a simple RapGAP/RapGEF expression axis downstream of Sipa1l3 loss. The comparison is conservative, however, because Sipa1l3 RNA engagement was weak and restricted-neighbor ranks were similar to safe-target controls, so these relationships remain exploratory rather than pathway-confirming.

Trp53 did not show a convergent p53-family response in unstressed brain single-cell perturbations: Trp63 and Trp73 were likewise FDR-null, had near-zero score correlations with Trp53, and did not display clear target-transcript engagement. In this assay, the p53-family transcription factors therefore appeared silent and uncorrelated under basal conditions, suggesting weak expression or functional inactivity rather than interchangeability. Interpretation is limited because canonical p53-axis comparators such as Mdm2 and Mdm4, as well as other DNA-damage regulators, were not perturbed.

Ptprn showed a self-only transcriptomic perturbation pattern, and its secretory-granule neighbors Ptprn2, Cpe, and Pcsk2 behaved similarly, with target transcripts depleted but no shared significant nonself mRNA module. In contrast, the synaptic-fusion comparators Snap25 and especially Stxbp1 produced detectable non-target differential expression in the same dataset, separating regulated dense-core secretory vesicle biology from vesicle docking/fusion at the scRNA readout level. This contrast is dataset-level and may also reflect differences in target expression, perturbation strength, or cell fitness.

Syt14 showed no detectable on-target transcriptional effect in this assay: across 21 contrasts, its target transcript appeared in the tests but was never significantly depleted, and its transcriptome-wide signatures were essentially uncorrelated with those of the synaptotagmin paralog Syt2 in matched cell classes. By contrast, Syt2 produced significant self-transcript depletion in 155 MB Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, indicating that this dataset can register at least one synaptotagmin-family perturbation. This cautions against treating Syt14 and Syt2 as interchangeable readouts here, although the contrast cannot distinguish Syt14-specific biology from weaker guide performance or lower Syt14 expression.

Slc52a2 showed no FDR-supported transcriptional program across the 23 assayed neuronal classes, so canonical vitamin B2 riboflavin transport and FAD/FMN-linked mitochondrial biology appeared transcriptionally uncoupled from this perturbation. No recurrent redox, OXPHOS, or vitamin-B2 module emerged, and even the most recurrent nominal hit, Cox4i1, remained non-significant. This negative result should be interpreted cautiously because Slc52a1, Slc52a3, Rfk, and Flad1 were not targetable in the library, and the assay measured mRNA rather than riboflavin, FMN, FAD, or flavoprotein activity.

Sos1 showed no evident transcriptomic substitute in its paralog Sos2: in shared cell types, Sos2 perturbations had no FDR-significant gene responses, and Sos1–Sos2 score-vector correlations were essentially zero, indicating uncorrelated weak signatures within the SOS paralog RasGEF module. This suggests that, in this dataset, Sos2 did not phenocopy Sos1 at the whole-transcriptome level. However, both paralogs were weak perturbations here, and direct on-target RNA measurements showed only partial, cell-type-variable Sos1 depletion, so the lack of similarity cannot distinguish true functional non-equivalence from limited knockdown.

Ogt perturbation was accompanied by recurrent reduction of the opposing O-GlcNAcase transcript Oga, with negative scores in all 21 Ogt tests and FDR-significant downregulation in 6 of 21 cell types, consistent with O-GlcNAc cycling and homeostasis. This transcript-level pattern was seen in strong responders including 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, but Oga itself was not directly perturbed, so the result is best viewed as a compensatory readout rather than a direct perturbation comparison.

Tshz2 perturbation in brain cells did not detectably reactivate the proposed TSHZ2–GLI1/CtBP module: Gli1, Aebp1, Cxcr4, and Ctbp2 showed no measurable shift in any covered brain cell group. This contrasts with mammary epithelial tumor models, where TSHZ2 loss has been reported to release GLI1 and increase AEBP1 and CXCR4, so the brain data caution against projecting that mechanism onto these mouse brain cell classes. Interpretation is limited because several GLI-axis transcripts were very lowly expressed in the dataset.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
full_finding_text: Sp4 showed a notable caveat in this dataset: the Sp4 transcript increased rather than decreased in Sp4-assigned cells, including the strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and nominally in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and it was not FDR-depleted in any of the 22 profiled classes. Thus, Sp4 mRNA appears to be an inducible readout or retained mutant transcript rather than a proxy for SP4 protein loss. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the SP4 response was cell-class-selective, with recurrent Tsga10 and Abhd11 upregulation, 151-specific Stxbp2/Tspan17 downregulation, no canonical NMDAR/NT3/Nwk2 mRNA activation, and divergence from assayed SP/KLF perturbations; SP4 protein was not measured.

Rmnd1 showed a weak mitochondrial/OXPHOS perturbation response in this dataset: unlike Opa1, Ndufs2, and Ndufs8, which produced clear genome-wide FDR-level effects, Rmnd1 had no multiple-testing-corrected downstream hits and near-zero full-transcriptome correlations with those stronger comparators, while the STRING-neighbor Clpp showed a similarly buffered, non-convergent profile. This pattern was seen even in 052 Pvalb Gaba, the best on-target depletion context, and in 155 MB Glut, where Rmnd1 produced only nominal mt-Co2 induction despite strong comparator responses. Comparators differ in function and target engagement, and the correlation analysis used precomputed Wilcoxon scores rather than raw single-cell counts.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Tardbp showed a distinct loss-of-function transcriptomic program that Fus and Matr3 did not phenocopy in Tardbp-sensitive hindbrain/thalamic groups, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In these contexts, Tardbp produced strong non-target responses and recurrent modules, whereas Fus and Matr3 signatures had near-zero correlation or no phenocopy despite being functionally linked RNA-binding proteins, with Fus also serving as an ALS-family comparator. This divergence is based on transcriptomic readouts only and only in cell types where comparator engagement was measurable.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Slc9a9 showed a null-like result in this dataset: its endogenous transcript was not significantly depleted in any assayed cell class, and its transcriptome score vectors did not converge with the related intracellular Na+/H+ exchanger Slc9a7. In contrast, Slc9a7 was measurably depleted in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 155 MB Glut, yet Slc9a9–Slc9a7 correlations remained near zero (-0.071 to 0.055). This suggests the Slc9a9 null is not a general failure to detect organellar cation/proton exchangers, while noting the comparison is between paralogs with overlapping but distinct organelles.

Upf3b was the most recurrent nominal positive regulator of Inpp5f across the perturbation panel, with positive nominal recurrence for Inpp5f seen across eight cell types and Upf3b ranking as the top Inpp5f inducer in seven of them. This makes the Inpp5f response appear more Upf3b-skewed than a single-cell-type view would suggest, while also showing partial convergence from RNA-processing or decay neighbors Hnrnpc, Srsf1, and Xrn1, which recurred across five, four, and three cell types, respectively. The pattern is hypothesis-generating because it is defined by nominal recurrence for one measured gene, and direct contrasts with UPF3B paralogs or core NMD/EJC factors were not available.

Tecr knockdown did not produce compensatory transcript induction in the canonical very-long-chain fatty-acyl-CoA elongation and lipid-regulatory program: across 566 measured rows, Elovl1-7, Hacd1-4, Hsd17b12, Pecr, Decr1, Fads1/2, Scd1/2, Srebf1/2 and related transcripts showed no FDR-significant changes. This suggests the measured RNA network was not transcriptionally rebalanced despite TECR’s placement in ER VLCFA and sphingolipid pathways, although key direct genetic comparators were not perturbed and lipid flux or products were not measured.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
full_finding_text: Vps35l did not phenocopy Vps35 in this screen: across shared cell types including 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Vps35l-to-Vps35 transcriptomic correlations were near zero, with only a weak correlation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut. Vps35l perturbation showed buffered mRNA responses without FDR-significant downstream signatures even where self-depletion was nominally strongest, and although Washc4 and Vps35 were assayed, direct Retriever/Commander comparators such as Vps26c, Vps29, Ccdc22, and Ccdc93 were absent, limiting epistasis testing within the SNX17-Retriever-CCC-WASH endosomal cargo recycling pathway.

P2rx2 showed a weak perturbation response in this dataset, and the available purinergic relatives P2ry12 and P2ry14 behaved similarly: all had zero genes at adjusted p<0.05, and P2rx2 signatures were not positively correlated with the two P2Y perturbations within cell types, with near-zero correlations in most contexts. In 308 CB GABA, P2rx2 showed only moderate whole-signature correlations, including an anticorrelation with P2ry14, but its CB GABA genes were still FDR-negative. These results refine broader purinergic pathway links, noting that P2Y receptors are GPCRs rather than P2X ion-channel subunits, and direct P2X paralog perturbations were not assayed.

Smarca4 perturbation did not produce detectable Smarca2 mRNA induction across the assayed brain cell types, including the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population, where the SMARCA2/SMARCA4 alternative ATPase module also showed only weak ATPase-subunit signatures relative to selected core subunits. Thus, in this acute mouse-brain Perturb-seq setting, any buffering of Smarca4 loss does not appear to occur through transcriptional upregulation of Smarca2. This does not exclude compensation via basal SMARCA2 protein, paralog redistribution, or other remodelers, which would not be captured by a Smarca2 mRNA readout.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Zfp799 did not phenocopy Setdb1 despite the expected KRAB/C2H2 zinc-finger–KAP1/TRIM28–SETDB1 repression link. Across shared cell types, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 308 CB GABA, Setdb1 showed corrected responses in several classes, but Zfp799–Setdb1 coding-gene vectors remained near zero correlation and Zfp799 had no target depletion or corrected DE genes, with only weak nearest-neighbor structure in 308 CB GABA. This uncoupling may reflect Setdb1’s global chromatin role, Zfp799’s predicted sequence specificity, or weak Zfp799 knockdown.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
full_finding_text: Zfp799 showed no corrected signatures in the atlas, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where it was a nominally strong context and Setdb1-responsive context, with no target depletion, no FDR hits, and no Setdb1-like vector. This silence does not appear to reflect a generic zinc-finger perturbation failure, because broad zinc-finger controls such as Zfp423 and Zfp236 produced corrected signatures, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. However, the panel lacked the close Zfp799 paralogs Zfp870 and Zfp871, so direct tests of redundancy or interchangeability within the local Zfp799 cluster were not possible.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
full_finding_text: Ube3a did not phenocopy core mTOR-pathway perturbations in this screen: across 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA, Tsc1 and Tsc2 produced strong, FDR-significant transcriptional states, whereas Ube3a was weak and nearly uncorrelated with either target. Even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the strongest Ube3a signal had FDR 0.1367 and no resolved downstream genes. This lack of convergence should be interpreted cautiously, because Ube3a is an upstream E3 ligase linked to p18/LAMTOR1 turnover and mTORC1, not a core TSC brake, and the perturbation was a partial knockdown with protein-level substrates.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Zmynd11 showed a much weaker chromatin-regulator perturbation response than several related perturbations in the same neuronal strata. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut cells, Zmynd11 had nominal target depletion but no FDR-significant downstream signature, whereas Chd8, Zmynd8, Adnp, Kdm5c, Deaf1, and Mga produced significant signatures, indicating the Zmynd11 null is not a generic inability of these classes to report chromatin perturbation. In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Zmynd11 showed its strongest target-transcript decrement, but the effect remained limited to the target row. Comparator guide sets and cell counts differed, so stronger comparator signatures do not by themselves prove equal target engagement.

Tbx1 perturbation did not elicit the canonical TBX1 cardiogenic readouts in this neuronal assay: Isl1, Fgf8, and Fgf10 were all unchanged across neuronal cell classes, consistent with the TBX1 cardiogenesis/second-heart-field ISL1-FGF8-FGF10 program being uncoupled here. This negative result was observed at steady-state mRNA only, and the assayed cells were brain neurons rather than embryonic pharyngeal mesoderm or second-heart-field progenitors, so the screen did not place Tbx1 within its known developmental circuitry in this context.

Foxp2 did not show convergent transcriptomic signatures with the available FOXP-family perturbations, as Foxp2 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Foxp1 and Foxp3, despite reported FOXP-family relatedness and dimerization-dependent transcriptional mechanisms. This suggests the Perturb-seq run did not recover the expected FOXP-family transcriptional module. However, Foxp4 was not included, and Foxp1 and Foxp3 perturbations also lacked FDR-supported differential expression, so this should be interpreted as a failure to recover relatedness rather than evidence for antagonistic FOXP biology.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
full_finding_text: Cckbr perturbation in 052 Pvalb Gaba showed only nominal Cckbr mRNA depletion and no corrected downstream differential expression, indicating a weak or subtype-diluted RNA response rather than a broad Pvalb transcriptional program. This pattern is consistent with CCK2 receptor biology in which signaling may be acute and cell-subtype-specific, including calcium/cation pathways, so the lack of a corrected transcriptomic response should not be overinterpreted as lack of function. A key caveat is that prior evidence comes from rat hippocampal PV basket cells, whereas this dataset pools mouse Pvalb neurons across regions and measures RNA rather than electrophysiology or calcium.

Htr3b showed a transcriptional response that was essentially uncoupled from Htr3a, despite both encoding partner subunits of the serotonin-gated cation-selective 5-HT3 receptor. In matched cell types, Htr3a-versus-Htr3b perturbation score correlations stayed near zero, and the two subunit perturbations did not yield detectably similar RNA signatures. However, both perturbations also lacked target-transcript depletion, so this contrast reflects a failure of detectable RNA coupling in the Perturb-seq readout rather than evidence that the subunits have distinct channel physiology.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
full_finding_text: Ncoa3 perturbation did not show corrected evidence of compensatory Ncoa1 induction. Across three glutamatergic classes—027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut—Ncoa1 was only weakly lower at nominal significance, with all changes failing correction (FDR=1.0), and Ncoa1 perturbation signatures were not similar to Ncoa3 signatures. In the SRC/p160 nuclear-receptor coactivation context, this exploratory pattern argues against a strong Ncoa1 up-regulation buffer after Ncoa3 loss, but it should not be taken as evidence for paralog repression.

Cd3e perturbation in 22 tested brain cell classes was uncoupled from canonical TCR signaling at the transcriptomic level: despite CD3E being placed upstream of CD3/TCR-zeta phosphorylation, ZAP70 recruitment, and downstream TCR signaling, no gene set or individual transcript showed supported activation or repression of these pathways. No downstream transcript met conventional or relaxed multiple-testing thresholds, Cd3e itself showed no supported on-target depletion or induction, and related CD3/TCR perturbations such as Cd247 likewise did not reveal a robust transcriptional program. This null result is limited by transcriptomic readouts, which do not directly measure proximal phosphorylation events such as ZAP70 or ITAM phosphorylation.

Pak3 perturbation showed no evidence of transcriptional compensation by its group-I paralogs: Pak1 and Pak2 mRNAs were not induced in any assayed Pak3 cell type, including 155 MB Glut, 308 CB GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. More broadly, transcripts in RAC1/CDC42-activated group-I PAK signaling, such as Rac1, Cdc42, Limk1, Mapk1, Map2k1, Arhgef6, and Arhgef7, were not reproducibly changed. This suggests that any buffering of PAK3 loss is unlikely to reflect a broad Pak1/Pak2 mRNA feedback loop, although weak Pak3 self-knockdown means stronger protein loss could still reveal compensation.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
full_finding_text: Gria3 showed only a single exploratory signal: in 145 MH-LH TH Glut cells, Jmjd1c was upregulated, but Gria3 itself was not reduced in that same contrast. Because this comparison was supported by only 37 perturbed cells and the effect crossed only an FDR < 0.1 threshold, the result is better viewed as an isolated, hypothesis-generating cell-state signal rather than evidence for a Gria3 loss-of-function or AMPA receptor pathway response.

cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
full_finding_text: Mcts1 showed no convincing on-target transcriptional program in this dataset. The strongest adjusted near-hit was Lpgat1 up-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, but this signal was uncoupled from Mcts1 transcript engagement: in the same cell type, Mcts1 RNA was unchanged and ranked 9958/16539 genes by nominal p value. Because Lpgat1 also narrowly missed FDR < 0.05 and lacks orthogonal guide-level or protein validation, it is better treated as an unstable or possibly off-target-associated marker rather than evidence for a basal-ganglia GABA-specific Mcts1 program.

Calm2 showed much weaker RNA-level perturbation than its identical-protein paralogs Calm1 and Calm3: target transcripts passed FDR in only 1 of 22 cell types for Calm2, versus 10 of 22 for Calm1 and 13 of 22 for Calm3, with median on-target logFCs of -0.170, -0.629, and -0.746, respectively. Thus Calm2 nulls are better read as weak-perturbation nulls than as evidence that calmodulin is dispensable. In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, related calcium/calmodulin perturbations produced secondary transcriptional effects, but Calm2 did not because on-target depletion was weak; in 155 MB Glut, the Calm1/2/3 core showed on-target depletion with buffered downstream RNA. Guide activity, transcript abundance, and cell sampling are confounded, and protein knockdown was not measured.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
full_finding_text: Pex14 showed stronger target engagement than related peroxin perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Pex14 was strongly self-depleted, including the second-strongest FDR-significant depletion and, in one case, the only FDR-significant gene. By contrast, Pex1 and Pex13 did not significantly deplete their own transcripts, so they were not clean phenocopies of the peroxisomal matrix-protein import / PEX13-PEX14 docking program. In 151 TH cells, Pex13 showed only a weak Insig1 sterol echo, best treated as an engagement caveat rather than evidence that the Pex14 program is unique.

Rorc perturbation in the assayed brain populations showed no detectable RORγt/Th17–IL-17 module response: across all 22 Rorc-assayed cell types, there were no multiple-testing-significant differential genes, and Il17a, Il17f, Il23r, and Ccr6 were not induced or repressed. This brain-cell negative result refines, rather than contradicts, immune literature on RORγt, because the experiment profiled neuronal classes rather than Th17 cells or lymphoid-tissue inducer contexts, so the absence of canonical Th17 effector signatures is expected and should not be taken as CNS safety evidence.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
full_finding_text: Plxna1 perturbation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA showed a nominal increase in Arhgap35, a RhoGAP-like gene that nearly reached FDR significance, but Plxna1 itself was essentially unchanged in the same contrast. This makes the observation a biologically suggestive yet unsupported near miss rather than evidence of canonical semaphorin/plexin cytoskeletal signaling activation. In the broader pathway context, Plxna1 changes were generally accompanied by sparse, uncoupled, or subthreshold downstream mRNA responses, including Arhgap35.

Ywhag showed consistent depletion of its own transcript in every perturbation contrast, yet no non-target FDR hits, indicating a transcriptionally buffered response within 14-3-3 phosphoserine-adapter signaling. Ywhae and Ywhaz likewise lacked secondary FDR hits, but their own transcript depletion was much weaker than Ywhag, so this comparison serves as a negative control rather than evidence that 14-3-3 paralogs are interchangeable or biologically silent. The screen did not include Ywhaq, Ywhab, Ywhah, or Sfn, and paralog protein depletion was not measured.
